About SNMP Top About SNMP The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a trouble-free network management tool that can monitor and manage of diverse range of devices on a computer network, such as routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers.

Title: About SNMP
About SNMP Top About SNMP The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a trouble-free network management tool that can monitor and manage of diverse range of devices on a computer network, such as routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. Any SNMP network management system requires the following components: - A manager, which is responsible for managing and monitoring SNMP devices, by performing the required network management functions. Note: Any computer or terminal running a SNMP manager is known as a Network Management Station (the NMS). - An agent (NOT to be confused with an Adroit Agent or tag-type), which is simply a piece of software running on a device that is required to be managed. This agent is responsible for retrieving and setting management data, known as managed objects, for its device. Note: Any device that does not have an agent is referred to as being unmanageable. These SNMP managed objects might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and so on, that directly relate to the current operation of the device in question. For details, see SNMP Managed Objects . -->

About SNMP Traps About SNMP Traps SNMP traps are unsolicited SNMP messages that devices send to notify an SNMP manager of significant events.

Title: About SNMP Traps
About SNMP Traps About SNMP Traps SNMP traps are unsolicited SNMP messages that devices send to notify an SNMP manager of significant events. Each message is known as 'a trap of the event', hence the term SNMP traps. IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. Using SNMP traps can reduce the number of SNMP managed objects (values) that you need to monitor (poll) for each device. In other words, instead of monitoring every OID value on every device, by using SNMP traps, a device can simply inform its SNMPManager agent of the important values, which are then pushed to the SNMPManager when an event occurs. Note: This will also increase your required scan point allocation, since one scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. To enable the receipt of traps for an SNMPManager agent: Check the Enable traps checkbox (BOOLEAN trapEnabled slot), in the Connection settings section of the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog, which is cleared (disabled) by default. Note1: You also need to Enable polling (the start slot) before you will receive traps. Note2: Adroit relies on the SNMP Trap Service to receive traps, which is installed with the SNMP Service. By definition a trap can either be simple - one OID (unique or not) OR complex- multiple OIDs (unique or not). Click for how to handle traps: - you need to create a script to process non-unique OIDs - you can manually add unique OIDs to the OID list, so that the value of its associated Tag is updated when this trap is fired. The SNMP Manager provides the following two trap handling Queues (which are FIFO in nature i.e. First In, First Out): Note: The trap queues are processed from the oldest to the newest trap. - the first or main trap queue collects all the incoming traps - the second or work queue is used to hold the remainder variable sets (described below) for external parsing. This queue ensures that the trap handling scripts no longer need to ensure stack integrity. So now the script ONLY needs to monitor the following two size slots to ensure correct operation: - trapCount (INTEGER): The number of OIDs traps (and their sub-traps) contained in the main trap queue (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is the number of OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap). - trapWorkCount (INTEGER): The number of remainder OIDs sub traps contained in the working trap queue (for simple traps this is NOT used, for complex traps this is the number of remainder OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap, minus the first one which was passed through to the trap slots directly). One trap event may consist of one or more trap variable sets, and one trap variable set consists of the following set of slots: - trapGeneric (INTEGER): An Integer value of the generic code or identification of this trap OID. - trapSpecific (INTEGER): An Integer value of the specific code or identification of this trap OID. - trapOID (VARSTRING): The OID, in numeric format, which identifies the SNMP managed object for this event. - trapValue (VARSTRING): The value of the OID specified by trapOID . - trapTime (TIME): The time that the value, specified by trapValue , occurred. - trapType (INTEGER): An Integer indicator of the return type of the value, specified by trapValue , for information purposes only. For details, see OID Return Type Indicators.

This indicator can help you to determine which tag you should use to store this value.

Title: About SNMP Traps
This indicator can help you to determine which tag you should use to store this value. These slots are marked as empty when there is no trap to parse, so triggering trapPop is this case does nothing. Once the SNMPManager agent receives the traps for the device that it is managing: - the Traps status bit is enabled (set) - these incoming SNMP messages are stored in the main trap queue Triggering the trapPop will transfer the trap variable set to the slots above for use by a domain specific script. - trapPop (BOOLEAN): Set this slot to 1 (via a script or button etc.) to read the first trap off the main trap queue, which reduces the trapCount slot by the number of OIDs in this trap (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is more than 1). Simple traps (only one set) are therefore pushed directly to the set slots and not stored in the work queue at all, which is only of the remainder sets. WARNING! Once a trap has been read off a queue it is discarded and cannot be accessed again. Note1: You also need to Enable polling (the start slot) before you will receive traps. Note2: Adroit relies on the SNMP Trap Service to receive traps, which is installed with the SNMP Service. (It is advisable to add these two services to the Agent Server dependencies list if running the Agent Server as a service.) -->

By definition a trap can either be simple - one OID (unique or not) OR complex- multiple OIDs (unique or not). Click for how to handle traps: - you need to create a script to process non-unique OIDs - you can manually add unique OIDs to the OID list, so that the value of its associated Tag is updated when this trap is fired. The SNMP Manager provides the following two trap handling Queues (which are FIFO in nature i.e. First In, First Out): Note: The trap queues are processed from the oldest to the newest trap. - the first or main trap queue collects all the incoming traps - the second or work queue is used to hold the remainder variable sets (described below) for external parsing. This queue ensures that the trap handling scripts no longer need to ensure stack integrity. So now the script ONLY needs to monitor the following two size slots to ensure correct operation: - trapCount (INTEGER): The number of OIDs traps (and their sub-traps) contained in the main trap queue (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is the number of OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap). - trapWorkCount (INTEGER): The number of remainder OIDs sub traps contained in the working trap queue (for simple traps this is NOT used, for complex traps this is the number of remainder OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap, minus the first one which was passed through to the trap slots directly). One trap event may consist of one or more trap variable sets, and one trap variable set consists of the following set of slots: - trapGeneric (INTEGER): An Integer value of the generic code or identification of this trap OID. - trapSpecific (INTEGER): An Integer value of the specific code or identification of this trap OID.

- trapOID (VARSTRING): The OID, in numeric format, which identifies the SNMP managed object for this event.

Title: About SNMP Traps
- trapOID (VARSTRING): The OID, in numeric format, which identifies the SNMP managed object for this event. - trapValue (VARSTRING): The value of the OID specified by trapOID . - trapTime (TIME): The time that the value, specified by trapValue , occurred. - trapType (INTEGER): An Integer indicator of the return type of the value, specified by trapValue , for information purposes only. For details, see OID Return Type Indicators. This indicator can help you to determine which tag you should use to store this value. These slots are marked as empty when there is no trap to parse, so triggering trapPop is this case does nothing. Once the SNMPMgr agent receives the traps for the device that it is managing: - the Traps status bit is enabled (set) - these incoming SNMP messages are stored in the main trap queue Triggering the trapPop will transfer the trap variable set to the slots above for use by a domain specific script. - trapPop (BOOLEAN): Set this slot to 1 (via a script or button etc.) to read the first trap off the main trap queue, which reduces the trapCount slot by the number of OIDs in this trap (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is more than 1). Simple traps (only one set) are therefore pushed directly to the set slots and not stored in the work queue at all, which is only of the remainder sets. WARNING! Once a trap has been read off a queue it is discarded and cannot be accessed again. Note1: You also need to Enable polling (the start slot) before you will receive traps. Note2: Adroit relies on the SNMP Trap Service to receive traps, which is installed with the SNMP Service. (It is advisable to add these two services to the Agent Server dependencies list if running the Agent Server as a service.)

About the AlarmManagement Database Top About the AlarmManagement Database The OLE DB compatible database specified by an AlarmManagement agent is the repository of all the logged incidents.

Title: About the AlarmManagement Database
About the AlarmManagement Database Top About the AlarmManagement Database The OLE DB compatible database specified by an AlarmManagement agent is the repository of all the logged incidents. This database allows you to obtain reports and KPIs focused around delivering a clear set of information on which the operators can act. The AlarmManagement agent provides the View Data and View Graph dialogs to allow users to analyse the data contained in its database. However, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. For this reason, it is necessary to know the structure of the tables within the OLE DB database that the AlarmManagement agent populates. This database records all the incidents including the time of incident, time of acknowledgement and time the incident cleared. IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. Each incident is logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent, so that it is possible to unify your alarm management for your enterprise and have more than one AlarmManagement agent log incidents to the SAME database. In this case please ensure that your AlarmManagement agent are uniquely named. The two primary tables in this database are the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents and Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents tables, which store all the logged incidents. An important field in these tables is the IncidentID field, which uniquely identifies each incident in this database. So by querying an entry in this field you can find out ALL the information pertaining to a specific alarm/event, such as every time this incident has been logged. ALL incidents found in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table as a result of the last Agent Server session are marked as acknowledged and their active times are set to zero.

- If these entries do not require reasons and/or notes then they are automatically added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table.

Title: About the AlarmManagement Database
- If these entries do not require reasons and/or notes then they are automatically added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. - If the entries require reasons and/or notes, then they will remain in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table until these entries have been completed by the operator. For a description of each of the tables and their fields, see AlarmManagement Database Tables . -->

About the Connectors Top About the Connectors The Adroit DB Generator requires a specific Connector to connect to and access the information stored in each required database of the 3 rd party application.

Title: About the Connectors
About the Connectors Top About the Connectors The Adroit DB Generator requires a specific Connector to connect to and access the information stored in each required database of the 3 rd party application. Each Connector can create one or more Links that actually connect to the specific applications and are configured to create .WGP files from them. Since these Connectors are separate modules (.DLL files) that can be added or removed, you can develop your own Connectors to allow the Adroit DB Generator to creates Adroit agent databases from your 3 rd party application. The Connector DLL files: - Adhere to the following naming convention: dbconn_*.dll, where * represents the unique name of the specific Connector. For instance, the CSV Connector file is called dbconn_csv.dll - Are located in the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . There are two categories of Connectors: - Device-centric Connectors : This is the more common Connector where its Links configure agents from information (tags) within individual front end devices. For instance the OPC Connector Link configures agents from the items within an OPC Server. - Complex Connectors : This Connector creates Links that globally configure agents (NOT device specific). For instance, a CSV Connector Link can create a fully configured Adroit agent database (.WGP file) from information contained in CSV files. Note: The Connector category determines how the Links of these Connectors are named. The functionality of the Connector determine the following Connector attributes: - if the 3 rd party Connector can be remotely accessed or not, determines whether the Adroit DB Generator can access the Agent Server remotely or whether it has to be installed on the same Agent Server computer on which such 3 rd party programs themselves are installed. - if the Connector supports templates, determines whether you can use templates to determine your own customised agent creation, scanning, logging and/or alarming default settings or not. Note : Those Connectors that support templates, implement them uniquely by using the features and fields of information available to the Connector’s specific 3rd party application. To create a Link: each Link can create a WGP file from the selected 3 rd party application. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the required Connector on the required Agent Server computer.

- Select the Create Link menu item.

- Select the Create Link menu item. - Provide a name for this Link, as follows: If this Connector is Complex: - Type in a name for the Link. - Click the OK button. If the Connector is Device-centric: - Double click the required device from the Select device tree, which lists the applicable protocol drivers and their configured devices for the selected Agent Server. - Configure this Link using the displayed configuration dialog, if one is provided by this Connector. This Link is added beneath this Connector with one of the following icons: - : a healthy Link that can be used to create a .WGP file from the specified 3rd party application. - : a Link that is currently unavailable Available Connectors : this lists the available Connectors and their specific functionality and configuration of their Links, such as their support and/or implementation of templates. About the Connector Links : describes the Links and the various configuration options that they can provide. -->

These events can be viewed in an Event Log viewer window on this computer. - 3: this route is intended for reporting your active process events , in other words any incident that is provided for INFORMATION ONLY e.g. if a set point value has changed. About the GSM_SMS driver Top About the GSM_SMS driver The sole function of the GSM_SMS driver is the sending and receiving of SMS messages to and from SMS GSM modems.

Title: About the GSM_SMS driver
About the GSM_SMS driver Top About the GSM_SMS driver The sole function of the GSM_SMS driver is the sending and receiving of SMS messages to and from SMS GSM modems. This driver has been specifically designed to simply its use with any cellular SMS protocol. For this reason, Windows drivers for the modem are NOT required, since this driver provides its own interface to the modem via the serial port assigned to it. Note: This driver is ONLY designed to work with SMS GSM modems and, in particular, has been designed and tested using the WAVECOM WMOD2 GSM modem. The devices configured for this driver, can be used in one of following two modes, depending upon the configuration of its Use with Command Agent checkbox setting: Note: For details, concerning the configuration of devices, see Configuring Devices . - If checked, the default setting, this device can only be used by a Command agent, which bypasses the scanning sub-system, so that the full SMS message of up to 160 characters can be utilised. In addition, the Command agent provides extensive functionality for both sending and receiving SMS messages. For further details, see Command Agents . - If unchecked, this device uses the scanning sub-system, as normal, replacing the former User-driver functionality, which was also difficult to configure, of sending 79 character SMS messages, configured in the Text, String or Notifier agents. Therefore the Notifier agent can still be used to automatically route alarms from Adroit by SMS to the relevant personnel. For details, see Notifier Agents . Note: The driver only handles the transmission of the intended message, which can originate as an alarm, a message entered by an operator or via programming performed in Adroit . -->

Therefore the Notifier agent can still be used to automatically route alarms from Adroit by SMS to the relevant personnel. For details, see Notifier Agents . About the Templates Top About the Templates Templates can customise or fine-tune your agent creation, scanning, logging and/or alarming default settings, when using the Adroit DB Generator to create Adroit agent databases (.WGP files) from information stored in 3 rd party applications.

Title: About the Templates
About the Templates Top About the Templates Templates can customise or fine-tune your agent creation, scanning, logging and/or alarming default settings, when using the Adroit DB Generator to create Adroit agent databases (.WGP files) from information stored in 3 rd party applications. The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the specific source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Note: Connectors that supports templates, implement them differently by using the features and fields of information available to this Connector’s specific 3rd party application. The following four template types are displayed in the left hand explorer type pane of the Adroit DB Generator utility, within the Templates folder: - Agents : You can create one or more template per agent type and configure the required default slot values that should be used when an agent of this type is created when using this template. For more details, see Agent Templates . - Scanning : You can specify the default scanning (communicating) parameters that are specified in the Tag scanning configuration dialog, when scanning the slots of agents in Adroit . For more details, see Scanning Templates . - Alarming : You can configure the default alarming settings that are used per alarm type (an alarmed condition or state within an agent). For more details, see Alarming Templates . - Logging : You can specify the default logging configuration for each log set. For more details, see Logging Templates . Available Connectors : this lists the available Connectors and their specific functionality and configuration of their Links, such as their support and/or implementation of templates. About the Adroit DB Generator : an overview of the Adroit DB Generator utility which creates Adroit agent databases (.WGP files) from information stored in 3 rd party applications, such as front-end devices. -->

Accessing Agent Slots Top Accessing Agent Slots Because of Adroit ‘s open architecture, it is extremely easy to read and/or write agent slot values, provided you know the name of the agent and slot.

Title: Accessing Agent Slots
Accessing Agent Slots Top Accessing Agent Slots Because of Adroit ‘s open architecture, it is extremely easy to read and/or write agent slot values, provided you know the name of the agent and slot. For details, see About Agents or About Agent Data (Slots) . Slots within agents can be accessed, as follows: - The actual agent itself may change values within one or more of its slots. An Expression agent, for example, will generate a new value whenever one of its inputs changes. - Another agent within the same Agent Server may read or write one or more agents’ slots. For example, a Scan agent updates the agent(s) and slot(s) it scans whenever values in the front-end device change. - Windows within the Adroit user interface can access slot values within agents. For example, Mimic Display Value Behaviours read slot values, whereas Mimic Operator Action Behaviours write slot values. - Custom applications using the Agent Server Applications Programming Interface can access slot values. For instance OLE Interface or ActiveX Control . Note: All slots generally offer safe read access, but caution must be exercised when writing slot values. -->

- Open a graphic form.

Title: To access data within a DataBinder:
Steps:
- Open a graphic form. (If necessary, create a project and add a graphic form to it first.) - In the Toolbox window open the Data category and select the VIZNETDataBinder component. - Click on the graphic form to add this component, which launches the DataBinder configuration dialog. - Select the OLE DB datasource name that represents your required database from the Select DataSource list. - If necessary, select the name of the required DataBinder from the Select DataBinder list. - Select which of this DataBinder's tables to display on this graphic form, from the left Select the Tables to View list. Note: Only the tables that are checked will be displayed. The Create Controls option is selected, by default. This automatically generates controls on this graphic form that allow users to display and navigate and/or modify the records within the selected tables. Note: Only clear this option if you are an advanced user and want to create your own controls and link them manually to the DataBinder. For more details, see VIZNETDataBinder components . - If using Create Controls: You can adjust the display order of a table by selecting the required table name and clicking the or buttons to promote or demote its displayed order accordingly. Tables appear from top to bottom, in the specified order. For each selected table: Note: Only the checked items are displayed. - If necessary, select which of its available fields should appear individually on the graphic form, in the Required Field Controls tab of the right list: In this case each selected field will have an associated label, indicating the name of this field and an appropriate control containing the value of this field for the currently displayed record. This control, which is typically a TextBox, can both display and/or modify this value. Tip: Adjust the display order of a field by selecting the required field name and clicking the or buttons to promote or demote its displayed order accordingly. Fields appear from top to bottom, in the specified order. Fields may appear in two or more columns, depending on the size of the control used to represent their table. This is recommended when information on a specific item is required, such as information about a particular user or asset. - If necessary, select which of its available fields should appear in a DataGridView control, in the Required DataGrid Columns tab of the right list: Tip: Adjust the display order of a field in the DataGridView control by selecting the required field name and clicking the or buttons to promote or demote its displayed order accordingly. Fields appear in the specified order, from left to right. This is recommended when you want to view large amounts of data in a spreadsheet-like view. - If a relationship exists between two selected tables, then use the DataGrid Lookup Columns tab of the right list to specify the column (known as the Lookup column) which describes the ID column of the other table. So that the descriptive entries will be displayed and used instead of the IDs. - Select Finish , once you are happy with your configuration. The relevant components and/or controls are added to this graphic form and the tasks pane is displayed. For details of these tasks, see VIZNETDataBinder components task menu . DataBinders : this describes how DataBinders allow your users to view and/or modify the data within an OLE DB datasource. -->

Accessing tool windows Top Accessing tool windows Accessing a tool or dockable window a window that can be either be attached to a docking area or that can float anywhere on the screen.

Title: Accessing tool windows
Accessing tool windows Top Accessing tool windows Accessing a tool or dockable window a window that can be either be attached to a docking area or that can float anywhere on the screen. See floating mode; docked mode; docking area. can be difficult as it does not have a fixed location. Choose one of the following methods to access the required tool window: Tip: Dragging an item over a docked window tab, selects this window tab so that it can be dragged into this tool window. - To access a tool window in its default location: click on the name or icon of its tab. - To access a tool window from a customised location: if the tool window is in docked mode, locate it manually and if necessary click on the name and/or icon of its tab. Note: If the tool window has been auto hidden then its icon and/or name of its tab will be located at the top, bottom, left or right of the application window. If the tool window is in floating mode, simply click on its title bar. - To access a tool window that cannot be located: - Open the View tab of the ribbon. The Content section displays the list of icons of the tool windows currently available in the SmartUI Designer application window - hovering over each icon displays the associated name of the tool window. - If the entry is not selected (icon has a white background): click this item to turn it on (the background changes from white to yellow). - If the entry IS selected (icon has a yellow background): click this item to turn it off (the background changes from yellow to white), then open the View tab again and select this icon again. - This will immediately locate and open the required tool window in the SmartUI Designer application window. The Spider Configuration Mode section of View tab of the Designer ribbon determines the visibility and user interaction within the Spider Configuration window, as follows: Note: When changing from one mode to another, you need to close all open graphic forms. - Beginner : (default selection for new installs) the Spider Configuration window is not accessible at all and therefore does not appear in the Content list. This provides the added advantage that graphic forms open faster, since the visual components of the configured spiders are not loaded. Note: This mode is required when using graphic forms that have an excessively large number of spiders. - Intermediate : the Spider Configuration window can be accessed (is added to the Content list) but is not displayed by default and any spider regions associated with configured Behaviours cannot be accessed (they remain closed). - Advanced : grants full access to the Spider Configuration window and opens this window. However, with regard to spider regions associated with configured Behaviours, you are ONLY able to edit the existing spiders and are therefore prevented from: - dragging spiders into or out of this region - adding spiders to this region - deleting spiders from this region Note: Tool windows can be arranged to increase the available designing space. - To reset the layout of your tool windows: select one of the following options provided by the View tab of the Designer ribbon: - Reset Window Layout: Restores the docked tool windows to the saved layout. This layout is saved when the Designer is closed (or when the default layout is applied). - Reset to Default Layout: Restores the docked tool windows to the default or standard layout (specified by the product not the user). Note: When this is performed the current layout is overwritten with this layout.

Tip: Use this option when your last saved layout is messed up, so that you can return your Designer to a functional state.

Title: Accessing tool windows

Account Policy Top Account Policy The Windows based Account policy controls how passwords must be used by all user accounts.

Title: Account Policy
Account Policy Top Account Policy The Windows based Account policy controls how passwords must be used by all user accounts. It defines such things as the maximum password age, minimum password age, minimum password length, and whether or not a password history is maintained. The Account policy determines whether all user accounts are subjected to lockout. If lockout is enabled, then a user account becomes locked if there are a number of incorrect attempts to log on to that account, occurring with no more than a specified amount of time between any two of the bad logon attempts. A locked account remains locked until an administrator unlocks it or a specified amount of time passes. Locked accounts cannot log on. The Account policy also determines whether or not a remote user will be forcibly disconnected from all connections to servers in the domain if that user’s logon hours expire, and whether users must log on before changing their passwords. -->

- Red slot names indicate configuration slots.

Title: Slot List for the Agent
- Red slot names indicate configuration slots. - Blue slot names indicate operator/process driven slots. - All other slots are driven/controlled by the agent. Slot Name Type Function connection VARSTRING This slot contains an optional connection string to the SQL Server database that is required for this agent to maintain a history of the differential values for each period. Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . - Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. - Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. - Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. - At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. deadband REAL The deadband slot is used to desensitise the value alarm limits to prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. - This slot is optional and specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area outside these alarm limits. - The deadband value must reduce before the alarm becomes inactive and is cleared. Important: This deadband slot ONLY applies to the alarm limits for the differential value and NOT for the rate of change alarm limits! disableOnStandby BOOLEAN Set this slot on [1] to disable SQL Query transactions on the standby clustered partner to prevent the standby Agent Server from logging duplicate records. - By default this slot is set to on [1]. elapsedTime REAL This slot captures the amount of time, in minutes, that has passed from the start of the current period. enable BOOLEAN Set this slot on [1] to enable this agent. - You must enable this agent before it can start analysing the accumulating process value and calculating its differential value for each period and its rate of change. - If necessary, log the values of each period to the specified history table in the specified SQL Server database. housekeepDays INTEGER Set this slot value, if you want to provide automatic management of the database history table. - If this agent is logging records, then use this slot to specify how many days of data you want this table to retain, to ensure that only the most recent records are kept. Note: The default value of 0 disables this functionality. inputTag TAGNAME This is an optional tag that defines the accumulating process value.

If used, the value of this tag will be transferred to the inputValue slot.

Title: Slot List for the Agent
If used, the value of this tag will be transferred to the inputValue slot. inputValue REAL This slot contains the ever increasing process value. - If an inputTag is not used, then you need to drive the inputValue slot. - You do this by scanning this slot value to the required accumulating process variable stored on the front end device or by means of a script or expression. interval INTEGER The number of minutes that define the duration of each period. Note: This slot is ONLY applicable if you are using an intervalMode of 3 or 4. Important: ONLY when you use intervalMode 3 must you ensure that the specified interval is divisible into 60 or is a multiple of 60, if not, period timing errors will occur. intervalMode INTEGER Use this slot to determine how you want to specify the constant interval of time over which the differential increases in value will be calculated. The selected mode determines which additional slots are used to determine this period. The first three intervalMode options make use of the intervalTag , which is a tag that you can monitor to determine when the end of an interval has occurred, as follows: - 0 =Interval tag value goes to zero. - In this case the end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. - 1 =Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero. - In this case the end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from zero [0] to any non-zero value. - 2 =Any interval tag value change. - In this case the end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes in value to any other value (a different value from its current value). The next option allows you to define the required interval duration using the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the number of minutes for the duration of each period: - 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) - In this case the agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interval number of minutes to this starting time.

- For example, if the agent is configured to use this intervalMode 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22 etc.

Title: Slot List for the Agent
- For example, if the agent is configured to use this intervalMode 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22 etc. For the final option, you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or an expression. or alternatively, this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to. - 5 =Manual trigger Note: The rate of change and its alarm limits only applies when using periods that have regular intervals. intervalTag TAGNAME A tag that defines the value that will indicate the end of an interval. Note: This slot is ONLY applicable if you are using an intervalMode of 0, 1 or 2. lastValue REAL The differential value of the previous period. periodCount INTEGER Number of elapsed periods for the current agent server session. rate REAL The rate of change of the differential value for the last period, specified as a value per hour. rateHiHi REAL The optional second alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHighHigh status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the RHighHigh default alarm type. Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. rateHi REAL The optional first alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHigh status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the RHigh default alarm type. Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. rateLo REAL The optional first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLow status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the RLow default alarm type. Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. rateLoLo REAL The optional second alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action.

- When the rate lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to 1 (enabled) .

Title: Slot List for the Agent
- When the rate lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the RLowLow default alarm type. Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. startTime TIME The start time of the current period. startValue REAL The inputValue as recorded at the start of the current period. tableName STRING The table name of the database that will store these records, if one has been specified via the connection slot. - By default, this table name is set to the name of this Accumulator agent. triggerNow BOOLEAN Performs a manual end of period, which is effective in any mode selected by the intervalMode slot. - The differential value for the current period, i.e. inputValue minus startValue. - This value would obviously be equal to 0 at the beginning of each period. value REAL The differential value for the current period, which is inputValue minus startValue . - This value is always equal to 0 at the beginning of each period, since startValue = inputValue . valueHi REAL The optional first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHigh status bit is set to 1 (enabled). - This slot can be alarmed using the VHigh default alarm type. Tip: The deadband slot, can be used to desensitise this alarm limit to prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. valueHiHi REAL The optional second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHighHigh status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the VHighHigh default alarm type. Tip: The deadband slot, can be used to desensitise this alarm limit to prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. valueLo REAL The optional first alarm limit for a low value , which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLow status bit is set to 1 (enabled) . - This slot can be alarmed using the VLow default alarm type. Tip: The deadband slot, can be used to desensitise this alarm limit to prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating.

valueLoLo REAL The optional second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action.

valueLoLo REAL The optional second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLowLow status bit is set to 1 (enabled). - This slot can be alarmed using the VLowLow default alarm type. Tip: The deadband slot, can be used to desensitise this alarm limit to prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating.

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title: Specifications
Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 endofperiod Pulsed (set to ON [1] momentarily and then set back to OFF [0]) at the end of each period. status bit 17 sqlerror ON if there is a problem connecting to the database, when the connection to this SQL database has been specified. status bit 18 VHighHigh ON when the differential value is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the valueHiHi alarm limit. status bit 19 VHigh ON when the differential value is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the valueHi alarm limit. status bit 20 VLow ON when the differential value is LESS THAN OR EQUAL to the valueLo alarm limit. status bit 21 VLowLow ON when the differential value is LESS THAN OR EQUAL to the valueLoLo alarm limit. status bit 22 RHighHigh ON when the differential rate of change is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the rateHiHi alarm limit. status bit 23 RHigh ON when the differential rate of change is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the rateHi alarm limit. status bit 24 RLow ON when the differential rate of change is LESS THAN OR EQUAL to the rateLo alarm limit. status bit 25 RLowLow ON when the differential rate of change is LESS THAN OR EQUAL to the rateLoLo alarm limit.

ACK Commands Top ACK Commands Function: To acknowledge alarms reported by an agent within the Agent Server.

Title: ACK Commands
ACK Commands Top ACK Commands Function: To acknowledge alarms reported by an agent within the Agent Server. Note1: Alarms are always globally acknowledged. Note2: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a security and operational risk through the remote acknowledgment of alarms. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note3: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. To globally acknowledge an alarm via SMS: ack,tag[.alarm type] Where ‘ tag ’ is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, ‘[.alarm type]’ is optional and allows you to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance “ANA_1.High” only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas “ANA_1” acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format: ack,tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type] To globally acknowledge alarms via Putslot: use the new globalAck slot of the Command agent and use the following format: tag[.alarm type] Note: This method does NOT use SMS to acknowledge alarms, nor are you limited to only using the Putslot utility, any method can be used that sets the value of this slot. Where ‘ tag ’ is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, ‘[.alarm type]’ is optional and allows you to to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance “ANA_1.High” only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas “ANA_1” acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To globally acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format in this globalAck slot: tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type] -->

Title: Active Link Monitoring
AcknowledgeAtStartup Top Active Link Monitoring WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". The following Active Link Monitoring registry settings can remedy or troubleshoot slow (or unresponsive) Agent Servers and/or clients, which may occur when: - there are a large number of clients connected to an Agent Server AND/OR - there is a misbehaving network and/or clients resulting in an inability to effectively send subscriptions to the Agent Server. These (REG_)DWORD registry settings need to be added to the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI registry key: ActiveLinkMonitor : when set to a value of 1, this enables an Agent Server’s link manager to actively monitor connections to remote Agent Servers instead of simply relying on broadcasts from the remote Agent Server to assume that the connection is healthy. This setting works hand in hand with the KillSlowClients registry setting, for instance, if the remote Agent Server has KillSlowClients enabled, then the remote Agent Server will force a disconnection to the local (this) Agent Server should the remote Agent Server be unable to send subscriptions to the local (this) Agent Server. The ActiveLinkMonitor setting allows the local Agent Server to recognise this closed channel within 5 seconds - instead of the legacy 30 to 45 seconds that potentially causes secondary issues with the local Agent Server and any clients connected to it. The default value is off (0). KillSlowClients : when set to a value of 1, this instructs the Agent Server to close the channel to the remote client if it is unable to send a subscription to the remote client. If this happens, an Agent Server side debug event message is generated. This setting has the effect of disconnecting misbehaving clients and thereby keeping the local server free of delays and lockups that have the potential to cause failures in the local Agent Server. The default value is off (0). This setting is typically used in conjunction with the ActiveLinkMonitor setting. The following registry settings can provide related informative/warning events: Note: These events are only displayed if you have checked the Enable logging of agent server system events checkbox in the Advanced Agent Server Configuration dialog of the Config Editor or PSEXE. ShowSlowClientEvents : when set to a value of 1, this will display Agent Server side system events when slow clients are detected, which simply means that the remote client is unable to deal with the speed of subscriptions being sent to it by the Agent Server. The default value is off (0). MonitorSubsChannelsize : we suggest setting this to a decimal value of 100000, in this case an event is generated by an Agent Server client every time the number of bytes differs by 100,000 from the previously displayed event, whether the number of bytes is increasing or decreasing. These client side system events provides client side monitoring of the incoming subscription pipe showing how full this pipe is. WARNING: Improper use of this setting could overload the event system thereby further crippling the ability of the client to deal with subscriptions! -->

AcknowledgeAtStartup Top ConnectionProtocol WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY.

Title: ConnectionProtocol
Steps:
AcknowledgeAtStartup Top ConnectionProtocol WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Note: This setting can be configured using the Advanced Agent Server Configuration dialog of the SmartUI Config Editor . From Adroit 10 Agent Servers allow clients to connect to them by using sockets over and above the legacy named pipes - Sockets give you better performance when a remote client (running on another computer) connects to an Agent Server. - Named pipes gives you better performance when a local client (running on the same computer) connects to an Agent Server. To specify the required mechanism that Adroit client software want to use when connecting to local and remote Agent Servers, add the following key or set it to appropriate value: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI (REG_)DWORD ConnectionProtocol , the default (legacy) value is 0. - 0 =Uncompressed Named Pipes (UNP) both locally and remotely: this is the legacy default. - 1 = UNP locally, and Sockets (TCP) remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications and where network traffic needs to be controlled across switches etc. - 2 = Compressed Named Pipes (CNP) both locally and remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications with restricted connectivity. - 3 = TCP both locally and remotely: TCP is slower for local connections when compared to UNP. IMPORTANT: Please ensure that all Adroit computers across your enterprise are configured for either named pipes or sockets, but not a mixture thereof! -->

Active Clusters Foundation Top Clustering Agent Servers Clustered Agent Servers, previously known as hot standby, provide both client and server redundancy enabling high availability of the system.

Title: Clustering Agent Servers
Steps:
Active Clusters Foundation Top Clustering Agent Servers Clustered Agent Servers, previously known as hot standby, provide both client and server redundancy enabling high availability of the system. Typically, redundancy can be applied to all the levels within the plant. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . There are three general components in Adroit which are aware of redundancy, namely, the clients, the servers and the server I/O, as illustrated below: In Adroit , an Agent Server can be setup to be a cluster server, which is a set of two Agent Servers running a replicated database (WGP file) on the same project. A cluster Agent Server can be networked with other normal (non-cluster) Agent Servers. The general idea of clustering is that the master server services all the I/O and client tasks, while the standby server replicates the master server. If the master server or computer fails, the standby server takes over as master and the UI’s and scanning tasks take appropriate action. There are three key mechanisms in Active Clusters namely catch-up , replication and switchover . A clustered Agent Server: - can be networked with other normal (non-cluster) Agent Servers. - is either in the mode of master or standby server - is either in the state of healthy or unhealthy. A cluster Agent Server is either in the mode of master or standby server and can either be in the state of healthy or unhealthy. Note: Certain agent types on a cluster server require synchronization of internal data structures with their master partner. For details, see Real-time Catch-up . Also, some agents in an Agent Server have internal states that are unknown to and unsynchronised with the standby computer. Examples of such agents are: the Expression agent, the Recipe agent, the Counter agent, the Statistical agent and all other internal agents that do some calculation internal to the Agent Server. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. Basic principles of Agent Server mode assignment strategies Configuring Agent Server cluster options For more details on detecting and solving issues that most frequently prevent clustered Adroit Agent Servers from working, see Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers . -->

Title: To add a group:
- If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. - Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . - Click the Add Group button to display the Create New Group dialog. - In the Group Title edit box, specify a name for this tag group, which must not be more than 90 characters in length. - In the Group Type list box, select the communication type required by the tag links within the group, from the following options: - Normal: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) should ONLY be fetched (read) from the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. - Control: This should contain tag links, whose local values (located in the Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer) can be BOTH fetched (read) from AND sent (written) to the specified remote tag values via the required WanServers. - In the Poll Period edit box, specify the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and specifies a 1 second polling rate. Note: Poll periods can be specified from 1 to 2000 seconds. - Click the Ok button to add the group or the Cancel button to discard the settings and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the OK button is clicked, without all the fields being completed, a message box appears requesting that all the fields are completed first. -->

- If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu.

Title: To add a link:
- If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. - Ensure that the required server is selected in the Select server list box. For details, see Servers . - Ensure that the required tag group is selected in the Select group list box. For details, see Tag Groups . - Click the New Link button to display the New Link dialog. - In the Remote Tag edit box, specify the name of the required Adroit tag (agent.slot), located in the Agent Server residing on the WanServer computer. - In the Local Tag edit box, specify the name of the required Adroit tag (agent.slot), located in the local Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer. - The Method list box, is disabled, since this only applies to tags within normal groups, in which case the WanServer will return the current value of the specified remote tag. - Click the Ok button to add the link or the Cancel button to discard the settings and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the OK button is clicked, without all the fields being completed, a message box appears requesting that all the fields are completed first. -->

- If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu.

Title: To add a server:
- If necessary launch the WanClient and open the WanClient Configurator, by selecting the Open Configurator item from the File menu. - Click the Add Server button to display the New Remote Server dialog. - In the Full server title edit box, specify a name for the server, not more than 90 characters in length. - In the Database name edit box, specify the name to be used by this server to store its tag groups and tag links. This will be saved as a CSV file in the database folder , which is created in the folder in which WanClient has been installed. Tip: This file can also be edited manually for bulk configuration of tag groups and bulk configuration of tag links . Note: This filename should be not more than 90 characters in length. - In the IP Address (or PC name) edit box, either specify the exact IP address of the WanClient computer or specify the computer name of this computer instead. Note: If the computer name is specified then the WAN requires a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve the computer name into its corresponding IP address. - The Port field, displays the port address that is being used by WanLink and cannot be changed. - The Connect timeout edit box, is not used currently by Wanlink. - In the Transaction timeout edit box, specify the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. The default value of 5 is required for fast networks and a value from 15 – 20 can be used for slower networks. - In the Retries edit box, specify the number of reties to be automatically attempted when attempting to establish a connection to this WanServer computer. - In the Ping timeout edit box, specify the period in seconds to wait after the communications fail before the client will retry to establish communications. - Click the Ok button to add the server or the Cancel button to discard the settings and return to the WanClient Configurator. Note: If the OK button is pressed, without all the fields being completed, a message box appears requesting that all the fields are completed first. -->

Title: Adding a graphic form to another graphic form
Steps:
Adding a graphic form to another graphic form Top Adding a graphic form to another graphic form If you want a graphic form to contain another, drag the required graphic form onto another and then select the appropriate configuration dialog which configures the size of each copy and arranges multiple copies on the host graphic form for you. Typically you will be dragging a SmartUI Template A graphic form that has one or more configured aliases and is therefore designed to be displayed within a TemplateGO control. onto a graphic form. For details, see Working with SmartUI Templates . The following three options are provided when dragging or copying a graphic form or SmartUI Template onto a graphic form: IMPORTANT: When copying SmartUI Templates ONLY use the Graphic Form by Reference option as this is the ONLY option that creates TemplateGO controls so that you can configure its aliases. - Paste Graphic Form Contents: In this case, ONLY the contents of this graphic form or SmartUI Template are added to this graphic form. - Graphic Form by Reference: In this case, each copy of the added graphic form refers to the original graphic form and TemplateGO controls are created for each. Use this method, if you want ALL the copies of this graphic form to look the same and be centrally configuration. In other words, when you modify the original (copied) graphic form ALL of its copies on other graphic forms are immediately updated. However, this means that any change made to a copy will be OVERWRITTEN when the original graphic form is modified. Configuring the Graphic Form by Reference: - In Enterprise Manager , drag the graphic form that you want to copy onto the required graphic form. Tip: These graphic forms do not need to be in the same project. - Specify the required number of copies of this graphic form, in the No. of References spin control. - If necessary, specify how you want to arrange multiple copies in the Layout Panel section, as follows: - Select the required method of arranging multiple copies from the Layout Panel Type list box, as follows: - Flow: Copies of the graphic form are added from left to right horizontally onto the host graphic form, wrapping down the graphic form as required Note: In this case, ANY further control that you add to the parent graphic form is added next to the last one. - Table: The SAME as Flow, except, each copy is added to its own cell, so you can add other controls to each of the configured cells. Note: In this case each copy has a row and column property and can be spanned over adjacent rows and/or columns. - VIZNETFlow: The SAME as Flow , except that this flow can be broken later so that you can manually move (re-position) these graphic forms, by clicking Move Controls from the Tasks list of the flow container (accessed by clicking its glyph a glyph is a specific graphic symbol, for instance employed by form components, which when clicked launch alternate configuration dialogs. , which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the flow container). - Configure the initial size of the Layout Panel , as follows: specify the required Width and Height in pixels. Note: Depending upon the configured size of the Layout Panel, you may not be able to see all the added copies. - Specify the size of each copy, in the Template GO section, as follows: - Either check the Auto Resize checkbox, so that each copy expands to fit all the controls of the copied graphic form.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Click for generic instructions on how to add and name a datasource: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - Right-click on the name of the required SmartUI Server or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Add Datasource . The Add Datasource configuration dialog is launched displaying each datasource plugin a generic type of data supplier that interfaces between the Server and this specific type of data, so that it is exposed to the Server in the format of data elements. See data element. that you can connect to. Note: Only the datasource plugins, which have been licensed, appear in this list. - Click the datasource you require and then click the Finish button. Tip: You can also simply double-click the required datasource. The Add A New Datasource configuration dialog is displayed to configure this datasource: - Type an appropriate name for this datasource into the Name edit box. When naming this datasource, please be aware of the following: WARNING! Once a datasource has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note1: The following non-standard text characters are NOT supported for datasource names: \ / : * ? < > | # " Note2: Datasource names are case sensitive. Note3: The specified name cannot be the same as any other datasource that has been already been connected to this Server. Tip: Although the datasource name can be up to 50 characters long - use a descriptive name that is as concise as possible. This will ensure that users will BOTH easily identify and navigate to it within the Enterprise Manager .

- Select the Agent Server type, as follows: - Standalone: This should be used when connecting to a single standalone Agent Server that is running the required agent database containing the configured agents and slots.

Title: Configuration
- Select the Agent Server type, as follows: - Standalone: This should be used when connecting to a single standalone Agent Server that is running the required agent database containing the configured agents and slots. This requires specifying this Agent Server in the Agent Server drop down selection box. WARNING! This must be specified and cannot be left blank. - Redundant: This should be used when connecting to an Adroit Cluster i.e. a set of two Agent Servers each running a replicated agent database. This requires specifying the names of both cluster partners in the Agent Server and Partner Server drop down selection boxes provided. To use a drop down selection box to specify an Agent Server: Click the button to the right of the required drop down selection box. This process depends upon whether the required Agent Server is displayed in the list box or not, as follows: Note: The list box is populated by all the Adroit Agent Servers on the Server computer and within its network domain. - If the required Adroit Agent Server is displayed in the list box, select it to immediately add it to the drop down selection box. Note: If the required Agent Server has been started after opening this dialog, click the button to the right of the drop down selection box to update this list. - If the required Adroit Agent Server is not specified in the list box, then type it into the drop down selection box, using the following format: ComputerName.AgentServerName . Where: ComputerName is the network or computer name of this Agent Server, if required. AgentServerName is the name used to uniquely identify this Agent Server. This is the first name displayed in the title bar of the Adroit Agent Server window. Note: The onus is upon the user to ensure that the specified computer name and Agent Server name is correct. - Click Finish once the required Agent Server has been specified and the datasource has been named. This adds an Adroit datasource to the Datasources category in the Enterprise Manager , identified by either the specified name or icon . Note 1 : If the added Adroit datasource is identified by this icon , there is a problem connecting to the specified Agent Server. For details, see Troubleshooting Adroit datasources . Note2: The connected Agent Server can also be configured, if necessary. For details, see Configuring the Agent Server .

Title: Adding allowed users and groups
Adding allowed users and groups Top Adding allowed users and groups Typically, add each user or group that uses a SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. to the lists of allowed users or groups maintained by each SmartUI Server. IMPORTANT: Ensure that each user is assigned a password, which is MANDATORY when logging onto the SmartUI Server. Click for more information: - Using groups makes it easier for you to manage large numbers of users. For details, see Working with user accounts and groups . - It is not necessary to create user accounts for all users since it is also possible to impersonate an allowed user. For details, see Impersonating users . - It is also possible to remove user(s) or group(s) from these lists, if necessary. - When the SmartUI Server is deployed on a domain with a large number of users and/or groups, there is long delay before the user and group lists are displayed. For details on reducing or eliminating this delay, see Specifying user and group subsets . - One or more high-level groups and/or users can have unrestricted access to each SmartUI Server. For more information, see Global security groups and users . Allowed users and groups are configured for each SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , by using the Security component within the Management category. To add a user to the allowed users list: Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Management category. - Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Expand the Users and Groups icon . - Expand the Users icon . - Right-click the Allowed Users icon or its name and select Set Allowed Users . The Set Allowed Users configuration dialog is launched. Note: If the Server is deployed on a domain with a large number of users, its list of Available Users will take a long time to be populated. For details on reducing or eliminating this delay, see Specifying user subsets . - Select the name of the required user from the Available Users list. Note: The Available Users list may include both local and global users, where applicable. - Click the << button to add this user to the Selected Users list Tip: You can also add users by double-clicking the required entry in the Available Users list to immediately add it to the Selected Users list. Note: Only the users listed in the Selected Users list, will be used when configuring access to the Server, the configured datasources and their data elements and/or special functions, if necessary. - Repeat this for all the users that you want to add. Tip: It is also possible to add users to the Allowed Users list by expanding the All Users icon and dragging the relevant users onto the Allowed Users icon . Note: If necessary, allowed user(s) can be removed. For details, see Removing allowed users . To add a group to the allowed groups list: Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows .

Do not rename the series Title , since this name corresponds to a separate component on the graphic form that provides advanced series settings. - If necessary, choose and configure the required Type of series to display your data in this charting control, as follows: The following types of series are available: Note: The available series types are dependant upon the selected charting control. - Bar : a series of horizontal bars representing values. If selected this provides: the Bar Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. If selected this provides: the FastLine Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. For details, see Displaying a FastLine series or Configuring value labels . Note: A FastLine series provides less configuration options than a Line series so that it is drawn faster and is recommended for trending real-time data. - Line : a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. If selected this provides: the Pie Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. For details, see Displaying a Surface series or Configuring value labels . - XYPlot : a series of points that are plotted from two sets of values, one providing the X or horizontal coordinate and the other providing the Y or vertical coordinate of each point.

Title: Adding components to a MAPS project
Adding components to a MAPS project Top Adding components to a MAPS project Each component in a MAPS project provides a right click option that allows you to add a sub-component to it. For example, you can add a plant Area to the MAPS project or a PLC to a plant Area; however you SHOULD have PLANNED for these higher level components already BEFORE creating a MAPS project. For more details, see How to use the MAPS project wizard to add a MAPS project . You may however, need to add: - a unit a logical grouping of the electrical and/or instrumentation equipment within a PLC to a PLC - to represent a complex item of equipment that consists of more than one items of electrical and/or instrumentation equipment, such as a conveyor or - an item of electrical or instrumentation equipment to a unit . BEFORE adding equipment to an existing project (either by adding units or individual items of equipment), ensure that you update the Last Used address for the IO types of the relevant PLC, by clicking the Get Last Used button in the PLC Settings table of the PLC properties. This ensures that when SmartUI allocates the IO that you do NOT get duplicate addresses being allocated. For details of the other PLC properties and the properties of the other project components, see Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project . Note: Also do this when REMOVING equipment, to ensure that you do not have ‘holes’ in your allocated addressing and use all the freed up IO. How to add a unit to a PLC of a MAPS project: - In the MAPS window, right click the required PLC and select Add Unit . The Add unit wizard should open, in which you specify the required Name and Description of this unit and then click Next . WARNING! You CANNOT rename this unit name. - Specify ALL the types of electrical equipment and their quantities as required for this site ( MAPS project) in the Electrical Data page. Note: You will only advance to the Electrical Data page once all the MANDATORY fields are correctly completed for all the added units. In MAPS , each type of electrical equipment requires an associated MAPS template. For more details, see Electrical equipment templates . In the case of complex items of equipment that consist of more than one piece of electrical and/or instrumentation equipment, like conveyors - create a Unit for this item of equipment and associate all the component electrical equipment to MAPS templates. The Electrical Data page opens so that you can specify the required quantities of MAPS templates to represent your electrical equipment within this process site ( MAPS project). Add a row to the Electrical Data table for each type of MAPS template that you need and complete the following fields: - Select the MANDATORY Template Name for this type of electrical equipment from the list. Default Electrical equipment templates : the electrical equipment templates Once a template is selected, click the Template Description field to display a description of exactly which type of electrical equipment this MAPS template represents. - Specify the MANDATORY Quantity of this type of electrical equipment. This should specify the TOTAL number of this type of electrical equipment with the entire process site ( MAPS project). WARNING! Once you click the Next button, you are UNABLE to return to this page again, so ensure that this is correctly specified. Tip: If your estimation is NOT exact, you can always add other MAPS templates manually. - Click Next to configure each item of electrical equipment in the Electrical Detail Data page.

Title: Adding components to a MAPS project
Note: You will only advance to the Electrical Detail Data page when quantities are specified for all the added electrical equipment templates. The Electrical Detail Data page opens so that you can configure the individual items of electrical equipment of this process site ( MAPS project). Each row of the Electrical Equipment Detail Data table represents an item of electrical equipment that is associated to a MAPS template, which requires the configuration of the following fields: By default, the quantities of each MAPS electrical equipment template, as specified in the Electrical Data page, are added as individual rows. Note: Rows can be manually added and configured from scratch, if you need additional items of electrical equipment. - The MANDATORY Template Name is the MAPS template that represents this item of electrical equipment (or one of its electrical equipment sub-components in the case of complex equipment). - Specify the MANDATORY Unit Name (logical grouping) to which this electrical item of equipment belongs. - Specify the MANDATORY Name of this item of electrical equipment, which is used to identify this item of equipment in the SCADA and PLC. By default, the following suggested naming format is provided: a name that is prefixed by the specified plant area code (if any) and an incrementing counter as a suffix. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this equipment name. Note: Do not rely on the uniqueness of the specified suffix, if you manually add rows this suffix resets itself to 0001. Tip: If you specify any duplicate equipment names, these are flagged (one-by-one) when you click the Next button, so that you can correct these. - Specify a MANDATORY Description for this item of electrical equipment, which describes its function or purpose. - Specify the MANDATORY Graphic that represents this item of electrical equipment in the SCADA representation of this unit. The available graphical representations depend upon the selected template. For details, see Electrical equipment templates . Typically the provided template graphics will always list one or more ISO representations (of the associated ISO 14617 symbol, if one exists for this item of equipment) at the top of the list, which may be followed by one or more physical representations of this item of equipment. Ensure that you select the graphical representation, which provides the required orientation of this item of equipment. Note: To change the Graphic after you have selected it - highlight the name of the selected graphic and press the DELETE key, then the list box appears so that you can choose another graphic. - If necessary, check the Create tags checkbox to create the necessary SCADA tags in Adroit for this item of equipment and to perform any other necessary SCADA configuration required by this template, such as scanning, logging, alarming and/or trending. Note: If you check the Create tags checkbox, this will increase the time required to create the SmartUI project. If you do NOT check the Create tags checkbox for this item of equipment, then AFTER finishing this wizard, select the Sync tags right click option for this MAPS project in the MAPS window. - Click Next and specify ALL the types of instrumentation equipment and their quantities as required for this site ( MAPS project) in the Instrumentation Data page. Note: You will only advance to the Instrumentation Data page once all the MANDATORY fields are correctly completed for your electrical equipment and all of their names are unique. In MAPS , each type of instrumentation equipment requires an associated MAPS template. For more details, see Instrumentation equipment templates .
