Title: To add a DataBinder:
- In the Enterprise Manager expand the required OLE DB DataSource. - Right click the DataBinders folder and select Add DataBinder . - Specify the required DataBinder Name in the Add DataBinder configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a DataBinder has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other DataBinder that has been already been specified. Tip: Give this DataBinder a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified. Try not to use all 50 characters. - Click Next , once the name has been specified. - Select the fields that this DataBinder should contain: Select the required Tables by clicking the checkbox next to each table’s name in the tree view. By default, this selects all the fields of the table, clear the checkboxes of the undesired fields. If necessary, expand the Views node and check the checkbox of each view and their field/s that you would like to be queried, by clicking on it. Note1: The default View includes all the specified fields. Note2: Selecting a table, view or field does not necessarily mean that it needs to be displayed. Note3: Each selected table or view has its own Select statement in the Select Statements (lower) list. The Preview button, provides as easy way to debug your DataBinder as you create it. Simply select the required view or table in Select Statements (lower) list before clicking this button. This returns all the records that the currently configured DataBinder will return for this table or view, in the pane at the bottom of the configuration dialog. In this way you can ensure that your DataBinder provides the required data. It is important to select BOTH the fields that you want the DataBinder to display and those that are needed to configure the DataBinder. So select the fields you want to use to create relationships between, define constraints for and use to sort the displayed results. IMPORTANT: If you will require users to add or remove records or update data from a table then select all the primary key fields defined for this table. Tip: The primary key A primary key is one or more fields in the table of a database that uniquely identify each record stored in this, so they can locate records. Therefore, the primary key column/s must have unique values for each their rows.

fields are highlighted in the table and field tree, so that they appear in brown unlike the other fields and table names that appear in black.

Title: To add a DataBinder:

Note: If there are relationships between tables, select BOTH of the related tables to represent the relationship. - Click Next , once the required tables, views and/or fields are selected. - If necessary, add or remove relationships between the selected tables and/or views in the Table Relationships Setup dialog: In this case a relationship is simply a pair of selected fields, usually in different tables or views, whose values are required to be identical in order for a record to be returned. Tip: Select the required view or table in Select Statements (lower) list and press the Preview button to test your defined relationships, since an exception will be displayed if any of the data types of the related fields are NOT identical. To add a relationship: - Click the Add Relationship button to create a relationship between two of the selected fields, as follows: - Click the drop-down list box button at the right of each Field list and select the required field from both tables or views. This list only displays the fields selected in the previous dialog, in the following syntax: [Tablename].[Fieldname] or [Viewname].[Fieldname]. To delete a relationship: Click the Delete Relationship button to remove the last relationship from the Relationships list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the relationship at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. Note: These do not affect the relationships that you may have already created within your database. Typically, you create relationships between tables in order to perform lookups on fields between different tables, such as between a primary key s of two tables. - Click Next , once the required relationships have been defined. - If necessary, add or remove constraints for the values of one or more of the selected fields in the Constraints dialog: To add a constraint: - Specify the main View or the name of the table or view you want to constrain in the top list box. - Click the Add Constraint button. - If this constraint is NOT the first for the selected View or Table, specify how to relate this constraint to the previous constraints, as follows: - AND: This is the default option, which makes this constraint mandatory.

For instance, if there are two constraints with an AND between them, then the data will be restricted by BOTH constraints.

Title: To add a DataBinder:
For instance, if there are two constraints with an AND between them, then the data will be restricted by BOTH constraints. - OR: Use this option, to make the specified constraint optional. For instance, if there are two constraints with an OR between them then the data can be restricted with EITHER of these constraints. - AND NOT: This makes the INVERSE of this constraint mandatory - OR NOT: This makes the INVERSE of this constraint optional. - Select the field, whose values you want to limit, from the Field drop-down list box. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: Only if the main View is selected is the syntax for the fields [Tablename].[Fieldname] or [Viewname].[Fieldname] , otherwise this is simply [Fieldname]. - Select the method by which the values of this field are to be constrained or limited from the Constraint drop-down list box. For details, see Available constraint operators . - Specify the constraining value or parameter in the Value field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this criterion, for instance, if different users require different values. For details, see Adding parameters . Note1: If you use parameters, then you must add controls to the required graphic form so that your users can specify these values and link these controls to each parameter. For details, see Linking DataBinder parameters to controls . Note2: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the DataBinder will not work. Tip: Click the Preview button to test your defined constraints, since an exception will be displayed if any of the data types of the related fields are NOT identical for the currently selected View or Table. When previewing constraints containing parameters, a dialog box will appear so that you can provide a temporary value for each of them. To delete a constraint: - Specify the View or the name of the Table you want to constrain in the Select View/Table list box. - Click the Delete Constraint button to remove the last constraint from the Constraints list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the constraint at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. As you define the constraint(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the Select Command field, which cannot be edited.

Note: You need to constrain the View and each selected table separately.

Title: To add a DataBinder:
Note: You need to constrain the View and each selected table separately. Typically, you constrain or limit the values of a field to only return those records that you require. This is why it is a good idea to use parameters instead of hard-coded values since your users’ fields of interest may vary. - Click Next , once the required constraints have been created. - If necessary, define the sorting order of the resultant records in the Ordering dialog: To add a sorting order: - Specify the main View or the name of the table or view you want to sort in the top list box. - Click the Add Order button. - Select the field, whose values you want to sort, from the Field drop-down list box. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: If the main View is selected the syntax for the fields is [Tablename].[Fieldname] or [Viewname].[Fieldname], otherwise this is simply [Fieldname]. - Select the method by which the values of this field are to be sorted from the Constraint drop-down list box, as follows: - ASC: The default value, which sorts the values of the specified field in ascending order. The method used to sort the values,depends on the data type of the specified field, as follows: - String: This displays records beginning with non-text characters such as ‘_’ or ‘!”, then records from 0 to 9, then records from A to Z, with lowercase letters preceding uppercase letters e.g. for text like fgfd and Fgfd, the ASC order is fgfd and then Fgfd. - Numeric: This displays records from 0 to 9. - Date Time: This will display the records in this field from newest to oldest. - DESC: This sorts the values of the specified field in descending order, which is the reverse of the ASC order. To delete a sorting order: - Specify the required View or the name of the Table in the Select View/Table list box. - Click the Delete Sort Order button to remove the last sort order from the Sort Orders list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the sort order at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. As you define the sort order(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the Select Command field, which cannot be edited. Note: You need to sort the View and each selected table separately.

Typically, you sort a view or table to ensure that the records are displayed in order of importance or relevance.

Title: To add a DataBinder:
Typically, you sort a view or table to ensure that the records are displayed in order of importance or relevance. Although more than one field can be used to sort the data, the closer the field is to the top of the list, the greater the impact it has upon the sorting process. Typically multiple fields are used to sort tables, when their entries are related – for instance can be used when sorting by surnames and then sorting by their first names. It may also be useful to sort by identity (ID) fields or by Country, when viewing a list of orders etc. - Click Next , once the required sort orders have been set up. - The Custom View dialog allows you to customise the main View that is created for this databinder. Only check the Use Custom View checkbox, if you do not want the default main View and have the SQL know-how to create your own customised view in the SQL editor. When creating a customised view, parameters can be added so that their requirements can be specified before the main View is displayed. For details on specifying and using parameters, see Adding parameters . Note1: The Preview button, provides as easy way to debug your main View as you manually edit it. Clicking this button will return all the fields, in the pane at the bottom of the configuration dialog, that the current main View would return. In this way you can ensure that your main View returns what you want it to. This displays the records that comply with the configured relationships, constraints and/or sorting orders in the pane at the bottom of the configuration dialog.

Note: If the required records are not displayed or an error is returned, then press the Previous button to locate the required page to rectify this problem.

Change the keyboard (default input) language and/or install other languages as required. To add input locales to a Windows XP system: - Open the Start menu, select Settings , select Control Panel . - Open the Regional and Language Settings applet. - Click on the Languages tab. - If necessary, check the "Install files for East Asian languages" or “Install files for complex script and right-to-left languages (including Thai)” checkbox and click OK. Note: Some languages may require additional configuration. Determine this by clicking the specified Keyboard layout/IME entry for this new language, under the Installed services group and see if the Properties… button is enabled. If so, configure these additional settings. Once finished, you see the language bar displayed in the Taskbar , just to the left of the tray bar, displaying the two letters representing the currently selected language. Title: Adding the slots we're interested in
Steps:
Adding the slots we're interested in Top Adding the slots we're interested in For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . Initially the Properties collection object contains no Property objects, but it provides a method named Add that is used to add Property objects to the Properties collection. Each Property object in the Properties collection defines a slot to be monitored. The Add method accepts one parameter, the required slot name. The following VBA code shows how to add the value and rawValue slots to the Properties collection: Set prop = props.Add("value") Set prop = props.Add("rawValue") Once the Properties collection is set up, it must be associated with a tag as part of a Request object. In order to facilitate this, each Request object provides a method named Add that handles the creation of the Request object. The Add method accepts a tag and properties collection (i.e. agent name and list of slot names) as parameters. The following VBA code creates requests for Analog tags AN01 and AN02, value and rawValue slots: Set req = reqs.Add("AN01", props) Set req = reqs.Add("AN02", props) -->

Title: To add your own query:
- Open SQL Server Management Studio and connect to the SQL Server that contains the database that the required AlarmManagement agent is connected to. - Display the db.Adr_AM_UserQueries table. - Right click this table and select Edit top 200 rows . This displays an editable grid of the queries. - Select the bottom new (NULL) record and type in the name of this custom query into the Name field e.g. “Custom downtime”. This is name that is displayed in the Query list box when selecting the query. - If necessary, provide the necessary Description to help your operators and other users to know what this query will return e.g. “Provides the actual reasons and the downtime in hh:mm:ss time format...”. - Either type in the required SELECT SQL statement into the Query field or, in this case, paste it. Note: When pasting in a query, ensure that this SELECT SQL statement copies as a SINGLE line without any carriage returns! - Select the next NULL record to commit (save) this query (newly edited record). - Restart the Classic User Interface and open the View Data dialog of this AlarmManagement agent to use this new query. You will now find a new query called “Custom downtime” in the Query list.

- If necessary your query can support: One or more of the following constraints: these constrains are provided by the View data dialog so that your users can choose which incidents they need to analyse.

Title: Other things you can do:
- If necessary your query can support: One or more of the following constraints: these constrains are provided by the View data dialog so that your users can choose which incidents they need to analyse. - Top (%t): This allows your users to specify the number of topmost (most recent) incidents that are to be returned by the query. For instance, this %t constraint is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC - From (%b) and/or To (%e): These constraints allow your users to specify the time period during which the required incidents occur. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# AND dt < #%e# If necessary, you can provide ONLY one of these constraints, without the other. For instance: WHERE dt > #%b# - Now (%now). This allows users to specify the current date and time. For instance you can obtain the last 8 hours in SQL by using the following expression: WHERE dt > DATEADD(Hour, -8, '%now') AND dt < GetDate() - Shift times: This constraint is enabled when you specify the From (%b) and/or To (%e) constraints (see above), which allows your users to specify the shift during which the required incidents occur. - Operator ( %o). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged against a specific operator. For instance: WHERE Operator='%o' - Category ( %c). This allows your users to display all the incidents that are logged for a specific category. For instance: WHERE CategoryId='%c' One or more of the following KPI target values: these are the ideal values that you want to achieve. - Average alarm rate (%AAR). This per hourly count is 6 by default. For instance, this %AAR KPI target value is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT TOP(%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC - Burst rate (%BR). This per hourly count is 60 by default. - Percent upset count (%PUC). This number is 30 by default. - Percent upset (%PU). This percentage is 2 by default. - Intermittent alarm period (%IAP). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. - Bulk acknowledgement period (%BAP). This time period in seconds is 1 by default. - Average alarm duration (%ALD).

This time period in seconds is 60 by default.

Title: Other things you can do:
This time period in seconds is 60 by default. - Average acknowledgement duration (%AKD). This time period in seconds is 10 by default. If necessary, you can customise these default KPI target values and/or add your own and reference them in your queries by using the % prefix. For details, see Customizing KPI target values . Add your own KPI target values : once added, your custom queries can ALSO use these KPI target values! - If you want the data returned by this query to be viewed as a chart, then specify which chart you want to use by configuring the ChartType field, as follows: - 1 = Bar chart - 5 = Pie chart - 6 = Line chart Note: By default the ChartType field is -1, which indicates that you do not want this query to appear in the View Graph dialog. -->

Additional Alarming Configuration Top Additional Alarming Configuration The alarming system in Adroit is very flexible and provides the following additional capabilities: - Incident Acknowledgement : Acknowledgment of incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type.

Title: Configuration
Additional Alarming Configuration Top Additional Alarming Configuration The alarming system in Adroit is very flexible and provides the following additional capabilities: - Incident Acknowledgement : Acknowledgment of incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). is typically recommended for alarms i.e. all incidents that require some sort of reaction or attention from the operator. When you create incidents, you can specify whether it needs to be acknowledged before it can be removed from the Alarm List Viewer window. - Prioritizing or Filtering Incidents : One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance. Since some alarms are critical, whereas others are more informational in nature. - Delaying Incidents : Delay an active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. incident from entering the alarm system to: - prevent intermittent alarms from flooding your alarm system or to - ensure that this alarm is raised when the operator needs to respond to it. - Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents : To implement first-up alarming, which ensures that each incident is unique and does not duplicate existing active incidents, which can unnecessarily distract your operators. - Temporarily Suspending Alarming : Usually you need to do this when you are performing maintenance on a plant section or a particular item of equipment or when an alarm indicator is not functioning correctly or is being tested. - Bulk alarming configuration : Bulk-alarming configuration can be performed by exporting Alarm agents, configuring them in a third party CSV editor and then importing them. - Creating incident-specific documents : If you are using the AlarmManagement agent, you can specify an optional document that clarifies the incident and provides assistance on how to deal with it or react to it. This document can then be launched from the Alarm List Viewer window. For details, see Configuring Listed Incidents. -->

Title: Configuration
Spider menu: This describes the additional menu item that is displayed. Note: This can be accessed by selecting the spider and right-clicking its title bar. - Filter DataSet: This can be used to display the Filter Dataset configuration dialog to specify the required columns and tables, constraints and/or sorting. For details, see Filtering datasets . - Apply Table Style Formatting: When enabled, this displays the Table Style Date Time Format input, which can be used to customise the display of all the date time fields in this dataset. This is enabled by default. Inputs and outputs: This describes the additional available inputs displayed in the default configuration view of this spider. Note: Before the spider can be configured, its configuration view needs to be displayed. For details see Displaying spider configuration views . - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Note: These inputs can either be configured within the spider itself and/or may require their values to be supplied by other spiders or Data spiders (e.g. properties or data elements). For details, see Creating silks . Input Data Function Filter String String This can be used to specify a string that is used to filter a data table’s rows and apply sorting. Note: It is also possible to specify the required filtering and sorting using the Filter DataSet configuration dialog. For details, see Filtering datasets . Table Style Date Time Format String This input can be used to customise the display of all the date time fields. For details on specifying the required formatting string, see Date and Time formatting syntax . Note: This input is only displayed when the Apply Table Style Formatting menu item is enabled. Append Data Updates Boolean By default, when this checkbox is cleared, all the existing data is read initially and thereafter only the newly added or changed data will be displayed. Check this checkbox, if the data updates from the Server needs to be merged with the data from previous updates. For details, see Displaying both existing and updated dataset data . For instance, typically data updates from the Event Log datasources only send changed data after each poll period. If you need to show all the historical data as well as any new events that come through, then tick this checkbox. Note: This input is NOT configured within the Filter DataSet configuration dialog.

Title: Adroit Automation (MISSRVR) Interface
Adroit Automation Interface Top Adroit Automation (MISSRVR) Interface This describes the OLE Automation or Programmability Interface for Adroit OLE Server Data Objects. The programmability interface is a set of OLE Automation methods and properties exposed by Data Objects. The methods are callable as functions and the properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. In order to facilitate interfacing to Adroit , this provides the following methods or functions: - AlarmTag : to configure an agent for alarming - Connect : to connect to a Agent Server on a remote computer - CreateAgent : to add a new agent directly to the currently connected Agent Server - Fetch : to read a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). from the currently connected Agent Server - FetchTags : to read multiple tags from the currently connected Agent Server - FetchChanges : to retrieve a list of actual logged values from the Adroit proprietary datalog files - FetchValues : to retrieve a list of interpolated logged values from the Adroit proprietary datalog files - GetSlotInfo : to get information about the different slots supported by an agent - Join : to make a list of agents join an existing AgentGroup - Leave : to make a list of agents leave an existing AgentGroup - LogTag : to configure an agent for historical data logging - Poke : to change a tag in the currently connected Agent Server - RemoveAgent : to remove an agent directly from the currently connected Agent Server - ScanTag : to configure a tag (agent.slot) value for scanning -->

Title: Adroit datasources
Adroit datasources Top Adroit datasources Adroit is a SCADA product that is used to supervise and control processes. The Agent Server is the storage facility for all the real time and historical data. Click for more details: This data is stored and managed by intelligent objects, known as agents, of which there are different types. Each agent contains externally accessible data attributes, or slots, which in addition to being displayed can, if necessary, be used to interact with and configure their agent too. Tip: See Moving from the Classic Adroit UI for Classic UI feature equivalents in SmartUI . An Adroit datasource exposes the configured agents and their slots of either a standalone Adroit Agent Server on a specific computer or to an Adroit Cluster (a set of two replicated Agent Servers). Note: When displaying Adroit tags you can display bad-tag status indicators on relevant controls and/or vectors. For details, see Bad tag status indicators . This datasource is added within the Datasources category of the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Adroit datasources . Click for advanced Adroit datasource usage information: When connecting to an Adroit Cluster, the Adroit datasource seamlessly switches between the two Agent Servers in the cluster, when one becomes unavailable. However, the automatic tracking of the active master Agent Server within the cluster is NOT supported. The Adroit datasource connects to the primary Agent Server (first specified Agent Server) and connects to the secondary ( Partner Server ) when the primary fails. Therefore the Adroit datasource does not connect to the master Agent Server, if the Agent Server it is currently connected to becomes the standby. The Adroit datasource can be updated, locked or removed, if necessary. For details, see Updating datasources , Locking datasources or Removing datasources . Note1: You can also configure the Agent Server. For details, see Configuring the Agent Server . Note2: It is possible to use the Adroit Agent Server licence to license the SmartUI Server. For details, see Alternative Adroit licensing method . Note3: When adding an Adroit datasource, one remote connection will be used, from the Adroit license of the connected Agent Server. Note4: When data is fetched from this Adroit datasource, scan point licenses will be used, from the Adroit license of the connected Agent Server. Note5: If necessary, the access to this Adroit datasource, its agents and their slots can be controlled. For details, see Securing datasources . An added Adroit datasource is identified in the Enterprise Manager by its specified name and its icon . Note: If the following icon is displayed: , then there is a problem connecting to the specified Agent Server. For details, see Troubleshooting Adroit datasources . When this datasource is opened, the agents and their slots contained within the specified Agent Server are displayed, in the following hierarchy: Note: If necessary, the common Header slots of each agent, including the GROUP agents can also be displayed. For details, see Including header slots . - The AgentGroup is displayed immediately below the Adroit datasource, which contains all the agents that have been configured on this Agent Server and their slots. - The agent types are listed alphabetically beneath the AgentGroup. This specifies all the possible categories of agent that can be configured by this Agent Server. Click for more details: Note1: Only the agent types with a plus box to their left actually contain configured agents. Note2: The common Header slots, if included, of the GROUP agents are listed in the *Group Slots list beneath each agent type, that has configured agents. For details, see Including header slots . - The configured agents are listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type.

Contact details PLEASE NOTE: If you try to use your EXISTING Adroit 8, 7, 6, 5, 4x driver in Adroit 10, THEY WILL NOT WORK!!!. 1.) Backward Compatibility of Adroit 10 ----------------------------------------------- Note: Adroit 10 is backwardly compatible with the previous versions of Adroit i.e. projects created in previous versions can be run using Adroit 10. You can also refer to the 'Upgrading from an older version of Adroit' section. Users of existing Adroit installations, need to be aware of the following: 1. All previous versions of Adroit must first be uninstalled before installing Adroit 10. Note: Ensure the Adroit system folder does not contain any DLL files (especially protocol driver files) after uninstalling the older version of Adroit. 2. Any project (.WGP) files modified with Adroit 10 will render them incompatible with previous version of Adroit. This is because the status slots used to affect how a slot (value) was scanned are now being stored in the Agent Database (.wgp) file along with the other scanning related settings, such as the scan address, scan rate etc, as an IO flags setting. When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. IMPORTANT: When starting the Adroit 10 Agent Server for the first time and loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version, devices will most likely NEVER show healthy once all the devices are started. You need to save the Agent Database (.wgp) file FIRST and then restart the Agent Server and then you should see all the devices going healthy. 3. While we do not expect you to experience any problems, it is recommended to completely back up all the existing Adroit projects, before installing Adroit 10 to ensure that all the Adroit data, system, registry and event files are backed up. 4. If the existing Adroit installation is being used in a distributed environment, it is essential that EVERY Adroit Agent Server and Classic user interface be upgraded to Adroit 10. 5. Existing Adroit users will also require a HASP upgrade before installing Adroit 10. IMPORTANT: Adroit 10 HASPs are NOT backwardly compatible with previous versions of Adroit due to a change in the internal licensing structure of the HASPs from Adroit 10 onwards.

In Adroit 10, the logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Although if the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration, then the SQL... button of the Datasource field will be visible in the Edit Datalog agent dialog. Hence the Datalog agent should only be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period (Length...) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 24 hours. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. PLEASE NOTE: Protocol Drivers from ALL previous Adroit versions are INCOMPATIBLE with the Adroit 10 protocol drivers! Furthermore only a subset of the Adroit protocol drivers are provided, if you are using a driver that is not currently supported in Adroit 10 then contact support so that this driver can be added to Adroit 10. Therefore, when doing an uninstall/reinstall from Adroit 8 a check is now done for both the Supported and Unsupported Legacy Drivers (EXCL the drivers that are automatically installed): o If Unsupported Legacy Drivers are found then the user will see a confirmation dialog that defaults to NO - where he is told these are NOT supported, contact support to add them. Do you want to continue? If No it EXITS; if Yes then the drivers are moved to the .\LegacyDrivers\UNSUPPORTED folder (off the current installation folder) o If Supported Legacy Drivers are found (EXCL the drivers that are automatically installed) then the user will see a confirmation dialog that defaults to NO - where he is told since they cannot be used as-is and need to be reinstalled, these drivers have been moved into the .\LegacyDrivers folder (off the current installation folder), to allow you to decide which of these drivers you need to install BEFORE you can run your project. 9.

Ensure that the Windows operating system on which you intend to install Adroit has been and remains legally licensed and ACTIVATED, since Adroit is not supported when it is run on an unlicensed Windows operating system. 3. When installing and running Adroit on an operating system that provides User Account Control (UAC), such as Windows 7 or Windows Server 2008, please ensure that UAC is always ENABLED, since Adroit is not supported when it is run with UAC disabled. 4. Please be aware of the following limitations of total number of allowed connections imposed by Microsoft Workstation operating systems (such as Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 8.1 or Windows 10): o the total number of external connections is set to 10: this means that ANY connection to a workstation’s resources, whether via shares, printers, UI client etc. takes up one of these client connections. o the total number of simultaneous IIS connections is set to 5: this means that ONLY a maximum of 5 SUI Clients can connection to the SUI Server, over the Internet regardless of the number of concurrent Client connections specified by the license. So if you need more connections then you need to install a Server operating system (such as Windows Server 2008 R2, Windows Server 2012 and Windows Server 2012 R2) IMPORTANT: ALSO ensure that you are not using the built-in Administrator account to run Adroit, since UAC is automatically disabled whenever this built-in Administrator account is used. If the built-in Administrator account is accidentally enabled on your computer, disable it as follows: Log on to Windows with either the built-in Administrator account that is accidentally enabled, or with any other account that has administrative privileges. Right click the Start button and select Computer Management. On the opened Computer Management snap-in, from the left pane, expand the Local Users and Groups tree. Click to select Users. From the right pane, right-click the Administrator account. From the context menu, click Properties.

If this is not installed then the installation uses an offline installation that it provides to install this for you (so no further downloading is required). 6. When you install this 32 bit Adroit installed on a 64 bit operating system (OS), 64 bit versions of MS Excel and other 64 bit host applications cannot attach to the 32 bit versions of Adroit’s MIS Server or AS_API.DLL and other 32 bit components. Therefore you need to install and use 32 bit Excel programs and other 32 bit host applications; run script files that connect to Adroit’s MIS Server OLE Automation object from a 32 bit environment; 32 bit CMD command prompt windows (c:\windows\syswow64\cmd.exe) must be used; 32 bit CSCRIPT.EXE and WSCRIPT.EXE (as found in the c:\windows\syswow64 folder) must be used. IMPORTANT: By default, Start/Run/cmd on a 64 bit OS will run 64 bit versions of these programs so you must manually execute the 32 bit versions of these programs from the c:\windows\syswow64 folder 7. The Smart UI Performance Anywhere component, which allows your users to use Performance Anywhere dashboards (WebPortal clients) to create numerous pages in which you can place and configure widgets (controls) to display and in some cases configure your data, also requires a computer that has MS Internet Information Services installed, but for this component the default installation of IIS will suffice. This component also requires that the Smart UI Web Service component is also installed, typically on the same computer on which you install Performance Anywhere. You can use a single instance (ONE Performance Anywhere client) free of charge without any changes to your product license. If you require more than 1 concurrent Performance Anywhere client then you need to add the necessary number of Web Clients to your product license. If you have exceeded the number of available Web client (Performance Anywhere) licenses, then you will see the following error when you try to login: Error fetching XXX dashboard! Error! Number of connections licensed exceeded (where XXX is the specified username). Performance Anywhere Client (Dashboard) Internet Browser Requirements: On Windows 10: Microsoft Edge by default is unable to connect to computer names in their URLs, also it is not easy to determine when MS Edge is the default Internet browser so we enforce the use of Internet Explorer to launch the Performance Anywhere shortcut on Windows 10, since Internet Explorer is not hamstrung by these issues. In other words when you use Microsoft Edge to open the URL to Performance Anywhere it may not open, but you can use any other Internet browser, which is able to open this URL. When using Internet Explorer, please ensure that you use Internet Explorer 11 or later. IMPORTANT: Windows 7 does not come shipped with Internet Explorer 11, so you can either download the latest Google Chrome or download the Internet Explorer 11 update for Windows 7 via either Microsoft website or via Windows Update.

HMI Mode ---------------- HMI mode is a lower cost, simpler version of Adroit, which is a stand-alone solution that supports the addition of up to 2 clients. This cannot be incorporated into a larger distributed project and does not support redundancy.

text:
In HMI mode, the Adroit Agent Server has the following restrictions: • ONLY loads the following agent types: o Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required.

Title: How to set up Adroit Installation Read Me
Steps:
In HMI mode, the Adroit Agent Server has the following restrictions: • ONLY loads the following agent types: o Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! o Basic agents: Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, String, StringList and Timer IMPORTANT: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. o Advanced agents: AgentGroup, Alarm, AlarmList (only Default), AlarmManagement, Command, DBAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Script, Shift and Statistical o IT agents: Perfmon o System agents: Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan and SystemInformation • prevents the use of the following agent types: Accumulator, AREC, Audit, Custom, DumpConfig, Frame, ICMP, MaxDemand, Multistate, OEE, PID, Recipe, Scheduler, SNMPMgr, SystemDatalog and Text IMPORTANT: Due to this change, standard Agent Servers and their projects will be INCOMPATIBLE with HMI licensed Agent Servers and their projects, when they use any of these HMI-unsupported agent types. • the Agent Server can only be run in stand-alone mode and not cluster or cluster-aware mode. Note: In HMI mode, when the Agent Server is run, it is forced to run in stand-alone mode, regardless of its current setting. When installing Adroit for the first time, you can choose whether you want your default configuration to be in HMI mode or not. When using multiple configurations (when engineering multiple projects) in the Configuration dialog of the Adroit Config utility, you can specify which configurations runs in full or HMI mode, when creating them, depending upon your project's requirements. Note: If you have only installed the Agent Server and not the Smart UI Server, then you can manually put the Agent Server in and out of HMI mode by configuring the HMIMode registry value (this requires restarting the Agent Server). See the help file for more details. • if the Agent Server is licensed for HMI and Adroit has not been configured for HMI mode the Agent Server will display a message box that it cannot continue and it will terminate. The user must either enable the HMI configuration or change the HASP. • if Adroit has been configured for HMI mode and the Agent Server is not licensed for HMI, then the Agent Server will continue in HMI mode. 6.) Scan Point Licensing ---------------------------- Normally a scan point license is consumed whenever a tag is scanned to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other areas that consume scan point licenses as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. 1. Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. 2. Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. 3. Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot), using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface (MISSRVR) or the Adroit ActiveX component (AdroitX.OCX) will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked".

text:
Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses.

Title: How to set up Adroit Installation Read Me
Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. 4. Any tag (agent.slot) writes from the Adroit OPC Server will consume one scan point license per unique tag. 5. Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and / or used to send SMS messages to it. 6. The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for each unique value of an SNMP object that is polled (monitored), written (controlled) or trapped (received as an SNMP event). 7. Any agent created for a UDT agent type created by the UDT Agent Type Designer consumes (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. ONLY in HMI Mode: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. 7.) Adroit Compatibility with Anti-virus Software --------------------------------------------------------- Your IT department usually determines which Anti-virus software you will use. Adroit is compatible with all antivirus software, as long as it is configured not to interfere with the network settings nor should it block any of the Adroit executables from communicating on the network. Please ensure that you define your policy and procedure for updating this Anti-virus software clearly. For instance, if there is no internet connection then the updates will need to be loaded manually. In this case, perhaps schedule these manual updates by means of your maintenance planning system at a frequency determined by your IT department. 8.) Upgrading from an older version of Adroit ------------------------------------------------------ IMPORTANT: Existing Adroit users require NEW licenses for Adroit 10, since the entire licensing mechanism has changed! Although BOTH the Adroit 10 license and former Adroit 8 license can exist side by side on the SAME HASP - so that it is easy to roll back to Adroit 8 if needed. Note: Read the section: Backward Compatibility of Adroit 10, above. When upgrading, it is recommended that no other applications are running. Since the upgrading of an Adroit installation will fail if any of the existing Adroit components are in use. For instance, the Performance Monitor, Event Viewer and MISSRVR (OLE) client applications all make use of Adroit components. If you have one or more Custom agents and you update your Adroit version or upgrade to a newer version, you may need to republish these Custom agents, especially if the Custom agent has been updated, subsequent to when you originally published these agents. In this case: 1. Launch your Adroit Custom Agent Designer (for instance on Windows 10: Click the Start Menu, All apps, Adroit 10 and select the Custom Agent Designer). You will be prompted if a newer version of the custom agent (t_custom.dll) is in the CustomAgents folder of the Adroit projects folder, which is typically C:\AdroitProject\CustomAgents. 2. Stop the Agent Server, Adroit UI and any other Adroit components. 3. Select each custom agent and click the Publish button. 4. This will copy the necessary custom agent files (.CSV, .DLL and .VBS if you are using scripting) into the Adroit installation folder on this computer, typically C;\Adroit. 5. Restart your Agent Server, Adroit UI and any other Adroit components. Note: If there are any remote Adroit installations that connect to this Agent Server, these derived custom agent files must also be MANUALLY copied to their Adroit system directories as well.

Use the following syntax when specifying the user name: For users on the local computer: UserName For users on a domain: domainName\UserName. IMPORTANT: Ensure that the specified password does not expire, otherwise you will need to manually reconfigure this yourself each time the password changes. If you uncheck the the "Configure services" option, this will NOT install the Agent Server service NOR configure the startup of this (and the Smart UI Server) service. However, the Smart UI Server service will be installed and the Service Manager will also be displayed as a notification icon but ONLY the Smart UI Server service will be displayed. Note: This setting is a configurable via the "Theme" list box at the bottom of the Adroit Config Editor. Note: A restart of the computer is ONLY required if BOTH the Adroit Agent Server and the Smart UI Server is installed by the selected installation option OR if a system file required by the Adroit install could not be installed as it was in use at the time. The Agent Server starts the Smart UI Server, as follows: Note: This functionality requires the currently logged on user to either be an Administrator or a Power User. If the Agent Server is started as a service then: a. Adroit will attempt to start the Smart UI Service. b. If the Smart UI Service fails to start, Adroit will attempt to start the Smart UI Server. The Adroit Technologies Service Manager manages (starts and/or stops) the services of all the Adroit Technologies products installed on the computer, which in the case of Adroit 8 is the Agent Server service and/or the Smart UI Server service. If the Agent Server is started as an application then: a. Adroit will attempt to start the Smart UI Server only. b. If the Smart UI Server fails to start, nothing happens.

Windows 7: @echo off taskkill /IM explorer.exe /F cd /d %userprofile%\AppData\Local del IconCache.db /a start explorer.exe Windows 8 and 10: @echo off taskkill /IM explorer.exe /F cd /d %userprofile%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer del iconcache* /a start explorer.exe Then run this CMD file as an Administrator to force Windows to rebuild its icon cache, which will sort out your mismatched icon problems. 10.) Installing Adroit over the Network ---------------------------------------------- This may be required, if Adroit 10 is required on a networked computer. IMPORTANT: The installation menu is NOT designed to work off network shares. So if you copy the contents of the installation media to a shared folder on a PC on the network and try to launch the installation menu from this network location you will receive a Microsoft .NET Framework unhandled exception, something like: Value of '\\networkShare\Path\Adroit 10\Launcher\images\Adroit.ico' is not valid for 'filePath'. To workaround this, create a drive mapping for the \\networkShare\Path up to the name of the folder containing the installation media and then run it from there, for instance if you create a drive mapping called P:\ for the \\networkShare\Path in the above example (which you can do via the Command Prompt using the following command: subst p: "\\networkShare\Path"), so that the path to the installation media, using the mapped path, in this example, would be P:\Adroit 10 (as it would be if this were being run from a DVD or flash drive). Then have your users run the installation menu from this path. 11.) Title: How to set up Adroit Installation Read Me

Your product license can either be a HASP and a soft license, each of which have the following important differences: o A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk. o A Soft license is bound to a specific computer and therefore cannot be transferred to another computer. Therefore if the computer fails then the soft license will no longer work. IMPORTANT: In order to get or update a product license you need to be able to send and receive files via email, either directly or remotely via another device. How to get a new HASP license or update an existing one: 1. Launch the Adtech Licensing Utility, typically via the Adroit Utilities on the Desktop and then select this utility from this menu. 2. Ensure that your HASP is inserted into the computer. If necessary, click the Rescan HASPs button in the lower right corner. The Request HASP Update button should now be enabled. 3. If the Request HASP Update button is disabled then there is a problem reading your HASP, in which case do the following: Click the Status tab and right click this page and click the Select all menu item. Then right click this page and click the Copy menu item. Email the contents of this tab to your sales representative for further assistance. 4. Click the Request HASP Update button. This will temporarily disable the Refresh Current License and the Apply License (V2C) buttons, indicating that this request is being processed. 5. Once the .c2v (Customer to vendor) file has been created for this HASP license: Windows Explorer is opened, displaying the folder in which this .c2v file has been copied, which adheres to the following syntax: it begins with HL- followed by the unique serial number of your HASP.c2v The Main tab of the Adtech Licensing Utility also displays the location of this .c2v file and the email address to which this file should be sent. 6a. If you have an email client on your local computer, then do the following: Click this email address link, which opens your default email client and creates the License Request email message for you that is addressed to the required email address. In this case simply attach the .c2v file and send it off. 6b. If you cannot email from the local computer, then do the following: Make a note of the required email address Copy the resultant .c2v file to a device that is able to email Create an email that is addressed to the specified email address that is entitled "License Request : " and then copy the entire name of your .c2v file Attach this .c2v file and send it off. 7. Once the .v2c (Vendor to Customer) file is emailed back to you, copy this file to a folder on the computer on which you have installed Adroit 10 Agent Server. 8. Click the Apply License (V2C) button. 9. In the Open Vendor to Customer (.v2c) Filedialog, browse to the folder in which you copied the . v2c file and select this .v2c file and click the Open button. Your license is updated and your license details are displayed in the License tab. How to get a new soft license or update an existing one: 1. Specify the name of the virtual directory that must be created for this web service in the Name edit box. By default the virtual directory is called VIP. 2. If necessary, specify the website in which this virtual directory must be created, by selecting it from the Site list box. By default, the Default Web Site is selected. NOTE: The Smart UI Web Service does not work on a 32 bit Windows 10 (possibly Windows 8 as well). The symptom is that clients (Operators or Performance Anywhere clients) cannot login via the web connection even though everything seems to be installed correctly and running. TO FIX THIS: open IIS (typical by right clicking the Windows menu and selecting Computer Management and then under Services and and Applications, select Internet Information Services), then select the topmost Application Pools item (immediately under the selected computer name) and select the relevant Application Pool under which the web service is running, typically SUIAppPool and right click it and select Advanced Settings..., in this dialog in the "Process Model" section locate the Identity field and click the browse button to the right of this field and in the "Application Pool Identity" dialog, select the Custom account option and click the Set.. button and specify the credentials of the required user account that has administrative privileges, and then OK all the open dialogs. Then right click this Application Pool (SUIAppPool) again and select its Recycle... option to restart it and effect this change in Identity. 3. The Web Service Config file contains a number of settings that pertain to the operation of the Web Service. Typically the default values of these settings should be adequate for Performance Anywhere, although you may need to adjust the following settings by editing this file yourself to resolve the following Performance Anywhere connection and performance issues: Note: Be VERY careful when editing this file; since if you corrupt the file structure nothing will work. Please ask support for help if you need it and BACKUP the existing file before you start editing it. File location: This file is called Web.config and is located in the root folder of the Web Service component, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice IMPORTANT: After editing the Web.config file, you need to restart IIS, which you can do by opening the Command Prompt (Admin) and entering the following command: iisreset •If the Smart UI Server is on another computer than the Smart UI Web Service. Then edit the <add key="server" value="localhost"/> to specify the computer name or IP address of the Smart UI Server computer. •If the Smart UI Server is running on a port other than 9010. Then uncomment the <add key="serverPort" value="9500"/> and change the port value to the port value that the Smart UI Server is running on. •If the Performance Anywhere clients are experiencing problems where the Charting widgets are taking too long update or do not have any data; or images take too long to load or the Data Element Browser either does not display any tags or takes to long to load etc. Then edit the <add key="ServiceRequestTimeout" value="60"/> and increase this timeout which specifies the timeout in seconds for any requests made by the Web Service or Performance Anywhere to the Smart UI Server. IMPORTANT: When using large Agent databases, even changing this setting may not fix the issue where the Data Element Browser either does not display any tags.

Known Issues ---------------------- At the time of release the following known issues concerning the operation of Adroit 10 was noted: 1. Object Model: a. This is caused by a bug in the Softing library that is being used, where they cannot resolve local endpoints when using IP6 addressing which all machines do by default. By default both the install and the .bat file used to create the OPCUA certificates run the following two commands to force the system to favour IP4 over IP6 when resolving its addresses: netsh interface ipv6 set prefix ::/96 60 3 AND netsh interface ipv6 set prefix ::ffff:0:0/96 55 4 If after running these commands manually via an elevated command prompt you are STILL unable to enumerate endpoints on a local OPC UA server, which may occur when your computer has multiple network cards, then phone support to resolve this issue. 22. If you uncheck the the "Configure services" option during the installation then this will NOT install the Agent Server service NOR configure the startup of this (and the Smart UI Server) service. However, the Smart UI Server service will be installed and the Service Manager will also be displayed as a notification icon but ONLY the Smart UI Server service will be displayed. If necessary you can install the Agent Server service later in the "Agent Server Configuration" page of the Adroit Config Editor. PLEASE NOTE: Refer to the 'changelog.txt' file that is installed in the Adroit installation folder, which contains a complete history of the specific file changes made to this release after its initial release date. 17.) Adroit Licensing Top Adroit Licensing The only component in Adroit that needs to be licensed is the Agent Server.

Title: Adroit Licensing
Adroit Licensing Top Adroit Licensing The only component in Adroit that needs to be licensed is the Agent Server. For details on licensing the Agent Server, see Licensing the Agent Server . Typically, the Agent Server is licensed via a HASP software protection key, which is inserted into either the parallel or USB port of the computer on which the Agent Server is running. This HASP is then programmed in accordance with your specific license agreement. In situations where it is not possible to use a physical HASP, it is also possible to license Adroit via a software license, which is only available on request. For further details, contact the Adroit support department. For further details on how to get, view and/or update your product license, see Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility . Note: It is also possible to evaluate Adroit freely, by using the limited time license HASP, which runs the Agent Server with a 58 minute operating license with 30000 scan points and 2 remote connections. For details, see Limited Time License HASP . The Agent Server licence typically specifies the following components: - The unique serial number that identifies this Adroit Agent Server. - The version of the Adroit product that this licence applies to. - The available number of scanned point licences these are also known as "scan points". These are consumed when information is being manipulated in some way, typically when communicating (scanning) a value to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other consumers of scan point licenses. For details, see Scan Point Licensing Exceptions . Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. IMPORTANT: The former Remote Nodes licenses that applied to all types of clients have been DISCONTINUED . These have now been replaced by the following client specific node licenses, each of which have different costs: - Clients : typically Operators and/or Designers and - Web Clients : typically Performance Anywhere clients. Note: Agent Server to Agent Server connections do not require remote connection licenses. - Whether any OEM licenses or component counts have been specified. These are programmatic components that require separate licensing before they can be used. - Whether the Agent Server in being run in HMI mode or not. The HMI mode reduces the functionality of the Agent Server to provide a cost-effective, bulk implementation of HMI software. - If necessary, the expiration date of the HASP, which can be used to safeguard the software. When a running Agent Server reaches the expiration date of the license (HASP), then the scanning is stopped but the clients are not disconnected. But when this Agent Server is restarted, both scanning and client connections will be prevented. Note: Once the expiration date of the HASP has been exceeded, the HASP will no longer be detected until it has been re-licensed. When the Agent Server starts up, this license information is displayed in its application window , as follows: HASP SN : Serial Number, [PARTNER SN: Serial Number of clustered Agent Server,] ID: ID Number, Ver: Adroit version i.e. 1000 is Adroit version 10.0, Scan: Scan Points, Drivers=1 (if licensed for drivers), Designer:#, Operator:#, Web:# (number of licensed remote client connections), HMI: Status of HMI mode, Expiry: Expiry date of the HASP.

Licensing when using Terminal clients (Remote Desktop): EACH Adroit client application launched using new terminal client (Remote Desktop) takes a (remote node) connection licence.

Title: Adroit Licensing
Licensing when using Terminal clients (Remote Desktop): EACH Adroit client application launched using new terminal client (Remote Desktop) takes a (remote node) connection licence. When Adroit clients are launched via a remote desktop using the session of the console user (either session 0 or 1 depending on the operating system), then these Agent Server connections are treated as legacy local connections which do NOT require connection licences. See Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit . For further details relating to HASP software protection keys, see HASP Software Protection Key . For an overview of what Agent Servers do, see About Agent Servers . -->

Adroit Logging Factor Top Adroit Logging Factor When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world.

Title: Adroit Logging Factor
Steps:
Adroit Logging Factor Top Adroit Logging Factor When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world. Up until 1992 the generally accepted default practice was for users to datalog all points at 1 second. However, due to CPU, HDD speeds and serial protocol speeds, the fastest data could only logged at 4-5 seconds. Therefore the log file created by Adroit was deliberately engineered to always be 20% of the expected size, since Adroit only stores data when it in physically changes. This logging design started to become a problem when hardware and protocol speeds improved OR where high logging time deadband values (or sample rates) were used especially for Analog agents where one could be assured that its value WAS going to be different at each sample period. In these cases, only 20% of the specified historical data is actually recorded. The legacy default for Adroit ’s proprietary logging of using a 20% datalog compression factor has been REMOVED for all new installations, since it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods. However, if a legacy WGP file is opened by a new installation of Adroit , that the logging periods configured for some or all of the Datalog agents will exceed the allowable size limit of 5000000 samples (or 95 MB) per Datalog agent. This will occur since the legacy method of accommodating this 20% datalog compression factor allowed the required log period to be up to 5 times greater. In these cases these "non-compliant" Datalog agents will display "error load completion" events. Note: Ensure that you have enabled the logging of Adroit system events in order to identify these non-compliant Datalog agents. For details, see Enabling the logging of Adroit system events. To remedy these "non-compliant" Datalog agents either set the LogCompressionFactor value in the Adroit registry back to its legacy default of 5 and restart the Agent Server OR reconfigure the logging periods of the affected Datalog agents, which should typically require the currently specified logging period to be divided by 5. -->

In Adroit certain components require a SEPARATE license BEFORE they can be used, this is known as an OEM licensed component. Note: Any pokes performed, using this Adroit ActiveX component will require a scan point license for each unique tag that is "poked". The adroitx.htm sample file provides an example of how to use the Adroit ActiveX control in a web page. If installed, this is located in C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \Samples\Web folder. -->

Title: General Settings
- Server: Specify the name of your SmartUI Server that contains the required OLEDB Datasource. - Datasource: Select the OLEDB Datasource on this SmartUI Server that is connected your AlarmManagement agent SQL Server database. - Best Fit Columns: This checkbox is checked by default to force all the displayed columns in the grid to automatically resize their widths so that their contents fit in the control without requiring any horizontal scrolling. - Columns: Click the browse (...) button to choose which columns are displayed in the grid, their order and their specific properties as you would when using the Columns tab of a relevant configuration dialog. For details, see Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns . - Use Paging : This checkbox is checked by default to group the available alarms in the grid into pages of alarms. Paging makes it easier for users to browse a large number of alarms. Note: When unchecked this disables (greys out) the 4 paging navigation buttons and the Page size edit field on the left of the toolbar . - Page size: This is ONLY displayed when paging is used to specify the default number of alarms that are displayed on each page. - Enable Filtering : This checkbox is checked by default to allow users to add and/or use filters to restrict or limit the number of displayed alarms initially. However, even if unchecked users can still select the Enable Filtering option from the Filter tool menu to use filters. - Predefined Filters: This allows you to create general-purpose filters that always appear in the Filter list of the toolbar, which your users can immediately use to refine the displayed alarms. More details: Click the browse (...) button to display the CustomFilter Collection Editor . Click the Add button, then specify the required FilterName and its FilterString of this filter Tip: An easy way to determine the required FilterString , is to run the graphic form and then click the Filter tool menu of the toolbar and select the Add Filter... item and then click the + button or press the INSERT key and define the required filter that you want and then write down the filter string displayed at the bottom of this Add Filter dialog and type this into this FilterString edit field.

FilterString Examples: DateTime <= 2015-08-03 : [DT] <= #2015-08-03# Incident Begins with D : [Incident] Like 'D%' - Enable Find : This checkbox is checked by default to displays the Find bar beneath the toolbar, so that users can type in a string so that ONLY rows containing this specified text string is displayed.

Title: General Settings
FilterString Examples: DateTime <= 2015-08-03 : [DT] <= #2015-08-03# Incident Begins with D : [Incident] Like 'D%' - Enable Find : This checkbox is checked by default to displays the Find bar beneath the toolbar, so that users can type in a string so that ONLY rows containing this specified text string is displayed. However, even if unchecked users can still select the Enable Find tool to display the Find bar themselves. - Group Summaries: These are summaries or group-specific calculations that are ONLY displayed when you group data, by dragging the relevant column/s into the grouping bar above the column headers. More details: Note: By default these summaries are displayed next to each grouped item, whether expanded or collapsed, unless you specifically specify the ShowInGroupColumnFooter field, in which case the group summary bar is displayed and this group summary will be displayed in the column for each specific group is displayed. Click the browse (...) button to display the GroupSummary Collection Editor . Click the Add button, then specify the required summary, by specifying the following fields: - FieldName : the field that the summary operation applies to, this is the actual name of the database field, for instance DT and not the displayed description, in this case DateTime - ShowInGroupColumnFooter : if this is left BLANK then the specified summary is displayed next to each grouped item, whether expanded or collapsed; otherwise the group summary bar is displayed and this group summary will be displayed in the column for each specific group is displayed. - SummaryDisplayFormat : display format of the resultant summary calculation and any additional text that this should provide, for instance: {0:n0} rows - SummaryType : the type of the summary calculation that is required, for instance: Count. Tip: A useful group summary is displaying the number of rows contained within each group, which you can configure as follows: FieldName: DT ShowInGroupColumnFooter: leave this BLANK SummaryDisplayFormat: {0:n0} rows SummaryType: Count - Refresh Mode or Subscription Update Mode : Select the required method used to refresh this control with recent alarms, depending on how the Historical Incidents table of the AlarmManagement database has been connected to this control. For more details, see Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls .

- Toolbar Visible : This checkbox is checked by default to displays the toolbar in the control, so users can use its tools to view and/or locate and/or filter the historical alarms they require and/or configure the display of this grid and its columns at runtime.

Title: Appearance Settings
- Toolbar Visible : This checkbox is checked by default to displays the toolbar in the control, so users can use its tools to view and/or locate and/or filter the historical alarms they require and/or configure the display of this grid and its columns at runtime. - Toolbar color : specify the required background color of the toolbar, since this is NOT changed by the selected Look and Feel Skin . - Look and Feel Skin : select the required theme which ONLY affects the color and formatting of the grid; although you can separately configure the background color of the toolbar via the Toolbar color . - Alternate Row colors : This checkbox is unchecked by default to not enable the Alternate Row color tool by default to display the odd and/or even rows in the grid with the colors specified by the Appearance tab of the relevant configuration dialogs, since these colors are not configured by default. -->

Title: Tools provided for AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls:
- Paging : When paging is used to browse the available alarms in this grid, these controls allows you to move between the available pages and/or define the required page size (the number of alarms on each page). Note: The Use Paging checkbox in the Tasks menu (UsePaging property) determines whether this control uses paging, which is enabled by default, if set to False all of these controls are disabled (grayed out). - Columns : This displays the Columns Configuration dialog so that users can choose which columns are displayed in the grid, their order and their specific properties. For details, see Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns . - Constraints : This displays the Constraints Configuration dialog to further refine the displayed alarms to eliminate unnecessary alarms. For details, see Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer columns . - Filter : This menu, enables or disables the use of filters and/or allows you add and/or remove filters that you want to create: - Enable Filtering : when enabled this is highlighted, which allows you to add and/or use filters to restrict or limit the number of displayed alarms, this option can be enabled by default. - Add Filter... : this displays the Add Filter dialog, which allows you to define the required filter as follows: - Specify a descriptive name for this filter so that you can easily identify what it does in the Filter Name field. - If necessary click the default And and select how this condition is required to relate to other conditions specified for this filter. For details, see the Available relationships: Note: It is possible to separate your conditions into groups, which act like parentheses in this logical expression. - Click the Plus button or press the INSERT or + key to define the required condition that must be met in order for alarms to be displayed, as follows: - If necessary, click the [DateTime] item to select the required column in the grid that this condition applies to. For details, see the Available columns: - If necessary, click the Equals to specify the required operator or what the values of this column need to do in order to successfully fulfill the requirements of this condition. For details, see the Available operators: - Click the <enter a value> to specify the specific value requirement of this condition. Note: To remove a condition, click its Delete button or press the DELETE or - key. Tip: You will notice that at the bottom of this dialog, the actual filter query syntax is specified, which you can write down and type this into the FilterString edit field, when creating predefined filters. - Delete All Filters : to delete all filters that have been added using this Filter menu, this will NOT remove any predefined filters i.e. any filters that were already in the filter list box when this graphic form was opened. - Enable Find : When this tool is selected, the Find bar is displayed beneath the toolbar, so that users can type in a string so that ONLY rows containing this specified text string is displayed. - Print Preview : This displays a WYSIWYG What you see is what you get print preview of the grid, that provides additional options, such as selecting which printer to use and other options that configure the printed output, which you can preview before using. - Printing : This immediately sends the grid and its current contents to the printer, using the print settings specified via the Print Preview dialog; which is the default printer unless otherwise specified!

- Exporting : Export the columns and rows of the grid to a number of different document formats, such as PDF or HTML typically for reporting purposes or to CSV or the applicable MS Excel spreadsheet format typically to allow you to perform third party application reporting of this data.

Title: Tools provided for AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls:
- Exporting : Export the columns and rows of the grid to a number of different document formats, such as PDF or HTML typically for reporting purposes or to CSV or the applicable MS Excel spreadsheet format typically to allow you to perform third party application reporting of this data. - Alternate Row Color : This enables the display of the odd and/or even rows in different colors to make it easier to differentiate between the different alarms in the grid, which depend upon whether these have been configured via the Appearance tab of the relevant configuration dialog. For details, see Configuring AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer appearance . - General Configuration : This tabbed dialog allows you to configure the generally applicable settings of this control, namely: how it is updated with the most recent alarms via its DataSource tab; configuring its Columns; configuring the applicable Constraints, such as the time period of applicable alarms and/or specifying its Appearance, such as configuring its alternate row colors. For details, see General configuration settings . - Manual Refresh : Populates the grid with the latest contents of the Alarm Management table, so this action updates the grid with the most recent alarms. Note: This button does not appear when subscription updates are used to update this grid with more recent alarms. For details, see Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls . - Help : This displays this help topic. -->
