Advanced Agent Server Configuration Top Advanced Agent Server Configuration Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Advanced Agent Server Configuration Top Advanced Agent Server Configuration Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. - Agent Server Parameters : settings affecting the configuration and saving of the Adroit database (.WGP) file and the location of the Adroit system folder. - Distributed Event Routing: settings that allow you to route distributed error reports to a particular route number. For each event type: Connected , Connection lost, Tag not found , or Duplicate tagname , a route number may be specified. It is RECOMMENDED to NOT CONFIGURE these settings. - WGP Versioning: settings that configure the automatic backup of WGP files and its versioning. - The Delete WGP backup files older than # days to and a maximum limit of # files edit boxes are used to configure the optional automatic backup of WGP files, for details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . - The Enable WGP version description entries checkbox, is used to enable or disable the appearance of the Save WGP file pop-up dialog when the WGP file is manually saved - so that a description of the changes made to it since its previous save can be entered. For details of this and the other versioning information saved to each WGP file, see Versioning WGP Files . - Server Auditing: allows you to audit the Agent Server, in other words to log each Agent Server session each time an application is started and stopped on a computer constitutes a single session of this program. and selected activities performed during these sessions to an OLE DB database. For details, see Agent Server Auditing . - Debug Flags: settings used primarily by Adroit support engineers, for diagnosing system problems. WARNING! Turning these on SLOWS the Agent Server down . For details, see Adroit About Debug Flags . - Processor affinity: allows you to select which processors the Agent Server runs on simultaneously, for computers that have more than one physical processor, by checking the required checkboxes. By default ONLY the first processor is selected. The following items are only provided by Adroit Config Editor : - Event Logging: check the Enable logging of Agent Server system events checkbox, to enable the logging of such events as: when time-stamped data is rejected by a mimic for being to old etc. - Agent Server Connectivity: From Adroit 10 Agent Servers allow clients to connect to them by using sockets over and above the legacy named pipes. - Sockets give you better performance when a remote client (running on another computer) connects to an Agent Server. - Named pipes gives you better performance when a local client (running on the same computer) connects to an Agent Server. Therefore Adroit client software need to specify which of the following mechanisms they want to use when connecting to local and remote Agent Servers: - Uncompressed Named Pipes (UNP) both locally and remotely: this is the legacy default. - UNP locally, and Sockets (TCP) remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications and where network traffic needs to be controlled across switches etc. - Compressed Named Pipes (CNP) both locally and remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications with restricted connectivity. - TCP both locally and remotely: TCP is slower for local connections when compared to UNP. IMPORTANT: Please ensure that all Adroit computers across your enterprise are configured for either named pipes or sockets, but not a mixture thereof! - Legacy UI Parameters: When converting your existing Classic UI mimics and/or trends into SmartUI graphic forms, then check the Enable Xaml Saving checkbox.

Note: You need to RESTART the Classic UI after changing this setting.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Note: You need to RESTART the Classic UI after changing this setting. This enables the “secondary” xaml saving functionality in the Classic UI. So when saving a mimic (with this setting enabled) in the Classic UI, you will be prompted to save the mimic as a .xaml file as well as a .mim file. This .xaml file is used to import this mimic document into the SmartUI. This also enables the “secondary” xml saving functionality in the Classic UI. So when saving a trend (with this setting enabled) in the Classic UI, you will be prompted to save the trend as a .xml file as well as a .trn file. This .xml file is used to import this trend document into the SmartUI. -->

The following items are only provided by Adroit Config Editor : - Event Logging: check the Enable logging of Agent Server system events checkbox, to enable the logging of such events as: when time-stamped data is rejected by a mimic for being to old etc. - Agent Server Connectivity: From Adroit 10 Agent Servers allow clients to connect to them by using sockets over and above the legacy named pipes. - Sockets give you better performance when a remote client (running on another computer) connects to an Agent Server. - Named pipes gives you better performance when a local client (running on the same computer) connects to an Agent Server. Therefore Adroit client software need to specify which of the following mechanisms they want to use when connecting to local and remote Agent Servers: - Uncompressed Named Pipes (UNP) both locally and remotely: this is the legacy default. - UNP locally, and Sockets (TCP) remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications and where network traffic needs to be controlled across switches etc. - Compressed Named Pipes (CNP) both locally and remotely: this provides the best performance for LAN/WAN applications with restricted connectivity. - TCP both locally and remotely: TCP is slower for local connections when compared to UNP.

IMPORTANT: Please ensure that all Adroit computers across your enterprise are configured for either named pipes or sockets, but not a mixture thereof!

Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) Top Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) This dialog provides global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub system.

Title: Configuration
Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) Top Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) This dialog provides global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub system. To display this dialog: - If necessary, launch the Classic User Interface, as follows: click the Start menu, Programs, Adroit 10 and select the Classic User Interface item). - Click on the Configurator toolbar button to display the Agent Configuration dialog box. Ensure that the System checkbox is checked to display the Datalog agent type in this list. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list - Click the Datalog agent type. - Click any of the agents in the Agents list. - Click the Edit button. - Click the Advanced… button in the Edit Datalog Agent dialog. Note: This dialog can only be displayed, once you have logged an agent and have thereby created a Datalog agent. These settings are divided into the following three main sections: Note: The settings in the General and SQL logging sections require the Agent Server to be RESTARTED before applying the configured setting/s. Tip: Click the section headings to show or hide their settings. General: Datalog system buffer size (Kb) This setting specifies the size of the global "datalog change queue", which is 500 Kb, by default. Click for more details: All changes arriving at the data logging subsystem are added to a "datalog change queue". This ensures that these historical updates do not affect the throughput of any real-time updates. These changes are stored in this queue until Adroit reads them off. Therefore, the size of the queue must be able to handle the maximum spike of changed values that a plant can expect. This maximum number of changes is generally proportional to the number of tags logged. The default size of 500Kb, allows for approximately a spike of 11000 changes. It is possible that the sustained (not the instantaneous) rate of plant changes will exceed the rate at which the data logging subsystem is able to operate. In this case, the Agent Server is simply not capable of handling the data logging requirement and the computer will require upgrading or the data logging task musts be split over separate Agent Servers OR less tags need to be logged. For this reason we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor "SubManQueueLen" performance counter of the Agent Server to ensure that it always tends towards 100%, as this counter indicates the free datalog buffer queue. If this value is steadily decreasing, then the rate of datalogging is exceeding the rate at which the values can be committed to disk and the Flush lazily global logging setting should be turned ON. Note: The default value is big enough to handle short term spikes in putslot rates and should not need to be changed. Tip: When specifying the required buffer queue size, use the provided buttons to increase/decrease this value in 64 KB increments/decrements. Disable legacy file compression of 5:1 (LogCompressionFactor =1) This setting removes the legacy default 20% datalog compression setting when using the proprietary logging of Adroit and is ON (checked) by default for new installations. This setting is removed as it unnecessarily misleads users when configuring logging periods and has been outmoded by the newer hardware. Click for more details . Flush lazily (LazyFlushing = 1) This setting determines how Adroit writes logged values to disk, which is ON (checked) by default, so that Adroit logs its values to the file cache of the Windows operating system. If you uncheck this option (turn it OFF) then logged data is immediately written to disk.

Click for more details: - If checked (the default option), this results in a DELAY before this cache saves the data, due to the amount of file I/O activity on the computer.

Title: Configuration
Click for more details: - If checked (the default option), this results in a DELAY before this cache saves the data, due to the amount of file I/O activity on the computer. Therefore, if the computer is not on a UPS and there is a power failure, ALL datalog values that have not been committed to disk by Windows will be LOST. - If unchecked, all logged values are IMMEDIATELY written to disk but this increases the CPU load and slows the Agent Server down. Therefore we recommend that you use the PerfMon agent to monitor the CPU load for very high values and also monitor the "SubManQueueLen" performance counter of the Agent Server, which indicates the free datalog buffer queue and should remain around 100%. If this value is steadily decreasing, then the rate of datalogging is exceeding the rate at which the values can be committed to disk and flush lazily should be turned ON. In this case a UPS is highly recommended to allow operators to effect a controlled shutdown of the Agent Server computer, thereby preserving all datalogged values. Disable first datalog entries on startup of agent server (SuppressLogAtStartup = 1) This setting determines whether a value is logged at startup for each value that you have logged (the Post_Startup_Value For every session (the period between the startup and shutdown of the Agent Server), Adroit will always denotes the first and last entries in the log as the Post_Startup_Value and Last_Known_Value. All intermediate values will be marked as normal or bad. :), which is OFF (unchecked) by default, so that this ‘Post_Startup_Value’ is logged by the Agent Server. However, if you have logged a large number of values (this amount is site-dependant) to SQL, then the logging of these Post_Startup_Values can significantly increase the time the Agent Server takes to startup. Note: ONLY suppress the logging at startup IF there IS a real issue with startup times when logging to SQL. In this case, you can check this setting (turn it ON), which stops the Agent Server from retrieving any logged values to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Note: When this setting is ON, then you are unable to determine from the logged data, where an Agent Server was restarted. Support compression algorithm on demand logging (SupportCompressionOnDemand = 1) This setting enables the use of Datalog compression algorithms when using the Demand Mode of datalogging, by default, this setting is OFF (unchecked) so you are unable to use compression algorithms when Demand logging. Click for more details about Demand logging: The Demand mode of data-logging, unlike the default Continuous mode, only logs a data value when the LogNow or Trigger slots of the Datalog agent are activated. This allows you to decrease the size of your log files by using a script (or some other external intelligence) to drive the logging of a datalog. For instance, by only triggering the log when the value is between certain limits or at particular times of the batch, instead of logging every change in value. For further details, see Demand Logging . To further reduce the size of your datalogs, you can check this setting (turn it ON), so that you can specify a Time deadband and employ one of the datalog Compression Methods. For details, see Data Logging Compression Methods .

Settings that affect the operation of the data logging system that are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =1) This setting causes the Agent Server to attempt to create the necessary tables in SQL at startup, for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, which is ON (checked) by default.

Title: Configuration
Settings that affect the operation of the data logging system that are typically applied irrespective of the selected Datasource (the Adroit proprietary log files or SQL logging) SQL logging: Check for existence of database tables on startup (CreateTablesOnStartup =1) This setting causes the Agent Server to attempt to create the necessary tables in SQL at startup, for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, which is ON (checked) by default. This can increase the time the Agent Server takes to startup, especially if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL. If this option is UNCHECKED (turned OFF): - Adroit creates the necessary tables when creating NEW datalogs (from the Configurator). - Adroit does NOT check for the existence of these tables when the Agent Server starts up. This means that datalogs will NOT write if their tables do not exist. Therefore, if you have a large number of values that are being logged to SQL and you have ensured that the datalogs for these EXISTING values have their necessary tables, then UNCHECK this option (turn it OFF) to reduce the time taken by the Agent Server to startup. Disable database table name prefixes (DisableADOTableNamePrefix = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to create tables for each value that is being logged to a SQL database, by using the following table name format AdroitRawLog_[tablename], which is OFF (unchecked) by default. If you prefer Adroit to ONLY specify the table name and hence create shorter table names, then check this setting (turn it ON). This removes this "AdroitRawLog_" table name prefix, so that Adroit only uses the specified table name. Add normal timestamp fields to database tables (LogADODataTimes = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server NOT to log readable timestamps for values that are logged to SQL databases, which is OFF (unchecked) by default. So that ONLY the Adroit timestamp of the change in value is provided, this is not ‘readable’ in SQL as this does not conform to the DateTime value type. If you want Adroit to provide an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, then you can check this setting (turn it ON). However, then you must DELETE all your existing database tables and allow Adroit to re-create them with an added timestamp column. Tip: We recommend that you check this setting (turn it ON) before logging values to the SQL database. Use only proprietary logged data for trends (ProprietarySetPreference =1) This setting prevents Adroit from using data from SQL for trending, regardless of the circumstances, this is OFF (unchecked) by default. Typically you would turn this setting ON if you use at least 2 log sets to log ALL your values, one that logs to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and another that logs to SQL. In this case, by enabling this setting Adroit will ONLY trend data from the log set that logs values to Adroit ’s proprietary log files and NEVER trend data from a log set that logs values to SQL. This ensures that your trends quickly retrieve and display their historical data. Settings that ONLY apply when using OLEDB Data Logging or the SQL Datasource. IMPORTANT: Although reference is only made to SQL in these settings, they apply to any OLEDB compatible database. UI settings (no restart required): Create datalog agents automatically (AutoCreate = 1) This setting causes the Agent Server to immediately create a Datalog agent when you log an agent from the Configurator, which is ON (checked) by default.

Since each agent has a default logging slot that is automatically selected, you can uncheck this option (turn it OFF) if you usually need to log another slot.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Since each agent has a default logging slot that is automatically selected, you can uncheck this option (turn it OFF) if you usually need to log another slot. In this case, a confirmation dialog is launched, asking the user whether a new Datalog agent should be created, before a slot of an agent can be logged. Settings that ONLY apply to the Configurator dialog within the Classic User Interface. -->

Advanced OEE agent configuration options Top Advanced OEE agent configuration options When editing an OEE agent, click the Advanced button to display the Advanced OEE options dialog, which allows you to configure the following: - Optional tag references : instead of manually specifying them or scanning the relevant slots directly, you can browse in tag values to specify the following values: - Available tag : a BOOLEAN value used to determine when to calculate OEE.

Title: Configuration
Advanced OEE agent configuration options Top Advanced OEE agent configuration options When editing an OEE agent, click the Advanced button to display the Advanced OEE options dialog, which allows you to configure the following: - Optional tag references : instead of manually specifying them or scanning the relevant slots directly, you can browse in tag values to specify the following values: - Available tag : a BOOLEAN value used to determine when to calculate OEE. Typically you will browse in the BOOLEAN value slot of the pre-configured Scheduler agent Note : This value should only be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. - Running tag : a BOOLEAN value used to determine when to calculate a KPI. Note: Running time is typically automatically incremented by the agent while this BOOLEAN value is ON. - Input1 tag : a REAL value that is either the measurement variable used to calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment or plant or the FIRST variable of the KPI. Typically the REAL input1 slot is scanned directly. - Input2 tag : a REAL value that is the SECOND variable of the KPI. Typically the REAL input2 slot is scanned directly. - Reject count tag : a REAL value used to determine the Quality factor of the OEE calculation. If you are logging the data to an OLE DB database, then you can specify: - Product tag : a STRING value that specifies an optional product name that will be recorded with the database entries. - Batch ID tag : a STRING value that specifies the optional batch ID that is recorded with the database entries. - The Setpoints section: - When calculating the OEE you can define the Target value , the Low alarm and/or Low-low alarm values for the three separate calculated production factor percentages for the current shift, namely Quality% , Performance% and Availability% and/or the overall OEE% calculation. - When calculating a KPI you can define the Target value , the Low alarm and/or Low-low alarm values for this KPI . Note: These alarms are calculated in real time. - If necessary, specify an OLE DB connection to a SQL database, using the SQL connection string field to save the OEE or KPI data for later analysis, as follows: Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . - Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut.

- Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item.

Title: Configuration
- Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. - Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. - At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. If the connection string is specified then this agent logs shift data, manually triggered snapshots and 1 minute sample data to a table called ADR_OEE. IMPORTANT: The current version of the OEE agent does NOT support housekeeping operations on this table. It is up to the user to ensure that “obsolete” records are deleted as required. For instance by running SQL queries in SQL Server Management Studio. Housekeeping SQL query example: DELETE FROM ADR_OEE WHERE [dt]<’2010/01/01’ The Disable SQL on standby checkbox (the BOOLEAN disableStandby slot), prevents this agent from logging to the database, when its Agent Server is part of a cluster and is in standby node - to prevent the logging of DUPLICATE information. Alternatively, the OEE agent can support database transactions to a table for the purposes of data warehousing. This requires specifying the required Data warehouse sample rate from 1-60 minutes. By default this is 0 = DISABLED. Each datawarehouse record contains the following data: Note: This data is measured over the period determined by the specified . These attributes are solely intended to assist the support and troubleshooting of protocol driver problems: - size: The size of the file, designated by Filename , in bytes. - Adroit Version: The version of Adroit that the driver was created for. - Note: This must NEVER be less than the current Adroit version. - Creation: The date at which the file, designated by Filename , was created. - Status: This information is intended for future use only, typical values are Simulation and Real, if this field is blank then the driver may come from a 3rd party. - Features: A list of features specific to the operation of this driver i.e. whether it only supports polling or is telemetry or supports tag browsing etc. Note: If this list of reported features ends with a …, it is necessary to expand the width of the Value column. -->

Advanced Scanning Settings Top Advanced Scanning Settings Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings
Advanced Scanning Settings Top Advanced Scanning Settings Launch the Adroit Config Editor . - Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click Driver Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click the Advanced Driver Options button in the bottom right of this page. This replaces the Installed Drivers and Devices list with the Advanced driver options list, which allows the following commonly used global settings that affect scanning, to be added or modified: - Demand scanning enabled: checkbox, which is enabled by default, to allow any NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. protocol driver to provide demand scanning. For more details, see Demand Scanning . - Halt agent server on startup if device/s fail to load: By default this is disabled. - Mark tags bad if device agent stopped: If this checkbox is cleared then Adroit will NOT grey scanned tags once their device has stopped. This is enabled by default. - Allow changes in scan-inhibit and output-enable to affect tags immediately: If this checkbox is ticked, then the scanning sub-system will create an extra subscription to each tag that is being scanned to detect changes made to their output-enable and scan-inhibit statuses, so that they take affect immediately. Note: For details concerning the scanning strategy in which this setting can be used, see Read Only Scanning Strategy . By default, when this checkbox is cleared, the scan-point must be re-added or the device re-started for the scanning sub system to detect a status (output-enable or scan-inhibit) bit change. This setting will also allow "read only" scanned tags to display the correct values if the values are manipulated from within the Agent Server or from a mimic. However, this is not generally a problem because "read only" scanned tags should not normally be configured with operator actions that allow their values to be changed unless they are configured to be output enabled i.e. to be read/write scanned tags. PLEASE NOTE: Turning on this setting will increase the number of subscriptions (1 for each scanned tag) within the server, this will have a small effect on device stopping and starting times because each subscription, for tags scanned by a device, is destroyed when stopping the device and recreated when starting the device. - Text agents convert bit strings into status bits: If this checkbox is ticked, then a Text agent will convert a string of up to 16 1's and 0's into the corresponding status bits (16 thru 32). By default this is cleared. Note: This setting will affect all the Text agents in the system. PLEASE NOTE: The following marshalling functionality of the Multistate agent has been superceded by the Marshal agent , which is specifically designed to do this task and is more powerful and easier to use. - Multistate agent status bits 16-31 are equal to the rawValue slot: Tick this checkbox, if you intend using some of your Multistate agents as marshalling agents. Then any Multistate agent that does not have states defined, will result in its value slot and status bits reflecting the rawValue slot directly and its states will NOT be processed. By default this is cleared. - Multistate bits are reversed: Tick this checkbox, if you are using your Multistate agents as marshalling agents and are using large endian ordering when scanning its I/O to the PLC.

This reverses the rawValue slot and places this value into the value slot of the agent.

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings
Steps:
This reverses the rawValue slot and places this value into the value slot of the agent. By default this is cleared. Note: This setting will affect all the Multistate agents in the system. - Outputs are sent before values are read on device start: Tick this checkbox, to enable the resending of the Adroit value to the front-end device when a tag that is output enabled receives a value from the front-end device that is different from the value currently in Adroit . By default this is cleared. Note1: This setting ONLY has effect if the tag’s scan inhibit bit is on. Note2: For details of the scanning strategy, in which this setting should be used, see Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy or for further details on combining the various scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . - Check for Comm port availability: Tick this checkbox to allow the device configuration dialog to check the availability of each COM port. Each ports’ availability is represented in the port selection box, by a green icon if available and a red icon if unavailable. But when you are connecting to virtual ports, such as MOXA, you should DISABLE this setting, because if these virtual ports are unavailable it takes a LONG time to determine this, which delays the loading of the device configuration dialog. - Interval (ms) between starting any 2 devices during Agent Server startup: When the Agent Server starts up, all the devices are started one at a time with a 2 second delay between each device. If a huge amount of traffic is generated during this time, secondary failures can be caused in the scanning subsystem. If so, change this delay, it is recommended to set this value to 5000 ms instead of its default setting of 2000 ms. Note: This value can also be set to 1000 ms to speed up the starting of devices if you are happy that the system can handle it. -->

Advanced Scanning Settings Top Advanced Scanning Settings Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list.

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings
Advanced Scanning Settings Top Advanced Scanning Settings Using the Adroit Configuration Setup : Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. - Click on the Drivers tab and right click in the Installed Drivers and Devices list. Note: Ensure that Advanced View option is enabled, so that a tick ( ) appears next to it. - Select the Registry settings option. This displays this Advanced scanning settings dialog, which allows the following commonly used parameters that affect scanning, to be added or modified: Note: Previously, these settings could only be modified directly in the registry. - Halt agent server on startup if device/s fail to load properly. (HaltOnStartupFailure): Tick this checkbox… By default this is cleared. - Mark tags bad if device agent stopped. (MarkBadIfDeviceStopped): If this checkbox is cleared then Adroit will NOT grey scanned tags once their device has stopped. This is enabled by default. - Allow changes in scan-inhibit and output-enable to affect the tag immediately. (monitorStatus): If this checkbox is ticked, then the scanning sub-system will create an extra subscription to each tag that is being scanned to detect changes made to their output-enable and scan-inhibit statuses, so that they take affect immediately. Note: For details concerning the scanning strategy in which this setting can be used, see Read Only Scanning Strategy . By default, when this checkbox is cleared, the scan-point must be re-added or the device re-started for the scanning sub system to detect a status (output-enable or scan-inhibit) bit change. This setting will also allow "read only" scanned tags to display the correct values if the values are manipulated from within the Agent Server or from a mimic. However, this is not generally a problem because "read only" scanned tags should not normally be configured with operator actions that allow their values to be changed unless they are configured to be output enabled i.e. to be read/write scanned tags. PLEASE NOTE: Turning on this setting will increase the number of subscriptions (1 for each scanned tag) within the server, this will have a small effect on device stopping and starting times because each subscription, for tags scanned by a device, is destroyed when stopping the device and recreated when starting the device. - Text agents convert bit strings into status bits. (EnableTextBitStreams): If this checkbox is ticked, then a Text agent will convert a string of up to 16 1's and 0's into the corresponding status bits (16 thru 32). By default this is cleared. Note: This setting will affect all the Text agents in the system. PLEASE NOTE: The following marshalling functionality of the Multistate agent has been superceded by the Marshal agent , which is specifically designed to do this task and is more powerful and easier to use. - Multistate agent status bits 16-31 are equal to the rawvalue slot. (InputsToStatus): Tick this checkbox, if you intend using some of your Multistate agents as marshalling agents. Then any Multistate agent that does not have states defined, will result in its value slot and status bits reflecting the rawValue slot directly and its states will NOT be processed. By default this is cleared. - Multistate bits are reversed. (ReverseMultiStateBits): Tick this checkbox, if you are using your Multistate agents as marshalling agents and are using large endian ordering when scanning its I/O to the PLC. This reverses the rawValue slot and places this value into the value slot of the agent. By default this is cleared. Note: This setting will affect all the Multistate agents in the system.

- Outputs are sent before values are read in when devices starts (ForceOutputs): Tick this checkbox, to enable the resending of the Adroit value to the front-end device when a tag that is output enabled receives a value from the front-end device that is different from the value currently in Adroit .

Title: Advanced Scanning Settings

By default this is cleared. Note1: This setting ONLY has effect if the tag’s scan inhibit bit is on. Note2: For details of the scanning strategy, in which this setting should be used, see Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy or for further details on combining the various scanning settings, see The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings . - Check for Comm Port Availability (CheckPortInUse): This setting is enabled by default because it allows the device configuration dialog to check the availability of each COM port. Each ports’ availability is represented in the port selection box, by a green icon if available and a red icon if unavailable. But when you are connecting to virtual ports, such as MOXA, you should DISABLE this setting, because if these virtual ports are unavailable it takes a LONG time to determine this, which delays the loading of the device configuration dialog. - Interval in millseconds between starting any 2 devices during load-up of the Agent Server. (DeviceStartDelay): When the Agent Server starts up, all the devices are started one at a time with a 2 second delay between each device. Advanced Script Agent Properties Top Advanced Script Agent Properties This dialog allows an initialization and a clean-up subroutine to be specified, which are separate from the main subroutine and can be executed when needed.

Title: Advanced Script Agent Properties
Advanced Script Agent Properties Top Advanced Script Agent Properties This dialog allows an initialization and a clean-up subroutine to be specified, which are separate from the main subroutine and can be executed when needed. This dialog box is divided into the following sections: - Initialization subroutine: This subroutine can be used to initialise global variables, establish database connections, or to open file handles. Its called directly after a script has been compiled i.e. after the Agent Server has started up or whenever the agent is modified from within the Agent Configurator. This subroutine can be used to perform the initialization normally performed on Agent Server startup; this is particularly useful for triggered scripts that are only executed when a trigger tag changes after the Agent Server starts up. The browse … button next to the edit box, allows the selection of the initialization subroutine from the list of available subroutines in the added modules. The run button, will execute the initialization subroutine. - Cleanup subroutine: This subroutine can be used to close all open database connections, or to close all open file handles, etc. The cleanup subroutine gets called directly as soon as a script is completed. The browse … button next to the edit box, allows the selection of the clean-up subroutine from the list of available subroutines in the added modules. The run button, will execute the cleanup subroutine. -->

Agent Functionality Top Agent Functionality The "functionality" of an agent can be defined as the sum total of all the inherent knowledge built into an agent type or the operation or method of the agent.

Title: Agent Functionality
Agent Functionality Top Agent Functionality The "functionality" of an agent can be defined as the sum total of all the inherent knowledge built into an agent type or the operation or method of the agent. For details, see About Agents . The functionality of an agent is structured, much like the data or slots of an agent as having both generic and type-specific functionality. For details, see Data Structure of an Agent . Generic functionality is something that all types of agents possess, whereas type-specific functionality is confined only to agents of the specific type. Some of the generic functionality possessed by all agent types are, for example, the ability to add, remove, copy, save, and load instances. Agent List CSV File Format Top Agent List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store the agents which are alarmed by this agent.

Title: Agent List CSV File Format
Agent List CSV File Format Top Agent List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store the agents which are alarmed by this agent. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx- AGNTLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: - Tagname: the name of the agent that is being alarmed. Note: This does not specify which slot (value) of this agent is being alarmed. - Typeindex: this specifies the zero-based index number of the required alarm type. This can be calculated when the required TYPLST.CSV file is opened in MS Excel, by subtracting two from the specified row number of the required alarm type. For example if the required alarm type is in row 51, then its index value will be 49. For details of the format of this CSV file, see Type List CSV File Format . - Route number: A valid route number from the route list file. - Acknowledge: 1 is a normal acknowledgeable alarm, while 0 is an alarm that cannot be acknowledged. - Reserved: 1 - Reserved: 0 - Reserved: 0 - Inhibit time: The future date/time when this incident (alarmed tag) will be re-enabled, as specified using the Inhibited until checkbox of the Alarming dialog. It is saved to the CSV as the two parts of a FILETIME variable e.g. if this is not set then the following value is saved: ",0 0" Note: Inhibit times are DISCARDED when IMPORTING alarm configurations. - Delay time: The number of seconds that the alarm system should wait, once this incident (alarmed tag)becomes active, before this incident is recognised as being ‘officially’ active. - Conditional expression: An expression that must be true before this incident becomes active. -->

Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) Top Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) The first bit in the status word, statusBad or statusBit00 , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot.

Title: Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling)
Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) Top Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) The first bit in the status word, statusBad or statusBit00 , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For further details of this status word, see Agent status words or Slot status words . This bit itself is a combination of statusConnectionBad (a.k.a. statusRemoved), statusScanBad and statusAgentBad . For details, see Connection Bad , Scan Bad or Agent Bad . Note: This statusBad bit CANNOT be set directly but will only be set depending upon the values of the other three bits for the specified agent (agent status word) or slot (slot status word). If the statusScanned bit of an slot is set, on start up the Agent Server switches also turns on the statusScanBad bit of this slot as well, until the first successful scan transaction for the slot, at which time the Scan Agent will reset the statusScanBad bit of this slot. -->

Agent Persistence Files Top Agent Persistence Files Agent persistence files are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent.

Title: Agent Persistence Files
Agent Persistence Files Top Agent Persistence Files Agent persistence files are files that store the data calculated by a Counter or Statistical agent. Their purpose is to ensure that none of this data is lost. Previously this data could only be saved by frequently saving the entire Agent database via a Script or Expression agent. However, this practice is dangerous as .WGP files can corrupt if a power failure occurs during the save. Note: This is a GLOBAL setting for each agent type, which is set in the respective agent configuration dialog. Once enabled, a persistence or (.WORK) file is created for each agent, which is saved when the data of this agent is updated. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Statistical and/or Counter agents, saving their persistence files can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. These persistence files are stored in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. These agent persistence settings are currently saved to the following location in the registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Persistence See Also: Project folder . Statistical agent configuration . Counter agent configuration . Agent database (.WGP) file . -->

Agent Referencing Convention Top Agent Referencing Convention The following convention can be used when referring to agents: [\\AgentServerName\]AgentName This allows agents to be specified or referred to, as follows: - Explicitly , by including the Agent Server name.

Title: Agent Referencing Convention
Agent Referencing Convention Top Agent Referencing Convention The following convention can be used when referring to agents: [\\AgentServerName\]AgentName This allows agents to be specified or referred to, as follows: - Explicitly , by including the Agent Server name. For instance \\AS1\ANA001 This ensures that there is no ambiguity in specifying the required agent. In general, this format may be used in any Classic UI dialog except when adding or copying agents. - Implicitly agent names, by omitting the Agent Server name. For instance ANA001 In this case Adroit will first search the Agent Server it is currently connected to for that agent, implicitly assuming it is on that server. If it does not find the agent, it will look in all the other Agent Servers in the same project for agents of the same name. If only one agent is found on a remote Agent Server, it will use that one. If more than one agent of that name is found on the remote Agent Servers, then the action taken depends on the mode of the local Agent Server (as specified in the Adroit Setup utility), as follows: - If this is a Stand-alone / Distributed server then any duplicate agent names found on two or more remote Agent Servers will be ignored by the user interface. - If this is a Cluster aware server or Cluster server then the duplicate tag name found on the first (alphabetically) remote Agent Server will be used. When that becomes unavailable, the tags on the next Agent Server will be used by the user interface, and so on. Note: If a duplicate agent name is found on the local Agent Server (if running) and any remote Agent Servers, the local agent will always be used. -->

Agent Server Communication within Networks Top Agent Server Communication within Networks Agent Servers with the same project name are typically connected by means of Agent Server broadcasts, so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Servers in the project.

Title: Agent Server Communication within Networks
Agent Server Communication within Networks Top Agent Server Communication within Networks Agent Servers with the same project name are typically connected by means of Agent Server broadcasts, so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Servers in the project. For further details on projects, see About Adroit Projects . Note: Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds, to indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. Agent Server broadcasts are highly effective for relatively small Agent Server networks, which are connected on the same domain. However, this approach is inflexible and explicit Agent Server connections are required instead for the following two networking configurations: - Inter-domain Agent Server networks, since the Agent Server broadcasts do not operate across domains or over a WAN - Large scalable Agent Server networks , since it may be undesirable to maintain a large, potentially resource intensive, grid of fully connected Agent Servers. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. For further details of mechanisms provided by Adroit to connect Agent Servers together and their limitations and how to configure each of these mechanisms, see Agent Server Connection Methods . -->

Agent Server Connection Methods Top Agent Server Connection Methods Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain.

Title: Agent Server Connection Methods
Agent Server Connection Methods Top Agent Server Connection Methods Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. In other words, the ability to refer to agents within another Agent Server. Note: Proxy agents are automatically created when an Agent Server accesses an agent that exists in a remote Agent Server. Using the Project Name: This is the default method for connecting distributed Agent Servers, in which case you specify the SAME project name for ALL the Agent Servers that need to connect to each other, which adds them to this project. Network broadcasts are then made between ALL these Agent Servers to provide each other with two-way access to their agents. Click here for the limitations of this method and/or how to configure this method: Disadvantages: - In practice each Agent Server within a project typically only connects to agents in SOME of the other specified Agent Servers, which results in unnecessary network traffic between the Agent Servers that are not actually communicating with one another. - This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across domains or routers/switches (a WAN). You need to use the explicit connection mechanism to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. Configuration: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. - Specify the SAME Project Name . Note1: Project names must not contain any embedded spaces. Note2: When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters of each Project Name are UNIQUE. Note3: When more than one Agent Server is being used within a project, ensure that the first 7 characters of each Agent Server Name are UNIQUE. - If necessary, ensure that the remote Agent Server broadcasts are enabled, by clicking the Options… button to the right of the Project Name field and ensuring that the Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server checkbox is checked in the Project Options dialog (this is the default setting). Creating Explicit Agent Server Connections: This is the ONLY way to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. In this case you specify exactly which Agent Servers you want your Agent Server to connect, however, these connections are not two-way. Click here for further details of this method, its limitations and/or how to configure this method: In other words if Agent Server 1 has an explicit connection to Agent Server 2 then Agent Server 1 will be able to see data on Agent Server 2. If Agent Server 2 needs to see data on Agent Server 1 then an explicit connection to Agent Server 1 must be configured on Agent Server 2. Disadvantages: - This method requires more administration overhead, in that you need to manually configure ALL the connections you require and if two-way connections are required, then you need to configure these explicit connections on BOTH computers. - The explicit connection mechanism can create unnecessary network traffic as it requires each Agent Server to continuously poll its explicit partners even if they are not up and running. Configuration: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane.

Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane.

Title: Agent Server Connection Methods
Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. - Ensure that an appropriate Project Name and Agent Server Name have been specified for BOTH of the computers that you want to connect. - Click the Options button to the right of the Project Name field to display the project-specific settings. - Check the Explicit connections checkbox. This is unchecked by default. - Click the add button to add an entry to the end of the Agent Servers list, for which you need to provide the following details: - The Machine Name that is used to identify this remote Agent Server computer on the network. Click for more details: this can be found by extracting all the words up to the first ‘.’ from in the Full computer name field of the Computer Name tab of the System applet in the Control Panel . For example if the Full computer name field is ‘bob.domain’, then simply specify ‘bob’. Tip: You can either specify the textual computer name or the IP name of this computer e.g. 10.10.10.96 - The Agent Server Name , which is the name of the remote Agent Server running on this computer, such as AS1. - If necessary, specify the required Servers timeout (seconds) , which specifies how often ALL the explicit connections are tested. If there is no response from the specified Agent Server, then it is assumed to be off-line until the next poll. Note: To remove an Agent Server from the list, select a cell of the required Agent Server and click the delete button. Tip: You should ONLY clear the Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server checkbox if you ONLY use this method of explicit connections to connect this Agent Server to other remote Agent Servers. Note: If your computer network does not have a method of resolving computer names (such as WINS stands for Windows Internet Name Service, which predates DNS as the method used to resolve (translate) computer names and their IP addresses in a network. Unlike DNS which uses a hierarchical namespace, WINS uses a flat namespace. or DNS stands for Domain Name System and is one of the industry-standard suite of protocols that comprise TCP/IP, which is used to translates domain (computer) names to and from their IP addresses. ), then you can use IP addresses in place of the PC name in explicit connections to connect to other Agent Servers. Using the Projects / Servers list: In this case you can specify exactly which Agent Servers and/or projects an Agent Server can connect to. Since this connection mechanism works in tandem with the Using the Project Name method above, these connections are made IN ADDITION TO the Agent Server/s that are in the SAME project as this Agent Server. IMPORTANT: In order for this connection mechanism to work, each Agent Server that is either uniquely specified or within a specified project of the Projects / Servers list of an Agent Server MUST enable this connection mechanism EVEN when their own Projects / Servers list is EMPTY. The safest rule to use is that if this mechanism is enabled on any one Agent Server, enable it on all your Agent Servers . These specific connections also rely on Agent Server broadcasts but are NOT two-way in nature. Click here for further details of this method, its limitations and/or how to configure this method: In other words Agent Server A’s Projects / Servers list allows it to access agents from any Agent Server or project configured in this list.

If you require two-way access to these agents then Agent Server A’s project or server name must to be added to each remote Agent Server’s Projects / Servers list.

Title: Agent Server Connection Methods
If you require two-way access to these agents then Agent Server A’s project or server name must to be added to each remote Agent Server’s Projects / Servers list. Disadvantages: - This connection mechanism requires more administration overhead than when using project names, in that you need to ensure that the Additional connections checkbox is enabled in the Project Options... dialogs of the Adroit Configuration Setup utilities that are associated with all the referenced Agent Servers. - To configure two-way connections, you need to configure this connection mechanism on BOTH Agent Servers. - This connection mechanism uses Agent Server broadcasts, which do not work across domains or routers/switches (a WAN). You need to use the explicit connection mechanism to connect Agent Servers that are in DIFFERENT domains or on OPPOSITE sides of a router or switch or any other network component that blocks network broadcasts. Configuration: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Agent Server Configuration again in the right hand pane. - Ensure that an appropriate Project Name and Agent Server Name have been specified for BOTH of the computers that you want to connect. - Click the Options button to the right of the Project Name field to display to display the project-specific settings. - Check the Additional connections checkbox. This is unchecked by default. - Click the add button to add an entry to the end of the Projects / Servers list, for which you need to provide the following details: Note: You ONLY need to specify those Agent Server/s and/or projects that this Agent Server needs access to IN ADDITION TO the Agent Server/s that are within its project. - The required project name, as specified by the Project Name field of the Adroit Configuration Setup utility for the associated Agent Server/s. Tip: The advantage of specifying a project name is that in ONE entry you immediately allow this Agent Server to access agents on all the Agent Servers within this project; otherwise you need to add individual entries for each of the Agent Servers within this project. - The required Agent Server name, as specified by the Agent Server Name field of the Adroit Configuration Setup utility for the associated Agent Server. In other words, do NOT also provide the computer name. For instance, specify AS1 and not BATCHPC.AS1. Note: Any entries that contain invalid characters (\ / . or space characters) will simply be ignored. IMPORTANT: Please ensure that ALL the remote Agent Servers specified by this Projects / Servers list ALSO has their Additional connections checkbox checked in the Project Options dialog of their Adroit Configuration Setup utility – EVEN WHEN their own Projects / Servers list is EMPTY. Note: To remove an entry from the list, select a cell of the required entry and click the delete button. - Ensure that the Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server checkbox is checked. -->

Title: Agent Server Grid
Agent Server Grid Top Agent Server Grid The Agent Server grid, consists of the following fields, each of which displays relevant runtime information about the current Agent Server session, as follows: Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options . - The first untitled field numbers the information items in the grid. - Item: This field specifies the configuration item, which is being displayed. - Value: This field specifies the current configuration of the specified item, which cannot be edited. The following list describes what the listed Items of the selected Agent Server object refer to: - Server mode: This indicates the current mode of this Agent Server i.e. Master or Standby , if it is part of a cluster or Normal if it is a standalone Agent Server. - Previously stopped at: This indicates the time at which the previous Agent Server session was stopped. - Started at: This indicates the time at which the current Agent Server session was started. - Running time (hours): This indicates the current duration of the current Agent Server session in hours. - Licenced scanpoints: This indicates the number of points that are currently scanned out of the total licensed number of scanned points that are allowed by current Agent Server session. - Licenced Clients: This indicates the number of Client licenses that are currently being made to this Agent Server out of the total licensed number of Client licenses that are allowed to the current Agent Server session. - Licenced Web Clients: This indicates the number of Web Client licenses that are currently being made to this Agent Server out of the total licensed number of Web Client licenses that are allowed to the current Agent Server session. - Licenced for Adroit drivers: This indicates whether the current Agent Server session is licensed to use Adroit drivers, a 1 indicates that this license is in effect. - Licenced for HMI mode only: This indicates whether the current Agent Server session is licensed to only operate in HMI mode , a 1 indicates that this license is in effect. - Licence expiry: This indicates the expiry date of the HASP being used by the current Agent Server session - Total putslots: This indicates the total number of putslots made within the current Agent Server session. - Total subscriptions: This indicates the total number of subscriptions made within the current Agent Server session.

Agent Server clients can subscribe to particular values within the agents, and they are only notified when these values change.

Agent Server Parameters Top Agent Server Parameters Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Agent Server Parameters
Steps:
Agent Server Parameters Top Agent Server Parameters Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. The Agent Server Parameters group contains the following settings: Note: By default the Agent Server reserves storage space for up to 199000 agents on all the connected Agent Servers and ONLY when memory is a serious constraint, should you alter this new default setting by adding and configuring the MaxAgents setting. - Channels: this is the maximum number of possible Client-Server connections from the Agent Server to the outside world, such as to the User Interface, other Agent Servers, DDE links. The default setting is 20. - Remote Timeout: this is the time the system waits before reporting a lost connection between any two Agent Servers, or an Agent Server and the user interface. - Agent Path: this is typically the installation folder in which the Adroit executables and dynamic link libraries are stored. - Save WGP file on exit: check to ensure changes are saved at Agent Server shutdown. Tip: The Agent Server can also be saved using the saveNow and saveAsName slots of the SystemInformation agent . Note1: Saving can take a long time for large installations. For quick shutdowns, leave unchecked and manually save at planned intervals. Note2: This setting does not work if the Agent Server is installed as a service. -->

Agent Server Window Top Agent Server Window This window contains a list of events, along with the date and time at which they were logged to this window, detailing the loading of the Agent Server e.g.

Title: Agent Server Window
Agent Server Window Top Agent Server Window This window contains a list of events, along with the date and time at which they were logged to this window, detailing the loading of the Agent Server e.g. the component Adroit agents, it also contains the following troubleshooting tools and aids. - The Agent Server window title bar , displays both the current status of the Agent Server and the current Adroit configuration. - The status bar displays the percentage of physical memory being used by the system. When this is greater than 100 % then all physical memory is occupied, requiring the use of the virtual memory (the paging file), which will slow down the performance of the system and of the Agent Server. Ideally, this figure should not exceed 75%. - The File menu, contains the following commands: - The Save Messages command, allows a text file and path to be selected, into which the current logged events in this Agent Server window can be saved, by default, a "message.txt" file will be saved to the "My Documents" folder. - The Exit command closes the Agent Server window. - The View menu, contains the following commands: - The Explorer command, which launches the Adroit Project Explorer once the Agent Server has loaded. For details, see The Project Explorer . - The Status Bar command, displays or hides the status bar at the bottom of this window. A tick symbol indicates the status bar is visible. - The Options menu, contains the following commands: - The Spacer command inserts a line into the Agent Server window with the current date and time, containing the following text "====SPACER====" - The Jotting command provides you with a dialog box, so that related details or comments can be entered into this Agent Server window, along with the date and time at which the entry is made. - The Pause command suspends the loading process, a tick symbol alongside this command, indicates that the loading process is currently being suspended. To resume loading click this command again, removing this tick. - The Debug sub-menu which contains the following commands: - Debug Flags… containing all the debug flags that were originally located in the Adroit setup program. These are off by default and are only intended to be used by the Adroit support engineers, for diagnosing system problems. (see Adroit Support Debug Flags for a description of these flags) - Note: When these debug flags are enabled, the performance of the Agent Server will decrease. - Log thread creation events , this logs an event to the Agent Server window, whenever a thread is created. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. - Log thread destruction events , this logs an event to the Agent Server window, whenever a thread is destroyed. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. - Log system events , this enables all internal events in the Agent Server to be logged to the event log. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. Note: the Debug Flags… and Log system events items are not saved when they are set from the Agent Server window. To save these items, they must be configured from the Adroit Setup program . - The Minimise to tray command, affects where and how the Agent Server window appears when it is minimised. Normally, when minimised this window appears in the task bar along with any other currently open program. When this command is selected, however, the Agent Server window appears as the following icon , which is placed into the tray in the bottom right of the screen.

A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that the Agent Server window will become a tray icon when it is minimised.

Title: Agent Server Window
A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that the Agent Server window will become a tray icon when it is minimised. The Agent Server window Tray Icon . Note: If this Minimise to tray command is selected, then on the next startup the Agent Server window will immediately startup as a tray icon; similarly if this is disabled then on the next startup the Agent Server will startup as an Agent Server window. - The Help menu, contains the About… command, which displays the Adroit version information dialog. -->

Agent Status Top Agent Status The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a header or generic slot and so is common to all agent types, and shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad.

Title: Agent Status
Agent Status Top Agent Status The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a header or generic slot and so is common to all agent types, and shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad. In contrast, the statusRaw header slot the agent shows the status of the agent, without any regard for the status of the individual slots. For instance, if one of the agent slots is scan bad, the agent status slot will not necessarily show scan bad unless the agent itself has been marked as scan bad. For details on the structure of data in an agent, see Data Structure of an Agent . This status slot is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent. Each bit of this 32 bit word is also exposed as a slot, allowing up to 32 status flags to be accessed at any time. Note1 : In addition to this overall agent status word, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent, which can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. For details, see Slot Status Words . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note3: These bits can be viewed and/or set via the Agent Header configuration dialog. For details, see Editing the Header of an Agent . This status slot is divided into two portions: - The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each having a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration bits. For details, see Common Status bits . - The second 16 bits (16 to 31) are known as the Specific Status bits and they are agent type-specific. Their equivalent slots are called statusBit16 up to statusBit31. For details of these slots, see the Agent Types and their Slots Reference . For instance an Analog agent uses the first type-specific bit to indicate a Low Alarm condition, whereas an Expression agent uses this bit to indicate a result value Equal to Zero. Write access is restricted to the control bits (agentStatusBit xx ), where xx is: 01,02,03,05,08,09, or 11. -->

Agent Subscriptions Top Agent Subscriptions The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of “listening” for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot).

Title: Agent Subscriptions
Agent Subscriptions Top Agent Subscriptions The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of “listening” for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). - The process of subscribing is setting up the “listener”, by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. - Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any “listeners”. - The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs. - Subscriptions are the basis of most communication within the Agent Server, and between the Server and the connected clients, (Operators for example) . -->

Agent Templates Top Agent Templates You can create one or more Agent template per agent type to specify (customise) your own default slot values, when this template is used to create an agent of this type.

Title: Agent Templates
Agent Templates Top Agent Templates You can create one or more Agent template per agent type to specify (customise) your own default slot values, when this template is used to create an agent of this type. Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage example: For instance, you can create a template for Analog agents that represent 12 bit A to D water temperature signals from a PLC. In this case, you will create an Analog agent template, possibly called 12BWATERTEMP. Then you would set the default values for its rawMax and engMax slots of 4095 and 100 respectively. Each time an Analog agent is created using the 12BWATERTEMP template; these default slot values are used. Default templates: Agent templates are added for the Analog and Digital agent types called _AnalogDefault and _DigitalDefault respectively, providing the Adroit default settings, which you can customise accordingly. To create an agent template for a new agent type: this creates an agent template for an agent type that is not yet listed beneath the Templates folder, this also adds the selected agent type as its own category to the Templates folder. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Templates folder. - Select the Create template… menu item. - Click the to the right of the Agent Type list box. - Select the required agent type. - Type in the Template name that you want to create for the selected agent type. Tip: Provide a brief name that makes it easy to identify the purpose of this template. - Click the OK button. The specified agent type is added as a separate agent template category beneath the Templates folder, containing the name of the added template. The configuration dialog for this agent type is launched so that you can specify the default values of the displayed slots for the specified template. - Click OK once you have finished configuring the new default configuration of this dialog. - Click Yes to Retrieve All Changes , which retrieves ALL the changes you have made to this dialog. Agent Type Slot Reference Top Agent Type Slot Reference Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, most of which are accessible to clients of the Agent Server, each of which is known as a slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set.

Title: Agent Type Slot Reference
Agent Type Slot Reference Top Agent Type Slot Reference Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, most of which are accessible to clients of the Agent Server, each of which is known as a slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of the agent. A tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is simply a de-referenced slot. For further details, see About Agents or About Agent Data (Slots) . This describes the slots that are available for each agent type, as follows: - Slots that are COMMON to all agent types: Header Slots . - Slots that are SPECIFIC to each defined agent type: Accumulator Agent Slots : this agent requires an input a value that accumulates over time to calculate the difference in value between successive events or periods. AgentGroup Agent Slots : this agent combines agents that have something in common into groups. Alarm Agent Slots : this agent manages how incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are communicated to the necessary personnel and/or applications. AlarmList Agent Slots : this agent lists current or unacknowledged incidents to display in an Alarm List Viewer window. AlarmManagement Agent Slots : this agent configures and records your active incidents so you can improve your alarming configuration. Alias Agent Slots : this agent creates a reference to an existing agent to adopt its Behaviour and state information. Analog Agent Slots : this agent stores a real (floating point) value and provides engineering functionality such as scaling. ARec Agent Slots : this agent configures up to 256 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. Audit Agent Slots : this agent supplements the auditing of the Agent Server by selecting tags to monitor for any change in value. Beeper Agent Slots : this agent provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker. Boolean Agent Slots : this agent stores a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). value. Command Agent Slots : this agent sends and receives SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. messages to remotely configure or report on your process. Coordinate Agent Slots : this agent stores the GPS coordinates of assets on the GIS platform. Counter Agent Slots : this agent is a simple counter and averager. DataLog Agent Slots : this agent manages the historical logging of a process value ( tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). ). Date Agent Slots : this agent holds time and date information broken down into the date and time constituents. DBAccess Agent Slots : this agent performs a transaction on a row in an OLE DB compatible database. DBLog Agent Slots : this agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent. DBQuery Agent Slots : this agent provides a methodology for asynchronously executing OLE DB transactions. Device Agent Slots : this agent transfers process values between Adroit and FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . Digital Agent Slots : this agent stores a Boolean value and provides engineering functionality such as value inversion. DumpConfig Agent Slots : this agent simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. EventLogging Agent Slots : this agent manages the logging of events by Adroit to Windows event logs and to a database.

EventOutput Agent Slots : this agent directs event log messages to output devices (printers, files, databases).

Title: Agent Type Slot Reference
EventOutput Agent Slots : this agent directs event log messages to output devices (printers, files, databases). Expression Agent Slots : this agent performs user-defined calculations to calculate an output value. Frame Agent Slots : this agent stores up to 32 indexed strings. ICMP Agent Slots : this agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Integer Agent Slots : this agent stores an integer number +/– 2147483647 (32 bits). IOT Agent Slots : this agent can represent any object containing multiple properties (or slots), which are defined AFTER adding the IOT agent. Marshal Agent Slots : this agent provides the functionality of 16 digital agents in a single agent. MaxDemand Agent Slots : this agent monitors your electricity usage so that you remain within your agreed usage limits. MultiMedia Agent Slots : this agent runs a variety of Windows compatible multi-media files such as .WAV, .AVI and .MID. MultiState Agent Slots : this agent defines up to 16 discrete states to create operating and/or control sequences. Notify Agent Slots : this agent directs alarms to pagers and also to cellular phones via SMS. OEE Agent Slots : this agent either calculates the OEE stands for Overall Equipment Effectiveness, which typically identifies the productivity or utiltization of a machine or an entire plant, as a percentage. for the monitored equipment and/or plant or measures a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . PerfMon Agent Slots : this agent monitors up to 16 Windows Performance counters to detect performance bottlenecks. PID Agent Slots : this agent provides the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with an external PID controller. Proxy Agent Slots : this agent provides continuous updates of the value of an agent referenced from a remote Agent Server. Real Agent Slots : this agent stores a real (floating point) value. Recipe Agent Slots : this agent provides basic sequencing and batching and reporting capabilities. Scan Agent Slots : this agent communicates one or more tags to an FED, these agents are managed by Device agents. Scheduler Agent Slots : this agent defines one or more time periods of time to enable or disable other agents. Script Agent Slots : this agent performs one or more Visual basic or Java scripts to do complicated tasks. Shift Agent Slots : this agent determines the current shift number as defined by a configurable shift pattern. SNMPMgr Agent Slots : this agent monitors and/or manages network devices using SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. . Statistical Agent Slots : this agent provides the basic functionality to create a statistical process control strategy. String Agent Slots : this agent stores a "string" of text characters, only the first 79 of which can be used for scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). . StringList Agent Slots : this agent stores an unlimited number of indexed ASCII character strings of variable length. SystemDataLog Agent Slots : this agent administers the backing up of datalogs and synchronises datalogs in an Adroit cluster. SystemInformation Agent Slots : this agent acts as an information center containing data that is global to the Agent Server. Text Agent Slots : this agent stores a 79-character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). Timer Agent Slots : this agent performs several commonly used timing operations. For the slots that are saved to the Adroit database (.WGP) file for each agent type and the format of these saved values, see: Agent Type Saved Format Reference . -->
