Title: Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values
Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values Top Agents, Slots, Tags and their relation to Values Agents are the fundamental building blocks of Adroit . They are called agents because, in addition to containing data, like simple database records, they also usually contain the ability to operate or act on their own data. For further details, see About Agents . Note: In Adroit , the data or values contained within agents are called slots. For further details, see About Agent Data . Therefore the following method is used when referring to values within Adroit : agentName.slotName, which specifies both the name of the value and its associated agent. Note: In Adroit , this fully qualified named value (or agentName.slotName reference) is known as a tag. For example, a tag containing the value of the rawValue slot of an Analog agent called ANA1, would be written as: ANA1.rawValue -->

Title: Alarm Route Destination agents
Alarm Route Destination agents Top Alarm Route Destination agents All alarms are routed to the following destination agents that are designed to announce, record, organise and display the alarm state of the alarmed agent. For further details of alarm routes, see About Alarm Routes . Alarm route destination agents: - Alarmlist agent , contains a list of current or unacknowledged alarms and events. This list can be viewed by one or more Alarm windows and receives acknowledgment decisions from them. - Beeper agent , provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker. For multimedia capable computers, the MultiMedia agent may be a better option for routing of audible alarm signals. - Notify agent , provides another alarm route destination using a pager service. Alarms can be transmitted via cellular phone Short Message Service (SMS) or paging service direct to a designated person. Eventlog route destination agents: Note: Eventlog Route Destinations are GLOBAL settings that apply to ALL alarm agents. - EventLogging agent , handles all the event logging in Adroit . Events can be directed to computers running Windows anywhere on the network. - EventOutput agent , directs event log messages to output devices (printers, serial ports, and parallel ports) and to SQL compliant databases. -->

Alarm Shelving Top Working with Alarm Shelving (Alarm Inhibiting) This is process of temporarily removing (deactivating) one or more alarms from the entire alarm system (not just the local client), typically for a specific time period.

Title: Working with Alarm Shelving (Alarm Inhibiting)
Alarm Shelving Top Working with Alarm Shelving (Alarm Inhibiting) This is process of temporarily removing (deactivating) one or more alarms from the entire alarm system (not just the local client), typically for a specific time period. Then when the time is up, if the alarm was active at the time that it was shelved, it will again be added to the alarm system. However, in Adroit -speak a shelved alarm is typically referred to as an inhibited alarm. Currently alarm inhibiting (shelving) can be managed via the following routes: - The Manage Configured Alarms graphic form (part of the default System Information project) : this allows you to inhibit (shelve) or uninhibit every configured alarm in an Agent Server, regardless of its alarm list or whether it is active or not. For instance, if you have planned maintenance for a specific plant section, then you can use this graphic form to select all the alarms in this section and inhibit them until the maintenance is over. For details, see Alarm Shelving via the Manage Configured Alarms graphic form . - The AlarmViewer control: this allows you to inhibit (shelve) or uninhibit any active alarm in an alarm list (of a specific Alarm or AlarmList agent). For details, see Alarm Shelving via the AlarmViewer control . You can also manually configure alarm inhibiting (shelving) via the Alarm agent. For details, see Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting) . -->

- Select the alarms that you want to inhibit (shelve) in the list.

Title: To inhibit (shelve) alarms:
- Select the alarms that you want to inhibit (shelve) in the list. - Click the More options link (in the bottom right corner) and its Inhibit selected alarms option. IMPORTANT: This option is only enabled when one or more alarms are selected. In the Inhibit alarms with reason dialog: Tip: The list of the currently selected alarms are provided to check if the required alarms are selected. - Specify the required Inhibit until date and time, as follows: - as a specific Date and time , this is the default option which is set to inhibit the selected alarms until the next day (24 hours from the current time), although you can specify any time period as long as it is not in the past, - otherwise you can inhibit the selected alarms Forever , which effectively deactivates the selected alarms. - Specify the required Reason for shelving (inhibiting) these alarms. The Operator (the currently logged in user) is also automatically added to this alarm inhibiting event. - Click the Inhibit button. Note: Once you inhibit an alarm it is both acknowledged and cleared so it is removed from the alarm list.

Title: To uninhibit alarms:
- Click the More options link (in the bottom right corner) and its View inhibited alarms option. In the View inhibited alarms dialog: - Select which of the alarms that have already been inhibited in this alarm list that you want to uninhibit, either using the Select All button or manually select the required ones. By default this list is sorted by the Inhibit until column in descending order, so that the alarms that are configured to be inhibited for the longest time are displayed at the top of the list. The Operator (the currently logged in user) is also automatically added to this alarm uninhibiting event. - Click the Uninhibit button. Note: After uninhibiting an alarm that was active, it is put back into an active state so that it reappears in the alarm list. In addition to providing the options required to inhibit (shelve) and uninhibit alarms the More options link (in the bottom right corner of the AlarmViewer control) also provides the ability to globally acknowledge ALL the alarms displayed in the alarm list. Typically the AlarmViewer control displays the Global Acknowledge , in which case the Global Acknowledge All option is provided. However, if the Local Acknowledge button is displayed then this option becomes Local Acknowledge All . -->

Title: Alarm Types
Alarm Types Top Alarm Types An alarm is triggered when one or more of the status mask bits in an alarm type of an Alarm agent matches any status bits in the agent being monitored. For an agent to be monitored, you have to apply one or more alarm types to the agent (see Alarming an Agent ). The creation of alarm types is discussed here. Alarm Types are defined on a per Agent Type basis, which are pre-configured in the postload Adroit database file . This means that one set of Alarm types will be created for Analog agents and another set for Digital agents. Agent Types may take the form of a descriptive abbreviation, e.g. "Overheating" for Analog agent types, or "Tripped" for Digital agent types. Each Alarm Type must be edited to define the alarm triggers that take the form of a descriptive abbreviation, e.g. "Overheating" for Analog agent types, or "Tripped" for Digital agent types. Each Alarm type must be edited to define the alarm triggers that take the form of a status word mask wherein specific bits are set. To add or edit an alarm type . -->

Alarming in Adroit Top Alarming in Adroit Alarm agents can monitor other agents for preset conditions or states.

Title: Alarming in Adroit
Steps:
Alarming in Adroit Top Alarming in Adroit Alarm agents can monitor other agents for preset conditions or states. So that when a monitored condition occurs in an agent its Alarm agent uses predefined reporting methods to alert the necessary people and/or applications. That is why alarming primarily involves the configuration of the following two things: - The preset conditions or states of each agent that you need to alarm, known as alarm types, which each constitute a separate alarm or event. - The alarm routes that specify which alarm destinations (reporting mechanisms) you need to use to communicate the generated alarms and events to the necessary personnel and/or applications. Therefore, you need to select the following for each agent that you want to alarm: - Which predefined alarm type/s you want the selected Alarm agent to monitor. - Which alarm route each alarm type should be reported by this Alarm agent. When a monitored agents enter into conditions defined by a specified alarm type, these are known in Adroit as an incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). . However, an incident is ONLY an alarm, if it needs to be responded to ; otherwise it is an event. Is it recommended that you create an alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. BEFORE you start alarming agents to determine how best this can be achieved. For instance, you cannot alarm one agent using two different Alarm agents. For more details about how alarm types are configured and managed, see About Alarm Types . For details about how alarm routes are configured and managed, see About Alarm Routes . For details of the other alarming settings, see Additional Alarming Configuration . For some reasons for and recommendations when creating an alarming strategy, see About Alarming Strategies . For more details about the requirements for an effective alarm, see Effective Alarm Characteristics . Alarms are typically viewed using Alarm List Viewer windows. For more details see Displaying Alarms or About Alarm List Viewer Windows. -->

text:
Alarming Overview Top Alarming Overview The alarm system is a critical component for any process, which alerts your operators when components of the process are operating outside of their normal functioning.

Title: Alarming Overview
Alarming Overview Top Alarming Overview The alarm system is a critical component for any process, which alerts your operators when components of the process are operating outside of their normal functioning. Adroit provides a flexible alarming capability in that any slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of any agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. can be alarmed. In this way any situations, ranging from plant upsets or process variable excursions to failures within the Adroit system itself can be monitored. Alarming is managed by an Alarm agent, which communicates the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). when they occur, to the relevant personnel and/or applications. You can announce an alarm by using one or more of the following methods: - by a siren or through the activation of audiovisual multimedia - by a list of unacknowledged and acknowledged alarms - by SMS or mobile pager messages or electronic sign display - by logging the alarm to an OLE DB compliant database - by logging the alarm to the Windows application event log - by printing the alarm to hardcopy - by launching a process-specific page of hypertext help - by graphical display on a mimic - by textual display on a mimic In the past alarms were hardwired into the panels, which limited their number; now alarms are software-driven, which can lead to an unlimited number of alarms. While one’s intention is often to keep the operators better informed by increasing the number of alarms, the result is that operators become overloaded and confused and may even start ignoring alarms! Therefore LESS alarms are MORE effective. Alarm Management is therefore an important aspect of process control as it counteracts inefficient alarming. This allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. For more details about creating alarms in Adroit , see Alarming in Adroit . For more details about displaying alarms in Adroit , see Displaying Alarms in Adroit . For more details about industry guidelines concerning Alarm Management and how this is addressed by Adroit , see About Alarm Management . -->

Alarming strategy Top About Alarming Strategies BEFORE any agent is alarmed it is RECOMMENDED to create and use an Alarming strategy.

Title: About Alarming Strategies
Steps:
Alarming strategy Top About Alarming Strategies BEFORE any agent is alarmed it is RECOMMENDED to create and use an Alarming strategy. An alarming strategy is simply a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Also once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, if required. Although this may seem unnecessary to take the time to create such a strategy, as with all planning a little time spent in the beginning is richly rewarded by the end of a project. An alarming strategy is necessary for the following reasons: - It simplifies the initial engineering of the alarming. - It ensures that the required alarms will be sent to the desired destinations and can be correctly filtered. - It eliminates confusion, with regard to the often complex routing of alarms. - It prevents the re-engineering of the alarming, if a mistake is detected after the initial alarming configuration has been performed. Although this is not a definitive description of creating an alarming strategy, the following issues need to be considered when this is being formulated: - Display of Alarms: Determine which alarm destinations will be used i.e. how the alarms will alert the relevant plant personnel and the standards that are to be used for each destination. For instance: capitalization rules; the number and width of columns to display etc. In this way it is possible to ensure a consistent look and feel for the displayed alarms, which will assist the plant personnel in responding to alarms quickly. - Filtering of Alarms: An alarm priority can be specified for each agent, so that alarm agents can filter out all the alarms generated by low priority agents, if necessary. However, since this alarm priority is tag-specific rather than alarm-specific, it cannot be used as an efficient alarm filtering mechanism, for instance if we only want to display a sub-set of the alarms configured for an agent. The only mechanism in Adroit that can achieve this is to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism. - Routing of Alarms : Construct a routing schematic, which details the alarm destinations that are to be used by each route, in each Alarm agent: Note: By default Operator Action Behaviours are routed along route 1, specify the LMOperatorAction registry value if you need to specify another alarm route. - Decide on the number of agents to alarm per Alarm agent - there is no limitation for this. - Decide on required number of alarm routes to use. Note: Do not use route 0 or 1 as these are predefined Adroit system routes. - Decide which routes need to be logged persistently i.e. to the Eventlog and which should be sent to DbAccess for access from 3rd party MES applications etc. Note: Ensure that the alarms generated from a single agent are routed using the SAME alarm agent. For instance, the Hi and HiHi alarms of an Analog agent must both be routed using the SAME Alarm agent. - Decide which alarms must be sent as SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. , by allocating a route for SMS's. Although you probably will need to have more than one route that uses a Notify agent or Command agent as a destination. - Decide which alarm types will go on which route – IMPORTANT if using more than one Alarm agent in this strategy – you can't alarm a tag on 2 different Alarm agents.

For instance, considering the following two alarms of an Analog agent called Tank_level: - The Hi alarm could be sent along route 2 for an operator to act on (via an alarm window).

Title: About Alarming Strategies
Steps:
For instance, considering the following two alarms of an Analog agent called Tank_level: - The Hi alarm could be sent along route 2 for an operator to act on (via an alarm window). - The HiHi alarm actually sends an SMS to someone. Therefore, if your strategy involves using different Alarm agents to split other various sections of our plant up, these routes will be different but end in the same destinations e.g. same alarm list. For further details about using alarm lists, see Displaying Alarms . -->

Alarming Templates Top Alarming Templates You can add Alarming templates to configure the alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type).

Title: Alarming Templates
Alarming Templates Top Alarming Templates You can add Alarming templates to configure the alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type). settings for one or more alarm types, which are usually manually specified when alarming agents. Alarm types, in Adroit , define the conditions or states of your process values (agents) that are set when they no longer operate within their normal operating range. Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage Example: You can create an alarming template for a particular agent type, like Analog agents and pre-configure the required alarming settings for each of their default and/or custom alarm types, to save your users engineering time. Default templates: Since these templates are alarm type-specific, NO default template can be created. Each alarming template allows you to specify ONE alarm agent that is used to monitor the alarm types that you specify. Then you can specify the following settings for EACH alarm type: - The name of the alarm Type: The string defining the alarm agent, which is MANDATORY as there is NO default value for this, hence the “?” is displayed in the Default value column for this field. Note: This string is CASE SENSITIVE; please provide the EXACT case and combination of letters that specify the required alarm type. - The required Route , which specifies the required mechanisms (agents) used to report this incident to the necessary personnel and/or applications. Click here for more details: - The Adroit default for this is 2, which is the route specified for process alarms, which is any incident that requires remedial action from an operator. - If this alarm type, specifies an event i.e. an incident that is for information only and requires no input from an operator then assign it to route 3 of the defaultAlarmAgent, which is intended for all process events. - The Acknowledge required status: The Adroit default for this is 1. Process alarms should have this set to 1, while process events should have this set to 0. To create an alarming template: this creates an alarming template for the Alarming category that is listed beneath the Templates folder. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list.

In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Alarming category within the Templates folder.

Title: Alarming Templates
In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Alarming category within the Templates folder. - Select the Create template… menu item. - Type in the required Template name . Tip: Provide a brief name that makes it easy to identify the purpose of this template. - Click the OK button. This selects and adds this template to the bottom of the list of templates beneath the Alarming category. The default alarming-specific settings (slots) for the alarm type specified by this template are displayed in the right hand pane. - Provide the required settings (slots) for the alarm type specified by this template, as follows: Note: Ensure that this alarm type exists in the Alarm agent specified by this alarming template. To change the value of a slot in the alarming template: - Double click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Provide the required default value for this slot in the Edit template slot value dialog. - Click the OK button. To delete a slot from the alarming template: - Right click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Select the Delete slot menu item. WARNING! The selected slot is IMMEDIATELY removed. Note: If you delete one of these slots then the Adroit default value will be used. WARNING! You should NOT delete the alarm type, as all the settings relate to this. Note: By default only ONE alarm type is specified. To add another alarm type to an alarming template: by default each alarming template provides a single alarm type for a specific Alarm agent, although you will usually need to add more alarm types. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the required alarming template in the Alarming category in the Templates folder. - Select the Add type... menu item. The default alarming-specific settings (slots) for the new alarm type are displayed in the right hand pane (see above for a detailed description of each one). - Provide the required settings (slots) for this alarm type, as follows: To change the value of a slot in the alarming template: - Double click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Provide the required default value for this slot in the Edit template slot value dialog. - Click the OK button.

To delete a slot from the alarming template: - Right click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane.

Title: Alarming Templates
To delete a slot from the alarming template: - Right click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Select the Delete slot menu item. WARNING! The selected slot is IMMEDIATELY removed. Note: If you delete one of these slots then the Adroit default value will be used. WARNING! You should NOT delete the alarm type, as all the settings relate to this. Note: Ensure that the alarm types that you add, exist in the Alarm agent specified by this alarming template. To sort the list of alarming templates: by default each template is added to the end of the existing list of alarming templates, it is possible to sort this list, alphabetically, in ascending order, to make it easier for users to select the templates. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Alarming category within the Templates folder. - Select the Sort menu item. This rearranges the list of alarming templates alphabetically, in ascending order. To delete an alarming template: to remove an existing alarming template. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the required alarming template in the Alarming category in the Templates folder. - Select the Delete template… menu item. The selected template is removed from the list of templates. For more details about alarm types and their configuration, see About Alarm Types . For more details about the defaultAlarmAgent and its preset route configuration, see About the defaultAlarmAgent . About the Adroit DB Generator : an overview of the Adroit DB Generator utility which creates Adroit agent databases (.WGP files) from information stored in 3 rd party applications, such as front-end devices. -->

Slot Name Type Function alarmListRequest STRING Requests a list of alarms by using one of the following methods of determining which alarms should be retrieved: - all : this displays all the configured alarms in the Alarm Management agent. - alarmagent=defaultalarmagent : in this case all the alarms of the defaultalarmagent Alarm agent will be displayed. - agent=tanklevel : in this case all the alarms for the agent that is called 'tanklevel' will be displayed. - incident = tanklevel.high : in this case all the alarms generated for this specific 'tanklevel.high' incident will be displayed. - context=3 : in this case, you can specify the unique number of the category, whose incidents you want to retrieve - in this case all the incidents added to the category = 3 are retrieved. - inhibitedincidents : this displays all the incidents that are currently inhibited in ALL the Alarm agents. IMPORTANT: After setting this slot, immediately read the AlarmListXml slot to retrieve the list of retrieved alarms in XML format. alarmListXml VARSTRING Contains the XML recordset of the retrieved list of alarms once the alarmListRequest slot is set. catchupData RAWBYTES NOT IMPLEMENTED commitReason VARSTRING For internal use by VIZNET only. connection VARSTRING The connection string to the specified OLE DB database (preferably MS SQL). Note: You CANNOT connect to an MS Access database because of its known performance issues contextXml VARSTRING An XML recordset of the Adr_AM_Categories table to allow the solution to display a unique context so that it can customise the categorization of its incidents. debug BOOLEAN For support use only: if the “Log system events” setting is enabled and this is set to 1, then debugging events for the AlarmManagement agent are logged to the event log. debugStr VARSTRING For support use only: when debug mode is enabled for this agent, this slot displays the last debug message string. disableStandby BOOLEAN When set to TRUE (1) this will disable the logging of incidents to the database on standby cluster nodes. documentName STRING The document name for the incident as specified in the documentRequest slot. This document name may be a UNC name or local name. This should always remain at 0. engineState INTEGER For support use only. housekeepCount INTEGER The number of days to use for housekeeping the removal of unnecessary records from a database , the length of time specified depends on: - the storage capacity you have available for your database and - how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. AlarmManagement Database Tables Top AlarmManagement Database Tables The AlarmManagement agent creates and maintains the following tables in its associated OLE DB database: IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly.

Title: AlarmManagement Database Tables
AlarmManagement Database Tables Top AlarmManagement Database Tables The AlarmManagement agent creates and maintains the following tables in its associated OLE DB database: IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. - Adr_AM_AssociatedValues: This table stores the values of the tags that are associated with each incident. Each tag associated with an incident is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - IncidentIdx: The unique incident index value of the associated incident record, which is an Idx value in either the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents or Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. - Tag: The name of the tag associated with the incident specified by IncidentIdx . - TagValue: The value of the associated Tag . - Adr_AM_Categories: This table defines the hierarchical structure used to categorise the incidents. Each category is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): - CategoryId: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - ParentId: The unique category ID of this category’s immediate parent i.e. the category that is above this category in the hierarchy. - Category: The name of the category specified by CategoryId . - OperatorTag: An optional field for a tag that contains the name of the Operator that will be logged for all the incidents in this category and, if necessary, its sub-categories too. - Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents: This table is the initial destination for every incident generated by the alarm agents and logged by the AlarmManagement agent/s. Incidents are ONLY moved to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table if they are valid and they have been cleared and/or acknowledged and when any mandatory reasons and/or notes have been specified. Note: All entries in this table are DELETED when an Agent Server starts. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number for each incident that is logged to it. - dt: The date and time of the occurrence of this incident. - Process: The name of the AlarmManagement agent that logged this incident. This is required to uniquely identify incidents across the enterprise (if multiple agents log to the SAME database. Note: These names have a maximum of 30 characters. - CategoryId: The unique identification of the category in which this incident is located. - IncidentID: This is an important field as it uniquely identifies each incident in this database. This is simply the index ( Idx field) that is used for an incident the FIRST time that the incident is logged to the database. - Incident: The name of the incident, which is the agent name and alarm type combination e.g. KILNTEMP.HI - Data: The Reported data values for this incident as received from Adroit . - Description: The description of the agent causing the incident. - Filter: The Agent filter group as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. - Priority: The Agent priority as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident.

- Shift: The Shift number in which incident occurred, in other words the dt is greater than the starting time of this shift and less than the starting time of the next shift.

Title: AlarmManagement Database Tables
- Shift: The Shift number in which incident occurred, in other words the dt is greater than the starting time of this shift and less than the starting time of the next shift. - Operator: This is the value of the tag configured for the Operator tag setting of the category in which this incident is located (or of the CLOSEST higher-level categories, if any). - Acknowledged_dt: The date and time that the incident was acknowledged. Note: This time is equal to the dt field, if the incident does not require acknowledgement. - Acknowledged_by: The name of operator who acknowledged the alarm. In other words the name of the currently logged on user of the Adroit client (or Windows). - Cleared_dt: The date and time that this incident was cleared. - Delay: The Delay field from the Incident table. In other words the number of seconds the incident needs to be active ( Cleared_dt field – dt field) in order to be considered valid. If the alarm is cleared before this Delay then the incident is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. - ReasonId: The Idx field from the Reasons table that is associated with the currently specified reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no reason has been specified. - SubReasonId: The Idx field from the SubReasons table that is associated with the currently specified sub-reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no sub-reason has been specified. - Notes: The text specifying any notes that have been specified for this incident. - Record_dt: The date and time that this incident was received by the SQL database, which can be used to improve the quality of the AM reports. - Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents: This table stores every completed incident in other words the incidents from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table that have been cleared and/or acknowledged and whose mandatory reasons and/or notes have been specified. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is the unique Idx field that this incident had in the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table, before it was moved to this table. - dt: The date and time of the occurrence of this incident. - Process: The name of the AlarmManagement agent that logged this incident. - CategoryId: The unique identification of the category in which this incident is located. - IncidentID: This is an important field as it uniquely identifies each incident in this database. Tip: Querying this field will obtain all the information concerning a specific event/alarm in the database. - Incident: The name of the incident, which is the agent name and alarm type combination e.g. KILNTEMP.HI - Data: The Reported data values for this incident as received from Adroit . - Description: The description of the agent causing the incident. - Filter: The Agent filter group as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. - Priority: The Agent priority as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. - Shift: The Shift number in which incident occurred. - Operator: This is the value of the tag configured for the Operator tag setting of the category in which this incident is located (or of the CLOSEST higher-level categories, if any). - Acknowledged_dt: The date and time that the incident was acknowledged. Note: This time is equal to the dt field, if the incident does not require acknowledgement. - Acknowledged_by: The name of operator who acknowledged the alarm. In other words the name of the currently logged on user to Adroit client (or Windows). - Cleared_dt: The date and time that this incident was cleared. - UnacknowledgedTime: The number of seconds ( Acknowledged_dt field – dt field) it took to acknowledge the incident.

- ActiveTime: The number of seconds ( Cleared_dt field – dt field) it took for the alarm to be cleared.

Title: AlarmManagement Database Tables
- ActiveTime: The number of seconds ( Cleared_dt field – dt field) it took for the alarm to be cleared. - ReasonId: The Idx field from the Reasons table that is associated with the currently specified reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no reason has been specified. - SubReasonId: The Idx field from the SubReasons table that is associated with the currently specified sub-reason. If this is 0 then it is assumed that no sub-reason has been specified. - Notes: The text specifying any notes that have been specified for this incident. - Record_dt: The date and time that this incident was received by the SQL database, which can be used to improve the quality of the AM reports. - Adr_AM_Incidents: This table defines the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). and their optional settings. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - CategoryID: The unique identification of the category in which this incident is located. - Name: This ALWAYS displays the actual name of the incident, which is the agent name and its default alarm type combination e.g. TANKLEVEL.High - AliasName: This field returns: the Agent field + '.' + the AgentType field to display customised incidents (i.e. incidents with overridden alarm types). For instance TANKLEVEL.Overflow instead of the actual incident, which is TANKLEVEL.High. - Agent: The name of the agent for the agent causing the incident. - AgentType: The agent type of the agent causing the incident, which can be overridden if necessary e.g. the default alarm type "High" can be changed to "Overflow". - AlarmType: The alarm type specified for the incident. - Document: : An optional UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name path to a HTML document that further clarifies the incident and provides assistance on how to deal with it or react to it. - Delay: An optional delay time, in seconds, that must elapse before the incident is considered to be valid. - Condition: An optional BOOLEAN tag whose value must be TRUE for the incident to be valid. - ReasonRequired: An option to enforce the entry of reasons on each occurrence of the incident – default value FALSE. - NotesRequired: An option to enforce the entry of notes on each occurrence of the incident – default value FALSE. - AssociatedTags: Optional, comma delimited tags whose values must be recorded when the incident occurs. - Adr_AM_Licence: This table is for internal use only and should not be used by customers. - Adr_AM_Operators: This table stores each new operator name and is provided to make it easier to query these operators. This table has the following field (column): - Name: The name of the operator. - Adr_AM_Reasons: This table contains an indexed list of reasons that can are used to determine the cause of incidents. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - Reason: The Reason that is displayed in the reasoning dialog. - Description: An optional description of this reason, this is NOT referenced by Adroit . - Adr_AM_SubReasons: This table contains an indexed list of sub-reasons for the reasons specified in the Reasons table that can are used to determine the cause of incidents.

This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number.

Title: AlarmManagement Database Tables
This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. Ensure that this is the SAME as the Idx field in the Reasons table, in order to specify sub-reasons for a particular reason. - SubReason: The Sub-reason that is displayed in the reasoning dialog. - Description: An optional description of this sub-reason, this is NOT referenced by Adroit . - Adr_AM_UserKPIs: This table allows users to configure the values of the KPI targets used by the queries of the AlarmManagement agent. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number for each KPI added to this table - Id: A unique short name (acronym) identifier for the KPI, which is a maximum of 5 characters. Note: This field can be used with a % prefix to parameterise user queries where it makes sense to do so. - Description: An English description of the KPI target. - Value: The user configurable Integer value for this KPI target. - Adr_AM_UserQueries: This table contains all the queries that made available to the View Data and, if necessary to the View Graph dialogs, so that users can analyse the database from the Classic User Interface. Note1: If necessary, you can create your own queries and add them to this table so that they too will appear in these dialogs. For details, see Adding your own Queries . Note2: It is NOT recommended that you edit the existing queries especially the first 6 queries otherwise the functionality provided by the AlarmManagment agent will be compromised. AlarmManagement Database Tables Top AlarmManagement Database Tables The AlarmManagement agent creates and maintains the following tables in its associated OLE DB database: IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. - Adr_AM_AssociatedValues: This table stores the values of the tags that are associated with each incident. Each tag associated with an incident is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - IncidentIdx: The unique incident index value of the associated incident record, which is an Idx value in either the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents or Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. - Tag: The name of the tag associated with the incident specified by IncidentIdx . - TagValue: The value of the associated Tag . - Adr_AM_Categories: This table defines the hierarchical structure used to categorise the incidents. Each category is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): - CategoryId: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - ParentId: The unique category ID of this category’s immediate parent i.e. the category that is above this category in the hierarchy. - Category: The name of the category specified by CategoryId . - OperatorTag: An optional field for a tag that contains the name of the Operator that will be logged for all the incidents in this category and, if necessary, its sub-categories too. - Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents: This table is the initial destination for every incident generated by the alarm agents and logged by the AlarmManagement agent/s. Incidents are ONLY moved to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table if they are valid and they have been cleared and/or acknowledged and when any mandatory reasons and/or notes have been specified. Note: All entries in this table are DELETED when an Agent Server starts. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number for each incident that is logged to it. - dt: The date and time of the occurrence of this incident. - Process: The name of the AlarmManagement agent that logged this incident. This is required to uniquely identify incidents across the enterprise (if multiple agents log to the SAME database. Note: These names have a maximum of 30 characters. - CategoryId: The unique identification of the category in which this incident is located. - IncidentID: This is an important field as it uniquely identifies each incident in this database. This is simply the index ( Idx field) that is used for an incident the FIRST time that the incident is logged to the database. - Incident: The name of the incident, which is the agent name and alarm type combination e.g. KILNTEMP.HI - Data: The Reported data values for this incident as received from Adroit . - Description: The description of the agent causing the incident. - Filter: The Agent filter group as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident. - Priority: The Agent priority as received from Adroit for the agent referenced by the incident.

- Shift: The Shift number in which incident occurred, in other words the dt is greater than the starting time of this shift and less than the starting time of the next shift.

Note: This time is equal to the dt field, if the incident does not require acknowledgement. - Acknowledged_by: The name of operator who acknowledged the alarm. Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Top Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources.

Title: Alternate Secondary Port Enabled
Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Top Alternate Secondary Port Enabled Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources. Adroit drivers can make use of a different PLC addressing to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the PLCs used need to have separate addresses and both PLCs need to be able to be independently accessed by the Adroit drivers. Note: This only applicable to network-able (RS485, RS232, Ethernet, L2, Allen-Bradley Data Highway, Modbus + etc...) communications. A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: - Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. - Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front-end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary PLC address, if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves the driver connecting to the alternate (address Y) port and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. -->

This is the difference between successive value changes, which typically would be the scan period. sqRoot BOOLEAN SQRT input conditioning flag statsAverage REAL The average of all the recorded values. statsBuffer VARSTRING For INTERNAL USE: this stores all the value slot values recorded for the current period from which the statistics are calculated. statsDirection INTEGER This compares the newest recorded value (the current value slot) to the oldest recorded value and displays the results of this comparison, so that you can determine the general direction in which it is changing (its trend) as follows: - 0 typically means that the value has not changed. - 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up - -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. statsDirDev REAL An optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction specified by the statsDirection slot only indicates significant changes in value. Title: AnalogRawComms
Steps:
AnalogRawComms Top AnalogRawComms WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". WARNING: When using this registry value, it is up to you to ensure that the alarm limits and engineering limits are correctly specified for all Analog agents. -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Input String or Numeric This value must comply with the specified requirement, specified by the Operator and Constraint inputs, in order for this logical expression to evaluate as TRUE. For details, see Creating logical expressions . Operator List This list box contains all the comparison operator, which can be used to compare the two values. For details, see Available comparison operators . Note: The comparison operator that is used determines the type of data that can be compared. Constraint String or Numeric This input together with the specified Operator defines the requirement condition that must be met for this logical expression to evaluate as TRUE. Logical Result Boolean If this input is specified, then the result of the logical expression (specified by the other 3 inputs) is ANDed with this input and this result is assigned to the Logical Result output. For details, see ANDing logical expressions . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Logical Result Boolean If the Logical Result input is not specified, then the logical outcome of the logical expression (specified by the other 3 inputs) will be assigned to this output. If the Logical Result input is specified, then this input is ANDed with the result of the logical expression. Therefore, BOTH the result of this logical expression AND this input need to be TRUE for this output to be TRUE. -->

- Select the required AND spider.

Title: To AND two logical expressions
- Select the required AND spider. - In the Inputs section, connect the other Boolean input (typically the output of another logical spider) to the Logical Result input. Note1: The value of this input can be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note2: Although the Logical Result input can accept any Boolean value, by connecting it to the Logical Result output of another logic spider, allows two logical expressions to be ANDed. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Logical Result input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value, only "1" or "true" or "0" or "false" (without the "") will be correctly interpreted. Both the result of the logical expression specified within this spider and the Logical Result input must be TRUE for the Logical Result output to be TRUE. -->

Title: Animating graphic forms
Animating graphic forms Top Animating graphic forms Animating a graphic form involves connecting data to the graphic form and its added form components. The purpose of animating a graphic form, is literally to enliven a graphic form, causing it to both display data and to allow the end-users to interact with and manipulate your data in the SmartUI Operator. For an example of using a DataBinder to read and/or write data in a database to and/from a control on a graphic form, see How to write and or read database data from a control . Graphic forms can be animated using one or more of the following interchangeable methods: - Programmatically : Adding scripting to the graphic form to create an event handler An event handler is a method that is inserted into your graphic form script, so that you can determine what actions will be performed when the event that it is managing occurs. See event. for each event an incident (a significant occurrence) that does NOT require user action, unlike an 'alarm' which DOES require user interaction. exposed by the graphic form and its added controls and components. This is an advanced method that requires a knowledge of scripting. For details, see Graphic form scripting . - Visually: Connecting data to the properties exposed by the graphic form and its form components a general term encompassing all the controls, components and / or graphic elements that can be added to graphic forms, to provide the required user interface for its end-users. See control; component; graphic element; graphic form. , via: - Behaviours: Perform common actions to animate the visible form components a general term encompassing all the controls, components and / or graphic elements that can be added to graphic forms, to provide the required user interface for its end-users. See control; component; graphic element; graphic form. that you have added to your graphic form. Title: Applying data element security to allowed groups
Applying data element security to allowed groups Top Applying data element security to allowed groups Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the relevant category. - Click the plus box to the left of the relevant datasource icon. Tip: It is also possible to display its components by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Right-click the relevant data element name or icon and select Security . Note: This Security option will only appear if the currently logged on user has been assigned the Configure Access security permission for this data element. The Security configuration dialog is launched. Note: If the Server is deployed on a domain with a large number of groups, its list of Available Groups will take a long time to be populated. For details on reducing or eliminating this delay, see Specifying group subsets . - Ensure that the Security For Data Element field, beneath the Data Element Information group, specifies the required data element. - If the security permissions for these group(s) are required to be the same as those configured for the datasource of this data element, check the Inherit From Parent checkbox beneath the Data Element Information group. This will disable the Data Element Security group. Note1: This Inherit From Parent setting applies to all the selected groups and users. Note2: The Apply To Children checkbox has no effect upon the security applied to data elements that are not datasources. - Use the Groups And Users group to select the allowed group(s) that will be assigned security permissions for this data element. - Select the name of the required group from the Available Groups list, which contains all the allowed groups configured for the Server. - Click the << button to add this group to the Selected Groups list. - Repeat this for all the allowed groups that are to be assigned security permissions for this data element. Tip: You can also add groups by double-clicking the required entry in the Available Groups list to immediately add it to the Selected Groups list. - Use the Data Element Security group to assign the required security permissions to the selected group(s). Note: For details on these security permissions, see Available data element security permissions . In addition to these security permissions you can also specify which data elements can be audited and/or have their value changes authenticated. For details, see Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes . Note: This group will only be enabled, if the Inherit From Parent checkbox beneath the Data Element Information group is cleared. - Select a group from the Selected Groups list. Tip: Select multiple groups from this list, if more than one group is to have the same security permissions assigned to them. - Empty the checkboxes next to the security permissions that do not apply to the currently selected group(s). Tip: Clicking on the name of the security permission will check or empty its checkbox. - Repeat this until all of the selected groups have been assigned the correct security permissions for the selected datasource. Click for more detailed instructions: -->

Applying Security Policies Top Applying Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager allows you to implement the specified security settings on the local and/or a remote computer.

Title: Applying Security Policies
Applying Security Policies Top Applying Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager allows you to implement the specified security settings on the local and/or a remote computer. It is also possible to save these security settings to create a global Adroit security policy (security configuration), which can be applied to another Adroit computer, by simply opening this policy in its Adroit Security Manager. For instance: you may have one security configuration for your remote Classic User Interface or operator–only computers and one for your Agent Server computers. To implement all the enabled security policies on the local computer: this applies ALL the security policies (options) that you have enabled to the local computer. Note: It is recommended that you log off the computer to ensure that these changes are made. - Click on the Apply policy menu item. This applies all the security policies to the local computer that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked. IMPORTANT: These security policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. To apply or deploy the selected options on a remote computer: this allows you to apply ALL the security policies (options) that you have enabled to a remote computer. IMPORTANT: These security policies affect ALL the users and groups on this computer and not just the Adroit users and groups. - Click on the Deploy policy … menu item. - Select the required computer using the Browse for Computer dialog. This applies all the security policies that have their Apply Policy checkbox checked to this remote computer. Note: It is recommended that the specified computer is logged off to ensure that these security changes are made. Note: You need Adminstrative rights on the selected computer in order to perform this configuration. To save the security configuration: this saves the configured Adroit groups and users and their group memberships and all the security policies that have been enabled and/or the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings. This allows you to create different Adroit security configurations for different computers. For instance: you may have one security configuration for your remote Classic User Interface or operator–only computers and one for your Agent Server computers. - Click on the Save as … menu item. - Specify the name of the required security profile (*.sec.ini) that will contain these settings. - Click the Save button.

To apply a saved security configuration: this applies the Adroit groups and users and their group memberships and all the security policies that have been enabled and/or the Classic UI document and/or menu security settings to this local computer.

Arranging tool windows Top Arranging tool windows The primary reason for arranging tool windows is to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace .

Title: Arranging tool windows
Steps:
Arranging tool windows Top Arranging tool windows The primary reason for arranging tool windows is to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace . For details, see Design workspace . Note: Accessing a tool window can be difficult as it does not have a fixed location. For details on this and for how to reset your current layout of your tool windows in the Designer, see Accessing tool windows . Although tool windows can be either be arranged singly, it is also possible to group one or more tool windows together. Once grouped, these tool windows behave exactly the same as a single tool window, even occupying the same area on the screen. For details, see Grouping tool windows . For this reason, the following techniques, for conserving space in the work environment, can be similarly applied to both single or grouped tool windows alike: - Docking tool windows: To typically snap a tool window to one of the four borders of the Design workspace . For details, see Docking tool windows . - Floating tool windows: To separate the tool window from the Designer application so that it floats on top of the other windows where it CANNOT be docked. For details, see Floating tool windows . - Automatically hiding and showing tool windows: To minimise a tool window along the respective edge of the Designer application window. For details, see Automatically hiding and showing tool windows . Note: Auto hidden windows are incompatible with many of these other methods of arrangement. - Hiding and displaying available tool windows: The View menu displays a content sensitive list of the currently available tool windows and can be used to hide and display these windows. For details, see Hiding and displaying available tool windows . - Displaying tool windows on different monitors: If you have a second monitor, and your operating system supports using it, you can choose which monitor to display your tool windows on. For details, see Displaying tool windows on different monitors . Note: If necessary, your profile can be used to save any changes you make to the location of the tool windows. For details, see Customizing connections and work environment . -->

Title: Assigning global security to groups and users
Assigning global security to groups and users Top Assigning global security to groups and users Each SmartUI Server can give specific users and groups total or global security access to the Server, so that they become “master” users and groups that: - permanently become allowed users and allowed groups i.e. they cannot be removed from the lists of the allowed users and groups maintained by this Server. Note: This ensures that these users and groups cannot lock themselves out of the SmartUI Server. - are always able to log in to and have unrestricted access to this Server, its datasources and their data. Note: R restricted security access can only be assigned to non-global groups and users. For these reasons, it is recommended that: - careful consideration be given to which users and groups are given global security access to a Server. Typically, this should only be given to the Administrator user and the Administrators group respectively, which are the default settings. - these global security users and groups should administer the SmartUI Server security by adding the other allowed users and groups and assigning the necessary access rights to each of them. For details of configuring these global security groups and users, see Server security settings . -->

Associating policies with allowed users and groups Top Associating policies with allowed users and groups Each policy represents a specific service or activity that can be performed by a Server.

Title: Associating policies with allowed users and groups
Associating policies with allowed users and groups Top Associating policies with allowed users and groups Each policy represents a specific service or activity that can be performed by a Server. By associating the allowed users and/or groups with each policy, you can control the extent of access of each user and group to this SmartUI Server and its datasource plugins. Click for more information: - Policies can only be secured once the allowed groups and/or users have been added. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . - Any group(s) and/or user(s) that is assigned global security access to this Server, is automatically associated with every policy. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . - You can specify one or more additional groups that are initially associated with every policy (service) of this Server. For details of configuring this setting, see Server security settings . To associate a policy with allowed users: Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Management category. - Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Expand the Policy icon . This will display the Available policies. The Apply Profile to Users/Groups list box, contains all the allowed users and groups that have been configured on the Server. - Check the checkbox of each user and group that this profile will be applied to, by clicking on it. Click for more details: - An empty checkbox means that this profile is not applied to this user or group. - Since only one profile can be associated with a user or group at a time, if any of these selected users or groups are associated with other profiles, these associations are CANCELLED, when the Finish button is clicked. - If this profile specifies the currently logged on user, then this profile will immediately be applied to this user, when the Finish button is clicked. Audit Policy Top Audit Policy Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer’s security log.

Title: Audit Policy
Audit Policy Top Audit Policy Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer’s security log. Windows can record a range of security event types, from a system-wide event such as a user logging on, to an attempt by a user to read a specific file. Both successful and unsuccessful attempts to perform an action can be recorded. Use the Audit policy to determine the types of security events Windows NT-based Operating Systems will log. When administering domains, the Audit policy affects the security logs of the domain controller and of all servers in the domain, because they share the same Audit policy. When administering a Windows computer that is not a domain controller, this policy affects only the security log of that computer. Entries in a security log can be reviewed using Event Viewer. -->

Authorizing changes made to values Authorizing changes made to values This is only needed when you have configured one or more data elements to require authorization via the data element security dialog in the Smart UI Designer.

Title: Authorizing changes made to values
Steps:
Authorizing changes made to values Authorizing changes made to values This is only needed when you have configured one or more data elements to require authorization via the data element security dialog in the Smart UI Designer. When a value (data element) requiring authorization is changed then this change in value (write) must be authorized (before it is effected) as follows: - If the currently logged on user does NOT have write access to at least one of the data elements that are being written to, then the User Rights Elevation dialog is displayed by the Smart UI Operator or Designer, to provide the Username and Password of a user with write access to the specified data element, along with Comments , if required. Then the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog is displayed so that this or any other unauthorized changes (writes) made to the values (data elements) can immediately be authorized, as described by the next point. - If the currently logged on user has write access to at least one of the data elements that are being written, then the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog is displayed by the Smart UI Operator or Designer,so that this or any other unauthorized changes (writes) made to the values (data elements) can immediately be authorized. Note: This dialog does NOT display any data elements whose write authorizations have been deferred. Specify the Username and Password of the authorizing user, if required Comments , which typically provides the justification for granting the requested change/s. Note: The user who initiates the write cannot be the user that authorizes this write . A successfully authenticated authorizing user requires write access to a data element in order to authorize its change in value. If you are unable to obtain immediate authorization for this change in value, then click the Defer button, which adds this write to the list of deferred writes, so that it can be authorized later. For more details, see Authorizing deferred writes to data elements . If you want to stop or abandon this write (change in value), then click the Cancel button. -->

Title: Authorizing deferred writes to data elements
Authorizing deferred writes to data elements Authorizing deferred writes to data elements This is only required when: - you have changed a data element, whose data element security settings require authorization and - you are unable to have this data element write authorized, on the spot, in the Authorize Data Element Writes dialog. In this case click the Defer button of this dialog to add this write to the list of deferred writes, so that it can be authorized later. This list of deferred writes: - is not persisted (saved) so any changes to values that are waiting for deferred authorization are lost, if there is a power failure or the Smart UI Server computer is shut down. - is automatically maintained on a most recent change basis so that “old” changes are removed when a newer change is entered. Therefore, only the last (newest) change made to each value will be authorized. Currently the System Information project, provides the sample Authorize Deferred Writes graphic form (in the Data Element Authorization folder), to obtain a list of the currently deferred changes made to data elements, so that these can be authorized by the applicable user. The authorizing user: - needs to be an allowed user (or a member of an allowed user group) of the Smart UI Server - requires write access to a data element to authorize its change in value. - CANNOT be the initiating user (the user who made the change) If necessary, click the Refresh button to populate the list with all the currently deferred data element writes (changes to values). Select which value change/s you want to authorize in the list. Specify the User Name and Password and, if required a Comment , typically the justification for granting the requested change/s. Click the Authorize button. Note1: Only the last change made to the value is authorized, when more than one deferred change is made or requested for the same value (data element), Note2: Any data elements that the authorizing user does NOT have write access to will remain in this list. Repeat this as often as needed. In future versions, deferred authorizations will also be performed by a control. For details on configuring the authorizing of value changes, see Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes. -->

- Starting conditions for a new cluster server.

Title: Rules and implications
- Starting conditions for a new cluster server. Each server can be optionally configured to make itself master after a configurable period of time elapsed after this server has started (loaded). When this time period has elapsed after startup, if the server has not yet detected another cluster server in that project, then it will set itself to master. If, however, it does detect other cluster servers and no master server exists in that list of servers, then it will elect itself as master if it is the lowest alphabetically named server (i.e. closest to ‘a’) in its list of healthy standby cluster servers. - Consequences on the cluster of adding a new cluster server. No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when adding a new server to the cluster. All cluster servers loadup as standby servers. Therefore, if a master already exists in the cluster, adding a new server will not cause an automatic master mode switch between the servers. If it is required that a newly started server take over as master, and then the options in (4) below can be used. - Consequences on the cluster of removing a cluster server. The process of removing a server incorporates both normal program termination and abnormal program termination (software or hardware failures). No automatic changes are incurred on any cluster server when removing a standby server from the cluster. However, when the master server is removed, the remaining healthy standby server will become master. - Consequences on the cluster when changing a server’s serverMode and/or serverState slots: - The serverMode slot of a healthy standby server is set to master. The server hosting this operation will first set the remote cluster server serverMode slot to standby and only then set itself to master. - The serverMode slot of a healthy master server is set to standby. The server hosting this operation will not take any further action. The healthy remote standby server will detect the change and switch to master mode. - The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action. - The serverState slot is set from healthy to unhealthy for a master server. The master server will simultaneously set itself as standby, so that an unhealthy master is never obtained in the cluster. The remote server will detect the change (from healthy master to unhealthy standby) and become the master server. - The serverState slot is set from unhealthy to healthy for a standby server. The remote cluster server will not take any action.

- a healthy master server is removed - when the current healthy master server becomes unhealthy - the user sets the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or - the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby.

Title: An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when:
- a healthy master server is removed - when the current healthy master server becomes unhealthy - the user sets the serverMode slot of a healthy standby server to master or - the user sets the serverMode slot of a master server to standby. This results in a new master and the Adroit system will ensure that the existing master is relegated to standby, thereby ensuring that two master servers cannot exist in the cluster.

Title: Suggested method of operation
Start both Agent Servers in the cluster at the same time, and then the server with the lowest alphabetical name (i.e. closest to ‘a’) will become the master server. In an unplanned master server computer or software termination, the standby server will take over and the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. If, however, a master server takeover is planned, simply set the desired standby server as master and the current master will be delegated to standby. Thereafter, the automatic UI’s will switch to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. A planned takeover can be implemented either before a planned computer shutdown occurs or when the repaired computer is brought back into the cluster and is instructed, using the manual override, to take over as master. -->

Automatic Sending of Values Top Automatic Sending of Values The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values.

Title: Automatic Sending of Values
Automatic Sending of Values Top Automatic Sending of Values The Command agent is able to send an automatic SMS message that contains the value of a tag (agent.slot) to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For details of the other methods of sending SMS messages, see Sending SMS Messages . The following mechanisms can be used to send these automatic messages: - On change: In this case an SMS message is sent whenever the value of the specified tag changes. For details, see Automated Sending On Change of Value . - On significant change: In this case an SMS message is ONLY sent when the change in the value of the specified tag exceeds a specified deadband. For details, see Automating Sending On Significant Change of Value . - By triggering: In this case, an SMS message is ONLY sent when it is triggered by another tag i.e. when the value of this tag changes. For details, see Automating Sending By Triggering . Tip: This last mechanism can be used to send or report values at pre-configured intervals, simply by configuring an Expression or Script agent to provide an appropriate trigger. The received automatic SMS message, adheres to the following format: <SUB UPDATE> tagName = value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. Note: If the default formatting of real numbers has been configured for this Command agent, this format will be used to display real or floating-point values. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . -->
