Automatic WGP File Backups Top Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost.

Title: Automatic WGP File Backups
Automatic WGP File Backups Top Automatic WGP File Backups Adroit WGP files can be automatically backed up when they are saved to ensure that at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Both the number of days for which these files are to be saved for and the maximum number of backup files can be specified to avoid backup duplication and conserve disk space. WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note1: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: - name: is the normal name of the WGP file - yymmdd: is the date of the save e.g. 20041101 - hhmmss: is the time of the save e.g. 163715 - v: is an incremental version number Note: This version number will increment when this WGP file is saved, even if nothing has been changed in the WGP file. - n is the number of agents stored in the WGP file Note: This is still stored in the first line of the WGP file, as before. Note: In addition to automatic backup, Adroit WGP files also contain version information. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . -->

The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.wgp Where: - name: is the normal name of the WGP file - yymmdd: is the date of the save e.g. 20041101 - hhmmss: is the time of the save e.g. 163715 - v: is an incremental version number Note: This version number will increment when this WGP file is saved, even if nothing has been changed in the WGP file. - n is the number of agents stored in the WGP file Note: This is still stored in the first line of the WGP file, as before. Note: In addition to automatic backup, Adroit WGP files also contain version information. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . -->

Title: Automatically hiding and showing tool windows
Automatically hiding and showing tool windows Top Automatically hiding and showing tool windows Docked tool windows support an auto-hiding feature to conserve space within the work environment. When auto hidden, a tab is created for the tool window on the respective border of the SmartUI Designer, depending upon its docking area. For instance if the tool window is docked to the left of the Design workspace , then a tab will be created on the left border of the SmartUI Designer application window. Auto hidden windows are accessed when the mouse pointer is moved over this tab, which causes the window to slide back into view, ready for use. To auto hide a tool window: - Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - Click the (pushpin) icon on its title bar, so that it appears as follows: . To disable auto hide: - Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - Click the (pushpin) icon on its title bar, so that it appears as follows: . The auto hide tab is created as follows: - When a single tool window is auto hidden, both the tool window name and icon are visible on this tab. - When grouped tool windows are auto hidden only the icons of its component tool windows are displayed by its tab. Only the name of the tool window that was last or is currently accessed is also displayed next to its icon in this tab. For details, see Grouping tool windows . Note1: For details of the names and icons that will be used for all the tool windows provided by the SmartUI Designer application window, see Available tool windows . Note2: When an auto hidden window loses focus, it automatically slides back to its tab on the edge of the SmartUI Designer application window. Note3: Once a window is auto hidden, it cannot be grouped nor can it be placed into floating mode. Note4: If an auto hidden tool window is hidden and then re-displayed, the tool window is displayed in docked mode and this auto hide feature is not enabled. -->

Title: Automatically populating this window with tags:
Each AgentGroup agent (which provide a means of logically grouping agents) provides a exposeViaOpc slot (the Slots to expose via OPC Server (comma separated) field, which allows you to specify which slots, of the agents that have been added to this group, that you want to be populate the item-address browser of the Adroit OPC Server with. Available Agents Top Available Agents The most fundamental building blocks of Adroit are intelligent objects called agents, which in addition to being able to manipulate their own data can read and write to other agents and so influence them.

Title: Available Agents
Steps:
Available Agents Top Available Agents The most fundamental building blocks of Adroit are intelligent objects called agents, which in addition to being able to manipulate their own data can read and write to other agents and so influence them. For further details, see About Agents or How agents can be used . An Adroit configuration is therefore made of many different agents, each of which is a unique instance of one of the supported agent types. For details about how to reference agents, see Agent Referencing Convention . Each agent type provides externally accessible data attributes, or slots. For a description of the slots provided by each agent type, see Agent Type Slot Reference . The following is an alphabetic list of all the available agent types: - The Accumulator agent : to analyse an accumulating process value to calculate its difference in value (or delta) between successive events or over a specific time period. - The AgentGroup Agent : combines agents that have something in common into groups. - The Alarm Agent : manages how incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). are communicated to the necessary personnel and/or applications. - The AlarmList Agent : lists current or unacknowledged incidents to display in an Alarm List Viewer window. - The AlarmManagement Agent : configures and records your active incidents so you can improve your alarming configuration. - The Alias Agent : creates a reference to an existing agent to adopt its Behaviour and state information. - The Analog Agent : stores a real (floating point) value and provides engineering functionality such as scaling. - The ARec Agent : configures up to 256 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. - The Audit agent : supplements the Agent Server auditing by monitoring one or more tags for ANY change in value. - The Beeper Agent : provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker. - The Boolean Agent : stores a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). value. - The Command agent : sends and receives SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. messages to remotely configure or report on your process. - The Counter Agent : a simple counter and averager. - The Custom Agent: a generic agent type used to create user-defined agent types. Since this agent CANNOT be used in its generic format, the Custom Agent Designer utility, facilitates the creation of these user-defined agent types. For details, see How to Use the Custom Agent Designer - The DataLog Agent : manages the historical logging of process values ( tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). ). - The Date Agent : holds time and date information broken down into the date and time constituents. - The DBAccess agent : performs a transaction on a row in an OLE DB compatible database. - The DBLog Agent : is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. - The Device Agent : transfers process values between Adroit and the FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . - The Digital Agent : stores a Boolean value and provides engineering functionality such as value inversion. - The DumpConfig Agent : stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. - The EventLogging Agent : manages the logging of events by Adroit to Windows event logs and to a database.

- The EventOutput Agent : directs event log messages to output devices (printers, files, databases).

Title: Available Agents
Steps:
- The EventOutput Agent : directs event log messages to output devices (printers, files, databases). - The Expression Agent : performs user-defined calculations to calculate an output value. - The Frame Agent : stores up to 32 indexed strings. - The Hasp Agent: displays the current Adroit license information. - The ICMP (PING) Agent : determines the existence of a remote device on the network. - The Integer Agent : stores an integer number +/– 2147483647 (32 bits). - The IOT Agent : can represent any object containing multiple properties (or slots). - The Marshal Agent : provides the functionality of 16 Digital agents in a single agent. - The MaxDemand Agent : monitors your electricity usage so that you remain within your agreed usage limits. - The MultiMedia Agent : runs a variety of Windows compatible multi-media files such as .WAV, .AVI and .MID. - The MultiState Agent : defines up to 16 discrete states to create operating and/or control sequences. - The Notify Agent : directs alarms to pagers and also to cellular phones via SMS. - The OEE Agent : EITHER calculates the OEE stands for Overall Equipment Effectiveness, which typically identifies the productivity or utiltization of a machine or an entire plant, as a percentage. for the monitored equipment and/or plant or measures a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. for a measured production value. - The PerfMon Agent : monitors up to 16 Windows Performance counters to detect performance bottlenecks. - The PID Agent : provides the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with an external PID controller. - The Proxy Agent : provides continuous updates of the value of an agent referenced from a remote Agent Server. - The Real Agent : stores a real (floating point) value. - The Recipe Agent : provides basic sequencing and batching and reporting capabilities. - The Scan Agent : communicates one or more tags to an FED, these agents are managed by Device agents. - The Scheduler Agent : defines one or more time periods of time to enable or disable other agents. - The Script Agent : performs one or more Visual basic or Java scripts to do complicated tasks. - The Shift Agent : to configure your required shift patterns globally, for use by any interested agents. - The SNMPMgr Agent : monitors and/or manages network devices using SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. . - The Statistical Agent : provides the basic functionality to create a statistical process control strategy. - The String Agent : stores a "string" of text characters, only the first 79 of which can be used when scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). . - The StringList Agent : stores an unlimited number of indexed ASCII character strings of variable length. - The SystemDataLog Agent : administers the backing up of datalogs and synchronises datalogs in an Adroit cluster. - The SystemInformation Agent : acts as an information center containing data that is global to the Agent Server. - The Text Agent : stores a 79-character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). - The Timer Agent : performs several commonly used timing operations. - The UDT Agent: a generic agent type used to create user-defined agent types that typically duplicate the structure of your UDTs in your PLCs, by adding properties (basic data types) to them. Since this agent CANNOT be used in its generic format, the UDT Agent Type Designer utility, facilitates the creation of these user-defined agent types, see UDT Agent Type Designer . -->

The StringList Agent : stores an unlimited number of indexed ASCII character strings of variable length. - The SystemDataLog Agent : administers the backing up of datalogs and synchronises datalogs in an Adroit cluster. - The SystemInformation Agent : acts as an information center containing data that is global to the Agent Server. - The Text Agent : stores a 79-character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). - The Timer Agent : performs several commonly used timing operations. - The UDT Agent: a generic agent type used to create user-defined agent types that typically duplicate the structure of your UDTs in your PLCs, by adding properties (basic data types) to them. Since this agent CANNOT be used in its generic format, the UDT Agent Type Designer utility, facilitates the creation of these user-defined agent types, see UDT Agent Type Designer . -->

Available comparison operators Top Available constraint operators The Constraints dialog specifies requirements that the values of the selected fields must meet before they can be selected.

Title: Available constraint operators
Available comparison operators Top Available constraint operators The Constraints dialog specifies requirements that the values of the selected fields must meet before they can be selected. The following methods can define how the specified Value (requirement) relates to the value of each Field: Operator Name or Meaning Usage = Equal to If Field = value, then row is displayed. > Greater than If Field > value, then row is displayed. < Less than If Field < value, then row is displayed. >= Greater than or equal to If Field >= value, then row is displayed. <= Less than or equal to If Field <= value, then row is displayed. <> Not equal to If Field <> value, then row is displayed. !< Not less than If Field is not < value, then row is displayed.?? != Not equal to (the same as <>) If Field is not equal to value, then row is displayed. !> Not greater than If Field is not > value, then row is displayed. EXISTS (subquery) The 'subquery' argument of EXISTS is a SELECT statement The subquery is evaluated to determine whether it returns any rows. If the subquery returns at least one row, the result of EXISTS is TRUE. LIKE A character string comparison for SIMILAR pattern matching. LIKE "string" searches for values matching specified "string". If Field = string, then row is displayed. NOT LIKE A character string comparison for EXCLUSIVE pattern matching. NOT LIKE "string" searches for values not matching specified "string". If Field <> string, then row is displayed. The "string" specified for the LIKE and UNLIKE comparison operators support the following wildcards: - ‘%’ can be used as a placeholder for ANY number of characters. For instance “AB%” returns fields whose values are: “AB”, “ABC”, “ABCD” etc. Tip: "%AB%" returns all fields containing "AB" anywhere in their values. - ‘_’ can be used as a placeholder for a SINGLE character’. For instance “AB_” returns fields whose values are: “AB”, “ABC” but NOT “ABCD”. - '[]' specifies the required RANGE for a SINGLE character. For instance “[C-G]AB” OR "[CDEFG]AB" returns fields whose values ending with 'AB' and beginning with any single character between C and G, for example CAB, FAB etc. - '[^]' specifies any SINGLE character NOT within the specified RANGE. For instance “[^C-G]AB” OR "[^CDEFG]AB" returns fields whose values ending with 'AB' and that do not start with any single character between C and G, for example BAB, PAB etc. Note1: Wildcards can be inserted in ANY position within the string.

For example, 'A%B'.

Title: Available constraint operators
For example, 'A%B'. Note2: It is possible to combine these wildcards into wildcard expressions. For instance "de[^l]%" returns all fields beginning with 'de', where the following letter is not 'l'. IS IS If Field = value, then row is displayed. IS NOT IS NOT If Field <> value, then row is displayed. IN IN IN expression , defines the expression in which all valid values are located. If Field is found in expression , then row is displayed. NOT IN NOT IN IN expression , defines the expression in which all invalid values are located. If Field is not found in expression , then row is displayed. BETWEEN BETWEEN BETWEEN begin_expression AND end_expression defines the range of valid values. If Field >= begin_expression and <= end_expression , then row is displayed. NOT BETWEEN NOT BETWEEN NOT BETWEEN begin_expression AND end_expression defines the range of invalid values. If Field < begin_expression and > end_expression , then row is displayed. -->

Available graphic elements Top Available graphic elements The Vectors list of the Toolbox tool window, contains the following fundamental vector-based graphical elements: Note: Once added, vectors (graphic elements) can be edited and arranged.

Title: Available graphic elements
Available graphic elements Top Available graphic elements The Vectors list of the Toolbox tool window, contains the following fundamental vector-based graphical elements: Note: Once added, vectors (graphic elements) can be edited and arranged. For details, see Editing graphic elements or Arranging graphic elements . Tip1: A Vector Group can also be created to house one or more graphic elements. For details, see Arranging graphic elements . Tip2: To speed up the drawing of vectors, support has been added for the predictive drawing of certain vectors. For details, see Predictive vector drawing . - Button: to create a button control. To add a button: - Select the Button graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the button. Important properties: - Hovercolor : displayed when the mouse pointer hovers over this button; - Presscolor : displayed when the mouse clicks this button. - Line: to create a straight line between two points. To add a line: - Select the Line graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the line to start from. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the line to end. A straight line will connect these two points. Tip: These points can also be adjusted using the StartPoint and EndPoint properties. To add a vertical or horizontal line: - Select the Line graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the line to start from. - Hold down the SHIFT key. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the line to end. A horizontal or vertical line will connect these two points, depending upon the relation of the second point to the first. Tip: These points can also be adjusted using the StartPoint and EndPoint properties. - Rectangle: to create squares and/or rectangles. Tip: You can round the corners of a Rectangle vector by setting its RoundedRectangleRadius property as required. To add a rectangle: - Select the Rectangle graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the rectangle to appear and drag to define the correct size. Tip: If you just click without dragging then a default rectangle appears with its top left corner at the specified location. Note: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape. For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . To add a square: - Hold down the CTRL key. - Select the Rectangle graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the square to appear and drag to define the correct size. The width is made equal to height or vice versa (whichever is smaller) to create a square. Note: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape. For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . - Ellipse: to create circles and /or ellipses. To add an ellipse: - Select the Ellipse graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the ellipse to appear and drag to define the correct size. Tip: If you just click without dragging then a default ellipse appears with its top left corner at the specified location. Note: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape. For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . To add a circle: - Hold down the CTRL key. - Select the Ellipse graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window.

- Click on the graphic form, where you want the circle to appear and drag to define the correct size.

Title: Available graphic elements
- Click on the graphic form, where you want the circle to appear and drag to define the correct size. The width is made equal to height or vice versa (whichever is smaller) to create a circle. Note: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape. For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . To add an arc: - Select the Ellipse graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the circle to appear and drag to define the correct size. - Set its boolean VisibleBackcolor property to False. - Configure the ArcStartAngle and ArcSweepAngle properties to define where the arc should start and stop. Example: In the following screen shot the ArcStartAngle is left at 0 and the ArcSweepAngle is set to 270: Tip: You can also change this arc into a pie (a solid shape), by changing the boolean PieArc property to True. - Picture: to display an array (sequence) of pictures of the following formats (.bmp, .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .ico) based on an index. To add a picture sequencer: - Select the Picture graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want this. Use its Pictures property to define a list of indexed pictures and then drive its PictureIndex property to select which picture to display. Important properties: - Pictures : to define the list of indexed pictures. This can be configured by clicking this vector's glyph and selecting the Choose Pictures link from the Tasks menu. This displays the Image Collection Editor , where you can click the Add button to browse in the required images and/or use the and arrows to determine the required sequence of images in this list. - DrawPicturesAtOriginalsizes : this Boolean property, when enabled, resizes the Picture vector to the size of the currently displayed picture - this is enabled (True) by default. - PictureIndex : determines which picture is displayed by this vector, with the first picture ( PictureIndex = 0) as the default. - Polyline: to create a series of connected straight-line segments that can be closed to create a polygon shape. To add a polyline: - Select the Polyline graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the polyline to start from. - Click at each of the ends of the lines that are required to make up this shape and right-click to end. Tip1: If you want to close your polyline, set its Closed property to True (this automatically adds a line joining the beginning and ending lines). Tip2: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape (if closed). For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . To add a node (line) to an existing polyline: - Select the polyline graphic element in the graphic form. - Hold down the SHIFT key. - Position the mouse pointer over the node ( ) that the new line should be joined to, so that the cursor becomes the node-editing cursor ( ) and click on this node. This adds a new node on top of the selected node. - Release the SHIFT key. - Drag this new node to the required position. - If necessary, add another node by repeating steps b to e. To remove a node (line) from an existing polyline: - Select the polyline graphic element in the graphic form. - Hold down the CTRL key. - Position the mouse pointer over the node ( ) that the new line should be joined to, so that the cursor becomes the node-editing cursor ( ) and click on this node. This removes this node and its line from the polyline.

- If necessary, remove another node by repeating steps c again.

Title: Available graphic elements
- If necessary, remove another node by repeating steps c again. - Release the CTRL key. Tip: If you have removed the incorrect line, then press the Undo button from the Edit toolbar to restore it. - Spline: to create one or more connected curves, that may be open or closed. To add a spline: - Select the Spline graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the spline to start from. - Click at each of the ends of the lines that are required to make up this shape and right-click to end. Tip1: If you want to close your spline, set its Closed property to True (this automatically adds a curve joining the beginning and ending lines). Tip2: If necessary, you can both color and/or fill this shape (if closed). For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . To add a node (curve) to an existing spline: - Select the spline graphic element in the graphic form. - Hold down the SHIFT key. - Position the mouse pointer over the node ( ) that the new curve should be joined to, so that the cursor becomes the node-editing cursor ( ) and click on this node. This adds a new node on top of the selected node. - Release the SHIFT key. - Drag this new node to the required position. - If necessary, add another node by repeating steps b to e. To remove a node (curve) from an existing spline: - Select the spline graphic element in the graphic form. - Hold down the CTRL key. - Position the mouse pointer over the node ( ) that the new curve should be joined to, so that the cursor becomes the node-editing cursor ( ) and click on this node. This removes this node and its line from the spline. - If necessary, remove another node by repeating steps c again. - Release the CTRL key. Tip: If you have removed the incorrect curve, then press the Undo button from the Edit toolbar to restore it. - Scale: to create a graduated scale e.g. a sliding control. To add a scale: - Select the Scale graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the scale to appear and drag to define the correct size. Tip1: If you just click without dragging then a default scale appears with its top left corner at the specified location. Tip: Hold down the CTRL key while dragging to ensure that its width is made equal to height or vice versa (whichever is smaller). Important properties: - MinValue : The minimum value at the low end of the scale. - MaxValue : The maximum value at the high end of the scale. - Major : The number of major divisions over the scale range. - Majorcolor : The color of the major ticks. - MajorLength : The length of the major ticks. - MajorLineThickness : The thickness of the major ticks. - Minor : The number of minor divisions between major divisions. - Minorcolor : The color of the minor ticks. - MinorLength : The length of the minor ticks. - MinorLineThickness : The thickness of the minor ticks. - ScaleType : specify the scale to be a round type scale (gauge) or square/rectangular in nature. - ScaleStartAngle : The starting angle for the round scales corresponding to the position of the MinValue. - ScaleSweepAngle : The angular range between the MinValue and MaxValue for round scales. - DrawScaleEdgeLine : Draw a line along the outer or left edge of the scale. - ScaleEdgeLinecolor : The color of the line segment along the edge of the scale. - ScaleEdgeLineThickness : The thickness of the line segment along the edge of the scale. - DivisionsPosition : changes where the scale appears within the vector i.e.

on the Left, Center or Right of it.

Title: Available graphic elements
on the Left, Center or Right of it. - DrawTest : this draws a scale test. - ScaleTextcolor : The color to use for the scale test. - Text: to create static text labels. To add text: - Select the Text graphic element from the Vectors list of the Toolbox window. - Click on the graphic form, where you want the text to appear and drag to define the correct size. Tip1: If you just click without dragging then a default scale appears with its top left corner at the specified location. Tip2: Hold down the CTRL key while dragging to ensure that its width is made equal to height or vice versa (whichever is smaller). Important property: - TextScaling : - this Boolean property is False by default. Note: If set to True , then when resizing this vector, the text itself will also be similarly resized. - set this Boolean property to False if you do not want to resize the text when the vector is resized. Warning! If set to False , then the text will not rotate and will remain horizontal regardless of the rotation of this Text vector. -->

Available operators Top Available operators The expression string is a sequence of operators and their operands the term(s) or sub-expression(s) that an operator acts upon.

Title: Available operators
Available operators Top Available operators The expression string is a sequence of operators and their operands the term(s) or sub-expression(s) that an operator acts upon. , which are evaluated and resolved to produce the Result output. The operators follow a strict precedence, which define the order in which their operands are evaluated. In addition to this, operators also act on either the operand on their left or the operand on their right, which is known as their "associativity". Click for more details: The following table shows the precedence and associativity of operators (from highest to lowest precedence): The first column of the table also specifies how the operator is to be used, and designates the operands, as follows: - Primary: primitive members of expressions like constants, variables or functions. - Terms: separable parts of expressions, and can be signed terms or the product, quotient or modulus of two signed terms. Note1: Operators in the same segment of the table have equal precedence and are evaluated from left to right in an expression. Note2: This order of precedence can be overridden through the use of brackets '('..')', to force some parts of an expression to be evaluated before others. Operations within brackets are always performed before those outside. Although within the brackets operator precedence is maintained. Available spiders Top Available spiders Spiders and their links (silks) are essentially a visual programming language, which allows data to be transferred and/or manipulated, typically by means of drag and drop.

Title: Available spiders
Available spiders Top Available spiders Spiders and their links (silks) are essentially a visual programming language, which allows data to be transferred and/or manipulated, typically by means of drag and drop. Click for more information: For an overview, see Introduction to spiders and silks . Spiders are usually only manually added to the spider workspace, to perform additional manipulation or formatting of data. For details on how to add a spider to the spider workspace, see Adding spiders . Tip: In addition to manually configuring spiders and silks, it is also possible to perform bulk configuration, by exporting and importing this configuration. For details, see Importing spiders and silks . Spiders are organised into the following categories to make it easier to selected the required spider: - Advanced: Spiders that perform advanced functionality or configuration, such as, providing scripting functionality, adding performance counters, executing special functions, formatting string values or changing the visible level of a graphic form or dynamically changing the names of data elements and if necessary configuring their values. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Levels And Layers: To change the visible level of a graphic form at runtime. For details, see Levels And Layers spiders . - Performance Counter: To add performance counters to monitor the performance of your system. For details, see Performance Counter spiders . - Script Engine: To create script objects that interact with the Client and if necessary with the Server, to perform customised functionality. For details, see Script Engine spiders . - Special Function: To execute any special function provided by any of the configured datasources. For details, see Special Function spiders . - String Format: To format one or more values, if necessary, and display them as a single formatted string. For details, see String Format spiders . - Variable Data Element: To dynamically change a portion of or the entire names of data elements and if necessary configure their values. For details, see Variable Data Element spiders . - Animation: Spiders that animate graphic forms, for instance, by varying the colors displayed by color properties of components within the graphic form. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Blinking: To start and stop a color alternating between two pre-defined colors at a specified interval and to display another pre-defined color when this blinking is stopped. For details, see Blinking spiders . - Multi-state color: To define colors that provide a visual indication of the current value/s of either String, Double or Integer value/s. For details, see Multi-state color spiders . - Application: Spiders that perform application-level tasks, such as opening or closing graphic forms within the Operator application or that display dialogs to enter data values or that launch other applications and command files. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Application: To open or close a graphic form in the SmartUI Operator. For details, see Application spiders . - Data Entry: To enter a data value by displaying a dialog for this purpose at runtime. For details, see Data Entry spiders . - Execute Command: To run an application (.EXE), command file (.CMD) or a batch file (.BAT) and, if necessary, specify any command-line parameters. For details, see Execute Command spiders . - Databasing: Spiders that perform database-specific tasks, such as performing queries or interacting with DataBinders. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - DataBinder Trigger: To display or to save changes made to the data of a table in a DataBinder. For details, see DataBinder Trigger spiders . - Query: To perform queries and execute statements provided by any OLE DB datasource. For details, see Query spiders .

- Extended Type: Spiders that can configure or expose properties, such as specifying color or font properties that can dynamically change, splitting a data row into its column values, exposing hidden properties of objects, displaying the properties of data elements or mapping inputs to outputs to simplify the configuration of reusable graphics.

Title: Available spiders
- Extended Type: Spiders that can configure or expose properties, such as specifying color or font properties that can dynamically change, splitting a data row into its column values, exposing hidden properties of objects, displaying the properties of data elements or mapping inputs to outputs to simplify the configuration of reusable graphics. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - color: To select a color using a color edit box or define a color by individually manipulating its color constituents. For details, see color spiders . - Data Row Splitter: To filter out a row from dataset tabular data or data that is contained within one or more tables; each table contains one or more columns and each column consists of one or more rows. data and expose the values of its columns as outputs of this spider. For details, see Data Row Splitter spiders . - Extended Data Element: To either display the properties of an existing data element or to create a data element from any input. For details, see Extended Data Element spiders . - Font: To select a new font using the standard font dialog or to modify an existing font by independently adjusting certain of its attributes. For details, see Font spiders . - Hidden Property: To expose and/or manipulate properties of the specified object that are normally hidden. For details, see Hidden Property spiders . - Mapping: To map (connect) inputs to outputs, so that each input has an associated and identically named output. This spider is intended to act as a connection interface for reusable graphics to connect its necessary data easily i.e. without needing to configure its individual properties and/or spider inputs again. For details, see Mapping spiders . - Multi-State: To create more than one “state” for a specific String, Double or Integer value, so that when this value falls within a defined state, the spider returns the value associated with this state. For details, see Multi-state spiders . - Tooltip: To add a tool tip to a form component, to display additional information, which can include values. For details, see Tooltip spiders . - Logic: Spiders that construct logic expressions to perform various tasks by triggering one or more spiders, as an alternative to writing script. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - AND: To create a logical expression and, if necessary to AND its result with another Boolean input. For details, see AND spiders . - IF: To either create a logical expression. For details, see IF spiders . - Logic Trigger: To create list of spiders that are triggered in order from top to bottom, when its Boolean Logical Result input becomes TRUE after having been FALSE. For details, see Logic Trigger spiders . - OR: To create a logical expression and, if necessary to OR its result with another Boolean input. For details, see OR spiders . - NOT: To NOT (inverse) its Boolean Logical Result input. For details, see NOT spiders . - Mathematical: Spiders that perform mathematical calculations, such as providing constants, creating custom expressions, scaling values, summing values, multiplying or dividing values. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Constant: To create user-defined constants and/or use the existing (standard) constants within other spiders. For details, see Constant spiders . - Expression: To implement user-defined calculations, which can make use of variables. For details, see Expression spiders . - Multiply and Divide: To multiply and divide multiple numerical values to produce the result. For details, see Multiply and Divide spiders . - Operator Action: To perform various operations on an numerical or Boolean input.

It is possible for this change in value to be confirmed and/or logged to an event log.

Title: Available spiders
It is possible for this change in value to be confirmed and/or logged to an event log. For details, see Operator Action spiders . - Scaling: To convert raw (unscaled) values into engineering (scaled) values. For details, see Scaling spiders . - Summation: To add and subtract multiple numerical values to produce the result and to total all the values that are added and all the values that are subtracted. For details, see Summation spiders . - Simulation: Spiders that produce customizable simulated data, this is especially useful when the Designer is not connected to any datasources. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Simulation: To create simulated data. For details, see Simulation spiders . - Spider Workspace: Spiders that are used to perform spider-specific functionality, such as changing the active template set or triggering selected spiders. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Template Set: To change the active template set at runtime. For details, see Template Set spiders . - Trigger: To create list of spiders that are triggered in order from top to bottom, whenever it is itself triggered. For details, see Trigger spiders . - Statistical: Spiders that perform statistical operations, such as counting on and off events or calculating statistical functions from an analog value. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Counter: To record the number of On and Off events that occur, for a Boolean value, and the individual and total time of these events. For details, see Counter spiders . - Statistical Functions: To collect data from an analog (floating point) value and calculate statistical information (maximum, minimum, mean, standard deviation and total) from this collected data. For details, see Statistical Functions spiders . - XML: Spiders that either operate on or produce data in the XML format. This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Extended XML: To expose XML properties defined within an XML document as outputs so they can be used individually, as required. For details, see Extended XML spiders . - Data Elements: Spiders that represent a data element a finite component of data contained within a datasource that behaves in a generic manner; typically a value. See datasource. . This briefly describes the operation performed by each of its spiders: - Data Element: To create either a data element substitution for a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. or a place holder for a data element of a datasource that is currently unavailable. For details, see Data Element spiders . Note: Data spiders (data elements and/or properties) are a special 'hidden' subset of spiders, which are typically added automatically to the spider workspace. These are called Data spiders as they manage the transfer of data to and from the spider workspace. For details, see Data spiders . -->

Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files Top Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration.

Title: Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files
Steps:
Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files Top Backing Up Adroit Database (.WGP) Files The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For this reason, it is essential that this file, along with the other Adroit project files, be frequently backed up to ensure that the integrity of this data is preserved. Since if this file is either deleted or becomes corrupted without having a recent backup, many man hours of effort will be lost. Adroit WGP files, from Adroit 6 onwards, provide two additional features to assist with their regular back up, as follows: WARNING! These features are merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! - Automatic backup of WGP file on each save: To further ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups, WGP files can now be automatically backed up each time they are saved. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . Note1: If this is implemented, then at most only the changes made since the last save will be lost. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. - Version information saved in the WGP file: In addition to providing an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes, this versioning information can also be used to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. For details, see Versioning WGP Files . For details on creating a backup procedure to guarantee disaster avoidance and to easily transfer a project to another system, see Creating Backup Procedures . -->

Backing up and restoring MAPS projects Top Backing up and restoring MAPS projects You can backup your MAPS projects for safe keeping and/or to move them to another Server and restore them later.

Title: Backing up and restoring MAPS projects
Backing up and restoring MAPS projects Top Backing up and restoring MAPS projects You can backup your MAPS projects for safe keeping and/or to move them to another Server and restore them later. To backup a project: - Right click the required MAPS project in the MAPS window and select the Backup option. This creates a copy of your MAPS project and a compressed .ZIP file, whose file name is the date and project name, e.g. 6-14-2011_ACME.zip. - Both this ZIP file and the copy of your MAPS project folder, is saved to the MAPS project path that you specified when creating the project. Typically this is C:\MAPS \ProjectBackups\YourProjectName. To restore a previously backed up project: - Right click on the MAPS root node of the MAPS window and select the Restore option. - Select the .ZIP file of the required MAPS project that you want to restore. This will restore this project, if it does not already exist. -->

Bad tag status indicators Bad tag status indicators When displaying Adroit tags in your graphic forms, to assist in their troubleshooting, by default, both the Smart UI Designer in Run (runtime) mode and the Smart UI Operator display bad-tag status indicators.

Title: Bad tag status indicators
Bad tag status indicators Bad tag status indicators When displaying Adroit tags in your graphic forms, to assist in their troubleshooting, by default, both the Smart UI Designer in Run (runtime) mode and the Smart UI Operator display bad-tag status indicators. Note: The (Misc) ShowStatusBadIndicators Boolean value in Smart UI Designer and Operator CONFIG files, controls the display of these bad status indicators, which is True, by default. Tip: The Show (All) Information right click option provided by the Smart UI Operator, lists the good tags in green and the bad tags in red. For details, see Working with Show (All) Information . The following indicator icons are displayed, in the bottom right corner of the controls (or vectors) that have the applicable bad tags connected to them: Note: While each tag only displays the most relevant bad status indicator, if there is more than one bad tag linked to the control or vector, then the bad status indicator of the tag that changed last is displayed. - general bad: , which usually means the value of the tag is outside of its minimum or maximum range. - scan bad: , which usually means either the tag not been scanned correctly or the device has not started. - invalid tag: , which usually mean that the tag does not exist. Example: Clicking the displayed indicator, possibly displays the name of the tag and displays the name of the property that this tag is linked to. This only displays the name of the tag if it has been directly linked to this control or vector. Example: Therefore, if an intermediary method of linking has been used, such as a spider, then the tag name is not be displayed. In the case of using a spider, all you see is the name of the spider output that is linked to this property. Example: Clicking on the displayed text, displays the following options: - Status : this indicates the status or reason of why the specified (first detected) tag directly linked to this item is problematic (BAD, SCANBAD, NONEXISTING). - Copy : to copy the specified tag name (when this has been directly linked) to the clipboard, for reference purposes. Note: When an indirect method of linking has been used, such as a spider, this will only copy the name of the spider output to the clipboard. - Copy all : to copy all the tag names (when multiple problematic tags are directly linked to this item) to the clipboard, for reference purposes. - Edit : to open the Adroit Agent Configurator with this tag (agent) selected (if it can be found), so that it can be edited. Note: Since the editing of tags in the Smart UI Operator poses a security risk, the display of this option is controlled via the AllowEditTags Boolean setting of the Operator Settings page of the profile dialog, which is False (hidden) by default. -->

Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Top Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database.

Title: Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents
Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Top Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. The table will consist of a number of fields or columns; and each field may be linked to a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . Note1: Table names and field names should not contain spaces as each database vendor supports spaces differently. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. The following transactions are supported: insert, update, delete and retrieve: - An insert or an update transaction is used to transfer information from Adroit into the table, as follows: - An insert transaction simply takes the values of tags and inserts a new entry into the end of the table, this is useful for accumulating a history of information on tags. - An update transaction is responsible for keeping a record or a row in a table updated with the values of tags. - A delete transaction can be used to remove a number of rows in a table. - A retrieve transaction is used to transfer information from the table to Adroit . This is useful for applying a recipe management system or for updating Adroit with the results obtained from a 3 rd party application. These database transactions can be executed in the following ways: - On demand by poking a one into the agent's runNow slot, or, by clicking the "Trigger now" button, when editing the agent. - By scheduling , based on a simple schedule; e.g. to transact every three seconds, or, to transact every twenty-four hours synchronised at six 'o clock in the morning. - By triggering , based on a list of tags e.g. when the digital tag PUMP.value switches on, or, when the analog tag DAM_LEVEL.value changes. - By using a combination of triggering and scheduling . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the transactions, e.g. to transact every five seconds but only if the tag DAM_LEVEL.value has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple transactions. -->

Title: Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit
Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit Top Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means. It is the user's method of informing the Agent Server that something in the server is not healthy and it needs to relinquish it's master state. Manual master mode assignment . The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc.

Title: Project Directory Structure
Steps:
The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc. For this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created at the root drive (or wherever the data files are required to be stored), typically called ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default ', this project folder should contain the following directories: - \CSV, which should contain all your exported data. - \CustomAgents, which contains all the custom agents created for the project. - \Data, which should contain all the configuration pertaining to the Agent Server, such as .WGP files, *.BAS and database files used for reporting etc. - \Datalogs, which should contain all datalog files. - \Mimics, which should contain all mimic, trend, alarm and event windows, bitmaps etc. Note: This folder is typically the only subfolder that should be added to the Adroit Path . - \Wizards, which should contain all wizards. - \Work, which can contain persistence files for Counter and/or Statistical agents, which save the statistical values these agents calculate. For more details, see Agent Persistence Files Note: This project folder structure is created for all new installations and the \Mimics subfolder is automatically added to the Adroit Path . -->

Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector.

Title: Bind Value Behaviours
Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector. Usage examples: - Displaying a value on a label or button with applied string formatting. - Driving a gauge control from the value of an Adroit agent. - Driving a slider control from the value of an Adroit agent and writing this value back to Adroit when the slider is manually adjusted. The Bind Value Behaviour provides the following options: - To Control Property: this is the default option, where a value (data element) is linked to a property of a control/vector. If this is a String property, then you also have the option of applying string formatting to this value before it displayed. This allows a data element (value) to drive the value of a property of a control/vector. - From Control Property: this connects a property of a specific control or vector to a value (data element) and specifies which event of this control or vector is used to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. - Both (To/From Control Property): this both sets a property of a control or vector to a data element and when a specific user event occurs to this control or vector, then the current value of this property is written back to this data element. This facilitates a two-way feedback connection between the specified property of the control/vector and the data element. To bind a value to a property of the currently selected control or vector: - Add or edit a Bind Value Behaviour for the currently selected control or vector to display its configuration dialog. - If necessary, click the To Control Property option, which displays the To Control Property tab. Configure the To Control Property tab, as follows: - Click the browse button to the right of the From Data Element edit box to select the value (data element) that you want to drive the value of a property of this control/vector, as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element. The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner.

If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window.

Title: Bind Value Behaviours
If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. Note: If a DataSet value is selected, such as a field of a database, the Filter DataSet configuration dialog is displayed to select which value to display. - Select the property that this data element will drive (supply its value to) from the To Property list, as follows: Typically this list displays the commonly used properties and their data types for the currently selected control or vector. If you want to select a property or sub properties that is not listed, then click the browse button to the right of this property list to manually select it from the Property Selection Browser , which displays the currently selected property, by default. Note: Any properties or sub properties that you select will be stored for you in your user profile settings so that they will be listed, by default, in future - this means that you do not need to browse for them again. - If the Type of selected property is String , then you can also use the String Formatting edit box to align and/or format this value before it is displayed, as follows: The required formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: {0[, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} - either type in the required formatting string directly and/or For further assistance on creating format strings, see String formatting syntax . - click the browse button and using the Format String Editor configuration dialog to specify and/or preview the specified formatting. Tip: This is usually required when the default formatting of the value is not expressive or informative enough to be useful.

Title: Bind Value Behaviours
Bind Value Behaviours Top Bind Value Behaviours This Behaviour can drive a data element (value) to and/or from the value of a property of a control or vector. Usage examples: - Displaying a value on a label or button with applied string formatting. - Driving a gauge control from the value of an Adroit agent. - Driving a slider control from the value of an Adroit agent and writing this value back to Adroit when the slider is manually adjusted. The Bind Value Behaviour provides the following options: - To Control Property: this is the default option, where a value (data element) is linked to a property of a control/vector. If this is a String property, then you also have the option of applying string formatting to this value before it displayed. This allows a data element (value) to drive the value of a property of a control/vector. - From Control Property: this connects a property of a specific control or vector to a value (data element) and specifies which event of this control or vector is used to update this data element with the current value of this property. This allows the value of a property of a control or vector to drive the value of a data element. - Both (To/From Control Property): this both sets a property of a control or vector to a data element and when a specific user event occurs to this control or vector, then the current value of this property is written back to this data element. This facilitates a two-way feedback connection between the specified property of the control/vector and the data element. To bind a value to a property of the currently selected control or vector: - Add or edit a Bind Value Behaviour for the currently selected control or vector to display its configuration dialog. - If necessary, click the To Control Property option, which displays the To Control Property tab. Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function StartStop Boolean (Numeric, String) Any value other than 0 (zero) will start the color to alternate between the Oncolor and Offcolor at the specified Interval. ONLY the value of 0 (zero) will stop the blinking colors and displays the Stopcolor instead. Oncolor color A color edit box, that can be used to select one of the colors which will be alternately displayed, when the StartStop input starts the blinking. For details, see Selecting colors . This color is Green by default. Offcolor color A color edit box, that can be used to select the other color which will be alternately displayed, when the StartStop input starts the blinking. For details, see Selecting colors . This color is Red by default. Stopcolor color A color edit box, that can be used to select the color that will be displayed when the StartStop input stops the blinking. For details, see Selecting colors . This color is Control by default Interval Integer The required time over which the Oncolor and Offcolor will each be alternately displayed, when the StartStop input starts the blinking. This interval is 1000 milliseconds (1 second) by default. - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function color color Depending on the value of the StartStop input, this is either an alternating color or the Stopcolor . This either indicates the name of the color in square brackets ("[]") or, if a custom color has been selected or defined, this indicates the individual values of the A, R, G and B constituents of this color respectively. Title: How to use this OPC Browser to obtain an OPC Item Address:
- Before the OPC Item Browser for all OPC Servers is displayed, it connects to all the local OPC Servers, and any remote OPC Servers specified in the device’s configuration, that are running Note: If no OPC Servers are running then the OPC Item Browser will not open - Once the OPC Item Browser for all OPC Servers is displayed, the required OPC Server can be opened in the left pane and the configured tree structure can be browsed. Tip: Use the Esc key to abort the current browse operation. The right windowpane displays all the configured items that exist for the currently selected branch of the tree in the left windowpane. Tip: When browsing OPC Servers with large lists, use the Filter list box to limit the displayed items and easily locate the required item. - When an OPC item a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. is selected (highlighted), the status bar is filled with the data pertaining to it. Note: The Detail mode in the browser has been enhanced for use with certain OPC Servers. Tip: Check the Persistent checkbox to save and restore the last selected OPC item between browser sessions. So that it is no longer necessary to re-browse for it, when the OPC Browser is displayed again. - To select an item in the right windowpane, double click on the required item. This places the selected item into the third windowpane and copies this fully qualified path of this item to the clipboard. - If necessary, paste this item address into the required field of the dialog. Tip: Use the CTRL+V keyboard shortcut to paste this item address. - Continue the scan procedure as usual. For details, see How to Scan a Tag . WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies".

Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Top Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Instead of using the Tag scanning configuration dialog to configure the scanning of a large number of tags (agent.slot) for the same device, it is also possible to scan a single tag, export the scanning configuration to a spreadsheet application, perform the required bulk configuration and import this configuration.

Title: Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import
Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Top Bulk Scanning or Scanning Import Instead of using the Tag scanning configuration dialog to configure the scanning of a large number of tags (agent.slot) for the same device, it is also possible to scan a single tag, export the scanning configuration to a spreadsheet application, perform the required bulk configuration and import this configuration. Note1: This method is ONLY recommended when adding more than 100 scan points to the same device: Note2 : Check that your communications are working before and after the importing of the scan points. - Backup your Adroit database file (.WGP). For details, see Backing Up Adroit Database Files . - Scan at least one tag (agent.slot) to the required device . - Export the Device agent type , i.e. click the No button for all the other preceding agent type message boxes. - In the Choose file to contain conversion dialog, select the location to save the Device agent files, it is recommended to leave this as the default location of the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and save the ‘Device.CSV’ file, then save the scan files for each of the device agents, of the name format DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent. - When the next agent type message box is displayed, click Cancel , to stop the exporting process. - In either a CSV or text editor, open the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent that the tags have been scanned to. This file will contain four columns or comma-separated values, from left to right as follows: Address, agent.slot, Scanning Interval (period), Deadband Note: These fields are identical to those displayed in the Currently scanned tags list, when adding a scanning a tag. For details, see Scanning Example . - Add the agents and their slots that are to be scanned, their required scan addresses and if necessary the required periods and deadbands. - Save and close this CSV file. - Edit the required Device agent . - Stop this device agent . Note: If the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV contains only new scan points, skip the following step. - Remove all the scan points from this device. - Click Import… button and browse in the required Devicename-SCAN.CSV file, where DeviceName is the name of the selected Device agent. Note: If messages are displayed during the importing of this scanning configuration, see Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure for the possible reasons. - Start this device agent . - Verify that the communications are still fine and all I/O tags work as expected. - Save your Adroit database file (.WGP) again and finally perform a full test by restarting the Agent Server to verify proper loading etc. -->

Title: Calculating statistics from Analog values
Calculating statistics from Analog values Top Calculating statistics from Analog values The Analog agent can be enabled to calculate the following statistics from its value slot: sum (total), average, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and direction of change (trend). These statistics are only calculated, when the Integer statsPeriod slot is set to the number of minutes that you want the value slot to be recorded for statistical evaluation. This is a "rolling" period, which specifies the maximum sampling time from "now" (the current time) into the past for the specified period. In this case the value slot is recorded every second over this timespan and the statistics are calculated from these recorded values. IMPORTANT: Since the calculation of these statistics can affect performance if used excessively, please ensure that you ONLY calculate statistics for the Analog values you need them for. Setting the statsPeriod slot to 0 (the default value) disables the calculation of these statistics for an Analog agent. Tip: You can use the Statistical period (mins), 0 to disable field of the configuration dialog to configure this statsPeriod slot for an Analog agent. These statistics are saved into the following slots of the Analog agent, so that they can be separately reported, as needed: Note: If necessary, you can reset these statistical calculations by setting the Boolean statsReset slot to 1 (True) which clears the recorded values. - statsAverage : The average of all the recorded values. - statsMax : The highest recorded value. - statsMin : The lowest recorded value. - statsStdDev : The standard deviation of all the recorded values. - statsSum : The total of all the recorded values. - statsDirection : This compares the newest recorded value (the current value slot) to the oldest recorded value and displays the results of this comparison, so that you can determine the general direction in which it is changing (its trend) as follows: - 0 typically means that the value has not changed. - 1 if the current value is higher, so that the trend of the value is moving up - -1 if the current value is lower, so that the trend of the value is moving down. However, you can also specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value.

In this case set the statsDirDev slot, to the required decimal percentage value (a value from 0 to 1) so that deviations in value less than or equal to this specified percentage result in the statsDirection slot being set to 0 meaning “no change”.

Title: Calculating statistics from Analog values
In this case set the statsDirDev slot, to the required decimal percentage value (a value from 0 to 1) so that deviations in value less than or equal to this specified percentage result in the statsDirection slot being set to 0 meaning “no change”. For instance, if you set the statsDirDev slot to 0.10, then only when the newest recorded value differs from the oldest recorded value by more than 10 % will the statsDirection slot display whether the current value is higher (1) or lower (-1). -->

Title: Calculations in Expressions Top Calculations in Expressions Examples of expressions . An expression can be thought of as a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, which are evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Mathematical Operators . Mathematical Functions . This order can be overridden by using brackets. Each term of the expression is composed of primary elements, which can either be signed (or complemented) numbers or variables (v1 to v20, and v99 which is equivalent to "value"), or sub-expressions. This recursive definition of an expression means that expressions can be nested to any level of complexity. Note

Catch-up Top Catch-up When a new server is added to the cluster, it must become a mirror image of the active member of the cluster.

Title: Catch-up
Catch-up Top Catch-up When a new server is added to the cluster, it must become a mirror image of the active member of the cluster. The new server must restore its historical data (historical catch-up) that it lost during the down time. This historical synchronization or Datalog catch-up is facilitated by a new agent called the SystemDatalog agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. Note: Datalog catch-up is not supported when OLE DB logging is being used as this would only further delay a task which is already time consuming and CPU intensive. As OLE DB logging is logging to a database, this database could be equipped with the querying/replication tools required to fill any holes that exist. Historical data catch up of the newly added standby server -->
