text:
Changing from using the Classic UI Top Changing from using the Classic UI What you should know when using the SmartUI Designer as a user interface to the Adroit Agent Server: Although the SmartUI provides similar functionality, the means by which this functionality is implemented has changed somewhat from the Classic UI.

Title: Changing from using the Classic UI
Steps:
Changing from using the Classic UI Top Changing from using the Classic UI What you should know when using the SmartUI Designer as a user interface to the Adroit Agent Server: Although the SmartUI provides similar functionality, the means by which this functionality is implemented has changed somewhat from the Classic UI. For details on how to import your existing Classic UI projects into the SmartUI , see Converting Classic UI projects into SmartUI projects . - To familiarise yourself with this new designing environment, see Working with the Designer - For a quick start guide to using this new designing environment, see Quick designing guide . Classic UI Feature SmartUI UI Equivalent Accessing agent data Add an Adroit datasource and connect it to the required Agent Server. For details, see Adroit datasources . Agent server configuration Once an Adroit datasource has been added, its associated agent server can be configured. For details, see Configuring the Agent Server . User Interface security In addition to customizing the user interface display, profile settings can also be used to limit the access users have within them. For details, see Working with profiles . Mimics (Picture windows) Mimics are now known as graphic forms. For details, see Working with graphic forms . Note: When displaying Adroit tags you can display bad-tag status indicators on relevant controls and/or vectors. For details, see Bad tag status indicators . Tip: You can import your existing Classic UI mimcs directly into the SmartUI, see Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms . Vector graphics Vector graphics are collectively known as graphic elements, which can be added to graphic forms (mimics). For details, see Working with vectors (graphic elements) . Behaviours Behaviours are provided to graphically display your values. For details, see About Behaviours . You can also use spiders, which in addition to animating controls on graphic forms (mimics) also provide a visual programming language that is able to manipulate data, by means of drag and drop. For details, see Introduction to spiders and silks . Trend windows This is now performed by a charting controls that can be added to a graphic form (mimic). For details, see Charting controls or specifically LineChart controls . Tip: You can import your existing Classic UI trends directly into the SmartUI, see Converting Adroit Classic UI mimics into SmartUI graphic forms . Alarm Viewer windows This is now performed by a custom control that can be added to a graphic form (mimic). For details, see AlarmViewer controls . Event Log windows Events within event logs can now be exposed by using the Event log datasource. Once this datasource has been added, event logs can be displayed within a EventViewer control on any graphic form (mimic). For details, see Event Log datasources or EventViewer controls . Wizards Wizards or the ability to create re-usable controls from graphic forms, that can be inserted in other graphic forms is provided by TemplateGO controls and through the creation of Wizards. For details, see TemplateGO controls and Working with wizards . Recipe windows Since a native recipe control, does not exist in this UI, it will need to be manually created as a graphic form, if necessary. Tip: This recipe graphic form can also be re-used, by using TemplateGO controls. Template mimics and trends SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time, like template mimics. For details, see Working with SmartUI Templates . Template sets can now be used to create sets of data, which can be selectively displayed by a graphic form.

Changing scripting languages Top Changing scripting languages Scripts can either be written in Microsoft Visual Basic.NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp) scripting languages.

Title: Changing scripting languages
Changing scripting languages Top Changing scripting languages Scripts can either be written in Microsoft Visual Basic.NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp) scripting languages. Typically the profile associated with the currently logged in user, specifies the default scripting language used when creating scripts in the SmartUI Designer. For details, see Customizing default scripting language . However, you can change this language manually, if necessary, since the currently selected scripting language is used, as follows: - for compiling of the script and - for providing the default source code (text) that is automatically added to each new script to provide it with the standard functions and declarations. Note: It should only be necessary to change the scripting language when creating a script, since its script object will store the selected language when it is saved. For details on scripts and their script objects in general, see Working with scripts . To change the scripting language for a script in the Script Editor: - If necessary, edit the required script. If the Script Editor is displayed: - Click on the Build menu and select the Languages menu. The currently selected language will have a tick mark to the right of it. - If necessary, select the required language, either Visual Basic.NET or CSharp . Note: When the script it saved, its script object will save this language setting Note: If the language of a new script has been changed, it is recommended to change the default text of the script to the selected language too. WARNING! This will overwrite the currently displayed script with the default text for the currently selected language. To reset the default text for the script in the Script Editor: - If necessary, edit the required script. If the Script Editor is displayed: - If more than one script is opened, select the tab of the required script in the Editor workspace . - Click on the Build menu and select the Languages menu. - Select Reset Script Source . WARNING! This will overwrite the currently displayed script with the default text for the currently selected language. If this is not required select No when the confirmation dialog is displayed. - Click Yes , when the confirmation dialog is displayed; to replace the current text with default text. Editing script objects Working with the script editor . -->

- Zoom in 10% : This "increases the magnification" of the data by reducing the current scaling by 10%.

Title: Tools that apply to all charting controls:
- Zoom in 10% : This "increases the magnification" of the data by reducing the current scaling by 10%. - Zoom out 10% : This "decreases the magnification" of the data by increasing the current scaling by 10%. - Zoom home : This returns to the original or default scaling thereby cancelling any zooming effects. - Rotate chart : This toggle-button, when enabled allows you to rotate the chart by clicking and dragging the mouse pointer. - Print Setup and Preview : This displays the Page Setup to configure the print settings and then displays a preview of the current page, which you can immediately print. Note1: If the previewed chart contains a data legend, this is not previewed even though it is printed. Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) AllowPrintPreview property to enable this toolbar button, if set to False this button is disabled (grayed out). - Print chart : This selects the required printer and prints the chart, using default printing settings, unless the chart is previewed first. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) AllowPrint property to enable this toolbar button, if set to False this button is disabled (grayed out). - View chart in 3D mode : This toggle-button, either enables or disables the three dimensional view of the chart. - Export Chart : This exports the current chart as an image file and/or to export the current chart configuration settings as a template file(.ten) and/or to export the charted data to a file. For details, see Exporting charts. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) ExportChartButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. - Import Chart : This imports a chart configuration settings template file which configures the chart accordingly. For details, see Importing chart templates. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) ImportChartButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. - Runtime Axis Configuration : This enables users to change the scaling, position and axis ticks of the axes of the chart in runtime mode. For details, see Configuring axes at runtime . - Runtime Configuration : This enables users to add values to the chart in runtime mode. For details, see Configuring charted series at runtime . Note1: Enable the (Toolbar) ViewButtonEnable property to display this toolbar button. Note2: These configuration changes will ONLY be saved if the (Behavior) ViewName property is NOT empty. - Help : This displays the help topic for this charting control. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) HelpButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. Tools that specifically apply to Line and XYPlot charting controls: most of these tools are used when the chart is trending live data as they allow users to move back and forward between the historical and real time data. Note : The Interval and Timespan properties are typically configured in the Time Details tab of the Time Details dialog. - Page Left or Page Right : This moves the “window” of displayed data left (or backward in time) or right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). Note1: The current charting width is specified by the TimeSpan property. For details, see the TimeInfo property configuration in Important charting control properties. Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) PageLeftVisible and PageRightVisible properties to display these toolbar buttons. - Scroll Left or Scroll Right : This moves the “window” of displayed data left (or backward in time) or right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property of this chart. Note1: The Interval property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) ScrollLeftVisible and ScrollRightVisible properties to display these toolbar buttons.

Title: Tools that apply to all charting controls:
- Go to real time mode : This moves the chart forward until the real time values of the data are displayed in the chart. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) ScrollRealTimeVisible property to display this toolbar button. - Scroll line to view historical values : This toggle-button, when enabled displays a vertical black and blue scroll line, which can be each be dragged left or right to display the value and time of a historical value, in the legend. Each scroll line typically displays the interpolated historical value of current point in the chart. But this is NOT desirable when charting discreet values like digital values, so in this case, to turn off this value interpolation - enable the Stairs setting of this series in the Series Setup page of the chart configuration wizard, so that it does not display fractions of these discreet values. Note1: When enabled, four additional columns are added to the legend, namely Hist1 and Time1 , which display the value and the date and time of the historical value currently selected by the black scroll line and Hist2 and Time2 for the blue scroll line. Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) ScrollLineButtonVisible properties to display this toolbar button. Tip: Enable the (ScrollLine) ShowScrollLineMarkers property, to display the point at which each scroll line intersects the series of the chart, by means of a dot, which has the same color as the series. - Mark tips for series points : This toggle-button, when enabled and you hover position the mouse pointer over a specific item on the screen. over a point, the X and Y values of this point are displayed in a tool tip. - Modify the time details : This toolbar button, if displayed, displays the Time Details dialog to configure the charted time period . For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime . Note: Enable the (Toolbar) TimeDetailsButtonEnabled and TimeDetailsButtonVisible properties to display this toolbar button. WARNING! Any configuration of the charted time period, performed in runtime, will not be saved. -->

text:
- Zoom in 10% : This "increases the magnification" of the data by reducing the current scaling by 10%.

Title: Tools that apply to all charting controls:
- Zoom in 10% : This "increases the magnification" of the data by reducing the current scaling by 10%. - Zoom out 10% : This "decreases the magnification" of the data by increasing the current scaling by 10%. - Zoom home : This returns to the original or default scaling thereby cancelling any zooming effects. - Rotate chart : This toggle-button, when enabled allows you to rotate the chart by clicking and dragging the mouse pointer. - Print Setup and Preview : This displays the Page Setup to configure the print settings and then displays a preview of the current page, which you can immediately print. Note1: If the previewed chart contains a data legend, this is not previewed even though it is printed. Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) AllowPrintPreview property to enable this toolbar button, if set to False this button is disabled (greyed out). - Print chart : This selects the required printer and prints the chart, using default printing settings, unless the chart is previewed first. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) AllowPrint property to enable this toolbar button, if set to False this button is disabled (greyed out). - View chart in 3D mode : This toggle-button, either enables or disables the three dimensional view of the chart. - Export Chart : This exports the current chart as an image file and/or to export the current chart configuration settings as a template file(.ten) and/or to export the charted data to a file. For details, see Exporting charts . Note: Enable the (Toolbar) ExportChartButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. - Import Chart : This imports a chart configuration settings template file which configures the chart accordingly. For details, see Importing chart templates . Note: Enable the (Toolbar) ImportChartButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. - Runtime Axis Configuration : This enables users to change the scaling, position and axis ticks of the axes of the chart in runtime mode. For details, see Configuring axes at runtime . - Runtime Configuration : This enables users to add values to the chart in runtime mode. For details, see Configuring charted series at runtime . Note1: Enable the (Toolbar) ViewButtonEnable property to display this toolbar button. Note2: These configuration changes will ONLY be saved if the (Behaviour) ViewName property is NOT empty. - Help : This displays the help topic for this charting control. Note: Enable the (Toolbar) HelpButtonVisible property to display this toolbar button. Tools that specifically apply to Line and XYPlot charting controls: most of these tools are used when the chart is trending live data as they allow users to move back and forward between the historical and real time data. Note 1 : The Interval and Timespan properties are typically configured in the Time Details tab of the Time Details dialog. Note2: You can show or hide the standard chart time navigation tools and/or configure up to 5 tools that specify custom chart timespans (chart durations)via the Navigation tab of the Time Details dialog. For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime - Page Left or Page Right : This moves the “window” of displayed data left (or backward in time) or right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). Note1: The current charting width is specified by the TimeSpan property. For details, see the TimeInfo property configuration in Important charting control properties . Note2: Enable the (Toolbar) PageLeftVisible and PageRightVisible properties to display these toolbar buttons. - Scroll Left or Scroll Right : This moves the “window” of displayed data left (or backward in time) or right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property of this chart.

Title: Charting controls right click menu
Charting controls right click menu Top Charting controls right click menu Charting controls provide a right click menu, which provide a number of menu items in the following order: - Delete Series...: this allows you to remove one or more series from the charting control, as follows: - Right click the charting control and select the Delete Series... menu item. - This displays the Delete Series... dialog. - Check the Index field of the series that you want to remove. Note: If necessary you can remove more than one series at a time. - Click the Finish button. - Edit Chart...: This launches the configuration dialog for this charting control, which is the RECOMMENDED method of CONFIGURING the chart. For details, see General chart configuration dialog . - Edit Time Details...: To launch the Time Details configuration dialog to specify the default time details and/or time navigation tools for a historical trend (for Line and XYPlot charts ONLY). For details, see Specifying the default time details and/or time navigation tools for a historical trend . - Add/Delete Tools...: this displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog that allows you to add or remove the available charting tools to or from this charting control. For details, see Charting tools . Note: You can add more than one instance of each tool, if necessary. - Chart Help: this displays the help topic associated with this chart. - Properties: this displays the Properties tool window containing the properties of this chart. - Export Selection: this allows you to export this charting control to a .XML file so that you can create a library of commonly used controls, whose properties are fully or partially configured. For details, see Exporting and Importing controls . - Add Segment or Slice...: this allows you to add another value (slice/bar/column) to a Pie/Bar/Column chart, as follows: - Right click the charting control and select the Add Segment or Slice... menu item. - This displays the Add Segment or Slice... dialog. - Check the Index field of the series that you want to add another value (slice/bar/column) to. Note: If necessary you can add additional values to more than one series at a time. Tip: The other fields display the name of the series and the number of values (slices/bars/columns) the series already has. - Click the Finish button. - Delete Segment or Slice...: this allows you to remove the last value (slice/bar/column) from a Pie/Bar/Column chart, as follows: - Right click the charting control and select the Delete Segment or Slice... menu item. - This displays the Delete Segment or Slice... dialog. - Check the Index field of the series that you want to remove the last value (slice/bar/column) from. Note: If necessary you can remove values from more than one series at a time. Tip: The other fields display the name of the series and the number of values (slices/bars/columns) the series already has. - Click the Finish button. - New XXX Series , where XXX is the type of series: this adds the specified series to the charting control. -->

- Show Title: To hide or display the main heading of the chart.

Title: Appearance Settings
- Show Title: To hide or display the main heading of the chart. - Chart Title: To specify the text of the main heading of the chart. - Chart Legend Position: To specify where you want the legend displayed relative to the charting area. - Chart Legend Style: To specify what the legend on the chart itself (not the data legend) displays i.e. names or values of the series. Typically you display series values for pie, bar and column charts and series names for Line and XYPlot charts, these are the default selections. - Use Series color in Legend Font: If enabled, the text color used for the names of each series in the chart legend (not the data legend) use in the colors of the series themselves; otherwise these names are displayed in black. - View 3D: To display the chart in three dimensions, which adds depth to your chart and allows you to rotate, zoom and/or move the plotting area of the chart. - Show Toolbar: To display a toolbar that allows your end users to manipulate and configure this chart themselves - Show Data Legend: To display the data legend for this chart. - Data Legend Height Autosize: If checked, this automatically increases the size of the data legend grid to display all the trended series. - Data Legend Height : To manually specify the size of the data legend of this charting control, in pixels. Note: Depending on the number of series, this size could result in one or more of the series not being displayed by the data legend grid, in which case use the scroll bar to see the hidden series. - Data Legend Fractional Digits: To specify the number of significant places to use when values are rounded off in the data Legend. - Background Image: to browse for an image to display in the background of this charting control.

- Realtime: To trend real time data against a date time X axis.

Title: Data Settings (for Line and XYPlot charts ONLY)
- Realtime: To trend real time data against a date time X axis. Disable this when you want to report historical data. Typically this is only required by Line and XYPlot charts. - Extrapolate Data: To extrapolate data (estimate its value) from its last known value. More details: In other words, when the value of a charted series is not received, its extrapolated value is charted instead of inserting a gap where this value should have been. If enabled, this displays the Extrapolate Data as Bad color option, which if enabled charts any extrapolated data using the Bad data color (configured using the Bad color color box). - Historical Data Sample Rate (ms): To limit the retrieved number of historical data points to improve the performance of historical trending. More details: This Integer property, mainly applies to the LineChart series and serves to limit the retrieved number of historical data points to improve the performance of historical trending. This data sampling rate is specified in milliseconds. Historical data sampling is AUTOMATICALLY DISABLED when the specified sample rate is SMALLER than 10 x your current time frame window. In other words, the default sample rate of 5 seconds is only applied when the time frame window is greater than 50 seconds. Setting this sample rate to 0 PERMANENTLY DISABLES historical data sampling and always returns all the available historical data.

Charting tools Top Charting tools Charting tools can be added or removed from charting controls as needed.

Title: Charting tools
Steps:
Charting tools Top Charting tools Charting tools can be added or removed from charting controls as needed. Note: Each tool provides a property spider, so you can retrieve and/or drive its values. To add an instance of a charting tool: - Right click the charting control and select the Add\Delete Tools menu item. This displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog - Select the required charting tool from the Tool Type list box - Click the Add button. This adds an instance of the selected tool to the list box beneath the buttons. Note: You can add more than one instance of each tool, if necessary. To remove an instance of a charting tool: - Right click the charting control and select the Add\Delete Tools menu item. This displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog - Select the instance of the charting tool that you do not require from the list box beneath the buttons. - Click the Delete button. The following charting tools are provided: - CursorTool: This is a horizontal and/or vertical line that you associate with a specific series, which you can use as follows: - Either drag these around the chart manually, in which case their current position (X and Y values) are reported via the associated property spider - Or use the associated spider to drive (reposition) these lines instead, in which case this tool can provide limit lines to specify the required or desired maximum or minimum limit for a charted series. Tip: This tool should only be used for Line and XYPlot charting controls; however it does not work well for time based charts. CursorTool configuration: this describes how to display the configurable settings for an instance of the CursorTool charting tool and the more important settings. - If necessary, right click the charting control and select the Add\Delete Tools menu item. This displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog - Select the instance of the CursorTool that you want to edit from the list box beneath the buttons. The Cursor Tool Settings are displayed in the right hand pane for the selected instance of this tool. - The Active checkbox allows you to show (if checked) or hide (if cleared) this tool from this charting control. - Specify the Series that this tool should be associated with from this list box. Note: This tool is ONLY able to retrieve the values for this series. - Specify whether you want a Vertical, Horizontal or Both (vertical and horizontal) line to appear on the chart for this tool from the Style list box. - If necessary, you can provide a label for this cursor, by adding an Annotation charting tool and specifying its zero based index in the Annotation list box. Click for more details: Labeling a cursor means is that the text specified by this Annotation tool follows this cursor so that users can easily see which cursor is being used. This is typically needed when you have a large number of cursors in a chart. The zero based index of the Annotation tool is the position of this Annotation tool within the list of ALL the added charting tools added to this chart. For instance, if you have added a CursorTool, AxisArrow and Annotation tool to a chart, then the zero based index specified for this Annotation tool is 2. Note: If you are using an Annotation tool to label your cursor, please ensure that its Position parameter is set to Custom; otherwise its text will NOT follow the cursor. - Specify the available display options for these lines.

- Specify the options that configure the display of the actual lines, such as the color and style and thickness of the lines.

Title: Charting tools
Steps:
- Specify the options that configure the display of the actual lines, such as the color and style and thickness of the lines. Alternative clear the Visible checkbox to ONLY use the default settings. Configuring the associated property spider: all the instances of the CursorTool for a charting control can be configured using the Cursors property spider, within the Data sub-category of properties of the relevant charting control. - Ensure that the required charting control is currently selected in the graphic form. - Open the Spider Configuration window and if necessary display the properties pane on the right. - Open the Data sub-category of properties for this charting control. - Right click the Cursors property and select the Show Property Spider menu item. The Cursors property spider for this charting control is displayed in the central spider workspace pane. Note: Each CursorTool instance is described by the instance name CursorZ, where Z is a zero-based index Each instance of the CursorTool provides the following four Inputs: these can be externally driven (specified). - CursorZ [Series]: the series of this charting control that is associated with this instance. - CursorZ [Visible]: whether the cursor associated with this instance is hidden (False) or displayed (True) in the chart. - CursorZ [XValue]: the required X (horizontal value) for this cursor in the chart. - CursorZ [YValue]: the required Y (vertical value) for this cursor in the chart. Each instance of the CursorTool provides the following two Outputs: these can be displayed on a graphic form or used to drive another value etc. - CursorZ [XValue]: the current X (horizontal value) of this cursor in the chart. - CursorZ [YValue]: the current Y (vertical value) of this cursor in the chart. - DrawLines: This allows your users to draw lines on the chart at runtime, which they can then reposition and/or rotate and/or delete these lines, as follows: To draw a line: click and drag in the direction of the required line. Note: By default the left mouse button is used to draw lines, although this is a configurable setting. To reposition a line: click the line and move it to the required location. To rotate a line: click the required anchor (end box) and move it around. To delete a line: click the line and press the DELETE key. DrawLines configuration: this describes how to display the configurable settings for an instance of the DrawLines charting tool and the more important settings. - If necessary, right click the charting control and select the Add\Delete Tools menu item. This displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog - Select the instance of the DrawLines that you want to edit from the list box beneath the buttons. The DrawLine Tool Settings are displayed in the right hand pane for the selected instance of this tool. - The Active checkbox allows you to show (if checked) or hide (if cleared) this tool from this charting control. - Specify the Series that this tool should be associated with from this list box. - If necessary, specify which Button should be used to draw these lines. Note: do not select the Right mouse button. - Check the Enable Draw checkbox to allow your users to draw lines on the chart. Note: You can ONLY draw line for ONE DrawLines instance at a time, therefore if multiple instances have this checkbox enabled ONLY lines for the last instance can be drawn. - Check the Enable Select checkbox to allow your users to select the lines on the chart, to reposition, rotate and/or delete them.

- Specify the options that configure the display of the actual lines, such as the color and style and thickness of the lines.

Title: Charting tools
Steps:
- Specify the options that configure the display of the actual lines, such as the color and style and thickness of the lines. Alternative clear the Visible checkbox to ONLY use the default settings. Configuring the associated property spider: all the instances of the DrawLines for a charting control can be configured using the DrawLines property spider, within the Data sub-category of properties of the relevant charting control. - Ensure that the required charting control is currently selected in the graphic form. - Open the Spider Configuration window and if necessary display the properties pane on the right. - Open the Data sub-category of properties for this charting control. - Right click the DrawLines property and select the Show Property Spider menu item. The DrawLines property spider for this charting control is displayed in the central spider workspace pane. Note: Each DrawLines instance is described by the instance name DrawLineZ, where Z is a zero-based index. Each instance of the DrawLines tool provides the following four Inputs: these can be externally driven (specified). - DrawLineZ [EnableDraw]: to enable (True) or disable (False) your users to draw lines on the chart. Note: You can ONLY draw line for ONE DrawLines instance at a time, therefore if multiple instances have this checkbox enabled ONLY lines for the last instance can be drawn. - DrawLineZ [DataSet]: specify dataset data to automatically create and /or dynamically configure these lines. This dataset requires the following four columns: X1, Y1, X2, Y2 which are the coordinates of the start and end points of each line. - DrawLineZ [EnableSelect]: to allow (True) or prevent (False) the selection of the drawn lines on the chart, to reposition, rotate and/or delete them. - DrawLineZ [Visible]: whether you can (True) or cannot (False) see the drawn lines on the chart. Each instance of the DrawLines provides the following two Outputs: these can be displayed on a graphic form or used to drive another value etc. - DrawLineZ [DataSet]: this provides a dataset that provides the start and end points of the drawn lines. This dataset provides the following four columns: X1, Y1, X2, Y2 which are the coordinates of the start and end points of each line. - AxisArrow: This allows your users to add arrows to axes which can be used for scrolling horizontal axes left/right or scrolling vertical axes up/down. AxisArrow configuration: this describes how to display the configurable settings for an instance of the AxisArrow charting tool and the more important settings. - If necessary, right click the charting control and select the Add\Delete Tools menu item. This displays the Add\Delete Tools configuration dialog - Select the instance of the AxisArrow that you want to edit from the list box beneath the buttons. The AxisArrow Tool Settings are displayed in the right hand pane for the selected instance of this tool. - The Active checkbox allows you to show (if checked) or hide (if cleared) this tool from this charting control. - Specify the Axis that this tool should be associated with from this list box. - Specify whether you require a scrolling arrow on one or both sides of this axis by selecting the required option from the Position list box, as follows: - Start: This ONLY adds a scrolling arrow to the: - Top end of a vertical axis (e.g. Left or Right axis) - Left end of a horizontal axis (e.g. Top or Bottom axis) - End: This ONLY adds a scrolling arrow to the: - Bottom end of a vertical axis (e.g. Left or Right axis) - Right end of a horizontal axis (e.g.

Title: Code to implement the ImageList component
Code to enable ImageList component usage Top Code to implement the ImageList component The Imagelist component is a graphic form component that can be added to a graphic form from the Windows Forms category of the Toolbox window. This component maintains a developer-provided list of images typically for use with controls that need to display more than one image. For instance, this can be used to provide images for the different states of a button. Before the Imagelist component can be used, however, it needs to be associated with the control(s) on this graphic form that will use it. This association can be performed programmatically, by adding code to the Form_Load event of a graphic form. For instance, in the example code below an ImageList component (called “imageList”) is associated to a Button control (called “button”): ImageList __img = (System.Windows.Forms.ImageList)MyController[ "imageList" ]; Button __btn = (System.Windows.Forms.Button)MyController[ "button" ]; __btn.ImageList = __img Note : The ImageIndex property of the associated control (in this case called “button”) must also be set in this Form_Load event, if it is not set at design time. -->

Title: color Behaviours
color Behaviours Top color Behaviours You can apply this Behaviour to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to achieve the following effects: - To assign colors to the two states of a Boolean or digital value, so that depending on its value, this object will alternate between these two pre-defined colors. - To blink a specific color property of the object (alternate between two pre-defined colors at a specified interval in milliseconds) and display another pre-defined color when this blinking is stopped. This blinking can either be continuous or be started and stopped by a value. - To blink the visibility of the object (alternate between hiding and showing the object at a specified interval in milliseconds) . This blinking can either be continuous or be started and stopped by a value. - To define colored states, each associated with specific value/s, which provides a visual indication of a specific String, Double or Integer value. If necessary, one or more of these states can blink. - To define colored bit masks, each having an associated by an Integer value that represents a specific sequence of bits that are set (to 1) for up to 32 bits. If necessary, one or more of these bit masks can blink. Note: Only numerical and Boolean values can be used to activate blinking. Invalid values grey out the associated object. Title: coloring and filling graphic elements
coloring and filling graphic elements Top coloring and filling graphic elements All graphic elements that provide an enclosed graphic area can be colored using a specific color style and filled. Click for more details: The selected color style determines the appearance of the surface of the graphic element. These graphic elements include Ellipse, Rectangle, Polyline, Spline, Text and Scale. In addition to being colored, these graphic elements can also be filled, in other words, they can indicate a rising level from 0 to 100%. This appearance of this rising level is also displayed by using a specific color style. The following properties can be used when coloring and filling graphic elements: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. Property / (Category) Function (Appearance) Backcolor This property configures the default appearance of the graphic element, which is determined by selecting and configuring the required color style. For details, see Graphic element coloring styles . Note: When driving the Backcolor property of vectors, its Solid sub-property is added and configured automatically. Fillingcolor This property configures the painted appearance of the rising level used when a graphic element is being filled. This rising level fills the graphic element by the percentage specified by the FillPercent property. Its appearance should be distinguished from the default appearance determined by the Backcolor property and is determined by selecting and configuring the required color style. For details, see Graphic element coloring styles . FillPercent This Double property specifies the required percentage of the graphic element that should be filled, when using the appearance specified by the Fillingcolor property, with 0 being the lowest point of the graphic element and 100 being the highest. Any percentage of the graphic element not covered by the Fillingcolor property coloring, will display the default appearance determined by the Backcolor property instead. VisibleBackcolor IMPORTANT This Boolean property either enables or disables the ability of this graphic element to be colored and therefore whether its filling will be seen. If this setting is disabled then the graphic element will not be colored (and its filling will be invisible) , despite the configuration of the other coloring properties. This property is only enabled (True) by default, for those graphic elements that are closed, such as ellipses or rectangles etc. -->

Columns of event data Top Columns of event data The EventViewer control provides the following standard event columns: Note: If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by dragged it onto the DataSource property, then the Filter Dataset configuration dialog can be used to specify which of these columns are displayed.

Title: Columns of event data
Columns of event data Top Columns of event data The EventViewer control provides the following standard event columns: Note: If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by dragged it onto the DataSource property, then the Filter Dataset configuration dialog can be used to specify which of these columns are displayed. For details, see Filtering datasets . Name Description Type The general purpose / severity of the event, as follows: Error: A significant problem, such as loss of data or loss of functionality. For example, if a service fails to load during startup, an Error is logged. Warning: An event that is not necessarily significant but may indicate a possible future problem. For example, when disk space is low, a Warning is logged. Information: An event that describes the successful operation of an application, driver, or service. For example, when the server loads successfully, an Information event is logged. Note: Use the event Type classification, such as “Information", when filtering this column of the displayed event log i.e. Type=’Information’. Time The date and time at which the event occurred on the computer. Source The name of the software that logged the event. This will either be the name of the application itself or the name of the system or application component, such as a driver name. Category A further classification of this event by its Source, the program that generated the event. Event ID A number identifying the particular event type that occurred. Tip: Product support personnel can use this to help understand what occurred in the system. User The name of the user that was logged on when the event occurred. Computer The name of the computer where the event occurred. Message A textual description of the event that occurred. Data An optional field, containing binary data which is generated by the program that was the source of the event that occurred. Note: If your application makes use of this data field, this can only be interpreted through the use of a specifically created spider. When this control displays Adroit events that are logged to the Windows Application event log, this also displays the following columns of Adroit -specific information: Name Description Action The action performed/achieved by the event e.g. Digital Toggle, Status Message etc.. Adroit ID The internal Adroit identification of this event. Adroit Data The Extra Data associated with this event.

Value The Reported Data of this event. In other words the statement describing the result of the Action of the event e.g. Off - > On or Transaction Report etc. Version The version of this event. Sub Source This is similar to the Object , as it identifies the source in Adroit responsible for logging this event = for instance this provides the name of the logged in user for User information events;' Agent Server' for Agent Server Message events and the name of the Alarm agent for alarm-related events. For details, see GET Commands . allowRepCommand BOOLEAN NOT IN USE allowSetCommand BOOLEAN If enabled (set to TRUE) this allows this Command agent to perform SET commands that it receives. For details, see Diagnosing the GSM_SMS Device . defaultAnalogueFormat STRING This can specify the default format that is used to display any real or floating point numbers in messages that are sent from this Command agent. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . delReportTime INTEGER Timeout period for monitoring network delivery reports, if this is exceeded then the SMS message can be sent via another Command agent to someone else. For details on the necessary configuration, see Configuring GSM_SMS devices . disableSendingInStandby BOOLEAN When using this agent in a clustered Agent Server, set this slot to 1 to disable the sending of SMS’s when the Agent Server is in Standby mode to AVOID sending duplicate messages. emptyQueue BOOLEAN Empty the queue of current messages to be sent, for instance, for testing purpose or when the message queue has been filled with unwanted or unnecessary messages. For details, see Managing Message Queues .

enableCmdInStandby BOOLEAN NOT IN USE enableSmsSending BOOLEAN In order for the Command agent to send and/or receive SMS messages, it needs to specify a GSM_SMS protocol driver device that will be used to send and, if necessary, receive SMS messages.

Title: Slots:
enableCmdInStandby BOOLEAN NOT IN USE enableSmsSending BOOLEAN In order for the Command agent to send and/or receive SMS messages, it needs to specify a GSM_SMS protocol driver device that will be used to send and, if necessary, receive SMS messages. If true, this Command agent will attempt to connect to the GSM_SMS device, specified by the device slot. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . enforcePassword BOOLEAN NOT IN USE escalationTag TAGNAME The name of another Command agent to which SMS messages are to be sent when the timeout specified by either the delReportTime or recipResponseTime slots have expired. Although, this will only be used if either the reqDelReport or reqRecipResponse slots is enabled (set to TRUE). For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . expandPsuedos BOOLEAN When enabled (set to TRUE), pseudonyms and macros specified in a received message will be correctly interpreted and any outgoing messages will have the pseudonyms replaced with the full tag. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . globalAck VARSTRING To globally acknowledge alarms via Putslot, use the following syntax: tag[.alarm type] Note: This method does NOT use SMS to acknowledge alarms, nor are you limited to only using the Putslot utility, any method can be used that sets the value of this slot. Where ‘ tag ’ is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, ‘[.alarm type]’ is optional, this is used if a used wants to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance “ANA_1.High” only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas “ANA_1” acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To globally acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format in this globalAck slot: tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type] ignoreTime INTEGER If the Command agent is able to process SET commands, then it is possible to specify the period, in minutes, for which these commands are of valid for, which is calculated from the time the message is originally sent. For details, see Ignoring Delayed SET Commands . lastMsgReceived VARSTRING Contains the last message that was received by this Command agent. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . lastMsgReceivedTime TIME Displays the time of the last message received. lastMsgReceivedTimeStr VARSTRING Displays the time of the last message received, as a (var)string.

lastMsgSent VARSTRING Contains the last message that was sent from this Command agent to the designated GSM_SMS driver.

Title: Slots:
lastMsgSent VARSTRING Contains the last message that was sent from this Command agent to the designated GSM_SMS driver. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots or Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . lastMsgSentTime TIME Displays the time of the last message sent. lastNumberReceived STRING Stores the cellphone number of the last message received by this agent. password STRING NOT IN USE phoneNumber STRING The recipient phone number for sending of alarms, subscriptions, and commands. The Command agent has been designed to only send SMS messages to this phone number. For details, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . pseudoData VARSTRING Contains the list of configured pseudonyms and macros. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . queueCount INTEGER Number of messages currently in the queue, which you can compare to the queuesize slot to determine how full the current queue is. queuesize INTEGER The maximum queue size, once this maximum has been reached, any further messages that arrive will be discarded and will not be sent. For details, see Managing Message Queues . rawValue VARSTRING The most recent data received by this slot is sent by the Command agent to its associated GSM_SMS device. For details, see Sending SMS Messages or Message Sending and Processing Slots . recipientList VARSTRING The list of phone numbers allowed to issue commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Authorised Caller Access . recipResponseTime INTEGER Timeout period for monitoring recipient responses in which the SMS message must be returned to the Command agent, if this is exceeded then the SMS message can be sent via another Command agent to someone else. Although the reqRecipResponse slot must be enabled before this is used. For details, see Monitoring Message Response . reportData VARSTRING NOT IN USE reqDelReport BOOLEAN If enabled (set to TRUE) this monitors when the recipient receives a sent SMS message by requiring a delivery report to be sent as soon as the SMS messages arrives, which is then logged to the event log for auditing purposes. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt . reqRecipResponse BOOLEAN If enabled (set to TRUE) this monitors when the recipient acknowledges a sent SMS message by requiring each message to be sent back to the Command agent on arrival, in which case all incoming messages (to its configured GSM_SMS device) are logged to the event log for auditing purposes. For details, see Monitoring Message Response .

Each device contains primary and secondary parameters that define the available connection channels (or routes) and parameters.

Title: Primary and secondary parameters
Steps:
Each device contains primary and secondary parameters that define the available connection channels (or routes) and parameters. The secondary information is optional and is used in the event of a failure on the primary connection, or vice versa. How this secondary port works is simple, if the driver is using the primary configuration parameters and the communication fails, the driver will switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible. Once the primary port becomes available again, the driver may be forced into reverting to it by breaking the secondary port link, long enough to force the driver to do the switch back. This cycle may be repeated as often as fault conditions occur. Communication Failure Handling .

This group of details relates to how to address the FED (front-end device), and will contain details such as routing information or ID’s on a multi-drop that is specific to the FED’s protocol.

Title: PLC Details
This group of details relates to how to address the FED (front-end device), and will contain details such as routing information or ID’s on a multi-drop that is specific to the FED’s protocol. Necessary details such as the model in the range may appear here. Selecting the incorrect model will most often cause problems.

Port configuration parameters are often required by a driver to allow it to decide which port to use on the Adroit computer.

Title: Local Details
Steps:
Port configuration parameters are often required by a driver to allow it to decide which port to use on the Adroit computer. Any additional parameters in this group will show default settings that may need to be changed. Only parameters that are configurable on the FED will be shown here. In other words, if the FED does not support different baud-rates, this setting will not be optional in our driver.

Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure Top Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure When importing scanned tags (agent.slot) from the CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file, the following messages may be displayed: "Invalid device address" or "slot already scanned". Common Status bits Top Common Status bits The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent, each bit of which is also exposed as a slot.

Title: Common Status bits
Common Status bits Top Common Status bits The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is a 32 bit word containing configuration and run-time status information about the agent, each bit of which is also exposed as a slot. For details, see Agent Status . The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are known as the Common Status bits as they are common across all agent types, each bit has a fixed purpose. Their equivalent slots each have unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. These Common Status bits are further classified into control, condition and configuration groups, as follows: Note1: These are NOT contiguous groupings of bits, for instance the first bit statusBit00 is a condition bit NOT a control bit! Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . - The first group is called Control bits, which can be modified by the user. Each bit can therefore be set or reset by the user, to control an agent’s operator, logging, alarming, and scanning functionality. - The second group is called Condition bits, which are not directly modifiable by the user, and may only be viewed. They report on an agent’s integrity and alarm state, etc. Note: All agent Specific Status bits are also Condition bits, since they are not directly modifiable by the user. - The third group is called the Configuration bits, which are also not directly modifiable by the user, since they only provide configuration information about an agent, namely whether or not it has been scanned and/or alarmed. -->

Component Bit Configuration Top Component Bit Configuration Each row of the grid represents a component bit, which has the functionality of a digital agent.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Component Bit Configuration Top Component Bit Configuration Each row of the grid represents a component bit, which has the functionality of a digital agent. The following columns permit the configuration of the 16 component bits: Note: It is possible to manually change the width of any column and to auto-size the width of any column , in the grid. - Description: A General description of this bit e.g. HeaterNo. 7 - Name: The name of this bit. By default this name ranges from dig0 through dig15. However this name can be changed to switch0, switch15 etc. This will also change the name of the slot e.g. dig0.value then becomes switch0.value. Note: The following characters CANNOT be used when specifying the Name of the bits: Space Percent % Dollar $ Period . Back slash \ - Value: The corresponding value of this bit as extracted from the value slot of the Marshal agent. This value can be manually toggled, select the ‘Value’ cell, to reveal the following: - This value can be switched between the two states, using the left mouse click. The value of the value slot of the Marshal agent will change accordingly. The names of the two states are determined by values of State0 and State1 - Rawvalue: The corresponding value of this bit as extracted from the raw value slot of the Marshal agent. This value can be manually toggled, select the ‘Rawvalue’ cell, to reveal the following: - This value can be switched between the two states, using the left mouse click. The value of the raw value slot of the Marshal agent will change accordingly. The names of the two states are determined by values of State0 and State1. - Invert: The default, unchecked, action is to cause the value of this bit to always correspond to the rawvalue , e.g. if the rawvalue is State0, then value will be State0. If checked, then the value will correspond to the inverted rawvalue , e.g. if the rawvalue is State0, then value will be State1. - State0: The text value that is used to describe the state of 0 for this bit. - State1: The text value that is used to describe the state of 1 for this bit. - Pulse: The default, unchecked, action does not pulse the value of the bit, so it will remain unchanged. If checked, then the value of the bit will be pulsed i.e. the period for which the digital is 1 is timed, when the timer expires then the bit is returned to 0. This is useful for emulating the action of a push button. - Delay: The amount of time that a pulsed bit will remain in state 1, in milliseconds. The default value is 3 seconds. To alter this value, select the ‘Delay’ cell, to display: Either alter the value by using the left mouse button to click on the arrow buttons or modify the existing delay value using the keyboard, like any other edit box. - Coldstart: The default, unchecked, action does not allow for a cold start value, so that no value is sent to a front-end device when the Agent Server is loaded. If checked, then the initial value of this bit will be stored for later use. - Coldstart Value: The value of this bit is stored and will be sent to a front-end device when the Agent Server is first loaded. -->

Title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Top Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) Condition Bits fan-in, which means that an agent condition bit is automatically set to 1 whenever one of the corresponding slot condition bits is set to 1. The converse, however, is not true, i.e. an agent condition bit being set to 1 does not cause the corresponding slot condition bits to be automatically set to 1. Note: The condition bit fan-in uses positive logic: only one slot bit needs to be set for the corresponding agent bit to be set, and resetting a slot bit does not necessarily cause the corresponding agent bit to be reset (because the corresponding bit for another slot may be set). Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don’t want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset. Bad . Connection Bad . Alarm(s) Unacknowledged . Subscriptions active . text:
Configuration of an ARec Truth Table Top Configuration of an ARec Truth Table - Edit an agent of type: ARec .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuration of an ARec Truth Table Top Configuration of an ARec Truth Table - Edit an agent of type: ARec . The Edit AREC Agent dialog box is displayed. - Ensure the State I/O configuration tabbed page is displayed. - In the No of tags edit box, enter the number of I/O bits that are to be used to define the truth table, from 1 to 32. press the TAB key to create the required number of rows in the State I/O configuration grid below. - In the No of outputs edit box, enter the number of low order I/O bits that are to be used as outputs e.g. if No of tags = 9 and No of outputs = 5, then bits 0 to 4 will be outputs and bits 5 to 8 will be the inputs. press the TAB key to configure the required number of outputs in the State I/O configuration grid below, these will have a yellow background. Note: There can never be more outputs than the specified No of tags . - Tick the Cold Start Value checkbox, in order to specify a binary cold start value for the 32 bits, e.g. a value of 10 will set bits 3 and 1 and all the others will be set to 0. The default value is 0 i.e. no bits are set. - Use the State I/O configuration grid to add , configure and remove up to 32 I/O bits, slots of the ARec agent. Note: The grid provides standard configuration options . - Click the Update button to save the change(s) made to the configuration of the agent. - Click the Refresh button to determine the current configuration of the agent. - Click on the State configuration tab. - In the No of states edit box, enter the number of states that need to be configured, from 1 to 255. press the TAB key to create the required number of rows in the State configuration grid below. Note: State 0 is reserved as the Undefined state, hence only 255 states can be configured. - In the Output pulse width edit box, enter the time in milliseconds that the outputs, if used, are to be pulsed for. - Tick the Enable outputs checkbox, so that any configured output bits can be Set or Clear ed. - The Current value indicates which of the configured I/O bits are currently set. - The Current state indicates which the index number and the description of the state, which is associated with the Current value . If no such state has been defined, the Undefined state of index 0 is displayed. - Tick the Binary mode checkbox, to display the bit masks in binary format, instead of displaying its equivalent value. Note: In binary mode, bit 0 is on the right. - Use the State configuration grid to add , configure and remove up to 255 states that define the truth table of the ARec agent and to set or clear any output bits that have been configured. Note: The grid provides standard configuration options . - Click the Update button to save the change(s) made to the configuration of the agent. - Click the Refresh button to determine the current configuration of the agent. -->

When configuring serial communications of any type, be sure to specify the correct data and stop-bit settings if available for selection.

Title: Serial communications
When configuring serial communications of any type, be sure to specify the correct data and stop-bit settings if available for selection. If these settings are unknown, then the documentation for the remote device should be examined to find out the following information: - whether the settings are fixed and unchangeable - whether they exist as dipswitch settings - whether the devices are software configurable In the case of dipswitches or software configuration, it may be necessary to re-start the device for the settings to take effect. Because some of our older serial protocol drivers do not interpret error codes and translate them to English, I include a brief listing of serial communications error codes. These codes are separate from the Win32 codes. They can also be OR'ed together, and for that reason we supply the hex values here. 0x0001 = Receive Queue overflow 0x0002 = Receive Overrun Error 0x0004 = Receive Parity Error 0x0008 = Receive Framing error 0x0010 = Break Detected 0x0100 = TX Queue is full 0x0200 = LPTx Timeout 0x0400 = LPTx I/O Error 0x0800 = LPTx Device not selected 0x1000 = LPTx Out-Of-Paper 0x8000 = Requested mode unsupported (e.g. An error value of 12 is equal to 8 + 4 which means "Receive parity" and "Receive framing" error.)

If the communications are via a protocol such as TCP/IP, NetBIOS or other LAN protocol, the resource may be connected to the existing office LAN.

Title: Networks
If the communications are via a protocol such as TCP/IP, NetBIOS or other LAN protocol, the resource may be connected to the existing office LAN. To eliminate the possibility of interference, a "private" network should be created to reduce the chances of poor network termination or excessive traffic causing problems. Networking programs and Adroit protocol drivers rely on certain network drivers being operational before they can run. If this is the case, you will have to install any networking protocols required in the documentation. If the front-end computer is using one protocol, the Adroit scanning station must be running similar or compatible network layers before communication can be established. To see which network software you have loaded in Windows, you must open the Network Connections in the Control Panel , select the existing network connection, right-click and select Properties , select the software component and network card in question in this dialog, and click on the Configure button. Also check that there are no disabled networking software components. -->

- If necessary, add and/or select the required Tooltip spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Tooltip spiders . Tip: Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. - In the Input section, format the tool tip as follows: - Backcolor : specify the background color of the tool tip box. - Forecolor : specify the color of the tool tip text - Font : specify the font of the tool tip text. - Initial Delay : specify the delay, in milliseconds, after which the tool tip is triggered to be displayed to prevent the unintended display of this tool tip text. - Auto Pop Delay : specify how long, in milliseconds, this tool tip should be displayed before it closes. - Anchor : select the required position on the form component to display the tool tip from the available options. If you choose Custom then use the Location input to specify the offsets relative to the Top, Left corner, in pixels. - If you want to add one or more values or other variables to the tool tip text: - Double click the + New Input to add their placeholder inputs, typically 0, 1, 2 etc. - Then link the required values to these inputs to dynamically provide the values of these inputs. - Type in the required Text input and manually add any value placeholder that you want to display in this text, these placeholders take the form of the respective input number enclosed in braces '{}', for instance '{0}'for input 0. - In the Event Output , specify the name of the form component on this graphic form that should display this tool tip. - In the Event Name , specify the event of this form component that displays the tool tip, typically this will be MouseHover , although you can use any event to trigger the display of this tool tip. -->

Configuring a Binding Source to plot a series Top Configuring a Binding Source to plot a series The BindingSource tab allows you to specify which table or View within a DataBinder contains the data you want use for a series, as follows: Note1: This tab is only displayed if the Datasource field of the currently selected series specifies BindingSource .

Title: Configuration
Configuring a Binding Source to plot a series Top Configuring a Binding Source to plot a series The BindingSource tab allows you to specify which table or View within a DataBinder contains the data you want use for a series, as follows: Note1: This tab is only displayed if the Datasource field of the currently selected series specifies BindingSource . Note2: In order to use this option, you need to create a DataBinder for an OLE DB datasource and add a VIZNETDataBinder component to this graphic form, which creates the necessary BindingSource components. This provides the unique ability to chart each record separately. This means that when the VIZNETBindingNavigator control displays a record, the values of its selected fields can be charted typically in a Pie or Bar/Column chart. To chart the fields of the current record: - Specify the BindingSource component for the table or View from the BindingSource list of available BindingSource components on this graphic form - Check the Single Record Navigation checkbox. - Choose which fields you want to chart by checking or clearing the checkboxes of the Value Members list box. This list contains all the fields that were selected from this table by this DataBinder. The Selected Fields list box contains the fields that will be charted for the current record. To chart all the records within the selected table or View: - Specify the BindingSource component for the table or View from the BindingSource list of available BindingSource components on this graphic form. - Ensure that the Single Record Navigation checkbox is cleared. - Choose which fields you want to chart by checking or clearing the checkboxes of the Value Members list box. This list contains all the fields that were selected from this table by this DataBinder. The Selected Fields list box contains the fields that will be charted for the current record. For information about DataBinders, see About DataBinders . For more details about VIZNETBindingNavigator controls, see VIZNETBindingNavigator control . For details regarding the naming conventions of BindingSource components, see VIZNETDataBinder components . -->

text:
For a line series: these options are displayed when the Type field of the currently selected series specifies Line.

Title: Configuration
For a line series: these options are displayed when the Type field of the currently selected series specifies Line. - Specify the field to plot on the Y axis from the YValue Member list box, this is typically a value field. - Specify the field to plot on the X axis from the XValue Member list box, this is typically an ID field. - Specify the field to use to label the points of this line series from the Label Member list box, this is typically a String field. - If necessary, specify the field to use to color the points from the color Member list box, as follows: this column must be of type system.object and contain the name of the required system colors objects such as color.White, color.Blue etc. which is usually done in code. Typically you will use the YValue , XValue and Label members. For a pie series: these options are displayed when the Type field of the currently selected series specifies Pie. - Either select the field that specifies the size of each slice from the PieValue Member list box, this is typically the required value field. This is the recommended as it is more widely applicable. - Or select the field to specifies the size of each slice as an angle, in degrees, from the Angle Member list box, as follows: if necessary, instead of using values to specify the size of each slice, you can specify the angular displacement of the required slices i.e. values starting from 0 and ending at 360. - Select the field that labels each slice of this pie series from the Label Member list box, this is typically an ID field. - If necessary, specify the field to use to color the slices from the color Member list box, as follows: this column must be of type system.object and contain the name of the required system colors objects such as color.White, color.Blue etc. which is usually done in code. Typically you will only use the PieValue and Label members. For a bar series: these options are displayed when the Type field of the currently selected series specifies Bar. - Specify the field to plot on the Y axis from the BarValue Member list box, this is typically a value field.

Title: Configuration
Configuring a Scheduled Period of Time Top Configuring a Scheduled Period of Time The grid of the Scheduler agent, is comprised of the following columns, which are used to define a specific period of time as follows: Note1: This Edit Scheduler agent dialog can be resized, to view the entire width of this grid, if necessary. - The first untitled field is the index of the periods of time in the grid. - Start datetime: This column can specify the date and/or time at which this period of time is scheduled to commence. The default value is the current date and time. If this is left blank, then this cell is disabled and all date/times are valid. - End datetime: This column can specify the date and/or time at which this period of time is scheduled to end. The default value is the current date and time. If this is left blank, then this cell is disabled and all date/times are valid. Click the cell of the required column and configure it, as follows: Note: To ONLY specify a time and NOT a date, then enter the following date: 1 /1 / 1970 - Either click the downward arrow of the list box and use the supplied calendar to select the required date; the current date is selected by default. Note: Use the << and >> buttons to select the required year; use the < and > buttons to select the required month and then click on the required date. - Or click in the list box, over the required date and time digits to select them, then either type in the required unit or use the spin control arrows to increase or decrease the value accordingly. Note1: Only numbers can be typed in and if the number that is entered is too great for the specified unit it will be disregarded Note2: The date and time is displayed as per the Regional Settings of the computer. - Weekdays: This column can specify the days of the week, which need to be included during this scheduled period of time. By default all the days of the week are included. Click the cell of this column and configure it, as follows: - Click the downward arrow on the right of this cell. - Ensure that the tick boxes of the days for which this period of time, is NOT applicable, are cleared.

Configuring a UDT agent Top Configuring a UDT Agent The UDT Agent Type Designer creates UDT agent types that emulate the structure of a UDT in a PLC.

Title: Configuration
Configuring a UDT agent Top Configuring a UDT Agent The UDT Agent Type Designer creates UDT agent types that emulate the structure of a UDT in a PLC. Once created you need to add one or more agents to these UDT agent types (templates). Then configure and scan these agents to their corresponding UDTs in the required PLCs. PLEASE NOTE :Every instance (agent created) of an UDT agent type will consume (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. To edit a UDT agent: how to display the edit dialog of a defined UDT agent. - Ensure that your Agent Server is started. - If the Adroit User Interface of your choice. - Open the Agent configuration dialog. - Select the name of the required UDT agent type from the Type list box. - Type the name of the required agent in the Name edit field. - Click the Add button. PLEASE NOTE :Every instance (agent created) of an UDT agent type will consume (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when the rawvalue slot is scanned. - Double click this agent in the Agents list box to display its edit dialog. IMPORTANT When you edit UDT agents you must also remove all existing agent instances of this UDT agent type from the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file! When you change the structure of a UDT agent (by using the UDT agent designer), then any UDT agents of that type that are already saved in a WGP file will prevent the WGP file from loading because their saved structures are now incorrect. Therefore when you change the structure of a UDT agent, you must remove all instances of this UDT agent type from the WGP file. For example if you have a UDT agent type called MOTORE, whose structure you have changed, then you need to: EITHER manually delete all agents of this MOTORE agent type. OR you can use the WGP Remove utility to do this for you and back up the original WGP file. Note: This utility can be installed from the Additional Components install that provided on the Adroit 10 DVD or can be downloaded from the Adroit website. In this case, open the Command prompt, in Administrator mode (in Windows 8.1, right click the Windows button and select the Command Prompt (Admin) item). Type in: wgpremove motore This removes all instance of the MOTORE agent type from the currently configured WGP file in Adroit Config (if using the SmartUI) or in the Classic Adroit Setup (if using Classic Adroit) and back up the original WGP file. To configure a UDT agent: how to configure the edit dialog of a defined UDT agent. - Check the Live checkbox, to immediately save changes made to the configuration of this agent, without needing to click the Update button first. - Check the Auto-refresh checkbox, to immediately refresh the dialog to display the latest values of these properties, without needing to click the Refresh button first. Tip: Only use this setting for monitoring the UDT property values; do NOT use this when you are changing UDT properties values from this dialog. - For each of the properties that are defined for this UDT, you can configure the following: - Value: This is ONLY editable if the Readonly checkbox for this property is cleared in the UDT Agent Type Designer utility. - Tag reference: Specify a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). whose value will be mirrored with this property value.

In other words the current value of this property will be copied into the specified tag.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
In other words the current value of this property will be copied into the specified tag. Clicking the browse button to select this tag using the tag browser. For details, see Selecting a tag . - Click OK once you have configured this agent appropriately. To scan this UDT agent: how to communicate the UDT this agent represents to its corresponding UDT in the required PLC. - Right click this agent in the Agents list box. - Select the Scan… menu item to display the Tag scanning configuration dialog. - Select the device that communicates to this PLC from the Device list box. Note : Currently you can only specify devices that communicate using theBeckhoff and Alan Bradley protocols. This automatically selects both this Agent name and its required Slot , in this case rawValue . - Specify the Address of the corresponding UDT in this PLC. - If necessary, specify the required Scan Rate , in milliseconds and Deadband settings. Note : These settings apply to ALL the properties specified within this UDT. - You should NEVER check the Scan (input) inhibited checkbox. - It is NOT recommended to check the Output Enabled checkbox when your UDT contains properties that are a mixture of read and write variables. Click for more details: when a control is done the ENTIRE UDT is written back to the PLC which may overwrite the values of readonly properties. - Click the Scan button. Repeat this procedure for all the UDTs you need to configure. Note: The value slots are saved and the agent edit dialog is resizable. -->
