These first three interval options use the intervalTag , which is a tag you can browse to set when the end of an interval has occurred: 0 = Interval tag value goes to zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0].

Title: IntervalMode options 0 - 2
These first three interval options use the intervalTag , which is a tag you can browse to set when the end of an interval has occurred: 0 = Interval tag value goes to zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from a value of zero [0] to any non-zero value. 2 = Any interval tag value change The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes in value to any other value (a different value from its current value).

The next two options let you to define the required interval by making use of the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the duration of each period in minutes: 3 = Synchronised (to clock - default) - The agent forces the periods to be synchronised with the system time (i.e.

Title: IntervalMode options 3 - 4
The next two options let you to define the required interval by making use of the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the duration of each period in minutes: 3 = Synchronised (to clock - default) - The agent forces the periods to be synchronised with the system time (i.e. the time of the Agent Server computer) . Therefore, the initial period of the current hour always begins at the start of the current hour (0 seconds or 0 minutes) which is how the current period is calculated when this agent is enabled. - As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 minutes past the hour and end at 20 minutes past the hour, and so on. - A further example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 3 with an interval of 10 minutes and the agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:10 for this mode (a partial interval of only 8 minutes to enforce the ending time of this period, which began at 10:00 even though the agent was only enabled at 10:02) . - However, if this same agent is enabled at 10:45, then the first period will end at 10:50 for this mode (a partial interval of only 5 minutes to enforce the ending time of the current period, which began at 10:40). Important: If you are using this method, then you need to ensure that the specified interval is divisible into 60 or is a multiple of 60 otherwise period timing errors will occur. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) - The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interval number of minutes to this starting time. - For example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22, and so on.

If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to.

Title: IntervalMode option 5
If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to. 5 = Manual trigger The rate of change and its alarm limits only applies when using periods that have regular intervals. 4. Configure the required alarm limits and if necessary their deadband If necessary, you can configure the alarm limits and the deadband when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. In other words, this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area outside these alarm limits, which the value must reduce by before the alarm is cleared. Important: The deadband slot ONLY applies to the alarm limits for the differential value and NOT to the rate of change alarm limits.

The following alarm limits can be defined for the differential value in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog: - The valueHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action.

Title: Limitations
The following alarm limits can be defined for the differential value in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog: - The valueHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHighHigh default alarm type. - The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHigh default alarm type. - The valueLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLow default alarm type. - The valueLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLowLow default alarm type Note: Whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low alarm must, by definition also be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed.

The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits.

Title: Rate of change
The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. - The rateHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHighHigh default alarm type. - The rateHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHigh default alarm type. - The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLow default alarm type. - The rateLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLowLow default alarm type. 5. Configure the SQL Server database to store the values of each period To maintain a history of the differential values for each period you must specify the SQL Server database and table that is used to store these records: - Specify the connection string to this SQL Server database in the connection field by using the Data Link Properties dialog. - For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . - Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. - Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. - Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. - At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string.

- Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field.

Title: Rate of change
- Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field. By default, this table name is set to the name of this Accumulator agent. - When you are using a clustered Agent Server, then the standby clustered partner will, by default, not log these records to this database, thus preventing duplicate records. However, you can change this, if required, by configuring the disableOnStandby slot setting. - Each record specifies a unique index (idx) ; the date and time at which the period ended (dt) ; the differential value (value) and the inputValue - the value of the accumulating process variable (accumulator) at this time. If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table will be created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period If you want automatic management of this data, then specify how many days worth of data you want this table to store in the housekeepDays field, to ensure that you keep the most relevant (most recent) records only. Note: The default value of 0 disables this functionality. 6. Enable the agent To start analysing the accumulating process: - You should enable this agent to start analysing the accumulating process value and calculate its differential value for each period and its rate of change and, if required, also log the values of each period to the specified history table in the SQL Server database. - To enable this agent, set the enable slot of this agent (in the General section of this properties dialog) to True. 7. Values calculated by the agent for each period At the end of every period: - The differential value of the previous period is saved to lastValue . - The differential value of the current completed period is calculated as: inputValue - startValue. - The rate of change of the previous differential value and period is calculated as: lastValue * 60 (minutes per hour) / (last period length in minutes) = value per hour. - A new record is added to the tableName (in the database by connection , if specified) containing the period start and end times, values and differential value and rate for the period. - A new period will commence immediately and the startValue will be assigned to the inputValue .

Tip: You can view the amount of time that has passed (elapsed) from the start of the current period, in minutes, by viewing the elapsedTime slot.

Title: Rate of change
Tip: You can view the amount of time that has passed (elapsed) from the start of the current period, in minutes, by viewing the elapsedTime slot. -->

Title: IntervalMode options 0 - 2
These first three interval options use the intervalTag , which is a tag you can browse to set when the end of an interval has occurred: 0 = Interval tag value goes to zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from any non-zero value to a value of zero [0]. 1 = Interval value goes (from zero) to non-zero The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes from a value of zero [0] to any non-zero value. 2 = Any interval tag value change The end of the interval occurs when the value of the intervalTag changes in value to any other value (a different value from its current value).

Title: IntervalMode options 3 - 4
The next two options let you to define the required interval by making use of the system time (the time of the Agent Server computer) and the interval slot, which specifies the duration of each period in minutes: 3 = Synchronised (to clock - default) - The agent forces the periods to be synchronised with the system time (i.e. the time of the Agent Server computer) . Therefore, the initial period of the current hour always begins at the start of the current hour (0 seconds or 0 minutes) which is how the current period is calculated when this agent is enabled. - As an example, if you have an interval of 10 minutes, the first period of this hour starts on the current hour to 10 minutes past the hour; the second period of this hour starts at 10 minutes past the hour and end at 20 minutes past the hour, and so on. - A further example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 3 with an interval of 10 minutes and the agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:10 for this mode (a partial interval of only 8 minutes to enforce the ending time of this period, which began at 10:00 even though the agent was only enabled at 10:02) . - However, if this same agent is enabled at 10:45, then the first period will end at 10:50 for this mode (a partial interval of only 5 minutes to enforce the ending time of the current period, which began at 10:40). Important: If you are using this method, then you need to ensure that the specified interval is divisible into 60 or is a multiple of 60 otherwise period timing errors will occur. 4 = Not synchronised (to clock) - The agent sets the starting time of the periods to the exact time that this agent is enabled and calculates all the successive periods by adding the specified interval number of minutes to this starting time. - For example, if the agent is set to use the intervalMode of 4 with an interval of 10 minutes and this agent is enabled at 10:02, then the first period will end at 10:12 for this mode (a full interval from the starting time) and the next period will end at 10:22, and so on.

If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to.

Title: IntervalMode option 5
If you choose the final option then you typically need to devise a method of driving the triggerNow slot via a script or expression or this agent can calculate the differential value whenever you choose to. 5 = Manual trigger The rate of change and its alarm limits only applies when using periods that have regular intervals. 4. Configure the required alarm limits and if necessary their deadband If necessary, you can configure the alarm limits and the deadband when required, for this differential value, and the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period. Tip: The deadband slot is used to desensitise these alarm limits and prevent unnecessary alarms if the value is oscillating. In other words, this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area outside these alarm limits, which the value must reduce by before the alarm is cleared. Important: The deadband slot ONLY applies to the alarm limits for the differential value and NOT to the rate of change alarm limits.

The following alarm limits can be defined for the differential value in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog: - The valueHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action.

Title: Limitations
The following alarm limits can be defined for the differential value in the Value alarm levels section of the properties dialog: - The valueHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHighHigh default alarm type. - The valueHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the VHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VHigh default alarm type. - The valueLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLow default alarm type. - The valueLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low value , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the value is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the VLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the VLowLow default alarm type Note: Whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low alarm must, by definition also be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed.

The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits.

Title: Rate of change
The following alarm limits can be defined for the rate of change of this differential value over the specified period in the Rate alarm levels section of the properties dialog: Note: The deadband slot does NOT apply to these rate alarm limits. - The rateHiHi alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHighHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHighHigh default alarm type. - The rateHi alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a high rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate reaches or exceeds this alarm limit, the RHigh status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RHigh default alarm type. - The rateLo alarm limit specifies the first alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should require corrective action as soon as possible. - When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLow default alarm type. - The rateLoLo alarm limit specifies the second alarm limit for a low rate , which if reached, should typically require urgent and immediate corrective action. - When the rate is lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached, the RLowLow status bit is set to [1] (enabled) , which can be alarmed using the RLowLow default alarm type. 5. Configure the SQL Server database to store the values of each period To maintain a history of the differential values for each period you must specify the SQL Server database and table that is used to store these records: - Specify the connection string to this SQL Server database in the connection field by using the Data Link Properties dialog. - For more details, see Creating a SQL Server database connection string . Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . - Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. - Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. - Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. - At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string.

- Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field.

Title: Rate of change
- Specify the required table name in this database to store these records in the tableName field. By default, this table name is set to the name of this Accumulator agent. - When you are using a clustered Agent Server, then the standby clustered partner will, by default, not log these records to this database, thus preventing duplicate records. However, you can change this, if required, by configuring the disableOnStandby slot setting. - Each record specifies a unique index (idx) ; the date and time at which the period ended (dt) ; the differential value (value) and the inputValue - the value of the accumulating process variable (accumulator) at this time. If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table will be created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period If you want automatic management of this data, then specify how many days worth of data you want this table to store in the housekeepDays field, to ensure that you keep the most relevant (most recent) records only. Note: The default value of 0 disables this functionality. 6. Enable the agent To start analysing the accumulating process: - You should enable this agent to start analysing the accumulating process value and calculate its differential value for each period and its rate of change and, if required, also log the values of each period to the specified history table in the SQL Server database. - To enable this agent, set the enable slot of this agent (in the General section of this properties dialog) to True. 7. Values calculated by the agent for each period At the end of every period: - The differential value of the previous period is saved to lastValue . - The differential value of the current completed period is calculated as: inputValue - startValue. - The rate of change of the previous differential value and period is calculated as: lastValue * 60 (minutes per hour) / (last period length in minutes) = value per hour. - A new record is added to the tableName (in the database by connection , if specified) containing the period start and end times, values and differential value and rate for the period. - A new period will commence immediately and the startValue will be assigned to the inputValue .

Tip: You can view the amount of time that has passed (elapsed) from the start of the current period, in minutes, by viewing the elapsedTime slot.

Property Configuration DisplayName changes the name of the column heading in the grid.

Title: Available column properties:
Property Configuration DisplayName changes the name of the column heading in the grid. BestFit determines whether the column auto-sizes (if True) or not, in other words if it changes its width to accommodate the largest entry. Width configures how wide the column is, in pixels, which is 100 by default. FormatString a string of data type specific format specifiers in {} braces that specify how the entries of this column are formatted. The default is column-specific. For details, see the Value formatting syntax. GroupIndex this determines whether this column is automatically used to group the data of the other columns and if so what its relative order is, if more than one column is configured to automatically group data, as follows: -1 the default, which means do not initially group data using this column; 0 = 1st level grouping; 1 = 2nd level grouping; 2 = 3rd level grouping etc. Note: These grouping settings only affect the initial grouping of the data, but users can choose to remove all grouping columns and/or group data using any column. GroupInterval when this column initially groups the data, this allows you to select how the data within this column is used to group the other data. Hence these settings are data specific so the data time settings only apply to date time data etc. SortIndex when multiple columns are initially sorting the data, this defines the order in which these columns are used, as follows: -1, this is the default, which means do not initially use this column to sort the data; 0 = primary sorting column; 1 = secondary sorting column; 2 = tertiary sorting column etc. Note: These sorting settings only affect the initial sorting of the data, but users can choose to remove all sorting and/or sort data using any column. SortOrder when this column initially sorts the data, this defines how the data in the column is sorted, as follows: - None (the default): this does not sort the data - Ascending: from smallest to biggest (a to z). - Descending: from biggest to smallest (z to a) By default the control is sorted in Descending order of the Date Time column, so that the latest alarm is displayed at the top.

SummaryType this allows you to perform a calculation on all the entries in this column and display the result of this calculation in the summary row, which the last row at the bottom of the grid.

Title: Available column properties:
SummaryType this allows you to perform a calculation on all the entries in this column and display the result of this calculation in the summary row, which the last row at the bottom of the grid. The default is column-specific. - Sum: the summary row displays the total of all the values in this column; - Min: the summary row displays the minimum (lowest) value for this column; - Max: the summary row displays the maximum (highest) value for this column; - Count: the summary row displays the number of items in this column - which is the default setting of the DateTime (DT) column - Average : the summary row displays the average value for this column; - None (the default): no summary calculation is performed on this column's entries SummaryDisplayFormat when a column is calculating a summary, this allows you to specify the required format specifier string for the summary value in {} braces and any descriptive text that should also be displayed. For instance the default summary format for the DateTime (DT) column is: {0:n0} rows. For details about formatting the calculated value, see the Value formatting syntax. Fixed determines whether the column is frozen like in Excel so that this column is always visible when scrolling left and right, as follows: - None (the default) - the column takes part in left and right scrolling - Left: the column is anchored to the left edge of the grid and is always visible when scrolling left and right. - Right: the column is anchored to the right edge of the grid and always visible when scrolling left and right. -->

Configuring Agent Server auditing Top Configuring Agent Server Auditing The configuration settings that enable the auditing of the Agent Server and that specify the required OLE DB The open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources. An OLE DB data provider is required, before a database can become OLE DB compliant. compatible database are located in the Server auditing group section of the Advanced Agent Server Configuration dialog. To display the auditing configuration settings: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. To specify the auditing database: to select the OLE DB compatible database that will store the audit records for this Agent Server. By default an MS Access database file is used. - If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). - By default, if the Custom OLE DB connection field is left blank and the Agent Server is started then a MS Access database file, called adroit_audit.MDB, is created in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. Tip1: It is recommended to use this default database, since this is a single file that can easily be backed up elsewhere. Tip2: If necessary, you can secure this Access database and provide the user/password details in the connection string. - Click the browse button to the left of the Custom OLE DB connection field to specify another OLE DB compatible database. For details, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . For instance, you can use a central SQL database for all the Agent Servers on your network, since the identification (Session ID) used for the logged events contain the name of the computer and Agent Server. In this case, if you do not have SQL installed then you can install MS SQL EXPRESS. To stop auditing the Agent Server: this prevents additional records from being added to the auditing database - If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). - Clear the Enable checkbox, which is enabled by default.

Tip: If you want to analyse your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your Agent Server auditing and tag auditing, where Agent Server auditing includes any activities on the Agent Server, while the tag auditing is concerned specifically with data logged by any Audit agents.

By default an MS Access database file is used. - If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). - By default, if the Custom OLE DB connection field is left blank and the Agent Server is started then a MS Access database file, called adroit_audit.MDB, is created in the Work subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. Tip1: It is recommended to use this default database, since this is a single file that can easily be backed up elsewhere. Tip2: If necessary, you can secure this Access database and provide the user/password details in the connection string. - Click the browse button to the left of the Custom OLE DB connection field to specify another OLE DB compatible database. For details, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . For instance, you can use a central SQL database for all the Agent Servers on your network, since the identification (Session ID) used for the logged events contain the name of the computer and Agent Server. In this case, if you do not have SQL installed then you can install MS SQL EXPRESS. To stop auditing the Agent Server: this prevents additional records from being added to the auditing database - If necessary, display the auditing configuration settings (see above). - Clear the Enable checkbox, which is enabled by default.

Tip: If you want to analyse your audited data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Audit Reports report pack, which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse both your Agent Server auditing and tag auditing, where Agent Server auditing includes any activities on the Agent Server, while the tag auditing is concerned specifically with data logged by any Audit agents.

Configuring Analog Agents Top Configuring Analog Agents You can configure an Accumulator agent to calculate the difference in value (or delta) of an ever increasing or accumulating process value between successive events or over a specific time period (interval), as follows: Note: You can also calculate statistics from the value slot every second, for a specific rolling period (specified in minutes).

Title: Configuration
Configuring Analog Agents Top Configuring Analog Agents You can configure an Accumulator agent to calculate the difference in value (or delta) of an ever increasing or accumulating process value between successive events or over a specific time period (interval), as follows: Note: You can also calculate statistics from the value slot every second, for a specific rolling period (specified in minutes). For details, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . If necessary, open the Edit Analog Agent dialog, as follows: - If necessary, add an Analog agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Analog Agent dialog. Note: To reduce the loss of accuracy in scaling caused by IEEE conversion issues, the Analog agent bypasses the scaling calculation, when the scaling is 1:1. To edit or view the current value: to view or change this value manually. - The Engineering field (the value slot) of the Value section, displays the last refreshed value, which is scaled within the specified Engineering Span . - The Raw field (the rawvalue slot) of the Value section, displays the corresponding value that is specified within the Device Span . If you edit either value manually click the Update or OK button to save the changes BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise this value change is lost. Note: This value will ONLY be changed to the specified value if it is NOT being scanned. Tip: Use the value slot to display this value, so the tag would be AnalogAgentName.value. To scale this value: typically specified when using a value contained in a front-end device that needs to be scaled to an engineering or display value. IMPORTANT CHANGE FOR ANALOG AGENTS: Changed the default method of handling what happens when the rawvalue slot goes out of range (either exceeds the rawMax value or is lower than the rawMin value), from now this causes the Analog agent to set the new OutOfRange status bit (which can be alarmed if needed). This is to prevent the entire agent from being marked at as being bad, as happened previously, which causes all the instances of this value to be greyed out (disabled) on the mimics which display them.

Note: If you prefer the legacy method of marking the agent bad (setting the statusAgentBad condition bit) when the rawvalue slot goes out of range, then you need to add the OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad registry setting.

Title: Configuration
Note: If you prefer the legacy method of marking the agent bad (setting the statusAgentBad condition bit) when the rawvalue slot goes out of range, then you need to add the OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad registry setting. - Device Span: use this section to specify the Minimum (the rawmin slot) and Maximum (the rawmax slot) limits of the Raw value (the rawvalue slot) that will be scanned (communicated) from the front end device. Please ensure that the correct span is specified for this value in the device, otherwise the value may be truncated to fit within this value range. Check the Sqrt Extraction checkbox (the sqRoot slot) if you want this agent to apply square root conditioning to the raw value. For instance, this can be used to make flow inputs linear. - Engineering Span: use this section to specify the Minimum (the engmin slot) and Maximum (the engmax slot) limits of the Engineering value (the value slot), which is typically the value that is displayed on mimics and trended etc. These limits correspond to the limits specified in the Device Span section and are used to scale the raw value, received from the device, into an engineering or display value. Note: If you require reverse polarity for ALL Analog agents , so that the Maximum limit of the Engineering Span is LOWER THAN its Minimum limit, then you need to add the AnalogRawComms value to the registry. For details, see AnalogRawComms . If necessary specify the Unit (the unit slot) in which this value is measured. This unit is displayed when this value is trended or charted. Tip: The default scaling values correspond to the settings required for 12 bit A to D water temperature signals from a PLC, so the Maximum values for the Device Span and Engineering Span are 4095 and 100 respectively. To specify the engineering units to use for this value: these units are displayed when this value is trended or charted. Edit the Unit field (the unit slot) in the Engineering Span section of this dialog. To configure alarm limits and/or deadbands for this value: to specify one or more alarm limits and/or their deadbands for the Engineering value (the value slot) of this agent.

The following alarm limits can be defined in the Alarms section of this dialog: - The High-high alarm limit (the hiHi slot) specifies the second alarm limit for a high Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require urgent and immediate corrective action.

Title: Configuration
The following alarm limits can be defined in the Alarms section of this dialog: - The High-high alarm limit (the hiHi slot) specifies the second alarm limit for a high Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require urgent and immediate corrective action. More details: When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit the High-high status bit is set to 1 (enabled), which can be alarmed using the High-high default alarm type. If necessary, you can also specify this alarm limit for the Raw value, by using the rawHiHi slot, that is NOT displayed by this dialog. Note: The High alarms engineering deadband value (the hiDeadBand slot), specified in the Deadbands section, is used to de-sensitise this alarm limit. WARNING! This deadband value does NOT work with alarm time deadbanding (configured by using the Delay setting when alarming this agent). Therefore if you are using alarm time deadbanding then you must SET this deadband value to 0. - The High alarm limit (the hi slot) specifies the first alarm limit for a high Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. More details: When the value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit the High status bit is set to 1 (enabled), which can be alarmed using the High default alarm type. If necessary, you can also specify this alarm limit for the Raw value, by using the rawHi slot, that is NOT displayed by this dialog. - The Low alarm limit (the lo slot) specifies the first alarm limit for a low Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require corrective action as soon as possible. More details: When the value lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached the Low status bit is set to 1 (enabled), which can be alarmed using the Low default alarm type. If necessary, you can also specify this alarm limit for the Raw value, by using the rawLo slot, that is NOT displayed by this dialog. Note: The Low alarms engineering deadband (the loDeadBand slot), specified in the Deadbands section, is used to de-sensitise this alarm limit. WARNING! This deadband value does NOT work with alarm time deadbanding (configured by using the Delay setting when alarming this agent). Therefore if you are using alarm time deadbanding then you must SET this deadband value to 0.

- The Low-low alarm limit (the loLo slot) specifies the second alarm limit for a low Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require urgent and immediate corrective action.

Title: Configuration
- The Low-low alarm limit (the loLo slot) specifies the second alarm limit for a low Engineering value (the value slot), which if reached should require urgent and immediate corrective action. More details: When the value lower or equal to this alarm limit is reached the Low-low status bit is set to 1 (enabled), which can be alarmed using the Low-low default alarm type. If necessary, you can also specify this alarm limit for the Raw value, by using the rawLoLo slot, that is NOT displayed by this dialog. - The Rate of change alarm limit (the roc slot) specifies the maximum difference between any two consecutive Engineering values (the value slot) in one second. More details: When the rate of change of this value reaches or exceeds this alarm limit the Rate-of-change status bit is set to 1 (enabled), which can be alarmed using the Rate-of-change default alarm type. If necessary, you can also specify this alarm limit for the Raw value, by using the rawRoc slot, that is NOT displayed by this dialog. Note: If this field is set to 0 this effectively disables this alarm limit. IMPORTANT: If you want to configure these alarm limits externally, such as from a front-end device, then you need to add the AnalogRawComms value to the registry. For details, see AnalogRawComms Registry Value . The deadbands for the low-low, low, high and high-high alarm limits can be specified in the Deadbands section of this agent as follows: WARNING! These value deadbands do not work with alarm time deadbanding (configured by using the Delay setting when alarming this agent). Therefore if you are using alarm time deadbanding then you must SET these value deadbands to 0. - The High alarms field (the hiDeadBand slot), specifies the engineering value used to de-sensitise the High and High-high alarm limits. In other words this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area below these alarm limits, which the level must reduce by before the alarm becomes inactive (is cleared). This can prevent unnecessary alarms if the level wavers up and down as it is stabilised. - The Low alarms field (the loDeadBand slot), specifies the engineering value used to de-sensitise the Low and Low-low alarm limits.

In other words this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area above these alarm limits, which the level must increase by before the alarm becomes inactive (is cleared).

Title: Configuration
In other words this specifies the ‘band’ (size of) the ‘dead’ area above these alarm limits, which the level must increase by before the alarm becomes inactive (is cleared). This can prevent unnecessary alarms if the level wavers up and down as it is stabilised. Note: Deadbands can be specified to reduce the sensitivity of these alarm limits, so that you do not create unnecessary alarms. WARNING! These value deadbands do not work with alarm time deadbanding (configured by using the Delay setting when alarming this agent). Therefore if you are using alarm time deadbanding then you must SET these value deadbands to 0. For a detailed description of how these alarm limits and their deadbands are used when monitoring a process value, see Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits . To monitor this value for changes : if enabled, any change in value instantaneously sets the Changed specific status bit of this agent and records the previous value. To enable and specify a default (cold-start) value: to specify the default value to use when the Agent Server is started and it does not have a value specified for this agent. If enabled, this value is sent to the front-end device when the Agent Server starts up. - Check the Enable checkbox in the Cold start section. - Specify the required default engineering value in the Value field (the initValue slot). This value is sent to the scanned front-end device for this Analog agent when the Agent Server is first loaded. Tip: The and buttons can display the edit dialogs of the agents above and below this agent in the Agents list of the Configurator dialog. -->

Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. The following settings are contained within the WGP Versioning group: - These files are created when the WGP file is saved for the period of time specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box, where # is the required number of days. The default period is 90 days and any backup WGP file older than this time will be deleted every time the WGP file is saved. Tip: It is recommended to set this value to the period of your existing Adroit backups, so as to avoid backup duplication. Note: A value of 0 will disable this feature and remove all the backup files on the next save. - The minimum number of backup files that will always remain can be specified using the … but keep a minimum of # backup files edit box, where # is the required number of files. This should be used as a failsafe to prevent ALL the previous backups from being deleted if the WGP file is saved after the period specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box has elapsed. The default minimum number of files is 3, which ensures that the folder will always contain the 3 most recent backups. - The total number of backup file that are created can be limited, by specifying the required number in the … and a maximum limit of # files edit box, where # is the required number of files. In this way it is possible to regulate the amount of disk space that is used for these backups. The default number of files is 10, after which the oldest backup file will be deleted each time the WGP file is saved. Note: A value of 0 will remove this limitation, so that a separate backup file will be created each time the WGP file is saved for the specified number of days. For further details, such as the naming format of these automatically created backup copies, see Automatic WGP File Backups . -->

This should be used as a failsafe to prevent ALL the previous backups from being deleted if the WGP file is saved after the period specified by the Delete WGP backup files older than # days edit box has elapsed. The default minimum number of files is 3, which ensures that the folder will always contain the 3 most recent backups. - The total number of backup file that are created can be limited, by specifying the required number in the … and a maximum limit of # files edit box, where # is the required number of files. In this way it is possible to regulate the amount of disk space that is used for these backups. The default number of files is 10, after which the oldest backup file will be deleted each time the WGP file is saved. Note: A value of 0 will remove this limitation, so that a separate backup file will be created each time the WGP file is saved for the specified number of days. For further details, such as the naming format of these automatically created backup copies, see Automatic WGP File Backups . -->

- Select the Runtime Axis Configuration toolbar button from the toolbar of the required charting control to display the Axes Scaling configuration dialog.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Select the Runtime Axis Configuration toolbar button from the toolbar of the required charting control to display the Axes Scaling configuration dialog. - If necessary, Select an Axis to configure from this list box. To customize the scaling of this axis: determine whether to manually or automatically scale this axis and/or invert the scaling and/or hide the scaling and/or to improve the readability of the axis. Click the Axis Scales tab to do one or more of the following: Note: You may need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to display these settings. To automatically configure the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Automatic checkbox is checked, this also checks the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. Tip: It is recommended to use automatic scaling (the default setting) when trending data with the Line or XYPlot chart. To manually configure the scaling of this axis: Tip: This is typically required when you are using Bar or Column charts so that you can see the differences in values between two series. - Ensure that the Automatic checkbox is cleared, this also clears the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. - Manually specify the Minimum and Maximum values, by using the Value spin control to specify the required value. To scale the axis logarithmically: Note: You need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to edit these settings. - Check the Logarithmic checkbox to scale the selected axis logarithmically settings include: Note: The Minimum and Maximum values of this axis should be greater than zero, and the Axis cannot be of type DateTime . - Then specify the required Logarithmic Base for this logarithmic scaling. To invert the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Inverted checkbox is checked (this is an Advanced feature). To hide the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Visible checkbox is cleared. To customize the positioning of this axis: determine the relative position and the actual size of this axis relative to the total dimension of the charting area. Click the Axis Position tab to specify one or more of the following axis positions: Relative Position : the position of this axis, as percentage (0-100%) of the length or width of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the Bottom border and 100 is the Top. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the Left border and 100 is the Right. Start Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the starting position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area. End Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the ending position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area.

To customize the display of the axis and its scaling demarcations or ticks: determine to display the axis, its major demarcations or ticks and their grid lines and to configure the colors of these items.

Title: Configuration
Steps:

Click the Axis Ticks tab to specify the visibility and/or the displayed color of the following axis components: Axis Pen Visible : This checkbox displays/hides this axis. Axis Colour : Configure the required color of this axis. For details, see Using the color edit box to select a color . Ticks Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the major ticks (demarcations) of this axis. Ticks Colour : Configure the required color of these major ticks. Grid Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the grid lines, displayed within the charting area, from each major tick (demarcation) of this axis. Grid Colour : Configure the required color of these grid lines. - Click Close when you have finished configuring the axes. To customize the axis labelling: typically used to specify the required scientific notation and/or rounding for each value or to display the values on the axis at an angle. - Click the Axis Labels tab, then: To hide the labels - uncheck the Visible checkbox. If necessary specify the required Style , although the default of Auto should suffice. To specify the required scientific notation and/or rounding for each value: - Specify the required Values Format . Note: The displayed options depend upon the type of data currently selected for the values of this axis. - If you are unable to locate the required formatting then simply type in the required format string. - Click the Set button. To display values on the axis at an angle: - Specify the required angle, in degrees, for the labels using the Angle spin control. The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element. The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path.

If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. By default this is name of the first series that is added to this charting control. Double-click this name in order to edit it or select the name of an existing series from the list box. - If necessary, change the charting Color of this value. For details, see selecting a color from the color edit box . - If you need to prevent the interpolation between successive data points then check the Steps checkbox, this is particularly useful when charting discreet data such as Boolean or digital values. - If you want to chart this series on a custom left (Y) axis then check the Axes checkbox. Configuration required for a Pie, Bar or Column series: - If necessary, change the Series field to specify the name of an existing pie, bar or column series, as configured in the charting configuration dialog. Double-click this name in order to edit it or select the name of an existing series from the list box. Note: If the specified name differs from the current series then a new pie or set of bars and columns is added for this value. Tip: The default series name is the name of the first series that is added to this charting control. - Specify the Label that describes this new value of the specified series. Double-click this name in order to edit it. - If necessary change the charting Color of this value. For details, see selecting a color from the color edit box . - Select the Finish button once all the values have been configured as required to close the Series Configuration configuration dialog. -->

Title: Configuration
- Either right click the gauge or click the glyph of this control and select the Configuration option This displays the Configuration configuration dialog. - In this dialog, select the Ranges tab and then specify the required number of ranges you need to define in the Number of Ranges field, you can define up to 5 different value ranges (or value groupings) on a gauge . - For each range, select the required number of this range in the Range list box and then, specify the following details: - Start Value : the value at which this range (group of numbers or state) begins. - End Value : the value at which this range (group of numbers or state) ends. Note: If you specify the same Start Value and End Value for two ranges then the second range will overwrite the first. - Offset :this specifies the position of this value color range within the gauge control. More details: Tip: Typically you should NOT configure this field and leave its default value unchanged. With a value of zero being on top of the graduations of the scale. Positive values move this value range outward. Negative values move this value range inward. The default value is 20, which keeps the value range above the scale graduations. Example: The following screenshot shows a gauge with three ranges, with different offsets: the yellow range has an Offset of 0; the green range has an Offset of 20 and the red range has an Offset of -40. - color : Specify the color used on the gauge to indicate this value range (group of numbers or state). For instance, you would typically use red to indicate high or over-limit values and more neutral colors to indicate the values within the normal operating ranges. Tip: To delete a range, select the required row and press the DELETE key. For details on how to add a gauge control, see Adding Gauge controls . -->

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring Command Agents Top Configuring Command Agents The Command agent can receive textual commands in SMS messages that it is able to remotely configure or "command" Adroit . SMS messages can also be sent either manually or automatically and, if necessary, be sent via another Command agent to another recipient, such as a colleague or escalated up the management chain. This agent requires a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver, to be added and correctly configured, in order to send and receive SMS messages. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Each Command agent is able to send SMS messages to a single recipient. For details see, Sending SMS Messages or for details on specifying this required phone number, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . Note: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Sent SMS messages can be monitored for auditing purposes and if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period can also be sent to another recipient via another Command agent, which can be used to escalate this message up the management chain, if necessary. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . Note: Although Command agents can also receive SMS messages from their recipient, one or more additional cell phone numbers can also be specified that are able to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . If a Command agent is required to receive COMMANDS within these received messages, this must be MANUALLY ENABLED. Since once enabled, these commands can be used to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . PLEASE NOTE: Once a Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and/or used to send SMS messages to it. Note: Pseudonyms and macros can also be created to simply the process of specifying these commands by acting as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . If necessary, it is also possible to configure the following Command agent–specific settings: To specify default format used for displaying real numbers in sent messages . To manage the message queue that is maintained by this agent . -->

In the Inputs section: Note1: The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. - DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected.

Title: Configuration
- DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected. - DBLog2 writes data to Table2 and housekeeping is configured: So the specified housekeeping WILL run on Table2, as expected. - DBLog3 and DBLog4 writes data to the same table Table34 - - DBLog3 is configured with no housekeeping AND - DBLog4 is configured with 30 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping WILL run on Table34 as per DBLog4’s housekeeping configuration for this SHARED table. - DBLog5 and DBLog6 writes data to the same table Table56 - - DBLog5 is configured with 30 days housekeeping AND - DBLog6 is configured with 90 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping will run on Table34 as per DBLog5’s housekeeping configuration and the data older than 30 days will be deleted, since the SHORTEST housekeeping period is always used as this is the period that is reached first for this SHARED table. This depends upon the storage capacity you have available for your database and how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. Specify the maximum number of days to keep records for (the INTEGER housekeepDays slot). Note1: A value of 0 disables this housekeeping functionality, provided NO OTHER DBLog agents log to the specified table that have configured housekeeping! Note2: By design, one additional day's worth of data is kept for you. If necessary, when performing housekeeping you can also specify an OPTIONAL Backup folder to backup the old data to, before it is deleted from the table (the VARSTRING housekeepFolder slot). IMPORTANT1: Please ensure that the specified folder exists on the computer where SQL is installed (this is NOT the Agent Server computer when using a remote SQL Server) or housekeeping will not happen! IMPORTANT2: ALSO ensure that the specified folder name does NOT contain SPACES or housekeeping will ALSO not happen! IMPORTANT3: ALSO ensure that the database has the necessary permissions needed to add these files to this specified folder or housekeeping will ALSO NOT HAPPEN! Note1: This path is specified relative to the computer where SQL is installed (this is NOT the Agent Server computer when using a remote SQL Server). Note2: Leaving this field empty disables this backup functionality.

When this backup folder is being used each DBLog agent creates a daily flat cabinet (.CAB) file of the data that is to be deleted (by the SHORTEST Housekeeping setting if multiple DBLog agents log to the same table).

Title: Configuration
When this backup folder is being used each DBLog agent creates a daily flat cabinet (.CAB) file of the data that is to be deleted (by the SHORTEST Housekeeping setting if multiple DBLog agents log to the same table). These files are self-extracting SQL scripts, which you need to manually execute against the required SQL database, in order to import your data. PLEASE NOTE: It is up to you to manage the files stored in this folder yourself. Once the DBLog Agent has been configured and enabled, it creates table /s in the specified database with the following fields: - id : a unique indexing identifier - dt : the Timestamp of the logged value - Tagname : the name of the tag being logged - Value :– the value of the tag being logged - Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad data has a bad status when data is missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated. . This agent ALSO creates the Adr_DBLog_AgentDetails table, which contains all the agents referenced by all DBLog agents to provide more details about these referenced agents, which can be used to provide more context about them for reports.

This table is updated when: the agent is started; or when its tag list is changed; and unconditionally every morning at 01h00 and this table contains the following fields: - ID – integer key: a unique indexing identifier - Owner – varchar(255): the DBLog agent name for future use to remove entries owned by the agent - AgentName – varchar(255): the name of the agent of the tag being logged - AgentDescription - varchar(255): the description of the agent being logged - AgentType – varchar(255): the agent type of the tag being logged - TagName – varchar(255): the tag being logged - TagDescription – varchar(255): a description of the tag being logged; always equal to AgentDescription unless agent type is Marshal whereupon it contains the description of the bit - Units - varchar(255): for Analog agents only - OffText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only - OnText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only - RawMin - float: Raw (device-scale) minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only - RawMax - float: Raw (device-scale) maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only - EngMin - float: Engineering minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only - EngMax - float: Engineering maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only - LoLo - float: Low-low alarm level for Analog agents only - Lo - float: Low alarm level for Analog agents only - Hi - float: High alarm level for Analog agents only - HiHi - float: High-high alarm level for Analog agents only Note: If you do not intend to make use of this table then you can prevent this table from being created by all of your DBLog agents, by adding the following registry value and setting it to 0: DumpAgentDetailsEnabled .

Configuring Device Agents Top Configuring Device Agents A device must first be added for an installed protocol driver before a Device agent of the same name can be added to the Agent Server when an Adroit tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring Device Agents Top Configuring Device Agents A device must first be added for an installed protocol driver before a Device agent of the same name can be added to the Agent Server when an Adroit tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is scanned to it. For further details, see Device Agents . Each Device agent, is responsible for managing and configuring the following: - The Scan agents, which it creates or removes when Adroit tags (agent.slot) are scanned to or unscanned from it. For details, see Scanning Tags . Note1: Adroit automatically optimises the I/O points for the most efficient scanning and traffic loading, executing either block reads or single transactions to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. Note2: It is recommended to stop the Device agent when adding and removing (and importing) more than one scan-point. To Scan a Tag (a Slot of an Agent) . To Scan from Another Agent’s Slot . To Scan more than one Tag to Contiguous Addresses . Bulk Scanning or Importing Scanned Points . To Remove a Scanned Point from a Device . - The ‘device’ created in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility, through which the communication actually occurs to its front-end device. This not only manages the communication (scanning) to and from this front-end device, but also its communication settings, which are specific to the protocol driver to which it has been added. For details, see About Protocol Drivers . Note1: The rates at which the scanning or communication occurs can be defined for the individual I/O ports. Note2: These changes only take effect when the device is first created automatically, or after the Agent Server starts up. PLEASE NOTE: If a front-end device is off-line, un-available or disconnected, then its device should be stopped, since both Adroit and this device will continue to attempt to resume communications to the exclusion of most other functions of the scanning sub-system. Therefore any scanning or unscanning of Adroit tags to or from its Device agent will be impeded. To Stop or Start the Scanning to or from a Device . Stopping and Starting Devices Remotely . To Configure the Protocol Driver Settings of a Device . To View the Details of a Device . -->

Configuring Digital Agents Top Configuring Digital Agents You can configure a Digital agent to provide change and/or value monitoring, value inversion, textual descriptions of its two states and other functionality to a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring Digital Agents Top Configuring Digital Agents You can configure a Digital agent to provide change and/or value monitoring, value inversion, textual descriptions of its two states and other functionality to a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). value, as follows: If necessary, open the Edit Digital Agent dialog, as follows: - If necessary, add an Digital agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Digital Agent dialog. To edit or view or display the current value: to view or change this value manually. - The current state of the value slot is displayed and configured by the list box in the Value section that displays the textual description of the current state (the textValue slot ). - The Raw value field of the Value section displays the current value of the rawValue slot. - To edit the value (the value slot) of this Digital agent, select the required state from the list box in the Value section. Note1: Click the Update or OK button to save the changes BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise this value change is lost. Note2: This value will ONLY be changed to the specified value if it is NOT being scanned. Note: Adroit uses positive logic, so that OFF = 0 and ON = 1. Tip: Use the value slot to display this value, so the tag would be DigitalAgentName.value. To invert the raw value: when you want to use and display the OPPOSITE state that is scanned in from the device. - Check the Value Inverted checkbox (the invert slot) of the Value section. Note: Click the Update or OK button to save the changes BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise this configuration change is lost. This causes the value slot to always be opposite to the Raw value (the rawValue slot), which is typically this is the value that is scanned from the front-end device.. Note: The current state of the value slot is displayed and configured by the list box in the Value section that displays the textual description of the current state (the textValue slot). Therefore if the rawValue slot is 0, the value slot is set to 1, then changing the value slot to 0, sets the rawValue slot is 1. To change the textual description displayed when the value slot is 0: this is usually required if your process uses different terminology, from the default of OFF to refer to this state. - Edit the OFF state field (the state0 slot) in the Text section appropriately. Typical options for this field are: OFF, OUT, 0, DISABLED. Note1: Click the Update or OK button to save the changes BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise this value change is lost. Note2: This will change the value displayed for this state in the list box of the Value section and, if necessary, the value of the textValue slot too. To change the textual description displayed when the value slot is 1: this is usually required if your process uses different terminology, from the default of ON to refer to this state. - Edit the ON state field (the state1 slot) in the Text section appropriately. Typical options for this field are: ON, IN, 1, ENABLED. Note1: Click the Update or OK button to save the changes BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise this value change is lost.

Note2: This will change the value displayed for this state in the list box of the Value section and, if necessary, the value of the textValue slot too.

Title: Configuration
Note2: This will change the value displayed for this state in the list box of the Value section and, if necessary, the value of the textValue slot too. To monitor this value for changes : if enabled, any change in value instantaneously sets the Changed specific status bit of this agent and records the previous value. To enable and specify a default (cold-start) value: to specify the default value to use when the Agent Server is started and it does not have a value specified for this agent. If enabled, this value is sent to the front-end device when the Agent Server starts up. - Check the Enable checkbox in the Cold start section. - Select the required state of this value from the State list box (the initValue slot). This state is sent to the scanned front-end device for this Digital agent when the Agent Server is first loaded. To enable and specify a pulsed output: to specify how long this digital should maintain its ON (1) state and can be used to emulate the action of a push button. - Check the Enabled checkbox in the Pulsed output section. - Specify the required Delay , in milliseconds, that the value slot should remain at 1 for. Note slot, if this value is inverted value applies to the Delay: Since this(the invert slot set to 1) then the effect of the pulsed output is ALSO inverted. In other words the Delay specifies the length of time that the value slot remains at 0 for. Tip: The and buttons can display the edit dialogs of the agents above and below this agent in the Agents list of the Configurator dialog. -->

Configuring EventLogging Agents Top Configuring EventLogging Agents The EventLogging agent manages the logging of events in Adroit and/or can log events to an OLE DB compatible database. This assumes that the Edit EventLogging Agent dialog is open, which can be done, as follows: - Select the default EventLogging agent called eventLog. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit EventLogging Agent dialog. Note: There is only one default instance of this agent per Agent Server, called eventLog . To disable event logging for specific routes: Select the required alarm route number from the Select route number list box. - Check the Disable this route checkbox. To disable event logging from ALL alarm routes: - Check the Disable all routes checkbox in the General Event Logging details section (set the totalDisable slot to 1). To set the default alarm route that events are logged for ALL Alarm agents: - Specify the number of the required alarm route in the Default Routing edit box (the defaultRoute slot) in the General Event Logging details section. For more details about alarm routes, see About Alarm Routes . To configure the MAXIMUM priority level of the EventLogging agent: this will DISCARD any event from an agent or incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). that has priority level LOWER than the configured level. This setting can be used to filter out unnecessary events, by simply not logging them. - Specify the highest Alarm priority (an integer from 0 to 4) in the Discard Level edit box (the discardLevel slot) in the General Event Logging details section. Note: The default setting of 9999 disables this feature. For details of configuring the Alarm priority setting for an agent or an incident, see Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities . To log events to an OLE DB compatible database: this allows you to log events to an OLE DB compatible database preferably on the SAME computer as the Agent Server. This allows you to use the in-built querying functionality of the database to assist you in performing queries on the logged events to analyse them. Note: These logged events cannot be viewed in the Event Log Viewer window - If necessary, check the Enabled checkbox in the Local OLE DB logging section. - Click the browse button to the right of the Custom OLE DB connection edit box, to specify the required OLE DB compatible database. For details on specifying this connection string, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . By default, Adroit deletes events older than 90 days from this database to ensure that the database does not become too large. If necessary, specify the MAXIMUM number of days that you need to keep the logged events for in the Delete records older than edit box. The Destinations section of this dialog displays which physical event log files (one per computer) and which EventOutput agents are allocated to each route. Typically these are configured within the Alarm agent edit dialog. For details, see Global Incident Destinations . -->
