To configure the MAXIMUM priority level of the EventLogging agent: this will DISCARD any event from an agent or incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). that has priority level LOWER than the configured level. This setting can be used to filter out unnecessary events, by simply not logging them. - Specify the highest Alarm priority (an integer from 0 to 4) in the Discard Level edit box (the discardLevel slot) in the General Event Logging details section. Note: The default setting of 9999 disables this feature. For details of configuring the Alarm priority setting for an agent or an incident, see Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities . To log events to an OLE DB compatible database: this allows you to log events to an OLE DB compatible database preferably on the SAME computer as the Agent Server. This allows you to use the in-built querying functionality of the database to assist you in performing queries on the logged events to analyse them. Note: These logged events cannot be viewed in the Event Log Viewer window - If necessary, check the Enabled checkbox in the Local OLE DB logging section. - Click the browse button to the right of the Custom OLE DB connection edit box, to specify the required OLE DB compatible database. For details on specifying this connection string, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . By default, Adroit deletes events older than 90 days from this database to ensure that the database does not become too large. If necessary, specify the MAXIMUM number of days that you need to keep the logged events for in the Delete records older than edit box. The Destinations section of this dialog displays which physical event log files (one per computer) and which EventOutput agents are allocated to each route. Typically these are configured within the Alarm agent edit dialog. For details, see Global Incident Destinations . -->

Configuring Groups and Users Top Configuring Groups and Users The Adroit Security Manager allows you to configure the necessary groups and their users, as follows: Tip .About Adroit Security Groups : Security in Adroit works best with an INCLUSIVE security policy, see Select whether you will use a workgroup or domain: this is the most important consideration when configuring your groups and users.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring Groups and Users Top Configuring Groups and Users The Adroit Security Manager allows you to configure the necessary groups and their users, as follows: Tip .About Adroit Security Groups : Security in Adroit works best with an INCLUSIVE security policy, see Select whether you will use a workgroup or domain: this is the most important consideration when configuring your groups and users. Click for more details: - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - If necessary, click the Workgroup / Domain branch in the left hand tree pane. To configure groups and users on the LOCAL computer: the specified groups and users ONLY apply to the local computer and this configuration MUST be duplicated on ALL the computers that will run Adroit in this Workgroup - Click the Workgroup option. The branch name changes to Workgroup. To configure groups and users on a domain: the specified groups and users apply to ALL the computers on this Domain. - Type in the name of the required domain in the edit box next to the Domain option. - Click the Domain option. This connects to the specified domain and changes this branch name to Domain. Although running outside of a domain is less costly, it is harder to manage groups and user accounts when deploying a distributed Adroit system – especially if there are a large number of users that need to interact with Adroit . If you are using a Workgroup, then the Adroit Security Manager utility can reduce this management overhead by exporting your users and groups, as follows: Once you have created the necessary groups and/or users on one computer, you can export these users and groups ( Tools menu\ Export ) and then import them in the Adroit Security Manager running on another computer ( Tools menu\ Import ) to automatically create the users and/or groups that do not exist on this computer. For more details, see Exporting and Importing Groups and Users . Specify the necessary groups of users: add all the groups of users that you require for securing your Adroit installation. Click for more details: Adroit security works best if you create a hierarchy of user groups, where the users of higher groups are also members of all the lower groups. This is known as an INCLUSIVE security policy. - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - If necessary, click the Workgroup / Domain branch in the left hand tree pane. - Click on the Groups option. To create the default Adroit security groups: this can create the recommended Adroit groups, so that you can create an INCLUSIVE security policy or hierarchy of user groups. This also creates the typical user ‘DefaultOp’, which is automatically added to the lowest Adroit security group ‘Users’. Note: ONLY do this if you have a new Adroit installation and have not created user groups yet. - If necessary, specify a prefix in the Adroit group prefix edit box that is added to these default Adroit user group names. This prefix can help to distinguish your Adroit user groups from any other groups that you have created. For instance: ‘ Adroit _’. Note: If you do not specify a prefix then ALL the configured groups of this computer or domain are displayed. - Click the Create default… button. The following groups and user are added automatically to either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or to the domain (if the branch is Domain ): - The default Adroit groups, in alphabetical order: Admins; Engineers: Managers; Operators; Supervisors and Users.

- The user called 'DefaultOp' is made an automatic member of the ‘Users’ group; this user is typically used as an auto logon user.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- The user called 'DefaultOp' is made an automatic member of the ‘Users’ group; this user is typically used as an auto logon user. To create a user group: typically used to add another user group to your existing Adroit security groups. - Click the Add button. - Specify the name of the required group in the displayed dialog. Note: If you have specified an Adroit group prefix then this is added to the group name that you specify. - Click the OK button. This group is added to either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or to the domain (if the branch is Domain ). To remove a user group: typically used to remove a user group that is no longer required for your Adroit security. - Select the name of the group that is no longer required in the Groups list. - Click the Delete button. - Click the OK button. - Click the Yes button of the confirmation dialog. This specified group is removed from either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or to the domain (if the branch is Domain ). Note: Any users that are members of this group ONLY have their MEMBERSHIP to this group REMOVED, this does NOT DELETE the USERS themselves. Specify and/or configure the necessary users and/or add them to groups: add all the users that you require for securing your Adroit installation and if necessary assign them to the necessary groups and/or manage their user account settings. Click for more details: If you are creating the recommended INCLUSIVE security policy, then you need to add the users of the higher groups to all the lower groups as well. - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - If necessary, click the Workgroup / Domain branch in the left hand tree pane. - Click on the Users option. The right hand pane provides upper and lower pairs of lists, as follows: - The upper pair of lists allows you to configure the account setting properties of each user, to create and delete Adroit _Users and to move users between the All users and Adroit _Users lists. Note1: ALL the users listed in the Adroit _Users list are automatically added to the Adroit Users group. Note2: ONLY the users listed in the Adroit _Users list can be added or removed from the Adroit groups that are specified in the lower pair of lists. - The lower pair of lists specifies and configures the groups that the currently selected user in the Adroit _Users list is a member of. Example: if you have a new Adroit installation and you created the default security groups, then you will have one Adroit _Users user called DefaultOp, which is a member of the Users group. When this user is selected the Users group is displayed in the Current memberships list. To move existing users to the Adroit _Users list: instead of adding new users you can also add existing users to the Adroit _Users list. - Select the required user in the All users list. - Click the button above this list. The selected user is added to the Adroit _Users list. Note: This user is also automatically added to the Adroit Users group of either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ). To add a new Adroit user: typically everyone who uses Adroit should have their own user account. - Click the Add button. - Specify the name of this user in the displayed dialog. - Click the OK button.

This user is immediately added to the Adroit Users group of either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
This user is immediately added to the Adroit Users group of either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ). IMPORTANT: Adding an Adroit user does NOT set its password, so unless you specify a password this user is unable to log on. To configure the password for this user: if the Adroit Security Manager utility adds an Adroit user, then you need to set its password so that it is able to log on to either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ). - Select the required user in either the All users or Adroit _Users list. - Click the User Account Settings button. Tip: You can also double click the required user. The User details dialog is displayed. - Click the Set password … button. - Specify the required password twice and click the OK button. Note: You can also use this dialog to manage the user account settings for this user, see below for more details. To add an Adroit user to a Adroit group: once you have added a user to the Adroit _Users list, you can add this user to any of the Adroit groups that are listed in the Available memberships list. - Select the required user in the Adroit _Users list. The Available memberships list lists all the Adroit groups of either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ) that this user is NOT yet a member of. - Select the required Adroit group that this user should join in the Available memberships list. - Click the button above this list. This group is added to the list of Adroit groups that this user is currently a member of, which is listed in the Current memberships list. To remove an Adroit user from a Adroit group: if necessary you can remove user in the Adroit _Users list from any of the Adroit groups that this user is currently a member of, which are listed in the Current memberships list. - Select the required user in the Adroit _Users list. The Current memberships list lists all the Adroit groups of either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ) that this user IS a member of. - Select the required Adroit group that this user should join in the Current memberships list. - Click the button above this list. This group is added to the list of Adroit groups that this user is NOT currently a member of, which is listed in the Available memberships list. To manage the user account settings of a user: this allows you to configure such settings as setting the password for this user and/or changing the password settings and/or disabling the user account itself. - Select the required user in either the All users or Adroit _Users list. - Click the User Account Settings button. Tip: You can also double click the required user. The User details dialog is displayed. - If necessary, modify the Full Name and/or Description fields to better identify and/or describe the purpose or function of this user. - If necessary, enable (check) the following password-related settings: User must change password at next logon : User cannot change password: This setting is recommended for the users of all the user groups except Administrators. Password never expires: If you are going to use the auto logon feature, this setting is recommended for this user account. In a multi-user environment this setting poses a security risk.

ONLY check the Account disabled setting if you want to temporarily prevent this user from logging onto the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or to the domain (if the branch is Domain ).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
ONLY check the Account disabled setting if you want to temporarily prevent this user from logging onto the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or to the domain (if the branch is Domain ). To configure the password for this user: if the Adroit Security Manager utility adds an Adroit user, then you need to set its password so that it is able to log on to either the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ). - Click the Set password … button. - Specify the required password twice and click the OK button. To remove an Adroit user: this ONLY removes the currently selected user from the Adroit _Users list and is UNABLE to remove users from the All users list. - Click the Delete button. - Click the OK button. - Click the Yes button of the confirmation dialog. This removes the currently selected user from the Adroit _Users list. This user is either removed from the local computer (if the branch is Workgroup ) or the domain (if the branch is Domain ). To move users from the Adroit _Users list: instead of deleting users from the Adroit _Users list, you can simply move them to the All users list, where they are available for use if needed. - Select the required user in the Adroit _Users list. - Click the button above this list. The selected user is added to the All users list. Tip: In this case, it may be useful to disable these user accounts until they are needed, see managing user accounts below for more details. Exporting and Importing Groups and Users : how to use the Adroit Security Manager to export and import configured users and groups. -->

Configuring Historical Alarm mode Top Configuring Historical Alarm mode Historical alarm mode allows an UNLICENSED AlarmManagement agent to log your historical alarms, instead of providing the fully fledged AlarmManagement system to be used for one hour.

Title: Configuration
Configuring Historical Alarm mode Top Configuring Historical Alarm mode Historical alarm mode allows an UNLICENSED AlarmManagement agent to log your historical alarms, instead of providing the fully fledged AlarmManagement system to be used for one hour. - If necessary, add an AlarmManagement agent. Note1: Please ensure that this agent name is no more than 27 characters long. Note2: You can only add ONE AlarmManagement agent. - Edit all the Alarm agents that are required to send their alarms/events to this AlarmManagement agent, by adding the AlarmManagment agent to their required routes as an output agent, as follows: In the Routes dialog, of each of these Alarm agents, select the required route number and add this AlarmManagement agent to the Output agent list. Do this for each of the required routes. - Edit the AlarmManagement agent to display the Edit AlarmManagement Agent dialog. - Specify the location to the SQL database in the Connection field. Note: If you need to configure the Alarm Management agent from remote computers, it is safer to use SQL authentication ( Use a specific user name and password ) when creating this connection and NOT Windows authentication ( Use Windows NT Integrated Security ) unless you are sure that the logged on users at the remote computers have the necessary access rights to this SQL database. More details: If the SQL connection string configured in the Alarm Management agent has been configured using Windows authentication and you then try and connect from a remote UI to configure, it will more than likely not work (in other words the configured incidents will not appear). This would happen if the Windows User on this remote computer has not been given access rights to the SQL database. Use an existing (or create) a SQL database for your alarm management. Note1: If you do not have SQL installed then install at least SQL Server 2008 R2 or its Express version. Note2: If multiple AlarmManagement agents (possibly from different Agent Servers) connect to the SAME database, then ensure that each agent is UNIQUELY named since incidents are logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent. Click the ... browse button to the right of this field and use the Data Link Properties dialog to create the required connection string to your SQL Server database. Provider TAB The Data Link Properties dialog specifies the location and the security credentials required to connect to this database. Double-click the Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server item in the Provider tab of the Data Link Properties dialog. Important: If the computer, on which SQL Server was installed, was renamed, then SQL Server may need to be re-installed. If the computer was renamed after installing SQL Server, then SQL Server must be re-installed, to function correctly. Run the following check: - Execute the following T-SQL (Transact-SQL) script in SQL Server Management Studio: SELECT @@SERVERNAME - If the resulting server name is different to the actual name of the computer, then the name of the computer has been changed after SQL Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. Note: If you need to configure or view this database and its data from remote computers, then you should use a UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN).

UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name path and not a local file path this path, as opposed to a UNC path, can ONLY be accessed from the computer that it refers to, this path adopts the following general format: <driveletter>:\directories\filename.

Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls The available method used to update the grid of the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control with recent alarms depends upon how the Alarm Management database (specifically the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table) has been connected to the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control, as follows: Typically, the DataSource tab Initial Configuration and/or General Configuration Settings and/or Configure DataSource Connection configuration dialogs, connect the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control via an OLE DB datasource, as follows: In the DataSource tab of the Initial Configuration dialog, the Server should already specify your current Smart UI Server, if necessary select the required one; if you already have an OLEDB Datasource for your AlarmManagement agent SQL Server database, select the name of this datasource from the list box or click the New button to create this OLEDB datasource.

Title: Configuration
Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls The available method used to update the grid of the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control with recent alarms depends upon how the Alarm Management database (specifically the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table) has been connected to the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control, as follows: Typically, the DataSource tab Initial Configuration and/or General Configuration Settings and/or Configure DataSource Connection configuration dialogs, connect the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control via an OLE DB datasource, as follows: In the DataSource tab of the Initial Configuration dialog, the Server should already specify your current Smart UI Server, if necessary select the required one; if you already have an OLEDB Datasource for your AlarmManagement agent SQL Server database, select the name of this datasource from the list box or click the New button to create this OLEDB datasource. For details, see Creating a new OLEDB datasource . Tip: The advantage of this method is that you do not have to explicitly create the OLEDB datasource first, you can do this during the configuration process. In this case, you can use the Historical Data Update Settings section of the DataSource tab of the relevant configuration dialog and/or the Refresh Mode list box provided by the tasks menu to select the following methods for this control to refresh the grid with more recent alarms: - Manual Refresh Mode (the default) in this case the user needs to manually click the Manual Refresh tool at runtime to update the grid with more recent alarms. - Auto Refresh Mode, specify the required Auto Refresh Interval in Minutes, to update the grid by refreshing the grid with new data at this specified interval, however users can still click the Manual Refresh tool. However, you can also manually drag the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table from the OLEDB datasource (that connects to your Adroit Alarm Management SQL database) onto the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control, and then select To Control Property... > AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control > DataSource . Then click Finish in the displayed Filter DataSet configuration dialog. Note: This method requires you to explicitly create the OLEDB datasource that connects to your Adroit Alarm Management SQL database and DISABLES the Server and OLEDB Datasource fields in the DataSource tab of the relevant configuration dialogs. In this case, subscription updates are used by this control to refresh the grid with new data.

metadata.title: Configuring how to update AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer controls

text:
The advantage of subscription updates is that as an alarm is added to the Historical Incidents table it is immediately displayed by this control.

Title: Configuration
The advantage of subscription updates is that as an alarm is added to the Historical Incidents table it is immediately displayed by this control. However, the PROBLEM with subscription updates is that if you are busy configuring this control to search or filter it and a new alarm is added to the grid then the entire contents of this control will automatically refresh itself, which will LOSE ANY CONFIGURATION made since the last save in design time and at runtime it will ALWAYS cause this configuration to be lost! For this reason the initial setting is set to Ignore , which ignores all subscription updates. In this case, you can use the Historical Data Update Settings section of the DataSource tab of the relevant configuration dialog and/or the Subscription Update Mode list box provided by the tasks menu to select the other subscription updating methods: - When set to Prompt , then the control displays a confirmation dialog, to allow you to choose if you want to receive the update or not - this is useful when configuring the control, if you choose No then you can continue configuring and if Yes then it will update the entire control with the latest data. - When set to Auto , then whenever a historical alarm is added to the table then it will be added to this control, refreshing the entire contents of the grid in the process. Therefore, this setting should only be enabled is your operators will not be creating filters and searching and it is imperative that it displays the latest alarms as soon as they are added to the Historical Incidents table. -->

Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities Top Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance so that you can filter your incidents, based on their priority.

Title: Configuration
Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities Top Configuring Incident (Alarm) Priorities One way to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms is to prioritise your alarms into categories of importance so that you can filter your incidents, based on their priority. There are two ways to prioritise your incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). : - Per Agent: Use this method if ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent have the SAME priority. Alternatively, use this method to specify the LOWEST priority for the incidents (alarm types) of this agent and then use the other per-incident method to specify the incidents that differ. Five levels of importance are supported from 0 the lowest up to 4 the highest. To configure an agent-specific priority: - Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator dialog. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Click the Header button. - Specify the required priority level for ALL the incidents (alarm types) of this agent, in the Alarm priority edit box in the lower right corner of the Agent Header dialog, as follows: 0 : lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 2 (normal). The Alarm agent will discard any alarms that are triggered if its own priority filter is greater than that of the alarmed agent it is monitoring. - Per Incident: Use this method if SOME incidents of an agent have DIFFERENT priorities. For instance the High alarm limit of an Analog agent will have a lower priority than the HighHigh alarm limit. Note: The agent priority setting is the default priority used when configuring an incident for the first time, thereafter the incident priority setting is always used. To configure an incident-specific priority: - Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. - Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. - Click the button of the Priority list box, in the lower right corner of the dialog. - Select the required level of priority for this incident, as follows: 0 : lowest 1: low 2: normal 3: high 4: highest The default is 3 (high). For further details about filtering incidents based on their priority level, see About Filtering Prioritised Incidents . -->

Configuring levels and layers Top Configuring levels and layers Levels and layers are configured in the Levels and Layers tool window for the current graphic form displayed in the Design workspace .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring levels and layers Top Configuring levels and layers Levels and layers are configured in the Levels and Layers tool window for the current graphic form displayed in the Design workspace . For more details on why you would configure a level or layer for a graphic form and how they work, see Working with levels and layers . The Levels and layers tool window consists of a grid, where the columns represent the levels and the rows represent the layers, which support the following tasks in order of importance: Click for more information about each task: - Adding levels : each level can be selected by the end-user of this graphic form to display the associated layers and their visible form components. Note: At runtime, the user can select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. any configured level of a graphic form, so ensure that each level has a unique configuration of layers associated with it. Tip: Ensure that the first level in the grid contains the graphic form components that need to be viewed by default, since this is the default view of the graphic form. - Adding layers : each layer should contain a sub-set of visible form components are need to be selectively hidden or displayed on this graphic form. Note1: After adding a layer you need to associate it with at least one level. Note2: Layers that have not been associated with levels are indicated by cells in the grid, which have the default background color. Tip: If necessary, after you have added a form component to a layer, you can move it to another layer, by right clicking it and selecting its Move to layer item (provided that this graphic form provides two or more layers). - Associate layers with levels : so that their visible form components are displayed on the graphic form, when the required level is selected. Tip1: A single layer can be added to any number of levels. Tip2: To quickly determine which layers have been added to each level, each layer or row is assigned its own unique color in this grid when layers are associated with levels. - Identifying edited layers : form components are added to the currently edited layer, in the Levels and Layers tool window. - Identifying visible levels : identify a level as the visible level, in the Levels and layers tool window, to display the form components associated with its layers in the graphic form. Tip: When editing a graphic form, it is recommended to add and identify a level containing ALL the controls that will appear at the same time, so that they can be arranged. - Renaming layers : to assist the designers in identifying the controls it contains, since the end-user does not see the layer names. - Removing layers : to remove BOTH the layer and its added controls. WARNING! ALL the form components attached to this layer are also removed and cannot be recovered. Therefore save the graphic form before removing any layers. For details, see Saving graphic forms . - Renaming levels : to assist the end-user to identify the contents of this level when its graphic form is displayed at runtime. - Removing levels : remove levels that are no longer needed or which are associated with the SAME layers as another level. - Hiding or showing configured levels : for instance to hide the levels, if the Levels and Layers tool window is very narrow. Note: This has no effect upon the display of levels within the graphic form itself. -->

In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit MaxDemand Agent dialog: To enable this agent during periods of high electricity consumption: since your electricity provider only calculates maximum demand during high consumption periods, this agent should only be enabled at these times. This agent can be selectively enabled as follows: - Check the Enable OR use tag checkbox (the enable slot) to browse in a Boolean or Real tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). that turns this agent on during maximum demand periods. For example, you could create a Scheduler agent to define these high consumption periods. This is the recommended approach, since the Scheduler agent is designed to specify time periods that take weekends and holidays and other non-essential times into account OR - leave the Enable OR use tag checkbox unchecked, do NOT browse in a tag and use Script or Expression agent to drive the Boolean enable slot OR - leave the Enable OR use tag checkbox unchecked, do NOT browse in a tag and scan the Boolean enable slot of this agent to a PLC that has knowledge of the maximum demand periods. WARNING! A scanning overrun this occurs when the scan task takes longer than the required scan rate due to an overloaded or defective scanning subsystem. will affect the accuracy of the periods in which this agent is enabled. Since this would cause the enabling pulse to arrive late, so that the measuring block period will be out by a couple of seconds or more. To synchronise the block periods with your electricity provider: it is important to ensure that the block periods are synchronised with the SAME duration as those used by your electrical provider to ensure that the predicted and actual maximum demands calculations are the same. Use ONE of the following methods to ensure this: - Time-based block periods: The block period duration is specified and each block period is synchronised with the local system time of the computer. In this case: - specify the required block period, in minutes, in the Block period (mins) edit box (the blockPeriod slot) and - CLEAR the Enable block pulses checkbox (the blockPulseEnable slot). Note: If this method is used, it is essential that the system time of the computer reflects the actual time; otherwise, the predicted values may not be the same as those calculated by your electricity provider. - Pulse-based block periods: Your electricity provider sends a pulse (signal) to you to synchronise the start of each block period. In this case: - specify the Block period (mins) edit box, - check the Enable block pulses checkbox, and - ensure that the BOOLEAN blockPulse slot of this agent is scanned to this external pulse, preferably at 1 second to maintain accuracy. WARNING! Any scanning overruns will affect the accuracy of the predicted and actual maximum demands calculations due to timing differences between the Agent Server and your electricity provider. Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
So you can alarm the ‘ blockPeriod value (the Block period (mins) status bit is set when the timing of these external block pulses are compromised, in other words as soon as a pulse does not occur at the period specified by the PulseError . Use the ' PulseError ’ alarm type for this agent to warn you when this occurs. To specify the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent: if this limit is exceeded an alarm can be generated. Use the Max demand limit edit box (the mdLimit slot). Tip: If may be useful to specify a value slightly LESS THAN the actual maximum demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, so that there is time for counteractive measures to be taken when this is exceeded. To set the MaxDemand status bit when the limit is exceeded: this will set the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. By alarming the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, you can be warned when this occurs. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot). To reset the monthly maximum demand calculation: since this agent stores the largest maximum demand calculated over any block period for the current billing period (month), you need to specify when this billing period ends to reset this value. Both the day of month and time of day can be specified, as follows: - Day of month (0 denotes the last day of month) (the resetDay slot): This edit box specifies the required day at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 0 (the last day of the month). - Time of day (the resetTime slot): This spin control specifies the time (hours:minutes:seconds) of the specified day (in 24 hour format) at which the at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 12 am (midnight). Note: The BOOLEAN resetNow slot, if set to one, resets all the calculated values to zero. To specify the instantaneous kVA (apparent power) input: this is required to calculate maximum demand for the current block period and for the current monthly billing period. Specify this input as follows: - Either scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage and leave the kVA edit box empty. - Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kVA edit box (the kVATag slot) that specifies the total instantaneous kVA usage. Tip: Use the browse button to the right of the kVA edit box to locate this tag. For details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Built-in Agent Explorer . To specify the instantaneous kW (real power) input: this is required if you also want this agent to calculate the instantaneous reactive power and/or power factor. Specify this input as follows: - Either scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage - Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kW edit box (the kWTag slot) that specifies this value. If necessary, you can also display your instantaneous kVAr (reactive power) input (the kVAr slot) for information purposes only. Current Block Period Information: this describes the information provided by the MaxDemand agent for the current block period. Last pulse time (the blockPulseTime slot): This value depends upon the method used to determine the block period, as follows: - Time-based block periods: The time at which this block period was synchronised with the local system time of the compute. - Pulse-based block periods: The time at which the scanned pulse started the current block period.

Tip: Alarm the error alarm type for this agent to warn you when the timing of these external block pulses is compromised.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Tip: Alarm the error alarm type for this agent to warn you when the timing of these external block pulses is compromised. Time left (mins) (the blockTimeLeft slot): The available time-in-hand (in minutes) to the end of this block period. In other words, this specifies the available time in which the maximum demand for this block period can still be controlled. Current demand (the demand slot): The actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot): This estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the Current demand (the demand slot) against the remaining time for this block period. Note: If this value exceeds the specified Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) then the MaxDemand status bit is set if the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) is enabled. Then alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent to warn you when this occurs. Tip: It is possible to use the MaxDemand status bit in a Script agent to control the maximum demand by using it to turn off non-essential equipment. Predicted over/under (the mdOverUnder slot): This displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Time to max demand (mins) (the timeToMD slot): This indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot): The recommended kVA consumption to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Spare KVA (the kVASpare slot): The spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Current demand (the demand slot) and the Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot). This either specifies a negative amount of kVA that needs to be shed (removed) or a positive amount of kVA that can be added to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. MaxDemand Agent Calculations: the MaxDemand agent only performs these calculations when correctly licensed and provided with the necessary inputs. Note: This agent needs a separate OEM a component in Adroit that requires a SEPARATE license BEFORE it can be used, which is added to the Agent Server license by means of an appropriate textual description of this component. license before performing background calculations. Tip: To determine if this agent is correctly licensed, ensure that its Unlicensed status bit is NOT set. kVAr* (the kVArCalc slot): This calculates the instantaneous kVAr (reactive power) value, which requires both the mandatory kVA input (the kVA slot) and optional kW input (the kW slot). PF (the pf slot): This calculates the instantaneous power factor, which requires both the mandatory kVA input and optional kW input. For details on how this can save you money, see About Power Factor . TotalKWh (the kVAhTotal slot): This calculates the total real power in KWh (kilowatt-hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month . TotalKVArh (the kVArhTotal slot): This calculates the total reactive power in KVArh (Kilo Volt Amps Reactive Hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month, either from the calculated kVAr* value or the optional kVAr input. Current month MD (the mdActual or value slot): This is the highest recorded maximum demand for any block period of the current month.

Note: When the monthly values are reset this becomes the Last month MD value.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Note: When the monthly values are reset this becomes the Last month MD value. Last month MD (the mdPrev slot): This specifies the previous month’s actual maximum demand for comparison purposes only. This also provides the following additional slots: kVAOptimal , mdOverUnder and timeToMD . See MaxDemand Agent - Slot Details . Related Links: Maximum Demand Quick Start : To explain how to use this agent to monitor your maximum demand. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. -->

Since this would cause the enabling pulse to arrive late, so that the measuring block period will be out by a couple of seconds or more. To synchronise the block periods with your electricity provider: it is important to ensure that the block periods are synchronised with the SAME duration as those used by your electrical provider to ensure that the predicted and actual maximum demands calculations are the same. Use ONE of the following methods to ensure this: - Time-based block periods: The block period duration is specified and each block period is synchronised with the local system time of the computer. In this case: - specify the required block period, in minutes, in the Block period (mins) edit box (the blockPeriod slot) and - CLEAR the Enable block pulses checkbox (the blockPulseEnable slot). Note: If this method is used, it is essential that the system time of the computer reflects the actual time; otherwise, the predicted values may not be the same as those calculated by your electricity provider. - Pulse-based block periods: Your electricity provider sends a pulse (signal) to you to synchronise the start of each block period. In this case: - specify the Block period (mins) edit box, - check the Enable block pulses checkbox, and - ensure that the BOOLEAN blockPulse slot of this agent is scanned to this external pulse, preferably at 1 second to maintain accuracy. WARNING! Any scanning overruns will affect the accuracy of the predicted and actual maximum demands calculations due to timing differences between the Agent Server and your electricity provider. Use the Max demand limit edit box (the mdLimit slot). By alarming the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, you can be warned when this occurs. Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot). To reset the monthly maximum demand calculation: since this agent stores the largest maximum demand calculated over any block period for the current billing period (month), you need to specify when this billing period ends to reset this value. Both the day of month and time of day can be specified, as follows: - Day of month (0 denotes the last day of month) (the resetDay slot): This edit box specifies the required day at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 0 (the last day of the month). - Time of day (the resetTime slot): This spin control specifies the time (hours:minutes:seconds) of the specified day (in 24 hour format) at which the at which the monthly values are reset, the default is 12 am (midnight). Specify this input as follows: - Either scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage and leave the kVA edit box empty. - Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kVA edit box (the kVATag slot) that specifies the total instantaneous kVA usage. Tip: Use the browse button to the right of the kVA edit box to locate this tag. For details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Built-in Agent Explorer . To specify the instantaneous kW (real power) input: this is required if you also want this agent to calculate the instantaneous reactive power and/or power factor. Specify this input as follows: - Either scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage - Or specify a REAL tag (agent.slot) value in the kW edit box (the kWTag slot) that specifies this value. If necessary, you can also display your instantaneous kVAr (reactive power) input (the kVAr slot) for information purposes only. Current Block Period Information: this describes the information provided by the MaxDemand agent for the current block period. Last pulse time (the blockPulseTime slot): This value depends upon the method used to determine the block period, as follows: - Time-based block periods: The time at which this block period was synchronised with the local system time of the compute. - Pulse-based block periods: The time at which the scanned pulse started the current block period.

Time left (mins) (the blockTimeLeft slot): The available time-in-hand (in minutes) to the end of this block period. In other words, this specifies the available time in which the maximum demand for this block period can still be controlled. Current demand (the demand slot): The actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot): This estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the Current demand (the demand slot) against the remaining time for this block period. Note: If this value exceeds the specified Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) then the MaxDemand status bit is set if the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) is enabled. Then alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent to warn you when this occurs. Tip: It is possible to use the MaxDemand status bit in a Script agent to control the maximum demand by using it to turn off non-essential equipment. Predicted over/under (the mdOverUnder slot): This displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Time to max demand (mins) (the timeToMD slot): This indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot): The recommended kVA consumption to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Spare KVA (the kVASpare slot): The spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Current demand (the demand slot) and the Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot). PF (the pf slot): This calculates the instantaneous power factor, which requires both the mandatory kVA input and optional kW input. For details on how this can save you money, see About Power Factor . TotalKWh (the kVAhTotal slot): This calculates the total real power in KWh (kilowatt-hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month . TotalKVArh (the kVArhTotal slot): This calculates the total reactive power in KVArh (Kilo Volt Amps Reactive Hours) consumed for the maximum demand periods of the current month, either from the calculated kVAr* value or the optional kVAr input. Configuring Monitored Tags Top Configuring Monitored Tags The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so.

Title: Configuration
Configuring Monitored Tags Top Configuring Monitored Tags The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . The Tags tabbed page is displayed by default, when this utility is launched. This page contains and manages the list of tags (agent.slot), whose values are monitored by this utility. Interaction with this page is dependent upon whether the status of the tag monitoring process, as follows: Note1: The list of tags configured by this page is saved, when the utility is saved. For details, see Saving the Tag Monitor Utility . Note2: The status bar also displays the current operational status. For details, see Current Operational Status . When the tag monitoring process is started i.e. the Start button is clicked and is currently greyed out. The right-click menu is disabled and this tag list cannot be modified, instead the current values of these tags are displayed. This list, consists of the following columns: - Tag: The name of the tag (agent.slot), whose value is being monitored. - Value: The current value of this tag. - Time: The time at which the value of this tag last changed. When the tag monitoring process is stopped i.e. the Stop button is clicked and is currently greyed out. The right-click menu is enabled, so that the list of tags (agent.slot) displayed by this page can be edited, as follows: - Add to graph: Add a selected tag to the Graph tab, this will allow the value of this tag to be trended against time. Note: If more than one tag is selected, all selected tags are added to the Graph tab on the graph and legend. - Copy: This will copy the selected tag (agent.slot) to the clipboard, so that it can be pasted into this utility etc. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the tag and pressing F2 . - Paste: This will paste (add) a tag (agent.slot) to the end of the current list from the clipboard. Tip: This can also be performed by pressing F3 . - Add: This will display the Add a tag dialog, so that the name of the required tag, from the currently connected Agent Server can be typed in.

This tag will be added to the end of the current list.

Title: Configuration
This tag will be added to the end of the current list. Tip: This can also be performed by pressing F5 . - Edit: This will display the Edit a tag dialog, so that the name of the selected tag can be modified. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the tag and pressing F6 . - Insert: This is identical to the Add command except that the Insert a tag dialog is displayed and the tag is inserted to the list into the currently selected row, instead of being added to the end of the list. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the required row and pressing the Insert key. - Delete: This removes the currently selected tag(s) from the list. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the required tag(s) and pressing the Delete key. - Move up: This will move the currently selected tag up in the list. Note: This operation will not work if more than one tag is selected. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the required tag and pressing F7 . - Move down: This will move the currently selected tag down in the list. Note: This operation will not work if more than one tag is selected. Tip: This can also be performed by selecting the required tag and pressing F8 . -->

Configuring Multiple Log Sets in Adroit Top Configuring Multiple Log Sets Create a SEPARATE log set for ALL the different log settings required for the SAME tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName).

Title: Configuration
Configuring Multiple Log Sets in Adroit Top Configuring Multiple Log Sets Create a SEPARATE log set for ALL the different log settings required for the SAME tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . Therefore you need to configure ALL of the following settings for EACH log set: - Each log set must specify the following items: - Destination: the location of the logs of this value as determined by the method you are log this value with i.e. proprietary Adroit log files: specify the full path and file name of the required log (.LGD) file or OLE DB-compliant database: specify the connection string to the required database. - Log Period: the required length or time period for logging this value e.g. 48 hours - Log Interval: the time deadband for this logged value e.g. 1 second - Compression method: the method used to determine the logged value, if using a log Interval i.e. actual, minimum, maximum or average. - Value deadband: specify the MINIMUM amount which the value must EXCEED in order for it to be logged e.g. 0 - The Clear data at start option. - The Interpolate option. - The Double entries option. - The following items are global settings (for all sets of a DataLog agent): - Start/Stop - Logging mode i.e. continuous/demand/both - Demand trigger tag - Log now - The Datalog agent includes the following three read only set-specific slots: Slot Type Description CfgSet INTEGER This slot is for the sole use of the data log dialog to select the current set being configured. ClientSet INTEGER This slot is updated by the datalog agent to contain the set number from which the data was retrieved after a client data retrieval request. Sets INTEGER The total number of configured log sets. It is possible to view the ClientSet slot on a picture and verify that the trend retrieved its data from the correct set as illustrated in the above example. Each time the trend is positioned to each of the three history positions, the ClientSet slot should display the log set that was used for the last retrieve operation. -->

Title: Configuration
Configuring Node names and descriptors Top Configuring Node names and descriptors When you Add / Edit a node, you can specify the Node name , which is the literal description used when navigating the defined hierarchy and Node descriptor which is typically a 3 character code to reference the specific contextual area that is represented by this node. Note: The specified descriptor is always CAPITALISED. The Descriptor path specifies all the defined Node descriptors up to the current level and only adds the descriptor of this new node once you define it. This is typically used when creating object instances, whose names and substitution/s use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created. For details, see Creating contextually sensitive object instances . Note: You are unable to specify any character that is not allowed for agent names. Tip: Any parent or grand parent node that you have not defined a descriptor for will NOT appear in the specified Descriptor path . By default these node descriptors are not separated using the '_' character, however you can click the Configure view in the bottom tool bar of this window and uncheck the Use separators checkbox to remove this separator character or specify the required separator character in the Separator edit box. -->

Configuring projects Top Configuring projects Projects are configured within the Projects category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager , by adding, copying or importing graphic forms and organizing these within a hierarchy of folders.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring projects Top Configuring projects Projects are configured within the Projects category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager , by adding, copying or importing graphic forms and organizing these within a hierarchy of folders. For details, see Working with projects . Note: Projects are saved in separate folders, with the exact structure of the project being maintained, to easily locate your graphic forms, so that they can be backed up, copied and/or moved. For details, see Locating saved projects . The following project-specific commands are provided: Note: These commands can only be performed if the currently logged on user has the necessary security permissions. For details, see Securing projects . - Open a project : to expose its configured graphic forms and folders. Add one or more of the following components to your project: Tip: You could also copy an entire project or folder from another project using Copy sub-items and paste it into this project, although any items that are named the same as the copied items will be overwritten. - Create a graphic form : to add a new graphic form to a project. - Create a wizard : to add a wizard to a project. - Create a folder : to organise graphic forms within a project. Tip: Projects and their folders provide an an Open ... Folder right click menu in the Enterprise Manager that will open this specific folder in Windows Explorer, when this project is on the same computer, so that content can be manually copied into or out of it. Note: You can also prevent the unauthorised editing of graphic forms and/or wizards, by password-protecting entire projects, folders and/or individual graphic forms and wizards. For details, see Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards . Other possible operations: - Close a project : to hide its configured graphic forms and folders from view. - Remove a project : to delete it and its configured graphic forms and folders. - Rename a graphic form : to change the name of a graphic form. - Export a graphic form : to copy a graphic form to disk for archiving or later re-use. - Import a graphic form : to import a graphic form from disk. - Copy a graphic form : to duplicate a graphic form in another project or folder. - Paste a graphic form : to insert a copied graphic form into a project or folder. - Remove a graphic form : to delete a graphic form. - Open and close a folder : to expose/hide its configured graphic forms and folders. - Rename a folder : to change the name of a folder. - Remove a folder : to delete a folder. Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . -->

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Note: When typing values into this edit dialog, click the Update button to register these changes. - If necessary, open the Edit Timer Agent dialog, as follows: - If necessary, add an Timer agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Timer Agent dialog. - If necessary, the timer can be started or stopped manually within this edit dialog, by checking or clearing the Start timer checkbox, which configures the start slot directly. Note: The Input tag edit box is ignored, since this timer CANNOT be started automatically by subscribing to another tag in the Agent Server. - Use the Delay time (ms) field to specify the period, in milliseconds, that this generated pulse is required to be OFF for i.e. after which the specified Pulse width (ms) period will begin. During this time the Boolean output ( value slot) of this agent will be disabled (set to FALSE). - Use the Pulse width (ms) field to specify the period, in milliseconds, that this generated pulse is required to be ON for i.e. the width of the required pulse. During this time the Boolean output ( value slot) of this agent will be enabled (set to TRUE). - The period of the generated pulse is the sum of the Delay time (ms) and Pulse width (ms) fields. For example: if Delay time (ms) = 59000 and Pulse width (ms) = 1000, then the Boolean output (value slot) of this agent will be enabled for 1 second every 60 seconds, until the Boolean start slot of this Timer agent is disabled (set to FALSE). Note: The Timer output checkbox indicates the current status of the value slot of this agent. - The Free running checkbox must be enabled (checked) for this timing operation. - If necessary, set the Granularity (ms) field to specify the required period, in milliseconds, for monitoring the time during this timing operation. When this period is less than the required duration of the timer, then the timeleft slot ( Time left field) indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds. WARNING! The smaller this Granularity value the greater the amount of work the Agent Server is required to perform in updating its clients with the timeleft slot value. Note1: The default value of 0 forces this granularity period to equal the required timer duration, so that the timeleft slot ( Time left field) is never calculated. Note2: Although this setting has a minimum of 100 ms, a minimum of 1000 ms is recommended. The Auto-reset checkbox is greyed out, since this timer cannot be restarted automatically. -->

This default triggering Behaviour can also be disabled if required. For details, see Triggering spiders or Disabling silk triggering of spiders . - Delete: This will remove this silk from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing silks . WARNING! The selected silk and any attached Data spider(s) will immediately be removed from the spider workspace. - Template Sets: This menu can be selected to associate this silk with one or more template sets. So that it will be enabled when this template set is activated. This will allow the spiders it connects able to transfer their data and therefore perform their functions. The following properties can be modified, for each of the added simulated data outputs: Property Description Amplitude The maximum value that will be generated for this output. Note: This is ignored if the RANDOM simulator is selected. Frequency The numeric difference between successively generated values. The lower the number the less the simulated values change. Name The name of this simulated output. Running This allows one to stop or start the generation of these simulated values, when the spider workspace is in running mode. SimulationType Determine how the simulated values are generated: - SIN: Sine values between + and - Amplitude . - COS: Cosine values between + and - Amplitude . - SQUARE: Values are squared between 0 and the Amplitude . - RAMP: A value increasing linearly from 0 to the Amplitude and then decreasing linearly back to 0. - RANDOM: Any number (ignores the Amplitude ) - DATASET: A dataset of 2 columns and 2 rows. UpdateRate The time in milliseconds between successively generated values. - If necessary, select the name of another simulated data output in the left pane so that it can be configured in the right pane. - Click the Finish button once all the outputs have been configured as required. -->

Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Smart UI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - Right click the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically, and select Create Tag . - Specify the required Tag Name or agent name. The following rules apply when naming agents: - Agent names have a maximum of 27 characters. - Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. - Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ - If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes the purpose or describes the value of this tag (agent) for ease of reference. - Click the Finish button. If necessary, locate the required agent, as follows: In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . For more details, see About SNMP Traps . - Select the SNMP managed objects (OID values) that you want to get and/or set by using the SNMP Objects Browser . For details, see Selecting OIDs . For details, see Enabling the Monitoring of OID Values or Enabling the Changing of Values . - Select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) in the Poll settings section, to start managing this device, by polling (getting), writing (setting) and/or trapping (enabling events) its OID values. For further details, see Global Device Management Settings . Note: The SNMPManager agent consumes a scan point for every unique OID that is polled, written to and/or trapped. The Error status bit is set when non connection-related errors occur. For details of the errors that this bit can indicate and how they affect the management of the device, see Specific Status Bits . Tip: The and buttons can display the edit dialogs of the agents above and below this agent in the Agents list of the Configurator dialog. If necessary, use the Advanced button to specify the name of the GLOBAL SNMP configuration file, which is called 'snmp.wgx' by default. This file contains the OID configuration of all your SNMPManager agents and allows them to store an unlimited number of OIDs. Ensure that this file is backed up. SNMP Error Codes: Lists the SNMP error codes implemented by Microsoft for troubleshooting SNMP-related problems. -->

Configuring the Agent Server Top Configuring the Agent Server The Agent Server is the storage facility for all real time and historical data. For further details, see About Agent Servers . The real time data resides within intelligent objects, known as agents, which exchange messages with other agents or picture objects either from their local host computer or from remote computer nodes elsewhere on the network. For details, see About Agents . Historical data is written to disk where it is available for rapid retrieval and on-line analysis. For details, see Logging Values . The Adroit database (.WGP) file or load file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. For details, see About Adroit Database Files . The Agent Server Configurator creates, manages and stores the configured agents and their slots (values) in the Agent Server. For further details, see the list of available agent types and their slots (values). Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Note: The Project Explorer can also be used to configure the Agent Server. For details, see The Project Explorer . Before you can create or edit any agents you must be connected to an Agent Server. If necessary, you can manually specify which Agent Server the Configurator should connect to and configure. For details, see Connecting to an Agent Server via the Classic UI . Note1: Only when these changes made to agents are saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents . Note2: These agents can also be exported to CSV files for editing by 3rd party applications and then imported into the Agent Server. For details, see Exporting and Importing Agents . Related topics Agent Server Connection Methods : Adroit provides three methods for allowing multiple distributed Agent Servers to seamlessly share their agents and the data that they contain. Proxy servers : An Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Clustering Agent Servers : A mechanism for providing client and server redundancy, previously known as hot standby. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . For more details on detecting and solving issues that most frequently prevent clustered Adroit Agent Servers from working, see Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers . -->

Once you add your incidents to this database, you can obtain statistical information about these incidents by querying this data and analyzing these queries. Note: Currently this agent only provides correctly formatted queries for MS Access and SQL databases. - Use the Housekeeping section to specify how long, in days, that you want to store your logged alarms/events. This depends upon the storage capacity you have available for your database and how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. By default, this is disabled, which means that you need to perform the required housekeeping the removal of unnecessary records from a database . Note: You cannot specify an number of days less than 30, since you need some historical records to determine your alarming trends. - Use the Shift times section to specify the starting times of your shifts (the shift1Time , shift2Time and shift3Time slots), as each incident specifies the shift number in which it occurs. In other words: Any incident that occurs between shift1Time and shift2Time , is logged as a Shift 1 incident. Any incident that occurs between shift2Time and shift3Time , is logged as a Shift 2 incident. Any incident that occurs between shift3Time and shift1Time , is logged as a Shift 3 incident. Note: Instead of configuring this shift pattern information here, you can instead configure these shift patterns globally, by using a Shift agent. For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . Tip: If you only have two shifts then specify the same shift time for shift two and three. - Ensure that the Start Alarm Management agent checkbox (the enable slot) is checked, to start adding incidents to the selected database. By default, all the incidents (the alarms and/or events that occur on the routes of the alarm agent/s you configured in step 2) are added to the _Uncategorised category of the Categories tree. - If you have clustered Agent Servers that both log incidents to the same database then check the Disable recording on standby server checkbox (the disableStandby slot) to prevent double entries from being added. - Typically you will create your own hierarchical (logical) structure of categories for your incidents, in the Categories tree, as follows: Tip: This edit dialog can be maximised and resized to enlarge the screen area to design and view this Categories tree. Adding Categories : Categories can make your incidents easier to query and analyse. For more details, see Reasons for categorizing your incidents . Configuring Categories : Where necessary, specify the ‘Operator tag’ setting for categories that represent sections of your process that are controlled by different operations. To ensure that the incidents you assign to this category (and if necessary its sub-categories) are logged using the name of the correct operator. Adding Incidents : To add new and existing incidents to categories in the Categories tree. Note1: You can only assign an incident to a SINGLE category. Note2: The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident. For details, see Incident icon colors . Removing Incidents : To reassign incidents to other categories or to permanently remove an incident from the alarm management database.

For details, see Customizing KPI target values . - The View data… button displays a dialog to use queries to analyse the logged incidents and display the results in a grid or table. For details, see Querying recorded incidents . Tip: You can also launch this dialog directly from a Classic UI mimic. For details, see Launching the View Data dialog . - The View graph… button displays a dialog to use queries to analyse the logged incidents and display the results graphically, as a chart. For details, see Viewing Incident Queries Graphically . Tip: You can also launch this dialog directly from a Classic UI mimic. For details, see Launching the View Graph dialog . - The View reasons… button displays a dialog that ONLY lists the current incidents that still require reasons and/or notes to be specified. If necessary, these reasons and/notes can be specified for these incidents from this dialog. For details, see Viewing Incidents Requiring Reasons and/or Notes . Tip: You can also launch this dialog directly from a Classic UI mimic. For details, see Launching the View Reasons Dialog . WARNING! We do NOT RECOMMEND using the View data and View graph dialogs for an alarm management database that contains a huge number of historical incidents - this can cause your system to become unstable. Note: Although these dialogs can help you to analyse this data, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. For details of the database (the tables and their fields) that is maintained by the AlarmManagement agent, see About the AlarmManagement Database .

Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes Top Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes The SmartUI Server includes the following data element security functionality: Note: This functionality is part of the SmartUI Server and is available even when one does not want to use 21 CFR 11 mode.

Title: Configuration
Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes Top Configuring the auditing and/or authorizing of value changes The SmartUI Server includes the following data element security functionality: Note: This functionality is part of the SmartUI Server and is available even when one does not want to use 21 CFR 11 mode. - auditing functionality: to audit ANY data element by completely tracking changes made to its value through the SmartUI . - change authorizing functionality: when enabled this requires an additional user to provide authorization before a change can be made (written) to a data element. Tip: If you are employing a 21 CFR 11 compliant project then ensure that you have enabled 21 CFR 11 mode. For more details, see Working with 21 CFR 11 mode . Before your Windows user accounts and/or groups can participate in the auditing and/or authentication of value (data element) changes, they need to be added as "allowed" users and groups on each SmartUI Server. - Since these users are required to access the SmartUI Server computer directly then to preserve the integrity of the 21 CFR 11 functionality, these users must only be given minimal rights (from a Windows security context). Only administrative users may be given extended rights. IMPORTANT: Therefore ONLY specify your system administrator users and/or groups in this the Security Settings page of the SmartUI Server in the Adroit Config Editor , since these users and/or groups have immediate GLOBAL access to every aspect of your project, which includes the ability to write to all of the data elements. For details, see Server security settings . For this reason, you should rather configure your allowed users and groups within the SmartUI Designer, as you can then manually configure the extent of their access. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . - Since, you need to know beforehand exactly which values to audit and/or authorise, you can only configure specific, individual data elements and not entire groups of data elements. In other words, the Apply To Children setting is NOT supported For instance, when used with the Adroit datasource and you apply it to an Analog agent it does nothing, you need to manually select and configured the value slot security. Although a default (the most commonly used) slot for each agent type, may be implemented later. In the SmartUI every value is known as a data element of a datasource, so you use data element security to configure the auditing change of values (data elements) and/or their authorization, as follows: IMPORTANT: Unlike the data element security permissions, the auditing and authorizing settings are data element specific and NOT user or group specific. So they are enabled or disabled for ALL the selected users and/or groups. However, ONLY users or groups with the Write Data security permission can authorise changes to a data element. Note: Currently these security options can only be applied to data elements and not to special functions of a datasource. - Right-click the required datasource or data element in the Enterprise Manager and select the Security menu option: In the Security configuration dialog, ensure that the Security For Data Element field, beneath the Data Element Information group, specifies the required data element. - Use the Groups And Users group to select the allowed user(s) and/or groups to be assigned security permissions for this data element. Either by clicking the << button or double-clicking the required entry in the Available list to immediately add it to the Selected list.
