text:
- Assign security settings to allowed users and groups, as follows: - Select a user or group from the Selected list.

Title: Configuration
- Assign security settings to allowed users and groups, as follows: - Select a user or group from the Selected list. Tip: Select multiple users or groups, if more than one is to have the same security permissions assigned to them. - Empty the checkboxes that do not apply to the currently selected user(s) or group(s). Tip: Clicking on the name will check or empty its checkbox. - Repeat this until all of the selected users or groups have been assigned the correct security settings for the selected data element. - Use the Data Element Security group to assign the required security permissions to the selected users and/or groups. For details, see Available data element security permissions . - Use the Auditing group to assign the required value auditing and/or authorizing settings to this data element, as follows: IMPORTANT: Unlike the Data Element Security group, the settings of the Auditing are data element specific and NOT user or group specific. So they are enabled or disabled for ALL the selected users and/or groups. Note1: These settings IGNORE the Apply To Children and Inherit From Parent settings as they ONLY apply to specific data elements and NOT to groups of data elements and therefore cannot be inherited from data element groups. Note2: BOTH these settings need to be applied to the applicable data elements for 21 CFR 11 compliance. - Audit Writes : when checked any change made to this data element is recorded to an auditing database with the user who initiated the change and if applicable the user who authorised this change. For further details, see Working with audited data element values . These recorded (logged) changes include: the timestamp of the change; the change made; the initiating user and, if applicable the authorizing user, and a computed hash of all these fields to detect tampering. - Requires Authorization : when checked any change made to this data element needs to be authorised by one of the selected user/s and group/s. Once set, then any change made to this data elements needs to be authorised by a DIFFERENT allowed user or group, than the user or group who makes the change (the initiating user the currently logged on user or group that changes the value (data element) that requries authorization; See authorizing user ). For details, see Authorizing changes made to values . IMPORTANT: If a data element is marked as requiring authorization then no single individual may change the value of this data element. Note: ONLY users or groups with the Write Data permission can authorise changes. Furthermore, the authorizing user is recorded along with the other details of this change in value, when the writes of this data element are audited. The system responds to write requests made to this data element, as follows: User Access Authorization Required Response to Write Attempt Read No Prompt for credentials Read Yes Prompt for credentials Write No Write operation carried out unchallenged Write Yes User prompted to provide authorizing user credentials OR to defer the operation for later authorization OR to cancel the write. Authorise No N/A Authorise Yes User prompted to provide authorizing user credentials (other than this user) OR to defer the operation for later authorization OR to cancel the write -->

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit Notify agent dialog: - Leave the default Notify agent edit dialog unchanged and click the Advanced… button. In the e-Mail section of the Advanced options dialog: - Check the Enable checkbox. - Specify the required email recipients for the email messages sent using this Notify agent in the To , CC and/or Bcc fields, as follows: IMPORTANT: Use a comma (,) NOT a semi-colon (;) to separate multiple email addresses. - The To field is for people that the message directly affects, in other words those people that need to do something about this message. - The Cc field is for people that need to know about the message, but are not directly involved - to keep them informed. - The Bcc field is used when you want other people to receive the message, but you don't want the other recipients to know they got it. When an e-mail is received, the recipients see all the email addresses in the To , CC and From fields - but not the Bcc field. Tip: Only use the Bcc field when sending an e-mail to more than 50 recipients to prevent them from seeing the e-mail addresses of the other recipients. - Specify the generic Subject of these Notify agent email messages, which is the title of the email that appears in the InBox of the recipients. - Specify the generic Body of these Notify agent email messages. - If necessary, you can specify any file as the attachment of this email message in the Attachment field. Either type in or browse in the full path of this file including its extension. Note: Only 1 file can be attached to the email message.

Note: Macros are NOT SUPPORTED in manually-created email messages, so any specified macros in the Subject or Body fields are sent as-is (undecoded). Slot Description Email-To The To field is for people that the message directly affects, in other words those people that need to do something about this message. Email-CC The Cc field is for people that need to know about the message, but are not directly involved - to keep them informed. Email-BC The Bcc field is used when you want other people to receive the message, but you don't want the other recipients to know they got it. When an e-mail is received, the recipients see all the email addresses in the To, CC and From fields - but not the Bcc field. Email-Subject The Subject line of the email message, which is the title of the email that appears in the InBox of the recipients. Email-Body The Body (actual message) of this email. Email-Attachment The OPTIONAL full path and filename of the file attachment of this email message. Note: Only 1 file can be attached to an email message. - Add a mechanism, typically a button to send a 1 to the BOOLEAN Email-Send-Now slot. Sending a 1 to the BOOLEAN Email-Send-Now slot, encapsulates the other VARSTRING Email- slots into the RAWBYTES Email-rawValue slot, which is then scanned to applicable device of the Email driver that sends this message. -->

Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit Scheduler Agent dialog box: Note: This Edit Scheduler agent dialog can be resized , to view the entire width of this grid, if necessary. - Tick the Enabled checkbox if the output of the Scheduler agent is to be determined by the defined periods of time. - Clear the Enabled checkbox, if the output of the Scheduler agent is to be manually controlled, for instance, from this configuration dialog, from a mimic, the scanning subsystem or any other legal method of changing an agent’s slot. More details: When the Enabled checkbox is cleared, the Value checkbox is enabled, and it determines the status of the Scheduler agent’s output, ignoring the configured Dates to exclude and any scheduled periods of time. To Manually Enable the Value Tickbox . - If required, tick the UCT Times checkbox, to specify the times using the UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time format instead of using local time. This is required if you intend to create schedules of times from around the world. - The Scheduler agent also provides a global method for automatically configuring the schedule lists of multiple Scheduler agents, via the configuration of a "master" Scheduler agent. More details: Note: When specifying a master Scheduler agent the schedule list of the slave agent is replaced with that of the master and the list of excluded dates of the master is ADDED to that of the slave. Click for more details: This by design, to ensure that any excluded dates specified in a slave Scheduler agent will not be overwritten by someone updating the master. However, this means that if you remove an excluded date from the Master Scheduler agent, then in order to remove this excluded date from your slave Scheduler agent/s, that you need to explicitly remove this date from each of the slave Scheduler agent’s "Dates to exclude" field. This "master" Scheduler agent acts as the repository of the schedule lists. Then when configuring a "slave" Scheduler agent, specify the name of this "master" Scheduler agent in the Master agent edit box. Either type this master agent name in directly or click on the browse button ( ... ) on the right of this edit box, so that this agent can be selected using the agent browser . Note: A "slave" Scheduler agent, is a Scheduler agent that will receive any schedule list changes implemented on the "master" Scheduler agent. - The Dates to exclude edit box, this field is optional and only needs to be configured if there are specific dates, which must be excluded from the scheduled periods of time. More details: Either type these dates in manually or use the browse button ( ... ) on the right of this edit box, which opens the Select date to exclude dialog . Multiple dates are separated by semi-colons. Note1: The date format used is determined by the Regional Settings of the computer.

If unsure, use the Select date to exclude dialog to select these dates instead.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
If unsure, use the Select date to exclude dialog to select these dates instead. Note2: The Dates to exclude field is NOT copied from the "master" Scheduler agent. - The Command to run edit box, this field is optional and only needs to be configured if an application is required to be launched as soon as this agent’s output changes into a TRUE state. More details: This must contain the full path and name of the application, which can either be typed in manually or browsed in, by using browse button ( ... ), which opens the file browser. If necessary, any command-line parameters can also be added. Note: Paths containing spaces need to be enclosed in double quotation marks (""). - Use the grid to add, configure and remove the scheduled periods of time, during which the output of the Enabled Scheduler agent will be TRUE. For details, see Configuring a Scheduled Period of Time . Note: The grid provides standard configuration options . - Click the Update button to save the change(s) made to the configuration of the agent. - Click the Refresh button to determine the current configuration of the agent. -->

Configuring the Shift agent Top Configuring the Shift Agent Edit an agent of type: Scheduler .

Title: Configuration
Configuring the Shift agent Top Configuring the Shift Agent Edit an agent of type: Scheduler . Please use the following sequence when adding shift patterns: - Entries that contain a Special date or Day of month value must always be specified first. - Special date entries must use the format “yyyy/mm/dd” e.g. 2010/04/04. An example of a “special date” is a public holiday which falls on a different day every year e.g. Easter Monday. - Day of month entries must use the format “mm/dd”. An example of a “day of month” is a public holiday which falls on the same day every year e.g. New Years day. Note1: Entries containing a Special date cannot contain a Day of month value too. Note2: Entries containing a Special date or Day of month value force (disable) their Day of week value. Tip: Use the DEL key to delete unneeded Special date or Day of month field entries - The last entries should be the default shift patterns that ONLY contains a Day of week value and NO Special date or Day of month values. Shift pattern examples: This screenshot exemplifies the required order of entries and provides the following shift patterns: - For the 1 st of January of any year. - For the 25 th of December for any year. - ONLY on the 4 th of April 2010 - For ALL Saturdays and Sundays - For ALL normal weekdays Notice how the shift patterns that do NOT contain a Special date or Day of month column are at the END of this list. The Shift agent caters for a maximum of 6 shifts per day. If you need less than 6 shifts, then specify the starting time of the last applicable shift for the unneeded shifts. For instance, if only 3 shifts are used, then specify the starting time of shift 3 as the starting times of shifts 4, 5 and 6. Shift number examples: This screenshot shows the following shift time configurations: - The first has TWO shifts one starting at 2 AM and the other at 2 PM. - The second has THREE shifts, which start at 2 AM, 10 AM and 6 PM Notice how the unneeded shifts ALWAYS specify the starting times of the last applicable shift.

SQL connection string : If specified, the shifts are added to the Adr_Grouping_Details table as the shifts occur in real time, which is used by Adroit SCADA Intelligence.

Configuring Windows Security Policies Top Configuring Windows Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager provides the following security policies, which affect the Windows operating system of the computer that these policies are applied to, as follows: - Configure Power Users: All Adroit users must, at least, belong to the LOCAL "Power Users" security group over and above the default "User" group; otherwise they are not able to perform all the functions necessary to run Adroit on this computer.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring Windows Security Policies Top Configuring Windows Security Policies The Adroit Security Manager provides the following security policies, which affect the Windows operating system of the computer that these policies are applied to, as follows: - Configure Power Users: All Adroit users must, at least, belong to the LOCAL "Power Users" security group over and above the default "User" group; otherwise they are not able to perform all the functions necessary to run Adroit on this computer. For instance: if you are NOT part of the Power Users group, although you will able to start the User Interface, you will not be able to start the Agent Server or the Adroit Setup utility. Also if the Agent Server is installed as a service, then the Agent Server will also start. Note: If you are running a domain and you are configuring the domain controller computer, you do not need to perform this configuration as this computer already has a POWER USERS group and the Adroit users are already assigned to this group. - Enable Auto-Logon: If enabled this setting allows other users to start your computer and use the account that you establish to automatically log on. For instance: many SCADA installations create a user that is part of the Adroit Operator security group called DefaultOP, which is used to auto logon to Windows. For this reason, if you choose to create the default groups, this user is created for you; however you need to make this user a member of the Adroit Operators default group yourself. WARNING! Although enabling auto logon makes your computer more convenient to use, it can pose a security risk. Therefore it is recommended that the user account that you specify has the LOWEST access permissions for the computer and the Adroit installation. To BYPASS the Windows automatic logon to log on as a different user: - Hold down the SHIFT key after you log off or after Windows XP restarts. Note: This ONLY applies to the first logon attempt of the computer. - Replace the Shell: This is the easiest method of creating a restricted workstation for your operators, as this simply replaces the default Explorer shell with the Classic UI. This means that when Windows is launched, the Classic UI is displayed by default and NOT the Windows Desktop. Tip: By applying the Disable Alt-Tab and Disable Ctl-Esc policies you can run the Classic UI on top of the XP (without removing shell) and STILL prevent your operators from accessing Windows. To enable a security policy: this allows you to specify which of the available security policies you want to apply. - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - If necessary, expand (double click) the Windows Security Options branch in the left hand tree pane. - Click on the required option. - Ensure that the Apply Setting checkbox is checked. - If necessary, perform any additional configuration. IMPORTANT: Simply enabling a policy (option) does NOT change this policy on this computer; you need to APPLY the policy to a specific computer in order to change the security settings of this computer. For details on how to save and/or apply the specified security settings, see Applying Security Policies . -->

Connect ActiveX Method Top Connect ActiveX Method Connection Functionality . Method Connect(computer, server : string) : boolean; This method connects to a specific Agent Server. This call provides backward compatibility as changing the Server property achieves the same result if AutoConnect is TRUE. Using this method will clear the Cluster property. Parameters: - Computer - contains the name of the computer where the Agent Server exists or full Agent Server pathname (computer.server). - Server - contains the name of the Agent Server to connect to. This parameter is ignored if the Computer parameter contains a full Agent Server pathname (e.g. john.as). Returns: If the connection succeeds the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE. Use LastError / LastErrorNum to determine the cause of failure. -->

Title: Connecting graphic forms to TemplateGO controls
Connecting graphic forms to TemplateGO controls Top Connecting graphic forms to TemplateGO controls You can use the following methods to choose which graphic form the TemplateGO control displays: Note: You can also select the graphic form on which you have added this TemplateGO control. - To immediately display the connected graphic form in Designer: this method is recommended when using a TemplateGO control to contain a single graphic form, which may or may not expose properties of its form components through the use of aliases. Note: This method simplifies the process of further designing as one can immediately see exactly how the selected graphic form appears. - Either use the Browse for Graphic Form task: this task is provided by the Task menu, which is displayed when the control is initially added and can be accessed by clicking its glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the selected control. Using the Browse for Graphic Form task: - If necessary, add the TemplateGO control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding TemplateGO controls . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this TemplateGO control. - If necessary, click the glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of this control, to display the menu of tasks - Click the Browse for Graphic Form... hyperlink to display the Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog. This contains an explorer view of all of the projects and their graphic forms configured within the Projects category of each Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . - Select the required graphic form within this explorer view. Tip: It is also possible to select the required graphic form by double-clicking on it. - Only check the Include Server Name in selection checkbox if you SPECIFICALLY want this control to ONLY connect to this specific Server, otherwise if unchecked the control will look for this graphic form on the currently specified default (logon) Server. - Check the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox option, if you want to ensure that the specified graphic form will still be located when the project name is renamed or when this graphic form is copied to another project, while preserving its relative path. - Click Finish . The fully qualified namespace of the currently selected graphic form is displayed in the field at the bottom of the explorer view, which adheres to the following format: ProjectName.{Folder(s)Name(s)}.GraphicFormName, where {..} indicates that the Folder(s)Name(s) are optional and depend upon the organization of this project. Note: If the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox is checked then this does NOT provide the ProjectName portion. If the Include Server Name in selection checkbox is checked then this also includes the following at the beginning: [MachineName] ServerName. - The specified graphic form should be displayed within the control. Note: This control can be configured to automatically resize to contain this graphic form, by enabling its AutoResize property. - Or use the GraphicFormPath property of this control to browse for the required graphic form. Using the GraphicFormPath property: - If necessary, add the TemplateGO control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding TemplateGO controls . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this TemplateGO control. - Open the Properties tool window, navigate to the GraphicFormPath property and select it. - Click on the browse button to the right of its value cell.

Connecting to an OLE DB database Top Creating a SQL database connection string Click the ...

Title: Creating a SQL database connection string
Connecting to an OLE DB database Top Creating a SQL database connection string Click the ... browse button to the right of this field and use the Data Link Properties dialog to create the required connection string to your SQL Server database. Provider TAB The Data Link Properties dialog specifies the location and the security credentials required to connect to this database. Double-click the Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server item in the Provider tab of the Data Link Properties dialog. Important: If the computer, on which SQL Server was installed, was renamed, then SQL Server may need to be re-installed. If the computer was renamed after installing SQL Server, then SQL Server must be re-installed, to function correctly. Run the following check: - Execute the following T-SQL (Transact-SQL) script in SQL Server Management Studio: SELECT @@SERVERNAME - If the resulting server name is different to the actual name of the computer, then the name of the computer has been changed after SQL Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. Note: If you need to configure or view this database and its data from remote computers, then you should use a UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name path and not a local file path this path, as opposed to a UNC path, can ONLY be accessed from the computer that it refers to, this path adopts the following general format: <driveletter>:\directories\filename. to specify the location of this database. Connection Tab - Type in the computer name of the SQL Server that you want to connect to, in the Select or enter a server name field. - Tip: This is the fastest method if you know the name of the SQL Server. - Alternatively, click the drop-arrow button to the right of the Select or enter a server name box and select the name of the required SQL Server from the list. - Specify the required security credentials to connect to the selected SQL Server: Important: - If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to run the Agent Server service using the Local System account , then use SQL Server Authentication .

text:
- If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to Use Windows NT Integrated security, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer has the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database.

Title: Creating a SQL database connection string
- If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to Use Windows NT Integrated security, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer has the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. - Use Windows NT Integrated security: this option uses the username and password of the currently signed in Windows user. - Tip: We recommend that you configure your SQL Servers to use this option to avoid requiring additional database security. - SQL Server Authentication: this option uses the User name and Password configured within the SQL Server you are attempting to connect to. - Note: In this case, it is recommended to select the Allow saving password checkbox. - Select the name of the required database from the Select the database on the server list box. - Click the Test Connection button to ensure that you are able to connect to this database using these details. Only proceed once 'Test connection succeeded' is displayed. - Click the OK button. - Your connection string will be created. Advanced Tab The Advanced tab of this dialog allows you to specify access permissions for this connection string. - If you are unsure about these settings, then never set these permissions to Read , otherwise this connection string will fail. - These security credentials are database specific and should not be confused with application security. - if necessary, you can edit this string directly, once it has been created. -->

Title: To connect to the distribution computer:
Steps:
- Run the SmartUI Launcher, as follows: - If you have installed the SmartUI Launcher: use the Launcher shortcut on the Desktop by the installation or from within the VIP Launcher r program group. - If SmartUI supports the use of the Launcher and you have the Operator or Designer components already installed, then double click the SmartUI Launcher executable in the installation folder, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI . The SmartUI Launcher is displayed. - If necessary, selecting File menu and its Connection item to display the Connection dialog. - If necessary, select how this distribution computer is to be reached i.e. over the LAN or over the Internet. Note: By default, this dialog displays the fields required when connecting to a distribution computer over the LAN. If this connection is required over the LAN: - Specify the network name of this required computer that has the SmartUI Distributor service installed and configured in the Computer/URL edit box. - Ensure that the LAN or WAN selection is selected. - In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. Note: At least the User field needs to be completed, in order for a connection to be created; a Password does not need to be specified. - Click the Connect button, once the necessary details, have been correctly specified. If this connection is required over the Internet: Note: Before a connection can be made over the Internet to the Server, the Web service needs to be installed. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service . - Specify the Internet address (URL) of the Web service, which makes this Internet connection possible, in the Computer/URL edit box, which is typically: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory/wsdistributor.asmx. Where: - ComputerName is the name of the IIS server hosting the distribution service (on which the Web service has been installed) - VirtualDirectory is the name of the virtual directory containing the wsdistributor.asmx file, which was specified when installing the SmartUI Web Service , which is typically: SmartUI Tip: The 'http://' prefix and '/wsdistributor.asmx' suffix will be added to this URL on connection, if they have not been specified. For further details, open this web page: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory e.g. http://localhost/ SmartUI , which can be used to download the Launcher application and also contains instructions on how to connect and download the distribution files too. Note: The SmartUI Web Service does not need to be installed on the same computer as the Distributor service, as long as these two computers can communicate over the LAN. - Ensure that the Internet selection is selected. - In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. - If a proxy server is required for this Internet connection, check the Enable Proxy checkbox and click the Proxy Settings button. This displays the Proxy Settings dialog, so that the necessary connection settings for this Proxy server can be specified, as follows: - Specify the network name of this Proxy server or its IP address in the Machine Name or IP edit box. - Specify the port that this Proxy Server uses in the Port edit box, this is typically port 8080. Tip: If necessary, the required port for this proxy server can also be determined from Internet Options (typically launched from the Tools menu in Internet Explorer), by selecting the Connections tab and its LAN Settings… button. - If user authentication is required when connecting to this proxy server, then check the Authenticate checkbox and supply the necessary User and Password. - Click OK .

- Run the SmartUI Launcher, as follows: - If you have installed the SmartUI Launcher: use the Launcher shortcut on the Desktop by the installation or from within the VIP Launcher r program group. - If SmartUI supports the use of the Launcher and you have the Operator or Designer components already installed, then double click the SmartUI Launcher executable in the installation folder, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI . The SmartUI Launcher is displayed. - If necessary, selecting File menu and its Connection item to display the Connection dialog. - If necessary, select how this distribution computer is to be reached i.e. over the LAN or over the Internet. Note: By default, this dialog displays the fields required when connecting to a distribution computer over the LAN. If this connection is required over the LAN: - Specify the network name of this required computer that has the SmartUI Distributor service installed and configured in the Computer/URL edit box. - Ensure that the LAN or WAN selection is selected. - In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. Note: At least the User field needs to be completed, in order for a connection to be created; a Password does not need to be specified. - Click the Connect button, once the necessary details, have been correctly specified. If this connection is required over the Internet: Note: Before a connection can be made over the Internet to the Server, the Web service needs to be installed. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service . - Specify the Internet address (URL) of the Web service, which makes this Internet connection possible, in the Computer/URL edit box, which is typically: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory/wsdistributor.asmx. Where: - ComputerName is the name of the IIS server hosting the distribution service (on which the Web service has been installed) - VirtualDirectory is the name of the virtual directory containing the wsdistributor.asmx file, which was specified when installing the SmartUI Web Service , which is typically: SmartUI Tip: The 'http://' prefix and '/wsdistributor.asmx' suffix will be added to this URL on connection, if they have not been specified. For further details, open this web page: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory e.g. http://localhost/ SmartUI , which can be used to download the Launcher application and also contains instructions on how to connect and download the distribution files too. Note: The SmartUI Web Service does not need to be installed on the same computer as the Distributor service, as long as these two computers can communicate over the LAN. - Ensure that the Internet selection is selected. - In the Authenticate group, specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer. - If a proxy server is required for this Internet connection, check the Enable Proxy checkbox and click the Proxy Settings button. This displays the Proxy Settings dialog, so that the necessary connection settings for this Proxy server can be specified, as follows: - Specify the network name of this Proxy server or its IP address in the Machine Name or IP edit box. - Specify the port that this Proxy Server uses in the Port edit box, this is typically port 8080. Tip: If necessary, the required port for this proxy server can also be determined from Internet Options (typically launched from the Tools menu in Internet Explorer), by selecting the Connections tab and its LAN Settings… button. - If user authentication is required when connecting to this proxy server, then check the Authenticate checkbox and supply the necessary User and Password. - Click OK .

Title: To connect to a SNMP device:
Specify the following settings in the Connection settings section of the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog: - IP address (STRING ipAddress slot): Specify the IP address of the device that is to be monitored and/or managed by this SNMPManager agent. For details on the requirements and guidelines regarding the use of this agent to monitor and/or manage devices, see Usage Requirements . Tip1: Use the arrow keys to navigate between the digits separated by periods. Tip2: When monitoring the local computer, the following IP address always returns the local address: 127.0.0.1. - Port address: this allows SNMP devices to be addressed via a gateway where the IP addresses are not unique and so a unique port address is required. - Read comm. (STRING readCommunity slot): If you ONLY want to retrieve (poll) values from this device then specify its read-only SNMP Community String. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings. Tip: Since most equipment ships from the factory with a read-only community string that is set to "public", this is its default value. - Write comm. (STRING writeCommunity slot): If you want to write (set) values for this device then specify its read-write SNMP Community String. - Timeout (ms) (INTEGER timeout slot): If necessary, specify the maximum time (in milliseconds) to establish a connection to this device. This is 2.5 seconds, by default. - Retries (INTEGER retries slot): If necessary, specify the number of attempts to connect to the device, before deeming this device to be unavailable. This is 2 times, by default. - Only check the Enable traps checkbox (BOOLEAN trapEnabled slot): if you want to receive SNMP traps from this device. For more details, see About SNMP Traps . Note: If the Update button is clicked after modifying the IP address or Read comm. or WriteRead comm. settings, the agent will attempt to reconnect to the device using these new settings. The Invalid connection checkbox (InvalidConnection status bit) indicates if this agent CAN (if empty) or CANNOT (if checked) connect to the specified device. BUT this checkbox is ONLY validated when you press the Update button or select the Enable polling option for this agent, so it will ALWAYS be CHECKED when the Disable polling option is selected. Note1: If you are monitoring a computer and have NOT installed the SNMP service, then the InvalidConnection status bit will be set.

text:
Connecting to the required Agent Server Top Connecting to the Required Agent Server The Scanning Monitor utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server, so this information can be used to manually fine-tune the scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance.

Title: Connecting to the Required Agent Server
Steps:
Connecting to the required Agent Server Top Connecting to the Required Agent Server The Scanning Monitor utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server, so this information can be used to manually fine-tune the scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance. For details, see Monitoring Scanning in Adroit . For this reason, it is necessary to specify the Agent Server whose scanning configuration is to be monitored. This can be performed as follows: On launching, the Scanning Monitor utility can connect to its default Agent Server, this is either the Agent Server running on the same computer as the utility or a specified remote Agent Server. For details, see Launching the Scanning Monitor Utility . Note: The name of the currently selected Agent Server and any connection-related errors are displayed within the status bar of this utility. For details, see Current Agent Server Connection Details . Once launched, the required Agent Server can also be selected as follows: - The Servers combo box, contains a list of all the Agent Servers that are detected within the current network domain/workgroup in which the local computer is a member. To connect to a detected Agent Server: - Simply click on the combo box below the Servers title (in the top right hand corner). This will display a list of all the Agent Servers that are detected within the current network domain/workgroup, as follows: computerName.AgentServerName(ProjectName). - Select the name of the required Agent Server. - The Connect… button can be used to manually connect to any other Agent Servers that are not displayed in the Servers list box. For instance, any Agent Server, running in other domains/workgroups or across a network switch. To connect to an undetected Agent Server: - Click the Connect… button. The Enter AS to connect to dialog is displayed. - Type in the name of the required Agent Server and the network name of the computer upon which it is running in the following format: computerName.AgentServerName - Click the OK button. Note: Once an Agent Server has been connected to, reselecting the same Agent Server again will refresh the list of devices that have been used to scan one or more tags in the WGP file currently opened on this Agent Server. For details, see Devices within Selected Agent Server Database . -->

You can edit the Default context to create your own logical organisation of your objects and other data, by either: - Adding the necessary hierarchy of nodes , or - if you have implemented Alarm Management, you can import your existing hierarchy of categories as nodes , with or without the agents that are associated with their configured incidents. - For detailed steps to editing the default context, see Editing the Default context . Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits. Title: Configuration
Steps:
In particular, consider the following points: Note1: Mimics that have been saved in a zoomed state are automatically normalised before the mimic is exported. Note2: Scale picture elements are currently not supported and need to be recreated after importing. Note3: Rotated Rectangle picture elements are imported as polylines and therefore will NOT have rounded corners. - Ensure that you have performed the required alignment of your picture elements before exporting the mimic, since the SmartUI uses a different method of aligning objects that takes practice to do. - Ensure that all your configured Behaviours are working as desired before exporting the mimic, so that you do not need to reconfigure them after importing the mimic. IMPORTANT: This especially applies to any template mimics that are being exported, because currently if their Behaviours are edited after importing then they lose their functionality and need to be re-configured. More details: during the importing process, SmartUI Template Sets are configured (which employ alternate sets of spider silks for each template), but when these Behaviours are configured after importing, their configuration is automatically changed to use SmartUI Templates instead (which uses a totally different mechanism of templatization, namely the use of graphic form aliases) This means that unless the appropriate aliases are configured, then this Behaviour loses ALL of its functionality until the necessary aliases are configured appropriately. For details, see SmartUI Templates . - Convert all Operator Action Behaviours that use Ramp as a % to use unit(s) instead, since the % Ramp value increment/ decrement is not currently supported. - Ensure that the Text picture elements have not been stretched in the Classic UI and that any stretched Text picture elements are replaced with a Text picture element of the correct size that has its font set to the required size. So that these do not need to be corrected after importing. Back to top

text:
Save your mimic in the Classic UI, as normal Select Yes to the confirmation dialog to also create a XAML file.

Title: Save your mimic in the Classic UI to a XAML file
Steps:
Save your mimic in the Classic UI, as normal Select Yes to the confirmation dialog to also create a XAML file. This XAML file is created in the same folder in which the mimic is created and simply appends the .XAML extension to the end of this name after the .mim. If this confirmation dialog is NOT displayed, then configure the Adroit 10 Classic UI to save mimics as XAML files (and trends as XML files) first, as follows: - Launch the SmartUI Config Editor - Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Locate the Legacy UI Parameters: group at the bottom of this dialog. - Ensure that the Enable Xaml Saving checkbox is checked. Note: You need to RESTART the Classic UI after changing this setting. Tip: You can also automatically export ALL mimics in a specific folder to XAML , by starting the Classic UI from the command line and using the <path_name>\*.mim parameter, as follows: if the required path to your mimics and/or path to the Classic UI has spaces then use double quotes e.g. "C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\adroit.exe" "E:\My Documents\Mimics\*.mim", otherwise omit these e.g. adroit c:\adroitproject\mimics\*.mim. The *.mim command line parameter exports all the mimics in the specified folder to XAML and then shuts down the Classic UI. Ensure that the XAML conversion was successful, as follows: After exporting the mimic to XAML, open the .XAML file in Internet Explorer, by double clicking on it, to see if anything went wrong during the XAML conversion process, as follows:. - If the XAML conversion was successful, then the mimic is displayed in Internet Explorer - If the XAML conversion was unsuccessful, then the mimic is NOT displayed and instead the first exception that was encountered is displayed, for instance “Font size must be greater than 0”. In this case, attend to this problem in your Classic UI mimic and then re-save this mimic to XAML and re-open it in Internet Explorer – if necessary reiterate this process until your mimic is displayed in Internet Explorer. Back to top

Title: Import this mimic into the SmartUI
Steps:
- If necessary, create the required project in the Enterprise manager. For details, see Creating new projects . IMPORTANT: Avoid using folder structures in this project as this will cause the navigation to fail. If a folder structure is used, then post importing configuration is required to ensure the Execute Command behaviours point to the correct files. - Add a graphic form to this project, as follows: right-click on the project name or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Create Graphic Form . Rename this graphic form to match the original Classic UI mimic file name. Tip: It is recommended to copy and paste this name from the mimic in Windows Explorer, since spelling mistakes will cause your mimic navigation to fail This is to ensure that your mimic navigation will continue to work i.e. that any configured execute command behaviours open/close etc. the correct graphic forms. IMPORTANT: This graphic form name must not include the .mim nor the .xaml extensions – in other words, if the mimic is called Pic1 then this graphic form name should be Pic1 and not Pic1.mim nor Pic1.mim.xaml. To rename a graphic forms later: right-click on this graphic form or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Rename . - Ensure that this graphic form is opened and is currently displayed within the central Design workspace window. - Import the XAML mimic into this graphic form, in one of two ways: - Right click on this graphic form select Import Adroit Classic -> Mimic menu items. - From the Designer ribbon, select the Import tab and click the Import Mimic tool. This tab of the ribbon is only displayed when a graphic form is open. In the displayed Import Mimic dialog: - Click the browse button to the right of the Browse in a XAML file to import field and select the saved .XAML mimic document. By default, any images in this mimic that does not have a specified path, is assumed to be in the folder specified by the Base Url i.e. for images field. - Click the Advanced View button. - Click the Behaviour Settings tab: - Ensure that the Adroit DataSource field, specifies the Adroit datasource that connects to the Agent Server containing the Adroit tags (agents) referenced by the configured behaviours of this imported mimic. - Ensure that the Project Name field specifies the name of the project that contains or will contain the imported mimics (graphic forms) that are interacted with (opened, closed etc.) via any Execute Command Behaviours of this imported mimic. By default, this is the name of the project in which the currently opened graphic form is in. - We typically recommend that you leave ALL the settings of the Import Settings tab at their default values. More details: Ensure the Enable Vectors Grouping checkbox is checked and the Keep the Import the following XAML Controls As: settings specify Vectors to maintain the currently configured object ordering and the look and feel of the imported mimic and to prevent major post-importing configuration. ONLY use the Adjust Font sizes By setting when the font sizes of the Text objects of the imported mimic are incorrect. In this case use this setting to enlarge or reduce the font sizes as a positive or negative percentage or font point size and then import this mimic again until you are content with the displayed fonts.

IMPORTANT: This especially applies to any template mimics that are being exported, because currently if their Behaviours are edited after importing then they lose their functionality and need to be re-configured. More details: during the importing process, SmartUI Template Sets are configured (which employ alternate sets of spider silks for each template), but when these Behaviours are configured after importing, their configuration is automatically changed to use SmartUI Templates instead (which uses a totally different mechanism of templatization, namely the use of graphic form aliases) This means that unless the appropriate aliases are configured, then this Behaviour loses ALL of its functionality until the necessary aliases are configured appropriately. For details, see SmartUI Templates. - Convert all Operator Action Behaviours that use Ramp as a % to use unit(s) instead, since the % Ramp value increment/ decrement is not currently supported. - Ensure that the Text picture elements have not been stretched in the Classic UI and that any stretched Text picture elements are replaced with a Text picture element of the correct size that has its font set to the required size. So that these do not need to be corrected after importing. Back to top

Title: Save your mimic in the Classic UI to a XAML file
Steps:
Save your mimic in the Classic UI, as normal Select Yes to the confirmation dialog to also create a XAML file. This XAML file is created in the same folder in which the mimic is created and simply appends the .XAML extension to the end of this name after the .mim. If this confirmation dialog is NOT displayed, then configure the Adroit 10 Classic UI to save mimics as XAML files (and trends as XML files) first, as follows: - Launch the SmartUI Config Editor - Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Locate the Legacy UI Parameters: group at the bottom of this dialog. - Ensure that the Enable Xaml Saving checkbox is checked. Note: You need to RESTART the Classic UI after changing this setting. Tip: You can also automatically export ALL mimics in a specific folder to XAML , by starting the Classic UI from the command line and using the <path_name>\*.mim parameter, as follows: if the required path to your mimics and/or path to the Classic UI has spaces then use double quotes e.g. "C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\adroit.exe" "E:\My Documents\Mimics\*.mim", otherwise omit these e.g. adroit c:\adroitproject\mimics\*.mim. The *.mim command line parameter exports all the mimics in the specified folder to XAML and then shuts down the Classic UI. Ensure that the XAML conversion was successful, as follows: After exporting the mimic to XAML, open the .XAML file in Internet Explorer, by double clicking on it, to see if anything went wrong during the XAML conversion process, as follows:. - If the XAML conversion was successful, then the mimic is displayed in Internet Explorer - If the XAML conversion was unsuccessful, then the mimic is NOT displayed and instead the first exception that was encountered is displayed, for instance “Font size must be greater than 0”. In this case, attend to this problem in your Classic UI mimic and then re-save this mimic to XAML and re-open it in Internet Explorer – if necessary reiterate this process until your mimic is displayed in Internet Explorer. Back to top

Title: Import this mimic into the SmartUI
Steps:
- If necessary, create the required project in the Enterprise manager. For details, see Creating new projects. IMPORTANT: Avoid using folder structures in this project as this will cause the navigation to fail. If a folder structure is used, then post importing configuration is required to ensure the Execute Command behaviours point to the correct files. - Add a graphic form to this project, as follows: right-click on the project name or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Create Graphic Form . Rename this graphic form to match the original Classic UI mimic file name. Tip: It is recommended to copy and paste this name from the mimic in Windows Explorer, since spelling mistakes will cause your mimic navigation to fail This is to ensure that your mimic navigation will continue to work i.e. that any configured execute command behaviours open/close etc. the correct graphic forms. IMPORTANT: This graphic form name must not include the .mim nor the .xaml extensions – in other words, if the mimic is called Pic1 then this graphic form name should be Pic1 and not Pic1.mim nor Pic1.mim.xaml. To rename a graphic forms later: right-click on this graphic form or its icon and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Rename . - Ensure that this graphic form is opened and is currently displayed within the central Design workspace window. - Import the XAML mimic into this graphic form, in one of two ways: - Right click on this graphic form select Import Adroit Classic -> Mimic menu items. - From the Designer ribbon, select the Import tab and click the Import Mimic tool. This tab of the ribbon is only displayed when a graphic form is open. In the displayed Import Mimic dialog: - Click the browse button to the right of the Browse in a XAML file to import field and select the saved .XAML mimic document. By default, any images in this mimic that does not have a specified path, is assumed to be in the folder specified by the Base Url i.e. for images field. - Click the Advanced View button. - Click the Behaviour Settings tab: - Ensure that the Adroit DataSource field, specifies the Adroit datasource that connects to the Agent Server containing the Adroit tags (agents) referenced by the configured behaviours of this imported mimic. - Ensure that the Project Name field specifies the name of the project that contains or will contain the imported mimics (graphic forms) that are interacted with (opened, closed etc.) via any Execute Command Behaviours of this imported mimic. By default, this is the name of the project in which the currently opened graphic form is in. - We typically recommend that you leave ALL the settings of the Import Settings tab at their default values. More details: Ensure the Enable Vectors Grouping checkbox is checked and the Keep the Import the following XAML Controls As: settings specify Vectors to maintain the currently configured object ordering and the look and feel of the imported mimic and to prevent major post-importing configuration. ONLY use the Adjust Font sizes By setting when the font sizes of the Text objects of the imported mimic are incorrect. In this case use this setting to enlarge or reduce the font sizes as a positive or negative percentage or font point size and then import this mimic again until you are content with the displayed fonts.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Currently the conversion of Classic UI trends only caters for the basic trend configuration and hence there are a number of advanced trend settings are either not exported or are not imported, some of which are listed below: - The SmartUI Line chart control imports area plotting is imported as a normal line plot, in other words trended series that were filled in the Classic UI are not filled in the imported charting control in the SmartUI . - The imported Unit in the SmartUI Line chart control does not currently support value substitutions. - The SmartUI Line chartcontrol does not support multi state colors based on value. - The SmartUI Line chartcontrol does not import vertical and horizontal grid settings. - Only the Font settings for the time (X) axis are imported in the SmartUI Line chartcontrol. Therefore you will need to re-apply or re-configure these settings after you have converted your Classic UI trend as a Line chart control in a SmartUI graphic form.

Copying form components Top Copying form components You can copy added form components either within the same graphic form or to another graphic form.

Title: Copying form components
Copying form components Top Copying form components You can copy added form components either within the same graphic form or to another graphic form. Once copied these form components can then be modified as normal. Click for more details: In addition to copying the selected form components themselves, you can ALSO copy any spiders that have been associated with the properties of these form components and/or any Behaviours that have been configured for this form component - which further reduces the amount of designing required. To copy BOTH the form components and their associated spiders and/or Behaviours: - Open the graphic form containing the form components you want to duplicate. For details, see Opening graphic forms . - Select the required controls or graphic elements. For details, see Selecting multiple controls or Selecting multiple graphic elements . - Either right click and select the Copy with Spiders or Copy with Behaviours option or hold down the SHIFT key and then select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Copy from the Clipboard group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. - If necessary, open the graphic form in which these form components are required or if the graphic form is already open, then select its tab, so that it is currently displayed in the Design workspace . - Select Paste from the Clipboard group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. The pasted selected form components will be offset, so that they are placed to the right and below their original position, by a grid width and height in this graphic form. This ALSO does the following in the Spider Configuration tool window associated with this graphic form: - adds and renames the spiders, associated with these pasted form components. - creates new Behaviours for the pasted form components, with new spiders and new Behaviour regions, which adhere to the following naming convention: ControlName.BehaviourName. Tip: It is also possible to use the keyboard shortcuts of SHIFT+CTRL+C and CTRL+V, to copy and paste these form components too. Only ensure that the required graphic form is currently selected before using the CTRL+V shortcut. To ONLY copy form components without their associated spiders and/or Behaviours: - Open the graphic form containing the form components you want to duplicate. For details, see Opening graphic forms . - Select the required controls or graphic elements. For details, see Selecting multiple controls or Selecting multiple graphic elements . - Either right click and select the Copy option or select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Copy from the Clipboard group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. This will ONLY copy the selected form components and not any spiders and/or Behaviours that have been connected to their properties. - If necessary, open the graphic form in which these form components are required or if the graphic form is already open, then select its tab, so that it is currently displayed in the Design workspace . - Select Paste from the Clipboard group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. The pasted selected form components will be offset, so that they are placed to the right and below their original position, by a grid width and height in this graphic form. Tip: It is also possible to use the keyboard shortcuts of CTRL+C and CTRL+V, to copy and paste these form components too. Only ensure that the required graphic form is currently selected before using the CTRL+V shortcut.

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Digital Input Boolean The digital (Boolean) value, which will be monitored and recorded by the counters in the Outputs section. Start Stop Boolean Use to start (1) and stop (0) the monitoring period of the selected Digital Input . For details, see Monitoring digital values . Reset Boolean [A Button] To reset all of the outputs to 0 and restart their counters during the monitored period of the selected Digital Input . For details, see Resetting the counters . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Note: At any time during the monitoring period, click the Reset button to reset all of these output values to 0 and to restart their counters. Output Data Function Off Counts Double The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0) over the monitored period or since the last reset. Current Off Time TimeSpan When the Digital Input is currently in the Off state (0), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the Off state. The time is displayed in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. Last Off Time TimeSpan This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0). The time is displayed in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. Total Off Time TimeSpan The total time at the Digital Input has spent in the Off state (0), this is effectively the sum of all the Last Off Time periods during the monitored period or since the last reset. The time is displayed in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. On Counts Double The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the On state (1) over the monitored period or since the last reset.

Current On Time TimeSpan When the Digital Input is currently in the On state (1), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the On state.

Create Table queries Top Create Table queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Create Table queries
Create Table queries Top Create Table queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Create Table Queries can create tables in the database with specific structures. Click for more information: If necessary specify primary keys and lookup columns (foreign keys) for fields. By parameterizing the table and/or field names you can create a library of common table configurations, in which you only perform the laborious configuration once for all. Note1: If necessary, parameterise the table and/or the field names to specify them before performing the query. Note2: This query is ONLY able to create a SINGLE table. To add and configure a Create Table query: Add a Create Table Query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. - If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option.

Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases.

Title: Create Table queries
Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query. For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Create Table query: Note: This configuration dialog does NOT provide a Preview button to prevent incorrect tables from being added to your database. Therefore please ensure that you configure the values for these fields correctly. The Tables and Fields dialog is displayed. - Specify the table name. - To specify a fixed (unchangeable) name for this table, enter this name in the Specify a New Table Name edit box. - To specify a parameter for this table, so that it can be changed before the query is performed, check the Parameterised Table Name checkbox. This is recommended if you need to create more than one table with the identical structure. Note1: This ignores any name added to the Specify a New Table Name edit box. Note2: If necessary edit the parameter name for this table in the Custom Query dialog. - Specify the columns (fields) of this table, as follows: To add a column (field) to this table: - To specify a fixed (unchangeable) name for this column (field), enter this name in the Column Name entry. - To specify a parameter for this column, so that it can be changed before the query is performed, check the Parameterised checkbox. This is only recommended if you have parameterised the Table name and different tables required identically configured fields with different names. Note1: This ignores any name added to the Column Name entry. Note2: If necessary edit the parameter name for this column in the Custom Query dialog. - If necessary, select the required data type for the values of this column (field) from the Type list box. - If necessary, change the default width of the selected data type in the size entry. - If necessary, specify whether this column is able to have NULL values or not, by checking or clearing the Allow Nulls checkbox accordingly. Typically null values are NOT required in primary or foreign key columns. To remove a column (field) from this table: - Select the row that defines this column and press the DELETE key.

To set or clear a column (field) as a primary key for this table: Typically primary key columns have unique values, which are used to identify rows in this table.

Title: Create Table queries
To set or clear a column (field) as a primary key for this table: Typically primary key columns have unique values, which are used to identify rows in this table. - Right-click the row that defines this column and select Set Primary Key . - This adds or removes the PK row identifier. To assign a default value for a column (field): - Select the required row and enter it into the Default Value field. Note: Please ensure that you specify the correct default values these fields, as there is no error checking. To automatically increment the value of a NUMERIC column (field): Typically required for primary key fields containing ID numbers. - Select the row of that defines this column that has a numerical data Type . - If necessary, select the Column tab below the list of columns. - Select Yes from the Identity list box. Note: Select Yes(Not For Replication) when you want the identity values of all the replicated rows to remain unchanged, while the identity values of rows native to this table will change as required. - Specify the number to start incrementing from, in the Identity Seed spin control (either by typing it in directly or using the arrows to select it). - Specify how many numbers to increment each value by in the Identity Increment spin control (either by typing it in directly or using the arrows to select it). For instance the default of 1 creates consecutive numbers. To configure a column (field) to be a foreign key: Typically, foreign keys are created to create a relationship with another table. - Select the row of that defines this column. - If necessary, select the Column tab below the list of columns. - Check the Lookup Column checkbox. This displays the Lookup tab. - Select the Lookup tab below the list of columns. The Lookup Field tree view displays all the tables and fields of the database connected to this OLE DB datasource. - Select the field (from another table) that this column should be linked to. - If necessary use one or both of the following rules to ensure that values in this column remain synchronised with the lookup field's values: Note: The default NO ACTION rule does not attempt to keep the values of these fields synchronised. On Update Rule: when the reference ID of the lookup table changes then CASCADE ensures that any changes made will cascade down to this table.

On Delete Rule: when the reference ID of the lookup table is deleted then CASCADE ensures that the changes made will cascade down to this table and this value will become NULL.

Title: To create an alarm type:
Steps:
- Open the Edit Alarm Type dialog, using one of the following methods: When editing the Alarm agent: this allows you to configure agent types for all your agents from one dialog. - Edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: - If necessary, add an Alarm agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - Select the Types tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - Select the required agent type from the Agent Type drop down list box. - Click the Add an entry button. When alarming a specific agent: this allows you to add specific or unique alarm types, when the need arises to the applicable agent (type). - Display the Alarming dialog for the required agent, as follows: - If necessary, add the required agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Alarm... menu item to display the Alarming dialog. - Select the required Alarm agent. - Click the button above the Available alarm types list. - Type the required name for this alarm type in the Alarm Type edit field. Tip: Provide a descriptive name for this condition, so that it is easy for engineers and operators to recognise. - Select the status bits (check their checkboxes) from the Alarm Trigger section that must be simultaneously ENABLED (set) enabled in order for this condition to occur. Note1: ALL the status bits that should not be used for alarm type definitions are disabled. Note2: ONLY if you need to specify a condition in which specific status bits are DISABLED (off) then ensure that the Alarm Off States checkbox is checked. - If necessary, specify which values of this agent (and their order) should be reported when this condition occurs. These slots and their order are specified in the Reported Data section of this dialog, as follows: To add a reported slot: - Double-click the required slot/s from the Available list box. This adds them to the Current list box, which displays the slots in the order in which they will be reported. Tip: You can also select the required slot in the Available list box and click the << button. To change the order of a reported slot: - If necessary, remove this slot from the Current list, by double-clicking it. Tip: You can also select the required slot in the Current list box and click the >> button. - Click the slot in the Current list that the required slot should be ABOVE. - Select the required slot in the Available list box - Click the << Insert button This adds the selected slot ABOVE the slot that was selected in the Current list. To insert a new slot into an existing list of reported slots: - Click the slot in the Current list that the required slot should be ABOVE. - Select the required slot in the Available list box - Click the << Insert button This adds the selected slot ABOVE the slot that was selected in the Current list. - Click on the OK buttons to close the open dialogs. For further details about alarm types and their purpose in alarming, see About alarm types . -->
