Title: To create an object instance:
Display the Create New Instance configuration dialog for the required object instance: From the Object Model datasource in the Enterprise Manager: (missing or bad snippet) - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the Object Model datasource (by using the arrow or double clicking it). - If necessary, expand the Templates folder. - Right click the required template and select Create new instance of this template . This displays the Create New Instance configuration dialog. From the Context View window: - If necessary, select the Default context from the list of contexts to the left of the bottom tool bar of this window and click the Edit button. - If necessary, Add new user node and/or expand the necessary node . - Right click the node and select Create new instance . Use the modified Data Element browser dialog to select the required template. Tip: You could also drag an existing Object Model template from the Enterprise Manager onto this node directly to skip the step where you need to specify the required template. This displays the Deployment Options configuration dialog. For more details about the Default context of the Context View window, see Editing the Default context .

By default the New instance name is the name of the template, prefaced by "INST_" instead of "TPL_", which you can edit as needed.

Title: Specifications
By default the New instance name is the name of the template, prefaced by "INST_" instead of "TPL_", which you can edit as needed. Typically you will need to edit this name to provide the unique, detailed name for this object. To ensure that the specified Template is the template that you want to create an instance of, hover the mouse over this template and any child templates that have been specified in the Template hierarchy tree, which displays a preview of what each template looks like. Note: Only the parent template has the specified instance name, whereas any child templates retain their template names. The Attributes for: table displays any attributes specified by the selected template along with their default values that you can change as needed, such as its power rating. Furthermore you can also add additional instance-specific attributes (in other words attributes that only apply or further describe this instance). (missing or bad snippet) Tip: Typing in the first letter of an existing attribute immediately inserts the full text of this attribute name. (missing or bad snippet) Note: You can only delete the additional instance-specific attributes that you add. Click Next , once you are happy with this instance name and its specified attributes. Click Cancel , if you selected the incorrect template.

In this step you need to specify and configure the agents that each template referenced by this object instance requires.

Title: Configuration
In this step you need to specify and configure the agents that each template referenced by this object instance requires. Firstly, this page displays a table containing a separate group of agents required for each template that this object references. These group names use dot notation to represent the template names specified in the Template hierarchy tree of the previous page. Clicking a group, displays more details concerning this template in the Instance tab of the Configuration pane below this table. Note: The Datasource property indicates the name of the Adroit datasource (Agent Server) that is used to validate, create and configure these agents. Any template containing a substitution is prefixed with the icon that indicates that values need to be inserted for these substitutions. Note: You cannot leave this page until every icon has been removed by providing the required substitution values. If necessary, click the required group heading to expand it (or click the Expand All button to expand all the groups at once). Then click either the Substitution Names or Substitution Values cell in the row where a icon is displayed to open the Substitution Values dialog, in which you need to type in the required Value for each substitution. Use the <- and -> buttons to quickly navigate to the previous or next substituted value. Note: Multiple substitutions and their values are separated by commas in their cells. Tip: Use the Name cell to determine the eventual format of the entire substituted name. The background color of the Name cell indicates whether the resultant agent name already exists or is new, as follows: Typically you will specify new tags that does not already exist. However, you can also specify an existing tag, which you need to reuse, such as an AlarmManagement agent. Once an agent name has been specified, then use the Configuration pane below this table, to configure its available Slots , Scanning , Logging and/or Alarming as predefined by the template/s, by clicking the relevant tabs. However, instead of having to query each agent individually for their scan addresses, click the Bulk scan address editing button in the top right corner to view to configure all the scan addresses associated with this object in a single list view. The Bulk scan address editing dialog displays the list of all the scan addresses that are classified by the Device , Tag and Address columns.

Either change each Address manually, by typing the required entry into each cell in this list.

Title: Configuration
Either change each Address manually, by typing the required entry into each cell in this list. Or use a text file editor of your choice change these addresses, as follows: - Click the Copy addresses to clipboard button. Tip: You can also select all or deselect all rows by clicking the top left cell in the list (and use the CTRL+C shortcut to copy these to the clipboard). - Open MS Excel or the text file editor of your choice. - Paste these fields into it. - Bulk configure the Address column as needed. - Select ALL of these columns and copy them. - Click the Paste addresses from clipboard button. Click Next , once you have replaced all the icons with valid values and have configured each of the agents appropriately.

In this step you need to specify and configure the devices that each template will use to scan their values, which are listed in the Devices list.

Title: How to set up Creating an Object Instance
In this step you need to specify and configure the devices that each template will use to scan their values, which are listed in the Devices list. The background color of the Device cell indicates whether the current device already exists or is new, as follows: IMPORTANT: When the background color is red ( ) for the device then Setup required means that you need to manually add this device name via the Config Editor first before you can continue. For more details, see Adding a Device to an installed Protocol Driver . This typically only occurs when a template uses a protocol driver that is not natively supported by the Object Model. Note: If the device already exists then any specified properties are NOT applied to it during the deployment of this object. If the specified new or existing device is natively supported by the Object Model, then you can configure their Primary and/or Secondary device-specific Properties . IMPORTANT: The onus rests on the user adding this instance to possess the technical know-how to determine which of these device-specific values need to be specified! Note: If the device already exists then any specified properties are NOT applied to it during the deployment of this object. Click Next , once all the required devices have been added and have had their required properties specified.

This is the final step, which can create the instance of this object using the settings that you have specified.

Title: Deployment Options:

IMPORTANT: When deploying a template the following rule is applied, if a referenced agent exists then NONE of its properties will be changed. Since if the template is being deployed on a running plant it is important that it does not affect any existing values for safety reasons. The following two options are provided: Deploy now : After creating and saving the instance(s), the instance(s) will also be deployed to the relevant Agent Server Deploy later (the default option): Only create and save the instance(s), but deploy later by right-clicking on the saved instance. Title: To create an object instance:
From the Object Model datasource in the Enterprise Manager Display the Create New Instance configuration dialog for the required object instance: - Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager tab. - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - The connection name is prefixed with the SmartUI Server name. - Expand the remaining category folders Datasources > Object Model > Templates . - Right-click on the required template in the list, then select Create new instance of this template . - The Create New Instance configuration dialog opens. From the Context View window: - Select Context View tab at the bottom of the right-side panel in the Default Layout window. - Select the Default context from the list of contexts in bottom toolbar of this window then click the Edit button. - If required, Add new user node and expand the necessary node . - Right-click the node and select Create new instance . - Use the modified Data Element browser dialog to select the required template. - Tip: You could also drag an existing Object Model template from the Enterprise Manager onto this node directly to skip the step where you need to specify the required template. - The Deployment Options configuration dialog opens. For more information about the Default context of the Context View window, see Editing the Default context . Step 1: Create New Instance

. - By default, the New instance name is assigned the name of the template and is prefixed with "INST_" instead of "TPL_".

Title: Specifications
. - By default, the New instance name is assigned the name of the template and is prefixed with "INST_" instead of "TPL_". - You can edit the name as you prefer. - Typically, you edit the name to create a unique and detailed name for this object. - To ensure that the specified Template is the template that you want to use to create an instance. - Hover the mouse pointer over the template name or any child template that is listed in the Template hierarchy tree. - A preview image of each template is displayed. - Note: Only the parent template has the specified instance name, whereas any child templates retain their template names. - The table labelled Attributes for displays any attributes specified for the selected template including their default values - You may change the value as required, such as its power rating. - You can also add additional instance-specific attributes that only apply to or further describe this instance. - Any custom attributes that you add are saved in your current profile and are available for future use to all users who use your profile. - You can click the Reset the attribute library button to clear the custom attributes that are specified for the current profile. - Note: This only removes the custom attributes from the list, which will no longer be available for selection. It does not remove any custom attributes that you have previously added to deployed objects, so these still appear in the Context View window. Tip: Typing in the first letter of an existing attribute immediately inserts the full text of this attribute name. - The Object Model datasource then uses the specified attributes to configure the Context View window automatically. - When object instances are deployed, each Name of their defined attributes creates a different context (tree-view) in the Context View window and instances that have the same Value of an attribute are grouped in this context. - A simple one-level deep tree-view is created for each attribute Name , in which a node is created for every unique value specified for this attribute. - Important: Only the Value and Instance names can be searched in the Context View and not the attribute Name , which is added to the list of contexts at the bottom of the Context View . Note: You can only delete the additional instance-specific attributes that you add.

Click Next , once you are satisfied with the instance name and its specified attributes.

Title: Specifications
Click Next , once you are satisfied with the instance name and its specified attributes. Click Cancel , if you selected the incorrect template. Step 2: SCADA Configuration: In this step, you specify and configure the agents that are associated with each template referenced by this object instance. - The SCADA Configuration dialog displays a table containing the group of agents required for each template referenced by the object. These group names use dot notation to represent the template names as specified in the Template hierarchy tree shown on the first ‘Create New Instance’ dialog. - Selecting the INST_<GroupName> group displays the instance details for the template in the Instance tab of the Configuration pane below the Agents table. - Note: The Datasource property indicates the name of the Adroit datasource (Agent Server) that is used to validate, create and configure these agents. - If each group heading does not display a list of agents, then click the Expand All button to expand all the groups to display the list of required template agents. - If any template row containing a substitution displays a icon, it is an indication that some substitution values require insertion. - To correct the value, click either the Substitution Names or Substitution Values cell in the row where a icon is displayed to open the Substitution Values dialog. - Type in the Value for each required substitution. - Note: You cannot proceed from this dialog until you have inserted all the required substitution values for each row containing a icon. - Use the < and > buttons to navigate to the previous or next substituted value. - Note: Commas separate multiple substitutions and their values in their cells. - Tip: Use the Name cell to determine the eventual format of the entire substituted name. - The background colour of the Name cell indicates whether the resultant agent name already exists or is new, as follows: - Typically, you specify new tags that do not already exist. However, you can also specify an existing tag, which you want to reuse, such as an AlarmManagement agent.

Once an agent name is specified, then use the Configuration pane below the table to configure its Scanning , Logging , Alarming , and Slots as predefined in the templates by selecting the relevant tabs.

Title: Configuration
Once an agent name is specified, then use the Configuration pane below the table to configure its Scanning , Logging , Alarming , and Slots as predefined in the templates by selecting the relevant tabs. - Instead of querying each agent individually for their scan addresses, click the Bulk scan address editing button to configure all the scan addresses associated with this object in a single list view. - The Bulk scan address editing dialog displays the list of all the scan addresses that are classified by the Device , Tag and Address columns. - You can also change each Address manually, by typing the required entry into each cell in this list. - Alternatively, you may use a text file editor of your choice to change these addresses. - Click the Copy addresses to clipboard button. - Tip: You can also select all or deselect all rows by clicking the top-left cell in the list and use the CTRL+C to copy these to the clipboard. - Open MS Excel or the text file editor of your choice. - Paste the clipboard into it. - Bulk edit the Address column as needed. - Select all of these columns and copy them. - Click the Paste addresses from clipboard button. - Click Next , once you have replaced all the icons with valid values and have configured each of the agents appropriately. Step 3: Device Setup In this step, you specify and configure the devices that each template uses to scan their values. These devices are listed in the Devices table. - The background colour of the Device cell indicates whether the current device already exists or is new, as follows: - Important: If the background colour of the device row is red (Setup required ) for the device, then you must manually add this device-name via the Config Editor first before you can continue. This typically only occurs when a template uses a protocol driver that is not natively supported by the Object Model. - For more information using the Config Editor , see Adding a Device to an installed Protocol Driver . - Note: If the device already exists then any specified properties are not applied to it during the deployment of this object. - If the Object Model natively supports the specified new or existing device, then you can configure their Primary and Secondary device-specific Properties .

- Important: The onus rests on the user, who is adding this instance, to possess the technical know-how to determine which of these device-specific values need to be specified.

Title: Configuration
- Important: The onus rests on the user, who is adding this instance, to possess the technical know-how to determine which of these device-specific values need to be specified. - Note: If the device already exists then any specified properties are not applied to it during the deployment of this object. - Click Next , once all the required devices have been added and have had their required properties specified. Step 4: DBLogs This step only applies if one or more DBLog agents are selected for this template. - You can configure each of the selected DBLog agents in the DBLogs list. - You can also view which slots of the other agents in this object are allocated, to each DBLog agent, in the Tags table below. - You can also see if you can configure their Deadband . - Click Next , once all the deadbands of the values in the DBLog agents are correctly specified. Step 5: Graphic Substitutions This step is typically only required when you have changed the substitution names when creating the instance and the name of the substitution used in the SCADA Configuration step differs from the name used in the referenced wizard. - Note: You cannot proceed from this dialog until you have inserted all the required substitution values for each row containing a icon. - Select the required row in the Graphic Form list that contains a icon and then the Value cell in the Substitutions table below and type in the required value. - Note: The background colour of the Result cell shows whether the specified value is . - Tip: If you keep the same substitution names as those used in the wizard, this makes it easier to implement your instances, since you only need to configure these substitutions once ; otherwise you must specify substitutions both during the SCADA Configuration and Graphical Substitution stages. - Click Next , once you have replaced all the icons with their required substitution values. Step 6: Deployment Options This is the final step, which lets you deploy the instance of this object using the settings that you have specified. - Important: When deploying a template, the following rule is applied. If a referenced agent exists then none of its properties are changed. The reason is if the template is currently in use on a running plant, it is critically important that it does not affect any existing values for safety reasons.

- The following two options are provided: - Deploy now : After creating and saving the instances, the instances are deployed to the relevant Agent Server.

Title: Configuration
- The following two options are provided: - Deploy now : After creating and saving the instances, the instances are deployed to the relevant Agent Server. - Deploy later (the default option) : Only create and save the instances, but deploy later by right-clicking on the saved instance. For example, you may want to create the instance of an object at another site. - If you select the Deploy now option, then the On deployment group is displayed. - When deployed, this object and all of its configuration are created immediately, such as: - Any new agents. - Any new devices and their scanning. - The specified alarming, logging and DBLog agents. - Important: When the global destinations (i.e. the Output / Event Logs categories) of the specified alarm routes contain agents that do not exist in the Agent Server then the deployment is not created as these agents could cause potential issues. - The Save Agent Server checkbox is also selected by default which saves this configuration to the Agent Database file of the Agent Server of the specified Adroit datasource . - To run the script defined for this object, select the Run Script checkbox as this is not selected, by default. - Note: If the Run Script checkbox is disabled (greyed out) , then the script was not defined or did not compile successfully. - Note: Currently only the script defined for this object may be run. Any scripts defined for child objects are ignored, even when no script is defined for the parent object. - Tip: Use the View button to display the associated script action before it is run. - Perform a partial deployment at this time, by clearing some of the following checkboxes: - Create agents - Create devices and scanning - Start devices - Create alarming - Important: When the global destinations (i.e. the Output / Event Logs categories) of the specified alarm routes contain agents that do not exist in the Agent Server then the deployment is not created as these agents could cause potential issues. - Create data logging - Create DB logging - Note: This configuration is only saved to the Agent Database file of the Agent Server of the Adroit datasource when you select the Save Agent Server on deployment completion checkbox. - Click the Finish button. In the case of a partially deployed or non-deployed instance, you can deploy it fully or partially at a later stage. For more information about later deployment, see Deploying an Object Instance .

- If you selected any of the deployment checkboxes, then the Object Model Deployment Status progress dialog appears.

Title: Configuration
- If you selected any of the deployment checkboxes, then the Object Model Deployment Status progress dialog appears. - For more information about the deployment status, see the Object Model Deployment Status dialog . - When you create an instance of an object template, you can view the template- and object-specific attributes that you defined along with their configured values for the object. - For more information about defined attributes, see Viewing the defined attributes of an Object Instance . -->

Open a graphic form that contains an instance of a wizard for which the necessary SCADA configuration (the scanning logging and alarming etc.) and any other agents that this object needs has been created and is working well.

Title: To create an object template:
Open a graphic form that contains an instance of a wizard for which the necessary SCADA configuration (the scanning logging and alarming etc.) and any other agents that this object needs has been created and is working well. Right click this wizard instance in the Designer and select Create Object Template . This displays the first page of the Create Object Template configuration dialog: IMPORTANT: if you Cancel the configuration dialog then you will lose any configuration that you have done. However, you can use the Previous and Next buttons to navigate back and forward between the steps, which retains the current configuration of each step. To edit an existing object template: (missing or bad snippet) - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the Object Model datasource (by using the arrow or double clicking it). - If necessary, expand the Templates folder. - Right click the required template and select Edit . This displays the first page of the Edit Template configuration dialog: IMPORTANT: if you Cancel the configuration dialog then you will lose any configuration that you have done. However, you can use the Previous and Next buttons to navigate back and forward between the steps, which retains the current configuration of each step.

By default the Template Name is the name of the wizard that the selected wizard instance is an instance of, prefaced by "TPL_".

Title: Step 1 of 12: Validate Wizard Data Elements
By default the Template Name is the name of the wizard that the selected wizard instance is an instance of, prefaced by "TPL_". This wizard is further described by the Path edit field of the Primary wizard tab, which displays the exact path to this wizard when the mouse hovers over its name and/or representation. You can also specify a Template Descriptor , which is the last portion of the default deployed object name, that relates to the object itself and not its context. Typically, this is a standardised abbreviation for this object, such as PMP for pump, after which you typically need to provide the unique, detailed name for this object e.g. PMP_SUMP_01. By default a number of predefined descriptors have been created for you. However you can add a custom descriptor: To add a custom template descriptor: click the list button to the right of the Template Descriptor field and then click the Add new descriptor... button at the bottom of this dialog, in which case you need to specify their required Category and Description , in addition to the required Descriptor - so that they can be easily identified in this list of predefined descriptors. The Wizard Data Elements table should contain the valid names of the specified data elements used for the substitutable values of this primary wizard, so no further configuration should be required. This displays all the data elements from all the datasources that apply to the specified wizard, however only the Adroit -specific data elements will be processed, since the purpose of a template is to specify the necessary SCADA configuration for this primary wizard. If necessary, click the Associated wizards tab to specify related wizards that use the SAME substitutable values as this primary wizard (or LESS of these substitutable values). Note: Another wizard can ONLY be associated when it has the SAME or LESS substitutions as the Primary wizard. Examples of valid Associated wizards: - if you have created different graphical orientations for the same item of equipment like a left or right or top or bottom view, which use the SAME substitutable values - if you have a simpler view of the primary wizard, in other words a wizard that uses LESS of the substitutable values Click Next , once you are happy with the template name and have specified any associated wizards.

text:
By default the Agents tree displays the list of Adroit tags directly referenced by the wizard.

Title: Step 2 of 12: Select Agents
Steps:
By default the Agents tree displays the list of Adroit tags directly referenced by the wizard. If an agent is used by (referenced within) another agent, such as an expression, these agents are added to the Related Agents list. Note: Only DBLog agents that have been enabled will appear in this list, when they reference one of the selected agents. Then the template designer needs to decide which of the agent relationships are required by the template, as these intra-agent relationships may become complex depending upon how nested they are. By default only the first level of agents are linked to by default. This task is best suited to a user who has an in-depth knowledge of how their SCADA system (Agent Server) has been designed. You may also need to manually add any agents not directly linked to the agents in this wizard, which are also required. Such as Script agents or an AlarmManagement agent etc, by clicking the Add agent button and selecting these agents. Any added agent, both existing or created at this time, is displayed in blue . IMPORTANT: Currently the Object Model only supports the following agent types: alarm, alarmmanagement, alarmlist, analog, beeper, counter, dblog, digital, eventoutput, expression, icmp, integer, marshal, maxdemand, oee, pid, real, shift, snmpmgr, statistical, string, stringlist, text and timer. Note: Do NOT include the agents used to directly alarm, log or scan the agent. Tip: You can also create agents at this stage, if necessary. Click Next , once all the relevant agents have been specified.

This step is where you decide which portions of the agent name you want to be substitutable or which may need to be variable when creating instances of this object.

Title: Step 3 of 12: Assign Agent Substitutions
This step is where you decide which portions of the agent name you want to be substitutable or which may need to be variable when creating instances of this object. So that they adhere to any tag naming conventions that are applicable. Typically the substitutions for all the values used within the referenced wizard are listed here, prefixed by the Adroit datasource name. Tip: If you keep the SAME substitution names as those used in the wizard, this will make it easier to implement your instances, since you will only need to configure these substitutions ONCE, otherwise you will need to specify substitutions both during the SCADA Configuration and Graphical Substitution stages. Unless the substitution included the datasource name, in which case and for any manually added agents, the tag name is used instead and you need to manually add the required substitutions. You can also modify the existing substitutions at this point too, if needed. IMPORTANT: Any tag that is NOT substituted will be referenced by ALL the instances of this template. Note: Templates do not support the obtaining of tags from two different Adroit datasources - all the specified tags need to exist on the same Agent Server. In this case, double click the row containing the required agent and then specify each required substitution within curly brackets {...} in the Substitutions dialog. For instance, if there is a plant area code and an equipment code : {PlantAreaCode}_{EquipmentCode}.value Alternatively you can use a single substitution for both the agent name and slot value, such as {AnalogTag} Note: It is not possible to substitute the Adroit datasource name, however you can specify which Adroit datasource (Agent Server) you want to use when creating an instance of this template. Tip: When you click the Remove Substitution(s) button, this removes all the specified substitutions of the current row (only if one has been selected) replacing these substitutions with the name of the specified agent. Click Next , once all the relevant substitutions have been specified.

Typically each agent that is selected for use in this template, provides a filtered list of values (slots) that a user can configure.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Typically each agent that is selected for use in this template, provides a filtered list of values (slots) that a user can configure. Select the row containing an agent whose values (slots) you want to configure, which displays this filtered list in the Slots table below. Note: Any agent used to scan, log or alarm this agent are NOT configured at this point, such as the DBLog agent. However, since the purpose of the object template is to create specific objects to simplify the lives of your users, you need to decide how informed each of your users will be i.e. complex your objects need to be and therefore which of these values should be configured by selecting one of the following four configuration modes: - Agent Default (Not displayed) : these values are pre-configued for this object and are hidden from your users. - User Default (Read-only) : these values are pre-configued for this object and are also displayed for information purposes so that your users can still see them, even though they cannot edit them (like alarm limits or set points). - Editable with a default value : a recommended or suggested value is provided, which a user can change when adding an instance if they want to. This is the DEFAULT option. - Editable with NO default value : in this case users MUST specify these values when creating each instance. Note: This ONLY applies to values are NOT of type String (since a blank string can be valid). Click Next , once you have appropriately configured the slots of EACH agent referenced by this object.

This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being scanned and some of their commonly configured scanning settings, such as the device and the scan address in this device, along with the scan rate and deadband and the four scanning IO settings that affect how this value is scanned.

Title: Configuration
This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being scanned and some of their commonly configured scanning settings, such as the device and the scan address in this device, along with the scan rate and deadband and the four scanning IO settings that affect how this value is scanned. For more details, see "IO Flags" on page 1 . Note: If you want to make changes to these scanning settings, then ensure that the Update all devices on edit checkbox is checked Click Next , once you are happy with how each of these slots are being scanned.

This step allows you to configure the devices that values are being scanned to specify any default settings that will be used when creating an instance of this object.

Title: Configuration
This step allows you to configure the devices that values are being scanned to specify any default settings that will be used when creating an instance of this object. (missing or bad snippet) Note: This step may or may not be required, depending upon the requirements of your site and how you intend deploying the instances of this template. Select the row containing the device you want to configure, which displays the protocol driver-specific list of primary properties (settings) that can be specified for this device in Primary tab of the Properties table below. Either leave these properties blank - so that when creating an instance these will be specified or type in a default value as needed. Click Next , once you have appropriately configured the primary settings of all the required devices.

This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being datalogged and some of their commonly configured logging settings that affect how this value is being logged.

Title: Step 7 of 12: Data Logging Summary
This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being datalogged and some of their commonly configured logging settings that affect how this value is being logged. If necessary, you can modify one or more of these logging settings. Click Next , once you are happy with how each of these slots are being logged.

This step allows you to configure each of the selected DBLog agents and view which of the slots of the other selected agents have been allocated to each DBLog agent.

Title: Step 8 of 12: DBLogging Summary
This step allows you to configure each of the selected DBLog agents and view which of the slots of the other selected agents have been allocated to each DBLog agent. Select the row containing the DBLog agent you want to configure in the DBLogs list, which displays the slots of the other selected agents in the Tags table below, for information purposes only. Click Next , once you have appropriately configured the DBLog agents.

This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being alarmed and some of their commonly configured alarming settings that affect how this value is being alarmed.

Title: Step 9 of 12: Alarming Summary
This step lists all the slots (values) of the selected agents that are being alarmed and some of their commonly configured alarming settings that affect how this value is being alarmed. If necessary, you can modify one or more of these alarming settings. (missing or bad snippet) Click Next , once you are happy with how each of these slots are being alarmed.

This step allows you to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers that you can use to filter or classify the objects that you create in the Context View window.

Title: Step 10 of 12: Add Attributes
This step allows you to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers that you can use to filter or classify the objects that you create in the Context View window. Each specified attribute will apply to all the object instances and requires both a Name and a Value . Note: You cannot edit the Name once you create it, if you need to change it then delete this attribute and add it again. In other words these provide user-friendly terms that can be used to identify this object, such as equipment Type, whose value is motor or valve etc. or perhaps the power specification, such as 'kWh' and then specify the required value for each object. (missing or bad snippet) To add an attribute: - Click the button. - Either, type in a new attribute or click the drop-down list button on the right to select one of the existing attributes. Tip: Typing in the first letter of an existing attribute immediately inserts the full text of this attribute name. The following general attributes always appear in this list: Manufacturer; Description; Model and Type - Click the Finish button. (missing or bad snippet) Since these attributes and their values are displayed on the first page when creating an instance, you can add the default Description attribute to provide a detailed description of this template, so that a user can know that they are adding the required object instance. Note: The Delete button deletes the currently selected attribute, which by default is the last attribute in the list. Tip: In addition to these attributes, when adding an instance your users can specify additional instance-specific attributes too.

This step allows you to define logical parent-child relationships between this template (the parent) and any other related object model templates (the children), for example, by adding a PLC template to a Plant Area template.

Title: Step 11 of 12: Add Child Templates
This step allows you to define logical parent-child relationships between this template (the parent) and any other related object model templates (the children), for example, by adding a PLC template to a Plant Area template. These template relationships are only defined and viewable in the SmartUI and only affects Adroit as to which tags and their configuration to create when this template is deployed. IMPORTANT: Even though these child templates are deployed along with the parent template, you still need to separately drag them onto the required graphic forms in order to display them. Note: You need to create your lower-level or commonly used object templates first as you can only select existing templates as child templates. To add a template, simply click the Click here to add child template link and select the required template from the Templates list. This template is added to the root User folder of the Templates folder of the Object Model datasource in the Datasources category of the Enterprise Manager. (missing or bad snippet) Once you create an object template then any instance that you create of this template will provide the referenced wizard to provide the graphical components and uniquely configure the specified SCADA configuration for the process values that you specify for each object. For details, see Creating an Object Instance . (missing or bad snippet)

This step allows you to define a script for this Object Model Template, so that when deploying an instance users can run this script (only if it compiles successfully).

Title: Step 12 of 12: Run A Script
This step allows you to define a script for this Object Model Template, so that when deploying an instance users can run this script (only if it compiles successfully). Note: Currently only the script defined for the template can be run. Therefore any scripts defined for child templates will be ignored, even if no script is defined for the parent template. By default, the Include script in this template checkbox is unchecked. If this option is checked, then click the Launch Script Editor button to launch the Script Editor with the default (sample) script. Then edit and ideally compile this script and then close the Script Editor window to save this script. Note: A warning is displayed when the current script has not been compiled yet or has not compile successfully (so in this case click the Launch Script Editor button to edit and compile the script). However, this does not stop you from clicking the Finish button, but when an instance of this template is deployed it will NOT run this script (unless it has been edited in the interim to successfully compile). When deploying an instance of a template, a new checkbox is provided called Run Script , which is unchecked by default and will be greyed out if a script was not specified or when the specified script does not successfully compile. Click Finish , once you are happy with the configuration of this object template. Tip: You can use the Previous and Next buttons to navigate back and forward between the steps, to edit any of the steps before clicking Finish . -->

- You can also specify a Template Descriptor , which is the last portion of the default deployed object name and relates to the object itself but not its context.

Title: Template Descriptor
- You can also specify a Template Descriptor , which is the last portion of the default deployed object name and relates to the object itself but not its context. - Typically, this is a standardised abbreviation for this object, such as MOT for Motor, after which you typically need to provide the unique, detailed name for this object e.g. MOT_PUMP_01. - By default, a number of predefined descriptors are available to you. You can, however, create new custom descriptors . - Click the selection list button adjacent to the Template Descriptor box, then click Add new . - Select the required Category then type in a Description and the required Descriptor , ensuring that the new descriptor can be easily identified in the list of predefined descriptors. - Click OK to save.

The Data Elements table should contain the valid names of the specified data elements used for the substitutable values of this primary wizard, so no further configuration should be required.

Title: Wizard Data Elements
The Data Elements table should contain the valid names of the specified data elements used for the substitutable values of this primary wizard, so no further configuration should be required. - The table displays all the data elements from the datasources that apply to the specified wizard. - Only the Adroit -specific data elements will be processed. - The purpose of a template is to assign the necessary SCADA configuration for this primary wizard. - If necessary, click the Associated wizards tab to select related wizards that use the SAME substitutable values as this primary wizard (or LESS of these substitutable values) . - Caution: Another wizard can ONLY be associated when it has the SAME or LESS substitutions as the Primary wizard. - Examples of valid Associated wizards: - If you have created different graphical orientations for the same item of equipment, like a left or right or top or bottom view , which use the same substitutable values. - If you have a simpler view of the primary wizard, in other words a wizard that uses less of the substitutable values. - Click Next , when you are satisfied with the template name and any associated wizards. Step 2 of 12: Select Agents The Agent tree displays the list of Adroit tags directly referenced by the wizard. - Important: Currently the Object Model only supports the following agent types: alarm, alarmmanagement, alarmlist, analog, beeper, counter, dblog, digital, eventoutput, expression, icmp, integer, marshal, maxdemand, oee, pid, real, shift, snmpmgr, statistical, string, stringlist, text and timer . - Executing this action is best done by a user who has an in-depth knowledge of how their SCADA system (Agent Server) has been designed. - If an agent is used by (i.e. referenced within) another agent, such as an expression, the relevant agent is added to the Related Agents list. - Note: Only DBLog agents that have been enabled and are referencing one of the selected agents will appear in this list. - The template designer decides which of the agent relationships are required by the template. - These intra-agent relationships may become complex depending on how deeply nested they are. - Only the first level of agents are linked by default. - You may also manually add any agents that are not directly linked to the agents in this wizard, but are required. - Agents such as Script agents, the AlarmManagement agent and others, may be added by clicking the Add agent button.

- Any added agent, both existing or created at this time, is displayed in blue .

Title: Wizard Data Elements
- Any added agent, both existing or created at this time, is displayed in blue . - Note: Do not include the agents used to directly alarm, log or scan the agent. - Tip: If necessary, you can also create agents at this stage. - Click Next , once all the required agents have been selected. Step 3 of 12: Assign Agent Substitutions You can use this step to assign portions of an agent name for substitution, or to be variable, when creating instances of this object. This ensures that they adhere to tag naming conventions that are applicable. - Typically, the substitutions for all the values used within the referenced wizard are listed here and are prefixed by the Adroit datasource name. - Tip: If you keep the same substitution names as those used in the wizard, this makes it easier to implement your instances, because you will only configure these substitutions once , otherwise you will need to specify substitutions both during the SCADA Configuration and the Graphical Substitution stages. - Unless the substitution includes the datasource name and any manually added agents, the tag name is used instead. - You will have to manually add any required substitutions. - You may also modify existing substitutions at this point. - Important: Any tag that is not substituted will be referenced by all the instances of this template. - Note: Templates do not support obtaining tags from two different Adroit datasources. All the specified tags must exist on the same Agent Server. - To insert a substitution, click the Insert Substitution button containing the agent and specify each required substitution within curly brackets {...} in the Substitutions dialog. - To modify any substitution, double-click the row containing the agent and specify each required substitution within curly brackets {...} in the Substitutions dialog. - For example, if a plant area code and an equipment code is required: {PlantAreaCode}_{EquipmentCode}.value - Alternatively, you can use a single substitution for both the agent name and slot value, such as {AnalogTag} - Note: It is not possible to substitute the Adroit datasource name. However, you can specify which Adroit datasource (Agent Server) you want to use when creating an instance of this template. - Tip: When you click the Remove button, this removes all the specified substitutions of the current row (i.e. if only one has been selected) replacing these substitutions with the name of the specified agent. - Click Next , once all relevant substitutions have been specified.

Step 4 of 12: Configure Slots Each agent that is selected for use in this template provides a filtered list of values (slots) that a user may configure.

Title: Wizard Data Elements
Step 4 of 12: Configure Slots Each agent that is selected for use in this template provides a filtered list of values (slots) that a user may configure. - Select the row containing the agent you want to configure. The Slots table below displays a filtered list of available agent slots and their values . - Note: Any agent, such as DBLog and AlarmManagement , used to scan, log or alarm is not configured at this point - The underlying purpose of the object template is to create specific objects that simplify the SCADA objectives of your users. - You must determine how complex your objects need to be. - Also which values should be configured by using one of the following four configuration states: - Agent Default (Not displayed) : these values are preconfigured for this object and are hidden from your users. - User Default (Read-only) : these values are preconfigured for this object and are displayed for information purposes so that your users can still see them, even though they cannot edit them (like alarm limits or set points) . - Editable with a default value : a recommended or suggested value is provided, which a user may change when adding an instance. This is the default option. - Editable with NO default value : users must specify these values when creating each instance. - Note: This only applies to values that are not of type String (a blank string can be valid) . - Click Next , once you have appropriately configured the slots of each agent referenced by this object. Step 5 of 12: Configure Scanning This step lists all the slots values of the selected agents that are scanned and also their commonly configured scanning settings: - The selected device and its scan address for the device. - The scan rate and the alarm deadband setting. - The four scanning IO settings that affect how this value is scanned. - For more information about the IO settings, see IO Flags . - Note: If you want to update these scanning settings on all listed devices, then select the Update all devices on edit checkbox. - Click Next , when you are satisfied with how each of these slots are being scanned. Step 6 of 12: Configure Devices This step lets you configure the properties of each device that will be scanned. - These properties specify the default settings used when you create an instance of this object.

- - Currently, the Object Model supports the following commonly-used drivers (devices) : Modbus Ethernet, Mitsubishi Q, QnA, L, R and iQF Series Ethernet (3E Frames) , OPC Client and Siemens Ethernet.

Title: Wizard Data Elements

This step lists all the slot values of the selected agents that are alarmed and also their commonly configured alarming settings: that affect how this value is being alarmed. - You can modify one or more of these alarming settings, where necessary. - Best Practice: Always alarm agents from route 2 onwards never use routes 0 and 1.

These routes are used internally by Adroit for reporting the system alarms and events.

Title: Wizard Data Elements
These routes are used internally by Adroit for reporting the system alarms and events. - Click Next , once you are satisfied with how each of these slots are being alarmed. Step 10 of 12: Add Attributes This step lets you to add one or more attributes, searchable strings or identifiers that you can use to filter or classify the objects that you create in the Context View window. - Each attribute applies to all the object instances and requires both a Name and a Value . - Note: You cannot edit the Name once you create it. If you need to change the Name then delete the attribute and add it again. - These attributes provide user-friendly terms that can be used to identify this object, such as the equipment Type , containing a value of ‘motor’, or ‘valve’, etc. or perhaps even a power specification, such as 'kWh'. You can then specify the required value for each object attribute. - The Object Model datasource then uses the specified attributes to configure the Context View window automatically. - When object instances are deployed, each Name of their defined attributes creates a different context (tree-view) in the Context View window and instances that have the same Value of an attribute are grouped in this context. - A simple one-level deep tree-view is created for each attribute Name , in which a node is created for every unique value specified for this attribute. - Important: Only the Value and Instance names can be searched in the Context View and not the attribute Name , which is added to the list of contexts at the bottom of the Context View . To add an attribute: - Click the button. - Type in a new attribute or click the drop-down selection list button then select one of the existing attributes. - Tip: Typing in the first letter of an existing attribute immediately inserts the full text of this attribute name. The following general attributes always appear in this list: Manufacturer, Description, Model, and Type - Click the Finish button. - Any custom attributes that you add are saved in your current profile and are available for future use to all users who use your profile. - You can click the Reset the attribute library button to clear the custom attributes that are specified for the current profile. - Note: This only removes the custom attributes from the list, which will no longer be available for selection.

It does not remove any custom attributes that you have previously added to deployed objects, so these still appear in the Context View window.

Title: Wizard Data Elements
It does not remove any custom attributes that you have previously added to deployed objects, so these still appear in the Context View window. - As these attributes and their values are displayed on the first page when creating an instance, you can add the default Description attribute to provide a detailed description of this template, so that a user can know that they are adding the required object instance. - Note: The Delete button deletes the recently selected attribute, which by default is the last attribute in the list. - Tip: In addition to these attributes and when adding an instance, your users can specify additional instance-specific attributes too. Step 11 of 12: Add Child Templates You can add specialised sub-folders and move your templates into these folders. - You can do this within the Enterprise Manager , or you can use Windows Explorer . - When next the SmartUI Server loads it acquires the folder structure as you have created it. You can, therefore, create a workflow that suits your project best. - If you do choose to use Windows Explorer, these templates are stored in the following physical location on the SmartUI Server computer: C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \ObjectModel\Templates - Note: This path assumes that you are using the Default configuration, otherwise replace "Default" with the name of your currently active Configuration, which you can retrieve from the Configurations page of the SmartUI Config Editor . - When you create an object template. - Any instance that you create using this template will provide the referenced wizard to provide the graphical components. - It will also uniquely configure the specified SCADA configuration with the process values that you specify for each object. - For detailed steps to creating on Object instance, see Creating an Object Instance . - You can also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. - For more details, see Object Model Template Export Import Utility . Step 12 of 12: Run A Script This step lets you to define a script for the Object Model Template. When deploying an instance your users could run this script but only if it compiles successfully. - Note: Currently only the script defined for the template can be run.

Therefore any scripts defined for child templates will be ignored, even if no script is defined for the parent template.

Title: Wizard Data Elements
Therefore any scripts defined for child templates will be ignored, even if no script is defined for the parent template. - The Include script in this template checkbox is not selected, by default. - If selected then click the Launch Script Editor button to open the Script Editor with the default (sample) script. - You may edit and compile the script. - When you are done, close the Script Editor window to save the script. - Note: A warning is displayed when the script did not compile successfully or did not execute. To clear any errors, click the Launch Script Editor button again to edit and compile the script. - Important: This does not prevent you from clicking the Finish button, but be aware that when an instance of this template is deployed, the script will not run until it has been edited in the interim to successfully compile. - When deploying an instance of a template, a additional checkbox is displayed labelled Run Script , which is not selected by default and will be greyed out if a script was not specified or when the specified script does not successfully compile. - Click Finish , once you are satisfied with the configuration of this object template. - Tip: You can navigate between the steps using the Previous and Next buttons to edit any of the steps before clicking Finish . -->

Title: Configuration
- Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the required alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see Locating an agent . - Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. - Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. - Specify the required expression for this alarm type in the Conditional expression field at the bottom of this dialog. Typically you will create a logical expression, whereby the required tag is followed by a value condition, such as: Logical expression Condition for success Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) = 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) <> 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is not equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) > 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is greater than the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) >= 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is greater than or equal to the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) < 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is less than the value Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) <= 80 SUCCESSFUL if the tag is less than or equal to the value Note: You need to enclose each tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). within the Tag() specifier e.g. Tag(systeminfo.second) IMPORTANT: If a tag is NOT enclosed within a Tag() specifier then this incident will NEVER become active. Tip: When adding a tag to the expression, click the browse button and use the Adroit Agent Browser to locate and copy the required tag for you (then use the CTRL+V shortcut to paste it into the expression). This saves you from having to type in the tag yourself and ensure that there are NO spelling errors. Your expressions can make use of one or more of the following elements: Note1: Multiple items are separated by commas ','. Note2: Where necessary the description of an operator is displayed in brackets () after the operator. Element Type Operators / Example Other logical operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) Arithmetic operators +, -, *, /, % (modulus),^ (power) Parentheses (), {}, [] Scientific notation 3E+10 Constants 2, 3, 50 Functions MIN(4,5), SQR(34) By making use of these elements, you can create expressions that contain more than one tag, such as: (Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) < 20) | (Tag(TANKLEVEL.value) > 80) This will be SUCCESSFUL if the tag (Tanklevel.value) is less than 20 or greater than 80.

Click here for a list of Functions that you can use in your expressions: Note1: These functions can take either constants or tags as their parameters.

Title: Configuration
Click here for a list of Functions that you can use in your expressions: Note1: These functions can take either constants or tags as their parameters. Note2: For simplicity sake, the tag specifiers have been omitted so Tag1 = Tag(agent1.slot1) Function Usage MIN : returns the minimum value MIN(2, 3, 4, 5) is 2. MAX : returns the maximum value MAX(2, 3, 1, 0) is 3. IF(condition, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse) IF(1, 2, 3) is 2 SUM : adds the values together SUM(1, 2, 3, 4) is 10 AVG :averages the values AVG(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is 3 SQR: returns the square of the value SQR(Tag1) SQRT: returns the square root of the value SQRT(Tag1) EXP : Returns E raised to the power of the value EXP(Tag1) INTPOW(Base, power): raises the Base to an integral power. INTPOW(2, 3) = 8 POW(Base, power): raises the Base to any power. Note: For fractional exponents or exponents greater than MaxInt, the Base must be greater than 0. POW(2,3) = 8 LN: returns the natural logarithm of the value LN(Tag1) LOG: returns the base-10 logarithm of the value LOG(Tag1) LOGN(Base, value): returns the log Base of the value LOGN(10, 100) = 2 ABS: returns the absolute value ABS(Tag1) SIGN: returns the sign of the value SIGN(Tag1) returns -1 if Tag1<0; +1 if Tag1>0, 0 if Tag1=0 TRUNC: discards the fractional part of the value TRUNC(-3.2) is -3, TRUNC(3.2) is 3 CEIL: returns the value rounded up, away from zero CEIL(-3.2) = -3, CEIL(3.2) = 4 FLOOR: returns the value rounded down, toward zero FLOOR(-3.2) = -4, FLOOR(3.2) = 3 SIN: returns the sine of the value (an angle in radians). SIN(Tag1) COS: returns the cosine the value (an angle in radians). COS(Tag1) TAN: returns the tangent of the value (an angle in radians). TAN(Tag1) ATAN: returns arctangent, or inverse tangent, of the value. The returned angle is specified in radians. ATAN(Tag1) SINH: returns the hyperbolic sine of the value. SINH(Tag1) COSH: returns the hyperbolic cosine of the value. COSH(Tag1) COTAN: returns the cotangent of the value. COTAN(Tag1) -->

Creating connections Creating connections The Create Connection configuration dialog configures the connection that is created during the login between the Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Creating connections
Steps:
Creating connections Creating connections The Create Connection configuration dialog configures the connection that is created during the login between the Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. and the Smart UI Server computers and if necessary can store these settings in a login profile. How you display this dialog depends on the application that you are in, as follows: - In the Login dialog, click the Change button. - In the Designer , open the Enterprise Manager , right click the Servers or its icon and select New Connection . Specify the physical connection between this Client computer and the required Smart UI Server computer in the Connection Type dialog, as follows: WARNING! The connection type cannot be reconfigured when modifying the connection properties. Select one of the following connection types: - Local Area Network: The Smart UI Client computer connects to the required Smart UI Server computer by means of a network. Note: These computers do not need to be part of the same domains, although the Smart UI Client computer need to have access rights to the Smart UI Server computer. - Internet: The Smart UI Client computer connects to the required Smart UI Server computer by means of the Internet. More details: Note1: This connection type is only possible when the Smart UI Web Service is installed on the Smart UI Server computer itself or on another computer that can communicate to the Server computer. Note2: If using the Intranet then use the Local Area Network connection type instead. Note3: This connection uses the default HTTP port and so is able to connect to the Server even if it is behind a firewall. Tip: It is recommended to only connect the Smart UI Operator to the Smart UI Server using this connection type, since this connection will be very slow if the Smart UI Designer is used. If selected, then if a proxy server is required for this Internet connection, complete the Proxy Settings displayed on this page, as follows: - Specify the network name of this Proxy server or its IP address in the Proxy edit box. - Specify the port that this Proxy Server uses in the Port edit box, this is typically port 80. Tip: Use Internet Options to determine the required port for this proxy server (typically launched from the Tools menu in Internet Explorer), by selecting the Connections tab and its LAN Settings… button. - If user authentication is required when connecting to this proxy server, then supply the necessary User name and Password . Click Next . Configure the Connection Settings configuration dialog, as follows: - Specify the required Smart UI Server computer. As follows, when connecting via the local area network: - Either press the Detected Servers... button and double-click the required Server from the list of available Servers, which specifies each Servers' address, port, number of currently connected Clients and version. This is the simplest method. - Or type in the name or IP address of the required Server computer, in the Insert the computer's name or it's IP address edit box or click the Network Servers... button below this field to use the Browse for Computer dialog to locate this computer’s name as you would in Windows Explorer. Note: If the ServerPort setting of this Server is not 9000 (the default), then add a colon “:” after the specified name or IP address to specify this port number. For instance, the following entries connect to a Server computer using a custom port of 9010: 'localhost:9010' or '10.10.10.124:9010'.

As follows, when connecting via the Internet: Type in the web location of the Smart UI Server in the Insert the URL to connect to edit box.

Title: Creating connections
Steps:
As follows, when connecting via the Internet: Type in the web location of the Smart UI Server in the Insert the URL to connect to edit box. This is the web site name and virtual folder specified when installing the Smart UI Web Service of this Smart UI Server as follows: http://webSiteName/virtualFolder Tip: Click the Test Connection button to ensure that this Smart UI Server can be located at the specified address. - Specify the User login details of the required user account on this Server computer, in the Name and Password edit boxes. WARNING! ALWAYS specify these details, even if they to remain the SAME - otherwise this connection will FAIL. Note: Ensure that the specified login details are correct and that this user account is either an allowed user or part of an allowed group on this Smart UI Server computer. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups. - If necessary, open the Communication method list and select the required way in which you want to transfer data between the Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. and Smart UI Server, from the available options. For details on the differences between these communication methods, see About connection communication methods . Note: The available method(s) depends upon the specified connection Type or how the two computers are physically connected. - Click the Save Login Profile button, if you want to save these connections settings to a login profile, for future use when logging into this Client. In this case, specify the required name for this profile in the displayed dialog. Try to keep the names less than 35 characters in size. - Click Finish once these communication settings are complete. This will create this connection, provided the Server is available and the login details are correct. -->

Creating contextually sensitive object instances Top Creating contextually sensitive object instances Creating an object instance from a node in the Default context can be particularly useful when its name and substitutions use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created. Tip: If you drag an existing Object Model template from the Enterprise Manager directly onto the applicable node, then you can skip the step where you need to specify the required template. To make the best use of this feature, you need to: - Define the necessary hierarchy of Nodes, which typically represent each specific contextual area and specify each Node descriptor , typically a 3-character reference code for each contextual area. - For more information about naming details, see Configuring Node names and descriptors . - Define the process variable names if your object employs multiple substitutions. You should ensure that these substitutions are specified in the template and are in the logical order of the defined contextual areas. When an object instance is created in a node, then each defined Node descriptor , up to the current level, are used to define its name and its substitutions, as follows: - The Map Descriptors to Substitutions dialog lets you do one of two things: - Assign the Descriptor path , a string that assigns all the Node descriptors that are separated by 'underscore _' characters to a specific substitution. - You can specify which Node Descriptor in the Descriptor path is used for each of these substitutions, if you have created multiple substitutions that are combined to specify the required contextual naming convention, such as {site}_{area}_{section}_...., - By default, this dialog immediately assumes that the first substitution maps to the first defined Node descriptor , and the second substitution maps to the second defined Node descriptor and so on, up to the current node level of the displayed object instance. - It is most useful when the order of the first substitutions matches the order of the Node Descriptors meaning no further configuration is required. - You can, however, manually select the required substitution values, if required. - Tip: The Template Descriptor (if one was specified for this template) the last portion of the default deployed object name, that relates to the object itself and not its context, is also specified as an available option in this list.

Title: Expression Function Usage
Your expressions can also use one or more of the following functions: Note: These functions can take either constants or slot values as their parameters. For simplicity, the slot specifiers have been omitted, where Slot1 = Slot(SlotName) Functions Usage MIN : returns the minimum value MIN(2, 3, 4, 5) is 2. MAX : returns the maximum value MAX(2, 3, 1, 0) is 3. IF(condition, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse) IF(1, 2, 3) is 2 SUM : adds the values together SUM(1, 2, 3, 4) is 10 AVG :averages the values AVG(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is 3 SQR: returns the square of the value SQR(Slot1) SQRT: returns the square root of the value SQRT(Slot1) EXP : Returns E raised to the power of the value EXP(Slot1) INTPOW(Base, power): raises the Base to an integral power INTPOW(2, 3) = 8 POW(Base, power): raises the Base to any power Note: For fractional exponents or exponents greater than MaxInt, the Base must be greater than 0. POW(2,3) = 8 LN: returns the natural logarithm of the value LN(Slot1) LOG: returns the base-10 logarithm of the value LOG(Slot1) LOGN(Base, value): returns the log Base of the value LOGN(10, 100) = 2 ABS: returns the absolute value ABS(Slot1) SIGN: returns the sign of the value SIGN(Slot1) returns -1 if Slot1<0; +1 if Slot1>0, 0 if Slot1=0 TRUNC: discards the fractional part of the value TRUNC(-3.2) is -3, TRUNC(3.2) is 3 CEIL: returns the value rounded up, away from zero CEIL(-3.2) = -3, CEIL(3.2) = 4 FLOOR: returns the value rounded down, toward zero FLOOR(-3.2) = -4, FLOOR(3.2) = 3 SIN: returns the sine of the value (an angle in radians) SIN(Slot1) COS: returns the cosine the value (an angle in radians) COS(Slot1) TAN: returns the tangent of the value (an angle in radians) TAN(Slot1) ATAN: returns arctangent, or inverse tangent, of the value. The returned angle is specified in radians ATAN(Slot1) SINH: returns the hyperbolic sine of the value SINH(Slot1) COSH: returns the hyperbolic cosine of the value COSH(Slot1) COTAN: returns the cotangent of the value COTAN(Slot1)

Title: The default IOT agent dialog looks as follows
The default IOT agent dialog looks as follows: The 1st IOT dialog shows the slot definition with a Tagname slot, followed by a slot that will contain the value of the specified tag, for example, systeminfo.second. - The dialog shows an expression that will also control the status bit 16 when the temperature value goes above 30. This status slot can be alarmed by creating an IOT Alarm agent . - Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag), for example, value(“systeminfo.second”). The 2nd IOT dialog shows a slot definition and an expression that will also control status bit 16 when the Z value goes above 100 when values X and Y are added together. - The sample XML structure below contains the agent name and description attributes as shown in first line below. These attributes are disregarded when the same XML is used in a XML template load file. <IOT Name="Add01" Description="Addition agent"> <SlotDefinitions> <Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot> <Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot> <Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot> </SlotDefinitions> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name="hi"/> </HeaderSlots> <Expression> <Line Text=”Z=slot(x) + slot(y)”/> </Line> <Line Text=”status16=slot(z)>100”></Line> </Expression> </IOT>

Title: Templates
You can build your XML structures in an external text editor and save as an XML file template. - The Load template button allows you to load an XML file defining the slot structure of the IOT agent. - The Save template button allows you to save the slot structure of the IOT agent to an XML file.

If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would.

Title: Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot
If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would have the following structure: <IOT Name="AddingTwoNumbers" Description="This adds two real values together"><Slots><Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/></HeaderSlots></IOT> And the expression slot of this agent would saved as: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 Which, appears in the Expression edit box in the configuration dialog of this IOT agent as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 Note: The use of the empty line between these expressions, indicates that they are separate independent expressions.

Title: Expressions using external tag values
Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag) e.g. value(“systeminfo.second”). The following example of the xml The following example provides the xml slot that defines an IOT agent that obtain the value of the systeminfo.second tag and stores this in a secs Integer slot. Then it provides the expression slot that enables the status bit 16 when the number of seconds exceed 30. SecsInMinute . xml =<IOT Name="SecsInMinute" Description="Alert when the seconds exceed 30"><Slots><Slot Name="source" Description="Source of the seconds value" Type="Tagname">systeminfo.second</Slot><Slot Name="secs" Description="The actual seconds" Type="Integer">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots></HeaderSlots></IOT> SecsInMinute . expression =status16=slot(secs)>30 Note: This example also shows that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent in order for them to be used, in this case they need to be referred to using the convention status nn in any expressions that you create (where nn is the required status bit number from 16 to 31).

However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention.

Title: Expressions using status slots
However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention. So when you use: status16 = slot(z) > 100 You can also use: status(hi) = slot(z) > 100 In addition to referring to the status slots as the status nn or the named status( slotname ) convention, interchangeably, you can also use these on the right hand side of the equation, if needed. As a result, you could have the following expression: status17 = if(status(enabled), slot(abc) > 100

You can build your XML structures in an external text editor and save as an XML file template. - The Load template button allows you to load an XML file defining the slot structure of the IOT agent. - The Save template button allows you to save the slot structure of the IOT agent to an XML file.

If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would.

Title: Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot
If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would have the following structure: <IOT Name="AddingTwoNumbers" Description="This adds two real values together"><Slots><Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/></HeaderSlots></IOT> And the expression slot of this agent would saved as: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 Which, appears in the Expression edit box in the configuration dialog of this IOT agent as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 Note: The use of the empty line between these expressions, indicates that they are separate independent expressions.
