text:
Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag) e.g.

Title: Expressions using external tag values
Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag) e.g. value(“systeminfo.second”). The following example of the xml The following example provides the xml slot that defines an IOT agent that obtain the value of the systeminfo.second tag and stores this in a secs Integer slot. Then it provides the expression slot that enables the status bit 16 when the number of seconds exceed 30. SecsInMinute . xml =<IOT Name="SecsInMinute" Description="Alert when the seconds exceed 30"><Slots><Slot Name="source" Description="Source of the seconds value" Type="Tagname">systeminfo.second</Slot><Slot Name="secs" Description="The actual seconds" Type="Integer">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots></HeaderSlots></IOT> SecsInMinute . expression =status16=slot(secs)>30 Note: This example also shows that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent in order for them to be used, in this case they need to be referred to using the convention status nn in any expressions that you create (where nn is the required status bit number from 16 to 31).

However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention.

Title: Expressions using status slots
However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention. So when you use: status16 = slot(z) > 100 You can also use: status(hi) = slot(z) > 100 In addition to referring to the status slots as the status nn or the named status( slotname ) convention, interchangeably, you can also use these on the right hand side of the equation, if needed. As a result, you could have the following expression: status17 = if(status(enabled), slot(abc) > 100

These status slots used in expressions can be alarmed using IOT Alarm agents .

Title: Alarming status slots
These status slots used in expressions can be alarmed using IOT Alarm agents . -->

Note1 : The Advanced... button of this dialog allows you to configure Advanced Properties, which should ONLY be modified if you know what you are doing. Note2 : The Data Links... button of this dialog, opens the Data Link Properties dialog, which allows you to configure both these advanced properties via the All tab and may allows you to specify access permissions for this connection string via the Advanced tab. Once again ONLY modify these settings if you know what you are doing. Note3 : These security credentials are database specific and should not be confused with application security. Note4: You can also edit this connection string directly, once it has been created, if necessary. If you have an Adroit datasource that connects to an Agent Server containing this AlarmManagement agent and this Agent Server is running, then click the Adroit Alarm Management Agent Connection Settings option and specify the required Adroit datasource and the name of the AlarmManagement agent. Creating silks Top Creating silks Silks are created, within a spider workspace to connect Data spiders (properties and data elements) and/or other spiders together.

Title: Creating silks
Creating silks Top Creating silks Silks are created, within a spider workspace to connect Data spiders (properties and data elements) and/or other spiders together. Click for more information: Silks are created by dragging the output of one spider to the input of another. Note1: A silk will only be created, if the data type of both the specified output and input entries are compatible. If necessary the output can be converted to data type of the input. For details, see Converting output data types . Note2: When the spider workspace is running, the silk’s output spider will be triggered, whenever the value of the silk’s input spider changes. For details, see Triggering spiders . To create a silk originating from a Data spider: - Open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, display the required tree pane adjacent to the spider workspace by using the pane display bar and expand this tree to display the required node e.g. property, data element etc. For details, see Working with pane display bars . - Ensure that you are also able to see the required destination for this silk e.g. spider or Data spider (property, data element, virtual data element). Note1: If connecting to a spider, this may require adding the required spider to the spider workspace and moving it, if necessary. For details, see Adding spiders . Note2: If connecting to a Data spider (property, data element, virtual data element), this may require displaying the required tree pane adjacent to the spider workspace by using the pane display bar and expanding this tree to display the required node. - Drag the silk from the required tree node e.g. property, data element etc. to connect it to the required destination. Note1: A Data spider will be added to the spider workspace when this node (property, data element, virtual data element) is dragged from the tree, which is demonstrated by a blue line appearing to the left of this node. Note2: It is possible to inadvertently add other Data spiders to the spider workspace, by dragging this node (property, data element, virtual data element) over any other node in this or another tree. However any Data spider that has no silks connected to it will automatically be removed when the spider workspace is saved. For details, see Saving spider workspaces . To create a silk originating from a spider: - Open the required spider workspace.

- If necessary, add the required spider(s) to the spider workspace.

Title: Creating silks
- If necessary, add the required spider(s) to the spider workspace. For details, see Adding spiders. - Open the configuration view of the spider, whose output you want to link to the destination spider or Data spider (property, virtual data element). For details, see Displaying spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide its configuration view. - If this configuration view contains a New Outputs section, you may want to create a custom output first. For details, see Creating customised spider outputs . - Ensure that you are able to see the required destination for this silk e.g. spider, property or virtual data element. Note1: If connecting to a spider, this may require moving this spider appropriately or adjusting the size of the spider workspace by using the pane display bars and splitter bars, where necessary. For details, see Working with pane display bars . Note2: If connecting to a Data spider (property, virtual data element), this may require displaying the required tree pane adjacent to the spider workspace by using the pane display bar and expanding this tree to display the required node. - Drag the silk from the required entry beneath the Outputs section of this spider to connect it to the required destination. To connect a silk to a spider: Once a silk has been dragged from either a Data spider (property, data element) or from another spider, complete the required link to this spider, as follows: Note: The required spider must be visible in the spider workspace in order to connect the silk to it. - If the configuration view of this spider is already displayed, then select the required compatible entry beneath the Inputs section that the silk to required to connect to and release the left mouse button. Note: If this spider’s configuration view contains a New Inputs section, you can immediately create a custom input, by selecting the required compatible entry beneath the New Inputs section and releasing the left mouse button. For details, see Creating customised spider inputs . - If the configuration view of this spider is not displayed, then when the mouse pointer is dragged over the title bar or icon of this second spider: - If this spider only has one entry in its Inputs section, which has a compatible data type, then simply release the left mouse button to create the silk will automatically connect to this input.

- If this spider has more than one entry in its Inputs section, then its configuration view will automatically be displayed.

Title: Creating silks
- If this spider has more than one entry in its Inputs section, then its configuration view will automatically be displayed. Select the required input entry, with a compatible data type, and release the left mouse button to create the silk. - If this spider does not currently have any inputs configured, but New Inputs types are available, then its configuration view will automatically be displayed. Note: Do not specify the required name of this state within quotes. - For Integer or Double values, specify the range of values that the default Value or additional input ( i1 etc.) must lie within, as follows: - To specify a specific range: connect the minimum and maximum values with ":" character, for instance: 5.5:6.5 or -20:-10. - To create infinite ranges , you can use one of the following operators: > for instance: >5.5. >= for instance: >=6.5 < for instance: <-20 <= for instance: <=-10 <> for instance: <>7 Note: Ensure that there are NO spaces between the specified numbers and the operator characters. - To compare the values of one or more inputs , create a logical expression using the following Boolean operators: Example of a logical expression that compares more than one input values: (Value>3)||(i1<34) Note: If a state uses multiple inputs, these need to be added and the correct values need to be assigned to them before the state can be evaluated. Although these boolean operators are typically used to compare the values of more than one input, you can also use them to define states for the single default Value input, for instance: (Value>23)&&(Value!=25) IMPORTANT: When adding multiple “&&” , “||” and other expressions, each expression MUST be enclosed in parentheses “()” (see the examples above). If these parentheses are left out, these expressions do not evaluate correctly.

Creating the Requests collection Top Creating the Requests collection For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data .

Title: Creating the Requests collection
Steps:
Creating the Requests collection Top Creating the Requests collection For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data . One of the objects exposed by the Data Object is the Requests collection, a collection of individual descriptions for required real-time data. Each description consists of a tag (or agent name) plus the names of all the slots to be monitored. The slot names are gathered into another collection called the Properties collection. Since the Data Object provides the Requests collection as one of its properties, the VBA code to gain access to the Requests collection is simply: Set reqs = dataObj.Requests A single request consists of the tag plus the names of all slots to be monitored. The Requests object provides a method (function) for the creation of blank sets of fields (the Properties collection). This method is named CreateProperties . VBA allows us to create the Properties collection by directly calling the CreateProperties method, which returns a Properties collection: Set props = reqs.CreateProperties() -->

- Specify the first property (component data type) of this UDT in the Add new UDT property dialog.

Title: Specifications
- Specify the first property (component data type) of this UDT in the Add new UDT property dialog. Note: A property of a UDT is equivalent to a slot of an agent. - Type in the required name of this data type. Note: If necessary, you CAN rename a property later, by selecting the required property and clicking the Rename selected UDT property... button. WARNING! Renaming properties invalidate any configurations using the older slot (property) name. - Click the OK button. - Open the Type list box and specify the required data type for this property. Tip :Ensure that the Selected UDT Properties section indicates the correct basic Adroit data types to represent this property. Note : If you cannot find the required data type then contact support so that we can add it for you. - Only clear the Readonly checkbox, if you want to prevent the user from editing the value of this property in the agent edit dialog. - Only clear the Public checkbox, if you want to hide this property from the agent edit dialog. - Click the Add new UDT property... button in the Selected UDT - Properties section and repeat steps 5 to 10 for each of the component data types within this UDT. Note : Please ensure that you add these data types in the EXACT order as they appear in the UDT of the PLC. If necessary, edit the property descriptions. The UDT Agent Type Designer dialog increments the Scan size of the resultant UDT after each property is added or modified.

In the Selected UDT - Status Bit section: - Select the required status bit/s from the Status bits list, do the following for each, as required: - Rename this status bit, by typing in the required name in the Status bit name edit field - you can use a maximum of 18 characters for this name.

Title: Specifications
In the Selected UDT - Status Bit section: - Select the required status bit/s from the Status bits list, do the following for each, as required: - Rename this status bit, by typing in the required name in the Status bit name edit field - you can use a maximum of 18 characters for this name. Note1: The “Status bit xx” naming convention is ONLY used for display purposes in this dialog. Therefore any status bit that is NOT renamed will not be added as a status bit name within the UDT agent instances. Note2: If a customised status bit name is cleared, the “Status bit xx” naming convention will be re-applied. - Specify the required expression to calculate the value of this status bit, in the Status bit expression edit field, which define the state of this UDT that needs to be alarmed. For details, see Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions . Therefore the expected expression result should be True (1) or False (0), Examples of such expressions are: - Slot(value) > 95 - Slot(Open) & (Slot(value) > 95) The following expression language used for this feature is exactly the same as the expression language used in conditional alarming. - If necessary, configure another UDT agent by repeating steps 2 to 12. IMPORTANT: Ensure that the Agent Server is stopped. - Click the Close button of the UDT Agent Type Designer to save the UDT configuration to the registry and create the udt.reg file. Click for more details: The udt.reg file is in the created in the Data subfolder of the designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data. This file can be copied to remote computers then simply open this utility and click the Import button to import it. Note: If you are using an Adroit cluster ensure that you import your UDT configuration into the UDT Agent Type Designer of the cluster partner. Your UDT agent type DLLs are created EVERY time the Agent Server is started. Click for more details: These DLLs are created in the Adroit installation folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and adhere to the following naming convention: t_TypeName.dll, where TypeName is the name you specified. -->

Title: To create one or more variable data elements
Steps:
- If necessary, add and/or select the required Variable Data Element spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Variable Data Element spiders or Selecting spiders or Displaying spider configuration views . - If required, create the required number of named inputs, each of which can be used to replace a portion of a data element name, instead of or in addition to using the default {0}, as follows: in the New Input section, double-click the + New Input entry and specify the required name of this input. This adds the specified name in {} to the Inputs section. - In the New Output section, double-click the + Variable DE entry. This will add 2 inputs, namely vde # [DE Name (Segment)] and vde # [Return DE] to the Inputs section and an output called vde # to the Outputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 0. - Specify the required data element name for this vde # [DE Name (Segment)] input. IMPORTANT: The value of this input should NOT be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk, but instead should be typed in manually . Double-click the value column to the right of the vde # input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. Tip: Use an Extended Data Element spider to quickly and easily obtain this required data element name. Simply link the required data element to this spider and then copy (CTRL+C) and paste (CTRL+V) its Name input into the value column of this vde # input. For further details, see Extended Data Element spiders . When specifying the name of the required data element, the string input {0} and/or any named inputs, should specify the variable portion/s of the data element name/s that are to be dynamically driven by another spider or string type input. For example if the data element was ‘MyServer.DatasourceName.DataElement’, then ‘MyServer.{0}.DataElement’ can dynamically change the name of the required datasource at runtime. Tip: You can also concatenate the string input {0} and/or any named inputs to replace more than one portion of a data element name. For example: {AgentServer}.{PUMP}.value allows you to dynamically specify the value of any pump on any Agent Server. - Specify the required value, of the {0} and/or the named inputs, which will be dynamically inserted into the variable data element input at runtime. Values can either be typed in directly or obtained from another spider, data element or property, for details, see Creating silks . - If necessary, specify the value that will be written to the dynamically modified data element, specified by the vde # [DE Name (Segment)] and {0} inputs, by specifying this value in the vde # [Return DE] input. Note: The value of this input should typically be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk, so that it can dynamically vary, however it can be typed in manually. - If necessary, connect the associated vde # output to the required destination for the dynamically modified data element (specified by the vde # [DE Name (Segment)] and {0} inputs), such as another spider or property etc. - If necessary add other variable data elements and/or other named input variables and repeat this until all the required variable data elements have been added and configured. Note: To remove an unnecessary named input or variable data element, right click it in the Inputs section and select Delete . -->

Creating wizards Top Creating wizards You have two main options when creating wizards, typically in the Enterprise Manager window: - Either create the wizard from scratch: in this case, right click a project or folder and select Create Wizard . Note: When creating a wizard from scratch, the default size of the wizard is 200 by 200 pixels, since wizards are typically small by nature. If necessary customise this default, by using the Designer.CONFIG setting in the Misc group, called DefaultWizardsize . - Or convert an existing graphic form into a wizard: in this case, open the required graphic form and select the Save as Wizard graphic form toolbar button. Then use the Substitution configuration dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. Tip: When you substitute a data element that is used in numerous locations within the graphic form, all these locations use the specified substitution name. The graphic form toolbar contains the Optimise Graphic Form size button (at the end), which resizes the wizard to the size of the added controls and vectors, so that there are no overlaps at the top, bottom, left or right sides. -->

Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Top Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Tag groups are primarily used manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers.

Title: Criteria for Creating Tag Groups
Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Top Criteria for Creating Tag Groups Tag groups are primarily used manage the communication settings for the tags whose values need to be communicated to or from the remote Agent Servers via their associated WanServers. For details, see Tag Groups . The following criteria are used for creating different tag groups: - Physical location: Tags from different parts of the process or plant, can be placed in different groups. - Polling Requirements: Tags that require different poll rates need to be placed in the appropriately configured groups. - Communication type (Read/Write requirements): Tags requiring the same read / write ability need to be within the same group, as follows: - Tags within Normal groups are only able to have their tag values read i.e. to have one-way communication from WanServer to WanClient - Tags within Control groups are able to have their tag values read and written i.e. to have two-way communication from WanServer to WanClient AND also from WanClient to WanServer. -->

Current Operational Status Top Current Operational Status The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so.

Title: Current Operational Status
Current Operational Status Top Current Operational Status The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . The status bar of this utility displays the following details, concerning the status of the tag monitoring process: - The first text box (from the left), displays the operational status of the tag monitoring process i.e. whether it has Started or Stopped . - The second text box, displays the operational phase of the tag monitoring process, for instance Editing (when Stopped ) or Monitoring (when Started). Other transitory phases include Opening , Subscribing , Desubscribing , Closing and Delaying . - The third text, displays the status of the currently connected Agent Server, for instance AS OK when it is operating correctly or AS ERROR , when it is not. For details, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . - The fourth text box displays the total amount of memory committed by the computer, for information purposes only. - The fifth text box displays the number of updates being received per second, for instance 68 updates @ 1 subs/s. -->

Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Top Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Since the introduction of the Custom agent a number of customers have put this agent to good use, which is what it is there for.

Title: Custom Agent Usage Guidelines
Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Top Custom Agent Usage Guidelines Since the introduction of the Custom agent a number of customers have put this agent to good use, which is what it is there for. But as with all tools there is both a proper and improper way of using them and the method used directly affects the achievable results. Therefore the following points or guidelines are recommended concerning the prudent use of this agent: - If the Custom agent is used purely as a pure container agent i.e. no scripting attached, this should not cause any problems. - When using large numbers of intelligent Custom agents (those containing scripts): - Always monitor the virtual memory usage of the AS.EXE (Agent Server) process (from startup) during the design and commissioning phase - typically by using the Windows Performance Monitor. Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc As this KPI determines when you should convert your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents, as follows: For 32-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 2 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: - exceeds 1.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. - approaches 1.5 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. For 64-bit operating systems , which allocate a maximum of 4 GB per process, when the virtual memory used by the AS.EXE process: - exceeds 2.0 GB then you SHOULD convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. - approaches 3.0 GB then you MUST convert your intelligent Custom agents to C++ agents. - Always monitor the CPU usage of the AS.EXE process. Natively, the AS.EXE process runs at about 1-2% CPU load, very rarely over 5%. If your custom agent configuration causes the CPU load to exceed 10-20%, then you should ALSO consider converting your intelligent Custom agents into properly written C++ agents. - Ensure that the code used to create an intelligent Custom agent is optimised. Since EACH instance of this agent uses the SAME CODE to perform its functions. So when the code is poorly written, EVERY error is exacerbated, which can reduce the performance of the entire Adroit system. - Custom agents normally have multiple slots scanned, which is no problem in itself. But please ensure that ONLY the required INDIVIDUAL slots are output enabled and NOT the ENTIRE Custom agent. Click for more details: Note: The scan dialog does this by default. Historically, users have simply output enabled the whole agent and this practice was acceptable because, typically, only one slot was scanned in the analog, digital or marshal agents. However, when an agent has multiple slots scanned AND is globally output enabled, any changes to ANY of this agent’s slot values will cause a write message to the scanning subsystem resulting in scan degradation. In the case of Custom agents the extent of this scanning degradation depends on the number of Custom agents being used and the level of activity on these agents. Note: This rule also applies when configuring scan inhibit. How to Use the Custom Agent Designer -->

- If necessary, add this control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding AlarmViewer controls . - In the Design workspace , select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the AlarmViewer control. - Open the Properties tool window. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the AlarmColumnInfo property, which is listed in the Alarm category. - Click the browse button in the value column to the left of this property. This will display the alarm column selection dialog. Example: To hide a column from display: - Select the column in the left Visible Columns list that should be hidden. - Click the button to add it to the right Hidden Columns list. To display a previously hidden column: - Select the column in the right Hidden Columns list that should be displayed. - Click the button to add it to the left Visible Columns list. To specify the required width of a column: - Select the column in the left Visible Columns list. - Specify the required number of pixels in the Width field, in the central property pane, the default value depends on the selected column. To change the order in which a column is displayed in this control: Select the column in the left list, whose order of display needs to be changed. Either click the Move up button to move this column up the column listing. This will move to column closer to the left of the control, so that it is more prominent or easier to be displayed. Or click the Move Down button to move this column down the column listing. This will move to column closer to the right of the control, so that it is less prominent or harder to be displayed. -->

Title: To customise the auto logoff settings
Steps:
Note: If you want to DISABLE this auto logoff then uncheck the Logoff users assigned to this profile checkbox, which is checked by default. - Create a profile or edit the profile that applies to the current user. Tip: Any user not associated with a profile has the Default profile applied to them. For details, see Default profiles . - In the Profile Configuration dialog, select the Profile Properties dialog, from the left pane. - Ensure that the Logoff users assigned to this profile checkbox is checked. - Specify the required period of inactivity, in seconds, during which no mouse or keyboard activity should occur to enforce this log off. By default this is 600 seconds (10 minutes). - Instead of completely logging off after the inactivity timeout, you can specify a default user that should be logged on instead - simply check the Revert to Default User checkbox and then specify the required User Name and Password of this default user in the edit boxes.

Title: How to create a custom project report template:
Steps:
- Right click the MAPS project and select Report . - Click the Edit button. - Customise the GENERIC project report template using the provided report editor. For instance, add your company logo to the top of the report. - Click the Save button and save this customised project report template to the required location, using the required name. Tip: It is recommended create and/or choose a folder within your MAPS Project - to make backing up easier. - Right click the MAPS project and select Properties . - Click the Browse button to the right of the Default Project Report , in the Project Settings section. - Specify the location and file name of the customised project report template that you have saved. Customizing the work environment Customizing the work environment The Smart UI Operator displays configured graphic forms, so they can be operated or interacted with and allows you to customize the working environment, as follows: The display and the amount of interaction that a user has with the Smart UI Operator window, is determined by: - the user profile configured for this user in the Smart UI Designer.

Title: Customizing the work environment
Steps:
Customizing the work environment Customizing the work environment The Smart UI Operator displays configured graphic forms, so they can be operated or interacted with and allows you to customize the working environment, as follows: The display and the amount of interaction that a user has with the Smart UI Operator window, is determined by: - the user profile configured for this user in the Smart UI Designer. For details, see Operator customization . - and/or the command line argument options used to launch the Smart UI Operator. For details, see Operator command line arguments . Note: The INITIAL display of the Smart UI Operator and configuration of the work environment can be configured by Smart UI Operator settings. For details, see Operator user interface settings. The work environment of the Smart UI Operator consists the workspace and tool windows. For details, see Operator workspace . Note: The tool windows can be hidden to increase the viewing space. For details, see Available tool windows . The work environment can be further customized by right-clicking the Smart UI Operator window and selecting one of the following menu items: Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - To display or hide the tool windows and document tabs, press CTRL+O or right-click and select Toggle Operator Mode . Note: The default setting can also be configured using the Boolean InitialOperatorMode Smart UI Operator setting of the user profile configured in the Smart UI Designer. - To display or hide document tabs within the Operator window, press CTRL+T or right-click and select Toggle Graphic Form Tabs . For details on the use of these tabs, see Operator workspace . - To enable or disable the running or "live" state of the currently displayed graphic form, either press F5 or right-click and select Running . This may be necessary if a running graphic form consumes excessive bandwidth ( for instance when using an Internet connection). - To print the currently displayed graphic form, press CTRL+P or right-click and select Print . - To assist in troubleshooting your graphic forms you can allow all or a single control or vector to display the list of all the data elements connected to its properties. For more information, see Working with Show (All) Information . Note: When using Adroit tags you can also display bad-tag status indicators on relevant controls and/or vectors. For details, see Bad tag status indicators . - To enable or disable the display of the Smart UI Operator window above all other applications, right-click and select Always On Top . - To enable or disable the full screen display of the Smart UI Operator window (filling the entire screen without a title bar), press F11 or right-click and select Full Screen . - To display the current bandwidth speeds for sending and retrieving data from the Smart UI Server and the amount of data that is being sent and received, press F6 or right-click and select Transfer Statistics . - To log off the Smart UI Operator, either press CTRL+N or right-click and select Disconnect . - To close the Smart UI Operator window, either press ALT+F4 or right-click and select Exit . -->

Title: Data Element spiders
Data Element spiders Top Data Element spiders The Data Element spider is a Data spider, which allows you to connect a data element a finite component of data contained within a datasource that behaves in a generic manner; typically a value. See datasource. or a placeholder for a data element to or from another data element or a property of a graphic form a document that belongs to a project, which can be designed to graphically display data to the user and to accept input from the user when it is being operated. or one of its form components a general term encompassing all the controls, components and / or graphic elements that can be added to graphic forms, to provide the required user interface for its end-users. See control; component; graphic element; graphic form. . This spider has the following two modes of creation and operation: - Automatic : this is the typical usage, in which this spider is added automatically whenever the user drags a data element of an existing datasource onto the associated graphic form or directly onto another spider in the spider workspace. More details: In this case the namespace one or more names separated by periods (or dots), where each name represents an individual item and the entire namespace indicates the relationship or lineage of the leftmost term i.e. grandparent.parent.child. of this spider should be the EXACT name of its associated data element, which is typically: ServerName.datasourceName.dataElementName. Note: It is also possible to alter this ServerName, at any time, for all of its data elements used within a spider workspace. For details, see Changing data element referencing . - Manual : this spider can be manually added to the spider workspace to create either a data element substitution for a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. or a place holder for a data element of a datasource that is currently unavailable. More details: - For details on creating a data element substitution a placeholder for a data element in a wizard. for a wizard, see Working with substitutions . IMPORTANT: These substitutions ONLY apply to wizards and NOT to graphic forms! - When creating a place holder for a data element of a datasource that is currently unavailable or will be added later: In this case the namespace one or more names separated by periods (or dots), where each name represents an individual item and the entire namespace indicates the relationship or lineage of the leftmost term i.e. grandparent.parent.child. of this spider should be the EXACT name of its associated data element, which is typically: ServerName.datasourceName.dataElementName. Note: It is also possible to alter this ServerName, at any time, for all of its data elements used within a spider workspace. For details, see Changing data element referencing . When the spider workspace (engine) is started, an initial bulk read of all the data elements is performed and their initial values are retrieved. After this, Data Element spiders only receive changes made to their data elements from the Server. Triggering: When you trigger the action of causing a spider to perform its specific operation, which usually involves communicating and / or manipulating data from its set of inputs to its set of outputs. See spider. a Data Element spider its input value is written to the Server: Although, this assumes that its datasource and its security configuration allows the value of this data element to be modified.

By default, this spider is triggered by means of silks, although it can also be triggered by events.

Title: Data Element spiders
By default, this spider is triggered by means of silks, although it can also be triggered by events. These triggering methods can be configured via its spider menu, see Configuration below. Note: Triggering only occurs when the spider workspace is running i.e. this only occurs for graphic forms when they are loaded in Run mode or opened in the SmartUI Operator. Configuration: This describes the available menu items and inputs and outputs of this spider: Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note1: This menu can be accessed by selecting the spider and right-clicking its title bar. For details, see Selecting spiders . Note2: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: When this triggering method is enabled, this spider is triggered after the specified event is raised. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Substitutions: To create either a data element substitution for a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. or a place holder for a data element of a datasource that is currently unavailable. For details, see the details provided for the manual creation method above. Tip: The Substitutions dialog is also displayed by clicking the Substitutions spider toolbar button. - Enable Silk Triggering: When this triggering method is enabled, a silk triggers this spider, after it has set this spider’s input value. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. Note: A silk is only able to trigger this spider in this way, if its Trigger Output Spider setting is enabled. For details, see Disabling silk triggering of spiders . - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. Note1: Before the spider can be configured, its configuration view needs to be displayed. For details see Displaying spider configuration views . Note2: For details on using the general fields and sections of the configuration view, see Working with spider configuration views . This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Note: These inputs can either be configured within the spider itself and/or may require their values to be supplied by other spiders or Data spiders (e.g. properties or data elements). For details, see Creating silks . Input Data Function Value DE This contains the specified data element. - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Note: Some or all of these outputs can be used to supply the inputs of other spiders or Data spiders (e.g. properties or data elements). Output Data Function Value DE This contains the specified data element. Note: Since the Data Element spider automatically fetches the most recent value of its data element value from the Server, there is no way to re-read or force a read of a data element value from the Server. Message String The informative message or instruction that is displayed above the value edit box within the dialog itself. This is 'Change the value to:' by default. Confirmation message String The informative text that is displayed by the confirmation dialog. This is 'Change the value from {0} to {1}?' by default. When specifying this text, the following placeholders can be used: {0}: The Default Value . {1}: New (entered) value {2}: User name, of the currently logged in user, when the value was changed. Log change event? Boolean This enables or disables the logging of an event to an event log when the value is changed. For details, see Logging data entry changes .

Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration Top Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration Data Execution Prevention (DEP) prevents damage from viruses and other security threats that attack by running (executing) malicious code from memory locations that only Windows and other programs should use. However, when this is NOT configured to use the default setting (typically this occurs on Windows Server 2003 although can occur on other operating systems that provide this such as Windows XP etc.), then the Agent Server can become unable to read the HASP at start up, which will cause the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. To check whether DEP is enabled on your computer and to ensure that it is appropriately configured for Adroit to function correctly, please perform the following steps: - Right click on My Computer and select Properties . - Select the Advanced tab and click the Settings button under the Performance heading. This will display the Performance Options dialog. - Select the Data Execution Prevention tab - if you do not see this tab, it is not installed on your computer. - The default setting is Turn on DEP for essential Windows programs and service only , however computers that exhibit the above symptom will have Turn on DEP for all programs and services except those I select enabled . If not, the problem lies elsewhere. - If the DEP option has been enabled for all programs, click the Add… button and browse for and add both the AS.EXE and ASS.EXE executables from the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . - Reboot the computer. -->

Purpose: to display various statistics for an analogue (floating point) process variable (PV), which are calculated over a during a rolling time period, which specifies the maximum sampling time from "now" (the current time) into the past for the specified period.

Title: Analogue Data Links
Purpose: to display various statistics for an analogue (floating point) process variable (PV), which are calculated over a during a rolling time period, which specifies the maximum sampling time from "now" (the current time) into the past for the specified period. In this case the values are recorded every second over this timespan and the statistics are calculated from these recorded values. For more information, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . Certain analogue data links also allow users to configure the required setpoint (SP) value associated with this PV. PLEASE NOTE: These statistics are ONLY calculated by the Analog agent representing the process variable, when its statsPeriod slot is set to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10 (minutes), since the default value of 0 DISABLES the calculation of these statistics, since if used excessively they can affect performance. Description: A rectangle with a grey background displaying the following information: - the analogue process variable (PV) - the value slot of the Analog agent - in black, - the units of this value (the unit slot of the Analog agent), if specified, below this in light grey (otherwise it is not displayed) and - below this the average value of this process variable (PV) calculated over the rolling period Note: This value will always be 0 until you set the statsPeriod slot of this Analog agent to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10. - below this an optional setpoint (SP) value, in blue, which is a separate analogue whose value can be set from this wizard, by clicking on this value and entering the required value in the input dialog. - an alarm priority indication, when applicable and only when the associated alarm bit has been specified User interaction: Clicking on the Data Link displays a tool tip that contains the following additional statistical information calculated for this analogue process variable (PV) for an agent-specific rolling period: - Avg Max : the maximum value recorded for this value during the current rolling period. - Avg Min : the minimum value recorded for this value during the current rolling period. - Avg Deviation : the standard deviation of all the recorded value during the current rolling period. Note: These values will always be 0 until you set the statsPeriod slot of this Analog agent to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10.

When the wizard displays a setpoint (SP) value, then by selecting this value an operator can enter the required value in the input dialog that opens and then click its Finish button.

Data Logging Compression Methods Top Data Logging Compression Methods Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes.

Title: Data Logging Compression Methods
Data Logging Compression Methods Top Data Logging Compression Methods Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged. - Using the Time deadband: One of the following Compression Method algorithms is used to determine which value is logged, if the logged value changes MORE THAN ONCE during the specified deadband period: IMPORTANT: To use a logging Compression Method, you need to use a Time logging deadband that is greater than 0. Actual The logged value is the value at the end of the specified Time deadband. Average a time-weighted average is maintained for all the changes that occur and this is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Minimum The lowest or minimum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Maximum The highest or maximum value is logged at the end of the specified Time deadband. Of the provided methods, the Average method is recommended, since it calculates a time-weighted average of all the values that were recorded during the Time deadband period and this average is then logged at the end of this period. For this reason a 1-hour average (as opposed to a 1-hour interval raw log) will provide a more accurate representation of what happened in the plant, than the same raw log. Since the raw log value will only represent the instantaneous value in the hour, not the average for the hour. -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Dataset Data DataSet This should provide the dataset (table) that contains the required rows and their columns. Once the required dataset data has been added to this spider, the columns within this dataset are exposed as outputs of this spider. For details, see Exposing dataset columns . Note: The topmost row in each column is used to name these outputs. Filter Column String Specify the name of the column that is to be used to filter out the row from this dataset data. For details, see Filtering out a row . Tip: Typically this requires typing in the name of the output that specifies the required column name. Filter Key String, Numeric, DateTime Specify the value that the specified Filter Column must match to filter out the required row. Note1: This displays the FIRST entry that matched this value. Note2: No sorting of this dataset is performed by this spider. -->

Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent Top Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent The method of data sampling offered by the Statistical agent is called STREAMING, whereby all the collected input values are placed in one sample for analysis.

Title: Specifications
Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent Top Data Specification Method for Statistical Agent The method of data sampling offered by the Statistical agent is called STREAMING, whereby all the collected input values are placed in one sample for analysis. Each input value may be collected on an event basis, and is called a STREAM EVENT. The Stream Event method takes the input agent’s values, either when triggered by another agent, or when its input value changes, and calculates the statistical data (Maximum, Minimum, Average, Standard Deviation, Total and Rate) for all the values collected, treating the values as being part of a single sample. -->

However, the start and end points of the silks to or from the Data spiders are specified, by the direction of their arrows within the spider workspace. Example: Note: The Data spiders to which silks are linked can also be inferred from the starting or ending position of the silk relative to the respective tree, which changes accordingly as tree nodes are expanded and collapsed. Data spiders also behave differently within the spider workspace, when their configuration views are hidden or displayed, as follows: - In Expanded mode, in addition to displaying its configuration view the Data spider also graphically indicates its associated data element or property. This is denoted by a light-purple ray, which expands from the position of the data element or property tree node to the appropriate side of the configuration view. If the associated node is collapsed, then the ray points to the topmost collapsed branch hiding this tree node. For details on closing its configuration view, see Hiding spider configuration views . Example: - In Collapsed mode, Data spiders may disappear from view in the spider workspace and are located in their respective tree nodes and cannot be further configured, although, silks can still be dragged to and from these tree nodes. For details on displaying its configuration view, see Displaying spider configuration views . Data Structure of an Agent Top Data Structure of an Agent Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, which are referred to as agent attributes.

Title: Data Structure of an Agent
Data Structure of an Agent Top Data Structure of an Agent Most agents are designed to contain multiple items of data, which are referred to as agent attributes. Most of these attributes are accessible to clients of the Agent Server as slots of the agent. For details, see About Agent Data (Slots) . An agent's "state", at any instant in time, is defined as the collective values of all its data. Agents have both generic and type-specific data. - Generic or header slots are found in all types of agents. Note: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Examples of header slots are: - agentDescription for describing purpose of the agent - status a 32 bit word recording agent status - Type-specific slots pertain only to agents of the specific type. Examples of type-specific slots, this time taken from an Analog agent, are: - rawValue: used to hold the raw or unconditioned value read in from a front end device - value: conditioned or scaled value of the Analog rawValue in engineering units of your choice - engMin: minimum scaled value in engineering units An illustration of the actual values for some of the slots found in an instance of an Analog agent is shown below: Slot Name Slot Value Header slots agentTypeName agentDescription status Analog Level of Tank No.1 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 Type-specific slots rawValue value engMin 2661.75 65.0 0 -->

Current behaviours work on the principle that you must first select a control or vector, which displays the relevant behaviour types available for the selected control or vector.

Title: Configuration
Current behaviours work on the principle that you must first select a control or vector, which displays the relevant behaviour types available for the selected control or vector. You can select and configure a behaviour required for the control or vector. The above process is not suitable for all Database Behaviour action scenarios and requires modification to allow for a slightly different flow for the following reason: It is possible that without a Database Behaviour action, you may use the current configuration options available with spiders and silks, to successfully execute a query without interacting with a control or vector at all. For example, an Update , Delete or Insert query can be triggered through the following methods, Propagate at Startup or Trigger from event (for example, the Form.Click event) . The Database Behaviour is always selectable regardless of whether a control (or vector) is used or not. Let’s go through each step required to configure a new Database Behaviour. STEP 1: Launching a Database Behaviour The Database icon is always available for selection, regardless of whether a control or vector is selected. One of the following two scenarios can be used to create a new Database Behaviour: - As with other behaviours, you may select the relevant control or vector to display the resultant dataset from a query. - Click the Behaviours toolbar menu item then select the Database icon in the Behaviours ribbon of the SmartUI Designer. - Alternatively, click the Smart Tag on the selected control or vector, then select the Database Behaviour option from the selection list of available behaviours. - If control or vector is not selected in the graphic form itself, you can still select the Database icon in the Behaviours ribbon. - You use this option to execute a query type that does not return a resultant dataset to a control or vector on a graphic form. - For example, an Insert query only does database-side processing and does not return a dataset to the DataGridView control. STEP 2 (Optional): Select the appropriate Apply to property option to apply to the query dataset Note: If no control or vector is selected before opening the Database Behaviour dialog, the property list won’t be available, and this step becomes irrelevant, then proceed to step 3 . The following default properties are available, depending on the type of properties contained in the selected control or vector. You can change the selected property, if necessary: - For a control with a DataSource property, such as the DataGridView control, this property is selected by default. - The DataSource property can consume an entire data table but is only appropriate for SelectQuery types. - All other properties using simple types, such as int , string or bool , are also included in the property list. - Complex property types are excluded. - For a control with both a DataSource and a DisplayMember property, such as a Listbox or Combobox control. - The DataSource property is selected by default. - All other properties using simple types, such as int , string or bool , are also included in the property list. - For a control that does not contain a DataSource property. - All properties using simple types, such as int, string or bool, are included in the property list. - An appropriate default property is selected depending on the selected control and its property list. - For example, the Text property is selected by default for a Label or Button control. - If a control has no DataSource property and no properties using simple types. - The Apply to property option is hidden. - You can still trigger the selected query from an event on a control.

STEP 3: Select the Server to retrieve your resultant query dataset Similar to the Query Spider in the Spider Configuration: - The Default Server placeholder name and all available servers are listed for selection in the Enterprise Manager of the SmartUI.

Title: Configuration
STEP 3: Select the Server to retrieve your resultant query dataset Similar to the Query Spider in the Spider Configuration: - The Default Server placeholder name and all available servers are listed for selection in the Enterprise Manager of the SmartUI. - The Default Server is selected as the default option. STEP 4: Select the OLEDB Data Source to retrieve your resultant query dataset Similar to the Query Spider in the Spider Configuration: - All the configured data sources of type OLEDB for the server, selected in the previous step, are listed for selection. - You will encounter one of the following scenarios, when: No OLEDB data sources are configured for the selected server. - A New Data Source button is available. - Click the button to create a connection to the required source of data. - You can create a new OLEDB data source without closing the behaviour dialog and then reopening it to continue. One or multiple OLEDB data sources are configured for the selected server. - The list of data sources available for connection are listed alphabetically, but none are selected by default. - You may still click the New Data Source button to create a connection to a required source of data. - A Connection Details button is available to view the details of the currently selected OLEDB data source. When a valid data source has been selected. - The Query Type option becomes visible. STEP 5: Select the Query Type you want to use to retrieve your resultant query dataset Similar to the Query Spider in the Spider Configuration: - All available query types are listed in the Query Type selection list for the selected OLEDB Data Source . - No query type is selected by default. - In the selection list, each query type displays the number of currently configured queries for that specific type, in brackets, after the query type name, e.g. SelectQuery (3). - You will encounter one of the following scenarios, where: None of the available query types have any queries configured for them for the selected OLEDB data source. - After selecting a query type, a New query button is available that you may click to create a new query for the selected query type. One or more of the available query types has one or more queries configured for them for the selected OLEDB data source. - Each query type that has queries configured for it displays the number of configured queries, in brackets, after the query type name, e.g. SelectQuery (3) . - After selecting a query type that has one or more queries configured for it, a New query button becomes available. Two additional things will occur: When a valid query type has been selected. - The Query Name option becomes visible. For all query types other than the SelectQuery type. - The Apply to property option at the top of the Database Behaviour dialog is hidden because this option is irrelevant for non-SelectQuery types. - All other query types only do database-side processing, with no resultant dataset to display. - The reason is that only a SelectQuery returns viewable data (i.e. a dataset) , that can be used to display database records on a control or vector. STEP 6: Select the Query Name you want to execute After you’ve selected the query you want to run from the available list of queries, or a new query you have created, you will have access to a View query button that may be used to view the actual SQL query statement associated with the query. Related to the selected query, you will encounter one of the following scenarios: Query Type Selection Effect Query type SelectQuery selected.

- The selected property is DataSource .

Title: Configuration
- The selected property is DataSource . - The selected control or vector has a DisplayMember property. - Field Name option is made visible. - For example, with a Listbox or Combobox control, only one data field record can be displayed. Query type SelectQuery selected. - The selected property is DataSource . - The selected control or vector does not have a DisplayMember property. - Field Name option is hidden. - For example, with a DataGridView control, all the data field records are displayed. Query type SelectQuery selected. - The selected property is a Simple data type . - For example, an int , a string or bool. - Field Name option is visible. - For example, with a Label or Button control, only one record from one field is displayed using the Text property. - SelectQuery type is not available for selection. - The selected control or vector does not have any valid properties. - A resultant dataset for a query type SelectQuery cannot be displayed. For all other query types selected. - These are not of type SelectQuery. - The Apply to property option is hidden. Query selected contains parameters. - The Parameters tab is visible. - Lets you select the source inputs of each parameter. - Configuring Parameters is discussed in the next section . STEP 7 (Optional): Select the Field Name you want to display For one of the scenarios in the previous step where the Field Name option is made visible. - When selecting a field name, Database Behaviour only displays records from that field in the selected control or vector. - Only relevant to queries of type SelectQuery . STEP 8 (Optional): Do you want to be prompted for confirmation before the query is executed? The Confirm Action option only applies to queries that are not of type SelectQuery . - By default, the non-compulsory Confirm Action option is not selected. - If Confirm Action is selected, the Database Behaviour prompts you to confirm that the query must be executed. STEP 9 (Optional): Do you want the execution of the query be triggered from an event? The Trigger from event option applies to all query types. - By default, this non-compulsory Trigger from event option is not selected. - If not selected, the Database Behaviour is triggered through Propagate at Startup . - If selected, you can choose from the available selection list of Event Objects and Event Names , to trigger the behaviour.

It is possible to create queries where not all the parts of the query are known at the time of creating it.

Title: Configuration
It is possible to create queries where not all the parts of the query are known at the time of creating it. It is especially true that you might want to generate dynamic query results by supplying or inserting different values into the WHERE clause of the query just before the query is executed. - To help facilitate this process, the Query Spider currently provides inputs for parameters that can be driven either by a default value or from the output silk of another spider, such as a Property Spider of the Text property of a Textbox or Label control. - Warning: This type of configuration is currently a manual process and requires an advanced understanding of spiders to correctly and successfully achieve this. - The Database Behaviour solves this by giving all types of users, from beginners to advanced, access to this level of configuration without having to know and understand how to do it manually. The following steps guides you through a simple process to follow and shows you how to configure the source inputs for each parameter in the query: STEP 1: Selecting a query that contains parameters Access to the setup of parameters for a query starts with the selection of a query that contains parameters. - When a valid query is selected, the Parameters tab becomes visible. - By default, an error icon indicates that errors exist, implying that values must be provided for the parameters present in the query. The values that must be provided should consist of the following types: - The source of the input for the parameter. - Component Property is selected by default. - The value of the input for the parameter. - The parameter is blank by default. - The Default value of the parameter. - The parameter is blank by default and only applies when the Propagate at startup option is selected. STEP 2: Opening the parameter setup dialog To set up parameters for a query, you begin with the selection of a query that contains parameters and then select the Parameters tab. - You click either the Value or Default cell of the parameter you want to edit. - The Parameter Setup dialog will open. Starting with the first dialog, the following options are available: - Previous and Next arrow buttons can be used to browse through all the available parameters, without having to close the dialog and select another parameter. - The name of the current parameter is displayed.

- The Source selection box provides you with the following three options to select from: - Component Property – if selected, you can choose the property of a control or vector for the parameter.

Title: Configuration
- The Source selection box provides you with the following three options to select from: - Component Property – if selected, you can choose the property of a control or vector for the parameter. - Constant – if selected, you can enter any alphanumeric value for the parameter. - Data Element – if selected, you can browse for, or type in, any Data Element value for the parameter. - The Value of the current parameter being configured and is relevant to the Source selected. - The Default value used for the parameter and only applies when the Propagate at startup option is selected. - The Close button will close the dialog and apply the last parameter configuration to the Database Behaviour . STEP 3: After all parameters have been configured If you have configured all the parameters correctly and no errors are displayed on the Parameters tab, you click Finish to save the behaviour. To edit a parameter that has already been configured. - Simply click on the Value or Default selection lists of the parameter you wish to edit. - This will launch the Parameter Setup dialog again. -->

Datalog Catchup Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog Top Datalog catch-up Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog - The progress slot: This displays the progress of the current synchronization process as a percentage of datalog agents that have been synchronised on that Agent Server in the cluster. - The tagRestoring slot: This displays the datalog agent that is currently being synchronised by the systemDatalog agent. - The information slot: This contains general information regarding the synchronization process including error messages if an error occurs or if the synchronization process is stopped unexpectedly, for instance by putting a 0 unto the start slot, or if the cluster partner is unavailable. - The realTimeRate slot: This indicates how many points were datalogged by all of the datalog agents in the last second. - The catchupRate slot: This indicates the rate at which data points are being merged into the local datalogs from the cluster partner. - The totalRate slot: This is the sum of the realTimeRate and the catchupRate slots. - The Qfree slot: This represents the percentage of the datalog buffer queue that is currently free. -->

Title: Server Scripts datasources
The MinimumScriptSchedulingTime SmartUI Server setting specifies the minimum interval time (in seconds) for scheduling of a script in a SmartUI Server Script Datasource. The default minimum interval is 30 seconds.

The way to set this up is as follows: The format argument consists of one or more codes; as in printf, the formatting codes are preceded by a percent sign (%). Characters that do not begin with % are copied unchanged to string. The time category of the current locale as set in the Control Panel affects the output formatting. The formatting codes are listed below: %a - Abbreviated weekday name %A - Full weekday name %b - Abbreviated month name %B - Full month name %c - Date and time representation appropriate for locale %d - Day of month as decimal number (01 - 31) %H - Hour in 24-hour format (00 - 23) %I - Hour in 12-hour format (01 - 12) %j - Day of year as decimal number (001 - 366) %m - Month as decimal number (01 - 12) %M - Minute as decimal number (00 - 59) %p - Local AM / PM indicator for 12-hr clock %S - Second as decimal number (00 - 59) %U - Week of year as decimal number, with Sunday as first day of week (00 - 51) %w - Weekday as decimal number (0-6; Sunday is 0) %W - Week of year as decimal number, with Monday as first day of week (00 - 51) %x - Date representation for current locale %X - Time representation for current locale %y - Year without century, as decimal no. (00 - 99) %Y - Year with century, as decimal number %z, %Z - Time-zone name or abbreviation; no characters if time zone is unknown %% - Percent sign As in the printf function, the # flag may prefix any formatting code. In that case, the meaning of the format code is changed as follows: %#c Long date and time representation, appropriate for current locale. For example: "Tuesday, March 16, 1993, 12:41:29". %#x Long date representation, appropriate to current locale. For example: "Tuesday, March 16, 1993". %#d, %#H, %#I, %#j, %#m, %#M, %#S, %#U, %#w, %#W, %#y, %#Y Remove any leading zeros hour INTEGER The hour of day. localTime TIME The local time. This is the local time for the UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time in the time zone where the Agent Server is running. The breakdown of minutes etc. in the integer slots are local time. Note: It is not possible to externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent, for instance via a mimic EXCEPT by using the "Set to now" button of the date agent dialog or by using the "settime" slot of the date agent which also "sets the date and time to now". milliSecond INTEGER The millisecond of second. minute INTEGER The minute of hour. month INTEGER The month of year. second INTEGER The second of minute. setTime BOOLEAN Set agent to current time. uctTime TIME The time in Coordinated Universal Time ( UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). ). This is the native form for all times in the Agent Server. The native form for Client applications is Local Time.

Therefore, what a Client application should do when getting a Time, is always convert it to local time before displaying it.
