Date and Time formatting syntax Top Date and Time formatting syntax The following format specifiers can be used when formatting date and/or time data: Commonly used date and time format specifiers: These produce standard date and time formats.

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
Date and Time formatting syntax Top Date and Time formatting syntax The following format specifiers can be used when formatting date and/or time data: Commonly used date and time format specifiers: These produce standard date and time formats. These date and time format strings, consist of a single format specifier character from the following table. Note: If the format string is longer than a single character (even if the extra characters are white spaces), the format string is interpreted as a custom format string. The following table describes these standard date and time format strings. Note1: The output produced by some of these format specifiers is influenced by the current Regional Options settings. Computers using different settings will generate different results. Note2: The example outputs specified in this table assume that a DateTime value of 8/20/2004 11:12:45 AM is being formatted. Format Specifier Name Description Format string = Output d Short date pattern This formatting may vary. d = 8/20/2004 D Long date pattern This formatting may vary. D = Friday, August 20, 2004 t Short time pattern This formatting may vary. t = 11:12 AM T Long time pattern This formatting may vary. T = 11:12:45 AM f Full date/time pattern (short time) Displays a combination of the long date and short time patterns, separated by a space. f = Friday, August 20, 2004 11:12 AM F Full date/time pattern (long time) This formatting may vary. F = Friday, August 20, 2004 11:12:45 AM g General date/time pattern (short time) Displays a combination of the short date and short time patterns, separated by a space. g = 8/20/2004 11:12 AM G General date/time pattern (long time) Displays a combination of the short date and long time patterns, separated by a space. G = 8/20/2004 11:12:45 AM M or m Month day pattern This formatting may vary. M = August 20 R or r RFC1123 pattern This formatting always adheres to the following defined standard pattern: "ddd, dd MMM yyyy HH:mm:ss G\MT". Note: The time displayed is for local, rather than universal (GMT) time. r = Fri, 20 Aug 2004 11:12:45 GMT s Sortable date/time pattern; conforms to ISO 8601 This formatting always adheres to the following custom pattern "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss".

s = 2004-08-20T11:12:45 u Universal sortable local date/time pattern This formatting always adheres to the following defined standard pattern: "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ssZ".

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
s = 2004-08-20T11:12:45 u Universal sortable local date/time pattern This formatting always adheres to the following defined standard pattern: "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ssZ". Note: The time displayed is for local, rather than universal (GMT) time. u = 2004-08-20 11:12:45Z U Universal sortable GMT date/time pattern Note: The time displayed is for the universal (GMT), rather than local time. U = Friday, August 20, 2004 9:12:45 AM Note: This currently non-sortable format is caused by .NET. Y or y Year month pattern This formatting may vary. y = August, 2004 If these commonly used date and time format specifiers do not provide the type of formatting you require, you can use the following custom format strings to further enhance your output: Custom date and time format specifiers: Combine one or more of the following custom format specifiers to construct a format that yields the output you prefer. The following table describes the custom format specifiers and the results they produce. Note1: The output produced by some of these format specifiers is influenced by the current Regional Options settings. Computers using different settings will generate different results. Note2: The example outputs specified in this table assume that a DateTime value of 8/20/2004 1:14:48 PM is being formatted. Format Specifier Name Description Format string = Output d Single or double digit day Displays the current day of the month, as a number between 1 and 31, inclusive. If the day is a single digit only (1-9), then it is displayed as a single digit. Note: If this single 'd' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard short date pattern format specifier. %d = 20 dd Double digit day Displays the current day of the month, as a number between 1 and 31, inclusive. If the day is a single digit only (1-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). dd = 20 ddd Abbreviated day name Displays the abbreviated name of the day. ddd = Fri dddd (or more d's) Full day name Displays the full name of the day. ddddd = Friday f, ff, fff, ffff, fffff, ffffff, fffffff Second fractions Displays seconds fractions represented by a number of digits, which are determined by the number of f's that are used (up to 7 digits).

Note: If this single 'f' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the full (long date + short time) format specifier.

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
Note: If this single 'f' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the full (long date + short time) format specifier. %f = 7 ffff = 7724 g (or more g's) Era Displays the era (A.D. for example) . Note: If this single 'g' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard general format specifier. gg = A.D. h Single or double digit hour Displays hours in the range 1-12, representing whole hours passed since either midnight (12) or noon (12). If this format is used alone, then the same hour before or after noon is indistinguishable. If the hour is a single digit (1-9), it is displayed as a single digit. Note: No rounding occurs when displaying the hour. For example, a time of 5:43 returns 5. h = 1 hh (or more h's) Double digit hour Displays hours in the range 1-12, representing whole hours passed since either midnight (12) or noon (12). If this format is used alone, then the same hour before or after noon is indistinguishable. If the hour is a single digit (1-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). hhh = 01 H Single or double digit hour, 24hr format Displays hours in the range 0-23, representing whole hours passed since midnight (0). If the hour is a single digit (0-9), it is displayed as a single digit. H = 13 HH (or more H's) Double digit hour, 24hr format Displays hours in the range 0-23, representing whole hours passed since midnight (0). If the hour is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). HHHHH = 13 m Single or double digit minute Displays minutes in the range 0-59, representing whole minutes passed since the last hour. If the minute is a single digit (0-9), it is displayed as a single digit. Note: If this single 'm' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard month day pattern format specifier. %m = 14 mm (or more m's) Double digit minute Displays minutes in the range 0-59, representing whole minutes passed since the last hour.

If the minute is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09).

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
If the minute is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). mmmm = 14 M Single or double digit month Displays the month, as a number between 1 and 12, inclusive. If the month is a single digit (1-9), it is displayed as a single digit. Note: If this single 'M' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard month day pattern format specifier. %M = 8 MM Double digit month Displays the month, as a number between 1 and 12, inclusive. If the month is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). MM = 08 MMM Abbreviated month name Displays the abbreviated name of the month. MMM = Aug MMMM (or more M's) Full month name Displays the full name of the month. MMMM = August s Single or double digit second Displays seconds in the range 0-59, representing whole seconds passed since the last minute. If the second is a single digit (0-9), it is displayed as a single digit only. Note: If this single 's' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard sortable date/time pattern format specifier. %s = 48 ss (or more s's) Double digit second Displays seconds in the range 0-59, representing whole seconds passed since the last minute. If the second is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). sss = 48 t Abbreviated A.M./P.M. designator Displays the first character of the A.M./P.M. designator. If the total number of whole hours passed is less than 12, then the A.M. designator is used. Otherwise, the P.M. designator is used. Note: If this single 't' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard long time pattern format specifier. %t = P tt (or more t's) Full A.M./P.M. designator Displays the full A.M./P.M. designator. If the total number of whole hours passed is less than 12, then the A.M. designator is used. Otherwise, the P.M. designator is used. ttttt = PM y Single or double digit year Displays years, by omitting the first two digits of the year.

If the year is a single digit (1-9), it is displayed as a single digit.

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
If the year is a single digit (1-9), it is displayed as a single digit. Note: If this single 'y' format specifier is used alone, without other custom format strings, it will be interpreted as the standard short date pattern format specifier. %y = 4 yy Double digit year Displays years, by omitting the first two digits of the year. If the year is a single digit (1-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09). yy = 04 yyyy Four digit year Displays years, including the century. If the year is less than four digits in length, then preceding zeros are appended as necessary to make the displayed year four digits long. yyyy = 2004 z Single or double digit time zone offset in hours. Displays the time zone offset for the system's current time zone in whole hours only. The offset is always displayed with a leading or trailing sign (zero is displayed as "+00"), indicating hours ahead of Greenwich mean time (+) or hours behind Greenwich mean time (-). The range of values is –12 to +13. If the offset is a single digit (0-9), it is displayed as a single digit with the appropriate leading sign. The displayed offset is affected by daylight savings time. z = +2 zz Double digit time zone offset in hours. Displays the time zone offset for the system's current time zone in whole hours only. The offset is always displayed with a leading or trailing sign (zero is displayed as "+00"), indicating hours ahead of Greenwich mean time (+) or hours behind Greenwich mean time (-). The range of values is –12 to +13. If the offset is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09) with the appropriate leading sign. The displayed offset is affected by daylight savings time. zz = +02 zzz (or more z's) Full time zone offset (hours and minutes) Displays the full time zone offset for the system's current time zone in hours and minutes. The offset is always displayed with a leading or trailing sign (zero is displayed as "+00:00"), indicating hours ahead of Greenwich mean time (+) or hours behind Greenwich mean time (-). The range of values is –12:00 to +13:00. If the offset is a single digit (0-9), it is formatted with a preceding 0 (01-09) with the appropriate leading sign.

The displayed offset is affected by daylight savings time.

Title: Date and Time formatting syntax
The displayed offset is affected by daylight savings time. zzzz = +02:00 : Time separator Separates the components within a displayed time. hh:mm:ss = 01:14:48 / Date separator Separates the components within a displayed date. dd/mm/yyyy = 20/14/2004 %c Standard format specifier usage override for identical custom format specifier characters. Where 'c' is both a standard format specifier and a custom format specifier, this will display the custom format pattern associated with the format specifier. Otherwise 'c' would be interpreted as a standard format specifier. %d = 20 -->

Date and Time Settings Top Date and Time Settings By using the Date and Time option you can change the date, time and time zone of your system's clock.

Title: Date and Time Settings
Date and Time Settings Top Date and Time Settings By using the Date and Time option you can change the date, time and time zone of your system's clock. It is important that your system date and time are always accurate as many of the Adroit applications use this to record information and to print reports. For example the Event viewer and Scheduler. To set the date and time . WARNING: Never turn the PC clock backwards because certain internal transactions made after the back-tracking are ignored or rejected due to their timestamp now being "suddenly in the future". This will cause erratic Behaviour in Adroit . The Support Desk cannot deal with problems caused by rolling the system clock backwards. Golden Rule: Don't fiddle with your PC clock!! -->

DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering Top DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering This enables the remote execution of the configured transaction by the DbAccess Agent.

Title: DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering
Steps:
DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering Top DbAccess Transaction Scheduling and Triggering This enables the remote execution of the configured transaction by the DbAccess Agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling are configured in the dialog box which is displayed after clicking the Edit… button in the main edit window of the DbAccess Agent. The remote-execution mechanisms of the transactions are: - Triggering only: This is used when the transactions are only required after a particular condition has been met by the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions . When one of the conditions, in the list of triggers, is met – then database transactions are executed by the DbAccess Agent. - Scheduling only: This is used when the transactions are required at a set period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the scheduling to be configured . - Triggering and Scheduling: In this case a transaction will be executed when its scheduled and whenever a condition in the list of triggers is met. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling . (Note the And only if triggered option remains disabled for this option) - Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the scheduled transaction will only be executed if a condition in the list of triggers is met at the configured transaction ‘Run Every’ time. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple transactions. This requires configuring one or more triggering expressions and configuring the scheduling and enabling the And only if triggered option. -->

Note: If you specify global , the Global OLE DB connection string of the Agent Server is used, which is specified in the Adroit Config Editor . - Typically, you can launch this tool from the Desktop shortcut. - Select the Agent Server Configuration Welcome menu item. - Select the Advanced Agent Server Configuration option. - At the bottom of the dialog, the Global OLE DB connection field is available for you to specify this connection string. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN Disable SQL logging on standby cluster node – default is TRUE housekeepDays INTEGER Specifies the maximum number of days to keep records for. Title: DBQuery Agent Slot Detail
Steps:
DBQuery Agent Slot Detail Top DBQuery Agent Slot Detail The DBQuery agent contains various slot categories. Select the options below to view more information on each category. DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. - If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds may be entered that will determine the execution interval of the transaction. - A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value goes to zero. 1 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value leaves zero. 2 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value changes. The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. tagList LIST Sets the list of tag values to be retrieved by the built-in SELECT statement. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. triggerTag TAGNAME The trigger tag to be used. - Indicates the trigger tag used in conjunction with the trigger method. - This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . - The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). - A value of [0] will disable the pulse. - Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. - The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that will be applied to the built-in SELECT statement. DBQuery Information slots The following slots are used for information only and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description badTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every unsuccessful transaction and denotes the number of bad transactions since starting the agent server. goodTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every successful transaction and denotes the number of good transactions since starting the agent server. lastDuration INTEGER A slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. - Successful transactions will display “None”. lastErrorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. - This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently set to on [1]. lastQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the last SQL Query that was executed. lastTime TIME This slot captures the last time a transaction was executed. resetRunNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ this slot will cause the agent to automatically reset the runNow slot value to ‘0’ after a transaction has completed. - The default value is set to enabled.

- This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC.

Title: DBQuery Agent Slot Detail
Steps:
- This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC. runNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ the agent will execute a transaction ONLY if the agent is enabled AND connected to the database. totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started. DBQuery Runtime slots The following slots are used for runtime operations and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery agent functions. Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. - If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. - The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. - Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. - Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. SuccessPulse Also known as StatusBit18 A short pulse is generated on a successful transaction. - The default length of this pulse can configured using the pulseWidth configuration slot. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms or as set in the pulseWidth slot) , if the last transaction succeeded. -->

Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. - If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. - The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. - Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. - Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. SuccessPulse Also known as StatusBit18 A short pulse is generated on a successful transaction. - The default length of this pulse can configured using the pulseWidth configuration slot. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms or as set in the pulseWidth slot) , if the last transaction succeeded. -->

MaxDemand, OEE, PID - IT : these agent types facilitate the integration and management of SCADA and IT Audit, DumpConfig, ICMP, Perfmon, SNMPMgr - System : these agent types are used internally to perform certain SCADA and other specific functions. Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan, SystemDataLog, SystemInformation - Primitive : these agent types are primitive because they offer limited value and are limited in functionality when compared to the Basic agents, they are essentially single value containers. Default Alarm Management Queries Top Default Alarm Management Queries The following queries are displayed by the View data and unless otherwise noted the View graph dialogs: Tip: You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
Default Alarm Management Queries Top Default Alarm Management Queries The following queries are displayed by the View data and unless otherwise noted the View graph dialogs: Tip: You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements. Click for more details: Click the Edit KPI's button in the Edit AlarmManagement agent dialog; in the Edit Alarm Management KPI values dialog, double click the appropriate KPI (row) to change its value. Current incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions are still active and/or which have NOT been fully responded to. In other words they still need to be acknowledged and/or have their required reasons specified and/or have their required notes specified. On the basis of 6 alarms per hour this should never have more than 6 incidents under normal operating conditions or 60 under abnormal operating conditions. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents: All incidents whose alarmed conditions have returned to normal and which have been fully responded to, if necessary, for the specified period of time. In other words they have been acknowledged and/or had their required reasons specified and/or had their required notes specified. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration during set time periods. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by operator: Incidents which have been logged against the specified operator. This can be used to analyse the effectiveness of your operators. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Historical incidents by category: Incidents which have occurred for a specific category. This can be used to analyse your alarm configuration for specific process areas. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Outstanding reasons and notes: All incidents that still need reasons and/or notes specified. Only those current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled are added to this list. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Incident count per hour: The total number of incidents that occur over each hour of the specified duration. In other words this query returns the number of logged incidents per hour for the specified duration. Typically each number should be between 6 (normal conditions) to 60 (abnormal conditions).

But different industries have different standards.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
But different industries have different standards. Burst rate: The number of incidents that occur in a 10 minute window. Calculation: Burst rate = 6 * Maximum alarm count in a 10 minute period. (this is calculated as a per hour count, hence the 6 *) This is an important measure of the usability of an alarm system and the operator's capability to deal with alarms. Typically this should be between 1 (normal conditions) to 10 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Percent upset: The number of hours where there are more than 30 incidents per hour. If you want to specify a more appropriate maximum number of alarms, then change the PUC [Percent upset count] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. Calculation: Percent upset = 100 * [Number of hours where alarms exceeds 30/hour]/[Total number of hours]. This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: - Overloaded > 50% - Reactive 25%-50% - Stable 5%-25% - Robust 1%-5% - Predictive < 1%. Priority distribution: The priority distribution for incidents occurring over a period of time. Typically this should be 5% high priority alarms (>Normal priority), 15% medium priority alarms (=Normal priority) and 80% low priority alarms (<Normal priority). But different industries have different standards. Standing alarms: The number of current incidents at the end of an hour. Typically this should be 9. But different industries have different standards. Most frequent alarms (count by type): The most frequent alarms over time, filtered only by the type. The top 20 of these alarms can account for almost 50% of total alarm generation. If properly reviewed, you will find that most of these incidents should not be classified as alarms at all, since they do not meet the proper criteria that defines an alarm, namely that they need to be responded to. Most frequent alarms (count by type and category): The most frequent alarms over time, filtered by type AND category. Intermittent incidents: The incidents that activate and deactivate within 10 seconds. If you want to specify a more appropriate time interval, then change the IAP [Intermittent alarm period (secs)] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. If properly reviewed, you will find that most of these incidents should not be classified as alarms at all, since they do not meet the proper criteria that defines an alarm. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog.

Intermittent counts: The number of incidents that activate and deactivate within 10 seconds.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
Intermittent counts: The number of incidents that activate and deactivate within 10 seconds. If you want to specify a more appropriate time interval, then change the IAP [Intermittent alarm period (secs)] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. If properly reviewed, you will find that most of these incidents should not be classified as alarms at all in that they do not meet the proper criteria that defines an alarm. Count by agent: The number of incidents specified per agent. This shows the agents that generate the greatest and least number of incidents. Count by operator: The number of incidents by operator. This shows of incidents that each operator has had to contend with. Total active time by incident: The total amount of time individual incidents have remained active. This shows how quickly or slowly incidents are being responded to. Total unacknowledged time by incident: The total amount of time individual incidents have remained unacknowledged. This shows how quickly or slowly incidents are being responded to. Hourly count grouped by hour of the day: Indicates what time of day incidents tend to occur more frequently. Hourly count by incident: The total number of individual incidents that occur per hour. This shows which incidents cause more noise during different times of the day. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Daily count: The total number of incidents occurring per day. This shows which incidents cause more noise during different times of the week. Average acknowledge time: The average time it takes for incidents to be acknowledged. This is a measure of how quickly your operators respond to incidents. Note: This query is NOT displayed by the View graph dialog. Average acknowledge time per incident: The average time it takes for individual incidents to be acknowledged. This shows which incidents take longer to acknowledge and therefore is an indication of the amount of work an operator has to do for an incident before acknowledging it. Average alarm rate: The average number of incidents that occur per hour over the specified time period. This query produces a single averaged value for the specified duration. Calculation: Average rate = [number of logged incidents]/[number of hours] Typically this should be between 6 (normal conditions) to 60 (abnormal conditions). But different industries have different standards. Bulk acknowledgement counts: The number of alarms acknowledged within a specific time period, typically 1 second.

If you want to specify a more appropriate time interval, then change the BAP [Bulk acknowledgement period (secs)] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
If you want to specify a more appropriate time interval, then change the BAP [Bulk acknowledgement period (secs)] entry in the Adr_AM_UserKPIs table. This monitors the acknowledgement behaviour of operators. This count should be equal to the number of alarms over the same period indicating that each alarm is receiving proper attention/action. Incidents not configured for acknowledgement: Lists the incidents that are not configured for acknowledgement. This advises the user that, by definition, these incidents are not alarms, but rather events. Customizing KPI target values : If necessary you can set KPI target values used by your own custom KPI queries and certain default queries to better comply with your specific requirements. -->

Default profiles Top Default profiles The SmartUI Server automatically creates a standard user profile called ‘Default’ that contains the default settings for the SmartUI Designer and SmartUI Operator. Click for more details: This profile is automatically applied to all the allowed user(s) and/or group(s) configured on the SmartUI Server, unless another profile is applied to them. For details on applying profiles to users, see Using profiles . Note: The Default profile cannot be renamed. Whenever a user logs off, the ‘Default’ profile is immediately applied to the SmartUI Designer or SmartUI Operator. To configure the work environment for all SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. users: - Edit the profile called Default and change the necessary settings. For details see Editing profiles . To reset the default profile settings: - Delete the profile called Default . For details, see Removing profiles . Title: To define a color using its ARGB sub-properties
Steps:
- If necessary, add and/or select the required color spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding color spiders . - Right-click its title bar and select Add ARGB Properties . Note: Once you add these color sub-properties you cannot remove them from this spider. This adds the following four additional Integer inputs to the Inputs section: Note: All four of these inputs only accept Integer values from 0 to 255. - A: The Alpha property, representing the transparency of this color. Transparency determines how much of the background is visible “through” this color. A value of 0 is completely transparent so that only the background and not the specified color will be visible and a value of 255 is not transparent at all. Note: For the following color properties, a value of 0 creates a color that has none of the specified color in it. - R: The Red property, representing the red component of the color. - G: The Green property, representing the green component of the color. - B: The Blue property, representing the blue component of the color. - The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note: If a String or Double value is typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either this value is removed or an Integer value is entered instead. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the A , R , G or B input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. The color input, only displays the color defined by these R, G, B properties and not the A (transparency) property. -->

Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks.

Title: What is demand scanning and how should it be used?
Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: - when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or - as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used.

Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button.

Title: Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning:
Steps:
- Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. - Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. - Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. - We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: - the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and - the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Demand scanning requires a global setting Demand scanning enabled checkbox to be checked in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor, which is accessed by clicking the Advanced Driver Options button in the bottom right of this page. This requires an Agent Server restart and sets the following DWORD registry value to 1, from the default value is 0, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\ Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI\EnableDemandScanning) The device’s ability to support demand scanning is available to the system via the new Boolean demandScanningEnabled slot in the Device agent, which is only enabled when the device (its protocol driver) supports demand scanning. IMPORTANT: Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that have been written to support it. All other drivers should have the demand scanning checkbox disabled. Note: Since it requires a lot of memory to manage these subscriptions, only enable this global setting if you need it. The Subscriptions active condition bit in the agent header (Status Bit 15 or the statusSubscribed slot) shows whether the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarmed, logged or subscribed to by any other agent will have this bit set. Note: This status bit in the agent header dialog only works if global demand scanning is enabled. In other words if global demand scanning setting is NOT enabled, this status bit is ALWAYS off. The scanning configuration dialog now contains a Demand scan checkbox, that is configurable for each scanned item and is saved in the IO flags field. The availability of this checkbox depends on the following: - will NOT be visible if the global demand scanning flag is OFF - will be visible if the global demand scanning flag is ON, in which case this will: - be disabled if the currently selected device driver type does NOT support demand scanning - be enabled if the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning -->

All other drivers should have the demand scanning checkbox disabled. Note: Since it requires a lot of memory to manage these subscriptions, only enable this global setting if you need it. The Subscriptions active condition bit in the agent header (Status Bit 15 or the statusSubscribed slot) shows whether the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarmed, logged or subscribed to by any other agent will have this bit set. Note: This status bit in the agent header dialog only works if global demand scanning is enabled. In other words if global demand scanning setting is NOT enabled, this status bit is ALWAYS off. The scanning configuration dialog now contains a Demand scan checkbox, that is configurable for each scanned item and is saved in the IO flags field. The availability of this checkbox depends on the following: - will NOT be visible if the global demand scanning flag is OFF - will be visible if the global demand scanning flag is ON, in which case this will: - be disabled if the currently selected device driver type does NOT support demand scanning - be enabled if the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning -->

Title: To fully or partially deploy a created object instance:
Steps:
Display the Deployment Options configuration dialog for the required object instance: From the Object Model datasource in the Enterprise Manager Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - Go to the Enterprise Manager category folders Datasources > Object Model > Instances - Right-click the required instance and select Deploy . - The Deployment Options configuration dialog opens. From the Context View window - Select the Context tab at the bottom of the SmartUI Designer window. - Select the required context from the list, which is typically the Default context. - Expand the necessary node . - Right-click the node and select Deploy instance(s) . - The Deployment Options configuration dialog opens. For more information about the Context View window, see the Context View tool window . Deploying the object instance By default, most of the On deployment checkboxes of the Deployment Options configuration dialog are selected: - When deployed, this object and all of its configuration are created immediately, such as: - Any new agents. - Any new devices and their scanning. - The specified alarming, logging and DBLog agents. - Important: When the global destinations (i.e. the Output / Event Logs categories) of the specified alarm routes contain agents that do not exist in the Agent Server then the deployment is not created as these agents could cause potential issues. - The Save Agent Server checkbox is also selected by default which saves this configuration to the Agent Database file of the Agent Server of the specified Adroit datasource . - To run the script defined for this object, select the Run Script checkbox as this is not selected, by default. - Note: If the Run Script checkbox is disabled (greyed out) , then the script was not defined or did not compile successfully. - Note: Currently only the script defined for this object may be run. Any scripts defined for child objects are ignored, even when no script is defined for the parent object. - Tip: Use the View button to display the associated script action before it is run. - Perform a partial deployment at this time, by clearing some of the following checkboxes: - Create agents - Create devices and scanning - Start devices - Create alarming - Important: When the global destinations (i.e. the Output / Event Logs categories) of the specified alarm routes contain agents that do not exist in the Agent Server then the deployment is not created as these agents could cause potential issues. - Create data logging - Create DB logging - Note: This configuration is only saved to the Agent Database file of the Agent Server of the Adroit datasource when you select the Save Agent Server on deployment completion checkbox. Tip: In the case of partial deployment, only the steps that have not yet been deployed are processed. In addition to these checkboxes, the dialog provides a list of agents both new and existing that the object references and a Remove current deployment button. - Important: Only the agents that are not being used by (subscribed to) other agents will be removed. - Note: The Remove current deployment button is only enabled if one or more of the referenced agents exist (i.e. they have a green background, and the instance has already been partially or completely deployed). Finally, click Deploy to perform the currently selected deployment operations or Cancel to quit. - If you selected any of the deployment checkboxes, then the Object Model Deployment Status progress dialog appears. - For more information, see the Object Model Deployment Status dialog . -->

Although there are no restrictions to the number of SmartUI Servers that any one Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Possible Client connections:
Although there are no restrictions to the number of SmartUI Servers that any one Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. can connect to, the following two constraints determine the maximum number of Clients that any one Server can be connected to: - The operating system that is running on the Server computer i.e. any Server that is not running on a Windows Server operating system, e.g. Windows Server 2003, is only able to allow 5 Clients to connect to the Server, over the Internet, at any one time. Also if more than 10 Clients are required to connect to the Server, over the LAN, at any one time, it is also recommended to use a Server operating system, as otherwise this may cause performance problems. - The licencing of the SmartUI Server i.e. this will determine the total number of possible Clients that can connect to a Server at any one time. Note: The licencing of the Server also determines if the Server has access to any additional components, such as datasources, spiders etc. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server .

When connecting Clients to Servers, the most important decision is what network topology should be used to connect the Client to the Server i.e.

Title: Network topology used for Client connections:
When connecting Clients to Servers, the most important decision is what network topology should be used to connect the Client to the Server i.e. whether to use the LAN or the Internet. Note: By default, the SmartUI Launcher can be used to deploy and update the Operator application via the selected network topology. Although this can also be used to deploy and update the Designer and additional components, such as datasources, spiders etc. if necessary. For details, see Working with the Launcher . - It is recommended that only the SmartUI Operator application be connected to the Server over the Internet, unless you are using a high bandwidth Internet connection. This is because the Designer, unlike the Operator, requires a two-way flow of data between itself and the Server, when designing graphic forms. - If one or more Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. can connect to the Server over the Internet, then the SmartUI Server needs to communicate to IIS and the firewall, if present, will also need to be configured, so that the Server can communicate to IIS and the Clients. For details, see Firewall configuration . Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . Note1: The SmartUI Web Service needs to be installed on the web server (IIS computer) to facilitate the communication between the Client and the Server. For details, see SmartUI Installations . Note2: Since the SmartUI Server only needs to communicate to IIS, these applications can be on different computers, which can even be in different domains, providing the necessary trust relationships exists between these computers. Note3: IIS is also required when exposing Web services to the Internet. -->

Designer connection settings Top Designer connection settings This page of the Setting up the Designer component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this SmartUI Designer and the specified SmartUI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the SmartUI Designer is launched, it needs to log into a SmartUI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the SmartUI Designer.

Title: Designer connection settings
Designer connection settings Top Designer connection settings This page of the Setting up the Designer component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this SmartUI Designer and the specified SmartUI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the SmartUI Designer is launched, it needs to log into a SmartUI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the SmartUI Designer. - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Designer option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Designer may not be installed. - Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Login Server: this specifies the default SmartUI Server computer that this SmartUI Designer connects to during the login process. Note: ONLY the user profiles configured on this specified SmartUI Server can be applied to the users of this SmartUI Designer. To specify the login Server computer name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Please ensure that the name of this computer is correctly spelt; otherwise the login process will not succeed. The following are typical login errors that occur when this name is incorrectly specified: - “Requested service not found” -> The Server has not completed loading yet - “No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer. To specify the required communication method: Select the required option. The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer, as follows: - Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth.

- Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection.

Title: Designer connection settings
- Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection. - Poll(send most recent values) : recommended when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. For further details concerning these methods, see About connection communication methods . The bandwidth requirements for this connection depends upon a number of factors, such as the update requirements and the size of the graphic forms. However, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: - Keep the graphic form sizes small; for example use JPG files instead of BMP files. - Plan the graphic forms beforehand with the end-user in mind, including the bandwidth that will be available. - Develop an end-to-end prototype to test in a production environment in order to satisfy all requirements (including the communication requirements). - Only once this prototype has been successfully tested should the project be completely engineered. Connection status check frequency: specify how often the SmartUI Designer should test that the SmartUI Server connection is still healthy and is not disconnected. To specify the required interval between checking the connection, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. Tip: There is little reason to change this default value, as this connection monitoring process only consumes a small amount of bandwidth and CPU usage. This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Designer settings. For details, see Setting up the Designer . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Designer settings, see the Advanced Designer settings page . -->

Title: Designer scripting settings
Steps:
Designer scripting settings Top Designer scripting settings This page of the Setting up the Designer component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that determine the default scripting environment for this SmartUI Designer : To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Designer option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Designer may not be installed. - Select the Scripting Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Default script references: specify the list of external assemblies or dynamic linked library (.DLL) files that are automatically added to each script. Note: The longer the list of references, the longer it takes to load and compile every script. Tip: This setting allows 3 rd party users to expose their product-specific assemblies (DLLs) to all their scripts. To add a default script reference: Click the Add button and browse for the required assembly. Note : Ensure that the paths of all of these files are added to the Script references paths setting so they will be located. To remove a default script reference: Select the assembly that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The reference to the selected assembly is immediately removed, so ensure that you select the required assembly. Graphic form scripting: to enable or disable the ability to script event handlers to programmatically achieve a more interactive user experience for graphic forms. For further details, see Graphic form scripting . Note: If this functionality is not required then disable it to increase the speed of loading graphic forms. To configure graphic form scripting: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. Visual Studio debugging: if you have Visual Studio 2010 or later installed, then you can use this application to edit and debug your scripts instead of the generic script editor, which only provides limited debugging functionality. To debug your scripts using Visual Studio: Either select Yes to debug your scripts using Visual Studio or No to use the generic script editor. Note: When debugging your scripts in Visual Studio, the scripts are exported to the ScriptsExport subfolder of the SmartUI ProgramData folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \ScriptsExport) in a Visual Studio-compatible format. Search paths for script references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that are referenced by your scripts. For further details regarding script references, see Managing references . WARNING! Only specify the locations to assemblies (.DLL files) that you use frequently, since an extensive list will delay the loading and compilation times of all scripts. To add a path that is to be searched: Click the Add button and browse for the required folder. To remove a path from the list: Select the path that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The selected path will immediately be deleted, therefore ensure that the required path is selected. Title: Designing graphic forms
Designing graphic forms Top Designing graphic forms Open a graphic form in the Design workspace to design it. Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . Tip: The Shapes Wizards & Examples tab of the Designer ribbon, provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project so that you can easily design your graphic forms. For details, see Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples . In particular this contains the Situational Awareness category, which contains sub-categories of wizards that allow you to create process control user interfaces that strive to minimise operator fatigue and increase their response times. For more details, see Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) . Design or configure a graphic form for the following reasons: - To provide the functionality or user interface that will allow end-users to interact with and examine the data displayed by the graphic form. - To connect data to this graphic form, gathered from any datasource. - If necessary, to manipulate data before it is displayed on the graphic form. Note: A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured (animated) graphical object that can be used to simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. For details, see Working with wizards . The graphic form toolbar provides tools to analyse and/or optimise the structure of your graphic forms. For details, see Optimizing graphic forms or Graphic form statistics . How to design a graphic form: - Add form components to the graphic form to create the user interface of a graphic form, which you can do by adding one or more Window Forms or a customised control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form. See form component. and component a hidden form component that provides additional functionality to this graphic form and some or all of its form components. See form component. and also graphic element a form component that typically provides drawing functionality for the graphic form. See form component. . For details, see Adding form components . Note: The TableLayoutPanel control allows you to add and arrange controls in a table, so that these controls can change dynamically as the application environment changes. For details, see TableLayoutPanel controls . Please Note: To specify an ampersand character '&' in a text property of a control, type in && and not just &. Since if only one '&' character is specified then when displayed, the & character does not appear and the following word is underlined instead. Tip1: Added form components can also be copied within the same graphic form or to another graphic form, effectively reducing their design time. For details, see Copying form components . Tip2: It is also possible to reuse controls and/or graphical objects that have been created from one or more configured graphic elements. For details, see Exporting and Importing controls or Exporting and importing graphic elements . Note: To make it easier to design and arrange controls, the visibility of controls cannot be modified in Design mode. This restriction, however is lifted in Run mode and in the Operator. - Connect data to the properties of the graphic form and/or the added form components . This is known as animating the graphic form, since it allows the graphic form to both display the data and provide the necessary user interaction with it.

This can be performed as follows: - Select the icon of most form components to displays a menu of common tasks.

Title: Designing graphic forms
This can be performed as follows: - Select the icon of most form components to displays a menu of common tasks. Most notably this menu allows Behaviours to be added to controls and graphic elements, which typically display the values of your data, either actually or graphically, by using the available properties of the selected control or graphic element. For details, see About Behaviours . - If you want to simply connect data to a property or vice verse, you can do this by means of drag and drop between the Enterprise Manager and the Design workspace . For details, see Quick linking . Note: To make it easier to design and arrange controls, the visibility of controls cannot be modified in Design mode. However, this restriction is lifted, in Run mode and in the Operator. For details, see Animating graphic forms . Note: Each graphic form also has an associated script which can be used to add intelligence to the events exposed by the graphic form, its controls and components. For details, see Graphic form scripting . For details, see SmartUI Templates and automatic alias creation . Tip3: Press F11 to activate the Fullscreen mode which hides everything except the selected graphic form in the Design workspace , a floating Toolbox window and floating tool and menu bars. Tip4: When designing a graphic form, click the Run toolbar button, to display exactly what an operator would see when viewing and interacting with the real-time animated graphic form. For details, see Running graphic forms . In Run mode the spider configuration window is greyed out and the ‘Preview’ watermark is displayed in the right hand bottom corner. Adding a graphic form to another graphic form : drag the required graphic form onto another and then select the appropriate configuration dialog which configures the size of each copy and arranges multiple copies on the host graphic form for you. -->

See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description DRV=string The name of protocol driver DLL, typically an eight-character string RLN=n The size of the binary dump (REG) in bytes. REG=bin_dump A binary dump of the registry configuration of the device. This makes the WGP file more portable between computers, in that if the device entry is not found in the registry it is automatically created. However the onus remains on the user to ensure that the specified driver DLL (DRV) is installed. To remove this REG entry, configure the following settings as such: RLN=0 REG= CNT=n Count of subscription specifications (@ type scanning) SUBS1=string First subscription specification SUBS2=string Second subsription specification ... ... SUBSn=string n th subscription specification CNT=m Count of scanning specifications SCAN1=string First scanning specification SCAN2=string Second scanning specification ... ... SCANm=string m th scanning specification RCV=nnnn Recovery/Cooldown period in milliseconds AGS=0 Agent Stop/Start State (0 = Stopped; 1 = Started) -->

Device Management Settings Top Device Management Settings Each SNMPMgr can manage a single device by getting and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device.

Title: Device Management Settings
Device Management Settings Top Device Management Settings Each SNMPMgr can manage a single device by getting and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. (values). The Poll settings section of the Edit SNMP Mngr Agent dialog, either enables or disables this device management and can specify a rate at which values are retrieved from the managed device and how many values are included in each polling transaction, as follows: PLEASE NOTE: If the Unlicensed checkbox (status bit indicator) is checked, then you need to correctly license your Agent Server before you can run 2 or more SNMPMgr agents. To start managing the device: to start polling (monitoring) and/or writing (controlling) and/or trapping (enabling events) of the OID values of this device. - Select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). - Click the Update button. This sets the Started (status bit 18), which checks the Started checkbox. Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. WARNING! If a SNMPMgr agent requires more than your available scan points then ALL these OID operations are DISABLED and its Error status bit is set. IMPORTANT: If the InvalidConnection status bit is set (the Invalid connection checkbox is checked), then NONE of these OID operations will be performed as the agent cannot connect to this device To stop managing the device: to stop polling and/or writing and/or trapping OID values of this device and to release the scan point licenses the agent was using for these OID operations. - Select the Disable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). - Click the Update button. The Stopped (status bit 17) is set, which checks the Stopped checkbox The Started (status bit 18) is cleared, which clears the Started checkbox. To configure the poll rate: the default rate, in milliseconds, that the agent fetches OID values (that are enabled for polling in the list) and copies these values into their associated tags. - Specify the Poll rate (INTEGER scanRate slot) in milliseconds. Note: The lowest rate is 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds). text:
Diagnostic Counters Screen Top Diagnostic Counters Screen The "Diagnostic Counters" Protocol Driver Monitor screen provides a comprehensive list of counters maintained by Protocol Driver.

Title: Diagnostic Counters Screen
Diagnostic Counters Screen Top Diagnostic Counters Screen The "Diagnostic Counters" Protocol Driver Monitor screen provides a comprehensive list of counters maintained by Protocol Driver. Example screenshot: These counters are all zeroed when the Agent Server starts, and for some drivers, also when the device agent starts. These diagnostic counters can be used to troubleshoot your device communication problems, by providing the following information: - “ Transactions ” increment every-time a transaction succeeds. A transaction fetches one or more data points. - “ Retry's ” increment every-time a transaction is retried. - xxx errors increment when there is a problem communicating. For example, Write errors increment when DTR signaling is configured but not received; by device failure or the cable not having that line wired in. - xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: - Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. - Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. - Retry’s: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. - Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. - Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. - Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. - Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. - Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. - Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. - Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. - Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. Note: These default driver performance counters, as well as any driver-specific counters, can also be displayed using the Perfmon agent . This agent is also able to copy the value of these counters into tags, which could then be reported, as required. -->

Title: Disabling silk triggering of spiders
Disabling silk triggering of spiders Top Disabling silk triggering of spiders By default, each silk connected to the input of a spider can trigger this spider. If this is not desired, then the default triggering of some or all of these silks can be disabled. This can be performed using two methods: - Disabling silk triggering per silk: This method is recommended when you need to disable the triggering of particular silk(s) connected to a spider. To disable silk triggering per silk: - Open the required spider workspace. - Right-click the required silk and select the Silks menu. - From the Silks menu select the description of the required silk. This will display a menu of options that apply to the required silk. - If a tick mark appears to the left of Trigger Output Spider , select it to remove this tick mark and disable this option. Note: Once this triggering option is disabled, this method will need to be performed again to enable the triggering of this silk. Tip: The spider workspace visually indicates the status of this property. For details, see Visual property indicators . - Disabling silk triggering per spider: This method is recommended when you need to disable all the silks that are connected to a spider, since this merely overrides the default triggering of these silks and can easily be undone if necessary. To disable silk triggering per spider: - Open the required spider workspace. - Select the required spider. - Right-click the title bar of this spider. - Select the Enable Silk Triggering item, if a tick mark appears to the left of it, to disable this option. Note: Once this triggering override is enabled, this method will need to be performed again to disable the override, so that the spider can be triggered by its input’s silks again. Working with spider workspaces . Selecting spiders . Spider title bars . -->

Note: If the default (login) Smart UI Server connection is disconnected when launching the Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. is unavailable, the launching fails until either this Smart UI Server becomes connected or you connect to another available Smart UI Server. Connections are either identified in the Enterprise Manager of the Smart UI Designer or the Projects tool window of the Smart UI Operator, as follows: - Disconnected connections are identified, by the following icon . Note: A connection that is currently disconnected needs to be updated in order for the Client to determine whether this Server is available. For details, see Updating connections. - Once this Smart UI Server becomes available, this connection will be identified, by the following icon . This icon indicates that the Smart UI Client is not logged in to the Smart UI Server. To remedy this, it is necessary to log onto this connection’s Server again. For details, see Modifying connection properties. Note: This icon will always be displayed whenever the Client is not logged into the required connection’s Server. - Once this Smart UI Server has been successfully logged in to, the connection will again be identified, by this icon and its data will be displayed. Note: If any of the data on this Server, has been used to animate graphic forms or is mapped to virtual data elements, these values will automatically be fetched from the Server too. -->
