Title: Display Value Behaviours
Display Value Behaviours Top Display Value Behaviours This Behaviour can ONLY configure controls that have String properties that end-users can see, to display the value of a specific data element. If necessary, this value can be formatted before it is displayed. Note: It is not recommended to add more than one Display Value Behaviour as typically ONLY the value of the last defined Behaviour is displayed. To configure a control to display (and format) a value: - Add or edit a Display Value Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Click the browse button to the right of the Input Data Element edit box to select the value (data element) to display, as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element. The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window.

- The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog.

Title: Display Value Behaviours
- The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. Note: If a DataSet value is selected, such as a field of a database, the Filter DataSet configuration dialog is displayed to select which value to display. - If necessary, use the String Formatting edit box to align and/or format this value before it is displayed , as follows: The required formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: {0[, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} - either type in the required formatting string directly and/or For further assistance on creating format strings, see String formatting syntax . - click the browse button and using the Format String Editor configuration dialog to specify and/or preview the specified formatting. Tip: This is usually required when the default formatting of the value is not expressive or informative enough to be useful.

- If necessary, click the Advanced View button to display the Control Property drop down list to select the required String property (other than the default for this type of control) that should display this value, as follows: The Control Property drop down list displays the String properties that the end-user will see.

Title: Display Value Behaviours
- If necessary, click the Advanced View button to display the Control Property drop down list to select the required String property (other than the default for this type of control) that should display this value, as follows: The Control Property drop down list displays the String properties that the end-user will see. By default, the Text property is selected, if it exists, since this is the most common used String property. To select another property from this list: Click the drop down list to open it and select another property. To select a property not in the list: Click the browse button to the right of this list; select the required property or sub-properties of this form component and press the Finish button. Tip1: When adding a Behaviour to a SmartUI Template A graphic form that has one or more configured aliases and is therefore designed to be displayed within a TemplateGO control. , you can use {} notation to automatically create an alias for any data element field. For more details, see Working with SmartUI Templates . Tip2: When adding a Behaviour to a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. , you can use {} notation to automatically create a substitution for any data element field. For more details, see Working with wizards . To add a Behaviour to a control or graphic element: Ensure that you have added the required control or graphic element to the graphic form. - Select the required control or graphic element. - If necessary, select the Behaviours tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: Any Behaviour that cannot be applied to this control or graphic element will be greyed out. - Select the required Behaviour from the relevant group. Tip: You can also select its glyph to display its task menu and then select the required Behaviour from the New Behaviour drop down list. This displays the configuration dialog of this Behaviour. Tip: When you add or edit a Behaviour you can name it, which makes it easier to identify the spiders and their regions associated with your Behaviours. To edit a Behaviour of a control or graphic element: - Right click the required control or graphic element to the graphic form.

- Select the required BehaviourName# menu item, where BehaviourName is the name of the added Behaviour and # usually only appears if more than one of same type of Behaviours have been added.

Title: Displaying Alarms
Displaying Alarms in Adroit Top Displaying Alarms In Adroit incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). (alarms) are stored in alarm lists, which allow them to be displayed and/or acknowledged, typically by using Alarm List Viewer windows in the Classic UI which connect to a SINGLE alarm list at a time. Both the Alarm agent and AlarmList agent provide alarm lists, with the following differences: - While the alarm list of an Alarm agent contains ALL the incidents of the agents that it is monitoring, an AlarmList agent ONLY contains the incidents of the agents that are specifically routed to it. - ONLY the alarm list of an AlarmList agent allows users to LOCALLY acknowledge alarms. - BOTH alarm lists (of an AlarmList and Alarm agent) allow users to GLOBALLY acknowledge alarms. Typically AlarmList agents are only required when you want to view alarms by process area or device. However, if you use MORE THAN ONE Alarm agent, you are UNABLE to display ALL the active incidents for your process in ONE Alarm List Viewer window, UNLESS you create a GLOBAL AlarmList agent and route ALL your incidents of ALL your Alarm agents to this GLOBAL AlarmList agent. This may mean that you need to specify more than one AlarmList as an alarm route destination for an incident, if you ALSO want to route an incident to another AlarmList agent, say one that only displays incidents for a specific plant section. For more detail on the merits of globally and locally acknowledging alarms, see About Alarm Acknowledgement . For details about using Alarm List Viewer windows to display active incidents, see Alarm List Viewer Window. -->

Title: To display the properties of an existing data element
Steps:
- If necessary, add and/or select the required Extended Data Element spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Extended Data Element spiders . - In the Inputs section, drag the required data element into the DataElement input. For details, see Creating silks . - Ensure that spider workspace is running (e.g. that the associated graphic form is in preview mode in the SmartUI Designer) and trigger the spider. This populates the other inputs and outputs with the properties of this data element, which are described as follows: Input / Output Data Function DataElement DE The data element that contains the value specified in the Value input. Name String The fully qualified namespace of the data element. Separator Character The character(s) used to separate the sub-names within the namespace of this data element specified by the Name input. SeparatorCount Integer The number of the occurrences of the separator character in the Name . ShortName String The last of the sub-names within the Name input i.e. the leaf node. ServerName String The first of the sub-names within the Name input i.e. the root node. Formatter String This may specify the default format for the Value , which is recommended by its datasource. Value variant type:Object The latest data provided in the data element. Timestamp DateTime The date and time at which the value of this data element was last updated. Status VIZNET Status Enumeration This specifies whether the value of this data element was able to be successfully read or not i.e. either GOOD or BAD, which could also indicate that the connection was lost. Dirty Boolean This essentially specifies whether the value of this data element has changed, either True or False. If Dirty is True, then the value of the data element has changed and, when applicable, the SmartUI Server has also not yet saved this value. Error Object The error object, detailing the last error experienced by this data element. Note: This is not immediately accessible, if necessary use the Reflection spider to expose its properties. For details, see Reflection spiders . CheckSerializable Boolean This specifies whether this data element can be communicated or not i.e. either Yes or No. Save Boolean This value is either Yes or No is used as a flag by the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. or Server to instruct its components (e.g. a Server datasource or UI control) as to whether they must save this value or not. It is the responsibility of the user of the data element to set or use this flag. -->

Docking tool windows Top Docking tool windows Tool windows are dockable, as such they have both a floating and docked display mode.

Title: Docking tool windows
Docking tool windows Top Docking tool windows Tool windows are dockable, as such they have both a floating and docked display mode. When a tool window is docked, it is attached to the Designer application by means of a docking area, which is usually along any of the four borders of the Design workspace window. To dock a tool window: - Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Note: Ensure that this tool window is not being auto hidden, if so deactivate this feature first. For details, see Automatically hiding and showing tool windows . - Drag the window into the required window and use the overlay menu items (namely ) to dock this window appropriately - only the supported overlay menu options indicate where this window will be placed. This will display a shadow over the selected tool window, indicating where this window will be docked - if correct then release the mouse button to accept this position. Example: Note: The position of the mouse pointer, not the edges of the tool window that you are dragging, determines which overlay menu option you select. Tip1: To move a tool window without snapping it into place or docking it, press CTRL or SHIFT while dragging it to the location you desire. Things you need to do first: - Add the required charting control to the graphic form.

Title: To drag the required data element to drive a series attribute:
Things you need to do first: - Add the required charting control to the graphic form. - Add a series to this control, as follows: right click the control and select New XXX Series from the menu, where XXX is the required series type. - Display the graphic form in the editor and ensure that this charting control is visible. - If necessary, open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, open the required datasource in the Enterprise Manager and expose the required data element. - Drag this data element from the Enterprise Manager onto the charting control in the Design workspace . - Select To Control Property… and the name of the selected charting control. - If the Series property is displayed, select it. Otherwise, select Customise…: The Edit Common Properties dialog is displayed. - Ensure that you highlight the Series property, by selecting its name, before clicking Finish . Note: Checking this property will add it to the list of immediately available properties for this control. Note: If only one series was added this is immediately connected to it - If one or more series has been added to this charting control: The Select Item To Connect To dialog is displayed, which provides the following columns: - The Input item column, specifies the name of the series and then the specific series attribute in braces e.g. line1 [color] - The Currently Linked column, displays the data element that is currently being used to drive this series attribute. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the series and the required series attribute that the selected data element should drive and click Finish . WARNING! Since more than one data element can be connected to a single series, ensure that only the required data element is connected to each series attribute, as specified in its Currently Linked column. -->

Drivers Configuration Top Driver Configuration This page of the Agent Server Configuration component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, allows you to manage your protocol drivers and their devices.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Drivers Configuration Top Driver Configuration This page of the Agent Server Configuration component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, allows you to manage your protocol drivers and their devices. In other words, this allows you to install the necessary protocol drivers and add, configure and remove their devices, so that the necessary scanning configuration can be performed in Adroit . To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Agent Server Configuration option. Note: If this option does not appear then Adroit may not be installed. - Select the Driver Configuration option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Note: On opening this page any configured protocol drivers and their devices are loaded, any protocol drivers that are unable to be loaded will display a warning. This dialog allows you to manage your protocol drivers and their devices via the Installed Drivers and Devices list, as follows: Install a Protocol Driver Display Protocol Driver Documentation To select an installed protocol driver: click on the name of the required protocol driver ( ) in the list. Installed protocol driver details: the attributes displayed in the information pane at the top right corner when an installed protocol driver ( ) or its device ( ) is selected. - Description: The literal name of the installed protocol driver. - File Name: The full path and name of the DLL file used by this installed protocol driver. - File Version: The Adroit version of this installed protocol driver. Note: The last number of this File Version: specifies the current revision of this installed protocol driver. - Devices: The number of devices configured for this driver. Adding and Configuring a Device To select a configured device: if necessary, click on the collapsed icon: to the right of required installed protocol driver ( ) icon and click on the name of the required configured device ( ) in the list. Device details: the attributes displayed in the information pane at the top right corner when a device ( ) of an installed protocol driver ( ) is selected. - Status: This indicates the status of the device itself and will either be: not loaded, no Agent Server connection, stopped or started. - Healthy: This indicates status of the communications or scan-tasks assigned to this device, as follows: - healthy, indicates that all of its all of its scan-tasks have started successfully. - not healthy, indicates that either the selected device has stopped or a problem has occurred when starting this device or there may be a license/HASP problem (to test, run the Agent Server in demo mode). For details, see Limited Time License HASP . - I/O Count: This specifies the number of I/O points that have been scanned using this device; this number excludes any 'at' or @ scanned items. Click the Refresh Driver List button to refresh the status of the devices of the installed drivers.

Configuring a Device of a Protocol Driver Removing a Device from a Protocol Driver Diagnosing installed Protocol Drivers and their configured Devices Displaying Protocol Driver Device Documentation Configure settings that affect the scanning of values : these are global Advanced driver options such as the option to enable or disable demand scanning.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuring a Device of a Protocol Driver Removing a Device from a Protocol Driver Diagnosing installed Protocol Drivers and their configured Devices Displaying Protocol Driver Device Documentation Configure settings that affect the scanning of values : these are global Advanced driver options such as the option to enable or disable demand scanning. This replaces the Installed Drivers and Devices list with the Advanced driver options list, which allows the following commonly used parameters that affect scanning, to be added or modified For details on scanning in general, see Scanning Overview . -->

Driving aliases with wizard substitutions Top Driving aliases with wizard substitutions Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates, as follows: In this case ensure that the aliases that you want to drive have the same names as their corresponding wizard substitutions.

Title: Driving aliases with wizard substitutions
Driving aliases with wizard substitutions Top Driving aliases with wizard substitutions Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates, as follows: In this case ensure that the aliases that you want to drive have the same names as their corresponding wizard substitutions. For instance, consider the situation where: a tank wizard is a rectangle with Percentage Fill Behaviour that is driven by a substitution called {Tank_Level}. This wizard then launches a SmartUI Template, when the tank is clicked that contains a digital gauge that has a Display Value Behaviour, driven by the {Tank_Level} alias. In this case when configuring the Execute Command - Open graphic form Behaviour of the tank wizard, in the Aliases tab of the Advanced View , you specify {Tank_Level} in the Input column of the Tag alias. IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. Example of the configured Execute Command dialog: When this wizard is added to a graphic form the data element (value) that is specified for its Tag substitution to drive its level is also displayed by the digital gauge. Example of the wizard in operation: Note : These linked aliases and substitutions will also be correctly updated when the wizard is updated. -->

Drop Table queries Top Drop Table queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Drop Table queries
Drop Table queries Top Drop Table queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Drop Table Queries can delete tables or views in the database. Click for more information: Note1: If necessary, parameterise the table and/or the field names to specify them before performing the query. Note2: This query is ONLY able to remove a SINGLE table or view. To add and configure a Drop Table query: Add a Drop Table Query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. - If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option. Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query.

For details, see Creating customised queries .

Title: Drop Table queries
For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Drop Table query: Note: This configuration dialog does NOT provide a Preview button to prevent tables from being removed from your database. Therefore please ensure that you configure the values for these fields correctly. The Tables and Fields dialog is displayed. - Choose whether you want to delete a view or table, by selecting the required Table Type option. - Specify the table or view name, as follows: - To specify a specific table or view, select the name from the Select a ... to Drop list box, which lists all the tables or views of the database connected to this OLE DB datasource. - To specify a parameter for this table or view, so that its name can be changed before the query is performed, check the Parameterised ... Name checkbox. This is recommended if you need to delete more than one table or view. Note1: This ignores any table or view specified by the Select a ... to Drop list box. Note2: If necessary edit the parameter name for this table or view in the Custom Query dialog. As you specify the required table name, the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. WARNING! If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages. Once you click the Next button the query configuration dialog ends and any further modifications to the query can only to be performed manually. - Click Next , once the required fields and their values have been defined, to end the query configuration dialog. The Custom Query dialog is displayed, which allows you to manually configure this query, if necessary. Note: This dialog should be used to rename any parameters that were specified for table and/or field names. - If necessary, type or modify the existing SQL querying commands in the SQL Query editor, which highlights keywords and makes it easier to customise your queries. - Click Finish , once you are satisfied with this query. This adds this query with its specified name beneath the Drop Table Queries subfolder of the Queries folder of the applicable OLE DB datasource, in the Enterprise Manager .

Dual mode tags Top Dual mode tags When using tags within control groups, it is recommended to also add these tags to normal groups too, so that these tags become ‘dual mode’ tags.

Title: Dual mode tags
Dual mode tags Top Dual mode tags When using tags within control groups, it is recommended to also add these tags to normal groups too, so that these tags become ‘dual mode’ tags. However, the ORDER in which these groups are defined within the WanClient tag link database is important, as follows: - The normal group is defined ABOVE the control group: This will update the local Agent Server with the current tag value within the remote Agent Server on the appropriate WanServer computer first. - The normal group is defined BELOW the control group: This is akin to making the client Agent Server the master for this tag, in that the current tag value within the local Agent Server on the WanClient computer will always be sent first. Note: Tags within control groups can be written to a remote WanServer Agent Server, to update their tag values. This is in addition to merely receiving their tag values, as is the case within normal groups. However, in BOTH cases, dual mode tags enable the Mark bad scan bad indication methodology to be successfully employed when using the On comms start event. For further details, see Scan Bad Indication Methodologies . -->

Editing controls and components Top Editing controls You can edit each control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form.

Title: Editing controls
Editing controls and components Top Editing controls You can edit each control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form. See form component. that you add to a graphic form, as follows: Note: You need to select controls before they can be edited. For details, see Selecting controls . - Moving: Drag the selected control/s to their required location. Note: By default, when moving a selection, it snaps (jumps) to the snaplines (displayed in blue) of the other form components, so as to be aligned with these components. This means that you are not able to place this selection in certain places on the graphic form. Tip: Hold down the ALT key while dragging to disable the default this snapping mode and provide free movement. - Sizing: The current selection provides sizing handles small boxes that appear around the perimeter of a selected item, which if dragged changes the size of this item. See drag. that can be dragged to resize all the controls in the selection. When the mouse cursor passes over a sizing handle it changes into a double-headed arrow ( ), indicating the directions in which the selection can be sized. - Properties: Each control has properties, which affect how it appears and behaves etc. Properties can either be manually configured or driven by external values for animation purposes. Note1: The Properties tool window displays the available properties of the selected control/s. Note2: If more than one control is selected then only the properties shared by all the selected controls are displayed. Note3: A component a hidden form component that provides additional functionality to this graphic form and some or all of its form components. See form component. also has properties, which can affect how they behave. Please Note: To specify an ampersand character '&' in a text property of a control, type in && and not just &. Since if only one '&' character is specified then when displayed, the & character does not appear and the following word is underlined instead. - Behaviours: Controls provide a task menu, opened by clicking its icon, which can add one or more display Behaviours. These Behaviours use external data to typically modify the appearance of its associated item. For details, see About Behaviours . Note: Only one of each of the Behaviours can be added. Note: To make it easier to design and arrange controls, the visibility of controls cannot be modified in Design mode. This restriction, however is lifted in Run mode and in the Operator. -->

Editing graphic elements Top Editing graphic elements After adding one for more graphic elements can be edited as follows: Note: Graphic elements need to be selected before they can be edited.

Title: Editing graphic elements
Editing graphic elements Top Editing graphic elements After adding one for more graphic elements can be edited as follows: Note: Graphic elements need to be selected before they can be edited. For details, see Selecting graphic elements . Tip: The RoundedRectangleRadius property, specified in pixels, adds support for rounded corners for the following graphic elements: Rectangle, Text, Picture and Button - by default this is 0 (disabled), except for Button which is 2. Values from 5 onward result in rounded corners. - Moving: Drag the selected graphic elements and/or controls to their required location. Note1: By default, when moving a selection, it snaps (jumps) to the snaplines (displayed in blue) of the other form components, so as to be aligned with these components. This means that you are not able to place this selection in certain places on the graphic form. Note2: When moving a selection, the X and Y axis displacement (in pixels) of the current position relative to its original position is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button. Tip: Hold down the ALT key while dragging to disable the default this snapping mode and provide free movement. - Sizing: The current selection provides sizing handles small boxes that appear around the perimeter of a selected item, which if dragged changes the size of this item. See drag. that can be dragged to resize all the graphic elements in the selection. When the mouse cursor passes over a sizing handle it changes into a double-headed arrow ( ), indicating the directions in which the selection can be sized. Note: When resizing Text graphic elements, the text itself will ALSO be resized. Tip: To draw perfect squares and circles, hold down the CTRL key while resizing their graphic elements. - Rotating: Use the rotation handle above the center of the vector as its rotation site for rotating the selection. When the mouse cursor approaches the outer edge of the rotation site it changes into a rotation cursor ( ), which when dragged rotates the selection clockwise or anti-clockwise. Note1: Each selection provides a center-point indicated by a circle ( ) around which it rotates. If necessary, drag this center-point to another position before rotating the selection.

Note2: When rotating a selection, the angle (in degrees) of the current rotation relative to its original position is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button.

Title: Editing graphic elements
Note2: When rotating a selection, the angle (in degrees) of the current rotation relative to its original position is displayed next to the center-point in red, so that you can know when to release the mouse button. Clockwise rotation is positive and anti-clockwise rotation is negative. Note3: If necessary, the center-point can be reset by right-clicking and selecting the Reset Center-point item. Graphic elements provide a task menu, opened by clicking its icon, which also contains a Reset Center-point item. - Editing nodes: Graphic elements that are collections of basic shapes have nodes at the start and end of each constituent, represented as a small square box ( ). Nodes allow these constituent shapes to be moved, deleted and added. For instance the Polyline which is made up of separate lines, the Spline is made up of curves. Nodes are edited using the node pointer ( ), as follows: - Move nodes by dragging them, if the node is attached to two constituents BOTH of them will readjust to their new starting or ending position. - Delete nodes by pressing CTRL and clicking the required node, this removes the constituents attached to this node. - Add nodes by pressing SHIFT and selecting the existing node that is to be the start or end of the new constituent. This adds the new node on top of the selected node, which needs to be dragged to the required position. - Properties: Each graphic element has properties, which affect how it appears and behaves etc. Properties can either be manually configured or driven by external values for animation purposes. For instance, most graphic elements can be colored and filled (indicates a rising level from 0 to 100%). For details, see coloring and filling graphic elements . Other important properties: - Location and size - to dynamically adjust the size and location of this graphic element at runtime. - StartPoint and EndPoint: adjusts the size and location of a Line. - Rectangle: adjusts the location and dimensions of a Rectangle, Ellipse, Scale and Text. - Closed: closes a Polyline or Spline if set to True - this automatically joining the beginning and ending points. - ScaleType: changes the displayed scale of a Scale. Supported scale types - Scale vector: the DivisionsPosition property changes where the scale appears within the vector i.e. on the Left, Centre or Right of it.

- Button vector: important properties: Hovercolor : displayed when the mouse pointer hovers over this button; Presscolor : displayed when the mouse clicks this button.

Title: Editing graphic elements
- Button vector: important properties: Hovercolor : displayed when the mouse pointer hovers over this button; Presscolor : displayed when the mouse clicks this button. - Text vector: the Boolean TextScaling property is True by default. Set this property to False if you do not want to resize the text when the vector is resized. Warning! This also means that the text will not rotate and will remain horizontal regardless of the rotation of this Text vector. - Text, TextAlign, Textcolor: change the content and appearance of the text of a Text. - RoundedRectangleRadius , specified in pixels, adds support for rounded corners for the following graphic elements: Rectangle, Text, Picture and Button - by default this is 0 (disabled), except for Button which is 2. Values from 5 onward result in rounded corners. Note1: The Properties tool window displays the available properties of the selected graphic element/s. Note2: If more than one graphic element is selected then only the properties shared by all the selected graphic elements are available. - Behaviours: Graphic elements and grouped graphic elements provide a task menu, opened by clicking its icon, which can add one or more display Behaviours. Editing the Header of an Agent Top Editing the Header of an Agent All agents types, regardless of their function, have common header attributes or values that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server.

Title: Editing the Header of an Agent
Editing the Header of an Agent Top Editing the Header of an Agent All agents types, regardless of their function, have common header attributes or values that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server. These can be edited in the Agent Header configuration dialog, as follows: Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator, as follows: - Ensure that the Basic , Advanced and/or System checkbox is checked to display the required agent type in this list. These checkboxes use these default agent groups to help you select the required agent quickly. Tip: If no checkboxes are selected, then all the available agent types will be displayed in the Type list box. This is useful if the required agent type has not been categorised. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list - Locate the required agent type, using the scroll bar and click on it. - In the Agents list, click on the name of the required agent (if necessary scroll down to locate this). Tip: Right-click to display a menu of commands to perform upon the selected agent(s). - In the Agent Configuration dialog, select the Header button in the Configurator dialog box, or from within the edit agent dialog box or simply select the required agent and right-click and select Header… from the menu. For details, see Right-click Configurator Menu . - Edit the Description of the agent, if it was not done when the agent was first added. - The User edit box can record user-defined information by using the agentIcon slot of the agent. For instance, this slot can be placed on a mimic so that operators could communicate and leave messages with regard to this agent. Click for more details: add a Text picture element and assign a Display Value Behaviour and an Operator Action Behaviour - set to Data Entry , for the agentIcon slot of the applicable agent). - This dialog then displays the 32 bits of the Agent Status word that contains configuration and run-time status information about the agent. This status word is divided into the following two groups: - The first 16 bits (0 to 15) are labeled Common Status bits , which are common to all agents, with each of these 16 bits having a fixed purpose. These have a unique slotname, which follows the naming convention of statusXxxxxxXxxxxx. e.g. statusScanBad. - The second 16 bits (16 to 31) are labeled Specific Status bits and their purpose varies with each agent type. They are named statusBit16 up to statusBit31. - The View derived agent status checkbox, affects how the Control status bits for the agent are displayed, as follows: - Unchecked: This is the default view and displays the raw agent status. The Control status bits can be set or cleared for the ENTIRE agent i.e. once a Control bit is set or cleared, this setting will fan out and force this value of this Control bit for ALL the slots of this agent. - Checked: This is a view-only display of all the agent slot Control bit statuses OR'd together.

Typically, a filter group denotes a plant area to which the agent belongs and is used to filter events and/or alarms per plant area. Title: Editing the Master Recipe
Editing the Master Recipe Top Editing the Master Recipe Firstly, select a Step from the Master Recipe list. Enter new information into the Ingredient (Tag) , Verification (Tag) or Tag/Value field. To update the master recipe data select any other field. When selecting a Phase Action the master recipe data will automatically be updated. It may happen, when updating a master recipe that the "Master And Control Recipe Reconciliation" dialog will show. Adroit attempts to keep the master and control recipes in step with each other. e.g., if a step is deleted in the master recipe, the same step in the control recipes will be deleted. - The first list shows all control recipes where this was successfully accomplished. - The second list shows all control recipes where this could not be accomplished. Although this only happens occasionally, these control recipes will have to be edited and validated. Additional Master recipe configuration options: - Add Master Recipe: Add a new step to the end of the master recipe. - Insert Master Recipe: Insert a new step before the currently selected step. - Remove Master Recipe: Remove the selected step from the master recipe. - Import Master Recipe : Import a master recipe and its associated control recipes from a .CSV file - Export Master Recipe : Export the master recipe and all of its control recipes to a .CSV file. - Test Master Recipe : Test the validity of the master recipe. - Editing Control Recipes: The Recipes button allows you to edit the control recipe list. See the following sections on Creating and Editing Control Recipes for more information. - Advanced Master Recipe Properties : Edit the advanced properties of the master recipe. - Header Master Recipe: Displays the agent’s header information. -->

Effective Alarm Characteristics Top Effective Alarm Characteristics The characteristic of an effective alarm is that it should be: - Relevant: requiring acknowledgment and corrective action i.e.

Title: Effective Alarm Characteristics
Effective Alarm Characteristics Top Effective Alarm Characteristics The characteristic of an effective alarm is that it should be: - Relevant: requiring acknowledgment and corrective action i.e. NOT an event that can simply be ignored. - Unique: does not duplicate another alarm and is not a secondary consequence of a previous alarm. - Timely: is not triggered too long before any response is needed or too late to do anything. For instance, when monitoring for over temperature the High alarm is the most important event, not the High-High alarm because the damage is probably already done at this point! - Prioritised: indicates the importance with which the operator deals with the problem. - Understandable: has a message that is clear and easy to understand. - Diagnostic: identifies the problem that has occurred. - Advisory: indicates the action that is to be taken. - Focusing: draws attention to the most important issues. While the AlarmManagement agent can ensure that the first four characteristics are met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. For details about using the AlarmManagement agent, see Quick Start to Configure and Record Incidents (Alarms/Events) . For details about specifying a document for incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). , see Configuring Incidents . -->

Electrical equipment faceplates Top Electrical equipment faceplates Each electrical equipment template provides an intelligent equipment-specific faceplate, accessed by clicking its graphical representation.

Title: Electrical equipment faceplates
Electrical equipment faceplates Top Electrical equipment faceplates Each electrical equipment template provides an intelligent equipment-specific faceplate, accessed by clicking its graphical representation. The Home ( ) faceplate page is launched by default and provides the following: Example: - The name of this item of electrical equipment at the top. - The left Status section contains the following items: - The associated ISO 14617 representation, if one exists for this item of equipment - One or more of the following status indicators and their meanings: Operating mode : Automatic (PLC) control or Field-based control and/or Hand (Manual control) Warning (a fault or alarm) Interlock (a safety, process and/or start interlock is in effect) Simulation (PLC function block works but does not start the equipment) Maintenance (manual control with PLC control interlocks overridden) - One or more common equipment-specific interlocks and/or faults - The top right panel, allows one to change how this item of equipment is controlled and, if necessary, operate this equipment, as follows: - The Control Mode section: Auto: The equipment is controlled by the PLC. Manual: In this control mode, the Desk / Field section determines where this item of equipment is being controlled from. - The Desk / Field section: only applies if the Manual control mode is being used, in which case it specifies where this item of equipment is being controlled from, as follows: Desk: This equipment is controlled from the SCADA. Field: This equipment is controlled via the on/off switch in the field (plant floor). - The Operation section: only applies for the Desk (SCADA) control method, in which case, the equipment can be turned on and off. The bottom right panel provides the Reset button, which clears all the warnings/errors for this equipment, and one or more of the following buttons that open and close other windows: : Displays the AlarmEvent page to view any alarms or events associated with this item of equipment. : Displays any trends associated with this item of equipment. : Displays the Setup page to change this item of equipment into Simulation or Maintenance modes and to view/set other equipment-specific values, such as alarm limits etc. - Simulation: a testing mode, where the associated function block works in the PLC, but does not set any outputs. For instance, you can use this mode to safely test the whole startup process of a motor. - Maintenance: an manual operational mode in which this equipment bypasses any process interlocks.

Example: : Closes the current window.

Electrical equipment templates Top Working with Electrical equipment templates In MAPS each piece of electrical equipment requires an associated template.

Title: Working with Electrical equipment templates
Electrical equipment templates Top Working with Electrical equipment templates In MAPS each piece of electrical equipment requires an associated template. For complex items of equipment consisting of more than one piece of electrical equipment, like conveyors, create a unit for item of equipment and associate all their component-electrical equipment to individual MAPS templates. You can also create custom (user-defined) templates too. Default Electrical equipment templates : the templates of the electrical equipment provided by MAPS . Template naming convention: The first section is the abbreviated or full name of the equipment e.g. DOL (Direct on line motor) or VALVE. The second section can further classify the equipment e.g. for valves _S_ indicates 'single actuating and _D_ indicates 'double actuating'. The second or third section of the template will be _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced), indicating the level of complexity or diagnostic information provided by this template. For each piece of equipment there can be up to 3 templates, each providing different levels of complexity or diagnostic information, the names of these templates indicate the provided level of complexity as follows: _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced). IMPORTANT: The greater the level of complexity provided by a template, the more signals are required for this item of equipment, which therefore increases the number of the required SCADA tags. This can increase the size and cost of your Adroit licence, as in Adroit you pay for each tag that you scan to a PLC. So ensure that you assign the templates to your equipment carefully. The third or fourth section provides the version of this template e.g. v1_0 stands for version 1.0 Each MAPS template: - Provides one or more SCADA graphical representations providing an intelligent faceplate. For details of these faceplates, see Electrical equipment faceplates . Typically the provided template graphics will always list one or more ISO representations (of the associated ISO 14617 symbol, if one exists for this item of equipment) at the top of the list, which may be followed by one or more physical representations of this item of equipment. Select the graphical representation, which provides the required orientation of this item of equipment. These graphical representations also displays status indicators, so that operators can immediately see which operational mode this equipment is in. For details, see Status indicators provided by electrical equipment graphics . Note: The SAME status indicators are also used by the associated faceplate to indicate these operational modes. Example: - Provides an associated PLC function block for this item of equipment. -->

Title: To enable a user to change or enter a data value
If necessary, add and/ or select the required Data Entry spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Data Entry spiders . In the Inputs section: Note1: The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Note2: The Minimum and Maximum inputs are IGNORED when a String value is specified. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. - If necessary, use the Default Value input to specify an initial value that will be displayed in the edit box of the data entry dialog. - If necessary, use the Minimum and Maximum inputs to specify the range within which a numerical value MUST be specified. Note: Numerical values that do not comply with these limits CANNOT be entered. Instead, the incorrectly entered value; the Minimum and Maximum labels and their values, in the dialog, will be displayed in red until a valid numerical value is specified. - If necessary, use the Caption input to specify the caption (title) and text that is displayed in the caption image bar at the top of the dialog. This is 'Input Required...' by default. When specifying this text, the following two placeholders can be used: - {0}: The Default Value . - {2}: The user name, of the currently logged in user. - If necessary, use the Message input to specify the informative message or instruction that is displayed above the value edit box within the dialog itself. This is 'Change the value to:' by default. Note: No placeholders can be used in this text. - Use the Boolean Confirm change? input to enable or disable the display of a confirmation dialog before the value is changed. Note: A confirmation dialog will ONLY be displayed if the Default Value input has been specified for this Data Entry spider. If this is enabled (True) then use the Confirmation message input to specify the confirmation text that is displayed by the dialog. This is 'Change the value from {0} to {1}?' by default. When specifying this text, the following placeholders can be used: - {0}: The Default Value . - {1}: The newly entered value.

Note: This displays the name of the spider or data element that the Value output is connected to. For details on configuring or viewing the location of the Server event log where this event will be logged, see General Server settings . Note: If more than one data element or spider value is set by this spider (i.e. if the Value output is connected to more than one destination), then a separate event is logged to the event log for EACH destination. -->

This assumes that the edit dialog is displayed and the required OID value has already been added to the list.

Title: To enable the writing of a selected OID value:
This assumes that the edit dialog is displayed and the required OID value has already been added to the list. - Click the Name field of the required OID value to select this row in the list. - Click the Browse tag button and use the built-in agent explorer to create and/or select the Tag that will contain this value. For details, see Select a Tag Using the Agent Explorer. Note: Ensure that the return type of this OID value be saved in this agent type and can be written to. For help on this, see SNMP Object Value Return Types. - Click the W field of this row to place a tick in this tick box. This only indicates that you want to change this OID value when the value of the specified Tag changes. - Ensure that you either click the Update or OK button BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise these configuration changes will be lost. This value will only be written to the device, when: - you select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) in the Poll settings section of this agent - you have specified connection settings that allow this device’s OID values to be written - the value of its specified Tag changes At this point a single scan point license is consumed for this service. If the write fails, then the SNMPManager agent polls the device for this OID value to obtain its original value and the Current Value field is updated accordingly. Tip: The lastWriteStatus STRING slot, displays a text message that indicates whether the last value written to the device was successfully changed in the device or not. Global Device Management Settings : How to configure the agent to change the OID values. Connecting to a SNMP Device : How to allow the OID values of a device to be changed. List of Selected SNMP Objects : Describes each of the fields of the selected OID value list. -->

This assumes that the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog is displayed and the required OID is in the list. - Click the Name field of the required OID to select this row in the list. - Click the Browse tag button and use the built-in agent explorer to create and/or select the Tag that will contain this value. This only indicates that you want to enable automatic polling for this value. - By default, this value is polled at the global Poll rate for this agent. If this value changes faster or slower than the global rate then use the Rate field of this row to specify this specific rate in milliseconds (you may need to enlarge this dialog to see this field or use the horizontal scroll bar to do this). Note: The specific poll rate allows you to specify a rate faster than 5 seconds (the limitation of the global rate) and is ONLY used if it is greater than 0. - Ensure that you either click the Update or OK button BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise these configuration changes will be lost. This value will only be retrieved from the device, once you select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) in the Poll settings section of this agent, at which point a single scan point license is consumed for this service and the Current Value field is updated when you refresh this dialog at the applicable poll rate. Title: EnvisaLinkTPI-1-08
EnvisaLink TPI Programmer s Document DEVELOPER DOCUMENTATION VERSION 1 08 February 10 2017 1 0 Overview The EnvisaLink Third Party Interface TPI consists of a set of commands and responses designed to allow third party command and control applications to interface directly with the EnvisaLink module and in turn the security system over a TCP IP connection The goal in releasing this programmer s interface is not only to allow existing home automation software greater interaction with the EnvisaLink module but also to encourage the development of third party applications on mobile platforms 2 0 Connecting to the Envisalink 2 1 Hardware Connections Please refer to Envisalink installation or Quick Start document 2 2 TCP Connection The Envisalink acts as a server for the TCP connection and the user application is the client The Envisalink listens on port 4025 and will only accept one client connection on that port Any subsequent connections will be denied The Envisalink will close the connection if the client closes its side To initiate a connection the application must first start a session by establishing a TCP socket Once established the TPI will send a 5053 command See section 3 0 for a detailed description of the protocol requesting a session password The client should then within 10 seconds send 005 login request The 005 command contains the password which is the same password to log into the Envisalink s local web page Upon successful login the Envisalink s TPI will respond with the session status command 505 and whether the password was accepted or

Evaluation Options for Expressions Top Evaluation Options for Expressions There are two options available to you in this group, whether the expression is to evaluate continuously or only when triggered by a change in the trigger input slot.

Title: Evaluation Options for Expressions
Evaluation Options for Expressions Top Evaluation Options for Expressions There are two options available to you in this group, whether the expression is to evaluate continuously or only when triggered by a change in the trigger input slot. If the continuous option is selected then a new result will be generated whenever any of the inputs change or even if the expression itself changes. By design, a triggered Expression agent will always generate subscription updates for the value slot even if the value slot has not actually changed, which can lead to unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. These unnecessary subscription updates can be disabled, by adding the PropagateTrigger registry value. Note: When selecting the Continuous option ensure that there are no cyclic relationships between outputs and inputs. If such cyclic dependencies exist for a continuously evaluating expression Adroit is likely to become unresponsive. -->

Event Log datasources Top Event Log datasources An Event Log datasource exposes the events contained within the Windows event logs of the specified computer.

Title: Event Log datasources
Event Log datasources Top Event Log datasources An Event Log datasource exposes the events contained within the Windows event logs of the specified computer. Click for more details: These events can be used to gather information about any hardware, software, and/or system problems that this computer may be experiencing. For instance, certain applications make use of the Application event log to record application-specific events, such as errors, warnings and other relevant information. This datasource is added to the Datasources category of the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Event Log datasources . Click for advanced Event Log datasource usage information: You can configure this datasource to specify the following GLOBAL settings: the required polling interval to retrieve updated events and the maximum and minimum number of events to retrieve and user authentication if using a remote event log. For details, see Configuring Event Log datasources . In addition, the datasource can also be updated, locked or removed, if necessary. Note1: The Event Log service enables the viewing of the event logs on a computer. Access to this service is usually provided by default when one accesses the computer, either locally or remotely. Note2: You can control the access to this Event Log datasource (NOT its exposed event groupings and their events). For details, see Securing datasources . An Event Log datasource is identified in the Enterprise Manager by its specified name and its icon . When this datasource is opened, the events of the specified computer are displayed, in the following hierarchy: - The names of the event log file(s) , containing all the events have been logged to these files, are listed alphanumerically beneath this datasource. - Within each event log file name the events are further grouped by their source names i.e. the name of the software that logged the event, which are listed alphanumerically. Each event contains a number of fields or columns of data. For details, see Columns of event data . Note1: Use the EventViewer control to display these events in a graphic forms. For details, see EventViewer controls . Note2: Typically data updates from the Event Log datasources ONLY send CHANGED data after each polling period. In order to show ALL the historical data AND any new events that come through, CHECK the Append Data Updates checkbox of the required Property spider . For details, see Displaying both existing and updated dataset data . -->

Example of Master Recipe with Two Control Recipes Top Example of Master Recipe with Two Control Recipes Example: Master Recipe with two Control Recipes - Cool and Heat. When the control recipe Cool is active, the following will happen: - Set MESSAGE.value = "Started Cool". - Set SWITCH.value = 1. - Initiate the verification check for phase 1 (Step 1-2). That is, wait for the preconfigured verification time before continuing. - If SWITCH.value = SWITCH_ON.value = 1, verification passed. - Go to step 6. - Set MEASURE.value = 0.5. - End of phase 2 (Step 6). Go to step 3. - Set CELSIUS1.value = -5.5. - Set CELSIUS2.value = 5.5. - Set SWITCH.value = 0. - Initiate the verification check for phase 3 (Step 3-5). That is, wait for the preconfigured verification time before continuing. - If CELSIUS1.value = -5.5, CELSIUS2.value = 5.5 and SWITCH.value = SWITCH_OFF.value = 0; verification passed. - Go to step 7. - End of phase 4 (Step 7). If CONTINUE.value = 0, wait until it becomes a positive number between 1 and 6 and perform one of the actions described above. - Assuming that some time later, CONTINUE.value becomes equal to one. Then move to the next step, step 8. - End of phase 5 (Step 8). Pause for 1000 milli-seconds. - Set MESSAGE.value = "Finished Cool". - Phase 6 (Step 9), the final phase, has ended. Execution of control recipe Cool has ended. - If at any time the verification check were to fail, verification rollback would occur. If verification rollback is not configured, the recipe execution would stop. -->

Title: Example of Master Recipe with Two Control Recipes
Example of Master Recipe with Two Control Recipes Top Example of Master Recipe with Two Control Recipes Example: Master Recipe with two Control Recipes - Cool and Heat. When the control recipe Cool is active, the following will happen: - Set MESSAGE.value = "Started Cool". - Set SWITCH.value = 1. - Initiate the verification check for phase 1 (Step 1-2). That is, wait for the preconfigured verification time before continuing. - If SWITCH.value = SWITCH_ON.value = 1, verification passed. - Go to step 6. - Set MEASURE.value = 0.5. - End of phase 2 (Step 6). Go to step 3. - Set CELSIUS1.value = -5.5. - Set CELSIUS2.value = 5.5. - Set SWITCH.value = 0. - Initiate the verification check for phase 3 (Step 3-5). That is, wait for the preconfigured verification time before continuing. - If CELSIUS1.value = -5.5, CELSIUS2.value = 5.5 and SWITCH.value = SWITCH_OFF.value = 0; verification passed. - Go to step 7. - End of phase 4 (Step 7). If CONTINUE.value = 0, wait until it becomes a positive number between 1 and 6 and perform one of the actions described above. - Assuming that some time later, CONTINUE.value becomes equal to one. Then move to the next step, step 8. - End of phase 5 (Step 8). Pause for 1000 milli-seconds. - Set MESSAGE.value = "Finished Cool". - Phase 6 (Step 9), the final phase, has ended. Execution of control recipe Cool has ended. - If at any time the verification check were to fail, verification rollback would occur. If verification rollback is not configured, the recipe execution would stop. -->

Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Top Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Note: By using the Email driver, Notify agents can also send email messages.

Title: Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages
Steps:
Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Top Example of using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages Note: By using the Email driver, Notify agents can also send email messages. For details, see Configuring Notify agents to send email messages. Consider the scenario of a plant with an existing Adroit configuration. The existing Adroit configuration must be extended to provide support for the routing of only certain important alarms to various personnel. The plant consists of four dams that are modeled using the four analog agents, dam_level_1, dam_level_2, dam_level_3 and dam_level_4. Each of the analog agents are currently alarmed on the high and high-high alarm limits using route 2 of the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Route 2 sends alarms to an alarm list agent, dam_level_alarm_list, and to the local event log. The high-high alarms for the analog agents, dam_level_1 and dam_level_2 are very important to Harry and Sally and they would like these alarms to be routed to their cellular phones when these alarms become active. Both Harry and Sally have cellular phones on the Vodacom network. Larry is concerned about the high-high alarm of dam_level_1. He has a cellular phone on the MTN network. However, neither Harry, Sally nor Larry want the remaining plant alarms to be routed to their cellular phones, that is, the alarms for dam_level_3 and dam_level_4. In order to access the cellular or pager network, install the user-defined protocol driver in the Drivers section of the Adroit setup program. Then add a device for each cellular network. Name these devices, for instance, VODACOM and MTN. Both devices will make use of a modem installed on the Agent Server computer. Notice that each Pager device represents a cellular or pager service network, while each Notify agent represents a person to be notified. Create three Notify agents to represent each person, Harry, Sally and Larry; namely HARRY, SALLY and LARRY. Edit each Notify agent and insert that person’s cellular-phone number in the field entitled "User Code". The cellular number required in this field is the number excluding the 082 or 083 network code. The alarm can be transmitted the instant it occurs by checking Transmit an Alarm when it is raised . Each alarm routed to a Notify agent will be kept in a separate list of alarms for each Notify agent. An alarm will be removed from the list only when it has been cleared and acknowledged. It is also possible to send the list periodically to keep people informed of alarms that have not been cleared or acknowledged. The format of the alarm record structure can also be specified as desired. Scan the "rawValue" slot of the Notify agents using the relevant pager devices. HARRY.rawValue and SALLY.rawValue will be scanned using the VODACOM device. LARRY.rawValue will be scanned using the MTN device. Start each device. It is possible to test the device configuration by sending a message to each person. Simply set the "value" slot of each Notify agent to any string value and verify the message gets through to each cellular-phone. Now modify the alarm routes for the alarm agent, dam_level_alarms. Edit the alarm agent and add a new route, route 3. It is important to note that the new route includes the routing information of route 2 (the alarm list agent dam_level_alarm_list and the local event log), that is, the new route should be a superset of the old route.

Examples of Expressions Top Examples of Expressions IMPORTANT : There are cases when certain operators do NOT follow their prescribed order of precedence - so please use parentheses to enforce the required precedence in your expressions. Example of altered precedence: Consider the expression: v1 | v2 & v3 These operator precedence rules say that & has precedence over | So this IS the same as: (v1 | (v2 & v3)) However, you add a ! to one of the variables, this appears to influence this precedence ! Consider the expression: !v1 | v2 & v3 According to the operator precedence rules this should be the same as ((!v1) | (v2 & v3)) However, this is not the case, it is actually treated as the following by expression agents: (((!v1) | v2) & v3) Do if true – else stay the same v1? v2 : v99 IF v1 TRUE, value = v2, ELSE value = old value (v99) Logic expression !v1 & !v2 means value IS (NOT v01) AND (NOT v02) ( e.g. if v1=1 and v2=1, then v99=0) v11| v12 means value IS v11 OR v12 Nested expression v01 <= v02 ? 0 : (v01 >= v03)?1 : v99 means: Turn a digital on then value goes too low, but leave it on until the value goes above the HI, with: v1=input value, v2=lo and v3=hi Totaliser expression (v02==v06) && (v03==v07) ? 0 : v99 + v01 means IF (v02 EQUALS v06) AND (v03 EQUALS v07) THEN value IS 0 ELSE value IS value PLUS v01 Ramp expression v01 ? (v99 + 0.05) : v99 means IF v01 TRUE THEN value IS value PLUS 0.05 ELSE value IS value (i.e. no change) Control expression (!v02| v03) ? !v04 : v04 means IF (NOT v02 OR v03) TRUE THEN value IS NOT v04 ELSE value IS v04 Prioritization expression (v01<<0) | (v02<<1) | (v03<<2) | (v04<<3) means value IS v01 SHIFTED 0 BITS LEFT OR v02 SHIFTED 1 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 2) OR v03 SHIFTED 2 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 4) OR v04 SHIFTED 3 BITS LEFT (i.e. multiplied by 8) Angular expression atan(v01/v02) means ANGLE IN RADIANS whose TANGENT is v01 DIVIDED by v02 Power expression pow2(v03) means v03 RAISED TO THE POWER OF 2 (i.e. squared) Remainder expression v1%v2 means v01 MODULUS v02 ( e.g. if V01=34 and v02=5, v99=4) Exponentiation expression exp(v1) means NATURAL LOG BASE ‘e’ RAISED TO THE POWER v01 (ev01 ) ( e.g. if v1=4 then 2.7182818284= 54.59815003) Note: v01 may not exceed 422 Raising the power exp( v2 * log(v1) ) v1 RAISED TO THE POWER OF v2 i.e. v1v2 Bitwise negation expression ~v1 means 1’S COMPLEMENT OF V01 ( e.g. if v1= 1, v99 = –2) -->

Title: To add a command to a control or vector:
- Add or edit an Execute Command Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Select the required command from the Command list and configure it as follows: Start application: to launch an application and specify any required parameters, you configure this command as follows: - Application Name: browse in the required application. - By default this specifies an absolute path. - Check the Exclude path checkbox to specify a relative path, from the folder in which the Client executable is being run from, which is typically the installation folder. IMPORTANT: You need to ensure that this application is located in the specified path of your Operators and/or Web Operators. - Parameters: specify any parameters required by this application. Open graphic form : to open a specific graphic form, you configure this command as follows: - Graphic Form: click the browse button to launch the Graphic Form Selection dialog to select the required graphic form from the configured projects on the available SmartUI Servers. - Open As : specify how the graphic form opens, as follows: - Modal Form : the graphic form opens as a separate window that requires the user to interact with it or close it before being able to continue using the application. This is the default selection. - Modeless Form : the graphic form opens as a separate window that allows the user to interact with it and also return to a previous task without closing it. - Tab Page : the graphic form opens as a another tabbed page within the workspace. - Replace : the graphic form replaces the currently displayed graphic form. - Template Graphic Object : the graphic form is opened within a specific Template Graphic Object control. This option displays the TemplateGO field to specify the name of the required TemplateGO or TemplateGONavToolbar control, from the list - assuming that one or more of these controls have been added to the graphic form on which this Execute Command Behaviour is on. - Position : specify where, on the screen, the graphic form opens, as follows: - Center of Screen : opens the graphic form in the center of the screen (the default setting). - Location : uses the Location settings to specify the required X and Y position of the top left hand corner of the graphic form. - Mouse cursor : opens the graphic form at the current position of the mouse cursor - Template Set : specify which pre-configured template set to activate, when this graphic form opens.

text:
- Level : specify which pre-configured level to show, when this graphic form opens.

Title: To add a command to a control or vector:
- Level : specify which pre-configured level to show, when this graphic form opens. - size : specify the dimensions of the opened graphic form, as follows: - By default, this conforms to the size of opened graphic form. - If you check the Custom checkbox then specify the required Width and Height dimensions of the opened graphic form. Note1: The Advanced View provides an Aliases tab for this Open Graphic Form command, which lists any configured aliases of the specified graphic form, so that these values can be set either by specific data elements or by static values. This tab can be used to Drive alias values with wizard substitutions or Pass alias values from parent to child SmartUI Templates . Note2: If the specified graphic form does not exist (for instance if it was typed in incorrectly or if this Behaviour was copied from another project), then when this Behaviour is performed in the SmartUI Operator, it opens the specified graphic form containing the text 'graphic form not found'. IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. Tip: If necessary this graphic form can be opened within a specific TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form. control on this graphic form. Close graphic form : to either close a specific graphic form or the currently open graphic form, you configure this command as follows: - Either specify the required graphic form to close, as follows: Graphic Form: click the browse button to launch the Graphic Form Selection dialog to select the required graphic form from the configured projects on the available SmartUI Servers. - Or check the This form checkbox to close the graphic form that is currently open, when this command is performed. Print graphic form : to send the currently displayed graphic form to the default printer.

Title: To add a command to a control or vector:
If you check the Show Print Dialog option, then your users can choose which printer is used to print this graphic form and/or which print settings are used when printing this graphic form, such as the required page orientation. Otherwise you the currently displayed graphic form will be sent to the default printer. Log off : to log off the current Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. user, you configure this command as follows: - No further configuration is required to simply log off the current user. - If you have configured an auto-login account for this Client, then you can check the Auto login checkbox to automatically log in again using the specified auto-login user credentials. This, in effect, performs a “switch user” operation for the pre-configured auto-login user. Log on : to perform a “switch user” operation by logging in another user, you configure this command as follows: - Username: either type in the name of the required Allowed or Impersonated user or use the browse button to use the User Browser to specify this user name. - Password: type in the required password of the selected user. If necessary, click the Advanced View button to specify some or all of the following additional configurable options: Confirmation: provide pre and/or post confirmation for this command, by selecting one or both of the following checkboxes: - Log action : logs (records) this command in the Application event log for forensic or audit trail purposes. - Confirm action : pops up a yes/no confirmation message box before the command is performed. Security: ensure this action is only performed when the designated user/s and/or group/s are logged on, as follows: - Either click the browse button to specify a String data element, which contains the names of the required users and/or groups. Note: The user and group names in this string must be delimited by semi colons “;”. - Or click the Security button to open the Security configuration dialog to select the required users and/or groups. Tip: Instead of using the buttons to move users and groups from the Available and Selected lists, you can simply double click them.
