Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Browser String This specifies the full path and file name of the application (.EXE), command file (.CMD) or batch file (.BAT) that will be executed when the spider is triggered. For details, see Running applications, command files or batch files . Parameters String This optional input, specifies the required command-line parameters for the specified file, as you would at the command prompt e.g. if using MS Word to open a document include "" around document names with spaces etc. Confirm Action? Boolean This enables or disables the display of a confirmation dialog before the item, specified by the Browser input, is launched. Confirmation message String The informative text that is displayed by the confirmation dialog. This is 'Launch the application {0}?' by default. When specifying this text, the following placeholders can be used: {0}: The name of the item, specified by the Browser input. Typically this is the full path and file name unless only a file name is specified at runtime. {1}: User name, of the currently logged in user, when this item is launched. Log Actioned Event? Boolean This enables or disables the logging of an event to an event log whenthe item, specified by the Browser input, is launched. For details on configuring or viewing the location of the Server event log where this event will be logged, see General Server settings . Event Log message String The text that is displayed by the logged event. This is '[{1}] has launched the application {0}' by default. When specifying this message, the following placeholders can be used: {0}: The name of the item, specified by the Browser input. Typically this is the full path and file name unless only a file name is specified at runtime. {1}: User name, of the currently logged in user, when this item is launched. - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider.

Execute Statements Top Execute Statements Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Execute Statements
Execute Statements Top Execute Statements Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Execute Statements can perform the predefined stored procedures or user-functions of the database, which are listed by the Procedures branch. Click for more information: If these statements include input parameters, these can be specified before they are performed. Note This can ONLY perform a SINGLE predefined procedure or function. To add and configure an Execute Statement: Add an Execute Statement: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. - If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option. Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query.

For details, see Creating customised queries .

Title: Execute Statements
For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Execute Statement: Note: This configuration dialog provides a Preview button since the stored procedure/user-defined function apart from performing database operations will typically also return results as records or values. The Procedures/Functions dialog is displayed. - Select the required procedure or function from the Select a Procedure/Function to Execute tree. The names of procedures and functions support SQL schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a procedure or function is part of a different schema, then the name of this schema is indicated in brackets after the name of the procedure or function. This means that a procedure or function can have the SAME name as another procedure or function as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note1: Only ONE procedure or function can be selected. Note2: System procedures and functions are not displayed. - If the selected statement has parameters, these are exposed in the Procedure/Function Parameters table for information purposes only, as follows: Note: Values are set for the input parameters in the Query spider when this stored procedure/user-defined function is executed Parameter: This name is also used for the parameter input name when this is executed in the Query spider. Direction: This indicates what the parameters are used for in the stored procedure/user-defined function, as follows: - Input parameters: these are prefixed by '@' and provide the stored procedure/user-defined function with values and are exposed in the Query spider. - Output/Result parameters: these values are returned when the stored procedure/user-defined function is executed. WARNING! If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages. Once you click the Next button the query configuration dialog ends and any further modifications to the query can only to be performed manually. - Click Next to end the query configuration dialog. The Custom Query dialog is displayed. - If necessary, type or modify the existing SQL querying commands in the SQL Query edit box, which is finally editable. - Click Finish to end the Add Execute Statement configuration dialog.

Add and configure the Query spider to run this query: - Open the Spider Configuration tool window. - Right-click the spider workspace itself and select the Create New Spider menu. - Click the Databasing sub-menu and its Query item to add a Query spider. - Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. - Select the required query from the Inputs section of this spider, as follows: - Click the Server containing the required OLE DB datasource from the Server list box. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, when referring to the Server that you use to log in, instead of its actual name as this makes it easier to transfer this spider to another Client. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required OLE DB datasource from this list of available OLE DB datasources on this Server. The first OLE DB datasource created on this Server is selected by default. - Click the required type in the Query Type list. The Select Query category is selected by default. - From the Query Name list box, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the required query.

Note: It is important to name your queries clearly, so that it is easy to select the correct one.

Title: Exporting and importing controls
Steps:
Exporting and Importing controls Top Exporting and importing controls You can export one or more configured controls for reuse, by importing them into the same or other graphic forms. Click for more details: In this way it is possible to create a library of commonly used controls, whose properties are fully or partially configured – instead of creating these controls from scratch each time they are required. Note: Only the controls and their MANUALLY configured properties can be exported, in other words any spiders, Behaviours or other methods that are used to configure their properties will NOT be exported. To export controls: - Select the required control/s. For details, see Selecting controls . - Right-click and select the Export Selection menu option. This will display the Save As dialog. Note: An Invalid Selection error message is displayed if no controls are currently selected when this option is used. - Browse for the required folder and then type in the required file name and press the Save button. Note1: The name and especially the extension of this file is immaterial and does not affect the importing process. Note2: If only a file name is specified then the .XML file extension is provided. This will save the selected controls to the specified file. Note: When these controls are imported, their location depends upon where the cursor is in this graphic form. To import controls: - Ensure that the Windows Explorer and the SmartUI Designer application windows are positioned in such a way that the exported file containing the required controls is visible in Windows Explorer and the required graphic form into which these controls are to be added is also visible in the SmartUI Designer. - Drag the file containing the exported controls from Windows Explorer into the required graphic form in the SmartUI Designer. Note: The imported controls are initially added to this graphic form in the SAME position from which they were exported. The imported controls are immediately selected so that they can be moved to another location, if necessary. Note: Only the attributes of the imported controls are imported. -->

Exporting and Importing Groups and Users Top Exporting and Importing Groups and Users If you need to create the same groups and/or users on more than one computer, such as when you use a Workgroup, then the Adroit Security Manager utility can reduce this management overhead as follows: - Create the necessary groups and/or users on one computer.

Title: Exporting and Importing Groups and Users
Exporting and Importing Groups and Users Top Exporting and Importing Groups and Users If you need to create the same groups and/or users on more than one computer, such as when you use a Workgroup, then the Adroit Security Manager utility can reduce this management overhead as follows: - Create the necessary groups and/or users on one computer. - Export these users and groups via the Adroit Security Manager to a users.ini file - Launch the Adroit Security Manager on the required computer and import these users and groups, which do not exist on this computer, from this users.ini file. This functionality makes configuring Adroit security on a workgroup a lot easier, since you can simply create all the Adroit users and their groups ONCE and import these on ALL the other computers in your workgroup. To export the created groups and users: this allows you to export all the groups and the users on this computer and the groups that each user is a member of OR to only export the Adroit groups and Adroit users that have been created on this computer and their group memberships. - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - Open the Tools menu. - Click on the Export … menu item. - Click Yes to export ALL the groups and users and their group memberships on this computer. This ALSO exports the local Power Users group and the Adroit users that are members of this group, if the Configure Power Users option has been applied. - Click No to ONLY export the Adroit groups and Adroit users and their Adroit group memberships that are configured on this computer. - Click Cancel to NOT export ANY groups and users. The exported groups and users, if any, are saved to a file called export.users.ini , which is typically located in the Adroit installation folder, which is typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . - If necessary rename this file and copy it to the required Adroit computer/s that you would like to identically configure their Adroit users and groups and then import this file using their Adroit Security Manager utility. To import groups and users: this allows you to import all the groups and the users that have been created on another Adroit computer and exported to a user file (*.users.ini). - Ensure that the necessary users file (*.users.ini) is accessible from this computer. - Press the Windows key and start typing in Security Manager and select it from the list. - Open the Tools menu. - Click on the Import … menu item. - Locate the necessary users file (*.users.ini) - Click the Open button. The groups and users and their group memberships contained in this file are created, if they do not already exist. -->

Exporting categories and their incidents Top Exporting categories and their incidents The Categories tree of the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog allows you to add and configure categories and incidents.

Title: Exporting categories and their incidents
Steps:
Exporting categories and their incidents Top Exporting categories and their incidents The Categories tree of the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog allows you to add and configure categories and incidents. You can use the Export button to save and/or edit these categories and incidents in a .CSV file editor instead. Benefits: - Ability to bulk add and/or configure categories and/or their incidents. Note: If necessary, you change the category of an incident to another existing category, in which case this new Category ID is applied to any occurrences in the current and historical tables. - Ability to save your existing configuration to import this configuration into another AlarmManagement agent (in this case save this .CSV file to the name of the required agent first before importing it). To export/import categories and their incidents: this described the process involved when bulk configuring the categories and/or incidents of the Categories tree for an AlarmManagement agent. - Click the Export button in the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog. Note: A message box is displayed if there is nothing to export. This exports a .CSV file to the Work subfolder of your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. This file typically has the same name as this AlarmManagement agent. If you have MS Excel installed then this file opens in it, otherwise it opens in your default .CSV file editor. - Save this file, once you have performed the necessary changes to it and closed your .CSV editor. - Click the Import button in the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog. - Specify the required .CSV to import, by default the file with the same name as this AlarmManagement agent is selected. Note: The imported changes are immediately made to the Categories tree, so you do not have to click the Update button. The exported file contains the following columns: this describes the columns of this file and the possible reason for configuring each of them. - Category: This column specifies a separate entry (row) for each category in the hierarchical structure you create and a row for each of the incidents assigned to a category. The hierarchical structure of categories is represented in dot notation. For instance: Root.Category 1.Category 2. This makes it possible to: - rename and move categories as required and - move incidents and add other incidents as required. - Operator tag: This category-specific column specifies the tags that identify which operator names should be used when logging incidents within each category. Note: This column only applies to the categories that represent specific areas of your process that are managed by different operators. - Incident: This column specifies unique incidents (AgentName.AlarmType) for each of the categories. Note: If you specify the same incident for two categories ONLY the first incident is imported. If one of these incidents is already added to the incident tree, then the duplicate is discarded regardless of its position in the tree. - The other incident-specific columns, specify their optional configurable settings. For more details on their configuration, see Optional Incident Configurable Settings . -->

Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel Top Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel The main purpose or use of this Export to / Import from Excel functionality is to allow you to bulk configure your MAPS project after creating it using the MAPS project wizard.

Title: Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel
Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel Top Exporting MAPS projects to and importing them from Excel The main purpose or use of this Export to / Import from Excel functionality is to allow you to bulk configure your MAPS project after creating it using the MAPS project wizard. For instance, when creating a plant with 100 conveyors, it may be useful to add one conveyor using the MAPS project wizard and then export the project and bulk configure the other 99 conveyors in Excel and then import this modified project. Note: You need Microsoft Excel 2003 or later installed before you can use this functionality. Tip: We recommend that you first use the MAPS Project wizard to create at least one Plant Area, PLC, Unit and Equipment – to understand the required syntax and requirements for the fields on each of the worksheets of this Excel file. To export a project to Excel: - Right click the required MAPS project in the MAPS window and select the Export to Excel option. - Specify the path and file name of the required Microsoft Excel Spreadsheet (.xls file). This creates and populates a separate worksheet for each hierarchical component of this MAPS project. Note: If you make mistakes during the editing process, the Excel spreadsheet is analysed before the importing occurs and detailed feedback is provided on all mistakes that have been made. To import a previously exported project: - Right click on the MAPS root node of the MAPS window and select the Import from Excel option. This displays the Import from Excel dialog, which you configure as follows: - In the Excel file path field, browse for (specify) the path and file name of the required Microsoft Excel Spreadsheet (.xls file) that contains the required MAPS project that you want create or update. Tip: We recommend that you click the Test Excel file configuration button, click for more details: this parses the specified Excel file and ensures that it has been correctly configured (is error free) before doing the import or to report any errors found so that these can be fixed. This step is automatically performed before the import occurs. - Choose whether you want to: - Create an entirely new project from the configuration of this Excel file: In this case, select the Create new project option and then provide its unique Name and Description . MAPS automatically performs the Initialise project , Build Operator View and Rebuild All Graphics tasks, after the specified Excel file is successfully imported, therefore these options are disabled. You can choose whether you want to Create Tags after the import is successful , by checking this option which performs a Sync Tag operation… - Overwrite an existing project with the configuration of this Excel file: In this case, select the Overwrite an existing project option and the required MAPS project from the combo box. MAPS automatically performs the Initialise project and Create Tags after the import is successful tasks, after the specified Excel file is successfully imported, therefore these options are disabled. However, you can choose whether you want to Build Operator View and Rebuild All Graphics . Typically you only need to Build Operator View if you have added an extra Plant Area or PLC or Unit. However, in general we recommend that you do NOT Rebuild All Graphics as this overwrites ALL the changes you have made to the default graphic forms. So if you only need to update a few of your Unit graphic forms, then use their Update Graphic right click menu option to do this instead. -->

Title: To expose the required properties of the selected object
Note: It is only possible to expose properties once an object has been selected. For details, see Selecting the required object . - Select the required Hidden Property spider. - Right-click its title bar and select Expose Object Properties . The Property Browser configuration dialog is displayed to expose one or more of the properties of the specified Object input for this spider. To manually specify one or more properties: In the Expose Object Properties dialog on the right: - Specify the name of the required property in the Property Name edit box. Note: Property names are case sensitive, if the specified case is incorrect this property will not be recognised and therefore cannot be manipulated. - Clear the checkboxes, which determine whether you want this property to have an associated input and/or output, as follows: - Clear the CanRead checkbox, if the specified property cannot be read from (e.g. a write only property), this will prevent this property from being added to the Outputs of this spider. - Clear the CanWrite checkbox, if the specified property cannot be written to (e.g. a read only property), this will prevent this property from being added to the Inputs of this spider. - Click the Add button. This adds the specified property to the Added Inputs and/or the Added Outputs columns, depending on which checkboxes were cleared. - If necessary, add another property manually or select an existing property instead. - Click the Finish button, once all the required properties have been added. To select one or more existing properties: - In the Expose Object Properties dialog on the right: - Either click the View Properties button, to immediately display the existing properties for the specified object in the Select Properties dialog on the right. Note: The tree of properties will only be displayed if the properties of this object are already known by the reflection spider. If they do not appear, then click the Browse button and manually locate the assembly that defines these properties instead. - Or click the Browse button, to manually locate the assembly, which defines the properties of the specified object. For example the System.Windows.Forms.dll assembly, could be browsed in for a Windows Control. The properties defined by the selected assembly are then displayed in the Select Properties dialog on the right. Note: The onus is upon the user to ensure that the correct assembly is selected.

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now! : This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. - Edit Expression... : This can be used when creating a complex cumulative expression to display a multi-line edit box. For details on creating expressions, see Creating expressions . Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Expression String This is a single-line edit box, which is used to specify simple expressions. For details, see Creating expressions . Note: If creating a complex cumulative expression, right-click the spider's title bar and select Edit Expression... to display a multi-line edit box, which facilitates the editing of these expressions. - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function + Input Variable This will add a variable called i# to the Inputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1, which can be used within the expression of this Expression spider. For details, see Adding input variables . Note1: You must create the required input variables that the expression requires in order for the expression to be successfully computed. Note2: Input variables can also be removed from this spider. For details, see Removing input and output variables . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Result Double Displays the result of the last assignment statement (outputvariable = expression) within the Expression input, if the Evaluated output is True, otherwise if it will continue to display the result of the last valid expression, if any. Evaluated Boolean Indicates the success (True) or failure (False) in calculating the specified expression. Extended SQL Querying Top Extended SQL Querying If no row identifier is specified, then the selected (update, delete or retrieve) transaction could return multiple records and even if a row identifier was specified, the first record returned was always used for the transaction.

Title: Extended SQL Querying
Extended SQL Querying Top Extended SQL Querying If no row identifier is specified, then the selected (update, delete or retrieve) transaction could return multiple records and even if a row identifier was specified, the first record returned was always used for the transaction. Note: It is assumed that the user is familiar with the SQL querying language and is able to perform SQL queries unassisted. However it is also possible to specify which record is to be returned first, by adding the following commands to the SQL Query in the Identify Row edit box: - In order for the DBAccess agent to use the first sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname - In order for the DBAccess agent to use the last sorted record, append the following commands: $ORDER BY fieldname DESC Note1: "fieldname" refers to the name of the field by which the table will be sorted in ascending order (from the largest to the smallest) Note2: Only add the "$" character if this is the ONLY SQL query command. Furthermore, the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, for both the retrieve and delete transactions, supports free SQL format queries, these are identified from the normal SQL queries by starting the SQL query with two ‘$’ characters. Note: The update and insert transactions do not support free SQL format queries. - This is an example of a free SQL format delete query: $$DELETE FROM tablename WHERE fieldname=value1 OR fieldname=value2 Note: The "tablename" does not need to match the name of the table, currently specified in the Table name edit box. - This is an example of a free SQL format retrieve query: $$SELECT fieldname1,fieldname2 FROM tablename WHERE fieldname3=value ORDER BY fieldname4 DESC Note1: The field name(s) used after the SELECT keyword (fieldname1, fieldname2), in retrieve queries must be the same as the field names specified in the tag to field mapping grid. Note2: The "tablename" does not need to match the name of the table, currently specified in the Table name edit box. Note: To test the syntax of the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, click on the Trigger now button, then click the Details… button and check that this transaction succeeded in this dialog box. -->

Externally Accessing the OID List Externally Accessing the OID List Typically you can view and/or modify the list of OIDs you select from the device from within the edit dialog of the SNMPManager agent itself.

Title: Externally Accessing the OID List
Steps:
Externally Accessing the OID List Externally Accessing the OID List Typically you can view and/or modify the list of OIDs you select from the device from within the edit dialog of the SNMPManager agent itself. However, you can also select and configure the records in this list outside of this agent by using certain slots of this agent that provide the following functionality: These slots can be used to navigate the listed OIDs. To select a record (row) from the OID list: to display and/or configure one or more fields of this record. - Set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the list. This populates the following slots with the following fields of this selected record: idxEnabled : E field of the selected record; idxWriteable : W field of the selected record; idxOID : OID field of the selected record; idxName : Name field of the selected record; idxType slot = the Integer indicator of the return type of the selected record. For details, see OID Return Type Indicators; idxValue : Current Value field of the selected record; idxRate : Rate field of the selected record; idxLastPollTime slot = the last time the value of the selected record was automatically polled; For details of the fields that these slots represent, see OID List . To change the OID of the selected record: to monitor and/or control different SNMP managed objects. - If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list. - Set the idxOID slot to the numeric format of a valid OID. This automatically changes the Name ( idxName slot) of the selected record to “Unknown”, since this field is usually set by the OID browser, when the OID is selected. Note: Please ensure that the OID you specify is correct and supported by the managed device. To change the Name of the selected record: to change the OID description. - If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list. - Set the idxName slot to the required description. Tip: This is usually required after manually changing the OID. To perform a manual poll of the selected record: to retrieve the value ( idxValue slot) of ANY item in the list. - If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list. - Set the idxPoll slot to 1. The idxValue slot will contain the retrieved value. Note: This polling occurs immediately, over and above the normal poll cycle. Note: This can poll OID values that are not enabled for polling. To change the polling configuration of the selected record: to enable or disable polling for this item. - If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list. - Set the idxEnabled slot to 0 or 1 to disable or enable the polling of the selected record. Note: If you enable polling, this item will ALWAYS be polled EVEN if an tag is NOT specified to receive this value. To change the writing configuration of the selected record: to enable or disable writing for this item. - If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list. - Set the idxWriteable slot to 0 or 1 to disable or enable the writing of the selected record. Note: If you enable writing, the value of this item will ONLY be changed when the tag associated with this record changes in value. To perform a manual write of the selected record: this ONLY applies to items that are enabled for writing.

- If necessary, set the idx slot to the index of the required record in the OID list.

The OEE agent uses a background engine to update the monitored KPI or OEE in real-time.

Title: Calculation duration
The OEE agent uses a background engine to update the monitored KPI or OEE in real-time. Any changes made to the input slots, determines how this background engine does its calculations. Note: Ensure that your Adroit license has specified the required number of OEE agents, which are specified in groups of 10. WITHOUT specifying the licensed number of OEE agents, only one instance of an OEE agent has its background engine enabled. All other agents will appear not to be running. By default, the agent records the OEE or KPI based on shift numbers, which are determined by the Shift agent specified by the Shift tag field of the edit dialog ( shiftAgent slot). For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . At the end of each shift the OEE or KPI is recorded and automatically reset for the start of the next shift. If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a “per batch” basis, then: - Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and - Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. Note: The action of resetting the agent, automatically creates an OEE data snapshot entry before resetting the data. Tip: If the KPI or OEE is affected by the type of product being produced, then use different OEE agents for the different products.

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text:
KPI calculations are performed against runtime.

Title: Running time
KPI calculations are performed against runtime. Therefore the OEE agent uses the BOOLEAN running slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference runningTag ) that informs the agent whether the process (or machine) is running. Running time is typically automatically incremented by the agent while this BOOLEAN value is ON. IMPORTANT: The OEE agent only supports BOOLEAN tags - so you cannot use an expression value tag. Note: The OEE agent expects that this slot will be OFF if the available slot is OFF. If not, runtime will continue to increment even though availability is OFF. However, it is possible that the process/machine is running but there is no physical production because, for example, a gear has stripped. This causes the measurement variable (the input1 slot) to remain static or go to zero i.e. inactive. If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the running time and will raise a downtime alarm status. As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the running time. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot.

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text:
Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production.

Title: Available time
Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum available time. - This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. - If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF. Tip: This slot can be controlled by the output of a Scheduler agent that is configured with the applicable maintenance/lunch/tea times etc. For details, see Configuring the Scheduler agent .

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text:
To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ).

Title: Complex mode and KPI calculation
To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case the input1 slot is divided by time. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode. Note: OEE agents operating in complex mode CANNOT calculate OEE. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Total for the Shift for input 2)/Target KPI

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text:
The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production.

Title: OEE calculations
The OEE agent performs OEE calculations using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production. Calculated as the equipment uptime (actual production – see 2.5 above) divided by the time that the equipment was available (see 2.3 above) for use. Performance Percent of total parts produced against the design capacity (optimal production rate) per time frame. Quality Percent of good sellable parts out of total parts produced per time frame multiplied by the Quality factor % value.

metadata.title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations

text:
Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality.

Title: Quality factor
Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefore, the OEE agent calculates the quality using the reject and total counts for the shift, which is multiplied by an external quality factor, expressed as a percentage. This Quality factor % value (the qualityFactor slot) is the external quality factor whose value (0 to 100) must be driven externally. The default value is 100%. -->

Note2: This cannot retrieve numeric values that are of type STRING. VARIANT FetchValues ( LPCTSTR AgentSlot, const VARIANT FAR& Start, const VARIANT FAR& End, const VARIANT FAR& Samples ) The function takes one input parameters, of type constant ANSI or UNICODE character string (LPCTSTR), and three of type VARIANT reference (VARIANT FAR&) - AgentSlot: Name of agent and slot to retrieve data for. - Start: Start time of retrieval period. - End: End time of retrieval period. - Samples: No. of samples to interpolate. Title: Filtering datasets

Filtering event log files Top Filtering event log files The EventViewer control exposes the events recorded in an event log file, so that these events can be monitored.

Title: Filtering event log files
Filtering event log files Top Filtering event log files The EventViewer control exposes the events recorded in an event log file, so that these events can be monitored. Effective monitoring of events requires the filtering out of unnecessary or unimportant events. This control is also able to filter Adroit specific data. The EventViewer control provides the following methods of filtering an event log file: - If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by dragged it onto the DataSource property, then the Filter Dataset configuration dialog can be used to specify filters. For details, see Filtering datasets . - If an event log file is connected to this EventViewer control by means of its ConnectionInformation property then you can filter these events by a specific Source . For details, see Connecting event log files to EventViewer controls . - Design-time filtering: This involves the creation of filter strings that are saved in the FilterString property of the EventViewer control and are therefore ALWAYS applied when this control is displayed. For details, see Design-time filtering of event log files . - Run-time filtering: If enabled, this involves the creation of on-the-fly filter strings by your users that are NOT saved. For details, see Run-time filtering of event log files . Note: You can use BOTH the design-time and run-time methods of filtering simultaneously. -->

Finding spiders Top Finding spiders Finding a spider or selecting and displaying its configuration view can often be hindered when a large number of spiders have been added or when all the unselected spiders are being hidden.

Title: Finding spiders
Finding spiders Top Finding spiders Finding a spider or selecting and displaying its configuration view can often be hindered when a large number of spiders have been added or when all the unselected spiders are being hidden. For this reason, the spider workspace toolbar provides the following methods to locate a specific spider and display its configuration view, while collapsing any other currently open spider configuration views: Note: If unselected spiders are being hidden this also displays all the spiders connected to the specified spider. To perform a general spider find: - If necessary, open the required spider workspace . - Click the drop-down list box button to the right of the button of the spider workspace toolbar. This lists all the spiders in this spider workspace, in the order in which they were added. - Browse for and select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the required spider. The configuration view of the specified spider will be displayed, which may have required moving to this location in the spider workspace. Note: Any other spider configuration views that were open will have been collapsed. To perform an advanced spider find: - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Advanced Find toolbar button, from the spider workspace toolbar. This displays the Advanced Spider Find dialog. - Click the drop-down list box button at the right of the Spider Category combo box. This list displays all the different spider categories that have been added to this spider workspace. Note: This list can also be resized or closed , if necessary. - Select the name of the required category. Tip: Alternatively, simply start typing the name of the required category into the Spider Category field and the nearest match will immediately be selected. - Similarly (using steps 3-4), select the name of the required spider, within this specifiedcategory, from the Spider Name combo box. The configuration view of the specified spider will be displayed, which may have required moving to this location in the spider workspace. Note: Any other spider configuration views that were open will have been collapsed. - Click the Close button to close the Advanced Spider Find dialog.

Tip: The Advanced Find method is recommended to locate a spider in a spider workspace that contains a large number of spiders.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Firewall configuration Top Firewall configuration If you are using firewall software then ensure that the following configuration is performed, in order for the SmartUI Server and Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications to be able to communicate with one another. Note: If you are running Windows XP SP2, then Microsoft Firewall has been installed on your system and will need to be configured. - When the SmartUI Server is required to communicate over the LAN to Clients: - Server computer configuration : ensure that port 9000 is unblocked for communication i.e. allowed to communicate to and from other computers. - Client computer configuration: ensure that the Designer and/or Operator applications are unblocked for communication i.e. allowed to communicate to and from other computers on any port. WARNING! Unblocking applications does require more maintenance than ports, for instance, they need to be re-enabled if their installation folders are changed. - When the SmartUI Server is required to communicate over the Internet via IIS to Clients: - Server computer configuration : ensure that port 80 is unblocked for communication i.e. allowed to communicate to and from other computers. - Client computer configuration: ensure that port 80 is unblocked for communication i.e. allowed to communicate to and from other computers. Note: If the Server is required to communicate to Clients over the LAN and the Internet, ensure that both of these ports have been unblocked i.e. allowed to communicate to other computers. - When using the VIP Distributor service , ensure that port 9010 is unblocked for communication i.e. allowed to communicate to and from other computers. For details on using this service, see Using the Launcher . To unblock an application using Microsoft Firewall: - Either: Choose to unblock the required application, when it is first run, from the dialog that is displayed. - Or: - Open the Microsoft Windows Firewall application. This will display the Windows Firewall dialog. - Select its Exceptions tab. - Select the Add Program… button and then browse for the required .EXE file. To unblock a port using Microsoft Firewall: - Open the Microsoft Windows Firewall application: - Select the Start menu, Settings and Network Connections item. - In the Network Connections dialog, right-click the required LAN connection and select Properties . - In the Local Area Connection Properties dialog, select the Advanced tab and the Settings... button in the Windows Firewall group. - In the Windows Firewall dialog, select its Exceptions tab. - Select the Add Port… button. - In the Add a Port dialog, in the Name edit box, specify the name of the service or application that requires this port to be unblocked and then specify the required port number in the Port number edit box. Also ensure that the TCP selection is selected and click OK . To open the Microsoft Windows Firewall application: - Select the Start menu, Settings and Network Connections . This will display the Network Connections dialog. - Right-click the required Local Area Connection and select Properties . This will display the Local Area Connection Properties dialog. - Select the Advanced tab and the Settings... button within the Windows Firewall group. -->

text:

Title: To define the required picture sequence of a Picture vector:
By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. - The PictureIndex of the Pictures list determines which image is displayed. This PictureIndex is calculated as follows: PictureIndex = (Input Data Element value – Base Value) / Increment , where: - Base Value is the starting value, all Input Data Element values <= the Base Value display the image referenced by PictureIndex = 0. - Increment is only used when the Input Data Element value > the Base Value , in which case it determines the amount that the Input Data Element value needs to increase before this Behaviour selects another PictureIndex to display its referenced image. Note: The first PictureIndex is always 0. Configuration examples: to ensure the Picture vector displays the correct sequence of images. - If the Input Data Element contains a BOOLEAN value, such as a Digital value: Set the Base Value to 0 and the Increment value of 1 to ensure that ONLY TWO PictureIndex values are calculated (0 and 1). Only the first two images in the Pictures list are displayed. If this value was toggled between 0 and 1, the following sequence will occur: The first image is displayed (PictureIndex=0) The second image is displayed (PictureIndex=1) The first image is displayed (PictureIndex=0) - If the Input Data Element (agent.slot) contains an INTEGER or REAL (FLOATING POINT) value, such as an Analog value: In this case MULTIPLE PictureIndex values can be generated to display multiple images. For example, to display a series of four images for a value with a range of 0 to 100, configure the Base Value = 50, an Increment = 10 and ensure that the Pictures list only contains 4 images. In this case these images are displayed in the following sequence as the Input Data Element value progresses from 0 to 100: 0 – 49 the first image is displayed (PictureIndex=0) for the Base Value range 50 - 59 the first image is AGAIN displayed (PictureIndex=0) for first interval 60 - 69 the second image is displayed (PictureIndex=1) for the second interval 70 - 79 the third image is displayed (PictureIndex=2) for the third interval 80 - 89 the fourth image is displayed (PictureIndex=3) for the fourth interval 90 - 100 the fourth image is AGAIN displayed (PictureIndex=3) as there are no further PictureIndexes in the list Tip1: When adding a Behaviour to a SmartUI Template A graphic form that has one or more configured aliases and is therefore designed to be displayed within a TemplateGO control. , you can use {} notation to automatically create an alias for any data element field. For more details, see Working with SmartUI Templates . Tip2: When adding a Behaviour to a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. , you can use {} notation to automatically create a substitution for any data element field. For more details, see Working with wizards .

Title: Floating tool windows
Floating tool windows Top Floating tool windows Tool windows are dockable, as such they have both a floating and docked display mode. When a tool window is floated, it becomes a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen that CANNOT be docked. To float a tool window: - Locate and open the required tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Note: Ensure that this tool window is not being auto hidden, if so deactivate this feature first. For details, see Automatically hiding and showing tool windows . - Double-click the title bar of this docked window, which makes this a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen. Tip: This window will be re-docked in its previous position when its title bar is double clicked again. Note1: A floating tool window is always on top of all other windows and can be resized as required. Note2: It is possible to float both a single tool window or grouped tool windows in the same way. For details, see Grouping tool windows . Note3: Floating tool windows provide a number of methods for conserving space in the within the work environment, however they do not support auto-hiding - hence the pushpin icon is not displayed on its title bar. For details, see Arranging tool windows . -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. - Add Font Properties: This adds six additional inputs to the Inputs section, which can be used to modify an existing font. For details, see Modifying fonts . Note: Once you have add these properties you cannot remove them from this spider. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Font Font The Font dialog box can be displayed to manually select a font by clicking the list button to the right of this input field. For details, see Selecting fonts . Once a font has been selected from this dialog, this also displays the values of the following font properties: Name: The name of the typeface selected for the font. size: The point size of the specified font. Units: The index number of the unit of measure used to specify the size . GdiCharSet: A byte value that specifies the GDI character set of the specified font. GdiVerticalFont: A Boolean value that indicates whether this font is derived from a GDI vertical font. - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Font Font This contains the font that has been selected and/or the values of the added font properties. This also displays the values of the following font properties: Name: The name of the typeface selected for the font. size: The point size of the specified font. Note: If the Font size attribute is remotely driven this displays the most current value, when the associated graphic form is in runtime modee.g. being previewed in the SmartUI Designer. Units: The index number of the unit of measure used to specify the size . GdiCharSet: A byte value that specifies the GDI character set of the specified font. GdiVerticalFont: A Boolean value that indicates whether this font is derived from a GDI vertical font. -->

Title: Formatting pager or SMS alarm messages
Formatting pager or SMS alarm messages Top Formatting pager or SMS alarm messages This dialog is displayed by clicking the Format… button in the main edit window of the Notify agent. This dialog allows the selection and format of the relevant information fields that are to be sent to the off site personal: - Use the Information to send table to select the information that is to be sent. The table has the following columns: - Field: Use this column to select or unselect the various information fields, by using the clearing or checking the checkbox, in each of the following rows: Source, Date, Time, Agent, Description, Alarm Type, Reported Data, Computer, Sub-Source, Category, Action, Event ID, Extra Data, Filter Group and Priority. For a description of each of these rows, see To Specify the Column Format for Event Output Agents . - Width: This column displays the configured width of the Field s. - Sample: This is a hard-coded sample of the typical information to be found in each of the Field s. - Use the buttons to organise the Fields in the Information to send table, by moving the highlighted Field up or down. - Enter the desired width of the currently selected Field , in the Width , edit box, which is automatically selected as soon as a Field is specified. - Check the Trim spaces option, so that all empty spaces are removed from the Fields that are sent. - Check the Include field name in message with separation text option, so that field names are also included, separated from the field value by the specified separator. - Enter the desired Field by field separation text . - Sample , using the existing sample values, this displays how an alarm will appear when it is received. Note1: The most frequently used configuration of the Fields is the following: Date (Width=5); Time (Width=5); Description (Width=20); Alarm Type (Width=10); Reported Data (Width=8). Note2: The message length is limited to 70 characters. -->

Title: Configuration
General chart configuration options Top General chart configuration options The chart configuration dialog provides the following generally applicable configuration sections: To launch the configuration dialog: right click the charting control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. - Title: To specify the main Header title of the chart. Tip: You can also specify this by using the tasks menu of the charting control. - Titles Setup: To configure the display of the chart titles and, if necessary, to add additional chart titles. - Legends Setup: To display the chart legend and specify and what the elements of each series are displayed in the legend and the format of these elements. Specify which elements of each series are displayed in the legend (names or values) from the Legend Style list. If the legend displays values, then use the Text Style to specify their required value/s and format. Note: Typically you display series values for Pie, Bar and Column charts and series names for Line and XYPlot charts, which are the default selections. Other noteworthy options: To allow your users to select which series they want charted, ensure that the Checkbox option if checked. To display a legend for this chart, ensure the Visible option is checked. - 3D Settings: To display the chart in three dimensions to add depth to your chart and rotate, zoom and/or move the plotting area of the chart. To enable these settings ensure the 3 Dimensions checkbox is checked. The 3D % spin control specifies the required depth or third dimension of this chart. The Horiz Offset moves the plotting area left/right. The Vert Offset moves plotting area up/down. Tip: The Default Settings button always brings the chart back into the viewing area. Use the Quality list box to specify how the chart should be plotted. The is a tradeoff between speed and the level of detail, with the lower options in this list becoming progressively more detailed and therefore slower. Tip: Change this Quality setting to Best Speed for SurfaceChart controls for better performance, since the drawing of these charts is sluggish as they require a lot of processing. - Fill Effects Settings: To configure how the chart and/or plot area or graph is colored and/or shaded. Note: The ‘Walls’ of the Plot Area appear when the chart is in 3D mode.

Note1: Since most of these settings alter the display of the chart, use the preview pane to customise these settings to meet your needs.

Title: Configuration
Note1: Since most of these settings alter the display of the chart, use the preview pane to customise these settings to meet your needs. Note2: The preview pane uses RANDOM data, NOT the actual data that you are charting. -->

General Server settings Top General Server settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following generally applicable SmartUI Server settings: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: General Server settings
Steps:
General Server settings Top General Server settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following generally applicable SmartUI Server settings: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Server option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Server may not be installed. - Select the General Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Server name: specify the name to identify this SmartUI Server and differentiate it from others SmartUI Servers in the same network. To specify the Server name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note: The only naming limitation is that the Server name may not contain the separator character, which is typically the “.” character. Tip: It is recommended to use a descriptive name, which is as concise as possible. Server event log: specify the computer and Windows event log name where the events generated by the SmartUI Server are stored. These events are typically generated by each task that is performed by the SmartUI Server and can provide detailed information if a problem arises. For more details, see Logging diagnostic events to the event log . Note: Each SmartUI application provide an EventLogSource property that defines which application name is specified when logging an event to this event log. To specify the computer on which these events are logged: Either type in the name of the required computer directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for the required computer. Tip: It is recommended to use the browse button to avoid the possibility of typing the name of this computer incorrectly. To specify the name of the event log in which these events are logged: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note: If this name is not specified, then this uses the following default event log name: Application . Server licensing method: select how you want to license this SmartUI Server. For details, see Licensing methods . To specify the normal licensing method: Ensure that No is selected. To specify the Agent Server licensing method: Ensure that Yes is selected. If the Agent Server is running on this Server computer no further configuration is necessary. However if the Agent Server is running on a remote computer, then specify both the network name of the relevant computer and the name of its Agent Server, in the following format: ComputerName.AgentServerName This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Server settings. For details, see Setting up the Server . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Server settings, see the Advanced Server settings page . -->

GET Commands Top GET Commands Function: To obtain the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server.

Title: GET Commands
GET Commands Top GET Commands Function: To obtain the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server. Note1: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a security risk through the remote retrieval of process values. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. The decision of which of the following command formats to use, is essentially a tradeoff between the prior configuration in the Command agent and the required amount of typing, when specifying the SMS command itself: Note1: It is also possible to retrieve the values of tags automatically, for instance, to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For details, see Automatic Sending of Values . Note2: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Basic command syntax: GET, tagName In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed. For instance: get,dig_01.value This is the simplest format of this command, which requires the least prior configuration in the Command agent, it is able to retrieve the value of any tag, however it does require the most typing when specifying the command. Pseudonym usage: GET, pseudonym In this case, a pseudonym or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the required tag (agent.slot). For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command can be specified as: get,dig01v Although pseudonyms save on the typing when specifying the command, ONLY the tags that have defined pseudonyms for this Command agent can be used. For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms . Macro usage: macro In this case, a macro or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the entire GET command. For instance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1?’ is created to represent ‘get,dig_01.value’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1?". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command names, they require the most pre-configuration in this Command agent and are therefore most restrictive. For details on creating and using macros, see Creating Macros .

The received SMS message, adheres to the following format: <GET RESPONSE> tagName = value Where tagName is the name of the tag (agent.slot) whose value is displayed, i.e.

Title: GET Commands
The received SMS message, adheres to the following format: <GET RESPONSE> tagName = value Where tagName is the name of the tag (agent.slot) whose value is displayed, i.e. the pseudonym or macro, if used, is replaced with the actual tag name. Note1: Invalid requests, for instance for the values of tags that do not exist, will be preceded by <GET FAILURE> instead. Note2: If the default formatting of real numbers has been configured for this Command agent, this format will be used to display real or floating-point values. For details, see Default Real Number Formatting . -->

Getting to know the Collections Top Getting to know the Collections WOSA/XRT Data Objects make extensive use of the OLE collection construct.

Title: Getting to know the Collections
Getting to know the Collections Top Getting to know the Collections WOSA/XRT Data Objects make extensive use of the OLE collection construct. A collection is an object that is implemented such that a well-known set of methods exists for iterating over the collected sub-objects. The defined Behaviours provide for enumeration, addition, deletion, and access via index. A collection contains only objects of the same class. The way collections are named is to typically call the collection the plural of the collected object name. For example, if we create a collection of objects of class Tag, we would name the collection Tags. In this way, VBA language constructs can take advantage of them, since VBA implements a language semantic known as For Each...In . In practice, once could write VBA code that looks like: For Each T in Tags REM... do something with T.Property Next The code fragment above would enumerate through the Tag objects in the collection. Notice that we can call the current object in the collection whatever we want (in this case T). Since the collection manages only one type of object, VBA assigns the object to the name we specify. WOSA/XRT defines three collection objects: Requests, Properties, and DataItems. The following sections will explore these collections and the objects that they manage. -->

Global Device Management Settings Global Device Management Settings Each SNMPManager can manage a single device by getting and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed objects (values).

Title: Global Device Management Settings
Global Device Management Settings Global Device Management Settings Each SNMPManager can manage a single device by getting and/or setting and/or trapping its SNMP managed objects (values). The Poll settings section of the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog, either enables or disables this device management and can specify a global rate at which values are retrieved from the managed device, as follows: PLEASE NOTE: If the Unlicensed checkbox (status bit indicator) is checked, then you need to correctly license your Agent Server before you can run 2 or more SNMPManager agents. To start managing the device: to start polling (monitoring) and/or writing (controlling) and/or trapping (enabling events) of the OID values of this device. - Select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). - Click the Update button. This sets the Started (status bit 18), which checks the Started checkbox. Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. WARNING! If a SNMPManager agent requires more than your available scan points then ALL these OID operations are DISABLED and its Error status bit is set. IMPORTANT: If the InvalidConnection status bit is set (the Invalid connection checkbox is checked), then NONE of these OID operations will be performed as the agent cannot connect to this device To stop managing the device: to stop polling and/or writing and/or trapping OID values of this device and to release the scan point licenses the agent was using for these OID operations. - Select the Disable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot). - Click the Update button. The Stopped (status bit 17) is set, which checks the Stopped checkbox The Started (status bit 18) is cleared, which clears the Started checkbox. To configure the global poll rate: the default rate, in milliseconds, that the agent fetches OID values (that are enabled for polling in the list) and copies these values into their associated tags. - Specify the Poll rate (INTEGER scanRate slot) in milliseconds. Note1: The lowest rate is 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds). Note2: If necessary, you can override this global rate for individual selected OID values, by specifying a non-zero rate in their Rate field. This rate can be less than 5 seconds. To view the activity of this agent: to allow advanced users to use the Datascope window to monitor the state and current activity of this agent.

Note: Ensure that you Enable polling before you can monitor this agent.

Title: Global Device Management Settings
Note: Ensure that you Enable polling before you can monitor this agent. - Click the Monitor button. - In the Adroit Protocol Driver Monitor dialog, type 1 to select the Datascope option. - In the Datascope window, type A to convert the Datascope from HEX to ASCII. This window displays the current STATE of this agent, where [1] means running and [2] means stopped. The other messages indicate the current activity of the agent, such as tree building, reading writing polling general activity. In general this facility allows you to know if the agent is working or not. Specific Status Bits .: Lists the non connection-related errors that the Error status bit can indicate. Accessing the SNMP Device and its Objects : How to connect to the required device. Usage Requirements : Requirements in order to use this agent. -->

Global Incident Destinations Top Global Incident Destinations The Eventlog route (global) destinations () section in the Routes tab of the Edit Alarm Agent dialog specify possible destinations for active incidents that apply to ALL Alarm agents.

Title: Global Incident Destinations
Global Incident Destinations Top Global Incident Destinations The Eventlog route (global) destinations () section in the Routes tab of the Edit Alarm Agent dialog specify possible destinations for active incidents that apply to ALL Alarm agents. Click here for more details: in other words, route 2 of the defaultAlarmAgent routes incidents to the same Output(s) and EventLog(s) destinations as will route 2 of myAlarmAgent etc. This section consists of the following categories: Outputs , which allows you to report active incidents using the following destinations: - The AlarmManagement agent, which can collect and if necessary, configure incidents from one or more alarm agents and send them to an OLE DB compatible database, so they can be analysed to improve your alarm configuration. - The EventOutput agent, which can print incidents locally or remotely; save them to a .CSV file and if necessary, log them to an OLE DB compatible database for reporting and/or analysis purposes. Tip: The EventLogging agent accessed from the Event Logs list provides the simpler method for logging incidents to an OLE DB compatible database. - The Notify agent, which can transmit incidents via SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. or a paging service direct to a designated person. This can inform off site personal of unacknowledged alarms and if necessary of process values and operator messages. To add an Outputs destination: - If necessary, edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: - If necessary, add an Alarm agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - If necessary, select the required route number. - Select the Add button above the Outputs list in the Edit Alarm Agent dialog box. - Browse for the required agent in its respective folder in the left pane of the dialog. For more details, see . Tip: If necessary, you can create a new agent by clicking the Add… button. - Click on the OK button. To edit an Outputs destination: - If necessary, edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: - Select the name of this Alarm agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - If necessary, select the required route number.

- Select the required agent in the Outputs list in the Edit Alarm Agent dialog box.

For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - If necessary, select the required route number. - Select the required agent in the Outputs list in the Edit Alarm Agent dialog box. - Click the Delete button above this Outputs list to remove this entry from this list. Note: This only removes the selected agent from the list and does NOT DELETE the agent from the Adroit agent database. This adds an event log called LOCAL to the Event Logs list of the selected route.

Note: If an event log called LOCAL already existed there will now be TWO such event logs in the list, in this case delete the second instance.
