Global Post Committing Options Top Global Post Committing Options The Adroit DB Generator provides a number of options that determine the default actions that Adroit performs after committing the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector.

Title: Global Post Committing Options
Steps:
Global Post Committing Options Top Global Post Committing Options The Adroit DB Generator provides a number of options that determine the default actions that Adroit performs after committing the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector. These options are GLOBAL, in that they apply to ALL the Connectors. To display the global post committing options: this launches the DBGEN Options dialog containing the available global options that are performed after committing the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. - Click the Tools menu and select the Options… menu item. The DBGEN Options dialog is displayed. The available global post committing options, are divided into the following two groups: Before committing import: this lists all the options that Adroit can perform before committing the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector to the specified Agent Server. Currently no such options are provided. After committing import: this lists all the options that Adroit can perform after committing the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector to the specified Agent Server. - Start datalogs: If enabled, the logging (recording) of all the Adroit tags that have been configured to be logged are started. - Start devices: If enabled, the Devices that are specified when scanning process values are started, so that these values can be scanned (communicated) to and/or from their respective front end devices. - Save WGP file: If enabled, the agent database (.WGP) file generated from the imported configuration for a Link of a Connector is saved. To enable an option: Check the checkbox of the required option. To disable an option: Clear the checkbox of the required option. -->

After creating and configuring all the graphic forms for the project: - Ensure that the Graphic Form tab of the project translation table contains all the languages required by the graphic forms within a project.

Title: The following translation process is recommended:
After creating and configuring all the graphic forms for the project: - Ensure that the Graphic Form tab of the project translation table contains all the languages required by the graphic forms within a project. For details, see Adding languages to projects . Note: Languages are added to both the Graphic Form and Data tabs of the project translation table. So only add languages as required by most graphic forms. If certain languages are graphic form specific, then it may be simpler to only add these languages to these specific graphic form translation tables. - Add the translation strings required by any or all of graphic forms within a project to the Graphic Form tab of the project translation table. By typing them in manually or you can Fetch them from the required graphic forms themselves . For details, see Fetching translation strings from graphic forms . - Translate these strings into the required languages. - Push (copy) translations, either entirely or selectively to the required graphic form/s from the project translation table. This automatically adds any languages to the graphic form translation tables that are missing. For details, see Pushing translations to graphic forms . - You may need to perform translations that are graphic form specific i.e. that may require languages and translations that are not common to other graphic forms in the project. For details, see Editing translations within graphic forms . After creating and configuring the datasources used by the project, for any string or textual values that are displayed by your graphic forms: - Ensure that the Data tab of the project translation table contains all the languages required by the graphic forms within a project. For details, see Adding languages to projects . - Add the translation keys for all the string data values displayed by any or all of graphic forms within a project. By typing them in manually or clicking the browse button and using the Data Element browser to select them. For details, see Browsing for data translation keys . - Translate these Key strings into the required languages. Note: Each Key represents the full string value of a data element, this does not do partial string matches. In other words, only textual data elements (from any datasource) whose values EXACTLY match any of the Key column strings will be translated when the graphic form is displayed. For details about specifying the user profile setting that specifies the primary translation language of new graphic forms and the preview language of new and existing graphic forms, see Customizing the graphic form language . For details about translating graphic forms, see Translating graphic forms . For an overview of the process of translating or localizing projects and their graphic forms, see Working with graphic form translation . -->

Title: Glossary Glossary @scan (pronounced at-scan), which is a method of linking the value of one tag to another, by scanning the required tag value directly. active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. agent group an agent that facilitates the logical grouping of other agents. For example, an AgentGroup agent could contain all agents related to a specific section of a plant, or all agents required for a specific report. alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type). alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Behaviours can be assigned to picture elements to display process values either actually or graphically to provide a dynamic visual indication of events taking place in the process. block period the interval over which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand, which is typically 30 minutes. Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). cleared the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) has returned to its normal operating state. CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. data logging the process of recording changes in agent slot values over time for the purpose of analysis. Datalog catchup only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. dialog a window that appears when an application requires further information from the user, also known as a wizard. DLL a dynamically linked library file DNS stands for Domain Name System and is one of the industry-standard suite of protocols that comprise TCP/IP, which is used to translates domain (computer) names to and from their IP addresses. driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. EEMUA the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association EEMUA 191 guidelines a document created by the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association ( EEMUA) of alarm management guidelines, developed by the users of alarm systems, and is the globally accepted and leading guide to good practice for alarm management. event an incident (a significant occurrence) that does NOT require user action, unlike an 'alarm' which DOES require user interaction. event logging the process of recording significant system and process events. For example, a process event such as changing a PID setpoint, or a system event, such as a printer fault. FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. glossary term This glossary term is for illustrative purposes only to demonstrate how glossary terms are displayed in this help system. HMI An acronym for Human Machine Interface. An HMI is a software application that presents information to an operator or user about the state of a process, and to accept and implement the operators control instructions. housekeeping the removal of unnecessary records from a database ICMP The Internet Control Message Protocol is used to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. IIS Internet Information Services incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). jotting text entered manually by an operator in the Execute Command Behaviour. KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. local file path this path, as opposed to a UNC path, can ONLY be accessed from the computer that it refers to, this path adopts the following general format: <driveletter>:\directories\filename. log also known as data log, the process of recording the changes in a value over time to a log file or OLE DB compatible database. log set this provides the ability to log the same slot (value) to a different destination and/or use a different logging rate and/or use a different logging period. MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. NTFS this stands for NT File System, the secure and robust file system for Windows NT operating systems. It allows you to set permissions for groups or individual users to access files. OEE stands for Overall Equipment Effectiveness, which typically identifies the productivity or utiltization of a machine or an entire plant, as a percentage. OEM a component in Adroit that requires a SEPARATE license BEFORE it can be used, which is added to the Agent Server license by means of an appropriate textual description of this component. OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. OLE stands for Object Lnking and Embedding, which is a software technology designed to allow different applications to exchange data. OLE DB The open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources. An OLE DB data provider is required, before a database can become OLE DB compliant. OPC stands for OLE for Process Control, which is designed to alllow an I/O server developed by a 3rd party to communicate to any SCADA. OPC client an application that uses the data provided by an OPC server. OPC HDA OPC Historical Data Access (OPC HDA) is used to retrieve and analyse historical process data. OPC item a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. picture a collection of one or more picture elements representing a process or a specific plant item, when a picture is toggled into Operate mode then it is known as a mimic. picture elements primitive graphical objects such as a Rectangle or Ellipse used to construct pictures, which can have one or more associated Behaviours to enhance its display. PLC a Programmable Logic Controller or programmable controller is a digital computer used for the automation of industrial processes. precedence rules that state which mathematical operators should be executed first in an expression. protocol a set of rules or conventions governing the exchange of information between a computer and a front-end device. putslot the process of writing (or the utility that writes) a specific value to a slot of a specific agent. Real-time Catchup The Real-time catchup is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers. The process occurs during the start up of a standby agent server, if a master agent server is already running. If this is the case, then every agent that is loaded from the WGP file and also supports real-time catchup will request the current state of the agent from the master server and then synchronise itself. round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. RTU an Remote Terminal Unit is a device installed at a remote location that collects data and transmits this data back to a central station, or master. SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). scanning overrun this occurs when the scan task takes longer than the required scan rate due to an overloaded or defective scanning subsystem. select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. session each time an application is started and stopped on a computer constitutes a single session of this program. shelve alarm shelving is the process of removing an alarm from the entire alarm system for a specific time period. This also known as inhibiting an alarm. slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. SMS Short Message Service is a service (protocol) for sending short text messages to and from mobile phones. SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. SNMP agent DO NOT confuse this with an Adroit agent, this is simply software running on a device that allows it to be managed by SNMP. SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. SNMP manager a program that is responsible for managing and monitoring SNMP devices, such as the Adroit SNMPManager agent. SNMP traps unsolicited SNMP messages sent by a device to notify an SNMP manager of significant events. Sparkline A sparkline is a very small line chart, typically drawn without axes or coordinates. It presents the general shape of the variation in some measurement, such as temperature or stock market price, in a simple and highly condensed way. subscription an economical method of accessing the data within agents whereby an agent subscribes to a specific slot (value) of another agent; then when this value changes the agent that has subscribed to this slot is notified of this change in value. tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). telemetry an automated communications process by which measurements and other data are collected at remote or inaccessible points and transmitted to receiving equipment for monitoring. UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name URI stands for Uniform Resource Identifier, which simply identifies the name and location of a file or any resource in a uniform format to provide a standard way for resources to be accessed by other computers across a network or over the Internet (or a private intranet or extranet). While a URL is the most common type of URI, the Uniform Resource Name (URN) is the historical name for the URI. URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator and is a reference (an address) to a resource, typically a document, on some computer on the local network or the World Wide Web(Internet). UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). WINS stands for Windows Internet Name Service, which predates DNS as the method used to resolve (translate) computer names and their IP addresses in a network. Unlike DNS which uses a hierarchical namespace, WINS uses a flat namespace. WYSIWYG What you see is what you get XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable.

Title: Graphic element coloring styles
Graphic element coloring styles Top Graphic element coloring styles When a graphic element is required to be colored and/or filled, its Backcolor and Fillingcolor properties need to be configured respectively. When configuring these properties, the color Settings dialog, can be displayed to select and configure the required coloring style. Note: These coloring styles and their configurable elements are also exposed as sub-properties, which can be individually configured or manipulated, if required. To display the color Settings dialog: - Open the required graphic form. For details, see Opening graphic forms . - In the Design workspace , select the required graphic element(s). For details, see Selecting graphic elements . - Open the Properties tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - Select the Fillingcolor or Backcolor property and press the browse button that appears to the right of its value cell. Note: If one of the selected graphic elements is a line or group, then these properties will not be displayed. To select and configure coloring styles using the color Settings dialog: Select the required coloring style, using the color Style list, which displays the following methods: - Solid: The selected graphic element(s) are painted using a solid color. Configuration: - color: Use this color edit box to select the color that will be used to paint the selected graphic element(s) - Transparency: If required, specify the required transparency of this color. This number determines how see-through the painted color is i.e. whether it is possible to see things through this color or not. The default setting of 255 is not transparent at all, while 0 makes the painted color entirely invisible. Gradient : The selected graphic element(s) are painted using a multicolor linear gradient. Configuration: - Transparency: If required, specify the required transparency of this color. This number determines how see-through the painted color is i.e. whether it is possible to see things through this color or not. The default setting of 255 is not transparent at all, while 0 makes the painted color entirely invisible. - Angle: This determines the angle, from the vertical, of the colors added to this multicolor gradient fill. The default value of 0 is vertical, 90, is horizontal, 180 is an inverted vertical and 270 is an inverted horizontal. Note: To set the angle, either press ENTER or use the buttons of this control to specifying the required angle.

- Position: This can be used to create a multicolor gradient by defining the positions and colors of each color.

Title: Graphic element coloring styles
- Position: This can be used to create a multicolor gradient by defining the positions and colors of each color. Each defined color is blended with its adjacent color(s) using a linear color gradient. The position of each color is specified BOTH as a fractional percentage from 0 to 1 and graphically using color position markers ( ) along a slider . Apart from the mandatory color positions at 0 and 1, additional color position markers can be added or removed as required. Note1: By default there are three color position markers, which have the following colors configured: at 0 (black), 0.5 (white) and 1 (black). Note2: Once a color position marker is added, it can be dragged left or right between its two adjacent color position markers, to change its current position. Note3: The currently selected color position marker is black, while the unselected markers are white. Tip: When selecting a color position marker, try to select the left or right corner of the triangle of this marker. To add a color position marker: Simply double-click at the required position along the slider to specify where a color is desired. To change the color of a color position marker: Select the required color position marker, so that it becomes solid black and then select the required color using the provided color edit box . Note: When a color position marker is added, its default color is black. To delete a color position marker: Select the required color position marker, so that it becomes solid black and then press the DELETE key to remove it. - Shape: The selected graphic element(s) are painted using a multicolor gradient that adapts itself to the shape of each graphic element. This dialog displays all the supported image file types. - WrapMode: If the selected image is smaller than the selected graphic element, this determines how this image will be used to cover the remaining area of the selected graphic element, as follows: - Tile: the image is simply duplicated as-is until the graphic element is covered. Example: - FlipX: the image is tiled, so that it is flipped about the X axis and appears as a series of horizontal mirror images. Example: - FlipY: the image is tiled, so that it is flipped about the Y axis and appears as a series of vertical mirror images. Example: - FlipXY: the image is tiled, so that it is flipped about the X axis and Y axes and the columns and rows of images appear mirrored both horizontally and vertically. Example: - Clamp: the selected image is placed in the top left hand corner of the graphic image and is NOT tiled. This is the default selection. Graphic form statistics Top Graphic form statistics When designing large graphic forms, especially when more than one person has designed it, it can become difficult to determine at first glance the number of components that have been added.

Title: Graphic form statistics
Graphic form statistics Top Graphic form statistics When designing large graphic forms, especially when more than one person has designed it, it can become difficult to determine at first glance the number of components that have been added. Therefore the Designer provides the Statistics button in the graphic form toolbar, which displays a dialog that reports the number of vector objects and windows controls used to create the user interface and the number of spiders and silks used to animate this user interface along with the size and name of this graphic form and the time and date at which it was last saved. Note: The graphic form needs to be saved first before these statistics can be displayed. Possible uses for these graphic form statistics are: - As a diagnostic tool to identify possible inefficiencies in the design of the current graphic form, that could be affecting its loading time . - As a means to determine the efficacy of the graphic form optimization process, by comparing an optimised graphic form to its original, for instance, to see the difference in the number of design elements that are being used. -->

Grouping Agents Together Top Grouping Agents Together An Agent Group is a logical grouping of agents, contained within an AgentGroup agent, either for user convenience or to identify a section or a function of a plant.

Title: Grouping Agents Together
Grouping Agents Together Top Grouping Agents Together An Agent Group is a logical grouping of agents, contained within an AgentGroup agent, either for user convenience or to identify a section or a function of a plant. For example, all the I/O agents associated with Boiler No. 1, or all DataLog agents needed to compile, say, a Production shift report could be placed in groups. This has already been done for each of the agent types and for the three pre-defined agent groups of BASIC, ADVANCED and SYSTEM as determined by the postload Adroit database file . An Agent Group can also be used to control several agents contained within a group. For example, the control bits of an Agent Group agent can be used as a way of setting or resetting the equivalent bits for all agents in the group. An agent can belong to more than one Agent Group and these may be displayed by selecting the agent type from the Type list box and its specific name from the Tags list box and then clicking the Groups button. A list of current Groups to which the agent belongs is shown. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Counter agent, will appear in the Current groups list, prefaced by an asterisk (*) e.g. *TRIGGER. These ARE NOT group names. Similarly, the membership list of a given Agent Group can be displayed by selecting the group from the Group drop down list box, whereupon the members will be listed in the Tags list box. The AgentGroup Agent To create a new agent group . Adding agent types to an agent group : this adds one or more agent types to an AgentGroup agent. Adding agents to an agent group : this adds one or more agents to an AgentGroup agent. Listing the contents of an agent group : this displays the agents and agent types that have been added to an AgentGroup agent. -->

HASP Software Protection Key Top HASP Software Protection Key Adroit is licensed via the Agent Server.

Title: HASP Software Protection Key
HASP Software Protection Key Top HASP Software Protection Key Adroit is licensed via the Agent Server. Typically, this is typically licensed via a HASP software protection key, which is programmed in accordance with the required licence. Note: If using a previous Adroit version HASP with an Adroit 10 installation, the message "Hasp Failure" will appear in the Event Log. Tip: To minimise the possibility of damage or theft, the HASP key may be installed internally within the computer case, using the AladdinCARD, which also provides additional parallel or USB ports. The key must be attached to one of the parallel ports (LPT1 or LPT2) or to a USB port on each Agent Server to provide network-wide protection. A printer cable can be attached to the other end of the key (when attached to a parallel port). WARNING! If this HASP key is lost, the cost of replacement is the current full value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. IMPORTANT: When the HASP is removed from the Agent Server computer, if it is NOT re-inserted within the grace period of 5 minutes then ALL SCANNING will be SHUTDOWN and all the scanned tags will be marked BAD and the HASP will need to be reinserted and the Agent Server restarted to re-enable scanning. To this end the HASP system agent provides the following new status bits which can be separately alarmed and monitored so that preventative action can be taken: - HaspWarning : ON when the HASP is unplugged and the Agent Server is running within the grace period. - HaspFailure : ON when the HASP is unplugged and the grace period has expired, so ALL SCANNING is SHUTDOWN and all the scanned tags will be marked BAD and the HASP will need to be reinserted and the Agent Server restarted to re-enable scanning. If the licence is updated or modified then the HASP key must be reprogrammed to reflect the changes, which requires the restarting of the Agent Server. For details, see Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility . Note: HASP software version upgrades can occur without immediately upgrading the Adroit software. Adroit continuously checks that the HASP key is present. If it is not detected at startup, a message will be displayed informing you that the Adroit system will revert to using the limited time license HASP . Note: When a HASP is not detected when the Agent Server is started and the Agent Server is not being otherwise licensed, then the Agent Server will automatically run in limited time license mode. So all Agent Servers must start up and continue to have a HASP, including proxy servers, which at least require a zero remote node HASP and AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. PLEASE NOTE: When Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is incorrectly configured, this can cause the Agent Server to be unable to read the HASP, at start up causing the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. For further details, see Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration .

HASP Troubleshooting : this provides solutions to common HASP problems, such as when Adroit cannot read the HASP For further details of what is licensed by an Adroit (Agent Server) licence, see Adroit Licensing .

Title: HASP Troubleshooting
HASP Troubleshooting Top HASP Troubleshooting Typically, Adroit is licensed via a HASP software protection key, which is programmed in accordance with the required licence. PLEASE NOTE: When Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is incorrectly configured, this can cause the Agent Server to be unable to read the HASP, at start up causing the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. For further details, see Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration . When Adroit cannot read the HASP details: IMPORTANT: Do not do this via a remote desktop session as this does not allow the reading of the HASP. - Check which version of the HASP drivers are installed by doing the following: - Browse to the following folder in Windows Explorer: C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Common - Open a Command Prompt in this folder – this is most easily done by holding down SHIFT and right clicking the Common folder - In the Command Prompt type the following command: haspdinst.exe -info - Click Yes if a UAC confirmation box pops up for Sentinel and wait after a while the Sentinel Run-time Environment Installer dialog should appear. - Take note of the version number in the title bar. - Browse to the HASP driver download available for Adroit 10 on the Adroit website and compare this version with the version of your installed HASP drivers. - If this Sentinel Run-time Environment Installer dialog does not appear or the version number is less than the latest HASP drivers – then download and install the latest HASP drivers install for Adroit 10 from the Adroit website, the downloaded file is called LatestHASPDrivers.exe. - If the currently installed HASP drivers are newer than the ones contained in the LatestHASPDrivers.exe, then we suggest that you manually uninstall your existing HASP drivers – by running the haspdinst.exe –r command (see steps a - c above) and then running the LatestHASPDrivers.exe to install this HASP driver instead. - If you still are struggling to remove your existing HASP drivers, then run the following command to manually remove your HASP drivers: haspdinst.exe -purge (see steps a - c above) and then re-run the LatestHASPDrivers.exe. - If this does not help, then it is possible under extremely rare conditions, the HASP or its parallel or USB port may have failed/blown. If a printer is plugged into the back of the hasp it may have caused this, to test this, try using the HASP on another computer with Adroit , run up an empty Agent Server and then check that way. - Also ensure that the BIOS setting for the parallel port modes, is set to EPP and not Normal. - If it still does not work, contact Adroit Support. -->

Header Slots Top Agent Header Slots All agents types, regardless of their function, have header attributes that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server.

Title: Agent Header Slots
Header Slots Top Agent Header Slots All agents types, regardless of their function, have header attributes that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server. These slots are identifiable by the fact that their names are all prefixed with word agent . Note1: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBit00 ( statusBad) , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of this agent. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note2: The remaining slots for each agent are specific to the agent type. For details, see Agent Type and Slot Reference . Slot name Slot type Function Alternate Slot names agentAlarmVersion INTEGER For future use. agentAllowCopy INTEGER If agent can be copied, set to 2. agentConfigXML VARSTRING For future use. An XML configuration view of this agent that categorises its slots, to provide an alternative means from using the Configurator to view an agent. agentDebugFlag INTEGER Debugging level of an agent. agentDeconfigure TAGNAME Used by the object model layers to have an agent deconfigure a secondary agent from it’s configuration e.g. tell the MODBUS device agent to deconfigure (unscan) an Analog agent. agentDeleteFlag INTEGER Set this if the Agent construct function has failed and the agent must be deleted. You may also set it at any other time the Agent Server calls the agent, to delete this agent. The statusConnectionBad (statusRemoved) bit in the status word may also be used for this purpose. agentDescription STRING An 80 character alpha-numeric field for storing a detailed description of the agent. agentEndValidity TIME The time at which agent information becomes invalid. Does not accept subscription requests. agentFilter INTEGER For future use. To be used to indicate a subset of the set of all AgentGroups. It will be the AgentGroups that this agent is joined to. agentFullTagName TAGNAME Tagname includes the Agent Server name. agentIcon STRING This slot provides the content for the User edit box and can provide agent-specific notes for operators, like the jotting functionality of the Execute Command Behaviour. agentId AGENTID The agent ID handle. agentInvalidSlot NO TYPE Set if you subscribe to a non-existent slot. agentLogVersion INTEGER For future use. agentMemberIds RAWBYTES This is an array of the AgentIds of all members of this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMemberInfo LIST Lists member names, IDs and typenames. agentMemberNames LIST This is a listslot containing one column with the agent names of all members of this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembers INTEGER Number of members the agent has (other agents that have joined this agent). An agent cannot be deleted if it has outstanding members. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembershipIds RAWBYTES This is an array of the AgentIds of all agents this agent is a member of. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembershipNames LIST This is a listslot containing one column with the agent names of all agents this agent is a member of. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMemberShips INTEGER The number of agents joined by this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentNoSave INTEGER When TRUE, indicates that the Agent must not be saved to disk. agentOverlayLoad BOOLEAN TRUE if an agent is to be overlayload enabled, and FALSE if an agent is to be overlayload disabled. agentPicture STRING For future use. agentPriority INTEGER The priority of the Agent. Possible values are 0 (lowest), 1 (low), 2 (normal), 3 (high), 4 (highest). Default value is 2 (normal).

agentProxyHeader HEADER For Proxy agents only.

Title: Agent Header Slots
agentProxyHeader HEADER For Proxy agents only. agentRealId AGENTID The real agent ID handle (for Aliases). agentRealTagName TAGNAME For Proxy agents only. Name of the actual agent being proxied. agentRealType INTEGER For Proxy agents only. Agent type of the actual agent being proxied. agentRealTypeName TAGNAME For Proxy agents only. Agent type name of the actual agent being proxied. agentScanVersion INTEGER For future use. agentsize INTEGER size of the agents header which may fluctuate, for example, due to its memberships. agentStartValidity TIME The time at which information becomes valid. Does not accept subscription requests. agentStepPtr INTEGER Pointer to agent step number. agentTagName TAGNAME A unique tag or name, by which all users refer to the agent. agentTimeStamp TIME A date/time variable that is updated after every successful modification of an agent slot. Does not accept subscription requests. agentTotalHeaderSlots INTEGER Total number of header slots. agentTotalSlots INTEGER Total number of slots owned by agent. Includes the agentTotalHeaderSlots count. agentType INTEGER A handle to the agent type. (for internal use by Agent Server). agentTypeName TAGNAME An alphabetic description of the agent type of this agent. agentUID STRING For future use. agentValuesXML VARSTRING Stores the values of the slots of an agent in XML format. agentVersion INTEGER A variable that is incremented after every successful modification of an agent slot. status INTEGER The 32-bit status word discussed below, shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad. Each individual bit can be accessed by the agentStatusBit xx slots. agentStatus statusBit00 BOOLEAN Bad - This is set when at least one of the following bits is on: statusScanBad, statusConnectionBad (a.k.a. statusRemoved) or statusAgentBad. It is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit00, statusBad statusBit01 BOOLEAN Global Inhibit - Equivalent to Scan Inhibit plus Log Inhibit plus Alarm Inhibit. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit01, statusGlobalInhibit statusBit02 BOOLEAN Operator Inhibit - Disallows an operator from changing any slot in the agent. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit02, statusOperatorInhibit statusBit03 BOOLEAN Log Inhibit - Disables any configured data logging for the agent or slot. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit03, statusLogInhibit statusBit04 BOOLEAN Alarm(s) Unacknowledged Agent has one or more unacknowledged alarms. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit04, statusAlarmsUnacked statusBit05 BOOLEAN Alarm Inhibit - Disables any configured alarming on the agent. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit05, statusAlarmInhibit statusBit06 BOOLEAN Alarm(s) Active Agent has one or more active alarms. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit06, statusAlarmsActive statusBit07 BOOLEAN Alarmed Agent is configured for alarming. This is a configuration bit and doesn’t fan in or out. agentStatusBit07, statusAlarmed statusBit08 BOOLEAN Scan Inhibit - Disables any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. This is a control bit and fans out. Note: To Scan Inhibit values when scanning, this needs to be added to their IO Flags bit mask . For details, see IO Flags . agentStatusBit08, statusScanInhibit statusBit09 BOOLEAN Legacy - used to be Output Enable - this is now being stored within the IO Flags bit mask for each scanned value. statusBit10 BOOLEAN Scan Bad - Communications with the front-end device are not happening successfully. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit10, statusScanBad statusBit11 BOOLEAN Legacy - used to be Output Initialise - this is now being stored within the IO Flags bit mask for each scanned value. statusBit12 BOOLEAN Connection Bad - Proxy agent link to real agent has failed. It could also mean that an agent has been removed.

Set this bit to delete an agent!

Title: Agent Header Slots
Set this bit to delete an agent! This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit12, statusRemoved, statusNetBad, statusConnectionBad statusBit13 BOOLEAN Scanned - This is usually set per slot, and it means that a slot is scanned. A slot may not be scanned more than once. This is a configuration bit and doesn’t fan in or out. agentStatusBit13, statusScanned statusBit14 BOOLEAN Agent Bad - is set if the agent is unable to perform an operation or calculation due to invalid (out of range) data. For example syntactically incorrect Expressions will set this bit. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit14, statusAgentBad statusBit15 BOOLEAN Subscriptions active - is set when the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarmed, logged or subscribed to by any other agent will have this bit set. This is a condition bit and fans in. Note: This status bit in the agent header dialog only works if global demand scanning is enabled. In other words if global demand scanning setting is NOT enabled, this status bit is ALWAYS off. agentStatusBit15, statusSubscribed statusBit16 to statusBit31 BOOLEAN Agent type dependent. These are condition bits and fan in (the specific names of the agent type’s status bits will also suffice as slot address). agentStatusBit16 to agentStatusBit31 statusRaw INTEGER The same as the status word, except that all fan-ins from the same and lower levels (i.e. the slot statuses and the bad bit) are discounted. In other words, the agent raw status word shows the status of the agent, without any regard for the status of the individual slots. For instance, if one of the agent slots is scan bad, the agent status slot will not necessarily show scan bad unless the agent itself has been marked as scan bad. agentStatusRaw -->

Header Slots Top Agent Header Slots All agents types, regardless of their function, have header attributes that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server.

Title: Agent Header Slots
Header Slots Top Agent Header Slots All agents types, regardless of their function, have header attributes that are assigned and managed by the Agent Server. These slots are identifiable by the fact that their names are all prefixed with word agent . Note1: The overall status of an agent can be determined from its status slot, which is common to all agent types. For details, see Agent Status . Note2: The first bit in the status word, statusBit00 ( statusBad) , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of this agent. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . Note2: The remaining slots for each agent are specific to the agent type. For details, see Agent Type and Slot Reference . Slot name Slot type Function Alternate Slot names agentAlarmVersion INTEGER For future use. agentAllowCopy INTEGER If agent can be copied, set to 2. agentConfigXML VARSTRING For future use. An XML configuration view of this agent that categorises its slots, to provide an alternative means from using the Configurator to view an agent. agentDebugFlag INTEGER Debugging level of an agent. agentDeconfigure TAGNAME Used by the object model layers to have an agent deconfigure a secondary agent from it’s configuration e.g. tell the MODBUS device agent to deconfigure (unscan) an Analog agent. agentDeleteFlag INTEGER Set this if the Agent construct function has failed and the agent must be deleted. You may also set it at any other time the Agent Server calls the agent, to delete this agent. The statusConnectionBad (statusRemoved) bit in the status word may also be used for this purpose. agentDescription STRING An 80 character alpha-numeric field for storing a detailed description of the agent. agentEndValidity TIME The time at which agent information becomes invalid. Does not accept subscription requests. agentFilter INTEGER For future use. To be used to indicate a subset of the set of all AgentGroups. It will be the AgentGroups that this agent is joined to. agentFullTagName TAGNAME Tagname includes the Agent Server name. agentIcon STRING This slot provides the content for the User edit box and can provide agent-specific notes for operators, like the jotting functionality of the Execute Command Behaviour. agentId AGENTID The agent ID handle. agentInvalidSlot NO TYPE Set if you subscribe to a non-existent slot. agentLogVersion INTEGER For future use. agentMemberIds RAWBYTES This is an array of the AgentIds of all members of this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMemberInfo LIST Lists member names, IDs and typenames. agentMemberNames LIST This is a listslot containing one column with the agent names of all members of this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembers INTEGER Number of members the agent has (other agents that have joined this agent). An agent cannot be deleted if it has outstanding members. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembershipIds RAWBYTES This is an array of the AgentIds of all agents this agent is a member of. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMembershipNames LIST This is a listslot containing one column with the agent names of all agents this agent is a member of. Does not accept subscription requests. agentMemberShips INTEGER The number of agents joined by this agent. Does not accept subscription requests. agentNoSave INTEGER When TRUE, indicates that the Agent must not be saved to disk. agentOverlayLoad BOOLEAN TRUE if an agent is to be overlayload enabled, and FALSE if an agent is to be overlayload disabled. agentPicture STRING For future use. agentPriority INTEGER The priority of the Agent. Possible values are 0 (lowest), 1 (low), 2 (normal), 3 (high), 4 (highest). Default value is 2 (normal).

agentProxyHeader HEADER For Proxy agents only.

Title: Agent Header Slots
agentProxyHeader HEADER For Proxy agents only. agentRealId AGENTID The real agent ID handle (for Aliases). agentRealTagName TAGNAME For Proxy agents only. Name of the actual agent being proxied. agentRealType INTEGER For Proxy agents only. Agent type of the actual agent being proxied. agentRealTypeName TAGNAME For Proxy agents only. Agent type name of the actual agent being proxied. agentScanVersion INTEGER For future use. agentsize INTEGER size of the agents header which may fluctuate, for example, due to its memberships. agentStartValidity TIME The time at which information becomes valid. Does not accept subscription requests. agentStepPtr INTEGER Pointer to agent step number. agentTagName TAGNAME A unique tag or name, by which all users refer to the agent. agentTimeStamp TIME A date/time variable that is updated after every successful modification of an agent slot. Does not accept subscription requests. agentTotalHeaderSlots INTEGER Total number of header slots. agentTotalSlots INTEGER Total number of slots owned by agent. Includes the agentTotalHeaderSlots count. agentType INTEGER A handle to the agent type. (for internal use by Agent Server). agentTypeName TAGNAME An alphabetic description of the agent type of this agent. agentUID STRING For future use. agentValuesXML VARSTRING Stores the values of the slots of an agent in XML format. agentVersion INTEGER A variable that is incremented after every successful modification of an agent slot. status INTEGER The 32-bit status word discussed below, shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, for instance if one of the agent slots is scan bad, then the agent status slot will show scan bad. Each individual bit can be accessed by the agentStatusBit xx slots. agentStatus statusBit00 BOOLEAN Bad - This is set when at least one of the following bits is on: statusScanBad, statusConnectionBad (a.k.a. statusRemoved) or statusAgentBad. It is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit00, statusBad statusBit01 BOOLEAN Global Inhibit - Equivalent to Scan Inhibit plus Log Inhibit plus Alarm Inhibit. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit01, statusGlobalInhibit statusBit02 BOOLEAN Operator Inhibit - Disallows an operator from changing any slot in the agent. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit02, statusOperatorInhibit statusBit03 BOOLEAN Log Inhibit - Disables any configured data logging for the agent or slot. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit03, statusLogInhibit statusBit04 BOOLEAN Alarm(s) Unacknowledged Agent has one or more unacknowledged alarms. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit04, statusAlarmsUnacked statusBit05 BOOLEAN Alarm Inhibit - Disables any configured alarming on the agent. This is a control bit and fans out. agentStatusBit05, statusAlarmInhibit statusBit06 BOOLEAN Alarm(s) Active Agent has one or more active alarms. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit06, statusAlarmsActive statusBit07 BOOLEAN Alarmed Agent is configured for alarming. This is a configuration bit and doesn’t fan in or out. agentStatusBit07, statusAlarmed statusBit08 BOOLEAN Scan Inhibit - Disables any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. This is a control bit and fans out. Note: To Scan Inhibit values when scanning, this needs to be added to their IO Flags bit mask . For details, see IO Flags . agentStatusBit08, statusScanInhibit statusBit09 BOOLEAN Legacy - used to be Output Enable - this is now being stored within the IO Flags bit mask for each scanned value. statusBit10 BOOLEAN Scan Bad - Communications with the front-end device are not happening successfully. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit10, statusScanBad statusBit11 BOOLEAN Legacy - used to be Output Initialise - this is now being stored within the IO Flags bit mask for each scanned value. statusBit12 BOOLEAN Connection Bad - Proxy agent link to real agent has failed. It could also mean that an agent has been removed.

Set this bit to delete an agent!

Title: Agent Header Slots
Set this bit to delete an agent! This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit12, statusRemoved, statusNetBad, statusConnectionBad statusBit13 BOOLEAN Scanned - This is usually set per slot, and it means that a slot is scanned. A slot may not be scanned more than once. This is a configuration bit and doesn’t fan in or out. agentStatusBit13, statusScanned statusBit14 BOOLEAN Agent Bad - is set if the agent is unable to perform an operation or calculation due to invalid (out of range) data. For example syntactically incorrect Expressions will set this bit. This is a condition bit and fans in. agentStatusBit14, statusAgentBad statusBit15 BOOLEAN Subscriptions active - is set when the agent is actively being subscribed to or not, and all agents that are alarmed, logged or subscribed to by any other agent will have this bit set. This is a condition bit and fans in. Note: This status bit in the agent header dialog only works if global demand scanning is enabled. In other words if global demand scanning setting is NOT enabled, this status bit is ALWAYS off. agentStatusBit15, statusSubscribed statusBit16 to statusBit31 BOOLEAN Agent type dependent. These are condition bits and fan in (the specific names of the agent type’s status bits will also suffice as slot address). agentStatusBit16 to agentStatusBit31 statusRaw INTEGER The same as the status word, except that all fan-ins from the same and lower levels (i.e. the slot statuses and the bad bit) are discounted. In other words, the agent raw status word shows the status of the agent, without any regard for the status of the individual slots. For instance, if one of the agent slots is scan bad, the agent status slot will not necessarily show scan bad unless the agent itself has been marked as scan bad. agentStatusRaw -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. - Expose Object Properties: This displays the Property Browser configuration dialog to expose one or more of the properties of the specified Object input for this spider. For details, see Exposing properties . Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Object System A drop-down list of the names of all the spiders, which have already been added to this spider workspace and/or controls, which have already been added to the currently edited graphic form. For details, see Selecting the required object . The properties of the selected object are able to be exposed as inputs and/or outputs. For details, see Exposing properties . -->

Hiding and displaying available tool windows Top Hiding and displaying available tool windows The View tab of the Designer ribbon displays the list of icons of the tool windows currently available in the SmartUI Designer application window, which can be used to hide or display these windows - hovering over each icon displays the associated name of the tool window.

Title: Hiding and displaying available tool windows
Hiding and displaying available tool windows Top Hiding and displaying available tool windows The View tab of the Designer ribbon displays the list of icons of the tool windows currently available in the SmartUI Designer application window, which can be used to hide or display these windows - hovering over each icon displays the associated name of the tool window. For a list of the available icons and which tool windows they represent, see Available tool windows . This and other techniques can be used to conserve space within the work environment. For details, see Arranging tool windows . To hide an available tool window: - Open the View tab of the Designer ribbon. - If the entry IS selected (icon has a yellow background): click this item to turn it off (the background changes from yellow to white). Tip: It is also possible to access the required tool window itself and click the close icon on its title bar. Note: This will only hide and not remove this tool window from Designer application window. To display a hidden tool window: - Open the View tab of the Designer ribbon. - If the entry is not selected (icon has a white background): click this item to turn it on (the background changes from white to yellow). - If the entry IS selected (icon has a yellow background): click this item to turn it off (the background changes from yellow to white), then open the View tab again and select this icon again. - This will immediately locate and open the required tool window in the SmartUI Designer application window. Note: This will both display and select this tool window in the Designer application window. -->

Hiding or displaying Header slots Top Hiding or displaying Header slots You can display or hide the common Header slots of each agent within the connected Agent Server of an Adroit datasource.

Title: Hiding or displaying Header slots
Steps:
Hiding or displaying Header slots Top Hiding or displaying Header slots You can display or hide the common Header slots of each agent within the connected Agent Server of an Adroit datasource. Click for more information: Note: This ALSO displays or hides the Header slots of the GROUP agents, which if displayed are listed in the *Group Slots list beneath each agent type, that has configured agents. These slots are usually used for general overview displays, to easily monitor the statuses of all the configured agents. For instance, by monitoring the statusAlarmed slot for the Analog GROUP agent, it is possible to determine whether one or more of the configured Analog agents are currently alarmed. Note: If the Adroit datasource is currently opened, this change will only take effect once it is refreshed or closed and reopened. To display the Header slots of agents within an Agent Server: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - Right-click the name of the required Adroit datasource or its icon and ONLY if you see a menu item called Include Header Slots then select it. When an agent is expanded in the Enterprise Manager it will also display its Header slots too. This will also change the name of this option to Exclude Header Slots . To hide the Header slots of agents within an Agent Server: Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - Right-click the name of the required Adroit datasource or its icon and select Exclude Header Slots . When an agent is expanded in the Enterprise Manager it will NOT display its Header slots. This will also change the name of this option to Include Header Slots . Note: You can also display or hide these common Header slots, by default, by configuring the Boolean AdroitIncludeHeaderSlots Server setting accordingly. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Server settings . -->

- Open and display the required graphic in the Design workspace .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Open and display the required graphic in the Design workspace . - Open the Levels and Layers tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - Click the second column of the grid to display or to hide the configured levels (columns). Tip: The symbols displayed by this second column, indicate whether the levels are currently displayed or hidden . -->

Hiding spider configuration views Top Hiding spider configuration views You often need to hide the spider configuration views, to provide room to work within the spider workspace.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Hiding spider configuration views Top Hiding spider configuration views You often need to hide the spider configuration views, to provide room to work within the spider workspace. Click for more details: Once the configuration view is hidden, the spider will usually display its distinctive icon beneath its title bar. Note: Data spiders disappear from view when their configuration view is hidden. To hide the configuration views of all the spiders in the spider workspace: - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - Either press the Collapse All Spiders toolbar button, from the spider workspace toolbar. - Or right-click the spider workspace and select the Collapse All Spiders menu item. This makes it easier to rearrange and add other spiders. Although it is also possible to automatically arrange the spiders too. For details, see Rearranging spiders . Tip: This is the best method of closing a large number of spider configuration views at once, although Data spider configuration views are not as easy to reopen. To hide the configuration view of any particular spider or Data spider: - Open the required spider workspace. - Select the required spider. For details, see Selecting spiders . - Right-click the title bar of this spider and select Detail View . Tip: You can also double-click the spider title bar. The configuration view collapses upward and expands to the left and downward from the position of the title bar of the icon of the spider. -->

Hiding unselected spiders and regions Top Hiding unselected spiders and regions Use the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions spider workspace display option to simplify an otherwise cluttered spider workspace.

Title: Hiding unselected spiders and regions
Hiding unselected spiders and regions Top Hiding unselected spiders and regions Use the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions spider workspace display option to simplify an otherwise cluttered spider workspace. Click here for more information: In addition to hiding ALL the unselected spiders and regions directly associated with the currently selected spider or region or form component, there are 3 other selective hiding filters. For instance, consider a scenario when Alias spiders are in conjunction with Variable Data Element spiders to connect the required data elements, so most of the spiders would be connected. Note1: When a spider is located or manually selected in the spider workspace, with this option enabled, then only it and the spiders that it is connected to will be displayed, in accordance with the currently specified hiding filter. For details, see Finding spiders . Note2: If the graphic form itself, is selected, then all the spiders which are connected by silks to properties of this graphic form and its form components will be displayed. But any standalone spiders or spiders which are not connected to any form components will not be displayed, such as Script Engine spiders. Note3: This does NOT display spiders that are triggered by the events of the selected form components. Note4: All the selective hiding filters, add a watermark to the right hand bottom corner of the spider workspace indicating which selective hiding filter is being applied. Tip: Click the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions toolbar button to apply the currently selected hiding filter to the spider workspace. To hide all spiders/regions not directly associated with the selected item: In other words this shows all the upstream and downstream spiders/regions that are linked to the inputs and outputs of the currently selected control/spider/region. - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, select the required form component, spider or region. - Right-click the spider workspace and open the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions menu and ensure that there is a tick mark to the left of the All item. Before / After Example: Before applying this setting: After applying this setting: To also hide all spiders/regions connected to the outputs of the selected item: In other words this shows all the spiders/regions that are linked to the inputs of the currently selected control/spider/region and all the spiders/regions that these spiders/regions are connected to (all the upstream spiders/regions). - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, select the required form component, spider or region. Tip: If you want to select more than one spider or region, hold down the CTRL key to multi-select. - Right-click the spider workspace and open the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions menu and ensure that there is a tick mark to the left of the Show Incoming item. Tip: Hold down the CTRL key to select spiders or regions without applying this hiding filter. Before / After Example: Before applying this setting: After applying this setting: For instance, to show all the spiders/regions that connect to the spiders/regions that configure the properties of the currently selected form component. To also hide all spiders/regions connected to the inputs of the selected item: In other words this shows all the spiders/regions that are linked to the outputs of the currently selected control/spider/region and all the spiders/regions that these spiders/regions are connected to (all the downstream spiders/regions). - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, select the required form component, spider or region.

Tip: If you want to select more than one spider or region, hold down the CTRL key to multi-select.

Title: Hiding unselected spiders and regions
Tip: If you want to select more than one spider or region, hold down the CTRL key to multi-select. - Right-click the spider workspace and open the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions menu and ensure that there is a tick mark to the left of the Show Outgoing item. Tip: Hold down the CTRL key to select spiders or regions without applying this hiding filter. Before / After Example: Before applying this setting: After applying this setting: For instance, to show the spiders/regions that the currently selected form component configures and all the spiders/regions that these spiders/regions configure in turn. To also hide all spiders/regions that are not direct inputs/outputs of the selected item: In other words this only shows the spiders/regions that are linked to the inputs and outputs of the currently selected control/spider/region. - If necessary, open the required spider workspace. - If necessary, select the required form component, spider or region. Tip: If you want to select more than one spider or region, hold down the CTRL key to multi-select. - Right-click the spider workspace and open the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions menu and ensure that there is a tick mark to the left of the 1 Level In-Out item. Tip: Hold down the CTRL key to select spiders or regions without applying this hiding filter. Before / After Example: Before applying this setting: After applying this setting: For instance, to view all the spiders/regions that configure and that are configured by the selected form component. To apply a hiding filter to more than one spider/region at a time: This allows you to view the spiders/regions associated with more than one spider/region at a time. - Hold down the CTRL key and select the spiders/regions that you want to view. - Then apply the currently selected hiding filter (by clicking the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions toolbar button). To select a spider/region without applying the currently configured hiding filter: This allows you to configure one or more of the displayed spiders/regions without hiding the others. - Hold down the CTRL key and select the required spider/region. To turn off the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions filtering: In other words this shows all the spiders/regions that are currently configured in this spider workspace. - Either: click the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions toolbar button to disable this option. - Or: Right-click the spider workspace and open the Hide Unselected Spiders/Regions menu and ensure that there is a tick mark to the left of the None item. Spider workspace toolbar : describes the spider workspace that assists in the adding, arranging and configuring spiders and silks -->

Historical Alarm mode Top Historical Alarm mode Historical alarm mode allows an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent to save your historical alarms to a SQL Server database.

Title: Historical Alarm mode
Historical Alarm mode Top Historical Alarm mode Historical alarm mode allows an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent to save your historical alarms to a SQL Server database. Up to now, an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent only allowed the fully fledged AlarmManagement system to be used for one hour. The main advantage of using this Historical alarm mode is that previously the life-cycle of an alarm, such as when it was initiated, when viewed, when acknowledged and when cleared (removed) could only be determined by looking at several lines from the relevant AlarmList, but now this Historical Alarm mode you allows you to see the full life-cycle of each alarm in a single row in the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table of the Adroit Historical Alarms database that is created for you in the specified SQL Server that you need to specify. IMPORTANT: But this Historical alarm mode does not give you access to the other functionality provided by a licensed AlarmManagement agent, which allows you to fine-tune and optimise your alarming system. Note: This table only contains those historical alarms whose conditions for complete acknowledgment have been fulfilled, in other words if reasons and/or notes are mandatory for them that these have been specified in addition to acknowledging the alarm. Therefore, ONLY when your Agent Server license is not licensed for AlarmManagement does the AlarmManagement dialog contain a Historical Alarm mode check box. When you check this check box, then the next time that you start the Agent Server, the existing AlarmManagement database tables, if any, are removed and replaced with a minimal set of tables. IMPORTANT: You cannot run the AlarmManagement agent in both alarm management mode and this Historical Alarm mode at the same time and therefore after enabling Historical Alarm mode the AlarmManagement reports will not work! Note1: As usual, you need to have installed Microsoft SQL Server (Express) in order to use this Historical Alarm mode . Note2: If you do not check this checkbox then you can freely use (demo) the fully fledged AlarmManagement system for one hour. However, after enabling this checkbox you no longer have access to the fully fledged AlarmManagement system, unless you uncheck the Historical Alarm mode check box and restart the Agent Server. You can use the AdroitHistoricalAlarmViewer control in the SmartUI to connect to the AlarmManagement database and allow your users to locate and/or filter and/or print and/or export the historical Adroit alarms. Configuring Historical Alarm mode : describes how to configure an unlicensed AlarmManagement agent to log your alarms, so these historical alarms can be viewed later. -->

Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server Top Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server When a standby server joins a cluster, the historical data stored on the master server must be mirrored over to the standby server.

Title: Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server
Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server Top Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server When a standby server joins a cluster, the historical data stored on the master server must be mirrored over to the standby server. This is done in an intelligent manner by only copying over the data that it requires, that is, the data stored by the master during the period that the newly added standby server was down. Note: This is only possible if the cluster Agent Servers have their system time synchronised . This data catch-up is performed by the SystemDataLog agent, called systemDl. For details, see The SystemDatalog Agent . Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. -->

Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract that retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting of DataLog agents, or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period.

Title: Extracting Logged Data
Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract that retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting of DataLog agents, or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period. The data is then converted into a CSV (comma separated value) file format that can be opened by a third party application such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports.

Adroit also provides a utility for merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents .

Title: Merging Data Logs
Adroit also provides a utility for merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents . The .CSV file may have been originally created by the EXTRACT utility above, or by choosing the Export... button in the Datalog Retrieval dialog, or by using a text editor to modify existing files taking care to adhere to the format. -->

HMI Mode Top HMI Mode HMI mode is a lower cost, simpler version of Adroit and SmartUI , which is a stand-alone solution that supports the addition of up to 2 clients.

Title: HMI Mode
HMI Mode Top HMI Mode HMI mode is a lower cost, simpler version of Adroit and SmartUI , which is a stand-alone solution that supports the addition of up to 2 clients. This cannot be incorporated into a larger distributed project and does not support redundancy. HMI mode is licensed via the HASP and provides for a cost-effective, bulk implementation of HMI software. The Hasp agent LICENCE has a read-only slot called "HMIMode". If a HMI mode HASP is present then the slot value will be 1, otherwise it will be 0 for standard Agent Servers. HMI mode is therefore one of the components of an Adroit license. HMI mode is typically configured on installation. However, you can create configurations using the Full or HMI mode by using the Configuration dialog of the Adroit Config Editor utility. Note: You can only see if the current (active) configuration is running in Full or HMI mode, after checking the Allow Multiple Configurations checkbox. When using multiple configurations (when engineering multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running in Full or HMI mode. You can also create additional configurations that are based on existing ones, as needed. Note: If you have only installed the Agent Server and not the SmartUI Server, then you can manually put the Agent Server in and out of HMI mode by configuring the HMIMode registry value (this requires restarting the Agent Server). - if the Agent Server is licensed for HMI and Adroit has not been configured for HMI mode the Agent Server will display a message box that it cannot continue and it will terminate. The user must either enable the HMI configuration or change the HASP. - if Adroit has been configured for HMI mode and the Agent Server is not licensed for HMI, then the Agent Server will continue in HMI mode. An HMI licensed Agent Server has the following restrictions: - ONLY loads the following agent types: - Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! - Basic agents: Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, String, StringList and Timer IMPORTANT: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. - Advanced agents: AgentGroup, Alarm, AlarmList (only Default), AlarmManagement, Command, DBAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Script, Shift and Statistical - IT agents: Perfmon - System agents: Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan and SystemInformation - prevents the use of the following agent types: Accumulator, AREC, Audit, Custom , DumpConfig , Frame , ICMP , Integer, MaxDemand, Multistate, OEE, PID, Real, Recipe, Scheduler , SNMPMngr , SystemDatalog and Text IMPORTANT: Due to this change, standard Agent Servers and their projects will be INCOMPATIBLE with HMI licensed Agent Servers and their projects, when they use any of these HMI-unsupported agent types. - the Agent Server can only be run in stand-alone mode and not cluster or cluster-aware mode. Note: In HMI mode, when the Agent Server is run, it is forced to run in stand-alone mode, regardless of its current setting. For further details of what is licensed by an Adroit (Agent Server) licence, see Adroit Licensing . -->
