Note: You can only see if the current (active) configuration is running in Full or HMI mode, after checking the Allow Multiple Configurations checkbox. When using multiple configurations (when engineering multiple projects), you can specify which configurations run in Full or HMI mode, depending upon your project's requirements. This allows you to easily switch between projects (configurations) running in Full or HMI mode. You can also create additional configurations that are based on existing ones, as needed. Note: If you have only installed the Agent Server and not the SmartUI Server, then you can manually put the Agent Server in and out of HMI mode by configuring the HMIMode registry value (this requires restarting the Agent Server). - if the Agent Server is licensed for HMI and Adroit has not been configured for HMI mode the Agent Server will display a message box that it cannot continue and it will terminate. The user must either enable the HMI configuration or change the HASP. - if Adroit has been configured for HMI mode and the Agent Server is not licensed for HMI, then the Agent Server will continue in HMI mode. An HMI licensed Agent Server has the following restrictions: - ONLY loads the following agent types: - Primitive agents: Boolean, Integer, Real The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! - Basic agents: Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, String, StringList and Timer IMPORTANT: Each Marshal agent used, consumes 16 scan license points. - Advanced agents: AgentGroup, Alarm, AlarmList (only Default), AlarmManagement, Command, DBAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Script, Shift and Statistical - IT agents: Perfmon - System agents: Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan and SystemInformation - prevents the use of the following agent types: Accumulator, AREC, Audit, Custom , DumpConfig , Frame , ICMP , Integer, MaxDemand, Multistate, OEE, PID, Real, Recipe, Scheduler , SNMPMngr , SystemDatalog and Text IMPORTANT: Due to this change, standard Agent Servers and their projects will be INCOMPATIBLE with HMI licensed Agent Servers and their projects, when they use any of these HMI-unsupported agent types. - the Agent Server can only be run in stand-alone mode and not cluster or cluster-aware mode. Note: In HMI mode, when the Agent Server is run, it is forced to run in stand-alone mode, regardless of its current setting. For further details of what is licensed by an Adroit (Agent Server) licence, see Adroit Licensing . -->

Title: How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy
How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy Top How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy The ISA S95 standard divides the manufacturing enterprise into: plant floor automation control, MES and ERP. This standard focuses on MES and ERP, as its goal is to seamlessly coordinate business and production processes. The ISA S88 standard, originally created for batch processes, can be used to structure ANY process. This standard focuses on plant floor automation control. BOTH standards share a SIMILAR hierarchy describing the structure of automation projects, as follows: MAPS implements (and enforces) the following extended physical model: Note: These hierarchical categories ALL have a 1 to many relationship with their components i.e. a Site can contain MANY Areas, an Area can contain MANY Process Cells (PLCs) etc. - The Site level is the MAPS project. So you will have one MAPS project per site. For example, XYZ Foods. - The Area level is the defined Plant area/s of the MAPS project. For example, Batching Plant. - The Process Cell level is the PLC/s of each defined plant area. For example, BATCHING PLC. - The Unit level is the collection/s of equipment items within each PLC. Typically these relate to the plant area-specific operations, such as Filling, Packing, Flocculation etc. For example, Batching. However, you can ALSO create a unit for each item of complex equipment i.e. equipment that consist of more than one Electrical or Instrumentation item, such as conveyors. - The Equipment module and the Control module levels are NOT separately implemented because this is not supported by the PLC programming architecture. These levels are the defined items of equipment that are classified into either the Electrical or Instrumentation categories for each of the defined units. -->

Title: Maximum demand calculation example:
Assuming that the power consumption on a plant over a block period of 30 minutes is comprised of 5 different episodes of consumption as follows: - 800 kVA for 5 minutes - 200 kVA for 5 minutes - 400 kVA for 10 minutes - 800 kVA for 8 minutes - 1500 kVA for 2 minutes Adroit calculates the maximum demand for that 30 minute period as follows: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA During each of the above five episodes the predicted maximum demand would have been: - Episode1: (800*30) / 30 = 800 kVA - Episode2: ((800*5) + (200*25)) / 30 = 300 kVA - Episode3: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*20)) / 30 = 433.33 kVA - Episode4: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*10)) / 30 = 566.66 kVA - Episode5: ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA If this agent had a configured maximum demand limit of 600 kVA and the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled, then the MaxDemand status bit would have been on during episodes 1 and 5.

Title: To alarm an agent (process value):
For instance: we will alarm an agent called ANA001 of the Analog agent type, using the defaultAlarmAgent: the Alarm agent that is created by default by Adroit . Things to be aware of when alarming process values: Since the Alarm agent manages the alarming of agents, you need to ensure that the Alarm agent you use provides the following: - Alarm routes that provide the required destinations (methods) to communicate these alarms or events to the relevant personnel. In this case we will use the default configuration for alarm route 2 and 3 provided by the defaultAlarmAgent, which routes alarms to the LOCAL Alarm List (within the Alarm agent itself) where they can be displayed in the Alarm List Viewer window and the LOCAL event log, where they can be displayed in the Event Log Viewer window. - Alarm types that represent ALL the necessary alarm-able state/s for the agent type of the agent that contains this process value. In this case we will use the default alarm types for the Analog agent type. Tip: Is it recommended that you create an alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. BEFORE you start alarming agents to determine how best this can be achieved. If necessary, create an Analog agent. For instance: in this case, called ANA001. . For details, see To Add a New Agent . Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator, as follows: - Ensure that the Basic , Advanced and/or System checkbox is checked to display the required agent type in this list. These checkboxes use these default agent groups to help you select the required agent quickly. Tip: If no checkboxes are selected, then all the available agent types will be displayed in the Type list box. This is useful if the required agent type has not been categorised. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list - Locate the required agent type, using the scroll bar and click on it. - In the Agents list, click on the name of the required agent (if necessary scroll down to locate this). Tip: Right-click to display a menu of commands to perform upon the selected agent(s). - Right-click this agent and select its Alarm… menu item. - If necessary, select the Alarm agent that will monitor the agent, from the Use alarm agent list box. By default, the defaultAlarmAgent is selected, so in this case we do not need to change this agent. - Double click each Available alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. (an alarm-able state), you want to monitor for this agent. For instance: in this case ANA001 to add it to the Current list.

Note: ONLY the alarm types in the Current list are monitored by the Alarm agent as potential incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type.

Title: To alarm an agent (process value):
Note: ONLY the alarm types in the Current list are monitored by the Alarm agent as potential incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). . Tip: The default alarm types (alarm-able states) typically correspond to the specific status bits of the selected agent type, which describe how these states are triggered (become active). - For each alarm type in the Current list, you can specify the following: - The route of this Alarm agent that you require this incident to be sent to when it occurs, by selecting the required route number from the Select route list box. - Whether this incident requires acknowledgement (is an alarm) or not (is an event), by checking or clearing the Acknowledgement required checkbox. For instance: - Add the High , High-high , Low and Low-low alarm types to the Current list and for each of them Select route 2 and leave the Acknowledgement required checkbox checked, since these are ALARMS which require a response and ACTION from the operator. - Add the Changed alarm type to the Current list and Select route 3 and clear Acknowledgement required checkbox, since this is an EVENT, which ONLY PROVIDES INFORMATION, in this case indicating that a value has changed. - Now when any of these incidents occur (becomes active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. ), it is routed along the specified route to ALL the destinations on this route, which are specified in the Route details section of the Alarming dialog. For instance: both these alarms and events can be viewed in the Alarm List Viewer window and Event Log Viewer window. - If necessary, you can also specify the following for each alarm type: - Priority: Typically you prioritise your incidents to ensure that your operators ONLY receive IMPORTANT alarms - since some alarms are critical, whereas others are more informational in nature. For details, see Prioritizing or Filtering Incidents . - Delay (secs): Typically you delay an active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. incident from entering the alarm system to prevent intermittent alarms from flooding your alarm system or to ensure that this alarm is raised when the operator needs to respond to it. For details, see Delaying Incidents . - Conditional expressions: Typically you specify a conditional expression to ensure that each incident is unique and does not duplicate existing active incidents. For details, see Creating Conditional Expressions for Incidents . - Inhibited until: Typically you temporarily suspend alarming when you are performing maintenance on a plant section or a particular item of equipment or when an alarm indicator is not functioning correctly or is being tested. For detail, see Temporarily Suspending Alarming .

text:
The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval.

Title: Configuration
The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. This provides various different logging methods, such as “log on change”, “log on interval” etc. For a detailed description of configuring the DBLog agent, see Configuring DBLog Agents . Tip: Typically you need to separate the Analog and Digital tags that you want to log into different DBLog agents, due to their unique logging requirements. Once the DBLog Agent has been configured and enabled, it creates table /s in the specified database with the following fields: - id : a unique indexing identifier - dt : the Timestamp of the logged value - Tagname : the name of the tag being logged - Value :– the value of the tag being logged - Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad data has a bad status when data is missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated. . This agent ALSO creates the Adr_DBLog_AgentDetails table, which contains all the agents referenced by all DBLog agents to provide more details about these referenced agents, which can be used to provide more context about them for reports.

text:
This table is updated when: the agent is started; or when its tag list is changed; and unconditionally every morning at 01h00 and this table contains the following fields: - ID – integer key: a unique indexing identifier - Owner – varchar(255): the DBLog agent name for future use to remove entries owned by the agent - AgentName – varchar(255): the name of the agent of the tag being logged - AgentDescription - varchar(255): the description of the agent being logged - AgentType – varchar(255): the agent type of the tag being logged - TagName – varchar(255): the tag being logged - TagDescription – varchar(255): a description of the tag being logged; always equal to AgentDescription unless agent type is Marshal whereupon it contains the description of the bit - Units - varchar(255): for Analog agents only - OffText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only - OnText - varchar(255): for Digital and Marshal agents only - RawMin - float: Raw (device-scale) minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only - RawMax - float: Raw (device-scale) maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only - EngMin - float: Engineering minimum scaling limit for Analog agents only - EngMax - float: Engineering maximum scaling limit for Analog agents only - LoLo - float: Low-low alarm level for Analog agents only - Lo - float: Low alarm level for Analog agents only - Hi - float: High alarm level for Analog agents only - HiHi - float: High-high alarm level for Analog agents only Note: If you do not intend to make use of this table then you can prevent this table from being created by all of your DBLog agents, by adding the following registry value and setting it to 0: DumpAgentDetailsEnabled .

text:
The function of this query is to return the names of all tags whose values are being logged by the DBLog agent.

Title: Create the Select Tags query
The function of this query is to return the names of all tags whose values are being logged by the DBLog agent. - Add a Select Query to this LoggingDB OleDB datasource, called Tag Names , which returns a unique and sorted set of values from the Tagname field of the database table that the DBLog agent logs to. For details, see Select queries . - Select the appropriate table from the database, specified by this OleDB datasource, which is typically called “Adr_DBLog”. - Ensure that the resultant query adheres to the following syntax: SELECT DISTINCT [Adr_DBLog].Tagname FROM [Adr_DBLog] ORDER BY [Adr_DBLog].Tagname ASC Back to top

text:
The function of this query is to return the values of a specific tag between a specific starting and ending time.

Title: Create the Select Tag Values query
The function of this query is to return the values of a specific tag between a specific starting and ending time. - Add a Select Query to this LoggingDB OleDB datasource, called Tag Values , which returns a set of values logged for a specific tag starting from a specific time and ending at a specific time. This query therefore uses the following three parameters, whose values will eventually be specified by using suitable controls on the graphic form: - tagname: this parameter specifies the required name of the tag, whose values should be returned, - startdate: this parameter specifies the date and time at which the required values of the specified tag should be retrieved from - enddate: this parameter specifies the date and time at which the required values of the specified tag should be retrieved to - Ensure that the resultant query adheres to the following syntax: SELECT [Adr_DBLog].[dt], [Adr_DBLog].[Value] FROM [Adr_DBLog] WHERE [Adr_DBLog].[Tagname] = '<!!tagname!!>' AND ([Adr_DBLog].[dt] between '<!!startdate!!>' and '<!!enddate!!>') Note: You can simply copy and paste this query as-is into the Custom Query dialog, you do not need to specifically add parameters and/or constraints by using the Select Query Builder dialogs. The required parameter data type is specified by its specific formatting in the query string, whether this is typed in manually or selected from the right click menu. Back to top

text:
By default the LineChart is configured to chart real-time values, so you need to change its properties as you are charting historical (logged) data from a database.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
By default the LineChart is configured to chart real-time values, so you need to change its properties as you are charting historical (logged) data from a database. - If necessary, add the required project and/or graphic form to this project. - Add a LineChart control to this graphic form, from the Data category of the Toolbox window. - Click Cancel to close the chart configuration dialog that is automatically displayed. - In the Properties window, ensure the (Trendline) UseTrendLines Boolean property of this LineChart control is set to False, from the default value of True, so that this linechart control will only use Line and not Trendline series to chart the logged values. - Click the glyph a glyph is a specific graphic symbol, for instance employed by form components, which when clicked launch alternate configuration dialogs. , in the top left corner of the LineChart control, which lists its commonly-used properties and configuration tasks. In the Data Settings section of this task list: - Uncheck the Realtime checkbox, which is checked by default and not required since this chart is trending data from a database and not real-time data - Uncheck the Extrapolate Data checkbox, to ensure that only the logged values are charted and no interpolation will occur between successively logged values - this is the most accurate method of trending data, although it may be not as visually appealing as extrapolated data. In the Configuration Dialogs section of this task list: - Click the Edit Time Details... link to display the Time Detail Settings dialog: Change the Period Type to Start DateTime to End DateTime from the default of End Datetime - Timespan , since in this example the start and end date times define the charting value range. - Click the Edit Chart... link to display the LineChart configuration dialog. In the Series Setup page, change the Datasource column of the initial series from Values to DataSet . This displays the DataSet tab beneath the series table, which you need to configure as follows: - In the Data Element field, browse in the required table of the configured OleDB datasource, in this case: the Adr_DBLog table of the LoggingDB datasource, so theshould be: LoggingDB.Tables.Adr_DBLog. - In the YValue Member field, specify the value field (row) of this table, in this case this is the Value field. - In the XValue Member field, specify the datetime field (row) of this table, in this case this is the dt field. Note: In this case only a single value is being trended at a time so only one series is required. Example: Click Finish to save these changes and close the LineChart configuration dialog. Back to top

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Note: Query spiders can perform queries and execute statements provided by any OLE DB datasource. - Right click the spider workspace and select Create New Spider and select the Query spider from the Databasing category. - Double click the spider icon to display its spider configuration dialog. - Double click the default name, for instance Query1 and type in the new name: Tag Names . - Configure the Inputs section of this spider to specify the Select Query created for the LoggingDB OleDB datasource, which is called Select Tags , as follows: - Set the Server input to Default Server ; the OLEDB Data Source input to LoggingDB ; and the Query Type input to Select Query and the Query Name input to Select Tags - Configure this Query spider to perform this query when the graphic form is opened, by configuring the Event Trigger section, to select Form as the Event Object and Load as the Event Name . Troubleshoot query and link the Return Object output to the ComboBox control - Right click the Spider header (bar at the top of this Tag Names spider) and select Trigger Now! to get the initial dataset for this Query spider. Note: Ensure that the Success output is True (i.e. the query ran successfully), if this is False then there is either a problem with the query syntax or another problem preventing this query from running. Tip: The Rows Exist output is only True when the query returns data and is False if an empty dataset is returned. - In the graphic form, click the comboBox control to display this control's properties in the Objects tree on the right of the spider workspace. - In the Outputs section of the Tag Names Query spider, drag the Return Object output onto the Data property group (to expand it) and then onto the Datasource property of the comboBox control to connect them with a Silk. Title: To chart databinder data:
Steps:

WARNING! Do not rename these series, since this name corresponds to a separate component on the graphic form that provides advanced series settings. - If necessary, choose and configure the required Type of series to display your data in this charting control. The following types of series are available: Note: The available series types are dependant upon the selected charting control. - Bar : a series of horizontal bars representing values. If selected this provides: the Bar Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. For details, see Displaying a Bar series or Configuring value labels . - Column : a series of vertical columns representing values. If selected this provides: the Column Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. For details, see Displaying a Column series or Configuring value labels . - FastLine : a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. Note: A FastLine series provides less configuration options than a Line series so that it is drawn faster and is recommended for trending real-time data. - Line : a series of points that are usually connected to form lines. If selected this provides: the Line Style tab to specify how to display the series and a Series Marks tab to optionally specify additional labels for each or some of the values for this series. - Select a SmartUI Server computer, which will be used to as the template for the cluster on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then copied to ALL the other Server machines in the cluster .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Select a SmartUI Server computer, which will be used to as the template for the cluster on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then copied to ALL the other Server machines in the cluster . - Perform the following configuration on this computer: - Run the SmartUI Config application and open the SmartUI Server or SmartUI Service configuration under the Advanced section, depending upon whether this Server is being run as a service or not. Ensure that its ServerName property is set to the name of the cluster . Figure 1: Locating the ServerName property for a SmartUI Server - Run the SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer and ensure that ALL the projects and data sources have been set up and finalised. - Close the Designer and Server. - Now ensure that the following components are copied from this Server computer to all the Server computers in this cluster : - The Data and Projects folders. - The VIPServer.exe.config and VIPService.exe.config files. - If necessary, configure the following settings that configure the UDP broadcasts that inform cluster aware Operators of the availability and load of each cluster partner: - The BroadcastEnabled Server setting enables (the default setting) or disables these UDP broadcasts. - The BroadcastTimePeriod Server setting specifies the time, in milliseconds, between broadcasts, which is 2 seconds (2000 milliseconds) by default. Although decreasing this setting reduces the network traffic it also prevents the Operators from quickly responding to changes in Server load and/or availability. - The BroadcastPortRange Server setting specifies the UDP port range which the Server uses for its broadcasts, by default this is 11000-11010. IMPORTANT : If you CHANGE this setting for a Server then you need to change the BroadcastPortRange setting of each Client that you want to receive these broadcasts from this Server. Back to top

- Select an SmartUI Operator computer, which will be used as the template for all the Operator clients that are to connect to this cluster, on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then will usually be copied to the other Operator clients.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Select an SmartUI Operator computer, which will be used as the template for all the Operator clients that are to connect to this cluster, on which all the necessary configuration will be initially performed and then will usually be copied to the other Operator clients. - Run the SmartUI Config application on this Operator computer and open the SmartUI Operator configuration page under the Advanced section. Ensure that the Cluster Settings group of properties are configured, as follows: Figure 2 : Locating the Cluster Settings group of properties for a SmartUI Operator - The ClusterEnabled property must to be set to true - Since a SmartUI Operator can be configured to connect to more than one cluster, the ClusterNames property is a comma separated list, which specifies the names of each of the clusters that this SmartUI Operator can connect to. In this case as we only want to connect to one cluster, this should be set to Cluster1. - The last and most important setting is the ClusterServers setting, which contains a comma separated list of the Servers that form part of the cluster. This list is in the following format: “clustername~computername~port~connectionmechanism~ communicationmechanism;…” - Since it is possible for the Servers that make up a cluster to either be located on the LAN or hosted on the Internet, this determines how these Servers are described by this setting, as follows: - An example of a Server connection string for a LAN cluster server is: Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE - An example of a Server connection string for an INTERNET cluster server is: Cluster1~http://201.201.201.1~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL - In our example, all the Servers that form part of the cluster exist on the LAN, and more specifically on three computers – Computer1, Computer2 and Computer3. For this reason this ClusterServers setting will appear as follows: Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE However, if all the Servers that form part of this cluster existed on the Internet, and more specifically on three computers with the following IP addresses– 201.201.201.1, 201.201.201.2 and 201.201.201.3. Then this ClusterServers setting will appear as follows: Cluster1~http://201.201.201.1~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL; Cluster1~http://201.201.201.2~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL; Cluster1~http://201.201.201.3~80~WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE_POLL - Ensure that this configuration file ( VIP Operator.exe.config ) is copied to and used by ALL the SmartUI Operator clients that will connect to this cluster. Note : This is possible since these SmartUI Operator clients connect to a single cluster. However, if different Operators are required to connect to different clusters, it may be necessary to manually configure their configuration files individually, depending upon the complexity required. Back to top

When configuring load balancing, it is often useful to group the SmartUI Operators that connect to a cluster into more than one set.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
When configuring load balancing, it is often useful to group the SmartUI Operators that connect to a cluster into more than one set. Then modify the ClusterServers setting for each of these sets, so that the order in which they connect to the Servers within the cluster differ. For example, if we have three sets of SmartUI Operators that need to connect to this cluster, then each of their CONFIG files could be configured with three different ClusterServers settings. In this way each SmartUI Operator in the three different sets connects to a different SmartUI Server on start up. For instance: Set 1 Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE Set 2 Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE Set 3 Cluster1~Computer3~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer1~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE; Cluster1~Computer2~9000~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE

The INITIAL connection for the SmartUI Operator MUST have a running SmartUI Server.

Title: Notes
Steps:
The INITIAL connection for the SmartUI Operator MUST have a running SmartUI Server. In other words, if a SmartUI Operator is configured to connect to the SmartUI Server on Computer3, this SmartUI Server MUST be running, otherwise the initial log on of this SmartUI Operator will fail. From then on if this SmartUI Server fails, this SmartUI Operator will hunt until it finds an active connection. The speed at which this occurs is determined by its switch-over time. This switch-over time is the time taken for a SmartUI Operator to become aware that its current connection has failed and to search for and connect to another SmartUI Server. This is configured by the ClientPingInterval setting of the SmartUI Operator, which is grouped under the ConnectionSettings in the SmartUI Operator.exe.config file. The ClientPingInterval setting determines how often the SmartUI Operator will query the Server for an active connection and its configuration has the following effect upon the performance of the Operator: - If this interval is too frequent interval, this will increase client-server chatter and use up bandwidth unnecessarily. - If this interval is too infrequent interval, then the SmartUI Operator will take a long time to realise that the Server it is currently connected to is no longer available. A ping interval between 5 and 10 seconds should suffice for most cluster configurations. -->

Have Adroit 8 (MAPS 3) or later installed.

Title: Prerequisites
Have Adroit 8 (MAPS 3) or later installed. Note: If you are using a version later than this then this how to will probably also apply to your version too, although some dialogs and/or commands may have changed slightly. This document describes how to connect a TrendConfigurator control to a LineChart control for runtime chart configuration, when the physical structure of its tags (adhering to the ISA S95 and S88 standards) are sourced from a database. Note: This document assumes that the reader has a basic working knowledge of using SQL databases and using databases in SmartUI . This document describes the following steps that are required: - Add an Adroit Datasource that connects to the Agent Server containing the tags to trend . - Add an OleDB datasource and connect it to the database where the structured list of the areas, devices and their tags are stored . - Create the following three Select queries for this OleDB datasource : - Areas Select query - DevicesPerArea Select query - TagsPerDevice Select query - Add a LineChart control to trend the tags . - Add a TrendConfigurator control to perform the runtime configuration of the LineChart . - Link the three TrendConfigurator combo boxes to their respective Select queries: - Add and configure a Query spider for the Areas Select query - Troubleshoot query and link the Return Object output to the AreaList property - Add and configure a Query spider for the DevicesPerArea Select query - Link the CurrentArea property to supply the value of its area (parameter) input - Troubleshoot query and link the Return Object output to the DevicesList property - Add and configure a Query spider for the TagsPerDevice Select query - Link the CurrentArea property to supply the value of its area (parameter) input - Link the CurrentDevice property to supply the value of the device (parameter) input - Troubleshoot query and link the Return Object output to the PenList property - Operate the TrendConfigurator control at runtime . Back to top

Title: Add three Select queries to this OleDB datasource
The TrendConfigurator provides three drop-down list fields, per configured series or tag, namely Area , Device and Pen which can be driven by using their respective properties AreaList , DeviceList and PenList - either via Select queries on an OleDB datasource or via direct links. Note: Driving both the Area and Device drop-down lists are optional, if you do not wish to select a list of tags per device per area and just want to drive the Pen column drop-down list with a list of all tags instead. Tip: You can hide both the Area and/or Device columns by setting the AreaColumnVisible and/or DeviceColumnVisible property to False. If ONLY driving the Pen combo box, then the required syntax of the Select Query that populates this combo box, is as follows: SELECT DISTINCT [Table].[Tags] FROM [Table] , assuming that the field of Table containing the tags is called Tags . text:
Typical runtime configuration: Note: By default, the run-time configuration of all TrendConfigurator controls are stored in a user profile variable called TrendConfigurator .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Typical runtime configuration: Note: By default, the run-time configuration of all TrendConfigurator controls are stored in a user profile variable called TrendConfigurator . Therefore if you want to maintain separate lists of sets for your TrendConfigurator controls, then rename this variable of each TrendConfigurator control in the The Setting Name to use to load and save the Set configuration to the Users Profile field of the General Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog (the UserProfileSetting property). For each Pen (tag or value) that you select to be trended as part of a set, you can specify the following: IMPORTANT: You need to click the Save Set button (on the right of the TrendConfigurator control ) after adding or configuring one or more series to this list, to save these changes to the current set (as specified by the Set Name drop-down list on the right of the TrendConfigurator control). Otherwise when you close this graphic form, the new series and/or configuration changes will be lost. Note: You may need to click the Refresh Chart button to view with any series that you add to the current set. - color: Use the color box to choose the required color for this series or value (and its axis color if it has its own custom axis) in the associated LineChart control. - If displayed, the Area column typically allows the specific plant area to be specified, in which this tag is physically situated (unless the PresetArea property has been specified). - If displayed, the Device column typically allows the specific FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. device to be specified, in which this tag is being communicated (unless the PresetDevice property has been specified). - Pen: The name of the tag of this series. When using the Adroit mode: A browse (...) button appears to the right of this field so that users can also browse in additional tags to the Pen drop-down list at runtime. Note: These additional tags can be removed from the Pen drop-down list at runtime, by selecting the required tag in the list and clicking the button on the right. - Title: Edit the name of the series or value that is displayed in the legend of the associated LineChart (if you choose this value to be visible in the legend by checking its Leg checkbox). Note: By default this column displays the description of the tag as this is usually more descriptive than the tag name itself. However, if you want the series to display the tag name [AgentName.Property(Slot)Name] instead then uncheck the Use Pen (Tag) Description for Series Names instead of Tag Names checkbox in the General Settings tab (the UsePenDescForSeriesName property). - Value: The current value of the tag being used for this series when it was selected. - Unit: If necessary, specify the required unit to specify on the custom axis of the series on the LineChart for the trended value or series. If you are using the MAPS or Adroit modes, then this is retrieved for you, for Analog tags. - Vis: This checkbox toggles the series or value visibility on the associated LineChart. In other words this series is displayed in the LineChart when checked (the default setting) and it is hidden when unchecked. - Leg: This checkbox toggles the series or value visibility in the legend of the associated LineChart. In other words this series is displayed in the legend when checked (the default setting) and it is hidden when unchecked.

text:
- Axes: This checkbox determines whether this series or value will be charted using the default Y (or value) axis when unchecked OR whether a custom Y axis will be used, when this is checked (the default setting).

Title: Configuration
- Axes: This checkbox determines whether this series or value will be charted using the default Y (or value) axis when unchecked OR whether a custom Y axis will be used, when this is checked (the default setting). When using custom Y axis then, the following fields are used to configure the display of this axis in the associated LineChart: - X-Pos: Specify the horizontal position of this custom Y axis, relative to the position of the default Y axis, as a percentage of the total horizontal width (size) of the default X axis. In other words, a value of a 100 moves the custom Y axis to the other side of the LineChart. Note: A positive value shifts this custom Y axis to the right of the default Y axis, by the specified amount; while a negative value shifts this custom Y axis to the left of the default Y axis, by the specified amount. - Y-Pos: Specify the vertical position or topmost end of this custom Y axis, relative to the top of the default Y axis, as a percentage of the total vertical height (size) of the default Y axis. In other words, a value of a 100 hides this custom Y axis and therefore this series too. Note: A positive value decreases the height of this custom Y axis below that of the default Y axis, by the specified height; while a negative value increases the height of this custom Y axis above that of the default Y axis, by the specified height. - size: Specify the size of this custom Y axis, from the specified Y-Pos location in the direction of the X axis (lower-left corner), as a percentage of the total vertical height (size) of the default Y axis. In other words, a value of 100 is the size of the actual Y axis. - Min: The minimum value of this Custom Y axis, which depends upon the value being charted. By default this is set to 0, although, if possible, this control will obtain this value from the applicable Adroit datasource for the selected agent. Note: Any series value below the specified Min value will be hidden from view. - Max: The maximum value of this Custom Y axis, which depends upon the value being charted. By default this is set to 100, although, if possible, this control will obtain this value from the applicable Adroit datasource for the selected agent. Note: Any series value above the specified Max value will be hidden from view. - Adv: This column provides a browse (...) button that launched the tabbed Advanced Pen Configuration dialog, that allows the following advanced settings to be configured per pen: Note: You typically need to click the Refresh Chart button after making changes to these settings to view them on the associated LineChart. Series settings: These settings affect how the series of this pen will be charted, as follows: - You can select one of the following series styles from the Type drop-down list: Line, FastLine, Area and XYPlot. - You can specify the width of the line representing this series, in pixels, from the Width spin control. - You can check the Stairs/Steps checkbox to change the series to be charted in stairs/step mode (when unchecked, the default setting, the series uses a smoothly interpolated line between successive data points). - You can check the Pointers checkbox to display rectangular data points representing this series (when unchecked, the default setting, these data points are hidden).

text:
Custom Axis settings: These settings affect the display of the vertical Y-Axis of the LineChart for the pen, as follows: Note: The bottom chart axis for each set can now be configured via the Advanced Set Configuration dialog.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Custom Axis settings: These settings affect the display of the vertical Y-Axis of the LineChart for the pen, as follows: Note: The bottom chart axis for each set can now be configured via the Advanced Set Configuration dialog. - You can check the Automatic Scales checkbox to turn on automatic scaling for the entire axis or for only the minimum (by checking the Minimum Auto checkbox) or maximum (by checking the Maximum Auto checkbox) of the scale. - You can specify the required frequency or number of the axis ticks and labels, by specifying the required Increment interval. - You can change the Axis color . - You can display the axis on the right-hand side by checking the Other side checkbox (when unchecked, the default setting, this axis is displayed on the left side). Using buttons, on the right of the TrendConfigurator control, you can change how the values of the current set are trended in the associated LineChart, as follows: To view added series for the current set that are not yet displayed: click the Refresh Chart button. To set the time interval of the X-axis for all series: Click the Range button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. This displays the Time Details Settings dialog so you can configure the starting and ending times that apply to all the values that you are trending. Note: This affects the time interval for all series of all the sets that you display on this LineChart until you close the SmartUI Operator, at which time this configuration will be lost. The following axes-stacking actions change both the Custom and default Y axes parameters, which you can edit if you want to change their resultant settings: Note: These Axes stacking actions only apply if you have configured one or more custom Y axis for this set of trended values. In other words, you have at least one Axes checkbox checked. To view each custom Y axis on its own axis: This is particularly useful when you are trending values, whose custom Y axes have differing scales (differing maximum values), since this separates each custom Y axis for easier readability. Click the Stack Axes Horizontally button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. Note: This automatically configures the horizontal positioning ( X-Pos ) of the Custom Y axes for the best fit. To trend each series using their own Y (value) axis: This allows you to compare the trend of each series (value) without confusing or hiding the trends of the other series. Click the Stack Axes Vertically button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. Note: This automatically configures the vertical positioning ( Y-Pos ) and size of the Custom and default Y axes of each trended series, so that each series has their own Y axis that is the same size, one above the other. To configure the chart axes at runtime: This allows you to configure the scaling, position and/or axis ticks of one or all the axes of the associated LineChart in the Operator. Click the Axes button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. In the displayed Axis Configuration dialog, configure the axes of the associated LineChartconfigured, as follows: If necessary, Select an Axis to configure from this drop-down list box. To customise the scaling of this axis: determine whether to manually or automatically scale this axis and/or invert the scaling and/or hide the scaling and/or to improve the readability of the axis.

text:
Click the Axis Scales tab to do one or more of the following: Note: You may need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to display these settings.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Click the Axis Scales tab to do one or more of the following: Note: You may need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to display these settings. To automatically configure the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Automatic checkbox is checked, this also checks the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. Tip: It is recommended to use automatic scaling (the default setting) when trending data with the Line or XYPlot chart. To manually configure the scaling of this axis: Tip: This is typically required when you are using Bar or Column charts so that you can see the differences in values between two series. - Ensure that the Automatic checkbox is cleared, this also clears the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. - Manually specify the Minimum and Maximum values, by using the Value spin control to specify the required value. To scale the axis logarithmically: Note: You need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to edit these settings. - Check the Logarithmic checkbox to scale the selected axis logarithmically settings include: Note: The Minimum and Maximum values of this axis should be greater than zero, and the Axis cannot be of type DateTime . - Then specify the required Logarithmic Base for this logarithmic scaling. To specify a margin or offset above and/or below the axis scaling for improved readability: specify the required Offset (blank space) below the Minimum value and/or above the Maximum value, in pixels (this is an Advanced feature). To invert the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Inverted checkbox is checked (this is an Advanced feature). To hide the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Visible checkbox is cleared. To customise the positioning of this axis: determine the relative position and the actual size of this axis relative to the total dimension of the charting area. Click the Axis Position tab to specify one or more of the following axis positions: Relative Position : the position of this axis, as percentage (0-100%) of the length or width of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the Bottom border and 100 is the Top. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the Left border and 100 is the Right. Start Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the starting position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area. End Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the ending position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area. To customise the display of the axis and its scaling demarcations or ticks: determine to display the axis, its major demarcations or ticks and their grid lines and to configure the colors of these items.

text:
Click the Axis Ticks tab to specify the visibility and/or the displayed color of the following axis components: Axis Pen Visible : This checkbox displays/hides this axis.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Click the Axis Ticks tab to specify the visibility and/or the displayed color of the following axis components: Axis Pen Visible : This checkbox displays/hides this axis. Axis color : Configure the required color of this axis. For details, see Using the color edit box to select a color . Ticks Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the major ticks (demarcations) of this axis. Ticks color : Configure the required color of these major ticks. Grid Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the grid lines, displayed within the charting area, from each major tick (demarcation) of this axis. Grid color : Configure the required color of these grid lines. Using buttons, on the right of the TrendConfigurator control, you can manage and configure sets of your values that are trended in the associated LineChart, as follows: To create a new set: - Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the New Set entry. - Add and configure the series (values) that you want to trend in this set in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control. - Click the Save Set button to name this set and add it to the Set Name drop-down list. To save and name a new set: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, which prompts you for the required name for this set of trended values, which is then added to the Set Name drop-down list. Tip: Ensure that you provide a descriptive or unique enough name so that you will remember exactly which trend values this set contains. To configure and/or trend the series (values) that you have added to a set: Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the name of the required set. This loads the series (values) and their configured properties in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control and then updates the associated LineChart to trend these series. To configure the display of the bottom chart axis for each set: to specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels and the required DateTime format of these labels. Note: This configuration is stored per set in the currently logged on user’s profile. Click the Advanced Set Configuration button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, to the right of the Set Name drop-down list to configure the bottom chart axis for the currently selected set. In the displayed Advanced Set Configuration dialog: - Specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels i.e. 1 minute, 1 hour etc. by selecting and configuring the required Scaling Increment options, as follows: - Check the Exact Date Time checkbox to enable Standard and to calculate the Axis Labels in exact 1 hour intervals. Unchecking this checkbox, the default setting, selects the Custom option. - Select the Standard option and specify the required datetime interval e.g. 1 hour, 1 minute etc. from the drop-down list. - Select the Custom option, if the Standard datetime intervals do not specify the interval that you require and then specify this required time interval in hours:minutes. - Specify the required DateTime Format of the Labels of this axis by specifying the required standard DateTime formatting string specifier i.e. yyy-MM-dd etc. from the list and then clicking the Set button. To update the current set with newly added and recently configured series: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control.

text:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit OEE Agent dialog: - Check the Enable agent checkbox (the enable slot). - Click the browse button to the left of the Shift tag checkbox and select the Shift agent you created to specify the required shift patterns and to determine the current shift number. For details, see Selecting a tag using the Agent Explorer . By default the OEE agent resets the recorded OEE at the end of each shift. If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a “per batch” basis, then uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox and programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch. - For a simple or complex KPI, scan the primary measurement variable to the input1 slot of this OEE agent (OR use the input1Tag optional tag reference for the input1 slot - Advanced OEE options dialog, Input 1 tag ). ONLY for a complex KPI - scan the secondary or dividing measurement variable to the input2 slot of this OEE agent (OR use the input2Tag optional tag reference for the input2 slot - Advanced OEE options dialog, Input 2 tag ). - Specify the type of input signal of the primary measurement variable, from the Input 1 type list, as follows: Note: Select the method that is used to add up this value. - Accumulator: The input1 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 1 type must be reset to 0 at the end of every shift using the ShiftEnd status bit as a trigger. - Total: The input1 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 1 type is never reset to 0. - Rate/hr: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/min: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/sec: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - ONLY if you are calculating a complex KPI (where one measured variable is divided by another) then change the Input 2 type list from the default setting of Unused and specify the type of input signal of the secondary or dividing measurement variable, as follows: - Accumulator: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 2 type must be reset to 0 at the end of every shift using the ShiftEnd status bit as a trigger. - Total: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 2 type is never reset to 0. - Rate/hr: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value.

metadata.title: How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI

text:
- Rate/min: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
- Rate/min: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/sec: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. IMPORTANT: If calculating a simple KPI whose measured variable should be divided by time and NOT another variable, then ensure that the Input 2 type list is ONLY set to Unused , the default setting. - If necessary, specify the units for the primary measured variable input1 in the top Totalised units edit box (the units1 slot) and ONLY if you are calculating a complex KPI then also specify those of the secondary or dividing measurement variable input2 in the bottom Totalised units edit box (the units2 slot). - Since KPI calculations are calculated against the time that the Machine/process running checkbox (the running slot) is ON - this should ONLY be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. Note: The OEE agent ALSO expects that this slot will be OFF if the available slot is OFF. If not, runtime will continue to increment even though availability is OFF. Therefore instead of manually checking this checkbox: - Create a Scheduler agent that is configured with the applicable OFF times for the monitored machine/process - such as maintenance/lunch/tea times etc. - Click the Advanced button of this edit dialog and in the Optional tag references section, browse for BOOLEAN value slot of this Scheduler agent as the Running tag (the runningTag slot). In this way, this Scheduler agent will drive the running slot of this OEE agent directly. - If necessary, specify an activity "deadband" or an acceptable level of inactivity for the monitored machine or process, in seconds, in the Inactive Period (secs) field (INTEGER inactivityPeriod slot). Note: To disable the inactivity period alarming, specify a value of 0. If the primary measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a longer time than this period, then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the running time and the Downtime status bit is activated. Click for more details: As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the running time. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot. - If necessary, you can use the Setpoints section of the Advanced OEE options dialog (displayed by clicking the Advanced button) to define the Target value , the Low alarm and/or Low-low alarm values for the overall KPI% calculation. Note: These alarms are calculated in real time. - If necessary, you can also use the Advanced OEE options dialog to specify an optional OLE DB connection to a SQL database, to: - EITHER log shift data, manually triggered snapshots and 1 minute sample data - OR log data warehouse records to a table called ADR_OEE. In this case you can use: The Batch ID field to manually specify an optional batch ID that is recorded with these database entries (the batchID slot) OR use a tag value instead, which you specify using the Batch ID tag in the Advanced OEE options dialog ( batchIDTag slot). The Product field to specify an optional product name that will be recorded with database entries (the product slot) OR use a tag value instead, which you specify using the Product tag in the Advanced OEE options dialog ( productTag slot).

text:
For more details on configuring the Advanced OEE options dialog (display this by clicking the Advanced button of the edit dialog), see Advanced OEE agent configuration options .

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
For more details on configuring the Advanced OEE options dialog (display this by clicking the Advanced button of the edit dialog), see Advanced OEE agent configuration options . - Once OEE agent has been configured and working, you can: - Check the Auto-refresh checkbox, to view the real-time calculation of the production factors and the resultant OEE for the monitored machine or process. If you are logging this data to an OLE DB database, then you can: - Click the Reset... button to reset the current OEE data. - Click the Reset all... button to reset ALL the recorded OEE data. WARNING! Since these buttons cannot be secured, it is recommended that you ensure that your operators NOT have access to the dialog! Note: You ONLY need to perform these functions if there is “rubbish” in the shift data caused by faulty sensors etc. - The following slots provide the calculated KPI, which you may want to display or use elsewhere: Slot Name Type Function kpiPercent REAL calculated KPI as a percentage. kpiCurrShift REAL calculated KPI for the current shift as a percentage. kpiPrevShift REAL calculated KPI for the previous shift as a percentage. kpiToday REAL calculated KPI for the current day as a percentage. kpiTodayShift n REAL calculated KPI for the current day's shift n as a percentage where n = 1 to 6. kpiYesterday REAL calculated KPI for the previous day as a percentage. kpiYesterShift REAL calculated KPI for the current (same) shift on previous day as a percentage. kpiYesterShift n REAL calculated KPI for the previous day’s shift n as a percentage where n = 1 to 6. In addition to these calculated values, the following slots are also provide useful information concerning this OEE agent and the monitored process or machine: Slot Name Type Function statusStr STRING The status of the OEE agent, as follows: Not available(A=0,R=0), running (A=1,R=1), stopped (A=1,R=0) total1CurrShift REAL The totalised value of the input1 slot for the current shift. Note: This agent allows putslots to this slot to correct the integrated totals. total1Predicted REAL The predicted total of input1 for the shift total1PrevShift REAL Total value of the input1 value for previous shift totalToday REAL Total value of input1 for the day. totalTodayShift n REAL Total value of input1 for today’s shift n where n = 1 to 6 totalYesterday REAL Total value of input1 for yesterday totalYesterShift n REAL Total value of the input1 value for shift n on previous day where n = 1 to 6. If calculating a complex KPI, then you can also refer to these slots: total2CurrShift REAL The total value of the input2 slot for the current shift. Note: This agent allows putslots to this slot to correct the integrated totals. total2Predicted REAL The predicted total of input2 for the current shift. total2PrevShift REAL Total value of the input2 value for previous shift total2YesterShift REAL Total value of input2 for the same shift yesterday. Related Links: OEE Agent - Specific Status Bits : to indicate various quality and other alarm conditions, the status of the agent, OLE DB connection and the current shift. -->

Note: This Input 1 type is never reset to 0. - Rate/hr: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/min: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/sec: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - ONLY if you are calculating a complex KPI (where one measured variable is divided by another) then change the Input 2 type list from the default setting of Unused and specify the type of input signal of the secondary or dividing measurement variable, as follows: - Accumulator: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 2 type must be reset to 0 at the end of every shift using the ShiftEnd status bit as a trigger. - Total: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. Note: This Input 2 type is never reset to 0. - Rate/hr: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value.

text:
- Rate/min: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
- Rate/min: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. - Rate/sec: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. IMPORTANT: If calculating a simple KPI whose measured variable should be divided by time and NOT another variable, then ensure that the Input 2 type list is ONLY set to Unused , the default setting. - If necessary, specify the units for the primary measured variable input1 in the top Totalised units edit box (the units1 slot) and ONLY if you are calculating a complex KPI then also specify those of the secondary or dividing measurement variable input2 in the bottom Totalised units edit box (the units2 slot). - Since KPI calculations are calculated against the time that the Machine/process running checkbox (the running slot) is ON - this should ONLY be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. Note: The OEE agent ALSO expects that this slot will be OFF if the available slot is OFF. If not, runtime will continue to increment even though availability is OFF. Therefore instead of manually checking this checkbox: - Create a Scheduler agent that is configured with the applicable OFF times for the monitored machine/process - such as maintenance/lunch/tea times etc. - Click the Advanced button of this edit dialog and in the Optional tag references section, browse for BOOLEAN value slot of this Scheduler agent as the Running tag (the runningTag slot). In this way, this Scheduler agent will drive the running slot of this OEE agent directly. - If necessary, specify an activity "deadband" or an acceptable level of inactivity for the monitored machine or process, in seconds, in the Inactive Period (secs) field (INTEGER inactivityPeriod slot). Note: To disable the inactivity period alarming, specify a value of 0. If the primary measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a longer time than this period, then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the running time and the Downtime status bit is activated. Click for more details: As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the running time. Therefore the actual production time is determined by a combination of the running slot and an active input1 slot. - If necessary, you can use the Setpoints section of the Advanced OEE options dialog (displayed by clicking the Advanced button) to define the Target value , the Low alarm and/or Low-low alarm values for the overall KPI% calculation. Note: These alarms are calculated in real time. - If necessary, you can also use the Advanced OEE options dialog to specify an optional OLE DB connection to a SQL database, to: - EITHER log shift data, manually triggered snapshots and 1 minute sample data - OR log data warehouse records to a table called ADR_OEE. In this case you can use: The Batch ID field to manually specify an optional batch ID that is recorded with these database entries (the batchID slot) OR use a tag value instead, which you specify using the Batch ID tag in the Advanced OEE options dialog ( batchIDTag slot). The Product field to specify an optional product name that will be recorded with database entries (the product slot) OR use a tag value instead, which you specify using the Product tag in the Advanced OEE options dialog ( productTag slot).

If you are logging this data to an OLE DB database, then you can: - Click the Reset... button to reset the current OEE data. - Click the Reset all... button to reset ALL the recorded OEE data. WARNING! Since these buttons cannot be secured, it is recommended that you ensure that your operators NOT have access to the dialog! Note: You ONLY need to perform these functions if there is “rubbish” in the shift data caused by faulty sensors etc. - The following slots provide the calculated OEE and its three component operational factors (Quality, Performance and Availability), which you may want to display or use elsewhere: Slot Name Type Function availabilityPercent REAL The availability component of the OEE value as a percentage.

text:
- Log onto the computer on which the SmartUI Server is installed with a user that has administrative rights.

Title: Creating user accounts on the SmartUI Server computer
Steps:
- Log onto the computer on which the SmartUI Server is installed with a user that has administrative rights. - Right-click the Start button and select the Computer Management item. - Navigate to the Users folder, in the left pane of the Computer Management dialog. In the right pane, right-click below the configured users and select New User… Figure 1 : How to add a new user account - Provide the required usernames and passwords for each of the Operator and Administrator users. Note : Since all users created in this manner are assigned to the Users group on the computer, by default, the Operator user has been appropriately configured. - However, the Administrator user must removed from the Users group and assigned to the Administrators group, as follows: - Right click the Administrator user and select the Properties item, as follows: Figure 2 : Displaying the Properties dialog for this user - Select the Member of tab in the Administrator Properties dialog, select the Users group and press the Remove button, as follows: Figure 3 : Removing the Users group assigned to this user by default - Then press the Add… button and then the Advanced… button in the Select Groups dialog, as follows: Figure 4 : Opening the advanced pane of this dialog - Then press the Find Now… button to locate all the local groups on this computer and OK all the open dialogs, since the Administrators group is selected by default: Figure 5 : Selecting the required group for this user Having created the necessary user accounts on the SmartUI Server computer, it is now necessary to add them to the list of allowed users for this SmartUI Server, so that they are able to log into the Server and therefore use the SmartUI Designer or SmartUI Operator. text:
The Administrator user is usually assigned global access to the SmartUI Server as this user will administer the SmartUI Server and its security and thereby manage the other users that will access this Server.

Title: Adding users to the allowed users of this SmartUI Server
The Administrator user is usually assigned global access to the SmartUI Server as this user will administer the SmartUI Server and its security and thereby manage the other users that will access this Server. Assign global access privileges to the Administrator user as follows: - Launch the SmartUI Config utility and display the Server Settings page of this SmartUI Server. Figure 6 : Displaying the security settings for the SmartUI Server - Simply double-click the ‘administrator’ user in the Available Users list of the Choose Users section in the middle of this page, which will add it to the Selected Users list, as follows: Figure 7 : Assigning global access privileges to the Administrator user It is not recommended to provide the Operator user with global access since this user should typically only be allowed access to certain projects and datasources etc. (not all). Although it is recommended to ensure that the group to which the Operator belongs is able to initially perform all services provided by this SmartUI Server. As this saves configuration time, since instead of adding this user to all the services it needs to be part of, it is ONLY necessary to remove this user from those that the user should not be part of. This is configured via the following setting on this Security Settings page. Figure 8 : Time-saving setting for the Operator user group However, in this case, nothing needs to be done since the Users group is automatically added by default. - The Administrator user must now add the Operator user to the Allowed users of this SmartUI Server from within the SmartUI Designer, as follows: - Launch the SmartUI Designer and log into the SmartUI Server using the user name and password of the Administrator user. - In the Enterprise Manager window of the SmartUI Designer, expand the All Users item, as follows: Figure 9 : Locating the Operator user in the Enterprise Manager window - Then drag the ‘operator’ user onto the Allowed Users item to add it to the users that are allowed to log into this SmartUI Server via a SmartUI Designer or SmartUI Operator, as follows: Figure 10 : Operator user is added to the Allowed users for this SmartUI Server Therefore, the Administrator user is able to log onto and access EVERY datasource and policy provided by this SmartUI Server, by default. Likewise, the Operator user is also able to log onto the SmartUI Server, but can ONLY access the datasources that this user has been explicitly granted access to. Back to top

Install the SmartUI Web Service , either on the Server computer itself or on any other machine that is able to communicate to the Server computer.

Title: How to set up How to Connect to the SmartUI Server over the Web
Steps:
Install the SmartUI Web Service , either on the Server computer itself or on any other machine that is able to communicate to the Server computer. Provided this machine has BOTH the .NET framework (necessary for SmartUI to install) and Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) installed. For the purposes of this scenario, this will be installed on a computer called “pserver”, which is running the firewall for the company. This is recommended so as to provide secure connectivity to the SmartUI Server. - Insert the SmartUI installation media and wait for the autorun Setup menu to appear. - Click the Install option. - Accept the license agreement and click Next and Next again. - Select the Custom installation option and click Next . - Then ONLY select the Web Service component from the list of available components and click Next . Note : You are unable to continue if you do not have IIS installed on this computer, then an error message is displayed and a valid installation option is selected instead. The SmartUI Web Service ALSO requires the ASP.NET sub-component of Internet Information Services (IIS), which is NOT installed by default, when adding the IIS feature to Windows, please ensure that this component is installed, as follows: If you have Windows 7 / Windows Server 2008 R2 installed: - Launch Control Panel -> All Control Panel Items -> Programs and Features -> click the "Turn Windows features on or off" link on the left hand side: - In the displayed "Windows Features" dialog, scroll down to: - Internet Information Services -> World Wide Web Services -> Application Development Features -> ASP.NET (ensure that this check box is checked) - Click the OK button. If you have Windows 8/8.1 / Windows Server 2012/R2 installed: - Launch Control Panel -> All Control Panel Items -> Programs and Features -> click the "Turn Windows features on or off" link on the left hand side: - In the displayed "Windows Features" dialog, scroll down to: - Internet Information Services -> World Wide Web Services -> Application Development Features -> ASP.NET 4.5 (ensure that this check box is checked) - Click the OK button. If you have Windows 10 installed: - Launch Control Panel -> All Control Panel Items -> Programs and Features -> click the "Turn Windows features on or off" link on the left hand side: - In the displayed "Windows Features" dialog, scroll down to: - Internet Information Services -> World Wide Web Services -> Application Development Features -> ASP.NET 4.6 (ensure that this check box is checked) - Click the OK button. - Click the Install button and if necessary, specify the Name of the required Virtual Directory and the Web Site in which this Virtual Directory will be created. For this scenario these have been left as their defaults i.e. SmartUI and Default Web Site respectively. - Click Next to install the necessary files. - Once installed, it is recommended to ensure that both the web service itself and the virtual directory that is created during this installation is fully operational, as follows: - Launch your web browsing application. - Type in the required path of your newly created virtual folder, as follows: http://WebSiteName/VirtualDirectoryName, since the ‘Default Web Site’ is selected, this will simply be: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectoryName i.e. http://pserver/ VIP . - If everything has been successfully installed and configured, this should immediately display the default web page, which explains how you can use the Web Service. - By default the SmartUI Web Service assumes that the Server is on the local computer. Since, the Server is on a remote computer, in this scenario, the following additional configuration after successfully installing the SmartUI Web Service: - Launch the Windows Explorer (Windows Key + E).
