text:
Practical DBLog agent recommendations: - As stated above this agent is NOT suited to logging data at a high resolution (logging rates below a minute) and this also places an unnecessary strain on the database and requires increased database management.

Title: Using the DBLog agent for the bulk logging of values to databases
Practical DBLog agent recommendations: - As stated above this agent is NOT suited to logging data at a high resolution (logging rates below a minute) and this also places an unnecessary strain on the database and requires increased database management. So aim for a minimum logging interval of 5 minutes . Factors affecting your achievable logging interval are: - Each agent added to a DBLog agent generates its own SQL transaction, so the maximum number of agents per DBLog agent depends upon their required logging interval (rate). In other words, the number of agents that you need to log determines their possible or achievable logging rate, in that the greater the number of agents you choose to log, the lower their achievable logging rate. - Your hardware configuration also affects your achievable logging interval, as you are typically able to log data at a higher resolution to a SQL Server that is located on a separate computer than your SCADA Server, so that these database transactions do not affect your SCADA Server. - Due to the different logging requirements of numeric (e.g. Analog) and Digital tags, it is recommended to separate the numeric from the Digital tags, so that one DBLog agent only contains numeric tags and another only contains Digital tags. - For ease of management do NOT add more than 1000 agents to a single DBLog agent , instead create additional DBLog agents to share the load of the agents being logged. - While DBLog agents typically log Numerical and Digital values or bits, they can be configured to convert ALL values to Strings, by checking the String logging checkbox - but this is NOT recommended for general use , since it requires MORE SPACE to store String values compared to Numerical values and this can also cause formatting problems. This should typically ONLY be set when you need to log string values in bulk, such as when providing the source data for the SCADA Intelligence tool to analyse your data in detail. Recommendations for selecting the correct Logging Method: The DBLog agent provides a number of bulk logging methods, so it is important that you select the correct one and configure its related settings correctly to ensure that the relevant data is being logged.

text:
- For ANY data that is being retrieved from a telemetry system use the Log on change method, since it is possible to miss this data when using the Log all on interval method.

Title: Using the DBLog agent for the bulk logging of values to databases
- For ANY data that is being retrieved from a telemetry system use the Log on change method, since it is possible to miss this data when using the Log all on interval method. - For NUMERICAL data that is being regularly logged: - either use the Log all on interval method, if all the specified tags that have been added to the DBLog agent are being logged at a similar rate so that the specified Logging interval ensures that all the changes in values of these tags are logged. - or use the Log on change method, in which ONLY the tags that change are logged, typically when their value or quality status changes. For this logging method specify the required VALUE deadband for each tag to ensure that only meaningful changes in value are logged via the Deadband column of either the CSV file or the Tag list . In other words, specify the MINIMUM Value which the value being logged must EXCEED for it to be logged. Since, if the change in value is LESS than this value then this value is NOT logged. Note: To prevent this logging method from logging the tags when their quality status changes, add the following registry value and set it to 1: DisableOnQualityChangeLogging . The Log all on change logging method logs all the listed tags if ANY of their tag values change, if you decide to use this method then also specify the VALUE Deadband for each tag to ensure that only meaningful changes in value are logged. - For DIGITAL data that is being regularly logged: Use the Log on change method, in which ONLY the tags that change are logged, typically when their value or quality status changes. IMPORTANT: When using this logging method for DIGITAL values, ensure that the value Deadband is 0 , otherwise NO values will be logged. Note: To prevent this logging method from logging the tags when their quality status changes, add the following registry value and set it to 1: DisableOnQualityChangeLogging . However, if you are trending these DIGITAL tags in a chart, then you ALSO need to create another DBLog agent for these same Digital agents that uses the Log all on interval method, whose Logging interval is set to the charting period to ensure that the current state of all these DIGITAL tags will be displayed.

text:
More details: When charting DIGITAL tags, the chart ONLY displays the value of each tag for the time specified by the specific charting period.

Title: Using the DBLog agent for the bulk logging of values to databases
More details: When charting DIGITAL tags, the chart ONLY displays the value of each tag for the time specified by the specific charting period. But if you ONLY use the Log on change logging method, then if a DIGITAL tag does not change in value during this charting period then no data is returned, even though it has an existing valid state. This is why you need the other DBLog agent for the same Digital agents that uses the Log all on interval method, whose logging interval is set to the charting period, which ensures that the last known state of each DIGITAL tag will be displayed by the chart. The following triggering methods are seldom used as they generally are used for batch processing: - Log all on trigger value -> zero : all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag goes to zero. - Log all on trigger value -> non-zero : all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag leaves zero. - Log all on trigger any value change :all the listed tags are logged when the value of the specified Trigger tag changes value. Other important DBLog agent settings The following top checkboxes of the DBLog agent configuration dialog affect the general operation of this agent, as follows: - The Enable checkbox allows you to start/stop this agent from logging the listed tags. IMPORTANT: If this Enable checkbox is not checked then this agent will NOT log tags. - The Disable on standby checkbox allows you to disable this agent, when its Agent Server is part of a cluster and is in standby node - to prevent the logging of DUPLICATE tags. - The String logging checkbox, when enabled logs the tag values as Strings and not numeric values; this also allows you to log other string slots (this will log the first 79 characters). Note: This is unchecked by default as it is NOT recommended for general use, since it requires MORE SPACE to store String values compared to Numerical values and this can also cause formatting problems. This should typically ONLY be set when you need to log string values in bulk, such as when providing the source data for the SCADA Intelligence tool to analyse your data in detail. In this case it is recommended that you ONLY add string values to this DBLog agent.

text:
In order to help you ensure that you ONLY store the most useful data in the database, by default the DBLog agent implements Housekeeping , so that any records older than 90 days are deleted, by default.

Title: Using the DBLog agent for the bulk logging of values to databases
In order to help you ensure that you ONLY store the most useful data in the database, by default the DBLog agent implements Housekeeping , so that any records older than 90 days are deleted, by default. Housekeeping is simply a cleanup action triggered on the table, specified by the SQL table name field of the database identified by the SQL connection string field. Modify this setting, by increasing or decreasing the maximum period that records should remain in the table, depending upon the storage capacity you have available for your database and how useful this data becomes to you the older it gets. Note1: A value of 0 disables this housekeeping functionality, provided NO OTHER DBLog agents log to the specified table that have configured housekeeping! Note2: By design, one additional day's worth of data is kept for you. By default housekeeping takes place at the turn of midnight, however you can change this by adding the HousekeepingHour registry setting to specify the hour of the day that you want this housekeeping performed. As mentioned previously Housekeeping is a cleanup action triggered on the specified table that a DBLog agent logs its tags to. Furthermore, multiple DBLog agents can log to the same table. Therefore when multiple DBLog agents log to the same table that have DIFFERENT Housekeeping periods configured, the SHORTEST period will always be used! By way of explanation, consider the following Housekeeping configuration examples: - DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected. - DBLog2 writes data to Table2 and housekeeping is configured: So the specified housekeeping WILL run on Table2, as expected. - DBLog3 and DBLog4 writes data to the same table Table34 - - DBLog3 is configured with no housekeeping AND - DBLog4 is configured with 30 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping WILL run on Table34 as per DBLog4’s housekeeping configuration for this SHARED table. - DBLog5 and DBLog6 writes data to the same table Table56 - - DBLog5 is configured with 30 days housekeeping AND - DBLog6 is configured with 90 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping will run on Table34 as per DBLog5’s housekeeping configuration and the data older than 30 days will be deleted, since the SHORTEST housekeeping period is always used as this is the period that is reached first for this SHARED table.

text:
Furthermore, when performing housekeeping you can also specify an OPTIONAL Backup folder , which is used to backup the old data before it is deleted from the table.

Title: Using the DBLog agent for the bulk logging of values to databases
Furthermore, when performing housekeeping you can also specify an OPTIONAL Backup folder , which is used to backup the old data before it is deleted from the table. If you implement this Backup folder , we recommend that this is located on a backup or external drive that will not affect your drive on which your database is installed. IMPORTANT1: This folder needs to exist on the computer where the database is installed (this is NOT the Agent Server computer when using a remote database); otherwise HOUSEKEEPING WILL NOT HAPPEN! IMPORTANT2: ALSO ensure that the specified folder name does NOT contain SPACES or housekeeping will ALSO NOT HAPPEN! IMPORTANT3: ALSO ensure that the database has the necessary permissions needed to add these files to this specified folder or housekeeping will ALSO NOT HAPPEN! This Backup folder therefore specifies a path that is relative to the computer on which the database is installed (this is NOT the Agent Server computer when using a remote database). Note: Leaving the Backup folder field empty disables this backup functionality, which is the default setting. When this backup folder is being used each DBLog agent creates a daily flat cabinet (.CAB) file of the data that is to be deleted (by the SHORTEST Housekeeping setting if multiple DBLog agents log to the same table). These files are self-extracting SQL scripts, which you need to manually execute against the required SQL database, in order to import your data. PLEASE NOTE: It is up to you to manage the files stored in this folder yourself. Once the DBLog Agent has been configured and enabled, it creates the table specified by the SQL table name field, which has the following predefined structure : - id : a unique indexing identifier - dt : the Timestamp of the logged value - Tagname : the name of the tag being logged - Value :– the value of the tag being logged - Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad. In addition to this table the DBLog agent also creates the Adr_DBLog_AgentDetails table, which is updated when: the agent is started; or when its tag list is changed; and unconditionally every morning at 01h00. This table contains all the agents referenced by all DBLog agents to provide more details about these referenced agents, which can be used to provide more context about them for reports.

How to improve performance when trending of large amounts of data with a LineChart Top How to improve performance when trending of large amounts of data with a LineChart By default when trending series that have a large number of points in the Line chart, you may find that the data takes a long time to be charted as a lot of pressure is put on the CPU to draw it.

Title: How to improve performance when trending of large amounts of data with a LineChart
Steps:
How to improve performance when trending of large amounts of data with a LineChart Top How to improve performance when trending of large amounts of data with a LineChart By default when trending series that have a large number of points in the Line chart, you may find that the data takes a long time to be charted as a lot of pressure is put on the CPU to draw it. Therefore you can employ the following strategies to minimise, if not prevent, any lag in the trending of a series and thereby reduce the required CPU load: Change a Line series to a FastLine series: a FastLine series is an optimised (extremely simplified) Line series, which is to draws its points as fast as possible, you can do this as follows: - Open the graphic form that contains the required LineChart control. - Right click this control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. - Ensure that the default Series Setup dialog of the Configuration: LineChart configuration dialog is displayed. - Click the Type dropdown list box of the Line series you wish to change and select the FastLine series type from the list of available series types. Reduce the number of data points that the FastLine series needs to plot: instead of drawing all the points within a series, you can use reduce the number of points when large numbers of points occur at the same location or date time. In this case ONLY the FastLine series provides methods to reduce the number of plotted points. We recommend that you use the First method, which only plots the first point at each location or date time, which you can configure as follows: - Open the graphic form that contains the required LineChart control. - Right click this control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. - Ensure that the default Series Setup dialog of the Configuration: LineChart configuration dialog is displayed. - Select the required FastLine series that you want to configure, this is indicated in the series list by displaying a filled right arrow in the first column. - In the default Line Style tab, uncheck Draw All checkbox in the Draw All Points section and ensure that the list box specifies First , the default option. Note: The other option provided by this list box is the MinMax option, which plots both the minimum and the maximum point at each date time (X value). Tip: ONLY the FastLine series allows for this configuration, you will NOT find this option when a Line series is selected. Direct2D mode and Anti-aliasing (as a last resort): configure chart-specific settings that speed up the drawing process. Note: These settings are only available from MAPS 3.4.1 or Adroit 8.4.1 onwards. By default the Line chart control renders the charts using the GDI+ API. To speed up the drawing process there is an option to draw the charts using the much faster Direct2D API, by setting the Boolean Direct2DMode property of the Line Chart to True. You can also turn off anti-aliasing to speed up the drawing of the chart but the chart will not appear as smooth, by setting the Boolean AntiAliased property of the Line Chart to False. -->

Title: To Log a process value:
Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator, as follows: - Ensure that the Basic , Advanced and/or System checkbox is checked to display the required agent type in this list. These checkboxes use these default agent groups to help you select the required agent quickly. Tip: If no checkboxes are selected, then all the available agent types will be displayed in the Type list box. This is useful if the required agent type has not been categorised. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list - Locate the required agent type, using the scroll bar and click on it. - In the Agents list, click on the name of the required agent (if necessary scroll down to locate this). Tip: Right-click to display a menu of commands to perform upon the selected agent(s). - Click the Log... button to display the Edit DataLog Agent for dialog. Tip: You can also right-click the agent and select the Log… menu item. - Select the value of this agent that you want to log from the Slot list box. Click for more details: This must be a REAL , INTEGER, BOOLEAN or a 7 character STRING (the 8th character will be forced to 0). For example, the value slot of an Analog agent. - Select the required data-logging Mode, as follows: - Continuous: Adroit logs data values when the value changes, provided the value does not change more frequently than the configured Time deadband ( see below). - Demand: Adroit only logs a data value when the LogNow or Trigger slots of this Datalog agent are activated. This can be used if you want to avoid logging every change during a batch process, and only want to log the values at the end of the batch. The Trigger tag may be browsed in here and a Log Now button is provided for manually triggering the logging.

If necessary, use the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by adding the SupportCompressionOnDemand registry value.

Title: To Log a process value:
If necessary, use the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by adding the SupportCompressionOnDemand registry value. - Both: This uses both the Continuous and Demand data logging modes. - The DataLog agent can accommodate multiple log sets for a given agent and slot, which allow you to log a given tag (agent.slot) using different sample and/or logging destination settings etc. Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. Add a Set number if more than one log set is required, and configure the following per set: - The Datasource field, allows you to select a proprietary data file - enter or browse in the name of the file you wish to log to, using the … browse button. This defaults to the same name as the current agent file loaded, and has a .LGD extension. If a new filename is specified, it will only be created when the DataLog agent has its Start radio button activated. Note: If the specified file path does NOT exist, Adroit will attempt to create it - if this path cannot be created (because the drive does not exist or file security disallows this etc) then this value will NOT be logged. Typically the legacy SQL… button ONLY appears when the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration to allow it to be configured. But even in this case you are encouraged to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. - Select Disable logging on standby , when a clustered Agent Servers log to the same OLE DB compatible database to prevent the duplication of database entries by only logging entries from the master server. The default state is unchecked. Note: This setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which do not require this setting as each Agent Server logs to their own datalog files. - Click the Length button and enter the Log Length in the time units of your choice for this set.

The default setting is 10 days BUT this should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes.

Title: To Log a process value:
The default setting is 10 days BUT this should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. Click for more details: In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. Note1: A rule of thumb is that the Log Length should not exceed 500000 x Shortest Logging Interval (this factor is true only when using the same time units). Note2: If Adroit proprietary logging is selected and the logging period is increased ensure that the WGP file is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . - Specify the required logging Deadbands (methods to reduce the number of records logged for this value) as follows: - Time deadband: click the Time... button and specify the Shortest Logging Interval (how often this value must be logged). The default setting is 10 seconds. This setting can reduce the amount of logging required for this value, as follows: if this value changes more than once during this period then the specified Compression Method is used to determine what value is actually recorded. - Value deadband: specify the MINIMUM Value which the value being logged must EXCEED for it to be logged. This reduces the amount of logging for this value, as follows: if the change in value is LESS than this value then the value will NOT be logged. Note: When logging DIGITAL values, ensure that this Value deadband is 0 , otherwise NO values will be logged. Tip: The Time deadband setting actually specifies the required logging rate of this value. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data.

Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend.

Title: To Log a process value:
Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend. - If necessary, configure the Out of limit logging to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range). For details, see Out of limit data logging . - Choose the required Compression Method for the value to be logged. For details, see Available Logging Compression Methods . Tip: To facilitate data compression it is RECOMMENDED to use a non-zero Deadband Value. The units are the same as for the slot being logged. - If necessary, the Options section provides the following options that apply to ALL Datalog agents: - Select Clear at Start to clear any records from memory or disk each time logging commences. - Select Interpolate if you are logging continuously changing values. Leave unselected if the values are discrete and change in a stepwise fashion. - Select Double entries to log both the old and new value of a step change at the same time. This is necessary if you want to export the data to an Excel spreadsheet and avoid interpolation when plotting the data. - Use the Backup period list etc., when the Datasource is a proprietary data (.LGD) file, to configure when and how this logged data should be backed up using .LGB files, when the LGD file wraps. This backed up historical data can then be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . IMPORTANT: .LGB files are used when backing up datalogs as these can have their stored historical data seamlessly retrieved for trending and reporting. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . Note: To disable datalog backups for a particular Datalog, set the backupPeriod slot of this Datalog agent to 0 . - If necessary, click the Advanced button to configure the Flush lazily setting and other GLOBAL DATA LOGGING SETTINGS. For more details on when and how to configure each of these settings, see Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) . If necessary, use the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging, by adding the SupportCompressionOnDemand registry value.

Title: To Log a process value:

The default setting is 10 days BUT this should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes.

Title: To Log a process value:
The default setting is 10 days BUT this should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. Click for more details: In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. The default setting is 10 seconds. This setting can reduce the amount of logging required for this value, as follows: if this value changes more than once during this period then the specified Compression Method is used to determine what value is actually recorded. - Value deadband: specify the MINIMUM Value which the value being logged must EXCEED for it to be logged. This reduces the amount of logging for this value, as follows: if the change in value is LESS than this value then the value will NOT be logged. Note: When logging DIGITAL values, ensure that this Value deadband is 0 , otherwise NO values will be logged. Tip: The Time deadband setting actually specifies the required logging rate of this value. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records. This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data.

Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend.

When troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device.

Title: Introduction
When troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device. Adroit provides a utility known as the Driver Monitor that is used for just this purpose and one of its functions allows it to display the Datascope window, which allows you to view and log the exact communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. This procedure describes how to create an HTML log file of the communication messages and errors as they occur between Adroit and the specified front-end device. So that if you are not a driver expert, you can email this log file to Adroit support, who will then be able to assist you with your driver problem. The advantage of an HTML log file over a text file is that this file format preserves the color of the Datascope window, which makes the troubleshooting process easier.

metadata.title: How to log the communication of a driver

text:
- Have Adroit 8.4 or later installed.

Title: Prerequisites
Steps:
- Have Adroit 8.4 or later installed. Note: If you are using a version earlier than this, then the method used to launch the Driver Monitor will differ. - Ensure that you have installed the required driver and created and named the necessary devices for them, each of which handle the communications to each of your front end device/s. - Ensure that the Agent Server is running. - Ensure that any previous log file for this device is deleted. This log file is located in C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit folder and have the same name as the device you created for this driver, with a .HTM extension. Otherwise this log file will be appended to, which will cause confusion.

metadata.title: How to log the communication of a driver

text:
The following steps summarise what we will be doing: - Launch the Driver Monitor - Monitor the required device of an installed driver Tip: You can also do this via the Adroit Config Editor , as follows: Launch the Adroit Config Editor utility: click Agent Server Configuration and then Driver Configuration in the right hand pane, then right click the required configured Device ( ) of the installed Protocol Driver ( ) in the Installed Drivers and Devices list and select its Diagnostics option.

Title: Configuration

The status you can determine from the icon of the device as displayed in the Device name list, as follows: Tip: One of the Options... of the Driver Monitor allow you to configure how fast these statuses are updated. In this case the BATCHOPC device is idle, so the following information is displayed by the Datascope screen: Since the ASCII checkbox of the Driver Monitor dialog is checked by default, your datascope will be displayed in ASCII mode by default, which is the recommended way to view the datascope, even for known Binary (hex) type protocols, because most drivers also provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format - you can press the A key to toggle between these viewing modes. Title: Specifications
How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time Top How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time One application of the Counter agents is to monitor device running/stopped bit to display motor running hours. Due to control system starts, stops, backups and communication breaks, it is often necessary to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) as an operator entry function. text:
This document aims to describe how SmartUI users can configure each SmartUI Server and Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Introduction
This document aims to describe how SmartUI users can configure each SmartUI Server and Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. to ensure the best user experience. This document aims to describe the three COMMUNICATION mechanisms and two CONNECTION mechanisms that SmartUI provides, each intended to optimise the use of a specific network infrastructure:

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- Graphic form size: 50-100 kb.

Title: Requirements
- Graphic form size: 50-100 kb. - Computer: Pentium IV with 512MB RAM. - Bandwidth: 512KB/sec [slower GPRS/3G links may still provide acceptable response times] - Install the latest available version of SmartUI - Start your SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer and log in to the SmartUI Server.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- A LAN based communication mechanism where the SERVER will PUSH data to the CLIENT.

Title: Subscribe
- A LAN based communication mechanism where the SERVER will PUSH data to the CLIENT. - This mechanism is the fastest and the CLIENT will receive changes as they happen on the SERVER. - This mechanism does not optimise bandwidth usage, but is the fastest.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet.

Title: Subscribe-Poll
- A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet. - This mechanism does NOT PUSH any data to the CLIENT, but relies on the CLIENT to POLL for the data. - ALL the changes since the last POLL cycle will be retrieved from the SERVER. - This mechanism attempts to reduce latency by minimising round-trips to the SERVER.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet.

Title: Poll
- A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet. - This mechanism does NOT PUSH any data to the CLIENT, but relies on the CLIENT to POLL for the data. - Only the LAST change will be retrieved from the SERVER for each interested data point e.g. if there has been 5 changes to a set point, only the last change will be fetched (the most recent change). - This mechanism attempts to reduce latency by minimising round-trips to the SERVER. It will also try to optimise bandwidth usage by retrieving as little data as possible. TIP : On slower networks, opt to use the SUBSCRIBE-POLL mechanism first and then the POLL mechanism.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
The following settings can be applied to the communication mechanisms on the SmartUI Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): - ClientPollTime : The time (in seconds) which will be used to POLL the SERVER for any changes.

Title: Configuration
The following settings can be applied to the communication mechanisms on the SmartUI Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): - ClientPollTime : The time (in seconds) which will be used to POLL the SERVER for any changes. - ClientPingInterval : An “IsAlive” period in which the CLIENT will determine whether the SERVER is still available.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
SmartUI offers the following TWO connection mechanisms that can be used with some or all of the communication mechanisms, as follows:.

Title: Connection mechanisms:
SmartUI offers the following TWO connection mechanisms that can be used with some or all of the communication mechanisms, as follows:

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- A direct, binary connection to the SERVER using a proprietary protocol.

Title: MAINDATAPROVIDER
Steps:
- A direct, binary connection to the SERVER using a proprietary protocol. - The channel can be encrypted using some of the configuration options discussed below. - The communication to the SERVER is normally on port 9000. - All three communication mechanisms may be used.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
- An indirect, Web Service (XML) connection to the SERVER via IIS.

Title: WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER
- An indirect, Web Service (XML) connection to the SERVER via IIS. - Packets are compressed before they are made available to the CLIENT. - The communication to the SERVER is normally via IIS on port 80 and then from IIS to the SERVER on port 9000. - Only the SUBSCRIBE-POLL and POLL mechanisms may be used.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
The following settings can be applied to the connection mechanisms on BOTH the SmartUI Server and Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): - NetworkBindAddress : This setting determines which subnet the SERVER and CLIENTS communicate on and is required for computers with multiple network cards or IP ranges .

Title: Configuration
The following settings can be applied to the connection mechanisms on BOTH the SmartUI Server and Client applications (Designer and/or Operator): - NetworkBindAddress : This setting determines which subnet the SERVER and CLIENTS communicate on and is required for computers with multiple network cards or IP ranges . Note : ALL CLIENTS and SERVERS that need to communicate must have this setting specified in order to communicate with each other. Example : SERVER has TWO IP’s: 10.10.10.9 and 196.248.23.1; Client has TWO IP’s: 10.10.10.101 and 192.168.1.2; If both need to communicate set the SERVER NetworkBindAddress to: 10.10.10.9 and the CLIENT’s NetworkBindAddress to: 10.10.10.101; The following settings can ONLY be applied to the connection mechanisms on the SmartUI Server: - BroadcastEnabled : This setting causes the SERVER application to broadcast it’s availability to the subnet and is ONLY required for clustered systems, so DISABLE this setting if not in a clustered SmartUI environment.. This setting only applies to the local subnet and does NOT apply to Internet/WAN connected CLIENTS. Note : This setting INCREASES general network traffic. - ServerPort : This setting specifies the port that the SERVER listens for incoming connections. Note : If this port is changed, make sure it is changed on the CLIENT as well.

metadata.title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks

text:
Caching can optimise the transfer of data between the CLIENT and the SERVER.

Title: Caching:
Steps:
Caching can optimise the transfer of data between the CLIENT and the SERVER. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. There are TWO main caching techniques, both of which are configured on the CLIENT: - Using the DataElementCachingEnabled setting : This method determines whether the SERVER contains a more recent version of an object than the CLIENT: - If it does, the CLIENT cache will be updated. - If it does not, the CLIENT will simply use the object from it’s local cache. In other words, a cached graphic form will ONLY be loaded by the Client if it remains unchanged when it is opened again. In other words, no further design changes have been made to this graphic form that is stored on the Server. Note : This method requires a roundtrip to the SERVER. - Using the DataElementCachingRetrieveRegardless setting : This method retrieves the cached object (if it exists) regardless of whether a more recent version exists on the SERVER. Note : This method is faster as it does NOT require a roundtrip to the SERVER. This greatly improves the user experience but requires the additional administrative overhead of ensuring that the local cache is updated to include any changes made to the graphic forms of the project/s that it displays AND then copy this updated local cache to all the Operators that use this project/s.

Wizards: Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time.

Title: Design-time reuse
Wizards: Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time. In other words, a wizard is a reusable design-time object, much like a Windows control. Also wizards have the facility to update their instances that have been added to graphic forms to their current configuration, when they are modified after having been used. For details, see How to create and use wizards . Use the Favorites tool window, which: - allows you to create your own custom set (library) of your favorite graphic forms and wizards, which you frequently use. - helps to speed up the process of designing your graphic forms, since you can directly drag these from this tool window onto your graphic forms without having to find them in their relevant projects. Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . Manually create and manage a library of graphical components : Another method of design-time reuse is creating a library of graphical components that can be copied and pasted to the required graphic forms and then connecting the necessary values to the properties of these components. In this case, you can export the required graphical components to XML files and then simply drag the file into a graphic form that is being designed in the SmartUI Designer. For details, see How to export a graphical component to a XML file . Although this reduces the amount of repetition required, it does not eliminate the task of reconnecting the data every time to every new component. Furthermore, should the specification of a component change (say its look and colors) then the user would need to go and manually update every instance of this component. Mapping spiders : Facilitates the simple connection of data to the required properties of this reusable graphical component. In other words, this eliminates the process of manually locating the properties of the reusable graphical component, in order to provide their values with live data. While using Mapping spiders makes it easier to map data to the properties of controls, it does not solve the problem of having to update every instance of a graphical component should a global change be required.

This document also explores other techniques that you can use to implement a highly reusable component system.

Title: Run-time reuse
This document also explores other techniques that you can use to implement a highly reusable component system. Template GOs : By using a TemplateGO control, a graphic form can behave as a reusable graphical component. The advantage of this is that any changes made to it can immediately become available in all the places where this graphic form is used. SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time. The fundamental difference between a graphic form and a SmartUI Template is that a SmartUI Template has aliases, some of which are automatically created, which allow data elements within Behaviours and/or spiders to be dynamically driven. Typically SmartUI Templates are used for graphic forms that are displayed as pop-ups or within TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form. controls. For more details about using aliases, see Working with aliases . IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. When launching child SmartUI Templates from a parent SmartUI Template, you can automatically use the alias values of the parent SmartUI Template, instead of manually assigning values to the aliases of each child. For details, see Passing alias values from parent to child . Aliases allow you to expose specific properties of each graphic form (and/or their form components) that you add so that you can configure these properties and hence customise each SmartUI Template like any other form component that you add to a graphic form. Automatic alias creation Aliases can be automatically created for you, by using {} notation, in the following instances: - in the Properties tool window: for any String or Text properties, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring Behaviours: for any data element field, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring a charting control, for the applicable Series values specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring an Adroit Alarm Viewer control, specify the required name enclosed in { } braces for the Alarm List / Alarm Agent value. Use {} notation to specify aliases, as follows: - if you require the alias to specify the ENTIRE value/data element to be substituted then specify the single {requiredAliasName} - this is most typical. - if you require multiple parts of the value/data element name to be separately replaced then specify multiple aliases, such as {DataSource}.{Structure}.{DataName}.{Value}. For example: {tag} or by concatenating a number of hierarchical levels for this data element , for instance: {AS}.{tag} Example: Manual alias creation If you need to expose any other property of the graphic form or its configured form components, then you need to manually add the required alias to a graphic form and then manually assign them to the required properties of this graphic form and/or its added form components via the Spider Configuration tool window. For details on how to configure aliases in this manner, see Working with aliases . Using SmartUI Templates as run-time reusable graphic objects .

The following three options are provided when dragging or copying a graphic form or SmartUI Template onto a graphic form: IMPORTANT: When copying SmartUI Templates ONLY use the Graphic Form by Reference option as this is the ONLY option that creates TemplateGO controls so that you can configure its aliases.

Title: Run-time reuse
The following three options are provided when dragging or copying a graphic form or SmartUI Template onto a graphic form: IMPORTANT: When copying SmartUI Templates ONLY use the Graphic Form by Reference option as this is the ONLY option that creates TemplateGO controls so that you can configure its aliases. - Paste Graphic Form Contents: In this case, ONLY the contents of this graphic form or SmartUI Template are added to this graphic form. - Graphic Form by Reference: In this case, each copy of the added graphic form refers to the original graphic form and TemplateGO controls are created for each. Use this method, if you want ALL the copies of this graphic form to look the same and be centrally configuration. In other words, when you modify the original (copied) graphic form ALL of its copies on other graphic forms are immediately updated. However, this means that any change made to a copy will be OVERWRITTEN when the original graphic form is modified. Configuring the Graphic Form by Reference: - In Enterprise Manager , drag the graphic form that you want to copy onto the required graphic form. Tip: These graphic forms do not need to be in the same project. - Specify the required number of copies of this graphic form, in the No. of References spin control. - If necessary, specify how you want to arrange multiple copies in the Layout Panel section, as follows: - Select the required method of arranging multiple copies from the Layout Panel Type list box, as follows: - Flow: Copies of the graphic form are added from left to right horizontally onto the host graphic form, wrapping down the graphic form as required Note: In this case, ANY further control that you add to the parent graphic form is added next to the last one. - Table: The SAME as Flow, except, each copy is added to its own cell, so you can add other controls to each of the configured cells. Note: In this case each copy has a row and column property and can be spanned over adjacent rows and/or columns. - VIZNETFlow: The SAME as Flow , except that this flow can be broken later so that you can manually move (re-position) these graphic forms, by clicking Move Controls from the Tasks list of the flow container (accessed by clicking its glyph a glyph is a specific graphic symbol, for instance employed by form components, which when clicked launch alternate configuration dialogs. , which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the flow container). - Configure the initial size of the Layout Panel , as follows: specify the required Width and Height in pixels. Note: Depending upon the configured size of the Layout Panel, you may not be able to see all the added copies. - Specify the size of each copy, in the Template GO section, as follows: - Either check the Auto Resize checkbox, so that each copy expands to fit all the controls of the copied graphic form. - OR specify the required Width and Height for each copy in pixels. - Graphic Form by Instance: In this case the copied graphic form is added to this graphic form and can be configured within it, like any other control. Use this method if you need to customise most of the copies. This method requires less administration but you need to configure EACH copy manually. Configuring the Graphic Form by Instance: - In Enterprise Manager , drag the graphic form that you want to copy onto the required graphic form. Tip: These graphic forms do not need to be in the same project.

- Specify the required number of copies of this graphic form, in the No.

Title: Run-time reuse
- Specify the required number of copies of this graphic form, in the No. of Instances spin control. - If necessary, specify how you want to arrange multiple copies in the Layout Panel section, as follows: - Select the required method of arranging multiple copies from the Layout Panel Type list box, as follows: - Flow: Copies of the graphic form are added from left to right horizontally onto the host graphic form, wrapping down the graphic form as required Note: In this case, ANY further control that you add to the parent graphic form is added next to the last one. - Table: The SAME as Flow, except, each copy is added to its own cell, so you can add other controls to each of the configured cells. Note: In this case each copy has a row and column property and can be spanned over adjacent rows and/or columns. - VIZNETFlow: The SAME as Flow , except that this flow can be broken later so that you can manually move (re-position) these graphic forms, by clicking Move Controls from the Tasks list of the flow container (accessed by clicking its glyph a glyph is a specific graphic symbol, for instance employed by form components, which when clicked launch alternate configuration dialogs. , which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the flow container). - Configure the initial size of the Layout Panel , as follows: specify the required Width and Height in pixels. Note: Depending upon the configured size of the Layout Panel, you may not be able to see all the added copies. - Select the control that surrounds each copy on the host graphic form, from the Type of Container Control list, as follows: choose either a Panel or GroupBox control, the only difference between the two is that the GroupBox control allows you to add a title and a border around the controls; otherwise these controls function the same. - If necessary, specify the default label that is applied to each copy in the Title of Container Control field. - Specify the required size of each copy, using the size of Container Control , as follows: specify the required Width and Height in pixels. However, using SmartUI Templates are not desirable if you simply want to reuse a graphic form directly without making any copies or containing that form in other forms using a TemplateGO control. Spider Template Sets , which are named collections of silks, are ideally suited for this application. When a template set is active then all the silks that belong to that template set are active and allow communications from one spider to the next. In this way it is possible to control which data is communicated to which properties. In addition, a spider engine with this template set configuration can be exported and imported, making for simpler bulk configuration. PLEASE NOTE : Spider template sets have nothing to do with TemplateGOs or SmartUI Templates and should not be confused with them! Back to top

A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements, which can simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms.

Title: How to create and use wizards
A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements, which can simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. But, instead of directly specifying the values that drive these Behaviours, these are replaced with value or static text placeholders (substitutions). Each time a wizard is inserted into a graphic form, a dialog is displayed whereby values must be specified for all the substitutions that occur within this wizard. For instance, instead of redrawing a pump or a motor, each time one is required, a wizard can be created and simply inserted wherever a pump or motor is needed, at which time you link the required data elements (values) to its pre-defined substitutions. You have two main options when creating wizards, typically in the Enterprise Manager window: - Either create the wizard from scratch: in this case, right click a project or folder and select Create Wizard . Note: When creating a wizard from scratch, the default size of the wizard is 200 by 200 pixels, since wizards are typically small by nature. If necessary customise this default, by using the Designer.CONFIG setting in the Misc group, called DefaultWizardsize . - Or convert an existing graphic form into a wizard: in this case, open the required graphic form and select the Save as Wizard graphic form toolbar button. Then use the Substitution configuration dialog to create ALL the necessary substitutions for this new wizard. Tip: When you substitute a data element that is used in numerous locations within the graphic form, all these locations use the specified substitution name. The graphic form toolbar contains the Optimise Graphic Form size button (at the end), which resizes the wizard to the size of the added controls and vectors, so that there are no overlaps at the top, bottom, left or right sides. Now design the graphical components of your wizard as you would a normal graphic form. When you get to the point of where you must specify data elements (values), e.g. when creating a behaviour, instead of browsing in a data elements you simply type in the substitution name with curly brackets around the name, e.g. {PUMP}. For details, see Working with Wizard substitutions .

text:
After saving the wizard, you simply drag the wizard from the Enterprise Manager onto the graphic form where you want to use this wizard, at which point you’ll be prompted to assign valid data elements to the substitutions you specified in your wizard.

Title: How to create and use wizards
After saving the wizard, you simply drag the wizard from the Enterprise Manager onto the graphic form where you want to use this wizard, at which point you’ll be prompted to assign valid data elements to the substitutions you specified in your wizard. IMPORTANT NOTE : Since wizards are ONLY inserted into a graphic form, by instance NOT by reference, any subsequent change to the wizard will NOT be reflected in the instances of the wizard that you have ALREADY added to a graphic form, unless you update them again. Tip: You can also drag a wizard onto the Templates tool window if you intend to use this frequently for quick access when designing other graphic forms. If you change a wizard AFTER you have inserted it into one or more graphic forms, then you can choose which of these instances you want to update to the latest version. For details, see Updating wizard instances added to graphic forms . SmartUI Templates can also be used when creating wizards that contain a pop-up that needs to “inherit” or use the tag data that is substituted when the user drops the wizard down on the form. For an example of configuring this, see How to create a Wizard that contains a Template pop up . Tip: Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates. For details, see Driving aliases with wizard substitutions . Back to top

text:
The simplest method of reusing graphical components is to simply export the required graphical components to a XML file and then simply drag this file into the required graphic form that is being designed in the SmartUI Designer.

Title: How to export a graphical component to a XML file
Steps:
The simplest method of reusing graphical components is to simply export the required graphical components to a XML file and then simply drag this file into the required graphic form that is being designed in the SmartUI Designer. - If the component you want to export consists only of vectors (no spiders and no controls) - Select all the vectors. - Right click and select Create Vector Group . - Select the new group of vectors. - Right click and select export, and specify the filename and location to export the vector to. The vector will be exported to a file with an XML extension. - To reuse the vector, simply drag the file into a graphic form that is being designed in the Designer. - If the component you want to export consists of vectors and spiders (no controls) - Select all the vectors. - Right click and select Create Vector Group . - Select the new group of vectors. - Press CTRL+ALT+C - This will pop up a dialog asking you to specify a name. Type in a meaningful name for the component you are exporting. - Open a windows explorer window and browse to the folder that you want to export the component to. - Right click in the folder where you want to export the component to and select paste. - The component will be exported to a file with the name you specified and have an XML extension. - To reuse the component, simply drag the file into a graphic form that is being designed in the Designer. - If the component you want to export consists of vectors spiders and controls - Select all the vectors. - Right click and select Create Vector Group . - Select the new group of vectors. - Click on the control selection pointer in the pointer toolbar - While holding in the CTRL key click and select the controls that you want to include as part of the exported component. - Press CTRL+ALT+C - This will pop up a dialog asking you to specify a name. Type in a meaningful name for the component you are exporting. - Open a windows explorer window and browse to the folder that you want to export the component to. - Right click in the folder where you want to export the component to and select paste. - The component will be exported to a file with the name you specified and have an XML extension. - To reuse the component, simply drag the file into a graphic form that is being designed in the Designer. Notes: Spiders are copied along with the controls and vectors that they belong to by default when you press CTRL+C , CTRL+ALT+C , through the right click menu or the toolbar. To prevent the spiders from being copied press and hold the Shift key down when copying or exporting your component. Back to top

text:
Ultimately, data is connected to properties of controls or vectors, to animate them.

Title: Mapping Spiders
Ultimately, data is connected to properties of controls or vectors, to animate them. However, it is not always easy to know which property to connect the data to, especially considering the number of properties that a control can expose. Mapping spiders can be used to simply this process, by providing a central location where the data for a reusable graphical component can be connected, without needing to manually locate the required properties. In other words, the user ties the data to the inputs of the Mapping spider, which are custom-named so that it is easy to identify which data point goes to which input. This is made possible because the Mapping spider consists of input output pairs, so the user who creates the reusable graphical component also creates the Mapping spider and the required input-output pairs, which are named appropriately. Then the outputs of this Mapping spider are connected to the required properties and / or other spiders associated with this reusable graphical component. Then when this graphical component is copied, the Mapping spider will be copied and pasted along with it. How to use a Mapping spider with a reusable component How to use a reusable component containing a Mapping spider Back to top

- Draw the component using vectors and controls.

Title: How to use a Mapping spider with a reusable component
Steps:
- Draw the component using vectors and controls. It is helpful to name the various controls and vectors that make up the reusable component that you are designing. - Create a Mapping spider in the Spider Workspace window. Figure 1 : Default Mapping spider configuration dialog - Name the spider to something useful by double clicking the name at the top and typing in a meaningful name – you cannot name this spider to the same name as a control, vector or another spider. - Double click on the ‘New Mapping Pair’ cell to create a named input and output pair for each input/output that you need to ultimately connect to your component. It will help to give these mapping pairs useful names that communicate their purpose or use to the user who will ultimately connect them up to the data elements. Figure 2 : Renamed Mapping spider with three mapping pairs added - Make sure that ‘Enable Silk Triggering’ option is enabled for this spider. - For each property that needs to be animated from an external value, drag the corresponding output from the spider to the correct property. - For each property that will be used to drive an external value, drag the property to the corresponding input. Make sure that the necessary property spider is configured to trigger of the correct event raised by the object to ensure that the value is ‘written’ at the correct time. Figure 3 : Mapping spider with inputs and outputs connected from/to required properties - You can now save this form, with this component or export the component with the spider to an XML file that can be dragged into the Designer at a later stage when the component needs to be reused. For details, see How to export a graphical component to a XML file . Back to top

metadata.chunk_title: How to use a Mapping spider with a reusable component

text:
If the reusable component is located on another graphic form, copy that component, and paste it into the new form.

Title: How to use a reusable component containing a Mapping spider
Steps:
If the reusable component is located on another graphic form, copy that component, and paste it into the new form. OR If the reusable component is a XML file that is located on a disk, browse to the file and drag it into the form’s design surface, or copy and paste the file onto the design surface (using standard copy and paste commands). - Open the spider workspace and search for the Mapping spider linked to the component that has just been pasted into the design workspace. text:
While it is possible to use a Mapping spider to simplify the mapping of data to the properties of reusable graphical components, it would still be necessary to update every instance of this graphical component should a global change be required.

Title: Template Graphic Objects
While it is possible to use a Mapping spider to simplify the mapping of data to the properties of reusable graphical components, it would still be necessary to update every instance of this graphical component should a global change be required. This can be prevented, however, by using template graphic forms. There is a control called a TemplateGO control, which has the unique ability to contain another graphic form. By using this control, it is possible to reuse a graphic form as a component in another graphic form. Since this reusable component is actually a reference to another graphic form and not a copy of a reusable component, making changes to the reusable form can result in that change immediately becoming available in all the places where this graphic form is used. Furthermore, just as reusable components allow data to be connected to them to animate them, it is also possible to create a reusable graphic form that can have data connected to it via the TemplateGO control. This is accomplished, through the Aliases property of the graphic form, which can contain any number of user defined data entry points to the graphic form. In other words any of the properties of the controls used on the graphic form can be exposed by this Aliases property. Then when a TemplateGO control contains this graphic form, the Aliases property of the TemplateGO control exposes the Aliases property in this contained graphic form and the data entry points that have been configured so that data can be connected to them. In this case the property spider associated with the Aliases property provides a central location from which data can be connected to these exposed entry points, much like the Mapping spider. How to create a reusable graphic form How to use a reusable graphic form in a TemplateGO control Back to top

- Create a graphic form containing vectors, controls, and/or spiders but do not connect the spiders to the Server-side data elements.

Title: How to create a reusable graphic form
Steps:
- Create a graphic form containing vectors, controls, and/or spiders but do not connect the spiders to the Server-side data elements. - Select the form. - Select the Aliases property of the graphic form in the property grid content window and press the browse( ) button next to the property. - This will pop up a dialog where you fill in useful names of items that you want to expose or use to drive internal values and properties of controls and vectors on this form. - Click the Add button to add and name the inputs/outputs for this form. It helps to create items that have meaningful names. - Click the Finish button once you have added the items that you want to add. Figure 4 : Adding items to be exposed or driven by this graphic form to the Aliases property - In the spider workspace with the form being selected in the SmartUI Designer, find the form’s object in the property tree on the left of the spider content window. - Expand the tree and locate the Aliases property (under the VIZNET Extended category) - Right click on the tree node and select ‘Show property spider’ to bring the Aliases property spider into view. Figure 5 : Displaying the graphic form Aliases property spider with the added items - You will notice that the inputs and outputs are the items that you added when configuring the Aliases property. - Make sure that ‘Enable Silk Triggering’ is enabled for this spider. - For each property that needs to be animated from an external value, drag the corresponding output from the spider to the correct property. - For each property that will be used to drive an external value, drag the property to the corresponding input. Make sure that the property spider is configured to trigger of the correct event raised by the object to ensure that the value is ‘written’ at the correct time. - Save the Graphic form. Back to top

text:
While template graphic forms are useful when a single graphic form is required in multiple locations, this feature is unable to reuse a graphic form directly.

Title: Spider Template Sets
Steps:
While template graphic forms are useful when a single graphic form is required in multiple locations, this feature is unable to reuse a graphic form directly. In this case, the best approach is to configure the spider engine to contain multiple template sets. PLEASE NOTE : Spider template sets have nothing to do with TemplateGOs or SmartUI Templates and should not be confused with them! Template sets are essentially named collections of silks. When the template set is active then all the silks that belong to that template set are active and allow communications from one spider to the next. In this way, it is possible to control which data is communicated to which properties and/or spiders. Silks can belong to more than one template set. The Default template set is always active, so all the silks that belong to this template set are always active. In addition, the Template Set spider allows the user to view and change the active template set at runtime. Another advantage of using this method is that this template set configuration can be exported and imported via a Microsoft Excel readable XML spreadsheet, for simpler bulk configuration. How to create a reusable form using spider template sets How to use spider template sets Back to top

- Create a graphic form with the components and vectors that you need to connect to data.

Title: How to create a reusable form using spider template sets
- Create a graphic form with the components and vectors that you need to connect to data. - In the spider workspace window toolbar click on the “New Template Set” ( ) Button. - Create a template set for each reusable instance and name them accordingly. - In the drop down list box to the right of the Button, select “Default” to select the default template set. - All data that is connected while the Default Template set is active will always be active and are not dependant of which template set is currently active. i.e. Connect data that you want to be permanently connected irrespective of which template set is active. - Select one of the other template sets from the drop down list box. - Create silk connections between data elements and properties and other spiders which are relevant only for this template set. - Repeat the above step until you have configured all the silk connections for each template set. Note: If a silk should belong to more than one template set other than the Default template set, you can make the silk active for more than one set by right clicking on the silk and selecting the template set(s) that the silk belongs to under the ‘Template Sets’ sub menu. Back to top

This document aims to describe how SmartUI users can set the input parameter values of a spider and trigger the relevant spider using script, either by using a Script Engine Spider or the Graphic Form Script.

Title: Introduction
This document aims to describe how SmartUI users can set the input parameter values of a spider and trigger the relevant spider using script, either by using a Script Engine Spider or the Graphic Form Script. IMPORTANT: The screenshots and specified configuration settings relate to an OLD version of the SmartUI product and so your specific settings and screens may differ. This method of setting and triggering spiders is useful in the following scenarios: - To ensure that a spider in triggered only after all input parameter value(s) have been set. - When you have more than one spider that needs to be triggered and the relevant spiders must always be triggered in a specific order. - When the input parameter value(s) of the spider is so complex that it can only be calculated using script. - When the output data of a spider is needed in your script for further processing.

metadata.title: How to set spider inputs and trigger spiders through script

text:
- You need a thorough understanding and/or experience in the VB.Net or C# (Sharp) programming language.

Title: What you need to do before you can begin this procedure
Steps:
- You need a thorough understanding and/or experience in the VB.Net or C# (Sharp) programming language. - You need to be familiar with using SmartUI i.e. creating projects, adding datasources etc. - For this example you also need an OLE DB compliant database. - Install the latest available version of SmartUI - Start your SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer and log in to the SmartUI Server.

text:

Title: Adding the necessary components
- Add a new project to the SmartUI Designer; call it TestPrj or anything you like. - Create a new Graphic Form for this project. - Add an OLE DB datasource for your database, in this example the name of our OLE DB datasource is AlarmAnalysisDB. - Create a query in the OLE DB datasource that’s requires one or more Input Parameters. In this example we created a Select query, with the name of BurstRate, which requires the following 3 input parameters: StartDateTime, EndDateTime and Filters.

text:

Title: Configuration
- Create a Script Engine spider that will be used to trigger the query spider you’ve already created. - Click the Edit Script… button on the Script Engine spider to add the required script for triggering the Query spider. Figure 5 : Editing the script of the Script Engine spider. - Add the following Namespace: Imports VIZNET.Shared.DataElements.Engine - Add the required script to set input values and trigger the query spider, as follows: - Declare a variable of type DataElement for each Input Parameter that needs to be set on the Query Spider, e.g.: Dim startDE as DataElement. - Set the DataElement variables using the same name as the Input Parameter, e.g.: startDE = DataElementEngine.NewDataElement("StartDateTime"). - Set the Value property of the DataElement variables, e.g.: startDE.Value = "2008/07/01" - Declare a variable of type Spider for the Query spider, e.g.: Dim spider as Spider - Set the Spider variable using the same name as the Query Spider, e.g.: spider = MyController("qryQueryName"). - Set the Input Parameter of the Spider using the DataElement and the Input Parameter name, e.g.: spider.SetValue(startDE, "StartDateTime") - Once all the Input Parameters have been set with their relative DataElement variables and Input Parameter names then trigger the Query Spider, e.g.: spider.Trigger() - Go to the Build menu and select Compile Script to ensure that your script successfully without any errors. - Close the Script Editor and open the Spider Configuration window. - Right-click on the Script Engine spider’s header and select Trigger Spider From Event . Figure 1: Displaying the properties of the ComboBox control The most important properties of the Combobox control are grouped within the Data property grouping: - DataSource – this should be used if you if need to bind this control to a Dataset in order to set the DisplayMember and ValueMember properties.

Title: Figure 1
Figure 1: Displaying the properties of the ComboBox control The most important properties of the Combobox control are grouped within the Data property grouping: - DataSource – this should be used if you if need to bind this control to a Dataset in order to set the DisplayMember and ValueMember properties. In SmartUI terms we only get the Dataset at runtime so nothing will be displayed in this view. Note : To configure this property, simply dragged the Table onto the control and bind it to its DataSource property. - DisplayMember – is the property that should specify the name of the column (field) of the Dataset data that is bound to the DataSource property of this control. This is the first column from the table of this Dataset data, by default. To display another field of the table then you must manually type in this field name. Tip : If this graphic form is being Run, then the required field can simply be selected from the DisplayMember property’s value list box. To do this right-click the Graphic Form name in the Enterprise Manager and select Run . Note : The DisplayMember value that is selected from the control at runtime is returned in the Text property of the control. - Items – this is used to either type your own list from which the user can select an Item by adding a list manually in the property grid, or you can drag a database table onto the combo box and using the configuration dialog bind a field from that table automatically. Bare in mind that if you select more than on field in the configuration dialog it will concatenate the fields in the list box. If you use this method the value returned is contained in the Text property of the combo box. - Tag – this is a very important property in that you can use this to return any value to SmartUI . It is a freely configurable property that can be very useful in building a system. It will be dealt with in more detail later on in the document. - ValueMember – is the property that should specify the name of the column (field) of this Dataset data, whose value you want to be retrieved, when its associated DisplayMember value is selected at runtime. So the returned ValueMember will be based on what record/item you select as a DisplayMember from the list in the control. Typically, ValueMember will specify the field of this Dataset data that is more descriptive. This parameter is configured in exactly the same way as DisplayMember above, you can manually type it in or you can Run the form and then select it from the list displayed. (See The third usage scenario as to its usage) Note 1 : The ValueMember value that is associated with the DisplayMember value that is selected from the control at runtime, is returned in the SelectedValue property, of the control. SelectedValue is listed within the Hidden Properties list of this control, in the property tree in the Spider Configuration window. Note 2 : If you don’t set the ValueMember it will be set the same as the DisplayMember and visa-versa. Back to top
