text:
These are important should you wish to should you wish to operate or manipulate a control via a spider or a script.

Title: Important ComboBox (and ListBox) Control Events
These are important should you wish to should you wish to operate or manipulate a control via a spider or a script. - TextChanged – Whenever text changes in combo box this event gets raised, so if for example you are typing something every letter will raise this event, so be aware of this. - ValueMemberChanged – whenever you change the ValueMember property is changed usually this is set at design and won’t be raised in runtime. This is not the event to use if you want to trigger something on selection change from the list in the combo box (the would be the SelectedValueChanged event) - DataSourceChanged – only gets raised when the DataSource property gets changed, usually at design time only - DataMemberChanged – only gets raised when the DataMember property gets changed, usually at design time only - SelectedIndexChanged – gets raised whenever a selection is made in the combo box. This is a good event to use to trigger some desired result whenever you make a selection change. - SelectedValueChanged – will get raised providing you have defined the ValueMember property and it gets raised whenever the selected record in the DisplayMember property changes. Back to top

text:
In this example a fixed list is defined in a ComboBox control and then the item (record) that the user selects from this control is used to populate a text box.

Title: Populating a ComboBox Control from a Fixed List and Displaying the Selected Value in a Label Control
In this example a fixed list is defined in a ComboBox control and then the item (record) that the user selects from this control is used to populate a text box. - Add a ComboBox control to the graphic form, which is listed in the Windows Forms category of the Toolbox window. - Select the ComboBox, go to the “Data” portion of the properties window, and click on the small button next the Items property. Figure 2: Displaying the Items property of the ComboBox control This displays the following dialog in which you can simply type in a list if Items you would like to display to the user: Figure 3: Specifying the items the ComboBox control should contain - Type in the list that you would like to display to the User. In this case we have typed a list North Plant, East Plant etc - Put the form into Run Mode (by pressing the Run button) and select the pull down on the Combo Box control and you will notice that you get the list you have typed in the box. Note : The text property combobox1 is displayed by this ComboBox control by default. If you want that to be blank simply delete the text in the Text property of this control. You can type anything in here, remembering that if it is selected it will become the value effectively passed onto the next transaction via the Text property. - Display the selection of this ComboBox control, as follows: - Add a Label control to the graphic form - In the Spider Configuration window, connect the Text property of the combo box to the Text property of the label by firstly selecting the two controls on the form and then dragging and dropping from the Combobox.Text property to the Label.Text property. - The event you should use to trigger the spider is the SelectedIndexChanged of the ComboBox control, so that whenever a new item is selected the text of this item will be updated, as follows: - To expose the property spider right click on the Combobox.Text property and click on “Show Property Spider” or simply select the Combobox.Text property in the tree view hold your right button of your mouse down, move the mouse a little and then double-click. - In the Event Trigger section of this property spider ensure that the Event Object is comboBox1 and the Event Name is SelectedIndexChanged. Figure 4: Configuring the event used to trigger the Text property of the ComboBox Note : This Text could also be sent back to a SCADA system or be used to drive a parameter within a user defined query on a database. Back to top

If you want that to be blank simply delete the text in the Text property of this control. You can type anything in here, remembering that if it is selected it will become the value effectively passed onto the next transaction via the Text property . - Display the selection of this ComboBox control, as follows: - Add a Label control to the graphic form - In the Spider Configuration window, connect the Text property of the combo box to the Text property of the label by firstly selecting the two controls on the form and then dragging and dropping from the Combobox.Text property to the Label.Text property. - The event you should use to trigger the spider is the SelectedIndexChanged of the ComboBox control, so that whenever a new item is selected the text of this item will be updated, as follows: - To expose the property spider right click on the Combobox.Text property and click on “Show Property Spider” or simply select the Combobox.Text property in the tree view hold your right button of your mouse down, move the mouse a little and then double-click. - In the Event Trigger section of this property spider ensure that the Event Object is comboBox1 and the Event Name is SelectedIndexChanged. text:
A common usage of the ComboBox control (or ListBox control) is to select the index or key column of a database, however these values are usually not descriptive enough to be very user-friendly.

Title: Associating a Key to an Item Displayed in a ComboBox or ListBox Control
A common usage of the ComboBox control (or ListBox control) is to select the index or key column of a database, however these values are usually not descriptive enough to be very user-friendly. However, there is usually another column in the database that contains descriptive values. It is now possible to BOTH select the required index or key column value using the ComboBox control and to obtain the associated, more descriptive value, from the other column of this database too. This descriptive value can then either be displayed or used, for instance, by being passed as a parameter to a parameterised query. This is possible due to its DisplayMember and ValueMember data properties that both the ComboBox and ListBox controls have. For details. see Important properties of the ComboBox (and ListBox) control . This example assumes that there is a database called Northwind, which has a table called Employees with some fields. In this case it is required to select from a list containing the EmployeeID records and return the name of the Employee from the FirstName field. Figure 8: Fully configured graphic form Perform this configuration, as follows: - Add a ComboBox control to the graphic form, which is listed in the Windows Forms category of the Toolbox window. - From enterprise manager drag and drop the Employee Table and bind it to the combo box’s DataSource property and select the column to be displayed in the ComboBox from the Filter DataSet configuration dialog. Note : If the Datasource property doesn’t appear in the list when you drop the table onto the combo box control then simply expand the list by selecting “Customise” and the highlight and check the Datasource check box in the list. - Select the ComboBox, go to the “Data” portion of the properties window, and set the DisplayMember property to the displayed column name by typing it in manually, in this instance it will be “EmployeeID”. Do the same with the ValueMember property but set it to the column name that you want to associate with the DisplayMember, in this case select “FirstName”. Figure 9 : Configuring the DisplayMember and ValueMember properties of the ComboBox control - Add a Label control to the graphic form. Note : This will only be used to display the selected displayed member’s associated value. - Select the ComboBox and in the PropertyTree expand the hidden properties tree node in the spider configuration window. - Right click on the SelectedValue property node and select “Show Property Spider”. Figure 10 : Displaying the SelectedValue Property spider - Right click the spider heading and select “Trigger Spider from Event”. - Select the Event Object to be the Combobox, and the Event to be the SelectedValueChanged event. Figure 11 : Configuring the event used to trigger the SelectedValue Property spider - Select the Label control on the form. - Expand the controls properties in the PropertyTree to the Text property under the Appearance category. - Drag and drop the SelectedValue output from the comboBox1.SelectedValue property spider onto the expanded label’s Text property. Figure 12 : Connecting the SelectedValue property of the ComboBox control to the Text property of the Label control - Select the Run button of this graphic form. Select an Employee Id, in the Combo Box on the graphic form, the associated value member should appear in the label. Note : The selected value member can be passed as a parameter to a parameterised query, if necessary. -->

Once the backup has been completed, a message box is displayed, indicating the specified location of this backup, this is placed in a sub-folder of the specified backup path , which is named by the current date and the current time. Tip: Make a note of this backup location, so that you can locate this backed up data . -->

Title: To derive a new custom agent:
Steps:
Note: Click the New button to empty the current configuration and start a new agent type configuration. - In the Agent type name edit box, type in the name of your agent type e.g. DriveXYZ and press the TAB key. Alternatively, use the browse [ … ] button on the right of this edit box to select a previously configured custom agent. - In the Help document or command to run edit box: - EITHER: type in an optional help document name or program to run (complete with path names and parameters) when the Help button is pressed in the edit dialog of this agent. For instance: "c:\windows\Notepad.exe C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \DriveXYZHelp.txt". - OR leave this empty, if you have created a help file with the SAME name as your custom agent, so that Adroit will search for and launch this help file automatically, at run-time when the help is invoked and display nothing if this cannot be found. - Either select Data container agent only , if the derived agent is only to contain a number of values, or Has script engine , if scripting intelligence is also required, this selection will enable the Edit script button. Note: Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will require a scan point license. Tip: Custom agents created via the Custom Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). Select the Has script engine for this DriveXYZ agent. - Tick the Live dialog tick box, for changes made to the configuration of this agent to immediately be updated, without manually using the Update button, in this dialog, to do this. Note: This can be enabled within the edit dialog. Leave this unticked for the DriveXYZ agent. - Configure the first grid to define the slots (values) of this derived agent. For details, see Slot Configuration Grid . WARNING! The custom slot type "String" is a VarString type, which CANNOT BE SCANNED. If you need to scan a string slot use the String80 slot type instead, which can be configured for scanning. - Replace or edit the cell in the Status bit name column, of the second grid, to define the status bit names, if any, that this derived agent may require. Click here for more details: If the Script engine is not enabled these status slots values need to be driven externally, typically by the scanning subsystem. Note1: Ensure that these status bit names are unique and do not clash with any slot names specified in the first grid. Duplicate slot names are checked for and disallowed. Slot names starting with "agent" or "status" are also checked for and disallowed. Note2: The order in which these status bits are defined, determines the order of the slots, in which they will be displayed in the configuration agent dialog and which private status bit they will occupy i.e. the first status bit is StatusBit16. As with other agents, a maximum of 16 status bits may be defined. Note3: Changing the number of status slots at a later date will render any WGP files saved with this agent type unloadable. If you know what you are doing you can simply edit the WGP file in a text editor and remove the offending agents. For the DriveXYZ agent, type in the following status bits: TempHi and Trip. The "Trip" status bit will be turned on by the Script engine when the Tripped slot is on, for alarming purposes.

metadata.chunk_title: To derive a new custom agent:

text:
If the Script engine was not enabled, we could have decided instead that the DriveXYZ Trip status bit would have been scanned directly to the PLC and done away with the Tripped slot altogether.

Title: To derive a new custom agent:
Steps:
If the Script engine was not enabled, we could have decided instead that the DriveXYZ Trip status bit would have been scanned directly to the PLC and done away with the Tripped slot altogether. - lf scripting intelligence is also required, click the Edit script button to create the script code that provide any additional functionality for this agent and choose the required scripting engine either Yes to use JavaScript or No to use VBScript. - Click the Save button to create the necessary files in the CustomAgents subfolder of your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \CustomAgents. The following files can be created for this custom derived agent: t_AgentTypeName.CSV and t_AgentTypeName.DLL files and if the Script engine is enabled, a t_AgentTypeName.VBS / t_AgentTypeName.JAV file is also created. For the DriveXYZ agent, the following files will appear in the CustomAgent sub-folder: t_drivexyz.csv, t_drivexyz.dll and t_drivexyz.vbs / drivexyz.jav, since the script engine has been enabled. - Once the slots and status bits and the script (if scripting was required) have been configured, for this derived custom agent, the agent can be published or copied to the Adroit installation folder, typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . Publish derived custom agents as follows: - Stop the Agent Server and any other Adroit components - Click the Publish button to copy the custom agent files to the Adroit installation directory on the same PC. Note: If there are any remote Adroit installations that connect to the local agent server, these derived custom agent files must also be MANUALLY copied to those Adroit installation directories as well. For the DriveXYZ agent, the following files will be copied or "published" to the Adroit system folder: t_drivexyz.csv, t_drivexyz.dll and t_drivexyz.vbs / drivexyz.jav. When you click the OK , Save and Edit script buttons the Custom Agent Designer ensures that previously published derived custom agents are up to date with the latest "t_custom.dll", so that any discrepancies can be fixed. Similarly, should a published custom agent be found to be newer than the "t_custom.dll" this will then display an alert for this to be fixed. An example of the configured Custom Agent Designer for DriveXYZ: After the configuration of the slots and status bits, for the DriveXYZ agent, the Custom Agent Designer window, should look something like this: Using the Derived Custom agent within Adroit : this describes how to add an instance of a published, derived custom agent and how to test that it works and how to configure it. -->

Steps:
Note: Click the New button to empty the current configuration and start a new agent type configuration. - In the Agent type name edit box, type in the name of your agent type e.g. DriveXYZ and press the TAB key. Alternatively, use the browse [ … ] button on the right of this edit box to select a previously configured custom agent. - In the Help document or command to run edit box: - EITHER: type in an optional help document name or program to run (complete with path names and parameters) when the Help button is pressed in the edit dialog of this agent. For instance: "c:\windows\Notepad.exe C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \DriveXYZHelp.txt". - OR leave this empty, if you have created a help file with the SAME name as your custom agent, so that Adroit will search for and launch this help file automatically, at run-time when the help is invoked and display nothing if this cannot be found. - Either select Data container agent only , if the derived agent is only to contain a number of values, or Has script engine , if scripting intelligence is also required, this selection will enable the Edit script button. Note: Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will require a scan point license. Tip: Custom agents created via the Custom Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). Select the Has script engine for this DriveXYZ agent. - Tick the Live dialog tick box, for changes made to the configuration of this agent to immediately be updated, without manually using the Update button, in this dialog, to do this. Note: This can be enabled within the edit dialog. Leave this unticked for the DriveXYZ agent. - Configure the first grid to define the slots (values) of this derived agent. For details, see Slot Configuration Grid . WARNING! The custom slot type "String" is a VarString type, which CANNOT BE SCANNED. If you need to scan a string slot use the String80 slot type instead, which can be configured for scanning. - Replace or edit the cell in the Status bit name column, of the second grid, to define the status bit names, if any, that this derived agent may require. Click here for more details: If the Script engine is not enabled these status slots values need to be driven externally, typically by the scanning subsystem. Note1: Ensure that these status bit names are unique and do not clash with any slot names specified in the first grid. Duplicate slot names are checked for and disallowed. Slot names starting with "agent" or "status" are also checked for and disallowed. Note2: The order in which these status bits are defined, determines the order of the slots, in which they will be displayed in the configuration agent dialog and which private status bit they will occupy i.e. the first status bit is StatusBit16. As with other agents, a maximum of 16 status bits may be defined. Note3: Changing the number of status slots at a later date will render any WGP files saved with this agent type unloadable. If you know what you are doing you can simply edit the WGP file in a text editor and remove the offending agents. For the DriveXYZ agent, type in the following status bits: TempHi and Trip. The "Trip" status bit will be turned on by the Script engine when the Tripped slot is on, for alarming purposes.

Title: To derive a new custom agent:
Steps:
If the Script engine was not enabled, we could have decided instead that the DriveXYZ Trip status bit would have been scanned directly to the PLC and done away with the Tripped slot altogether. - lf scripting intelligence is also required, click the Edit script button to create the script code that provide any additional functionality for this agent and choose the required scripting engine either Yes to use JavaScript or No to use VBScript. - Click the Save button to create the necessary files in the CustomAgents subfolder of your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \CustomAgents. Similarly, should a published custom agent be found to be newer than the "t_custom.dll" this will then display an alert for this to be fixed. Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit ICMP agent dialog: - Specify the IP address of the network device, in the Remote IP address edit box (STRING ipAddress slot). Note: ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. Tip: Ideally copy and paste this address into the edit box to ensure that it is correct. - Specify how often you want to check the availability of this device on the network, in seconds, in the Poll rate (secs) edit box (INTEGER interval slot). - Specify how long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable in the Timeout (ms) edit box (INTEGER timeout slot). Note: If the specified timeout is too short then you will never get a "host unreachable" error because the network will not have the necessary time to respond. - Specify how many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable in the Retry count edit box (INTEGER retries slot). - Specify the time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send a message to the network device and receive a reply has moved outside its acceptable range and therefore implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible in the Round trip time: high alarm value (ms) edit box (INTEGER hi slot). - Specify the time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send and receive a message and from the network device has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and that urgent and immediate corrective action is now required in the Round trip time: high-high alarm value (ms) edit box (INTEGER hiHi slot). - Check the Enabled checkbox to start sending ICMP messages to the specified Remote IP address . - The dialog provides the following information concerning the attempts to contact the device: - The Round trip time (ms) edit box (INTEGER roundTripTime slot), displays the time taken, in milliseconds, to send the last ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. - The Failure count edit box (INTEGER failure_Count slot), indicates the number of attempts to contact the device that failed, in other words those attempts that timed out before a response from the device was received for the specified number of retries. Tip: If you need to reset the failures to 0, then type in a value of 0 into this edit box. - The Last execution time edit box (TIME last_Execution_Time slot), specifies when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. - Further mechanisms that you can use to obtain diagnostic information from this agent : - The status bits and their alarm types can be alarmed to alert you when the device cannot be contacted or when the round trip time exceeds the specified High and high-High times. For details, see Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent .

metadata.title: How to use the IOT agent to define an object
metadata.chunk_title: This agent does not possess any default status slots and is required to be configured externally.

text:
You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it.

Title: Creating the structure of an object
You should provide an appropriate name and then add the required IOT agent, which will enable the code that interfaces to the IOT device to identify it. As only this code knows the identification of the IOT device, it should use the addSlot OR xmlSlots slots of this agent to programmatically create the slots as required.

metadata.title: How to use the IOT agent to define an object
metadata.chunk_title: Creating the structure of an object

text:
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ?

Title: Using the addSlot
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above

metadata.title: How to use the IOT agent to define an object

text:
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section.

Title: Using the xmlSLot
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. - the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: - The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? - The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. - The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: - Boolean : a 1 or a 0 - Integer : a 4 byte signed integer - Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters - Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type - Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . - VarString : any number of characters - Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used.

metadata.title: How to use the IOT agent to define an object

text:
The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot.

Title: Example of the XML structure
The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot. To facilitate easier reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name=" hi "/> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> Any number of <Slots> may be defined. A maximum of 16 <HeaderSlots> (status bits) may be defined. The first specified header slot represents status bit 16 and subsequent header slots will represent status bits 17 to 31. The XML code above can be saved to an XML file as a template and loaded in the IOT agent dialog. An example of IOT values XML packet for rawValue is a simplified version of the xmlSlots schema as follows with custom text shown in blue : <IOT><Slots><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></Slots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotValues><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></SlotValues></IOT> For improved reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT> <SlotValues> <Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot> </SlotValues> </IOT> Important: This is very important!! – To send a Time slot type value within the rawValue XML … you MUST first convert the value to a UCT time.

text:
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ?

Title: Using the addSlot
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above

text:
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section.

Title: Using the xmlSLot
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. - the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: - The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? - The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. - The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: - Boolean : a 1 or a 0 - Integer : a 4 byte signed integer - Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters - Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type - Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . - VarString : any number of characters - Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used.

text:
Pre-requisites - Ensure that you have installed the SmartUI Server and or GX Works2.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Pre-requisites - Ensure that you have installed the SmartUI Server and or GX Works2. - Ensure that you can log into the SmartUI Designer to configure MAPS projects. - Create a list of ALL the items of electrical and instrumentation equipment required in each plant site that is organised according to an extended physical model of the S88/S95 hierarchical structure. For more details, see How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy . Note: You need to create a SmartUI project for EACH of your process Sites. - Specify the IO types in each PLC and group the virtual IO cards to ensure efficient scanning. - Configure the settings of each Agent Server - do not rely on the default settings. For details, see Setting up the Adroit Agent Server . - Create and configure the necessary PLC devices (instances) in Adroit for each PLC. - If necessary, start the SmartUI Server. - Log into the SmartUI Designer application and ensure that the MAPS window is displayed. - In the MAPS window, right-click the initial entry and select Add project . The Project Name page of the MAPS project wizard opens, so that you can configure the MAPS project-specific settings. - Specify the MANDATORY Project Name and Description , which identify the associated process Site. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this SmartUI Project name. - Specify the following Project Settings: Note: Use the Properties right click option to change these settings after creating a SmartUI project. - Project Path : specifies where the following items are saved: - the generated project reports, in the Reports sub-folder, - the generated project reports, in the Documents sub-folder, - Default Project Report: specifies the path and name of the report template used for the project reports. If this is BLANK, the default setting, then the GENERIC project report template is used. The GENERIC project report template provides the S88/S95 hierarchy, which includes the following separate lists of each hierarchy level: - A list of the configured Plant Areas and their settings. - A list of the configured PLCs (Process Cells) and their settings. - A list of the configured Units and their settings. - A list of each configured item of equipment and their signals. Tip: You can customise this GENERIC project report template, for example, by adding your company logo to its title. For details, see Customizing report templates . - MAPS Reporting Database SQL Connection String : if you want to use some or all of the Adroit Reporting Suite reports to analyse your Adroit alarming data to improve your alarming configuration and/or record any value that an operator manually changes for auditing purposes, then do the following: - manually create an empty SQL (SQL 2008 R2 with Advanced Services) database, typically via the SQL Server Management utility (which is installed by the SQL 2008 R2 with Advanced Services installation) and - specify the connection string to this database here, typically by clicking the browse button to the right of the MAPS Reporting Database SQL Connection String field and then use the displayed Connection Properties dialog to connect to this SQL database. Typically do NOT change the Data source from the default of .NET Framework Data Provider for OLE DB , unless you are connecting to a SQL Compact database. More details: in which case, click the Change... button and choose the datasource that corresponds to the correct version of SQL Compact and then the dialog will change so that you only need to browse in the required database file and specify the required password, if any.

metadata.title: How to use the MAPS project wizard to add a MAPS project

text:
Once this database is specified, then you can right click the MAPS Project in the Enterprise Manager and select the Create Adroit Report Suite right click command, which creates the following agents for this MAPS project: an AlarmManagement, an Audit agent and a DBLog agent, which are configured as follows: - The AlarmManagement agent re-creates the S88 MAPS structure of your project for all the alarmed tags.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Once this database is specified, then you can right click the MAPS Project in the Enterprise Manager and select the Create Adroit Report Suite right click command, which creates the following agents for this MAPS project: an AlarmManagement, an Audit agent and a DBLog agent, which are configured as follows: - The AlarmManagement agent re-creates the S88 MAPS structure of your project for all the alarmed tags. IMPORTANT: You need to purchase a separate license for the Adroit AlarmManagement agent before you can use this agent to log your alarming data, which you can analyse using the Alarm Management reports. - The Audit agent adds all the tags that are output enabled, so that any Operator change in value is audited (logged to this database) for later analysis. - The DBLog agent is enabled to start logging and all the agent values logged by the MAPS Templates of this project are also logged to this SQL database. The names of these created agents use the specified MAPS project name and the specific agent type name. For instance, if the MAPS project name is MYPROJ then the following three agents are created: MYPROJ_AMA, MYPROJ_AUDIT and MYPROJ_DBLOG. Then after installing the required reports of the Adroit Report Suite you can use them to analyse your alarms and/or audited items and/or the agent values logged by the DBLog agent. - Default Screen size: Specify the required screen resolution of ALL the graphic forms of your MAPS project, by selecting the required screen dimensions, in pixels, from the list. MAPS then automatically adjusts the size of ALL your graphic forms in this project to fit onto the selected screen resolution. Since one of the purposes of the Operator View, which is generated by each MAPS project, is to provide navigation through the defined plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment, MAPS projects allow you to Select Operator View Layout , as follows: - Advanced : this view provides a navigational structure of different panes, which each provide buttons that display the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Note: This view is more visually appealing and allows your operators to customise this view by hiding or showing the different panes, as needed. - Simple : this view uses menus and sub menus to navigate through the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Note: This view provides the same functionality as the Advanced view only in a simpler navigational format. - Show Equipment Title: specify whether you want to display or hide the names of your equipment on the graphic forms, by checking or unchecking the Show Equipment Title checkbox, which is checked (displayed) by default. Typically you will hide these equipment names to unclutter their graphic forms or when these names only serve to confuse your operators. IMPORTANT: Only check the Empty Project checkbox to MANUALLY add plant areas, PLCs, Units and equipment to this site ( SmartUI project) - in this case, clicking Next ends this wizard. - Click Next and define the required Plant Areas. The Plant Area Data page opens so that you can define the various areas within this process site ( SmartUI project). Add a row to the Plant Area Data table for each plant area and complete the following fields: Note: To delete a row, select it and press the DELETE key and click Yes in the deletion confirmation dialog. - The MANDATORY Name and Description of the plant area. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this plant area name. Note: Ensure that each plant area name is unique.

metadata.title: How to use the MAPS project wizard to add a MAPS project

text:
- The MANDATORY SmartUI Server Name that typically specifies the local SmartUI Server, which is the Default setting.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- The MANDATORY SmartUI Server Name that typically specifies the local SmartUI Server, which is the Default setting. If necessary, you can specify a remote SmartUI Server, as follows: if you have more than one SmartUI Servers on your network (and their BroadcastEnabled setting is TRUE), then their SmartUI Server names will also appear in this list (in the following format: [ComputerName] Literal Server Name) - simply select the name of the required remote SmartUI Server from the list. Typically this SmartUI Server provides a connection to a single Agent Server that contains the SCADA tags for this plant area. Click here if you have more than one Agent Server connected to a SmartUI server: Check the Advanced checkbox to display the Agent Server column and use this column to specify which Agent Server this plant Area should use. - Offline: When the Agent Server does not exist or is not available - in this case you are unable to create or synchronise tags. Note: If the Agent Server is specified as being Offline then you need to type in an appropriate Adroit Device name when configuring the PLCs. - Agent Server connection name: The name of the Adroit datasource - the connection that is made to an Agent Server from the specified SmartUI Server. Note: This is the name of the connection to the Agent Server as specified in the SmartUI Server and is NOT necessarily the name of the Agent Server as it is specified in Adroit . - The OPTIONAL Plant Area Code if specified, this (unique 5-character alphanumeric) code becomes the prefix that is used for all the equipment items defined within this plant area. This is recommended as it helps to ensure unique and identifiable tag names in the project, that allow you to easily differentiate your plant equipment. - Click Next to define the required PLCs and, if necessary, the IO address ranges for each PLC. Note: You will only advance to the PLC Data page once all the MANDATORY fields are correctly completed for all the added plant areas. The PLC Data page opens so that you can specify the PLCs containing the tags within each plant area. Add a row to the top PLC Data table for each PLC and complete the following fields: - The MANDATORY Name and Description of the PLC. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this PLC name. Note: Ensure that each PLC name is unique. - Select the MANDATORY plant area whose tags are contained in this PLC from the Plant Area Name list. This list specifies all the previously defined plant areas. - Select the MANDATORY device that Adroit uses to communicate to this PLC in the field from the Adroit Device list. Note: If the Agent Server specified for a plant area is Offline then type in an appropriate Adroit Device name, since you CANNOT continue to the next page until a device is specified for EACH PLC! - Use the bottom list to define the MANDATORY address ranges (the Start and End addresses) for each type of IO within each defined PLC. Select the required PLC (row of the top PLC Data table) and define its IO address ranges accordingly. Note: You are unable to continue to the next page of this wizard until you have specified a start and end value for ALL the specified IO of EACH PLC. - Click Next and define the required Units within each PLC . Note: You will only advance to the Unit Data page once all the MANDATORY fields are correctly completed for all the added PLCs.

metadata.title: How to use the MAPS project wizard to add a MAPS project

text:
The Unit Data page opens so that you can specify the unit/s (tag groupings) within each PLC of this process site ( MAPS project).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
The Unit Data page opens so that you can specify the unit/s (tag groupings) within each PLC of this process site ( MAPS project). Add a row to the Unit Data table for each unit and complete the following fields: - The MANDATORY Name and Description of the Unit. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this unit name. Note: Ensure that each Unit name is unique. - Select the MANDATORY PLC that contains the tags within this unit from the PLC Name list. This list specifies all the previously defined PLCs. - Click Next and specify ALL the types of electrical equipment and their quantities as required for this site ( MAPS project) in the Electrical Data page. Note: You will only advance to the Electrical Data page once all the MANDATORY fields are correctly completed for all the added units. In MAPS , each type of electrical equipment requires an associated MAPS template. For more details, see Electrical equipment templates . In the case of complex items of equipment that consist of more than one piece of electrical and/or instrumentation equipment, like conveyors - create a Unit for this item of equipment and associate all the component electrical equipment to MAPS templates. The Electrical Data page opens so that you can specify the required quantities of MAPS templates to represent your electrical equipment within this process site ( MAPS project). Add a row to MAPS the Electrical Data table for each type of SmartUI template that you need and complete the following fields: - Select the MANDATORY Template Name for this type of electrical equipment from the list. Default Electrical equipment templates : the electrical equipment templates Once a template is selected, click the Template Description field to display a description of exactly which type of electrical equipment this MAPS template represents. - Specify the MANDATORY Quantity of this type of electrical equipment. This should specify the TOTAL number of this type of electrical equipment with the entire process site ( MAPS project). WARNING! Once you click the Next button, you are UNABLE to return to this page again, so ensure that this is correctly specified. Tip: If your estimation is NOT exact, you can always add other MAPS templates manually. - Click Next to configure each item of electrical equipment in the Electrical Detail Data page. Note: You will only advance to the Electrical Detail Data page when quantities are specified for all the added electrical equipment templates. The Electrical Detail Data page opens so that you can configure the individual items of electrical equipment of this process site ( MAPS project). Each row of the Electrical Equipment Detail Data table represents an item of electrical equipment that is associated to a MAPS template, which requires the configuration of the following fields: By default, the quantities of each MAPS electrical equipment template, as specified in the Electrical Data page, are added as individual rows. Note: Rows can be manually added and configured from scratch, if you need additional items of electrical equipment. - The MANDATORY Template Name is the MAPS template that represents this item of electrical equipment (or one of its electrical equipment sub-components in the case of complex equipment). - Specify the MANDATORY Unit Name (logical grouping) to which this electrical item of equipment belongs. - Specify the MANDATORY Name of this item of electrical equipment, which is used to identify this item of equipment in the SCADA and PLC. By default, the following suggested naming format is provided: a name that is prefixed by the specified plant area code (if any) and an incrementing counter as a suffix. WARNING! You CANNOT rename this equipment name.

If you selected the Create tags checkbox for any electrical or instrumentation equipment, then their associated SCADA tags are created and any other necessary SCADA configuration is performed - provided the relevant Agent Servers have been started. - If you chose NOT to check the Create tags checkbox for any item of equipment, then: - start the relevant Adroit Agent Server applications - right click each Plant Area and select Sync Tags and when the Tag Data dialog is displayed click Finish. This creates the SCADA tags in Adroit for each item of equipment and performs any other necessary SCADA configuration required by each MAPS template, such as scanning, logging, alarming and/or trending.

Tip: You can also press the CTRL+C shortcut. The popup window appears again with the required text selected. - Right click and select the Copy menu item Paste this text into the required application. - Drop down text: these links appear as sampleText in topics. Tip: Use this if you know the approximate location of the help topic they are looking for, but not its exact name. Title: Using help
- The Favorites tab, to create your own list of help topics that you frequently use, as follows: - Select a help topic that you frequently use. - Open the Favorites tab. - If necessary, type in your own label for this help topic. - Click the Add button. Then when you next open the Favorites tab, use this label to open this help topic. Tip: Open or close this navigational pane, as needed, by using the Show or Hide toggle button of the help toolbar. - Viewed Topic Navigation: Use the Back and Forward toolbar buttons to navigating between previously viewed topics. - Printing topics: While using the online help system, you can print topics and information, by using the Print toolbar button from within the help viewer. To print a single topic: - Ensure the required topic is displayed in the help viewer. - Click the Print toolbar button. Note: If you are within the Contents tab, select the Print the selected topic option from the Print Topics dialog and click OK . The Print dialog is displayed. - Use the General page to select the required printer, the range of pages and number of copies. - Use the Options page to specify the required printing options: - Print all linked documents: This will also print all the topics that are linked to the currently displayed topic. - Print table of links: This will print a table at the end of this topic, which lists all the links found within this topic. To print all topics in a selected book: Note: This can only be performed when the Contents tab is selected. - Ensure the required topic is displayed in the help viewer. - Click the Print toolbar button. The Print Topics dialog is displayed - Select Print the selected heading and all subtopics and click OK . The Print dialog is displayed. - Use the General page to select the required printer, the range of pages and number of copies. - Use the Options page to specify the required printing options: - Print all linked documents: This will also print all the topics that are linked to the currently displayed topic. - Print table of links: This will print a table at the end of this topic, which lists all the links found within this topic. Tip: If topics include Drop down text , ONLY those that are currently expanded will be printed. - Options menu: The Options toolbar button opens a menu, which provides items that duplicate many of these functions and provide additional options too. This menu contains the following items: - Hide/Show Tabs : To close or open the left hand help tabs. - Locate: To find out where a topic located within the Index occurs in the table of contents i.e. the Contents tab. This will also open the Contents tab. - Back: To display the previously viewed help topic. - Forward: To display the prior help topic. - Home: To display the home page of the Designer . - Stop: To stop a help topic or Web page from loading. - Refresh: To update the information displayed in the window. - Internet Options...: To display the Internet Options dialog. - Print: To print the selected topic. - Search Highlight Off/On: To turn search highlighting on or off. If search highlighting is on then the word(s) that are being searched for will be highlighted in the displayed topics. -->

text:
- Backup your Adroit agent database file (.WGP).

Title: To make permanent scan rate changes:
- Backup your Adroit agent database file (.WGP). For details, see Backing Up Agent Database Files . - Stop the required device agent , and wait a few seconds for any backlogged polling to cease. - Export the Device agent type , i.e. click the No button for all the other preceding agent type message boxes. - In the Choose file to contain conversion dialog, select the location to save the Device agent files, it is recommended to leave this as the default location of the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit and save the ‘Device.CSV’ file, then save the scan files for each of the device agents, of the name format DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent. - When the next agent type message box is displayed, click Cancel , to stop the exporting process. - In either a CSV or text editor, open the DeviceName-SCAN.CSV, where DeviceName is the name of the Device agent that the tags have been scanned to. This file will contain four columns or comma-separated values, from left to right as follows: Address, agent.slot, Scanning Interval (period), Deadband - Increase the scan-times on all I/O points, particularly those that are not fast moving within your process. You will want to increase all of your tags poll rates up until the average "effscanrate" value, or increase most of them to double that value and leave just a few scanning quickly. - Save and close this CSV file. - In the User Interface, edit the required Device agent . - Remove all the scan points from this device (unscan them). - Click Import… button and browse in the edited Devicename-SCAN.CSV file, where DeviceName is the name of the selected Device agent from step 4. Note: If messages are displayed during the importing of this scanning configuration, see Common Reasons for Scanning Import Failure for the possible reasons. - Start this device agent . - Verify that the communications are still fine and all I/O tags work as expected. - Save your Adroit agent database file (.WGP) again and finally perform a full test by restarting the Agent Server to verify proper loading etc. If going through all of the above does not help, you may have a stuck continuous output. For details on using the Scanning Monitor to locate this, see Troubleshooting Continuous Writing . -->

metadata.title: How to use the SNMPMgr agent to Manage a Device

text:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog: - Specify the IP address of the device, in the IP address edit box (STRING ipAddress slot), in the Connection settings section or when a device does not have a unique IP address then specify the unique port address (INTEGER ipPort slot) that allows this SNMP devices to be uniquely addressed via a gateway. Note: ensure that the port used for SNMP communications is unblocked (enabled) in any firewalls that may exist, which is typically UDP port 161 for a fixed IP address or the unique port address for the device, when addressed via a gateway. - Select the required SNMP Version for this device supports, if this is version 3 then the following 3 additional connection settings are required: - Username (STRING userName slot): SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required user name. - Authentication (STRING authPassword slot): SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required password for authentication on this device. - Encryption (STRING encrPassword slot): SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required encryption password for this device. - If you ONLY want to retrieve (poll) values from this device then specify its read-only SNMP Community String in the Read comm. edit box (STRING readCommunity slot). - If you want to retrieve and/or write (get and/or set) values for this device then specify its read-write SNMP Community String in the WriteRead comm. edit box (STRING writeCommunity slot). - If you want to receive SNMP traps unsolicited SNMP messages sent by a device to notify an SNMP manager of significant events. from this device then check the Enable traps checkbox. - Click the Browse OID to add button to open the MIB Browser dialog. Tip: If this dialog is displayed then the specified connection settings are correct. - Select the values of this device that you want to monitor (retrieve) and control (change), as follows: - Either click the Walk device button, which then build the tree of the available OID values supported by this device. In this case the retrieved nodes of this tree are only indicated by their numbers. Note: If the monitored device is a computer and you receive an error when trying to walk this device, then ensure that you have installed the SNMP service on this computer AND configured its security settings appropriately. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service and SNMP Service Security Configuration . - Or click the Load MIB file... button to browse in a MIB file for this device, which provides the available OID values supported by this device. In this case the nodes of this tree display their textual descriptions, making it easier to select the required values. Browse the resultant tree and select the required OID value and click the Add to list button to add it to the OID list maintained by this agent. - Configure each selected OID values in the list as follows: - Click the Name field of the required OID to select this row in the list.

text:
- The Type field displays the following integer values that represents the type of data returned by this OID, which therefore determines which agent/s you can use to store this data: Value OID Return Type 2 Integer or Integer32 3 Bits 4 Octet String 5 Null 6 Object Identifier 16 Sequence or Sequence Of 64 IP Address 65 32-bit counter 66 32-bit gauge 67 Time ticks 68 Opaque 70 64-bit counter 71 Unsigned 32-bit value - Click the Browse tag button and use the built-in agent explorer to create and/or select the Tag that will contain and/or change this OID value.

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
- The Type field displays the following integer values that represents the type of data returned by this OID, which therefore determines which agent/s you can use to store this data: Value OID Return Type 2 Integer or Integer32 3 Bits 4 Octet String 5 Null 6 Object Identifier 16 Sequence or Sequence Of 64 IP Address 65 32-bit counter 66 32-bit gauge 67 Time ticks 68 Opaque 70 64-bit counter 71 Unsigned 32-bit value - Click the Browse tag button and use the built-in agent explorer to create and/or select the Tag that will contain and/or change this OID value. For details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Agent Explorer . Note: Ensure that the selected agent type can store the data of this OID value and, if necessary, that the return type of this OID value is writable. For help on this, see SNMP Object Value Return Types . - To poll (retrieve) this OID value: click the E field of this row to check (tick) this checkbox. Note: By default, this value is polled at the global Poll rate for this agent. If this value changes faster or slower than the global rate then use the Rate field of this row to specify this specific rate in milliseconds. Tip: You may need to enlarge this dialog or use the horizontal scroll bar to see this Rate field. - To change this OID value (when the value of the specified Tag changes): click the W field of this row to check (tick) this checkbox. Tip: The lastWriteStatus STRING slot, displays a text message that indicates whether the last value written to the device was successfully changed in the device or not. Note: Ensure that you either click the Update or OK button BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise these configuration changes will be lost. In the Poll settings section of this dialog: - If necessary, specify the default rate at which values are retrieved from the managed device, in milliseconds, in the Poll rate edit box (INTEGER scanRate slot). Tip: You can also specify the number of OID items in each polling transaction in the Pdu edit box. The maximum number is device dependant. - Select the Enable polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) to start managing this device, by polling (getting), writing (setting) and/or trapping (enabling events) its OID values. If necessary display, manipulate, log, trend, chart and or alarm the OID values that are returned from the device. Tip: Check the Auto-refresh values checkbox to immediately obtain the latest values of all the listed OIDs at their specified polling rates, without having to Refresh this dialog manually. Ensure that you backup the GLOBAL SNMP configuration file.

When a possible problem is detected in the operation of the Adroit application, use this Support program to gather together and compress the necessary Adroit files and ALSO provide a detailed description of the problem for the Support department, as follows: Note: If possible, ensure that the Agent Server is running. - Press the Windows key and start typing in the required application name and select it from the list, in this case: Support Program - Now complete this Support dialog , giving as complete a description of the problem as possible. - ONLY complete the Contact Details dialog, if this is the FIRST TIME that you are using the Support Program or details have changed, such as Adroit training that has recently been completed. - Click the Create Report button to display a progress bar for this process. Note: The More info required warning indicates that you have NOT specified a contact name and email address in the Contact Details dialog. - If the Agent Server is NOT running, then specify the Serial Number of its HASP license in the displayed dialog. - The Successfully created report dialog indicates that no problems occurred when creating this report. Note: If an existing file has the same date and time, then the report file will not be created. - Email this report file to the support department, as follows: If you CAN send emails from this computer, then do the following: - Click on the link provided by the Successfully created report dialog to automatically open and create the required email. - Attach the specified .ZIP file in the specified folder (using the Insert File toolbar button). - Send this email to specified email address. If you CANNOT send emails from this computer, then do the following: - Open the Start Menu and click on the Run… command. - In the Run dialog type in the path to the required ZIP file, as specified in C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \support - Click the OK button to display this folder. - In this folder, locate the .ZIP file, which has the following format support(day-month-year)Hour-minute.zip, select the .ZIP file with the current date and the most recent time. - Copy this ZIP file to a computer that has email and manually open an email message, attach this ZIP file and add an appropriate Subject Line. - Type the Adroit Support email address into the Address edit box. - Send this email to specified email address. The Adroit support department will contact you as soon as they receive this file and will keep you informed regarding the progress of your Adroit query. -->

How to use Wanlink Top How to use Wanlink Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another.

Title: How to use Wanlink
How to use Wanlink Top How to use Wanlink Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). The following diagram and explanation, briefly describes how Wanlink works and how it is configured: Where: Computer 1 is the "primary" Agent Server (AS1), which obtains its IO from its remote outstations. WanServer is also running on this computer, which is connected to AS1, no other configuration is required. When a remote Agent Server connects to the primary Agent Server using Wanlink, the remote WanClient will connect to and upload its configuration to the WanServer . The WanServer will then establish connection to the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1) and communication based on this configuration will commence from then on. Computer 2 is a Remote node, which is able to view and control data on (AS1) directly because it on the same LAN. Note : Since this computer does not have its own Agent Server, it directly accesses the primary computer’s Agent Server (AS1). Computer 3, 4 are the "remote Agent Servers", these Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4), may or may not have local data derived from other IO sources. WanClient needs to be running on each of these computers. The Configuration file of each WanClient , must essentially specify how to communicate to the WanServer and which local tags in these remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) need to be "linked" to tags that reside in the primary Agent Server (AS1) and the communication settings to its WanServer connected to the primary Agent Server (AS1). Note: It is not necessary to link to all the tags in the primary Agent Server (AS1), only link those tags that are required. The WanClient configuration, is performed using the WanClient Configurator , in the following order: - A server must be added , which contains the configuration necessary to communicate with the WanServer computer, the primary Agent Server (AS1) in this case and it specifies the database that will contain the links that need to be communicated. Note: This server is "remote" in that it is on the other side of the WAN from the computer that is running WanClient . - Now the tags that are required to be linked must be grouped and these groups must be added . The following criteria need to be considered, when group the tags into groups: - The primary consideration should be the type of communication is required between the two Agent Servers: - Select a Normal group, for links that require a one-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are only able to view the value of a "linked" tag and any changes made to this tag will not be made to its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1). - Select a Control group, for links that require a two-way communication, so that the remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) are able to modify the value of a "linked" tag and its associated tag on the primary Agent Server (AS1) will reflect this change. Note: With this method of linking a remote Agent Server ( Computers 3 and 4 ) can operate as if it was a remote node ( Computer 2 ) of the primary Agent Server it is being connected to ( Computer 1 ).

- The secondary consideration is the poll rate of the tags or the rate at which the WanClient will ask for changes from the WanServer , which only affects tag links that have been configured to be polled (this is described below).

Title: How to use Wanlink
- The secondary consideration is the poll rate of the tags or the rate at which the WanClient will ask for changes from the WanServer , which only affects tag links that have been configured to be polled (this is described below). - Once the tag groups have been created, the specific tag links must be added to their respective groups. When creating tag links, the following methods of linking can be used: - Polling , in which case the WanClient will ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer at a fixed rate, so that in this case the WanClient will requests the tag from the primary Agent Server (AS1) every x seconds. This method also requires tags with the same poll period to be grouped in the same group. - Subscribed , in which case the WanClient will only ask for changes to this tag from the WanServer on startup and when the value of the tag changes, this is recommended for critical data, since it is a more efficient method of linking tags over a WAN. Note: This is also possible to manually edit the CSV files in which the links , tag groups and servers are stored, in order to perform bulk configurations etc. PLEASE NOTE 1: The full tag description must be specified when configuring a remote or local link in the WanClient e.g. "MYDIGITAL.rawValue" If the slot name is omitted, the tag link will fail. PLEASE NOTE 2: Historical data cannot be transferred over Wanlink, only current runtime values will be sent and retrieved. It is possible for a linked tag on a remote Agent Server (AS3),(AS4) to be logged as usual, but then Wanlink connection must be maintained at all times to ensure that no "holes" in the remote datalogs occur. -->

Title: Display the Diagnostic Counters screen for the device
- In this case click the following option: 2 Diagnostic Counters . Note: The Error-log screen displays the live detailed reports of all the problems taking place within the Protocol Driver. This opens the Diagnostic Counters screen for this device, however the information that this screen displays depends upon the operational status of the device that you are viewing. The status you can determine from the icon of the device as displayed in the Device name list, as follows: Tip: One of the Options... of the Driver Monitor allow you to configure how fast these statuses are updated. In this case the BATCHOPC device is idle, so the following information is displayed by the Diagnostic Counters screen: Tip: If necessary, you can take a screenshot of this window and send it along with a Datascope log to the support. These counters are all zeroed when the Agent Server starts, and for some drivers, also when the device agent starts. These diagnostic counters can be used to troubleshoot your device communication problems, by providing the following information: - “ Transactions ” increment every-time a transaction succeeds. A transaction fetches one or more data points. - “ Retry's ” increment every-time a transaction is retried. - xxx errors increment when there is a problem communicating. For example, Write errors increment when DTR signaling is configured but not received; by device failure or the cable not having that line wired in. - xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: - Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. - Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. - Retry’s: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. - Port switches: If a secondary resource is allowed, this count is the number of times the driver switched between primary and secondary channels. - Protocol errors: This counter generally indicates invalid device responses, which are not legal or are unrecognised. - Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage. - Read errors: The number of times the driver failed to read an expected response. - Read timeouts: The number of times the driver failed to receive a response to a request, within the required time. - Write errors: The number of times the driver failed to send data because of a hardware problem. - Write timeouts: The number of times the driver timed out while waiting to send data because of a hardware problem. - Transactions/sec: This represents the number of successful transactions performed per second. -->

Steps:
To configure data binding, we first need to create an OLEDB datasource which will connect to our SQL Server database: For this example we will add an OLEDB datasoure that will connect to our Northwind database on our SQL Server. - Launch and login to the Designer and then right-click on the Datasources node of the Enterprise Manager tree and select Add Datasources , then select OLE DB and click Finish . Example: - In the Add A New OLEDB Datasource dialog, specify a name for your OLEDB datasource, in this case Northwind and click the browse (...) button to the right of the Connection String edit field to display the Connection Properties dialog. - In the Connection Properties dialog select Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server from the OLE DB Provider list and click the Data Links… button. Typically do NOT change the Data source from the default of .NET Framework Data Provider for OLE DB , unless you are connecting to a SQL Compact database. More details: in which case, click the Change... button and choose the datasource that corresponds to the correct version of SQL Compact and then the dialog will change so that you only need to browse in the required database file and specify the required password, if any. Example: - In the Data Link Properties dialog enter the required details to connect to your SQL Server database and then click Finish . Example: - In the Connection Properties dialog click Test Connection to verify that the connection details are correct and that we can connect to the SQL Server database and then click OK . Example: - Click Finish in the Add A New OLEDB Datasource dialog to add this new OLEDB datasource to the Server. Our newly added OLEDB datasource, in this case Northwind, should be listed under the Datasources node in the Enterprise Manager tree listing all the tables, views and stored procedures for this SQL Server database that you are connected too. Example: Back to top

text:
In order to bind controls to data in a specific table in our database we first need to create a server-side DataBinder in the OLEDB datasource, as follows: - Right-click on the DataBinders node of this OLEDB datasource in the the Enterprise Manager tree and click Add DataBinder .

Title: Creating a DataBinder for this OLEDB datasource
In order to bind controls to data in a specific table in our database we first need to create a server-side DataBinder in the OLEDB datasource, as follows: - Right-click on the DataBinders node of this OLEDB datasource in the the Enterprise Manager tree and click Add DataBinder . Example: - In the Add DataBinder dialog provide a descriptive name for your DataBinder as below, in this case CustomersDB, and click Next . - Select the tables and fields you wish to write and/or read data to and from. IMPORTANT: If you are writing data back to the database you need to make sure the primary key field of the selected table is also selected. This is mandatory as data binding requires a primary key field so that it is able to distinguish which rows in your table need to be updated or deleted. Example: - Click Next and then click Finish as for this example we are not going to do any further configuration. Tip: The Add DataBinder dialog allows you to configure multiple table relationships, constraints on rows and ordering of certain fields and adding custom views. For more information, see Adding DataBinders . Your newly added DataBinder, in this case CustomersDB, should now be listed under the DataBinders node of your OLEDB datasource tree. text:
In order to data bind to controls on your graphic form, you need to add a VIZNETDataBinder component to the relevant graphic form: - Drag this component from the Data category of your Toolbox window onto your graphic form.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
In order to data bind to controls on your graphic form, you need to add a VIZNETDataBinder component to the relevant graphic form: - Drag this component from the Data category of your Toolbox window onto your graphic form. Example: This displays the VIZNET Data Binder Configuration dialog, in which you need to select the OLEDB datasource you are using as well as the you just configured and you need to select (check) the table you wish to write and/or read data to and from. For this example we are connecting to our OLEDB datasource called Northwind and using our DataBinder called CustomersDB and binding to the Customers table in the Northwind database. Example: This VIZNETDataBinder component can create and bind controls for you to your tables and their fields on your graphic form which will allow your users to read and edit the data from your tables. We will now configure the VIZNETDataBinder component to create edit controls and a DataGrid on to your graphic form which will be bounded (linked) to the selected table and fields. - On the right-side tab control, in the Required Field Controls tab, check Select All Field Controls , which in this case, ensures that you will create and bind (link) edit controls on your graphic form to each selected field, although you can also manually select which fields you want. You can also specify the order of the fields by moving the fields up and down in the specific order you want with the up/down arrow buttons on the right hand side. Example: - In the Required DataGrid Columns tab, check the Select All DataGrid Columns , which in this case, ensures that you will display all the fields as columns on the DataGrid control that will be created on your graphic form and bounded (linked) to the selected table and fields, although you can also manually select which DataGrid columns you want. Again you can also specify the order of the columns by moving the columns up and down in the specific order you want with the up/down arrow buttons on the right hand side. Example: - Click Finish and the VIZNET DataBinder component will create all the necessary edit controls and DataGrids to your graphic form and bind them to the selected table and fields of your DataBinder. Title: Configuration
Steps:
The VIZNETDataBinder component does provide some additional post configuration options, accessed by clicking the glyph of this component (at the bottom of the graphic form) to display its VIZNETDataBinder Tasks menu. Example: The following Tasks menu options are important: - Auto Load – to automatically load data from the selected tables into their bounded controls when the graphic form runs. This Auto Load functionality can also be accomplished by using the DataBinder Trigger spider. For more details, see Updating changes made to a DataBinder table or Fetching data from a DataBinder table . - Max Records – this specifies how many records to fetch at a time per page. - Refresh Data – this specifies how to handle refreshing of the data on the edit controls and DataGrid when data is changed in the selected table in the SQL Server database. You can select one of the following three settings: - Selecting the Manual setting will prompt the user if he wishes to refresh all edit controls and DataGrids with the new data. - Selecting the Auto setting will automatically refresh all edit controls and DataGrids with the new data without prompting the user (you will lose any changes that have not been committed). - Selecting the Ignore setting will not refresh all the edit controls and DataGrids with the new data (this has the potential of overriding any new data in the database table if someone has made a change to data in the table before you have committed your changes.) -->
