Title: ICMP Agent - Database File Format
ICMP Agent - Database File Format Top ICMP Agent - Database File Format For a detailed description of any of its slots, see Slot Details . See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description ADDR==nnn.nnn.nnn.nnn IP address of the network device. ENABLED=n A Boolean value indicating whether ICMP message will be sent to the network device or not. RETRIES=n How many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable. TIMEOUT=nnnn How long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable. LSTEX=nnnnnnnnnn nnnnnnnn UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). FILETIME when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. FAILURES=nn The number of ICMP messages that were not received from the network device. INTVAL=n How often you want to check the availability of this device on the network, in seconds, also known as the required poll rate. HI=nnnn The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send a message to the network device and receive a reply has moved outside its acceptable range and therefore implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. HIHI=nnnn The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send and receive a message and from the network device has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. -->

Slot Name Type Function active BOOLEAN This is set to True when an ICMP message is being sent and/or received from the network device.

Title: Slots:
Slot Name Type Function active BOOLEAN This is set to True when an ICMP message is being sent and/or received from the network device. catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used for datalog and real-time data catch-up). disableStandby BOOLEAN Disable this agent on the standby Agent Server, when the Agent Server is being clustered. failure_Count INTEGER The number of ICMP messages that were not received from the specified ipAddress . hi INTEGER The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send a message to the network device and receive a reply has moved outside its acceptable range and therefore implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. hiHi INTEGER The time, in milliseconds, that indicates that the time to send and receive a message and from the network device has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and that urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. interval INTEGER How often you want to check the availability of this device on the network, in seconds, also known as the required poll rate. ipAddress STRING The IP address of the network device. Note: ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. last_Execution_Time TIME Specifies when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. pingNow BOOLEAN Performs an immediate ping. pingStatus STRING Provides a textual description of the status of the last ICMP message used to contact the device, as follows: - OK from [IP Address] if it succeeded; - Retries exhausted when retrying to contact the device (a timeout failure) and - Host unreachable from [IP Address] if it is not possible to contact the device. retries INTEGER Specify how many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable. roundTripTime INTEGER The time taken, in milliseconds, to send the last ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. start BOOLEAN This is used to enable/disable the sending of ICMP messages to the specified ipAddress . timeout INTEGER Specify how long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable. Note: If the specified timeout is too short then you will never get a "host unreachable" error because the network will not have the necessary time to respond.

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title: Specifications
Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 Healthy On when the last ICMP message was sent to and received from the network device successfully. status bit 17 General_Failure On when there is any failure preventing the network device from being accessed. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy). status bit 18 Destination_Unreachable On when the failure is caused because the destination IP address is not reachable on the current network, for instance when no routing is available to reach this IP address range. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when a timeout failure occurs. status bit 19 Destination_Timeout On when the failure is caused because no response has been received from the remote device within the configured timeout value. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when the remote device becomes unreachable. status bit 20 High On when the last round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. (INTEGER roundTripTime slot) is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hi slot). status bit 21 High-high On when the last round trip time is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high-high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hiHi slot). status bit 22 Busy On when an ICMP message is in the process of being sent and/or received from the network device.

Manual.

Note: ONLY IP addresses can be specified, so if you need to contact a web address, you need to resolve this to an IP address first. last_Execution_Time TIME Specifies when the last attempt to contact the device occurred. pingNow BOOLEAN Performs an immediate ping. pingStatus STRING Provides a textual description of the status of the last ICMP message used to contact the device, as follows: - OK from [IP Address] if it succeeded; - Retries exhausted when retrying to contact the device (a timeout failure) and - Host unreachable from [IP Address] if it is not possible to contact the device. retries INTEGER Specify how many times you want to query the availability of the network device before determining that it is unavailable. roundTripTime INTEGER The time taken, in milliseconds, to send the last ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. start BOOLEAN This is used to enable/disable the sending of ICMP messages to the specified ipAddress . timeout INTEGER Specify how long you want to wait, in milliseconds, to receive a response from the device before you determine that this device is unavailable. Note: If the specified timeout is too short then you will never get a "host unreachable" error because the network will not have the necessary time to respond.

Impersonating users Top Impersonating users When implementing SmartUI Server security you can create users that impersonate or masquerade as an existing allowed user.

Title: Impersonating users
Impersonating users Top Impersonating users When implementing SmartUI Server security you can create users that impersonate or masquerade as an existing allowed user. Click for more details: For instance, when users are not part of the Windows security or where you do not want to expose a domain username and password when someone logs in to a Server over the Internet. The impersonated user is then able to log in to the Designer and Operator and merely assumes the security privileges and profile of the Allowed user being impersonated. Note1: Since impersonated users are virtual users that do not exist, they cannot be used to implement security or be added to a user profile. Note2: You need to know the password of the allowed user that you want to impersonate. To impersonate an allowed user: Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Management category. - Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Expand the Users and Groups icon . - Expand the Users icon . - Right-click the Impersonated Users icon or its name and select Set Impersonated User . The Set Impersonated User configuration dialog is launched. - Under the Actual User group, select the name and password of the allowed user that is to be impersonated, as follows: - Select the name of the allowed user that is to be impersonated from the Actual User list. This list only contains the names of the allowed users configured on the Server. - Type in this allowed user’s password in the Password Of Selected User edit box. - Under the Impersonation group, specify the log in details for the virtual or impersonating user, as follows: - Type in the user name for this user in the Username edit box. - Type in the password for this user in the Password edit box and re-type it in the Confirm Password edit box. Tip1: You can use any character for the user name or password. Tip2: As in Windows the user name and password is case sensitive. To remove an impersonated user: Expand the Security component of the required SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Management category. - Click the plus box to the left of the Security icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the security components by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Expand the Users and Groups icon . - Expand the Users icon . - Expand the Impersonated Users icon . - Right-click the name of the required impersonated user or its icon and select Remove Impersonated User . WARNING! When you remove an impersonated user, it is immediately removed. -->

- Before setting up the SNMPManager agent, decide which devices you need to monitor.

Title: To implement SNMPManager agents to monitor a physical industrial network:
- Before setting up the SNMPManager agent, decide which devices you need to monitor. In other words determine the (SNMP) network topology. Tip: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualize the network, because this also assists in quickly detecting of the source of network bottlenecks too. Example of a typical SNMP monitoring mimic: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualize the (SNMP) network topology, not only because it helps in deciding which devices are going to be monitored but more importantly, because the source of bottlenecks can then easily be detected on such a mimic. Consider the example mimic below, where the different lights indicate whether a computer is deemed ‘healthy’ in terms of its bandwidth use or not. For instance a red light might indicate high bandwidth usage on a certain computer running an important network-driven process. - In the case of the network described by this mimic, it would be necessary to configure seven SNMPManager agents on the computer running the Agent Server. In other words one SNMPManager agent is required for each networked device that you need to manage. For details of the issues concerning the monitoring of computers by SNMP, see Usage Requirements . Note: Each networked device must have its own fixed IP Address. - Configure each of these SNMPManager agents to get and/or set the required OID values of their devices. For details, see Configuring SNMPManager Agents . Note: In addition to browsing the device for its SNMP objects, the SNMPManager agent also provides a collection of commonly used statistics for device management, known as General objects. For details, see Selecting General SNMP Objects . Some of these statistics are calculated from two or more OIDs, which are common to all devices. For instance, in this example, the ‘Bandwidth’,‘Unicast Packets/s’ and ‘Errors/Min’ are all examples of such calculated statistics. - Once the monitoring process has begun, the SNMPManager agent will start: - Polling : to receive values from the device and copy them into the associated tags. Which you can then trend, alarm or log in Adroit : For instance, it is possible to trend object information such as bandwidth; alarm certain conditions on the network, such a computer becoming unavailable and log information, which allows you to determine at which point in history an error or certain condition of the network has occurred, such as its degree of congestion etc. - Writing: to change values of the device when the value of their associated tags change. - Trapping: to receive events from the device, which are placed in a queue that you will typically interrogate by means of a script and respond to the important ones. Tip: If an SNMP trap identifies an OID that is not in the list then you can manually poll and/or manually write to it too. -->

Property / (Category) Function (Alarm) Alarmcolors This property allows the selection of the foreground (text) and background colors used to represent the state of each alarm displayed in the alarm list. For details, see Selecting alarm colors . AlarmColumnInfo This property allows the selection of which columns of information will be displayed by this control when listing the alarms and the order in which they are displayed and their column widths. For details, see Configuring alarm columns . For details, see Connecting alarm lists to AlarmViewer controls . Note: You can create template Adroit Alarm Viewer controls, since the Alarm List / Alarm Agent value supports the use of curly brackets {} to create an alias for SmartUI Templates or a data element substitution for wizards. updateThreshold This prevents the AlarmViewer control from updating too rapidly when its specified alarm list changes too frequently. Setting this to 0 disables this functionality, which is its default setting. AlarmType This property is used to specify the type of agent that is being used to display this list of alarms, either an AlarmAgent or an AlarmListAgent . AlarmDateTime Formatting This allows a format string to specified to customise the display of the dates and times displayed within this control, by using one or more of the following data and time format specifiers: Commonly used date and time format specifiers: These produce standard date and time formats. These date and time format strings, consist of a single format specifier character from the following table. Note: If the format string is longer than a single character (even if the extra characters are white spaces), the format string is interpreted as a custom format string. The following table describes these standard date and time format strings. Note1: The output produced by some of these format specifiers is influenced by the current Regional Options settings. Computers using different settings will generate different results. Note2: The example outputs specified in this table assume that a DateTime value of 8/20/2004 11:12:45 AM is assigned to input 0. Alternatively this can be disabled so that the user is able to set how many alarms should be displayed instead. This setting determines the initial setting of the Show All checkbox of this control. MaxAlarmsVisible This Integer property can be used to set the initial number of alarms that can be displayed by this control, by default this is 50. This setting determines the initial setting of the Maximum Alarms Visible spin control of this control. Tip: This property can be used to only show the most recent alarms, when the Alarm Time column is sorted in descending order. -->

Important charting control properties Top Important charting control properties This describes the functions of some of the more important properties that can be used to configure the charting controls.

Title: Important charting control properties
Steps:
Important charting control properties Top Important charting control properties This describes the functions of some of the more important properties that can be used to configure the charting controls. Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. General charting properties: properties that display the charting toolbar, enable the chart to configured in runtime and change the main title of this chart, amongst others Property Function AntiAliased This Boolean property, which is True by default, uses antialiasing to smooth the edges of the drawn chart. Note: You can turn this off to improve the charting speed but then the chart will appear more jagged. DataLegendDigits This Integer property allows you to specify the number of significant places to use when values are rounded off in the data Legend. Direct2DMode This Boolean property, which is False by default, uses GDI+ to chart the data, which is slower as the charting is only performed by the CPU and by the graphics card. When you set this property to True, then the charting is done using Direct2D, which is faster as this is performed using the graphics card and not the CPU. PrintingSettings Allows you to configure the default print settings that are applied when this chart is printed, by configuring the following sub-properties accordingly: - Grayscale : By default this is False to print the chart in full color, but if set to True it will print the chart in shades of grey (greyscale). - Landscape : By default this is False to print the chart in portrait orientation mode, but if set to True it will print the chart using the landscape orientation mode. - MarginUnits : Either specified as a HundredthsInch (hundredths of an inch) or as Percent. - PrintPanelBackground : Prints a transparent Chart Panel when set to False. - Proportional : Sets the print dimensions of the chart proportional to those onscreen when set to True. - Resolution : Sets chart printing detail resolution, from 1 to 100. - UseAntiAlias : By default this is False to print the chart using standard printing quality, but if set to True it will print the chart using high printing quality using a higher pixel resolution. Title This String property can specify the name of this chart. Note: If this property is cleared i.e. a blank string then more space is provided within the control for charting the data. ToolbarVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the charting toolbar. This toolbar allows end users allows your end-users to print and/or preview the chart, rotate the chart and if necessary chart additional data, amongst other actions. For details, see Charting control toolbar . Note: This toolbar is best suited to real time trending, as it allows one to move back and forward between the historical and real time data. For details, see the TimeInfo property below. View3D This Boolean property determines whether this chart is by default displayed in three dimensional view or not, by appropriately configuring the View chart in 3D mode toolbar button. ViewName This String property, determines whether the configuration changes performed by the Runtime Configuration toolbar button will be saved, as follows: - If empty, the runtime configuration of series will NOT be saved. - If not empty, this specifies the name of the variable that is used to save the runtime configuration of series to the profile of the currently logged in user. For details, see Configuring charted series at runtime . Note1: If a value is specified, this automatically enables the (Appearance) ViewButtonEnable property to display the Runtime Configuration toolbar button. Note2: If the value is deleted, this automatically disables the (Appearance) ViewButtonEnable property.

However, this property can still be manually enabled if necessary, although any runtime configuration will then NOT be saved.

Title: Important charting control properties
Steps:
However, this property can still be manually enabled if necessary, although any runtime configuration will then NOT be saved. Line, Surface and XYPlot charting control properties: properties that display the data legendand configure its height and column widths and visibility, display toolbar buttons and configure the charting time interval amongst others. Property / (Category) Function Badcolor This specifies the line color that is used to indicate that the plotted points have a bad status i.e. when data points are missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated. Data Legend-specific properties: DataLegendVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the data legend that appears at the bottom of this control, which is used to display statistical information concerning the charted values. For details, see Operating charting controls . Note: The data legend settings only apply if the data legend of this charting control is displayed, which is determined by the (Appearance) DataLegendVisible property. DataLegendHeight This Integer property allows the height of the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. Note: Depending on the number of series, this size could result in one or more of the series not being displayed by the data legend grid, in which case use the scroll bar to see the hidden series. Data LegendHeightAutosize This Boolean property toggles the ability to automatically increase the size of the data legend grid to display all the trended series. SeriesWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Series column in the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. MinWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Minimum column in the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. MinVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Minimum column in the data legend of this charting control. MaxWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Maximum column in the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. MaxVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Maximum column in the data legend of this charting control. AveWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Average column in the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. AveVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Average column in the data legend of this charting control. CurrentWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Current column in the data legend of this charting control to be specified, in pixels. CntWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Count column in the data legend to be specified, in pixels. CntVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Count column in the data legend of this charting control. SDevWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Std Dev column in the data legend to be specified, in pixels. SDevVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Std Dev column in the data legend of this charting control. ErrorsWidth This Integer property allows the width of the Errors column in the data legend to be specified, in pixels. ErrorsVisible This Boolean property can hide (False) or display (True the default) the Errors column in the data legend of this charting control. Charting data-specific properties: ExtrapolateData This Boolean property toggles the ability of charted data to be extrapolated from its last known value.

In other words, when the value of a charted series is not received, instead of inserting a gap in the trend where this value should have been, its last known value is charted instead.

Title: Important charting control properties
Steps:
In other words, when the value of a charted series is not received, instead of inserting a gap in the trend where this value should have been, its last known value is charted instead. HistoricalDataSampleRate This Integer property, mainly applies to the LineChart series and serves to limit the retrieved number of historical data points to improve the performance of historical trending. This data sampling rate is specified in milliseconds. Historical data sampling is AUTOMATICALLY DISABLED when the specified sample rate is SMALLER than 10 x your current time frame window. In other words, the default sample rate of 5 seconds is only applied when the time frame window is greater than 50 seconds. Setting this sample rate to 0 PERMANENTLY DISABLES historical data sampling and always returns all the available historical data. TimeInfo This composite property contains a number of sub-properties that specify the time-specific properties for the chart, as follows: Note1: This property only applies to Line and XYPlot charts. Note2: This property can also be configured at runtime, but any changes made will not be saved. For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime . RealTime This Boolean property determines whether the trending will be real-time (True) or historical (False). This also determines which of its sub-properties need to be configured to set the required trending period: - Real time trending: When RealTime is True, then the initial view of the trend will display data scrolling in realtime. When the trend is opened, it will fetch the historical data (if there is any) for the initial data period. This trending period is calculated as follows: - TimeSpan This specifies the time period that the real-time trend window displays. This value can be specified, as follows: "[-]d.hh:mm:ss.ff, where: "-" is an optional sign for negative TimeSpan values, the "d" component is days, "hh" is hours, "mm" is minutes, "ss" is seconds, and "ff" is fractions of a second. Note1: If an integer is typed into this value box it will be assumed to be a multiple of days. Note2: The StartTime and EndTime properties are meaningless for real time trending. - Interval This specifies the required update rate for the trended data (in milliseconds) i.e. how often the trend must update with the latest real time data and shift the data across the screen. - Historical trending: When RealTime is False, then the initial view of the trend will display the historical data specified between the start and end time, although it is also possible to view data that is being logged currently too. This trending period is calculated as follows: - TimeSpan This specifies the interval that is required between the StartTime and EndTime . This value can be specified, as follows: "[-]d.hh:mm:ss.ff, where: "-" is an optional sign for negative TimeSpan values, the "d" component is days, "hh" is hours, "mm" is minutes, "ss" is seconds, and "ff" is fractions of a second. Note: If an integer is typed into this value box it will be assumed to be a multiple of days. - StartTime This specifies the date and time, in the past, at which the trend is required to begin. This date and time is displayed in the format specified by your current Regional Settings. - EndTime This specifies the date and time, in the past, at which the trend is required to end. This date and time is displayed in the format specified by your current Regional Settings. Note1: The TimeSpan , StartTime and EndTime properties are all linked i.e.

changing the StartTime will recalculate the EndTime using the specified TimeSpan .

Title: Important charting control properties
Steps:
changing the StartTime will recalculate the EndTime using the specified TimeSpan . Note2: The Interval property is not required for static trends. Tip: You can configure the (Data) HistoricalDataSampleRate property to improve the performance of historical trending. Toolbar - specific properties: PageLeftVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Page Left toolbar button used to move back quickly in time. PageRightVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Page Right toolbar button used to move forward in time. ScrollLeftVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Scroll Left toolbar button used to move back in time. ScrollRealTimeVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Go to real time mode toolbar button used to move forward in time until the real time values of the data are displayed. ScrollRightVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Scroll Right toolbar button used to move forward quickly in time. ScrollLineButtonVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Scroll line to view historical values toolbar button used to enable/disable a vertical black and blue scroll line to display these historical values in the data legend. Tip: Enable the (ScrollLine) ShowScrollLineMarkers property, to display the point at which each scroll line intersects the series of the chart, by means of a dot, which has the same color as the series. TimeDetailsButtonEnabled This Boolean property toggles the enabling of the Modify the time details toolbar button that allows the charted time period to be altered in runtime mode. For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime . Note: If this property is disabled, while the TimeDetailsButtonVisible property is enabled then this button will appear greyed out in the toolbar. TimeDetailsButtonVisible This Boolean property toggles the display of the Modify the time details toolbar button. ViewButtonEnable This Boolean property toggles the display of the Runtime Configuration toolbar button that allows series (data elements) to be added to the chart in runtime mode. For details, see Configuring charted series at runtime . Note: Any series (data elements) that are added at runtime will ONLY be saved if the (Behaviour) ViewName property is NOT empty. -->

Important DataGrid properties Top Important DataGrid properties The following list describes the functions of some of the more important properties that can be used to configure this control: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window.

Title: Important DataGrid properties
Steps:
Important DataGrid properties Top Important DataGrid properties The following list describes the functions of some of the more important properties that can be used to configure this control: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. Tip: Since ONLY ONE table can be displayed by the DataGrid control there is no need to configure properties that are concerned with multi-table or related table navigation etc. Property / (Category) Function (Appearance) BorderStyle This determines how the borders of this control are displayed. GridLineStyle This determines how the grid lines between the cells of this control are displayed. CaptionText This String property can be used to specify the text that should appear in the blue bar at the top of this control, this text is displayed in the font specified by CaptionFont . Note: This only need to be specified if the caption is displayed, see CaptionVisible . Font This specifies the font that is used when displaying text within the control. (colors) Forecolor This is the color of the text (the font color) used when displayed data in the rows of the grid. Note: Any Fore… color indicates the text color (font color) that will be used. Backcolor This is the background color of the cells when displaying data within the even-numbered rows of the grid i.e. rows 0, 2, 4, 6 etc. Default is white. Note: Be careful to select a color that will not obscure the reading of display of the data. Use the colors available on the System colors palette to avoid this issue. AlternatingBackcolor This is the background color of the cells when displaying data within the odd-numbered rows of the grid i.e. rows 1, 3, 5, 7 etc. Default is white. This color therefore creates a visual means of differentiating successive rows in the grid. Note: Be careful to select a color that will not obscure the reading of display of the data. Use the colors available on the System colors palette to avoid this issue. Backgroundcolor This determines the color behind the grid itself, for instance if only a few rows are contained in the grid. (Data) DataSource This property should be connected to the required data element of type dataset. For details, see Connecting datasets to DataGrid controls . (Display) CaptionVisible This displays or hides the caption i.e. the blue bar that at the top of this control by default. Note: If this is hidden then more data can be displayed within this control. ColumnHeadersVisible This displays or hides the column headings within the grid. -->

Autosize This property affects the way in which the available space in the TableLayoutPanel control is allocated for each column and row when this TableLayoutPanel control is auto sized and hence affects how the configured sizeType property of each row and column style operate, as follows: false The TableLayoutPanel control proceeds from left to right, and allocates space for the column or row or in the following order.

Title: Auto sizing
Steps:
Autosize This property affects the way in which the available space in the TableLayoutPanel control is allocated for each column and row when this TableLayoutPanel control is auto sized and hence affects how the configured sizeType property of each row and column style operate, as follows: false The TableLayoutPanel control proceeds from left to right, and allocates space for the column or row or in the following order. - If the sizeType property is set to Absolute , this allocates the number of pixels specified by the width or height of the TableLayoutPanel control. - If the sizeType property is set to Autosize , this allocates the minimum number of pixels to fully contain the largest control in the column/row. - After space for all Absolute and Autosize columns or rows is allocated, any columns or rows with sizeType set to Percent are used to proportionally allocate the remaining free space. true Similar to the previous interaction, with the exception that the Percent columns or rows are treated as if they were Autosize . For details on editing the sizeType property, see Setting row heights and column widths in the TableLayoutPanel .

CellBorderStyle This property determines if the cell is outlined with a border or not.

Title: Layout
CellBorderStyle This property determines if the cell is outlined with a border or not. By default no border is displayed (None), however you can specify the following options: ◦ - None – No borders. - Single – A single-line border. - Inset – A single-line sunken border. - InsetDouble – A double-line sunken border. - Outset – A single-line raised border. - OutsetDouble – A double-line raised border. - OutsetPartial – A single-line border containing a raised portion. Columns Launches the Column and Row Styles editor, setting the Show field to Columns to edit the sizeType property of the available column styles that determines how the available space in the TableLayoutPanel control is allocated for each column. For details on editing this sizeType property, see Setting row heights and column widths in the TableLayoutPanel . Note: This sizeType property is affected by the current Autosize TableLayoutPanel property setting. Rows Launches the Column and Row Styles editor, setting the Show field to Rows to edit the sizeType property of the available row styles that determines how the available space in the TableLayoutPanel control is allocated for each row. For details on editing this sizeType property, see Setting row heights and column widths in the TableLayoutPanel . Note: This sizeType property is affected by the current Autosize TableLayoutPanel property setting. Note: The ColumnCount and RowCount properties are automatically incremented/decremented when you add and remove rows and columns in design time and the GrowStyle property appears to be ignored.

Layout For details on laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel control, see Laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel .

Title: Inherited control properties
Layout For details on laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel control, see Laying out controls in a TableLayoutPanel . ColumnSpan This integer value, whose default value is 1, allows this control to occupy (span) more than one (rightmost) columns in addition to the column that it is currently in. Note: After setting this property, you need resize this control accordingly to occupy all or part of the allocated columns. RowSpan This integer value, whose default value is 1, allows this control to occupy (span) more than one (bottommost) row in addition to the row that it is currently in. Note: After setting this property, you need resize this control accordingly to occupy all or part of the allocated rows. Location Cell The current position or location of this control in the table, specified by the Column , Row properties. Column The (vertical) column in which this control is located, which is an integer starting from 0 (the first column). Note: This property cannot be externally driven to change the location of a control within the TableLayoutPanel control's table. Row The (horizontal) row in which this control is located, which is an integer starting from 0 (the first row). Note: This property cannot be externally driven to change the location of a control within the TableLayoutPanel control's table. -->

Important TemplateGO properties Top Important TemplateGO properties Although a TemplateGO control appears to have the same properties as a standard graphic form, it also exposes the following additional properties: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window.

Title: Important TemplateGO properties
Steps:
Important TemplateGO properties Top Important TemplateGO properties Although a TemplateGO control appears to have the same properties as a standard graphic form, it also exposes the following additional properties: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. Property / (Category) Function Autosize This Boolean property determines whether this control will automatically resize itself to display a graphic form, if this control is smaller than the graphic form that it contains. This is disabled (False) by default. AutoScroll This Boolean property either enables or disables scrollbars that appear if the control is smaller than the graphic form that it contains. This is disabled (False) by default. Note1: Its sub-properties determine how much smaller the graphic form needs to be before these scrollbars appear. Note2: By enabling the Autosize property this control will initially be resized to the size of the graphic form it contains, after which its size can be adjusted as necessary. Aliases This property exposes any specified aliases of the hosted graphic form (properties of its form components), so that values can be assigned to them, if required. For details, see Working with aliases . AutoResize This Boolean property enables or disables the automatic resizing of the control to fit the size of the graphic form that it is hosting. This feature is disabled (False) by default. GraphicForm Although this property can be used to specify which graphic form is contained by this control it is not generally recommended because the specified graphic form will ONLY be loaded at runtime. In other words, the specified graphic from will ONLY be displayed when the graphic from containing the control is opened in Run mode or when using the Operator. This property also requires the required graphic form to be manually linked to it. For details on using this property, see Connecting TemplateGO controls to graphic forms . GraphicFormPath This is the generally recommended method of specifying which graphic form is contained by this control. Click on the provided browse button and browse in the graphic form that you want to contain within this control. The specified graphic form will immediately be displayed in this control in the Design viewing mode, so that any further configuration can easily be performed. For details on using this property, see Connecting TemplateGO controls to graphic forms . MaxDepth Given that the TemplateGO is a control within a graphic form, that can contain a graphic form itself, it is possible for circular references to be created i.e. for this control to display its own graphic form. In this case, instead of opening an infinite number of graphic forms, this Integer property specifies the maximum number of instances of each graphic form that can be opened. For instance if MaxDepth is set to 2 and GraphicFormA contains TemplateGOControlA, which hosts GraphicFormB containing TemplateGOControlB, which hosts GraphicFormA – then 2 instances of GraphicFormA and 2 instances of GraphicFormB will be opened. Run This Boolean property is able to start and stop the spider engine (spider workspace), associated with the graphic form that this control is hosting. By default, this is enabled (True) so that the spider workspace of the contained graphic form is started. Subscribe This Boolean property, determines whether the graphic form that is contained within the TemplateGO control will display any changes that are made to its original after it has been contained or not, as follows: - If it is enabled (True) then any changes made to the original graphic form will immediately appear in the graphic form contained within the TemplateGO control.

- If disabled (False), then the changes made to the original only appear when the graphic form containing the TemplateGO control is reloaded (refreshed).

Important TrendConfigurator properties Top Important TrendConfigurator properties The following properties are particularly useful when configuring TrendConfigurator controls , but can typically be configured via the Tasks menu and the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Important TrendConfigurator properties Top Important TrendConfigurator properties The following properties are particularly useful when configuring TrendConfigurator controls , but can typically be configured via the Tasks menu and the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog: Note: These properties can be viewed and configured in the Properties tool window. Property Function ChartName By default for new TrendConfigurator controls, the TrendConfigurator control will use the inbuilt LineChart. If you want the TrendConfigurator control to connect to an external LineChart control, then set the UseBuiltinChart property to False and select the required LineChart to link this control to (on the same graphic form) from this ChartName property. DataSourceMode Choose how (from which product) this TrendConfigurator control will obtain the tags (values) to use for the pens that will be charted, by selecting and configuring the required DataSource Mode : Note: Each mode provides its own data configuration which affect the default Column Settings that are available. - Adroit : In this case the tags (values) are located within an Adroit Agent Server, so specify the name of the required associated Adroit database, from the Adroit DataSource drop-down list. If you want default Adroit tags to be available for selection from the Pen drop-down list at runtime, then click the browse (...) button to the right of the Default Data Elements field to browse in a list of predefined tags that are unique to this TrendConfigurator control. Note: Any tags that you specify will always appear in the Pen drop-down list at runtime and cannot be removed from this list at runtime. Tip: This also be configured via the DefaultDataElements property (but not via the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog). If necessary, users can also browse in additional tags to the Pen drop-down list at runtime via the browse (...) button to the right of this field. Note: These additional tags can be removed from the Pen drop-down list at runtime, by selecting the required tag in the list and clicking the button on the right. Since this mode expects the list of tags that are to be charted to be directly browsed in, the Column Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog provide the following options: Note: Both the Area and Device columns are disabled and hidden as they are not used to locate the browsed in tags in this mode. - Pen: this column displays a drop-down list of all the browsed in tags. Specify the width (in pixels) of this column in the Pen (Tag Name) Column Width field. - Title: this is the Series name for this charted Pen . Specify the width (in pixels) of this column in the Title (Series Name) Column Width field. Note: By default this column displays the description of the tag as this is usually more descriptive than the tag name itself. However, if you want the series to display the tag name [AgentName.Property(Slot)Name] instead then uncheck the Use Pen (Tag) Description for Series Names instead of Tag Names checkbox in the General Settings tab (the UsePenDescForSeriesName property). - MAPS : In this case the tags (values) are located within a MAPS project so specify the required project from the MAPS Project drop-down list. You also need to select the name of the required associated Adroit database, from the Adroit DataSource drop-down list. This will expose all the tags that you want your users to trend (contained within the required plant areas and their devices) and automatically populates the provided lists with their values.

Since each MAPS project enforces an extended physical hierarchical structure of automation projects specified by the ISA S88 and S95 standards, when specifying which values (tags) need to be trended, the Column Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog provide the following options: Note: Of these columns only the Pen and Title is mandatory, both the Area and Device columns can be hidden if needed.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Since each MAPS project enforces an extended physical hierarchical structure of automation projects specified by the ISA S88 and S95 standards, when specifying which values (tags) need to be trended, the Column Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog provide the following options: Note: Of these columns only the Pen and Title is mandatory, both the Area and Device columns can be hidden if needed. - Area: this is the Area level of physical structure of automation projects described by the ISA S95 and S88 standards. The level above this is the Site level. The Area contains one or more Process Cells or PLCs, which in Adroit-speak are communicated to via Devices. Typically, when displayed this column provides a drop-down list of all the configured areas of this MAPS project. Note: If necessary, you can use the PresetArea property to specify a static value that is automatically selected for this column, that disables its drop-down list to prevent any other value from being specified. Tip: If necessary, hide this column from appearing in the control by unchecking the Show Area Column checkbox. Specify the width (in pixels) of this column in the Area Column Width field, which if it provides a list of values also needs to accommodate the width of the drop-down list button. - Device: this is the Process Cell level of physical structure of automation projects described by the ISA S95 and S88 standards. Which in SCADA projects equate to the PLCs of each defined plant Area. This is called Device, since Adroit uses a Device to communicate to each PLC, within a Plant Area . Each Device contains one or more values (Pens). Typically, when displayed this column provides a drop-down list of all the configured devices (for the specified area) of this MAPS project. Note: If necessary, you can use the PresetDevice property to specify a static value that is automatically selected for this column, that disables its drop-down list to prevent any other value from being specified. Tip: If necessary, hide this column from appearing in the control by unchecking the Show Device Column checkbox. Specify the width (in pixels) of this column in the Device Column Width field, which if it provides a list of values also needs to accommodate the width of the drop-down list button. - Pen: this is the Unit and Equipment module and the Control module levels of the physical structure of automation projects described by the ISA S95 and S88 standards. This contains the values (tags) within the specified Device . Important VIZNETDataBinder properties Top Important VIZNETDataBinder properties The VIZNETDataBinder component provides the following properties that manage how the data of its associated DataBinder DataBinders allow you to create a sub-set of the data contained within an OLE DB datasource to provide constant bi-directional communication with this database.

Title: Important VIZNETDataBinder properties
Important VIZNETDataBinder properties Top Important VIZNETDataBinder properties The VIZNETDataBinder component provides the following properties that manage how the data of its associated DataBinder DataBinders allow you to create a sub-set of the data contained within an OLE DB datasource to provide constant bi-directional communication with this database. This means that unlike the data returned by Select queries, this data can be viewed and/or modified and updated if it changes. is accessed: Note: All of these settings are in the Settings category. AutoLoad: Determines whether the associated VIZNETBindingNavigator controls initially fetch their data or not. If this is set to True, then when the graphic form is opened all the VIZNETBindingNavigator controls, associated with this component (as specified by the BindingNavigatorList property) immediately fetch the first page of records for their associated table or View (BindingSource component). Note1: In this case, all the parameters of the associated DataBinder, must have default values configured. Note2: The number of records fetched by each VIZNETBindingNavigator control is specified by the MaxRecords property. Note3: The AutoLoadList property allows you to select which tables you want to be automatically loaded. If this is set to False, the default value, then the user must press the Load Data button of each VIZNETBindingNavigator control individually. Note: This setting ONLY applies if you selected the Create Controls option when adding the VIZNETDataBinder component. AutoLoadList: Allows you to select which tables you want to be automatically loaded (by using the AutoLoad property). By default all the associated tables are selected, but if there are one or more tables that you do NOT want to AutoLoad, simply uncheck the checkbox of these tables, so that their data will NOT be automatically fetched. MaxRecords: Determines the maximum number of records retrieved from the database at any one time. By default this is 100. Configure this property to ensure that your users do not experience sizable delays when requesting further records. Since the larger this property the greater the potential delay that users could experience in waiting for this amount of records to be returned. The recommended size of this property is therefore dependant upon the average bandwidth of your users’ connection to the database. Click for more details: The default of 100 works well for both LAN and Internet usage. If you using Internet we recommend using less than or equal to 100. If you are using LAN then you may use more than 100, but this depends on how busy your network is. RefreshData: Determines what happens when external changes are made to the retrieved records. The following options are provided: • Manual: The default option in which a message box is displayed when the database is modified externally, asking whether the user wants the data updated to reflect the new changes. Use this option when you require the Operators of the system to be aware of any changes and want to ask them if they want to get the newest changes or not. • Auto: The data is immediately updated with the new changes. Use this option when there is only ONE client that changes the data in the database; while the other clients only view the data. You can also use this option if the VIZNETDatabinder is purely used for viewing the data. • Ignore: The data is NEVER updated with new changes. -->

Steps:
Importing Alarm Agents Top Importing Alarm Agents Bulk-alarming configuration can be performed by exporting Alarm agents, configuring them in a third party CSV editor and then importing them. Alarm agents can be imported INDIVIDUALLY, using the Import… button in the General tab of the Alarm agent edit dialog. Once this button is clicked, Adroit will look for the default import files for the selected Alarm agent in the current WGP file folder. These are the files that are created by Adroit when Alarm agents are exported. If these default files are found, then the user will be prompted to perform either a full (automated) import using these files ( Yes ) or a selective (manual) import ( No ). Note: If these files are NOT found then the Choose alarm types import file OR press 'Cancel' to bypass dialog is immediately displayed to perform a selective import. This same dialog is also displayed when No is selected in the Import alarm agent dialog. Alarm agents can only be imported individually because unlike other agents, THREE separate CSV files are created for EACH of the configured Alarm agents. It is therefore IMPORTANT to ensure that these 3 files are able to correctly relate to one another. For instance, the alarm types listed in the xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV file are referred to, by index, in the xxxxx-AGNTLST.CSV file. Therefore any alarm types added to the xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV file must be sorted in ascending order by column A and then column B. If not, the indexes in the xxxxx-AGNTLST.CSV file will be incorrect and will cause errors when importing this file. However, the recommended method of importing Alarm agents does away with the need of ensuring that these files are correctly sorted: -->

Title: Importing global project translations
Importing global project translations Top Importing global project translations Tip: Instead of importing translations, you can simply Push (copy) translations, either entirely or selectively to the required graphic form/s from the project translation table. This automatically adds any languages to the graphic form translation tables that are missing. For details, see Pushing translations to graphic forms You can import translations from the project translation table for the languages you have added to the graphic form translation table (NOT for the Graphic Form Language column whose header is bold and underlined). IMPORTANT: ONLY the translation entries (rows) of the imported language are imported, whose Graphic Form Language column entries MATCH in BOTH the graphic form and project translation tables! This is usually done to save time and effort and ensure that the common form components are consistently translated throughout the project. Note: You can only import ONE language of translations into the graphic form at a time. The following prerequisites MUST be met before the translation/s can be imported: - The default language of the profile of the currently logged on user must exist in both the graphic form and project translation tables. Note: You are unable to import translations for the default language column. - The language, whose translations are to be imported, must exist in both the graphic form and project translation tables. In addition, the translations for this language need to be configured in the project translation table. - ONLY the translation entries (rows) of the imported language are imported, whose Graphic Form Language column entries MATCH in BOTH the graphic form and project translation tables. Either a single translated value or all the translations for an entire language can be imported. To import a single translated value: - Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . - Open the Translation tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, add the required language first. For details, see Adding languages to graphic forms . - Right-click the translation that you want to be imported in the required language column. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. Import Language Cell Value . - If this translated value, exists in the global translation table will be inserted, otherwise an error message will be displayed. Note: If more than one translation exists, in the global translation table, for this translation then select the required translation from the list box. - Either press the ENTER key or click in another cell to continue translating or click the Finish button to close the translation table. To import all the translations for an entire language: - Ensure that the required graphic form is opened and displayed in the Design workspace . - Open the Translation tool window. For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, add the required language first. For details, see Adding languages to graphic forms . - Right-click on the required language column heading and select Import Language Values . WARNING! Any translation already made in this language column for a graphic form component in this graphic form that is different from its existing translation in the global translation table, will be overwritten. Note: If more than one translation exists, in the global translation table, then the first of these translations are used. - Either press the ENTER key or click in another cell to continue translating or click the Finish button to close the translation table. Including third-party form components Top Including third-party form components In addition to using the default form components provided by the Toolbox tool window, you can add third-party form components to further customise your graphic forms.

Title: Including third-party form components
Including third-party form components Top Including third-party form components In addition to using the default form components provided by the Toolbox tool window, you can add third-party form components to further customise your graphic forms. Click for more information: Before a third-party form component can be added to a graphic form, it needs to be added to the Toolbox tool window first. Note1: Any form components added to the Toolbox , will ONLY be stored in the profile assigned to the currently logged in user, if its Automatically update profile option is enabled. For details, see Customizing connections and work environment . This is stored in the User Profile Settings of your profile in the ToolboxItems variable. Note2: It is also possible to remove third-party form components. For details, see Removing custom form components . Adding third-party form components, involves the following two-step process: - Copy the files of the required form component(s) to the appropriate folder. - Add the third-party form component(s) to the Toolbox tool window. To copy the required form component(s) to the appropriate folder: - By default, the files for the required form component(s) need to be copied into the Plugins folder, which is relative to the installation folder of the SmartUI Designer, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . Note: The CustomControlsRelativePath setting of the SmartUI Designer designates the name of this sub-folder, which is the central repository for all custom form components. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Designer settings . - The category in which these form components will be listed in the Toolbox tool window, is determined, as follows: - The name of the category is usually determined by the name of the folder in which they are placed. Therefore instead of copying the files directly into this folder, it is possible to create one or more aptly named sub-folder(s) and copy these files into the required folder(s) instead. Note: Form components are also able to specify their required category programmatically. - By default, this icon identifies a custom category in the Toolbox tool window. However, this icon can also be customised, by placing an icon file called default.ico into each of the relevant folder(s) instead. To add the third-party form component(s) to the Toolbox: - If necessary, open the Toolbox tool window in the SmartUI Designer. - Right-click an existing category heading and select Add Controls . Note: The category, in which a form component is added, is dependent upon which form component is selected and NOT upon the category that is right-clicked. This displays the Custom Controls dialog, which alphabetically lists all the form components located within the specified custom controls folder (and its sub-folders). Tip1: Use the Name , Namespace , Assembly and/or Directory columns within this dialog to locate the required form components, as needed. Tip2: Select the column heading of a column to sort the list using this column and to change the sorting order between ascending and descending order. - If you cannot see a checkbox for the required control, click the Browse .NET Control button and browse to the file location, typically within the plugins folder and select the DLL of this control and click Open . This adds a checkbox for this control to the Custom Controls dialog. - Check the checkbox(es) of the required form component(s) that you want to add and click Finish . Tip: Double-clicking on a row, within this dialog, will check or empty its checkbox.

- The form component(s) are added to the Toolbox tool window within the category that is either specified by each form component itself or by the name of the folder in which it is located.

32 bit operating systems have a maximum of 4GB of addressable memory space.

Title: Implementation on a 32 bit operating system:
32 bit operating systems have a maximum of 4GB of addressable memory space. By default, Windows allows only 2GB per process and uses the other 2GB for Windows itself. To change this default, you need to do the following: - On 32 bit Windows Vista and later versions of Windows: Use the IncreaseUserVA element in BCDEdit . Click for more details: In other words specify the following command: BCDEdit /set [{ID}] increaseuserva Megabytes , where: - The /set command sets a boot entry option value in the boot configuration data store. - The {ID} is the GUID that is associated with the boot entry. If you do not specify an {ID}, the command modifies the current operating system boot entry. - The increaseuserva Megabytes specifies the amount of memory, in megabytes, that is available per proceess. This variable can have any value between 2048 (2 GB) and 3072 (3 GB) megabytes in decimal notation. Windows uses the remaining address space (4 GB minus the specified amount). Using the full 3 GB for this option CAN potentially cause the Agent Server (and/or other Windows applications) not too work, if Windows requires MORE THAN 1GB for dealing with this process. For instance: if the configuration of the Agent Server is such that the size of network packets between Adroit client and server components are too large, then Windows requires more memory for itself to handle the networking layers. In these cases, limit the amount of additional memory available to the process and hence increase the amount of memory available to Windows. - On 32 bit Windows Server 2003 and Windows XP, use the /3GB and optionally /USERVA parameters in the boot.ini file, which are ONLY valid for 32-bit versions of Windows on computers with x86 or x64-based processors. Click for more details: A standard boot.ini file is shown below: We strongly recommend that you add a new profile for 3GB operation as opposed to amending the one and only default profile . For instance, in the modified boot.ini file below, the last line allows the user to select "Microsoft Windows XP Professional /3GB" in addition to the default profile: The /3GB profile allows individual processes to use up to 3072 MB of virtual memory. The remaining 1GB is reserved for Windows.

Purpose: to graphically indicate the current value of an analogue (floating point) process variable (PV), by means of a sliding pointer along a horizontal or vertical range defined by the currently specified Maximum and Minimum engineering span of this Analogue process variable, while also indicating its currently specified normal operating range.

Title: Analogue Indicators
Purpose: to graphically indicate the current value of an analogue (floating point) process variable (PV), by means of a sliding pointer along a horizontal or vertical range defined by the currently specified Maximum and Minimum engineering span of this Analogue process variable, while also indicating its currently specified normal operating range. Description: A horizontal or vertical rectangle, whereby: - the normal operating range (the values between the High and Low alarm limits) is filled in light blue and - the minimum and maximum allowable range (the values between the High High and the High and the Low Low and the Low alarm limits) are filled in dark grey and - the minimum and maximum extremes (the values between the Engineering Maximum and the High High alarm limit and the Engineering Minimum and Low Low alarm limit) are filled in black and - the current value is indicated by means of dark blue triangle sliding pointer and - ONLY if the statsPeriod slot of the Analog agent representing this process variable is configured, then a directional arrow may also be displayed indicating the current direction of trend i.e. an arrow pointing up when the value is going up or another arrow pointing down when the value is going down or no arrow at all when the value is stable. For more details, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . PLEASE NOTE: This direction of trend is ONLY calculated by the Analog agent representing the process variable, when its statsPeriod slot is set to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10 (minutes), since the default value of 0 DISABLES the calculation of these statistics, since if used excessively they can affect performance. Tip: You can also configure the optional statsDirDev slot specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value (we recommend setting this value to 0.05).

The following analogue indicators are available: - Horizontal analogue indicators, where the minimum range is on the left and the maximum range is on the right and the sliding pointer is on the bottom, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Horizontal_v01: a small horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Horizontal_v01: a medium horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Horizontal_v01: a large horizontal analogue indicator - Vertical analogue indications, where the minimum range is on the bottom and the maximum range is on the top and the sliding pointer is on the right, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Vertical_v01: a small vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Vertical_v01: a medium vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Vertical_v01: a large vertical analogue indicator Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified.

Title: Analogue Indicators
The following analogue indicators are available: - Horizontal analogue indicators, where the minimum range is on the left and the maximum range is on the right and the sliding pointer is on the bottom, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Horizontal_v01: a small horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Horizontal_v01: a medium horizontal analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Horizontal_v01: a large horizontal analogue indicator - Vertical analogue indications, where the minimum range is on the bottom and the maximum range is on the top and the sliding pointer is on the right, in the following sizes: wzdAnalogueIndicator_Small_Vertical_v01: a small vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Medium_Vertical_v01: a medium vertical analogue indicator wzdAnalogueIndicator_Large_Vertical_v01: a large vertical analogue indicator Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Tip: These values are listed in the order they are specified in the wizard. - Browse in the Analog agent name (although this can specify the value slot, but no other slot name) representing the process variable (PV). The wizard will automatically use the Maximum and Minimum engineering spans configured for this Analog agent and the configured High High, High, Low and Low Low alarm limits to define the various range settings and the various statistical settings to determine the applicable direction of trend. PLEASE NOTE: This direction of trend is ONLY calculated by the Analog agent representing the process variable, when its statsPeriod slot is set to the required sampling period, we recommend a value of 10 (minutes), since the default value of 0 DISABLES the calculation of these statistics, since if used excessively they can affect performance. Tip: You can also configure the optional statsDirDev slot specify an optional minimum deviation or deadband to ensure that this trending direction only indicates significant changes in value (we recommend setting this value to 0.05). -->
