Insert queries Top Insert queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Insert queries
Insert queries Top Insert queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Insert Queries can insert records into a specific table or view, by specifying the values of selected fields. Click for more information: Note1: If necessary, parameterise one or more of these values to specify them before performing the query. Note2: This query is ONLY able to insert records in a SINGLE table or view. Tip: You can also specify calculations instead of single values. These calculations can involve numeric parameters. For instance ‘<!!param!!>*4’ multiples the value of this parameter by four. To add and configure an Insert query: Add an Insert Query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. - If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option.

Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases.

Title: Insert queries
Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query. For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Insert query: Note: This configuration dialog does NOT provide a Preview button to prevent incorrect records from being added to your database. Therefore please ensure that you configure the values for these fields correctly. The Tables and Fields dialog is displayed. - Choose whether you want to insert record/s into a view or table, by selecting the required Table Type option. - Select the required view or table from the Select a ... to Insert to list box. The names of tables and views support SQL schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table or view is part of a different schema, then the name of this schema is indicated in brackets after the name of the table or view. This means that a table or view can have the SAME name as another table or view as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note: Only ONE table or view can be selected. - Select which fields require values and provide values for them: . To specify a value for a field: - Click the Add New Field Values button. - Select the field, whose value you want to specify, from the Field drop-down list box, in the following syntax: [Fieldname]. Note1: This list displays all the fields of the selected table or view. Note2: If necessary, you can edit the selected field name yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. - Specify the value or parameter in the Value/Expression field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this. For details, see Adding parameters . Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work. Tip: You can also specify calculations instead of single values. These calculations can also involve numeric parameters. For instance ‘<!!param!!>*4’ multiples the value of this parameter by four.

To remove the last field: - Click the Delete New Field Values button to remove the last field from the list.

Title: Insert queries
To remove the last field: - Click the Delete New Field Values button to remove the last field from the list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the field at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. As you define values for the selected fields, the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. Note: Any fields that you do not specify will either have a NULL value inserted or the next consecutive number, if they are numbered automatically. WARNING! If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages. Once you click the Next button the query configuration dialog ends and any further modifications to the query can only to be performed manually. - Click Next , once the required fields and their values have been defined, to end the query configuration dialog. The Custom Query dialog is displayed, which allows you to manually configure this query, if necessary. - If necessary, type or modify the existing SQL querying commands in the SQL Query editor, which highlights keywords and makes it easier to customise your queries. - Click Finish , once you are satisfied with this query. This adds this query with its specified name beneath the Insert Queries subfolder of the Queries folder of the applicable OLE DB datasource, in the Enterprise Manager . If using SQL, please ensure that all time based queries adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd, as follows: - Either, set the short date format in Regional Settings to be yyyy-mm-dd, once for all. - Or convert ALL the date parameters for each query into this SQL standard format first, by using a string converter, such as the String Format spider. To perform an Insert query using a Query spider: this procedure describes how to perform a Insert query by clicking a Button control and to display the result of this operation in a TextBox control on a graphic form. This procedure assumes that the Insert query has been added and configured. Prepare the graphic form: - Open a new graphic form in the Design workspace . (If necessary, add a project and a graphic form first) - Add a Button control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to trigger the Query spider so that it will perform the query.

- Add a TextBox control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to display the results of performing this query.

Title: Insert queries
- Add a TextBox control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to display the results of performing this query. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the TextBox control in the graphic form. Add and configure the Query spider to run this query: - Open the Spider Configuration tool window. - Right-click the spider workspace itself and select the Create New Spider menu. - Click the Databasing sub-menu and its Query item to add a Query spider. - Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. - Select the required query from the Inputs section of this spider, as follows: - Click the Server containing the required OLE DB datasource from the Server list box. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, when referring to the Server that you use to log in, instead of its actual name as this makes it easier to transfer this spider to another Client. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required OLE DB datasource from this list of available OLE DB datasources on this Server. The first OLE DB datasource created on this Server is selected by default. - Click the required type in the Query Type list. The Select Query category is selected by default. - From the Query Name list box, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the required query. Note: It is important to name your queries clearly, so that it is easy to select the correct one. - If this selected query contains parameters , then the names of these parameters will be added as additional inputs to the Inputs section. Note1: The value of each parameter input can either be provided by a property or data element via a silk a line with an arrow at its end, which links the output of one spider to the input of another. or can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note2: If using SQL, please ensure that all the date parameters for this query adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd.

Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the parameter name in the Inputs section and type in the required value.

Title: Insert queries
Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the parameter name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. - It is recommended to use the Confirm Action checkbox to display a confirmation dialog before this query inserts a record into your database. This spider performs this query to insert a record, when it is triggered. WARNING! Please ensure that you have provided values for ANY parameters used by this query BEFORE triggering this spider otherwise an error will be displayed. Note: You will notice in the Event Trigger section of this spider that this Query spider is triggered by clicking the Button control. Connect the Query spider to the TextBox control: - If necessary, open the property tree by using the pane display bar on the right border of the central spider workspace pane. For details, see Working with pane display bars - In the Outputs section, drag the Return Information output onto the Appearance category beneath this TextBox control in the property tree and when this category expands, drop it onto the Text property. Note: The Return Information output either describes the reasons for NOT deleting a record or how many records were removed. Test that the query is correctly displayed: - Click the Preview toolbar button of this graphic form. - Press the Button control, if you used Confirm Action the confirmation dialog should be displayed. - The TextBox control should either display an error message or how many records were deleted. - Save the graphic form by pressing its Save toolbar button to save these changes. To edit this query . Tip: Right-click the required Insert query and select Edit Insert Query . To delete this query . Tip: Right-click the required Insert query and select Delete Insert Query . For details of parameterizing queries, see Working with parameters . -->

Title: How to set up Installing a Protocol Driver
Steps:
Installing a Protocol Driver Top Installing a Protocol Driver Launch the Adroit Config Editor . - Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click Driver Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click the Install new driver button. This displays the DriverInstallList dialog to allow new protocol drivers to be installed, by creating a list of available Adroit drivers from the installation path or the previously specified path. If the Adroit driver setup files cannot be found in the installation or previously specified path, then click the browse button to manually locate the disk or folder containing the protocol drivers. - Click the name of the driver ( ) to install. This copies the associated driver files into the Adroit system folder and opens the associated driver documentation. PLEASE NOTE: Read this driver documentation carefully, as it specifies which devices are supported, how to configure the driver, how to scan using the driver, diagnostic tips and any relevant protocol information. -->

If the Adroit driver setup files cannot be found in the installation or previously specified path, another Adroit driver install dialog is displayed, with the following three buttons: - Retry: This will attempt to reopen the installation or previously specified path for installing drivers. - Cancel: This will abort the driver installation process. - Browse …: This will display a dialog, to manually locate the disk or folder containing the Adroit protocol drivers. Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . - Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click Driver Configuration in the right hand pane. - Click the Install new driver button. This displays the DriverInstallList dialog to allow new protocol drivers to be installed, by creating a list of available Adroit drivers from the installation path or the previously specified path. If the Adroit driver setup files cannot be found in the installation or previously specified path, then click the browse button to manually locate the disk or folder containing the protocol drivers. - Click the name of the driver ( ) to install. This copies the associated driver files into the Adroit system folder and opens the associated driver documentation. PLEASE NOTE: Read this driver documentation carefully, as it specifies which devices are supported, how to configure the driver, how to scan using the driver, diagnostic tips and any relevant protocol information. -->

Title: How to set up Installing Internet Information Services
Steps:
Installing Internet Information Services Top Installing Internet Information Services The SmartUI Web Service and Click Once requires Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) to be installed. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service or Working with Click Once . When using a Windows desktop operating systems, such as Windows 7, it may be necessary to install IIS as it is not part of the default installation. However, when using a Server operating system IIS is installed by default. To install IIS on Windows 7: IMPORTANT: Simply selecting IIS is NOT enough on Windows 7 - you need to manually check ALL the ALL of the sub-components of its Application Development Features component. Note: Ensure that the Windows system files are located in the same location as when the operating system was installed, for instance, if having installed from the local drive ensure that the Windows installation media is in this drive. - Select the Start menu, Control Panel and Programs and Features item. - Select the Turn Windows features on or off link, on the left side of this applet. This will display the Windows Features dialog. - Click the checkbox to the left of the Internet Information Services component. This only selects some of its components by default - indicated by a filled checkbox. - Double click the Internet Information Services component to expand its options. - Expand the World Wide Web Services option. - Expand its Application Development Features option. - Ensure that there is a tick box next to ALL of the sub-components of this Application Development Features component. Tip: Once all the sub-components are ticked, a tick appears next to the Application Development Features component. Example - Click the OK button to install this component. - Close the open dialog boxes. To install IIS on Windows XP: Note: Ensure that the Windows system files are located in the same location as when the operating system was installed, for instance, if having installed from the local drive ensure that the Windows installation media is in this drive. - Select the Start menu, Settings , Control Panel and Add or Remove Programs item. This will display the Add or Remove Programs applet. - Select the Add or Remove Windows Components button, on the left side of this applet. This will display the Windows Components Wizard dialog. - In the Windows Components Wizard dialog, scroll down until the Internet Information Service (IIS) component is visible. - Click the tick box next to the Internet Information Service (IIS) component. Note: Ensure that there is a tick in this tick box. Example - Click the Next button to install this component. - Click the Finish button to close the Windows Components Wizard dialog and also close the Add or Remove Programs applet. -->

This will install this service, provided that the installation media or its files can be located on the computer. The SNMP Service will be started by default. text:
Installing WanServer as a Service Top Installing WanServer as a Service The WanServer can run either as a standard Application or as a Service within Windows.

Title: How to set up Installing WanServer as a Service
Steps:
Installing WanServer as a Service Top Installing WanServer as a Service The WanServer can run either as a standard Application or as a Service within Windows. The advantage of running this as a Service is that then the WanServer does not shutdown when the current user logs off. Tip: It is recommended that the WanServer is initially run as an Application, which provides more diagnostic information during the configuration period. ONLY once Wanlink is configured and running properly, then run the WanServer Service Setup application and install the WanServer as a Service. Note: For default use, this service must run as a Local System account , and the Allow service to interact with the desktop option should be disabled. If this is needed then the WanServer application icon will continue to appear in task bar. The Server Service Setup Wanlink component, launches the Wanlink Server Service Setup dialog. For details on launching this, see Launching Wanlink components . This dialog can be configured as follows: - If you wish to install the WanServer as a Service, then click on the Install WanServer Service button. - If you wish to uninstall the WanServer as a Service, then click on the Uninstall WanServer Service button. - The WanServer Path displays the path to the WanServer that is being or that has been installed as a service, for diagnostic purposes. - Click the OK button to accept the changes made and to exit. WARNING! If you have made changes to this configuration, the computer will need to be rebooted for these changes to be implemented. -->

Instrumentation equipment templates Top Working with Instrumentation equipment templates In MAPS each piece of instrumentation equipment requires an associated template.

Title: Working with Instrumentation equipment templates
Instrumentation equipment templates Top Working with Instrumentation equipment templates In MAPS each piece of instrumentation equipment requires an associated template. For complex items of equipment consisting of more than one piece of instrumentation equipment, like conveyors, create a unit for item of equipment and associate all their component-instrumentation equipment to individual MAPS templates. You can also create custom (user-defined) templates too. Default Instrumentation equipment templates : the templates of the instrumentation equipment provided by MAPS . Template naming convention: The first section is the abbreviated name of the equipment e.g. DI (Digital in) or AO (Analog out). The second section of the template will be _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced), indicating the level of complexity or diagnostic information provided by this template. For each piece of equipment there can be up to 3 templates, each providing different levels of complexity or diagnostic information, the names of these templates indicate the provided level of complexity as follows: _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced). IMPORTANT: The greater the level of complexity provided by a template, the more signals are required for this item of equipment, which therefore increases the number of the required SCADA tags. This can increase the size and cost of your Adroit licence, as in Adroit you pay for each tag that you scan to a PLC. So ensure that assign the templates to your equipment carefully. The third section provides the version of this template e.g. v1_0 stands for version 1.0 Each MAPS template: - Provides one or more SCADA graphical representations providing an intelligent faceplate. For details of these faceplates, see Instrumentation equipment faceplates . These graphical representations also displays status indicators, so that operators can immediately see which operational mode this equipment is in. For details, see Status indicators provided by instrumentation equipment graphics . Note: The SAME status indicators are also used by the associated faceplate to indicate these operational modes. Example: - Provides an associated PLC function block for this item of equipment. - Creates the SCADA tags for the various signals and their PLC variables and links these together. -->

The following is list of the available functions and subroutines supported by the Adroit system object: Function AgentName . Function FindFile . Function GetTag . Function TriggerActive . Function TriggerCount . Function TriggerName . Function TriggerValue . Function WaitForChange . Subroutine LogEvent . Subroutine RunApp . Subroutine SetTag . Subroutine Wait . Note1: Adroit also provides an OLE Server interface , which is NOT the same as this scripting interface, the Adroit system object. In fact, certain tasks can only be accomplished via these Adroit OLE Server Data Objects, like adding and removing tags, but it is possible to use the OLE Server interface within this scripting interface. Note2: The JScript language is case sensitive, therefore when using the Adroit system object, refer to it as ‘Adroit’ and not ‘adroit’. The case used for the function and subroutine names is not important. VBScript is not case sensitive. Note3: Language references for both JScript and VBScript can be installed, speak to the Adroit support department for more information. Note4: If you are using scripts to obtain datetime tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. -->

Title: Introduction to spiders and silks
Introduction to spiders and silks Top Introduction to spiders and silks Spiders and silks are essentially a visual programming language, which can transfer and/or manipulate data, typically by means of drag and drop. Spiders communicate and/or manipulate data from a set of inputs to a set of outputs, when they are triggered. A list of available spiders . Silks connect spiders together and can be grouped into template sets, which control how data is transferred between spiders. Spiders, silks and template sets are configured using a spider workspace, which can either be run on the Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. or the Server, depending upon their required application. For further details, see Working with spider workspaces . Note: The spider workspace is actually a spider engine as it has both a running and a stopped state. The transfer and/or manipulation of data can only occur while the spider workspace or spider engine is running. Although the potential use and areas of application for spiders are diverse, spiders and silks are primarily used to animate graphic forms by connecting data to the properties of graphic forms and their form components, which occurs on the Client. Click for more details: By using spiders, it is possible to provide a rich interactive environment for the end-user of a graphic form, without necessarily needing to write any scripting at all. This is provided, in part, by the ability of spiders to be operated or triggered by means of events or actions either performed by another spider or performed by a user on a control attached to the graphic form. In this way users are able to perform custom and/or complicated manipulation of data elements, literally at the touch of a button or a click of a checkbox etc. For details, see Animating graphic forms . Spiders are either added manually or automatically during the process of creating silks. Silks are created by dragging, as follows: - You can either drag from an item in the explorer tree(s), which border the spider workspace or from a spider. - You are then able to drag to either another item in an explorer tree or to another spider. -->

IO Flags Top IO Flags In an effort to simplify the scanning configuration, the following legacy status slots that used to affect how a slot (value) was scanned: Scan Inhibit, Output Enable and Output Initialise are no longer stored in the header of the each agent for each of its slots.

Title: IO Flags
IO Flags Top IO Flags In an effort to simplify the scanning configuration, the following legacy status slots that used to affect how a slot (value) was scanned: Scan Inhibit, Output Enable and Output Initialise are no longer stored in the header of the each agent for each of its slots. Note: The advanced header dialog no longer displays these statuses and putslots to these status bits are also disabled. Instead these settings are now stored in the scanning configuration of the Device agent in the Agent Database (.wgp) file along with the other scanning related settings, such as the scan address, scan rate etc, as an IO flags setting. Hence the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog contains an IO flags column in the list of scanned tags. Note: There is no slot that contains these IO flags, since they are now stored in the tag list of scanned values of a Device agent. When loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version of Adroit, Adroit 10 uses the saved status bit information to configure the IO flags setting of all the Device agents and when the Agent Database (.wgp) file is saved then these status bits are switched OFF in the Agent Database (.wgp) file. Therefore Adroit 10 Agent Database (.wgp) file are NOT backwardly compatible! IMPORTANT: When starting the Adroit 10 Agent Server for the first time and loading a Agent Database (.wgp) file from a previous version, devices will most likely NEVER show healthy once all the devices are started. You need to save the Agent Database (.wgp) file FIRST and then restart the Agent Server and then you should see all the devices going healthy. The IO flags setting is a bit mask as follows: Value Bit Description Default 1 0 Input disabled ON supercedes the legacy statusScanInhibit flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInhibit flag set, will force Bit 0 OFF. Note1: This setting is the INVERSE of the Input disabled (Scan inhibited) checkbox, when scanning a tag. Note2: You can still use the statusScanInhibit header slot of an agent to prevent any configured scanning of the agent from occurring. 2 1 Output enabled OFF supercedes the legacy statusOutputEnable flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusOutputEnable flag set, will force Bit 1 ON. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output enabled checkbox, when scanning a tag. 4 2 Output initialise OFF supercedes the legacy statusScanInitialise flag at the agent and slot level. Any legacy WGP file that has the statusScanInitialise flag set, will force Bit 2 ON. If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Note: This setting is enabled by checking the Output initialise checkbox, when scanning a tag. 8 3 Demand scan OFF New functionality – requires that the global configuration for demand scanning is enabled and that the currently selected device driver type supports demand scanning. The IO flags setting is a sum of the values whose associated bit is ON. So for a newly scanned tag, the default of bit 0 (enable reads) applies, in which case IO flags is 1. If bit 0 (enable reads) and 2 (output initialise) are ON then the IO flags is 5 (1 + 4). For more details on demand scanning, see Demand Scanning . -->

Title: IPEnableHeartbeat
IPEnableHeartbeat Top IPEnableHeartbeat WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". When using sockets as the communication mechanism between the Agent Server and its clients, the socket heartbeats will always occur, as clients will PING the Agent Server every 10 seconds. If you want the Agent Server to monitor that each connection remains healthy and to close unhealthy connections, then implement the following registry setting on the Agent Server computer: This setting enables the Agent Server to monitor the PINGs it received from each client and to also specify the required timeout value, in seconds, where if a PING has not been received within this time period then the connection to this client is deemed unhealthy and this connection (channel) is closed by the Agent Server. HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI (REG_)DWORD IPEnableHeartbeat The default value of 0 disables monitoring and any other positive value (typically 1) will enable the monitoring and specify the required timeout value, in seconds, which is the specified value multiplied by a factor of 30. For instance setting this registry setting to 1 results in a timeout of 30 seconds, setting it to 2 results in a timeout of 60 seconds etc. -->

Title: Motors
Purpose: to represent any kind of motor and indicate whether this motor is started (on) or stopped (off) or in an alarm state. Description: the ISO representation of a motor in either a horizontal or vertical orientation, which indicates the status of its Boolean process variable (PV) that indicates whether this motor is started (on) or stopped (off) and/or indicates when a specific alarm or "wrong" state is in effect, by changing its background color as described above. wzdMotorHorizontal_v01: the ISO representation of a motor in a horizontal orientation. wzdMotorVertical_v01: the ISO representation of a motor in a vertical orientation. Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Tip: These values are listed in the order they are specified in the wizard. - Browse in the alarm bit that indicates the alarm fault state of this motor. - Browse in the tag (such as the Digital agent name that can also specify its value slot) representing the Boolean process variable (PV) that indicates whether this motor is started (on) or stopped (off).

You cannot start the Agent Server as an application by using the Windows Remote Desktop (a terminal client). This is because Windows does not support USB ports when you use the Remote Desktop application, so any USB HASP is effectively invisible to the Agent Server. Note: This is not a problem when starting the Agent Server as a service from within a Remote Desktop. The resources (e.g. printer etc) of the computer used to remote desktop into the Agent Server computer are used by the Agent Server NOT the resources on the Agent Server's computer. This means that when you terminate the remote desktop session, these resources become unavailable which causes problems.

metadata.title: Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit

text:
Adroit has terminal client (remote desktop) connection licencing rules whereby every Adroit client application takes a (remote node) connection licence regardless.

Title: Problems running Adroit Client Applications
Adroit has terminal client (remote desktop) connection licencing rules whereby every Adroit client application takes a (remote node) connection licence regardless. An Adroit client is ANY application that makes a connection to an Agent Server, for instance: - Classic User Interface - Agent Configurator - Adroit utilities, such as the Agent Browser - Any Adroit OLE Automation (MISSRVR) or ActiveX client application. If the Classic User Interface is started from within a remote deskop session, and the Configurator is opened – then TWO connection licenses are required; otherwise either the Configurator and/or UI will be unable to connect to the Agent Server. Since BOTH the UI and the Configurator require their OWN connection licences when started using remote desktop. This change ALSO prevents the use of remote desktop for perform maintenance especially on stand-alone (no remote connection licences) installations. Since UIs cannot be restarted via Remote Desktop and/or the Configurator is unable to connect to the Agent Server. For this reason, Adroit has attempted to redress this limitation by NOT enforcing connection licences for the console user’s session. Typically when a user logs onto a computer, this user, known as the “console user”, always gets: - Session 0 (on Window Server 2003 or Windows XP operating systems or older) or - Session 1 (on Windows Server 2008 or Windows Vista operating systems or newer). When a remote desktop user logs on with the same user credentials as the console user, this remote desktop user inherits the same session number. When Adroit clients are launched via a remote desktop using the session of the console user (either session 0 or 1 depending on the operating system), then these Agent Server connections are treated as legacy local connections which do NOT require connection licences. Note: The resources (e.g. printer etc) of the computer used to remote desktop into the Adroit client computer are used by the Adroit client NOT the resources on the Adroit client's computer. This means that when you terminate the remote desktop session, these resources become unavailable which causes problems. -->

Large Scalable Agent Server Networks Top Large Scalable Agent Server Networks This network configuration typically contains a large number of Agent Servers that are required to share information as if they were part of the same project so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Server.

Title: Large Scalable Agent Server Networks
Steps:
Large Scalable Agent Server Networks Top Large Scalable Agent Server Networks This network configuration typically contains a large number of Agent Servers that are required to share information as if they were part of the same project so that any one Agent Server can directly gain access to any of the other Agent Server. However, maintaining a grid of fully connected Agent Servers can potentially be resource intensive, for the following reasons: - Many Agent Servers within a network all broadcasting their presence - many IT administrators do not like this. - Many Agent Servers within a network all on the same project causing large agent tables to be transmitted in a "one to many" relationship. Large agent tables are generally created when agents are added or deleted. Note: This is a problem for slower (10MB, WLAN) networks where bandwidth was at a premium especially if the network is not dedicated to SCADA operations. However, 100MB networks handle this easily. In this case, we recommend that you use the method, in which you can divide these Agent Servers into their own projects (or have each Agent Server in its own project if necessary), then use the list method for connecting these Agent Servers and/or projects together. For further details of this and the other methods of connecting Agent Servers together, see Agent Server Connection Methods . If these Agent Servers are in different domains then you need to use explicit Agent Server connections. Click for details: For instance, consider this situation in which each section in a plant has its own Agent Server and its own local Classic UI and where all of these plant section Agent Servers are connected to a central gateway computer (known as a proxy server ), which also has its own local (or remote) Classic UIs. In this case - The central gateway computer requires explicit Agent Server connections to be created for each of the plant section Agent Servers. - Each plant section Agent Server, will only require explicit Agent Server connections to those servers from which data is required i.e. if its local Classic UI refer to tags, which are located on other plant section Agent Servers. Diagram Key The central gateway computer = the grey circle. Each plant section Agent Server = a clear circle. -->

Launcher connection settings Launcher connection settings This page of the Setting up the Launcher component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, creates the customized or pre-configured Smart UI Launcher package that provides the necessary connection details to connect to your Smart UI Distribution service: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Launcher connection settings
Steps:
Launcher connection settings Launcher connection settings This page of the Setting up the Launcher component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, creates the customized or pre-configured Smart UI Launcher package that provides the necessary connection details to connect to your Smart UI Distribution service: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Launcher option. - Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. This page is divided into the following three sections: - The type of network used to connect the Distribution computer to your clients. - The network identification and login to the Distribution computer. - Additional configuration options and the Apply button that creates the customized Launcher executable. You can either connect to the Web Service using: - LAN or WAN - Internet, if this is selected then you can specify the required proxy server settings, as follows: - Check the Enable Proxy checkbox. - Then either specify the Machine Name or IP address and Port used by your proxy server. - If necessary, provide the required User and Password for your Proxy Authentication Details . Specify the name of the required Computer name or the URL required to connect to the Web Service: If necessary, provide the required User and Password for your Authentication Details for this computer. Tip: Click the Test Connection button to check that you are able to connect to this computer using the specified information. - If necessary, the Launcher installation can prompt for its required extraction path, by default this is: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI - If necessary, you can automatically run the Launcher after extraction - by default this option is checked. - Click the Apply button to create your customized Smart UI Launcher executable, which is called VIP Launcher Setup.exe and is created in the Smart UI Web Service installation folder ( C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice ). -->

Launching Wanlink Components Top Launching Wanlink Components Wanlink components are installed into the Adroit folder as part of the complete Adroit installation, alternatively its WanClient and WanServer components can be selectively installed during a custom installation.

Title: Launching Wanlink Components
Launching Wanlink Components Top Launching Wanlink Components Wanlink components are installed into the Adroit folder as part of the complete Adroit installation, alternatively its WanClient and WanServer components can be selectively installed during a custom installation. Note: Only one WanClient and WanServer can be launched on a computer. If there is an already an existing WanClient or WanServer running on a computer, then if either program is run again, a warning will appear reminding the user than only one instance of each application is allowed. Tip: Both the WanClient and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Press the Windows key and start typing in the required application name and select it from the list, in this case: - Adroit Wanlink Client , this launches the WanClient application. - Adroit Wanlink Client Auto-start , this launches the WanClient application, with the "/start" command-line parameter, so that it automatically starts its communication process . - Adroit Wanlink Server , this launches the WanServer . Note: If the WanServer is started with the " /p:nnn" command-line parameter, then it will be able to change the port on which the server is to operate (default 51114). Where nnn specifies the required port. To specify the port on which the Wanlink Server is to operate, the following DWORD registry value is provided: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\WanlinkServerPort (default value 51114). This setting can also be overridden with the /p:nnnn command-line parameter. If the /persist command-line parameter is used the /p:nnnnn value will be saved to the registry. - Adroit Wanlink Server Service Setup , this launches the Wanlink Server Service Setup . This also supports the Wanlink Server command line parameters when this service is started e.g. net start adrwanwerver /p:51115. For details of these components, see Wanlink components . -->

Title: Spanning controls across multiple rows and columns
Cells can be merged in the TableLayoutPanel control by spanning controls across rows and/or columns, as follows: Example: To span a control across two columns: select this control in the TableLayoutPanel control and set the ColumnSpan property of this control to 2. This allows this control to occupy the next (rightmost) column in addition to the column that it is currently in - now you need to resize this control accordingly to occupy all or part of the next column. To span a control across two rows: select this control in the TableLayoutPanel control and set the RowSpan property of the control to 2 This allows this control to occupy the next (bottommost) row in addition to the row that it is currently in - now you need to resize this control accordingly to occupy all or part of the next row. To span a control across two columns and three rows: select this control and set its RowSpan property to 3 and its ColumnSpan property to 2.

Licensing methods Top Available SmartUI Licensing methods The SmartUI Server can be licensed by one of the following methods , which are listed in the ORDER that the Server LOOKS for its license: Note1: The license for the FIRST licensing method that is detected is used to license the SmartUI Server Note2: ONLY when NONE of these licensing methods are found, does the SmartUI Server considers itself NOT to be licensed.

Title: Available SmartUI Licensing methods
Licensing methods Top Available SmartUI Licensing methods The SmartUI Server can be licensed by one of the following methods , which are listed in the ORDER that the Server LOOKS for its license: Note1: The license for the FIRST licensing method that is detected is used to license the SmartUI Server Note2: ONLY when NONE of these licensing methods are found, does the SmartUI Server considers itself NOT to be licensed. - HASP license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a HASP software protection key, which is inserted into the USB port of the computer on which the Server is running. This HASP is programmed in accordance with your specific license agreement. Click for more details: The Server continuously checks that the HASP key is present. If the HASP key cannot be found after 3 retries (which are logged to the Application event log) the Server shuts down displaying a 'HASP cannot be found' message. WARNING! If this HASP key is lost, the cost of replacement is the current full value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. Note1: If the licence is updated or modified then the HASP key must be reprogrammed to reflect the changes. Note2: You can use the SAME HASP to license BOTH Adroit and SmartUI , however, this requires a 4K “green” USB HASP. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is PORTABILITY, as unlike a soft license which is bound to a specific computer, you can install and use the Server ANY computer provided that you plug your HASP into one of its USB ports. - Soft license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a software license to a SINGLE computer and only remains valid while certain hardware and software or system characteristics of this computer remain unchanged. Click for more details: Note1: If ANY of the hardware and/or software items that the soft license monitors are modified, then the license will stop working and you will need to obtain a new license file. Note2: If the Server computer has more than one network card, the licence will only monitor ONE of the cards - should this card become disabled, then the Server will no longer be licensed. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is SECURITY, as unlike a HASP license which can be removed from a computer without your knowledge, this license is bound intrinsically to a specific computer. - Adroit license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by consuming a single connection license from the license of an Adroit Agent Server. This license provides LIMITED ACCESS to the datasources of the Server, by ONLY entitling the user to the Adroit datasources and the proprietary or unlicensed datasources, such as the Event Log, Simulation, Virtual and Project datasources. Click for more details: Typically the Server runs on this Adroit Agent Server computer and consuming the single connection license from this local Agent Server. However, you can specify a remote Agent Server from which this connection license should be taken. For details on configuring this alternative Server licensing method, see General Server settings . Note1: This licensing method applies whether the specified Adroit Agent Server is being run in licensed or in timed-license mode. Note2: The LICENSED datasources, such as OLEDB (databases), OPC and Server Scripts are ONLY AVAILABLE when the Server is licensed using the methods described above. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is REDUCED COST and EASE OF USE as you do not need to specifically apply for this license.

- Demo license: You can use the SmartUI Server freely, for 2 hours, which you can restart as many times as you like.

Title: Available SmartUI Licensing methods
Licensing methods Top Available SmartUI Licensing methods The SmartUI Server can be licensed by one of the following methods , which are listed in the ORDER that the Server LOOKS for its license: Note1: The license for the FIRST licensing method that is detected is used to license the SmartUI Server Note2: ONLY when NONE of these licensing methods are found, does the SmartUI Server considers itself NOT to be licensed. - HASP license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a HASP software protection key, which is inserted into the USB port of the computer on which the Server is running. This HASP is programmed in accordance with your specific license agreement. Click for more details: The Server continuously checks that the HASP key is present. If the HASP key cannot be found after 3 retries (which are logged to the Application event log) the Server shuts down displaying a 'HASP cannot be found' message. WARNING! If this HASP key is lost, the cost of replacement is the current full value of the corresponding license fee. We recommend, therefore, that you consider insuring this item against loss or theft. Note1: If the licence is updated or modified then the HASP key must be reprogrammed to reflect the changes. Note2: You can use the SAME HASP to license BOTH Adroit and SmartUI , however, this requires a 4K “green” USB HASP. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is PORTABILITY, as unlike a soft license which is bound to a specific computer, you can install and use the Server ANY computer provided that you plug your HASP into one of its USB ports. - Soft license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by a software license to a SINGLE computer and only remains valid while certain hardware and software or system characteristics of this computer remain unchanged. Click for more details: Note1: If ANY of the hardware and/or software items that the soft license monitors are modified, then the license will stop working and you will need to obtain a new license file. Note2: If the Server computer has more than one network card, the licence will only monitor ONE of the cards - should this card become disabled, then the Server will no longer be licensed. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is SECURITY, as unlike a HASP license which can be removed from a computer without your knowledge, this license is bound intrinsically to a specific computer. - Adroit license: In this case, the SmartUI Server is licensed by consuming a single connection license from the license of an Adroit Agent Server. This license provides LIMITED ACCESS to the datasources of the Server, by ONLY entitling the user to the Adroit datasources and the proprietary or unlicensed datasources, such as the Event Log, Simulation, Virtual and Project datasources. Click for more details: Typically the Server runs on this Adroit Agent Server computer and consuming the single connection license from this local Agent Server. However, you can specify a remote Agent Server from which this connection license should be taken. For details on configuring this alternative Server licensing method, see General Server settings . Note1: This licensing method applies whether the specified Adroit Agent Server is being run in licensed or in timed-license mode. Note2: The LICENSED datasources, such as OLEDB (databases), OPC and Server Scripts are ONLY AVAILABLE when the Server is licensed using the methods described above. Advantage: The MAIN advantage of this licensing method is REDUCED COST and EASE OF USE as you do not need to specifically apply for this license.

- Demo license: You can use the SmartUI Server freely, for 2 hours, which you can restart as many times as you like.

Title: Available SmartUI Licensing methods

Limited Time License HASP Top Limited Time License HASP IMPORTANT: When a HASP is not detected when the Agent Server is started and the Agent Server is not being otherwise licensed, then the Agent Server will automatically run in limited time license mode.

Title: Limitations
Limited Time License HASP Top Limited Time License HASP IMPORTANT: When a HASP is not detected when the Agent Server is started and the Agent Server is not being otherwise licensed, then the Agent Server will automatically run in limited time license mode. Use the limited time license HASP if the Agent Server is not currently licensed. This runs the Agent Server with a 120 minute operating license with 20000 scan points and 2 remote connections. When this period of time ends, the scanning of devices will stop and any remote server connections will be lost and not reconnected. Typically this can be launched from the Adroit Start menu by clicking on the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and clicking the Adroit Agent Server (timed license) item. Although it is also possible to launch the Agent Server with the following command line parameter: –demo e.g. C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \as.exe –demo There are message boxes and event log entries explaining these important events. Also the HASP agent provides the following status bits that indicate events relating to the use of this mode of licensing the Agent Server: - TimedLicence : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode, which automatically occurs when the Agent Server is started and the HASP cannot be found. - TimedLicenceExpired : ON when the Agent Server is running in time license mode and the timed license period has expired, so the Agent Server needs to be restarted to re-enable scanning. Note : To run the Agent Server Service in timed license mode, use the /-demo startup option, which is specified AFTER installing the Agent Server service, as follows: EITHER open CMD.exe and type in the following command: "net start agentserver /-demo" OR open the Services applet (in Administrative Tools), right click the AgentServer service, select Properties and specify –demo in the Start parameters edit field, then click the Start button and the Ok button. IMPORTANT: If using the Services applet, this ONLY starts this service in demo mode for a single session only. The demo mode is not applied to all instances of the service thereafter. -->

- Determine the field/s that you want the control to view and/or modify.

Title: Prerequisites for linking controls to BindingSource components:
Steps:
- Determine the field/s that you want the control to view and/or modify. - Identify the BindingSource component that contains these field/s and provides the required interaction. - Associate the appropriate databinding property of this control with this BindingSource component. To link a DataGridView control to the appropriate BindingSource component: Note: The following procedure assumes that a VIZNETDataBinder component has been added to this graphic form and associated it with a DataBinder. - Open the graphic form. - In the Toolbox window, open the Window Forms category and select the DataGridView control. - Drag the pointer to define the extent of this control. The DataGridView Tasks dialog is immediately displayed. - From the Choose Data Source list box select the required BindingSource component. - Configure the checkboxes to provide the appropriate levels of interactions that your users will have with this data. - Click the Run toolbar button of the graphic form to see that this control displays the correct data. Typically the DataGridView control is used to display all the fields (columns) of a table in a database, so that its records can be displayed in a spreadsheet-type manner. To link a TextBox control to the appropriate BindingSource component: Note: The following procedure assumes that a VIZNETDataBinder component has been added to this graphic form and associated it with a DataBinder. - Open the graphic form. - In the Toolbox window, open the Window Forms category and select the TextBox control. - Drag the pointer to define the extent of this control. - Open the Properties window and click on the toolbar item to arrange the properties alphabetically. - Expand the (DataBindings) property that is at the top of this window - Select the Text sub-property. - Click the button at the right of this field and select the required BindingSource component from the list and its field that will be displayed in this TextBox control. - Click the Run toolbar button of the graphic form to see that this control displays the correct data. Typically the TextBox control is used to display the value of a selected field (column) of a table in a database. To link a ComboBox control to the appropriate BindingSource component: Note: The following procedure assumes that a VIZNETDataBinder component has been added to this graphic form and associated it with a DataBinder. - Open the graphic form. - In the Toolbox window, open the Window Forms category and select the ComboBox control. - Drag the pointer to define the extent of this control. - Click the icon to display the ComboBox Tasks dialog. - heck the Use data bound items checkbox to display and configure the following data binding options: - Data Source: Select the required BindingSource component from the list. - DisplayMember: The name of the field, within the selected Data Source (BindingSource component) that this ComboBox control is required to select. - ValueMember: An optional property that is best used when the field specified by the DisplayMember is not descriptive enough to be very user-friendly. In this case, the ValueMember property can specify an associated field that contains suitably descriptive values. - Selected Value: An optional property to select the value from DisplayMember 's field that this ComboBox control should display by default. - Click the Run toolbar button of the graphic form to see that this control displays the correct data. Typically the ComboBox control (or ListBox control) is used to select the index or key field (column) of a table in a database. -->

Tip: Giving your parameters descriptive names, makes it easier to pair parameters with controls. - Select the name of the required parameter. - Specify the name of the control that will provide the value of this parameter in the Control (top) list box in the right pane. Title: Local Incident Destinations
Local Incident Destinations Top Local Incident Destinations The Alarm route (local) destinations section in the Routes tab of the Edit Alarm Agent dialog specify the possible destinations for incidents that ONLY apply to this Alarm agent. This section consists of the following categories: Alarm Lists , which allows you to report active incidents using the following destination: The AlarmList agent, stores a list of the current or unacknowledged active incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). that are routed to it. This allows you to separate your incidents by routing them to different alarm lists. For instance: all the incidents for plant section A can be routed along an alarm route that contains AlarmListA and all the incidents for plant section B can be routed along an alarm route that contains AlarmListB. For details of how alarm lists are used in Adroit and other aspects concerning the display of alarms, see Displaying Alarms . To add an Alarm Lists destination: - If necessary, edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: - If necessary, add an Alarm agent. For details, see To Add a New Agent . - Select the name of this agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - If necessary, select the required route number. - Select the Add button above the Alarm Lists list in the Edit Alarm Agent dialog box. - Select an existing agent from the AlarmList folder in the left pane of the dialog. For more details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Built-in Agent Explorer . Tip: If necessary, you can create a new AlarmList agent by clicking the Add… button. - Click on the OK button. To remove an Alarm Lists destination: - If necessary, edit the required Alarm agent, as follows: - Select the name of this Alarm agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item to display the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - If necessary, select the required route number. - Select the required AlarmList agent in the Alarm Lists list in the Edit Alarm Agent dialog box. - Click the Delete button above this Alarm Lists list to remove this entry from this list.

Note: This only removed the selected agent from the list and does NOT DELETE the agent from the Adroit agent database.

Title: Local Incident Destinations
Note: This only removed the selected agent from the list and does NOT DELETE the agent from the Adroit agent database. Audio Devices , which allows you to report active incidents using the following destinations: - The Beeper agent, which provides simple audio output using the built-in computer loudspeaker, as follows: Specify the start slot of the required Beeper agent to activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker, when an incident is received. The pitch of this beeping varies as follows: - The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new incident, and - The sound pitch will be lowered when an incident is acknowledged and the slot decremented. - The MultiMedia agent launches a Windows compatible multimedia file, such as .WAV, .MID, .AVI or .RMI, as follows: Specify the start slot of the required MultiMedia agent to start playing the selected multimedia file, when an incident is received. If necessary, you can configure the MultiMedia agent to automatically repeat this file. Note: You need to ensure that the computer provides the necessary media player. - An INTEGER or BOOLEAN slot of any other agent type to perform advanced functionality, such as using an INTEGER slot to keep a count of active and unacknowledged alarms, as follows: Routing an alarm to an audio device, actually increments or decrements the specified BOOLEAN or INTEGER slot, as follows: - New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and - Acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the slot value to be decremented. Therefore by specifying such a slot, you can use this value to perform other advanced functionality, for instance by using this in a Script or Expression agent. Location Behaviours Top Location Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically move the object linearly in a defined X-Y direction by means of a monitored value: In other words, you need to monitor a value, which has a defined minimum and maximum value and then specify the maximum required movement in the X (horizontal) and/or Y (vertical) dimensions, when the value reaches its maximum value.

Title: Location Behaviours
Location Behaviours Top Location Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically move the object linearly in a defined X-Y direction by means of a monitored value: In other words, you need to monitor a value, which has a defined minimum and maximum value and then specify the maximum required movement in the X (horizontal) and/or Y (vertical) dimensions, when the value reaches its maximum value. For example when the monitored value is at 50% of its maximum, then this object moves halfway. To dynamically move a control or vector: - Add or edit an Location Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the value in the Input Data Element field. - Specify the minimum value for this Input Data Element in the Minimum Data Element/value field. Note: Any value lower than or equal to this value has no effect upon this Behaviour. - Specify the maximum value for this Input Data Element in the Maximum Data Element/value field. Note: It is at this value that the full transformation of the object occurs. Logged Data Values CSV File Format Top Logged Data Values CSV File Format Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed.

Title: Logged Data Values CSV File Format
Logged Data Values CSV File Format Top Logged Data Values CSV File Format Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . After you have exported data logged values to a CSV Comma Separated Value file containing data, which consists of a number of fields in one or more rows, in which the different fields (values) are typically separated by commas. file, this file provides the following columns: date , time , value , comment - The purpose of the comment field is to label each data log entry indicating how and when the value was derived. - For every session, defined as the period between startup and shutdown of the Agent Server, Adroit always marks the first and last entries in the log as the post startup and last known values. Note1: To prevent logging the POST_STARTUP value after an Agent Server restart, configure the Disable first datalog entries on startup of agent server global datalogging setting. See Advanced Datalog Configuration (global settings) . Note2: Post startup values apply to all datalogs regardless of whether their input tag is scanned or not. - All intermediate values will be marked as normal or bad. - When retrieving data for viewing or analysis, the requested interval time may not coincide with the actual logging time. Therefore, Adroit calculates the values that occur between the recorded values either by estimation (if between sessions) or interpolation (if within the same session). The following symbols in the second column are used in the extracted .CSV file: Symbol Represented Value Description s Post_Startup_Value this is the first value logged after startup l Last_Known_Value this is the last value known before shutdown * Estimated_Value this estimated value lies between a last known value and a post startup value outside a session Interpolated_Value this interpolated value lies between two consecutive normal values within a session Normal_Value this value was logged normally by the DataLog agent b Bad_Value this value should not be trusted as the Bad status bit was set when it was logged ? Unknown_Value extracted value is unknown Note: When viewing this CSV file in a third party application program, such as Excel, ensure that the "Time" column format is set to the "hh:mm:ss" setting, so that the time value is not inadvertently truncated. -->

Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Top Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Tip: the EventLogging agent provides a simpler method for logging incidents to a SQL (OLE DB compatible) database.

Title: Logging Alarms to a SQL Database
Steps:
Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Top Logging Alarms to a SQL Database Tip: the EventLogging agent provides a simpler method for logging incidents to a SQL (OLE DB compatible) database. For details, see Configuring EventLogging Agents . In Adroit , an EventOutput agent can be used to log alarm events to a SQL database. This requires the following main steps: - Creating the SQL database and its associated ODBC data source , which is used by the EventOutput agent to refer to this SQL database. - Create your SQL Database and save it. Tip: It is recommended to limit the size of the table and field names as ONLY 80 characters is available to represent the comma delimited list of these names in the EventOutput agent. - Open the Start menu and select Run… - Type “odbcad32.exe” into the Run dialog and click OK . - Click on the System DSN tab in the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. - Click the Add... button. - Double-click the SQL Server entry in the Create New Data Source dialog. Tip: This should be the last entry in the list. - Specify the name of this ODBC data source in the Name field of the Create a New Data Source to SQL Server dialog. In this example the following name is used: AdrEvtSQL Note: This name will be used to specify this Access database, when configuring the EventOutput agent. - Specify the required SQL Server computer in the Server field and click Next to advance to the next configuration page. For more information on configuring the entries on both this and the subsequent pages, click the provided Help button. Tip: It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to test that the specified data source is able to connect to the specified SQL database. This can be done by clicking the Test Data Source button on the Finish page. - Click OK and OK again to close the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. Note: Please ensure that you are able to add records to the table that these events are to be sent to. This can be achieved through a simple utility such as Microsoft Query. If you are in doubt as to how to go about this, speak to your SQL administrator. - Adding and configuring an EventOutput agent to log alarms to this SQL database. - Open the Agent Configurator dialog. - Add a new EventOutput agent and click the Edit button. - In the Printer Type field, select the SQL option. You will notice that the "Printer Name" and "Setup Data" fields immediately default to a simple form of help. These defaults can be re-created by deleting the contents of the respective field, exiting the dialog box and re-entering. - In the Printer Name field, enter the ODBC data source name that refers to the required SQL database, followed by the username and password required to log on to this database as set up in SQL. Note: Ensure that commas separate these three items. Since no username or password has been specified in this case, this field is simply: AdrEvtSQL,joe,mypassword - In the Setup Data field, enter the table name (specified in the SQL database) followed by a comma delimited list of the required field names. Note: The MAXIMUM size of this Setup Data field is 80 characters, therefore ensure that the table and field names are small enough to all fit. Tip: It is recommended to add the fields ONE at a time and test that events are added to the SQL database before adding the next field. Any problem with any field will prevent records from being added to the database i.e.

In this case this field, after three testing iterations is: Evnts,AgtFld,AgtData,EvtTime , where Evnts refers to the table name. - Enable size Printing and disable Demand Printing and Time Printing to prevent duplicate, out of sequence entries in the SQL table. - Type a 1 into the size drop-down list box, so that size = 1, otherwise you will have to wait until the Page is Full or the File is Full before the agent logs to the database. - Click the Format... button and specify the required columns that are to be added to the fields specified in the Setup Data field. For details of these columns, see EventOutput Agent Column Formatting . Note1: Ensure that these columns correspond to order of the database fields specified in the Setup Data field (in step e), otherwise records may not be added to the database. Note2: Ensure that the specified column widths correlate with the widths of the database fields; otherwise, records may not be added to the database. Tip: Ensure that the total number of columns that you have selected is ONE LESS than the comma delimited items of information in the Setup Data field (in step e). - Click the Compress and OK . - In the Activate section select the Yes radio button and click the Update button to activate the EventOutput agent and click OK to close the edit dialog. - Adding this EventOutput agent to the required Alarm agent . - Then edit the required Alarm agent and browse in this newly created Event Output agent in the Event route (global) destinations section. - Testing that alarm events can be successfully logged to this database . - Place an agent into an alarm state and test that the alarm event(s) are added to the specified SQL database. Note: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting alarm events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry. Title: Logging Alarms to an Access Database
Logging Alarms to an Access Database Top Logging Alarms to an Access Database Tip : The EventLogging agent provides a simpler method for logging incidents to an Access (OLE DB compatible) database. For details, see Configuring EventLogging Agents . In Adroit , an EventOutput agent can be used to log alarm events to an Access database. This requires the following main steps: - Creating the Access database and its associated ODBC data source , which is used by the EventOutput agent to refer to this Access database. - Create your Access Database and save it. Tip1: It is recommended to limit the size of the table and field names as ONLY 80 characters is available to represent the comma delimited list of these names in the EventOutput agent. Tip2: It is recommended to save this database file in the Data subfolder of your Adroit project directory, which is typically ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data'. - Click the Start menu and type in “odbc” and select the appropriate version of the ODBC Data Sources. - Click on the System DSN tab in the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. - press the Add... button. - Double-click the Driver do Microsoft Access (*/.mdb) entry in the Create New Data Source dialog. Tip: This should be the second entry in the list. - Specify the name of this ODBC data source in the Data Source Name field of the ODBC Microsoft Access Setup dialog. In this example the following name is used: AdrEvtMDB Note1: This name will be used to specify this Access database, when configuring the EventOutput agent. Note2: The Description field is optional and adds a description for this data source in the System DSN tab of the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. - press the Select button in the Database group and browse in the path and name of the required Access database, created in step 1. - press OK and OK again to close the ODBC Data Source Administrator dialog. - Adding and configuring an EventOutput agent to log to this Access database. - Open the Agent Configurator dialog. - Add a new EventOutput agent and press the Edit button. - In the Printer Type field, select the SQL option. You will notice that the "Printer Name" and "Setup Data" fields immediately default to a simple form of help. These defaults can be re-created by deleting the contents of the respective field, exiting the dialog box and re-entering. - In the Printer Name field, enter the ODBC data source name that refers to the required Access database, followed by the username and password required to log on to this database as set up in Access. Note: Ensure that commas separate these three items. Since no username or password has been specified in this case, this field is simply: AdrEvtMDB,, - In the Setup Data field, enter the table name (specified in the Access database) followed by a comma delimited list of the required field names. Note: The MAXIMUM size of this Setup Data field is 80 characters, therefore ensure that the table and field names are small enough to all fit. Tip: It is recommended to add the fields ONE at a time and test that events are added to the Access database before adding the next field. Because any problem with any field will prevent records from being added to the database i.e. no warning messages are displayed. Problem areas are the widths of text field; date fields and specific field formatting such as the various Number formats in Access etc.
