Title: Logging diagnostic events to the event log
Logging events to the event log Top Logging diagnostic events to the event log When diagnosing the SmartUI Server, it is possible to log diagnostic information to the event log, which is typically logged to the Application event log category on the local Server computer. These events are typically used for troubleshooting the setting up and licensing the SmartUI Server and establishing the required security, profiles, datasources and projects. Note: Both the computer on which this event log resides and the event log category in which these events are logged are user-configurable. For details on configuring these settings, see General Server settings . When using the event log it may be necessary to clear these events either to pinpoint a current problem by only displaying the most current events or to prevent it from becoming too big. The manner in which these events can be viewed and/or cleared, depends upon how the Server has been launched, as follows: - If the Server is being run as an application then the Activity Monitor can be used. To use the Activity Monitor to display the logged events: Open the Activity Monitor - Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and the SmartUI Server item. - Click the Launch Activity Monitor to open the Activity Monitor. - Note: The Activity Monitor is only displayed if the ActivityMonitorFormEnabled setting for this Server is enabled. For more information on this setting, see Advanced Server settings . The ActivityMonitorFormTitle setting specifies the title of this application. - Warning: The Server window is not displayed if the SmartUI Server is running as a service . - If the server is already running, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - Tip: When the SmartUI Server is running as an application, you may also press the ALT+TAB KEYS repeatedly until the task switcher displays the Server window, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - If the server is already running as a service, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - The Activity Monitor opens and displays information on the Local Machine tab. Click the Display Server Events link from the Tasks panel. This will display the Events dialog. Tip: Press F5 to refresh the list of displayed events, so that the most current will appear at the top of this window. To use the Activity Monitor to clear the event log: Open the Activity Monitor - Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and the SmartUI Server item. - Click the Launch Activity Monitor to open the Activity Monitor. - Note: The Activity Monitor is only displayed if the ActivityMonitorFormEnabled setting for this Server is enabled. For more information on this setting, see Advanced Server settings . The ActivityMonitorFormTitle setting specifies the title of this application. - Warning: The Server window is not displayed if the SmartUI Server is running as a service . - If the server is already running, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - Tip: When the SmartUI Server is running as an application, you may also press the ALT+TAB KEYS repeatedly until the task switcher displays the Server window, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - If the server is already running as a service, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor .

Logging in to a Server Logging in to a Smart UI Server A Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Logging in to a Smart UI Server
Logging in to a Server Logging in to a Smart UI Server A Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. must login to a Smart UI Server, which provides the roaming user profiles and other user-specific settings and default data sources. During the login process a 'connection' is created to transfer data between this Client and Server. Note: When a touch screen is detected, a button appears to the right of the Login Name and Password edit boxes, which if pressed, launches a virtual keyboard for users to type in the required value. To login using existing login settings or a login profile: - Launch the Client to display the User Login configuration dialog. Note: If automatic login enabled this configuration dialog is grayed out as the configured login settings are used - press or hold down the SHIFT key to disable this. - If necessary, select the required profile from the Login Profile list box. The [Default] login profile is initially selected, which specifies the default login settings as specified by this Client. - If necessary, provide the required Login Name and/or Password . Note: If security is not an issue for you, you can bypass the login process by using an automatic login, by checking the Automatically login with these settings next time checkbox (if it is visible). - Click the Finish button. - If this login attempt is successful, then the work environment of this Client will be displayed. - If this login attempt is unsuccessful, see Troubleshooting a failed login attempt . To modify the existing login settings and/or to create a new login profile: - Launch the Client to display the User Login configuration dialog. Note: If automatic login enabled this configuration dialog is grayed out as the configured login settings are used - press or hold down the SHIFT key to disable this. - Click the Change button This launches the Create Connection configuration dialog. For details, see Creating connections . Note1: If either of the login details are modified within this configuration dialog, both the Login Name and Password fields will be correctly updated with these changes once this configuration dialog has been completed. Note2: This configuration dialog can create a login profile out of these new settings too. - Click the Finish button to create this new connection to the Server.

Logging Templates Top Logging Templates You can add Logging templates to configure the default log also known as data log, the process of recording the changes in a value over time to a log file or OLE DB compatible database.

Title: Logging Templates
Logging Templates Top Logging Templates You can add Logging templates to configure the default log also known as data log, the process of recording the changes in a value over time to a log file or OLE DB compatible database. settings for one or more log sets, which are usually manually specified when logging agents. Log sets, in Adroit , specify the logging settings, such as the rate and logging destination, for a particular slot of an agent (process value). Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage Example: You can create a logging template to use for a cluster, which automatically specifies 2 log sets, one for the master and the other for the standby Agent Server. Default templates: The _LoggingDefault template is added for you, providing the Adroit default settings, which you can customise accordingly. Each logging template allows you to specify the Slot (value) that if provided by the agent that you want to log, will be selected by default. The Adroit default for this is the value slot. Then you can specify the following settings for EACH log set: - The required log Set: Specify the zero based index of the required log set this provides the ability to log the same slot (value) to a different destination and/or use a different logging rate and/or use a different logging period. . In other words a value of 0 indicates the first set; 1 indicates the second set; etc. . In Adroit this is the first log set, by default (0). - The logging Destination: the location of the logs of this value, which is determined by the method you are using to log this value, as follows: - Proprietary Adroit log files: specify the full path and file name of the required log (.LGD) file and - OLE DB-compliant database: specify the connection string to the required database. Tip: It is recommended that you copy this connection string from another application instead of manually typing it in, due to its complexity. In Adroit this is not specified, by default (“”). - The log Period in days: specify the required length or time period for logging this value. The Adroit default for this is 10 days, but 31 days are used as the default setting for the logging templates.

- The log Rate in seconds: Specify how often this value must be logged.

Title: Logging Templates
- The log Rate in seconds: Specify how often this value must be logged. This setting can REDUCE the amount of logging required for this value, as follows: if this value changes more than once during this period then the specified Algorithm is used to determine what value is actually recorded. The Adroit default for this is 10 seconds, but 1 second is used as the default setting for the logging templates. - The value Deadband: Specify the MINIMUM amount which ANY change in value must EXCEED in order for it to be logged. This setting can also REDUCE the required number of logged entries for this value. In Adroit this is not specified, by default (0). - The Algorithm to be used: If you are using a Rate greater than 0, this algorithm determines the value that is logged when this value changes more than once during the Rate interval, as follows: 0: actual - the value at the end of the Rate interval. 1: average - a time-weighted average of all the changes that occur during this Rate interval. 2: minimum - the lowest or minimum value at the end of this Rate interval. 3: maximum – the highest or maximum value is logged at the end of this Rate interval. In Adroit this is 0 (actual), by default. Note: By default the slots of the logging template are usually set to the Adroit default settings. To create a logging template: this creates an logging template for the Logging category that is listed beneath the Templates folder. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Logging category within the Templates folder. - Select the Create template… menu item. - Type in the required Template name . Tip: Provide a brief name that makes it easy to identify the purpose of this template. - Click the OK button. This selects and adds this template to the bottom of the list of templates beneath the Logging category. The logging-specific slots are displayed in the right hand pane, with their Adroit Default value . - Customise the default logging parameters (slots) for this template, as follows: To change the value of a slot in the logging template: - Double click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane.

- Provide the required default value for this slot in the Edit template slot value dialog.

Note: If you delete one of these slots then the Adroit default value will be used. Logging Values Top Logging Values How to effectively log your data : guides you to use the fairly complex logging sub-system effectively.

Title: Logging Values
Logging Values Top Logging Values How to effectively log your data : guides you to use the fairly complex logging sub-system effectively. How to Log a Tag (agent.slot) : describes the procedure for logging process values in Adroit . The Datalog agent should ONLY be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. Therefore the logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Note: The DBLog agent is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval that supercedes SQL logging via the Datalog agent. For details, see The DBLog Agent . When recording or logging the values contained in agents in the Agent Server, first decide on the logging method that best suits your logging requirements. Adroit provides the following methods of storing data: Note: The Disable logging on standby setting is now configured PER datalog SET. So you can disable an OLE DB logging set WITHOUT disabling any proprietary logging sets, which typically do not require this setting as each Agent Server logs to their own datalog files. Proprietary Adroit log files: This logging method has been specifically designed for the needs of the SCADA industry to provide improved logging performance, typically achieving sub-second logging rates. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . This rate is determined by configuring the required Time and/or Value Deadbands.

Title: Configuration
Logical and Physical Device Configurations Top Logical and Physical Device Configurations In Adroit , while the installed protocol driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. is the language that needs to be communicated, the devices are the actual translators that use this language to communicate between the front-end devices and Adroit . Each device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. is essentially a logical connection to the front-end device that it is communicating to. Since a total of 65534 devices may be added and used for any one installed protocol driver, the following configuration options are possible: - One protocol driver, with one configured device (logical connection) communicating to one physical device. - One protocol driver, with many configured devices (logical connections) communicating to many physical devices. Each logical device may scan a different area of the PLC. or at different speeds e.g. it is possible to configure 3 devices for a protocol driver in identical fashion and then use one Device agent to scan high-speed items, another low-speed items and the third to scan at normal speeds. - One protocol driver, with many configured devices (logical connections) communicating to one physical device. Each logical device communicates via the same port. In some drivers, the communications are synchronised via this common port. - Many protocol drivers, each with one or more configured devices (logical connections) communicating to many physical devices, via several ports. Note1: Adroit will allow the use of as many protocol drivers (and their devices) as your computer has ports, but two or more different serial protocol drivers (and their devices) may not share the same port. Ethernet and shared media drivers do allow more than one Adroit driver to share the port. Note2: In the case of communications via a gateway or converter each device configured in Adroit must be configured identically except in respect of how it addresses the final front-end device, which the gateway connects to. It is therefore essential to ensure that all the devices that are to be scanned are installed, before any scanning configuration is done. For further details, see About Protocol Drivers and their Devices . -->

Main.csv Top Main.csv This file stores the specific configuration of all the servers within the WanClient.

Title: Main.csv
Main.csv Top Main.csv This file stores the specific configuration of all the servers within the WanClient. The columns, in the order that they appear in the file: - ID Number: This stores a unique number that identifies the server. Note: This number must never be greater than the number in the first column of the System.CSV file. - Server Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the server, if the server is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the server is disabled this is 0. - Server Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the server, if the server is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the server is not deleted this is 1. If the server is deleted then it will be added to the list of servers to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. - Server Title: This stores the name that has been given to the server, which must not more than 90 characters in length. - Server Database: This stores the name of the CSV file, that is also stored in the database folder . This file stores all the tag groups and tag links that belong to the server. - IP Address: This stores the IP address of the WanClient computer or its computer name (provided that the network has a LMHOSTS file or a WINS server to resolve IP addresses from computer names). - Port: This stores the IP port that is used by Wanlink for communications and this can only be set to 51114. - Retries: This stores the number of times that communications are to be reattempted when the communications to this WanServer fail. - Ping Period: This stores the period in seconds to wait after the communications to this WanServer fail before the WanClient will retry to establish communications. - Connect Timeout: This is not being used. - Transaction Timeout: This stores the time in seconds before a requested transaction made to the server fails. The default value of 5 is required for fast networks and a value from 15 – 20 can be used for slower networks. - Beep Enabled: This stores the Beep status of the server, which is configured from the Enable Beep menu item from the Diagnostics menu.

If the server is beep enabled this is 1 and the server will beep every communication cycle, otherwise if the server is beep disabled this is 0, and the server will be silent.

To enable debug disk logging set this to 1 and a file called "wanserverlog.txt", is generated in the Adroit folder, that contains a shadowed list of the transactions that are recorded in the WanServer window, for troubleshooting purposes. - ClusterNames: This setting lists the names of all the clusters that this SmartUI Operator should be aware of, where each cluster name identifies the SmartUI Servers within each cluster.

Title: Configuration
- ClusterNames: This setting lists the names of all the clusters that this SmartUI Operator should be aware of, where each cluster name identifies the SmartUI Servers within each cluster. Note: The cluster names should be separated by semicolons “;” in this list. - ClusterServers: This setting lists the connection details of each SmartUI Server within each of the clusters, specified in the ClusterNames setting, that this SmartUI Operator is able to connect to. The required communication details depend upon the method by which the SmartUI Operator connects to the SmartUI Server, as follows: Directly over the LAN Local Area Network : Clustername~MachineName~Port~CommunicationType~CommunicationMode, where: - Clustername: This is the name of the required cluster, which is ALSO the name of this SmartUI Server. For details on configuring this setting, see General SmartUI Server settings . - MachineName: This is the network name of the computer on which this Server is running; this can also be its IP address. - Port: This is the port used to communicate with this Server, which is specified by the ServerPort setting for this Server. By default this is 9000 . For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced SmartUI Server settings . - CommunicationType: This specifies the type of connection that is made by this Operator to this Server, which currently will always be: MAINDATAPROVIDER. - CommunicationMode: This specifies the manner in which the data is communicated between this SmartUI Operator and Server, this should typically be: SUBSCRIBE. For details of the various methods of communicating data, see Communication methods . For instance, Cluster1~Machine1~ 9000 ~MAINDATAPROVIDER~SUBSCRIBE. On the Internet via the Web service: Clustername~WebServiceURL~Port~CommunicationType~CommunicationMode, where: - Clustername: This is the name of the required cluster, which is ALSO the name of this SmartUI Server. For details on configuring this setting, see General SmartUI Server settings . - WebServiceURL: This is the Internet location of the SmartUI Web Service responsible for providing a gateway between this SmartUI Operator and Server. Managing references Top Managing references Each script object manages a list of external assemblies that is referenced by its associated script file.

Title: Managing references
Managing references Top Managing references Each script object manages a list of external assemblies that is referenced by its associated script file. Click for more information: Each assembly or dynamic linked library (.DLL file), within this list, is externally compiled and contains a collection of properties, methods etc., which are made available to this script and can be implemented within it. Note1: If every script requires the same reference(s) to be added, a common list of assemblies can be specified that will automatically be added to each script object. This list can be separately specified for the SmartUI Designer and Operator, for details see Designer scripting settings or Operator scripting settings . Note2: Any reference(s) that are specified for a script but which cannot be located will be logged to the Application event log for troubleshooting purposes. By default, the SmartUI installation folder (typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI ) and its subfolders are searched for the assemblies that have been or can be referenced by a script. You can specify additional paths that contain assemblies (.DLL files). Although these paths can be separately configured for the SmartUI Server, Designer and Operator applications, they can also be identically configured when these applications are installed on the same computer. Note: The SmartUI Server reference paths apply to scripts running on the Server and so may always vary from the references paths specified for the Operator and Designer. For details on configuring these paths, see Server directory settings . To add or remove a reference to an existing external assembly: - If necessary, edit the required script. The Script Editor is displayed. - If more than one script is opened, select the leftmost tab in the Editor workspace , since this is the only script object that can be edited within the Script Editor . - Click on the Build menu and select References . The Add Reference… configuration dialog is opened, which displays the list of assemblies that are available to be exposed to this script. Tip: This configuration dialog can also be opened by clicking the References toolbar button. - The upper Selected Components list, displays all the assemblies (.DLL files) that have already been added to the Designer . Note: If the required references do not reside in the SmartUI installation folder ( C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI ) and its subfolders then ensure that their locations have been specified in the appropriate reference path setting. For details on configuring this setting, see Server directory settings , Designer scripting settings or Operator scripting settings . Note: By default, this list of components is sorted in ascending order using the Component column. - Only check the checkboxes of the components that you want to create a reference to. Note: An empty checkbox means that a reference will not be created for this component. Tip: Double-clicking on the name of the component or its path will check or empty the checkbox. - Click the OK button of this configuration dialog to update the list of references for this script object and its associated script. To add a reference to a new external assembly for a script: - If necessary, edit the required script. The Script Editor is displayed. - If more than one script is opened, select the leftmost tab in the Editor workspace , since this is the only script object that can be edited within the Script Editor . - Click on the Build menu and select References . The Add Reference… configuration dialog is opened, which displays the list of assemblies that are available to be exposed to this script. Tip: This configuration dialog can also be opened by clicking the References toolbar button.

Use the lower New Components list to browse for and add these required components, as follows: Note: It is possible to add components that have the same name as existing components, in the Selected Components list, as long as the new component exists in a different location.

- There cannot be more than one master server in a cluster.

Title: Rules and implications
- There cannot be more than one master server in a cluster. Hence making a server master will immediately switch the other server to standby mode. - The serverMode and serverState slots between Agent Servers and within an Agent Server are not replicated. - All other server and client clustering operations will operate as normal given the slot values, irrespective of whether a manual or automatic master mode assignment method is used. For instance, the automatic switching UI will track the first healthy master server in its list even if the UI detects more than one healthy master server, when connected to more than one cluster.

As suggested in the above scenarios, start all or part of the cluster servers.

Title: Suggested method of operation
As suggested in the above scenarios, start all or part of the cluster servers. Set the desired master server as master through the various means available to set the serverMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Adding a new cluster server to the cluster will have no effect on the system. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. -->

Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Smart UI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - Right click the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically, and select Create Tag . - Specify the required Tag Name or agent name. The following rules apply when naming agents: - Agent names have a maximum of 27 characters. - Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. - Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ - If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes the purpose or describes the value of this tag (agent) for ease of reference. - Click the Finish button. If necessary, locate the required agent, as follows: In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . In the Edit Analog Agent dialog: - In the Device Span (raw) group, set the Maximum value to 10000000000000. - In the Engineering Span (eng) group, set the Maximum value to 78125000000 and click the OK button. Add and/or Edit a Statistical Agent and in the Edit Statistical Agent dialog: - In the Input Tag edit box, click the browse button to the right of this and select the VALUE slot of the Analog agent that was added in step 1. For details, see Selecting a Tag Using the Agent Explorer. - Click the Start button and then click the OK button. Add and/or Edit an SNMPManager agent and in the Edit SNMPManager Agent dialog: - Ensure that this agent can connect to the required computer. For details, see Connecting to the Managed Device or see SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements for potential issues when monitoring computers. - Click the Browse OID to add button to display the SNMP Objects Browser dialog, if the connection settings are correct. - Select the Browser tab and browse for the OIDs (values) of the required network bandwidth that you want to monitor. For details, see Browsing for SNMP Objects . To monitor the incoming bandwidth, expand the tree to expose this OID: interfaces.ifTable.ifEntry.ifInOctets. To monitor the output bandwidth, expand the tree to expose this OID: interfaces.ifTable.ifEntry.ifOutOctets - Once this branch has been expanded, select the node number that corresponds to required network card and click the Add to list button. Note: Node 1 is not a network card and should not be selected. Tip: To establish which network card corresponds to a node number, examine the values that are exposed by the following OID: interfaces.ifTable.ifEntry.ifPhysAddress, which displays the MAC addresses of the cards associated with each node number. To verify the MAC address of a card, enter 'ipconfig /all' in a command prompt (DOS window), on the required computer, and look at its specified 'Physical Address' value. - In the OID list of the SNMPManager agent, enable the polling of this OID and assign its value to the RAWVALUE slot of the edited Analog agent. - Select the Enable Polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) to start managing this device, by polling (getting), writing (setting) and/or trapping (enabling events) of its OIDs.

text:
For further details, see Global Device Management Settings .

Title: To manually calculate the network card bandwidth:
For further details, see Global Device Management Settings . - Display the rate slot of the edited Statistical agent, to display the selected network bandwidth in kbits/s for the specified network card. Tip: The first few values displayed by this rate slot will not be accurate, as the Statistical agent needs to obtain a number of samples first, before it can calculate the correct value. - Repeat this procedure, as necessary. Note: If any network card (or Microsoft Loopback Adaptor) is disabled, while the computer is being monitored, this will remove its associated node from the SNMP tree, which will prevent the monitoring of the network bandwidth for this node and possibly the others too. Technical explanation of this calculation: - The network bandwidth is an accumulative value of the number of bits that are either received (incoming) or sent (output) from the specified network card. Therefore, its current value must be calculated by subtracting it from the previous value, which is performed by the rate slot of the Statistical agent. - These bits are recorded as octets and so need to be multiplied by 8 before this value displays the number of bits, then the value needs to be divided by 1024 so that it is displayed as kilobits. The Analog agent performs this conversion, since its Device Span (raw) Maximum value of the Analog agent is set to 10000000000000, to ensure that this value will not be exceeded. Its Engineering Span (eng) Maximum value is set to 78125000000, because this is the Device Span Maximum value multiplied by 8 and divided by 1024. - This value must then be calculated over time to give you the value per second. This is why the rate slot of the Statistical agent needs to be displayed -->

Groups are stored in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server .

Title: To manually edit groups:
Groups are stored in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server . This .CSV file is located within the database folder and contains all the specific configuration of the tag groups and their tag links that have been configured within the specific server. The first 6 lines of the file are comment lines. The first two lines show both the name and IP address of the server, to which these tag groups and tag links are associated. The next four lines then provide configuration specific information. The columns, required when configuring a tag group, in the order that they appear in the file: - [GROUP]: This is used to identify that a tag group, as opposed to a tag link, is being specified. Note: This must not be any spaces before the [GROUP]’ indication. - Group Title: This stores the name that has been given to this tag group, which must not more than 90 characters in length. - Group Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the group, if the group is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the group is disabled this is 0. - Group Deleted: This stores the deleted status of the group, if the group is deleted this is 0, otherwise if the group is not deleted this is 1. If the group is deleted then it will be added to the list of groups to be recovered, until the Pack Database file menu item is executed, after which it is permanently removed from this file. - Poll Period: This stores the rate in seconds at which the WanClient should request this WanServer for changes to the tag links within this tag group. The default value of 0 implies "as fast as possible" and the rate will depend on the total number of configured groups. - Buffer size: This is not being used. - Group Type: This stores the communication type required by the tag links within the group. - A Normal group, indicated by a 0, only permits the values of the tags links within this group to be fetched from the WanServer so that the values on the WanClient are updated accordingly. - A Control group, indicated by a 2, also permits the tags links within this group to also send changes from the WanClient to the WanServer. -->

Links are stored together with groups in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server .

Title: To manually edit links:
Links are stored together with groups in the user-specified database filename of their applicable Server, specified when adding a server . This .CSV file is located within the database folder and contains all the specific configuration of the tag groups and their tag links that have been configured within the specific server. The first 6 lines of the file are comment lines. The first two lines show both the name and IP address of the server, to which these tag groups and tag links are associated. The next four lines then provide configuration specific information. Note: Tag links can only be entered into this file below a configured tag group [GROUP]-entry, to which they are then associated. The columns, required when configuring a tag link, in the order that they appear in the file: - Local Tag: This stores the name of the required Adroit tag, located in the local Agent Server, residing on the WanClient computer. - Remote Tag: This stores the name of the required Adroit tag, located in the Agent Server residing on the WanServer computer. - Link Enabled: This stores the enabled status of the link, if the link is enabled this is 1, otherwise if the link is disabled this is 0, and this tag link is not to be communicated to. - Link Method: This stores the communication method by which values are transferred between the two Agent Servers. - A Polled link, indicated by a 0, involves the use of a polling period in which the values are to be fetched. - A Subscription link, indicated by a 1, involves changes being fetched only when they change. -->

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function New Mapping Pair This will display the New Mapping Pair configuration dialog, so that the mapping pair can be named. Then an input and output with the specified name is added to the Inputs and Outputs sections of the spider. For details on adding and configuring mapping pairs, see Adding mapping pairs . Master Recipe Top Master Recipe The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded.

Title: Master Recipe
Master Recipe Top Master Recipe The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. The following are the components of the Master Recipe: - Step: Both master and control recipes consist of sequences of steps. Each step is numbered, and if any new steps are inserted or deleted, the steps are renumbered consecutively. It is important to note that any GOTO STEP references must be manually edited if there has been any change to the order or number of steps. - Ingredient: An agent and slot corresponding to the process variable to be set or downloaded to a front end device (e.g. PLC). The keyword <NONE> when used as an ingredient indicates that no process variable will change for the step. This allows a phase action to take place without having to set any process variable. The ingredient must either be a valid agent and slot having one of the slot types STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER, REAL, or a null entry <NONE> when a control Phase Action entry is needed. - Verification: This is the means of verifying the values written to a front-end device (e.g. PLC). It is represented by an agent.slot that is read after a definite period of the ingredient value being downloaded. This value must be a valid slot. If the value of this slot does not match the value written to the ingredient slot, verification fails. The verification check occurs at the end of a phase. - Phase Boundary: Any step that has a Phase Action marks the end of a phase. - Phase: A phase consists of all steps executed between phase boundaries. - Phase Actions and Tag/Value : A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. Specific Status Bits . -->

Slot Name Type Function blockPeriod INTEGER Block period length (mins).

Title: Slots:
Slot Name Type Function blockPeriod INTEGER Block period length (mins). If block pulses are enabled, this time must be equal to block pulse times. Valid values are from 2 to 60 minutes. blockPulse BOOLEAN External block period pulse scanned from the front-end device (PLC). blockPulseEnable BOOLEAN When True (1) this enables the external block period pulse. blockPulseTime TIME The time of the last external block period pulse. blockTimeLeft INTEGER Time-in-hand (minutes) to the end of the block period. If block pulses are used then this time is simply blockPeriod - (currenttime - blockPulseTime). This is value is zero if the agent is not enabled. catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use only (used for datalog and real-time data catch-up). demand REAL The actual demand for the current block period. This value is rest to zero at the end of the month and is zero if the agent is not enabled. enable BOOLEAN Inhibit maximum demand control input for the periods of the day when maximum demand is not counting. enableMDAlarm BOOLEAN Set Alarm bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds maximum demand limit. enableTag TAGNAME Browse in a Boolean or Real tag to control the value of the enable slot. kVA REAL The instantaneous kVA (apparent power) input. kVAOptimal REAL The recommended kVA consumption to meet maximum demand. kVAr REAL The instantaneous kVAr (reactive power) input (optional). kVArCalc REAL Calculated instantaneous reactive power kVArhTotal REAL Totalised reactive power for the month. If the kVAr slot value is zero, then the kVArCalc slot value is used. This value is reset to zero at the end of the month. kVArTag TAGNAME An optional dereferencing tag for kVAr value. kVASpare REAL The amount of spare kVA capacity for the current period = difference between the current and the optimal or recommended kVA. kVATag TAGNAME An optional dereferencing tag for kVA value. kW REAL The instantaneous kW (real power) input (optional). kWhTotal REAL Totalised kWh for the month kWTag TAGNAME An optional dereferencing tag for kW value. mdActual REAL The actual maximum demand for the month (same as the value slot). mdLimit REAL Maximum demand limit (kVA) mdOverUnder REAL The difference between the current period’s predicted demand and the configured maximum demand. mdPredict REAL The predicted maximum demand for current the block period. This value is zero if the agent is not enabled. mdPrev REAL The previous month’s actual maximum demand. pf REAL Calculated instantaneous power factor resetDay INTEGER Day of month for monthly meter reading/reset. 0 means the last day of the month, otherwise use 1 to 28. resetNow BOOLEAN When set to True (1) this forces a reset of all the calculated readings to zero. resetTime TIME The time of day for the monthly meter reading or reset. timeToMD TIME The time left before reaching the maximum demand at the current consumption for the current block period. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. value REAL The actual Maximum Demand for the month (same as the mdActual slot)

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title: Specifications
- Specify the duration of the block period that your electrical provider uses, in minutes, in the Block period (mins) edit box (the blockPeriod slot). For instance, 30 minutes. - Check the Enable block pulses checkbox (the blockPulseEnable slot) - Specify the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent, in the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) edit box. Tip: If may be useful to specify a value slightly LESS THAN the actual maximum demand limit imposed by your electricity provider, so that there is time for counteractive measures to be taken when this is exceeded. - Check the Enable max demand alarm checkbox (the enableMDAlarm slot) to enable the MaxDemand status bit when the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. - Leave the default Reset configuration, unless you do NOT want to reset the current month’s calculations at midnight on the last day of the month. - Click OK and close the configuration dialog of the MaxDemand agent.

- Alarm the ‘PulseError’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know if the timing of these external block pulses are compromised i.e. as soon as a pulse does not occur at the period specified by the Block period (mins) value. - Alarm the ‘MaxDemand’ alarm type for this agent, so that you will know when the maximum demand limit is exceeded.

Title: Scan the relevant values of this agent to the appropriate front-end device
- Scan the BOOLEAN blockPulse slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that monitors the pulse sent from your electricity provider to signal the start of each block period. - Scan the REAL kVA slot of this agent to a value in a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kVA usage. - If you ALSO want to calculate the instantaneous power factor and reactive power component then also scan the REAL kW slot of this agent to a PLC that measures the total instantaneous kW usage.

text:
- You could display some or all of the following MaxDemand agent slots: mdLimit : the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent.

Title: Display important values
- You could display some or all of the following MaxDemand agent slots: mdLimit : the maximum kVA demand limit for this agent. mdActual : the highest recorded maximum demand for any block period of the current month. demand : the actual power that has been used (kVA demand) for this block period. mdPredict : estimates the total power use (kVA demand) for this block period, by using the demand slot against the remaining time for this block period. mdOverUnder : displays the difference between the Predicted max demand (the mdPredict slot) and the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. timeToMD : indicates how long, in minutes, before the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) will be reached before the end of the block metered period, at the current demand. Note: If you are running safely, this will ALWAYS indicate the end of the current block period. kVAOptimal : the recommended kVA consumption to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. kVASpare : the spare kVA capacity for current period, which is the difference between the Current demand (the demand slot) and the Optimal KVA (the kVAOptimal slot). This specifies a positive or negative amount of kVA that needs to be removed or added to meet (and NOT EXCEED) the Max demand limit (the mdLimit slot) for this block period. Example: For instance, you can create a mimic that allows a manager to know that at the current consumption ( demand slot) that: - the configured maximum demand (the mdLimit slot) will be reached in 12 minutes ( timeToMD slot) which is 3 minutes before the end of the period (the blockTimeLeft slot - timeToMD slot) and - 30kW of load needs to shed (the kVASpare slot is a negative number) to not exceed the maximum demand OR if the process is running safely that 45kW of load can be added (the kVASpare slot is a positive number) to meet the maximum demand) for this block.

- If you want to control the maximum demand by using this agent, then use the MaxDemand status bit of this agent to turn off non-essential equipment via a script.

Title: If necessary, use this agent to control your maximum demand
- If you want to control the maximum demand by using this agent, then use the MaxDemand status bit of this agent to turn off non-essential equipment via a script. Since this status bit is ONLY set when the Enable max demand alarm checkbox is enabled and the predicted maximum demand exceeds this specified maximum demand limit. Related Links: Configuring the MaxDemand agent : A comprehensive description of all the configuration options provided by the MaxDemand agent. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. -->

Title: Merging Data Logs
Merging Data Logs Top Merging Data Logs Adroit provides a means of merging values from a .CSV file into an existing historical database of DataLog agents. The .CSV file may have been originally created by the EXTRACT utility, or by choosing the EXPORT... button in the Datalog Retrieval dialog, or by using a text editor to modify existing files taking care to adhere to the format. The syntax of the command is as follows: merge mc.as,csvfile > jnlfile The abbreviations and examples are as follows: Note: No spaces are required between arguments. Symbol Description Example mc computer name AEPCY4 as Agent Server WestPlant csvfile csv file name or existing agent.slot (of type string) PERIOD01.CSV or CSVFILE.value jnlfile journal file name name of journal file used to record any error messages that may be displayed -->

Message Sending and Processing Slots Top Message Sending and Processing Slots The Command agent provides the following slots that are responsible for processing commands and sending SMS messages, which can be externally manipulated if required: - The lastMsgReceived slot: the most recent data received by this slot, even if identical to its previous contents, will cause it to BOTH process the data and then to send this processed data to the rawValue slot.

Title: Message Sending and Processing Slots
Message Sending and Processing Slots Top Message Sending and Processing Slots The Command agent provides the following slots that are responsible for processing commands and sending SMS messages, which can be externally manipulated if required: - The lastMsgReceived slot: the most recent data received by this slot, even if identical to its previous contents, will cause it to BOTH process the data and then to send this processed data to the rawValue slot. Note1: If this slot receives a command, which has been enabled for this Command agent, then this command will be performed before it is sent to the rawValue slot. For details on enabling commands, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: If pseudonyms and macros have been configured and enabled for this agent, then they can be also used when specifying this data. For details, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . - The value slot: the most recent data received by this slot will also be sent to the rawValue slot. Since this is a standard 80-character String slot and NOT a VARSTRING slot, like these other lastMsgReceived and rawValue slots, other agents are able to be @ scanned to it, so that their STRING slots can be sent by the Command agent instead. The lastMsgReceivedTime slot displays the time of the last message received. The lastMsgReceivedTimeStr slot displays the time of the last message received, as a (var)string. For instance, the value slot of the Command agent can be @scanned to the rawValue slot of a Notify agent, so that the Notify agent's alarm message can be sent to the recipient of the Command agent instead. For details, concerning @scanning, see Scanning from a Slot of Another Agent . - The rawValue slot: this sends the most recent data received by this slot to its associated GSM_SMS device and as it leaves the Command agent, this data will also be placed in its lastMsgSent slot. For details on associating a GSM_SMS device with a Command agent, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Note1: This rawValue slot is also exposed as the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. Tip: The lastMsgSentTime slot displays the time of the last message sent. These slots can either be modified programmatically, via scripting or manually, such as by exposing the required slot and sending messages to it directly by exposing it on a mimic and associating a Data Entry, Operator Action Behaviour to it. For details, see Adding an Operator Action Behaviour or its Data Entry action. -->

Methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form Top Methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form Graphic forms are animated during their design process, by attaching any data element to any property of the graphic form itself or its form components.

Title: Methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form
Steps:
Methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form Top Methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form Graphic forms are animated during their design process, by attaching any data element to any property of the graphic form itself or its form components. Click for more information: Note1: Behaviours provide configuration dialogs that link data to properties. For details, see About Behaviours . Note2: This visual animation or data binding can be used to configure more than just display properties (for example, the Text property of a TextBox control) if required, such as the sizes of controls, their colors and images. Note3: It is also possible to link properties to data elements and properties to other properties too, if necessary. Note4: If a property is connected to a data element that contains more than one value i.e. of type dataset, then the Filter Dataset configuration dialog is displayed, to select which of these value(s) are required. For details, see Filtering datasets . Tip: Run a graphic form, in order to see what the end-user will see. For details, see Running graphic forms . Although the process of animating a graphic form can become involved, there are typically only two methods of linking data to properties within a graphic form: - Direct animation: in this case a data element is directly connected to a property, so that it displays the actual data element value(s). This can be achieved in one of following ways: Note: Although more than one data element can be linked to the same property, most properties will ONLY display the most recently received data element. - You can drag the required data element from the Enterprise Manager and drop it onto the required graphic element a form component that typically provides drawing functionality for the graphic form. See form component. or control a visible form component used to display data or accept user input in the graphic form. See form component. , within the graphic form in the Design workspace . Then select the required property and the necessary spiders and silks will be automatically created for you. For details, see Quickly linking data elements to properties . - If you need to connect a data element to a property of a component a hidden form component that provides additional functionality to this graphic form and some or all of its form components. See form component. , then you need to use the Spider Configuration tool window, to drag the data element, from the explorer tree, on the right, to the required property, in the property tree, on the left. This will manually create the necessary spiders and silk. For details, see Creating silks or Spider Configuration tool window . - Modified animation: in this case one or more data elements are connected to one or more added spiders, which are then connected to one or more properties, so that the properties display modified data element value(s). This can only be achieved within the Spider Configuration tool window and involves the following process: - Add one or more spiders to the center spider workspace. - If necessary, configuring one or more of these spiders as required. - Creating silks to connect: - one or more data elements to one or more of the added spiders - the added spiders together - one or more of the added spiders to one or more properties For details, see Creating silks . Tip: Whenever a property requires the name of a data element, simply drag the required data element to this property and its name will be automatically extracted to specify this property at runtime.

Title: To select the required graphic form
- If necessary, add and/ or select the required Application spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Application spiders . In the Inputs section: - Ensure that the Graphic Form input specifies the required graphic form, as follows: - Either drag the required graphic form onto the Graphic Form input. For details, see Creating silks . - Or specify the required graphic form, as follows: - Browsing: Press the browse button to the right of the Graphic Form input edit field, to browse for the required graphic form using the Graphic Form Selection dialog, which only displays the projects and their graphic forms on each of the connected Servers. - Type in the name of the required graphic form into the Graphic Form input edit field in the following format: [ServerName.]projectName.GraphicFormName. The ServerName component is only required when the graphic form is being opened from a non-default connection (from a Server other than the one used for logging on and off) and is the ServerName setting of this Server. Tip: It is recommended to browse for the required graphic form instead of typing in its name to ensure that this graphic form is correctly referenced. The method used to specify the graphic form affects the way in which this graphic form will be loaded and therefore the speed at which both this and the parent graphic form is opened. Click for more details: When the graphic form is dragged to the Graphic Form input, this preloads this graphic form, which slows down the overall loading of the form containing this Application spider, but will speed up the opening of the form, when this Application spider is triggered. When the graphic form is browsed or typed into the Graphic Form input, this does not preload the graphic form, so the form containing the Application spider opens faster, however, the user has to wait slightly longer for this graphic form to be opened once this Application spider is triggered, while this graphic form is loaded from the SmartUI Server. - Open the Action list box and select the required action. Title: Modifying chart time and/or navigation at runtime
Steps:
Modifying chart time at runtime Modifying chart time and/or navigation at runtime Note: This only applies to Line and XYPlot charts. If necessary, the Line or XYPlot charting control can be altered by your end-users at runtime, to: - configure the charted time details for a real-time or historical trend. Ensure the following Boolean properties of this charting control are enabled: ToolbarVisible , TimeDetailsButtonVisible and TimeDetailsButtonEnabled . Note: Any configuration of the charted time period that is performed in runtime will not be saved. Select the Modify the time details toolbar button from the toolbar. To modify the charted time details at runtime: use the Time Details tab to configure the charted time period and interval for a real-time or required charted time period for a historical trend. Configure the charted time period from the Time Details configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: For ease of use, this tab uses the previously specified Period Type and Timespan time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc. To configure the charted time period for a real-time trend: - Select the Real-time (Current - Timespan) from the list of available Period Type methods for calculating the trended time period. - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. Note: The Timespan property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. For instance, if the trended data is being compacted together then reducing this time-span will result in the data to becoming more clearly differentiated. - If necessary, specify the required update rate for the trended data, in milliseconds, in the Interval edit box. This specifies the interval or period of time in milliseconds that the trend advances in real time (shifts across the screen) or by which it is scrolled, by using the Scroll Left or Scroll Right tools (when provided by the chart toolbar). Note1: The Interval property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. Note2: The Interval property is not required for static trends. To configure the charted time period for a historical trend: Note1: The Timespan property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. Note2: IGNORE the Real-time (Current - Timespan) option! Select one of the following Period Type methods for calculating the required time period: - End Datetime - Timespan: This calculates the required starting date and time, by subtracting the Timespan from the End date and time: . - If necessary, change the currently specified End date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. For details, see Changing the date and/or time. - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. - Start Datetime + Timespan: This calculates the required ending date and time, by adding the Timespan to the Start date and time: - If necessary, change the currently specified Start date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. For details, see Changing the date and/or time. - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box.

For details, see Changing the date and/or time. To configure the chart time navigation tools at runtime: use the Navigation tab to specify which chart time navigation tools are displayed by the chart toolbar and/or configure up to 5 tools that configure custom chart timespans (chart durations). Use the Navigation group of the Navigation tab of the Time Details configuration dialog, to specify which of the following chart time navigation and/or configuration tools you want the chart toolbar to provide, by checking or clearing the relevant checkboxes: Note: The Interval and Timespan properties are typically configured in the Time Details tab of this Time Details dialog. - Show RealTime : when enabled (checked) this displays the Go to real time mode tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the chart right (forward in time) until the real time values of the data are displayed in the chart. - Show Page Right : when enabled (checked) this displays the Page Right tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed data right (forward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). - Show Scroll Right : when enabled (checked) this displays the Scroll Right tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property. - Show Scroll Left : when enabled this displays the Scroll Left tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed left (backward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property. - Show Page Left : when enabled this displays the Page Left tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed data left (backward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). - Show Custom Navigation : This enables (checked) the Custom Navigation group that always displays five tools that when selected configure the Timespan property of this chart to specific time durations. In the SmartUI Designer: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: To modify the properties of a connection:
Steps:
In the SmartUI Designer: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - Right-click the name or icon of the required Server connection and select Connection Properties . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Server computer name. Configure the Connection Settings configuration dialog, as follows: - Specify the required SmartUI Server computer. As follows, when connecting via the local area network: - Either press the Detected Servers... button and double-click the required Server from the list of available Servers, which specifies each Servers' address, port, number of currently connected Clients and version. This is the simplest method. - Or type in the name or IP address of the required Server computer, in the Insert the computer's name or it's IP address edit box or click the Network Servers... button below this field to use the Browse for Computer dialog to locate this computer’s name as you would in Windows Explorer. Note: If the ServerPort setting of this Server is not 9000 (the default), then add a colon “:” after the specified name or IP address to specify this port number. For instance, the following entries connect to a Server computer using a custom port of 9010: 'localhost:9010' or '10.10.10.124:9010'. As follows, when connecting via the Internet: Type in the web location of the SmartUI Server in the Insert the URL to connect to edit box. This is the web site name and virtual folder specified when installing the SmartUI Web Service of this SmartUI Server as follows: http://webSiteName/virtualFolder Tip: Click the Test Connection button to ensure that this SmartUI Server can be located at the specified address. - Specify the User login details of the required user account on this Server computer, in the Name and Password edit boxes. WARNING! ALWAYS specify these details, even if they to remain the SAME - otherwise this connection will FAIL. Note: Ensure that the specified login details are correct and that this user account is either an allowed user or part of an allowed group on this SmartUI Server computer. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . - If necessary, open the Communication method list and select the required way in which you want to transfer data between the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. and SmartUI Server, from the available options. For details on the differences between these communication methods, see About connection communication methods . Note: The available method(s) depends upon the specified connection Type or how the two computers are physically connected. - Click the Save Login Profile button, if you want to save these connections settings to a login profile, for future use when logging into this Client. In this case, specify the required name for this profile in the displayed dialog. Try to keep the names less than 35 characters in size. - Click Finish once these communication settings are complete. Note: If necessary, check the Remember this connection as the default Connection checkbox to make this connection the default connection, which is used when logging into this SmartUI Client. This SmartUI Client computer will then reconnect to the SmartUI Server using these settings. -->

Title: To modify a font by adjusting certain attributes
Steps:
- If necessary, add and/or select the required Font spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Font spiders . - Right-click its title bar and select Add ARGB Properties . Note: Once you add these properties you cannot remove them from this spider. This adds the following six additional Integer inputs to the Inputs section: - Regular: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, removes any Bold or Italic formatting specified for the font. Note: For this reason, you cannot set both the Regular and Bold or Italic properties at the same time. - Bold: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the font in Bold . - Italic: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, displays the font in Italic . - Font size: This Double attribute, specifies the point size of the specified font. - Underline: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, will cause the font to appear with underlines. - Strikethrough: This Boolean attribute, if set to True, will cause the font to appear with a horizontal line through it. Note: You are unable to set both the Underline and Strikethough properties at the same time. - The value of these inputs can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note: The Font size can be specified by a Double, whereas only Boolean values can be used to specify the values of the Regular , Bold , Italic , Underline and Strikethrough font attributes. If other values are typed in, the cell will not accept this input until either this value is removed or the required value is entered instead. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Regular , Bold , Italic , Underline , Font size or Strikethrough input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. The Font output, only displays the Font size attribute. Note: If the Font size attribute is remotely driven, the associated graphic form needs to be displayed in preview mode in the SmartUI Designer before the reported size changes. -->

- Before setting up the SNMPMgr agent, decide which devices you need to monitor.

Title: To implement SNMPMgr agents to monitor a physical industrial network:
Steps:
- Before setting up the SNMPMgr agent, decide which devices you need to monitor. In other words determine the (SNMP) network topology. Tip: It is recommended to create a mimic to visualise the network, because this also assists in quickly detecting of the source of network bottlenecks too. - In the case of the network described by this mimic, it would be necessary to configure seven SNMPMgr agents on the computer running the Agent Server. In other words one SNMPMgr agent is required for each networked device that you need to manage. - Configure each of these SNMPMgr agents to get and/or set the required OID values of their devices. For details, see Configuring SNMPMgr Agents . - Once the monitoring process has begun, the SNMPMgr agent will start: - Polling : to receive values from the device and copy them into the associated tags. Which you can then trend, alarm or log in Adroit : For instance, it is possible to trend object information such as bandwidth; alarm certain conditions on the network, such a computer becoming unavailable and log information, which allows you to determine at which point in history an error or certain condition of the network has occurred, such as its degree of congestion etc. - Writing: to change values of the device when the value of their associated tags change. - Trapping: to receive events from the device, which are placed in a queue that you will typically interrogate by means of a script and respond to the important ones. -->

Title: Monitoring Changing Values
Monitoring Changing Values Top Monitoring Changing Values The Analog and Digital agents provide a change monitoring feature, which is disabled by default, in which a Changed status bit is pulsed when the value (slot) of the agent changes. ONLY use this feature when your operators need to IMMEDIATELY be made aware of ANY change to an Analog or Digital value. In this case you need to: - Enable change monitoring for the Analog or Digital agent, as follows: Either edit the agent and check its Enable change monitoring for this agent checkbox or set its BOOLEAN enableChange slot to 1. When enabled, this feature will instantaneously pulse (set and then immediately reset) the Changed specific status bit of this agent. Note1: The valuePrev slot contains the previous value (the value slot) of this agent. Note2: The timePrev slot that provides the timestamp of this previous value ( valuePrev slot) and is only affected by putslots to the value slot NOT the time slot. This slot is not currently supported in realtime catch-up. - Alarm the Changed alarm type of this agent, so that you can report incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). via the various alarm routing destinations, such as by viewing it using an Alarm List Viewer window or logging it to a printer or database or sending it to an operator via SMS etc. Otherwise, if you want to know when the value of an agent changes, but your operators do not necessarily need to know about this change immediately, then audit the Agent Server and specify the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). in an Audit agent. This logs a record to the Agent Server audit database when this tag changes in value. This record also contains the previous and current values of this tag and the name of the currently logged on user at the time of the change. This method also allows you to keep track of important process values, which can reside in agent types other than Analog or Digital. For more details about auditing the Agent Server entails and how this can be used, see Agent Server Auditing . For more details about how the audit agent supplements the auditing of the Agent Server, see The Audit agent . -->

Title: To monitor a digital (Boolean) value
- If necessary, add and/or select the required Counter spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Counter spiders . - In the Inputs section: - Drag the required data element and/or property (Data spider) or output from a spider onto the Digital Input input. For details, see Creating silks . Note: Ensure that the data type of this value is Boolean, i.e. either 0 or 1, since any other numerical value will not record any events. - Set the Start Stop input to 1, to begin the monitoring period. The monitored period will end when this Start Stop input is set to 0 or any other value except for 1. Note: The value of this input can either be supplied by another spider or Data spider (e.g. property or data element) via a silk or it can be typed in manually. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the Start Stop input name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. - The following outputs in the Outputs section are calculated for this value, during the monitored period: Note: The times are displayed in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. Tip: At any time, you can reset these counters (set the values of all the outputs to 0 and restart their counters). - Off Counts: The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0) over the monitored period or since the last reset. - Current Off Time: When the Digital Input is currently in the Off state (0), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the Off state. - Last Off Time: This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the Off state (0). - Total Off Time: The total time at the Digital Input has spent in the Off state (0), this is effectively the sum of all the Last Off Time periods during the monitored period or since the last reset. - On Counts: The total number of incidents or events when the Digital Input was in the On state (1) over the monitored period or since the last reset. - Current On Time: When the Digital Input is currently in the On state (1), this value displays the actual time of this duration, which is incremented every second, while Digital Input remains in the On state. - Last On Time: This displays the last duration of time, during the monitored period or since the last reset, when the Digital Input was in the On state (1). - Total On Time: The total time at the Digital Input has spent in the On state (1), this is effectively the sum of all the Last On Time periods during the monitored period or since the last reset. -->

Monitoring Scanning in Adroit Top Monitoring Scanning in Adroit The Scanning Monitor utility is designed to assist experienced users in fine-tuning the Adroit scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance, by providing an intuitive report-like view of advanced diagnostic information.

Title: Monitoring Scanning in Adroit
Steps:
Monitoring Scanning in Adroit Top Monitoring Scanning in Adroit The Scanning Monitor utility is designed to assist experienced users in fine-tuning the Adroit scanning subsystem to achieve optimal performance, by providing an intuitive report-like view of advanced diagnostic information. This utility provides information on the scanning (communications) configuration for a particular Agent Server to and from its configured front-end devices, such as PLCs, RTUs etc. and is particularly useful in tuning polled driver's polling intervals. How to use the Scanning Monitor Tip: The Scanning Monitor utility can generate a report of your current scanning configuration of an Agent Server to indicate how well it has been configured. For details, see Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report . However, OPC Server devices not in "sync-poll mode", and telemetry applications will find this utility less useful. For additional ways to optimise the scanning configuration see Scanning Optimization Tips . To launch the Scanning Monitor Utility . For details on how to specify the Agent Server in order to monitor its scanning configuration, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . This utility consists of following three hierarchically arranged list boxes, each of which expose increasingly detailed communication information for the selected Agent Server: Note: The contents displayed in a list depend upon the selection(s) made in the list immediately above it. - The device list, which displays all the devices that have been configured in the .WGP file (Agent Server database file) of the selected Agent Server. For details, see Devices within Selected Agent Server Database . Note: This will ONLY list the devices, which have been used to scan tags within the current project that is running on the Agent Server, even though other devices may have been added and configured on the computer. - The scan job list, which displays the scan jobs for the selected device or devices. For details, see Scan Jobs within Selected Devices . Note1: Any configured @scans will NOT appear in this utility because scan agents are NOT involved in @scanning functionality - these are simply internal slot-to-slot subscriptions that change in real time mode. Note2: Scan jobs are automatically created by Adroit to group the scanned tags together in such a way as to minimise scanning load and to maximise throughput. - The tag list, which displays the tags (scan points) grouped within the selected scan job or jobs. For details, see Tags within Selected Scan Jobs . In addition to these lists, the Servers combo box and the Connect… button can be used to specify the Agent Server whose scanning configuration is to be monitored, while the Help button displays this help topic. Note: The name of the currently selected Agent Server and any connection-related errors are displayed within the status bar of this utility. For details, see Current Agent Server Connection Details . -->
