Monitoring Tags (Values) Top Monitoring Tags (Values) IMPORTANT: This utility is NOT included in the Adroit installation and must be separately installed from the Additional Adroit Components installation.

Title: Monitoring Tags (Values)
Steps:
Monitoring Tags (Values) Top Monitoring Tags (Values) IMPORTANT: This utility is NOT included in the Adroit installation and must be separately installed from the Additional Adroit Components installation. The Tag Monitor utility is designed to display the current values of one or more tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). values from a particular Agent Server without having to specifically draw a mimic to do so. While these values are initially displayed in tabular format, they can also be monitored in a trend format too. Launching the Tag Monitor Utility . For details on specifying the Agent Server whose tags are to be monitored, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . This utility contains the following three tabbed pages, each of which display a different view of the values of the tags that are being monitored by this utility from the selected Agent Server: - Tags: This is the default page, in which the list of tags monitored by this utility can be configured. This page displays the most current value of each tag, from the selected Agent Server, in tabular format and also allows tags to be added to the trend. For details, see Configuring Monitored Tags . Note: While the list of tags configured by this page are saved, the Graph and Subscription log pages are not. - Graph: This displays a trend of the values of any tags that have been trended. For details, see Trending Monitored Tags . - Subscription log: This contains a record of the most recent values that have been received for all the tags that have been added to this utility. For details, see Logging Recent Subscriptions . The utility also provides the following functionality that is common to all three tabs: - Close: This button saves and closes this utility. For details on what is saved, see the Save button below. - Start: This button starts the tag monitoring process. Note: In this operational mode, tags cannot be added or removed from the Tags tabbed page. - Stop: This button stops the tag monitoring process. Note: In this operational mode, tags can be added or removed from the Tags tabbed page. - Save: This button saves the list of tags monitored by this utility and a number of operational parameters but not the Graph and Subscription log pages. For details, see Saving the Tag Monitor Utility . - Write value: This button displays the Enter new value dialog, to change the value of the currently selected tag. Note: When modifying the value of a tag, only valid values will be accepted. - Browser: This button launches the agent browser utility. Note: Any tags that are double-clicked in the browser will be automatically added to Tags list of monitored tags, provided that this utility is in the stopped state. - Server info…: This button displays a dialog of information concerning the currently connected Agent Server, whose tags are being monitored. - Help: This button displays this help topic. - Both the Servers combo box and the Connect… button can be used to specify the Agent Server whose tags are to be monitored. For details, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . Note: The status bar displays information concerning the current operation of the tag monitoring process. For details, see Current Operational Status . -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Value String, Double or Integer This value of this String, Double or Integer is monitored and it determines the color of the color output. - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function New State This will open the Enter a State dialog, to either specify the required String value or the required range of Integer or Double values. For details, see Creating states . Note: These states can also be removed from this spider. For details, see Removing states . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function color color The color of this output is determined by the current value of the Value input, as follows: - For String values: if the current value matches any of the specified states then this output is set to its associated color. - For Double or Integer values: if the current value falls within the range of a defined state then this output is set to its associated color. - If the current value cannot be matched to any of the defined states, then the output displays the default "Control" color instead. Note1: These states are processed in order from top to bottom, until the first match is found, after which the remaining states are ignored. Multiple Log Sets Top Multiple Log Sets Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant.

Title: Multiple Log Sets
Multiple Log Sets Top Multiple Log Sets Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. Instead of specifying only a single rate and period per datalog agent configuration, you can create multiple log sets within a single datalog agent. In other words, if you need to log a given tag (agent.slot) at different sample/window settings, you can simply create multiple log sets with these different permutations for the SAME tag, without creating separate datalog agents for each permutation. Click for the advantages of using log sets: The advantage of using multiple log sets is this case is that it - prevents cumbersome configuration - reduces the number of required datalog agents - and subsequently decreases the memory requirements and thereby improves performance. Multiple log set usage example: For example, a user may wish to log a tag at 1 second for 2 days, and at 10 seconds for 7 days, and at 60 seconds for 30 days and at 1 hour for 365 days. Each of these interval/period specifications constitutes a log set. In the above diagram, two log sets are used for each of the two logged tags. The first log set may be at 1 second for 2 days and the other, 10 seconds for 7 days. It is possible to configure these sets in various combinations. For instance, all the slower logging rates for all tags may be logged to one file while the faster logging rate for all tags logged to another separate file. Alternately, the file for each tag (or set of tags) may be distinct from another tag (or another set of tags) even though each tag may have multiple sets of logging. Thirdly, it is also possible to place all logging into one central file. The data for each datalog agent can be extracted and saved to a CSV file for analysis. When multiple log sets are used, the data for each log set can be extracted and saved to a separate CSV file. Data log clients (for example, trends and OLE method calls) will always retrieve data from a matching sample rate set.

If there is no matching sample rate set, data will be retrieved from the best matching set.

Title: Multiple Log Sets
If there is no matching sample rate set, data will be retrieved from the best matching set. The matching criteria will take the requested rate and period into account. Therefore, trend windows configured at trend rates that match the data log rate will ensure that the data from an actual set is always displayed as long as the required period is within that set. Configuring multiple log sets . -->

MultiState Data Model Top MultiState Data Model The MultiState agent models a logic table or truth table , which can be used to define the operating and control sequence for equipment and is typically used to control drive groups.

Title: MultiState Data Model
MultiState Data Model Top MultiState Data Model The MultiState agent models a logic table or truth table , which can be used to define the operating and control sequence for equipment and is typically used to control drive groups. Its logic or truth table has the following properties: - Up to a maximum of 16 discrete states, such as, for example, Group Auto Ready and OFF, Group in hold, etc. Each state can have a description text up to 64 characters long. - A maximum of 16 inputs , various unique combinations of which are used to define the discrete states. These inputs can originate from any Boolean, Integer, or Real data, but will be converted to Boolean TRUE/FALSE indications on being stored in a MultiState agent. MultiState inputs can be sourced either from agents, such as existing Digital agents or directly from PLC registers. This latter option is facilitated by the ability to scan directly into MultiState agent’s inputs (. rawValue slot) without going through an interposing conditioning agent like a digital, and can yield some very substantial benefits in terms of reducing the total number of agents that need to be engineered for a project. - Any number of Boolean outputs , can be set TRUE or FALSE on attainment of a particular state. - A current state variable, containing the agent’s currently active state. Because there are a maximum of 16 states, 16 agent- Specific Status Bits are used to hold the current state. This approach, namely having a separate bit dedicated to each state, leads to a smooth integration with the Classic user interface multicolor Behaviour, by allowing a different text, line and/or background color for each discrete state. In addition, these bits can be individually alarmed using existing Adroit alarming mechanisms, which means a wide variety of alarm strategies can be developed. - If a Multistate input bit is driven by a Digital agent in addition to being scanned to the field, then this input bit will reflect the state of this Digital agent, ignoring any changes made to this Multistate agent’s "rawValue" slot from the field. Note: It is recommended that the Marshal agent be used for this type of application instead. - A current state string, containing the state description text for the MultiState agent’s currently active state.

- Each state therefore has the following properties: - A state number (1 -16), corresponding to the state’s bit position in the MultiState agent’s status word.

Title: MultiState Data Model
- Each state therefore has the following properties: - A state number (1 -16), corresponding to the state’s bit position in the MultiState agent’s status word. - A state description text string up to 64 characters long. - A 16-bit input-true mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be TRUE for the state to be active (see Common Status Bits ). - A 16-bit input-false mask, defining which, if any, of the 16 inputs need to be FALSE for the state to be active. - An output-true list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set TRUE on attainment of the state. - An output-false list, comprising any number of Boolean agent.slots that are automatically set FALSE on attainment of the state. -->

Furthermore, because of the distributed nature of Adroit it is possible for multiple Agent Servers to be part of the same project, so that Adroit cannot prevent agent names from being duplicated.

Title: Agent Naming in a Distributed System
Steps:
Furthermore, because of the distributed nature of Adroit it is possible for multiple Agent Servers to be part of the same project, so that Adroit cannot prevent agent names from being duplicated. Therefore, the following two approaches can be taken to resolve the potential duplication of names in a distributed installation when referencing agents: - Either the user can ensure all agent names on all Agent Servers are unique, perhaps by keeping a master list. Adroit will assist the user with a prompt to warn him that he is adding a duplicate agent name, with an option to continue or not, whenever he attempts to add an agent name that exists on another Agent Server. - Alternatively, the user may permit duplicate agent names to exist on different Agent Servers but prefix the required Agent Server name to explicitly specify these agent names. For details, see Agent Referencing Convention . For further details about agents, see About Agents . For further details on projects, see About Adroit Projects . -->

Title: Network and Sharing Settings

Network and Sharing Settings Top Network and Sharing Settings You can use the Network and Sharing Center option in the Control Panel to make changes in your computer's network configuration after installing Windows. To make changes to the Computer Name and Identification, Services, Protocols, Adapters and Bindings, you must be logged on as a member of the Administrators group for your computer. (For full details refer to the Windows Reference Manual). The Computer Name must not contain spaces and must be less than or equal to 11 characters long. If you are using Adroit as a standalone system, without a network card installed , the Agent Server will not be able to connect to the User Interface. To circumvent this problem, select the Adapters property sheet in the Network dialog and Add the MS Loopback adapter. -->

Non-english operating system security configuration Top Non-english operating system security configuration Currently if you install SmartUI on an operating system in an international (non-english) language, you need to perform the following configuration in order to login using the built in Windows Administrator user to give it full access to the SmartUI Server: - Create a new group in Windows.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Non-english operating system security configuration Top Non-english operating system security configuration Currently if you install SmartUI on an operating system in an international (non-english) language, you need to perform the following configuration in order to login using the built in Windows Administrator user to give it full access to the SmartUI Server: - Create a new group in Windows. Click for how to do this in Windows XP: click the Start menu, Settings , Control Panel , Administrative Tools , Computer Management , then right click the Groups folder of the Local Users and Groups and select the New Group... menu item. - Add your Administrator user (and if necessary, any other user you want to grant FULL access to the Server) to this group. - Open your SmartUI installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI ) and delete the Data sub folder. - Launch the VIP Config.exe (typically using the installed SmartUI Config shortcut from the Adroit 10 program group). - Open the Security Setting page of the VIP Server, as follows: from the Welcome page, click the Setting up the VIP Server and click the Security Settings option to display this page. - Add this group to the Selected Groups list of BOTH the group selectors (the GlobalSecurityGroups and InitialServiceGroups). This additional configuration is necessary because Microsoft.NET does not support multiple languages well. Click for more details: Built in Windows users, such as “Administrator” and also “Guest” or “User” are translated into the foreign language as is their required keyword BUILTIN\\, and the .NET Framework does not return the properly translated versions, resulting in the "Request time out" error message on log in. -->

Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Logical Result Boolean If this input is specified, then this Boolean value is NOTed and this result is assigned to the Logical Result output. For details, see NOTing logical expressions . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Logical Result Boolean This has the inverse value of the Logical Result input. -->

Obtaining KPI Values Top Obtaining KPI Values One of the possible uses of the database of incidents logged by your AlarmManagement agent/s is to determine how well your process or your operators are meeting the KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives.

Title: Obtaining KPI Values
Obtaining KPI Values Top Obtaining KPI Values One of the possible uses of the database of incidents logged by your AlarmManagement agent/s is to determine how well your process or your operators are meeting the KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. that you have set for them regarding alarming . The AlarmManagement agent provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1. If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. The AlarmManagement agent automatically calculates the following KPIs: - The kpi24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current 24 hour period. - The kpiMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current month. - The kpiPrev24Hrs slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous 24 hour period. - The kpiPrevMonth slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous month. - The kpiPrevShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the previous shift. - The kpiShift slot records the number of alarms per hour for the current shift. - The kpiTotal slot records the number of alarms per hour for the all incidents found in the database. Furthermore, the AlarmManagement agent provides you with the ability to obtain the values of 6 user-defined KPIs. IMPORTANT: Each KPI must be a SELECT query that is performed on the database of logged incidents that returns a SINGLE numeric value called kpi . Example of a KPI query: The following query returns a SINGLE value called kpi: SELECT COUNT(Idx) / (MAX(CONVERT(float, dt) * 24) - MIN(CONVERT(float, dt) * 24)) AS kpi FROM HistoricalIncidents These user-defined KPI Queries support the following optional parameters: The following parameters MUST ALL BE encased within a pair of SINGLE quotation characters: - %now - the current date and time Usage example (in SQL): The following example retrieves the average active time for the last 8 hours. SELECT AVG(ActiveTime) AS Kpi FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > DATEADD(Hour,-8,'%now') AND dt < GetDate() - %s1b - shift 1 start time - %s1e - shift 1 end time - %s2b - shift 2 start time - %s2e - shift 2 end time - %s3b - shift 3 start time - %s3e - shift 3 end time Usage example (in SQL): SELECT AVG(ActiveTime) AS Kpi FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE (dt >= '%s1b') AND (dt < '%s1e') The AlarmManagement agent therefore provides 6 sets of the following 3 slots, where [x] is a number from 1 to 6: - kpi[x]Query: A VARSTRING slot, that contains the KPI query, which is saved in the WGP file. - kpi[x]Description: A VARSTRING slot, that contains the description of this KPI, which is saved in the WGP file. - kpi[x]: A REAL slot, which retrieves the value of the KPI query. IMPORTANT: If the KPI query returns multiple columns and/or rows and not a SINGLE value, this kpi[x] slot will be set to 0.0. Note: These KPI queries are automatically executed by the AlarmManagement agent when a new record is added to the Historical Incidents table.

You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements AND add your own custom KPIs that your user-defined KPI Queries can use.

Title: Obtaining KPI Values
You can change the KPI values that are used by these default queries, so that they better comply with your specific requirements AND add your own custom KPIs that your user-defined KPI Queries can use. Customizing KPI target values : If necessary you can set KPI target values that your own custom KPI queries and certain default queries use, so that these queries better comply with your specific requirements. -->

Title: OEE Agent - Database File Format
OEE Agent - Database File Format Top OEE Agent - Database File Format For a detailed description of any of its slots, see Slot Details . See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description AUR The autoReset Boolean slot that determines whether this agent automatically resets the calculated OEE and KPI data at the end of every shift. TP1 Defines what type of signal is attached to input1 , as follows: 1=Accumulator: The input1 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. This input1 type must be reset to 0 at the end of every shift using the agent’s ShiftEnd status bit as a trigger. 2=Totaliser: The input1 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. This input1 type is never reset to 0. 3=Rate per hour: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. 4=Rate per min: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. 5=Rate per sec: The input1 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. TP2 Defines what type of signal is attached to input2 , as follows: 0=Unused: This means that input2 is not used. The KPI is calculated using input1 against time. 1=Accumulator: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. This input2 type must be reset to 0 at the end of every shift using the agent’s ShiftEnd status bit as a trigger. 2=Totaliser: The input2 slot is interpreted as an accumulated production count over time e.g. 123 bags. This input2 is never reset to 0. 3=Rate per hour: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per hour production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value 4=Rate per min: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per minute production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. 5=Rate per sec: The input2 slot is interpreted as a per second production rate which will be integrated by the agent over time to produce a totalised value. If type2 is not set to 0 (Unused), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode. UN1 Specifies the units for the input1 slot e.g. tons/hr UN2 Specifies the units for the input2 slot AVA The available Boolean slot that determines whether the machine/process is currently available for production. The state of this slot affects the accumulation of availableCurrShift time. RUN The running Boolean slot that determines whether the machine/process is currently running. The state of this input affects the accumulation of runtimeCurrShift and downtimeCurrShift times. ENA The enable Boolean slot that determines whether this agent is enabled for operation or not. CAP The designCapacity Real slot which is the designed rate/capacity of the process/machine, as a per hour value for use in OEE calculations. INA The inactivityPeriod Integer slot which is the period defined in seconds that determines an inactive input signal. If the measurement variable ( input1 slot) remains static for this configurable time, the agent will interpret the process/machine as not running.

QUA The qualityFactor Real slot, which is an external quality percentage factor used against the internally calculated quality component for OEE calculations.

Title: OEE Agent - Database File Format
QUA The qualityFactor Real slot, which is an external quality percentage factor used against the internally calculated quality component for OEE calculations. SHF The shiftAgent Tagname slot, which is the Shift agent that specifies the current shift information. If no Shift agent is specified, then it is assumed that the agent is running in a “batch mode” where the onus remains on the user to trigger an OEE data snapshot followed by a reset at the end of every batch. AVATAG The availableTag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the available slot. RUNTAG The runningTag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the running slot. IN1TAG The input1Tag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the input1 slot. IN2TAG The input2Tag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the input2 slot. REJTAG The rejectCountTag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the rejectCount slot. PROTAG The productTag Tagname slot,which is the optional tag reference for the product slot. BADTAG The batchIDTag Tagname slot, which is the optional tag reference for the batchID slot. KPIT The kpiTarget Real slot, which is the target KPI value. This value is used simply used for calculation of the kpiPercent slot value as a percentage. KPILO The kpiLo Real slot, which is the Low alarm value for the KPI value as a percentage. KPILL The kpiLoLo Real slot, which is the Low-Low alarm value for the KPI value as a percentage. QUAT The qualityFactor Real slot, which is the external quality percentage factor used against the internally calculated quality component for OEE calculations. QUAL The qualityLo Real slot, which is the Low alarm value for the quality component of OEE as a percentage. QUALL The qualityLoLo Real slot, which is the Low-Low alarm value for the quality component of OEE as a percentage. PERT The performanceTarget Real slot, which is the target for the Performance component of OEE as a percentage. PERL The performanceLo Real slot, which is the Low alarm value for the performance component of OEE as a percentage. PERLL The performanceLoLo Real slot, which is the Low-Low alarm value for the performance component of OEE as a percentage. AVAT The availabilityTarget Real slot, which is the target for the value for the Availability component of OEE as a percentage. AVAL The availabilityLo Real slot, which is the Low alarm value for the Availability component of OEE as a percentage. AVALL The availabilityLoLo Real slot, which is the Low-Low alarm value for the Availability component of OEE as a percentage. OEET The oeeTarget Real slot, which is the target for the OEE value for the oeeCurrShift slot. OEEL The oeeLo Real slot, which is the Low alarm value for the OEE value as a percentage. OEELL The oeeLoLo Real slot, which is the Low-Low alarm value for the OEE value as a percentage. CONN The connection Varstring slot, which is the optional OLE DB connection string for logging of KPI and OEE data. SRAT The sampleRate Integer slot, which is the rate at which samples are sent to the database, in minutes (1-60) or 0 to disable this. SBY Disable on standby – this disables writing to SQL on the standby server to avoid double entries. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 ShiftEnd Pulsed on at the end of every shift to allow interested parties to perform shift end operations. status bit 17 Downtime On when the process/machine is available but not running or the input1 slot is detected as being inactive (exceeded the configured inactivityPeriod slot without changing). status bit 18 KPILow On when the kpiPercent slot is equal to or below the low alarm ( kpiLo slot). status bit 19 KPILowLow On when the kpiPercent slot is equal to or below the low-low alarm ( kpiLoLo slot). status bit 20 QualityLow On when the qualityPercent slot is equal to or below the low alarm ( qualityLo slot). status bit 21 QualityLowLow On when the qualityPercent slot is equal to or below the low-low alarm ( qualityLoLo slot). status bit 22 PerformanceLow On when the perfomancePercent slot is equal to or below the low alarm ( perfomanceLo slot). status bit 23 PerformanceLowLow On when the perfomancePercent slot is equal to or below the low-low alarm ( perfomanceLoLo slot). status bit 24 AvailabilityLow On when the availabilityPercent slot is equal to or below the low alarm ( availabilityLo slot). status bit 25 AvailabilityLowLow On when the availabilityPercent slot is equal to or below the low-low alarm ( availabilityLoLo slot). status bit 26 OEELow On when the oeeCurrShift slot is equal to or below the low alarm ( oeeLo slot). status bit 27 OEELowLow On when the oeeCurrShift slot is equal to or below the low-low alarm ( oeeLoLo slot). status bit 29 Unlicenced On when the required OEE Count (which specifies the maximum allowable instances) as specified by the Agent Server license is either missing or has been exceeded. status bit 30 InvalidShift On when the Shift number is equal to zero … not necessarily an error as this can, for example, occur due to no shifts being defined on weekends. status bit 31 ConnectionError On when either connection string is invalid OR a transaction error has occurred.

OID List OID List The SNMPManager agent can manage a device by getting and/or setting SNMP managed objects (OID values) from a single device on the network.

Title: OID List
Steps:
OID List OID List The SNMPManager agent can manage a device by getting and/or setting SNMP managed objects (OID values) from a single device on the network. All the selected OIDs are added to the list in the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog. Tip: You can use the Export button to save and/or bulk configure these OIDs within a .CSV file. For details, see Exporting the OID List . Each OID in this list contains the following columns: - I (Index): The zero-based integer index of this SNMP object in this list. Note: This index is used to select and/or configure OIDs in this list from outside of this agent. For details, see Externally Accessing the OID List . - E (Enable): This checkbox determines whether the OID value will be copied into the specified Tag at the applicable rate, so that it can be monitored. For details, see Enabling the Monitoring of OID Values . - W (Writable): This checkbox determines whether this OID value will be changed when the value of the specified Tag changes. For details, see Enabling the Changing of Values . Note: Please ensure that the returned data type can be written to. For details, see: SNMP Object Value Return Types. - OID (Object Identifier): The OID of this SNMP object depends on the type of selected object: - A General SNMP object: This field simply states "General Object". For details, see Selecting General SNMP Objects . - A Browsed SNMP object: This field specifies the unique numeric description of this OID. For further details, see Selecting Browsed SNMP Objects . - Name: The textual description this OID, which also depends on the type of selected object: - A General SNMP Object: The name of this object is prefaced by [G#], where # indicates the order of this object in the General tab of the SNMP Objects Browser dialog. - A Browsed SNMP Object: This field typically provides a partial textual description of its OID field. - Type (Return type): This field displays the following integer values that represents the type of data returned by this OID, which therefore determines which agent/s you can use to store this data: Value OID Return Type 2 Integer or Integer32 3 Bits 4 Octet String 5 Null 6 Object Identifier 16 Sequence or Sequence Of 64 IP Address 65 32-bit counter 66 32-bit gauge 67 Time ticks 68 Opaque 70 64-bit counter 71 Unsigned 32-bit value Note: For a description of these data types, their recommended (appropriate) agent types and whether they can be written, see: SNMP Object Value Return Types. - Current Value: This field displays the last value of the OID that is ENABLED for monitoring. In other words, this field is ONLY updated when the corresponding E field is enabled and the Enable Polling option (BOOLEAN start slot) is selected and its value has changed within the last polling period. - Tag (Agent.slot): The appropriate tag that either contains or writes to this OID value. Use the Browse tag button to specify the required tag. For details, see Select a Tag Using the Agent Explorer. - Rate: If this OID value changes faster or slower than the default Poll rate for this agent, then specify the required rate, in milliseconds, in this field. If you specify 0 then the default rate of this agent is used. Note: This rate can be less than 5 seconds, the minimum for the Poll rate for this agent. The following buttons are also provided: - Add OID manually button: Displays the Add OID entry dialog to add one or more SNMP objects to the list manually.

For details, see Adding OIDs Manually .

Title: OID List
Steps:
For details, see Adding OIDs Manually . Tip: Use this when the SNMP enabled device is not physically connected to the computer. - Edit OID list button: Displays the Edit OID entry dialog to edit one or more SNMP objects in the list. For details, see Editing Listed SNMP Objects . - Browse OID to add button: Displays the SNMP Objects Browser dialog to add one or more SNMP objects to the list. For details, see Selecting SNMP Objects . - Remove selected row button: Deletes the currently selected row in the list of selected SNMP objects. WARNING! This deletion is performed immediately - no confirmation dialog is displayed. - Browse tag button: Displays the built-in agent explorer to specify the required tag (agent.slot) in the Tag field of the currently selected row in the list of selected SNMP objects. - Auto-refresh values checkbox: If checked, this retrieved the values of all the OIDs in the list, at their configured poll rates, so they change as fast as they are being monitored. This disables the Refresh button. - Refresh button: Queries the specified device for the latest values of all the OIDs in the list. - Update button: Saves any configuration changes that have been made, such as when you select the Enable polling or Disable polling options for this agent. Tip: Ensure this is clicked BEFORE clicking the Refresh button; otherwise the configuration changes may be lost. -->

OLE DB Datasources Top OLE DB datasources An OLE DB datasource exposes the data contained within an OLE DB compliant database or data store.

Title: OLE DB datasources
Steps:
OLE DB Datasources Top OLE DB datasources An OLE DB datasource exposes the data contained within an OLE DB compliant database or data store. This data is contained within fields in one or more tables. For a practical example of using Select queries one of which uses parameters, which are supplied by controls on a graphic form, see How to chart and/or report data from a database . For an example of using a DataBinder to read and/or write data in a database to and/from a control on a graphic form, see How to write and or read database data from a control . Click for more details: OLE DB is an open standard for accessing data from a variety of sources — both relational and non-relational data including: mainframe and hierarchical databases; e-mail and file system stores; text and graphical data and custom business objects etc. An OLE DB data or service provider is required, before a database or data store can become OLE DB compliant. This data provider ensures that the database shares its data in a uniform or consistent manner using OLE DB. This datasource is added to and configured within the Datasources category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . For more details, see Adding OLE DB datasources . Click for advanced OLE DB datasource usage information: - This datasource can be updated, locked or removed, if necessary. For details, see Updating datasources , Locking datasources or Removing datasources . - Instead of manually duplicating an OLE DB datasource from one Server to another, especially when many queries and/or stored procedures have been configured, it is possible to export and import the required datasource. For details, see Exporting datasources . - When connecting to a SQL database, the table, view, stored procedure and user function names support schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table, view, procedure or function has a different schema name, then this is indicated in brackets after the name of the table, view, procedure or function. This means that you can now have a table, view, procedure or function with the same name as another table, view, procedure or function as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note1: This datasource provides the following as its data elements: its tables, their fields and any queries which have been created. Note2: Currently both the Client and Server computers need the required OLE DB data provider to be installed. Both computers also need access to the required data store in order to establish a connection to it. Note3: If necessary, the access to this OLE DB datasource, its data and/or queries can be controlled. For details, see Securing datasources . Note4: Each table is monitored at an individually configurable interval for new or updated data by the Server. Note5: Queries can be executed, by using Special Function spiders. Also, if using SQL, please ensure that all time based queries adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd. For details, see Executing queries and stored procedures . An OLE DB datasource is identified in the Datasources category in the Enterprise Manager , which can be identified by its specified name or icon . When this datasource is opened, it displays the following main branches: - Tables : contains all the data exposed by this data store, within its tables and their fields. Title: OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR)
OLE Server Interface Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The OLE Server Interface allows third party client applications to interact with standalone or distributed Agent Servers. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™, Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. Note: The Adroit Server ActiveX Control (adroitx.ocx) is provided as an alternative to this OLE Server interface. See Adroit Server ActiveX Control . Monitoring Real-time Data describes the steps you need to take to provide continuously updating real-time data for your application. The examples are shown in VBA for ease of understanding. The Adroit Automation Interface describes the OLE Automation or Programmability Interface for Adroit OLE Server Data Objects, which is a set of OLE Automation methods and properties exposed by the Data Objects. These methods are callable as functions and these properties are settable/gettable as variables by container applications. Note1: Adroit also provides a scripting interface, namely the Adroit system object . This is not the same as the OLE Server interface; in fact, certain tasks can only be accomplished via the OLE interface, like adding and removing tags. It is possible, however, to use the OLE Server interface within this scripting interface. Note2: Any pokes performed, using this Adroit OLE Automation Interface will require a scan point license for each unique tag that is "poked". This also applies to the use of functions that use pokes internally, such as AlarmTag , LogTag , and ScanTag . Note3: Fetching values of logged data (by using the FetchChanges and/or FetchValues functions) does not use scan points. -->

OLE Server Interface API for Adroit Agent Servers Top OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) API for Agent Servers This OLE Server Interface Specification forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Agent Servers. It effectively defines a contract, by means of which third party client applications can interact in a rich variety of ways with standalone or distributed Adroit configurations. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™ , Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc. It is an implementation of the Windows Open Services Architecture, Extensions for Real-time Market Data (WOSA/XRT) standard, as created by the Open Market Data Council For Windows (Microsoft Part Number 098-54432). Unlike other WOSA standards such as MAPI, ODBC, and TAPI, WOSA/XRT does not require new APIs to be defined, nor does it require any production code from Microsoft (other than the OLE DLLs). This is possible because WOSA/XRT leverages the existing architecture and binary standard provided by OLE. Specifically, WOSA/XRT uses the existing OLE interfaces: Uniform Data Transfer and OLE Automation. The Basics . Visual Basic for Applications . Philosophy for End User Applications . This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own drivers or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. - An OPC Item

This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own drivers or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. - An OPC Item: is a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. - OPC Data Types: OPC is based on OLE, which uses Variants for all data transferred in transactions. A Variant is basically a block of data preceded by some information indicating the actual type of data in the block. A program will automatically convert Variants received to a data type that it is familiar with. Conversions are standardised, and automatically occur in high-level programming languages. - An OPC Server is a data source or I/O Server, conforming to the OPC Data Access Specification e.g. the Adroit OPC Server . - An OPC Client is an application, which uses the data provided by an OPC server, such as HMI software. -->

Title: How to perform an HDA operation to recover missing data:
Steps:
- You need to have scanned at least one tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). to an OPC server that supports Historical Data Access (HDA). - You need to know the extent of the missing data. In other words, the Adroit tags, scanned to this OPC HDA server, that are missing data and the start and end dates and times of this data loss. - You need to add the following Execute Command Behaviour to a picture element on a mimic, so that you can launch the OPC Historical Data Access (HDA) dialog that is used to retrieve the missing data, as follows: - Add/edit the required mimic and/or picture element. Tip: Right click the picture element to display its Associated Behaviours dialog. - Double click the Execute Command Behaviour in the Possible Behaviours list. - Select the Execute DLL function option from the Commands list. - Type the following into the File name edit field: adrhdacl.dll,OpenHDA,0 - Click the Finish button to close the open dialogs. - Click the Toggle view toolbar button to toggle this mimic into operating mode (and save the changes). - HDA operations can only be performed while the Agent Server is running. - Click the picture element that has the assigned Execute DLL function to launch the OPC Historical Data Access (HDA) dialog. - Specify the extent that the missing data, by providing the requisite dates and times in the From and To edit fields. - Choose one of the following methods to retrieve the missing data for the affected Adroit tags from the OPC HDA server, starting from the From date and time and ending at the To date and time: - Poll file: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags specified by a text file that you create, as follows: - Create a text file that contains a list of the affected tags, with each tag on its own line and use the following file extension, when saving this file: .hda.tags.txt – for instance myHDAtaglist.hda.tags.txt. - Click the Poll file… button to browse for and open this file. Tip: Use the Agent Browser utility to paste the required tags (agent.slot) names into this text file to ensure that there are no spelling errors when creating your list of tags. This method is recommended when the affected tags are spread across numerous OPC Client devices, making the other methods cumbersome to use. - Poll device: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags within this OPC Client device, as follows: - Select the name of the device, from the OPC Client Devices tree on the left hand side. - Click the Poll device button. This method is recommended when the majority of the scanned tags in this device are missing data and you want to fill in these data gaps for all the affected scanned tags. - Poll group: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags within one or more Scan agents (scan jobs) of a specific OPC Client device, as follows: - Select the name of the device, from the OPC Client Devices tree on the left hand side. - Select the required Scan agent, which contains some or all of the scanned OPC items that are missing their data. - Click the Poll group button. This method is recommended when you want to fill the data gaps for a subset of the scanned tags that are contained within specific Scan agents.

Tip: Both the tags and the OPC items that they are scanned to are displayed in the right hand Items pane, when you click on a Scan agent (scan job) in the Devices tree, so that you can identify the affected tags.

Title: How to perform an HDA operation to recover missing data:
Steps:
- You need to have scanned at least one tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). to an OPC server that supports Historical Data Access (HDA). - You need to know the extent of the missing data. In other words, the Adroit tags, scanned to this OPC HDA server, that are missing data and the start and end dates and times of this data loss. - You need to add the following Execute Command Behaviour to a picture element on a mimic, so that you can launch the OPC Historical Data Access (HDA) dialog that is used to retrieve the missing data, as follows: - Add/edit the required mimic and/or picture element. Tip: Right click the picture element to display its Associated Behaviours dialog. - Double click the Execute Command Behaviour in the Possible Behaviours list. - Select the Execute DLL function option from the Commands list. - Type the following into the File name edit field: adrhdacl.dll,OpenHDA,0 - Click the Finish button to close the open dialogs. - Click the Toggle view toolbar button to toggle this mimic into operating mode (and save the changes). - HDA operations can only be performed while the Agent Server is running. - Click the picture element that has the assigned Execute DLL function to launch the OPC Historical Data Access (HDA) dialog. - Specify the extent that the missing data, by providing the requisite dates and times in the From and To edit fields. - Choose one of the following methods to retrieve the missing data for the affected Adroit tags from the OPC HDA server, starting from the From date and time and ending at the To date and time: - Poll file: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags specified by a text file that you create, as follows: - Create a text file that contains a list of the affected tags, with each tag on its own line and use the following file extension, when saving this file: .hda.tags.txt – for instance myHDAtaglist.hda.tags.txt. - Click the Poll file… button to browse for and open this file. Tip: Use the Agent Browser utility to paste the required tags (agent.slot) names into this text file to ensure that there are no spelling errors when creating your list of tags. This method is recommended when the affected tags are spread across numerous OPC Client devices, making the other methods cumbersome to use. - Poll device: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags within this OPC Client device, as follows: - Select the name of the device, from the OPC Client Devices tree on the left hand side. - Click the Poll device button. This method is recommended when the majority of the scanned tags in this device are missing data and you want to fill in these data gaps for all the affected scanned tags. - Poll group: This method retrieves the data values for all the tags within one or more Scan agents (scan jobs) of a specific OPC Client device, as follows: - Select the name of the device, from the OPC Client Devices tree on the left hand side. - Select the required Scan agent, which contains some or all of the scanned OPC items that are missing their data. - Click the Poll group button. This method is recommended when you want to fill the data gaps for a subset of the scanned tags that are contained within specific Scan agents.

OPC Server Security Issues Top OPC Server Security Issues Note: If you still experience issues even after following this procedure, then consult the Configuring OPC DCOM Settings.pdf document in the Adroit Documentation folder of the Adroit DVD , which provides a clear description of the configuration of all the required DCOM settings.

Title: OPC Server Security Issues
Steps:
OPC Server Security Issues Top OPC Server Security Issues Note: If you still experience issues even after following this procedure, then consult the Configuring OPC DCOM Settings.pdf document in the Adroit Documentation folder of the Adroit DVD , which provides a clear description of the configuration of all the required DCOM settings. OPC client applications are generally unable to connect to remote OPC servers due to DCOM and Windows security reasons. We therefore recommend that both the OPC clients and OPC server computers reside within the same domain to reduce the possible security issues. If this is not possible then please: - ensure that the required user accounts (and their passwords) are configured on all OPC client and server computers and - ensure that any change to these access details (a user name and/or password) are replicated to all these computers. We also recommended that you configure the lowest or minimum level of DCOM security for both OPC client and server computers, as follows: These settings prevent the domain configuration and the login user names and passwords of each computer from affecting the OPC client to OPC server connection. Note1: In very rare cases, some 3rd party OPC Servers or Clients may enforce security, which overrides the following settings and not allow them to work. This is not a problem with the Adroit OPC components. Note2: Your network administrator may need to perform these settings. On OPC Client computers: - Set the Default Authentication Level to (None), as follows: - Click the Start menu and select the Run… option. - Type in DCOMCNFG.EXE and press ENTER. The Component Services dialog is displayed - locate My Computer in the left hand pane. (Console Root > Component Services > Computers > My Computer) Right-click this and select Properties to display the My Computer Properties dialog. Example screenshot: - Select the Default Properties tab in the displayed dialog. - Ensure that the Default Authentication Level list box is set to None . Example screenshot: - Select OK and close any opened dialogs. On OPC Server computers: - Set the Default Authentication Level to (None) ), as per the explanation above [except do NOT close the open dialogs at the end of this procedure] - Add the "Everyone" group to both the Default Access Permissions and Default Launch Permissions , as follows: Select the COM Security tab of the My Computer Properties dialog. - Click the Edit Default… button in the Access Permissions group - Select the Everyone group in the list and click the OK . - Click the Edit Default… button in the Launch and Activation Permissions group. - Select the Everyone group in the list and click the OK . - Select OK and close any opened dialogs. If an OPC client application is unable to browse OPC servers on some remote computers Perform the following procedure on each of these remote computers: - Click the Start menu and select the Run… option. - Type in DCOMCNFG.EXE and press ENTER. The Component Services dialog is displayed - locate DCOM Config in the left hand pane. (Console Root > Component Services > Computers > My Computer >DCOM Config) Locate OpcEnum in the right hand pane, right-click this and select Properties . Example screenshot: Select the Application tab, browse for OpcEnum in the list and double-click it. - Select the Identity tab in the OpcEnum Properties dialog. - Select This user and specify the user and password of an administrator. Note: Specify domain user names as "domainname\username". - Click the OK and close all the open dialogs. -->

OPC Server Troubleshooting Top OPC Server Troubleshooting See OPC Server Security Issues ,since these are the most prevalent issues relating to the use of OPC.

Title: OPC Server Troubleshooting
OPC Server Troubleshooting Top OPC Server Troubleshooting See OPC Server Security Issues ,since these are the most prevalent issues relating to the use of OPC. If for no obvious reason: - You are losing OPC communications when running Adroit (or any OPC client application) on a Windows XP computer . - It takes 30-45 seconds to connect to a remote OPC Server This is caused by a problem on Windows XP operating systems that allows you to add datagram DCOM protocols, even though these operating systems do not support datagram protocols for DCOM. To resolve this, remove the datagram protocols from the DCOM protocols, so that ONLY connection-orientated protocols are listed, as follows: - Launch the Component Services Administrative tool. For Windows 2000: From the Start menu, select Programs , Administrative Tools and then click Component Services OR run DCOMCNFG and the refer to step 4. For Windows XP: From the Start menu, select Settings , Control Panel , Administrative Tools , then click Component Services . - In the console tree of the Component Services Administrative tool, right-click the computer on which you want to configure the protocols to display the menu. - Click the Properties menu item to display the Computer Properties dialog box. - Click the Default Protocols tab. - If any Datagram protocol (UDP/IP or IPX) are listed, then select each one and click Remove . - If you do not have any of the connection-orientated protocols in the list, click Add to display the Select DCOM Protocol dialog box. - Choose Connection-orientated TCP/IP Protocol as the protocol sequence, and then click Ok . - Repeat step 7 to add other connection-orientated protocols to the default protocol. - Move the Connection-orientated TCP/IP Protocol to the top of the list. - Restart the computer for these changes to take effect. For more information on this subject refer to http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;EN-US;q245197 and/or http://support.microsoft.com/default.aspx?scid=kb;EN-US;q242022 -->

Title: To open a graphic form from an event
Specify the required graphic form, as follows: - If necessary, add and/ or select the required Application spider and/or open its configuration view. For details, see Adding Application spiders . In the Inputs section: - Ensure that the Graphic Form input specifies the required graphic form, as follows: - Either drag the required graphic form onto the Graphic Form input. For details, see Creating silks . - Or specify the required graphic form, as follows: - Browsing: Press the browse button to the right of the Graphic Form input edit field, to browse for the required graphic form using the Graphic Form Selection dialog, which only displays the projects and their graphic forms on each of the connected Servers. - Type in the name of the required graphic form into the Graphic Form input edit field in the following format: [ServerName.]projectName.GraphicFormName. The ServerName component is only required when the graphic form is being opened from a non-default connection (from a Server other than the one used for logging on and off) and is the ServerName setting of this Server. Tip: It is recommended to browse for the required graphic form instead of typing in its name to ensure that this graphic form is correctly referenced. The method used to specify the graphic form affects the way in which this graphic form will be loaded and therefore the speed at which both this and the parent graphic form is opened. Click for more details: When the graphic form is dragged to the Graphic Form input, this preloads this graphic form, which slows down the overall loading of the form containing this Application spider, but will speed up the opening of the form, when this Application spider is triggered. When the graphic form is browsed or typed into the Graphic Form input, this does not preload the graphic form, so the form containing the Application spider opens faster, however, the user has to wait slightly longer for this graphic form to be opened once this Application spider is triggered, while this graphic form is loaded from the SmartUI Server. Tip: If the selected graphic form contains aliases, then you can expose these aliases as inputs, by right clicking the title bar of the spider and selecting the Add Alias Inputs option. - Open the Action list box and select Open . This will add the Open Graphic Form As , TemplateSet and Level inputs.

Title: To open a graphic form from an event
- Open the Open Graphic Form As list box to specify how this graphic form is to be opened, as follows: - ModalForm: the graphic form opens as a separate window that requires the user to interact with it or close it before being able to continue using the application. This is the default selection - ModelessForm: the graphic form opens as a separate window that allows the user to interact with it and also return to a previous task without closing it. - TabPage: the graphic form opens normally, as another tabbed page within the workspace. - Replace: the graphic form replaces the graphic form that is currently displayed in the workspace. - Template Graphic Object : the graphic form is opened within a specific Template Graphic Object control. This option displays the Template Graphic Object input to specify the name of the required TemplateGO or TemplateGONavToolbar control, from the list - assuming that one or more of these controls have been added to the graphic form on which this Application spider is on. - The TemplateSet input can specify which template set to activate when this graphic form is opened, by linking it to an appropriate String input (to dynamically set this at runtime). - The Level input can specify which level should be visible when this graphic form is opened, by linking it to an appropriate String input (to dynamically set this at runtime). - Specify where this graphic form will open as follows: - Use the Location input to specify the location of the opened graphic form, by linking it to an appropriate location input (to dynamically set this at runtime). Click for more details: This location input, should be a Point data type the format of this data type are two integer values separated by a comma e.g. 34,56. or a String in the format: 'X,Y' - representing the X and Y coordinates of the upper left corner of the graphic form e.g. 50,50 For example, if the graphic form is opened on the mouse click event, then pass the mouse location as the Location input and the desired size , which can vary depending on where the user clicked. - Check the Center Screen checkbox (this is checked by default) to open this graphic form in the center of the screen. - Uncheck the Center Screen checkbox and use a Click event to trigger this spider and open this graphic form where the user clicks.

Title: End-user interaction:
- Sorting of columns: Click the heading of the column that you want to sort the displayed data by. This will sort the column in ascending order icon: , click the column heading again to sort the column in descending order icon: . Note: Only the selected columns are displayed. For details, see Selecting alarm columns. - Resizing of column widths: Position the mouse pointer to the left of the column heading until the pointer changes to the following icon . Either double-click to auto-size the column to fit the largest entry or click and drag to the required column size. - Setting number of displayed alarms: When the Show All checkbox is checked this control will only display the number of alarms currently specified by the Maximum Alarms Visible spin control. However, when the Show All checkbox is cleared then the number of displayed alarms can be selected using the Maximum Alarms Visible spin control. Note: The ShowAllAlarms and MaxAlarmsVisible properties determine the initial configuration of these controls. For details, see Important AlarmViewer properties. Tip: The specified number of displayed alarms will only be the most recent alarms, when the Alarm Time column is sorted in descending order. - Acknowledging of alarms: Select the required alarm and click the relevant button that is displayed beneath this AlarmViewer control, as follows: - Global Acknowledge: When an alarm is globally acknowledged, any remote stations that are also viewing this alarm, do not need to acknowledge this alarm, as they will see that it has been globally acknowledged elsewhere. Note: If a globally acknowledged alarm is removed from the alarm list, then the alarm will no longer be visible to the remote alarm windows. Tip: To globally acknowledge ALL the displayed alarms, click the More options link (in the bottom right corner of the AlarmViewer control) and its Global Acknowledge All option. - Local Acknowledge: When an alarm is locally acknowledged, any remote stations that are also viewing this alarm, will also need to acknowledge this alarm, even though they will see that it has been acknowledged elsewhere. Tip: To locally acknowledge ALL the displayed alarms, click the More options link (in the bottom right corner of the AlarmViewer control) and its Local Acknowledge All option. The acknowledged alarm will then change to the required color combination. For details, see Customizing alarm colors. Note: The following Boolean properties of the AlarmViewer determine which of these alarm acknowledgment options are available: AlarmGlobalAcknowledgeButtonEnabled , AlarmGlobalAcknowledgeAllMenuItemVisible , AlarmLocalAcknowledgeButtonEnabled and AlarmLocalAcknowledgeAllMenuItemVisible . - Inhibiting (shelving) alarms: you can both inhibit ( shelve alarm shelving is the process of removing an alarm from the entire alarm system for a specific time period. This also known as inhibiting an alarm. ) and uninhibit alarms via the More options link (in the bottom right corner of the AlarmViewer control), as follows: To inhibit (shelve) alarms: Note: Once you inhibit an alarm it is both acknowledged and cleared so it is removed from the alarm list. - Select the alarms that you want to inhibit (shelve) in the list. - Click the More options link (in the bottom right corner) and its Inhibit selected alarms option. IMPORTANT: This option is only enabled when one or more alarms are selected. In the Inhibit alarms with reason dialog: Tip: The list of the currently selected alarms are provided to check if the required alarms are selected. - Specify the required Inhibit until date and time, which by default is 24 hours from the current time. Either as a specific Date and time (which cannot be in the past) or Forever , which effectively deactivates this alarm. - Specify the required Reason for shelving (inhibiting) these alarms.

The Operator (the currently logged in user) is also automatically added to this alarm inhibiting event.

Title: End-user interaction:
The Operator (the currently logged in user) is also automatically added to this alarm inhibiting event. - Click the Inhibit button. To uninhibit alarms: Note: After uninhibiting an alarm that was active, it is put back into an active state so that it reappears in the alarm list. - Click the More options link (in the bottom right corner) and its View inhibited alarms option. In the View inhibited alarms dialog: - Select which of the alarms that have already been inhibited in this alarm list that you want to uninhibit, either using the Select All button or manually select the required ones. By default this list is sorted by the Inhibit until column in descending order, so that the alarms that are configured to be inhibited for the longest time are displayed at the top of the list. The Operator (the currently logged in user) is also automatically added to this alarm uninhibiting event. - Click the Uninhibit button. Note: The following Boolean properties of the AlarmViewer determine which of these alarm inhibiting options are available: AlarmInhibitSelectedAlarmsMenuItemVisible and AlarmViewInhibitedAlarmsMenuItemVisible . - Specifying Reasons and/or Notes: This is ONLY possible if your Adroit installation uses the AlarmManagement agent, as follows: Note: The Reasons and Notes button is ONLY displayed if the Boolean AlarmReasonsAndNotesButtonVisible property of this control is set to True, this is False by default. - Either, select a current alarm and click the Reasons and Notes button to specify any reasons or notes for this alarm or to view ALL the instances of this specific alarm that currently require reasons and/or notes to be specified. Tip: Click the View all button in the dialog, if you want to see ALL the alarm instances that currently require reasons and/or notes to be specified - Or simply click the Reasons and Notes button to view ALL the alarm instances that currently require reasons and/or notes to be specified. This either displays the Alarm Reasons and Notes dialog or an error message if your Adroit installation does NOT use an AlarmManagement agent. To specify a reason for an alarm: - If necessary, select the required alarm instance from the Current Incidents grid. - Click the required reason from the Reasons list. This displays the list of configured sub-reasons for this reason in the Sub-reasons list. - Click the required sub-reason. - Click the Commit button to save this change to the database. To specify a note for an alarm: - If necessary, select the required alarm instance from the Current Incidents grid. - Type this note into the Notes text box. - Click the Commit button to save this change to the database. The AlarmViewer control, like the Adroit Alarm Viewer window, displays the active alarms within the alarm list of an Alarm or AlarmList agent. For details, see AlarmViewer controls. -->

Operating charting controls Operating charting controls This topic briefly explains how end-users are able to interact with charting controls, in run-time i.e.

Title: Operating charting controls
Operating charting controls Operating charting controls This topic briefly explains how end-users are able to interact with charting controls, in run-time i.e. typically when its graphic form is opened in the Smart UI Operator. General charting control interaction: Charting toolbar : This toolbar allows your end-users to print and/or preview the chart, change the magnification of the charted data, rotate the chart and if necessary chart additional data, amongst other actions. Tip: You can hide or show this user toolbar, by using the following shortcut: CTRL+M. Note: Enable the (Appearance) ToolbarVisible property of this charting control to display this toolbar. The appearance of certain tools are also controlled by Boolean properties. Chart interaction: Users can interact with the plot area of the chart, as follows: - Display or hide series: Check or clear the relevant checkboxes in the series legend (on the chart), if these appear. - Zooming in: To zoom into a particular region of a chart - Click the top left most corner of the area that needs to be magnified or enlarged in the trend. - Hold the left mouse button down and drag down towards the bottom right hand corner of the required area. - This will display a dashed box that defines the area of the graph that will be enlarged. - Release the left mouse button once the required area has been defined. Tip: The toolbar button provides generalized zooming functionality, by decreasing the scaling by 10%. Note: When using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values, the width (Interval) of the chart cannot be changed when zooming. Tip: When using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values, scroll back by one interval and then zoom in. - Panning (moving the trended data): Right-click and drag to move to data that is above, below, to the left or right of the current chart area. Note: This is especially useful if you have zoomed into historical data when using a Line or XYPlot to trend real-time values. - Reset zooming and panning (return to original magnification and location): Click anywhere in the graph, hold the left mouse button down and drag upwards towards the top left hand corner and release the left mouse button. Note: Ensure that a sizable area has been defined before releasing. Tip: It is also possible to use the Zoom home functionality provided by the toolbar to reset the zooming. Line and XYPlot charting control interaction: Trending of data: The Line and XYPlot charting controls can trend live data, as follows: - When the charting control is displayed in run-time any historical data for the data elements connected to its series, is fetched from the relevant datasource(s) and displayed. Note: The configuration of the TimeInfo property determines whether this charting control displays real time or historical trending. For details, see Important charting control properties. - If this charting control has been configured for real time trending, then as the current data is received from the relevant datasources, this data is immediately plotted. Note: The rate at which the data is fetched is dependent upon the configuration of its Interval property. - If this charting control has been configured for historical trending, then only the data recorded for these data elements during the specified period of time will be displayed. Note: The charted time period can also be altered at runtime, however any changes made will NOT be saved. For details, see Modifying chart time at runtime .

Charting data legend: The data legend is typically displayed beneath Line and XYPlot charting controls to provide statistical information about the series: Each of the following columns, which are listed from left to right, can be sorted and resized, as required: - Series: The names of the charted series of data.

Title: Operating charting controls
Charting data legend: The data legend is typically displayed beneath Line and XYPlot charting controls to provide statistical information about the series: Each of the following columns, which are listed from left to right, can be sorted and resized, as required: - Series: The names of the charted series of data. - Minimum: The lowest value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. - Maximum: The highest value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. - Average: The average value of each series for the currently displayed “window” of charted data, which is updated continuously. Note: When the Scroll line to view historical values toolbar option is enabled, two additional columns are added to the legend after this column, namely Historical and Time , which display the value and the date and time of the historical value currently selected by the scroll line. - Current: The current or last value of each series of charted data, which is updated continuously. - Count: The number of values/points plotted by the current series. - Std Dev: The standard deviation of the current series or a measure of the degree of variance within this series. - Errors: When doing historical trending, this displays any historical data retrieval errors for this series. Note: Enable the (Appearance) DataLegendVisible property of this charting control to display this toolbar. Tip: The height of this legend and the widths of these columns can also be configured using the DataLegend properties of the charting control. -->

Operating FileBrowser controls Top Operating FileBrowser controls This topic briefly explains how end-users can view, edit, upload and/or delete documents provided by the FileBrowser control, at runtime.

Title: Operating FileBrowser controls
Operating FileBrowser controls Top Operating FileBrowser controls This topic briefly explains how end-users can view, edit, upload and/or delete documents provided by the FileBrowser control, at runtime. To open a document: navigate to and double click the document, just like when using Windows Explorer. To add a document: right click the required folder and select the Upload Document item. SmartUI transfers the file that you browse in to the SmartUI Server. To edit a document: open (double-click) a file and make the necessary changes and save and close it. SmartUI transfers this modified file to the SmartUI Server, ensuring that the SmartUI Server is always updated with the latest changes. To delete a document or folder: right click it and select the Delete menu item and then click the Yes button on the confirmation dialog. WARNING! This removes the selected files and/or folders and their sub-folders from the SmartUI Server – so use this with caution! To refresh the display of part or the entire folder tree: right click the required folder and select the Refresh item. Note: If this is applied to a folder, then all of its sub-folders are also refreshed. This displays all the files that you have added and removes any files/folders that you have deleted. -->
