This will display the Smart UI Operator window. - Open the required graphic form in the Projects tool window, as follows: - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name the Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . - If necessary, expand the Projects category. - Click the plus box to the left of the project icon of the required name. Tip: You can also open a project by double-clicking on its name or icon. - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name its required existing folder(s), until the required graphic form is displayed. - Double click this graphic form. This will open the selected graphic form in the Smart UI Operator window. - To display the Projects tool window, for instance, to open another graphic form, press CTRL+O or right click and select Toggle Operator Mode . - To switch between more than one graphic form, it is necessary to display document tabs within the Smart UI Operator window, by either pressing CTRL+T or right click and select Toggle Graphic Form Tabs and then select the tab, at the top of the Operator window that corresponds to the name of the required graphic form. - To display the Smart UI Operator window in full screen mode (without a title bar), right click and select Full Screen . - To configure the Smart UI Operator window to always be displayed above all other applications that may be open on your system, right click and select Always On Top . Note: These are only a few of the configurable options provided by the Operator, for more details, see Customizing the Smart UI Operator work environment . - To close the Smart UI Operator window, either press ALT+F4 or right click and select Exit . -->

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Operating TrendConfigurator controls Operating TrendConfigurator controls This topic briefly explains how end-users can define set/s of values, at runtime in the TrendConfigurator control, which are trended using the associated LineChart control. Note: By default, the run-time configuration of all TrendConfigurator controls are stored in a user profile variable called TrendConfigurator . Therefore if you want to maintain separate lists of sets for your TrendConfigurator controls, then rename this variable of each TrendConfigurator control in the The Setting Name to use to load and save the Set configuration to the Users Profile field of the General Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog (the UserProfileSetting property). For each Pen (tag or value) that you select to be trended as part of a set, you can specify the following: IMPORTANT: You need to click the Save Set button (on the right of the TrendConfigurator control ) after adding or configuring one or more series to this list, to save these changes to the current set (as specified by the Set Name drop-down list on the right of the TrendConfigurator control). Otherwise when you close this graphic form, the new series and/or configuration changes will be lost. Note: You may need to click the Refresh Chart button to view with any series that you add to the current set. - Color: Use the color box to choose the required color for this series or value (and its axis color if it has its own custom axis) in the associated LineChart control. - If displayed, the Area column typically allows the specific plant area to be specified, in which this tag is physically situated (unless the PresetArea property has been specified). - If displayed, the Device column typically allows the specific FED device to be specified, in which this tag is being communicated (unless the PresetDevice property has been specified). - Pen: The name of the tag of this series. When using the Adroit mode: A browse (...) button appears to the right of this field so that users can also browse in additional tags to the Pen drop-down list at runtime. Note: These additional tags can be removed from the Pen drop-down list at runtime, by selecting the required tag in the list and clicking the button on the right. - Title: Edit the name of the series or value that is displayed in the legend of the associated LineChart (if you choose this value to be visible in the legend by checking its Leg checkbox). Note: By default this column displays the description of the tag as this is usually more descriptive than the tag name itself. However, if you want the series to display the tag name [AgentName.Property(Slot)Name] instead then uncheck the Use Pen (Tag) Description for Series Names instead of Tag Names checkbox in the General Settings tab (the UsePenDescForSeriesName property). - Value: The current value of the tag being used for this series when it was selected. - Unit: If necessary, specify the required unit to specify on the custom axis of the series on the LineChart for the trended value or series. If you are using the MAPS or Adroit modes, then this is retrieved for you, for Analog tags. - Vis: This checkbox toggles the series or value visibility on the associated LineChart. In other words this series is displayed in the LineChart when checked (the default setting) and it is hidden when unchecked. - Leg: This checkbox toggles the series or value visibility in the legend of the associated LineChart.

In other words this series is displayed in the legend when checked (the default setting) and it is hidden when unchecked.

Title: Configuration
In other words this series is displayed in the legend when checked (the default setting) and it is hidden when unchecked. - Axes: This checkbox determines whether this series or value will be charted using the default Y (or value) axis when unchecked OR whether a custom Y axis will be used, when this is checked (the default setting). When using custom Y axis then, the following fields are used to configure the display of this axis in the associated LineChart: - X-Pos: Specify the horizontal position of this custom Y axis, relative to the position of the default Y axis, as a percentage of the total horizontal width (size) of the default X axis. In other words, a value of a 100 moves the custom Y axis to the other side of the LineChart. Note: A positive value shifts this custom Y axis to the right of the default Y axis, by the specified amount; while a negative value shifts this custom Y axis to the left of the default Y axis, by the specified amount. - Y-Pos: Specify the vertical position or topmost end of this custom Y axis, relative to the top of the default Y axis, as a percentage of the total vertical height (size) of the default Y axis. In other words, a value of a 100 hides this custom Y axis and therefore this series too. Note: A positive value decreases the height of this custom Y axis below that of the default Y axis, by the specified height; while a negative value increases the height of this custom Y axis above that of the default Y axis, by the specified height. - Size: Specify the size of this custom Y axis, from the specified Y-Pos location in the direction of the X axis (lower-left corner), as a percentage of the total vertical height (size) of the default Y axis. In other words, a value of 100 is the size of the actual Y axis. - Min: The minimum value of this Custom Y axis, which depends upon the value being charted. By default this is set to 0, although, if possible, this control will obtain this value from the applicable Adroit datasource for the selected agent. Note: Any series value below the specified Min value will be hidden from view. - Max: The maximum value of this Custom Y axis, which depends upon the value being charted. By default this is set to 100, although, if possible, this control will obtain this value from the applicable Adroit datasource for the selected agent. Note: Any series value above the specified Max value will be hidden from view. - Adv: This column provides a browse (...) button that launched the tabbed Advanced Pen Configuration dialog, that allows the following advanced settings to be configured per pen: Note: You typically need to click the Refresh Chart button after making changes to these settings to view them on the associated LineChart. Series settings: These settings affect how the series of this pen will be charted, as follows: - You can select one of the following series styles from the Type drop-down list: Line, FastLine, Area and XYPlot. - You can specify the width of the line representing this series, in pixels, from the Width spin control. - You can check the Stairs/Steps checkbox to change the series to be charted in stairs/step mode (when unchecked, the default setting, the series uses a smoothly interpolated line between successive data points).

- You can check the Pointers checkbox to display rectangular data points representing this series (when unchecked, the default setting, these data points are hidden).

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- You can check the Pointers checkbox to display rectangular data points representing this series (when unchecked, the default setting, these data points are hidden). Custom Axis settings: These settings affect the display of the vertical Y-Axis of the LineChart for the pen, as follows: Note: The bottom chart axis for each set can now be configured via the Advanced Set Configuration dialog. - You can check the Automatic Scales checkbox to turn on automatic scaling for the entire axis or for only the minimum (by checking the Minimum Auto checkbox) or maximum (by checking the Maximum Auto checkbox) of the scale. - You can specify the required frequency or number of the axis ticks and labels, by specifying the required Increment interval. - You can change the Axis Color . - You can display the axis on the right-hand side by checking the Other side checkbox (when unchecked, the default setting, this axis is displayed on the left side). Using buttons, on the right of the TrendConfigurator control, you can change how the values of the current set are trended in the associated LineChart, as follows: To view added series for the current set that are not yet displayed: click the Refresh Chart button. To set the time interval of the X-axis for all series: Click the Range button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. This displays the Time Details Settings dialog so you can configure the starting and ending times that apply to all the values that you are trending. Note: This affects the time interval for all series of all the sets that you display on this LineChart until you close the Smart UI Operator, at which time this configuration will be lost. The following axes-stacking actions change both the Custom and default Y axes parameters, which you can edit if you want to change their resultant settings: Note: These Axes stacking actions only apply if you have configured one or more custom Y axis for this set of trended values. In other words, you have at least one Axes checkbox checked. To view each custom Y axis on its own axis: This is particularly useful when you are trending values, whose custom Y axes have differing scales (differing maximum values), since this separates each custom Y axis for easier readability. Click the Stack Axes Horizontally button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. Note: This automatically configures the horizontal positioning ( X-Pos ) of the Custom Y axes for the best fit. To trend each series using their own Y (value) axis: This allows you to compare the trend of each series (value) without confusing or hiding the trends of the other series. Click the Stack Axes Vertically button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. Note: This automatically configures the vertical positioning ( Y-Pos ) and Size of the Custom and default Y axes of each trended series, so that each series has their own Y axis that is the same size, one above the other. To configure the chart axes at runtime: This allows you to configure the scaling, position and/or axis ticks of one or all the axes of the associated LineChart in the Operator. Click the Axes button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. In the displayed Axis Configuration dialog, configure the axes of the associated LineChartconfigured, as follows: If necessary, Select an Axis to configure from this drop-down list box.

To customize the scaling of this axis: determine whether to manually or automatically scale this axis and/or invert the scaling and/or hide the scaling and/or to improve the readability of the axis.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To customize the scaling of this axis: determine whether to manually or automatically scale this axis and/or invert the scaling and/or hide the scaling and/or to improve the readability of the axis. Click the Axis Scales tab to do one or more of the following: Note: You may need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to display these settings. To automatically configure the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Automatic checkbox is checked, this also checks the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. Tip: It is recommended to use automatic scaling (the default setting) when trending data with the Line or XYPlot chart. To manually configure the scaling of this axis: Tip: This is typically required when you are using Bar or Column charts so that you can see the differences in values between two series. - Ensure that the Automatic checkbox is cleared, this also clears the Auto checkboxes for the Minimum and Maximum values. - Manually specify the Minimum and Maximum values, by using the Value spin control to specify the required value. To scale the axis logarithmically: Note: You need to select the Advanced view in the Edit Chart dialog to edit these settings. - Check the Logarithmic checkbox to scale the selected axis logarithmically settings include: Note: The Minimum and Maximum values of this axis should be greater than zero, and the Axis cannot be of type DateTime . - Then specify the required Logarithmic Base for this logarithmic scaling. To invert the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Inverted checkbox is checked (this is an Advanced feature). To hide the scaling of this axis: ensure that the Visible checkbox is cleared. To customize the positioning of this axis: determine the relative position and the actual size of this axis relative to the total dimension of the charting area. Click the Axis Position tab to specify one or more of the following axis positions: Relative Position : the position of this axis, as percentage (0-100%) of the length or width of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the Bottom border and 100 is the Top. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the Left border and 100 is the Right. Start Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the starting position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area. End Position : at the specified Relative Position , this determines the ending position of this axes, as percentage (0-100%) of the total size of the charting area, as follows: For a horizontal (X) axis: 0 is the leftmost point and 100 is the rightmost point of the horizontal size of the charting area. For a vertical (Y) axis: 0 is the topmost point and 100 is the bottommost point of the length of the vertical size of the charting area. To customize the display of the axis and its scaling demarcations or ticks: determine to display the axis, its major demarcations or ticks and their grid lines and to configure the colors of these items. Click the Axis Ticks tab to specify the visibility and/or the displayed color of the following axis components: Axis Pen Visible : This checkbox displays/hides this axis.

Axis Colour : Configure the required color of this axis.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Axis Colour : Configure the required color of this axis. For details, see Using the color edit box to select a color . Ticks Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the major ticks (demarcations) of this axis. Ticks Colour : Configure the required color of these major ticks. Grid Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the grid lines, displayed within the charting area, from each major tick (demarcation) of this axis. Grid Colour : Configure the required color of these grid lines. Using buttons, on the right of the TrendConfigurator control, you can manage and configure sets of your values that are trended in the associated LineChart, as follows: To create a new set: - Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the New Set entry. - Add and configure the series (values) that you want to trend in this set in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control. - Click the Save Set button to name this set and add it to the Set Name drop-down list. To save and name a new set: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, which prompts you for the required name for this set of trended values, which is then added to the Set Name drop-down list. Tip: Ensure that you provide a descriptive or unique enough name so that you will remember exactly which trend values this set contains. To configure and/or trend the series (values) that you have added to a set: Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the name of the required set. This loads the series (values) and their configured properties in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control and then updates the associated LineChart to trend these series. To configure the display of the bottom chart axis for each set: to specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels and the required DateTime format of these labels. Note: This configuration is stored per set in the currently logged on user’s profile. Click the Advanced Set Configuration button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, to the right of the Set Name drop-down list to configure the bottom chart axis for the currently selected set. In the displayed Advanced Set Configuration dialog: - Specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels i.e. 1 minute, 1 hour etc. by selecting and configuring the required Scaling Increment options, as follows: - Check the Exact Date Time checkbox to enable Standard and to calculate the Axis Labels in exact 1 hour intervals. Unchecking this checkbox, the default setting, selects the Custom option. - Select the Standard option and specify the required datetime interval e.g. 1 hour, 1 minute etc. from the drop-down list. - Select the Custom option, if the Standard datetime intervals do not specify the interval that you require and then specify this required time interval in hours:minutes. - Specify the required DateTime Format of the Labels of this axis by specifying the required standard DateTime formatting string specifier i.e. yyy-MM-dd etc. from the list and then clicking the Set button. To update the current set with newly added and recently configured series: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. This updates the set that is currently displayed by the Set Name drop-down list, with all the newly added series (values) and any changes that have been made to the properties of the other series in this list. WARNING!

If you forget to do this and then close this graphic form or exit the Smart UI Operator, then ALL the newly added series and/or configuration changes will be lost.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
If you forget to do this and then close this graphic form or exit the Smart UI Operator, then ALL the newly added series and/or configuration changes will be lost. To export and import the configuration of all the sets in the currently logged on user’s profile to and from an XML file: This allows you to open this exported file in MS Excel or any XML editor and do bulk configuration or any other external editing and then import the edited file. To use this, click the Export and Import buttons, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. To delete the current set: Click the Delete Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control. This removes the set that is currently displayed by the Set Name drop-down list, from this list of sets, which therefore removes all of its added series (values) and their configuration. To remove all the series or values from the left list: click the Clear All button. Note: This action does not automatically stop these values from being trended by the associated LineChart. WARNING! After clearing all the series or values, ONLY click the Refresh Chart button if you want to remove all the series or values from the set that is currently displayed by the Set Name drop-down list. To programmatically select a specific set from the Set Name combo box: Specify the name of the required set to load in the Specify the Set Name to load if TriggerLoadSet is set to true through SpiderEngine field of the General Settings tab of the Advanced View of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog (or use the TriggerLoadSetName property) Then trigger the Boolean TriggerLoadSet property via a spider, for instance by using a Constant spider, whose output is set to True. This loads the series (values) and their configured properties in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control and then updates the associated LineChart to trend these series. -->

To customise the display of the axis and its scaling demarcations or ticks: determine to display the axis, its major demarcations or ticks and their grid lines and to configure the colors of these items. Click the Axis Ticks tab to specify the visibility and/or the displayed color of the following axis components: Axis Pen Visible : This checkbox displays/hides this axis. Axis color : Configure the required color of this axis. For details, see Using the color edit box to select a color . Ticks Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the major ticks (demarcations) of this axis. Ticks color : Configure the required color of these major ticks. Grid Visible : This checkbox displays/hides the grid lines, displayed within the charting area, from each major tick (demarcation) of this axis. Grid color : Configure the required color of these grid lines. Using buttons, on the right of the TrendConfigurator control, you can manage and configure sets of your values that are trended in the associated LineChart, as follows: To create a new set: - Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the New Set entry. - Add and configure the series (values) that you want to trend in this set in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control. - Click the Save Set button to name this set and add it to the Set Name drop-down list. To save and name a new set: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, which prompts you for the required name for this set of trended values, which is then added to the Set Name drop-down list. Tip: Ensure that you provide a descriptive or unique enough name so that you will remember exactly which trend values this set contains. To configure and/or trend the series (values) that you have added to a set: Open the Set Name drop-down list, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, and select the name of the required set. This loads the series (values) and their configured properties in the list on the left of the TrendConfigurator control and then updates the associated LineChart to trend these series. To configure the display of the bottom chart axis for each set: to specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels and the required DateTime format of these labels. Note: This configuration is stored per set in the currently logged on user’s profile. Click the Advanced Set Configuration button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control, to the right of the Set Name drop-down list to configure the bottom chart axis for the currently selected set. In the displayed Advanced Set Configuration dialog: - Specify the minimum datetime interval between the axis labels i.e. 1 minute, 1 hour etc. by selecting and configuring the required Scaling Increment options, as follows: - Check the Exact Date Time checkbox to enable Standard and to calculate the Axis Labels in exact 1 hour intervals. Unchecking this checkbox, the default setting, selects the Custom option. - Select the Standard option and specify the required datetime interval e.g. 1 hour, 1 minute etc. from the drop-down list. - Select the Custom option, if the Standard datetime intervals do not specify the interval that you require and then specify this required time interval in hours:minutes. - Specify the required DateTime Format of the Labels of this axis by specifying the required standard DateTime formatting string specifier i.e. yyy-MM-dd etc. from the list and then clicking the Set button.

To update the current set with newly added and recently configured series: Click the Save Set button, on the lower right of the TrendConfigurator control.

Title: Configuration

WARNING! If you forget to do this and then close this graphic form or exit the SmartUI Operator, then ALL the newly added series and/or configuration changes will be lost. To remove all the series or values from the left list: click the Clear All button. Note: This action does not automatically stop these values from being trended by the associated LineChart. WARNING! Operator Action Behaviours Top Operator Action Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to typically allow users to change the value of a specific data element at runtime. Click for more details: This change in value can be confirmed and/or logged to the event log, if necessary. Note: This change in value is only made if the specified data element can be written to (i.e. if it is NOT read-only). This Behaviour provides the following three methods of changing values at runtime: - Control Action: To increase or decrease a numerical value or to set (enable or disable) or invert a Boolean value. Note: The selected value should be either Numeric or Boolean. - Data Entry: To display a dialog so your end users can typically specify a numerical value, within a pre-defined range. Note1: If a String data element is specified the Minimum and Maximum fields are IGNORED (although are still displayed). Note2: Numerical values CANNOT be specified, at runtime, that do not comply with the specified Minimum and Maximum limits - in this case the Minimum and Maximum labels and their values become red until a valid numerical value is specified. - Data Element Set: To either specify another value (data element) or a static value to set this value. Any subsequent change to the specified data element will change the input value. Note: Ensure that the data of this value is compatible with the value you are configuring. To use a Control Action to change a value: - Add or edit an Operator Action Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the value in the Input Data Element field. - Specify the minimum value for this Input Data Element in the Minimum Data Element/value field. Note: Any value lower than or equal to this value has no effect upon this Behaviour. - Specify the maximum value for this Input Data Element in the Maximum Data Element/value field. Note: It is at this value that the full transformation of the object occurs. Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Action Type List This lists the actions that can be performed upon the Input Value input, as follows: Note: These actions are ONLY performed ONCE, irrespective of how many times this spider is triggered, until one of the input values change. - Increment: To add the amount specified by the Increment/Decrement Value input to the Input Value input and place the result in the Output Value output. For details, see Incrementing numerical values . - Decrement: To subtract the amount specified by the Increment/Decrement Value input from the Input Value input and place the result in the Output Value output. For details, see Decrementing numerical values . - Set Boolean True: To set the Output Value output to 1. For details, see Setting numerical values to TRUE . - Set Boolean False: To set the Output Value output to 0. For details, see Setting numerical values to FALSE . - Toggle Boolean: If the current Output Value output is non-zero it is set to zero, otherwise if it is currently zero then it is set to 1. For details, see Inverting Boolean states . Increment/ Decrement Value Numeric The amount that the numeric Input Value is to be increased or decreased, when Increment or Decrement action is selected from the Action Type list respectively. Input Value Numeric or Boolean The value on which the specified action from the Action Type list is to be performed, when this spider is triggered. Confirm Change? Boolean This enables or disables the display of a confirmation dialog before the value is changed. For details, see Confirming operator action changes . Note: A confirmation dialog will ONLY be displayed if the Input Value input has been specified. Confirmation Message String The informative text that is displayed by the confirmation dialog. This is 'Change the value from {0} to {1}?' by default. When specifying this text, the following placeholders can be used: {0}: The Input Value . {1}: New (modified) value.

{2}: User name, of the currently logged in user, when the value was changed.

Steps:

Operator cluster settings Operator cluster settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that required to make the Smart UI Operator aware of one or more of the available clusters: Click for more details: Servers can be clustered to handle their combined workload evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail.

Title: Operator cluster settings
Steps:
Operator cluster settings Operator cluster settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that required to make the Smart UI Operator aware of one or more of the available clusters: Click for more details: Servers can be clustered to handle their combined workload evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. An Operator can only connect to a clustered Server, if it is aware of this Servers's cluster. Note: An Operator can be aware of more than one cluster. To display this page of settings: When the Smart UI Operator is launched, it needs to log into a Smart UI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the Smart UI Operator. - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the Smart UI Operator may not be installed. - Select the Cluster Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Enable Clustering: determine whether this Operator will connect to clustered Servers or not. To specify cluster-awareness: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. Cluster Names: specify the names of all the clusters that this Operator will connect to. To specify the required cluster name: : Type the required name into the edit box and press the Add button. Note: The correct capitalization is not required as long as the name is correctly spelt. To remove a cluster name: : Select the required name in the list, below the edit box and press the Remove button. Simply specify the names of all the clustered Smart UI Servers that this Smart UI Operator should connect to, since the Smart UI Server name is the cluster name for a clustered Smart UI Server. Cluster Server connections: configure the connection between this Smart UI Operator and each of the Smart UI Servers within the specified clusters. Each connection, consists of the following parameters: - Clustername: The name of one of the specified clusters - simply select the required cluster name from the list. - Comms Type: Select the method of connecting to the Server, by selecting one of the following options: - MAINDATAPROVIDER: To directly connect to the Server computer via the local network (LAN). - WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER: To connect to the Server computer via the Internet. Note: This option requires the Smart UI Server to have the Smart UI Web Service installed and configured. - MachineName: Depending upon the selected connection type, specify the location of the Server, as follows: - LAN: This should either be the network name of the computer on which this Server is running or its IP address.

- Internet: The Internet location of the Smart UI Web Service, which adheres to the following format: http://webservice/folder, which by default is http://machineName/ Smart UI - Port: This is address of the port used to communicate with this Smart UI Server and this address depends upon the selected connection type, as follows: - LAN: Usually port 9000 is used to communicate with this Smart UI Server via the network.

Title: Operator cluster settings
Steps:
- Internet: The Internet location of the Smart UI Web Service, which adheres to the following format: http://webservice/folder, which by default is http://machineName/ Smart UI - Port: This is address of the port used to communicate with this Smart UI Server and this address depends upon the selected connection type, as follows: - LAN: Usually port 9000 is used to communicate with this Smart UI Server via the network. - Internet: Usually port 80 is used to communicate with this Server via the Internet. - Comms Mode: Select the appropriate method of communicating data to and from the Smart UI Server, from the provided list box, as follows: - LAN: SUBSCRIBE is recommended which provides the fastest response time and therefore requires the highest bandwidth. - Internet: SUBSCRIBE_POLL is recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection, otherwise POLL should be used when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. Note: Please ensure that the first Smart UI Server in this list is the Smart UI Server that this Smart UI Operator will log into and that the SAME settings are specified for this connection, as those in the Operator connection settings page. This page only configures the part of the essential Smart UI Operator settings. For details, see Setting up the Operator . For details on displaying all the related Smart UI Operator settings, see the Advanced Operator settings page . -->

Operator command line arguments Operator command line arguments The Smart UI Operator provides the following command line argument options that can customize its display and the permitted user interaction within the Smart UI Operator: Click for more usage details and examples: Note1: Many of these settings can also be configured by the user profiles configured for users in the Smart UI Designer.

Title: Operator command line arguments
Steps:
Operator command line arguments Operator command line arguments The Smart UI Operator provides the following command line argument options that can customize its display and the permitted user interaction within the Smart UI Operator: Click for more usage details and examples: Note1: Many of these settings can also be configured by the user profiles configured for users in the Smart UI Designer. Note2: Any command line options that you specify will override the respective user profile Operator-customization settings. Note3: If you need to customize more than one Operator then you need to create separate shortcuts for each required Operator and customize each separately. You can either specify a single command line parameter, such as: “VIP Operator.exe” -gf “TestProject.Folder1.GraphicForm” Or you can combine the command line parameters that you require, such as: “VIP Operator.exe” -p 1 -gf “TestProject.Folder1.GraphicForm” -t “False” –s 800,600 Operator Profile Setting Command Line Argument Required Parameter/s and meanings thereof Default Value AlwaysOnTop -at “True” or “False” "False" CanClose -cc “True” or “False” "True" DefaultGraphicFormLevel -gfl String name of the required level e.g. “level” DefaultGraphicFormPath -gf String path of the required graphic form e.g. “TestProject.Folder1.GraphicForm” DefaultGraphicFormTemplateSet -gft String name of the required template set e.g. “Template1” FullScreen -f “True” or “False” "False" InitialOperatorMode -o “True” or “False” "True" ShowContextMenu -cm “True” or “False” "True" ShowGraphicFormTabs -t “True” or “False” "False" ShowMaximize -mx “True” or “False” "True" ShowMinimize -mn “True” or “False” "True" StartupBorderStyle -bs Integer value between 0 and 6, as follows: 0 = None; 1 = FixedSingle; 2 = Fixed3D; 3 = FixedDialog; 4 = Sizable; 5 = FixedToolWindow; 6 = SizableToolWindow 4 (Sizable) StartupLocation -l x,y : Pixel location of the Operator window e.g. 100,100 Note: Do not specify any spaces. Tip: Depending on the configuration of your monitors, it may be necessary to specify negative numbers to move the Operator to the required monitor. 0, 0 StartupSize -s x,y : Pixel size of the Operator window e.g. 800,600 Note: Do not specify any spaces. 800, 600 StartupWindowPosition -p Integer value between 0 and 4, as follows: 0 = Manual; 1 = CenterScreen; 2 = WindowsDefaultLocation; 3 = WindowsDefaultBounds; 4 = CenterParent 0 (Manual) StartupWindowState -ws Integer value between 0 and 2, as follows: 0 = Normal; 1 = Minimized; 2 = Maximized 0 (Normal) -->

Operator connection settings Operator connection settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this Smart UI Operator and the specified Smart UI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the Smart UI Operator is launched, it needs to log into a Smart UI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the Smart UI Operator.

Title: Operator connection settings
Operator connection settings Operator connection settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that specify the default data connection that is established between this Smart UI Operator and the specified Smart UI Server at login: To display this page of settings: When the Smart UI Operator is launched, it needs to log into a Smart UI Server computer, which stores the data configured within the Smart UI Operator. - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the Smart UI Operator may not be installed. - Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Login Server: this specifies the default Smart UI Server computer that this Smart UI Operator connects to during the login process. Note: ONLY the user profiles configured on this specified Smart UI Server can be applied to the users of this Smart UI Operator. To specify the login Server computer name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Please ensure that the name of this computer is correctly spelt; otherwise the login process will not succeed. The following are typical login errors that occur when this name is incorrectly specified: - “Requested service not found” -> The Server has not completed loading yet - “No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between this Smart UI Server and Smart UI Operator. To specify the required communication method: Select the required option.

The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this Smart UI Server and Smart UI Operator, as follows: - Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth.

Title: Operator connection settings
The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this Smart UI Server and Smart UI Operator, as follows: - Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth. - Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection. - Poll(send most recent values) : recommended when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. For further details concerning these methods, see About connection communication methods . The bandwidth requirements for this connection depends upon a number of factors, such as the update requirements and the size of the graphic forms. However, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: - Keep the graphic form sizes small; for example use JPG files instead of BMP files. - Plan the graphic forms beforehand with the end-user in mind, including the bandwidth that will be available. - Develop an end-to-end prototype to test in a production environment in order to satisfy all requirements (including the communication requirements). - Only once this prototype has been successfully tested should the project be completely engineered. Connection status check frequency: specify how often the Smart UI Operator should test that the Smart UI Server connection is still healthy and is not disconnected. To specify the required interval between checking the connection, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. Tip: There is little reason to change this default value, as this connection monitoring process only consumes a small amount of bandwidth and CPU usage. This page only configures the part of the essential Smart UI Operator settings. For details, see Setting up the Operator . For details on displaying all the related Smart UI Operator settings, see the Advanced Operator settings page . -->

The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Operator may not be installed. - Select the Connection Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Login Server: this specifies the default SmartUI Server computer that this SmartUI Operator connects to during the login process. Note: ONLY the user profiles configured on this specified SmartUI Server can be applied to the users of this SmartUI Operator. To specify the login Server computer name: If necessary, type the required name into the provided edit box. Note : Please ensure that the name of this computer is correctly spelt; otherwise the login process will not succeed. The following are typical login errors that occur when this name is incorrectly specified: - “Requested service not found” -> The Server has not completed loading yet - “No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it” -> There is no running server Data communication method: select the required method that data is transferred within the established connection between this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Operator. To specify the required communication method: Select the required option. The optimal method depends upon the network (bandwidth) connecting this SmartUI Server and SmartUI Operator, as follows: - Subscribe : recommended when using a Local Area Network as this provides the fastest response time by requiring the highest bandwidth.

- Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection.

Title: Operator connection settings
- Poll(send all values) : recommended when using a high bandwidth Internet connection. - Poll(send most recent values) : recommended when using a low bandwidth Internet connection. For further details concerning these methods, see About connection communication methods . The bandwidth requirements for this connection depends upon a number of factors, such as the update requirements and the size of the graphic forms. However, you can ensure that the selected communication method provides sufficient bandwidth for the needs of your project, by adopting the following recommendations: - Keep the graphic form sizes small; for example use JPG files instead of BMP files. - Plan the graphic forms beforehand with the end-user in mind, including the bandwidth that will be available. - Develop an end-to-end prototype to test in a production environment in order to satisfy all requirements (including the communication requirements). - Only once this prototype has been successfully tested should the project be completely engineered. Connection status check frequency: specify how often the SmartUI Operator should test that the SmartUI Server connection is still healthy and is not disconnected. To specify the required interval between checking the connection, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. Tip: There is little reason to change this default value, as this connection monitoring process only consumes a small amount of bandwidth and CPU usage. This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Operator settings. For details, see Setting up the Operator . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Operator settings, see the Advanced Operator settings page . -->

- AllowEditTags: this setting applies, when linking tags from Adroit datasources to controls and vectors of graphic forms.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- AllowEditTags: this setting applies, when linking tags from Adroit datasources to controls and vectors of graphic forms. In this case, this option determines whether your Operator users have the ability to edit the exposed Adroit tags, which are displayed either through the use of Show (All) Information or the Bad tag status indicators. For details on these tag exposing mechanisms, see Working with Show (All) Information and Bad tag status indicators . IMPORTANT: This option is disabled (False) by default, due to the security risk posed by allowing your operators to edit tags on the fly. - AlwaysOnTop: to enable or disable the initial display of the Smart UI Operator window to be above all other applications. By default this is disabled (False). - CanClose: to allow users to close the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. Note: If the user CANNOT close the Smart UI Operator window, the close button will still appear in the top left hand corner but will not work. - DefaultGraphicFormLevel: to select which level is initially displayed by the graphic form, specified by the DefaultGraphicFormPath setting. Configuration: Type in or paste (right click and select Paste ) the required level name or leave this field blank to select the first level, as usual. Note: If the specified level does not exist in this graphic form, then the first level is selected. - DefaultGraphicFormPath: to select the default graphic form that is displayed when the Smart UI Operator window opens. Configuration: Click the browse button at the right of this field to launch the Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog to locate this graphic form from its required project within the correct Server or leave this field blank. - DefaultGraphicFormTemplateSet: to select which template set is initially activated in the graphic form, specified by the DefaultGraphicFormPath setting. Configuration: Type in or paste (right click and select Paste ) the required template set name or leave this field blank to select the "Default" template set, as usual. Note: If the specified template set does not exist in this graphic form, then the "Default" template set is selected. - FullScreen: to display the title bar at the top of the Smart UI Operator window (False) or not (True). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. - ShowContextMenu: to allow users to display the right-click menu in the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Note: This menu can close the Smart UI Operator window, configure its always-on-top property and toggle the Operator mode i.e. to hide or display the Levels and Layers window. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. Note: If this setting is disabled, this ALSO disables the Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+T shortcuts to entirely prevent this menu from being displayed in the Smart UI Operator. - ShowMaximize: to allow users to maximize the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. - ShowMinimize: to allow users to minimize the Smart UI Operator window (True) or not (False). Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required value. - StartupBorderStyle: to specify the window type used for the graphic forms, which determine how users can interact with each graphic form window.

Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select one of the following styles: Note: Each style has its own pre-set properties, experiment with these styles as necessary.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select one of the following styles: Note: Each style has its own pre-set properties, experiment with these styles as necessary. - FixedSingle: This has a title bar and frame, therefore you are able to close, move, minimize or maximize this window, although you are unable to resize it. - Fixed3D: Similar to FixedSingle , except that it has a 3D frame, which makes its contents seem sunken. - FixedDialog: Similar to FixedSingle , except that its a dialog. - Sizable: Similar to FixedSingle , except that you are also able to resize this window. - FixedToolWindow: Similar to FixedSingle , except its a dockable window that you are unable to resize. - SizableToolWindow: Similar to Sizable , except that its a dockable window. - StartupLocation: to MANUALLY set the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by specifying the required position of the top left corner of the window in pixels. Tip: The StartupWindowPosition setting provides preset system-dependent startup positions. Configuration: These pixel measurements are measured relative to the top left corner of the screen. The first digit specifies the leftmost (X) position and the second the topmost (Y) position. Either specify both positions separated by a comma or expand this setting and specify these positions separately. Note1: Only integer values can be used when specifying these positions. Note2: This setting is overridden if the StartupWindowPosition setting is NOT set to Manual . - StartupSize: to set the maximum dimensions of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by specifying the required window size in pixels. Configuration: These pixel measurements are relative to the size of the screen. The first digit specifies the width of the window and the second digit specifies its height. Either specify both dimensions separated by a comma or expand this setting and specify these dimensions separately. Note: Only integer values can be used when specifying these positions. - StartupWindowPosition: to set the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen, by selecting one of the preset system-dependent startup positions. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select one of the following preset system-dependent startup positions: - Manual: This is the default option, which uses the StartupLocation setting to determine the location of the Smart UI Operator window on the screen at startup. - CenterScreen: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window in the centre of the screen. - WindowsDefaultLocation: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and cascades the Smart UI Operator window at the Windows default location on the screen. - WindowsDefaultBounds: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window at the Windows default location on the screen and has its bounds determined by the Windows default. - CenterParent: This option overrides the StartupLocation setting and positions the Smart UI Operator window in the centre of its parent form, which is not applicable in this case. Note: These startup positions, with the exception of Manual , typically use the currently selected active monitor (monitor with the mouse cursor) when dual monitors are being used, which is determined by the windows video driver. Tip: It is recommended that this setting either be set to Manual (default) or CenterScreen . - StartupWindowState: to select the initial state of the Smart UI Operator window - in other words should this window be maximized, normal or minimized. Configuration: Click the drop-down list box button at the right of this field and select the required state.

Note : Ensure this user name is correctly spelt, otherwise it needs to be manually corrected before this, user can login. Operator scripting settings Operator scripting settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that determine the default scripting environment for this Smart UI Operator : To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Operator scripting settings
Steps:
Operator scripting settings Operator scripting settings This page of the Setting up the Operator component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that determine the default scripting environment for this Smart UI Operator : To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Operator option. Note: If this option does not appear then the Smart UI Operator may not be installed. - Select the Scripting Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs. Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Default script references: specify the list of external assemblies or dynamic linked library (.DLL) files that are automatically added to each script. Note: The longer the list of references, the longer it takes to load and compile every script. Tip: This setting allows 3 rd party users to expose their product-specific assemblies (DLLs) to all their scripts. To add a default script reference: Click the Add button and browse for the required assembly. Note : Ensure that the paths of all of these files are added to the Script references paths setting so they will be located. To remove a default script reference: Select the assembly that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The reference to the selected assembly is immediately removed, so ensure that you select the required assembly. Graphic form scripting: to enable or disable the ability to script event handlers to programmatically achieve a more interactive user experience for graphic forms. For further details, see Graphic form scripting. Note: If this functionality is not required then disable it to increase the speed of loading graphic forms. To configure graphic form scripting: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting. Search paths for script references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that are referenced by your scripts. For further details regarding script references, see Managing references. WARNING! Only specify the locations to assemblies (.DLL files) that you use frequently, since an extensive list will delay the loading and compilation times of all scripts. To add a path that is to be searched: Click the Add button and browse for the required folder. To remove a path from the list: Select the path that is no longer required and press the Remove button. WARNING! The selected path will immediately be deleted, therefore ensure that the required path is selected. Note1: The installation folder and its subfolders are searched by default and so do NOT need to be added to this list. Note2: It is NOT recommended that these locations exist on different computers due to many hindrances, such as security problems and time delays. This page only configures the part of the essential Smart UI Operator settings. For details, see Setting up the Operator . For details on displaying all the related Smart UI Operator settings, see the Advanced Operator settings page . -->

Operator workspace Operator workspace The Operator workspace is the main work area, that contains all the graphic forms, which are currently open in the Smart UI Operator.

Title: Operator workspace
Operator workspace Operator workspace The Operator workspace is the main work area, that contains all the graphic forms, which are currently open in the Smart UI Operator. The workspace either fills the entire Smart UI Operator application window or opens to the right of the tool windows, when displayed. Note1: You can increase the viewing space by hiding the tool windows (right-click and select ToggleOperatorMode ). Note2: Scrollbars provide easy navigation when viewing large graphic forms. For details, see Working with scrollbars . Each opened graphic form is identified by means of a tab, which is displayed at the top of this window. Click for more details: Use the tabs to select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required graphic form. Tabs for newly opened graphic forms are added to the right of the any existing tabs. Note1: Only one graphic form can be displayed within this window at a time. Note2: Hide or display these tabs by right-clicking and selecting Toggle Graphic Form Tabs . Note3: If the tabs are not displayed then you CANNOT select other graphic forms. Depending upon the graphic form that is displayed in the Operator workspace, various buttons are also displayed to the right of the tabs at the top of this window, as follows: - By default, the following button is displayed, which when clicked automatically selects the most recently opened graphic form i.e. the rightmost tab. - When a graphic form is displayed, this button appears in the top-right corner, which if pressed closes the graphic form. To display an opened graphic form in the Operator workspace: click on the tab, associated with the graphic form you require. -->

Title: To optimise a graphic form:
- Locate the required graphic form in the Enterprise Manager . - Do not open it yet, since you need to ensure that you have backed up this graphic form, since the optimization made are irreversible once the graphic form is saved. You can most easily backup this graphic form as follows: - Right click the graphic form and select Copy . - Right click the folder or project containing this graphic form and select Paste . Note: You will get a warning if this graphic form is currently open, if so close it and repeat this process. - Open the required graphic form. - Click the Optimizations toolbar button (that appears above the graphic form in the Design workspace ). - Select the optimization/s (specific searches) that you want to analyse your graphic form for, by checking their required checkboxes. - Click the Analyse button. - Once this process is finished, the brief results are displayed in the Findings and Results field at the bottom of this dialog. Typically these results will provide a hyperlink, which when clicked display the detailed results, in the Analysis Findings tab, which lists each item located by each optimization that you selected. These detailed results can also be displayed when you click the Advanced View > button. Usually you are required to view these detailed results to decide which of the detected item you want to remove from this graphic form, although in some cases an optimization will select certain items automatically. Tip: You can also use the Select All or Remove All buttons to help you select which items you want to remove or keep. - Click the Optimise button, once you are happy with your selections to remove these items from the graphic form or click the Cancel button to not perform any of these changes. After finishing the optimization process, the results are displayed in the Optimization Results tab, which details all the changes that have been made to this graphic form. - Click the Finish button. - If you are happy with these changes then Save this graphic form (CTRL+S). -->

Optional Incident Configurable Settings Top Optional Incident Configurable Settings Each incident in the Categories tree of the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog of an AlarmManagement agent provide a number of optional settings.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Optional Incident Configurable Settings Top Optional Incident Configurable Settings Each incident in the Categories tree of the AlarmManagement Agent edit dialog of an AlarmManagement agent provide a number of optional settings. If you diligently configure these settings then you will improve the efficacy of your alarming configuration and ensure that each alarm complies with the industry-approved effective alarm characteristics . Note: The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident. For details, see Incident icon colors . Tip: You can also bulk configure these settings for all your incidents by exporting the Categories tree to a .CSV file. For details, see Exporting the categories and their incidents . To manually configure a setting for a SINGLE incident: - Edit the required AlarmManagement agent. - Click the required category in the Categories tree. - Click the required incident in the top right hand Incidents list. - Double-click the Value cell next to the required entry in the Attribute column of the bottom right-hand incident details list. Note: You are UNABLE to configure incident settings when you select MORE THAN ONE incident from the top right hand Incidents list. The following OPTIONAL settings can be specified for each incident: - Reason required: When enabled (Yes), this enforces the entry of reasons for this incident. In other words when this incident is raised, the operator must specify a reason before this incident is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table and added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. Click for more details: A reason is simply the selection of the cause of the incident from a user-configurable list of reasons and, if necessary sub-reasons, which you need to specify. Note: Click the Edit reasons… button to edit the displayed reasons and their sub reasons for this AlarmManagement agent. Tip: Operators can specify these reasons and/notes from the right-click menu of the Alarm List Viewer window. - Notes required: When enabled (Yes), this enforces the entry of notes for this incident. In other words when this incident is raised, the operator must specify a reason before this incident is removed from the Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table and added to the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents table. A note is specific text that the operator must type in that is supplements a reason or replaces the need for a reason. - AssociatedTags: Specify one or more values to record with the incident. These values ensure that the alarm is relevant in that it provides the operator with information to respond to. If you are manually specifying this value, separate multiple tags with commas “,”. To add a value: Double click the AssociatedTags row and use the in-built Tag browser to select the required tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). . For details, see Selecting a Tag . To remove ALL the selected values: Select the AssociatedTags row and press the DELETE key. - Document: An optional document that can provide further information to clarify the incident and assistance on how to deal with it or react to it. This document can ensure that this incident (alarm) satisfies the last four of the Effective Alarm Characteristics . If left empty, a default HTML document is created by this agent for each active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. incident. Click for more details about the location and naming convention of this default document: - This document is created in the Data subfolder of your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data.

- This document adheres to the following naming format: AgentName.AlarmType.HTM e.g.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- This document adheres to the following naming format: AgentName.AlarmType.HTM e.g. ANA001.High-High.htm. Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Input String or Numeric This value must comply with the specified requirement, specified by the Operator and Constraint inputs, in order for this logical expression to evaluate as TRUE. For details, see Creating logical expressions . Operator List This list box contains all the comparison operator, which can be used to compare the two values. For details, see Available comparison operators . Note: The comparison operator that is used determines the type of data that can be compared. Constraint String or Numeric This defines the requirement condition that must be met for this logical expression to evaluate as TRUE. Logical Result Boolean If this input is specified, then the result of the logical expression (specified by the other 3 inputs) is ORed with this input and this result is assigned to the Logical Result output. For details, see ORing logical expressions . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Logical Result Boolean If the Logical Result input is not specified, then the logical outcome of the logical expression (specified by the other 3 inputs) will be assigned to this output. If the Logical Result input is specified, then this input is ORed with the result of the logical expression. Therefore, EITHER the result of this logical expression OR this input need to be TRUE for this output to be TRUE. -->

Out of limit data logging Top Out of limit data logging Out of limit monitoring enables Datalog agents to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the normal time deadband value and using the faster log rate specified by the out of limit time deadband instead.

Title: Limitations
Out of limit data logging Top Out of limit data logging Out of limit monitoring enables Datalog agents to immediately log out of limit values (values that are not within their specified operating range), by ignoring the normal time deadband value and using the faster log rate specified by the out of limit time deadband instead. In other words, as soon as the logged value that is being logged, enters or leaves its user-specified limit range it is logged unconditionally, and continues to be logged at the new time deadband as specified by the Out of limit logging time setting ( Time... ). This allows the Datalog agent to catch short spikes whose duration is less than the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ) Usage Example: A customer wants to monitor his incoming voltage of 220 V. Previously, without using out of limit monitoring: he would create a Datalog agent to log this voltage tag at a logging rate of 1 second for a period of 1 week. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 1 sec) to log all changes to the voltage at 1 second and always keep one week's worth of this data. Using out of limit monitoring: since he is actually not that interested in logging this voltage, if it remains within its normal operating voltage range of 215-225 volts, as long as the voltage is within this value range he is happy to log it at a far slower rate - say 10 seconds. But when the voltage breaches this range, then he wants this Datalog agent to log this value at 1 second intervals. So, in this case, this Datalog agent is configured ( Length = 7 days and Deadbands Time = 10 sec and Out of limit monitoring Time = 1 sec and Upper limit = 225 and Lower limit = 215). Note: In this case he will be able to catch short voltage spikes whose duration whose duration are less 10 seconds, the normal logging interval. Example of this configured dialog: Note: To disable out of limit data logging, set both of the limit values are zero (default values), then NO limit checking is done and the Datalog agent operates normally by ONLY using the normal time deadband logging interval ( Deadbands -> Time... ).

To configure out of limit data logging: the Datalog agent logs the value at the "out of limits" log interval when the value enters or leaves the specified limit range Note: This method of logging only applies to those values that have a range of values like Analog, Integer or Real values - and not discreet values like Boolean or Digital values.

These checkboxes use these default agent groups to help you select the required agent quickly. Configure the Out of limit monitoring section, at the bottom, of the Edit Datalog agent dialog, as follows: - Set the Time... (limitLogInterval slot) to the required out-of-limit logging interval, which is typically much faster than the in-range logging interval.

IMPORTANT: Configure this log interval at the required sample rate while the value is out of limits to catch its short value spikes.

IMPORTANT: Configure this log interval at the required sample rate while the value is out of limits to catch its short value spikes. - Configure the Upper limit (upperLimit slot) and Lower limit (lowerLimit slot) fields to define the normal operating range for the value that is being logged. Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards Top Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards To prevent the unauthorised editing of graphic forms and/or wizards, you can password-protect their entire projects , folders and/or individual graphic forms and wizards.

Title: Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards
Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards Top Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards To prevent the unauthorised editing of graphic forms and/or wizards, you can password-protect their entire projects , folders and/or individual graphic forms and wizards. While you are unable to open password-protected graphic forms in the SmartUI Designer, users can still view the password-protected graphic forms in the SmartUI Operator. Warning! If you forget the password you have specified then you are unable to access the graphic forms and/or wizards contained in the secured project, folder and/or individual graphic forms and/or wizards! Note1: You can delete password protected projects, folders and graphic forms and/or wizards. Note2: You cannot rename password protected graphic forms and/or wizards. When you password protect an entire project or folder - only the icons of the password protected graphic forms and/or wizards indicate that they are password protected. Note: Any graphic forms and wizards that are added after password protecting a project or folder need to be separately password protected. To password protect graphic forms and/or wizards: In the Enterprise Manager window: - Select the required project , folder or individual graphic form or wizard . - Right click and select Password Protect - Specify the required case-sensitive password twice. - Click the Finish button. The icons of each affected graphic form and/or wizard changes to indicate that they have been password protected and can only be edited by those who know this password in the SmartUI Designer. To remove password protection from graphic forms and/or wizards: In the Enterprise Manager window: - Select the required project , folder or individually protected graphic form or wizard . - Right click and select Unprotect - Specify the required case-sensitive password. - Click the Finish button. The icons of each affected graphic form and/or wizard reverts to normal to indicate that they are no longer password protected and can be edited by anyone in the SmartUI Designer. -->
