Title: Percentage Fill Behaviours
Percentage Fill Behaviours Top Percentage Fill Behaviours This Behaviour can ONLY be applied to graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically fill the object by means of a monitored value. In other words, you need to monitor a value, which has a defined minimum and maximum value and then completely fills the object when the value reaches its maximum value. For example, when the monitored value is at 50% of its maximum, then this object is half filled. To use a value to graphically fill a vector: - Add or edit an Percentage Fill Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the value in the Input Data Element field. - Specify the minimum value for this Input Data Element in the Minimum Data Element/value field. Note: Any value lower than or equal to this value has no effect upon this Behaviour. - Specify the maximum value for this Input Data Element in the Maximum Data Element/value field. Note: It is at this value that the full transformation of the object occurs. Click the browse button to the right of these edit boxes to select the required data elements, as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element.

The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner.

Title: Percentage Fill Behaviours
The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. - Specify the required Fill color , which represents the Input Data Element value. - If the color Style of the Fillingcolor property of this vector is Solid , then the specified Fill color is a solid color.

- If the color Style of the Fillingcolor property of this vector is Gradient , then the specified Fill color becomes the MIDDLE color of the color gradient.

This displays the configuration dialog of this Behaviour. Tip: The Behaviours tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon provides the Edit Behaviour list box that lists all the Behaviours configured for the currently selected form component.

Performance Monitoring Top Performance Monitoring The PerfMon agent has been created for measuring the performance of your own computer or other computers on a network.

Title: Performance Monitoring
Steps:
Performance Monitoring Top Performance Monitoring The PerfMon agent has been created for measuring the performance of your own computer or other computers on a network. On each computer, you can view the Behaviour of objects such as the Agent Server, processors, memory, cache, threads, and other processes. Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc Each of these objects has an associated set of counters that provide information on such things as device usage, queue lengths, delays, as well as information used for throughput and internal congestion measurements. Up to 16 counters can be added to a single PerfMon agent. The values of these counters are updated every second. The following list provides an overview of what you can do with the PerfMon agent to view the performance of objects: - Log the data from the configured counters. - The values of the counters can also be assigned to other Adroit tags, such as Analog agents, which can then be alarmed whenever this value goes over or under a user-defined value etc. - Create a trend of the configured counters. The following performance counters are added, by default, to first PerfMon agent created: - CPU load i.e. \\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time - Agent Server CPU load i.e. \\Process(as)\\% Processor Time - Total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes - Agent Server memory usage i.e. \\Process(as)\\Private Bytes - Agent Server put slots i.e. \\Agent Server(name (project))\\PutSlots -->

Title: To perform a Custom query
This procedure describes how to perform a Custom query by having users specify the query in a TextBox control, so its results can be displayed on a graphic form within a DataGrid control. Prepare the graphic form: - Open a new graphic form in the Design workspace . (If necessary, add a project and a graphic form first) - Add a TextBox control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to specify the required query that the Query spider should perform. - Add a DataGrid control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to display the records returned by the Custom query. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the TextBox control in the graphic form. Add and configure the Query spider to run the Custom query: - Add a Query spider. For details, see Adding Query spiders . - Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. - Select the required query from the Inputs section of this spider, as follows: - Select the SmartUI Server containing the required OLE DB datasource from the Server list box. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, when referring to the SmartUI Server that you use to log in, instead of its actual name as this makes it easier to transfer this spider to another SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. . - If necessary, select the required OLE DB datasource from this list of available OLE DB datasources on this Server. The first OLE DB datasource created on this Server is selected by default. - Select the Custom Query category from the Query Type list. - In the property pane (on the right of the spider workspace) open the Appearance category of the TextBox control's properties and drag the Text property onto the Query Name input to connect it via a silk. - Clear the Confirm Action checkbox unless you want a confirmation dialog to appear before this query is performed. - Now configure this spider to be triggered when the text of this TextBox changes i.e. after a user specifies the required query to perform from the Event Trigger section of this spider, as follows: - Select the name of the TextBox control from the Event Object list box, this is typically 'textBox'.

- Select the TextChanged event from the Event Name list box.

- Select the TextChanged event from the Event Name list box. Note: The Outputs section also contains the Return Information output which displays how many rows were returned or describes any errors, while the Boolean Success output, which displays the result of the execution of this query. Test that a custom query can be performed: - Click the Run toolbar button of this graphic form. - Specify the required query to perform in the TextBox control and see if the DataGrid control correctly displays the results of this query. - Save the graphic form by pressing its Save toolbar button to save these changes. -->

Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe Top Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it.

Title: Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe
Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe Top Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe A phase always ends with a Phase Action , and therefore may have several ingredient steps preceding it. A phase action can be any of the following keywords: GOTO STEP <step number>; DELAY <milliseconds> or VARIABLE. - A GOTO STEP action will cause an active recipe to jump to the step given in the Tag/Value field. The Tag/Value for a GOTO STEP action may either be an explicit step number or an agent.slot that holds the step number. - A DELAY action will delay the execution of an active recipe by the number of milliseconds given in the Tag/Value field. Note: The Tag/Value for a DELAY action may either be an explicit delay time or an agent.slot that holds the delay time. - A VARIABLE action will alter recipe execution based on the value of the agent.slot given in the Tag/Value field, as follows: Slot value Action 0 Wait until the slot value changes to a value between 1 and 6 and then perform the action associated with this number 1 Go to next step 2 Go to previous step 3 Go to first step 4 Go to last step 5 Perform verification failure rollback 6 Stop recipe execution Note: the Tag/Value for a VARIABLE action is usually an expression or a slot that returns a Boolean value. The Tag/Value field may also be an explicit number between 0 and 6. This is usually done to force the end of a phase and thus ensure verification checking to take place. -->

Philosophy for End User Applications Top Philosophy for End User Applications The general philosophy is for the user to create an instance of a coarse grained object, and then instruct the object to create many finer grained objects inside itself.

Title: Philosophy for End User Applications
Philosophy for End User Applications Top Philosophy for End User Applications The general philosophy is for the user to create an instance of a coarse grained object, and then instruct the object to create many finer grained objects inside itself. A coarse grained object corresponds to a connection to a known Agent Server, either running on the same computer as the application, or some other computer on a local- or wide-area network. In WOSA/XRT terminology, a coarse grained object is a Data Object , and a fine-grained object is a Request Object . A Request object formally describes the pieces of information we require from the Data object. It consists of data that identifies the information we want, plus data which names the specific fields related to that information. For real time Adroit data this corresponds to an agent and the associated slots we are interested in, whereas for historical data, it corresponds to a time and the associated agent.slots we are interested in. The individual fields of each request are stored as a Properties Collection . A single Request collection can hold many Request objects at once. Once we have created requests on the Data Object, the easiest way to get at the required data is to ask the object to paste links to the data into our containing application, which needs to be able to process the paste. When the links are pasted onto the application, the application activates the links, and the Data object supplies the application with ongoing updates. In addition to the basic WOSA/XRT features described above, our OLE server provides a number of Adroit -specific extensions. These include the provision of an output mode that permits the poking of values from a container application to an Agent Server, the ability to fetch values in a one-off fashion from an Agent Server, the ability to connect to a remote Agent Server, the ability to create and remove agents in an Agent Server, etc. -->

PID Alarm Limits Top PID Alarm Limits The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point).

Title: Limitations
PID Alarm Limits Top PID Alarm Limits The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point). As such it is possible to define L, LL, H and HH for the PV and an H and HH alarm for the %Error, for each instance of the PID agent. - The L (low)and H (high) inner alarms are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken, by the control algorithm, as soon as possible. - The LL (low low) and HH (high high) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action, by the control algorithm, is now required. Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit . Any Alarm agent subscribing to the PID agent will detect these status bits. -->

- A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series . This simplifies chart configuration and provides a preview pane in which you can see the effects of the various display options before they are implemented. To launch the configuration dialog: right click the charting control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. Note: The configuration dialog is the ONLY way in which you can chart data from a DataBinder. This configuration dialog also can assist you to chart DataSet data and/or data that consists of single values. Tip: You can connect several data elements to a single series to independently drive its following attributes: color, description, maximum and/or minimum values, engineering unit, value and/or its visibility. For details, see Dragging data to charting controls to configure series . - A right click menu , which launches the configuration dialog and provides alternate methods of adding and removing series and/or charting tools. - A Tasks menu , accessed from the glyph of the charting control, which provides fast access to common display configuration options instead of launching the configuration dialog. The configuration dialog, however, should still be used to configure the charted series. - Important properties , this describes the functions of the important properties that can configure this charting control, some of which specifically apply to xyplot charts. - A toolbar , which allows your end-users to interact with and configure this chart at runtime.

Title: PokeWithTime ActiveX Method

Method PokeWithTime(Agent, Slot : string; Value : variant; Timestamp : datetime) : boolean; This method changes the historical value of a tag. Note: This can ONLY be used to change PAST values of tags NOT current or future values. However, a value that is the SAME as the previous time sample will NOT be accepted. For instance, if a value is being logged hourly and the value at 10:00 is 1 then you will be unable to set the 11:00 value to 1. But if the value at 10:00 is 0 then you will can set the 11:00 value to 1. Parameters: - Agent: the name of the agent or tag (agent.slot) whose value is to be changed. - Slot: the name of the slot whose value is to be changed. This parameter is ignored if the Agent parameter contains a tag. - Value: the required value. - Timestamp: the (historical) time when this value was changed. Returns: If the call is successful the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE. Use LastError / LastErrorNum to determine the cause of failure. -->

Portal Installations Top SmartUI Installations Since SmartUI has been created using the .NET framework, its installations are both easier to deploy and maintain, when compared to conventional software in the past.

Title: How to set up Portal Installations
Portal Installations Top SmartUI Installations Since SmartUI has been created using the .NET framework, its installations are both easier to deploy and maintain, when compared to conventional software in the past. For details, see About .NET installations . SmartUI typically provides the following installation options; which may be named differently but will contain the same SmartUI components, as follows: Click for general SmartUI installation advice: Note1: Add-on components that are separately licensed may need to be separately installed, such as datasources and spiders. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server . Note2: Before beginning an installation ensure that the computer complies with both the software and hardware requirements for the required SmartUI application(s). For details, see System requirements . Note3: After installation, ensure that the necessary configuration is performed before launching the application(s). For details, see Configuration after installation . Note4: All of these installations except SmartUI Web Service also install the Launcher, which can be used to update their relevant files. For details, see Working with the Launcher . - Server: This installation option installs the SmartUI Server along with the SmartUI Designer and SmartUI Operator onto a computer. For details, see Installing SmartUI . Click for SmartUI -specific installation advice: this lists notices that apply specifically to the SmartUI Server installation, such as licensing the Server. Note1: It is possible use the Server freely, with a Designer and an Operator connections for 2 hours, after which the Server must be restarted. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server . Note2: The Server can be licensed by a HASP software protection key, a software license, an Adroit license or a demo license. For details of these licensing methods and their respective advantages, see Available licensing methods . Note3: The Server does NOT need to be licensed or run if the Designer and/or Operator connects to another Server. Note4: The number of Clients that can connect to a Server are dependent upon its operating system and licensing. For details, see System requirements for the Server . - Operator: This will only install the Operator on a computer. For details, see Installing the Operator . - Click Once: The Click Once install allows a user to use a fully fledged Operator, which is downloaded via Internet Explorer and runs normally, as a separate application. For details, see Working with Click Once . - Web Service: This additional installation is required if a Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. needs to connect to this Server via the Internet. For details, see Installing the SmartUI Web Service . Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . - Custom: This installation option is recommended for advanced users only, as it permits the selection of VIP components and their sub-components. Such as installing one or more unsupported components. -->

Title: Printers
Printers Top Printers The Printers option in the Start menu Settings option allows you to work with local and network printers. This makes the following tasks possible: - install local printers - set printer properties - connect to and share printers on a network - remotely administer printers To set up a new printer . To specify the default printer . -->

Printing Alarms Top Printing Alarms Before a new printer may be used, you must ensure that the host computer has the correct BIOS setting.

Title: Printing Alarms
Steps:
Printing Alarms Top Printing Alarms Before a new printer may be used, you must ensure that the host computer has the correct BIOS setting. The Parallel Port Mode must indicate Normal or Standard (SPP), NOT Enhanced (EPP). For further details see To set up a new printer. Note1: Typically, in order to perform line-by-line printing, no Windows driver should be installed at all, since the Windows spooler will internally cache printing until it has an entire page, so as to reduce CPU load while printing. However, specific printer drivers may be able to disable this spooling or page-caching method, and can thus work too. Note2: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry. Note3: The Time column of the EventOutput agent now supports MILLISECONDS. - In the Configurator dialog box, select EventOutput from the Agent Type drop down list. A list of agents is displayed in the Agent Tag list box. - Select an agent and click on the Edit button. The EventOutput Agent dialog box is displayed. - Ensure that the Activate option is set to No. - Select the type of printer connection from the Printer Type list box: PARALLEL, PRINT or SERIAL, where: - The PARALLEL and SERIAL options are for printers connected to local PC where the Agent Server is running. Such printers must NOT be configured in Print Manager as it creates a conflict in resource usage and hence will not work. - The PRINT option is for printers that are configured in Windows' Printer manager and are usually page based and shared by other users . WHEN USING THIS OPTION, DO NOT SELECT LINE BY LINE PRINTING or you will waste paper . - In the Printer Name list box, select the printer (\\<shared-directory>\<shared-printer>) , or the local serial port number (COM1, COM2 etc), or the local parallel port number (LPT1, LPT2 etc). Note: If any of the serial or parallel ports have already been assigned by Windows Printer Settings or for the mouse, they will not appear in the Printer Type List box. When setting up networked printers, avoid allocating the printer to an LPT# or COM# port. - For a serial printer, specify the following setup configuration in the Setup Data dialog: <baud-rate>, <nos-of-bits>, <parity>, <nos-of-stop-bits>, <flow-control> For instance: 9600, 8, none, 1, Xon/Xoff - Decide whether the printing will be based on Demand, size or Time , by selecting the necessary Yes radio button as follows: - Demand Printing: this prints all the events that have accumulated. As this option is represented internally by the demandPrint slot (of type Boolean) this can be externally triggered if necessary. For instance, a Button picture element with an Operator Action Behaviour attached using its Control Action option of Digital On can be used to do this. - size printing: this prints events when they reach the specified size of the printed page. Two sizes can be selected from the size list box, for all printer types, namely: File Full and Page Full . Note: A third option applies only to PARALLEL and SERIAL printers, which allows one to specify the Number of Lines by directly typing in an integer number, e.g. 1 for single line printing. - Time printing: this prints events at the specified time, which can either be a specific date and Time for printing the Event Log or a recurring Interval , e.g. 1 day, when the Event Log will be printed.

Simply click the required Set...

Title: Printing Alarms
Steps:
Simply click the required Set... button to configure this. Note: If the Demand Printing and/or the size Printing options are selected together with Time Printing (using a recurring Interval ) and a report is later activated on the Demand or on the size criterion, then the timer will reset to zero. - Format the output by specifying which columns will be printed , together with their position and width, by clicking the Format button. - When you are satisfied with the configuration, make the EventOutput agent ACTIVE by clicking the Activate radio button. Note: It is also possible to configure this agent to send events to a SQL database or to a file. For details, see Method for Sending Events to SQL or Method for Sending Events to a CSV File . -->

Title: Process Vessels
Process Vessels Top Process Vessels Purpose: when it is necessary to depict the level of a vessel to operators without undue emphasis or distractions. Description: a simple vessel with a vertical orientation, that provides a trend of its analogue level, between its maximum and minimum operating range: - The trend of the analogue level is a bold black line. - The Maximum operating range limit is a thin grey line at the top. - The Minimum operating range limit is thin grey line at the bottom. - The rolling time span of this trend is displayed in the base of the tank, which is 2 hours. wzdProcessVessel_Small_v01: a small process vessel wzdProcessVessel_Medium_v01: a medium process vessel wzdProcessVessel_Large_v01: a large process vessel Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified. Tip: These values are listed in the order they are specified in the wizard. - Browse in the maximum normal operating range of this analogue level, typically this is the high alarm limit (the hi slot) of the Analog agent e.g. tank1level.hi - Browse in the minimum normal operating range of this analogue level, typically this is the low alarm limit (the lo slot) of the Analog agent e.g. tank1level.lo - Browse in the Analog agent name (although this can specify the value slot, but no other slot name) representing the analogue level of this vessel e.g. tank1level.value -->

Production Charts Top Production Charts Purpose: when operators need to know how a production value is performing against a set target value: this charts the production value and a straight line graph of the set target value for the specific production period.

Title: Production Charts
Production Charts Top Production Charts Purpose: when operators need to know how a production value is performing against a set target value: this charts the production value and a straight line graph of the set target value for the specific production period. Description: a line chart with a value axis on the left and a time axis on the bottom, with a straight line in blue drawn from 0 to the specified target value, representing the required production rate and the production value is indicated by means of a grey filled area, so that its actual production rate can be monitored relative to its required production rate. Note: This production value is only displayed if its value is being logged or if it constantly changes over the specified time period. User interaction: Click the clock glyph in the top right corner of this wizard to configure the current Production Parameters , as follows: - Choose how the period of observing this production value is determined, by specifying the End Production Time , by using one of the following methods: - Current to End Time : specify the future dated end time from the Current time (now), by typically typing in the required digits. Tip: The LEFT and RIGHT arrow keys can be used to navigate between the digits. - Current + Timespan : this calculates the required ending time (in the future) by adding the specified Timespan to the Current time (now). If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. - Start Time to End Time : specify both the required starting and ending time, by typing in the required digits and/or using the calendar to specify the required date. - If necessary, change the Target Value that should be met by this production value within the specified production time period. - If necessary, click the Reset button to restart the monitoring of this production value, by recalculating the production time period. - Click Finish when done or Cancel to ignore any changes made. wzdProductionChart_ShiftAgent_DynamicTarget_v01 : this monitors a production value, that is produced during the current shift, as specified by a Shift agent, relative to a production target value which can be externally modified.

Therefore if an operator makes a process change, the required production target value can be automatically adjusted to change the required production rate as needed.

Title: Backing up project files:
Steps:
- On the SmartUI Server computer that contains the projects you want to copy: - Open the SmartUI Designer. Ensure that you save any graphic forms that are currently open in the Designer, which belong to these projects (assuming you want these changes to be copied). - Click on the Configuration tab of the Designer ribbon. - Click the Open Projects Folder tool, opens the folder containing the configured projects, in Windows Explorer, since these projects are on the same computer. - In Windows Explorer: Backup the relevant projects and/or specific folders and their files, either by directly copying them to the required backup directory or zipping them up into an archive.

Title: Restoring project files
Steps:
- On the SmartUI Server computer where you want to copy the backed up projects: - Open the SmartUI Designer. Ensure that you close any graphic forms that are currently open in the Designer, which belong to these projects that you are restoring. - Click on the Configuration tab of the Designer ribbon. - Click the Open Projects Folder tool, to open the folder containing the configured projects, in Windows Explorer, since these projects are on the same computer. Note: You do not need to shut down the SmartUI Designer and Server. - In Windows Explorer: Copy the backed up projects into this folder: - If you intend to replicate an entire project then delete it first - If you are copying a partial project (such as some of its folders) then overwrite the existing files. You can also backup and restore any datasources that your projects use too, which is useful for datasources that have extensive configuration, such as OLE DB datasources. Title: PropagateTrigger
Steps:
PropagateTrigger Top PropagateTrigger WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project Top Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project Note: In Adroit all MAPS -related PLC functionality is disabled.

Title: Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project
Steps:
Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project Top Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project Note: In Adroit all MAPS -related PLC functionality is disabled. Each hierarchy level or component of a MAPS project provides its own right click Properties item that can configure certain of its settings EXCEPT its name, such as viewing or changing its Description . Note: The Description is typically used by the tooltip of the specific component in the tree, equipment descriptions are also added as comments to the PLC program. Click the following components to display the most important tasks/settings you can achieve by editing/viewing its properties: Projects : to specify where the PLC projects are saved and those that affect the MAPS reports and other project-specific settings. - Project Path : specifies where the following items are saved: - the generated project reports, in the Reports sub-folder, - the generated project reports, in the Documents sub-folder, - Default Project Report: specifies the path and name of the report template used for the project reports. If this is BLANK, the default setting, then the GENERIC project report template is used. The GENERIC project report template provides the S88/S95 hierarchy, which includes the following separate lists of each hierarchy level: - A list of the configured Plant Areas and their settings. - A list of the configured PLCs (Process Cells) and their settings. - A list of the configured Units and their settings. - A list of each configured item of equipment and their signals. Tip: You can customise this GENERIC project report template, for example, by adding your company logo to its title. For details, see Customizing report templates . - MAPS Reporting Database SQL Connection String : if you want to use some or all of the Adroit Reporting Suite reports to analyse your Adroit alarming data to improve your alarming configuration and/or record any value that an operator manually changes for auditing purposes, then do the following: - manually create an empty SQL (SQL 2008 R2 with Advanced Services) database, typically via the SQL Server Management utility (which is installed by the SQL 2008 R2 with Advanced Services installation) and - specify the connection string to this database here, typically by clicking the browse button to the right of the MAPS Reporting Database SQL Connection String field and then use the displayed Connection Properties dialog to connect to this SQL database. Typically do NOT change the Data source from the default of .NET Framework Data Provider for OLE DB , unless you are connecting to a SQL Compact database. More details: in which case, click the Change... button and choose the datasource that corresponds to the correct version of SQL Compact and then the dialog will change so that you only need to browse in the required database file and specify the required password, if any. Once this database is specified, then you can right click the MAPS Project in the Enterprise Manager and select the Create Adroit Report Suite right click command, which creates the following agents for this MAPS project: an AlarmManagement, an Audit agent and a DBLog agent, which are configured as follows: - The AlarmManagement agent re-creates the S88 MAPS structure of your project for all the alarmed tags. IMPORTANT: You need to purchase a separate license for the Adroit AlarmManagement agent before you can use this agent to log your alarming data, which you can analyse using the Alarm Management reports. - The Audit agent adds all the tags that are output enabled, so that any Operator change in value is audited (logged to this database) for later analysis.

Title: Properties of each hierarchy level (component) of a MAPS project
Steps:
- The DBLog agent is enabled to start logging and all the agent values logged by the MAPS Templates of this project are also logged to this SQL database. The names of these created agents use the specified MAPS project name and the specific agent type name. For instance, if the MAPS project name is MYPROJ then the following three agents are created: MYPROJ_AMA, MYPROJ_AUDIT and MYPROJ_DBLOG. Then after installing the required reports of the Adroit Report Suite you can use them to analyse your alarms and/or audited items and/or the agent values logged by the DBLog agent. - Default Operator GF: Browse for the graphic form of this MAPS project that the Operator view should display by default. Typically the Operator view graphic form displays the plant area graphic form. But you can specify a unit or Custom graphic form instead. Since one of the purposes of the Operator View, which is generated by each MAPS project, is to provide navigation through the defined plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment, MAPS projects allow you to Select Operator View Layout , as follows: - Advanced : this view provides a navigational structure of different panes, which each provide buttons that display the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Note: This view is more visually appealing and allows your operators to customise this view by hiding or showing the different panes, as needed. - Simple : this view uses menus and sub menus to navigate through the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Note: This view provides the same functionality as the Advanced view only in a simpler navigational format. - Default Screen size: Specify the required screen resolution of ALL the graphic forms of your MAPS project, by selecting the required screen dimensions, in pixels, from the list. MAPS then automatically adjusts the size of ALL your graphic forms in this project to fit onto the selected screen resolution. - Show Equipment Title: specify whether you want to display or hide the names of your equipment on the graphic forms, by checking or unchecking the Show Equipment Title checkbox, which is checked (displayed) by default. Typically you will hide these equipment names to unclutter their graphic forms or when these names only serve to confuse your operators. - Database version: For troubleshooting purposes the installed version of the MAPS database is displayed at the bottom of the MAPS Project Properties dialog. Areas : to configure the associated plant area code, SmartUI Server and Adroit Agent Server - Plant Area Code: an OPTIONAL (unique 5-character alphanumeric) code becomes the prefix that is used for all the equipment items that you add to this plant area. Note: If you change this code, this will ONLY affect the equipment that you add from this point onward. Tip: The use of this code is recommended as it helps to ensure unique and identifiable tag names in the project, that allow you to easily differentiate your plant equipment. - The first of the Plant Area Settings , specifies the SmartUI Server Name , which is Default when this specifies the LOCAL SmartUI Server. If necessary, you can specify a remote SmartUI Server, as follows: if you have more than one SmartUI Servers on your network (and their BroadcastEnabled setting is TRUE), then their SmartUI Server names will also appear in this list (in the following format: [ComputerName] Literal Server Name) - simply select the name of the required remote SmartUI Server from the list. Typically this SmartUI Server provides a connection to a single Agent Server that contains the SCADA tags for this plant area.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
This depends upon the data being connected and the property type, as follows: General configuration: The following GENERAL menu options and inputs and outputs, are ALWAYS provided by this spider, for instance when connecting a property to a data element that contains a single value. Spider menu: This describes the generally available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note1: This menu can be accessed by selecting the spider and right-clicking its title bar. For details, see Selecting spiders . Note2: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: When this triggering method is enabled, this spider is NOT triggered , instead it is forced the read the value of its property and update its output. Any silks that are attached to the output of this Property spider transmit this value to their associated spider(s). For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Top Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Adroit provides extensive proprietary historical data logging facilities .

Title: Proprietary Data Logging to Disk
Steps:
Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Top Proprietary Data Logging to Disk Adroit provides extensive proprietary historical data logging facilities . As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values historically logged, subject to the proviso that they are of slot type Real , Integer , Boolean or 79 character String (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). When logged, the values are time stamped and are made available, via a DataLog agent , to any client . Examples of data log clients would be historical trends, the extract utility, OLE-aware 3 rd party applications such as external spreadsheets for reports etc. Historical values can be stored in one or more data files, each file containing the values of one or more DataLog agents. Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. Previously, when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files, the Adroit datalogging system only provided the historical logged data existing in the .LGD file and was unable to provide historical data from the SystemDatalog-created .CSV datalog backup files. Now each Datalog agent can create their own backup (.LGB) files to automatically retrieve this data, if required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . TWO files are created for each proprietary log, the .LDG file, which stores the raw data and its associated .LGI file, which is the lookup index file. The total amount of disk space required for data logging depends on the following factors: - the number of data files used - the number of agents being data logged - the total number of values logged per agent - the sampling time and length of time each value is logged for. Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. During logging, each DataLog agent will write to its pre-allocated dynamic buffer area in a data file and will overwrite itself from the beginning after it reaches the end of the buffer. The Datalog agent allows for a maximum of 53000000 records. This means that the specified datalog Length... (or period) and Time... deadband combination may not exceed 53000000 records.

This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms.

Title: Proprietary Data Logging to Disk
Steps:
This corresponds to a maximum of 1010.9 MB of data at 20 bytes per record, which means 613 days at 1 second or 30 days at 50 ms. Note1: The minimum Time... deadband allowed is 10 ms which only provides a maximum Length... (or period) of 6.13 days of logged data. Note2: When retrieving data from classic (legacy) trends the maximum number of datapoints that can be trended is 99999 therefore, for example, only 27.77 hours of data can be retrieved at 1 second on a classic (legacy) trend. PLEASE NOTE: Adroit ’s proprietary logging uses an in-built logging factor, which reduces the specified logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor . Note: If the logging period is increased ensure that this change is saved and the Agent Server is restarted, at least once, to allow the necessary LGD file compressions to occur. For details, see Increasing Logging Periods . Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . A data log file is composed of many buffers, one for each DataLog agent. Being event based, the speed at which each buffer is written depends on how often the value in the agent slot being logged changes, and its deadband. If necessary, the data log file can be periodically archived by file copy. Historical data can later be retrieved for viewing , used in trends, or exported as comma separated variable (CSV) files , a format recognised by many commercial spreadsheet and database packages. Adroit supports the merging of external data into existing log files , and logged data is accessible via OLE. Disk size estimation for the data log . Data Logging Compression Methods . -->

Protocol Driver Monitor Launcher Top Working with the Driver Monitor How to log the communication of a driver : when troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device.

Title: Working with the Driver Monitor
Protocol Driver Monitor Launcher Top Working with the Driver Monitor How to log the communication of a driver : when troubleshooting potential driver problems, it is essential to understand exactly how the specific device of an installed driver is communicating between Adroit and the specified front-end device. How to view the diagnostic counters of a driver's device : each driver installs a number of counters that provide important diagnostic information. The Driver Monitor utility allows users to monitor the operation of all the devices of your installed protocol drivers and provides many diagnostic capabilities, such as the Datascope window, which displays the data that is being transmitted between the SCADA and the front-end device (typically a PLC), as follows: - The Driver list is filled with all your installed Adroit Drivers. When a driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. is selected, its description is displayed below this list box, including the revision of the installed driver and the Device name list box is filled with all of its configured devices. For details on installing drivers, see Installing a Protocol Driver . Note: The Insert and Delete keys can be used to add and remove devices for the selected Driver . - The Device name list box contains a list of the currently selected driver’s devices. Each device added to an installed protocol driver to communicate using this protocol to a specific front-end device - in other words a logical connection to this FED. has it's own icon which corresponds to the state of the device to enable the user to see the current operational state of the device. The following explains the meaning of the various icons: IMPORTANT: Please ensure that you have selected a device of the required driver BEFORE performing one of the following commands: - Either double click the required device or click the Monitor button to display the Monitoring Screens for this device, most notably providing the Datascope screen. Tip: By launching the Options... and specifying Command line options you can automatically display and/or configure the screen that you always want to view by default, instead of always being presented with the option screen first.

Note: You can also delete devices from this list by selecting the unwanted device driver and pressing the DELETE key - Click the Configure button to configure this device by displaying its driver-specific Setup dialog.

Title: Working with the Driver Monitor
Note: You can also delete devices from this list by selecting the unwanted device driver and pressing the DELETE key - Click the Configure button to configure this device by displaying its driver-specific Setup dialog. - Click the Refresh button to update the statuses of this list of devices for the selected Driver . The icons have an "auto-refresh" feature which allow them to work almost like the modem lights applet. - Click the Options… button to configure the speed at which the device icons update and other advanced options. For details, see configuring the Driver monitor options . - Check the Show all checkbox to display any configured devices that are not currently loaded. - Check the ASCII checkbox to force the Datascope screen to always display the output in ASCII instead of the default hexadecimal view, which is the recommended method of viewing this screen and this is the same as using the /A command-line option in the Options... dialog. Tip: You can turn off the default Always on top setting for this window, by right clicking the titlebar and unchecking this option. -->

Proxy Servers Top Proxy Servers A proxy server is an Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents.

Title: Proxy Servers
Steps:
Proxy Servers Top Proxy Servers A proxy server is an Agent Server that creates proxy agents for agents that exist on remote Agent Servers on the same project because it itself does not contain any configured agents. Since it only contains Proxy agents, it will not support scanning, alarming or datalogging. Proxy servers generally use an empty WGP file. IMPORTANT: If your proxy Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the other Agent Servers. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: A Proxy Server (an Agent Server that is licensed for ZERO scan points) can proxy an unlimited number of agents, whereas a normal Agent Server is only able to create as many proxy agents as it has scan points and therefore must be licensed for AT LEAST the same number of scan points as the remote Agent Server. Proxy servers are used in environments where one or more clients need information from multiple Agent Servers. A client can only connect to one Agent Server so this server must have the capability to create proxies where needed. Proxy servers are also useful in environments where a user wishes to remove the burden of servicing multiple clients from an Agent Server. Those clients are connected to a proxy server and the remote server(s) then only services the proxy server leaving it more processor and network time for it's SCADA functions. Note: If your proxy server needs to proxy information from a remote Agent Server that is on a DIFFERENT domain or on DIFFERENT sides of a router/switch, then ensure that you are using an explicit connection to connect to this remote agent server. See Agent Server Connection Methods . All Agent Server types (Standalone, Cluster aware and cluster servers) have the capability to create proxy agents for agents that exist on remote agents servers on the same project. Cluster and Cluster Aware servers acting as proxy servers, have the unique feature of creating proxy agents even if there are more than one agent of the same name in a network of clustered Agent Servers. Therefore cluster proxy servers must be used if there are cluster servers on the same project. A Standalone server acting as a proxy server will not create proxies agents if two or more agents of the same name are found on a network. Therefore standalone proxy servers should only be used where there are no cluster servers on the same project. -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is enabled by default, since this spider will usually be triggered by this method. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Function Server A drop-down list of the names of all the connected Servers that are available. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, where possible, when referring to datasources on the login Server to simply the importing of this spider. Otherwise this Server input will need to be reconnected after this spider has been imported. OLEDB Data Source A drop-down list of the names of all the OLE DB datasources that have been configured on the Server that has been selected in the Server list box. The OLE DB datasource that was first added to this Server is selected by default. Note: This displays all the OLE DB datasources, whether they have queries configured or not. Query Type A drop-down list of the names of all the query categories or tasks provided by the OLE DB datasources. The Select Query category is selected by default. Query Name A drop-down list of the names of all the queries of the query category specified by the Query Type input for the specified OLEDB Data Source . Note: If the selected query contains parameters, the names of these parameters will be added as additional inputs to the Inputs section. Confirm Action If enabled, this displays a confirmation dialog before this query is performed. Typically this should be used when inserting, updating or deleting records and/or tables. This is enabled by default. - Outputs , this section contains the outputs for this spider. Output Data Function Return Object Boolean If the query produces an output, then this contains the this result when the query is successfully performed. For instance for the Select query this contains the DataSet of records that can be displayed by a control on a graphic form. Return Information String This displays additional feedback concerning the status of the Success output, such as how many rows were returned, updated or removed or this describes the cause of any errors. Success Boolean This is True when the query is successfully performed. If this fails (False) then there may be a problem with the query syntax or another problem preventing the running of the query. Rows Exist Boolean This is True when the query returns data (one or more records) and False when an empty dataset is returned.

This is typically a control added to the graphic form, such as a Button control, which uses its Click event to perform the query. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . -->

Querying Recorded Incidents Top Querying Recorded Incidents The AlarmManagement agent provides a dialog from which you can perform various statistical queries to analyse the logged incidents.

Title: Querying Recorded Incidents
Querying Recorded Incidents Top Querying Recorded Incidents The AlarmManagement agent provides a dialog from which you can perform various statistical queries to analyse the logged incidents. Many of these queries are derived from the EEMUA 191 guidelines a document created by the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association ( EEMUA) of alarm management guidelines, developed by the users of alarm systems, and is the globally accepted and leading guide to good practice for alarm management. . The incidents returned by these queries are displayed in a table, the columns of which are determined by the selected query. Note: While this dialog allows you to analyse your logged incidents, we recommend that you use a 3 rd party application (such as the Alarm Management and Analysis reporting utility) which is more suited to report and analyse this data. Tip: This dialog can be resized and maximised and its last size and position is saved for the current UI session. The currently selected Query , changes the following items of this dialog: - The title of this dialog to the name of this query. - The description of the selected query. - The columns of the table used to display the incidents returned by the query. - The available constraints. - The available user interaction with the displayed incidents. This dialog provides a number of default queries. For details, see Default Alarm Management Queries . Note: If necessary, you can add your own queries to this list. Certain queries support one or more of the following Constraints: These constraints are displayed by clicking the Constraints... button and can further refine the returned data. In other words they can eliminate unnecessary data. - Top: If enabled, specify the topmost number of incidents for this query to return. For instance, when the table records are ordered by time in ascending order, the specified number of the most recent records are returned. Likewise, when the table records are ordered by time in descending order, the specified number of the oldest records are returned. - From: If enabled, specify the date and time of the start of the interval of analysis. - To: If enabled, specify the date and time of the end of the interval of analysis. The Now button, if clicked, will return the incidents that have been added in the last day, by setting the To field to the current date and time and the From field to one day before the current date and time. - Or use shift times: If enabled, specify the required shift number to only view incidents that occur within this shift. - Operator: If enabled, select the name of the required operator from the list to only view the incidents that are logged to this operator. - Category If enabled, select the name of the required category (as specified in the Incident categorization (tree) containing the incidents that you are interested in. PLEASE NOTE: These constraints are provided by adding special constraint parameters to these queries, so it is NOT possible to execute any queries that contain constraint parameters from 3 rd party applications. To change the frequency at which the data in the table is updated: This will determine how often this query is performed on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the current chart. - Specify the required interval in the Auto-refresh (secs) spin control. Note: A value of 0 disables this automatic refreshing. Tip: Click the Refresh button to immediately perform the selected query on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the table.

text:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - If necessary, expand the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically. - Locate the required agent , which is also listed alphabetically beneath their applicable agent type. In the Enterprise Manager window: right click this agent and select Configure . When the Edit AlarmManagement agent dialog is displayed: - Ensure that the Start Alarm Management Agent checkbox is checked. - Specify the location of the SQL database in the Connection field. Note: If you need to configure the Alarm Management agent from remote computers, it is safer to use SQL authentication ( Use a specific user name and password ) when creating this connection and NOT Windows authentication ( Use Windows NT Integrated Security ) unless you are sure that the logged on users at the remote computers have the necessary access rights to this SQL database. More details: If the SQL connection string configured in the Alarm Management agent has been configured using Windows authentication and you then try and connect from a remote UI to configure, it will more than likely not work (in other words the configured incidents will not appear). This would happen if the Windows User on this remote computer has not been given access rights to the SQL database. Click the ... browse button to the right of this field and use the Data Link Properties dialog to create the required connection string to your SQL Server database. Provider TAB The Data Link Properties dialog specifies the location and the security credentials required to connect to this database. Double-click the Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server item in the Provider tab of the Data Link Properties dialog. Important: If the computer, on which SQL Server was installed, was renamed, then SQL Server may need to be re-installed. If the computer was renamed after installing SQL Server, then SQL Server must be re-installed, to function correctly. Run the following check: - Execute the following T-SQL (Transact-SQL) script in SQL Server Management Studio: SELECT @@SERVERNAME - If the resulting server name is different to the actual name of the computer, then the name of the computer has been changed after SQL Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. Note: If you need to configure or view this database and its data from remote computers, then you should use a UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name path and not a local file path this path, as opposed to a UNC path, can ONLY be accessed from the computer that it refers to, this path adopts the following general format: <driveletter>:\directories\filename. to specify the location of this database. Connection Tab - Type in the computer name of the SQL Server that you want to connect to, in the Select or enter a server name field. - Tip: This is the fastest method if you know the name of the SQL Server. - Alternatively, click the drop-arrow button to the right of the Select or enter a server name box and select the name of the required SQL Server from the list.

Title: Categorizing your incidents
By default, all the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). assigned to the alarm routes that use this AlarmManagement agent are added to the _ Uncategorised category of its Categories tree. Typically you will create and use categories for your incidents for one or both of the following reasons: - The more incidents in the _Uncategorised category, the harder it becomes to differentiate between these incidents. For this reason, you can create other categories to distinguish between the following: - different areas or sections of your process, such as crushing, flocculation etc. - different equipment within each of these areas and if necessary down to the individual tag level. Adding categories allows you to easily query (analyse) or report ONLY the incidents that you are interested in, instead of ALL the incidents, so that you can manage this data more effectively. - Categories also allow you to provide the name of the Operator that is responsible for the incidents allocated within it (and if necessary its sub-categories). This name is logged with these incidents, for auditing purposes. Therefore, this setting only applies to categories that represent areas of your process that have different operators overseeing them. The default _Uncategorised category is simply provided to make you aware of the incidents that you have not categorised. Therefore this category does NOT allow you to assign an operator name to these logged incidents. Tip: To quickly categorise your incidents, click the Learn alarms (incidents requiring acknowledgement) and/or Learn events (incidents NOT requiring acknowledgement) buttons to add ALL the applicable unassigned incidents, that are routed to this alarmmanagement agent, to the _Uncategorised category. We therefore recommend that you categorise your incidents as follows: Example: Categories tree shows a hierarchical structure of the categories, while the top right-hand Incidents list displays all the incidents in the selected category and the bottom right-hand category/incident details list displays the selected category/ incident configuration. Note: The incident details list is disabled when more than one incident is selected. - If necessary, in the Categories tree, rename the ROOT category to the HIGHEST category level that you require.

Title: Categorizing your incidents
For instance: if you are ONLY using this agent to manage the alarming of a single plant, call this category Plant XXX etc. - Add sub categories for every area of your process that is controlled by a different operator. In other words add one sub category for each operator (Clients). For instance: if your plant has two remote Operators, one which controls the crushing section of your plant and another that controls the flocculation section, then add two sub categories to the root node, one called Crushing and the other called Flocculation . - Configure the Operator Tag properties of each of your categories to specify the tag that provides the name of the operator that is controlling the specified areas of your process. Click for more details: This ensures that the incidents that arise from the applicable area of your process will be logged using the name of the operator that was currently in control of that process area. - If necessary you can create further sub-categories for sections that do not have an associated operator, in order to make your queries of the data more accurate. For instance: you can create sub categories for each process area or for each item of equipment in each process area or even for each instrument tag! - Add this AlarmManagement agent to the routes of the required Alarm agents. We recommend that you add this agent to route 2 and 3 of the defaultAlarmAgent. Note: A default HTML document is created for each active incident on the specified alarm routes, which you can edit to provide assistance on how to deal with it. Click for more details: this document is created in the Data sub folder of the your designated project folder, which is typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data. - Categorise your incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). , by assigning the incidents that are routed along each selected alarm route to their required category (or sub category). For instance: Assuming that you have a crushing section to your process, assign all the incidents (the alarmed alarm types) of the agents that relate to equipment within this section to the Crushing category.

Title: Incident icon colors and their meanings
The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident, as follows: - The white icon means that no reasons or notes are required. - The yellow icon means that ONLY reasons must be specified. - The blue icon means that ONLY notes must be specified. - The red icon means that BOTH reasons and notes must be specified. For instance: If you were monitoring the Low-Low; Low; High and High-High alarm limits for a tank, you may only want your operators to specify the reason why the High and Low alarm limits are reached. You may also want your operators to specify explanatory notes when the Low-Low and High-High alarm limits are reached, explaining why the High and Low alarm limits were exceeded.

Title: analysing the logged incidents
- Although the Alarm Management agent provides the following preliminary methods of analysing the logged data, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system: - Once your incidents are being logged to your database, you can launch the View data and View graph dialogs from mimics to perform queries to analyse this data. - A number of common KPIs Key Performance Indicators, quantifiable measurements that measure how well an organization or individual is accomplishing its goals and objectives. are provided and you can create up to 6 user-defined KPI values (single value queries) from the database to measure the effectiveness of your operators and/or alarming system. If necessary, click the Edit KPI's button to change the KPI target values used by certain default queries and your own custom KPI queries, so that these queries better comply with your specific requirements. Click for more details: In the Edit Alarm Management KPI values dialog, double click the appropriate KPI (row) to edit its value. . Related Links: Configuring the AlarmManagement Agent : Describes all the configurable options provided by this agent. How to create your own hierarchical (logical) structure of categories for your incidents: Tip: This edit dialog can be maximised and resized to enlarge the screen area to design and view this Categories tree. Adding Categories : Categories can make your incidents easier to query and analyse. For more details, see Reasons for categorizing your incidents . Configuring Categories : Describes how to specify the ‘Operator tag’ setting for categories. Adding Incidents : To add new and existing incidents to categories in the Categories tree. Note1: You can only assign an incident to a SINGLE category. Note2: The color of the incident icon indicates whether reasons and/or notes are required or not for this incident. For details, see Incident icon colors . Removing Incidents : To reassign incidents to other categories or to permanently remove an incident from the alarm management database. Configuring Incidents : You can configure one or more optional settings for each incident to improve the efficacy of your alarm management configuration. Note: These configuration settings do not affect the manner in which the legacy Adroit alarming functions.

Title: analysing the logged incidents
Tip: You can use the Export button to save and/or bulk configure categories and their incidents within a .CSV file instead. For details, see Exporting categories and their incidents . About the AlarmManagement Database : Describes the database (the tables and their fields) that is created and maintained by the AlarmManagement agent, which a 3rd party application can access directly to report and analyse this data. IMPORTANT: To clear the Alarm Management database - simply to delete all the tables and then restart the Agent Server, which recreates and populates the tables correctly. DO NOT use a script to empty this database, since many of the tables use an auto-incrementing index field, which is NOT reset in this case causing all manner of problems. WARNING! If you delete any of these tables, they will be recreated with their default configuration when the Agent Server is restarted, BUT you will LOSE any previous configuration or data that the tables may have contained. Obtaining KPI Values : Describes how to obtain the common KPI values calculated by this agent and/or to configure queries to obtain up to 6 user-defined KPI values and how these values are stored by this agent. The AlarmManagement agent now provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1. If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. Launching the View Data Dialog : Describes how to launch the View data dialogs from mimics to perform queries to analyse your data. For more details on using this dialog, see Querying Recorded Incidents . Launching the View Graph Dialog : Describes how to launch the View graph dialogs from mimics to perform queries to analyse your data. For more details on using this dialog, see Viewing Incident Queries Graphically . -->

You may also want your operators to specify explanatory notes when the Low-Low and High-High alarm limits are reached, explaining why the High and Low alarm limits were exceeded.

Title: Radar Plots
Radar Plots Top Radar Plots Purpose: to create a Pattern Recognition Object (PRO) that expresses the relationship between a number of related process variables as a shape instead of as a series of numbers, because the brain can remember shapes far more than sets of numbers. Typically radar plots are used to monitor and describe important (serious) process conditions, so that preventative action can be taken to prevent their reoccurrence. Description: the radar plot consists of a sequence of equi-angular spokes, called radii, with each spoke representing a process variable. A line is drawn connecting the data values for each spoke which produces the resultant shape. The length of these radii or spokes are determined by the difference between the specified maximum and minimum setpoints, as follows: - Minimum Setpoint : sets the value of the origin (centre-point), therefore typically ensure that this value will encompass the smallest of the specified process variables. - Maximum Setpoint : sets the outer value of all the radii, therefore typically ensure that this value will encompass the largest of the specified process variables. wzdRadarPlot_3_v01 : a radar plot for three related process variables. Required values: Note: When this wizard is added to a graphic form, all these values are MANDATORY and therefore must ALL be specified.
