The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers.

Title: How the Real-time catch-up process works
The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers. The process occurs during the start up of a standby agent server, if a master agent server is already running. If this is the case, then every agent that is loaded from the WGP file and also supports real-time catch-up will request the current state of the agent from the master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: - First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. - Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each agent subscribes to other agents when required by expression agents. - It is during this phase that the agent will synchronise itself, using real-time catch-up with the same agent in the master agent server. On completion of phase 2 above the agent server then enters the ready state. As an illustration of real-time catch-up: - Let’s assume we have an analog agent called TANKLEVEL. - The saved value of TANKLEVEL in the WGP file is very likely to be an old value (for example, 25%) that was relevant at the time the WGP file was last saved. - The current real-time value in the process is very likely to be different (let’s say 55%) from the saved value of 25%. - The TANKLEVEL agent in the newly started standby agent server will then synchronise its slot values with those of the master during the agent initialization phase. - Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value .

- In scenarios where Adroit installations only save their WGP files after a configuration change, it is important to realise that: - Adroit does not automatically save WGP files on shutdown of the agent server unless it is specifically configured to do so. - It is then very likely that the WGP files contain old saved values which makes the requirement for real-time catch-up a very important process. - Installations where a cluster is setup to extend the configuration on the standby server should execute the following procedure: - Let’s call the maser server AS1 and the standby server AS2. - Save the WGP file on the standby server AS2. - Switch the standby AS2 to master, resulting in AS1 becoming the standby. - Stop the standby agent server which is now AS1. - Copy the WGP file from standby AS2 to master AS1. - Restart the standby server AS1. - Optionally, once AS1 is back up and running correctly, switch AS1 back to master if this is the preferred master agent server. - When the synchronisation has completed, the agent server values contained in the newly copied WGP file may still be a few minutes old and will require further real-time catch-up to finalise current process values. -->

The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers.

Title: How the Real-time catch-up process works
The Real-time catch-up is a process that applies to clustered Agent servers only and not to stand-alone servers. The process occurs during the start up of a standby agent server, if a master agent server is already running. If this is the case, then every agent that is loaded from the WGP file and also supports real-time catch-up will request the current state of the agent from the master server and then synchronise itself. The WGP file is loaded in two phases: - First, all the agents are loaded from the WGP file. - Each agent is initialised synchronously. During this phase each agent subscribes to other agents when required by expression agents. - It is during this phase that the agent will synchronise itself, using real-time catch-up with the same agent in the master agent server. On completion of phase 2 above the agent server then enters the ready state. As an illustration of real-time catch-up: - Let’s assume we have an analog agent called TANKLEVEL. - The saved value of TANKLEVEL in the WGP file is very likely to be an old value (for example, 25%) that was relevant at the time the WGP file was last saved. - The current real-time value in the process is very likely to be different (let’s say 55%) from the saved value of 25%. - The TANKLEVEL agent in the newly started standby agent server will then synchronise its slot values with those of the master during the agent initialization phase. - Both servers should now reflect 55% for the TANKLEVEL.value .

Title: Reasons for categorizing your incidents
Reasons for categorizing your incidents Top Reasons for categorizing your incidents By default, all the incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). assigned to the alarm routes that use this AlarmManagement agent are added to the _ Uncategorised category of its Categories tree. Typically you will create and use categories for your incidents for one or both of the following reasons: - The more incidents in the _Uncategorised category, the harder it becomes to differentiate between these incidents. For this reason, you can create other categories to distinguish between the following: - different areas or sections of your process, such as crushing, flocculation etc. - different equipment within each of these areas and if necessary down to the individual tag level. Adding categories allows you to easily query (analyse) or report ONLY the incidents that you are interested in, instead of ALL the incidents, so that you can manage this data more effectively. - Categories also allow you to provide the name of the Operator that is responsible for the incidents allocated within it (and if necessary its sub-categories). This name is logged with these incidents, for auditing purposes. Therefore, this setting only applies to categories that represent areas of your process that have different operators overseeing them. The default _Uncategorised category is simply provided to make you aware of the incidents that you have not categorised. Therefore this category does NOT allow you to assign an operator name to these logged incidents. Tip: To quickly categorise your incidents, click the Learn alarms (incidents requiring acknowledgement) and/or Learn events (incidents NOT requiring acknowledgement) buttons to add ALL the applicable unassigned incidents, that are routed to this alarmmanagement agent, to the _Uncategorised category. -->

Slot Name Type Function active R INTEGER Master Recipe: equal to the currentRecipeId of the currently active control recipe. If no control recipe is active then this slot is equal to minus one. activeName STRING Master Recipe: the name of the control recipe that is currently executing or that has just executed. addRecipe BOOLEAN Master Recipe: used to add an empty control recipe. batchCounter INTEGER Control Recipe: the number to be appended to batchPrefix to make up the batch name. This counter is incremented after a control recipe has completed execution. batchPrefix STRING Control Recipe: batch prefix controlRecipe X VARSTRING Control Recipe: stores the control recipe currentBatchName R STRING Master Recipe: the batch name of the control recipe that was last active or is currently active. This slot is simply the control recipe slot batchCounter appended to the control recipe slot batchPrefix . This slot is updated when a control recipe is active. currentPhaseTrigger X STRING Master Recipe: the agent.slot to trigger the start of a new phase. If equal to one, then all events will be logged. If equal to two, then all events except those regarding phases will be logged. exportName STRING Complete Recipe agent: the full path and filename of the CSV file where the complete Recipe agent (both the master recipe and its control recipes) will be exported. Recipe Agent Overview Top Recipe Agent Description A recipe is a statement of the ingredients and procedures necessary for the making or compounding of some preparation or formulation.

Title: Recipe Agent Description
Recipe Agent Overview Top Recipe Agent Description A recipe is a statement of the ingredients and procedures necessary for the making or compounding of some preparation or formulation. It defines how the control system is to process its raw materials to make the desired product and byproducts. In Adroit , this is achieved by the Recipe agent which provides the means for automatically downloading information to process variables. These variables allow a plant to produce the final product. Mundane tasks can be automated saving time and removing the element of human error. In common with modern industry practice (SP88), the recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes. Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. For example, the Master Recipe could describe a Fruit Juice mixing plant. Several Control recipes would provide the data to manufacture various flavors and mixtures of fruit juice such as Orange, Mango, Pineapple, Mango and Orange, Pineapple and Orange etc. The Adroit recipe system allows: - Each Control recipe to be assigned a batch identification. - Accumulation of batch histories through event logging. - Downloading of process variables that are of type Boolean, Integer, Real or String. - The sequence of execution to be delayed by a specified amount of time, to be paused until a desired condition in the plant is met, or to be redirected to another step. - Master recipes and Control recipes to be imported or exported to files using the comma separated variable (CSV) format, for ease of viewing and editing by 3rd party products (e.g. Excel). - The progress of a working recipe to be monitored. - Verification of the values scanned out to PLC. - Optional Rollback can be performed should the verification fail. -->

The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. For example, the Master Recipe could describe a Fruit Juice mixing plant. Several Control recipes would provide the data to manufacture various flavors and mixtures of fruit juice such as Orange, Mango, Pineapple, Mango and Orange, Pineapple and Orange etc. The Adroit recipe system allows: - Each Control recipe to be assigned a batch identification. - Accumulation of batch histories through event logging. - Downloading of process variables that are of type Boolean, Integer, Real or String. - The sequence of execution to be delayed by a specified amount of time, to be paused until a desired condition in the plant is met, or to be redirected to another step. - Master recipes and Control recipes to be imported or exported to files using the comma separated variable (CSV) format, for ease of viewing and editing by 3rd party products (e.g. Excel). - The progress of a working recipe to be monitored. - Verification of the values scanned out to PLC. - Optional Rollback can be performed should the verification fail. -->

Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Top Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Microsoft recommends that you use the TableLayoutPanel control sparingly.

Title: Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls
Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Top Recommendations for using TableLayoutPanel controls Microsoft recommends that you use the TableLayoutPanel control sparingly. Note: You should NOT use it in all situations that require a resizable layout. The following list describes layouts that benefit most from using the TableLayoutPanel control: - Layouts in which there are multiple parts of the form that resize proportionally to each other. - Layouts that will be modified or generated dynamically at run time, such as data entry forms that have user-customizable fields added or subtracted based on preferences. - Layouts that should remain at an overall fixed size. For example, you may have a dialog box that should remain smaller than 800 x 600, but you need to support localised strings. The following list describes layouts that do not benefit greatly from using the TableLayoutPanel control: - Simple data entry forms with a single column of labels and a single column of text-entry areas. - Forms with a single large display area that should fill all the available space when a resize occurs. An example of this is a form that displays a single PropertyGrid control. In this case, use anchoring, because nothing else should expand when the form is resized. These recommendations have been taken as-is from the Best Practices for the TableLayoutPanel Control http://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/subscriptions/downloads/ms171689(v=vs.85).aspx ) Note: Avoid nesting TableLayoutPanels not only does this make it harder to debug your layouts but can also reduce your performance when resizing the graphic form. We recommend that you plan your intended layout of controls beforehand, when using this control. IMPORTANT: When you DELETE a TableLayoutPanel control an error occurs because it is only PARTIALLY removed at design time, so you need to save, close and reopen the graphic form to complete the removal of this control and its added controls. WARNING: Immediately after deleting a TableLayoutPanel control, although this control and/or the added controls may remain on the graphic form, any further configuration of them will be lost as these will be removed the next time you save and reopen this graphic form. -->

Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Top Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Since the configuration of each alarm agent is stored in THREE interrelated files , this can complicate the method of bulk-configuring Alarm agents as these files MUST be correctly sorted so that they will correctly relate to one another.

Title: Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents
Steps:
Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Top Recommended Method of Importing Alarm Agents Since the configuration of each alarm agent is stored in THREE interrelated files , this can complicate the method of bulk-configuring Alarm agents as these files MUST be correctly sorted so that they will correctly relate to one another. For details, see Importing Alarm agents . The following method of importing Alarm agents, however, is recommended as it does away with the need of ensuring that these files are correctly sorted: - Export the required Alarm agent(s). For details, see Exporting Agents . - Design their TYPLST and ROUTLST files first. For details of the formats of these CSV files, see Type List CSV File Format or Route List CSV File Format . - Perform a selective import of each alarm agent, only importing these files. In other words, click No when the Import Alarm agent dialog is displayed and then only select the xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV file and xxxxx-ROUTLST.CSV (where xxxxx represents the name of the Alarm agent). - Re-export the required Alarm agent(s). - Design the AGNTLST file using the indexes as per the newly exported TYPLST file. For details of the formats of this CSV files, see Agent List CSV File Format . - Perform a selective import of each alarm agent, only importing the AGNTLST file. Note: If you import a list of alarm types list into an existing Alarm agent, it is recommended that this Alarm agent is deleted and then re-created to quickly clear its list of already configured alarms, as these may conflict with the new alarm types. Tip: In addition to being able to select which of the three configuration files will be imported; the manual import option is also able to select DIFFERENT import files, other than the default files created on export. For this reason, it is possible to design a single TYPLST file, containing the default alarm types required by ALL alarm agents. Then import this file, using manual importing, into all the configured alarm agents. This not only saves configuration time, but also ensures that all the Alarm agents will have the same alarm types. -->

text:
- Verify that the Adroit installation directory has been added to the path, by typing ‘path’ in the CMD window.

Title: Configuration
- Verify that the Adroit installation directory has been added to the path, by typing ‘path’ in the CMD window. Note: If the installation is to form part of a distributed Adroit system with the ability to share data across the network within one project (i.e. it is not a simple standalone system) then it is essential that a number of additional requirements are met. For details, see Requirements for Distributed Systems. - Run the Adroit setup (psexe.exe) , make the necessary Agent Server and project settings and add the necessary drivers and their devices. - Install the other required programs–if Microsoft Office is installed then disable the office FindFast re-indexing service as this tends to adversely affect the computer’s responsiveness. - Reboot before re/installing your service pack now, for Windows 2000 this is SP2. The SP is always the last software to be installed. - Configure security in Adroit , which makes use of Windows security and presupposes a group-based security model. For details, see Adroit Security Configuration. - Configure the Event viewer, and set the Application event log to wrap, set the size for 1024k or more. - Now run an empty Adroit Agent Server from the icon, verify that the HASP is present by opening the Agent Server Agent Server window and looking for the line that begins with "HASP SN:…". To further determine that status of the HASP, open a UI window and then edit the LICENSE Hasp agent in the Configurator, if the HASP is correctly configured then the I/O Status should be: "Read memo OK". - Adroit provides the facility to allow operators to specify numerical and textual (alpha-numeric) values by means of the Adroit virtual keyboard. This is typically required when you are using touch screen user interfaces that do not provide keyboards. See Adroit Virtual Keyboard. - If this computer is a cluster or a backup, copy all the datalog files across and any other duplicated files, such as mimics and scripts, before you start up to speed up things. Run the intended Adroit database normally. - Verify that the front-end devices (PLCs) communications are established and that all the tags on the mimics are visible (that none of the tags are greyed out) and that the mimics work correctly and can be navigated between correctly. Ensure that the datalogs and hence the trends are working correctly.

Title: Configuration
- Set up the Agent Server service if required, once you have verified that the project and the Agent Sever are working as required. - Ensure that the Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is correctly configured, since this can cause the Agent Server to be unable to read the HASP, at start up causing the Agent Server to hang or fail and/or to display HASP exceptions in the Agent Server window. For further details, see Data Execution Prevention (DEP) Configuration . - Do a full Re-boot to test the system. - If your current Agent Server process is approaching the 1.6GB virtual memory limit, as measured by Performance Monitor (NOT Task Manager!), then increase the amount of virtual memory available to this process. For further details, see Increasing the virtual memory available to the Agent Server . Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit . -->

Registry Settings Top Registry Settings Windows security can be either bypassed or tightened further by specific changes to the Registry keys, and the functionality of certain agents may also be modified by adding new Registry keys IMPORTANT NOTE1: Use extreme care when changing any registry settings, as any erroneous changes may result in the re-installation of Windows. Ensure that you are conversant with the registry structure and have the appropriate access rights before entering or attempting to modify the settings. IMPORTANT NOTE2: After installing Adroit and all other relevant applications, CREATE AN EMERGENCY REPAIR DISK BEFORE MAKING ANY CHANGES TO THE REGISTRY. To start the registry editor, open the Start menu, select Run , type in ‘ regedit ’ and click OK . Registry Values affecting communications : an ALPHABETICAL list of the otherwise undocumented registry Values that affect the communication via the various protocol drivers between Adroit and the front-end devices. Note : Since our intention is to reduce the amount of registry configuration, many of the settings that were previously only configurable via the registry can be configured within the product itself. That concludes the Adroit configuration within Windows, any further interaction with the system for configuration, security or operation takes place from the Smart User Interface. -->

Title: Registry Values affecting the Agent Server
Registry Values affecting the Agent Server Top Registry Values affecting the Agent Server This is an ALPHABETICAL list of the otherwise undocumented registry Values that affect the Agent Server and therefore its agents and their operation: WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Note1: The Advanced Scanning Settings dialog can be used to configure the registry settings affecting the marshalling functionality of the Multistate agent and for enabling the 16 status bits of a Text agent to be set by the bit stream value of that text string e.g. "1110010011011000" (EnableTextBitStreams). Note2: Many global datalogging settings can be set in the Advanced settings dialog of the DataLog agent, whenever you log a tag, see Advanced Datalog Configuration . The StartupDelay setting to delay the start up of the Agent Server is configured in the Service tab of the Adroit Configuration Setup utility. For details, see Configuring Agent Server Startup Delay. AcknowledgeAtStartup : To ensure that the Agent Server automatically acknowledges alarms at startup, either do NOT add this key or if you have added it, then set it to 1. Active Link Monitoring : To remedy and troubleshoot slow (or unresponsive) Agent Servers and/or their clients. AnalogRawComms : To ensure the correct operation of the Analog agent, when communicating alarm limits and to also provide reverse polarity for all Analog agents. AutoCreate : To query the user as to whether a Datalog agent should be created when the Log button is clicked in the Configurator. ConnectionProtocol : To specify the required mechanism that Adroit client software want to use when connecting to local and remote Agent Servers CreateDumpFiles : To enable the creation of the Agent Server dump file (.DMP) when the agent database (.WGP) file is faulty. DisableADOTableNamePrefix : To remove the "AdroitRawLog_" table name prefix when logging to an OLE DB database. DisableEventOutputOnStandby : To prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode. DisableOnQualityChangeLogging : To disable DBLog agents from logging on quality change ONLY for the "Log on change" logging method. DumpAgentDetailsEnabled : To prevent all DBLog agents from creating the Agent Details table. EnableUnchangedValueWrites : To send an output to a PLC REGARDLESS of whether the scanned rawvalue slot of the Digital agent is changing or not. By default this only occurs when the rawvalue slot changes. Extensions : To enable column header names to be added to fetch calls, which return a string array. ExtractFloatResolution : To support decimal resolution for real logged values that are retrieved using the Extract utility. ForceJet : To use the DbAccess agent with databases that require square brackets around the field names, otherwise their SQL transactions fail. ForceSendIfDuplicate : To determine whether the same message can be resent or not from a Notify agent. HousekeepingHour : To specify the hour of the day that the housekeeping of DBLog agents should occur. IgnoreBadAlarms : To enable the alarming of agents that are currently in a bad status (ScanBad or Bad). IPEnableHeartbeat : When using sockets as the communication mechanism between the Agent Server and its clients, this setting allows the Agent Server to monitor the status of these client connections and to close any unhealthy connections. IsPostgress : To allow you to log to a postgress database.

text:
LazyFlushing : To enable the log data to be immediately written to disk.

Title: Registry Values affecting the Agent Server
LazyFlushing : To enable the log data to be immediately written to disk. LMOperatorAction : To change the default Alarm route used for Operator Action Behaviours from route 1. LogADODateTimes : To add an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, when datalogging to an ADO-compliant database. LogCompressionFactor : To override the 20% data log capacity or the "divide by 5" storage factor applied to datalog files by default. Managing Subscription Queue Length : To prevent the Subscription Manager queue length from overfilling. MarshalAlarmMode : To specify the type of information reported in the description field for Marshal agent alarms. MaxAgents : To specify the total number of expected agents on all the connected Agent Servers, which by default is set to 199000. Note: ONLY when memory is a serious constraint, should you alter this default setting by adding and configuring this registry setting. Memsize : To reduce the memory usage of the Alarm agent, when your very large alarming configuration spread over many Alarm agents is causing the virtual memory size of the Agent Server process to reach its upper 2 GB limit. OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad : To use the legacy method of marking your Analog agents are being bad when their rawvalue slot goes out of range PropagateTrigger : To disable subscription updates for the value slot of a triggered Expression agent, if the value slot has not actually changed, to prevent unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. RDAdminName : To allow Remote Desktop (RDP) clients to get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server. RestartOnZeroChannels : To prevent the Agent Server from restarting when the number of free channels is zero. ServiceCleanShutdown : To cause the Agent Server service to attempt a clean shutdown to ensure that the OPC client drivers disconnect from their OPC Servers so that these OPC Servers can clean up their resources and shutdown if necessary. SmartInhibit : To define how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms if an agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one and the agent is currently in alarm and/or unacknowledged. SubsWriteTimeout : To force the Agent Server to timeout once the network channel between it and a slow client has filled up. SupportCompressionOnDemand : To enable the use of the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging. SuppressLogAtStartup : To suppress the log of the POST_STARTUP value after an Agent Server restart. -->

DisableEventOutputOnStandby : To prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode. DisableOnQualityChangeLogging : To disable DBLog agents from logging on quality change ONLY for the "Log on change" logging method. DumpAgentDetailsEnabled : To prevent all DBLog agents from creating the Agent Details table. EnableUnchangedValueWrites : To send an output to a PLC REGARDLESS of whether the scanned rawvalue slot of the Digital agent is changing or not. By default this only occurs when the rawvalue slot changes. Extensions : To enable column header names to be added to fetch calls, which return a string array. ExtractFloatResolution : To support decimal resolution for real logged values that are retrieved using the Extract utility. ForceJet : To use the DbAccess agent with databases that require square brackets around the field names, otherwise their SQL transactions fail. ForceSendIfDuplicate : To determine whether the same message can be resent or not from a Notify agent. HousekeepingHour : To specify the hour of the day that the housekeeping of DBLog agents should occur. IgnoreBadAlarms : To enable the alarming of agents that are currently in a bad status (ScanBad or Bad). IPEnableHeartbeat : When using sockets as the communication mechanism between the Agent Server and its clients, this setting allows the Agent Server to monitor the status of these client connections and to close any unhealthy connections. IsPostgress : To allow you to log to a postgress database.

LazyFlushing : To enable the log data to be immediately written to disk.

Title: Registry Values affecting the Agent Server
LazyFlushing : To enable the log data to be immediately written to disk. LMOperatorAction : To change the default Alarm route used for Operator Action Behaviours from route 1. LogADODateTimes : To add an additional column containing readable timestamps to the database table, when datalogging to an ADO-compliant database. LogCompressionFactor : To override the 20% data log capacity or the "divide by 5" storage factor applied to datalog files by default. Managing Subscription Queue Length : To prevent the Subscription Manager queue length from overfilling. MarshalAlarmMode : To specify the type of information reported in the description field for Marshal agent alarms. MaxAgents : To specify the total number of expected agents on all the connected Agent Servers, which by default is set to 199000. Note: ONLY when memory is a serious constraint, should you alter this default setting by adding and configuring this registry setting. Memsize : To reduce the memory usage of the Alarm agent, when your very large alarming configuration spread over many Alarm agents is causing the virtual memory size of the Agent Server process to reach its upper 2 GB limit. OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad : To use the legacy method of marking your Analog agents are being bad when their rawvalue slot goes out of range PropagateTrigger : To disable subscription updates for the value slot of a triggered Expression agent, if the value slot has not actually changed, to prevent unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. RDAdminName : To allow Remote Desktop (RDP) clients to get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server. RestartOnZeroChannels : To prevent the Agent Server from restarting when the number of free channels is zero. ServiceCleanShutdown : To cause the Agent Server service to attempt a clean shutdown to ensure that the OPC client drivers disconnect from their OPC Servers so that these OPC Servers can clean up their resources and shutdown if necessary. SmartInhibit : To define how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms if an agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one and the agent is currently in alarm and/or unacknowledged. SubsWriteTimeout : To force the Agent Server to timeout once the network channel between it and a slow client has filled up. SupportCompressionOnDemand : To enable the use of the Datalog compression algorithm when using Demand logging. SuppressLogAtStartup : To suppress the log of the POST_STARTUP value after an Agent Server restart. -->

Replication Top Replication While catch-up deals with the requirement for a new server being added to the cluster to be a mirror image at the current point in time, replication is concerned with how changes that occur as a result of external influences on the cluster are dealt with.

Title: Replication
Replication Top Replication While catch-up deals with the requirement for a new server being added to the cluster to be a mirror image at the current point in time, replication is concerned with how changes that occur as a result of external influences on the cluster are dealt with. For instance, external changes affecting the cluster members can occur from a Adroit client application or from Agent Server scan inputs. Client changes are typically a result of changing a set point from within a UI. All these sources of change are replicated to all Agent Servers in the cluster in order to maintain the mirror image state of the clustered servers. Two instances of configuring replication within a cluster are: - Client Runtime Transaction Shadowing : All transactions initiated by a client on a server are shadowed to the other server in the cluster to provide total data replication. - Parallel scanning : Each cluster server is configured to replicate the scanning tasks to provide scan task replication, that is, each server performs scanning as if it were a normal server. This is an alternative to automatically shadowing the scanned data. -->

Title: Requirements
Requirements for Distributed Systems Top Requirements for Distributed Systems If the installation is to form part of a distributed Adroit system with the ability to share data across the network within one project (i.e. it is not a simple standalone system) then it is essential that the following requirements are met: - Check that all computers belong to the same Network Workgroup or Domain - Using Adroit Configuration Setup , check that all Agent Servers are configured as part of the same project by ensuring the Agent Servers have the same Project Name. Note: Project names must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. - Click the Project Options button, and ensure that Enable remote servers to automatically detect this server is checked. The checkbox Explicit Additional Server Connections should remain unchecked initially. - Ensure that each computer within the same project has a unique name for its local Agent Server. Note: The name " Adroit " is given by default, and if more than one Agent Server with this name is started, the message "Cannot start duplicate AS" will be displayed. (This message is also displayed when more than one Agent Server is started on a computer.) - If duplicate agent names exist in the Agent Servers, the one on the local Agent Server will be used. It is therefore advisable to ensure that agent names are unique over the whole project. For details, see Naming Agents . - Check that each computer has a HASP software protection key fitted - Check that each computer has every Adroit user set up identically by its local User Accounts applet , so that the same User Names and Passwords exist on all the computers in the project. - Verify that the Number of Connections (go to the Options/Agent Information menu option) equals the number of computers on the project that have an Agent Server running. - Check that all devices that are to be scanned have been installed using the Drivers dialog during the Configuration Setup procedure described earlier. - Check that the physical memory is 25% more than the committed memory (see Total Commit Charge in the Performance tab of the Task Manager). - Verify on each computer, using the Agent Server Configurator or Agent Browser that an AgentGroup tag exists for each Agent Server in the project.

For example, for a project name ‘Juice’ consisting of 3 Agent Servers called PLANT_A, PLANT_B and PLANT_X, you will see PLANT_A and PLANT_B as AgentGroup tags if you pull down the Group list box in PLANT_X’s Configurator.

Title: RDAdminName
Steps:
RestartOnZeroChannels Top RDAdminName WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can now get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server, by designating a virtual client running as a defined user to be considered as the local client. This is done by specifying the username of this defined user by adding and configuring the following WG.INI registry string value: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI (REG_SZ) RDAdminName = Windows username of the required user. By default this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required username to establish free connections for that user. The reason for this RDAdminName feature is because typically the concept of a local Agent Server in a virtual environment does not exist as the Agent Server process is available to ALL virtual clients. Rotation Behaviours Top Rotation Behaviours This Behaviour can ONLY be applied to graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically rotate the object by means of a monitored value. In other words, you need to monitor a value, which has a defined minimum and maximum value and then specify the maximum required rotation, in degrees, when the value reaches its maximum value. For example, if you specify a maximum rotation of 90 degrees, when the monitored value is at 50% of its maximum, then this object has rotated by 45 degrees. To dynamically rotate a vector: - Add or edit an Rotation Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the value in the Input Data Element field. - Specify the minimum value for this Input Data Element in the Minimum Data Element/value field. Note: Any value lower than or equal to this value has no effect upon this Behaviour. - Specify the maximum value for this Input Data Element in the Maximum Data Element/value field. Note: It is at this value that the full transformation of the object occurs. Routing to Audio Devices Top Routing to Audio Devices Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer.

Title: Routing to Audio Devices
Routing to Audio Devices Top Routing to Audio Devices Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented. The priority of a Beeper agent determines the interval between beeping i.e. a high priority will beep faster than a lower priority Beeper agent. If the start slot of a MultiMedia agent is used, this will activate the configured multi-media file. These files may be any Windows compatible multi-media standard such as .WAV, .AVI, .MID and .RMI. Alternatively, integer slots of any other agent type may be used to keep a count of active and unacknowledged alarms. To route the alarm to an audio device . To remove a current audio device . -->

Running the Click Once Operator Top Running the Click Once SmartUI Operator The Click Once SmartUI Operator is installed onto a web server (computer running IIS), which installs the files and creates the required virtual directory.

Title: Running the Click Once SmartUI Operator
Steps:
Running the Click Once Operator Top Running the Click Once SmartUI Operator The Click Once SmartUI Operator is installed onto a web server (computer running IIS), which installs the files and creates the required virtual directory. Use the resultant URL (web page) in Internet Explorer to download and run a fully fledged SmartUI Operator, which runs normally as a separate application. IMPORTANT: Ensure that Microsoft .NET Framework version 4.0 and Internet Explorer 7 or later is installed on the user's computer. Running the Click Once SmartUI Operator: This applies to the users who need access to the SmartUI Operator via the web. - Navigate to the click once URL and click the Run button to run the Operator. This URL is typically http://WebSiteAddress/ SUIClickOnce /publish.htm - where WebSiteAddress is the IP address or the domain name of your web site, such as www.msn.com) IMPORTANT: If you do NOT specify the publish.htm portion of this address, then you will get the following error (web page): Server Error 403 - Forbidden: Access is denied. Note: You typically need to receive this Click Once URL from your administrator or whoever manages this web server. - If the Application Run – Security Warning dialog is displayed, then click its Run button. The SmartUI Operator files are now downloaded from your web server. - When this process is complete, if the Windows Security Alert dialog appears, click the Allow Access button. The SmartUI Operator application is launched as a SEPARATE application and not as a Web Page within the Internet Explorer browser. Note: If the SmartUI Operator application EITHER does not appear OR displays an error (Operator.exe has stopped working), then close Internet Explorer and run it again as an Administrator (right click the shortcut and select Run as Administrator ) and repeat these steps again. Login into and use this SmartUI Operator as per normal. IMPORTANT: If you close this SmartUI Operator application then you need to click the Run button from the Operator installation web page, which will typically NOT download any additional files, but will simply launch the Operator application again. -->

text:
Running the Main Subroutine Top Running the Main Subroutine The Script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine.

Title: Running the Main Subroutine
Running the Main Subroutine Top Running the Main Subroutine The Script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine. This main subroutine can be executed in one of four different ways, namely: - On demand, by manually poking ( putslotting ) a one into the runNow slot. While the main subroutine is running any new request for it to run will be ignored. To stop the main subroutine from running, poke a zero into the runNow slot. This method will cause the script to be recompiled, as it needs to be re-initialised after termination. - By scheduling , which is based on a simple schedule; e.g. execute every hour starting from midnight on the 1 st of January. - By triggering , which is based on a list of tags. Each trigger has an identification number that corresponds to its position in the list of triggers. The first tag in the list has an identification number equal to one, etc. Reordering this list will change the trigger identification numbers. To determine from within your script the value of a trigger or the tag that triggered the script, use the system object denoted by Adroit . - By using a combination of scheduling and triggering . For instance, using scheduling on condition that triggering has occurred, will apply a time dead band to the triggering of the script, e.g. run every five seconds but only if a tag in the trigger list has changed. This prevents a flood of triggers initiating multiple executions. -->

Sample VBA Code Top Sample VBA Code For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data or List of all the OLE Functions The.

Title: Sample VBA Code
Sample VBA Code Top Sample VBA Code For details, see Steps required to Monitor Real-time Data or List of all the OLE Functions The following VBA subroutine illustrates the steps involved in monitoring real-time Adroit data: '-------------------------------------------------------- ' Subroutine Subscribe: establishes ongoing realtime ' subscription for a group of tags '-------------------------------------------------------- Sub Subscribe() ' Step1 - Create an OLE Server Data Object Set dataObj = CreateObject("AdroitServer") ' Step2 - Get the Requests collection Set reqs = dataObj.Requests ' Step3 - Add each slot we’re interested in as a ' property in a property set Set p = reqs.CreateProperties() colNo = 0 For Each col In Selection.Columns If colNo <> 0 Then Set pr = p.Add(col.Cells(1).Value) End If colNo = colNo + 1 Next rowNo = 0 For Each rw In Selection.Rows If rowNo <> 0 Then Set r = reqs.Add(rw.Cells(1).Value, p) End If rowNo = rowNo + 1 Next ' Step4 - Save the Data Object fileName = ActiveSheet.Name + ".MIS" dataObj.SaveAs (fileName) ' Step5 - Copy and Paste links dataObj.IncludeNamesOnClipboard = FALSE dataObj.Copy ActiveSheet.PasteSpecial Format:="Text", link:=True ' Step6 - Set update frequency and start the updates dataObj.UpdateFrequency = 1000 dataObj.Active = TRUE End Sub -->

Saving Alarms to a CSV File Top Saving Alarms to a CSV File Note1: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry.

Title: Saving Alarms to a CSV File
Saving Alarms to a CSV File Top Saving Alarms to a CSV File Note1: It is also possible to prevent the EventOutput agent from outputting events when its clustered Agent Server is in standby mode, so that the output destination does not receive duplicate entries, by adding the DisableEventOutputOnStandby value to the registry. Note2: The Time column of the EventOutput agent now supports MILLISECONDS. Note3: For this to work a TEMP folder, e.g. C:\Temp, must exist, which Win2k and WinXP no longer have by default. From the Agent Configurator, do the following: - Create a new EventOutput agent . For the purposes of this example, we will assume that you have used the name EO_FILE as the name of this new agent. - Double-click on the newly created agent. In the Event Output Agent configuration dialog box, do the following: - From the Printer Type list, select the FILE entry to cause the Printer Name field to default to the name of the EventOuput agent .CSV e.g. EO_FILE.CSV and the Setup Data field to default to "Fixed width = /p else CSV format is used" respectively. - The Printer Name field, in this case, is used to specify the path and filename of the file that you wish to send the events to. As long as the path is a valid one, Adroit will create the file if it does not exist. Note1: It is also possible to use the drive letters of mapped remote network shares. Note2: To re-activate the default file name, delete this field, exit the dialog box and re-edit this agent. - The Setup Data field, in this case, will only accept ‘/p’ (without the quotes), which creates a fixed width text file, by forcing the width of the file entries to be padded with spaces as per the configured settings in the Format dialog . Any other entry in this field will use comma delimiters between the columns creating a CSV file format. Note: In the case of CSV files, column widths are honored as maximum width settings, but not the column starting positions. - Disable (select No ) for both the Demand Printing and Time Printing otherwise it will create duplicate, out of sequence entries in your file. - Enable size Printing (select Yes ) and type a 1 in the size drop-down list box i.e. size = 1. - Lastly, add this EventOutput agent e.g. EO_FILE as a printer routing option to the required Alarm agent. While the Agent Server is running, the file being written to is available to other software packages as shared, read-only. -->

Saving data files Top Saving data files Data that is saved by the SmartUI adheres to the following format: Note: For details on the data that is saved by the SmartUI , see Locating saved data . - Data is always saved to two files without extensions: FileName and FileNameINDEX, where: FileName is where the data is actually stored and the INDEX file is used when referencing its data. - In addition to these two files, two backup files usually exist, which are prefixed with the word BAK: FileNameBAK and FileNameINDEXBAK, where these files are copies of the last version of these saved data files. Title: Methods of saving the Server’s data:
- Automatically: Typically the SmartUI Server will be automatically saved when it is closed (or when the service is stopped), however this can increase the time taken for the Server to shutdown. This automatic saving can either be enabled or disabled by configuring the SaveServerOnShutdown Server setting. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Server settings . Note: It is usually NOT recommended to disable this automatic saving when the Server is running as a service. For details, see Launching the SmartUI Server . In addition the SmartUI Server is also able to save its data continually, according to a user-configurable frequency, which by default saves this data every 2 hours. For details, see Server saving settings . - Manually: You can save the SmartUI Server manually, from within the SmartUI Designer, which configures the SmartUI Server, as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - Right-click the name or icon of the required Server connection and select Save Server Data . In addition to making remote configuration of the SmartUI Server possible, this also allows the SmartUI Server to be configured when it is being run as a service. It is also possible to save the SmartUI Server manually when it is run as an application, as follows: Open the Activity Monitor - Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and the SmartUI Server item. - Click the Launch Activity Monitor to open the Activity Monitor. - Note: The Activity Monitor is only displayed if the ActivityMonitorFormEnabled setting for this Server is enabled. For more information on this setting, see Advanced Server settings . The ActivityMonitorFormTitle setting specifies the title of this application. - Warning: The Server window is not displayed if the SmartUI Server is running as a service . - If the server is already running, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - Tip: When the SmartUI Server is running as an application, you may also press the ALT+TAB KEYS repeatedly until the task switcher displays the Server window, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - If the server is already running as a service, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - The Activity Monitor opens and displays information on the Local Machine tab. Click the Save Server Data link from the Tasks panel. -->

Saving the Tag Monitor Utility Top Saving the Tag Monitor Utility The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so.

Title: Saving the Tag Monitor Utility
Saving the Tag Monitor Utility Top Saving the Tag Monitor Utility The Tag Monitor utility can display current values of one or more tag values from a particular Agent Server, in tabular and trend format, without having to specifically draw a mimic or create a trend to do so. For details, see Monitoring Tags (Values) . This utility can either be saved by clicking the Close or Save button. When this utility is saved only the list of monitored tags and its operational parameters are saved, so that these settings will be enabled when this utility is restarted. However, any other configuration within the Graph and Subscription log pages; such as which of the monitored tags are trended and the subscription log messages will be lost. By default the list of the monitored tags are saved in the ‘default_tags.txt’ file located in the folder in which the utility is run, however it is possible to create different tag lists for different servers, simply by start the utility with a suitably named command-line parameter. For details, see Launching the Tag Monitor Utility . The following additional operational parameters are also saved, per tag list, in the ‘adrmonitor.ini’ file that is located in the folder in which the utility is run: - The currently connected Agent Server. - The current window position and size of this utility. - The operational status of this utility i.e. whether it is started or stopped. - The currently selected time span of the trend. -->

Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Top Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Each WanClient is able to determine how the scan bad status of all the tags that it communicates is set within its local Agent Server.

Title: Scan Bad Indication Methodologies
Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Top Scan Bad Indication Methodologies Each WanClient is able to determine how the scan bad status of all the tags that it communicates is set within its local Agent Server. This is a global setting, in that it applies to ALL the tag values that are communicated by this WanClient, irrespective of the number of WanServers that these values are communicated to and / or from. This is configured within the Tag bad philosophy group of the WanClient Configurator dialog, which is launched by selecting Open Configurator from the File menu. Note: Although these are actually ‘scan bad’ indication methodologies, whenever the ‘scan bad’ status bit is set for a tag, this will result in this tag being marked ‘bad’ i.e. its ‘bad’ status bit will also be set. Therefore the terms ‘scan bad’ and ‘tag bad’ can be used synonymously. The following four events can be used to determine how the scan bad status of these tags are set within the Agent Server that is on the WanClient computer: - On comms start: This event occurs when the WanClient begins communicating the tag values to and / or from the WanClients specified within its tag link database. - On comms fail: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is halted unexpectedly. - On comms stop: This event occurs when the communication of the WanClient to and / or from its listed WanClients is stopped. - On client shutdown: This event occurs when the WanClient application itself is exited i.e. the WanClient.exe is shut down. . For each of these four events, one of the following scan bad indication methodologies can be selected: - Do nothing: This leaves the current status of the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags unchanged. - Mark bad: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to ON. - Mark healthy: This sets the scan bad bit for all of the communicated local Agent Server tags to OFF. The Include control tags checkbox, can also be checked or cleared to include or exclude the tags within control groups for each of these scan bad indication methodologies.

However the following needs to be taken cognisance of when this option is enabled: If the tag is currently marked bad, WanClient will mark it healthy (set its scan bad status bit to ON) when it receives a valid value update from the required WanServer.

Title: Scan Bad Indication Methodologies
However the following needs to be taken cognisance of when this option is enabled: If the tag is currently marked bad, WanClient will mark it healthy (set its scan bad status bit to ON) when it receives a valid value update from the required WanServer. Since the values of tags within control groups are NOT received from the WanServer, the Mark bad methodology must NEVER be configured for tags within control group, when using the On comms start event, as this will result in the ‘scan bad’ bit ALWAYS being set for these tags. When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. Then again, this methodology CAN be used, if these tags are configured as dual mode tags i.e. tags that are members of BOTH a control and a normal group. For further details, see Dual mode tags . Note: An existing WanLink installation or when the WanLink database files are deleted, will impose the following default scan bad philosophy, that is backward compatible with existing installations, which implements a Mark healthy , for these events: On comms start , On comms fail and On client shutdown and a Mark bad for this event: On comms stop . -->

Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Top Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Scan point licenses or 'scan points' are just one of the components of an Adroit license.

Title: Scan Point Licensing Exceptions
Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Top Scan Point Licensing Exceptions Scan point licenses or 'scan points' are just one of the components of an Adroit license. These are consumed when information is being manipulated in some way. Their typical usage is when communicating (scanning) a value to a front-end device. However, there are a number of other consumers of scan point licenses, as follows: Note: This is in accordance with the generally adopted Adroit policy, where information is provided freely, but where you are obliged to pay for the service of manipulating information. - Each DbAccess and Script agent consumes a single scan point license to run. This license is checked before doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) or running the Script for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. - Any derived Custom agent, containing a Script engine, will consume a scan point license. - Any pokes performed (i.e. an operation that changes the value of an agent.slot) using either the Adroit OLE Automation Interface ( MISSRVR ) or the Adroit ActiveX component will consume a scan point license for each unique tag (agent.slot) that is "poked". Also, as the AlarmTag, LogTag and ScanTag functions all use pokes internally, calls to these functions will also consume scan point licenses. Also the FetchChanges & FetchValues functions of the Adroit ActiveX component also consume scan point licenses for the same reason. - Any tag (agent.slot) writes from the Adroit OPC Server will consume one scan point license per unique tag. - Once a Command agent has been allowed to perform commands, scan point licenses are consumed by every unique phone number specified by this agent and/or used to send SMS messages to it. For details, see Specifying Additional Callers . - The SNMPMgr agent consumes a scan point for each unique OID value that is monitored, written and/or trapped. - Any agent created for a UDT agent type created by the UDT Agent Type Designer consumes (number of slots-1) scan points. The other scan point will be consumed if and when its rawValue slot is scanned. -->

Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips Top Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips A significant change or noise filter can be specified in the Deadband field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName).

Title: Configuration
Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips Top Scanning Deadband Configuration Tips A significant change or noise filter can be specified in the Deadband field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . Any change in value less than this deadband limit will not be used to update this tag’s value. For details on scanning tags, see How to scan a tag or Scanning tags for general scanning information. The purpose of applying a deadband is to reduce the amount of internal updating of this value within the Adroit database (such as its related alarming, client UI updates and datalogging) in order to conserve PC resources. Note: This does not affect the usage of the commmunication channel itself, since it is performed after the data has arrived. Please consider the following recommendations when configuring this deadband: - Ensure that the deadband is specified in the same units as the slot of the agent being communicated. - The deadband operates best when used to filter out noise or minor variations in value from an integer or analog value that you do not need to see in Adroit . For instance, when using a 12 bit A/D input with 1 bit noise, then use a dead-band of 2. Also when measuring a level on a vessel or item that changes due to vibration, waves or instability, then specify a deadband only slightly greater than the amount of variance. - Do not use a deadband when scanning slots containing state information, as you may lose significant bits of information when decoding to binary format. -->

The simplest way of testing a network card is to check whether shared resources like printers and shares are visible to the computer, once the LAN software has loaded on the computer.

Title: Networks
Steps:
The simplest way of testing a network card is to check whether shared resources like printers and shares are visible to the computer, once the LAN software has loaded on the computer. If the card is not used to communicate on the LAN, then the configuration program for the card can be run, and used to test the card. To do this, the computer must be clean booted so that no drivers are loaded when the diagnostic software runs.

Plug in cards may be supplied with diagnostic software or in some cases with only a sample program.

Title: Other plug-in cards
Steps:
Plug in cards may be supplied with diagnostic software or in some cases with only a sample program. If neither the diagnostic software, nor the sample application can communicate then the card or hardware configuration may be at fault.

Scan the required tag as normal except for the following details: - Device selection: Although ANY device can be selected, it is good engineering practice to restrict all such agent-to-agent scanning to a single pseudo device rather than mixing genuine front-end device communications with agent-to-agent scanning within a single device.

Title: To @ scan a tag:
Scan the required tag as normal except for the following details: - Device selection: Although ANY device can be selected, it is good engineering practice to restrict all such agent-to-agent scanning to a single pseudo device rather than mixing genuine front-end device communications with agent-to-agent scanning within a single device. Either create a pseudo-device using the Adroit simulation protocol driver or use the ALIASSCAN device, which has been created, by default, for this purpose. - Specifying Address field: specify the tag (agent,slot) whose value is required to be copied into the tag that is being scanned, by typing in the required agent name and slot preceded by an @ in the Address field. - The Currently scanned tags list, only displays the following information once this tag is @scanned: - Tag column: destination_agent.slot, - Address column: @source_agent.slot. Note: When slots are "scanned" from other slots like this there is no concept of scan interval because all change events are continuously reported by the subscription mechanism of Adroit . WARNING: If a circular @ subscription is defined whereby destination_agent subscribes to source_agent which is already subscribing to destination_agent, even though via a circuitous route, then the performance of the Agent Server will be severely compromised. -->

Scanning Interval Configuration Tips Top Scanning Interval Configuration Tips A scanning interval can be specified in the Scan rate (ms) field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName).

Title: Configuration
Scanning Interval Configuration Tips Top Scanning Interval Configuration Tips A scanning interval can be specified in the Scan rate (ms) field when a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). is being scanned to a FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. . This is used to specify the time, in milliseconds, which will elapse before this value is communicated to or from this device. For details on scanning tags, see How to scan a tag or Scanning tags for general scanning information. Note: This field should ONLY be specified when configuring POLLED devices, since event-based or TELEMETRY devices do not use setting when communicating. Please consider the following recommendations when configuring this scanning interval: - It is good practice to make your scan-interval longer, for polled drivers, because this minimises the queuing of tasks to be performed by the driver. Scan-tasks are created by Adroit (not the driver) whenever the scan-interval expires. Once a scan task has been created it is given to the driver, where it joins the queue of existing tasks. Hence when scan-times are too short, the queue of existing scan-tasks to performed by the driver increases, which cause configuration-tasks, such as the adding or removal of scan-points or the starting/stopping of the devices, to arrive at the back of this same queue. If the scan-intervals are configured to be longer, then the queue of scan-tasks is reduced, so that the configuration-tasks can be dealt with sooner. Note: The length of the task queue also affects control actions or writes, to the device, which are usually not prioritised to the front of the queue. By slowing the scanning sufficiently, pauses can be created in which nothing is happening, which can be filled by a fast-scanning task. However there is a limit to the number of fast scanning tasks that can be accommodated i.e. if a large amount of fast scanning is required then more sluggish scanning is required too. Therefore, as scan tasks are added, the scanning intervals need to be constantly adjusted and increased to cater for the increased traffic. For details on grouping scanned data together with similar scanning intervals, see Scanning Optimization . - Drivers interlock all communications on a communication resource (e.g.

COM1) so that it is not possible for the driver to do 2 polls at the same time on a port, but is possible to do 2 polls at the same time on 2 different ports.

Title: Configuration
COM1) so that it is not possible for the driver to do 2 polls at the same time on a port, but is possible to do 2 polls at the same time on 2 different ports. Note: In this example RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) could also mean any other front-end device, such as a PLC. This means that the request to a RTU #1 has to complete before the request for data from RTU #2 starts. But if RTU #1 responds very slowly, the driver may timeout before this response has been given and so will query RTU #2 for a response but receive the response from RTU #1 instead. Hence the driver loses synchronization as a result of this confusing traffic. Although this problem can be prevented by making the scan-times longer, it would be better to make the timeouts longer to accommodate any late responses, since then no performance is lost when the RTU responds within the required time. -->

Scanning Optimization Top Scanning Optimization The optimization of scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED).

Title: Scanning Optimization
Scanning Optimization Top Scanning Optimization The optimization of scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). typically involves grouping data correctly within front-end devices, so as to prevent fragmentation of the data that usually creates a bottleneck for communication performance. Usually I/Os acquired from the plant are not needed by the SCADA, but are intermingled with the SCADA I/O. Therefore, it is recommended to allocate separate memory space in the controller for SCADA tags and the internal I/O. Although determining how much memory to reserve is never easy, it is recommended to plan correctly in this area. Certain front-end devices, such as Siemens controllers, make this process easier by using addressable data blocks or files that can grow in size. By scanning tags, whose slots belong to the same data type, which has contiguous addresses in the front-end device, will ensure that this device will require the least number of transactions to communicate its tags. For details, see Contiguous Scanning . Note: The reason for this is that a separate Scan agent is generally created by this device's Device agent, for a block of manageable contiguous addresses, the size of which is dependent upon the protocol being used to transfer this data to and from Adroit . When grouping data, ensure that the various data types are separated, such as Analogs and Digitals, examples of such groups are: Digital Inputs, Analog Inputs, Digital Outputs, Analog SPs etc. It is also recommended to further differentiate data with respect to their required scan rate. Typically Analog values for I/O, such as temperatures can be grouped together as these values generally change very slowly. Although, Digital data must always be scanned quite fast, it is possible to differentiate between feedback and event digitals that must be polled very fast and digitals that indicate situations that need not be acted on right away, such as a high level indicator that takes 15 minutes to overflow. Note: When scanning tags, remember that it is the data type of the SLOT that is being scanned that determines which group it should be scanned to and not its AGENT name. For details of optimizing the scanning for an Analog agent, see Analog Scanning Optimization Example . The following examples illustrates how various types of data types could be grouped: Note: Scan times of less than 1000 ms should only be used if the driver can poll fast enough. Using faster scan times may adversely affect communications error recovery and the sending of controls to the front-end device. A further tip to optimise scanning in Adroit: Save the WGP and then restart the Agent Server to potentially reduce the number of required Scan agents. Reason: It is only when saving the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file that the Adroit scanning sub-system sorts the scan list into the optimal order, but this .WGP file is only read again when the Agent Server is restarted. Example: After successively importing and deleting scanned items a system required 69 Scan agents. By simply saving the WGP file and restarting the Agent Server, without doing anything else, Adroit only required 30 Scan agents! -->

Scanning Slots in the Project Explorer Top Scanning Slots in the Project Explorer Expand the required agent type object in the tree view windowpane - Either select the required agent so that its slots are displayed in the Explorer Agent List grid windowpane on the left, then right click the required slot and select the Scan slot… menu item.

Title: Scanning Slots in the Project Explorer
Scanning Slots in the Project Explorer Top Scanning Slots in the Project Explorer Expand the required agent type object in the tree view windowpane - Either select the required agent so that its slots are displayed in the Explorer Agent List grid windowpane on the left, then right click the required slot and select the Scan slot… menu item. - Or right click the required agent, in the tree view, and select the Scan… menu item. This displays the Adroit Tag Scanning Dashboard dialog. Note: This dialog can be resized, to view lengthy scanning configuration, if necessary. - Select the required pre-configured device in the Device list box, from the list of available device drivers. Note: If there is a driver that was not setup during installation, it can be added later by running Adroit Setup and adding a new driver. The Agent Server will NOT need to be restarted. - Start or stop scanning from this selected Device by either selecting the Started (the default selection) or the Stopped options. The Add tag edit box, contain the currently selected agent and slot combination, when launched from the Explorer Agent List grid windowpane e.g. AgentName.AgentDescription. - In the Device address edit box, specify the protocol driver specific address in this Device to which the value of this tag will be stored. - In the Scan rate (ms) edit box, define the scanning interval or period in milliseconds between attempts to poll this item. Note: This will only apply to polled devices; telemetry devices will ignore this parameter. - In the Deadband edit box, specify the limit that the change in the scanned value must exceed before the agent’s slot is updated. This Deadband is in the same units as the tag that is being scanned. For performance reasons, it is advisable to give a non-zero Deadband for Analog or Integer values in order to filter out noise or minor variations in value, since applying a Deadband reduces the number of changes to the database thus improving performance. Note1: It is NOT advisable to use a Deadband when scanning tags that contain state information, as you may lose significant bits of information when decoding to binary form. Note2: The scan inhibit and/or output enable bits can be set “live” for the currently selected item i.e. it is no longer necessary to unscan the item, change its setting(s) and rescan the item. However, the device needs to be stopped and restarted before these settings can take effect. - If required, tick the Scan (input) inhibited checkbox, to stop this scanned tag from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). Note: This does not affect this scanned tag from updating the PLC (front-end device). - If required, tick the Output enabled checkbox, to enable this scanned tag to update the PLC (front-end device). Note: This does not affect this scanned tag from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). - If you want an initial value to be written to the Device to change the value in the FED, at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery, then check the Output initialise checkbox. By default this is OFF (cleared). - Click the Add button to add this slot-scanning configuration to the scanned tag list for this selected Device . Note1: The Update button makes it possible to modify the scanning settings for an item, with a single update, instead of having to unscan the item, change its details and then rescan it.
