Scanning Templates Top Scanning Templates You can create one or more Scanning templates to specify the default scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED).

Title: Scanning Templates
Scanning Templates Top Scanning Templates You can create one or more Scanning templates to specify the default scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). settings that are specified in the Tag scanning configuration dialog, when scanning the slots of agents in Adroit . Note: The Connector used by the Adroit DB Generator utility to connect to the required source (3 rd party application) determines whether templates can be used or not. Usage Example: You can create a scanning template per front end device that provides the default communication parameters required for this specific device. Each time an agent is scanned to this device then these default settings can be used to save your users engineering time. Default templates: The _ScanningDefault template is added for you, providing the Adroit default settings, which you can customise accordingly. Each scanning template allows you to provide default settings for one or more of the following scanning parameters: - The slot (value) to be scanned: if this slot is provided by the agent that you want to scan, will be selected by default. The Adroit default for this is the rawValue slot. - The rate at which the value should be scanned, in milliseconds. This is the amount of time that will elapse before this value is communicated to or from this Device. The Adroit default for this is 1 second (1000 milliseconds) - The applicable scanning deadband value, which can prevent unnecessary communication, as any CHANGE in value LESS than this deadband limit will NOT be communicated. In Adroit this is not specified, by default (0). - The scan inhibit status, if set this will prevent the scanned value from being changed by the Device ( FED front-end device, which is a device that is accessed directly by the user, such as a PLC or RTU. ). The Adroit default for this is OFF (0). - The output enabled status, if set this will allow the scanned value to be written to the Device to change the value in the FED. The Adroit default for this is OFF (0). - If necessary, a scanning suffix can be specified that will be added to the device-specific addresses. This is not specified, by default (“”). Note: By default the slots of the scanning template are set to the Adroit default settings.

To create a scanning template: this creates a scanning template for the Scanning category that is listed beneath the Templates folder.

Title: Scanning Templates
To create a scanning template: this creates a scanning template for the Scanning category that is listed beneath the Templates folder. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Scanning category within the Templates folder. - Select the Create template… menu item. - Type in the required Template name . Tip: Provide a brief name that makes it easy to identify the purpose of this template. - Click the OK button. This selects and adds this template to the bottom of the list of templates beneath the Scanning category. The scanning-specific slots are displayed in the right hand pane, with their Adroit Default value . - Customise the default scanning parameters (slots) for this template, as follows: To change the value of a slot in the scanning template: - Double click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Provide the required default value for this slot in the Edit template slot value dialog. - Click the OK button. To delete a slot from the scanning template: - Right click the required Slot entry in the right hand pane. - Select the Delete slot menu item. WARNING! The selected slot is IMMEDIATELY removed. Note: If you delete one of these slots then the Adroit default value will be used. To sort the list of scanning templates: by default each template is added to the end of the existing list of scanning templates, it is possible to sort this list, alphabetically, in ascending order, to make it easier for users to select the templates. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the Scanning category within the Templates folder. - Select the Sort menu item. This rearranges the list of scanning templates alphabetically, in ascending order. To delete a scanning template: to remove an existing scanning template. - Press the Windows key and start typing in DB Generator and select it from the list. In the explorer type view on the left of this application: - Right click the required scanning template in the Scanning category in the Templates folder. - Select the Delete template… menu item. The selected template is removed from the list of templates.

Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ Top Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ This topics provides answers to commonly experienced problems/issues associated with scanning: Q: When the Agent Server is started, 3 beeps are heard and the Agent Server disappears.

Title: Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ
Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ Top Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ This topics provides answers to commonly experienced problems/issues associated with scanning: Q: When the Agent Server is started, 3 beeps are heard and the Agent Server disappears. Why does this happen? A: The 3 beeps are produced when a driver is NOT loaded by the Agent Server, which can occur because of the following reasons: - the driver has not been configured and therefore cannot load properly - the port is already in use or does not exist - some other resource has run out. Look for the devices in the Adroit Setup drivers tab, and check the amount of free disk space. Make sure you do not have a folder in your installation directory with the same name as the device. Q: When writing to a register, the value does not change, why? A: This can be due to writing to an input; a driver automatically disallows writing values to inputs, since they are most likely not supported in that protocol. In the Modbus driver, for instance you cannot write to digital input 1XXXXX registers, nor to the analog input 3XXXX registers. A driver in most cases does not generate an error/alarm, but simply fails the transaction. This is noticeable by the tag greying out in the mimic, and then becoming healthy on the next scan. Note: Whenever you perform a write using any polled (not telemetry) driver, Adroit automatically queues that item/task for reading afterwards Q: The driver software does not run, and I do not get any messages explaining what is wrong. Where do I look now? A: The first place to look in event of an error is the Windows event log. Look at the last few entries in the Application and System event logs for more details on a problem. Often a problem is the result of an error reported a little further back in the log. Q: An error message appears about a buffer overrun in the protocol driver monitor just before the comms dies. What does this mean? A: Buffer overruns and underruns are caused when the buffer on the serial card overflows. This is because character reception and transmission relies on the CPU emptying the buffer as the computer receives characters in the line. If the computer is busy with some other task (which happens all the time in windows), the buffer is not serviced often enough. The solution is to use a card with a buffered UART (FIFO buffer). This provides a 16-byte buffer as opposed to the 1-byte buffer common in older cards. Q: I have a serial card with a Buffered UART of FIFO but I still get overruns, why? A: The serial card driver for Windows may not have detected the FIFO. Use the Ports applet in Control Panel to enable the use of the FIFO. Delete the affected ports, and re-boot. The operating system will auto-detect the FIFO on the port and add it in. If it is not added in, you may edit the port settings and go to the advanced dialog which allows changing IRQ’s etc. Check the box at the bottom of the dialog, in order to enable the FIFO. Q: I get error messages such as parity error or framing error in the driver monitor window, followed by communications failure. A: In this case, characters on the line are being corrupted or badly sent. To correct the problem, lower the baud-rate on both devices. Q: The (any serial) driver is not running.

When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears.

Title: Scanning Troubleshooting FAQ
When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears. Although no driver or hardware configuration was changed, there is no longer any communication. A: Make sure the mouse is plugged into the correct port. If the mouse is on the port the driver would use, the mouse will work but the Adroit driver will not. To correct this problem, either swap the mouse back and re-boot, or re-configure the driver to use the free port, and re-start Adroit . Q: Why does scanning not work for certain Analog agents? A: Please ensure that you scan the raw value slot and NOT the Engineering value as this can cause scanning to fail because the scanned value is out of range. Q: When I access a device agent, all I receive are event log entries about the failed device and the need to restart the Agent Server. A: This indicates that a device has not been attached at startup and as a result, its scanning configuration is not loaded. This occurs for intermittent Windows/PC resource/device unavailability/conflict at the time of Agent Server startup. The Agent Server needs to be restarted to gain access to these resources or to sort out a resource conflict; for example, your RAS connection (or other software) is still active which is using the same COM port as your device configuration. Q: When I install a protocol driver, it is copied without errors but does not appear in the "Available protocol drivers" list. A: A number of our Adroit drivers rely on 3rd party components being installed, if they are not, then you get the above symptoms. This is because the driver available list in setup uses the driver, which also uses the missing 3rd party component. Examples are: Allen Bradley RSLINX, Eagle, Lonworks, Modbus plus (+), Siemens H1, Siemens L2 and Siemens S7 Functions among others. In such cases, the required hardware and accompanying software must be installed (preferably before the driver). Note: Many network (Ethernet, H1 and TCP/IP) drivers also require the installation of the Windows TCP/IP protocol. If in doubt, open the relevant driver documentation file found in your Adroit system folder for more information. Q: Communication to the PLC is lost intermittently. A: This is a possible driver device failure. Reinstall or update with a new driver. -->

Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support Top Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support If Adroit is not scanning (communicating) with your PLC or FED, please do the following checks to try to resolve this issue yourself: - Is a HASP attached to your Agent Server computer?

Title: Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support
Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support Top Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support If Adroit is not scanning (communicating) with your PLC or FED, please do the following checks to try to resolve this issue yourself: - Is a HASP attached to your Agent Server computer? - If yes, ensure that the correct licence information appears in the Agent Server window? If not then check that both the port (use the port testing utility supplied in the utilities folder on the Adroit installation DVD in the ‘Utilities\comm port tester’ folder) also ensure that the HASP is not faulty. - If no, open the Agent Server window and ensure that the following message was not reported over three minutes ago: "Server shutting down scanning in 180 seconds", if so then the hour of free scanning has elapsed and the Agent Server must be restarted in demo mode for scanning to continue. - Open the Agent Server Configuration page of your Adroit Setup utility and determine if your Agent Server Type set to "Cluster server". For details, see Agent Server Project Configuration . If yes, take note of your Project Name and Agent Server Name fields and then open the Adroit Classic UI, open the Options menu, click Preferences and open the Connection tab and determine if your Agent Server is in Standby mode. If yes, ensure that Parallel scanning has been configured for the cluster, to do this open the Adroit Classic Setup utility (psexe.exe) and click the Options. . . button next to the Agent Server Type field. - Is the required device started? If not, start it. - Verify that you are physically connected to the device you are trying to communicate to. - Open your Adroit Setup utility, as in step 2, and select the Drivers page and double click the required device in the Installed devices list and verify that all the driver setup configuration parameters (comm. port etc.) make sense to you, and that any two drivers do not use the same resource/port. For more details, see Configuring a Device of a Protocol Driver . - Verify that your hardware is working, check that the cables are not damaged, and test continuity if applicable. If you are still unable to resolve this scanning issue, then please perform the following steps before contacting support about your driver communication problem, so that you can provide them with the necessary information so that they can determine and/or resolve this issue: - Launch the Driver Monitor Launcher , by selecting the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 and then the Driver Monitor Launcher item. - Select the driver that is causing the communication problems from the Driver list box. - Write down both the description and revision of this installed driver, which are displayed below this list box. - In the Device name list box, double-click on the name of the device that is causing the communication problem, to open its Driver Monitor. - Select this Driver Monitor and press the "3" key to display the "Error Log" screen and try to determine the nature of the problem from the live detailed reports for all problems in a driver, that are displayed in this screen. - If the nature of the problem cannot be detected, then press the "ESC" key, to return to the main menu and press the "1" key to display the "Datascope" screen. - If you are familiar with communication protocols, use the "Datascope" screen to try and analyse the problem.

Note: By default this screen opens in ASCII mode, which is indicated in the title bar of the window, to toggle the mode to HEX and vice verse (depending on protocol), type in "A".

Title: Scanning-issue Checklist before Contacting Support
Note: By default this screen opens in ASCII mode, which is indicated in the title bar of the window, to toggle the mode to HEX and vice verse (depending on protocol), type in "A". - If you are unfamiliar with communication protocols, create a log-file of the messages in the "Datascope" screen, which you can FAX/e-mail it to the Support desk, as follows: press the "L" key, waiting for the screen to fill with messages and then press the "L" key again. This will create a Devicename .txt file in your Adroit system folder e.g. C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit , where Devicename is the name of the device selected in step 4. Note: Having an Internet e-mail address available ensures that the Support desk can forward patches to your computer and/or that you can send your database (the .WGP file) and other relevant information to the Support desk. -->

Title: ScanTag ActiveX Method
ScanTag ActiveX Method Top ScanTag ActiveX Method PLEASE NOTE: This method uses scan points because it uses putslot functionality internally, therefore ensure that the Agent Server computer either is licensed (i.e. has a HASP Software Protection Key attached) or that the Agent Server is run using the Limited Time License HASP . SCADA Functionality . Method ScanTag (AgentOrSlot:String, Slot:String, Device:string, Address:String, Rate:Long, DeadBand:Long, OutputEnable:Long):Boolean; This method configures a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). for scanning. Parameters: - AgentOrSlot: the name of the agent or tag (agent.slot) that is to be scanned. - Slot: the name of the slot to be scanned. This parameter is ignored if the Agent parameter contains a tag. - Device: the name of the Device agent interfacing to the PLC or other front-end device, e.g. SIMPLC - Address: the scan address of the point to be scanned, e.g. DB2:DW0 - Rate: the scan period in milliseconds at which point is to be polled. Note: This parameter is ignored when this method is used to @scan . - Deadband: the scanning deadband in scanned units. Note: This parameter is ignored when this method is used to @scan. - OutputEnable: set to true if you want the scanned point to be an output. To UNSCAN a specified item, specify the Rate (at which this item was scanned) as a negative value, while keeping all the other parameters correct. In this case, the AgentOrSlot , Slot and Address parameters are case sensitive. For instance, if the item was scanned at a rate of 1500 milliseconds, then it is necessary to specify its Rate as –1500, in order to unscan it. Note: In order to create a Device agent and add scan points to it, first create the device agent, using CreateAgent , then perform a ‘dummy’ Fetch to initialise the Device agent, which does NOT initialise itself when it is created and then use this method to add the required scan points to it. -->

Title: Slots:
Slot Name Type Function catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used for datalog and real-time data catch-up) command VARSTRING The executable program (including parameters) to run when a scheduled time arrives. datesToExclude VARSTRING A list of specific dates, which must be excluded from the scheduled periods. enabled BOOLEAN If this is set to TRUE (1) then the "value" slot of the Scheduler agent is determined by the scheduled periods. If this is set to FALSE (0) then the "value" slot of the Scheduler agent can be manually controlled. masterAgent TAGNAME The master scheduler agent i.e. any changes made to its schedule slot is automatically transferred to all those Scheduler agents who refer to it as Master. Note: the datestoexclude slot is NOT transferred. recDaysOfMonth INTEGER This contains the value of the ‘Day of month’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify the required day, as a number, that this record is valid for. recDaysOfWeek INTEGER This contains the value of the ‘Weekdays’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify the decimal value of the 7 digit binary number that specifies which days of the week this record is valid for e.g. if all seven days are required (1111111), specify 127 or if only Tuesdays and Wednesdays are required (0110000), specify 48. recEndDate TIME This contains the value of the ‘End datetime’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify the date and time at which this record should terminate. recIndex INTEGER This is an index for the list of schedule records, with 0 representing the first record. Once a valid index is selected, the following slots, representing the individual parameters of the record, can be updated e.g. via a mimic or script: recStartDate, recEndDate, recDaysOfWeek, recDaysOfMonth, recLastDayOfMonth and recSpecial. recLastDayOfMonth BOOLEAN This contains the value of the ‘Last day of month’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify a 1 or 0 to turn this option on or off respectively. recSpecial BOOLEAN This contains the value of the ‘Special’ or ‘Auto delete’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify a 1 or 0 to turn this option on or off respectively.

recStartDate TIME This contains the value of the ‘Start datetime’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot.

Title: Slots:
recStartDate TIME This contains the value of the ‘Start datetime’ parameter for the schedule record specified by the recIndex slot. To alter this value, specify the date and time at which this record should commence. schedule LIST A list of time schedules where each entry contains the following parameters: - Start datetime – The start date/time of an entry. If left blank, the parameter is disabled and all date/times are valid - End datetime – The end date/time or time of an entry. If left blank, the parameter is disabled and all date/times are valid - Weekdays – The days of the week for which this entry is valid. If no weekdays are selected the entry is disabled. - Day of month – The day of the month on which this entry is valid. A value of zero disables the parameter. All weekdays should be enabled for a non-zero value to work properly. - Last day of month – If enabled, the entry is only valid if it is the last day of the month. - Special – If enabled, the entry will be deleted as soon as the end datetime is exceeded. uct BOOLEAN If this is set to TRUE (1) then any times specified in the schedule are specified using the UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time format instead of using local time. If this is set to FALSE (0), the default setting then local time is used instead. Note: The slot name is uct even though it refers to setting UTC time. value BOOLEAN If this is set to TRUE (1) then the current time is within a scheduled time. If this is set to FALSE (0) then the current time is NOT scheduled. Note: If the "Enabled" slot is set to FALSE then this can be manually controlled.

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title: Scheduling and Triggering Scripts
Steps:
Scheduling and Triggering Scripts Top Scheduling and Triggering Scripts This enables the remote execution of the main subroutine by the Script agent. The following combinations of triggering and scheduling can be configured: - Triggering only: This is used when the execution of the script is only required after a particular condition, defined within the script, has been met by one or more of the tags within Adroit . This requires checking Run when one of the following tags change and then configuring one or more triggers . - Scheduling only: This is used when the execution of the script is required at a set time period, which is set by the user. It is also possible to synchronise the start of the scheduling at a specified time. This requires the configuring the scheduling . Ensure that both the, only if one of the following tags change and Run when one of the following tags change options, are unchecked. - Triggering and Scheduling: In this case the script is executed when its scheduled to and when a value of the one of the triggers change. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, Run when one of the following tags change option, should be checked. - Scheduling if Triggered: In this case the script is only executed when it is scheduled to, if a value of the one of the triggers also change. This effectively applies a time deadband to the triggering, preventing a flood of triggers that would initiate multiple executions. This requires configuring one or more triggers and configuring the scheduling . Only the, only if one of the following tags change option, should be checked. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! -->

Scheduling Commands and Utilities Top Scheduling Commands and Utilities Commands and utilities can be scheduled to run today, tomorrow, or on a particular day of the week or month at a specified time using the Scheduler.

Title: Scheduling Commands and Utilities
Scheduling Commands and Utilities Top Scheduling Commands and Utilities Commands and utilities can be scheduled to run today, tomorrow, or on a particular day of the week or month at a specified time using the Scheduler. Typical examples of its use would be executing a batch file, starting a backup procedure, printing a report, archiving a file, extracting logged data or doing a putslot operation. The Scheduler utility also provides dialog boxes to assist in specifying the required details for the Adroit putslot , extract (datalogs) and merge (datalogs) operations. For details, see Specifying the Scheduled Command or Utility . Tip: This utility provides extensive use of tooltips to provide context sensitive help. If unsure about the function of a checkbox or list box hold the mouse pointer over it until the tooltip is displayed. To schedule a command or utility: - Launch the Scheduler . - Specify the command or utility that should be scheduled . - Specify when this command or utility should be executed . - Add these specified details to the list of scheduled entries (this also describes how to manage this list of scheduled entries). - Write the details of this scheduled command or utility to the registry . Note: Since this information is written to the registry, it is not necessary for the Scheduler to remain running in order to schedule the specified entries. -->

Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: To schedule a script:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - Click the plus box to the left of the Server Scripts datasource or its icon . Tip: It is also possible to display the script objects by double-clicking on this name or icon. - Right-click the required name of the script object or its icon and select Script Scheduling . The Schedule Script configuration dialog is launched - Specify the required Schedule Type from this list, as follows: - Interval: the default option, to trigger this script every ## seconds, as specified by the Trigger the script every spin control. The default value of 0 does NOT trigger the script IMPORTANT: In order to use the Interval Schedule Type, you must specify an interval that is >= the MinimumScriptSchedulingTime setting in the Server and Service .CONFIG file [in the DatasourceSettings group]. - One Time: to Trigger the script at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. - Daily: to Trigger the script Daily at the following time , which you specify as follows: select the required time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. - Weekly: to Trigger the script Weekly, synchronised at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. - Monthly: to Trigger the script Monthly, synchronised at the following Date and Time , which you specify as follows: select the required date and/or time unit and either type in the required unit or use the spin control's arrows to select this. - If you need this script to be performed as soon as the Server starts up, then check the Trigger on startup checkbox. - Specify the user account ( User Name and Password ) that this script should be run under, in the Run the script under the following user section. Note: A User Name and Password must be specified for scripts that interact with other datasources. In other words, those scripts that read and/or write data elements or call special functions etc. -->

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered - usually used for testing. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Enable Boolean If Enable = True (the checkbox is checked), then the associated script object will execute whenever this spider is triggered. Otherwise it will not. Thread based Boolean If Thread based = True (the checkbox is checked), then whenever the script is triggered, providing Enable = True, the script will be run using a separate thread. Otherwise it will be run using the Client’s thread. Note1: It is only recommended to set this input for scripts that perform their processing in the background and do not require user input to allow this processing to execute faster. Note2: The thread-based execution of the script object will not halt other processing of the Client. Script Object Script Object This can accept a script object from the Script Server that has been written to interact with the Client and if necessary the Server. For details, see Creating script objects or Adding script objects . Script Source Text This contains the raw text content of the specified script object. Note: This is an optional input that can be used to change the script text within the script object, specified by the Script Object input. Tip: When creating a script within this Script Engine spider, it is recommended to launch the Script Editor instead, so that the script and its references can be appropriately configured. For details, see Working with the script editor . - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function + input var This will add a variable called var # to the Inputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1, which can be used within the script of this Script Engine spider. For details, see Adding input variables . Note1: In order to use input variables within your script, ensure the IneedSpiderInfo interface has been implemented. For details, see Working with INeed Interfaces .

Note2: You must create the required input variables that the script requires before the script is run, otherwise a runtime error will result.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Note2: You must create the required input variables that the script requires before the script is run, otherwise a runtime error will result. Note3: Input variables can also be removed from this spider. For details, see Removing input and output variables . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Runtime errors ArrayList A list of the errors that occurred when the script was last executed. This list is updated after the script is run. Errors ArrayList A list of errors that occurred while the script was being compiled. This list is updated before the script is run. Note: Whenever the script is run, it is first compiled and only if there are no compilation errors, is it executed, after which any run time errors are identified. These outputs record both the compilation ( Errors ) and run time errors ( Runtime errors ) that occur when the script is last run. But only display the number of each type of error, within this configuration view. For details, see Debugging the script object . Tip: It is recommended to launch the Script Editor to view the descriptions of these errors in its Output window so that you may be able to locate and rectify them. Do this by clicking the Launch Script Editor button, within the Inputs section. For details, see Working with the script editor . - New Output , this section contains the output types configured for this spider. New Output Function + output var This will add a variable called var # to the Outputs section, where # is a unique number starting from 1, which can be used within the script of this Script Engine spider. For details, see Adding output variables . Note1: In order to use output variables within your script, ensure the IneedSpiderInfo interface has been implemented. For details, see Working with INeed Interfaces . Note2: You must create the required output variables that the script requires before the script is run, otherwise a runtime error will result. Note3: Output variables can also be removed from this spider. For details, see Removing input and output variables . -->

Script Procedures Top Script Procedures When a Has script engine Custom agent is derived the following empty procedures are created, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent: OnCompiled() Code that is executed every time the Agent Server detects a change in the script code.

Title: Script Procedures
Steps:
Script Procedures Top Script Procedures When a Has script engine Custom agent is derived the following empty procedures are created, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent: OnCompiled() Code that is executed every time the Agent Server detects a change in the script code. This procedure can be used to initialise any global variables. OnLoadComplete() Code that is executed once an agent has been loaded from the WGP file. This procedure can contain code to initialise slot values. OnChange(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a slot value is changed. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the slot and value thereof being changed, e.g. setting status bit slots. OnUpdate(slotid, value) Code that is executed every time a Tagname type slot receives a subscription update. This procedure should contain code that requires execution depending on the subscription received. OnBackground() Code that is executed every second in the background. This procedure should contain time-dependant and/or simulation code. -->

Title: To search the help for topics:
- Click the Search tab. - Type the search query that you want to locate in one or more help topics into the edit box or click the list button and select a previously entered search query from this list box. Basic searches: Guidelines or tips for creating the search query. - Searches are not case-sensitive, so you can type your search in either uppercase or lowercase characters. - You may search for any combination of letters (a-z) and/or numbers (0-9). - Punctuation marks such as the period ("."), colon (":"), semicolon (";"), comma (","), and hyphen ("-") are ignored during a search. - Group the elements of your search using double quotes or parentheses into phrases, where necessary e.g. (TermA TermB) or “TermA TermB”. Note1: The default operation between terms is AND, so unless you specifically group terms into phrases then all instances of each individual word will be searched for. Note2: You cannot search for quotation marks. Note3: If you are searching for a file name with an extension, you should group the entire string in double quotes, ("file name.ext"). Advanced searches: Additional items that can be added to your search query to help you narrow your searches for more precise results. - Wildcard expressions: These can be used as placeholders for one or more characters, within your search query. - Use a question mark (“?”) as a single-character placeholder e.g. 90?10, will return 90a10, 90610 etc. - Use an asterisk (“*”) as a multiple character placeholder e.g. water*, will return "WATER", "waterfall", "waterproof" etc. Note: These wildcard operators cannot be the only character in a term. - Boolean operators: These can be used to create specific relationships between the phrases or words in your search query. - TermA AND TermB: This will return topics that both contain TermA and TermB. - TermA OR TermB: This will return topics that either contain TermA or TermB. - TermA NOT TermB: This will return topics that contain TermA but not TermB. - TermA NEAR TermB: This will return topics that contain TermA within eight words of TermB. Note1: If no Boolean operator is specified, AND is used i.e. TermA TermB = TermA AND TermB. Note2: The |, &, and ! characters do not work as Boolean operators (you must use OR, AND, and NOT). - Nested expressions: These allow you to create complex search queries. - Use parentheses to nest expressions within a query. The expressions in parentheses are evaluated before the rest of the query. - If a query does not contain a nested expression, it is evaluated from left to right. Examples: TermA NOT TermB OR TermC will locate topics, which contain TermA without TermB or topics containing TermC. TermA NOT (TermB OR TermC) will locate topics, which contain TermA without either TermB or TermC. Note: You cannot nest expressions more than five levels deep. Note: If you are performing an advanced search and using one or more Boolean operators, click the button to select the required operators from the list. - If necessary, ensure that the required search settings have been set before the search is performed: - To only search topic titles and not their contents, ensure the Search titles only checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. - To find words similar to your search term, ensure the Match similar words checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. - To narrow your search, ensure the Search previous results checkbox at the bottom of the Search tab is ticked. - To highlight all instances of search terms that are found in topic files, click the Options toolbar button and select Search Highlight On.

Secondary Port Enabled Top Secondary Port Enabled Adroit drivers can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component.

Title: Secondary Port Enabled
Secondary Port Enabled Top Secondary Port Enabled Adroit drivers can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3-step process: - Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. - Timeout Phase : the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. If the retries are exhausted and there is still no valid response, the Adroit driver will use the secondary port if it is configured when this step is reached. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port. If, at some later time, the secondary port should fail, communications will switch back to the primary port, and will continue through the primary hardware if this has been repaired. After which scanning resumes immediately. However, there is also an Alternate Secondary Port Enabled scenario where the same PC port / resource is used but with different PLC ports / resources. -->

Securing datasources Top Securing datasources Once a datasource has been added, its data and its additional functionality, if provided, is exposed.

Title: Securing datasources
Securing datasources Top Securing datasources Once a datasource has been added, its data and its additional functionality, if provided, is exposed. Depending upon the sensitivity of this data and/or the exposed functionality, you may need to control the access to these items. Both the datasource itself and its data can be secured using the data element security. For details, see Working with data element security . This allows one to specify which user(s) and/or group(s) are allowed to view, configure and remove these items and/or who is able to configure their security settings. For details on how to control the access to the datasource and its data elements, see Assigning security permissions to data elements . Note: If the currently logged on user, does not have the necessary security permissions, then he/she may not even be able to see the datasource in the Enterprise Manager and/or some or all of the data elements. Furthermore he/she may be unable to configure or delete some or all of the data elements that are visible. Tip: If you need to reset the configured security settings for any reason, then right click the datasource and select the Reset configured security item. Click for more details: Note: Ensure that the specified allowed user(s) and group(s) are also associated with the required policies, so that they may be able to add and/or remove the specified datasource and in necessary, use its special functions. For details, see Available policies . If the datasource also exposes additional functionality, this can also be secured using the special function security. For details, see Working with special function security . This allows one to specify which of the allowed user(s) and group(s) are able to use these functions and/or who is able to configure their security settings. For details on how to control the access to the special functions, see Assigning security permissions to special functions . Note: If the currently logged on user, does not have the necessary security permissions, then he/she may not even be able to see some or all of the special functions. -->

Securing projects Top Securing projects Projects manage the creation, translation and storage of their graphic forms.

Title: Securing projects
Steps:
Securing projects Top Securing projects Projects manage the creation, translation and storage of their graphic forms. You therefore secure projects to control which users are able to access the project and its configured graphic forms. Tip: If you need to reset the configured security settings for any reason, then right click the project and select the Reset configured security item. Access to each project, its folders and/or graphic forms are controlled using data element security. Click for more details: this is because a project is actually a datasource and its configured folders and graphic forms are data elements. For details on how to distinguish the available datasources, see About datasources and data elements . This enables you to specify which user(s) and/or group(s) are allowed to view, configure and remove these items and/or who is able to configure their security settings. For details on how to use data element security to control the access to each project, its folders and/or graphic forms, see Working with data element security . In other words, if the currently logged on user, does not have the necessary security permissions, then he/she may not even be able to see some or all of the configured projects and/or their folders and graphic forms. Furthermore he/she may be unable to configure or delete some or all of the projects and/or their folders and graphic forms that are visible. For details on how to control the access to a project and its individual folders and graphic forms, see Assigning security permissions to data elements . -->

Security configuration Top Security configuration The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Security configuration Top Security configuration The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security. This is made possible by using a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups on each Server computer, known as the "allowed" users and groups, which provide the first or foundational level of ALL security and user management within the SmartUI ; hence their creation is mandatory for every Server. For further details on configuring roaming profiles to manage user management, see Working with profiles . Note: On each Server, it is also possible to give specific users and groups total or global security access to the Server and it is recommended to use these group(s) and/or user(s) to administer its security. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users or Configuring SmartUI Server security . Tip: As a further security precaution, it is possible to prevent users from using a domain user name and password, by configuring impersonated user names and passwords, which do not natively exist on the domain itself. In other words, unless a user is either an allowed user or a member of an allowed group he/she will be unable to login to the Server and use the SmartUI . For this reason, the necessary user accounts and/or groups need to be created within Windows first. For details, see Working with user accounts and groups . Tip: To save time when launching a Client, it is possible to specify automatic login settings that will be used whenever the Client is launched. For details, see Automatically logging into SmartUI Servers . -->

Select queries Top Select queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Select queries
Select queries Top Select queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Select Queries can select a sub-set of your data by tailoring your data to suit specific uses or requirements. Click for more information: In addition to selecting the required tables and/or views and their fields, you can also create relationships between fields in these tables and/or views. You can also add criteria that must be met by values in one or more fields. If necessary, parameterise the criteria values to specify them before performing the query. Note1: Unlike tables and databinders, the data obtained by a Select query is not updated by the Server and remains as current as the last time that it was executed. Note2: Unlike tables that ONLY display their last 1000 records, Select queries display ALL the records that match its specified criteria. Note3: Select queries can be queued to ensure that a query will not be lost when the connection to its database fails. For a practical example of using Select queries one of which uses parameters, which are supplied by controls on a graphic form, see How to chart and/or report data from a database . To add and configure a Select query: Add a Select query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters.

- If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query.

Title: Select queries
- If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language. Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option. Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query. For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Select query: - Select the required fields from the Tables and Fields tree in the New User Defined Query dialog. Check the checkbox of each table and their field/s that you would like to be queried, by clicking on it. If necessary, expand the Views node and check the checkbox of each view and their field/s that you would like to be queried, by clicking on it. The names of tables and views support SQL schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table or view is part of a different schema, then the name of this schema is indicated in brackets after the name of the table or view. This means that a table or view can have the SAME name as another table or view as long as it belongs to a different schema. Tip: Double-click on the name of a table or view to collapse it. As you select the fields, the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. Tip: Click the Preview button to display the fields that will be returned by this query, in the pane at the bottom of the configuration dialog. WARNING! If no fields / tables /views are selected, the query cannot be created and the Preview button will display, the following Error: " Syntax error in query. Incomplete query clause.

" Ensure that you select BOTH the fields that you wish the query to display and those that are required to refine this data (such as those you want to use to create relationships between and define constraints for).

Title: Select queries
" Ensure that you select BOTH the fields that you wish the query to display and those that are required to refine this data (such as those you want to use to create relationships between and define constraints for). Note: This is the only dialog that must be completed, within the query configuration dialog, so you can click the Finish button at this point. - Click Next , once the required fields are selected. - If necessary, add or remove relationships between the selected tables or views in the Relationship Setup dialog. Typically, you create relationships between tables in order to perform lookups on fields between different tables such as between the foreign key of one table and the primary key of a related table. Adding or removing relationships: In this case a relationship is simply a pair of selected fields, usually in different tables or views, whose values are required to be identical in order for a record to be returned. To add a relationship: - Click the Add Relationship button to create a relationship between two of the selected fields, as follows: - Click the drop-down list box button at the right of each Field list and select the required field from both tables or views. This list only displays the fields selected in the previous dialog, in the following syntax: [Tablename].[Fieldname] or [Viewname].[Fieldname]. Note: If necessary, you can edit the selected table, view and/or field names yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. To delete the last relationship: Click the Delete Relationship button to remove the last relationship from the Relationships list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the relationship at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. Note: Ensure that all the relationships are fully defined, otherwise the query will also not work i.e. delete any partially configured relationships. Tip: Press the Preview button to test your defined relationships, since an exception will be displayed if any of the data types of the related fields are NOT identical. As you define relationship(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. Note: These do not affect the relationships that you may have already created within your database. - Click Next , once the required relationships have been defined.

- If necessary, add or remove constraints for the values of one or more of the selected fields in the Constraints dialog.

Title: Select queries
- If necessary, add or remove constraints for the values of one or more of the selected fields in the Constraints dialog. Typically, you constrain values of one or more fields to prevent this table from being needlessly updated. If these constraints will change from user to user then use parameters instead of hard-coded values. Adding or removing constraints for the fields of this table: To add a constraint: - Press the Add Constraint button. - If this constraint is NOT the first, specify how to relate this constraint to the previous constraints, as follows: - AND: This is the default option, which makes this constraint mandatory. For instance, if there are two constraints with an AND between them, then the data will be restricted by BOTH constraints. - OR: Use this option, to make the specified constraint optional. For instance, if there are two constraints with an OR between them then the data can be restricted with EITHER of these constraints. - Select the field, whose values you want to limit, from the Field drop-down list box, in the following syntax: [Fieldname]. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: If necessary, you can edit the selected field name yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. - Select the method by which the values of this field are to be constrained or limited from the Constraint drop-down list box. For details, see Available constraint operators . - Specify the constraining value or parameter in the Value field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this criterion, for instance, if different users require different values. For details, see Adding parameters . Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work. To delete the last constraint: - Click the Delete Constraint button to remove the last constraint from the Constraints list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the constraint at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. Note: Ensure that all the constraints are fully defined, otherwise the query will also not work i.e. delete any partially configured constraints. As you define the constraint(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. WARNING!

If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages.

Title: Select queries
If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages. Once you click the Next button the query configuration dialog ends and any further modifications to the query can only to be performed manually. - Click Next , once the required constraints have been defined. - If necessary, define the sorting order of the resultant records in the Ordering dialog. Typically, you sort a query to ensure that the records are displayed in order of importance or relevance. Although more than one field can be used to sort the data, the closer the field is to the top of the list, the greater the impact it has upon the sorting process. Typically multiple fields are used to sort queries, when their entries are related – for instance can be used when sorting by surnames and then sorting by their first names. It may also be useful to sort by identity (ID) fields or by Country, when viewing a list of orders etc. Adding or removing sorting orders: To add a sorting order: - Press the Add Order button. - Select the field, whose values you want to sort, from the Field drop-down list box. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: If the View is selected the syntax for the fields is [Tablename].[Fieldname] or [Viewname].[Fieldname]. - Select the method by which the values of this field are to be sorted from the Constraint drop-down list box, as follows: - ASC: The default value, which sorts the values of the specified field in ascending order. The method used to sort the values, depends on the data type of the specified field, as follows: - String: This displays records beginning with non-text characters such as ‘_’ or ‘!”, then records from 0 to 9, then records from A to Z, with lowercase letters preceding uppercase letters e.g. for text like fgfd and Fgfd, the ASC order is fgfd and then Fgfd. - Numeric: This displays records from 0 to 9. - Date Time: This will display the records in this field from newest to oldest. - DESC: This sorts the values of the specified field in descending order, which is the reverse of the ASC order. To delete a sorting order: - Specify the required View or the name of the Table in the Select View/Table list box.

- Click the Delete Sort Order button to remove the last sort order from the Sort Orders list.

Title: Select queries
- Click the Delete Sort Order button to remove the last sort order from the Sort Orders list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the sort order at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. As you define the sort order(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. - Click Next , once the required sort orders have been set up, to end the query configuration dialog. The Custom Query dialog is displayed, which allows you to manually configure this query, if necessary. - If necessary, type or modify the existing SQL querying commands in the SQL Query editor, which highlights keywords and makes it easier to customise your queries. Note: The Preview button is as easy way to debug your query as you manually edit it. Clicking this button will return all the fields, in the pane at the bottom of the configuration dialog, that the current query would return. In this way you can ensure that your query does return what you want it to. - Click Finish , once you are satisfied with this query. This adds this query with its specified name beneath the Select Queries subfolder of the Queries folder of the applicable OLE DB datasource, in the Enterprise Manager . If using SQL, please ensure that all time based queries adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd, as follows: - Either, set the short date format in Regional Settings to be yyyy-mm-dd, once for all. - Or convert ALL the date parameters for each query into this SQL standard format first, by using a string converter, such as the String Format spider. To perform a Select query using a Query spider: this procedure describes how to perform a Select query by clicking a Button control, so its results can be displayed on a graphic form within a DataGrid control. This assumes that the Select query has been added and configured. Prepare the graphic form: - Open a new graphic form in the Design workspace . (If necessary, add a project and a graphic form first). - Add a Button control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to trigger the Query spider so that it will perform the query.

- Add a DataGrid control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to display the records returned by the Select query.

Title: Select queries
- Add a DataGrid control to this graphic form from the Toolbox - this will be used to display the records returned by the Select query. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the DataGrid control in the graphic form. Add and configure the Query spider to run this query: - Open the Spider Configuration tool window. - Right-click the spider workspace itself and select the Create New Spider menu. - Click the Databasing sub-menu and its Query item to add a Query spider. - Double click the title bar of this spider to open its configuration view. - Select the required query from the Inputs section of this spider, as follows: - Click the Server containing the required OLE DB datasource from the Server list box. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, when referring to the Server that you use to log in, instead of its actual name as this makes it easier to transfer this spider to another Client. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required OLE DB datasource from this list of available OLE DB datasources on this Server. The first OLE DB datasource created on this Server is selected by default. - Click the required type in the Query Type list. The Select Query category is selected by default. - From the Query Name list box, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the required query. Note: It is important to name your queries clearly, so that it is easy to select the correct one. - If this selected query contains parameters , then the names of these parameters will be added as additional inputs to the Inputs section. Note1: The value of each parameter input can either be provided by a property or data element via a silk a line with an arrow at its end, which links the output of one spider to the input of another. or can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note2: If using SQL, please ensure that all the date parameters for this query adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd.

Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the parameter name in the Inputs section and type in the required value.

Title: Select queries
Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the parameter name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. - It is recommended to use the Confirm Action checkbox to display a confirmation dialog before this query inserts a record into your database. This spider performs this query to insert a record, when it is triggered. WARNING! Please ensure that you have provided values for ANY parameters used by this query BEFORE triggering this spider otherwise an error will be displayed. Note: You will notice in the Event Trigger section of this spider that this Query spider is triggered by clicking the Button control. Connect the Query spider to the DataGrid control: - If necessary, open the property tree by using the pane display bar on the right border of the central spider workspace pane. - In the Outputs section, drag the Return Object output onto the Data category beneath this DataGrid control in the property tree and when this category expands, drop it onto the DataSource property. Note: Ensure that the Success output is True (i.e. the query ran successfully), if this is False then there is either a problem with the query syntax or another problem preventing this query from running. Tip: The Rows Exist output is only True when the query returns data and is False if an empty dataset is returned. Additional filtering and massaging of the displayed data: - This launches the Filter DataSet configuration dialog, whose first dialog can be used to select which of the selected tables and their fields you want to display. By default all of the tables and fields are selected. Note: If this configuration dialog does not launch automatically, double-click the DataSource property in the property tree and right-click this spider's title bar and select Filter DataSet from this menu. - If necessary, click Next to display the Filter dialog, which typically should not be required since the Select query allowed you to define your own constraints. Therefore, click Next to an display the Sort By dialog, in which you click the column heading that you want to sort the columns by in ascending or descending order and then click Finish . Test that the query is correctly displayed: - Click the Preview toolbar button of this graphic form.

- Click the Button control and see if the DataGrid control correctly displays the results of this query.

Selecting colors Selecting colors A color edit box is used to configure a color, which displays the currently selected color in a color box on the left and on the right of the definition of this color.

Title: Selecting colors Selecting colors A color edit box is used to configure a color, which displays the currently selected color in a color box on the left and on the right of the definition of this color. This color definition is either a color name or a custom color represented by at least three comma-separated numbers from 0 to 255, which indicate the proportions of the red, green and blue primary colors respectively. Note
Selecting colors Selecting colors A color edit box is used to configure a color, which displays the currently selected color in a color box on the left and on the right of the definition of this color. This color definition is either a color name or a custom color represented by at least three comma-separated numbers from 0 to 255, which indicate the proportions of the red, green and blue primary colors respectively. Note: If the color edit box currently displays a known color name, then double-clicking on it will display the next known color name in alphabetical order. To select a color from a location on the screen: this allows you to directly obtain the color from any location on the screen. - Right click the list box to the right of the required color edit box (square). - Hold down the right mouse button, so that the cursor changes to . - Drag the mouse to the required location on the screen that has the color that you want - Release the right mouse button to select this color. To select a color using the color edit box: this allows you to select a pre-defined color from the color-selection dialog. - Click on the required color edit box. This will display a drop-down list button at the far right of this edit box. - Click on this drop-down list button, to display the color-selection dialog. - Click the required tab and select the required color. - The color-selection dialog consists of the following three tabs: - System: This displays the colors specified by the Advanced Appearance settings of your system. To change your Advanced Appearance color settings: - Open the Desktop. - Right-click and select Properties - The Display Properties dialog is displayed. - Click the Appearance tab. - Click the Advanced button. The Advanced Appearance dialog is displayed. - Either click in the sample window or use the Item list box to select elements and change their colors. Note: If you change your Advanced Appearance settings, the colors displayed in this System tab will change accordingly. - Web: This displays colors commonly used when designing web applications. - Custom: This displays the custom palette, which contains 48 basic predefined colors. This also allows you to define and use up to 16 additional custom colors and/or specify the required transparency of this color, if this is supported. If necessary, define your own Custom color: - Click on the required color edit box. This will display a drop-down list button at the far right of this edit box. - Click on this drop-down list button, to display the color-selection dialog. - Click the Custom tab. - Right-click on one of the custom color cells in the lowest two rows of the palette to display the Define Color dialog. - Specify the hue, saturation and luminescence of the custom color– either by moving the mouse pointer across the color palette and clicking at the required position, or by typing in the required values, from 0 to 255, in the Hue , Sat and Lum edit boxes respectively. - Specify the relative proportions of the red, green and blue primary colors for the custom color – either by dragging the indicator up and down the scale on the right or by typing in the required values, also from 0 to 255, in the Red , Green , and Blue edit boxes respectively. Note: The Color|Solid color box, displays the customized color. - Click the Add Color button when finished. Some Custom colors also support an optional fourth parameter that specifies the required transparency of this color. The transparency determines how much of the background is visible “through” the specified color e.g. for the BackColor property for a button. To add transparency to a custom color: - Click on the color edit box that contains a custom color that is defined by comma-separated numbers from 0 to 255. - Type in the required transparency, as a number from 0 to 255, before the first of the three other numbers, which is also separated by a comma e.g. 0, 23, 255, 128. Note1: A transparency value of 255 is not transparent at all and a transparency of 0 will be completely transparent so that only the background and not the specified color will be visible. Note2: Only the color edit boxes of certain properties accept this parameter e.g. the BackColor property of buttons. -->

text:
Selecting General SNMP Objects Selecting General SNMP Objects The General tab of this SNMP Objects Browser contains a collection of commonly used statistics for device management.

Title: Selecting General SNMP Objects
Selecting General SNMP Objects Selecting General SNMP Objects The General tab of this SNMP Objects Browser contains a collection of commonly used statistics for device management. Note: You CANNOT write to the items you select from this General tab. To select an item from the General tab: - Ensure that the General tab of the SNMP Objects Browser dialog is selected. - Check the checkbox next to the required item. This immediately adds this item to the OID list of this SNMPManager agent, which is differentiated from browsed objects (those selected from the Browse tab), as follows: - their OID field is simply "General Object", - their Name field is prefaced by [G#], where # typically specifies the order of this object in this General tab. The statistics provided by this tab are divided into the following two groups: - General objects for computers only: SNMP managed objects that are computer-specific and can only be used when monitoring computers. In this case a number of specific usage requirements need to be met first. For details, see Usage Requirements . The statistics provided by this group is further classified into the following sub-groups: - Incoming network traffic: these statistics are generally used to determine the status of the network received by the specified computer. Note: These calculated statistics ONLY use the SNMP objects that refer to the FIRST network card on the monitored computer, so if there are more than one network cards these statistics will not present the full picture. - Bandwidth (kbit per second): This statistic measures the currently utilised networking bandwidth that is being received by the computer, in kilobits per second. Note: If the monitored computer has more than one network card, it may be necessary to perform this bandwidth calculation manually for the other network cards. For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation . - Unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of packets received by the computer per second, which are ONLY intended for this computer. Note: Unicast packets are packets that ONLY have a SINGLE device as their destination - Non-unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of broadcast packets received by the computer per second. Note: Non-unicast packets are broadcast packets meant for all devices or a group of devices on a network. - Errors per minute: This statistic measures the number of packet errors received by the computer per minute. - Outgoing network traffic: these statistics are generally used to determine the status of the network away from the specified computer. Note: These calculated statistics ONLY use the SNMP objects that refer to the FIRST network card on the monitored computer, so if there are more than one network cards these statistics will not present the full picture. - Bandwidth (kbit per second): This statistic measures the currently utilised networking bandwidth, which is being sent out of the computer, in kilobits per second. Note: If the monitored computer has more than one network card, it may be necessary to perform this bandwidth calculation manually for the other network cards. For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation . - Unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of unicast packets sent out of the computer per second. Note: Unicast packets are packets that ONLY have a SINGLE device as their destination. - Non-unicast packets per second: This statistic measures the number of broadcast packets sent out of the computer per second. Note: Non-unicast packets are broadcast packets meant for all devices or a group of devices on a network. - Errors per minute: This statistic measures the number of packet errors sent out of the computer per minute.

- System information: these are generally applicable computer management statistics.

Title: Selecting General SNMP Objects
- System information: these are generally applicable computer management statistics. - System available memory: This statistic measures the available RAM, on the computer being monitored, in Megabytes. For instance, this can determine whether this computer is under-performing or in other words is currently over-utilising its resources or not. - Available hard drive space (C:\): This statistic measures the available hard drive space on the <C:\> drive, on the computer being monitored, in Megabytes. Since the majority of Adroit -related information is stored on the <C:\> drive, this statistic can be used to determine when a computer is running out of storage space. - Adroit processes: these are commonly used Adroit applications that may be running on the specified computer. - Agent Server (as.exe): This Boolean value can be used to determine the current status of the Agent Server process on the device being monitored. For instance, when used to monitor a computer that is designated to run the Agent Server, this value can be used to trigger an alarm when the Agent Server is shut down. - Classic User Interface (adroit.exe): This Boolean value can be used to determine the current status of the Classic User Interface process on the device being monitored. For instance, when used to monitor a computer that is designated to run the Classic User Interface, this value could also trigger an alarm when this is shut down. - General objects for most devices: SNMP managed objects that are generally provided by all devices. - Host name: This statistic displays the textual (network) name of the device being monitored. - Host description: This statistic displays the textual system description of the device being monitored, which includes the processor type and operating system employed on this device. - System uptime: This statistic measures the time (in hundredths of a second) since the network management portion of the device was last re-initialized, in other words, since its SNMP service has been restarted. While some of these items are individual OIDs, others are calculations using the values of one or more OIDs. It is also possible to perform these calculations yourself within Adroit . For details, see Manual Network Bandwidth Calculation . -->
