Title: Selecting graphic elements
Selecting graphic elements Top Selecting graphic elements You typically need to select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. more than one graphic element a form component that typically provides drawing functionality for the graphic form. See form component. to arrange or bulk-edit them. Click for more details: Graphic elements are shape-aware, in other words, they can only be selected by clicking within the borders of their shape. Also if a graphic element has a hole in it (rectangles and ellipses can have holes using the Innersize property), clicking inside this hole will not select it either. When you select or highlight a group of graphic elements one of them, usually the first graphic element that is selected is the primary graphic element . This primary graphic element will be shaded, while the other graphic elements will appear as normal. Tip: Once a group of graphic elements is selected, click on the graphic element that you want to be the primary graphic element and the color of its sizing handles will change accordingly. When applying formatting options to this selected group of graphic elements, this primary graphic element will be the one from which all of the other graphic elements obtain sizing and formatting options. Note: In order to de-select the currently selected graphic elements, click outside of the group. To individually select multiple graphic elements: - Open the graphic form, which contains the required graphic elements. For details, see Opening graphic forms . - Hold down either the CTRL key or the SHIFT key and click on the required graphic elements. Tip: The first graphic element, that is clicked, will become the primary graphic element when a group of graphic elements are selected, this is the first graphic element that is selected and its attributes will be used if this group of graphic elements are formatted. See graphic element. . To bulk select multiple graphic elements: - Open the graphic form, which contains the required graphic elements. For details, see Opening graphic forms . - Hold down the SHIFT key. - Click where you want the upper-left corner of the intended group of graphic elements to be located, and drag to where you want the lower-right corner of the group of graphic elements to be located. A grey rectangle will indicate the currently selected area. All the graphic elements within this selected region, will be selected and grouped. Any controls within this region are also selected, but are not added to this graphic element group and therefore have their own primary control when a group of controls are selected, the sizing handles of this control are white and its attributes will be used if this group of controls are formatted. See control. . - If necessary, click the graphic element, which you need to be the primary graphic element. -->

Title: Selecting SNMP Objects
Selecting SNMP Objects Selecting SNMP Objects The SNMPManager agent is able to get and/or set SNMP managed objects (each of which is an OID) from a single device on the network. The SNMP Objects Browser can specify the required OIDs. Click for more details: Note1: You need to connect to the device to use this SNMP Objects Browser . Note2: You need to Enable polling before you can use this SNMP Objects Browser . Note3: If you cannot connect to the device then you can add OIDs manually. For details, see Adding OIDs Manually . Note4: Not all devices allow you to browse their OIDs. Launch the SNMP Objects Browser: click the Browse OID to add button in the Edit SNMP Manager Agent dialog. Note: A message box is displayed if the agent cannot connect to the device, indicating that the connection is invalid. The SNMP Objects Browser contains 2 tabs, each of which provide a different view of the values contained within this device, as follows: - General: This tab provides a collection of commonly used statistics for device management. Although some of these items are individual OIDs, others are calculations using the values of one or more OIDs. For more details, see Selecting General SNMP Objects . Note: You CANNOT write to items you select from the General tab. - Browser: This tab can browse for device-specific OIDs from the device's MIB hierarchy. For more details, see Selecting Browsed SNMP Objects . Note: You can read/write to OID values that you select from the Browser tab. -->

- Expand the branches in the tree to expose the required OID.

Title: To select an OID from the OID tree:
- Expand the branches in the tree to expose the required OID. Tip: Double-clicking a branch will expand its sub-branches, if any. - Click on the required object to display its details, in the Selected OID details pane, which provides the following information: - Object-identifier (OID): This specifies the name of the selected OID in numeric format. For further details, see OID Naming Formats . - Name: Typically this should correspond to the literal name of the OID, however due to the latest standard in displaying OIDs, this may only be a partial description of the international MIB database tree. - Return type: The type of data that is returned by the value of this SNMP object. If you intend writing to this value, please ensure that this return type CAN be written to. For details, see: SNMP Object Value Return Types . - Description: This is identical to the Name field, except that its text is wrapped, so that the full textual description of this object can be viewed. - Value: This obtains the value of this SNMP object within the specified SNMP device. Tip: Use the information displayed in these fields to determine if the selected OID is correct. - Click the Add to List button to add the highlighted OID to the selected OID list of this SNMPMgr agent. Tip: Double-clicking an SNMP object immediately adds it to the selected OID lists. -->

Selecting the default graphic form of the TemplateGOContextNav control Top Selecting the default graphic form of the TemplateGOContextNav control You can use the following methods to choose which graphic form the TemplateGOContextNav control displays by default: - Either use the Browse for a Default Graphic Form to load...

Title: Selecting the default graphic form of the TemplateGOContextNav control
Selecting the default graphic form of the TemplateGOContextNav control Top Selecting the default graphic form of the TemplateGOContextNav control You can use the following methods to choose which graphic form the TemplateGOContextNav control displays by default: - Either use the Browse for a Default Graphic Form to load... task: this task is provided by the Task menu, which is displayed when the control is initially added and can be accessed by clicking its glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the selected control. Using the Browse for a Default Graphic Form to load... task: - If necessary, add the TemplateGOContextNav control to the required graphic form, which is located in the Templates category of the Toolbox tool window. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this control. - If necessary, click the glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of this control, to display the menu of tasks - Click the Browse for a Default Graphic Form to load... hyperlink to display the Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog. This contains an explorer view of all of the projects and their graphic forms configured within the Projects category of each Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . - Select the required graphic form within this explorer view. Tip: It is also possible to select the required graphic form by double-clicking on it. - Only check the Include Server Name in selection checkbox if you SPECIFICALLY want this control to ONLY connect to this specific Server, otherwise if unchecked the control will look for this graphic form on the currently specified default (logon) Server. - Check the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox option, if you want to ensure that the specified graphic form will still be located when the project name is renamed or when this graphic form is copied to another project, while preserving its relative path. - Click Finish . The fully qualified namespace of the currently selected graphic form is displayed in the field at the bottom of the explorer view, which adheres to the following format: ProjectName.{Folder(s)Name(s)}.GraphicFormName, where {..} indicates that the Folder(s)Name(s) are optional and depend upon the organization of this project. Note: If the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox is checked then this does NOT provide the ProjectName portion. If the Include Server Name in selection checkbox is checked then this also includes the following at the beginning: [MachineName] ServerName. - The specified graphic form should be displayed within the control. Note: This control can be configured to automatically resize to contain this graphic form, by enabling its AutoResize property. - Or use the GraphicFormPath property of this control to browse for the required graphic form. Using the GraphicFormPath property: - If necessary, add the TemplateGOContextNav control to the required graphic form, which is located in the Templates category of the Toolbox tool window. - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this control. - Open the Properties tool window, navigate to the GraphicFormPath property and select it. - Click on the browse button to the right of its value cell. The Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog is displayed, which contains an explorer view of all of the projects and their graphic forms configured within the Projects category of each Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . - Select the required graphic form within this explorer view. Tip: It is also possible to select the required graphic form by double-clicking on it.

Sending SMS Messages Top Sending SMS Messages SMS messages will only be sent to the specified phone number of the recipient of this Command agent via the specified GSM_SMS device.

Title: Sending SMS Messages
Sending SMS Messages Top Sending SMS Messages SMS messages will only be sent to the specified phone number of the recipient of this Command agent via the specified GSM_SMS device. For details, see Specifying the Recipient Phone Number and Specifying the GSM_SMS Device . Note: If necessary, sent SMS messages can also be sent via another Command agent to another recipient, if they are not received and/or responded to within a specified period. For details, see Monitoring Message Receipt and Monitoring Message Response . SMS messages can be sent by means of the following methods: Note1: If the Require recipient response option is enabled, all sent messages will be prefixed by an asterisk "*" to indicate to the recipient that he/she needs to return the message to the Command agent. For details, see Monitoring Message Response . Note2: When the Resend message checkbox is cleared (its default setting) a message will ONLY be sent if the rawvalue of this agent HAS changed when dialog is either updated or closed. This effectively prevents the resending of identical messages. - Manually: By typing the required message in the Raw value edit box provided at the bottom of the Edit Command agent dialog. For details on displaying this dialog, see Editing Agents . Tip1: It is also possible to expose the required message processing and/or sending slot and send messages to it directly by using a mimic, for instance, by associating a Data Entry Operator Action Behaviour to it. For details on these slots, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . Tip2: In addition to simple text it is also possible to place commands into these slots so that they can be performed before the message is sent. Server clustering Top SmartUI Server clustering How to cluster SmartUI Servers SmartUI Servers can be clustered to provide both load balancing and redundancy.

Title: SmartUI Server clustering
Steps:
Server clustering Top SmartUI Server clustering How to cluster SmartUI Servers SmartUI Servers can be clustered to provide both load balancing and redundancy. Any number of SmartUI Servers can belong to the same cluster, in which case, they are known as cluster partners. Essentially, all cluster partners ( SmartUI Servers within a cluster), act as if they were a single Server, which means that certain characteristics of ALL the cluster partners in a cluster must be IDENTICALLY configured, as follows: - Server name: this also becomes the name of the cluster to which these cluster partners belong, for instance, all the SmartUI Servers whose Server Name is "MyCluster", belong to the "MyCluster" group of cluster partners. For details on configuring this setting, see General SmartUI Server settings . - Server configuration: this configuration encompasses the profiles, security, projects and all datasources that have been configured. For details on configuring the locations for these items, see SmartUI Server directory settings . Tip: It is recommended that you specify a shared network folder on RAID (failsafe disk) in which you provide the license and configuration files for all the cluster partners to refer to. Alternatively, these locations can be identically configured on each cluster partner, so that the required configuration is performed on one cluster partner and then copied to the other cluster partners. - System time: cluster partners need to be time synchronised, so that the same timestamp will be set regardless of which cluster partner performs the operation. Tip: Use time synchronizing software to do this, such as the NET TIME command, provided by the Windows operating system, which sets the time of the local computer to that of a specified remote computer. Example of use: The following example will set the time of the local computer to that of Computer1 (providing that it is in the same domain): NET TIME \\Computer1 /SET /Y The /Y option allows this command to be performed automatically without needing to be confirmed first, so that this command can then be added to a command (.CMD) file that could be run on startup or as often as needed. - Microsoft Windows security configuration: this means that any user who logs in to a specific clustered SmartUI Server, must be able to log in to all the other cluster partners, using the same user name and password. - Network location of users and groups: this means that all the cluster partners must be either be physically located in the same network domain or else must be members of a Workgroup that has the same security configuration on each of the cluster partners. This allows the same users and groups to secure these SmartUI Servers. For details of configuring this settings, see Server security settings . IMPORTANT: For clustering to work correctly, only one Server can run on a specific machine at any point in time. Currently cluster partners ONLY share the workload (load) generated by their SmartUI Operator clients that are cluster-aware, in which case they handle their combined load evenly and to provide continued operation in the event that one or more fail. Each SmartUI Server uses UDP broadcasts to inform each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. of its availability and/or load. The load of each SmartUI Server is determined by the number of SmartUI Clients that are currently connected to it.

This broadcast system can be disabled and both the range of UDP ports used for this broadcast and the frequency of broadcasts can be configured, as follows: - The BroadcastEnabled SmartUI Server setting enables (the default setting) or disables these UDP broadcasts.

Title: SmartUI Server clustering
Steps:
This broadcast system can be disabled and both the range of UDP ports used for this broadcast and the frequency of broadcasts can be configured, as follows: - The BroadcastEnabled SmartUI Server setting enables (the default setting) or disables these UDP broadcasts. - The BroadcastTimePeriod SmartUI Server setting specifies the time, in milliseconds, between broadcasts, which is 2 seconds (2000 milliseconds) by default. Although decreasing this setting reduces the network traffic it also prevents the SmartUI Operators from quickly responding to changes in Server load and/or availability. - The BroadcastPortRange SmartUI Server setting specifies the UDP port range which the Server uses for its broadcasts, by default this is 11000-11010. IMPORTANT: If you CHANGE this setting for a SmartUI Server then you need to change the BroadcastPortRange setting of each SmartUI Client that you want to receive these broadcasts from this Server. Each cluster aware SmartUI Operator maintains a list of SmartUI Servers for ALL the clusters that it connects to. The list is periodically updated by the SmartUI Operator, which obtains the availability and load of these Servers from their broadcasts. Cluster aware SmartUI Operators automatically switch over to the SmartUI Server with the lightest load. Upon login, if the default SmartUI Server (cluster partner) is NOT available then a cluster aware Operator will search for an available cluster partner. For details on how to make an SmartUI Operator aware of one or more clusters, see Making SmartUI Operators cluster-aware . -->

Server directory settings Top Server directory settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings to store the various SmartUI Server constituents or search for items: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor .

Title: Server directory settings
Steps:
Server directory settings Top Server directory settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings to store the various SmartUI Server constituents or search for items: To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Server option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Server may not be installed. - Select the Directory Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Note: Each Configuration is completely separate or insular, containing its own files, application settings and/or registry keys. For details, see Working with Configurations . Datasources location: specify where to reference the SmartUI Server datasources. These datasource plugins essentially determine which datasources can be created and/or used by each Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. of the SmartUI Server. For further details, see Working with datasources . To specify the location of the datasource plugins: Either type in the required path directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for and/or create the required folder. Note: If the specified location does not exist, the default setting will be used instead, which is the installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI ). Tip1: Change this default setting when clustering Servers so a single shared network folder can be specified for their combined use, to ensure that they all have access to the same datasource plugins. Tip2: Use the browse button to ensure that the specified location exists and that it is not incorrectly specified. WARNING! If the specified folder does not exist then the SmartUI Server will not load! Profiles storage location: specify where to store the user profiles of this SmartUI Server. These roaming user profiles allow users to retain their same user settings within the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications, regardless of the computer that they use. To specify where the profiles should be saved: Either type in the required path directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for and/or create the required folder. Note: If the specified location does not exist, the default setting will be used instead, which is the Data subfolder of the Default configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Data). Tip: Use the browse button to ensure that the specified location exists and that it is not incorrectly specified. Projects storage location: . specify where to store the projects that are created by the users of this SmartUI Server. Projects are essentially collections of graphic forms, which are created by the SmartUI Designer and viewed by the SmartUI Operator, to allow end users to display and manipulate data.

To specify where the projects should be saved: Either type in the required path directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for and/or create the required folder.

Title: Server directory settings
Steps:
To specify where the projects should be saved: Either type in the required path directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for and/or create the required folder. Note: If the specified location does not exist, the default setting will be used instead, which is the Projects subfolder of the Default configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Projects). Tip: It is recommended to use the browse button to ensure that the specified location exists and that it is not incorrectly specified. Server Scripts storage location: specify where to store the scripts of the Server Scripts datasource. The Server Scripts datasource provides a repository for scripts. For details concerning this datasource and the benefits of adding scripts to it, see Server Scripts datasources . To specify where the Server scripts are saved: Either type in the required path directly in the edit box or use the browse button to browse for and/or create the required folder. Note: If the specified location does not exist, the default setting will be used instead, which is the Data subfolder of the Default configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Data). Tip: Use the browse button to ensure that the specified location exists and that it is not incorrectly specified. The SmartUI Server ALWAYS saves its other data, such as: the security configuration; the external datasources that are connected to it and any data that these external datasources need to save, such as the queries created for an OLE DB datasource to the Data subfolder of the Default configuration folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Configurations\Default \Data). Saving or storage location recommendations: - keep all the Server data storage locations: for the profiles, projects, Server scripts and miscellaneous Server data in the same location for easier management (backup or replication). - storing these in a subfolder of the installation folder makes it easier to locate the necessary information. - storing in a shared network folder is useful when Servers are clustered, so that ALL the Servers in a cluster can use the same data folder and files. For details of the benefits of clustering Servers, see Server clustering . Search paths for script references: specify additional paths that contain the assemblies (.DLL files) that you frequently reference in your scripts. WARNING! ONLY specify the locations of the assemblies (.DLL files) that you frequently use, since an extensive list will hamper the loading and compilation times of all scripts. To add a path that is to be searched: Click the Add button and browse for the required folder. To remove a path from the list: Select the path that is no longer required and press the Remove button, which is immediately removed. Note1: The installation folder and its subfolders are searched by default and so do NOT need to be added to this list. Note2: It is NOT recommended that these locations exist on different computers due to many hindrances, such as security problems and time delays. This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Server settings. For details, see Setting up the Server . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Server settings, see the Advanced Server settings page . -->

Server saving and backup settings Top Server saving and backup settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that manage both the saving and backup of the SmartUI Server data: Tip: The Adroit Config Editor provides a System Backup and Restore feature that can backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration.

Title: Server saving and backup settings
Steps:
Server saving and backup settings Top Server saving and backup settings This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that manage both the saving and backup of the SmartUI Server data: Tip: The Adroit Config Editor provides a System Backup and Restore feature that can backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration. For details, see System Backup and Restore . To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Server option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Server may not be installed. - Select the Backup Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. Saving frequency: specify how often the Server saves its data. For further details relating to the saving Server data, see Saving the SmartUI Server . To specify the required interval between saves, in seconds: Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. The recommended setting depends on the lifecycle stage of the project, as follows: - frequently during the designing phase, such as every 2 hours or less, since changes are being made frequently. - reduce this frequency during the implementation phase, such as to once a day, since the number of changes decrease. Backing up the Server data: the SmartUI Server can backup its saved data, which includes the profiles, projects and other data - to guard against the possible corruption of this data, accidental deletion and other eventualities. For details, see Backing up SmartUI Server data . To configure the backing up of the Server data: Either select Yes to enable or No to disable this setting.. Normally backing up Server data will not affect the performance of the Server, since this operation only briefly affects the CPU usage and the backup does not consume a large amount of the hard drive space. However the larger the data files become, the more carefully one should configure the frequency of these backups. Backup storage duration: specify how long to store the backed up data, before it is deleted. To specify the number of days before backup files are deleted: : Either type in the required value directly or use the arrows of this spin control to obtain the required value. The recommended setting depends on the lifecycle stage of the project, as follows: - not be more than one or two days during the designing phase as the number of backups during this period can become quite sizable. - during the implementation phase as the changes decrease, this backup period should be increased, such as to once a week. This page only configures the part of the essential SmartUI Server settings. For details, see Setting up the Server . For details on displaying all the related SmartUI Server settings, see the Advanced Server settings page . -->

Title: Server Scripts datasources
Server Scripts datasources Top Server Scripts datasources The Server Scripts datasource provides a repository for scripts that can either be run on the SmartUI Server a "data portal" which exposes data from a number of disparate sources. or the Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. . Click for advanced Server Scripts datasource usage information: This datasource essentially manages one or more script object this contains a script and provides its self-contained environment within which it is run. , each of which contain a script that is run on the Server. For further details on scripts, see Working with scripts . These script objects can be added and edited from this Server Scripts datasource. For details, see Adding script objects or Editing script objects . If necessary, you can schedule the script objects to run at specific times, see Scheduling script objects . For details on specifying where these scripts are saved, see Server directory settings . Note: Access to both the Server Scripts datasource and its script objects can be controlled, if necessary. For details, see Securing datasources . This datasource is added within the Datasources category of the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Script datasources . A Server Scripts datasource is identified in the Enterprise Manager by its specified name and its icon . When this datasource is opened any script object added to it are displayed immediately below it. Advantages of adding a script object to a Server Scripts datasource: - Due to the self-contained nature of script objects, it is possible to create and store script objects, which will interact with either the Server or the Client or both of them, if necessary. Note: Scripts are able to interact with the Client and/or the Server through the use of INeed interfaces. For details, see Working with INeed Interfaces . In addition to this functionality, you are also able to provide additional functionality, by referencing external assemblies (.DLL files). For details, see Managing references . - Each script object is able to be used within a Script Engine spider. For details, see Script Engine spiders . Note: Scripts which are used within Script Engine spiders are run from the Client and not the Server. - Each script object is immediately accessible by all the Clients connected to its SmartUI Server. - Each script object becomes a data element and can therefore be secured, if necessary. Unlike a script object created within a Script Engine spider, which cannot be secured directly and instead relies upon the security applied to the graphic form with which this spider is associated. Note1: Running a script object from the Server or a Client, should not affect its speed of execution. Typically, the script execution speed is dependent on the script source, the utilization of external references and correct programming techniques and other system-dependent factors such as CPU load etc. Note2: When running a script object of the Server Scripts datasource, within the Script Editor, the script will be executed slower than if it was run normally. For details, see Working with the script editor . Note3: Scripts which are not used within Script Engine spiders can either be executed manually Running script objects or by using the ExecuteScriptObject special function provided by the Script datasources. -->

Server security settings Top Server security settings The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security.

Title: Server security settings
Server security settings Top Server security settings The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security. This uses a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups that are "allowed" on each SmartUI Server computer and are hence known as the Allowed users and groups. For details, see Working with security . This page of the Setting up the Server component of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog, provides the following settings that configure which Windows users and groups are given default access to the SmartUI Server and the services it provides: Click for more information: WARNING! Careful consideration should be given to which users and groups are specified. For further details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . Note: When the Server is deployed on a domain with a large number of users and/or groups, this page will take a long time to be displayed while the user and group lists are populated. For details on reducing or eliminating this delay, see Specifying user and group subsets . To display this page of settings: - Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The Welcome section is displayed by default, unless multiple configurations have been created, in which case the Configuration page is displayed by default, which needs to be expanded to display the Welcome section. For details, see Working with Configurations . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the Setting up the Server option. Note: If this option does not appear then the SmartUI Server may not be installed. - Select the Security Settings option. Tip1: You can navigate directly to this page using the left pane of the Adroit Config Editor configuration dialog. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . Tip2: Press the Next or Previous buttons to display the other pages of settings. To enable 21 CFR 11 mode: When engineering and commissioning a system, the system is not required to comply with 21 CFR 11, it is only once the system is deployed that 21 CFR 11 compliance is required. Therefore, you should ideally engineer your project, with 21 CFR 11 mode disabled, due to the design-restrictions that it imposes and then just before you start commissioning the project you can enable and configure the 21 CFR 11 mode. For more details of the controls and requirements required by 21 CFR 11, see 21 CFR 11 controls and requirements . Select the Yes option for the Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance option at the top of this page and provide the required password. This password secures the connection to the Adroit Agent Server and also prevents the unauthorised disabling of this 21 CFR 11 setting itself. IMPORTANT: If you forget your password then you MUST DELETE ALL your config files and project files and start again from scratch. Note: When running an Adroit Agent Server and a SmartUI Server on two separate computers, BOTH computers must be configured for 21 CFR 11 mode using the SAME password. This password is encrypted and stored in the configuration (.config) files on the SmartUI Server computer. Since 21 CFR 11 requires that system access be limited to authorised individuals, access to these configuration files need to be limited through the use of directory and file level security. Note: You can only change or disable this setting by providing the specified password.

Title: Server security settings

Select the Yes option for the Auditing question at the top of the Server Security Settings page of Adroit Config Editor . This displays the Connection String field in which you specify the connection string to this optional SQL Server database. Either type/paste this in directly or by click the browse button to the right of this field and use the Connection Properties dialog to specify the required connection string to the SQL Server database. Typically do NOT change the Data source from the default of .NET Framework Data Provider for OLE DB , unless you are connecting to a SQL Compact database. More details: in which case, click the Change... button and choose the datasource that corresponds to the correct version of SQL Compact and then the dialog will change so that you only need to browse in the required database file and specify the required password, if any. Network location of users and groups: if the SmartUI Server computer is part of a domain then this setting must specify the name of this network domain. Note: When a domain is specified - all users logging into this SmartUI Server must use their domain passwords and not their local user names and passwords (if these exist). However, if the Server computer is a member of a Workgroup, then this setting must be left empty. To specify the network location of the users and groups for the Server computer: Type in the required domain name or leave this empty if the Server is not part of a domain. This setting determines which users and groups are displayed by the user and group selectors for the other settings, as follows: - If this setting is empty then the selector will display the local groups or users that have been created on this Server computer. - If this setting specifies a domain, then the selector will display the groups or users that are available in this domain. Note: Click the Refresh button after changing this setting, so that the correct users and groups will be displayed in these selectors. Groups with global Server access: select which groups automatically become allowed groups for this SmartUI Server, which means the following: that their users can always log in and have unrestricted access to this SmartUI Server and its data. To add global security groups: - Select the name of the required group from the Available Groups list. - Click the << button to add this group to the Selected Groups list. Tip: You can also add groups by double-clicking the required entry in the Available Groups list to immediately add it to the Selected Groups list. Note: Only the groups listed in the Selected Groups list have global Server access. - Repeat this for all the groups that you want to add. To remove global security groups: - Select the name of the required group from the Selected Groups list. - Click the >> button to add this group to the Available Groups list. Tip: You can also remove groups by double-clicking the required entry in the Selected Groups list to immediately add it to the Available Groups list. - Repeat this for all the groups that you want to remove.

Servers Top Servers The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer.

Title: Servers
Servers Top Servers The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. Therefore, the WanClient creates and maintains a tag link database that stores a list of WanServer(s), that this WanClient is required to connect to, and a list of the tags whose values are communicated to each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers. Servers contain the settings required by the WanClient to communication to the required remote WanServer applications. Servers can be configured, as follows: - To add a new server . - To edit an existing server . - To delete an existing server . - To recover a formerly deleted server . - To manually edit servers – this may be necessary when adding a large number of servers at once. -->

ServiceCleanShutdown Top ServiceCleanShutdown WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". To cause the Agent Server service to attempt a clean shutdown to ensure that the OPC client drivers disconnect from their OPC Servers, add the following value and set it to 1: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup (REG_)DWORD ServiceCleanShutdown = 1, the default value is 0. SET Commands Top SET Commands Function: To modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server.

Title: SET Commands
SET Commands Top SET Commands Function: To modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server. Note1: This command must be enabled by the Command agent , which it is sent to, before it can be performed, because it can create a serious security and operational risk through the remote modification of process and control values. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands . Note2: Due to the seriousness of the potential security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict the usage of this command. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . Note3: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. The decision of which of the following command formats to use, is usually a tradeoff between the prior configuration in the Command agent and the required amount of typing, when specifying the SMS command itself: Note1: Both the command and its parameters are NOT case-sensitive; commands have only been capitalised for ease of reference. Note2: When using this command, it is the responsibility of the user to specify a value of the correct slot type for the tag (agent.slot) that is being modified. Basic command syntax: SET, tagName, value In this case, tagName is the name of the tag whose value is to be displayed and value is the required value for this tag. For instance: set,dig_01.value,1 This is the simplest format of this command, which requires the least prior configuration in the Command agent, it is able to modify the value of any tag, however it does require the most typing when specifying the command. Note: If the Only ‘Set’ by pseudonym setting has been enabled, then this command can ONLY be performed using pseudonyms or macros and NOT by typing in the name of required tag directly. For details, see SET Command Usage Restriction . Pseudonym usage: SET, pseudonym, value In this case, a pseudonym or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the required tag (agent.slot) and value is the required value for this referenced tag. For instance, assuming that a pseudonym called ‘dig01v’ is created to represent ‘DIG_01.value’, this command can be specified as: set,dig01v,1 Although pseudonyms save on the typing when specifying the command, ONLY the tags that have defined pseudonyms for this Command agent can be used.

For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms .

Title: SET Commands
For details on creating and using pseudonyms, see Creating Pseudonyms . Macro usage: macro In this case, a macro or alias needs to be created, beforehand, for the entire SET command. For instance, assuming that a macro called ‘Pump1ON’ is created to represent ‘set,dig_01.value,1’, then this command can simply be specified as: "Pump1ON". Although macros provide short yet intuitive command names, they require the most pre-configuration in this Command agent and are therefore most restrictive. For details on creating and using macros, see Creating Macros . -->

Set Time Period Top Set Time Period The Set Time Period is a generic dialog box that is used to specify time ranges.

Title: Set Time Period
Set Time Period Top Set Time Period The Set Time Period is a generic dialog box that is used to specify time ranges. Under Period Type , one or more of the following options may be available: - Start + Interval displays a period from a fixed start time forward in time at a specified interval. - End - Interval displays a period from a fixed end time backwards in time at a specified interval. - Start to End displays a period from a fixed start time to a fixed end time with a specified interval, and can be used to filter out alarms. - Current - Interval displays a real time period with the specified interval. Note: If used for a trend, Adroit will attempt to fetch historical trend data if it exists to fill in the trend window. - Datum +/- Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum forwards or backwards in time at a specified interval. - Datum - Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum backwards in time at a specified interval. - Interval - for DataLog agent Length and Time configuration. - Time - for EventOutput agent Time Printing setting. Under Period Details , one or more of the following options may be available: For the Start and End , Date and Time fields, click in the appropriate field, and select the required date and time digits. -->

Under Period Type , one or more of the following options may be available: - Start + Interval displays a period from a fixed start time forward in time at a specified interval. - End - Interval displays a period from a fixed end time backwards in time at a specified interval. - Start to End displays a period from a fixed start time to a fixed end time with a specified interval, and can be used to filter out alarms. - Current - Interval displays a real time period with the specified interval. Note: If used for a trend, Adroit will attempt to fetch historical trend data if it exists to fill in the trend window. - Datum +/- Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum forwards or backwards in time at a specified interval. - Datum - Interval - displays a period from a fixed datum backwards in time at a specified interval. - Interval - for DataLog agent Length and Time configuration. - Time - for EventOutput agent Time Printing setting. Under Period Details , one or more of the following options may be available: For the Start and End , Date and Time fields, click in the appropriate field, and select the required date and time digits. -->

Title: Configuration
Example I: Percentage styled columns attempt to fill the remaining space , so you would configure a 200px wide table with 20px absolute, an auto sized column and a 100% column, as follows: 1.Column1 Absolute: 20 px 2.Column2 Autosize: whatever the preferred size is... say this measures to be 100px 3.Column3 Percent: 100%: 200 - 20 - 100 = 80px. Example II: If there are two percentage style columns, the 80 pixels would be divided up between the two columns in proportion to one another - so if we had 20% and 80% it would be: 1.Column1 Absolute: 20 px 2.Column2 Autosize: whatever the preferred size is... say this measures to be 100px 3.Column3 Percent: 20%: (200 - 20 – 100) = 80px remaining space. 80px * .20 = 16px. 4.Column4 Percent: 80%: (200 - 20 – 100) = 80px remaining space. 80px * .80 = 64px. Example III: Exactly the same as above but the two percentage style columns are both 75%, the 80 pixels would be split equally between the two normalised columns: 1.Column1 Absolute: 20 px 2.Column2 Autosize: whatever the preferred size is... say this measures to be 100px 3.Column3 Percent: 75% (normalises to 50%): (200 - 20 – 100) = 80px remaining space. 80px * .50 = 40px. 4.Column4 Percent: 75% (normalises to 50%): (200 - 20 – 100) = 80px remaining space. 80px * .50 = 40px. -->

- Agent Server Type: Usually the default selection of Stand-alone/Distributed Server is required for a typical installation; but this also provides the following options: - Cluster Aware Server: This is required when you need stand-alone Agent Servers to operate with an Adroit Active Cluster pair (a set of hot-standby Agent Servers) in a distributed project.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Agent Server Type: Usually the default selection of Stand-alone/Distributed Server is required for a typical installation; but this also provides the following options: - Cluster Aware Server: This is required when you need stand-alone Agent Servers to operate with an Adroit Active Cluster pair (a set of hot-standby Agent Servers) in a distributed project. Since you are otherwise unable to have multiple Agent Servers with the same name in a Project. - Cluster Server: If you are setting up a hot standby solution (cluster pair) you need to select each of the Agent Servers in the cluster to be of type Cluster. - Project Name: Adroit shares information seamlessly between Agent Servers that have the same Project Name. So if you need to share data between Agent Servers, then give them a common name, such as the name of the your SmartUI project. By default this is the name of your computer. Note: You need unique agent (tag) names in a Project. - Agent Server Name: This is the logical name for the Agent Server. You can call this what you like, typically it might be the area of plant that you are controlling. - Auto-Load File Name: This is the logical name for the Adroit Agent Server tag database (WGP file). This stores the entire configuration of this Agent Server. You can call this file whatever you like, typically this might be the area of plant that you are controlling. Tip: You will notice that this file is saved to the Adroit project folder that you specified when installing Adroit , which is by default: C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data folder. Note: In addition to configuring the Agent Server, you can also install drivers and add and configure their devices (which you need to create for EACH PLC that your SmartUI project uses). For details, see Creating and configuring PLC devices in Adroit . Tip: You can either add a device to the Mitsubishi Q,QnA,L,R and iQF Series Ethernet(3E Frames) or Mitsubishi MX Components driver. -->

Title: Simulation datasources
Simulation datasources Top Simulation datasources The Simulation datasource provides a wide variety of different types of data for simulation or testing purposes, when you cannot connect to an actual datasource. Click for more information: Each simulation datasource, contains a number of simulation categories, whose data is either unchanging (static) or mathematically generated and therefore constantly varying. This simulated data is essentially a dependable source of data, which can be used when testing the animation of your graphic forms within the design phase. Note: It is also possible to use a Simulation spider to create and configure simulated data too, which is mathematically generated. For details, see Simulation spiders . This datasource is added to the Datasources category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Adding Simulation datasources . A Simulation datasource is identified in the Enterprise Manager by its specified name and its icon . When this datasource is opened the simulated data is displayed, in the following hierarchy: - The simulated data categories are listed alphanumerically beneath this datasource. - Each category can be expanded to reveal its simulated data, which is also displayed alphanumerically. The icons used to represent this data, vary according to the category selected. Tip: It is recommended to use this data, when animating graphic forms and not their simulation properties, if any, which are all static values. - Most of the simulated data, can be further expanded to reveal the following properties that govern the generation of their simulated values, which are also listed alphanumerically: Property Description Amplitude The maximum value that will be generated for this output. DE This contains the first simulated value of this data element. Note: It is not recommended to use this property when animating graphic forms, since it will NOT update. Frequency The cycle time of the simulation item in Hz, the lower the number the less the simulated values change. Name The fully qualified name of the simulated data, including its simulation category. Running This Boolean value, indicates whether this simulated value is being generated (True) or not (False), when the graphic form is in Run mode. For details, see Opening graphic forms . ShortName Only the name of the simulated data. SimulationType This specifies the format or generation of the simulated values: - DATASET: A DataSet consisting of 2 columns and 2 rows. - RAMP: A value increasing linearly, in increments specified by Frequency , from 0 to the Amplitude and then decreasing linearly back to 0. - SIN: Sine values between + and - Amplitude . - SQUARE: Values are squared between 0 and the Amplitude . - STATIC: An unchanging value. - CPU: The name of the performance counter used to obtain the % processor time of the system. UpdateRate The time in milliseconds between successively generated values. Note: Although the BulkSimulDE### data within the Bulk simulation category cannot be expanded, they too are RAMP values, where the number indicated by ### specifies the seed number from which the value begins to ramp upwards from. -->

Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) Top Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) This is a minimalistic standard of user interface design, which has come about through years of research and trial and error.

Title: Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA)
Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) Top Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) This is a minimalistic standard of user interface design, which has come about through years of research and trial and error. This standard moves away from the brightly colored and the almost photo-realistic process design of the past which used bright colors that while at the outset were visually appealing, proved in practice to only distract the operators from the process they were monitoring. Therefore this situational awareness standard (also known as High Performance HMI) strives at all times to create user interface elements that only present the operator with the information they need to discern exactly what is going on in the process they are operating, for this reason: - most of the colors are muted and bright colors are ONLY used to indicate issues that require IMMEDIATE attention. - great use is made of trends as these are visually efficient in relaying the necessary information without the operator needing to scrutinise reams of values and then calculate themselves how these values related to their normal operating conditions. In other words this operator interface design strives to minimise user fatigue and increase their response times, as follows: - Clarity : uncluttered displays using simple, easy to understand graphics, where abnormal conditions are clear, prominent and consistently distinguishable and only the most important information is displayed. The process layout should correspond to how the operators envisage the process and not how managers like to view it. Typically use grey backgrounds to minimise glare and avoid the gratuitous use of animation, process lines and the outlines of the process equipment should be dark grey or black, so that emphasis is provided by differing line thicknesses and not color. - Consistency : consistent and intuitive methods of navigation, data manipulation and graphics functions need to be employed, involving the minimum number of mouse clicks, typically no more than 3 clicks to get to any level of detail. Consistent visual and color coding of alarm indication and other events. For details, see Consistent alarm indication. Use a consistent hierarchical structure providing the progressive exposure of detailed information. - Feedback : important actions should require confirmation, such as two levels of confirmation to change critical set points to minimise the possibility of mistakes. Consistent alarm indication : the applicable situation awareness wizards use the same numbers and colors and graphical symbols to indicate your alarms. Situational Awareness design elements : the available sub-categories of wizards that can be used to design your process control mimics. Guidelines to implement situational awareness : a recommended continual process to ensure the success of your redesign of your process control mimics. -->

Situational Awareness design elements Top Situational Awareness design elements This lists the available sub-categories and describes their wizards that can be used to design your process control mimics so that they adhere to the situational awareness standard.

Title: Situational Awareness design elements
Situational Awareness design elements Top Situational Awareness design elements This lists the available sub-categories and describes their wizards that can be used to design your process control mimics so that they adhere to the situational awareness standard. - Data Links : These wizards often require more than one value, in which case one of these values can be set (written) from this wizard in addition to displaying the other and/or they display a large amount of information about their associated value. For details see Data Links . - Displays : these wizards textually display the value of the associated process variable. For details see Displays . - Indicators : these wizards graphically indicate the value of the associated process variable without actually displaying its value. For details see Indicators . - ISO Shapes : these wizards use ISO symbols to represent your common plant equipment, since these simple obvious shapes are easy to recognise immediately without needing any labeling. For details see ISO Shapes . Tip: Move away from labeling every item of equipment with their tag names or point IDs as these are NOT important and only add unnecessary visual clutter and use muted colors to indicate whether they are started or stopped. - Process Vessels : these wizards depict the level of a vessel to operators without undue emphasis or distractions. For details see Process Vessels . - Production Charts : these wizards should be used when operators need to know how a production value is performing against a set target value: this charts the production value by means of a filled grey area and plots a straight line graph of the set target value for the specific production period, for an easy comparison between the two. For details see Production Charts . - Radar Plots : these wizards create Pattern Recognition Objects (PROs) that describe the relationship between a number of related process variables as a shape instead of as a series of numbers, because the brain can remember shapes far more than sets of numbers. For details see Radar Plots . - Spark Lines : these wizards display a trend of how a process variable (PV) behaves with respect to its normal operating range without displaying its actual value. For details see Spark Lines . -->

size Behaviours Top size Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically resize the object linearly by means of a monitored value.

Title: size Behaviours
size Behaviours Top size Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to dynamically resize the object linearly by means of a monitored value. In other words, you need to monitor a value, which has a defined minimum and maximum value and then specify the maximum required width and/or height magnifications, when the value reaches its maximum value. For example, specifying a factor of 2 for both the width and height dimensions then the object doubles its size when the measured ( Input Data Element ) is at the specified Maximum Data Element/value value. Note: The object retains its original size when the monitored value is less than or equal to the specified Minimum value. To dynamically resize a control or vector: - Add or edit an size Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the value in the Input Data Element field. - Specify the minimum value for this Input Data Element in the Minimum Data Element/value field. Note: Any value lower than or equal to this value has no effect upon this Behaviour. - Specify the maximum value for this Input Data Element in the Maximum Data Element/value field. Note: It is at this value that the full transformation of the object occurs. Slot Configuration Grid Top Slot Configuration Grid This grid, consists of the following columns, which define each slot of the derived agent, as follows: Note: The grid provides standard configuration options , use the horizontal and vertical scroll bars, when visible, to navigate to the required fields.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Slot Configuration Grid Top Slot Configuration Grid This grid, consists of the following columns, which define each slot of the derived agent, as follows: Note: The grid provides standard configuration options , use the horizontal and vertical scroll bars, when visible, to navigate to the required fields. - The first untitled column, numbers the defined slots in the grid. - Replace or edit the cell in the Slot name column, to define a name for each slot required by the derived agent. Note: The order in which the slots are defined, defines the order of the slots, in which they will be displayed in the configuration agent dialog. It is good practice to keep slots with the same data type together. For the DriveXYZ agent, type in the following slots: Start , Stop , Tripped , Speed and Temperature . We will also add a Value slot that will denote the running status of the drive and a slot called HighTemp that will be used to store the high alarm value of the temperature variable. - Replace or edit the cell in the Slot type column, for each defined slot, to select its applicable data type, from the following selections in the list box: Boolean If the slot is to contain a 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE). Integer If the slot is to contain a valid 32 bit value. Real If the slot is to contain a valid 64 bit (8 byte) floating number. String If the slot is to contain a variable length string (i.e. a VarString slot). WARNING! This slot CANNOT be scanned. String80 If the slot is to contain a 79 character text string (i.e. a String slot). Note: ONLY String80 slots can be scanned. Datetime If the slot is to contain a valid datetime variable. Tagname If the slot is to contain the name of any valid tag (agent.slot), which will be automatically subscribed to. For the DriveXYZ agent, add the following descriptions to the configured slots: Start= Boolean , Stop= Boolean , Value= Boolean , Tripped= Boolean , Speed= Real , Temperature= Real and HighTemp= Real . - Replace or edit the cell in the Slot description column, for each defined slot, to specify a suitable slot description. For the DriveXYZ agent, add the following data types to the configured slots: Start= Start drive pulse , Stop= Stop drive pulse , Value= Drive is running , Tripped= Drive has tripped , Speed= Drive Speed (rpm) , Temperature= Temperature (degC) and HighTemp= Temperature high alarm value . - Replace or edit the cell in the WGP prefix column, for each defined slot that needs to be saved in the WGP file, to specify a suitable 3 to 5 character prefix for this slot. For the DriveXYZ agent, in practice only the HighTemp slot would need to be saved, since this is probably the only slot that is not scanned from a front-end device and is manually changed by an engineer/operator from a mimic. But for this example, all the slots will be saved so that the WGP file will always contains the slot values as at the last save. - Tick the tick box in the Disable editing column, to prevent this defined slot from being edited within this derived agent’s configuration dialog. A slot that is disabled for editing, prevents its simulation from within the configuration dialog, but will still allow it to be manipulated by others means e.g. from a mimic. This is not ticked by default.

For the DriveXYZ agent, only the following slots: Start , Stop and HighTemp will be edited from the configuration dialog, therefore tick this tick box for the following slots: Value , Tripped , Speed , Temperature , so that these slots will only reflect the values existing in the PLC or the last saved value.

Slot Status Words Top Slot Status Words In addition to an overall agent status word, which shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent.

Title: Slot Status Words
Slot Status Words Top Slot Status Words In addition to an overall agent status word, which shows the status as determined by the status of the individual slot, there is also a status word for each slot of an agent. This is an advanced feature that can provide better monitoring and control of the agent. The bit allocations and meanings for the slot status words are exactly the same as they are for the overall agent status. For details, see Agent Status and Slot Status . Note: The first bit in the status word, statusBad , is the only bit an application needs to monitor to determine the integrity of an agent or slot. For details, see Agent or Slot Integrity Monitoring (Bad Handling) . These slot statuses may be accessed by appending the relevant status slotname after the agent and slot, e.g. ANA01.status.statusBit00. Note: These bits can be viewed and/or set via the Slot Status configuration dialog, by clicking the Advanced button in the Agent Header configuration dialog. -->

SmartInhibit Top SmartInhibit WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY.

Title: SmartInhibit
Steps:
SmartInhibit Top SmartInhibit WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". To define how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms if an agent’s statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one and the agent is currently in alarm and/or unacknowledged, add the following DWORD registry value and configure it appropriately: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\WG.INI\ (REG_)DWORD SmartInhibit Configure this value as follows: SmartInhibit = 0 - The alarm, if active, will remain active. - The alarm, if unacknowledged, will remain unacknowledged. - The effect of the above is …. NOTHING changes SmartInhibit = 1 - The alarm, if active, will be cleared with reported data set to "Inhibited". - The alarm, if unacknowledged, will be globally acknowledged with reported data set to "Inhibited". - The combination of the above actions will make the alarm disappear off the list - This is the default operation . SmartInhibit = 2 - The alarm, if active, will be cleared with reported data set to "Inhibited". So the alarm list would show alarm as not active. - The alarm acknowledge status remains unchanged, regardless of whether it has already been acknowledged or not, globally or locally. -->

SNMP Community Strings Top SNMP Community Strings SNMP Community strings are like a user name or password that provide specific access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device.

Title: SNMP Community Strings
SNMP Community Strings Top SNMP Community Strings SNMP Community strings are like a user name or password that provide specific access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. ( OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. values) of a device. If the community string is correct, the device responds with the requested information. Otherwise the device simply discards the request and does not respond. The following three types of community strings determine the management commands that can be used, all of which are supported by Adroit: - SNMP Read-only community string – this only allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from the managed device. Note: By convention, most equipment ships from the factory with a read-only community string set to "public". - SNMP Read-Write community string – this allows information (OID values) to be retrieved from and modified within the managed device. - SNMP Trap community string – this allows SNMP Traps to be sent from a managed device. Traps are configured on a device to report when an error or specific event occurs. For instance, a common trap is the ‘Authentication Failure’ trap, that is sent when an incorrect community string is sent to a device. Note: Up to 16 community strings can be defined per device. Tip: Each device in a network can have its own unique set of community strings, although it may simplify network management if every device uses the same set of community strings. -->

SNMP Managed Objects Top SNMP Managed Objects Network devices that are managed by SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network.

Title: SNMP Managed Objects
Steps:
SNMP Managed Objects Top SNMP Managed Objects Network devices that are managed by SNMP Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to monitor and manage a diverse range of devices on a computer network. expose their management data as managed objects. These managed objects might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and so on, that directly relate to the current operation of the device. EVERY managed object (value) is uniquely described and organised hierarchically in an international database, known as the SNMP Management Information Base (MIB), by means of an associated Object Identifier (OID). This OID not only uniquely describes it in the MIB but also describes the exact location of this object within the tree-like structure of the MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. database too. For details on their naming convention, see SNMP Object Identifiers . Each SNMP agent DO NOT confuse this with an Adroit agent, this is simply software running on a device that allows it to be managed by SNMP. is responsible for maintaining its own virtual MIB, which ONLY contains the managed objects supported by its device. This virtual MIB is read by an SNMP manager a program that is responsible for managing and monitoring SNMP devices, such as the Adroit SNMPManager agent. to obtain a list of this device’s managed objects, so that it can know which values to get and/or to set. Note1: SNMP allows the extension of these standard objects (as defined in the international MIB) with objects that are specific to a particular agent through the use of private MIBs. Note2: SNMP also provides a limited security system, known as SNMP Community Strings, which control the access to these objects. For details, see SNMP Community Strings . -->

Title: SNMP Object Value Return Types
SNMP Object Value Return Types Top SNMP Object Value Return Types The following list describes the typical type of data that are returned by SNMP object values and the recommended tag (agent.slot) that can be used to store this value and whether this data type can be written to: Note: ONLY the specified return types are writable. - Integer32: An integer variable, between -2^31 (-2147483648 decimal) and 2^31-1 (2147483647 decimal) inclusive. This should typically be stored in an Integer agent. This is writable . - Unsigned 32-bit value: An integer variable, between 0 and 2^32-1 (4294967295 decimal) inclusive. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . - 32-bit counter: A counter variable that is a non-negative integer which increments until it reaches a maximum value of 2^32-1 (4294967295 decimal), when it wraps around and starts increasing again from zero. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . - 32-bit gauge: A gauge variable that represents a non-negative integer, which may increase or decrease, but shall never exceed a maximum value. This maximum value cannot be greater than 2^32-1 (4294967295 decimal). This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . - Time ticks: A timeticks variable represents a non-negative integer which represents the time, modulo 2^32 (4294967296 decimal), in hundredths of a second for a specific timer event, which should be identified by the description of its object. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . - 64-bit counter: A counter variable that is a non-negative integer which increments until it reaches a maximum value of 2^64-1 (18446744073709551615 decimal), when it wraps around and starts increasing again from zero. This should typically be stored in a Real agent. This is writable . - Real: A real variable that represents a double precision floating point number (64 bits). This should typically be stored in a Real agent. - String: A string variable. This should typically be stored in a String agent. - Bits: A variable that is an enumeration of named bits with non-negative, contiguous values, starting at zero. This should typically be stored in a String agent. - Object Identifier: An object identifier variable that represents administratively assigned names, which may have at most 128 sub- identifiers. This should typically be stored in a String agent.

- Sequence: An ASN sequence variable.

Title: SNMP Object Value Return Types
- Sequence: An ASN sequence variable. This should typically be stored in a String agent. This is writable . - IP Address: An IP address variable that represents a 32-bit Internet address, in network byte-order. This should typically be stored in a String agent. This is writable . - Opague variable: This should typically be stored in a String agent. This is writable . - Octet String: This should typically be stored in a String agent. This is writable . -->

SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements The following usage requirements must be met before the SNMPManager agent can monitor and/or manage your network devices: - The device must have a SINGLE (FIXED) IP address.

Title: Requirements
SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements SNMPManager Agent Usage Requirements The following usage requirements must be met before the SNMPManager agent can monitor and/or manage your network devices: - The device must have a SINGLE (FIXED) IP address. Note1: ONE SNMPManager agent CANNOT connect to MULTIPLE devices (IP addresses). Note2: You CANNOT specify an IP address that is ALREADY configured for another SNMPManager agent! - The device (computer) must be ACCESSIBLE on the network (able to be PINGed). - You ONLY need to run the SNMP service on a computer that you want to monitor using the SNMPManager agent. IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. So to monitor a computer, you will typically need to install the SNMP service - because this component is NOT included in the STANDARD installation of Windows (and/or Server) operating systems. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service. Note: You may need to configure the installed SNMP Service on Windows 7 before you can use the SNMPManager agent. For details, see Additional SNMP Service Configuration for Windows 7. - The security settings, of the SNMP managed devices and the Agent Server computer, on the network must ALLOW SNMP traffic. Therefore, ensure that the port used for SNMP communications, namely UDP port 161 is unblocked (enabled) in any firewalls that may exist, such as the Windows Firewall installed by Windows XP Service Pack 2. - To monitor/manage TWO OR MORE DEVICES, then your Agent Server license must include the necessary OEM license, WITHOUT which you can ONLY monitor and/or manage a SINGLE device. Tip: To check if you have the correct OEM license, simply create a second SNMPManager agent and ensure that its Unlicensed checkbox (status bit) is not enabled. - Ensure that your Agent Server license has enough available scan licenses, since a scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. WARNING! If an SNMPManager agent requires more than your available scan points then ALL these OID value operations are DISABLED and its Error status bit is set. - To monitor this device you require its community string that has READ ONLY rights. For details of community strings, see SNMP Community Strings.

- To control this device you require its community string that has READ WRITE rights.

Title: Requirements
- To control this device you require its community string that has READ WRITE rights. - To receive SNMP events (traps) from the device you need to create a script that processes the received traps. For further details, see About SNMP Traps . Note: Ensure that you backup the GLOBAL SNMP configuration file, which is called 'snmp.wgx' by default, as this file contains the OID configuration of ALL your SNMPManager agents! SNMP Error Codes: Lists the SNMP error codes implemented by Microsoft for troubleshooting SNMP-related problems. -->
