See the agent header slots for the information that is common to all agent types. .WGP File Line Description IPA=nnn.nnn.nnn.nnn The IP Address of the device to be monitored. COM=string The SNMP Community String required to access the SNMP objects and their values, for this device. WCOM=string The SNMP Community String required to write (set) values for this device. MON=string The name of the .WGX file that stores the OID list of this agent, which is typically saved in the following folder: C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Data and is called snmpmgr.wgx. IMPORTANT: Please ensure that you backup this 'snmpmgr.wgx' file in addition to the WGP file, which is stored in the same folder. RAT=nnnnn Scan rate in milliseconds for retrieving the values of the scanned and enabled SNMP objects in the selected objects list. STT=n A Boolean value indicating whether the monitoring (scanning) process of this agent is either started or stopped. TMT=n The Integer timeout value i.e. the maximum time (in seconds) to establish a connection to this device. RET=n The Integer retries i.e. the number of attempts to connect to the device, before deeming this device to be unavailable. TRAP=n A Boolean value indicating whether the traps are enabled for this agent or not. IPP=nnn The Integer IP port used for SNMP communication to this device. PDU=nnn The Integer number of OID values to include in each polling transaction. VER=n The Integer SNMP version the device supports. USER=string SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required user name. AUTH=string SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required password for authentication on this device. ENCR=string SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required encryption password for this device. MIB=string the name of the MIB file if this was used to specify the OID tree, instead of walking the device. -->

Slot Name Type Function authPassword STRING SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required password for authentication on this device.

Title: Slots:
Slot Name Type Function authPassword STRING SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required password for authentication on this device. catchupData RAWBYTES Internal use only (used with datalog catchup). datascope BOOLEAN Launches the Adroit Protocol Driver Monitor application so that you can open the Datascope window to view the activity of this agent - like clicking the Datascope button in the edit agent dialog. encrPassword STRING SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required encryption password for this device. errorMsg STRING This slot displays the reason why the Error status bit of this agent is currently set. For details, see the description for status bit 21 of this agent below. filename STRING The name of the global SNMP configuration file, which is called 'snmp.wgx' by default. This file contains the common OID configuration of all your SNMPMgr agents and allows them to store an unlimited number of OIDs. Ensure that this file is backed up. Note: This file name can also be specified using the Advanced button in the edit dialog. idx INTEGER To select a record (row) from the list of selected OIDs (records slot). This can be used to display and/or configure one or more fields of this record. Set this slot to the index of the required record in the list, to populate the following slots with the fields of this selected record: idxEnabled, idxWriteable, idxOID, idxName, idxType, idxValue and idxLastPollTime slot. idxEnabled BOOLEAN Indicates whether the value, specified by the idx slot, is enabled to be polled (retrieved from the device) or not. This can be configured as required. idxLastPollTime TIME Indicates the last time the value, specified by the idx slot, was automatically polled. idxName VARSTRING The textual description of the OID, specified by the idx slot. This can be configured as required, for instance after manually changing the OID, see the idxOID slot description. idxOID VARSTRING The OID, in numeric format, of the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. specified by the idx slot. This can be changed to another OID. If so this automatically changes the Name ( idxName slot) of the selected record to “Unknown”. idxRate INTEGER The rate, in milliseconds, that the OID value, specified by the idx slot, is polled (retrieved from the device). If this is 0 then the default poll rate ( pollrate slot) is used instead. This can be configured as required. idxTag STRING The name of the agent used to store this OID value, if one has been specified. idxTimestamp TIME The time stamp of the current OID value. idxType INTEGER An Integer indicator of the return type of the value, specified by the idx slot. For details, see OID Return Type Indicators . idxValue VARSTRING The current value of the OID, specified by the objectListIndex slot. idxWriteable BOOLEAN Indicates whether the OID value, specified by the idx slot, is enabled to be written to the device or not. This can be configured as required. ipAddress STRING The IP Address of the SNMP managed device to be monitored. Note: It is NOT possible to specify an IP address that has ALREADY been configured for another SNMPMgr agent! ipPort INTEGER The IP port of the SNMP managed device to be monitored - used when monitoring a device through a gateway. lastWriteStatus STRING Displays a text message that informs the user whether the last value written to the device was successfully changed in the device or not.

pollAllNow BOOLEAN If set to 1, this will cause all OIDs in the list to be manually polled now (ASAP), see Manually Polling OID Values.

Title: Slots:
pollAllNow BOOLEAN If set to 1, this will cause all OIDs in the list to be manually polled now (ASAP), see Manually Polling OID Values. pollIdx INTEGER To manually poll any OID (receive its value from the device) that you added to the list ( records slot), set this slot to the index of this OID in the list. readCommunity STRING The SNMP Community String required that ONLY provides READ access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. of the network device. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings . records VARSTRING The list of the selected OIDs (SNMP objects). Each list entry is enclosed in #’s and adheres to the following format: *Index*Enable*Writable*Object Identifier*SNMP name*Return type*Current Value* Adroit tag*PollRate retries INTEGER The number of times this agent will attempt to connect to the device, before deeming this device to be unavailable. scanRate INTEGER The default or global rate, in milliseconds, at which the polling-enabled OIDs are retrieved from the device. start BOOLEAN Determines whether the device is to be managed (1) or not (0). When enabled (1) the selected OID values will be polled and/or written to and SNMP traps will be received, if the trapEnabled slot is enabled (1). Note: A scan point is consumed for every unique OID value that is polled, written to and/or trapped. timeout INTEGER The maximum time (in milliseconds) for this agent to establish a connection to the specified SNMP managed device. trapCount INTEGER The number of SNMP traps (and their sub-traps) received from the managed device in the main trap queue (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is the number of OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap). trapEnabled BOOLEAN This enables the receipt of SNMP traps from the managed device. (This only occurs once the start slot is set to 1 and consumes a scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. for each unique OID that is trapped.) trapGeneric INTEGER An Integer value of the generic code or identification of this trap OID. trapOID VARSTRING The OID, in numeric format, which identifies the SNMP managed object for this event. trapPop BOOLEAN Set this slot to 1 (via a script or button etc.) to read the first trap off the main trap queue, which reduces the trapCount slot by the number of OIDs in this trap (for simple traps this is 1, for complex traps this is more than 1). This populates the trapTime , trapType , trapValue, trapGeneric , trapSpecific and trapOID slots with the information pertaining to trap that is first in the queue. This reduces the trapCount slot by 1. WARNING! Once a trap has been read off a queue it is discarded and cannot be accessed again. Note: The queue of traps is processed from the oldest to the newest trap. For more details concerning the handling of traps and the related queues, see About SNMP Traps . trapSpecific INTEGER An Integer value of the specific code or identification of this trap OID. trapTime TIME The time that the value, specified by the trapValue slot, occurred. trapType INTEGER An Integer indicator of the return type of the value, specified by the trapValue slot. For details, see OID Return Type Indicators . trapValue VARSTRING The value of the OID specified by the trapOID slot.

trapValueIsBinary BOOLEAN This is enabled set to 1 when the trap value reports as ascii and will need conversion to hex/binary.

Title: Slots:
trapValueIsBinary BOOLEAN This is enabled set to 1 when the trap value reports as ascii and will need conversion to hex/binary. trapWorkCount INTEGER For the current complex trap that is popped off the main trap queue, this contains all the OIDs [sub-traps] in this trap, except for the first OID that is transferred to the trap... slots. This work queue is provided to prevent the possible corruption of the main queue by popping off the incorrect number of sub-traps. userName STRING SNMP version 3 ONLY: the required user name for this device. version INTEGER An Integer value of the SNMP version that is supported by the network device. writeCommunity STRING The SNMP Community String that provides read AND WRITE access to the SNMP managed objects management data exposed by SNMP managed devices that might be hardware, configuration parameters, performance statistics, and any other data that directly relates to the operation of this device. of the network device. For further details, see SNMP Community Strings . This must be specified in order to change the values of OIDs in the device.

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title: Specifications
Note: These are of type BOOLEAN. Bit Number Name Function status bit 16 InvalidConnection On if the agent is UNABLE to access the specified device and its SNMP objects. To troubleshoot this, see Connecting to the Managed Device . Note1: This will ALWAYS be On if the agent is loaded in the Stopped state and is only validated when the agent is Started or Updated. Note2: When an invalid connection is specified this will cause a delay when closing and opening the Edit dialog of this agent, as the agent attempts to establish this connection. Note 3: This is set to On, by default, for new agents. status bit 17 Stopped On if the agent is ABLE to connect to the device BUT not getting, setting and/or trapping OID values. status bit 18 Started On if the agent is ABLE to connect to the device AND getting, setting and/or trapping OID values. For details on stopping or starting the managing of the device, see Device Management Settings . status bit 19 Unlicensed On if: - the Started (statusBit18) is set - Agent Server license does NOT contain the required OEM license and - it is NOT the first SNMPMgr agent that was added. For details regarding the licensing and use of this agent, see Usage Requirements . status bit 21 Error On when a non connection-related error has occurred, while the errorMsg slot can be used to determine the reason why this status bit is being set. This specifies that one of the following errors have occurred: Note: If this Error status bit is alarmed, using the default Error alarm type, then the contents of the errorMsg slot appears in the "Reported data" field of the alarm entry. - If the Started (statusBit18) is set and any agent assigned to an OID is not found. For instance, when an agent is removed from the Agent Server after it was assigned. Note: In this case the errorMsg slot contains the name of the missing agent. However, if multiple agents are not found, usually only the last agent that is "not found" will be displayed by this slot. - If the Started (statusBit18) is set and one or more of the polled, written and/or trapped OIDs cause the number of licensed scan points for this Agent Server to be exceeded. Note: In this case the errorMsg slot contains 'Not enough scan points'. WARNING!

This immediate disables the polling, writing and/or trapping of ALL the OIDs, even if this agent only attempts to consume one scan point more than the total number of licensed scan points for this Agent Server.

Title: Specifications
This immediate disables the polling, writing and/or trapping of ALL the OIDs, even if this agent only attempts to consume one scan point more than the total number of licensed scan points for this Agent Server. For details, see Adroit Licensing . status bit 22 Traps On when this agent receives 1 or more SNMP traps from the device and the trapCount slot is >= 1. These traps are stored in the trap queue for this agent, so that you can process them, typically by means of a script. For more details, see About SNMP Traps . status bit 23 Healthy On if the agent is UNABLE to connect to the specified device.

Title: Requirements
SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements Top SNMPMgr Agent Usage Requirements The following usage requirements must be met before the SNMPMgr agent can monitor and/or manage your network devices: - Typically the device must have a SINGLE (FIXED) IP address or at least a unique port address so that this SNMP devices can be uniquely addressed via a gateway. Note1: ONE SNMPMgr agent CANNOT connect to MULTIPLE devices (IP addresses). Note2: You CANNOT specify an IP address that is ALREADY configured for another SNMPMgr agent! - The device (computer) must be ACCESSIBLE on the network (able to be PINGed). - You need to know which SNMP version the device supports and you also need to know all of its connection settings. Since the SNMPMgr agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and SNMP version 3 supports additional connection settings. - ONLY WHEN MONITORING A COMPUTER: you need to run the SNMP service on this computer. IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. So to monitor a computer, you will typically need to install the SNMP service - because this component is NOT included in the STANDARD installation of Windows (and/or Server) operating systems and you need to you need to configure the security settings to browse its SNMP values. For details, see Installing the Windows SNMP Service and SNMP Service Security Configuration . - The security settings, of the SNMP managed devices and the Agent Server computer, on the network must ALLOW SNMP traffic. Therefore, ensure that the port used for SNMP communications is unblocked (enabled) in any firewalls that may exist, which is typically UDP port 161 for a fixed IP address or the unique port address for the device, when addressed via a gateway. - To monitor/manage TWO OR MORE DEVICES, then your Agent Server license must include the necessary OEM a component in Adroit that requires a SEPARATE license BEFORE it can be used, which is added to the Agent Server license by means of an appropriate textual description of this component. license. In other words, WITHOUT this OEM license you can ONLY monitor and/or manage a SINGLE device.

Tip: To check if you have the correct OEM license, simply create a second SNMPMgr agent and ensure that its Unlicensed checkbox (status bit) is not enabled.

WARNING! If an SNMPMgr agent requires more than your available scan points then ALL these OID value operations are DISABLED and its Error status bit is set. - To monitor this device you require its community string that has READ ONLY rights. For further details, see About SNMP Traps. Specific Status Bits of the Command Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Command Agent The Command agent can both send SMS messages either manually or automatically and can escalate messages to another Command agent, if necessary.

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the Command Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Command Agent The Command agent can both send SMS messages either manually or automatically and can escalate messages to another Command agent, if necessary. However, it is in receiving textual commands in SMS messages that it is able to remotely configure Adroit . The following status bits of this agent can be used for diagnosing the sending and receiving of SMS messages and to determine which commands this Command agent can receive and their additional configuration, as follows: - statusBit16 MsgSendError On if the last message could not be sent due to cell phone network-specific problems, such as signal problems etc. - statusBit17 AllCommands On when the Enable commands checkbox is checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to perform commands that it receives. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . - statusBit18 SetCommands On when the Allow ‘Set’ commands checkbox is checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to perform SET commands that it receives. For details, see Specifying Permitted Commands or SET Commands . - statusBit19 GetCommands On when the Allow ‘Get’ commands checkbox is checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to perform GET commands that it receives. For details, see GET Commands . - statusBit20 AckCommands On when the Allow ‘Ack’ commands checkbox is checked, to indicate that this Command agent is able to perform ACK and LACK commands that it receives. For details, see ACK Commands . - statusBit21 RepCommands Currently not in use. - statusBit22 SubCommands Currently not in use. - statusBit23 ExpandPseudos On when the Expand pseudonyms in messages checkbox is checked, to indicate that any pseudonyms and macros specified in an incoming message received by this Command agent will be correctly interpreted and any outgoing messages will have the pseudonyms replaced with the full tag. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros or for details on pseudonyms and macros, see Using Pseudonyms and Macros . - statusBit24 SignalError On if either the signalStrength slot is less than 29 % or the bitErrorRate slot is greater than 40 %. For details, see Diagnosing the GSM_SMS Device . - statusBit25 SetByPseudos On when the Only ‘Set’ by pseudonym checkbox is checked, to indicate that SET commands can ONLY use pseudonyms and macros. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions .

Note: This status slot is turned off before executing a new transaction but it is also possible to explicitly turn it off, via a script, before executing a transaction. - statusBit19 Overrun error ON if the transaction time took longer than the scheduled delay period. i.e. runTime in seconds > schedulePeriod in seconds. Works only for scheduled transactions. - statusBit20 Connection error ON if there is a problem connecting to the database. - statusBit21 Transaction success ON if a transaction with the database succeeds. Note: This status slot is turned off before executing a new transaction but it is also possible to explicitly turn it off, via a script, before executing a transaction. It is important to alarm the Transaction error and Overrun error as these indicate any problems associated with a DbAccess Agent. The alarm type created for alarming DbAccess Agents should use the information slot in the "Reported Data" field as this may indicate useful error information. If the error is too long to be displayed in an alarm list or an event viewer, edit the agent and click on the Details button to get a better description. -->

Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent The following status bit indicates whether the connection to the specified OLE DB database is healthy or not, as follows: - statusBit16 ConnectionError On when an OLEDB error occurs – either the specified connection string is invalid OR a transaction error has occurred.

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the DBLog Agent The following status bit indicates whether the connection to the specified OLE DB database is healthy or not, as follows: - statusBit16 ConnectionError On when an OLEDB error occurs – either the specified connection string is invalid OR a transaction error has occurred. If this is ON and the connection string is VALID, then you can use the following VARSTRING slots of this agent to determine the possible cause of error, as follows: - lastError : The last OLE DB transaction error. - lastErrorQuery : The query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. - statusBit17 TransactionError On when an error occurred during the last transaction to the specified OLE DB database, this can either be alarmed or displayed. - statusBit18 QueueFilling On when there is more than 1 item in queue, which could be indicative of a slow database link. - statusBit19 QueueDump This is pulsed On, when the number of items in the queue (waiting to be logged) exceeds a 1000 and these items are dumped to a SQL file, which requires manual intervention to "catch-up" this lost data. Note1: If this occurs it is usually indicative of a problematic connection to the specified database and so this condition can also be alarmed. Note2: An audit entry is also generated when the queue is dumped, if you have implemented Agent Server auditing. -->

text:
Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network.

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. The following status bits of this agent can be used for diagnosing the existence of the specified remote device on the network, as follows: - statusBit16 Healthy On when the last ICMP message was sent to and received from the network device successfully. - statusBit17 General_Failure On when there is any failure preventing the network device from being accessed. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy). - statusBit18 Destination_Unreachable On when the failure is caused because the destination IP address is not reachable on the current network, for instance when no routing is available to reach this IP address range. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when a timeout failure occurs. - statusBit19 Destination_Timeout On when the failure is caused because no response has been received from the remote device within the configured timeout value. This value is cleared when the device becomes accessible (Healthy) or when the remote device becomes unreachable. - statusBit20 High On when the last round trip time The time to send an ICMP message to the network device and receive a reply. (INTEGER roundTripTime slot) is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hi slot). - statusBit21 high-High On when the last round trip time is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL to the Round trip time: high-high alarm value (ms) (INTEGER hiHi slot). - statusBit22 Busy On when an ICMP message is in the process of being sent and/or received from the network device. -->

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the Script Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Script Agent The Script agent has the following specific status bits: - statusBit16 Idle ON if the main subroutine is not running. - statusBit17 Running ON if the main subroutine is running. - statusBit18 Compilation error ON if there is an error in the compilation of any of the specified module files. - statusBit19 Runtime error ON if the an error occurs in any of the subroutines during execution of the script. - statusBit20 Overrun error ON if the execution time of the main subroutine took longer than the scheduled delay period. i.e. runTime in seconds > schedulePeriod in seconds. Works only for scheduled transactions. It is important to alarm the Compilation error , Runtime and Overrun error as these indicate any problems associated with a script agent. If the error is too long to be displayed in an alarm list or an event viewer, edit the agent and click on the "Details" button to get a better description. -->

Specific Status Bits of the SNMPManager Agent Specific Status Bits of the SNMPManager Agent Each SNMPManager agent can manage a single device, by getting, setting and/or trapping its OID values.

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the SNMPManager Agent Specific Status Bits of the SNMPManager Agent Each SNMPManager agent can manage a single device, by getting, setting and/or trapping its OID values. The following status bits of this agent can be used for diagnosing the status of its connection to the device it is required to manage and the status of the managing process, as follows: - statusBit16 InvalidConnection On if the agent is UNABLE to connect to the specified device. To troubleshoot this, see Connecting to the Managed Device . Note1: This will ALWAYS be On if the agent is loaded in the Stopped state and is only validated when the agent is Started or Updated. Note2: An invalid connection will delay the closing and opening the Edit dialog of this agent, as the agent attempts to establish this connection. Note 3: This is On, by default, for new agents. - statusBit17 Stopped On if the agent is ABLE to connect to the device BUT not getting, setting and/or trapping OID values. - statusBit18 Started On if the agent is ABLE to connect to the device AND getting, setting and/or trapping OID values. For details on stopping or starting the managing of the device, see Global Device Management Settings . - statusBit19 Unlicensed On if: - the Started (statusBit18) is set - Agent Server license does NOT contain the required OEM code and - it is NOT the first SNMPManager agent that was added. For details regarding the licensing and use of this agent, see Usage Requirements . - statusBit20 BuildingTree On when the hierarchical tree of Available Objects (OIDs) is being fetched from the specified device by the SNMPManager agent, so that these can be browsed and selected. This process begins when the Browser tab of the dialog is selected and no tree has been built yet or when you click the Rebuild Tree button. For details regarding the browsing of OIDs, see Selecting Browsed SNMP Objects . - statusBit21 Error On when a non connection-related error has occurred, while the errorMsg slot can be used to determine the reason why this status bit is being set. This specifies that one of the following errors have occurred: Note: If this Error status bit is alarmed, using the default Error alarm type, then the contents of the errorMsg slot appears in the "Reported data" field of the alarm entry.

Title: Specifications
- If Started (statusBit18) is set and any agent assigned to an OID value is not found. For instance, when an agent is removed from the Agent Server after it was assigned. Note: In this case the errorMsg slot contains the name of the missing agent. However, if multiple agents are not found, usually only the last agent that is "not found" will be displayed by this slot. - If Started (statusBit18) is set and one or more of the polled, written and/or trapped OID values cause the number of licensed scan points for this Agent Server to be exceeded. Note: In this case the errorMsg slot contains 'Not enough scan points'. WARNING! This immediate disables the polling, writing and/or trapping of ALL the OIDs, even if this agent only attempts to consume one scan point more than the total number of licensed scan points for this Agent Server. - statusBit22 Traps On when this agent receives 1 or more SNMP traps from the device and the trapCount slot is >= 1. These traps are stored in the trap queue for this agent, so that you can process them, typically by means of a script. For more details, see About SNMP Traps . -->

text:
Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent The Timer agent is able to perform one of three commonly used timing operations.

Title: Specifications
Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent Top Specific Status Bits of the Timer Agent The Timer agent is able to perform one of three commonly used timing operations. The following status bits can determine, whether the configured timer is running or has expired: - statusBit16 Running On if the timer is enabled i.e. the timer is operating. - statusBit17 Expired On when the timer has terminated, which is timing operation-specific, as follows: - The pulse width time expires, when configured as an on timer. For details, see Configuring On Timers . - The delay time expires, when configured as an on delay timer. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . - The timer is not running, when configured as a pulse generator. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this agent, since these are sometimes independent elements i.e. the timer is not necessarily off when its value is FALSE. For details of the timing operations performed by this agent, see Timer agent . -->

text:
Specifying Additional Callers Top Specifying Additional Callers Once a Command agent has been linked to a device, it is possible to specify one or more additional cell phone numbers that are able to send SMS messages to it, in addition to the configured recipient phone number.

Title: Specifications
Specifying Additional Callers Top Specifying Additional Callers Once a Command agent has been linked to a device, it is possible to specify one or more additional cell phone numbers that are able to send SMS messages to it, in addition to the configured recipient phone number. For details, see Specifying the GSM_SMS Device or Specifying the Recipient Phone Number . However it is ONLY when the Command agent has been enabled to perform commands that commands received from these phone numbers will be performed. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . WARNING! Once the Command agent is configured to receive commands, scan point licenses are consumed by each unique phone number that is able to send an SMS command to this Command agent i.e. by both the configured recipient phone number and these additional cell phone numbers that are specified or used to send SMS messages to it. There are two methods by which these additional callers can be specified: - Anonymous access: This requires the least configuration, although it provides unrestricted access in that anyone who phones the recipient will be able to send commands to this Command agent. For details, see Configuring Anonymous Caller Access . PLEASE NOTE: In this case EVERY unique caller who phones the recipient and issues a command to the Command agent will consume a scan point license, which will not be released until the Agent Server is shutdown. - Authorised access: This requires the cell phone numbers of all the callers who are allowed to issue commands to this Command agent to be added to the Cmd phone numbers list. However, only these additional callers are able to ‘command’ this agent and hence will consume scan licenses. For details, see Configuring Authorised Caller Access . Note: This list can hold a maximum of 10 numbers. Tip: Since these commands are able to obtain and/or control any process value or slot exposed by the Agent Server, it is recommended to BOTH specify the authorised phone numbers AND to limit these command-able phone numbers for security reasons. -->

Specifying Incident Reasons and/or Notes Top Specifying Incident Reasons and/or Notes The AlarmManagement agent provides an Incident reasons and notes dialog to specify reasons and/or notes for a selected incident in the database.

Title: Specifications
Specifying Incident Reasons and/or Notes Top Specifying Incident Reasons and/or Notes The AlarmManagement agent provides an Incident reasons and notes dialog to specify reasons and/or notes for a selected incident in the database. In other words this dialog allows you to select the reason and its sub-reason that caused the incident to occur and/or to specify any other textual description or note concerning this incident. Tip: The ReasonsRequired status bit of the AlarmManagement agent is enabled when there are incidents that require reasons and/or notes (this can take up to 30 seconds to reflect the current status). Note: The dialog status is now sensitive to the Alarm Management agent name so that the correct set of outstanding reasons and notes are displayed in a proxy server environment, where multiple AlarmManagement agents may exist. Depending upon the configuration of the incident either the reason and/or note may be mandatory displays the current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled and as yet unspecified. To specify a reason: this requires you to select a reason AND a sub-reason that best describes the cause of this incident. - Select the most applicable reason for this incident from the Reasons list of the Incident reasons and notes dialog. - Select the most applicable sub-reason (or cause) of this incident from the Sub-reasons list. - Click the OK button. This logs the specified reason to the database of this AlarmManagement agent. To specify a note: this note should typically include some explanatory detail concerning the cause and action taken concerning this incident, especially if this is not adequately explained by the selected reason or sub-reason. - Type the required text into the Notes edit field of the Incident reasons and notes dialog. - Click the OK button. This logs the specified note to the database of this AlarmManagement agent. If necessary, you can also launch the Incident reasons and notes dialog from a button or another picture element on a Classic UI mimic, see Customizing the launching of the View Reasons Dialog . -->

text:
- Edit the required Command agent.

Title: To select which commands a Command agent is able to perform:
- Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. - If necessary, select the General tab, the default selection. - Under the Commands group, ensure that the Enable commands checkbox is checked. - Check or clear, the checkboxes next to the available commands, listed beneath each of the following checkboxes, as required: Note: For details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . - Allow ‘Get’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to retrieve the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the GetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see GET Commands or Specific Status Bits . Note: This command does not pose a security risk since process values are only received. - Allow ‘Set’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to modify the value of any tag (agent.slot) exposed by the Agent Server and the SetCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see SET Commands . WARNING! Since this command can cause a serious security and operational risk, additional settings are provided to further restrict its usage. For details, see Additional SET Command Restrictions . - Allow ‘Ack’ commands: If checked, this will allow this agent to globally and/or locally acknowledge alarms that have been reported by an agent within the Agent Server. The AckCommands specific status bit for this agent will also be checked, to indicate this. For details, see ACK Commands . Note: This command DOES pose a security risk since alarms can be acknowledged remotely. -->

- Either use the Browse for Graphic Form task: this task is provided by the Task menu, which is displayed when the control is initially added and can be accessed by clicking its glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the selected control.

Title: To select the default graphic form:
- Either use the Browse for Graphic Form task: this task is provided by the Task menu, which is displayed when the control is initially added and can be accessed by clicking its glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of the selected control. Using the Browse for Graphic Form task: - If necessary, add the TemplateGONavToolbar control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding TemplateGONavToolbar controls . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this TemplateGONavToolbar control. - If necessary, click the glyph, which is usually displayed in the top left corner of this control, to display the menu of tasks - Click the Browse for Graphic Form... hyperlink to display the Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog. This contains an explorer view of all of the projects and their graphic forms configured within the Projects category of each Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . - Select the required graphic form within this explorer view. Tip: It is also possible to select the required graphic form by double-clicking on it. - Only check the Include Server Name in selection checkbox if you SPECIFICALLY want this control to ONLY connect to this specific Server, otherwise if unchecked the control will look for this graphic form on the currently specified default (logon) Server. - Check the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox option, if you want to ensure that the specified graphic form will still be located when the project name is renamed or when this graphic form is copied to another project, while preserving its relative path. - Click Finish . The fully qualified namespace of the currently selected graphic form is displayed in the field at the bottom of the explorer view, which adheres to the following format: ProjectName.{Folder(s)Name(s)}.GraphicFormName, where {..} indicates that the Folder(s)Name(s) are optional and depend upon the organization of this project. Note: If the Exclude Project Name (Relative Path) checkbox is checked then this does NOT provide the ProjectName portion. If the Include Server Name in selection checkbox is checked then this also includes the following at the beginning: [MachineName] ServerName. - The specified graphic form should be displayed within the control. Note: This control can be configured to automatically resize to contain this graphic form, by enabling its AutoResize property. - Or use the GraphicFormPath property of this control to browse for the required graphic form. Using the GraphicFormPath property: - If necessary, add the TemplateGONavToolbarNavToolbar control to the required graphic form. For details, see Adding TemplateGONavToolbarNavToolbar controls . - Select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. this TemplateGONavToolbar control. - Open the Properties tool window, navigate to the GraphicFormPath property and select it. - Click on the browse button to the right of its value cell. The Graphic Form Selection configuration dialog is displayed, which contains an explorer view of all of the projects and their graphic forms configured within the Projects category of each Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . - Select the required graphic form within this explorer view. Tip: It is also possible to select the required graphic form by double-clicking on it. - Only check the Include Server Name in selection checkbox if you SPECIFICALLY want this control to ONLY connect to this specific Server, otherwise if unchecked the control will look for this graphic form on the currently specified default (logon) Server.

Specifying the default time period for a historical trend Top Specifying the default time details and/or time navigation tools for a historical trend Note: This only applies to Line and XYPlot charts.

Title: Specifications
Specifying the default time period for a historical trend Top Specifying the default time details and/or time navigation tools for a historical trend Note: This only applies to Line and XYPlot charts. When designing a charting control to display a historical trend, you can use the Time Details configuration dialog to: - configure the charted time details for a real-time or historical trend. - specify which standard chart time navigation tools are displayed by the chart toolbar and/or to display 5 tools that change the chart timespan (chart duration), each of which can be customised as needed. Add the required Line or XYPlot charting control and then click its smart tag a glyph that usually displayed in the top left corner of the selected control or vector that when clicked displays a list of the commonly used configuration tasks. and select the Edit Time Details... link at the bottom of the Tasks list. To specify the default time details for a chart: use the Time Details tab to configure the charted time period and interval for a real-time or required charted time period for a historical trend.. Configure the charted time period from the Time Details tab of the Time Details configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: For ease of use, this tab uses the previously specified Period Type and Timespan time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc. To configure the charted time period for a real-time trend: - Select the Real-time (Current - Timespan) from the list of available Period Type methods for calculating the trended time period. - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. Note: The Timespan property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. For instance, if the trended data is being compacted together then reducing this time-span will result in the data to becoming more clearly differentiated. - If necessary, specify the required update rate for the trended data, in milliseconds, in the Interval edit box.

metadata.title: Specifying the default time period for a historical trend

text:
This specifies the interval or period of time in milliseconds that the trend advances in real time (shifts across the screen) or by which it is scrolled, by using the Scroll Left or Scroll Right tools (when provided by the chart toolbar).

Title: Specifications
This specifies the interval or period of time in milliseconds that the trend advances in real time (shifts across the screen) or by which it is scrolled, by using the Scroll Left or Scroll Right tools (when provided by the chart toolbar). Note1: The Interval property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. Note2: The Interval property is not required for static trends. To configure the charted time period for a historical trend: Note1: The Timespan property is a sub-property of the TimeInfo property. Note2: IGNORE the Real-time (Current - Timespan) option! Select one of the following Period Type methods for calculating the required time period: - End Datetime - Timespan: This calculates the required starting date and time, by subtracting the Timespan from the End date and time: . - If necessary, change the currently specified End date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. For details, see Changing the date and/or time . - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. - Start Datetime + Timespan: This calculates the required ending date and time, by adding the Timespan to the Start date and time: - If necessary, change the currently specified Start date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. For details, see Changing the date and/or time . - If necessary, specify the required duration of time that is displayed, by selecting the required time dimension e.g. Hours, Days etc., from the list box to the right of the Timespan edit box and then specifying the required amount in this edit box. - Start Datetime to End Datetime: This calculates the required time-span to be displayed by this charting control, by subtracting the Start date and time from the End date and time: - If necessary, change the currently specified Start date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. - If necessary, change the currently specified End date and time , which is displayed as: day month year hours:minutes:seconds. For details, see Changing the date and/or time .

metadata.title: Specifying the default time period for a historical trend

text:
To configure the chart time navigation tools: use the Navigation tab to specify which chart time navigation tools are displayed by the chart toolbar and/or configure up to 5 tools that configure custom chart timespans (chart durations).

Title: Specifications
To configure the chart time navigation tools: use the Navigation tab to specify which chart time navigation tools are displayed by the chart toolbar and/or configure up to 5 tools that configure custom chart timespans (chart durations). Use the Navigation group of the Navigation tab of the Time Details configuration dialog, to specify which of the following chart time navigation and/or configuration tools you want the chart toolbar to provide, by checking or clearing the relevant checkboxes: Note: The Interval and Timespan properties are typically configured in the Time Details tab of this Time Details dialog. - Show RealTime : when enabled (checked) this displays the Go to real time mode tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the chart right (forward in time) until the real time values of the data are displayed in the chart. - Show Page Right : when enabled (checked) this displays the Page Right tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed data right (forward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). - Show Scroll Right : when enabled (checked) this displays the Scroll Right tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed right (or forward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property. - Show Scroll Left : when enabled this displays the Scroll Left tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed left (backward in time) by the period of time specified by the Interval property. - Show Page Left : when enabled this displays the Page Left tool in the chart toolbar, which moves the “window” of displayed data left (backward in time) by the period of time specified by the current width of the chart (i.e. by the chart Timespan property). - Show Custom Navigation : This enables (checked) the Custom Navigation group that always displays five tools that when selected configure the Timespan property of this chart to specific time durations. The specified duration becomes the label of each tool. The default chart durations are, as follows: 1 hour , 12 hours , 1 day , 7 days and 30 days . Note: You can customise the required Timespan and time units of each of these five tools , as needed. -->

metadata.title: Specifying the default time period for a historical trend

text:
- If necessary, add a Command agent.

Title: Specifications
- If necessary, add a Command agent. For details, see Adding Agents . - Edit the required Command agent. For details, see Editing Agents . This will display the Edit Command agent dialog. - Select the Phone tab. - Under the Phone Settings group, ensure that the Use ‘GSM_SMS’ Device checkbox is checked. Example: if the Server is on 10.10.10.10 the Clients must also be on the 10.10.10 subnet (only the last digit can differ). This provides the added advantage that graphic forms open faster, since the visual components of the configured spiders are not loaded. Spider regions Top Spider regions Spider regions organise (de-clutter) the Design view of spider workspaces.

Title: Spider regions
Spider regions Top Spider regions Spider regions organise (de-clutter) the Design view of spider workspaces. Each spider region is a logical grouping of spiders, which can be expanded or collapsed to display or hide these spiders. Typically you create a spider region when one or more spiders have something in common. Note1: Each spider can only belong to one spider region. Note2: Spider regions can be interacted with much like spider configuration views. To add a spider region to the spider workspace - Open the required spider workspace. - Right-click the spider workspace and select New Region . This adds the region with a default name of 'Spider_Region#', where # is added when there is more than one. Tip: Rename this region so that its purpose can be clearly identified. To rename a spider region - Open the required spider workspace and locate the required region. - Right-click the title bar of the required spider region and select Rename . - Specify the required name for this region, in the Rename Spider Region dialog. Tip: Provide a meaningful yet concise name - try to keep it less than the full 30 characters. To expand or collapse a spider region - Open the required spider workspace and locate the required region. - Double-click the title bar of the required spider region. Note: An expanded spider region resizes itself to contain all its added spiders and is displayed on top of any other spiders or spider regions. To add an existing spider to a spider region - Open the required spider workspace. - Right-click the title bar of the spider and select the Move To Region menu and choose the name of the required region from the list. - If the spider region is expanded, then drag the spider to the required position within the spider region. - If the spider region is collapsed, then drag the spider onto the title bar of this spider region. To add a new spider to a spider region - Open the required spider workspace and locate the required region. - Select the required spider region. - Right-click and select Create New Spider and select the required spider from the menu. Note: If using the Create New Spider toolbar button, move the spider to the required spider region, once it has been added. To move a spider region - Open the required spider workspace and locate the required region. - Drag the title bar of the spider region to the required position. To delete a spider region - Open the required spider workspace and locate the required region. - Right-click the title bar of the required spider region and select Delete . If this spider region contains spiders, a confirmation dialog is displayed to determine whether the spiders contained in this spider region should also be deleted or not. To delete all unused (empty) spider regions - Open the required spider workspace. - Right-click the spider workspace and select the Delete All Unused Regions item. You can also: Hide unselected regions . Rearrange regions . -->

For details, see Data spiders . - Double-clicking the title bar of the spider can be used to display or hide its configuration view. - Right-click the title bar of any spider to display a menu of available options. In addition to hiding ALL the unselected spiders and regions, three other selective hiding filters can be applied. Start Communications Top Start Communications Either if the Start Comms item in the File menu is selected after the WanClient is launched or if the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, this will initiate the following sequence of events: - A check is made to ensure that there is an Agent Server that is currently running on the local computer.

Title: Start Communications
Start Communications Top Start Communications Either if the Start Comms item in the File menu is selected after the WanClient is launched or if the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, this will initiate the following sequence of events: - A check is made to ensure that there is an Agent Server that is currently running on the local computer. If this fails, this error is reported in the WanClient message window and an appropriate warning message is displayed. - The main database is loaded - The main database is opened. If the main database does not contain any configured servers then this error is reported in the WanClient message window. - WanClient then connects to the local Agent Server - The database is then closed - WanClient then begins the process of connecting to the configured servers by PINGing them. - When a WanServer responds to the PING, the WanClient will send it its list of tags that it needs to subscribe to and the required polling periods of each tag. The WanClient will then request from the connected WanServers their changed data. Note: As soon as an error is reported, this communication process terminates. When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. -->

text:
Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe from Another Recipe Top Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe from Another Recipe Example: A Master Recipe with two Control Recipes, Run_Cool and Run_Heat, that run batches of control recipes Cool and Heat of the recipe agent SET_TEMPERATURE.

Title: Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe from Another Recipe
Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe from Another Recipe Top Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe from Another Recipe Example: A Master Recipe with two Control Recipes, Run_Cool and Run_Heat, that run batches of control recipes Cool and Heat of the recipe agent SET_TEMPERATURE. When the control recipe Run_Cool is active, the following will happen: - Set SET_TEMPERATURE.currentRecipeName = "Cool"; i.e. select control recipe Cool. - Initiate the verification check for phase 1 (Step 1). That is, wait for the preconfigured verification time before continuing. - If SET_TEMPERATURE.currentRecipeName = "Cool", then verification passed; i.e. the selection of control recipe Cool was successful. - End of phase 1 (Step 1), go to next step. - Set SET_TEMPERATURE.batchPrefix = "Cool#". - Set SET_TEMPERATURE.batchCounter = 1. Hence, the batch name for control recipe Cool becomes "Cool#1". - Set SET_TEMPERATURE.runRecipe = "Cool"; i.e. activate control recipe Cool. - End of phase 2 (Step 2-4). If SET_TEMPERATURE.statusBit17 = 0, wait until it becomes equal to 1 and move on to the next step. That is, wait for SET_TEMPERATURE to become Active and then continue. - End of phase 3 (Step 5). If SET_TEMPERATURE.statusBit16 = 0, wait until it becomes equal to 1 and move on to the next step. That is, wait for control recipe Cool to finish and then continue. - End of phase 4 (Step 6). Go to step 4. Hence, batches of control recipe Cool will be activated continuously until control recipe Run_Cool is stopped. -->

Statically or dynamically resizing graphic forms Top Statically or dynamically resizing graphic forms There are two ways to specify the size of your graphic form: - Statically : to manually specify the size of the graphic form within the Designer workspace and/or by using the Properties tool window.

Title: Statically or dynamically resizing graphic forms
Statically or dynamically resizing graphic forms Top Statically or dynamically resizing graphic forms There are two ways to specify the size of your graphic form: - Statically : to manually specify the size of the graphic form within the Designer workspace and/or by using the Properties tool window. In this case, the size of this graphic form is the actual size that the end-user will see too. To statically resize a graphic form in the Designer workspace: - Open the required graphic form. - Click on the graphic form itself to cause the eight sizing handles small boxes that appear around the perimeter of a selected item, which if dragged changes the size of this item. See drag. to appear, one at all four corners and one in the middle of each side. - Click and drag one of the white sizing handles that appear on the right and bottom borders of the graphic form. Note: The sizing handles on the top and left borders of the graphic form are grey because they cannot be moved. Tip: Pressing the ARROW keys while holding down the SHIFT key allows you to resize the form more precisely. To statically resize a graphic form using the Properties window: - Open the required graphic form. - Click on the graphic form itself to select its properties in the Properties tool window. - In the Properties tool window, click the size property and enter values for the width and height, separated by a comma. For details, see Accessing tool windows . Tip: You can expand the size property to enter the Width and Height values individually. - Dynamically : to cater for monitors of different aspect ratios by scaling the graphic form to fit the SmartUI Operator regardless of its displayed resolution. To dynamically resize a graphic form: - Open the required graphic form. - Click on the graphic form itself to select its properties in the Properties tool window. In the Properties tool window: - Click the ResizeChildren property and ensure that it is set to True . - If you want the graphic form scaling to maintain the aspect ratio of this graphic form, which is typically required for small graphic forms, then click the PreserveAspectRatio property and ensure that it is also set to True . Note1: This disabled the AutoScrolling property of this graphic form, since there is no need to display graphic form scroll bars, in this case.

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. - Configure: This displays the configuration dialog to select and configure the required data collection method. For details, see Selecting and configuring data collection methods . Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Analog Value Double The analog (floating point) value, from which data is collected to calculate statistical information, which is displayed in the Outputs section. For details, see Collecting data . Reset Boolean [A Button] To clear the collected data for Analog Value , which resets all of the calculated outputs to 0, except for Minimum and Maximum which are set to the current Analog Value at runtime. For details, see Clearing collected data . - Outputs , this section contains the outputs from this spider. Output Data Function Data Collection Method String The sampling method by which the data is collected. Minimum Double The minimum value of all the data currently collected. Maximum Double The maximum value of all the data currently collected. Total Double The sum of all the data currently collected. Mean Double The arithmetic mean or average of all the data currently collected. Standard Deviation Double The standard deviation of all the data currently collected. Note: At any time during the monitoring period, click the Reset button to clear all the collected data, resetting the calculated output values to 0. -->

- A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series . This simplifies chart configuration and provides a preview pane in which you can see the effects of the various display options before they are implemented. To launch the configuration dialog: right click the charting control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. Note: The configuration dialog is the ONLY way in which you can chart data from a DataBinder. Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations Top Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations IMPORTANT: It is compulsory that Adroit Distributed systems are time synchronised , since clustering and other important aspects of Adroit are compromised by an unsynchronised system.

Title: How to set up Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations
Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations Top Synchronizing Distributed Adroit Installations IMPORTANT: It is compulsory that Adroit Distributed systems are time synchronised , since clustering and other important aspects of Adroit are compromised by an unsynchronised system. This can be accomplished by ensuring that the W32Time service is enabled and working. If so, Active Directory domain member computers will automatically synchronise with the domain controller, however, Workgroup computers must ensure that they are synchronised to the same source. Also ensure that the country selection in the Regional Settings in the Control Panel is the same on all the computers. CAUTION: If the system clock is set back, the mimics, alarming and datalogging may appear to cease working and look as if the system has frozen. This is because Adroit will discard any time stamped data that is older than that currently held in the User Interface; since it always displays or records the latest events it receives. When the system clock reaches the time it was set back, the mimics, alarms and datalogging will come alive again. -->

Title: How to synchronise the SCADA tags in the MAPS database and in the Adroit SCADA:
Steps:
Tip: If necessary, you can now perform the Sync Tags process in silent mode, if you choose to do so then all confirmation dialogs normally displayed during this process are hidden and you are only presented with the final dialog showing the success or failure of this process. When creating a MAPS project, each plant Area has an associated Adroit Agent Server that contains the SCADA tags for the equipment within this plant Area. So you will typically: - Synchronise the SCADA tags in a specific plant area, as follows: Tip: This is recommended after adding/removing equipment to/from a number of units in a specific plant area In the MAPS window, right click the required plant Area of the MAPS project and select Sync Tags. - Synchronise the SCADA tags in a specific unit, as follows: Tip: This is recommended after adding/removing multiple equipment to/from a single unit - so that you ONLY need to synchronises this specific unit and not the entire plant area. In the MAPS window, right click the required unit of the MAPS project and select Sync Tags. Note: You can also select the Sync Tags right click option for each electrical or instrumentation equipment that you add. The Sync Tags command displays a splash screen, at the bottom of which you can see the total number of equipment whose tags need to be synchronised and as each item of equipment is analysed, the tag differences are displayed here too. Note: Depending upon the number of equipment, this process can take some time. Once the tag synchronization process is finished, the Tag Data dialog is displayed so that you can see which SCADA tags need to be added or removed to/from Adroit . If you are happy with this result, click Finish to add (and perform the SCADA configuration dictated by the respective MAPS template, such as scanning, logging, alarming and/or trending) or remove the SCADA tags; otherwise click Cancel to abort this operation. Note: Depending upon the number of tags, this process can take some time. -->

Tag Groups Top Tag Groups The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer.

Title: Tag Groups
Tag Groups Top Tag Groups The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. These tags are organised using one or more groups, which primarily manage their required communication settings. Although there are other criteria that can be used when organizing tags into groups. For details, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . While the groups provide the tag-specific communication settings, servers provide the group-specific communication settings to access the required WanServers. Therefore groups are server-specific i.e. they can only be configured after the required server(s) have been configured. For details, see Configuring Servers . Tag Groups can be configured, as follows: - To configure a new tag group . - To edit an existing tag group . - To delete an existing tag group . - To recover a formerly deleted tag group . - To manually edit tag groups – this may be necessary when adding a large number of tag groups at once. -->

Tag Links Top Tag Links The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer.

Title: Tag Links
Tag Links Top Tag Links The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. A tag link or tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server, which together provide the communication settings, required by the WanClient to connect to the necessary WanServers. For details, see Servers or Tag Groups . Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. Tag Links can be configured, as follows: - To configure a new tag link . - To edit an existing tag link . - To delete an existing tag link . Note: Any link that is deleted is permanently removed from the database and cannot be recovered later. - To manually edit tag links – this may be necessary when adding a large number of tag links to one or more groups at once. -->

Tag to Field Mapping Buttons Top Tag to Field Mapping Buttons To add a new tag-to-field mapping simply click the button. To remove a tag-to-field mapping, click the button. To send the timestamp of this transaction to the database, click Transaction Time button, either after adding another tag-to field mapping or selecting any cell of the mapping to be used for recording the time of the transaction. This button will automatically replace the Tag field with ‘ Transaction Time ’, which will generate the time and date of the transaction in a format recognised by all databases. Note1: By default the time that is generated by ‘ Transaction Time ’, contains millisecond resolution, which is NOT supported by the Date/Time fields in Access databases, use a Text field instead, if millisecond time resolution is required. Note2: If an alternate time and date format is required, make use of the date/time field specifiers , but if this format is not recognised by the database then the entire transaction will fail. Alternatively, both the analog and digital agents have a time slot that represents the timestamp of the value slot. This slot can also be sent to the database table if the timestamp is required. Note: You CANNOT export DBAccess agents that contain single quotes (‘) in their format strings. -->

Tag-specific Scanning Settings Top Tag-specific Scanning Settings These settings are the scanning-specific Control bits , which are usually configured in the required agent's header .

Title: Specifications
Tag-specific Scanning Settings Top Tag-specific Scanning Settings These settings are the scanning-specific Control bits , which are usually configured in the required agent's header . These settings apply to all the scanned slots of the agent for which they are configured. Note1: Changes made to these settings ONLY take effect when the device(s) used to scan the slots of the configured agent(s) is restarted. Note2: By this usage "scan" implies "reading", hence "scanOutput" implies "writing’. - Output Enable: If this bit is set, it will enable the agent to update the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanOutputEnable or statusBit09. - Scan Inhibit: If this bit is set, it will stop the agent from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). This does not affect the agent from updating a PLC (front-end device). Slot name: statusScanInhibit or statusBit08. - Output Initialise: If this bit is set, an initial value will be scanned out from the agent at startup, or after any communications failure and subsequent recovery. Slot name: statusScanInitialise or statusBit11. -->

Temporarily Suspending Alarming Top Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting) Usually you need to suspend ( shelve alarm shelving is the process of removing an alarm from the entire alarm system for a specific time period.

Title: Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting)
Temporarily Suspending Alarming Top Temporarily Suspending Alarming (Alarm Shelving or Alarm Inhibiting) Usually you need to suspend ( shelve alarm shelving is the process of removing an alarm from the entire alarm system for a specific time period. This also known as inhibiting an alarm. ) alarming temporarily when you are performing maintenance on a plant section or a particular item of equipment or when an alarm indicator is not functioning correctly or is being tested. Depending upon the scope of the required shutdown and the configuration of your alarming, you are able to temporarily suspend alarming in the following two ways: - Globally per Alarm agent: this option should only be used when an Alarm agent ONLY manages all the alarming of the plant section that is being shutdown or the plant item/s that are being shutdown for maintenance or repair. WARNING! If you do not have an alarming strategy and do not know which areas of the plant are controlled by which Alarm agents then DO NOT USE this method. To disable the alarming of an Alarm agent: - Edit the required Alarm agent. - Select the General tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - Click the No option in the Enable Alarming section of the General dialog. - Click the OK button. To enable the alarming of an Alarm agent: - Edit the required Alarm agent. - Select the General tab from the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. - Click the Yes option in the Enable Alarming section of the General dialog. - Click the OK button. - Individually per incident: this option should be used when an alarm indicator may be malfunctioning or may need to be repaired or replaced or in situations when you need to disable ALL the alarms of a particular item of equipment and you cannot disable the alarming of an Alarm agent. To temporarily inhibit incidents: this method requires you to specify the future time at which this incident will be re-enabled, in other words the time at which this temporary stoppage will end. - Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click this agent and select the Alarm… menu item. - Click on the required alarm type in the Current list of the Alarming dialog. - Check the Inhibited until checkbox at the bottom of this dialog.

- Specify the future time at which this incident will be re-enabled, in other words the time at which this temporary stoppage will end, as follows: To specify a future date: - Click the button of the list box - Specify the required date using the supplied calendar. The current date is selected by default. To specify a future time: Use the spin control to specify this time, as follows: The spin control displays the time in 12 hour format as HH:MM:SS AM/PM To change the hour: - Click the hour digits to the far left of the time control. - Either type in the required hour - Or use the spin control buttons to increment/decrement the current hour to select this. To change the minutes: - Click the hour digits to the far left of the time control. - Either type in the required hour - Or use the spin control buttons to increment/decrement the current hour to select this. To change the seconds: - Click the hour digits to the far left of the time control. - Either type in the required hour - Or use the spin control buttons to increment/decrement the current hour to select this. To change AM/PM: - Click the hour digits to the far left of the time control. - Either type in the required hour - Or use the spin control buttons to increment/decrement the current hour to select this. - If necessary, repeat this procedure until you have temporarily inhibited all the required alarm types. Advantage: ONLY the affected incidents are disabled for a predefined period of time, after which they are automatically enabled. Limitation: This requires prior planning and you need to know WHEN the stoppage will cease. To temporarily inhibit active and/or unacknowledged incidents: this method allows you to immediately inhibit current incidents that are active and/or unacknowledged. IMPORTANT: You must REVERSE the following change MANUALLY, when you need this agent to produce alarms again. - Select the required agent, in other words the agent containing the alarmed alarm type/s. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click this agent and select the Header… menu item. - If necessary, clear (uncheck) the View derived agent status checkbox. This should enable the Control bits section. - Check the Alarm inhibit checkbox in the Control bits section. - Click the OK button.

Testing that the Derived Custom agent Operates Correctly Top Testing that the Derived Custom agent Operates Correctly Check the functionality that is provided by the script by executing suitable tests on the agent. For the DriveXYZ agent, because some of the required slots that need to be tested are not configurable from the configuration dialog, some of the following tests are performed using the command-line putslot utility as follows: - Change the value of HighTemp slot to 50 and click the Update button, assuming the Live tick box is not enabled. - From Start menu, select the Run… command and type the following into the edit box: putslot drivexyz1.temperature,60 and click Ok . - Then click the Refresh button in the configuration dialog to ensure that this slot has changed appropriately. - Then click the Header button to ensure that TempHi status bit has been set in this agent’s header dialog. - From Start menu, select the Run… command and type the following into the edit box: putslot drivexyz1.tripped,1 and click Ok. - Then click the Refresh button in the configuration dialog to ensure that this slot has changed appropriately. - Then click the Header button to ensure that Trip status bit has been set in this agent’s header dialog. - Change the Start slot to 1 and click the Refresh button in the configuration dialog, continuously to check that this Start slot rests to 0 after 3 seconds. - Repeat step 4 for the Stop slot. -->
