When the agent is first enabled, it works as follows: - If the intervalMode slot property is set to 4, a new period will commence immediately.

Title: Operation
When the agent is first enabled, it works as follows: - If the intervalMode slot property is set to 4, a new period will commence immediately. - If the intervalMode slot property is set to 3, the period will commence immediately but will end at the next synchronised period. - At the end of every period, the value is saved as lastValue and the new value is calculated as inputValue minus startValue . - If a SQL Server connection is configured, a new record is added to the history table (see History below) containing the period end time, the value for the period as well as the current inputValue . - A new period commences immediately and the startValue (=inputValue) is recorded.

The minimum required configuration for the Accumulator agent: - Define an inputTag OR scan the inputValue and then enable the agent.

Title: Configuration
The minimum required configuration for the Accumulator agent: - Define an inputTag OR scan the inputValue and then enable the agent. - Define a triggerTag and triggerMode OR a method of driving the trigger slot.

When a trigger event occurs: - The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period.

Title: Trigger event
When a trigger event occurs: - The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period. - This results in a value which represents “the total production for the last hour or shift or day and so-on” . - It then calculates the rate of change in value, which is the differential value for the current period divided by the interval of this period (value per hour) .

You can also configure alarm limits for both the differential value and rate of change in value for the current period, which will monitor.

Title: Alarming
You can also configure alarm limits for both the differential value and rate of change in value for the current period, which will monitor the current value or rate against these alarm limits: - high-high - high - low - low-low Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bit , which can also be alarmed.

To maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals, you should connect the Accumulator agent to a SQL Server database: - Each record captures the start and end times of the period, the start and end values and the differential value for the period.

Title: History
To maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals, you should connect the Accumulator agent to a SQL Server database: - Each record captures the start and end times of the period, the start and end values and the differential value for the period. - To provide automatic management of this data, then a housekeeping period can be defined to ensure that it keeps the most relevant or most recent records only. - If a valid connection and table is specified, the History table is created as follows: Column name Type Description idx Int Auto incrementing index dt datetime Period end date and time value float Calculated value for period accumulator float The accumulator reading (inputValue) at the end of the period

For further details, read the following topics: - Configuring Accumulator Agents - How to configure some or all of the functionality for an Accumulator agent.

Title: Further Information
For further details, read the following topics: - Configuring Accumulator Agents - How to configure some or all of the functionality for an Accumulator agent. - Specific Status Bits of the Accumulator Agent - Specific status bits of the agent represent the agent-specific conditions that can be alarmed or directly displayed on a graphic form to indicate when these conditions occur. - Accumulator Agent - Slot Details - All the slots (values) contained in this agent. -->

The Agent Server Window Tray Icon Top The Agent Server Window Tray Icon Normally, when the Agent Server window is minimised, it appears in the task bar along with any other currently open program, such as on start up. But if the Minimise to tray command, in the Agent Server window's Options menu , is selected, then the Agent Server window appears as a tray icon in the bottom right of the screen, whenever it is minimised. Note: If the Minimise to tray command is selected then on the next startup the AS will immediately startup as a tray icon, similarly if this is disabled then on the next startup the AS will startup as an AS window. The Agent Server tray icon indicates the status of the Agent Server as follows: - The flashing yellow light indicates that the Agent Server is loading. - The green light indicates that the Agent Server is running. - The red light indicates that the Agent Server is shutting down. Note: If the mouse pointer is held over the icon, a tool tip will also appear indicating the current status of the Agent Server. Either right or left click on the tray icon, to display its menu with the following commands: - The Adroit Agent Server… command, this displays the Adroit version information dialog. - The Explorer command, which launches the Adroit Project Explorer once the Agent Server has loaded. - The Show server window command, this displays the Agent Server window and hence removes the Agent Server window icon from the tray. This icon is only returned to the tray when the Agent Server window is minimised. - The Log System events command, this enables all internal events in the Agent Server to be logged to the event log. A tick symbol alongside this command indicates that it has been selected. Note: This is a duplication of the command located in the Debug sub-menu of the Options menu in the Agent Server window. - The Stop server… command, this displays the confirmation dialog for closing down the Agent Server on the computer. -->

text:
The AgentGroup Agent Top The AgentGroup Agent Agents that are considered to have something in common can be combined into groups by means of AgentGroup agents.

Title: The AgentGroup Agent
The AgentGroup Agent Top The AgentGroup Agent Agents that are considered to have something in common can be combined into groups by means of AgentGroup agents. For instance, all agents belonging to the north side of a process plant could be grouped in the NORTH_PLANT agent group. Agent groups may, and usually do, have overlapping memberships (i.e. an agent is allowed to belong to more than one group). For details, see Grouping Agents Together . - Normal mode, the AgentGroup agent simply acts as a container for the agents grouped with it, and does not modify its status if any of its group member’s status changes. - Fan in status bits mode, the AgentGroup agent will set its status bits in accordance with the status bits of its members. Only one member agent needs to set a given status bit for it to be "fanned in" to the AgentGroup’s status bit. - Bulk editing of agent type mode, this is only possible if all the agents contained by the AgentGroup are of the same type, any changes made to an AgentGroup agent’s control status bits will "fan-out" to the same control bits belonging to the members of the group. Furthermore, only this mode will ungrey Edit Members button. Slots to expose via OPC Server (comma separated) : this field (the exposeViaOpc slot) allows you to specify which slots, of the agents that have been added to this group, that you want to be browsable by the Adroit OPC Server. Note1: This comma separated list of slots cannot exceed 80 characters in length. Note2: While this feature is not intended for mixed agent groups, any specified slot not supported by a member agent type will be ignored. Clicking the Edit Members button will bring up the appropriate Edit Agent dialog for the member type and allow bulk editing of the member’s slots. As an example, consider the situation when part of a plant (say the North Plant) is shut down for routine maintenance, and it is required to disable scanning of all agents belonging to this plant section. The AgentGroup Agent Top The AgentGroup Agent Agents that are considered to have something in common can be combined into groups by means of AgentGroup agents.

Title: The AgentGroup Agent
The AgentGroup Agent Top The AgentGroup Agent Agents that are considered to have something in common can be combined into groups by means of AgentGroup agents. For instance, all agents belonging to the north side of a process plant could be grouped in the NORTH_PLANT agent group. Agent groups may, and usually do, have overlapping memberships (i.e. an agent is allowed to belong to more than one group). For details, see Grouping Agents Together . - Normal mode, the AgentGroup agent simply acts as a container for the agents grouped with it, and does not modify its status if any of its group member’s status changes. - Fan in status bits mode, the AgentGroup agent will set its status bits in accordance with the status bits of its members. Only one member agent needs to set a given status bit for it to be "fanned in" to the AgentGroup’s status bit. - Bulk editing of agent type mode, this is only possible if all the agents contained by the AgentGroup are of the same type, any changes made to an AgentGroup agent’s control status bits will "fan-out" to the same control bits belonging to the members of the group. Furthermore, only this mode will ungrey Edit Members button. The AlarmManagement Agent Top The AlarmManagement Agent Alarm Management is an important aspect of process control required to counteract inefficient alarming.

Title: The AlarmManagement Agent
The AlarmManagement Agent Top The AlarmManagement Agent Alarm Management is an important aspect of process control required to counteract inefficient alarming. Alarm management allows you to create an alarming system that alerts the operator to the most relevant alarm for the current incident. In this case fewer alarms are more effective as the human mind can only focus on a few things at a time. For details, see About Alarm Management . The AlarmManagement agent logs all incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). and their details, including their time of occurrence, their time of acknowledgement and the time at which they were cleared to a database. This repository of incidents allows you to: - generate statistics from the data produced by the alarming system. This allows you to have efficient and meaningful incident reviews to identify and remove nuisance alarms by analysing the counts, frequencies, durations and acknowledgement times of alarms. - measure KPIs to improve your alarming configuration. For details, see Obtaining KPI Values . For the recommended method of implementing the AlarmManagement agent to configure and record your active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. incidents so that you can improve your alarming configuration, see Quick Start to Configure and Record Incidents (Alarms/Events) . Note1 : You can only add ONE AlarmManagement agent. Note2: Ensure that your Adroit license is licensed to enable your AlarmManagement agent to function. Tip: An unlicensed AlarmManagement agent can log your historical acknowledged alarms. For details, see Historical Alarm mode . Multiple Agent Servers may log incidents to the same database thereby unifying alarm management for the enterprise. However, in this case please ensure that your AlarmManagement agent is uniquely named as each incident is logged using the name of its assigned AlarmManagement agent.

Repeating this process at regular intervals will eventually create relevant alarms, which result in the following benefits: - Improves the operator environment, workload and efficiency - Avoids unplanned outages - Improves plant reliability The review process must be a repetitive and cyclical process, for the following reasons: - Alarms are generally added without prior forethought - Your process changes over time - Your equipment changes and degrades over time - Seasonal changes The AlarmManagement agent is designed to help you implement the first 3 of t he following 5 phases of ongoing Alarm Management: - Alarm and Event Archiving: although already accomplished by Adroit , this is improved by the new AlarmManagement agent.

The Alias Agent Top The Alias Agent An alias is an assumed or "false" name of another agent.

Title: The Alias Agent
The Alias Agent Top The Alias Agent An alias is an assumed or "false" name of another agent. By containing a reference to the agent it is aliasing, the Alias agent appears to have the same Behaviour and state information of the agent it is referencing, differing only in its identity. Aliases can be very useful when attaching Behaviours to picture elements, which are to be repeatedly reused for different scenarios, such as recipes, particularly if the source agent is unknown. By simply reconfiguring the Alias agent to reference the desired agent for each scenario, the need to re-edit all the Behaviours on each picture element is eliminated. For example, a rectangular picture element with fill Behaviour supplied by tag ALI01 can be switched from REC01 to REC02 by simply re-editing the Alias agent or by dynamically changing the contents of the Alias agent’s tagname slot from REC01 to REC02 using the Operator Action, Data Set Behaviour. To access the slots of the Alias agent directly (as opposed to the slots of the agent it is aliasing), preface it with a % symbol to override its de-referencing. Note: that when browsing the slots of an Alias agent using the Agent Explorer, you will not be able to see this slot. Instead, the % symbol and the tagname slot must be typed in manually into the relevant Behaviour dialog. E.g. %ALI01.tagname Note: Alias agents may not be scanned. Alias Agent - Slot Details . Alias Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Analog Agent Top The Analog Agent An Analog agent stores a real (floating point) value that provides the following functionality: - Scaling its value according to user defined minimum and maximum scaling settings.

Title: The Analog Agent
The Analog Agent Top The Analog Agent An Analog agent stores a real (floating point) value that provides the following functionality: - Scaling its value according to user defined minimum and maximum scaling settings. These scaling parameters are typically only specified, when a front-end device contains this value. The Analog agent provides support for up to 51 bit numbers, in that the new maximum range is 2,000,000,000,000,000 for unsigned numbers or -1,000,000,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000,000,000 for signed numbers. Note: To reduce the loss of accuracy in scaling caused by IEEE conversion issues, the Analog agent bypasses the scaling calculation, when the scaling is 1:1. - Monitoring its value against one or more of the following value-specific alarm limits: low-low, low, high, high-high and/or rate of change. Any infringement of these alarm limits causes the agent to set its corresponding status bits, which can be alarmed. - Specifying the engineering units used to measure this value. - Monitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a status bit, which can be alarmed. - Calculating statistics from the value slot every second, for a specific rolling period (specified in minutes). For details, see Calculating statistics from Analog values . - Recording the time this value changes, which is saved to the time slot a value (attribute) or field within an agent that can be retrieved and/or set. of this agent - Reverse polarity scaling and the remote configuration of the alarm limits - Square root extraction for the linearization of flow signals, - Alarm deadband settings for the high and low alarm limits - A cold start value initialization option when starting the Agent Server. For details on how to configure some or all of this functionality for an Analog agent, see Configuring Analog Agents . IMPORTANT CHANGE FOR ANALOG AGENTS: Changed the default method of handling what happens when the rawvalue slot goes out of range (either exceeds the rawMax value or is lower than the rawMin value), from now this causes the Analog agent to set the new OutOfRange status bit (which can be alarmed if needed).

This is to prevent the entire agent from being marked at as being bad, as happened previously, which causes all the instances of this value to be greyed out (disabled) on the mimics which display them.

Title: The Analog Agent
This is to prevent the entire agent from being marked at as being bad, as happened previously, which causes all the instances of this value to be greyed out (disabled) on the mimics which display them. Note: If you prefer the legacy method of marking the agent bad (setting the statusAgentBad condition bit) when the rawvalue slot goes out of range, then you need to add the OutOfRangeEqualsAgentBad registry setting. Typically Analog agents should be used for tank levels or any process value stored in a front-end device that needs to be scaled (converted) to and from its engineering value and/or that needs to be closely monitored and/or alarmed. If you ONLY want to store a real (floating point) value then use the Real agent instead. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue with the current configuration settings including its scaling and alarm limit settings. For details of the specific status bits of this agent that represent the agent-specific conditions that can be alarmed or directly displayed on a mimic to indicate when these conditions occur, see Specific Status Bits of the Analog Agent . For a description of all the slots (values) contained in this agent, see Analog Agent Slots . For a description of how this agent is saved in the Adroit database (.WGP) file, see Analog Agent Database File Format . -->

The ARec Agent Top The ARec Agent The ARec agent or "Associated digital Record" agent, is a fancy version of the Multistate agent that enables the configuration of up to 255 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits.

Title: The ARec Agent
Steps:
The ARec Agent Top The ARec Agent The ARec agent or "Associated digital Record" agent, is a fancy version of the Multistate agent that enables the configuration of up to 255 states using truth table type logic on up to 32 bits. These 32 bits can be mapped to individual digital tags or the complete 32 bit value can be scanned from an external value. Each state can be configured to test a mask of the bits for ON, OFF or DON'T CARE conditions and can also be tested for timeouts and can be used to set status bits. In addition, each state, or timed out state, can be configured to set or clear one or more of the 32 input bits, allowing this agent to be used as a sequence controller. It is also possible to configure the AREC agent as a numerical sequence , to display text, similar to the StringList agent, except that the AREC supports up to 255 sequence steps and enables these steps to set its status bits. To edit or configure an AREC agent . Configure a Truth Table . Configure the I/O Bits . Configure the States . Configuration a Numerical Sequence . Configure the Sequence Steps . Specific Status Bits . ARec Agent - Slot Details . ARec Agent - Database File Format . -->

Adr_Audit_Sessions table: these records provide the details of each Agent Server session each time an application is started and stopped on a computer constitutes a single session of this program. . This table contains the following fields: - Idx: A consecutive index for each session logged to this table. - dt: The date and time at which this session was started. The format of this field depends upon your Regional Settings. - Session ID : A unique session identification number generated by Adroit that the Adroit_Activity_Audit table uses to identify the session in which each activity is performed. Tip: Since the Session ID contains the name of the computer and Agent Server, you can create a central database for all Agent Servers on your network. - Computer : The name of the computer on which the Agent Server is running. - AS name : The name of the Agent Server, this is the name specified in the Agent Server Name field of the Agent Server tab in the Adroit Setup utility. - Cluster : The name of the cluster that this Agent Server is part of, if any, so that you can identify which Agent Servers are clustered pairs. - Shutdown : The date and time at which this session was stopped. Note: If there is no entry, this means that the session was forcibly closed, for instance via the Task Manager or due to a power failure. Adr_Audit_Activity table: these records provide the details of the activities performed within these Agent Server sessions. This table contains the following fields: - Idx : A consecutive index for each session logged to this table. - dt : The date and time at which this activity was LOGGED by the Agent Server and NOT the date and time at which this activity was PERFORMED.

In other words this data and time relates this activity to everything else that is being audited for this Agent Server.

The Basics of the OLE Server Interface Top The Basics of the OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The Adroit OLE server objects leverage OLE infrastructure.

Title: The Basics of the OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR)
The Basics of the OLE Server Interface Top The Basics of the OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) The Adroit OLE server objects leverage OLE infrastructure. This may seem daunting to an end user, but the use of OLE actually makes an end user’s life easier. When talking about objects, a whole litany of terminology tends to arise. In OLE, the coarse grained entities are typically referred to as objects and containers. The words of the great OLE architect, Tony Williams, define these best. He says: "There are things, and there are places to put things". The "things" are the objects. The "places" are containers. In our case, the "things" or objects are local or remote Agent Server(s), and the "places" or containers are shrink wrapped or custom applications, written using Visual Basic™, Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, or any other OLE-aware application development platform. WOSA/XRT forces us to address another piece of terminology: OLE Automation. Extending Tony’s quote, we can say: "There are things, places to put them, and ways to talk to them". The way we talk to a thing (object) is OLE Automation. OLE Automation is simply a way for software, structured as an OLE object, to expose internal functions such that other applications can call them. -->

The Beeper Agent Top The Beeper Agent The Beeper agent provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker and is usually controlled by an Alarm agent.

Title: The Beeper Agent
The Beeper Agent Top The Beeper Agent The Beeper agent provides simple audio output using the built-in PC loudspeaker and is usually controlled by an Alarm agent. The beeping sound is started when the value in the start slot is set to an integer greater than zero. The pitch or tone of the beeping sound depends on the contents of the start slot, and will become higher as it is incremented. The Alarm agent puts a value equal to the number of current unacknowledged alarms into this slot, to indicate that more than one agent is in alarm at the same time. Note: The pitch increases each time a new alarm is signaled, and decreases when an alarm is acknowledged. When the start slot is set to zero, or the reset slot is pulsed, the beeping sound will stop. The beeping sounds will become more urgent (i.e. interval between beeps will decrease) if the Beeper agent’s priority is increased from 0 to 4. This is a useful feature if you wish to route high priority alarms with high priority settings to one Beeper agent and low priority alarms with low priority settings to another Beeper agent. Normally, the contents of the start slot will not be saved to the loadfile (WGP file, by clicking the Save toolbar button or File menu item when the Configurator window is selected or when the Agent Server is Shutdown (if the SaveonExit advanced option is enabled). To save the contents of this slot, check the Store values when saving checkbox, which sets the dataPersist slot to 1. Beeper Agent - Slot Details . Beeper Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Command Agent Top The Command Agent The Command agent can send and receive SMS messages, by using a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver to bypass the scanning subsystem with its imposed scanning limitation of 79 character strings, so that the full 160-character SMS message length can be used.

Title: The Command Agent
The Command Agent Top The Command Agent The Command agent can send and receive SMS messages, by using a device of the GSM_SMS protocol driver to bypass the scanning subsystem with its imposed scanning limitation of 79 character strings, so that the full 160-character SMS message length can be used. Its name is derived from its ability to also receive commands within these textual messages, which can manage Adroit remotely. Note: The sole function of this new GSM_SMS driver is to send and receive SMS messages to and from a SMS GSM modem. For details, see About the GSM_SMS driver . For details, concerning the configuration and use of this agent, see Configuring Command Agents . This agent, unlike the Notify agent, provides the following functionality: Note: If necessary, this agent can be used to SMS alarms received by the Notify agent instead. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots . - The ability to BOTH send and receive SMS messages of up to the full 160 character SMS message limit, instead of being restricted to only 79 characters. - Send SMS messages to a single recipient, manually, programmatically or automatically to remotely monitor the status of important process values. For further details, see Sending SMS Messages . - Sent SMS messages can also be monitored for auditing purposes. The Configuration grid Top The Configuration grid The Configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which displays information about the Adroit configuration of the selected computer, as follows: Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
The Configuration grid Top The Configuration grid The Configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which displays information about the Adroit configuration of the selected computer, as follows: Note: The grid provides the following standard configuration options . For instance any cell entries that are displayed in blue, in the grid, can be both edited or replaced . - The first untitled field numbers the information items in the grid. - Item: This field specifies the configuration item, which is being displayed. - Setting: This field specifies the current configuration of the specified item. The following list describes what the listed Configuration Items refer to: - Server type: This field, specifies the current type of Agent Server that is running on the selected computer, as follows: - Type 0 - Cluster Server: In this case master or standby mode assignment is necessary and duplicate databases need to maintained on each. - Type 1 - Cluster aware server: In this case Proxy agents are created if remote duplicate tags are found. - Type 2 - Stand-alone server: In this case Proxy agents are not created if remote duplicate tags are found. - Server name: This field specifies the configuration of the Agent Server name to be used when it starts up. This must be unique across the same network and when more than one Agent Server is being used within a project, ensure that the first 7 characters are unique. - Project name: This field specifies the configuration of the project name to be used by the Agent Server when it starts up. This project name must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. - WGP file: This field specifies the path and name that the WGP or Agent Server database file will be saved to. - Adroit directory: This field specifies the path where the Adroit system files, executables and dynamic link libraries, are stored, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . - Channels: This field specifies the maximum number channels used by the Agent Server when it starts up. A channel is a Client-Server connection from the Agent Server to the outside world, such as to the User Interface, other Agent Servers, the Adroit OPC Server etc. The default setting is 20. - Max agents: This field specifies the maximum number of agents used by the Agent Server when it starts up. This number accounts for both the number of agents in the project and additional Agent Servers explicitly connected to the project. Hence determine the number of expected agents on all the connected Agent Servers and multiply this by two. - Save on exit: Change this Setting field to 1, to force the saving of the WGP file when the Agent Server is shut down. This is valid for the current session only. The default value is 0. - Installed devices: This field lists the currently configured devices to which tags can be scanned. Additional devices can be added using the Adroit Setup on this computer. For details, see Add Device . - Log system events enabled: Change this Setting field to 1, to enable the logging of such events e.g. when time-stamped data is rejected by a mimic for being to old. The default value is 0. -->

These parameters should be configured in Adroit Setup (Config) BEFORE the Agent Server is started.

Title: Parameters on startup
These parameters should be configured in Adroit Setup (Config) BEFORE the Agent Server is started. - startMaxChannels : This specifies the maximum number channels used by this Agent Server. A channel is a Client-Server connection from the Agent Server to the outside world, such as to the User Interface, other Agent Servers, DDE links. The default setting is 20. - startGranularity : This specifies the time granularity used by the Agent Server, which is the time interval, in seconds, that this SystemInformation agent updates itself. - startProject : This specifies the current project name of this Agent Server. This project name must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. - startName : This specifies the name of this Agent Server. This must be unique across the same network and when more than one Agent Server is being used within a project, ensure that the first 7 characters are unique. - startLoadFile : This specifies which agent database file is loaded by the Agent Server when it starts up. - maxAgents : This specifies the total number of agents that this Agent Server can use. This number accounts for both the number of agents in the project and additional Agent Servers explicitly connected to the project. Hence determine the number of expected agents on all the connected Agent Servers and multiply this number by two. - startSaveOnExit : The status of this checkbox indicates whether the WGP file is forced to save when the Agent Server is shut down. Note: On large installations, saving can take a long time, so for quick shutdowns, leave this unchecked and manually save at planned intervals. - startDebug : This is a bit mask of the Debug flags as found in Adroit Setup (Config), which should only be configured by advanced users. -->

The DataLog Agent Top The DataLog Agent Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created.

Title: The DataLog Agent
The DataLog Agent Top The DataLog Agent Note: Any datalogs that cause their .LGD file to be greater than 2 GB will fail to start and user is notified accordingly and an associated eventlog entry is also created. Adroit provides extensive historical logging facilities, this includes the existing proprietary data logging via the DataLog agent and the DBLog agent , which is a bulk OLE DB logging agent for typically logging Analog and/or Digital values to a specific table in a database for later retrieval. Note: If you export and delete Datalog agents that use Adroit 's proprietary log files, ensure that you restart the Agent Server before re-importing - so that they can remove the areas that they currently use in the LGD files. Click for more details: Multiple Datalog agents can potentially use a single LGD file, so when you delete a Datalog agent using proprietary logging all that happens is the area of the file that was used by the deleted Datalog agent is marked as unused and will be compacted at the next Agent Server startup. Therefore if you re-create the Datalog agent in the same Agent Server session, the LGD resource simply adds the space required for the newly added Datalog to the end of the LGD file i.e. it does not re-use the old area that has been marked as unused. This can cause the LGD file to become too big, resulting in errors such as an error message asking you to check your Datalog agent configuration (in Agent Server window you may also get a Datalog agent dll exception) and your Datalog agents may not start. When you restart the Agent Server , the old areas of the LGD file are compacted and room is left to re-create the datalogs. IMPORTANT: When modifying and/or creating Datalog agents via an exported CSV file, leave the UID column empty. Note: Multiple log sets are no longer required as Adroit provides the DBLog agent that should make SQL logging via the Datalog agent redundant. Also you no longer need multiple proprietary sets with increasing periods and larger time deadbands, since Adroit provides a new datalog backup feature with full trend-retrieval support. As with scanning, any slot of any agent can be configured to have its values historically logged, providing that it is a Real , Integer , Boolean or 79 character String (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). The agent is created by selecting the Log button in the Configurator dialog. When logged, the values are time stamped and are made available, via a DataLog agent, to any client. Examples of data log clients are historical trends, the extract utility, OLE-aware 3 rd party applications etc. Note: If an Agent Server, in HMI mode , is being used, then data logging is restricted to 24 consecutive hours. To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure . Advanced Datalog Configuration : global settings that affect the operation of the data logging sub system. Historical Data Management . Note: Backup (LGB) files can be created when logging to the Adroit proprietary datalog (.LGD) files so that this historical data can be retrieved by the datalogging system when needed. This can also create CSV files too, to make this historical data available to third party applications such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . Viewing logged data . Exporting logged data to a CSV file . DataLog Agent - Slot Details . DataLog Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Date Agent Top The Date Agent Date agents are particularly useful when used in conjunction with Extract , the historical log extraction utility, in which case slots of Date agents can be used to reference dates and times, instead of cumbersome command-line parameters.

Title: The Date Agent
The Date Agent Top The Date Agent Date agents are particularly useful when used in conjunction with Extract , the historical log extraction utility, in which case slots of Date agents can be used to reference dates and times, instead of cumbersome command-line parameters. The Date agent holds in its slots the localTime , universal UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time, which is a time standard that couples Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is based solely on the Earth's inconsistent rotation rate, with the highly accurate International Atomic Time (TAI). time, the time since 00h00 1st Jan 1970 as an integer (cTime) , and a breakdown of the local time into year , month , day , hour , minute , second and millisecond slots. The format slot governs the way in which the date and time are displayed in the asciiTime slot. Triggering the setTime slot causes the agent local time to be updated by the system clock. Any change to a slot (except the asciiTime slot) will cause all the slot values to be updated to their relevant values. Note: You should never externally manipulate the localtime slot of the Date agent from a mimic using an operator action. The localtime slot must be used for viewing the time and the ucttime slot MUST be used for manipulating the datetime value. This is by design of the Date agent only. All other time slots in Adroit can be viewed and edited directly. The format argument consists of one or more codes , which are preceded by a percent sign (%). Note: An additional flag (#) may prefix any formatting code after its % symbol. Date Agent - Slot Details . Date Agent - Database File Format . -->

The DbAccess Agent Top The DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle, by using OLE DB technology, supported by Microsoft.

Title: The DbAccess Agent
The DbAccess Agent Top The DbAccess Agent The DbAccess Agent provides a link between Adroit and various external databases such as Access, SQL Server, FoxPro and Oracle, by using OLE DB technology, supported by Microsoft. OLE DB connectivity means that Adroit can connect to any OLE DB provider, unlike ODBC that was only created to provide access to relational databases. The DbAccess Agent allows Adroit to share its information with 3rd party applications that use databases to store information. These 3rd party applications may be responsible for optimised control, reporting, MES, ERP or many other enterprise solutions. As each DbAccess agent is responsible for a transaction on a row in a database, it allows the user to specify how and where he wants the data to be stored which is ideal for reporting. Note: If a connection fails, due to network problems etc. the DbAccess agent will recover and continue transacting. The DbAccess agent allows the following transactions to be performed: new rows can be added to an existing table; existing rows can be updated with current information; specific rows or the entire table can be deleted and data can be retrieved from the table inserted into tags inside the Agent Server. These transactions can be done on demand, they can be scheduled and (or) they can be triggered. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. The DbAccess agent is ideally used in applications where data inside the Agent Server is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job) for reporting reasons. It is not suited for fast logging of data. Usage Guidelines . Basic Principles . Configuring the DbAccess Agent . Connection string Tag to database table field mapping . Field Format Specifiers . Using SQL Queries within Identify Row . Extended SQL Querying . Support has been added for databases, which require square brackets around the field names otherwise their SQL transactions fail. If required, add the ForceJet registry value . Transaction scheduling and triggering . Details . Specific Status Bits . To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input that is transferred to a database . DbAccess Agent – Slot Details . DbAccess Agent – Database File Format . -->

- DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected.

Title: Configuration
- DBLog1 writes data to Table1 and is configured with no housekeeping: So housekeeping will NOT run on Table1, as expected. - DBLog2 writes data to Table2 and housekeeping is configured: So the specified housekeeping WILL run on Table2, as expected. - DBLog3 and DBLog4 writes data to the same table Table34 - - DBLog3 is configured with no housekeeping AND - DBLog4 is configured with 30 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping WILL run on Table34 as per DBLog4’s housekeeping configuration for this SHARED table. - DBLog5 and DBLog6 writes data to the same table Table56 - - DBLog5 is configured with 30 days housekeeping AND - DBLog6 is configured with 90 days housekeeping: So Housekeeping will run on Table34 as per DBLog5’s housekeeping configuration and the data older than 30 days will be deleted, since the SHORTEST housekeeping period is always used as this is the period that is reached first for this SHARED table. - a method of dealing with a problematic connection to the specified database is (if the connection is lost) or when this agent is logging a large number of tags frequently so that it becomes overworked, as follows: This agent provides a queue of values waiting to be logged to the specified database (or buffer), when the number of items in this queue exceeds 5000, the currently unlogged transactions are dumped to a .SQL file in the C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work folder. These .SQL files can be manually loaded into SQL Enterprise manager and executed to “catch up” this data. Each file name uses the following format: DBLogAgentName_Y_M_D_H_M_S.sql. Tip: The INTEGER queuesize slot, specifies the current number of items in this queue, which you can use to determine how close the agent is to dumping these logging transactions to a .SQL file. Since this value should always tend to zero. Tip: If you want to analyse your logged data then, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the General Reports report pack, which includes standard reports on the DBLog agent data. Configuring DBLog Agents : to configure operational options, the tag list, the OLE DB database and table name and housekeeping parameters, if required.

Once the DBLog Agent has been configured and enabled, it creates table /s in the specified database with the following fields: - id : a unique indexing identifier - dt : the Timestamp of the logged value - Tagname : the name of the tag being logged - Value :– the value of the tag being logged - Quality : an indication of whether value of this logged tag was good or bad data has a bad status when data is missing, incorrectly reported or extrapolated.

Configuring the DBQuery agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below.

Title: Configuration
Configuring the DBQuery agent Configuration of the DBQuery agent is processed via the dialog, as shown below. The agent dialog provides the ability to set several options: (See the Configuration slots option for more information.) - Enable or disable the functionality of this particular agent. - Disable transactions executed on the standby server. - Select the trigger method to use and optionally also the trigger tag. - Enter the execution interval value in seconds. - Set the auto-reset runNow option. - Enter the SQL Server connection string. - Enter the required tag list. - Enter the required Table name . - Enter the WHERE clause containing tag names within an angled bracket (< >) pair. The agent automatically substitutes these tags into values first and then performs the following example SELECT statement transaction: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) - Enter a custom query. Let’s have a look at a few Custom Query examples. If a SELECT query returns more than one record, the agent will use the first record only. - Should you want to use the newest record from the result of a SELECT statement, you could use the example custom query as shown below: SELECT f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC Because Adroit only uses the first record returned, the example custom query could effectively be changed to: SELECT TOP 1 f3,f4,f5,f6 FROM Table_1 WHERE (f1=12) AND (f2=13) ORDER BY dt DESC NOTE: - Should a custom SELECT query be used then the ‘SQL table name’, ‘WHERE clause’ and ‘Field’ column entries in the tag list will be ignored because you would add this information to the custom query. - Custom SELECT queries will substitute the ‘Tagname’ entries in the tag list with values returned from the custom query, therefore it is important to ensure that the custom SELECT query requests the data in the order required by order of the ‘Tagname’ entries.

For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname.

Title: Other Custom Query examples
For the query below to work, the tag list should only contain only one entry specifying a tagname. SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM MyTable WHERE f1=12 - The ‘Field’ name is disregarded. - If more than one tag is specified the agent will assume failure with the above query.

The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019.

Title: Delete records
The query below will delete all records older than 1st Jan 2019. The query disregards the contents of the tag list in the dialog. DELETE FROM MyTable WHERE dt < “2019-01-01”

The queries below will insert a new record to the table.

Title: Insert records
The queries below will insert a new record to the table. The queries will disregard the contents of the tag list in the dialog. INSERT INTO MyTable (f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (1, 1, 123, 456 ,678, 901) or INSERT INTO MyTable (dt, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6) VALUES (<systeminfo.currenttime>, 1, 1, <f1.value>,<f2.value>,<f3.value>,<f4.value>)

The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes.

Title: Execute Query Automatically
The query below can use f1.value tag as a trigger tag to automatically have the DBQuery agent execute every time the tag value changes SELECT date,timestart,timeend FROM shift_adv_sh1 WHERE idx=<f1.value>

The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameters as may be required by the stored procedure EXEC spCheckRecords 1,5 For all SELECT queries or stored procedures which return data, these results will be substituted into the tags as specified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names.

Title: Running Stored Procedures
The query below will execute the spHousekeeping stored procedure EXEC spHousekeeping The query below will execute the spCheckRecords stored procedure with parameters as may be required by the stored procedure EXEC spCheckRecords 1,5 For all SELECT queries or stored procedures which return data, these results will be substituted into the tags as specified in the tag list and also as governed by the corresponding field names. If the field names are not supplied by the result, as may happen with stored procedures, you can do one of the following: - Simply apply the index number to use e.g. 0, 1 or 2. or - Leave the field name empty for the tag entry, The agent will then attempt to use the row number (beginning with 0) of the tag entry as the field name.

DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file.

Title: Agent Slots
Steps:
DBQuery Configuration slots The following slots are used for configuration and are saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description connection VARSTRING The OLE DB connection string | “global” can be selected to use the Agent Server’s audit connection string. customQuery VARSTRING An option for a valid SQL query statement to be performed on the database connection. - If a custom query is specified, this will always be executed instead of the built-in SELECT query statement. disableOnStandby BOOLEAN When set to [1], the slot indicates that the transaction should not be executed on the standby server. enable BOOLEAN When set to [1] the slot is enabled to Start or alternatively, when set to [0] to disable the agent. interval INTEGER An optional number of seconds may be entered that will determine the execution interval of the transaction. - A value of [0] (default) disables this feature. method INTEGER Sets a trigger tag check value. You can set method value to one of the following: 0 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value goes to zero. 1 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value leaves zero. 2 – Execute the query when the trigger tag value changes. The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. tagList LIST Sets the list of tag values to be retrieved by the built-in SELECT statement. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. triggerTag TAGNAME The trigger tag to be used. - Indicates the trigger tag used in conjunction with the trigger method. - This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . - The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). - A value of [0] will disable the pulse. - Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. - The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that will be applied to the built-in SELECT statement. DBQuery Information slots The following slots are used for information only and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description badTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every unsuccessful transaction and denotes the number of bad transactions since starting the agent server. goodTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every successful transaction and denotes the number of good transactions since starting the agent server. lastDuration INTEGER A slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. - Successful transactions will display “None”. lastErrorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. - This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently set to on [1]. lastQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the last SQL Query that was executed. lastTime TIME This slot captures the last time a transaction was executed. resetRunNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ this slot will cause the agent to automatically reset the runNow slot value to ‘0’ after a transaction has completed. - The default value is set to enabled. - This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC. runNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ the agent will execute a transaction ONLY if the agent is enabled AND connected to the database.

totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started.

Title: Agent Slots
Steps:
totalTransactions INTEGER This slot tallies the total number of transactions executed since the agent server was last started. DBQuery Runtime slots The following slots are used for runtime operations and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery agent functions. Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. - If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. - The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. - Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. - Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. SuccessPulse Also known as StatusBit18 A short pulse is generated on a successful transaction. - The default length of this pulse can configured using the pulseWidth configuration slot. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms or as set in the pulseWidth slot) , if the last transaction succeeded. -->

The default value is [1]. tableName STRING The name of the table that the built-in SELECT statement should use. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. tagList LIST Sets the list of tag values to be retrieved by the built-in SELECT statement. - This is available only if the custom query is not used. triggerTag TAGNAME The trigger tag to be used. - Indicates the trigger tag used in conjunction with the trigger method. - This is available for trigger methods only. pulseWidth INTEGER Edit this slot to set the pulse length of the Status slot: SuccessPulse [StatusBit18] . - The pulse length is set in milliseconds (ms). - A value of [0] will disable the pulse. - Note: Any value less than 5 ms will always cause a minimum pulse width of around 5 ms. - The default value is [100] ms. whereClause VARSTRING Sets the WHERE clause that will be applied to the built-in SELECT statement. DBQuery Information slots The following slots are used for information only and are NOT saved to the WGP file. Slot name Slot type Slot description badTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every unsuccessful transaction and denotes the number of bad transactions since starting the agent server. goodTransactions INTEGER A slot value that is incremented after every successful transaction and denotes the number of good transactions since starting the agent server. lastDuration INTEGER A slot value that represents the duration of time in milliseconds that the query took to execute the last transaction. lastError VARSTRING This slot captures the last OLE DB transaction error. - Successful transactions will display “None”. lastErrorQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the SQL Query that caused the last OLE DB transaction error. - This value is never cleared and is only valid if the FAILED status bit (StatusBit21 ) is currently set to on [1]. lastQuery VARSTRING This slot captures the last SQL Query that was executed. lastTime TIME This slot captures the last time a transaction was executed. resetRunNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ this slot will cause the agent to automatically reset the runNow slot value to ‘0’ after a transaction has completed. - The default value is set to enabled. - This should be disabled when the agent communicates the runNow slot value directly to the PLC. runNow BOOLEAN When set to ‘1’ the agent will execute a transaction ONLY if the agent is enabled AND connected to the database.

Slot name Slot type Slot description catchupData RAWBYTES For internal use during real-time catch-up. DBQuery Status slots The following slots indicate the status of certain DBQuery agent functions. Status name Status description Connected Also known as StatusBit16 This slot is set to on [1], if the Agent is connected to the database as of the last transaction. - If the agent is not enabled, the slot will always be set off [0]. - The slot will be also be set to off [0] should the agent become disconnected from the database. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database. - Important: It is important to note that some transactions may take up to one minute to transact, if there is a problem with the connection. Disconnected Also known as StatusBit17 This slot is set to on [0], if the Agent is not connected to the database possibly due to a last transaction error or that the database is not available. - Note: Be aware that if the agent is not enabled, this slot will always be set on [1]. Failed Also known as StatusBit21 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction failed. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. The Device Agent Top The Device Agent Device agents are used to manage the Adroit -specific communication settings of one or more tags (agent.slot) for a device that has already been added to an installed protocol driver.

Title: The Device Agent
The Device Agent Top The Device Agent Device agents are used to manage the Adroit -specific communication settings of one or more tags (agent.slot) for a device that has already been added to an installed protocol driver. This device is typically a logical connection to a front-end device, with which it communicates. For further details concerning the role this agent plays in communicating values, see the Scanning Overview . For this reason, Device agents cannot simply be added to the Agent Server like other agents. Instead its associated ‘device’ must first be added to an installed protocol driver. For details, see About Protocol Drivers . Then it is only when this device, which appears in the Device list in the Tag scanning configuration dialog, is selected when scanning a tag (agent.slot), for the first time, that a Device agent with the same name is added to the Agent Server. For details, see Scanning Adroit tags . NASA, stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. For more details, see Demand Scanning . The purpose of a Device agent is simply to manage the Adroit tags that have been scanned to it and their communication to and from its associated front-end device, as follows: - The Device agent automatically creates Scan agents, which generally contain a manageable amount of tags that are scanned to contiguous addresses. Each Scan agent manages the scanning configuration of their assigned Adroit tags, such as their poll rate, deadband, timestamps etc. For details, see Configuring Device Agents . Note1: The Device agent also removes these Scan agents when Adroit tags are unscanned from it. Note2: Since Scan agents are created dynamically, it is not recommended to use their slots in other agents, such as Expression agents, since their names are not fixed. - The Device agent also exposes the ‘device’ created in the Adroit Configuration Setup utility, through which the communication actually occurs to its front-end device. So it is able to stop and start the communication to and from this front-end device and configure its communication settings, if necessary. For details, see Configuring Device Agents . -->

The Digital Agent Top The Digital Agent A Digital agent stores a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE).

Title: The Digital Agent
The Digital Agent Top The Digital Agent A Digital agent stores a Boolean a value that only has two discrete states, 0 (FALSE) or 1 (TRUE). value that provides the following functionality: - Monitoring the current state of this value and setting its On or Off status bits accordingly, which can be alarmed. - User-configurable textual descriptions of its two states. - Monitoring its value for changes, where any change in value causes the agent to log an event and set a Changed status bit, which can be alarmed. - Recording the time this value changes, which is saved to the time slot of this agent. - Inverting the Raw value (typically this is the value that is scanned from the front-end device). - A cold start value initialization option when starting the Agent Server. - A pulsed output option to specify a user-configurable delay to maintain its ON state. For details on how to configure some or all of this functionality for a Digital agent, see Configuring Digital Agents . Typically Digital agents should be used for Boolean process values stored in a front-end device that may need to be inverted first and/or which needs its states to be closely monitored and/or alarmed. If you ONLY want to store a Boolean value then use the Boolean agent instead. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue with the current configuration settings. For details of the specific status bits of this agent that indicate the current state of this value and other agent-specific conditions that can be alarmed or directly displayed on a mimic to indicate when these conditions occur, see Specific Status Bits of the Digital Agent . For a description of how this agent can be used to create a half hour average of a process input, see To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input . For a description of all the slots (values) contained in this agent, see Digital Agent Slots . For a description of how this agent is saved in the Adroit database (.WGP) file, see Digital Agent Database File Format . -->

When the agent is enabled, the agent will wait for one of three events to happen before performing a snapshot: - The occurrence of the next hourly period.

Title: How it works
When the agent is enabled, the agent will wait for one of three events to happen before performing a snapshot: - The occurrence of the next hourly period. - The very first period is synchronised to midnight, meaning that if you specify an hourly interval of 8, the first snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. - After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. - A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot - A non-zero value trigger event of a selected trigger tag, when one is specified.

Configuring this agent provides the following options: - Select the agent types to be recorded.

Title: Configuration
Configuring this agent provides the following options: - Select the agent types to be recorded. - For each agent, you can specify CSV strings of specific and also which instances are to be recorded. - By default, these entries are specified as [*] to indicate all slots and all instances are selected. - Should you want to select only A1 and A2 agent instances, for example, then the entry would read A1, A2 - Optionally enable snapshots for the alarming and scanning configurations. - Set the hourly interval at which these snapshots should be recorded. - Specify a trigger tag for snapshot recording. - Enter the database connection string where these snapshot tables are to be created. Click on the options below to read more detailed information. Configuring the DumpConfig agent You can set up the DumpConfig agent to specify the configuration of specific agents that you want to save to the OLE DB database, including the interval and triggers. - To create a new agent or find an existing agent: - To add a new DumpConfig agent, see To Add a New Agent . - To open an existing agent, see To Select an Agent . - To begin, open the Edit DumpConfig Agent dialog. - Select the Edit menu item to display the Edit DumpConfig Agent dialog. - Select the Enable option to activate the agent. - Add the Agent configurations you want to save to the OLE DB database: - Click the + button to add a row to the Agent type configuration table. - Type in the name of the required Agent Type , ensuring that you spell this name correctly. - By default, all the Agent slots of the specified agent type, indicated by an [ * ], are included in each configuration, and all are saved to the database. - However, you can enter a comma-delimited list of slots to explicitly include the slots that you want to be saved. - This will reduce the size of each configuration and the processing time taken to log this data. - If you do want to use a comma-delimited list of the header slots that you want to save, enter the list in the following format: - agentName.headerSlot1, agentName.headerSlot2, agentName.headerSlot3 , and so on. Important: The optional comma-delimited list of Agent slots or Agent instances for the specified Agent type cannot exceed 79 characters! - You may optionally enable recording of the alarming or scanning configuration. - Select the Dump full Alarming configuration option. - Select the Dump full Scanning configuration option.

- Specify the time interval or event that will save the specified agent configurations to the database.

Title: Configuration
- Specify the time interval or event that will save the specified agent configurations to the database. - If required, enter the required Dump interval (in hours, 0 to disable) . - If set to a number greater than 0, then this number indicates an hourly interval used to trigger this agent. - If set to 0, this will disable this method of triggering this agent. - If required, enter the required Dump trigger tag . - Type in the required tag (agent.slot) or select the ... button to browse for the required tag containing a Boolean, integer or real value. - Whenever the value of this slot changes to a non-zero value, the specified agent configurations are saved to the database. - Alternatively, you can manually save the specified configurations to the database by clicking the Dump now button. - Specify the target OLE DB database to save the agent configurations. - In the Connection string box, type or select the ... button to browse for the connection details of the required OLE DB database. - You may also use an existing (or create) a SQL Server database to save your agent configurations. Note: - If you configure this DumpConfig agent from remote computers, it is safer to use SQL Server authentication (Use a specific user name and password) when creating this connection. - Avoid using Windows authentication ( Use Windows NT Integrated Security ) unless you are certain that the logged on users at the remote computers have the necessary access rights to this SQL Server database. - If the SQL Server connection string in the DumpConfig agent has been configured using Windows authentication, it will more than likely not work, and agent configurations will not be saved - Occurs if the Windows User on this remote computer has not been given access rights to the SQL Server database.

Title: Data Link Properties
Click the ... browse button to the right of this field and use the Data Link Properties dialog to create the required connection string to your SQL Server database. Provider TAB The Data Link Properties dialog specifies the location and the security credentials required to connect to this database. Double-click the Microsoft OLE DB Provider for SQL Server item in the Provider tab of the Data Link Properties dialog. Important: If the computer, on which SQL Server was installed, was renamed, then SQL Server may need to be re-installed. If the computer was renamed after installing SQL Server, then SQL Server must be re-installed, to function correctly. Run the following check: - Execute the following T-SQL (Transact-SQL) script in SQL Server Management Studio: SELECT @@SERVERNAME - If the resulting server name is different to the actual name of the computer, then the name of the computer has been changed after SQL Server was installed, so you need to reinstall SQL Server. Note: If you need to configure or view this database and its data from remote computers, then you should use a UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name path and not a local file path this path, as opposed to a UNC path, can ONLY be accessed from the computer that it refers to, this path adopts the following general format: <driveletter>:\directories\filename. to specify the location of this database. Connection Tab - Type in the computer name of the SQL Server that you want to connect to, in the Select or enter a server name field. - Tip: This is the fastest method if you know the name of the SQL Server. - Alternatively, click the drop-arrow button to the right of the Select or enter a server name box and select the name of the required SQL Server from the list. - Specify the required security credentials to connect to the selected SQL Server: Important: - If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to run the Agent Server service using the Local System account , then use SQL Server Authentication .

- If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to Use Windows NT Integrated security, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer has the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database.

Title: Data Link Properties
- If you need to connect to a remote SQL Server database and want to Use Windows NT Integrated security, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer has the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. - Use Windows NT Integrated security: this option uses the username and password of the currently signed in Windows user. - Tip: We recommend that you configure your SQL Servers to use this option to avoid requiring additional database security. - SQL Server Authentication: this option uses the User name and Password configured within the SQL Server you are attempting to connect to. - Note: In this case, it is recommended to select the Allow saving password checkbox. - Select the name of the required database from the Select the database on the server list box. - Click the Test Connection button to ensure that you are able to connect to this database using these details. Only proceed once 'Test connection succeeded' is displayed. - Click the OK button. - Your connection string will be created. Advanced Tab The Advanced tab of this dialog allows you to specify access permissions for this connection string. - If you are unsure about these settings, then never set these permissions to Read , otherwise this connection string will fail. - These security credentials are database specific and should not be confused with application security. - if necessary, you can edit this string directly, once it has been created.

The DumpConfig Agent The DumpConfig agent A DumpConfig agent simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database.

Title: Configuration
The DumpConfig Agent The DumpConfig agent A DumpConfig agent simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. One example for its use is when you need to report on agents in the context of their configuration at the time of the report, alternatively this could be used as an extensive method of auditing changes made to specific agents. For details on how to specify which agents' configurations you want to save to the OLE DB database and at what time or events their configurations should be saved, see Configuring DumpConfig Agents . Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue with dumping the specified agent configurations. For details of the specific status bits of this agent can be used for diagnosing the status of its connection to the database and/or monitoring the process of dumping agent configurations to this database, see Specific Status Bits of the DumpConfig Agent . Note: You can only add ONE DumpConfig agent. For a description of all the slots (values) contained in this agent, see DumpConfig Agent - Slot Details . For a description of how this agent is saved in the Adroit database (.WGP) file, see DumpConfig Agent - Database File Format .

The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings Top The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings The purpose of this topic is to describe what you can expect to happen when you combine the various scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED).

Title: The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings
The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings Top The Effect of Combining Scanning Settings The purpose of this topic is to describe what you can expect to happen when you combine the various scanning the process of communicating a value (slot), typically to and/or from a front-end device (FED). settings. For details on the various scanning strategies, see Scanning Strategies . There are two types of scanning settings that can be configured: - Global scanning settings – these require the Agent Server to be restarted, before any new setting change takes effect. - Tag-specific settings – these require the device(s) used to scan the slot(s) of the configured agent(s) to be restarted, before any new setting change takes effect. Note: A ‘process value’ of a tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). , is the current value at the front end device (PLC), whereas its ‘Agent Server value’ is the value of the tag in Adroit at runtime since the last read. PLEASE NOTE: The purpose of Cold start is to set the process value to a pre-configured value on startup and NOT the last saved WGP value! - If a tag’s scan inhibit bit is on there are NO guarantees that its Agent Server value will be the SAME as its process value. - If a tag’s scan inhibit and output enable bits are on, then the Agent Server changes will always be sent out but there are NO guarantees that its Agent Server value will be the SAME as its process value. - Forceoutputs (a global registry setting) always tries to synchronise the process values with the Agent Server values using write instructions if the process value is found not to be equal to the Agent Server value after a process read. Note: Forceoutputs only has effect if the tag’s scan inhibit bit is on. - Forceoutputs always synchronises the Agent Server with the process on the first scan after Agent Server startup. This can be overridden by setting the tag’s Output Initialise bit or using the global SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan (a global registry setting), whereupon the saved tag’s value will be sent to the process on the first scan. Note: SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan should NOT be used without using the Forceoutputs setting and therefore also requires the scan inhibit setting to be used. - If a tag’s scan inhibit and output enable bits are on and Forceoutputs is on, see the Agent Server Master Write Scanning Strategy as to its effects, which also shows the effect of using SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan. - If a tag’s scan inhibit and output enable bits are on and Forceoutputs is off or not used, then see the Write Only Scanning Strategy as to its effects, which also shows the effect of using SyncProcessToServerOnFirstScan. Note: This scanning configuration is NOT RECOMMENDED. -->

The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Top Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Note: Asynchronous or non-polling exception-based (telemetry) drivers are particularly affected by shadowed cluster servers.

Title: Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers
Steps:
The Effect of Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Top Using Shadowed Cluster Servers with Drivers Note: Asynchronous or non-polling exception-based (telemetry) drivers are particularly affected by shadowed cluster servers. When a second cluster partner, is started, it will start in standby mode and then any Classic UIs configured to attach to this newly started server will display any tags that are linked to "telemetry" device(s) as being "greyed-out" or marked bad. This is by design, since Adroit has no way of knowing what which of these tags are healthy at startup because of the unsolicited nature of these telemetry drivers. Therefore Adroit errs on the side of caution and greys out all the tags, this also protects the shadow system from mismatched databases in the cluster. Note: Normally, this should only be a problem on the UI of an unmanned cluster node, which is configured to connect locally, since all other remote UIs should be tracking the master. When the clustered servers are both online and the standby is "bad" because it has been started up later than the master, try one of the following: - Stop and restart the affected devices on the master server. - Swap master and standby at least once so-that the standby will become master and thus healthy as normal, the old master will become standby and remain healthy, and normal shadowing will take place from there on ... until one of the servers is restarted, then either re-implement method 1 or 2 again. - Leave it alone! If the standby takes over as master it will automatically become healthy due to the switch-over-shadowing. -->
