The EventLogging Agent Top The EventLogging Agent The logging of events in Adroit is managed by the EventLogging agent, which is provided as a destination for one or more alarm routes.

Title: The EventLogging Agent
The EventLogging Agent Top The EventLogging Agent The logging of events in Adroit is managed by the EventLogging agent, which is provided as a destination for one or more alarm routes. This agent is able to log events to the following locations: - to the Applications event log on any Windows computer on the network. - to an OLE DB compatible database, such as MS Access or MS SQL. Note: Events logged to this database CANNOT be viewed in the Event Log Viewer window. Typically, events include undesirable states, process values and the malfunction of control devices. Logged events are used to analyse process conditions over a specified period. Some of the types of events that can be logged by Adroit include: - incidents signified by AgentName.AlarmType, which indicate that this agent has gone into the condition or state specified by this alarm type. Each incident can either be an alarm (requiring action) or an event (not requiring action). : agents going into alarm, being acknowledged and cleared - change monitoring events : when the values of Analog or Digital agents change that are configured for change monitoring - control events: any operator control action that is configured to log events, such as the opening or closing of a valve, changing the set-point of a process controller, recipes etc - system events: the start-up and shutdown of the Agent Server, communication failures, etc - jottings: typically notes entered by control staff via the Execute Command Behaviour to indicate an unusual event, occurrence or action. For details on configuring the EventLogging agent, see Configuring the EventLogging Agent . If logging events to an event log, then set the size of this event log large enough to contain and/or overwrite old events. Since this Applications event log is a standard feature of the Windows operating system, this is configured by Windows. For details, see Setting up the Event Log in Windows . Adroit also provides additional event-specific settings, such as logging detailed Adroit system events for troubleshooting or changing the language of the event descriptions and categories. Instead of using the Windows Event Viewer to view these logged events, Adroit provides an Event Log Viewer window as an alternative, which allow you to perform the following functionality: - allows these events to be filtered - allows you to export the filtered events to a .TXT file. - allows you to save separate windows with their own filter view settings to .EFF files - allows you to archive the basic event log to .EVT files - allows you to print the logged events For details, see Event Log Viewer Windows. For details of the slots provides by this agent see EventLogging Slots . For details of which of the slots are saved the agent database file by this agent, see EventLogging Database File Format . -->

The Expression Agent Top The Expression Agent The Expression agent can create powerful user-defined calculations.

Title: The Expression Agent
The Expression Agent Top The Expression Agent The Expression agent can create powerful user-defined calculations. It functions by gathering data from other agents, or from the plant directly by scanning into slots V01 to V20, and performs a user defined mathematical transformation to calculate an output value. This result can be fed into a front-end device on the plant, or to a picture in the Classic User Interface for display, or sent to another agent. Note1: The Expression agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: It is not advisable to use the slots of scan agents in expressions, since the names of these agents are not fixed, but are changed by Adroit according to the scanning configuration. Data Acquisition . Display Options . Evaluation Options . Calculations . Examples . Agent Slot Details . Database File Format . By design, a triggered Expression agent will always generate subscription updates for the value slot even if the value slot has not actually changed, which can lead to unnecessary Agent Server CPU loads and network traffic when remote UI clients have been deployed. These unnecessary subscription updates can be disabled, by adding the PropagateTrigger registry value. The Expression agent can be combined and connected to several other Expression agents, so encouraging the use of standard expression building blocks and the reduction of complexity. The Expression agent contains: - Value slot that displays the result of the calculation (value). - Units slot that displays the units of measurement of the value. - Variables containing 20 input slots (V01-V20). - Expression slot containing terms and mathematical operators. - Display options for selecting whether values or names are shown. - Evaluation options that determine whether the calculation is on a continuous basis or triggered. - Trigger slot with a Calculate command button, which performs a calculation on demand irrespective of the state of the expression trigger. This would normally be used to verify calculations when configuring the Expression agent. - Specific Status Bits to reflect whether the value is equal to zero, greater than zero, less than zero, greater than or equal to zero, or less than or equal to zero. Expression Agent - Slot Details . Expression Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Frame Agent Top The Frame Agent A Frame agent can store 32 character strings (in slots V01 to V32 ), each string having a length of up to 79 characters (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character).

Title: The Frame Agent
The Frame Agent Top The Frame Agent A Frame agent can store 32 character strings (in slots V01 to V32 ), each string having a length of up to 79 characters (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). These character strings are indexed (from 1 to 32) and the current string being pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. By suitable indexing, the text string in the value slot can be made to change in a predetermined manner. For example, the Frame agent FRA01 has the four character strings cold , cool , warm and hot edited into its slots v01, v02, v03 and v04. If the value in FRA01.index slot is 4, then the character string hot will be duplicated in the FRA01.value slot. In this way, by subscribing to another agent’s integer slot type, the Frame agent can translate the subscribed value into an appropriate meaningful text message using its indexing Behaviour. Frame Agent - Slot Details . Frame Agent - Database File Format . -->

The ICMP Agent Top The ICMP or PING Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network.

Title: The ICMP or PING Agent
The ICMP Agent Top The ICMP or PING Agent The ICMP or PING agent uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data. The most common use of the ICMP protocol is by the PING diagnostic utility. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. This round trip time is the time that it takes to send an ICMP message to the remote IP address and to receive its reply. How to use the ICMP or PING agent to ensure the availability of a networked device Specific Status Bits of the ICMP Agent : this describes the status bits of this agent that can be used for diagnosing the existence of the specified remote device on the network. ICMP Agent - Slot Details ICMP Agent - Database File Format -->

As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP.

Title: Specifications
As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP. - All that is required is to first copy the default Adroit IOT agent x_iot.dll to a new file called t_2KVAPump.dll in the Adroit system folder, which is typically found at C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . - The newly copied agent type is then available to Adroit. - A newly created IOT agent can represent any object containing multiple properties or slots. - Currently, the IOT agent does not support real-time catch-up .

By default, - The IOT agent in itself does not contain any useful slots that are usable for end-user process purposes.

Title: Management slots
By default, - The IOT agent in itself does not contain any useful slots that are usable for end-user process purposes. - It does, however, contain four management slots that may be used to build up the structure of the IOT agent after it has been created. - Select the Agent Specific Slots option below to view more information.

When this agent is created, it only contains the management slots, one being the xmlSlots slot which is used to create and configure the user-defined slots.

Steps:

The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions, which are saved in the expression slot.

Title: Expression slot
The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions, which are saved in the expression slot. - The expression engine is similar to the expression engine used by UDP-Based Protocol (UDT) agents for manipulating status slot values (See the “ Creating UDT Status Bit Expressions ” topic). - However, the IOT agent lets users create multi-line expressions where each unique expression is used to drive a single IOT slot or a single status slot.

text:
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ?

Title: Using the addSlot
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above

This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section.

Title: Using the xmlSLot
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. - the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: - The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? - The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. - The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: - Boolean : a 1 or a 0 - Integer : a 4 byte signed integer - Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters - Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type - Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . - VarString : any number of characters - Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used.

The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot.

Title: Example of the XML structure
The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot. To facilitate easier reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name=" hi "/> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> Any number of <Slots> may be defined. A maximum of 16 <HeaderSlots> (status bits) may be defined. The first specified header slot represents status bit 16 and subsequent header slots will represent status bits 17 to 31. The XML code above can be saved to an XML file as a template and loaded in the IOT agent dialog. An example of IOT values XML packet for rawValue is a simplified version of the xmlSlots schema as follows with custom text shown in blue : <IOT><Slots><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></Slots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotValues><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></SlotValues></IOT> For improved reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT> <SlotValues> <Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot> </SlotValues> </IOT> Important: This is very important!! – To send a Time slot type value within the rawValue XML … you MUST first convert the value to a UCT time.

Once the slots have been defined, you create expressions to specify the value of one or more of the specified IOT agent slot and the required condition that needs to be met to enable each of the specified status bits by using the expression slot.

Title: Expressions
Once the slots have been defined, you create expressions to specify the value of one or more of the specified IOT agent slot and the required condition that needs to be met to enable each of the specified status bits by using the expression slot. The expression slot is a multi-line expression engine, where multiple expressions are separated by blank lines. For more information, see Creating IOT Expressions . Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent to subscribe to external tags Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). device needs to subscribe to external tags, such as systeminfo.second . When using Tagname type slots, there is a rule that must be applied: - The Tagname slot must be immediately followed by the IOT agent slot that will ultimately contain the value of the specified tag. - If the Tagname slot contains a valid tag name, the IOT agent will automatically subscribe to the specified agent and will place any values received for this tag into the next slot. For example, to subscribe to systeminfo.second then the XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. slot value would look something like this: <IOT Name=" SecsInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds " Type=" Integer "> 0 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> In the above sample, - the Slot Name “ source ” defines the tag to which we want to subscribe. - the Slot Name “ value ” defines the slot where the subscribed tag value will be stored. Important: The slot names "source" and "value" used in the example above are merely placeholders to make this example clearer, you may use any names you choose. Creating IOT Expression creating expressions to drive the value of defined slots and status bits The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to allow you to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions. These expressions are saved in the expression slot. Note: You need to insert empty lines to separate multiple expressions.

The following example shows two separate expressions as they are displayed in the Expression edit box of the IOT agent dialog: Z=slot(x) + slot(y).

Title: Expressions
The following example shows two separate expressions as they are displayed in the Expression edit box of the IOT agent dialog: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 As a side note, the expression slot of the IOT agent would actually be saved as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100

Note: Any status or controlling IOT slot can be alarmed by creating an IOT Alarm agent to alert the user of an anomaly.

Your expressions can contain one or more of your defined slots, such as: Logical expressions Condition for success Slot(value) > 95 SUCCESSFUL if the.

Title: Expression Conditions
Your expressions can contain one or more of your defined slots, such as: Logical expressions Condition for success Slot(value) > 95 SUCCESSFUL if the Value slot is greater than the value of 95 Slot(Open) & (Slot(value) > 95) SUCCESSFUL if the Open tag is On and the Value slot is greater than the value of 95

Title: Expression Elements
Your expressions can use one or more of the following operator elements: Tip: - You need to enclose each slot name defined by this UDT within the Slot() specifier, e.g. Slot(Open) - If a slot is NOT enclosed within a Slot() specifier then the status bit will NEVER be True - Multiple items are separated by commas ',' - Where necessary, the description of an operator is displayed in brackets () after the operator Element Types Operators / Example Other logical operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) Arithmetic operators +, -, *, /, % (modulus),^ (power) Parentheses (), {}, [] Scientific notation 3E+10 Constants 2, 3, 50 Functions MIN(4,5), SQR(34)

Your expressions can also use one or more of the following functions: Note: These functions can take either constants or slot values as their parameters.

Title: Expression Function Usage
Your expressions can also use one or more of the following functions: Note: These functions can take either constants or slot values as their parameters. For simplicity, the slot specifiers have been omitted, where Slot1 = Slot(SlotName) Functions Usage MIN : returns the minimum value MIN(2, 3, 4, 5) is 2. MAX : returns the maximum value MAX(2, 3, 1, 0) is 3. IF(condition, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse) IF(1, 2, 3) is 2 SUM : adds the values together SUM(1, 2, 3, 4) is 10 AVG :averages the values AVG(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is 3 SQR: returns the square of the value SQR(Slot1) SQRT: returns the square root of the value SQRT(Slot1) EXP : Returns E raised to the power of the value EXP(Slot1) INTPOW(Base, power): raises the Base to an integral power INTPOW(2, 3) = 8 POW(Base, power): raises the Base to any power Note: For fractional exponents or exponents greater than MaxInt, the Base must be greater than 0. POW(2,3) = 8 LN: returns the natural logarithm of the value LN(Slot1) LOG: returns the base-10 logarithm of the value LOG(Slot1) LOGN(Base, value): returns the log Base of the value LOGN(10, 100) = 2 ABS: returns the absolute value ABS(Slot1) SIGN: returns the sign of the value SIGN(Slot1) returns -1 if Slot1<0; +1 if Slot1>0, 0 if Slot1=0 TRUNC: discards the fractional part of the value TRUNC(-3.2) is -3, TRUNC(3.2) is 3 CEIL: returns the value rounded up, away from zero CEIL(-3.2) = -3, CEIL(3.2) = 4 FLOOR: returns the value rounded down, toward zero FLOOR(-3.2) = -4, FLOOR(3.2) = 3 SIN: returns the sine of the value (an angle in radians) SIN(Slot1) COS: returns the cosine the value (an angle in radians) COS(Slot1) TAN: returns the tangent of the value (an angle in radians) TAN(Slot1) ATAN: returns arctangent, or inverse tangent, of the value. The returned angle is specified in radians ATAN(Slot1) SINH: returns the hyperbolic sine of the value SINH(Slot1) COSH: returns the hyperbolic cosine of the value COSH(Slot1) COTAN: returns the cotangent of the value COTAN(Slot1)

The default IOT agent dialog looks as follows: The 1st IOT dialog shows the slot definition with a Tagname slot, followed by a slot that will contain the value of the specified tag, for example, systeminfo.second.

Title: The default IOT agent dialog looks as follows
The default IOT agent dialog looks as follows: The 1st IOT dialog shows the slot definition with a Tagname slot, followed by a slot that will contain the value of the specified tag, for example, systeminfo.second. - The dialog shows an expression that will also control the status bit 16 when the temperature value goes above 30. This status slot can be alarmed by creating an IOT Alarm agent . - Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag), for example, value(“systeminfo.second”). The 2nd IOT dialog shows a slot definition and an expression that will also control status bit 16 when the Z value goes above 100 when values X and Y are added together. - The sample XML structure below contains the agent name and description attributes as shown in first line below. These attributes are disregarded when the same XML is used in a XML template load file. <IOT Name="Add01" Description="Addition agent"> <SlotDefinitions> <Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot> <Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot> <Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot> </SlotDefinitions> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name="hi"/> </HeaderSlots> <Expression> <Line Text=”Z=slot(x) + slot(y)”/> </Line> <Line Text=”status16=slot(z)>100”></Line> </Expression> </IOT>

If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would.

Title: Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot
If you want to create an x+y=z agent with alarming when the z value exceeds 100 then the xml slot of this agent would have the following structure: <IOT Name="AddingTwoNumbers" Description="This adds two real values together"><Slots><Slot Name="x" Description="X value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="y" Description="Y value" Type="Real">0</Slot><Slot Name="z" Description="Z value" Type="Real">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name="hi"/></HeaderSlots></IOT> And the expression slot of this agent would saved as: Z=slot(x) + slot(y)\r\n\r\nstatus16 = slot(z) > 100 Which, appears in the Expression edit box in the configuration dialog of this IOT agent as follows: Z=slot(x) + slot(y) status16 = slot(z) > 100 Note: The use of the empty line between these expressions, indicates that they are separate independent expressions.

Title: Expressions using external tag values
Expressions can also use external tag values in the format value(tag) e.g. value(“systeminfo.second”). The following example of the xml The following example provides the xml slot that defines an IOT agent that obtain the value of the systeminfo.second tag and stores this in a secs Integer slot. Then it provides the expression slot that enables the status bit 16 when the number of seconds exceed 30. SecsInMinute . xml =<IOT Name="SecsInMinute" Description="Alert when the seconds exceed 30"><Slots><Slot Name="source" Description="Source of the seconds value" Type="Tagname">systeminfo.second</Slot><Slot Name="secs" Description="The actual seconds" Type="Integer">0</Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots></HeaderSlots></IOT> SecsInMinute . expression =status16=slot(secs)>30 Note: This example also shows that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent in order for them to be used, in this case they need to be referred to using the convention status nn in any expressions that you create (where nn is the required status bit number from 16 to 31).

However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention.

Title: Expressions using status slots
However, when you provide names for your status slots, such as in the first example where the status16 was named as "hi", then you can also refer to the named status slot in any expressions that you create, in addition to using the statusnn numbering convention. So when you use: status16 = slot(z) > 100 You can also use: status(hi) = slot(z) > 100 In addition to referring to the status slots as the status nn or the named status( slotname ) convention, interchangeably, you can also use these on the right hand side of the equation, if needed. As a result, you could have the following expression: status17 = if(status(enabled), slot(abc) > 100

As an example, let’s create an IOT agent called 2KVAPUMP. - All that is required is to first copy the default Adroit IOT agent x_iot.dll to a new file called t_2KVAPump.dll in the Adroit system folder, which is typically found at C:\Program Files (x86)\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . - The newly copied agent type is then available to Adroit. - A newly created IOT agent can represent any object containing multiple properties or slots. - Currently, the IOT agent does not support real-time catch-up .

text:
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ?

Title: Using the addSlot
The format for this slot is as follows: slottypeidx,slotname[,slotdescription[,slotvalue]] Where: slottypeidx : is a slot type index as follows: 0 : boolean (1/0) 1 : integer (4 byte signed integer) 2 : real (8 byte float) 3 : string (79 characters) 4 : time 5 : tagname (67 chars) (see “Use of Tagname type slots” below) 10 : varstring (any number of characters) slotname : any valid slotname not exceeding 15 characters and not containing the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? slotdescription : any 79 character description describing the agent (object) instance slotvalue : any suitable slot value conforming to the slot type index above

This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section.

Title: Using the xmlSLot
This XML structure requires that you always specify: - the name and description of the IOT agent in the <IOT> section. - the name, description and values of each slot that you require in the <Slots> section, where: - The slot name is any valid slot name not exceeding 15 characters and does not contain the characters $ @ , \ & % * ? - The slot description is any 79 character description that describes the purpose of this property. - The slot type is one of the following (case sensitive) values: - Boolean : a 1 or a 0 - Integer : a 4 byte signed integer - Real : an 8 byte floatString : 79 characters - Time : Win32 64-bit FILETIME Type - Name : 67 chars. For more details, see How to use Tagname type slots . - VarString : any number of characters - Status bits, you can specify status bits in the <HeaderSlots> section, where only the status bit name is required. Note: You should note, however, that you do not need to specify a name for the status bits of an IOT agent for them to be used.

The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot.

Title: Example of the XML structure
The following is an example of the required XML structure for the xml slot of the IOT agent with custom text shown in blue for ease of reference: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "><Slots><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot></Slots><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotDefinitions><Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature "Type="Real"> 20 </Slot></SlotDefinitions><HeaderSlots><Slot Name=" hi "/></HeaderSlots></IOT> Important: This is the expected format when saving the XML structure to the xml slot. To facilitate easier reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT Name=" Fridge1 " Description=" Fridge in kitchen "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Temperature " Type=" Real "> 20 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> <Slot Name=" hi "/> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> Any number of <Slots> may be defined. A maximum of 16 <HeaderSlots> (status bits) may be defined. The first specified header slot represents status bit 16 and subsequent header slots will represent status bits 17 to 31. The XML code above can be saved to an XML file as a template and loaded in the IOT agent dialog. An example of IOT values XML packet for rawValue is a simplified version of the xmlSlots schema as follows with custom text shown in blue : <IOT><Slots><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></Slots></IOT> Alternatively, with Revision 7 or later of iot.dll, you should use <IOT><SlotValues><Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot></SlotValues></IOT> For improved reading, the expanded view of this XML structure is shown as follows: <IOT> <SlotValues> <Slot Name=" value "> 20 </Slot> </SlotValues> </IOT> Important: This is very important!! – To send a Time slot type value within the rawValue XML … you MUST first convert the value to a UCT time.

Once the slots have been defined, you create expressions to specify the value of one or more of the specified IOT agent slot and the required condition that needs to be met to enable each of the specified status bits by using the expression slot.

Title: Expressions
Once the slots have been defined, you create expressions to specify the value of one or more of the specified IOT agent slot and the required condition that needs to be met to enable each of the specified status bits by using the expression slot. The expression slot is a multi-line expression engine, where multiple expressions are separated by blank lines. For more information, see Creating IOT Expressions . Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent to subscribe to external tags Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). device needs to subscribe to external tags, such as systeminfo.second . When using Tagname type slots, there is a rule that must be applied: - The Tagname slot must be immediately followed by the IOT agent slot that will ultimately contain the value of the specified tag. - If the Tagname slot contains a valid tag name, the IOT agent will automatically subscribe to the specified agent and will place any values received for this tag into the next slot. For example, to subscribe to systeminfo.second then the XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. slot value would look something like this: <IOT Name=" SecsInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds " Type=" Integer "> 0 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> In the above sample, - the Slot Name “ source ” defines the tag to which we want to subscribe. - the Slot Name “ value ” defines the slot where the subscribed tag value will be stored. Important: The slot names "source" and "value" used in the example above are merely placeholders to make this example clearer, you may use any names you choose. Creating IOT Expression creating expressions to drive the value of defined slots and status bits The IOT agent provides a multi-line expression engine to allow you to calculate the defined slot values and status bit conditions. These expressions are saved in the expression slot. Note: You need to insert empty lines to separate multiple expressions.

The following example shows two separate expressions as they are displayed in the Expression edit box of the IOT agent dialog: Z=slot(x) + slot(y).

The Marshal Agent Top The Marshal Agent The Marshal agent is designed to replace the popular marshalling function of the Multistate agent, by gathering discreet binary data from its 16 bit rawvalue or value slot.

Title: The Marshal Agent
The Marshal Agent Top The Marshal Agent The Marshal agent is designed to replace the popular marshalling function of the Multistate agent, by gathering discreet binary data from its 16 bit rawvalue or value slot. By giving each of the individual bits the full functionality of a digital agent, the Marshal agent exceeds the former capabilities of a marshalled mode Multistate Agent. These bits can then be alarmed, pulsed, named, and the 1 and 0 states of each bit can be named (on/off, open/closed etc). Tip: You can implement and use the MarshalAlarmMode registry value, to specify the type of information reported in the description field for Marshal agent alarms. Only the ON state is reflected in the status bit header slots of the agent and therefore the alarming subsystem has been extended to allow the alarming of status bits that are ON or OFF. The rawvalue and value relationship can also be reversed i.e. mirrored. To address the individual properties of each bit in the Marshal agent, e.g. from a mimic, used the following convention: MarshalAgentName.BitName.slot , e.g. MSH1.Switch.Value - will address the Value slot of the Switch bit inside the MSH1 Marshal agent. Note: The MarshalAgentName.BitName.slotname must not exceed 50 characters. To configure the Marshal agent . To configure the component digital agents . The specific status bits . Only the ON state is reflected in the status bit header slots of the agent and therefore the alarming subsystem has been extended to allow the alarming of status bits that are ON or OFF. The rawvalue and value relationship can also be reversed i.e. mirrored. To address the individual properties of each bit in the Marshal agent, e.g. from a mimic, used the following convention: MarshalAgentName.BitName.slot , e.g. MSH1.Switch.Value - will address the Value slot of the Switch bit inside the MSH1 Marshal agent. The MaxDemand Agent Top The MaxDemand Agent What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?

Title: The MaxDemand Agent
The MaxDemand Agent Top The MaxDemand Agent What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? . The MaxDemand agent predicts the maximum kVA demand for the current block period the interval over which your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand, which is typically 30 minutes. so you can create alarms if the predicted consumption exceeds a predefined limit. This enables you to control the electricity consumption during each block period and prevent your actual “maximum demand limit” from being exceeded. For details on how to use this agent to monitor your maximum demand, see Maximum Demand Quick Start . Usually, control entails turning off machines which do not affect the main production process or which are not essential. While the primary aim of this agent is to monitor your power usage, it can also automate the control of your electricity consumption. In other words you can use its MaxDemand status slot in a script or expression agent to perform the necessary remedial actions. The MaxDemand agent can also calculate your instantaneous power factor, which also has the potential to save you money. Note: For those of you running a clustered Agent Server, this agent supports real-time catch-up so even if the master Agent Server fails, the standby will seamlessly continue monitoring your maximum demand. Related topics: Configuring the MaxDemand agent : To explain the various configuration options. Specific Status Bits : To describe how you can use the provided status bits of this agent. How Maximum Demand is Calculated : To better understand this value and see how it is calculated. About Power Factor : To describe the cost implications of this value. This agent also provides the following additional slots: kVAOptimal , mdOverUnder and timeToMD . See MaxDemand Agent - Slot Details . -->

Title: The Notify Agent
The Notify Agent Top The Notify Agent The Notify agent provides another alarm route destination, which provides the following methods of reporting alarms that are intended to keep off site personal informed of unacknowledged alarms, process values and operator messages : Methods of remotely sending messages to the Notify agent - alarms can be transmitted via cellular phone Short Message Service (SMS) or paging service direct to a designated person. Tip: The Command agent can SMS alarms that have been sent to a Notify agent, by @ scanning the valueEx (VARSTRING) slot of this agent to the value slot of the required Command agent, since this supported extended strings. For details, see Message Sending and Processing Slots or for details on the Command agent in general, see Command agents . Drivers are provided which support Zetron encoder paging, MTN cell phone paging and Vodacom cell phone paging, Autopage and Telstra paging services amongst others. Configuring the Notify agent to send pager or SMS messages . Formatting pager or SMS alarm messages Advanced Features for sending pager or SMS messages . Example of Using Notify agents to send pager or SMS messages . IMPORTANT: When scanning Notify agent slots that are displayed on mimics, set their scan rates to zero. If this is not done then Adroit will attempt to poll these tags and the driver (which cannot read SMSs) has no data to return, and thus fails to read, resulting in scan-bad tags when displayed on a mimic. - alarms can also be sent as email messages to the necessary recipients, by using the Email driver. For details, see Configuring the Notify Agent to send Email messages . In addition to automatically sending alarms as email message, the Notify agent can also send email messages manually. Note: Multiple email addresses in the To, Cc and Bcc fields of the email message need to be separated by the COMMA (“,”) character and not the semi-colon (“;”) The Body and/or Subject line of the AUTOMATICALLY sent email messages may contain text macros that are parsed to before the message is sent, if required. For details, see Adding Macros to Notify agent email messages . Note: Currently these macros are only parsed when automatically sending email messages via the Notify agent, NOT when it sending email messages manually. Each email message can include an optional file attachment. Note: You can enable the ForceSendIfDuplicate registry setting to determine whether the same message can be resent or not from a Notify agent. Notify Agent - Slot Details . Notify Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Object Model Template Export Import Utility Top Object Model Template Export Import Utility The Object Model Template Export and Import utility lets you export or import one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to and from a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file.

Title: Object Model Template Export Import Utility
The Object Model Template Export Import Utility Top Object Model Template Export Import Utility The Object Model Template Export and Import utility lets you export or import one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to and from a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file. You typically open the Object Model Template Export and Import utility via the Adroit Utilities on the Desktop and then select this utility from this menu. Export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates This utility lets you move your Object Model Templates or Configuration from one computer to another and also for backup purposes. Note: Since these templates are obtained directly from your hard drive, you do NOT need the SmartUI Server to be running. - Select the Export tab to open the template browser and detail panes. - Click the Get Template button, which lists both user and system templates directly from your hard drive, so you do not require the SmartUI Server to be running. - Note: This only lists the Object Model Templates of the currently Active Configuration, which you can check via the Configuration page of your SmartUI Config Editor . - The left-panel displays the Templates tree. Select the Templates folder checkbox to list all available templates and their folder structure in the System and User folders . - Note: The folders that contain templates with configuration issues and problematic templates will display an error icon to assist you in locating these problematic templates. - The Export Details panel displays on the displays the Number of templates that have been selected for export: - If you select a template entry, then the Templates Details section appears in the right-panel, which displays a summary of its configuration and displays any detected errors. - If one of the selected templates has a configuration issue, then the Number of templates label displays an error icon , and the number of Good (error-free) and Bad (errors) templates that are selected for export. - Note: In this case, you will be unable to provide a description and export any templates until the problematic templates are cleared. You should close this utility and fix the issues before attempting to export them. - If all the selected templates are configured correctly, then the Number of templates label displays a good icon . You may then enter a Description for these exported templates. The description is displayed when a user attempts to import the templates. - Note: This Description is not displayed in the name of the exported .TEF (Template Export File) file. - Click the Export button when all the problematic templates are cleared. - Note: If you click the Export button with problematic templates are still selected, a message box is displayed detailing the errors. The export process is then forbidden. - When the export process is successful, this automatically creates the following unique file name: “TEF [ # templates] date time .tef” , where # is the number of templates being exported, and data and time specify the date and time of the export. - By default, this file will be saved in the same folder that the Object Model Template Export and Import utility is opened. You can, however, select any folder that you want. Import Object Model Templates from a .TEF (Template Export File) file Important: You must shut down your SmartUI Server before you can import templates. Note: These templates are imported into a unique folder, which also specifies the date and time of the import, so they will not overwrite existing templates. - Select the Import tab. - Click the Browse for export file button and browse for and select the required .TEF file then click Open .

- In the left-panel, the Template list contains the names of the templates within the selected export file. - Tip: You can view the source path of an exported template by hovering over its name in the list. - Note: If you hover over the Template name then you can preview the Primary wizard . - If you select an exported template, then the Templates Details section appears in the right-panel and displays a summary of its configuration and displays any detected warnings or errors. - You should analyse the templates contained in the file to determine that you are importing the required wizards. - In the right-panel, the Import details section displays: - the Number of templates contained in this export file and lists the import status of them, as follows: - Good : all is OK with importing these templates. For example, no configured elements already exists. - Warning : a non-critical issue was found when importing these templates. For example, a configured element already exists, such as the primary wizard. - Note: In the case of an existing configured element, this element will not be replaced! - Bad : when one or more of these templates cannot be correctly referenced in the export file. For example, typically due to file corruption, then these templates cannot be imported at all. - the Description which provides a detailed description of these exported templates, so that you can determine if you have selected the correct templates to import. - when an incompatible SmartUI Server version is detected, which prevents these templates being imported, the Source and Destination Server section is then displayed to show the server details and versions. Normally, you may click the Show more button to view this information. - Click the Import button and click Yes to confirm the import. - Note: These templates will be imported into your Active Configuration, which you can check via the Configuration page of your SmartUI Config Editor . - Note: These templates will be imported into a unique folder, which also specifies the date and time of the import, so they do not overwrite any existing templates that have the same name. - At the end of this process, the Import results are displayed, listing all the events related to this import. - Note: You should not see any errors in these results. However, if you do, you can attempt to fix them. Depending upon their severity, you should delete this import folder and attempt to reimport the templates. - Click the Open the Templates folder in Windows Explorer button in the top right corner of the utility to view the folder of these newly imported templates, which uses this name format: - “IMPORT_# templates_date_time.tef” , where # is the number of templates that are exported, and data and time specify the date and time of the import. -->

The OEE agent can : - EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant.

Title: Why use the OEE agent?
The OEE agent can : - EITHER calculate the OEE for the monitored equipment and/or plant. Since targeting the three key OEE factors simultaneously, can effect significant improvements in production. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate OEE - OR measure a specific KPI Key Performance Indicator, a quantifiable measurement that measures how well something is accomplishing its goals and objectives. . In other words, individual OEE agents can be applied to any component or part of a process for which a variable denoting a measurement of output is available, as follows: Note: The number of OEE agents that you can add to your Agent Server is determined by the OEE Count parameter of your Adroit license. KPIs are typically the measurement of some production value over time OR one production value against (divided by) another production value. Therefore the OEE agent can measure TWO variables: - the FIRST variable (the REAL input1 slot) - the SECOND variable (the REAL input2 slot), used as a DIVISOR of the first (input1/input2). Note: If the SECOND variable is not specified, then the FIRST variable is simply divided by time. In this way it is possible to measure production figures, such as ton/hr, kWh/ton, total produced, actual run-hours, etc. The measured KPI can either compare actual performance with benchmark figures or compare shift performances or today’s performance with the previous day or the previous day's shifts. How to configure the OEE agent to calculate a KPI This agent supports real-time catch-up on a standby clustered Agent Server from a master server and Agent Server session persistence via a work file in the project work folder, typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default \Work. - OEE Agent Calculations : describes important factors that affect if and how the OEE agent calculates the OEE or KPI, such as whether this calculation is done on a per-shift or per-batch basis. - Advanced OEE agent configuration options : details the configuration of the options provided by the Advanced OEE options dialog, such as database (SQL) logging. - OEE Agent - Specific Status Bits : to indicate various quality and other alarm conditions, the status of the agent, OLE DB connection and the current shift. OEE Agent - Slot Details . OEE Agent - Database File Format . -->

The OPC Server Window Top The OPC Server item-address Browser Window This Adroit OPC Server item-address browser window displays all the agent.slot combinations, which the Adroit OPC Server is currently connected to. Note: Enabling the browser-populating feature, adds a number of items, by default, which are used to monitor the state of the Agent Server. The OPC Server graphically displays the status of connection to the specified Agent Server (node), as follows: all the added items are displaying all tags in red - Disconnection: a red font is used for each tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). displayed by this window. - Connection: a green font is used for each tag that is connected to an OPC client an application that uses the data provided by an OPC server. and all other tags are displayed using a grey font. Note: To optimise tag browsing tags are greyed out in the Adroit OPC Server window until an OPC client connects to a tag. Each tag ( OPC item a string, uniquely describing an individual data element residing in an OPC server. It may be up to 80 characters long, and structured hierarchically typically using a period "." to separate each level. ) displayed by this window adheres to the following addressing: nodename.agenttype.agentname.slotname . Click for more details: - nodename , specifies the node, which is like an Agent Server, but transparently provides redundancy (especially for Agent Server clustering).For details, see Working with Nodes . - agenttype is the agent type (e.g. Analog or Digital), - agentname is the name of the applicable agent (e.g. MYANALOG or AIRCON01_SP) and - slotname is the slot of the value that is required (e.g. Value). Automatically Populating the OPC Server Item Browser Window : in addition to enabling this feature, this allows you to configure which agent.slot combinations populate this item-address browser. The following columns provide additional information concerning the update activity of values from the Agent Server: - Update: which specify the number of good updates i.e. correct values. - Bad updates: which specify the number of bad updates received. To configure the width of the columns . To set the refresh rate of the browser . Title: The Other Slots SystemInformation Page
The Other Slots SystemInformation Page Top The Other Slots SystemInformation Page The System Information agent acts as an information center containing 5 tabbed pages of data slots that are global to the Agent Server. For details on how to access these pages of data, see Editing the SystemInformation Agent . Note: The actual slot names and NOT their literal descriptions are specified, for ease of reference, since you most likely will need to display one or more of these slots on mimics. - startPoolId: This displays the internal ID of the current Agent Server session. - typeLst: Double click on typeLst to display the list of agent types used within the Agent Server. - connections: This displays the number of remote connections made to the Agent Server, there will always be at least one i.e. the connection made to itself. - connectionLst: Double click on connectionLst to display the list of remote connections made to the Agent Server. - shutdown: If set to 1, this will force the Agent Server to cleanly shut itself down. - saveShutdown: If set to 1, this will save and then cleanly shutdown the Agent Server. - dayOfWeek: This specifies the day of the week as a number from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday). - serverType: This indicates the current Server configuration of this Agent Server: (0) Cluster, (1) Cluster aware, (2) Standalone/Distributed. - serverMode: This indicates the current mode of this Agent Server, if it is part of a cluster: (0) Master, (1) Standby, (2) Normal. - serverState: This indicates the current state of this Agent Server, if it is part of a cluster: (0) Unhealthy, (1) Healthy. - internalState: This specifies The internal state of the server. - internalStateStr: This specifies The internal state as a string. - serverModeStr: This specifies Master/Standby/Normal. - clusterName: This specifies the name of the cluster, if this Agent Server is part of a cluster. - clusterPartner: This specifies the server name of the cluster partner, if this Agent Server is part of a cluster. -->

The PerfMon Agent Top The PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent is used to monitor Windows Performance counters, which belong to performance objects such as the Agent Server, Processor, Memory, and others.

Title: The PerfMon Agent
The PerfMon Agent Top The PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent is used to monitor Windows Performance counters, which belong to performance objects such as the Agent Server, Processor, Memory, and others. These counters facilitate the monitoring of the computers performance and assist in detecting performance bottlenecks that could adversely affect the functioning of Adroit . The values of these counters are updated every second and can also be assigned to other tags, such as Analog agents, which can then be appropriately alarmed. Up to 16 performance counters can be monitored per agent. The following performance counters are added, by default, to first PerfMon agent created: - CPU load i.e. \\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time - Agent Server CPU load i.e. \\Process(as)\\% Processor Time - Total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes - Agent Server memory usage i.e. \\Process(as)\\Private Bytes and \\Process(as)\\Virtual Bytes - Agent Server put slots i.e. \\Agent Server(name (project))\\PutSlots Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc To edit or configure a PerfMon agent . To Add a Performance Counter to the Grid . PerfMon Agent - Slot Details . PerfMon Agent - Database File Format . -->

The PID Agent Top The PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent.

Title: The PID Agent
Steps:
The PID Agent Top The PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent. These values can then be scanned to the outside world, via their raw slots. This provides great savings in the overall number of agents required in the configuration of a project that contains PID controllers. Configurable high and low operation limits are provided for the SP (set-point) and CV (control variable) slots, which will prevent these values from being set to potentially harmful values, when they are being manually configured. This agent also triggers alarm conditions based on configurable alarm limits that are indicated by the specific status bits . Added support for realtime catch-up To edit or configure a PID agent . Note1: This agent does not currently provide internal PID algorithm control. Note2: The PID agent supports real-time catch-up . Specific Status Bits . PID Agent - Slot Details . PID Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Primitive Agents Top The Primitive Agents The primitive agent types Boolean, Integer, Real and String are the simplest building blocks.

Title: The Primitive Agents
The Primitive Agents Top The Primitive Agents The primitive agent types Boolean, Integer, Real and String are the simplest building blocks. Instances of these primitive agent types are used simply to hold a single value in the value slot. They do not contain any other slots or additional functionality such as inversion, pulsing, linearisation, etc, as found in the Digital, Analog and other agent types. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! These agents should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. - A Boolean agent will hold a Boolean value (0 or 1) - An Integer agent will hold an integer number -2147483648 to +2147483647 (32 bits) Note: The specific status bits of the Integer agent will be set if its value is between 0 and 15. - A Real agent will hold a double precision floating point number (64 bits) - A String agent will hold a 79 character text string (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). Due to the increasing need of customers for the Agent Server to support strings longer than 79 characters, the String agent now has a new slot called valueex that is able to contain these longer strings. Usage examples for these longer strings include queries that are created dynamically and long descriptions. WARNING! This new "valueex" slot is NOT supported by the scanning subsystem because the scanning subsystem cannot handle strings larger than 80 characters in length. Note: This new valueex slot is now identical to the String slot type of Custom agents, which have always supported strings that are greater than 79 characters. The legacy "value" slot of the String agent will still remain and contain the first 79 characters of the "valueex" slot. Therefore the "valueex" slot will always be equal to the "value" slot its string length is less than 79 characters (excluding the zero terminator). Note: When editing the String agent, only the "valueex" slot can be configured, although the content of the "value" slot is also displayed. -->

The Project Explorer Top The Project Explorer The Adroit Project Explorer is a separate utility, which configures and manages both local and distributed Adroit projects.

Title: The Project Explorer
The Project Explorer Top The Project Explorer The Adroit Project Explorer is a separate utility, which configures and manages both local and distributed Adroit projects. For details, see The Adroit Project Explorer Window . Note: When used within the Classic UI, this can be disabled using the Menu Security feature. Adroit -specific launching options . The Project Explorer provides access to one or more computers on a network. If these computers have Adroit installed on it then read and possibly write access may be gained to the following Adroit components on each computer: - The Agent Server, its agent types and their agents. - The configuration of Adroit on this computer. Note: This will only be possible if the Windows security configuration and the Adroit remote connection licenses permit such access. WARNING! If you wish to use this Project Explorer and your project has many (1000s) of analogs and other agent types, be aware that it will take a fairly long time to populate the lists in the grid and the tree windowpanes. This problem is further exacerbated when adding fields to the explorer lists which have a large number of slots or agents. -->

The Recipe Agent Top The Recipe Agent A Recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes.

Title: The Recipe Agent
The Recipe Agent Top The Recipe Agent A Recipe agent consists of a master recipe and one or more control recipes. This can be used to defines how the control system is to process its raw materials to make the desired product and byproducts. Description of recipe agent . Note: Names used in the recipe agent e.g. to define recipes and batches, CANNOT contain the ‘%’ character. The Master Recipe consists of all the process variables or "ingredients" and the sequence in which they are to be downloaded. It is here that the procedure and associated tag names will be defined. Components of a Master Recipe . Editing the Master Recipe . Each Control Recipe will contain specific quantities and values for customizing the Master Recipe for a given production run, thus allowing a plant to produce variants of its base product; for example, differing colors of paint, different flavors of cola. For each master recipe, there may be one or more Control Recipes. Components of a Control Recipe . Creating the Control Recipes . Editing a Control Recipe . Order of Execution of a Step . Starting and Stopping a Control Recipe . Example of Master Recipe with two Control Recipes . Importing & Exporting Recipes . The Recipe Monitor. Recipe Agent - Slot Details . Recipe Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Script Agent Top The Script Agent The Script agent provides a way for the user to execute complicated tasks such as batching, reporting or complex mathematical operations through a Visual basic script or Java script.

Title: The Script Agent
The Script Agent Top The Script Agent The Script agent provides a way for the user to execute complicated tasks such as batching, reporting or complex mathematical operations through a Visual basic script or Java script. IMPORTANT: If your Agent Server is running as a service and you create a script that needs access to protected network resources or that launch other Windows programs or perform any other function that requires a logged on user. Then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to perform these functions. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. Note: This agent does not replace the expression agent , as the expression agent can execute simple calculations far more efficiently and faster than the Script agent. Each Script agent can be configured to have an associated list of module files that contain user-defined variables, functions and subroutines. The Script agent allows the user to interact with the Agent Server , in order to access and manipulate data within the Agent Server. A script is compiled after the Agent Server has started up or whenever the script agent is modified from within the Agent Configurator. The script agent executes a single subroutine, or "main" subroutine, in one of four different ways. For details, see Running the Main Subroutine . PLEASE NOTE: There is no way for the Agent Server to protect itself from badly written or buggy scripts and Adroit Technologies does not take responsibility for badly written or buggy scripts written by users. Users also have the ability to launch other applications, or manipulate other applications via OLE automation, for example to configure reports in Microsoft Excel or Microsoft Word. The Script agent may also be used as an alternative to using the Recipe agent and it can be used to perform simple scheduled tasks. Note1: If you are using scripts to obtain datetime tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. Note2: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! Related links: Usage Guidelines . Adroit Scripting Service Policy . Configuring the Script agent . How to interact with the Agent Server using the Script Agent . Module Selection . Main subroutine scheduling and triggering . Trigger Configuration . Scheduling Configuration . Advanced Properties . Details . The Adroit system object . Adroit Script Functions and Subroutines . Specific Status Bits . Script Agent - Slot Details . Script Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Script Engine Top The Script Engine When the Edit script button is pressed, when deriving a Custom agent , you need to choose the required scripting engine either Yes to use JavaScript or No to use VBScript.

Title: The Script Engine
The Script Engine Top The Script Engine When the Edit script button is pressed, when deriving a Custom agent , you need to choose the required scripting engine either Yes to use JavaScript or No to use VBScript. Then Adroit Script Editor is launched and the following applicable script components are added by default to this derived custom agent’s script: - The slots of this derived agent are defined as constants, starting from 0 in the order in which they have been created. - Script procedures are created for this derived Custom agent, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine for the derived custom agent or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. Since this event can FLOOD the event log PLEASE ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! The Custom agent script code uses a Custom object to communicate with the Agent Server, via the following methods: AgentName GetSlot LogEvent SetStatus Sound CDateTime GetTag SetSlot SetTag IMPORTANT: You cannot pass a tag (string) as the parameter to the GetSlot function, you must pass the slot index of the Custom agent! Note: To gain help concerning the use of the Adroit Script Editor, press F1 when this editor is selected. For the DriveXYZ agent, click here for the fully commented VB script code that provides its additional functionality. -->

Then Adroit Script Editor is launched and the following applicable script components are added by default to this derived custom agent’s script: - The slots of this derived agent are defined as constants, starting from 0 in the order in which they have been created. - Script procedures are created for this derived Custom agent, which can either be left empty– to not provide a script engine for the derived custom agent or they can be coded to provide any additional functionality for this agent. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. Since this event can FLOOD the event log PLEASE ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! The Custom agent script code uses a Custom object to communicate with the Agent Server, via the following methods: AgentName GetSlot LogEvent SetStatus Sound CDateTime GetTag SetSlot SetTag IMPORTANT: You cannot pass a tag (string) as the parameter to the GetSlot function, you must pass the slot index of the Custom agent! Note: To gain help concerning the use of the Adroit Script Editor, press F1 when this editor is selected. For the DriveXYZ agent, click here for the fully commented VB script code that provides its additional functionality.

The Shift Agent Top The Shift Agent Various agents in Adroit , such as OEE, require knowing the current shift number.

Title: The Shift Agent
Steps:
The Shift Agent Top The Shift Agent Various agents in Adroit , such as OEE, require knowing the current shift number. Instead of configuring the shift pattern information into each instance of these agents, you can instead configure these shift patterns globally, in a Shift agent, for use by any interested agents. The value slot of the Shift agent should also be scanned, output enabled, to any PLCs that perform any shift end functions, such as resetting shift count accumulators. Tip: Multiple shift agents can define different shift patterns that may occur within a plant. The Shift agent continually monitors the current time and checks it against the configured shift pattern to determine the current shift number. If NO matching shift pattern is found, the shift value is set to 0. Configured shift patterns are selected using the following order of preference: In other words if one or more shift patterns have the current time configured, then the configuration of the shift pattern determines which is selected, in the following order: - Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. - Annually recurring holidays on a given day of the month, such as Christmas 25 Dec. - Weekly recurring patterns on a given day of the week, such as Sundays. This agent supports real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server. Configuring the Shift Agent : describes the required shift pattern configuration sequence and how to configure less than 6 shifts and provides configuration examples and other configuration options. Shift Agent - Specific Status Bits : to indicate when the current shift is at an end or the current shift configuration is invalid or when the OPTIONAL OLEDB connection string is invalid. Shift Agent - Slot Details . Shift Agent - Database File Format . -->

The SNMPManager Agent The SNMPManager Agent This agent can both monitor and manage devices on a network, by using the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP).

Title: The SNMPManager Agent
Steps:
The SNMPManager Agent The SNMPManager Agent This agent can both monitor and manage devices on a network, by using the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). Examples of devices that can be monitored using SNMP include routers, switches, hubs, UPSs, printers, modems and computers. For details on how to use this agent to monitor and/or manage a network device, see Quick Start to Manage a Device (Computer) . Each SNMPManager agent can access the data relating to the operation of a single device, in order to: PLEASE NOTE: For a comprehensive list of requirements regarding the use of this agent, see Usage Requirements . IMPORTANT: NEVER run the Windows SNMP Trap (listener) service because it conflicts with the Adroit SNMP trap functionality! Note: This agent does NOT require the Windows SNMP Service to function, this service is ONLY required on each computer that this agent monitors. - monitor this device: by writing the values of SNMP managed objects to one or more tag. This allows you to trend this data, such as bandwidth; alarm this data, such as when particular conditions arise like a device becoming unavailable and log this data, so you can analyze it for troubleshooting purposes. - control this device: by using tags to set the values of this data. This allows you to change set-points within the managed device that control its operational functionality. - receive SNMP traps (events) from this device, so that you can react to those that are important. This allows you to reduce the number of values that you need to monitor (poll) for each device. In other words, instead of monitoring every value on every device, by using SNMP traps, a device can simply inform its SNMPManager agent of the important values without solicitation. Each SNMPManager agent can manage a single SNMP managed device by monitoring (polling) selected OID values and, if necessary, changing (writing to) them. For details, see Configuring SNMPManager Agents . Furthermore, you can also retrieve SNMP traps from this device. For details, see About SNMP Traps . For the suggested procedure of using SNMPManager agents to monitor and manage a network, see Implementing SNMPManager Agents . For further details about SNMP, see About SNMP. SNMPManager Agent - Specific Status Bits : to diagnose the status of its connection to the device it is required to manage and the status of the managing process. SNMPManager Agent - Slot Details . SNMPManager Agent - Database File Format . -->

The Statistical Agent Top The Statistical Agent Statistical Process Control and Acceptance Sampling are methods used to detect significant changes in the manufacturing process and to monitor the quality of manufactured items being produced in batches.

Title: The Statistical Agent
The Statistical Agent Top The Statistical Agent Statistical Process Control and Acceptance Sampling are methods used to detect significant changes in the manufacturing process and to monitor the quality of manufactured items being produced in batches. The problem is to decide whether a batch should be accepted or rejected on the basis of a sample, which is randomly or otherwise, drawn from the batch. There are many ways to make a sample - whether at timed intervals or on triggered events. The Statistical agent provides the basic functionality for a user to build a statistical process control strategy using its built in data collection method and by linking the agent to other Adroit agents. Note1: The Statistical agent supports real-time catch-up . Note2: Use agent persistence files to prevent Statistical agents from losing their statistical data, instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . PLEASE NOTE: When exporting Statistical agents, ensure that the Floating average enabled checkbox is UNCHECKED, then save the WGP file and export. After importing, re-enable this checkbox for the applicable Statistical agents. There is a Statistical agent Wizard to demonstrate its operation, which can be found in the Wizards folder under the Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit \Wizards. Data Specification Method . To configure the Statistical agent for streamed events . Specific Status Bits . To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input e.g. to be transferred to a database. Statistical Agent - Slot Details . Statistical Agent - Database File Format . -->

Title: The StringList Agent
The StringList Agent Top The StringList Agent The StringList agent provides a superset of functionality of the existing Frame agent . It can store a virtually unlimited number of ASCII character strings, each string has a maximum length of 79 characters. These strings are indexed by an integer number beginning at 1. Note: These strings can contain commas ",". The current string pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. It is also possible to specifying the error message that is displayed when an invalid index is used. Stringlist agents CAN be imported, if necessary. When importing, the import is committed directly to the Agent Server, so the user no longer needs to click the Update button, after clicking the Import button. Note: Once an import file name is specified, this file name is remembered for the remainder of the Agent Server session each time an application is started and stopped on a computer constitutes a single session of this program. . The SystemDatalog Agent Top The SystemDatalog Agent The SystemDatalog agent manages the Datalog catch-up of all configured Datalog agents, which only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster.

Title: The SystemDatalog Agent
Steps:
The SystemDatalog Agent Top The SystemDatalog Agent The SystemDatalog agent manages the Datalog catch-up of all configured Datalog agents, which only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. This involves fetching stored historical data from the datalog agents on the cluster partner and merging the data with the local datalog agents. Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. Configuring the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog catch-up . Datalog catch-up Slots Omitted by the Configuration Dialog . Tip: Datalog Catchup can be performed via a graphic form, such as the Datalog Catchup Management tab of the System Management graphic form of the System Information project.
