The Tag-link Database Top The Tag-link Database Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database.

Title: The Tag-link Database
The Tag-link Database Top The Tag-link Database Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database. This database stores a list of WanServer(s) and tags whose values are to be fetched or sent to or from each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers and these database files are stored in the database-folder . The tag link database is typically (initially) created using the WanClient Configurator, which can be launched from the Open Configurator item of the WanClient File menu and is used to stores the following items: - The communication settings of each remote (Wan)Server whose Agent Server contains tags that either need to be fetched or sent. - The tag groups , these tag groups classify tag-links in terms of the type of communication that is required and are server-specific. For details on possible criteria to use for creating tag groups, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . - The tag-links , specify the required local and the remote tag name, whose values are ‘linked’ and are tag group-specific. - The local tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanClient computer, and typically received its value from the remote tag name UNLESS it is within a control group, in which case it can set the value of the remote tag. - The remote tag name, resides in the Agent Server on the WanServer computer, and typically supplies the value for the remote tag. Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. The name of the file that stores the tag-link database for each WanServer is user-defined, typically when adding or editing the communication details of a WanServer. This file can be edited manually, in Excel or any other CSV file editor, for bulk configuration purposes. The onus is then upon the user to ensure that all the values entered into these files are correct. For details, see bulk configuration of tag groups and bulk configuration of tag links . -->

The Timer Agent Top The Timer Agent The Timer agent can perform several commonly used timing operations.

Title: The Timer Agent
The Timer Agent Top The Timer Agent The Timer agent can perform several commonly used timing operations. This agent provides a Boolean value slot as an output, which is enabled (set to TRUE) and disabled (set to FALSE) by the agent, depending upon its current mode of operation. This slot can therefore be used as an enabling or disabling or scheduling tag for other agents. Note: Although the Timer agent does not provide a cold-start value, it does support real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server, which means that if the master Agent Server fails, the timing operation will seamlessly continue. This agent can perform one of following three timing operations or modes: Example: to illustrate the action of the three timing operations. This is a trend of the value and start slots of three Timer agents, to indicate their timing actions. In this example: - each Timer agent is named after its configured timing operation for the purposes of easy identification ONLY, you can name your Timer agents anything you like. - all the delays and pulse widths are 3 seconds long. - On timer: This mode can be used for the timing of specific events. The value slot is only enabled for the specified period (pulse width). For details, see Configuring On Timers . Note: This, in effect, provides the same functionality as a pulsed digital. - On delay timer: This mode can be used for the filtering out of specific events. The value slot is only enabled after the required period of delay has elapsed. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . - Pulse generator: This mode can be used for generating free running square waves. The value slot is enabled for the duration of the required pulse width and then disabled for the required period of delay. The period of the generated pulse is the sum of the delay and pulse width times. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . Note: All the timing operations, with the exception of the Pulse generator , can be automatically reset. The status bits of this agent can show when the timer is running or has expired. For details, see Specific Status Bits . Note: The operational status of the timer must not be confused with the value slot of this agent, since these are sometimes independent elements i.e. the timer is not necessarily off when its value is FALSE. Timer Agent - Slot Details . Timer Agent - Database File Format . -->

Time Stamping Top Time Stamping Adroit achieves its accuracy by time stamping data at the point of creation whenever possible.

Title: Time Stamping
Time Stamping Top Time Stamping Adroit achieves its accuracy by time stamping data at the point of creation whenever possible. Scanned values get their timestamp from the data packet returned by the front-end device, if the protocol driver is exception based and implements a time-stamping protocol. A time stamp may also be created in an agent when a user enters a value manually. The time is taken from the systemInformation agent, which in turns gets it from the system clock. The name of the operation which causes this is the putslot method, which as well as updating the value in the target slot (e.g. value ), also updates the agentTimeStamp slot. When the agent subsequently sends a subscription update to another agent, or picture element Behaviour, the same timestamp value is passed on. For example, if the Alarm agent receives a subscription update, it will route the timestamp it gets to whichever printers, event logs, alarm lists and beeper agents it has been configured with. Timestamps will propagate into the user interface, into mimics and ultimately into picture elements containing associated Behaviours. For this reason, it should be clear that tampering with the system clock is NOT advised. In particular, setting the clock backwards (say from 10:00 to 09:00) will have the effect of freezing all mimic updates, datalogging and existing alarms, for a period of 1 hour, until the timestamping mechanism "catches up" with the new time. Note: Sites using the SystemInformation time for calculations should be especially careful. -->

Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster Top Time Synchronization It is essential that both the cluster Agent Servers and their clients have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively.

Title: Time Synchronization
Steps:
Time Synchronization of an Adroit Cluster Top Time Synchronization It is essential that both the cluster Agent Servers and their clients have their system time synchronised, for clustering to work effectively. This is ALSO critical in a distributed Adroit installation (where there are multiple user interfaces and/or Agent Servers on different computers) that the system times of all of the computers are synchronised to a common source. Adroit will behave unpredictably on a system which system time is not synchronised with the computer it’s connecting to. Time synchronization is typically managed by the Windows Time service that is installed by the default installation of Windows XP and later operating systems. The following are symptoms of unsynchronised times: - The User Interface does not seem to be updating with the most recent information. - The Trend displays odd Behaviour: either the data seems to be inserted into the middle of the trend, or a strange unexplainable sudden change in the values being trended when pressing F5 to refresh the trend. - The data logs of the two unsynchronised Agent Servers in a cluster seem to get corrupted (as a result of the data being inserted into the wrong place) after doing a Datalog catch-up with the SystemDatalog agent. This corruption is most notable in a trend. Agent Servers generate an event every minute if remotely connected Agent Servers have a time difference of more than two seconds. To indicate that there is a time synchronization issue. This feature does NOT affect Adroit clients (UIs) that connect to a remote Agent Server. In this case time synchronization issues are not reported. -->

Slot Name Type Function autoReset BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this will automatically reset the start slot, 100 milliseconds after the timer has expired.

Title: Slots:
Steps:
Slot Name Type Function autoReset BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this will automatically reset the start slot, 100 milliseconds after the timer has expired. Not used if the freeRun slot is enabled. delayTime INTEGER The delay time (in ms) i.e. the time before the pulse (value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Timers . freeRun BOOLEAN If enabled (set to True) this enables the "pulse generator" mode of operation. For details, see Configuring Pulse Generators . granularity INTEGER The granularity (in ms) determines how often the Timer agent monitors the time after the timer has started. If less than the duration of the timer, then the timeleft slot indicates the remaining time, in milliseconds, before this timer expires. The default value of 0, forces the granularity period to equal the required duration of the timer, so that this timeleft slot is never calculated. WARNING! The smaller the specified granularity, the greater the amount of work the Agent Server is required to perform in updating its clients with the timeleft slot value. Note: Although this granularity value is has a minimum of 100 ms, a minimum of 1000 ms is recommended as a "safe" value. inputTag TAGNAME This can automatically start the timer by subscribing to another tag in the Agent Server. Note1: If this tag is numeric, then the start slot is enabled (set to TRUE) when it’s value is non-zero. Note2: If this tag is a string, then the start slot is enabled when this string is not empty. pulseWidth INTEGER The pulse width (in ms) OR the time at which the pulse ( value slot) is switched on (set to TRUE). This must be left at zero if an "on delay timer" is configured. For details, see Configuring On Delay Timers . start BOOLEAN Starts and stops the timer. Note: When this slot is set to FALSE, the value slot is also set to FALSE and the currently configured timer expires. timeLeft INTEGER If the granularity slot is set at 100 milliseconds or greater and is less than the required duration of the timer, then this slot displays the amount of time left in the timing cycle in milliseconds. value BOOLEAN The output of the timer. Note: This slot can be used to enable, disable or schedule other agents.

Note: These are of type BOOLEAN.

Title 21 CFR Part 11 (21 CFR 11) of the Code of Federal Regulations deals with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES).

Title: Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance
Title 21 CFR Part 11 (21 CFR 11) of the Code of Federal Regulations deals with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES). This defines the criteria and circumstances under which electronic records and electronic signatures are considered to be trustworthy, reliable and equivalent to paper records by the FDA. In short, for those records that remain subject to part 11, need to adhere to the following requirements: - the validation of computerised systems - computer-generated time-stamped audit trails to ensure the trustworthiness and reliability of the records - the need to provide investigators with reasonable and useful access to records during an inspection Furthermore, 21 CFR 11 also requires that the following controls and requirements be implemented: - limiting system access to authorised individuals - use of operational system checks - use of authority checks - use of device checks - determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks - establishment of and adherence to written policies that hold individuals accountable for actions initiated under their electronic signatures - appropriate controls over systems documentation -->

Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager .

Title: In the SmartUI Designer:
Select the required SmartUI Server in the Enterprise Manager , as follows: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - Navigate to Servers > [Server Name] . - Tip: The connection name is prefixed by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required Adroit datasource or its icon . - If necessary, expand the AgentGroup tree. - Right click the required agent type , which are listed alphabetically, and select Create Tag . - Specify the required Tag Name or agent name. The following rules apply when naming agents: - Agent names have a maximum of 27 characters. - Agent names cannot be the same as the names used for Agent Types or for Agent Groups. - Agent names cannot use the following characters: Space Percent % Comma , Period . back slash \ Dollar $ - If necessary, provide an optional Description that describes the purpose or describes the value of this tag (agent) for ease of reference. - Click the Finish button. -->

Ensure that you have created the required group.

Title: To add agents to an existing group:
Ensure that you have created the required group. For details, see To Create a New Agent Group . Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list, and select the required agent type (of the agent you want to add). - From the Agents list box, select one or more agents e.g. ANA02 an instance of an Analog agent, to be allocated to the Agent Group. - Click the Groups button in the Agent Configuration dialog box. The Agent Groups dialog box is displayed. Note: Any agents that have been browsed into the agent, e.g. the agents used in an Expression agent, or the agent used to trigger the Counter agent, will appear in the Current groups list, prefaced by an asterisk (*) e.g. *TRIGGER. These ARE NOT group names. - Select the required existing group from the Available list. - Click the Move to Left button ( << ). The selected group moves across from the Available to the Current Groups list. - Click the OK button to return to the Agent Configuration dialog box. -->

To Add Header Slots Top To Add Header Slots It is possible to also display one or more Header slots for the agents displayed in the Explorer Agent List. When the Explorer Agent List of the selected Agent type is displayed in the grid windowpane: - Right-click and select the Add column… menu item. The Add new column dialog is displayed. - Type the name of the required slot (such as statusbad ) in the provided edit box and click OK . Note1: Although any valid slot name can be entered, this is the ONLY method of adding header slots for this agent to this multiple agent grid view. Note2: Additional columns of non-header slots can be added to this grid, from the Explorer Slot List grid. Note3: If the specified slot name is incorrectly spelt, then a column filled with question mark entries (???) will be added. Note4: If the name of a slot that is already displayed is specified, no column will be added. -->

To Add or Edit an Alarm Type Top To Add or Edit an Alarm Type - From the Edit Alarm Agent dialog, select the Types tab.

Title: To Add or Edit an Alarm Type
To Add or Edit an Alarm Type Top To Add or Edit an Alarm Type - From the Edit Alarm Agent dialog, select the Types tab. The Types page is displayed. - From the Agent Type drop down list box, select the Agent Type for which the Alarm Types will be defined. - To add a new alarm type, click the Add button and enter the name, remembering that Alarm Types are case sensitive. - To edit an existing alarm type, select it and click the Edit button to get a further dialog box. - To allow the status bits to be alarmed in their off states, check the Alarm Off States checkbox, this is off by default. - Select the Alarm Trigger status mask bits that will be used to monitor the agents using that particular Alarm Type. - Choose the agent slots to be reported using the changeover buttons e.g. for an analog type, you may wish to report the data held in the value and unit slots. The Available list box displays all slots relevant to the selected agent type. The Current list box displays the slots in the order in which they will be reported. The Insert button is available to rearrange the order of the slots. - Click on the OK button to return to the Edit Alarm Agent dialog. -->

To Configure an Alarm Route Top To Configure an Alarm Route All alarms are routed to the following destination agents that are designed to announce, record, organise and display the alarm state of the alarmed agent.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Configure an Alarm Route Top To Configure an Alarm Route All alarms are routed to the following destination agents that are designed to announce, record, organise and display the alarm state of the alarmed agent. For further details of alarm routes, see About Alarm Routes . - From the Edit Alarm Agent dialog, select the Routes tab. The Routes dialog displays the following information: - Route Numbers – specify as many routes as you require. However, the defaultAlarmAgent reserves Routes 0 and 1 for system alarms such as software faults and communication errors. Therefore, when configuring route destinations in the defaultAlarmAgent , the route number must begin at Route 2. When more alarm agents are created, Routes 0 and 1 are not reserved. - Route Destinations – this is divided into: Alarm Route Destinations , which select the required Alarm Lists and Audio Devices for the selected route number, that only applies to this Alarm agent. Eventlog Route Destinations, which select the required Output Destination (EventOutput or Notify agents) and Event Logs for the selected route number. Note: Eventlog Route Destinations are GLOBAL settings that apply to ALL alarm agents. Hence, Route 2 of the defaultAlarmAgent routes to the same EventOutput(s) and EventLog(s) as will Route 2 of another alarm agent etc. - Select an existing route number, by using the Select route number list box. If necessary: - Click the Add Route button to create a new route number for this Alarm agent - Click the Remove Route button to remove the route currently selected in the Select route number list box. - Configure the Route Destinations for the selected Route Number. -->

If, for some reason, you’re not able to configure Windows to automatically logon by following the above method, please use this method: WARNING: Registry settings are recorded as ADVANCED information and should not be used unless you understand exactly how these will affect the operation of your Adroit installation, IF YOU HAVE ANY DOUBTS, PLEASE CONTACT Adroit SUPPORT, BEFORE CHANGING THE REGISTRY. PLEASE NOTE: When working on a 64 bit operating system, remember to add "\Wow6432Node" to the path of each registry setting after "\SOFTWARE", for instance: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Adroit Technologies". If the following settings are correct the system will automatically log you on the next time that you boot. If the changes are bad, a message box will notify you, closing the box will invoke the standard logon procedure. - From the Start menu, select Run …, type in REGEDIT and click OK - Go to the section: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\WindowsNT\CurrentVersion\WinLogon . - Select Add Value from the REGEDT32 Edit menu and enter the name of AutoAdminLogon with a data type of REG_SZ and a string value "1". - Select Add Value again and enter the name DefaultPassword with a data type of REG_SZ and a string that is the password for your computer. Note: that you must use a password or the logon will not function. - Ensure that the DefaultUserName and DefaultDomainName reflect the user name and domain or computer name that you want to use when you logon. You can change these values using the Edit String menu option. -->

To Configure the I/O Bits or Slots of the ARec agent Top To Configure the I/O Bits or Slots of the ARec agent The State I/O configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which define each I/O bit, as follows: Note1: The grid provides standard configuration options . Note2: Use the vertical scroll bar, when visible, to navigate to the required fields. - Bit: This field, which cannot be edited, specifies the I/O bit, which is being configured. - ID: Configure this field to specify a suitable name that will be used as a slot name for the AREC agent. By default, this column contain the following ID: _Bit##, where ## is a consecutive number from 00 to 31. - Description: Configure this field to describe the function that is performed by this I/O point. - Tag: If this ARec slot is not being scanned directly to the front-end device, then configure this field to specify an external Adroit tag to drive the value of this I/O bit. - Value: This displays the current value of this I/O bit, which is useful when testing that the output bits, if any, are being correctly set or cleared as defined by the configured states . Note: If during the testing of the configured states, when setting the Value field of an output bit, this value will be written to the tag specified in the Tag field. -->

To Configure the States of the ARec agent Top To Configure the States of the ARec agent The State configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which configures each state, as follows: Note1: The grid provides standard configuration options .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Configure the States of the ARec agent Top To Configure the States of the ARec agent The State configuration grid, consists of the following fields, which configures each state, as follows: Note1: The grid provides standard configuration options . Note2: Use the horizontal scroll bar beneath this grid (and the vertical scroll bar when visible) to navigate to the required fields. - The first untitled field, numbers the states in the grid. - Description: Use this field to type in a description of the condition that defines this state. - Mask: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which of the configured I/O bits (ARec slots) need to be considered, when testing for this state. Note: Any bit not set in this Mask field, effectively becomes a DON’T CARE condition for this state. - Test: Configure this bit-mask field to determine, which of the I/O bits specified by the Mask field, need to be set (ON) or cleared (OFF) for this state to be achieved. Note: This Test field effectively determines the ON and OFF conditions for this state. - Set: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which of the output bits, must be set when this state is achieved. - Clear: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which of the output bits, must be cleared when this state is achieved. - Timeout: Use this field to type in a timeout value, in milliseconds, for the state. If the ARec agent remains in this state for the specified time, then the Timeout set and Timeout clear functionality will then be implemented. A value of 0 disables this timeout functionality. - Timeout set: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which of the output bits must be set if the timeout value is reached. - Timeout clear: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which the output bits must be cleared if the timeout value is reached. - Status bits: Configure this bit-mask field to specify which of the 16 private status bits, if any, are to be set when this state is achieved so as to be able to alarm the agent. Note: Clear the Enable outputs checkbox, to prevent any configured output bits from being Set or Clear ed. -->

To Configure the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog Catchup Top Configuring the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog catch-up Datalog catch-up only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Configure the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog Catchup Top Configuring the SystemDatalog Agent for Datalog catch-up Datalog catch-up only applies to clustered Agent Servers and refers to the process of synchronizing, unsynchronised sections of logged data between the two Agent Server partners in the cluster. This involves fetching stored historical data from the datalog agents on the cluster partner and merging the data with the local datalog agents. Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. - Select the systemDl SystemDataLog agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item. This will display the Edit SystemDatalog Agent dialog. - Click the Edit… button next to the catch-up Time to specify the required Time period . All of the data between the two specified times in the datalogs on one of the cluster partners is mirrored across to the datalog agents on the other cluster partner. Tip: Analyzing the data in a trend window to determine the required start and end time of a particular hole. - Click the Update button to save these changes to the Agent Server. - Click the Start catch-up button, to begin the datalog catch-up process, using the configured options. Note: Datalog catch-up will only begin if this Agent Server is in a cluster. ONLY click the Stop catch-up button, to stop the datalog catch-up process, so that its configured options can be changed. - After editing this agent, save the Adroit configuration so that when the Agent Server restarts, these configuration changes will be loaded into the SystemDatalog agent. Note1: This configuration dialog does not include all the datalog catch-up slots , hence it does not display whether the synchronization process has started or its current state of operation etc. Note2: All the datalog catch-up progress and error messages will be sent to the event log if the enable logging of Adroit system events checkbox is selected, under the Eventlog tab of the Adroit setup program. -->

Note: For performance reasons, the SystemDatalog agent ONLY provides the Time datalog catchup method, of catching up the data between two specified date/times. - Select the systemDl SystemDataLog agent. For details, see To Select an Agent . - Right click and select the Edit... menu item. This will display the Edit SystemDatalog Agent dialog. - Click the Edit… button next to the catch-up Time to specify the required Time period . All of the data between the two specified times in the datalogs on one of the cluster partners is mirrored across to the datalog agents on the other cluster partner. Tip: Analyzing the data in a trend window to determine the required start and end time of a particular hole. - Click the Update button to save these changes to the Agent Server. - Click the Start catch-up button, to begin the datalog catch-up process, using the configured options. Note: Datalog catch-up will only begin if this Agent Server is in a cluster. ONLY click the Stop catch-up button, to stop the datalog catch-up process, so that its configured options can be changed. - After editing this agent, save the Adroit configuration so that when the Agent Server restarts, these configuration changes will be loaded into the SystemDatalog agent. Note1: This configuration dialog does not include all the datalog catch-up slots , hence it does not display whether the synchronization process has started or its current state of operation etc. Note2: All the datalog catch-up progress and error messages will be sent to the event log if the enable logging of Adroit system events checkbox is selected, under the Eventlog tab of the Adroit setup program . -->

Title: To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input
To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input Top To Create a Half Hour Average of a Process Input To create a half hourly average of some process input (e.g. TEMP1) that is to be transferred to a database, follow the following method: - Create a half hourly pulse: - Create a digital agent called HALFHOURPULSE and enable a pulse of 100 mS - Create an expression called EX_HALFHOURPULSE with v1=systeminfo.minute, value=HALFHOURPULSE.value and expression=(v1==0)||(v1==30) - Create a half hourly reset pulse that will activate immediately after the half hourly pulse: - Create a digital agent called HALFHOURRESET and enable a pulse of 100 mS. - Create an expression called EX_HALFHOURRESET with v1=HALFHOURPULSE.value, value=HALFHOURRESET.value and expression=!v1 - Implement the half hour averaging of TEMP1: - Create a statistical agent called TEMP1AVE and configure the input tag with TEMP1.value - @scan TEMP1AVE.reset on the SIMPLC device to HALFHOURRESET.value - Repeat step 3a and 3b for all inputs to be averaged - Create the DB transfer for TEMP1: - Create a DBAccess agent called DB_XFR to the required database and table triggered by the digital tag halfhourreset.value - Set up TEMP1AVE.average to a field in the table - Repeat step 4b for each statistical agents created -->

To Edit or Configure a Counter Agent Top Configuring a Counter Agent - Edit an agent of type: Counter .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure a Counter Agent Top Configuring a Counter Agent - Edit an agent of type: Counter . The Edit Counter Agent dialog box is displayed. - Enable Counter agent persistence: This GLOBAL setting prevents the loss of the statistical values calculated by Counter agents. Use this method instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Counter agents, this setting can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . - In the Input Tag box, enter the Input agent and slot. If the Input Tag field is left empty, the agent can use a value supplied from an Operator Action Behaviour linked to its inputValue slot, or directly using the Scheduler to run a PutSlot command, which inserts a new value into the inputValue slot. - Trigger contains the triggering agent name and slot and the Triggered checkbox must be checked to permit external triggering. External triggering is used to update the On/Off time calculations regularly, if the Input Tag is changing at infrequent intervals, then triggering is required at faster intervals. If Trigger is blank, the agent defaults to using each toggling of the input tag’s value to trigger the next count calculation, or in the case where Input Tag is blank, it uses each change in its inputValue slot to do this. - Enter the Time Format using the syntax described under the Date agent . The time slots are reported in this format, which can be changed at any stage, whether the agent is running or stopped. - The percentage of time spent On and Off for the Last and Total times is shown next to the relevant boxes. - Click the Alarms button. The Alarms dialog will appear. - Enter the alarm limits, or use the default limits. - Click OK when finished defining the Alarm limits. - Being event based, the counters are updated only in the event of one of the following slots changing: inputValue, refresh or trigger (if triggered is set). - Toggling the Pause / Continue button temporarily causes the agent to ignore subsequent possible updates to the computed values. How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time : how to allow operators to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) of a Counter agent. -->

For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . - In the Input Tag box, enter the Input agent and slot. If the Input Tag field is left empty, the agent can use a value supplied from an Operator Action Behaviour linked to its inputValue slot, or directly using the Scheduler to run a PutSlot command, which inserts a new value into the inputValue slot. - Trigger contains the triggering agent name and slot and the Triggered checkbox must be checked to permit external triggering. External triggering is used to update the On/Off time calculations regularly, if the Input Tag is changing at infrequent intervals, then triggering is required at faster intervals. If Trigger is blank, the agent defaults to using each toggling of the input tag’s value to trigger the next count calculation, or in the case where Input Tag is blank, it uses each change in its inputValue slot to do this. - Enter the Time Format using the syntax described under the Date agent . The time slots are reported in this format, which can be changed at any stage, whether the agent is running or stopped. - The percentage of time spent On and Off for the Last and Total times is shown next to the relevant boxes. - Click the Alarms button. The Alarms dialog will appear. - Enter the alarm limits, or use the default limits. - Click OK when finished defining the Alarm limits. - Being event based, the counters are updated only in the event of one of the following slots changing: inputValue, refresh or trigger (if triggered is set). - Toggling the Pause / Continue button temporarily causes the agent to ignore subsequent possible updates to the computed values. How to manually specify Total ON or OFF time : how to allow operators to manually specify the Total On Time (and/or Total Off Time) of a Counter agent. -->

text:
To Edit or Configure a PerfMon Agent Top Configuring a PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure a PerfMon Agent Top Configuring a PerfMon Agent The Perfmon agent . Since Adroit is a 32 bit application, if you have installed a 64 bit operating system then when you run the default Performance Monitor (PERFMON.EXE) all the counters for Adroit will be missing, because the 64 bit version of PERFMON is being run which can only load 64bit counter dlls! Therefore, in order to force Windows to load the 32 bit version of PERFMON, open the Command Prompt and specify the following statement: mmc /32 perfmon.msc - Edit an agent of type: PerfMon . The Edit PerfMon Agent dialog box is displayed. Note: Due to the long names of these performance counters, it is possible to resize this edit dialog appropriately. This edit dialog will remember these settings when it is next opened. - Use the grid to add, configure and remove the Performance counters. This grid is comprised of the following columns, which are used to configure the Performance counters, as follows: Note: The grid provides standard configuration options . - Counter: Use this field to specify a Performance counter, either type in this counter directly or click the Browse button, to launch the Browse Performance Counters dialog. - Tag: If necessary, use this field specify an external Adroit tag, to which the value of this Performance counter will be sent. Either type in this tag directly or click the Browse button, to launch the agent browser . For instance the total memory used i.e. \\Memory\\Committed Bytes could be sent to the value slot of an Analog agent, which could be alarmed if this value exceeded the physical memory of the computer. - Value: This column, which cannot be edited, only displays the value of the selected Performance counter, which is updated at one second intervals. - Click the Update button to save the change(s) made to the configuration of the agent. - Click the Refresh button to determine the current configuration of the agent. - The Browse button is used for browsing for Counters or Tags , depending upon which cell is currently selected in the grid. -->

text:
To Edit or Configure a PID Agent Top Configuring a PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure a PID Agent Top Configuring a PID Agent The PID agent is a simply a faceplate agent for external PID controllers, encapsulating the 25 signals and tuning parameters associated with a PID within a single agent. For details, see The PID agent . - Edit an agent of type: PID . The Edit PID Agent dialog box is displayed. - The PID agent’s data values can be broken down into 5 distinct groups with the following names and associated meanings: - PID Signals: this contains the input to and the output from the PID and its desired SP (set-point). For both the PV (process value) and the CV (control variable) this defines their minimum and maximum engineering values and their corresponding minimum and maximum values that the raw value can attain in the front-end device in order to scale the raw values into engineering values using meaningful units of measurement. Since this may vary between device types, the user should ascertain the correct front-end device span is used for each value. The value of these PID signals, including the SP (the required set-point) can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. Both SP and PV will always share the SAME minimum and maximum Engineering and Raw values. The SP and CV values provide a Max limit and Min limit which specify their effective operation range. Note: Once these limits are set these values cannot be manually set above and below these limits. The inner (H or L) and outer (HH or LL) High and Low alarm limits for the PV can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. Note: When the Cascade checkbox is ticked, the SP is controlled by the output (PV) of another PID agent, therefore the SP edit box is greyed out. Also when the Automatic checkbox is ticked, the CV is calculated by the PID controller, therefore the CV edit box is greyed out. - Tuning parameters: this contains the parameters for all the different control methods that can be used by the external PID controller i.e. the Proportional gain and Integral time and Derivative time . This defines their minimum and maximum engineering values and their corresponding minimum and maximum values that the raw value can attain in the front-end device in order to scale the raw values into engineering values using meaningful units of measurement. Since this may vary between device types, the user should ascertain the correct front-end device span is used for each value. The value of these tuning parameters can also be specified in engineering units, with their raw value equivalents being displayed. - %Error: this determines the Value of the %Error (the deviation of the PV from the SP), expressed as a positive or negative percentage, with a positive value indicating that the PV is above the desired SP and a negative value indicating that the PV is below the desired SP. The inner (H) and outer (HH) High alarm limits for %Error , also expressed as a negative or positive percentage, can also be specified. - General: this specifies general settings that apply to the entire PID agent. - A Units text field is provided to record the chosen measurement unit for the PID Signals. - The Cascade checkbox is provided to enable or disable the Cascade status of the external PID controller. - The Automatic checkbox is provided to enable the Automatic (if ticked) or Manual (if unticked) status of the external PID controller. The Local checkbox is for future use.

text:
- Control: currently this group is not used, although the PID agent may support its own PID algorithm for control, in the future.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- Control: currently this group is not used, although the PID agent may support its own PID algorithm for control, in the future. - This Edit PID dialog also contains the following buttons: - The Update button, this can be used after any of the configurable fields have been edited to update the display of the dialog, without closing and reopening this dialog. - The Refresh button, this can be used to update the display of the dialog with the most current values fetched from the field. - The Auto refresh button, this disables the Update button and effectively preventing any user-configuration of the dialog as the display of the dialog is constantly updated with the most current values fetched from the field, to be able to monitor the control by the external PID controller. Note: Do not try to edit values while this mode is on. -->

text:
To Edit or Configure the DbAccess Agent Top Configuring the DbAccess Agent The DbAccess agent .

Title: Configuration
To Edit or Configure the DbAccess Agent Top Configuring the DbAccess Agent The DbAccess agent . NB Read through the usage guidelines of this agent first. - Edit an agent of type: DbAccess . The Edit DbAccess Agent dialog box is displayed - Click the browse button to the right of the Connection string to specify the connection details to the OLE DB database that you want to transact on. For details, see Connecting to an OLE DB database . If remote User Interfaces are to configure these agents then the database folder must be shared and the location to the database file must be expressed in the UNC (Universal Naming Convention) format: \\ComputerName\ShareName\dataBaseFileName The DbAccess Agent only establishes one connection per database; so many DbAccess Agents may share the same connection if they transact with the same database. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database. This should NOT be the default Local System account. See Configuring Agent Server Service User Profile. - Check Connect to database , to allow the table to be selected from the database, in general use, this is used to determine whether the transactions between Adroit and the database can occur. - Then click the Update button, which updates the agent with the configuration changes. - In the Table name edit box, specify the name of the table in which the transactions are to occur, by: - Entering the name of the table directly into the edit box. - If there is at least one connection to the database identified in the connection string, then the browse button can be used to select the required table, from the list of tables available in the selected database. - If you have clustered Agent Servers that both access the same database then check the Disable on standby checkbox to prevent double entries for "Insert" transactions. The default state is unchecked. Note: If enabled, the master Agent Server will perform the Retrieve transaction and shadow the result to the standby Agent Server tags.

metadata.title: To Edit or Configure the DbAccess Agent

text:
If this option is NOT enabled and client runtime transaction shadowing is also enabled, then any Retrieve transactions performed by this DbAccess agent will be performed by both cluster nodes (Agent Servers).

Title: Configuration
If this option is NOT enabled and client runtime transaction shadowing is also enabled, then any Retrieve transactions performed by this DbAccess agent will be performed by both cluster nodes (Agent Servers). For details on enabling client runtime transaction shadowing, see Cluster Server Options . - Check Eventlog errors , to enable the event logging of any errors generated while connecting or transacting with the database. All events will be logged under the category DbAccess in the event log. Alternatively, monitor the information slot of the agent on a mimic. - Under Transaction Type , select the type of transaction that is required to be performed. The available transactions are: Insert row, Update row, Delete row and Retrieve row. - Enter the tag to field mapping i.e. the mapping of tags to the specific fields within the table of the database. These mappings are required for every transaction type, except for the delete transaction. Note1: When connecting to an Oracle database, after the tag to field mappings have been made, add the name of the required database to the Table name edit box, as follows: OracleDataBaseName.SelectedTableName e.g. DB1.Table1 Note2: Support has been added for databases, which require square brackets around the field names otherwise their SQL transactions fail. If required, add the ForceJet registry value . - Use the Identify row edit box, to identify the row in the table of the database, in which the transaction is to occur. This is required for every transaction type, except for the insert transaction. To delete all records in a table, leave this field blank, when using the delete transaction. - Under Transaction scheduling and triggering , either click the Edit… button to configure the scheduling and/or triggering of the transaction or click the Trigger Now button to force the transaction to occur immediately. - The Details… button , displays the Details dialog box, which gives the status of the transactions, by showing any database connection errors and the SQL statement that is being sent to the database. -->

Title: Configuration

text:
To Edit or Configure the Marshal Agent Top Configuring the Marshal Agent The Marshal agent .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure the Marshal Agent Top Configuring the Marshal Agent The Marshal agent . - Edit an agent of type: Marshal . The Edit Marshal Agent dialog box is displayed. - Configure each of the 16 component bits in the grid. . - When using the grid, select the initial row, by selecting the required cell with a left mouse click. - Once a row has been selected then all the values in that row, e.g. the toggled and checkbox values are immediately accessible. - When moving between rows the row must first be selected before the contents of the cell(s) can be altered. - Once a cell has been selected, it is possible to move through the grid using the arrow keys on the keyboard. PageUp and PageDown move the highlighted cell to the top and bottom of the current column, respectively. - Each row of the grid represents a component bit, which has the functionality of a digital agent. - Click Update All to save all the changes made to the Marshal agent. - Click Update Current to only save the changes made to the currently selected row. - Click Refresh to display the current state of the Marshal agent. - Check Reverse Mapping to reverse the direction in which the individual bits for the digital agents are stripped from the 16 bit raw value slot i.e. so that most significant bit e.g. dig0, before reverse mapping has been selected, becomes the least significant bit e.g. dig15. Note: this option is applicable for the entire Marshal agent. - The Value integer displays the value slot, which is the value of the raw value slot after the effects of the reversing of the individual bits have been determined. Manually editing this value will change the individual value states of the component bits and the value of the raw value slot accordingly. Note: This value slot also has an associated Time slot, which records the time stamp of this slot and is used when this slot is being logged. - The Rawvalue integer displays the value of the raw value slot. This integer would normally be scanned in from the PLC. The Marshal Agent splits this integer into the individual raw value states for each of the component bits. Manually editing this value will change the individual value states of the component bits and the value of the value slot accordingly. -->

text:
To Edit or Configure the MultiState Agent Top To Edit or Configure the MultiState Agent The MultiState agent .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure the MultiState Agent Top To Edit or Configure the MultiState Agent The MultiState agent . - Edit an agent of type: Multistate . The Edit Multistate Agent dialog box is displayed. - The bottom half of the dialog contains the Inputs group box. In this box is a slot for each input, labeled v01 through v16. To source the input from any other agent, the engineer simply types in the agent.slot string, or pastes it in by using the agent Browser to make an ongoing real-time connection to the agent and slot referenced. To see the value rather than the name of the data source, all the engineer needs to do is select the Values as opposed to the Names radio button at the bottom right hand corner of the dialog. - The v01-v16 input slots can be dynamically renamed for each MultiState agent. If the Names radio button is selected and a character string is typed into one of the v01 to v16 fields that is NOT recognised as an agent.slot name, it will be treated as a replacement slot name in place of the default slot name. - The top half of the dialog contains the States group box, and it is here that the engineer modifies the agent’s state configuration. Clicking either the Add... or Edit... buttons opens the MultiState State Configuration dialog, which allows you to: - Page sequentially forwards and backwards through the different states by using the Next and Previous buttons - Go directly to any one of the sixteen possible agent’s states by choosing it from the State No . list box - Enter or modify the state description text for the selected state. Note: In order to add a new state, a description of the new state must be entered into the Description box. - Remove a state by deleting a state’s description text - Specify the input-true and input-false masks that effectively define the state being configured. Select inputs from the list of available inputs into either the True or False list to ensure that this new state is not duplicated. - Specify two lists of outputs that will be automatically carried out on attainment of this state. Outputs in the True-List will be set TRUE and outputs in the False list will be set FALSE. Note: this output should not be fed back to the MultiState agent itself, either directly or indirectly. A circular reference error will be given, since agents are generally not recursive. Although this agent has the facility to be used as a marshalling agent this has been replaced by the Marshal agent, which is specifically designed to do this task and is more powerful and easier to use. For details, see The Marshal Agent . -->

text:
To Edit or Configure the Script Agent Top To Edit or Configure the Script Agent The Script agent .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure the Script Agent Top To Edit or Configure the Script Agent The Script agent . NB Read through the usage guidelines of this agent first. See Also: List of Script Functions (with usage examples) . - Edit an agent of type: Script . The Edit Script Agent dialog box is displayed. - Use the Select Language , list box, to choose the programming language, in which the script is written in. The two options are: - VBScript: refers to the Microsoft Visual Basic scripting language, the default selection. - JScript: refers to the Microsoft Java scripting language - Leave Disable scripting . in its default unchecked state. If checked, then the script will not run when the Script agent is triggered. - Check Eventlog errors , to enable the event logging of any script errors. Any compilation and run time errors will appear in the Adroit eventlog. Note: An event is logged if a script is executed that contains compilation errors, preventing it from being run. However, this event could result in the event log from being flooded, therefore ensure that the event log is closely monitored and that any buggy scripts are either fixed or disabled ASAP! - Use Modules to add, delete or edit the list of modules that constitute the script. Each module may contain variable declarations, subroutines and functions. If you use the Adroit search path you need only specify the module name. Note1: When using a remote User Interface, modules can only be edited and their sub-routines selected, if the script files have been browsed in using the UNC Universal Naming Convention (UNC) is used to specify the location of servers, printers, files and other shared resources on a local area network (LAN). UNC names begin with \\ (two backslashes) and take the form: \\Computer_name\Share_name file notation i.e. \\ComputerName\ShareName\scriptPath&FileName, otherwise it will use the path on the respective local drive of the remote computer, to locate the file. Note2: If you are using scripts to obtain datetime tags such as systeminfo.currenttime – the time is now returned as a local time, therefore NO time CONVERSIONS are REQUIRED. - Under Main subroutine: browse the name of the subroutine that will be executed (when the script is run), from the list of all the subroutines contained within the specified module files. Only input parameters (ByVal) may be passed to this subroutine. click in order to run the main subroutine immediately. Note1: Input parameters must be comma delimited, text input parameters must be enclosed in double quotes e.g. "TextParameter" and tags may not be used as input parameters. Note2: The name of this main subroutine CANNOT be the name of the Script agent. - Specify how this "main" subroutine is to executed. For details, see Running the Main Subroutine . - Click the Advanced… button, to display the Advanced Script Agent Properties dialog box, to specify a script initialization and /or cleanup subroutine. - Click the Update button, which updates the agent with the configuration changes. Usually this is done before clicking the Details… button. Note: If script modules are unchanged and unedited they will NOT be recompiled UNLESS you click the Update button. - The Details… button, displays the Details dialog box, which gives the status of the main subroutine, by showing any compilation or run time errors that occur. -->

text:
To Edit or Configure the Statistical Agent Top Configuring the Statistical Agent The Statistical agent .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Edit or Configure the Statistical Agent Top Configuring the Statistical Agent The Statistical agent . - Edit an agent of type: Statistical . The Edit Statistical Agent dialog box is displayed. - Enable Statistical agent persistence: This GLOBAL setting prevents the loss of the statistical values calculated by Counter agents. Use this method instead of saving the Agent database (.WGP) file frequently. WARNING! If there are large numbers of Statistical agents, this setting can increase the CPU load of the Agent Server computer. For further details, see Agent Persistence Files . - Input Tag contains the input agent and its slot name, if this field is left empty, the agent can use a value supplied from a picture element, using the Operator Action Behaviour linked to its inputValue slot. The Units edit box, contains the units of measurement. - The Data specification Method is StreamEvent - Measurement trigger contains the triggering agent name and slot and the Triggered checkbox must be checked to permit external triggering. If its blank then the agent defaults to using each change to the input tag’s value to trigger the next statistical calculation, or in the case where no Input Tag is specified, it uses each change in its inputValue slot. - Totaliser scale , contains factor (any real number) by which the Total is scaled. - Floating average , contains the number of measurements to be averaged, and is required, before this moving Average and Standard Deviation function is Enabled . - Click the Alarms button, and enter the alarm limits for each statistical data element (except for Standard Deviation), or use the default limits (see Specific Status Bits ) - Start the agent by clicking the Start button. Stop the agent by clicking the same button (its legend will change to Stop). The agent will reset itself by beginning its statistical analysis again using the next input value as the first measurement of a new sample. - If the agent is halted and then resumed using the Pause / Continue button, the statistical data will not be reset itself. -->

To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging Top To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging The user has no direct control over the speed at which the raw data log file will grow.

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging Top To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging The user has no direct control over the speed at which the raw data log file will grow. Therefore, it is important to calculate the maximum space each agent may occupy, before the data log file wraps around and overwrites itself from the beginning. This figure can be compared to the actual free disk space available on the host computer. Two files are involved in storing historical data: the raw data log file (.LGD) and its index file (.LGI) which uses comparatively little space. Tip: If you use datalog backups, which create .LDB files, then you can extend the potential amount of logged data without creating larger log files. In this case, while the active log (LGD) file can remain small, the log backup (.LDB) files can store historical data for much longer time periods. For details, see Datalog backup and retrieval . The amount of disk space reserved for data logging is a function of the rate at which the tag is being logged i.e. the time between each sample and the total logging period specified for each tag, summed for all the tags being logged. Each log record takes 20 bytes therefore it would be expected that the following formulae would be used to calculate the maximum raw disk space that may be used for each .LGD file: Raw Buffer size (bytes) = 20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate) Raw File size (bytes) = Sum of all Raw Buffer sizes Example of raw disk space calculations . However, the original design of datalogging made the assumption that the data would only change 5 times slower than the rate actually configured and therefore Adroit is designed to only reserve 20% of the space calculated above. Hence the following formulae must be used to accurately calculate the actual disk space that will be used for each .LGD file: PLEASE NOTE: Adroit ’s proprietary logging uses an in-built logging factor, which reduces the specified logging period by 80%. UNLESS a clean installation of Adroit is installed, in which case this logging factor is NOT applied. For details, see Adroit Logging Factor .

Title: To Estimate the Disk Space Required for Data Logging
Actual Buffer size (bytes) = [20 x (Logging Period/Logging Rate)]/5 Actual File size (bytes) = Sum of all Buffer sizes While the above design assumption can be considered true for faster logging rates such as 1 second, this is definitely not the case for slower rates such as 1 minute or 1 hour where the values (especially analog values) will have definitely changed. In the latter Adroit will only have capacity to log for 1/5th of the configured period necessitating the user to over specify his logging period by a factor of 5. Note: It is possible to override this 20% data log capacity or the "divide by 5" storage factor, by setting the LogCompressionFactor registry setting. Each Datalog agent has a maximum of 53 million records, which can provide at least 30 days of logging at a log rate of 50 milliseconds! For instance: if the log rate is 100 ms, 10 values are logged per second, 36000 values/hour, 864000 values/day, so the total logging length of this datalog file = 53000000/864000 = 61.34 days. Instead of using one log file for all agents, you can create different log files for agents (values) that require different logging speeds. For example, DAY.LGD, WEEK.LGD, MONTH.LGD and YEAR.LGD. Note: Adroit allows a slot of an agent to be datalogged once only. If multiple logfiles need to be created from, for example, an ANA01.value, then this can be done by using an intermediate agent such as an Expression agent called EXP01. Insert the ANA01.value into the Expression Agent’s slots v01, v02 and v03, and configure EXP01 for data logging, such that: ANA01.value is logged at 1 second intervals for 5 days into logfile DAY.LGD EXP01.v01 is logged at 15 second intervals for 7 days into logfile WEEK.LGD EXP01.v02 is logged at 120 second intervals for 31 days into logfile MONTH.LGD EXP01.v03 is logged at 8 hour intervals for 365 days into logfile YEAR.LGD -->

To Export an Agent Type Top Exporting an Agent Type If agents need to be exported (i.e. converted to a .CSV file) from an Agent Server loadfile (.WGP file): Note: The Adroit agent exporting utility cannot export numeric values when they are the type STRING. Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. - Select the Export… menu item of the Classic UI File menu. - Click Yes to the confirmation if the WGP file has been recently saved and continue with the Exporting operation. - First select the required Agent Server loadfile (.WGP file), from the Choose file to convert dialog. - A confirmation dialog appears for each agent type that has configured agents and that can be exported , beginning from the agents starting with the letter ‘a’ and continuing through them in alphabetic order, unless the exporting process is terminated: - If you do choose to export the specified agent type, the Choose file to contain conversion dialog appears, where you will be asked to supply a file name for the subsequent .CSV file that is created for the agent type. You may use any filename, but it must terminate with a .CSV file extension. WARNING: Ensure that the path and file name of the exported CSV file is less than 65 characters, when exporting your agents, since Adroit is unable to import agents from CSV files, which have paths in excess of 65 characters. To Import an Agent Type Top Importing an Agent Type Configuration data can be exported from Adroit and edited off-line in third party applications, like Microsoft Excel, as comma separated variable data (.CSV) and then converted into an Adroit .WGP load file format.

Title: Importing an Agent Type
Steps:
To Import an Agent Type Top Importing an Agent Type Configuration data can be exported from Adroit and edited off-line in third party applications, like Microsoft Excel, as comma separated variable data (.CSV) and then converted into an Adroit .WGP load file format. Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the Import item of the Classic UI File menu. Note1 : Agents that already exist are not imported at all. Therefore, ensure that the agents that are to be re-imported are deleted first, before importing the modified agents. Remember, agents cannot be deleted before they have been un-alarmed, unscanned and "undatalogged". Note2: DO NOT use commas in the agent descriptions – if a comma is required use a ‘~’ instead. Note3: Adroit is unable to import agents from CSV files, which have paths in excess of 65 characters, even though Adroit is able to export to these long paths. Therefore ensure that the path and file name of the exported CSV file is less than 65 characters, when exporting your agents. Alarm agents CAN be imported into Adroit , making bulk-alarming configuration possible. For details, see Importing Alarm Agents . A typical .CSV file, in this case for Analog agent type, looks like this: Each agent type has its own .CSV format If agents need to be imported from a .CSV file, then open the Agent Configurator, and select Import from the File menu and the Choose file to convert dialog will appear: Choose the .CSV file to convert, and then the data will be converted to the .WGP configuration file given in the Save As dialog. This file will be called Import.WGP by default, but the user may choose any filename he or she desires. The file can then be loaded on-line into the current Agent Server using the Load Agents... Classic UI menu item. Note1: When importing scanning information into a Device agent , use the Import button within the Device Agent’s configuration edit dialog Note2: When importing the Master recipe (and its associated Control recipes) into a Recipe agent , use the Import button within the Recipe agent’s Master recipe configuration edit dialog. -->

To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Top To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Typically the Agent Server is configured to run as a Service during the install, although you can do this after the install if necessary by using the following command line switches that the Agent Server process (as.exe) provides: - Press the Windows key + R shortcut to open the Run dialog.

Title: How to set up To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service
Steps:
To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Top To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service Typically the Agent Server is configured to run as a Service during the install, although you can do this after the install if necessary by using the following command line switches that the Agent Server process (as.exe) provides: - Press the Windows key + R shortcut to open the Run dialog. - Type in as.exe followed by following commands and press ENTER: /install /u:"[Domain\]Username" /p:"Password" /quiet This command will install the Agent Server as a service. The /u: and /p: parameters specify the credentials of the user account that the Agent Server service will run as, ensure that you specify a user that has the rights / permissions to access the network resources (printers, SQL Express, network shares) that the Agent Server requires access to. IMPORTANT: The username MUST NOT be "Administrator", the built-in Windows Administrator account, since UAC is automatically disabled whenever this built-in Administrator account is used, which causes a myriad of problems to occur. Note: The [Domain\] portion of the username ONLY applies if the specified user is on a domain. The /quiet parameter suppresses any feedback messages. /uninstall This command will remove the Agent Server as a service. -->

To Make a Copy of an Agent Top Copying an Agent Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents.

Title: Copying an Agent
To Make a Copy of an Agent Top Copying an Agent Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. Select the required agent in the Agent Configurator, as follows: - Ensure that the Basic , Advanced and/or System checkbox is checked to display the required agent type in this list. These checkboxes use these default agent groups to help you select the required agent quickly. Tip: If no checkboxes are selected, then all the available agent types will be displayed in the Type list box. This is useful if the required agent type has not been categorised. - Click the down arrow in the Type drop down list - Locate the required agent type, using the scroll bar and click on it. - In the Agents list, click on the name of the required agent (if necessary scroll down to locate this). Tip: Right-click to display a menu of commands to perform upon the selected agent(s). In the Name field, enter in the new agent’s name. For further details regarding the naming of agents, see Agent Naming Convention . If required, give it a suitable description in the Description field. Click the Copy button to make a copy of the selected agent. -->

To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure Top To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure The following steps can be taken: - Use only NTFS instead of FAT or FAT32 file partitions2.

Title: To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure
Steps:
To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure Top To Minimise the Risk of Datalog Corruption from a Power Failure The following steps can be taken: - Use only NTFS instead of FAT or FAT32 file partitions2. - Remove "flush lazily" setting on Adroit Logging. The adverse side effect of this is that duty cycle on disk will be much more intense, as every change will be flushed right through to disk. In consequence disk may need replacing after several months/years (who knows). In addition system throughput may be reduced. - Make sure a battery-backed UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is installed so that power is never removed from the server in an uncontrolled fashion. This option allows "flush lazily" to be enabled. Note: This option provides the only cast iron guarantee, but most sites find option 1 sufficient. -->

text:
To Modify the Scanning Configuration of Scanned Tags Top Changing the Scanning Configuration of Tags This will change the existing scanning configuration of tags that have been scanned by the selected device.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
To Modify the Scanning Configuration of Scanned Tags Top Changing the Scanning Configuration of Tags This will change the existing scanning configuration of tags that have been scanned by the selected device. Expand the required agent type object in the tree view windowpane - Either select the required agent so that its slots are displayed in the Explorer Agent List grid windowpane on the left, then right click the required slot and select the Scan slot… menu item. - Or right click the required agent, in the tree view, and select the Scan… menu item. This displays the Adroit Tag Scanning Dashboard dialog. Note: This dialog can be resized, to view lengthy scanning configuration, if necessary. - Select the required pre-configured device in the Device list box, from the list of available device drivers. Note: If there is a driver that was not setup during installation, it can be added later by running Adroit Setup and adding a new driver. The Agent Server will NOT need to be restarted. - In the scanned tag list, below this Device list box, click on the scanned tag that needs to be modified. - In the Add tag edit box, if required, modify the currently selected agent and slot combination. - In the Device address edit box, if required, modify the protocol driver specific address in this Device to which the value of this tag will be stored. - In the Scan rate (ms) edit box, if required, modify the scanning interval or period in milliseconds between attempts to poll this item. Note: This will only apply to polled devices; telemetry devices will ignore this parameter. - In the Deadband edit box, if required, modify the limit that the change in the scanned value must exceed before the agent’s slot is updated. This Deadband is in the same units as the tag that is being scanned. For performance reasons, it is advisable to give a non-zero Deadband for Analog or Integer values in order to filter out noise or minor variations in value, since applying a Deadband reduces the number of changes to the database thus improving performance. Note: It is NOT advisable to use a Deadband when scanning tags that contain state information, as you may lose significant bits of information when decoding to binary form. - If required, tick the Output enabled checkbox, to enable this scanned tag to update the PLC (front-end device). Note: This does not affect this scanned tag from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). - Click the Add button to modify the current selection in the scanned tag list for this selected Device . -->

Note: It is NOT advisable to use a Deadband when scanning tags that contain state information, as you may lose significant bits of information when decoding to binary form. - If required, tick the Output enabled checkbox, to enable this scanned tag to update the PLC (front-end device). Note: This does not affect this scanned tag from being updated by the PLC (front-end device). - Click the Add button to modify the current selection in the scanned tag list for this selected Device . -->

metadata.title: To Modify the Scanning Configuration of Scanned Tags

To Remove an Installed Protocol Driver Top Removing an Installed Protocol Driver In order to uninstall a protocol driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific.

Title: How to set up To Remove an Installed Protocol Driver
To Remove an Installed Protocol Driver Top Removing an Installed Protocol Driver In order to uninstall a protocol driver a DLL that interfaces Adroit to front end devices, these are the only Adroit components that are device specific. from Adroit , follow the following procedure: - Remove ALL the devices configured for this driver, by first removing all the scanned points from these Device agents. This will also perform the following operations: - Any registry values associated with these devices will be removed from the Adroit registry key, but not the registry key(s) themselves. - Any Performance Monitor counters added for the driver will be removed. - Read the installed driver documentation to determine if any other files were copied to the computer, if so they also need to be manually removed, also remove any additional 3 rd party software that was installed for this driver (if any). - Delete the DLL file associated with this driver from the Adroit source folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit . To confirm that the file has been deleted, open the Drivers tab of the Adroit Setup and the driver should no longer appear in the Available protocol driver list Tip: You can obtain the exact file and path of the required driver DLL file from the Filename attribute in the information pane on the right of the relevant Driver configuration dialog, after selecting the required protocol driver from the Installed Drivers and Devices list. For further details about protocol drivers, see Protocol Drivers . -->

Title: Specifications
To Specify the Column Format for Event Output Agents Top To Specify the Column Format for Event Output Agents From the Event Output Agent dialog, select the Format button. The Columns Format dialog box is configured as follows: - Transfer the required fields between the Available list and Current list by: - Double left clicking the item. - Using the appropriate move to, << and >> button. - The Insert button will place a selected field in the Available list above the selection in the Current list. - The Start and Width boxes identify the starting point and width of each field. Initially the default settings are specified. Adjust the widths to suit your report and then click the Compress button to reset the column widths. The following table describes the available Columns: Column Name Column Description Adroit Windows Date Date of event (e.g. 22/09/96) Yes Yes Time Time of event (e.g. 09:42:56.583) Note: This Time column supports MILLISECONDS, hence this column can be up to 12 characters in width i.e. HH:MM:SS.nnn, where nnn are the number of milliseconds that have elapsed. Yes Yes Agent tag Agent, object or Agent type Yes Alarm type msg Alarm Type as configured Yes Category Event category (alarm, control, jotting, general, software, recipe, information, warning, recoverable error, unrecoverable error, invalid message, no message file) Yes Yes Reported Data Data slots specified in Alarm Type configuration Yes Description Description of agent (found in Header) Yes Yes Action e.g. Set, Cleared, Acknowledged Globally, etc. Yes Computer Name of Computer (see Control Panel / System) Yes Yes Source Program name e.g. Agent Server Yes Yes Event Id Event identity number e.g. 17 Yes Yes Extra Data Additional binary data Yes Yes Filter Group -1 or 0 Yes Priority Priority of agent : Lowest (0) to Highest (4) Yes Sub-Source Name of Alarm agent, Username, Agent Server Yes User Username Yes - Select the OK button to accept the changes and return to the Event Output agent Edit dialog. -->

Press the Windows key and start typing in Classic Setup and select it from the list. - Click on the Drivers tab and then click the Install ( ) button, to display the Adroit protocol driver installation dialog. - If you need to specify another location from which to install Adroit protocol drivers, click the ( … ) browse button next to the Path edit box, to locate this disk or folder . - Click the Upgrades… button. This will search your Adroit system folder, typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit for any installed protocol drivers and compare the versions of these located files with the versions of the driver files located in the specified Path . - Any installed drivers, whose driver revisions are lower than the drivers in the specified Path are then displayed in the Available Protocol Drivers list. - Select the driver you wish to add from the Available protocol drivers list, using the scroll bar and clicking on the required entry. - Use the Details button to view the component files of the selected driver and the path into which each of the files are to be installed on your system. - Click the Copy button to copy the driver to your Adroit system folder. - Click the Close button to exit the dialog, once all the necessary protocol drivers have been installed. Note: When Adroit is uninstalled the installed Adroit drivers are not uninstalled. Using the Adroit Config Editor : This functionality is currently not provided. -->
