Tools for editing and designing vectors and/or controls Top Tools for arranging and designing vectors and/or controls The SmartUI Designer provides a number of tools to assist with arranging and designing form components a general term encompassing all the controls, components and / or graphic elements that can be added to graphic forms, to provide the required user interface for its end-users. See control; component; graphic element; graphic form. on the currently displayed graphic form. These tools are located within the Design tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon, which is displayed by selecting the Design tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon The Design tab provides the following groups of tools: - Vectors : tools for ONLY working with vectors (graphic elements). For details, see Vector tools for editing and designing vectors . - Workspace : tools for arranging and organizing ALL form components. For details, see Workspace tools for arranging form components . - Font : click a form component or a displayed text property, then use this to select or modify its font. - color : this section provides the following color-property specific tools: - color selection control: click a form component or ANY of its color properties to change its color. Click for more details on how to use this selection control: either use the top two scroll buttons to move up and down the rows within this selection control or click the bottom button to expand the selection control to display all the available selection options, which collapses once you have made your selection. The following tool ONLY applies to configuring graphical elements (vectors): - Gradient selection control: click a vector or vector group and then either click Gradient to apply the currently selected gradient or click the drop down list button to the right to change the current gradient by selecting one of the pre-defined Gradient Types and/or changing the required gradient color and/or the Intensity or transparency of the gradient fill. The following tool ONLY applies to configuring the Backcolor property of a form component: - Format Painter : click the form component whose Backcolor you want to copy to another form component, then click the Format Painter option and then click the required form component whose Backcolor property you want to configure. - Snapping : tools that assist in aligning or positioning form components with respect to existing form components, when dragging them within the graphic form. Note: Changing the current snapping method used for a graphic form, requires the graphic form to be saved and reloaded. Select the required snapping method that you want to use from the Snap Mode list box, as follows: Note: Unless the Enable Vector Snapping Check checkbox is checked, the selected snapping method ONLY applies to the controls on the graphic form and not the vectors. Tip: This checkbox should typically only be unchecked when using the SnapLines option, which can be very irritating especially when there are a lot of vectors that are randomly placed on the graphic form. - Off : to turn off all snapping of form components - if you find this feature annoying and/or want to manually align your form components. - SnapLines : to use snap lines, which are typically blue, when dragging controls to the sides of the existing controls (and if the Enable Vector Snapping Check checkbox is checked, these lines are also displayed when dragging vectors and this also allows controls and vectors to be snapped to the sides and/or centers of vectors). Note: When dragging controls that contain text, pink snap lines appear to align the text with the text of other controls.

Title: Tooltip Behaviours
Tooltip Behaviours Top Tooltip Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to display additional information usually concerning this object when the mouse cursor (pointer) hovers also called a mouse hover, is the action of putting the mouse cursor (pointer) over a designated area. over it. These tooltips are similar to those associated with toolbars, in that when the mouse pointer hovers over the object, a rectangle containing text appears. Tip: Apart from displaying the user-specified text, the tooltip can also display the values of one or more data elements. To add a tool tip to a control or vector: - Add or edit an Tooltip Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Specify the text for this tooltip to display in the Tooltip text edit box. Tip: You can use the ENTER key to move to the next line of text. In addition to text, you can add the value of one or more data elements, as follows: Specify the required values and, if necessary, their required formatting, in the table below the Tooltip text edit box, as follows: - Click the browse button to the right of the Data Element edit box to select the required data element (value), as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element. The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog.

- A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path.

Title: Tooltip Behaviours
- A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. - If necessary, use the Format field to specify the required formatting of each value (as it appears in the tooltip description), by: - either typing in the required formatting string directly and/or - clicking the browse button and using the Format String Editor configuration dialog to specify and/or preview the specified formatting. Insert the specified data element values into the text of the Tooltip text edit box, as follows: - EITHER: select the required row (data element) in the table and drag it to the required location in the Tooltip text edit box. - OR: select the required row (data element) in the table, click where in the Tooltip text edit box you want this value inserted and then click the Insert selected Data Element into Tooltip text at Cursor button immediately below the Tooltip text edit box. - Use the Tooltip position grid to determine the placement of the tooltip description box, relative to the object that it is added to. - Use the Tooltip preview section to test the placement and formatting of the tooltip text, since when your mouse cursor moves over the Hover here text in the Tooltip preview section, the tooltip with the current settings appears. Note: Since the Tooltip Preview displays exactly what is typed into the Tooltip text edit box, only the data element placeholders appear and if the Tooltip text edit box is empty then no tooltip appears. - If necessary, click the Advanced View button to specify some or all of the following additional configurable options: Tooltip settings : specify the font and/or background and text colors of this tooltip, as follows: - Click the browse button to the left of the Text font field and use the Font selection dialog to select the required font. For details, see Selecting fonts . - To specify custom background and text colors, uncheck the Use windows default tooltip color settings checkbox, then use the relevant color edit box to specify the required Background color and Text color for this tooltip. For details, see Selecting colors . Tip: Use the Tooltip preview section to try out these tooltip settings. Tooltip delays : configure the following delays, in milliseconds: - before the tooltip appears ( Delay time before open ) and - how long the tooltip is displayed for (kept open) after it appears ( Delay time after open ). Event Trigger : specify which event of this control or graphic element (vector) triggers this Behaviour, as follows: - Either select the required event from the list of common or frequently used events.

- Or click the browse button and use the Event Selector to select the required event.

Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is enabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is disabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function Text String The text string displayed by this tool tip. Backcolor color The background color of the tool tip box. Forecolor color The color of the tool tip text. Font Font The font of the tool tip text. Initial Delay Integer The delay, in milliseconds, after which the tool tip is triggered to be displayed to prevent the unintended display of this tool tip. Auto Pop Delay Integer How long, in milliseconds, this tool tip should be displayed before it closes. Anchor Location Select the required position on the form component to display the tool tip from the available options. If you choose Custom then use the Location input to specify the offsets relative to the Top, Left corner, in pixels. - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function New Input Add values or other variables that you want to add to the tool tip text, which appear as inputs, such as 0, 1, 2 etc. You can then link these inputs to the required values to provide these inputs. Note: You need to manually add place-holders to the Text input for each value that you want to display, these placeholders take the form of the respective input number enclosed in braces '{}', for instance {0}for input 0. - Event Trigger , configure this section to specify the form component that will display this tool tip, where: Event Output is typically the name of the required form component on this graphic form and Event Name is typically MouseHover , although you can use any event to trigger the display of this tool tip. -->

Title: Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents
Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents Top Transaction Types of DbAccess Agents The DbAccess agent can perform the following transactions: - Insert row: Use this transaction to insert a new record of tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). /s into a table, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is not required for this transaction, as the new record is inserted at the end of the existing records in the table. Note: If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then when a cluster is accessing the same database, this setting prevents both nodes (Agent Servers) in a cluster from executing the transaction thereby causing double entries for "Insert" transactions. - Update row: Use this transaction to update a row in a table with new tag/s, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Row identification is required for this transaction to take place. - Delete row: Use this transaction to delete one or many rows from a table in a database. This is the only transaction that does not require a tag-to-field mapping. IMPORTANT: If the row identification field is left empty , then all of the rows in the table are removed and the entire table is deleted . - Retrieve row: Use this transaction to update tag/s with value/s from a row of a table in a database, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. The DbAccess Agent has to know in what format date/time information is kept in the database to perform a successful translation. Note: This agent also supports the retrieval of time-stamped values from SQL into Adroit Filetime slot values. If the Disable on standby configuration setting is enabled, then the master Agent Server will perform the Retrieve transaction and shadow the result to the standby Agent Server tags. If this option is NOT enabled and client runtime transaction shadowing is also enabled, then any Retrieve transactions performed by this DbAccess agent will be performed by both cluster nodes (Agent Servers). For details on enabling client runtime transaction shadowing, see Cluster Server Options . -->

You also need to select the name of the required associated Adroit database, from the Adroit DataSource drop-down list. This will expose all the tags that you want your users to trend (contained within the required plant areas and their devices) and automatically populates the provided lists with their values. Since each MAPS project enforces an extended physical hierarchical structure of automation projects specified by the ISA S88 and S95 standards, when specifying which values (tags) need to be trended, the Column Settings tab of the TrendConfigurator Setup dialog provide the following options: Note: Of these columns only the Pen and Title is mandatory, both the Area and Device columns can be hidden if needed. - Area: this is the Area level of physical structure of automation projects described by the ISA S95 and S88 standards. The level above this is the Site level. The Area contains one or more Process Cells or PLCs, which in Adroit-speak are communicated to via Devices. Typically, when displayed this column provides a drop-down list of all the configured areas of this MAPS project.

Note: If necessary, you can use the PresetArea property to specify a static value that is automatically selected for this column, that disables its drop-down list to prevent any other value from being specified.

Title: To add a tag to the Graph tabbed page:
- Ensure that the tag monitoring process is stopped i.e. the Stop button is clicked and is currently greyed out. - In the Tags tabbed page, select a tag whose value is required to be trended. - Right-click and select Add to graph . The values of any tag(s) that have been added to this page, will be trended when the tag monitoring process is started i.e. the Start button is clicked and is currently greyed out. The view of the tag (agent.slot) values that have been or are being trended can be modified by means of the right-click menu that provides the following commands in this tabbed page: - Inspect: When this command is enabled for a trended tag, each distinct value is indicated by means of a square box, which when clicked, displays a tool tip containing the value and time at which this value occurred. To enable this command for a trended tag, click on the row representing the tag in the legend, at the bottom of the page, this will select the line (causing it to become white) then right-click this row and select Inspect . Note: This can also be performed by selecting the required trend line and pressing CTRL+I . - Stairs: This command, when enabled, changes the method of interpolation used when displaying the trended line between successive values from a straight connecting line to horizontal and vertical lines (steps). This command can be enabled or disabled as required, when enabled a tick mark appears to the left of this command in the right-click menu. Note: This viewing option can also be enabled or disabled by pressing CTRL+S . - Delete: This will remove the selected trended value from this tabbed page. To delete a trended tag, click on the row representing the tag in the legend, at the bottom of the page, this will select the line (causing it to become white) then right-click this row and select Delete . Note: This can also be performed by selecting the required trend line and pressing Delete . - Graph time span…: This displays the Change graph time span dialog, which allows the entire period of time displayed by this Graph window to be specified in the following format: hours:minutes:seconds. The default is one minute i.e. 00:01:00. Note: The required time span for the trend can also be configured by pressing CTRL+W . Furthermore, the view of the tag (agent.slot) values can be zoomed into or out of as follows: - Zooming in: It is possible to enlarge a portion of the displayed trend, for instance, to better inspect or determine the values of the trended values, as follows: - Click the top left most corner of the area that needs to be magnified or enlarged in the trend. - Hold the left mouse button down and drag down towards the bottom right hand corner of the required area. - This will display a white box that defines the area of the graph that will be enlarged. - Release the left mouse button once the required area has been defined. - Zooming out: It is possible to return the original magnification once an area has been zoomed in, as follows: - Simply click anywhere in the graph, hold the left mouse button down. - Drag upwards towards the top left hand corner and release the left mouse button. Note: Ensure that a sizable area has been defined before releasing. -->

Triggering spiders Top Triggering spiders Spiders need to be triggered so they can perform their functions.

Title: Triggering spiders
Triggering spiders Top Triggering spiders Spiders need to be triggered so they can perform their functions. Spiders can be triggered using a variety of methods, choose the method that best suits your purpose: - Silk triggering: The default triggering method, where each silk connected to the input of a spider can trigger this spider. In other words a silk will trigger its destination spider, after the output value of its source spider changes. Note: Certain spiders disable this triggering method by default. For instance, if spiderA is connected to spiderB, by silkA, then whenever the specified output value of spiderA changes, silkA will update spiderB’s input and then trigger spiderB to perform its operation. Note1: It is recommended to use silk triggering when transferring data between spiders instead of event triggering. Note2: It may be necessary to disable this default triggering of some or all of the silks connected to a spider, for instance, when using another means of triggering. For details, see Disabling silk triggering of spiders . - Event triggering: This involves triggering the spider after a specific event or action is performed: - by a spider, which has already been added to this spider workspace e.g. if an input of the specified spider is changed. - upon a control, which has already been added to the currently edited graphic form e.g. if the specified button control is clicked. Typically used to trigger spiders based on user input. For configuration details, see Triggering a spider from an event . Note: Title bars contain icons that indicate the status of the Trigger Spider on Event and Propagate Outputs At Startup spider properties respectively. For details, see Spider property indicators . - Manual triggering: This involves immediately triggering the spider, by manually selecting its Trigger Now! menu item to simplify the process of testing spider functionality. This method of triggering allows a user to easily trigger any spider, as and when is necessary. For details, see Configuring spiders . - Spider triggering: The Trigger spider, allows users to tailor the triggering of their existing spiders to their own requirements. This spider is able to trigger one or more spiders at the same time, whenever it is itself triggered. For details, see Trigger spiders . Note1: Triggering is supported by all spiders that are have inputs. Note2: Triggering only occurs when the spider workspace is running i.e. this only occurs for graphic forms when they are displayed in Run mode or within the SmartUI Operator. -->

Note: By default this screen opens in ASCII mode, which is indicated in the title bar of the window, to toggle the mode to HEX and vice verse (depending on protocol), type in "A". - If you are unfamiliar with communication protocols, create a log-file of the messages in the "Datascope" screen, which you can FAX/e-mail it to the Support desk. Note: Having an Internet e-mail address available ensures that the Support desk can forward patches to your computer and/or that you can send your database (the .WGP file) and other relevant information to the Support desk, when using the Support program, by selecting the Start menu, Programs, Adroit 10 , Utilities and then the Support Program item (if this has been installed). Select the Agent Server tab , is the Agent Server Type set to "Cluster server".

TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem Top TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure Determine which request is causing the communication failure.

Title: TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure
Steps:
TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem Top TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. But, if the retry also fails then either Adroit has a bug or has been incorrectly configured. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: - Backup your database (WGP file) - Unscan all the tags to that PLC. - Save and restart the Agent Server. - Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each. Watch for errors, typically by using the Datascope screen of the Driver Monitor. - When the problem occurs, you have the error somewhere in your last group of tags. - Check that the scan-points, within the group that have just been added have actual addresses in the PLC. Sometimes due to a driver bug, if you read the last register/value in a memory block, the driver tries to read the (invalid) one after it. Verify that is not happening. Note: The above steps only apply if the problem is observed on the datascope as being repeatable, i.e. the same driver request causing the same error. -->

Use the PING command to determine if your clustered Agent Server computers are networked correctly.

Title: Networking:
Use the PING command to determine if your clustered Agent Server computers are networked correctly. For instance, in the command prompt, type the following: ping –l 64000 –t partnerServerComputerName If you have a low success rate (many packets being lost or a high round trip time), then your network is the problem, which requires input and action from your I.T. department.

Try to copy a file from the one agent server machine, across the network, to the other agent server machine.

Title: Security:
Try to copy a file from the one agent server machine, across the network, to the other agent server machine. You should be able to achieve this without being prompted for authentication. If this fails, then your Windows security is not identical on the two machines and needs to be investigated.

- Different versions of the product on the two machines.

Title: Other common problems:
Steps:
- Different versions of the product on the two machines. To check this, open the Adroit File Version Information utility and ensure that the file versions of the installed files are identical on both computers. - Firewalls blocking communication between the clustered Agent Server computers. To test this, isolate the system, then switch off the firewalls on both Agent Server computers. If communication is suddenly possible, you need to add the Agent Server process to the allowed programs on both firewalls. - Inadequate licensing. Open the Adroit HASP License Reader and verify. All cluster information and operations including the historical synchronization can be viewed and managed within the UI by using the cluster-controlling graphic form. See the Active Cluster Control tab of the System Management graphic form in the System Information project. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when Clustering Agent Servers . For more details on clustering Adroit Agent Servers, see Active Clusters Foundation . -->

Title: To use the Scanning Monitor to locate a stuck continuous output:
- Launch the Scanning Monitor and connected it to the required Agent Server - Select the required device from topmost Device List . - Select each entry in the middle Scan Job List , This will display the scanned tags within each of these jobs in the bottom Tag List . - Observe the Output enable column of this tag list and investigate each of the tags that have this bit set within this device to locate the culprit. Troubleshooting failed log in attempts Troubleshooting failed login attempts If a Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Troubleshooting failed login attempts
Steps:
Troubleshooting failed log in attempts Troubleshooting failed login attempts If a Smart UI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. has been unable to login to the Smart UI Server computer, a message displays beneath the Password edit box of the Login configuration dialog, to assist you in troubleshooting the error. The following list indicates the possible error messages and their remedies: Error Message Remedy Error! User not allowed to login to environment - Firstly, ensure that the specified user name has been entered correctly and IS added to the Allowed Groups or Allowed Users for this Server. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups. - Secondly, ensure that the password that you are using has been entered correctly and MATCHES the specified user. For instance if you are logging in using a DOMAIN user, then provide the DOMAIN password, alternatively, if logging in using a LOCAL user, provide the LOCAL password. Note: Passwords are case-sensitive. Error connecting to host ...No connection could be made because the target computer actively refused it The Smart UI Server computer cannot be contacted, ensure that the Server computer is operational and then click the Finish button to retry the login. Generally this error is caused by the Smart UI Server and Smart UI Client having different versions. Or an application other than the Server is using the specified port. Note: This error will also occur if the Smart UI Server is NOT licensed. In this case, run the Smart UI Server as an application (NOT as a service) and ensure that the Server is licensed. For details, see Launching the Server. Requested service cannot be found The Smart UI Server computer cannot be contacted, ensure that the Smart UI Server computer is operational and then click the Finish button to retry the login. A required privilege is not held by the client. This will occur on all operating systems, if the user account or group that is being used to log on does not have the necessary user rights assigned. For details of the required user rights and how to apply them, see Windows security configuration. An error occurred. Do you want to attempt to re-connect? The error was: Error! Number of connections licensed exceeded. This message box is displayed when the Smart UI Server that you are trying to connect to, has no available Smart UI Client licenses. Close any connected Clients that are not being used and try to login to this Server again. For details, see Disconnecting all the logged on users. Note: These error messages are determined by the operating system of the Server computer. Only the most common of which are interpreted. For all other error messages, email or provide the support with the exact wording so as to obtain the required remedy. -->

Title: To troubleshoot the importing of spiders and silks:
The troubleshooting of this wizard, is displayed per dialog, as follows: The Import Configuration dialog: On clicking Next the specified XML file is opened, so that the spider and/or silk configuration contained within it can be imported into this spider workspace. Note: Microsoft Excel locks spreadsheet files that are currently open, which prevents them from being imported from. Therefore ensure that the specified file is closed in Microsoft Excel before importing the spider and/or silk configuration into this spider workspace. If the specified file could not be opened, any error(s) preventing this will be displayed in bold within this dialog, such as: - an invalid or nonexistent path or file - the file is read-only - the file has an incorrect format - the file was locked by another application - the file denied reading from to it The Map Worksheets dialog: On clicking Next the necessary spreadsheet name(s) are processed. Therefore: - If the Silk Linking spreadsheet name is incorrectly specified the "Silk linking worksheet in incorrect format" error will be displayed in this dialog. - If the Spider Definitions spreadsheet name is incorrectly specified the "Spider Definitions worksheet in incorrect format" error will be displayed in this dialog. Note: If ONLY importing silk or spider configuration, then ensure that the BLANK spreadsheet name is selected as the specified name for the OTHER spreadsheet, to prevent this incorrect format error. The Spider Configuration dialog: This displays the results of the comparison of the spiders referenced within the XML file with those present within this spider workspace, as follows: Note: This dialog will be displayed even if ONLY the SILK configuration is being imported, so that any referenced spiders that do not exist can be created. - The top list, displays the spiders that are ONLY referenced within the XML file and which need to be created. This list contains four columns, which provide important information concerning the success of importing these spiders, as follows: - Name: Only spiders that have DIFFERENT names than the existing spiders in this spider workspace will appear in this list. Therefore any spider that has the same name as an existing spider will NOT be appear in this list EVEN if it is of a DIFFERENT type.

Title: To troubleshoot the importing of spiders and silks:
- Type: If spiders of Type 'property' are listed in this list, they will ONLY be created if the appropriately named control and its specified property exists in the graphic form associated with this spider workspace. For instance, textBox.text will only be imported if a control with the name of 'textBox', which has a property 'Text' exists. WARNING! All names are case-sensitive, therefore ENSURE that the correct case is provided otherwise the specified items may NOT be recognised when they are imported. This includes the names of the spider types, data elements and controls, components and graphic elements and their property names. - Configured Inputs and Configured Outputs: These columns give an indication of how many inputs and outputs have configurations that need to be imported from the spider configuration spreadsheet. Note: Even if an input or output is specified as having been configured, this does not mean that it is actually connected to a silk. - The middle list, contains any duplicate spiders or the spiders referenced in the XML file that ALREADY exist in this spider workspace, which can be selectively imported, as required. WARNING! If any of these existing spiders are imported, they may MODIFY the existing configuration of these spiders, however they will not delete any existing inputs or outputs. Note: ALL spiders that have the SAME name as an existing spider in this spider workspace will appear in this list EVEN if it is of a DIFFERENT type. - Name: Empty the checkbox of each spider that should NOT be imported i.e. for each spider whose existing configuration should not be lost. By default all the checkboxes are ticked. Tip: Double-clicking on the name will check or empty the checkbox. - Type: This ONLY specifies the type of spider that is to be imported. However if an existing spider has the same name, but a different type, this spider will not be imported. - Configured Inputs and Configured Outputs: These columns give an indication of how many inputs and outputs have configurations that need to be imported from the spider configuration spreadsheet. Note: Even if an input or output is specified as having been configured, this does not mean that it is actually connected to a silk. - The bottom list, displays any spider-specific errors that have been detected that will prevent them from being successfully imported into this spider workspace.

Trust Relationships Top Trust Relationships Trust Relationships in Windows specify the domains that this domain trusts, and the domains that are allowed to trust this domain.

Title: Trust Relationships
Trust Relationships Top Trust Relationships Trust Relationships in Windows specify the domains that this domain trusts, and the domains that are allowed to trust this domain. A trust relationship is a link between two domains, where one domain honors the users of another domain, trusting that other domain to authenticate the logons of its own users. When trust relationships are properly established between the domains of a network, they allow a user to have only one user account in one domain, yet to access the entire network. All the computers on the network can recognise the user account, requiring a user to log on and provide a password only once to access any computer on the network. Trust relationships move the convenience of centralised administration from the domain level to the network level. -->

Type List CSV File Format Top Type List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created.

Title: Type List CSV File Format
Type List CSV File Format Top Type List CSV File Format This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. The rows in this CSV file are sorted alphabetically and the alarm type name is used as an index, so that the first alarm type name has an index of 0. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: - Alarm type: The name for this alarm type, which MUST NOT be duplicated per agent-type. - Agent type: The type of agent that this alarm type applies to. - Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. This is the sum of all the bit-positions, which are calculated as 2 n , where n is a position from 16 through 31 of the agent status bit as the built-in status bits occupy the positions from 0 to 15. - Value : If applicable, this contains the slot value that is shown with the alarm. For instance for Marshal agents this could be dig##.textValue. - Alarm off-states: 0 is the normal alarming of bits in the mask, while 1 is the alarm off state. -->

This means that when the graphic form is resized at runtime that its controls do not overlap one another, then configure your TableLayoutPanel control as follows: - Ensure that the Autosize property of this TableLayoutPanel control is set to False .

Title: Proportionally distribute space on resize
Steps:
This means that when the graphic form is resized at runtime that its controls do not overlap one another, then configure your TableLayoutPanel control as follows: - Ensure that the Autosize property of this TableLayoutPanel control is set to False . - Ensure that all the columns and/or rows containing controls that you want to proportionally resize have their sizeType property set to Percent . In this simple example the TableLayoutPanel control contains two columns whose sizeType property set to Percent 50%, which always maintain half the real estate of the form regardless of its size: Consider the following detailed example, which creates a graphic form that auto sizes two ListBox controls: - Add a TableLayoutPanel control and add 5 columns and 2 rows. - Set the Anchor property of the TableLayoutPanel control to top, left, bottom, right. - Insert a Label in row 1 column 1, with the text "Name:". - Anchor this Label to the right side of its enclosing cell via its Anchor property. - Insert a TextBox in row 1 column 3. - Set the inherited ColumnSpan property of this TextBox to 3 (this will permit the person’s name to extend into the last two columns). - Insert ListBox controls in row 2, columns 1 and 3. Anchor all four sides of these controls. - Insert a Button control in row 2, column 5 and anchor it to the top and left of the cell. - Set the CellBorderStyle of this TextBox to Single . Example: - Select the Columns property of the TableLayoutPanel, which automatically opens the Column and Row Styles dialog, and configure these 5 columns' sizeType properties, as follows: - Column1: Percent 37.5% - Column2: Absolute 10 pixels - Column3: Percent 37.5% - Column4: Absolute 10 pixels - Column5: Percent 25.0% Example: - Run the graphic form and stretch the graphic form to the right. You should see that the listboxes expand without interfering with each other:

To configure a dialog that provide controls that the user can resize as needed.

Title: Resizable dialogs
Steps:
To configure a dialog that provide controls that the user can resize as needed. In general, items such as labels and buttons will not need to be modified by the user. Title: How to implement a UDT:
Steps:
Tip : If you have already created one or more UDT agent types on another Agent Server, you can simply import these into this utility. For details, see Importing UDT Agent Types . - Stop your Agent Server. - Launch the UDT Agent Type Designer and add and configure their properties (component data types) and, if necessary, to configure status slots for the purposes of alarming. For details, see Creating UDT agent types . - Start your Agent Server. - Create the necessary agents (instances) of each UDT type you have defined. - Configure them, if necessary and scan them to their corresponding UDTs in the required PLCs. For details, see Configuring a UDT agent . IMPORTANT When you edit UDT agents you must also remove all existing agent instances of this UDT agent type from the Adroit agent database (.WGP) file! When you change the structure of a UDT agent (by using the UDT agent designer), then any UDT agents of that type that are already saved in a WGP file will prevent the WGP file from loading because their saved structures are now incorrect. Therefore when you change the structure of a UDT agent, you must remove all instances of this UDT agent type from the WGP file. For example if you have a UDT agent type called MOTORE, whose structure you have changed, then you need to: EITHER manually delete all agents of this MOTORE agent type. OR you can use the WGP Remove utility to do this for you and back up the original WGP file. Note: This utility can be installed from the Additional Components install that provided on the Adroit 10 DVD or can be downloaded from the Adroit website. In this case, open the Command prompt, in Administrator mode (in Windows 8.1, right click the Windows button and select the Command Prompt (Admin) item). Type in: wgpremove motore This removes all instance of the MOTORE agent type from the currently configured WGP file in Adroit Config (if using the SmartUI) or in the Classic Adroit Setup (if using Classic Adroit) and back up the original WGP file. -->

Typically when scanning process values to and from Adroit, the legacy drivers would create separate scan jobs for different: - Agent types, such as: Analog, Digital, Integer, String, Marshal and Multistate and their - Data type formats, such as: longs, words and dwords.

Title: Optimised scan tasks
Typically when scanning process values to and from Adroit, the legacy drivers would create separate scan jobs for different: - Agent types, such as: Analog, Digital, Integer, String, Marshal and Multistate and their - Data type formats, such as: longs, words and dwords. This would therefore increase the total number of scan jobs and therefore the overhead required to communicate your process values. For this reason, less than optimum scan rates were typically attained. With NASA drivers, both different Agent types and data type formats can co-exist within a single scan job, which ensures that the minimum number of separate transactions transmit the data to and from the front-end devices. This means that you will achieve improved throughput as the communication overhead is kept to an absolute minimum.

Previously, only specific legacy drivers supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio.

Title: Improved multi-channel performance
Previously, only specific legacy drivers supported multi channels, such as Modbus EMC or Modbus Radio. All NASA drivers provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. When enabled, NASA drivers can support up to 8 channels, which are utilised as-needed to service the required transactions to achieve parallel communication on a single device.

Legacy drivers would only attempt to reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded.

Title: Configuration
Legacy drivers would only attempt to reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry during an outright fail of the device, once the maximum number of retries were exceeded. NASA drivers also reload the primary and secondary configuration from the registry when the device is started and/or stopped to make it possible for online or runtime changes to running devices without needing to restart the Agent Server in order for these changes to take effect. Examples of possible runtime changes are adding additional debug information to the Datascope or to correct configuration errors like IP address typos etc.

text:
Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks.

Title: Demand Scanning
Demand scanning is only supported by NASA This stands for New Adroit Scanning Architecture and describes a sub-class of protocol drivers that are specifically written to take advantage of the scanning improvements and enhancements provided by NASA, such as demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. drivers that are specifically written to support it, legacy drivers do not provide this feature. Process values (tags) configured to be demand scanned are only communicated when they are being used (when there are one or more subscriptions or references to these tags). Note: In Adroit, a subscription to a process value essentially means that something else is using it. For instance if this process value is being: alarmed; actively logged; used by another Adroit agent or viewed by an operator. Therefore, demand scanning can reduce the number of process values that are communicated, which are especially useful in the following situations: - when you are communicating process values over networks where there is an expense attached to the amount of data that is being transferred like a telemetry system using a GSM network or possibly satellite communications or - as a means to improve the throughput (communication speeds) of a belabored network. But demand scanning can ONLY be used for any READ-ONLY process value that is typically ONLY displayed on a mimic (graphic form) or is used by any of its graphic form components like a Behaviour or spider on the graphic form. In other words a process value that is NOT alarmed or logged or used by any other agent. Click for more details: In this case, when the graphic form is opened that contains or references this process value, then the NASA driver will become aware that this graphic form requires this process value and so it will communicate (scan) this value from its front-end device. When this graphic form is closed, then the NASA driver will become aware that this process value is no longer being used and so it will stop communicating (scanning) this value from its front-end device. Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used.

Title: Demand Scanning
Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from demand scanning, in other words, do not configure process values for demand scanning that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed). WARNING: If you configure ALL your process values to be demand scanned then you could experience SLOWER system performance and not experience any other benefits since all the process values NOT used by ONLY one thing will ALWAYS be scanned anyway! Tip: You can determine which other agents are using (subscribed to) a tag, by opening the Agent Server Configurator and clicking the Used by… button.

metadata.title: Understanding the NASA drivers and their new features

text:
- Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent.

Title: Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning:
Steps:
- Demand scanning is NOT recommended for process values that are being alarmed or actively logged or used by another Adroit agent. Furthermore, any such tag configured for demand scanning could degrade the overall system performance due to the implicit overhead involved in constantly querying the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. - Currently when a process value has the Output Enabled scanning setting configured then it is CONSTANTLY being scanned and therefore CANNOT be demand scanned. - Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to “reuse” your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. - We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs. Therefore use the parallel clustering scanning strategy instead. Click for more details: Firstly, when a clustered pair of Agent Servers use shadow scanning, only the Master Agent Server performs the scanning and the Standby Agent Server does not. Secondly, when a client requests a tag from the proxy Agent Server, this proxy Agent Server it is UNABLE to specify which Agent Server partner it retrieves the requested tag from and only retrieves the tag from the first Agent Server in the list, as long as it is in a healthy state. Thirdly, demand scanning is the only type of scanning that requires at least one subscription to exist to the referenced tag before the tag is scanned. For this reason, if a remote client opens a mimic that has a demand scanned tag on it, it is possible for the proxy server to source the requested tag from the Standby Agent Server partner that is NOT being physically scanned (when its name is first in the list), which results in the WRONG VALUE being returned because: - the Standby Agent Server is given the subscription to this demand scanned tag, but is unable to service this request because it is NOT performing any scanning and - the Master Agent Server does NOT have a subscription to this demand scanned tag (since this subscription was made with the standby Agent Server) and so this tag will NOT be demand scanned! For this reason use parallel scanning instead, which ensures that BOTH the Standby and Master Agent Server scan all the tags and so the value would be demand scanned regardless of which clustered partner is selected by the proxy Agent Server. -->

Update Queries Top Update queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource.

Title: Update queries
Update Queries Top Update queries Queries provide common tasks for managing your database that is connected to an OLE DB datasource. The Update Queries can update the values of specific fields within a table or view of a database. Click for more information: If necessary, limit this updating by defining criteria for fields which must be met before the table or view is updated. If you do not provide constraints on which records to update, you may update all the records in the specific table, which will take a long time if your table or view has a large number of records. Note1: Both the field and/or criteria values can specified by parameters. Note2: This query is ONLY able to update the records of a SINGLE table or view. To add and configure an Update query: Add an Update Query: Click for generic instructions on how to add, name and specify the creation method for a query: - Open the Enterprise Manager . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required SmartUI Server connection . Tip: This connection name is prefaced by the SmartUI Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Datasources category. - If necessary, expand the required OLE DB datasource name or its icon . - Right-click Queries or its icon and select the Add XXX Query option, where XXX is the required query category. Tip: Alternatively, simply double click the subfolder of the required query category . - Specify the required Query Name in the Add XXX Query configuration dialog: WARNING! Once a query has been named, it is NOT possible to rename it later. Note: The specified name cannot be the same as any other query that has been already been specified.> Tip: Give this query a meaningful and concise name so that its purpose can be clearly identified - try not to use all 55 characters. - If supported by this query category - choose how you want to create this query, by selecting one of the following options: - XXX Query Wizard :This default option uses a structured configuration dialog to create the query. This method is especially recommended for those who are not familiar with the SQL querying language.

Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option.

Title: Update queries
Tip: Advanced users can use the configuration dialog to perform the basic configuration such as specifying the required tables and their fields and then customise the added commands using the final dialog, which is the SAME dialog provided by the Custom Query option. Note: This generates a generic SQL statement and will work with all types of OLE DB databases. - Custom Query : This method is intended for those users who are already conversant with the SQL querying language and want to quickly create their query. For details, see Creating customised queries . - Click Next , once the query is named and the required method of its creation is selected. Configure this Update query: Note: This configuration dialog does NOT provide a Preview button to prevent records from being incorrectly updated in your database. Therefore please ensure that you configure the values for these fields correctly. The Tables and Fields dialog is displayed. - Choose whether you want to update a view or table, by selecting the required Table Type option. - Select the required view or table from the Select a ... to Update to list box. The names of tables and views support SQL schemas. Click for more details: The default schema 'DBO' is NOT displayed. But if a table or view is part of a different schema, then the name of this schema is indicated in brackets after the name of the table or view. This means that a table or view can have the SAME name as another table or view as long as it belongs to a different schema. Note: Only ONE table or view can be selected. - Select which fields require values and provide values for them: . To specify a value for a field: - Click the Add Update Field Value button. - Select the field, whose value you want to specify, from the Field drop-down list box, in the following syntax: [Fieldname]. Note1: This list displays all the fields of the selected table or view. Note2: If necessary, you can edit the selected field name yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. - Specify the value or parameter in the Value/Expression field. Specify a value if your users will not need to change this, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this. For details, see Adding parameters .

Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work.

Title: Update queries
Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work. Tip: You can also specify calculations instead of single values. These calculations can also involve numeric parameters. For instance ‘<!!param!!>*4’ multiples the value of this parameter by four. To remove the last field: - Click the Delete Update Field Value button to remove the last field from the list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the field at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. As you define values for the selected fields, the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. Only specify the fields whose values need to be updated. Tip: Use parameters instead of hard-coded values, to allow your users to specify the values for these fields. - Click Next , once the required fields and their values have been defined. - If necessary, add or remove constraints for the fields of this table in the Constraints dialog. Typically, you constrain values of one or more fields to prevent this table from being needlessly updated. If these constraints will change from user to user then use parameters instead of hard-coded values. Adding or removing constraints for the fields of this table: To add a constraint: - Press the Add Constraint button. - If this constraint is NOT the first, specify how to relate this constraint to the previous constraints, as follows: - AND: This is the default option, which makes this constraint mandatory. For instance, if there are two constraints with an AND between them, then the data will be restricted by BOTH constraints. - OR: Use this option, to make the specified constraint optional. For instance, if there are two constraints with an OR between them then the data can be restricted with EITHER of these constraints. - Select the field, whose values you want to limit, from the Field drop-down list box, in the following syntax: [Fieldname]. Note1: This list only displays the selected fields. Note2: If necessary, you can edit the selected field name yourself - in this case ensure that you spell these names correctly. - Select the method by which the values of this field are to be constrained or limited from the Constraint drop-down list box. For details, see Available constraint operators . - Specify the constraining value or parameter in the Value field.

Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this criterion, for instance, if different users require different values.

Title: Update queries
Specify a value if your users will not need to change this criterion, otherwise specify a parameter if your users will need to change this criterion, for instance, if different users require different values. For details, see Adding parameters . Note: Ensure that the specified Value has the same data type as the specified Field , otherwise the query will not work. To delete the last constraint: - Click the Delete Constraint button to remove the last constraint from the Constraints list. WARNING! This will ALWAYS delete the constraint at the bottom of the list, regardless of the currently selected item. Note: Ensure that all the constraints are fully defined, otherwise the query will also not work i.e. delete any partially configured constraints. As you define the constraint(s), the appropriate SQL query commands are added to the SQL Query field, which cannot be edited. WARNING! If you need to configure or modify any of the previous pages, click the Previous button to navigate to these pages. Once you click the Next button the query configuration dialog ends and any further modifications to the query can only to be performed manually. - Click Next , once the required constraints have been defined, to end the query configuration dialog. The Custom Query dialog is displayed, which allows you to manually configure this query, if necessary. - If necessary, type or modify the existing SQL querying commands in the SQL Query editor, which highlights keywords and makes it easier to customise your queries. - Click Finish , once you are satisfied with this query. This adds this query with its specified name beneath the Update Queries subfolder of the Queries folder of the applicable OLE DB datasource, in the Enterprise Manager . If using SQL, please ensure that all time based queries adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd, as follows: - Either, set the short date format in Regional Settings to be yyyy-mm-dd, once for all. - Or convert ALL the date parameters for each query into this SQL standard format first, by using a string converter, such as the String Format spider. Tip: Use the Default Server selection, when referring to the Server that you use to log in, instead of its actual name as this makes it easier to transfer this spider to another Client. - If necessary, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the required OLE DB datasource from this list of available OLE DB datasources on this Server. The Select Query category is selected by default. - From the Query Name list box, select position the mouse pointer over the item and press the left mouse button; also known as clicking. the name of the required query. Note: It is important to name your queries clearly, so that it is easy to select the correct one. - If this selected query contains parameters , then the names of these parameters will be added as additional inputs to the Inputs section.

Note1: The value of each parameter input can either be provided by a property or data element via a silk a line with an arrow at its end, which links the output of one spider to the input of another.

Note1: The value of each parameter input can either be provided by a property or data element via a silk a line with an arrow at its end, which links the output of one spider to the input of another. or can be typed in manually. For details, see Creating silks . Note2: If using SQL, please ensure that all the date parameters for this query adhere to the universal date time standard for SQL, which is yyyy-mm-dd. Tip: When typing in a value manually, double-click the value column to the right of the parameter name in the Inputs section and type in the required value. - It is recommended to use the Confirm Action checkbox to display a confirmation dialog before this query inserts a record into your database. This spider performs this query to insert a record, when it is triggered. WARNING! To edit this query . Tip: Right-click the required Update query and select Edit Update Query . To delete this query . Tip: Right-click the required Update query and select Delete Update Query . Updating cached graphic forms Top Updating cached graphic forms By default, each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server.

Title: Updating cached graphic forms
Updating cached graphic forms Top Updating cached graphic forms By default, each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. caches the data that it requests from the SmartUI Server to improve its response time. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. Note: Use the (Caching) DataElementCachingEnabled setting to enable or disable this caching for a Client. By default, a cached graphic form will ONLY be loaded by the Client if it remains unchanged when it is opened again. In other words, no further design changes have been made to this graphic form that is stored on the Server. If you enable (set to ‘true’) the (Caching) DataElementCachingRetrieveRegardless setting, then the Client will ALWAYS load a cached graphic form from the local cache REGARDLESS of the subsequent changes that have been made to it, since the cache was last updated. This greatly improves the user experience but requires the additional administrative overhead of ensuring that the local cache is updated to include any changes made to the graphic forms of the project/s that it displays AND then copy this updated local cache to all the Operators that use this project/s. To save all graphic forms of a project to the local cache file: - Open the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Accessing tool windows . - If necessary, expand click the plus (+) box to the left of the current icon or name Servers . - If necessary, expand the name of the required Server connection . Tip: The connection name is prefaced by the Server computer name. - If necessary, expand the Projects category. - Right click the project icon of the required name and select Update Local Cache . This updates the local cache with all the changes that have been made to the graphic forms of this project. The local cache data is located within the Caching sub-folder of the SmartUI l installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) in the ‘CACHE’ and 'CACHEINDEX' files. Note: If you need to update more than one project then perform step 5 for each project to add these changed graphic forms to the cache. To copy the updated local cache to all the Operators that use its project/s: - Either: manually copy the Caching sub folder of the SmartUI installation folder (typically C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit ) into the SmartUI Operator installation folder of each of your SmartUI Operator computers. - Or: copy the updated Caching sub-folder into the Distribution folder with the other files required by the SmartUI Operator and then use the SmartUI Launcher (if supported) to distribute the SmartUI Operator (with the updated cache) to the necessary computers. -->

Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Top Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Note: All DbAccess Agents require a scan point license to run.

Title: Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents
Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Top Usage Guidelines for DbAccess Agents Note: All DbAccess Agents require a scan point license to run. This license is checked prior to actually doing a DbAccess transaction for the first time (on a per agent basis) and is only returned when the agent is deleted. For details of licensing, see Adroit Licensing . This is an alternative method to datalog agents by sending slow moving production and batch data values from the AS to OLE DB Servers. Whereas one datalog agent is required per value that is logged to an OLE DB Server, the DbAccess agent can transfer multiple tags in a single transaction and is therefore a more efficient mechanism. The DbAccess agents have the added functionality of retrieving data from OLE DB Servers. This is not intended for high speed logging i.e. data that changes within a minute. Instead, it is ideally suited to applications where data is periodically written to a database (such as at the end of a batch job or shift) for reporting reasons. These agents require careful consideration in terms of both the number of agents to be used and the amount of work that they are to do, as they are resource "hungry". Hence, both the Agent Server memory and overall memory usage should be monitored during configuration to avoid the excessive usage of these resources. The CPU usage should be monitored while during operation to ensure that the computer is able to handle the additional load. Note1: You CANNOT export DBAccess agents that contain single quotes (‘) in their format strings. Note2: The DBAccess agent encloses SQL statements field names in square brackets if the field names contain spaces. -->

These agents require careful consideration in terms of both the number of agents to be used and the amount of work that they are to do, as they are resource "hungry". Hence, both the Agent Server memory and overall memory usage should be monitored during configuration to avoid the excessive usage of these resources. The CPU usage should be monitored while during operation to ensure that the computer is able to handle the additional load. -->

User Rights Policy Top User Rights Policy The Windows User Rights policy manages the rights granted to groups and user accounts.

Title: User Rights Policy
User Rights Policy Top User Rights Policy The Windows User Rights policy manages the rights granted to groups and user accounts. A right authorises a user to perform certain actions on the system. A user who logs on to an account to which the appropriate rights have been granted can carry out the corresponding actions. When a user does not have appropriate rights, Windows blocks attempts to carry out those actions. Rights apply to the system as a whole and are different from permissions, which apply to specific objects. The rights granted to a group are provided to the members of that group. In most situations, the easiest way to provide rights to a user is to add that user’s account to one of the built-in groups that already possesses the needed rights, rather than by administrating the User Rights policy. -->

- The Low (the lo slot) and High (the hi slot) inner alarm limits are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible.

Title: Limitations
- The Low (the lo slot) and High (the hi slot) inner alarm limits are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. - The Low-low (the loLo slot) and High-high (the hiHi slot) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit. This implies that the first warning has been ignored and urgent and immediate corrective action is now required. Note: That whenever the Low-low alarm is on, the Low must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the High-high limit is reached, the High limit will already have been passed. The alarm will become inactive (be cleared) once the process value goes past the limit AND through its deadband, if configured. Click here for an illustration:

The Rate of Change status bit is set when the difference between any two consecutive engineering values in ONE second exceeds the defined Rate-of-Change limit.

Title: Limitations
The Rate of Change status bit is set when the difference between any two consecutive engineering values in ONE second exceeds the defined Rate-of-Change limit. Click here for an illustration: In other words, if this is set to 100, the default value, then if the engineering value (the value slot) of this Analog agent changes from 1 to 101 in 1 second then the Rate of Change status bit is set. But if the engineering value takes 2 seconds to change from 1 to 101 then the effective rate of change is (100/2 =) 50 so the Rate of Change status bit is NOT set. This rate of change measurement is independent of the condition of the low-low, low, high and high-high limits. The value change could be the result of a scan (from the front-end device), operator action or an output from another agent. -->

Using Pseudonyms and Macros Top Using Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros can be created to simply the process of specifying these commands by acting as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent .

Title: Using Pseudonyms and Macros
Using Pseudonyms and Macros Top Using Pseudonyms and Macros Pseudonyms and macros can be created to simply the process of specifying these commands by acting as placeholders for part or all of a textual command that is sent to a Command agent . Therefore they only need to be created for Command agents that have been enabled to receive commands. For details, see Allowing Commands to be Performed . Before pseudonyms and macros can be used in messages, it is necessary to alert the Command agent to their possible existence in its received messages, so that they can be correctly interpreted. For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Note1: Pseudonyms and macros are specific to the Command agent in which they are defined and are not global to all Command agents. However when a Command agent is copied, any defined macros and pseudonyms will also be duplicated. For details, see Copying Agents . Note2: Pseudonyms and macros can also be used to further restrict or limit the SET-table tags / commands that can be performed by this Command agent. For details, see Limiting SET Commands . A pseudonym is simply an abbreviation or alias for a tag (agent.slot), which once defined can be used to represent this tag in commands that are sent to this Command agent. For details, see Creating Pseudonyms . Note: Although pseudonyms can reduce the typing required to specify commands, they need to be defined for this Command agent before they can be used. A macro is simply an abbreviation or alias for an ENTIRE command, which once defined can be used when issuing this command to this Command agent. For details, see Creating Macros or for details of the available commands that can be performed, see Available Commands . Note: Although macros can provide the most intuitive and the shortest command names, they are also the MOST restrictive, since this entire command must be pre-configured in this Command agent, before it can be used. It is also possible to remove any pseudonyms and/or macros that are no longer required. For details, see Removing Pseudonyms and Macros . -->

Using SQL Queries within Identify Row Top Using SQL Queries within Identify Row For each of the update, delete and retrieve transactions; a row in a table has to be identified, by entering the required identification text into the edit box of Identify row .

Title: Using SQL Queries within Identify Row
Using SQL Queries within Identify Row Top Using SQL Queries within Identify Row For each of the update, delete and retrieve transactions; a row in a table has to be identified, by entering the required identification text into the edit box of Identify row . In most cases, specifying the cell in the required field can uniquely identify the row. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = ‘CellInFieldName’ If more than one field is required to identify a row uniquely, then the row is identified using the "OR" or "AND" SQL keywords. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = ‘CellInField1Name’ AND Field2Name = ‘CellInField2Name’ OR Field3Name = ‘CellInField3Name’ In order to reduce the number of DbAccess Agents required to select each row in the selected table, it is possible to substitute the value of the cell in the field with a StringList agent. This StringList agent will then hold various strings, so that a different row can be selected, by manipulating its index value. The required identification text in Identify row for this case is: FieldName = <StringListAgent.value> Note1: Ensure that the value of the tag A fully qualified named value in Adroit (agentName.slotName). matches the data type of the database field, for instance, this example assumes that the field of the database requires strings, but had this field accepted numbers, then a numerical value should have been used instead e.g. real, integer etc. Note2: The identification text must comply with the WHERE clause of a SQL statement. Note3: It is assumed that the user is familiar with the SQL querying language and is able to perform SQL queries unassisted. Extended SQL Querying . Note: To test the syntax of the SQL query in the Identify Row edit box, click on the Trigger now button, then click the Details… button and check that this transaction succeeded in this dialog box. -->

Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Top Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other).

Title: Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent
Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Top Using Tagname Type Slots in an IOT Agent Tagname type slots are used in an IOT agent when the IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) is the concept of connecting any device with an on and off switch to the Internet (and/or to each other). device needs to subscribe to external tags, such as systeminfo.second . When using Tagname type slots, there is a rule that must be applied: - The Tagname slot must be immediately followed by the IOT agent slot that will ultimately contain the value of the specified tag. - If the Tagname slot contains a valid tag name, the IOT agent will automatically subscribe to the specified agent and will place any values received for this tag into the next slot. For example, to subscribe to systeminfo.second then the XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, which defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. slot value would look something like this: <IOT Name=" SecsInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds " Type=" Integer "> 0 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> In the above sample, - the Slot Name “ source ” defines the tag to which we want to subscribe. - the Slot Name “ value ” defines the slot where the subscribed tag value will be stored. Important: The slot names "source" and "value" used in the example above are merely placeholders to make this example clearer, you may use any names you choose. -->
