Using the Agent Browser Top Using the Agent Browser The Agent Browser is a utility that allows one to browse the agents and slots of an Agent Server.

Title: Using the Agent Browser
Using the Agent Browser Top Using the Agent Browser The Agent Browser is a utility that allows one to browse the agents and slots of an Agent Server. This displays the status slot names and tag (agent.slot) values besides the slot type, description of the currently selected agent and slot. Launching the Agent Browser . For details on connecting this utility to the required Agent Server, see Connecting to the required Agent Server . Browsed agents and, if necessary, their slots are dynamically copied to the clipboard, so that it can be immediately pasted into any edit field in an Adroit user interface (or 3rd party application) that requires an agent (or agent.slot) entry. To select an agent and slot using the Agent Browser If the utility is launched with the /admin command line option, tag values can be modified and agents can be added or removed . To modify the value of a slot using the Agent Browser Adding or Removing Agents Using the Agent Browser This utility contains the following additional configuration checkbox options: - Stay on top , which keeps the dialog on top of all other open windows. - Include header slots , which lists all the status slots of the selected agent. - Paste slot names , to include the selected slot name with the selected agent name e.g. ANA01.value - Paste server name , to include the selected Agent Server name with the selected agent name e.g. \\SERVER\ANA01 The information panel at the bottom of this dialog, has the following name \\AgentServerName\AgentType, where AgentServerName is the name of the connected Agent Server and AgentName is the name of the currently selected agent. This displays the following information regarding the currently selected tag (agent.slot): - The description, of the currently selected agent. - The slot type of the currently selected slot. For details, see Slot Types . - The name (description) of the currently selected slot. - The value of the currently selected slot. Note: When the selected slot is a LIST slot then a browse (...) button is displayed to the right of the slot value, which when clicked displays the contents of this LIST slot in a table with the required headings. Double clicking an agent displays a dialog that allows you to view the real time status of an agent at a glance. By default this displays a categorised view, for instance the Status category displays agent specific statuses, although you can check the Sorted checkbox to display an alphabetical listing. You can also click the Previous / Next buttons (or use the PAGE UP / PAGE DOWN keys) to view other agents of the selected agent type. -->

Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently Top Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently Certain applications (including utilities) support command-line parameters, which allow various configuration settings to be performed as soon as the application is launched.

Title: Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently
Steps:
Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently Top Using the Same Command-line Options Frequently Certain applications (including utilities) support command-line parameters, which allow various configuration settings to be performed as soon as the application is launched. For details of other alternatives when launching applications with command-line parameters, see Launching Alternatives . When the same command-line parameters are required frequently, it is recommended to create another shortcut for this application, especially if it is necessary to launch the required program with more than one command-line parameters configuration, as follows: - Press the Windows key and start typing in the required application name and select it from the list. - Right click and select Open File Location . - Right-click the required application shortcut and select Send To and Desktop . - This will copy the shortcut to the Desktop. - Navigate to the Desktop , locate and right-click this shortcut and select Properties . The ApplicationShortcutName Properties dialog is displayed, where ApplicationShortcutName , is replaced by the name of this application shortcut. - Specify the required command-line parameters to the right of the Target field. Note: Ensure that a space is left between the application file and the start of the command line option(s). - Select the General tab and provide a descriptive yet concise name for this shortcut. - Click the OK button. Tip: If necessary this shortcut can also be dragged to another toolbar that is easier to access e.g. the quick launch toolbar. - Run the newly configured shortcut. -->

Title: This toolbar allows you to do the following:
To initially obtain the records from the table or View to populate the associated controls: Typically when the graphic form opens all the controls associated with a specific table or view are empty, such as the TextBoxes and DataGridViews. In this case, press the Load Data button to retrieve the first page of records from the associated table or View. This will also cause the count to specify the number of records that are retrieved. Note1: The MaxRecords property of the associated VIZNETDataBinder component, determines how many records are retrieved. Note2: If the AutoLoad property of the associated VIZNETDataBinder component is set to True, then this button is not required, as the data is automatically fetched when the graphic form is displayed. PLEASE NOTE: If a relationship exists between two tables, so that another table’s column also appears in the DataGridView control associated with the current table, then you need to load the data of the related table first. To navigate the required record of this table or View: Note: This requires the data for the associated table or View to be initially retrieved ( Load Data button). This toolbar allows you to move to the records on the boundaries of the following three ranges: The currently displayed Record: Note: The Current Position field specifies the number of this record, if this field is displayed. The Move to Previous Record button displays the record before the current record, if possible. The Move to Next Record button displays the record after the current record, if possible. Note1: If the current record is the last record in the page, then a delay may occur as the next page of records are retrieved from the database. Note2: The number of records that are fetched at a time are specified by the MaxRecords property of the associated VIZNETDataBinder component. The Page, which is all the retrieved records of the table or View: Note: The “page” that is referred to are ALL the retrieved records and NOT the individual pages of records that are retrieved when a user specifies a record that exceeds the MaxRecords property of the associated VIZNETDataBinder component. The Move to First Record in Page button displays the first record retrieved from the database. The Move to Last Record in Page button displays the last record retrieved from the database.

Value formatting syntax Top Value formatting syntax When you can format the appearance of a value, this formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: { # [, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} General syntax information: Note1: Only the matching curly brackets ("{" and "}") and the number '#' are compulsory.

Title: Value formatting syntax
Value formatting syntax Top Value formatting syntax When you can format the appearance of a value, this formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: { # [, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} General syntax information: Note1: Only the matching curly brackets ("{" and "}") and the number '#' are compulsory. Note2: Any text or numbers typed into the format string, which are not in curly brackets will be displayed as-is. Note3: Because opening and closing curly brackets are interpreted as starting and ending a format item, you must specify two opening curly brackets ("{{") in order to display one opening curly bracket ("{"), and, similarly, two closing curly brackets ("}}") to display one closing curly bracket ("}"). Note4: It is only possible to use one set of curly brackets when formatting a value. Where: - The compulsory # , is the unique number, starting from 0, which denotes the input that is being formatted. Typically this will be 0, unless more than one value has been added. Specific syntax information: Note1: The same # can be formatted multiple times in the same format string. For example, if the value is numeric, this can be formatted in hexadecimal, scientific, and number format, in the same format string, as follows: "{0:X} {0:E} {0:N}". Note2: The order in which the # values are formatted is unimportant. For example, if there are three values, you can format the second, first, and third value by specifying a format string like this: "{1} {0} {2}". Note3: A # value that is not referenced within the format string it will NOT be displayed. Note4: If you specify a # that designates an input which has not been added yet, the Format input cell will prevent you from entering this format string until either a valid # is specified or it is removed. - The optional alignment component is a signed integer indicating the preferred formatted field width, which can be specified for any value, irrespective of its data type. Specific syntax information Note1: The comma (,) is required if alignment is specified. Note2: If padding is necessary, white space is used. Note3: The examples specified in this table assume that a String value of ABCDEFGHIJ is assigned to input 0. Description Format String = Example If the value of alignment is less than the length of the formatted string, alignment is ignored and the length of the formatted string is used as the field width. ->{0,5}<- = ->ABCDEFGHIJ<- If the value of alignment is positive, the formatted data in the field is right-aligned. ->{0,15}<- = -> ABCDEFGHIJ<- If the value of alignment is negative, the formatted data in the field is left-aligned. ->{0,-15}<- = ->ABCDEFGHIJ <- - The optional dataFormat component, consists of one or more data type specific format specifiers to customise the display of values. The following types of data can be formatted: - Numeric Format Specifiers: This provides both the commonly used and custom numeric formats, along with examples. Commonly used numeric format specifiers: These produce standard numeric formats. These numeric format strings, take the form Axx, where: - A: is a single alphabetic character called the format specifier. Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Spider menu: This describes the available menu items and their default settings for this spider. Note: Menu items that are enabled will have a tick mark to the left of them. - Detail View: This can be used to display the configuration view of this spider, so its name, description, inputs and outputs can be configured. For details, see Working with spider configuration views . Tip: Double-click the title bar of the spider to display or hide the configuration view of the spider. - Delete Spider: This can be used to remove this spider from the spider workspace. For details, see Removing spiders . - Trigger Spider From Event: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by means of an event. For details, see Triggering a spider from an event . This is disabled by default. - Enable Silk Triggering: This enables the spider to be triggered (which will run its script) by any silks that are attached to the inputs of this spider. For details, see Triggering spiders . This is enabled by default. - Propagate Outputs At Startup: This enables the spider to supply the silks connected to its outputs with values as soon as its spider workspace enters into running mode. For details, see Working with spider workspaces or Sending spider outputs at startup . This is disabled by default. - Trigger Now!: This will cause this spider to immediately be triggered. Inputs and outputs: This describes the available inputs and outputs displayed by the default configuration view of this spider. This default configuration view of this spider, contains the following sections: - Inputs , this section contains the inputs to this spider. Input Data Function {0} String This input can be used as a placeholder when specifying the other variable data elements inputs. The value of this input can specify the variable portion of the required data element name(s) at runtime or you can create other named inputs and use these instead. For details, see Creating variable data elements . - New Input , this section contains the input types configured for this spider. New Input Function + New Input This allows you to create one or more named inputs, instead of or in addition to using the default {0}. When clicked this displays a dialog to specify the required name for this input. The specified name is added to the list of Inputs , enclosed in {} braces. Tip: You can manually type in and/or concatenate one or more named inputs in the vde #[DE Name (Segment)] inputs to replace one or more portions of a data element name. ' define the slot index numbers starting at 0 in the same order as defined in adrcusdes Const idx_Start = 0 Const idx_Stop = 1 Const idx_Value = 2 Const idx_Tripped = 3 Const idx_Speed = 4 Const idx_Temperature = 5 Const idx_HighTemperature = 6 ' define the status bit index numbers starting at 16 in the same order as defined in adrcusdes Const idx_TempHiStatus = 16 Const idx_TripStatus = 17 ' define the constant for three seconds Const ThreeSeconds = 0.00003472 ' 1 second = 1 day / (24 hours * 60 minutes * 60 seconds) StartTime = 0 StopTime = 0 Sub OnCompiled() 'global initialisation - called for each agent at startup and whenever this file is saved 'while AS is running ' DriveXYZ has nothing to do End Sub Sub OnLoadComplete() 'agent initialisation - called for each agent at when agent has been loaded from WGP file or 'newly created ' DriveXYZ - make sure that the start and stop controls are OFF Custom.SetSlot idx_Start, 0 Custom.SetSlot idx_Stop, 0 End Sub Sub OnChange(slotid, value) 'agent slot changed - called whenever a putslot has been done into one of this agents slots 'DriveXYZ - Versioning WGP Files Top Versioning WGP Files Adroit WGP files from version 6, contain versioning information to provide an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes and to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes.

Title: Versioning WGP Files
Versioning WGP Files Top Versioning WGP Files Adroit WGP files from version 6, contain versioning information to provide an audit trail of changes for debugging and troubleshooting purposes and to assist in locating the required backup file when recovering lost changes. Note: In addition to this version information, Adroit WGP files can ensure that changes made to the WGP file are safeguarded between the regular backups. For details, see Configuring Automatic WGP File Backups . WARNING! This feature is merely intended to AUGMENT the existing backup system and NOT to REPLACE it i.e. it is still imperative that an efficient backup system is in place! For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Adroit WGP file structure has been modified to contain this versioning information, as follows: - Line 1: This remains unchanged and contains the number of agents stored in the WGP file: SYS=#, where # is the number of agents currently added to this Agent Server. - Line 2: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains the version of Adroit : AVER=XYZ, where X is the major version number, Y is the minor version number and Z is the update number, therefore for Adroit 7.0.0, this number will be 700. Note: This is especially important for forward compatibility. - Line 3: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains a sequential version number: FVER=1 Note: This version number will increment EACH time the WGP file is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. - Line 4: From Adroit 6 onwards, this contains an optional version description for the WGP file, describing the changes made to it since its previous save: DVER= Adroit default configuration. The manner in which this description is specified, depends upon how this WGP file is being saved, as follows: - The WGP file is being automatically saved: In this case, the new wgpdescription String slot of the System Information agent, can be used to programmatically provide the required version description instead. - The WGP file is being manually saved: In this case, the Save WGP file pop-up dialog can be displayed to specify this version description or reason for changing the WGP file can be specified. This pop-up dialog only appears when the Enable WGP version description entries checkbox is checked, when configuring the WGP Versioning group of advanced Agent Server settings, which is displayed as follows: Using the Adroit Config Editor : Launch the Adroit Config Editor . Click Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. Click Advanced Agent Server Configuration in the right hand pane. This displays a page of grouped advanced Agent Server settings. -->

Note2: It is also possible to configure the communication settings that are used to communicate to and from its associated front-end device, by clicking the Setup… button. Viewing Incident Queries Graphically Top Viewing Incident Queries Graphically The AlarmManagement agent provides a dialog from which you can perform various statistical queries to analyse the logged incidents.

Title: Viewing Incident Queries Graphically
Viewing Incident Queries Graphically Top Viewing Incident Queries Graphically The AlarmManagement agent provides a dialog from which you can perform various statistical queries to analyse the logged incidents. Many of these queries are derived from the EEMUA 191 guidelines a document created by the Engineering Equipment & Materials Users' Association ( EEMUA) of alarm management guidelines, developed by the users of alarm systems, and is the globally accepted and leading guide to good practice for alarm management. . The incidents returned by these queries are then displayed in a chart. WARNING! We do NOT RECOMMEND using this dialog for an alarm management database that contains a huge number of historical incidents - this can cause your system to become unstable. Note: While this dialog allows you to analyse your logged incidents, we recommend that you install the Adroit Report Suite and specifically the Alarm Management Reports report pack , which provides you with the necessary tools you need to analyse and, more importantly, to improve your alarming system. Tip: This dialog can be resized and maximised and its last size and position is saved for the current UI session. The currently selected Query , changes the following items of this dialog: - The title to the name of this query and displays its description. - The description of the selected query. - The default chart used to display the data (incidents) returned by the query. - The available constraints. - The information displayed by the Legend and/or Labels for this chart. This dialog provides a number of default queries. For details, see Default Alarm Management Queries . Note: If necessary, you can create your own queries. Certain queries support one or more of the following Constraints: These constraints are displayed by clicking the Constraints... button and can further refine the returned data. In other words they can eliminate unnecessary data. - Top: If enabled, specify the topmost number of incidents for this query to return. For instance, when the table records are ordered by time in ascending order, the specified number of the most recent records are returned. Likewise, when the table records are ordered by time in descending order, the specified number of the oldest records are returned. - From: If enabled, specify the date and time of the start of the interval of analysis. - To: If enabled, specify the date and time of the end of the interval of analysis. The Now button, if clicked, will return the incidents that have been added in the last day, by setting the To field to the current date and time and the From field to one day before the current date and time. - Or use shift times: If enabled, specify the required shift number to only view incidents that occur within this shift. - Operator: If enabled, select the name of the required operator from the list to only view the incidents that are logged to this operator. - Incident categorization: If enabled, select the name of the required category (as specified in the Category tree) that contains the incidents that you are interested in. PLEASE NOTE: These constraints are provided by adding special constraint parameters to these queries, so it is NOT possible to execute any queries that contain constraint parameters from 3 rd party applications. To change the frequency at which the charted data is updated: This will determine how often this query is performed on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the current chart. - Specify the required interval in the Auto-refresh (secs) spin control. Tip: Click the Refresh button to immediately perform the selected query on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the chart.

This dialog provides the following chart configuration options: To create a .JPG image file of the displayed chart: - Click the Export… button.

Title: Viewing Incident Queries Graphically
This dialog provides the following chart configuration options: To create a .JPG image file of the displayed chart: - Click the Export… button. This exports the displayed chart as a .JPG image to the following file: - This file is saved to the system temp folder, typically C:\Documents and Settings[\UserName]\Local Settings\Temp. - This file adheres to the following naming format: QueryName as at YYYY_MM_DD HH_MM_SS.JPG. To print the displayed chart using the default printer: - Click the Print… button. To add a legend to the left of the chart: this displays the information for each data-point of the charted series. - Click the Legend checkbox. To rotate the labels of the X axis of the chart: when there are numerous data points on the X axis, some of their labels are not displayed for visibility reasons. In this case this option will display all these labels as their text is displayed vertically instead of horizontally. - Click the Rotate checkbox. Note: This ONLY applies to charts that have an X axis, therefore it has no effect for Pie charts. To toggle the three dimensional display of the chart: by default, charts are displayed in three dimensions but you can display them in two dimensions if necessary. - Click the 3D view checkbox. If this is cleared, the chart is displayed in 2 dimensions. If this is ticked, the chart is displayed in 3 dimensions, the default selection. To toggle between pie or bar charts: by default, charts are displayed using their default chart type but you change the type of chart to bar or pie charts. - Click the Swap pie/bar checkbox. If the current chart is a pie chart this becomes a bar chart and vice verse. To provide Y axis value labels for the charted series: this labels each charted data-point with its Y axis value. - Click the Value Labels checkbox. To provide full labels (both the X and Y values) for the charted series: - Click the Full Labels checkbox. Adding your own Queries : This describes how you can add you own queries so that they too can appear in this View Data dialog. Launching the View Graph dialog : This describes how you can also launch this dialog directly from a Classic UI mimic. -->

In this case this option will display all these labels as their text is displayed vertically instead of horizontally. - Click the Rotate checkbox. Note: This ONLY applies to charts that have an X axis, therefore it has no effect for Pie charts. To toggle the three dimensional display of the chart: by default, charts are displayed in three dimensions but you can display them in two dimensions if necessary. - Click the 3D view checkbox. If this is cleared, the chart is displayed in 2 dimensions. If this is ticked, the chart is displayed in 3 dimensions, the default selection. To toggle between pie or bar charts: by default, charts are displayed using their default chart type but you change the type of chart to bar or pie charts. - Click the Swap pie/bar checkbox. If the current chart is a pie chart this becomes a bar chart and vice verse. To provide Y axis value labels for the charted series: this labels each charted data-point with its Y axis value. - Click the Value Labels checkbox. To provide full labels (both the X and Y values) for the charted series: - Click the Full Labels checkbox. Viewing Incidents Requiring Reasons and/or Notes Top Viewing Incidents Requiring Reasons and/or Notes The AlarmManagement agent provides an Outstanding reasons and notes dialog which ONLY displays the current incidents that still require reasons and/or notes to be specified. In other words this dialog only displays the current incidents that have their Reasons required and/or Notes required settings enabled and as yet unspecified. Note: An incident is removed from this dialog once its reason and/or note is specified. Tip: This dialog can be resized and maximised and its last size and position is saved for the current UI session. To change the frequency at which the charted data is updated: This will determine how often this query is performed on the database to include the latest logged incidents requiring reasons and/or notes. - Specify the required interval in the Auto-refresh (secs) spin control. Tip: Click the Refresh button to immediately perform the selected query on the database to include the latest logged incidents in the chart. This dialog provides the following grid configuration options: this allows you to configure both the table (grid) and specify the reasons and/notes for the displayed incidents. To sort the table entries by a column: - Click the required column heading. This column heading displays the character when the rows of this table are sorted so that the contents of this column are displayed in ascending order. This column heading displays the character when the rows of this table are sorted so that the contents of this column are displayed in descending order. To change the widths of individual columns: This can be used to hide an unnecessary column from view. - Drag the right hand side of the column left or right, as required. Note: The changes made to the column widths are saved for the currently selected query. To resize the columns of the table to the width of their largest entry: this resets any changes that have been made to the column widths and displays any hidden columns. - Right-click the table and select Show all columns . Note: The changes made to the column widths are saved for the currently selected query. To specify the reasons and/notes for each incident in this dialog: this will remove the incident from the dialog. - Click the Reasons… button. This displays the Incident reasons and notes dialog.

Title: To view the current Server license information:
To open the License Information dialog from the Activity Monitor: this is displayed when the Server is running as an application. Open the Activity Monitor - Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and the SmartUI Server item. - Click the Launch Activity Monitor to open the Activity Monitor. - Note: The Activity Monitor is only displayed if the ActivityMonitorFormEnabled setting for this Server is enabled. For more information on this setting, see Advanced Server settings . The ActivityMonitorFormTitle setting specifies the title of this application. - Warning: The Server window is not displayed if the SmartUI Server is running as a service . - If the server is already running, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - Tip: When the SmartUI Server is running as an application, you may also press the ALT+TAB KEYS repeatedly until the task switcher displays the Server window, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - If the server is already running as a service, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - The Activity Monitor opens and displays information on the Local Machine tab. Click the Display Licence Information link from the Tasks panel. To open the License Information dialog from the Service Manager: this is displayed when the Server is running as a service. - If necessary, launch the Service Manager, by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 and the SmartUI Service Manager item. This displays a tray icon in the tray bar, located in the bottom right corner of the screen. - Right click the tray icon in the tray bar and select the Licence Information menu item. The License Information dialog is displayed, which provides a summary of the most important licensing details. Note: This Licence Information window remains open until you click the Close button at the top right of this dialog. For more information on licensing the SmartUI Server, see Licensing the Server . -->

Visibility Behaviours Top Visibility Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to enable or disable Boolean properties that end-users can see.

Title: Visibility Behaviours
Visibility Behaviours Top Visibility Behaviours This Behaviour can be applied to controls and graphic elements (vectors) to enable or disable Boolean properties that end-users can see. Note: The color Behaviour can be configured to blink the visibility of a control or vector (alternate between hiding and showing the object at a specified interval in milliseconds). For details, see color Behaviours. This Behaviour sets (enables or disables ) a Boolean property of the associated form component depending on the specified value. By default this controls the Visible property to hide or display this control or vector. Note: Only numerical and Boolean and the Boolean String values ("True", "False") can be used by this Behaviour. Invalid values grey out the associated form component. To use a value to enable or disable a visible Boolean property of a control or vector: - Add or edit a Visibility Behaviour to display its configuration dialog. - Click the browse button to the right of the Input Data Element edit box to select the value (data element) to control the Boolean property of this object, as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element.

The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner.

Title: Visibility Behaviours
The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. Note: If a DataSet value is selected, such as a field of a database, the Filter DataSet configuration dialog is displayed to select which value to use.

- Use the Visibility group to specify how this value can set this Boolean property, as follows: - Visible: this option enables the Boolean property when the value is true (a non-zero numerical value) and disables the property when it is false (zero).

Title: Visibility Behaviours
- Use the Visibility group to specify how this value can set this Boolean property, as follows: - Visible: this option enables the Boolean property when the value is true (a non-zero numerical value) and disables the property when it is false (zero). - Invisible: this option disables the Boolean property when it is true and enables the Boolean property when the value is false. - If necessary, click the Advanced View button to display the Property Name drop down list to select the Boolean property (other than the default of Visible) that is driven by this value, as follows: The Property Name drop down list displays the Boolean properties that affect the display of this object. By default, Visible is selected, to control the visibility of this form component. To select another property from this list: Click the drop down list to open it and select another property. To select a property not in the list: Click the browse button to the right of this list; select the required property or sub-properties of this form component and press the Finish button. Tip1: When adding a Behaviour to a SmartUI Template A graphic form that has one or more configured aliases and is therefore designed to be displayed within a TemplateGO control. , you can use {} notation to automatically create an alias for any data element field. For more details, see Working with SmartUI Templates . Tip2: When adding a Behaviour to a wizard A pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements. , you can use {} notation to automatically create a substitution for any data element field. For more details, see Working with wizards . To add a Behaviour to a control or graphic element: Ensure that you have added the required control or graphic element to the graphic form. - Select the required control or graphic element. - If necessary, select the Behaviours tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: Any Behaviour that cannot be applied to this control or graphic element will be greyed out. - Select the required Behaviour from the relevant group. Tip: You can also select its glyph to display its task menu and then select the required Behaviour from the New Behaviour drop down list. This displays the configuration dialog of this Behaviour.

Tip: When you add or edit a Behaviour you can name it, which makes it easier to identify the spiders and their regions associated with your Behaviours.

Title: Visibility Behaviours
Tip: When you add or edit a Behaviour you can name it, which makes it easier to identify the spiders and their regions associated with your Behaviours. To edit a Behaviour of a control or graphic element: - Right click the required control or graphic element to the graphic form. - Select the required BehaviourName# menu item, where BehaviourName is the name of the added Behaviour and # usually only appears if more than one of same type of Behaviours have been added. For example: Execute Command1 Tip: You can also select its glyph to display its task menu and then select the required link beneath the Behaviours heading. This displays the configuration dialog of this Behaviour. Tip: The Behaviours tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon provides the Edit Behaviour list box that lists all the Behaviours configured for the currently selected form component. Clicking its browse button displays the configuration dialog of the currently selected behaviour. To remove one or more added Behaviours from a control or graphic element: - Select the required control or graphic element. - If necessary, select the Behaviours tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon. - Select the Remove command from the Remove group. Tip: You can also select its glyph to display its task menu and then select the Remove link beneath the Behaviours heading. This displays the Behaviour Removal configuration dialog. - Select (check the checkboxes) of the Behaviour/s that you want to remove from this list in the Behaviour Removal configuration dialog. WARNING! Ensure that ONLY the Behaviour/s you do not require is selected, since no deletion confirmation dialogs are displayed. - Click the Finish button to remove the selected Behaviour/s or Cancel to abort. -->

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components
VIZNETDataBinder components Top VIZNETDataBinder components This component a hidden form component that provides additional functionality to this graphic form and some or all of its form components. See form component. makes the data of a DataBinder DataBinders allow you to create a sub-set of the data contained within an OLE DB datasource to provide constant bi-directional communication with this database. This means that unlike the data returned by Select queries, this data can be viewed and/or modified and updated if it changes. accessible to other controls and components on a graphic form. Click for more information: For details, see Accessing data within DataBinders . Note1: The VIZNETDataBinder component provides a number of properties that manage how the data of its associated DataBinder is accessed. For details, see Important properties . Note2: If necessary, other controls can access the data of the View and/or tables by being linked to the respective Bindingsource component. For details, see Linking controls to BindingSource components . This is made possible by creating BindingSource components for each of the tables and View of this DataBinder, which provide other controls and components on this graphic form with access to their data. Created BindingSource-specific components and their naming conventions: Note: These components do not require further configuration. - A single View BindingSource component, which only allows its data to be viewed and not modified, which adheres to the following naming convention: viewDataBinderNameBindingSource. For instance, if the DataBinder is called 'MyDtBndr': viewMyDtBndrBindingSource. - A BindingSource component for each table within this DataBinder, which allows both viewing and modification of its data and adheres to the following naming convention: TableNameBindingSource. For instance if the table name is 'SalesPerson': SalesPersonBindingSource. - A DataSet component that provides communication between the BindingSource components and the DataBinder's database. This component adheres to the following naming convention: OLEDBDatasourceNameDataBinderNameDataSet. For an OLEDB datasource called 'North Wind' and a DataBinder called 'MyDtBndr': north_WindMyDtBndrDataSet. Note1: If the component name already exists then its name will be appended by a unique number starting from 1. Note2: Any spaces or other illegal characters are replaced with underscores, when naming these components. Although BindingSource components provide access to the data, they do not provide direct access to this data. Instead they retrieve records from the database in pages or set quantities. It is these retrieved records that they provide to the other controls and components on a graphic form. This has a number of advantages: - Since you do not working directly on the database itself, you have the ability to undo changes that are made, before they are actually made. - Since you only receive pages or set quantities of records, you do not experience the potential performance lags associated with receiving all the records from the database at once. Note: Since all the controls that require data from the same table receive it from the same BindingSource component, when a specific record is selected this record is selected in ALL the associated controls. Configuration options: - A configuration dialog to select the required DataBinder : Launched when adding a VIZNETDataBinder component to a graphic form. This configuration dialog also provides the option to Create Controls , where you select which of the tables and their fields you want displayed and specify which controls should be used to display them. Use one or both of the following options of controls for your data: - labeled TextBoxes to display the value of the selected fields. This method is recommended when you require information about a specific item such as a particular user or asset. - a DataGridView containing the selected fields.

This method is recommended when the associated table contains large amounts of data that you want to view in a spreadsheet environment.

Title: VIZNETDataBinder components
This method is recommended when the associated table contains large amounts of data that you want to view in a spreadsheet environment. A toolbar ( VIZNETBindingNavigator control) is also added for each of the selected tables, which allows your users to view, navigate and modify your data, by communicating to the associated BindingSource component. Most notably, the Create Controls option adds a toolbar ( VIZNETBindingNavigator control) for each of the selected tables, which allows your users to view, navigate and modify your data, by communicating these requests to the associated BindingSource component. Note: If you do not use the Create Controls option, then you must implement your own method of communicating to the BindingSource components. For instance, use the DataBinderTrigger spider to load (fetch) and update their data. - A Tasks menu , which provides a list of important properties and configuration options for this component.. The configuration dialog, however, should still be used to select the required DataBinder and, if necessary create the required controls. - Important properties , this describes the functions of the important properties that can configure this component. -->

WanClient Configurator Top WanClient Configurator Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database that is stored in the database folder .

Title: Configuration
WanClient Configurator Top WanClient Configurator Each WanClient application needs to create and maintain a tag link database that is stored in the database folder . This database stores a list of WanServer(s) and tags whose values are to be fetched or sent to or from each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers. This tag link data is created using the WanClient Configurator, which can be launched from the Open Configurator item of the WanClient File menu, as follows: - Configure Servers : This specifies the communication settings of each WanServer and hence the Agent Server resident on this computer. - Configure Tag Groups : To assist in the communication of the necessary tag values, the tags are organised into one or more tag groups, which specify the communication settings of any tag that is added to them and are server-specific. For details on possible criteria to use for creating tag groups, see Criteria for Creating Tag Groups . - Configure Tag Links : A tag link or tag mapping, simply specifies the name of the local and the remote Adroit tag, whose values are to be ‘linked’. These are added to a tag group within a server. Note: The data type of the local and the remote tag must be identical. However, the WanClient Configurator, is also able to perform the following global communication configuration, which apply to all the WanServers that are being communicated to: - Scan bad philosophy configuration : This governs how this WanClient will set its local Agent Server tag bad information, for the tags, whose values it communicates. - Agent Server Cluster-specific configuration : This performs cluster-specific configuration, when using a WanClient is used to communicate tag values from a pair of clustered servers. -->

When the WanClient starts up, control tags are assumed to have dirty values until a value is received from the WanServer. Updates from a WanServer that fail to putslot in the local Agent Server will also cause values to be "dirty" again. Dirty values are NOT sent to WanServer to prevent "blind" value changes. Wanlink Components Top Wanlink Components Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. Wanlink Quickstart Top Wanlink Quickstart Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another.

Title: Wanlink Quickstart
Wanlink Quickstart Top Wanlink Quickstart Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). For further details, see General Description . In order to gain access to a local Agent Server from a remote Agent Server across a WAN (Wide Area Network) ensure that the following steps are followed: Note1: For ease of explanation the local Agent Server will be known as LOCAL and the remote Agent Server, will be known as REMOTE. Note2: This will assume that the FULL Adroit installation has been installed and that the Agent Servers have already been started on both computers. - On the LOCAL computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Server and select it from the list to run the WanServer. - On the REMOTE computer, press the Windows key and start typing in Wanlink Client and select it from the list to run the WanClient. Note: If the Agent Server is not started, then the WanClient application will wait for it and attach to it when it is opened. - On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, open the File menu and select the Open Configurator command. In the Configurator dialog do the following: - Click the Add Server button to configure the connection settings required to reach the LOCAL computer. (Add as many servers as there are Agent Servers that require data from this computer’s Agent Server.) - Click the Add Group button to configure a tag group , for the Select ed Server , that may only contain a subset of the total required Adroit tags, depending upon the requirements of the tags it is to contain e.g. the group type determines if the Adroit tags will be able to be modified by the other Agent Server or not. (Add as many groups as are needed to cater for the Adroit tags that are to be referred to by the selected server i.e. the current Select Server entry.) - Click the New Link button to configure a tag link in which an Adroit tag on this computer’s Agent Server (REMOTE in this case) is linked to which Adroit tag on the Agent Server of the computer on the other side of the WAN (LOCAL in this case). This link is added to the Select ed Group and also determines the method by which the data between these two Adroit tags is transferred. (Add all the linked tags that meet the criteria of the currently selected group i.e. the current Select Group entry.) - Once all the tags have been added to their relevant groups and all the groups have been added to necessary servers, then click OK. Note: This is a once-only configuration, the next time that the WanClient is opened; this step can be skipped, unless alterations or additions need to be made to the configured tag mappings. - On the REMOTE computer, in the WanClient program, after tag mappings have been configured, open the File menu and click on the Repack command and then open the File menu and click on the Reload command, to avoid stopping and restarting the WanClient. - The LOCAL Agent Server will now have access to all the configured tags on the REMOTE Agent Server. Note1: It is possible to configure the WanServer application to run as a service on the LOCAL computer, so that it start automatically whenever the Agent Server starts up.

The WanClient application does not have this facility, as it must be run from within windows.

Title: Wanlink Quickstart
The WanClient application does not have this facility, as it must be run from within windows. Note2: If the WanClient is started with the "/start" command-line parameter, then it will automatically start communications. Tip1: Both the WanClient (if using the "/start" command-line parameter) and WanServer applications can be started before the Agent Servers have started. Therefore once the Agent Servers are started/restarted the applications will resume communications as expected. Tip2: It is possible to start the WanClient application from an Adroit mimic by using an Execute Command Behaviour, in this case, specify "/start" after wanclient.exe in the "Application name:" field. This will saves the operator from opening WanClient manually each time and because the "/start" command-line parameter is used, will automatically start communicating. -->

What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?

Title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Top What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it? Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Both this amount and the cost of providing this power are agreed between you and your electricity provider, with the condition that if you exceed this amount then you will pay heavy penalties. Your electricity provider monitors your maximum demand in “block” periods (in South Africa these are every 30 minutes) during these peak times. Your monthly electricity bill uses the highest recorded block kVA usage as the kVA for the whole month. In other words, at the end of the billing month you pay the penalty resulting from the largest divergence from your maximum demand for a block period, for the ENTIRE month. For instance, if you exceed your maximum demand in the first block period of the month, you will pay this penalty for the entire month, even if you turn off your plant at this point! Needless to say, the cost penalties for the excess power are very high and this is why power management is so important. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage. However, it is recommended to automate this monitoring, such as by using an MaxDemand agent, because one mistake can easily exceed your maximum demand limit for the current billing period. For details on how to monitor your maximum demand, see Maximum Demand Quick Start . -->

The SmartUI applications now support the following two themes that affect how these applications are displayed: Light Dark Users can select which theme they want to use, when installing the SmartUI Operator, Designer or Server for the first time (in other words this is not displayed when any of these components are installed subsequently), from the following installation dialog: Tip: You change this theme at any time by opening the Adroit Config Editor and specifying the required option from the Theme list box at the bottom of this application.

Title: Product theme, icons and shortcuts
Steps:
The SmartUI applications now support the following two themes that affect how these applications are displayed: Light Dark Users can select which theme they want to use, when installing the SmartUI Operator, Designer or Server for the first time (in other words this is not displayed when any of these components are installed subsequently), from the following installation dialog: Tip: You change this theme at any time by opening the Adroit Config Editor and specifying the required option from the Theme list box at the bottom of this application. The product icons have been revised and updated and standardised and are now classified using different colored vertical bars on their left hand side. Each color representing the following categories of function to make them easier to recognise and use: The Adroit Utilities has been added to provide a central location from which the installed utilities can be launched, instead of installing a host of separate shortcuts for each individual utility. This shortcut is also installed on the Desktop. This application also describes their supported command line options and by right clicking the utility you can specify which command line options you want to use when launching the utility.

- Added the Accumulator agent that calculates the difference in value (or delta) of a value that accumulates over time between successive events or over a specific time period (interval).

Title: Adroit Agent Server
- Added the Accumulator agent that calculates the difference in value (or delta) of a value that accumulates over time between successive events or over a specific time period (interval). You can also specify a MS SQL database to maintain a history of these periodic counts/totals. You can also configure alarm limits for both the (differential) value and rate of change in value for the current period. - Added the ICMP or PING agent that uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to troubleshoot network problems. By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. - Added the DumpConfig agent, which simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. One example for its use is when you need to report on agents in the context of their configuration at the time of the report, alternatively this could be used as an extensive method of auditing changes made to specific agents. - The following primitive agent types have also been added to HMI mode: Real and Integer, however these agents (including Boolean) should ONLY be used where efficient use of memory is required. PLEASE NOTE: These legacy primitive agents do not support Alarming and other SCADA functionality, use Analog/Digital agents instead! - The Analog agent now provides support for up to 51 bit numbers, in that the new maximum range is 2,000,000,000,000,000 for unsigned numbers or -1,000,000,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000,000,000 for signed numbers. To reduce the loss of accuracy in scaling caused by IEEE conversion issues, the Analog agent bypasses the scaling calculation, when the scaling is 1:1. - The AlarmManagement agent now provides the Integer kpiCalcRate slot that sets the maximum rate at which the KPIs should be calculated, in minutes, to improve the performance of this agent, which by default is set to 1.

If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0.

Title: Adroit Agent Server
If this slot is set to 0 then KPI calculations are NEVER executed on new or changed alarm occurrences and so also added the Boolean kpiCalcNow slot that pulses to allow users to perform a KPI calculation at any time, especially when they have set the kpiCalcRate slot to 0. - The Notify agent now provides a valueEx VARSTRING slot that is now SMS’d or emailed to subsystems that can handle long strings. It is also the slot that is saved to the WGP file. - Custom agents created via the Custom Agent Designer that require scripting intelligence now provides support for JavaScript (.jav file) or you can choose to use the existing VBScript (.vbs file). - The enhanced SNMPMgr agent replaces the legacy SNMPManager agent - This agent supports up to SNMP version 3 and allows an MIB SNMP Management Information Base, this is a database that lists uniquely described and organises SNMP managed objects hierarchically. file to be browsed in, in order to select which OID SNMP managed Object IDentifier, which describes the exact location of this value in the SNMP structure for its device. values you need to monitor and/or control and/or trap. - Any existing SNMPManager agent is converted to SNMPMgr agent when the Agent Server loads. - This agent does not use .wgx files as now the OID configuration of your SNMPMgr agents are saved to the Agent database (.wgp) file directly. - Various improvements have been made in the way the SNMPMgr agent handles reporting the quality (the bad or good state) of the OID list linked tags. - For a new project, the available agent types are now classified into the following default groups to better facilitate the selection of the required agent when designing your system: - Basic : these agent types form the basic building blocks of a system and are used for gathering, handling and processing data to and from the physical external world. Analog, Counter, Date, Digital, Expression, Marshal, MultiState, String, StringList, Timer - Advanced : these agent types provide powerful SCADA and integration functionality that allow the Basic agents to be alarmed and logged to databases and provides various means of reporting and/or controlling their values.

AgentGroup, Alarm, Alarm List, AlarmManagement, ARec, Command, DbAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Recipe, Scheduler, Script, Shift, Statistical - MIS/MES : these are very specific and usually quite complex agent types used to do monitor, control and solve higher level shop-floor and general industrial challenges.

Title: Adroit Agent Server
AgentGroup, Alarm, Alarm List, AlarmManagement, ARec, Command, DbAccess, DBLog, EventLogging, EventOutput, Multimedia, Notify, Recipe, Scheduler, Script, Shift, Statistical - MIS/MES : these are very specific and usually quite complex agent types used to do monitor, control and solve higher level shop-floor and general industrial challenges. MaxDemand, OEE, PID - IT : these agent types facilitate the integration and management of SCADA and IT Audit, DumpConfig, ICMP, Perfmon, SNMPMgr - System : these agent types are used internally to perform certain SCADA and other specific functions. Note: Instances of these Agents are created automatically and cannot be added manually by the user. Alias, Beeper, DataLog, Device, Hasp, Proxy, Scan, SystemDataLog, SystemInformation - Primitive : these agent types are primitive because they offer limited value and are limited in functionality when compared to the Basic agents, they are essentially single value containers. Boolean, Integer, Real, Text and Frame IMPORTANT: These agent types CANNOT be alarmed and their values are not scaled etc, so use the Basic agent types instead to represent your process values. Title: Adroit Agent Server
- Added the OPC UA client, a NASA driver, which communicates with OPC UA Servers in accordance with the OPC UA specification. OPC UA (OLE for Process Control Unified Architecture) is a standard specification that makes it possible for automation/control software applications and field systems/devices to interoperate and communicate data between each other. Since this is NASA driver it provides support for demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. - The logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Although if the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration, then the SQL... button of the Datasource field will be visible in the Edit Datalog agent dialog. The Datalog agent should therefore only be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. When the allocated size of the datalog (.LGD) file is filled, it wraps (starts again at the beginning). At which time one or more datalog backup (.LGB) files are created to store this older (historical) data. The datalogging sub-system automatically retrieves this historical data from these files, when this data is required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number of files that are created. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-22 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-22-m-11 In Adroit 10 , the name of the backup file only specifies the year and month so that now only one file is created for the month.

Title: SmartUI Designer
Steps:
- Added the Object Model datasource, which enables you to enhance your existing wizards, by adding SCADA configuration to them.

It saves you SCADA engineering time by allowing you to reliably duplicate objects that can have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured.

Title: What can the object model do for you?
Steps:
It saves you SCADA engineering time by allowing you to reliably duplicate objects that can have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured. The objects that you can create will typically be items of equipment, like pumps or motors and can be anything that you have already created a wizard to represent. You can also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers to them that you can use to filter or group the objects that you deploy in the Context View window.

metadata.chunk_title: What can the object model do for you?

text:
It does not help you create the graphical representation of the object, it requires a working instance of a wizard to begin.

Title: What does the object model NOT do for you?
Steps:
It does not help you create the graphical representation of the object, it requires a working instance of a wizard to begin. It does not help you create the SCADA configuration required by this object, it requires that all the necessary agents already exist for the wizard instance that you have selected and that these agents have already been configured. Practical example: Consider an industrial plant has a large number of similar pumps made by the same manufacturer, each of which had some characteristics that differed such as their power calibration. The engineer would initially create a wizard that provides the graphical representation of this pump. Then the engineer would implement the wizard and create the necessary SCADA configuration for this pump, such as its required scanning, logging and alarming. The engineer would then test that this SCADA configuration was working correctly. Then the engineer would create a template from this working wizard, ensuring that the characteristics that differed between these pumps would be substitutable. Using this template the engineer would then create multiple instances of the pump, changing each of their differing characteristics as needed. So each instance of this pump would then have their scanning, logging and alarming pre-configured. Improvements made to the Object Model datasource: - You can define a script for each object so that it can be run when an instance of this object is deployed. - When creating an instance of an object, you can now configure all the scan addresses of an object instance in a single list view (that can be copied and pasted to and from any text file editor like MS Excel for bulk configuration), instead of having to query each agent individually for these scan addresses. - The Context View window, logically groups or organises the deployed objects according to their defined attributes, so that they can be easily located and/or searched. In other words all the objects that have the SAME attribute are added a separate group or 'context'. Furthermore this grouping is hierarchical so that the objects are further classified or grouped according to their specified values of this attribute. This allows you to see which objects have the same values and/or view all the values that have been specified for a particular attribute. For instance, if an attribute defined the power rating for equipment, then you could see all your equipment that had the same power rating OR if an attribute defined the manufacturer, you could see how much of your equipment was made by each manufacturer. Therefore by defining common attributes for your deployed objects, the Context View window can become a very useful tool in managing not just your deployed objects but your entire process. While these automatically generated contexts cannot be edited, you can edit the Default context to create your own logical organisation of your objects and/or other data, by either: - manually adding the necessary hierarchy of nodes - or if you have implemented Alarm Management, you can import your existing hierarchy of categories as nodes , with or without the agents that are associated with their configured incidents. Nodes are like folders, each of which typically represent a specific contextual area and can contain additional nodes or a graphic form associated to them or have data elements and/or object model objects added to them. You can also use the TemplateGOContextNav control to display the graphic forms associated with the nodes and/or added to the nodes of this Default context.

text:
The Default context lends itself to the creation of object instances, especially those whose name and substitution/s use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created.

Title: What does the object model NOT do for you?
Steps:
The Default context lends itself to the creation of object instances, especially those whose name and substitution/s use a predefined naming convention that specifies the context in which the instance is created. However, make best use of this feature you need to: - define the necessary hierarchy of Nodes, each of which typically represent specific contextual areas and especially specify each Node descriptor , which is typically a 3 character reference code for each contextual area. - if your object employs multiple substitutions to define its process variable names, then ensure that these substitutions are specified in the template in the logical order of the defined contextual areas. - The primary purpose of a graphic form is to display data elements (tags). Over the years a number of separate mechanisms have been created to make this process as easy as possible and/or to facilitate their duplication to save on their engineering time. This means that: - locating all the references of a tag on a graphic form is a non-trivial task and so this tool is essential and - not all of these mechanisms allow the tag to be externally replaced by this tool, without breaking the mechanisms themselves. To work around this limitation, the following two utilities have been created which have different capabilities or uses: - The GLOBAL Find utility in the Project group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon, enables you to select one or more graphic forms of one or more projects to find where text, typically a tag (agent name), has been referenced and used, you can then export the list of located references to Excel. Note: This utility only appears when the Spider Configuration Mode section of View tab of the Designer ribbon is set to Advanced , since it is intended for advanced users only. This utility can save much time when redesigning large projects and when creating and maintaining multiple SCADA systems in keeping track of your agents or other graphic form components. Note: You need to close all open graphic forms before you can use this tool and you cannot perform any other action in the Designer while this utility is open. - The LOCAL Find and Replace utility in the graphic form toolbar, searches for the specified text, typically a tag (agent name), in the currently selected graphic form and unlike the other utility provides: - an Edit column in the Find Results tab that allows you to edit the indirect mechanisms so that you can change these references to the required replacement one at a time; - the Replace tab to replace the direct references to the searched for text with the specified replacement and - a moveable dialog, so that you can carry on working on others things or can find and replace text in more than one currently open graphic form. This utility also allows you to export the list of references to the searched for text to Excel, if needed. - Enhanced the Data Element Browser dialog by providing the ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - Added the facility to publish run-time versions of graphic forms, typically once a graphic form has been designed and is working as required.

Title: Product Licensing Changes
IMPORTANT: HASPs are NOT backwardly compatible with previous product versions due to a change in the internal licensing structure of the HASPs. The Adtech Licensing Utility allows you to get, view and/or update your Adroit product license. - The product license is now a .XML document to make it easier to read and is displayed in the License tab. - IMPORTANT: The former Remote Nodes licenses that applied to all types of clients have been DISCONTINUED . These have now been replaced by the following client specific node licenses, each of which have different costs: - Clients : typically Operators and/or Designers and - Web Clients : typically Performance Anywhere clients. - Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can now get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server, by adding and configuring the RDAdminName WG.INI registry string value. Note: By default this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required Windows username to establish free connections for this user. - The OEM (separately-licensed) components are no longer specified by their associated OEM codes but now included as separate textual entries in the product license, so that users can easily see exactly which components they are currently licensed for. Tip: Only the OEM components that you are licensed for will appear. - All product licenses have a GLOBAL expiry and can also support product-specific expiries, which can be used for product trials. - .V2C (Vendor to Customer) and .C2V (Customer to Vendor) files are now used to create and update product licenses instead of using .RUS files. Important differences between a HASP and a soft license: - A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk. - A Soft license is bound to a specific computer and therefore cannot be transferred to another computer. Therefore if the computer fails then the soft license will no longer work.

By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. - Added the DumpConfig agent, which simply stores the configuration of specific agents in an OLE DB database. text:
- Added the OPC UA client, a NASA driver, which communicates with OPC UA Servers in accordance with the OPC UA specification.

Title: Adroit Agent Server
- Added the OPC UA client, a NASA driver, which communicates with OPC UA Servers in accordance with the OPC UA specification. OPC UA (OLE for Process Control Unified Architecture) is a standard specification that makes it possible for automation/control software applications and field systems/devices to interoperate and communicate data between each other. Since this is NASA driver it provides support for demand scanning and highly optimised scan tasks. - The logging to ADO (SQL) databases by the Datalog agent is disabled by default (the SQL... button of the Datasource field is hidden in the Edit Datalog agent dialog). This is to force users to use the DBLog agent instead, which logs data to SQL more efficiently. Although if the Agent Server loads a legacy WGP file that ALREADY contains an ADO datalogging configuration, then the SQL... button of the Datasource field will be visible in the Edit Datalog agent dialog. The Datalog agent should therefore only be used for proprietary logging and the datalog period ( Length... ) should not exceed what is required for operational trending purposes. In other words, should an operator only need to see 24 hours of trend data to properly monitor and control his plant then the datalog period should only be set for 1 day. Historical data (i.e. data outside of the datalog period), if requested, will be retrieved from the backup files, if required. When the allocated size of the datalog (.LGD) file is filled, it wraps (starts again at the beginning). At which time one or more datalog backup (.LGB) files are created to store this older (historical) data. The datalogging sub-system automatically retrieves this historical data from these files, when this data is required by trends (charts) or other requests for historical data. In Adroit 10 , the naming convention of these backup files have improved compared to Adroit 8.4 to significantly reduce the number of files that are created. More details: When creating monthly datalog backup files in Adroit 8.4 , a separate file was created for each day of the month that had data logged, since the file name also included the day that the data was logged. For instance: 1. A data value with a timestamp of 2017-11-21 10:00:00 would go to a backup file called 2017-11-21-m-11 2.
