Working with pane display bars Working with pane display bars Pane display bars are used when tool windows or configuration dialogs contain at least one pane an entirely separate working area of a window, often separated by a pane display bar. See pane display bar. . These bars are located between two adjacent panes and can be used to do the following: - to increase the size of one pane by hiding the adjacent pane - to adjust the relative sizes of the two adjacent panes, like a splitter bar. - to display a pane which has been hidden Pane display bars are indicated by two arrows separated by a row of dots and are always positioned in the center of the left and/or right border of the pane that is able to be enlarged. Note: When a pane display bar is situated between two panes, the border above and below this pane display bar becomes a splitter bar, therefore point above or below the display bar, until the mouse pointer assumes the splitter bar icon and drag this bar to adjust the widths of these adjacent panes accordingly. The direction in which the arrows point, indicate whether a pane will be hidden or displayed, as follows: - If a pane display bar is between two adjacent panes, then the pane that the arrows point to will be hidden, when the pane display bar is clicked. Tip: This is especially useful if you need more space to display values or to work within the pane. - If a pane display bar is situated on the border of the window itself and the arrow is pointing in the direction of the window’s contents then a pane will be displayed, when the pane display bar is clicked. -->

Working with policies Top Working with policies Policies are configurable sets of rules, which provide a general (large-scale) level of control to safeguard the services and data that the SmartUI Server provides.

Title: Working with policies
Working with policies Top Working with policies Policies are configurable sets of rules, which provide a general (large-scale) level of control to safeguard the services and data that the SmartUI Server provides. In other words, policies control the access to a SmartUI Server and to each datasource plugin a generic type of data supplier that interfaces between the Server and this specific type of data, so that it is exposed to the Server in the format of data elements. See data element. for the allowed groups and/or users, as follows: - Each policy represents a specific service or activity that can be performed by this SmartUI Server. Certain policies are datasource plugin-specific. For details on the provided services, see Available policies . - By associating the allowed users and/or groups with each policy, you are able to determine the extent of their access to this SmartUI Server and its datasource plugins. For details, see Associating policies with allowed users and groups . - Any allowed user and/or group not associated with a policy is unable to perform the service that it represents. In this way, whenever a SmartUI Server receives a request for a service, it first determines whether the currently logged in user is part of the allowed users or groups that are able to perform this request, and then denies or grants access based on this result. Click for more information: Policies are configured per Server connection in the Enterprise Manager , by using its Security component within the Management category. - Any group(s) and/or user(s) that have been assigned global security access to this SmartUI Server, is automatically associated with every policy. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . - Additional groups, over and above those that are assigned global security access, may initially be associated with every policy. For details on configuring this security setting, see Server security settings . - Once a datasource plugin is secured using a policy, this security will be applied to all of its existing and future configured datasources. - In order to secure a specific datasource, data element security needs to be employed instead. For details, see Working with data element security . - Configuring Server security . - Adding allowed users and groups . -->

Working with profiles Top Working with profiles User management in SmartUI is performed through the use of roaming user profiles.

Title: Working with profiles
Working with profiles Top Working with profiles User management in SmartUI is performed through the use of roaming user profiles. By configuring user profiles you can customise the display and defaults of the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications and, if necessary limit the access users have within the SmartUI Operator application. Click for more details: User profiles allow users to use different computers and still retain their same user settings within the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications. - Profiles can only be applied to the allowed users and/or groups of a SmartUI Server. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . - Only the profiles that have been configured for the default (logon) SmartUI Server are applied to the users of the Designer and Operator. For details, see Specifying the default connection . - Existing profiles can also be copied to the same Server or to another Server and modified, if necessary. For details, see Copying profiles or Replicating profiles . - Since profiles are data elements you can secure them using data element security to specify which allowed users and groups are able to view, configure and remove each profile and/or to configure its security settings. For details, see Assigning security permissions to data elements . Create and edit profiles in the Enterprise Manager , by using the Profile component within the Management category. For details, see Creating profiles or Editing profiles . For details on configuring the profile settings to customise the Client applications and, if necessary limit the access users have within the SmartUI Operator application, see Configuring profiles . The SmartUI Designer automatically creates a standard profile called ‘Default’ containing the default settings for the SmartUI Designer and Operator. This profile is applied to all the allowed users and groups on the applicable SmartUI Server, unless another profile is applied to them. For details, see Default profiles . -->

Working with Project Navigation Top Working with Project Navigation When creating a project, you can choose how you want your end-users to navigate between the various graphic forms provided by your project by selecting the required Navigation Type .

Title: Working with Project Navigation
Working with Project Navigation Top Working with Project Navigation When creating a project, you can choose how you want your end-users to navigate between the various graphic forms provided by your project by selecting the required Navigation Type . Note1: Each navigation type is a navigation template project and when selected this copies the selected navigation project and their default graphic forms and folders to the root of your project. Note2: If you use the Default project style, then the style of the selected navigation project is also copied to your project, which you can configure this style as needed to use for any styled graphic forms that you create for this project. For details, see Working with Project Styles . Once you have chosen the type of graphic form navigation, you can apply a predefined or custom Navigation Theme to define the look and feel of this graphic form navigation. Note: If you specify the Default navigation theme, then the default colors of the selected Navigation Type are used. When creating a project, if necessary check the Show Project Styles and Navigation Configuration checkbox (or click the Advanced View button), which displays the Project Navigation tab. Click on the required image of the Navigation Type tab that describes how your end-users will select the required graphic forms provided by your project. Note: This will only contain the None theme if you unchecked the Include default projects i.e. Navigation Templates, Shapes Wizards and Examples, and System Information etc. checkbox when creating a new Configuration in Adroit Config Editor . Selecting any navigation type other than None displays the Navigation Theme tab, so you can choose a theme that defines the following project navigation colors: Example: - Graphic Form Background: this changes the background color of all the project navigation graphic forms and if you are using the Default style, then this also specifies the background color of any styled graphic forms that you create for this project. Note: The following three colors only affect the graphic form containing the navigation area. - Navigation Background :the background of the navigation area containing the buttons used to open the graphic forms of this project. - Button Background : the background color of the buttons used to open the graphic forms of this project. - Button Text : the text color of the buttons used to open the graphic forms of this project. You can either select a predefined theme from the Theme list and/or modify the Theme colors as required, to Save As... your own custom theme, which you can reuse when creating other projects. Tip: Any custom themes that are saved are added to the user profile of the currently logged in user. Example of a navigation type using the predefined Theme3 colors for its navigation area: -->

Working with Project Styles Top Working with Project Styles When creating a project, you can choose to associate either a predefined or custom style to the project, which creates a hidden graphic form, called !Style, which configures the following common graphic form display properties to save you design time and ensure a consistent look and feel: - size : their physical dimensions, specified in pixels: either select a Predefined width and height, which specify common monitor resolutions or specify your own Custom dimensions.

Title: Working with Project Styles
Working with Project Styles Top Working with Project Styles When creating a project, you can choose to associate either a predefined or custom style to the project, which creates a hidden graphic form, called !Style, which configures the following common graphic form display properties to save you design time and ensure a consistent look and feel: - size : their physical dimensions, specified in pixels: either select a Predefined width and height, which specify common monitor resolutions or specify your own Custom dimensions. - The Backcolor and Forecolor of the graphic form. Note: Depending on the controls that you add to this graphic form, they may inherit the specified Backcolor. - The default Font of the graphic form and any controls that you add to this graphic form. Note: After applying a style to a project you can further configure this project style by using the Project Style group of the Project tab of the Designer ribbon. Tip: This also allows you to edit the !Style graphic form to add a banner or a company logo that all your graphic forms will have in common. Once you have chosen a project style, the Create Graphic Form (Styled) option becomes available to create graphic forms that utilise the currently configured selected style. Note1: Any change that you make to a project style after creating a styled graphic form will NOT be made to this graphic form - so ensure that you are completely happy with your style before creating your styled graphic forms. Note2: You can still use the default Create Graphic Form option to add graphic forms to your project that do not use the specified style. When creating a project, if necessary check the Show Project Styles and Navigation Configuration checkbox (or click the Advanced View button), which displays the Project Style tab. Either select a predefined style from the Style list and/or modify the various settings as required, to Save As... your own custom style, which is added to the user profile of the currently logged in user, and can be reused when creating other projects. Example: Note: If you do not alter the settings of the Default style, then no style is applied to this project, which is the default setting. Tip: Use the Preview panel to test the look and feel of the style settings.

After applying a style to a project, the Project Style group of the Project tab of the Designer ribbon is enabled, so that you can further configure this project style: Tip: The caption of this group indicates the name of the currently selected styled project.

Title: Working with Project Styles
After applying a style to a project, the Project Style group of the Project tab of the Designer ribbon is enabled, so that you can further configure this project style: Tip: The caption of this group indicates the name of the currently selected styled project. In addition to the providing the project style settings, the Project Style group provides the Open Project Style item, which opens the project style graphic form (!Style), so that you can add form components to this project style graphic form, such as a banner (header) or footer or logo or any other element or graphic that all your styled graphic forms have in common and/or configure their default properties. After editing this project style graphic form, click the Save Project Style item to save these project style changes. Note: You can only edit the style of a single project at a time. -->

Working with projects Top Working with projects Projects manage the creation and storage of their graphic forms and make it possible to organise graphic forms through the creation of folders.

Title: Working with projects
Steps:
Working with projects Top Working with projects Projects manage the creation and storage of their graphic forms and make it possible to organise graphic forms through the creation of folders. For details, see Configuring projects or Working with graphic forms . Projects are created and configured within the Projects category of the required Server connection in the Enterprise Manager . For details, see Creating new projects . When creating projects you can either specify a style to configure certain default display settings of your styled graphic forms to save you design time and ensure a consistent look and feel and/or to specify how your end-users navigate between them. For details, see Working with Project Styles or Working with Project Navigation . Note: Projects and their folders provide a Preview Graphic Forms option to displays thumbnail snapshots of all the graphic forms located in their immediate or root level to either open the required graphic form or populate the Favorites tool window. For details, see Previewing graphic forms . Tip: Projects and their folders provide an an Open ... Folder right click menu in the Enterprise Manager that will open this specific folder in Windows Explorer, when this project is on the same computer, so that content can be manually copied into or out of it. However, their graphic forms do not need to be created from scratch, since it is possible to both import and export graphic forms to and from a project or to use wizards. For details, see Importing graphic forms or Exporting graphic forms or Working with wizards . Note1: Access to both the project and its graphic forms can be controlled, if necessary. For details, see Securing projects . Note2: You can also prevent the unauthorised editing of graphic forms and/or wizards, by password-protecting entire projects, folders and/or individual graphic forms and wizards. For details, see Password protecting graphic forms and/or wizards . A project exists in two main states: - The design state, which is used to add, import and configure or design the graphic forms within the SmartUI Designer. Note: The amount of user interaction provided by a graphic form is wholly dependent upon its design. For details, see Designing graphic forms . Tip: The Shapes Wizards & Examples tab of the Designer ribbon, provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project so that you can easily design your graphic forms. For details, see Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples . In particular this contains the Situational Awareness category, which contains sub-categories of wizards that allow you to create process control user interfaces that strive to minimise operator fatigue and increase their response times. For more details, see Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) . - The operational or run-time state, which is used to view and interact with these graphic forms, typically within the SmartUI Operator although it is also possible to do this within the SmartUI Designer too. For details, see Operating graphic forms . Each project is also an internal datasource and its folders and graphic forms are its data elements. For details on how to distinguish the available datasources, see About datasources and data elements . For this reason each project can also be updated or locked, if necessary. For details, see Updating datasources or Locking datasources . Note: Projects are saved in separate folders, with the exact structure of the project being maintained, to easily locate your graphic forms, so that they can be backed up, copied, moved or have external content added to them. For details, see Locating saved projects . -->

Working with scripts Top Working with scripts Scripts are usually created and edited in the SmartUI Designer using the generic Script Editor, however, users can also use Visual Studio 2010 (and later).

Title: Working with scripts
Working with scripts Top Working with scripts Scripts are usually created and edited in the SmartUI Designer using the generic Script Editor, however, users can also use Visual Studio 2010 (and later). These scripts can either be written in Microsoft Visual Basic.NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp) scripting languages. Click for more details: Both the default scripting and debugging environment and the default scripting language and other scripting settings are specified by the profile associated with the currently logged in user. For details, see Customizing default script editor or Customizing default scripting language . Note1: Graphic form scripts can also be created and edited in the Graphic Form Script tool window. For details, see Graphic form scripting . Note2: The onus rests upon the user to be familiar with these programming languages, since assistance with these languages is beyond the scope of this documentation. Articles related to scripting and converting scripts to the .NET Framework, are available on: http://msdn.microsoft.com; http://msdn.microsoft.com/netframework/ and http://www.codeproject.com. Each script is seamlessly encapsulated in a script object, which provides the self-contained environment within which the script is run. For details on writing scripts, see Writing scripts . For instance, the script object is responsible for managing the list of external assemblies formerly known as a dynamic linked libraries (.DLL files), which is externally compiled and contains a collection of properties or methods that can be implemented within a script. that are referenced by each script, so that their properties and methods etc. can be used within the script. For details, see Managing references . The following three types of scripts can be implemented: - Scripts that interact with and run on the SmartUI Server, these are added to the Script Server datasource. For details, see Script datasources . - Scripts that interact with and run on the SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. (the Designer / Operator), these are added to a Script Engine spider. For details, see Script Engine spiders . - Scripts that run on the SmartUI Server, but which interact with the SmartUI Client (the Designer / Operator) these are added to the Script Server datasource and connected to the required Script Engine spider. Note1: Scripts are able to interact with the SmartUI Server and/or the Client through INeed interfaces, which provide programmatic access to their various components. For details, see Working with INeed Interfaces or INeed interfaces object reference . Note2: Running a script object from the SmartUI Server or a Client, should not affect its speed of execution. Typically, the script execution speed is dependent on the script source, the utilization of external references and correct programming techniques and other system-dependent factors such as CPU load etc. -->

Working with security Top Working with security The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security.

Title: Working with security
Steps:
Working with security Top Working with security The SmartUI security system is user-centric and operates on top of the traditional Windows operating system security. This uses a configurable sub-set of the existing users and groups that are "allowed" on each SmartUI Server computer and are hence known as the Allowed users and groups. SmartUI Server security is configured in the Enterprise Manager , by using the Security component within the Management category. - The ONLY mandatory SmartUI Server security configuration are the Allowed users and groups, which provides the first or foundational level of ALL user security and management within the SmartUI . For details, see Configuring Server security . Note: SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. applications also provide security to control the access of the Allowed users and groups within these applications, amongst other functions. For details, see Working with Client security . - Additional SmartUI Server-specific security measures can stipulate who should or shouldn't have access to the SmartUI Server; each configured datasource a connection via a datasource plugin to a particular supply of data, to expose its data to the Server as data elements. See Server; datasource plugin;data element. , data element a finite component of data contained within a datasource that behaves in a generic manner; typically a value. See datasource. and/or special function optionally provided by a datasource plugin to perform additional functionality forinteracting with each datasource and / or its data. . Note: For those projects that require Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance, you can enable the 21 CFR 11 mode and implement the implicit security configuration such as specifying which data elements (values) are able to be audited and/or have their value changes authenticated. For further details, see Working with 21 CFR 11 mode . Click for more details: Security should typically be implemented during deployment, so that the initial allowed users and groups can be configured on each SmartUI Server. Then the access of these allowed users and groups should be specified within each Server and Client application. However, security configuration should continue throughout the life of the project to secure new datasources; limit the access of new users and modify the access levels of existing users, as required etc. Note: The lowest level to which SmartUI Server security can be applied is the data element. It is therefore useful to determine the available data elements. For details, see About datasources and data elements . -->

Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples Top Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples The Shapes Wizards & Examples tab of the Designer ribbon, provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project so that you can easily design your graphic forms.

Title: Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples
Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples Top Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples The Shapes Wizards & Examples tab of the Designer ribbon, provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project so that you can easily design your graphic forms. Note: This tab will be empty if this project fails to load, for instance if you unchecked the Include default projects... checkbox when creating a new Configuration in Adroit Config Editor . Tip: This now contains the Situational Awareness category, which contains sub-categories of wizards that allow you to create process control user interfaces that strive to minimise operator fatigue and increase their response times. For more details, see Situational Awareness (or High Performance SCADA) . By default this tab displays a drop-down list of the available Categories of items, on the left hand side, selecting the first category by default. Example: Note: These categories are alphabetically sorted. When a category is selected, its sub-categories of items are displayed horizontally and if they do not fit along the top of the Designer, you can scroll through them using the provided left and right arrows. Click a sub-category to display its items, in a vertical scrollable window. Example: Either click the required item and then click where you want it on the graphic form or wizard directly or right click the item and select Add to Favorites to populate your Favorites window with those items that you will frequently use when designing your graphic forms and/or wizards. -->

Working with Show (All) Information Working with Show (All) Information To assist in troubleshooting your graphic forms, the Smart UI Operator can allow a control or vector, on the displayed graphic form, to display the list of all the data elements connected to its properties, to do the following: - to view the quality (good or bad) status of the data element - allow you to copy this data element name and - in the case of Adroit can allow you to edit this tag.

Title: Working with Show (All) Information
Working with Show (All) Information Working with Show (All) Information To assist in troubleshooting your graphic forms, the Smart UI Operator can allow a control or vector, on the displayed graphic form, to display the list of all the data elements connected to its properties, to do the following: - to view the quality (good or bad) status of the data element - allow you to copy this data element name and - in the case of Adroit can allow you to edit this tag. Enable this troubleshooting facility, as follows: - To enable this for ONLY the topmost control or vector currently under the mouse pointer (for the current TEMPLATE SET), right-click and select Show Information . - To enable this for ALL the controls and vectors on the graphic form (for the current TEMPLATE SET), press CTRL+S or right-click and select Show All Information . Any control or vector that has this troubleshooting facility enabled, indicates this by displaying the icon in the top right corner. Example Clicking on the icon, displays the Elements menu item, which displays the list of datasources whose data elements (values) have been connected to the properties of the selected control or vector. Clicking the name of the required datasource displays the list of only its data elements that are connected to the properties of the selected control or vector. This list of data elements graphically indicates the quality of these data elements, by displaying good data elements in green and the bad data elements in red. Example: Tip: For Adroit datasources, you can also use the bad-tag status indicators, if displayed, to further troubleshoot any bad tags connected to the controls or vectors of your graphic forms. For details on using these, see Bad tag status indicators . Clicking one of the displayed data elements in this list display, the following datasource-specific options: - Copy : to copy the specified, fully qualified data element name to the clipboard (containing the datasource name and full path to this data element), for reference purposes. - Edit : for Adroit datasources ONLY, this option opens the Adroit Agent Configurator with this tag (agent) selected (if it can be found), so that it can be edited. Note: Since this option ONLY applies to Adroit datasources and even then the editing of tags in the Smart UI Operator poses a security risk, so the display of this option is controlled via the AllowEditTags Boolean setting of the Operator Settings page of the profile dialog, which is False (hidden) by default. Example: Note: The currently selected data element is displayed in light blue, which masks its quality indication. -->

Working with SmartUI Templates Top Working with SmartUI Templates SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time.

Title: Working with SmartUI Templates
Working with SmartUI Templates Top Working with SmartUI Templates SmartUI Templates are reusable graphic forms that can be used at run-time. The fundamental difference between a graphic form and a SmartUI Template is that a SmartUI Template has aliases, some of which are automatically created, which allow data elements within Behaviours and/or spiders to be dynamically driven. Typically SmartUI Templates are used for graphic forms that are displayed as pop-ups or within TemplateGO a Template Graphic Object control that displays a graphic form and connects data elements to any aliases of this graphic form. controls. For more details about using aliases, see Working with aliases . IMPORTANT: The default action for values entered into the Aliases tab of the Advanced View has been changed to always specify the text that is either manually entered or browsed in, unless the Use Tag Value checkbox is checked, at which time it will try to resolve the required data element value from the entered (typically browsed in) text. Therefore when passing substitutions or aliases, in curly {} brackets, ensure that the Use Tag Value checkbox is NOT checked, which is its default setting. When launching child SmartUI Templates from a parent SmartUI Template, you can automatically use the alias values of the parent SmartUI Template, instead of manually assigning values to the aliases of each child. For details, see Passing alias values from parent to child . IMPORTANT: When dragging or copying a SmartUI Template onto a graphic form ONLY use the Graphic Form by Reference option as this is the ONLY option that creates TemplateGO controls so that you can configure its aliases. For details on configuring this option, see Adding a graphic form to another graphic form . Automatic alias creation Aliases can be automatically created for you, by using {} notation, in the following instances: - in the Properties tool window: for any String or Text properties, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring Behaviours: for any data element field, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring a charting control, for the applicable Series values specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring an Adroit Alarm Viewer control, specify the required name enclosed in { } braces for the Alarm List / Alarm Agent value. Use {} notation to specify aliases, as follows: - if you require the alias to specify the ENTIRE value/data element to be substituted then specify the single {requiredAliasName} - this is most typical. - if you require multiple parts of the value/data element name to be separately replaced then specify multiple aliases, such as {DataSource}.{Structure}.{DataName}.{Value}. For example: {tag} or by concatenating a number of hierarchical levels for this data element , for instance: {AS}.{tag} Example: Manual alias creation If you need to expose any other property of the graphic form or its configured form components, then you need to manually add the required alias to a graphic form and then manually assign them to the required properties of this graphic form and/or its added form components via the Spider Configuration tool window. For details on how to configure aliases in this manner, see Working with aliases . A typical example of how to use SmartUI Templates as run-time reusable graphic objects: - Create a SmartUI Template with 2 aliases using 4 labels. - Create a normal graphic form with 3 buttons. - For each button, add an Execute Command behaviour that opens the SmartUI Template that you created. - Click the Advanced View button and the Aliases tab to browse in the appropriate data element for each Alias. Repeat this step for each Button.

- Once you’ve configured each button, clicking on each button in the Operator to display the same SmartUI Template but with different data element values.

For an example of configuring this, see How to create a Wizard that contains a Template pop up . Tip: Wizards that display one or more SmartUI Templates can use their substitutions to drive the values of the aliases of these child SmartUI Templates. For details, see Driving aliases with wizard substitutions . For more information and detailed procedures for this and other methods of re-using graphical components to speed up the process of creating graphic forms, see How to reuse graphical components . -->

Working with special function security Top Working with special function security Special functions are additional functionality provided by a datasource for interacting with its data (data elements).

Title: Specifications
Working with special function security Top Working with special function security Special functions are additional functionality provided by a datasource for interacting with its data (data elements). Click for more details: - Special functions can only be secured once the allowed groups and/or users have been added. For details, see Adding allowed users and groups . - Special functions need to be separately secured for EACH datasource that is created. - Special function security is unaffected by the security settings applied to the datasource itself. For details on securing datasources, see Working with data element security . - By securing special functions, you are actually securing specific functionality provided by the datasource itself. This becomes especially apparent when the special function is the only provided means for performing a specific action. The following strategy is the recommended for controlling access to special functions: - Specify which allowed users and/or groups are able to use special functions at all, by associating them to the Invoke Special Function policy. For details, see Associating policies with allowed users and groups . Note: Additional allowed users and groups may initially be associated to this policy. For details on configuring this security setting, see Server security settings . - Specify which special functions these allowed users for and/or groups are able to use for each datasource, so that they will be able to perform their required duties. For details, see Assigning security permissions to special functions . In this way, whenever a special function is used: - this SmartUI Server first determines whether the currently logged in user is part of the allowed users or groups that are able to use special functions. - if so then this SmartUI Server determines whether the user is actually allowed to use the special function associated with this specific datasource, and accepts or rejects the request accordingly. Note: By default, only those group(s) and/or user(s) that have global security access to each SmartUI Server have access to all special functions. For more information, see Assigning global security to groups and users . -->

Working with spider configuration views Top Working with spider configuration views Once a spider has been added to a spider workspace, it can be further configured through the use of its right-click menu and configuration view.

Title: Configuration
Working with spider configuration views Top Working with spider configuration views Once a spider has been added to a spider workspace, it can be further configured through the use of its right-click menu and configuration view. The configuration view of a spider can perform the following functions: - To add a description of its function and/or to rename the spider - To configure the required input(s) and output(s) of the spider. - To create silks to and from this spider. - If necessary, to configure the event used to trigger this spider. This configuration view of a spider can be displayed or hidden , either individually or for all the added spiders, as required. Note: When configuring this view a tool tip describing each of the configured inputs and/or outputs is displayed when you point over them. This configuration view always contains the following fields: - The first field, below the title bar of the spider, displays the name of the spider, which can usually be changed. For details, see Renaming spiders . Note: The name of a Data spider cannot be changed. - The second field is the description field, where you are able to add additional comments or reminders for future reference. This description is also displayed, along with the spider’s name, by the tool-tip text whenever the mouse pointer hovers over the title bar of a spider. For details, see Annotating spiders . This configuration view, will contain at least one of the following sections: Note: The type of spider that is selected, and the function that it performs, will determine which of these sections will appear. For details, see Available spiders . - The Inputs section: this contains a list of inputs that have been configured for the spider. Note1: If no inputs are configured for the spider, this section will not appear. Note2: These inputs can either be configured within the spider itself and/or may require their values to be supplied by other spiders or Data spiders (e.g. properties or data elements). - The New Input section: this contains a list of input types, which can be used to create custom inputs for the spider. For details, see Creating customised spider inputs . Note: If this functionality is not supported for the current spider, this section will not appear. Tip: When creating a silk, it is also possible to simply drag directly onto an input type, in the New Input section, to add an input to the Inputs section and connect it to the silk in one easy step. For details, see Creating silks . - The Outputs section: this contains a list of outputs that have been configured for the spider. Note1: If no outputs are configured for the spider, this section will not appear. Note2: A silk can be connected from each configured output to supply the inputs of other spiders or Data spiders (e.g. properties or data elements), although this is not always desired. Tip: If an output of a spider does not provide the necessary data type, you can convert it to the required data type and use this converted value instead. For details, see Converting output data types . - The New Output section: this contains a list of output types, which can be used to create custom outputs for the spider. For details, see Creating customised spider outputs . Note1: If this functionality is not supported for the current spider, this section will not appear. Note2: The output name of a spider is case sensitive. -->

Title: Working with spider workspaces
Working with spider workspaces Top Working with spider workspaces A spider workspace is used to transfer and/or manipulate data by adding, configuring and running spiders, silks and/or template sets. For a general overview of spider workspaces and their configurable items, see Introduction to spiders and silks . Spider workspaces can contain the following items to facilitate the transfer and/or manipulation of data: - Spiders, which communicate and/or manipulate data from a set of inputs to a set of outputs. For details, see Working with spiders . - Silks, which connect spiders together. For details, see Working with silks . - Template sets, which are sets of silks that control the transfer of data between spiders. For details, see Working with template sets . The spider workspace provides a visual or drag and drop view that is recommended for all users to create the initial spiders, silks and template sets. For details, see . The Spider Configuration Mode section of View tab of the Designer ribbon determines the visibility and user interaction within the Spider Configuration window, as follows: Note: When changing from one mode to another, you need to close all open graphic forms. - Beginner : (default selection for new installs) the Spider Configuration window is not accessible at all and therefore does not appear in the Content list. This provides the added advantage that graphic forms open faster, since the visual components of the configured spiders are not loaded. Note: This mode is required when using graphic forms that have an excessively large number of spiders. - Intermediate : the Spider Configuration window can be accessed (is added to the Content list) but is not displayed by default and any spider regions associated with configured Behaviours cannot be accessed (they remain closed). - Advanced : grants full access to the Spider Configuration window and opens this window. Click for more details: This spider workspace is the central pane of the Spider Configuration tool window, which is run from the Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. . Hence, the added spiders and silks are only live and able to produce their animations, when the graphic form is opened in preview mode in the SmartUI Designer or is viewed in the SmartUI Operator. The Boolean ShowComponentNames property of the graphic form can make it easier to locate the name of a form component quickly, by displaying the names of all the added form components in their top left corners. This is especially useful when linking to a form component manually in the spider workspace. For details, see Animating graphic forms . The following types of substitutions that can be made: - value substitutions : these are placeholders for values (data elements) and so you are actually adding Data Element spiders, which allow you to determine which portion/s of the specified data element should be replaced at runtime.

Title: Adding substitutions to wizards
The following types of substitutions that can be made: - value substitutions : these are placeholders for values (data elements) and so you are actually adding Data Element spiders, which allow you to determine which portion/s of the specified data element should be replaced at runtime. Each substituted value must be enclosed in curly braces {}, as follows: - if you require the ENTIRE Data Element to be substituted then specify {requiredValueName} - if you require multiple parts of the data element name to be separately replaced then specify multiple substitutions, such as concatenating a number of hierarchical levels for this data element: {DataSource}.{Structure}.{DataName}.{Value}. Note : A data element that is specified without curly braces is assumed to be an existing data element. - static substitutions : these are placeholders for text Substitutions are automatically created for you, by using this {} notation, in the following instances: IMPORTANT: In the case of String or Text properties, you can choose whether the substitution name enclosed in { } braces is either a static (text) or a value substitution. - in the Properties tool window: for any String or Text properties, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring Behaviours: for any data element field, you can specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring a charting control, for the applicable Series values specify the required name enclosed in { } braces. - when configuring an Adroit Alarm Viewer control, specify the required name enclosed in { } braces for the Alarm List / Alarm Agent value. - When you create or edit Data Element spiders and/or click its Substitutions spider toolbar button (or spider menu item) to specify the required substitution/s in the Substitutions dialog for this data element, which is typically used when you have saved a graphic form as a wizard. For more details about Data Element spiders, see Data Element spiders .

Wizards provide the ability to change (substitute) the values of certain data elements, these substitutions can be configured as follows: Tip : Not all values require substitutions – some or most values can be assigned to valid (unchanging) values, if desired.

Title: Substituting values in wizards
Steps:
Wizards provide the ability to change (substitute) the values of certain data elements, these substitutions can be configured as follows: Tip : Not all values require substitutions – some or most values can be assigned to valid (unchanging) values, if desired. - when creating and editing wizards: use the Substitutions Overview dialog to manage your substitutions, which displays all the data elements and/or substitutions provided by this wizard, in a single dialog and can be accessed using one of the following methods: - via the Substitutions wizard toolbar button - by right clicking a wizard and selecting Substitutions This dialog is useful, if you have been using valid data elements to drive specific values in a wizard and now you want to substitute these values. As this helps locate these values easily, without having to sift through the spider workspace. The method used to locate and manage these values/substitutions depends upon how they have been assigned, as follows: - For all data elements or substitutions directly assigned to the controls or vectors (in other words to their properties and/or Behaviours): - Select the required control or vector from the Graphic Objects list to display its configured Behaviours and/or Property spiders (properties), that either have substitutions or data elements assigned to them - This specifies the names of the assigned data elements and hence whether these data element names have configured substitution/s or not. - Then double click the required entries to edit or to create the required substitutions. - For all data elements or substitutions indirectly assigned to the controls or vectors (in other words through the use of associated spiders or other indirect methods): - Click the Other tab, which indicates where these data elements have been assigned and the names of the associated data elements and hence whether these data element names have configured substitution/s or not. - Again double click the required entries to edit or to create the required substitutions. - when adding a wizard to (or editing a wizard instance in) a graphic form: use the Substitution Assignment dialog, can be accessed using one of the following methods: - by dragging a wizard onto a graphic form - via the Substitution Assignment graphic form toolbar button - by right clicking a wizard instance and selecting Substitution Assignment - by clicking the glyph in the top right corner of a wizard instance and selecting the Substitution Assignment link from its Tasks menu. - by clicking the wizard glyph in the top left corner of a wizard instance. Example showing these features of a wizard instance: This Substitution Assignment dialog is re-sizable and verifies whether the specified data element values can be located. More details: The Result column background is green if the specified data element is Valid (has been located) or red to alert users that this data element is Invalid (does not currently exist, but is assumed that it will be added later). Note: Static substitutions are differentiated by a yellow background in the Substitution Assignment dialog, since they are placeholders for text and not data elements. When you have used multiple substitutions are used to create a single value (data element) name, then click the Context checkbox to display the complete substituted data element name so that you can clearly see which part of this name you are supplying a value for. Tip: Typically you should only use the data element browser, when the substitution refers to the ENTIRE data element name, otherwise after specifying the required data element, you need to MANUALLY delete the unnecessary portions (which are being handled by other substitutions).

This dialog allows you to specify the Wizard Name , which is the name of the wizard control that is added to this graphic form.

Title: Substituting values in wizards
Steps:
This dialog allows you to specify the Wizard Name , which is the name of the wizard control that is added to this graphic form. By default the name of the wizard is used, which is appended by a unique number if more that one control by this name already exists on the graphic form. Note: You cannot specify spaces for this Wizard Name , since spaces are NOT allowed in the names of controls. - By default the Grouped checkbox is enabled, which groups the vectors and/or controls of this wizard and therefore allows their substitution assignments to be edited after this is added to a graphic form. - If you uncheck the Grouped checkbox, then the vectors and/or controls of this wizard and added to the graphic form in situ (where they are dragged onto the graphic form) and you are UNABLE to edit their substitution assignments AFTER adding them to this graphic form, which you will be warned about. When specifying a substitution name enclosed in braces for a String or Text property of a control or vector, you can choose whether this will be a placeholder for a value (data element) or whether this will be a static substitution, which is a placeholder for text.

Working with template sets Top Working with template sets The PRIMARY function of template sets, is to connect DIFFERENT sets of data to the SAME graphic form.

Title: Working with template sets
Working with template sets Top Working with template sets The PRIMARY function of template sets, is to connect DIFFERENT sets of data to the SAME graphic form. In this case create the Template sets connecting each of them to the SAME properties; then the currently active template set determines which set of data is displayed. Click for more information: PLEASE NOTE : Spider template sets have nothing to do with TemplateGOs or SmartUI Templates and should not be confused with them! Tip: If you need the SAME graphic form to connect to DIFFERENT data, then use TemplateGO controls to display the SAME graphic form the required number of times. For more information and detailed procedures for this and other methods of re-using graphical components to speed up the process of creating graphic forms, see How to reuse graphical components . Template sets are essentially sets of silks, which are used to control the transfer of data between spiders, by determining which of the silks are enabled or active as only one template set can be active at a time. Note: The name of the currently active template set is specified in the top left corner of the spider workspace. Once a template set is activated, its associated silks are enabled and the silks not associated with it are disabled. Only when a silk is enabled, are the spiders it connects able to transfer their data and therefore perform their functions. For details on silks, see Working with silks . In this way, it is possible to vary the information and even its means of calculation, which is either displayed on a graphic form or mapped to a virtual data element. For details, see Animating graphic forms . Tip: In addition to manually configuring spiders and silks and template sets, it is also possible to perform bulk configuration, by exporting and importing this configuration. For details, see Importing spiders and silks . An example of its use: Consider the case where a graphic form is constructed to represent a pump, which displays its status, its flow rate, its pressure and flow, by linking this data to the necessary properties by means of silks. Now consider the case where a battery of similar pumps are required, each requiring this same information to be displayed. Instead of redrawing this pump and replicating in on multiple graphic forms graphic form and then attaching the correct data to each of these pumps individually, template sets can be used. In this case the silks required to supply each individual pump with its required data could be created to this single pump graphic form and then associated with its own template set. Then when the spider workspace is running, the active template set can be dynamically changed, as required, to display the correct information for each pump. Template sets can be implemented in the following manner: Click for more information about each step: - One or more template sets can be added to a spider workspace. For details, see Adding template sets . Note1: Every spider workspace has a template set called ‘Default’, which cannot be removed. Note2: Each template set is specific to the spider workspace in which they are added. - If necessary, specify which of these template sets is to be the active set. For details, see Activating template sets . This will enable all the silks associated with this template set are enabled and any silk(s) not associated with it is will be disabled. Note1: Any silk associated with the Default template set will ALWAYS be enabled, irrespective of the currently active template set.

Note2: Any silks that are created are immediately associated with the currently active template set.

Title: Working with template sets
Note2: Any silks that are created are immediately associated with the currently active template set. Note3: The active template set can be changed using a Template Set spider. For details, see Template Set spiders . - Silks can be associated with as many template sets as is required. These associations can also be removed, if necessary. For details, see Associating silks with template sets . WARNING! Any silk not associated with any template set will never be enabled. Note1: If a template set is removed which had silks associated with it, then only their association to this template set will be removed and not the silks themselves. For details, see Removing template sets . Note2: If a silk is only associated with a single template set, which is removed then it will remain deactivated until it is associated with an active template set. -->

Title: Working with the Activity Monitor
Steps:
Working with the Activity Monitor Top Working with the Activity Monitor The Activity Monitor is available when the SmartUI Server runs an application. Tip: It is recommended to run the SmartUI Server as an application, during the initial designing phase, to make use of the diagnostic features provided by the Activity Monitor. Then once the configuration is over to run it as a service, if necessary, which will ensure that it will not shutdown when you log off. Note: The System Information datasource of the SmartUI Server, extends the troubleshooting functionality provided by the Activity monitor. For details, see System Information . To run the Server as an application: Click the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 and the SmartUI Server item. This can be used to display the operational status of the SmartUI Server and also provides a number of SmartUI Server-specific features. Open the Activity Monitor - Launch the Server as an application by clicking the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 , and the SmartUI Server item. - Click the Launch Activity Monitor to open the Activity Monitor. - Note: The Activity Monitor is only displayed if the ActivityMonitorFormEnabled setting for this Server is enabled. For more information on this setting, see Advanced Server settings . The ActivityMonitorFormTitle setting specifies the title of this application. - Warning: The Server window is not displayed if the SmartUI Server is running as a service . - If the server is already running, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - Tip: When the SmartUI Server is running as an application, you may also press the ALT+TAB KEYS repeatedly until the task switcher displays the Server window, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - If the server is already running as a service, then right-click the Service Manager icon in the Taskbar tray to open the Service Manager dialog, then select Launch Activity Monitor . - The Activity Monitor opens and displays information on the Local Machine tab. The Activity Monitor window consists of the following features: The Tasks panel on the left of the window, which provides the following functions that can be performed by the Server, simply by clicking on the provided links: Note: This Tasks panel also displays the operational status of the Server below these function links. - Display Server Events : This can be used to troubleshoot the setting up and licensing the Server and establishing the required security, profiles, datasources and projects. - Clear Server Events : This will remove the old and existing events and can be used to pinpoint a current problem by only displaying the most current events. WARNING! This will immediately remove all the events from the Server's event log, without displaying a confirmation dialog first. - Display Licence Information : This indicates how the Server is currently being licensed. - Save Server Data : This will manually save the Server and its data and is required if the Server is not being saved automatically on shut down. - Disconnected All Users : This can be used to free up Client connection licenses when it is not possible or inconvenient to visit each Client to disconnect them individually. - Force Memory Cleanup: Typically this option should not be needed, as it is only used for advanced diagnostic purposes. - Shutdown Server : This is the same as pressing the close button in the title bar and will display a confirmation dialog, which if accepted will close the Activity Monitor and terminate the Server. - Restart Server : This will first shut the Server down and then start it up again.

- Restart With Rollback : This will first shut the Server down and then start it up again using the previous saved state (the previous data files).

- The product license is now a .XML document to make it easier to read and is displayed in the License tab.

Title: Important licensing changes:
- The product license is now a .XML document to make it easier to read and is displayed in the License tab. - IMPORTANT: The former Remote Nodes licenses that applied to all types of clients have been DISCONTINUED . These have now been replaced by the following client specific node licenses, each of which have different costs: - Clients : typically Operators and/or Designers and - Web Clients : typically Performance Anywhere clients. - Remote Desktop (RDP) clients can now get a free node connection to obtain engineering access to the Agent Server, by adding and configuring the RDAdminName WG.INI registry string value. Note: By default this registry entry does not exist and therefore all Remote Desktop (RDP) clients are subject to node licensing. This registry value must be created and set to the required Windows username to establish free connections for this user. - The OEM (separately-licensed) components are no longer specified by their associated OEM codes but now included as separate textual entries in the product license, so that users can easily see exactly which components they are currently licensed for. Tip: Only the OEM components that you are licensed for will appear. - All product licenses have a GLOBAL expiry and can also support product-specific expiries, which can be used for product trials. - .V2C (Vendor to Customer) and .C2V (Customer to Vendor) files are now used to create and update product licenses instead of using .RUS files. Back to top:

metadata.title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility

text:
Your product license can either be a HASP and a soft license, each of which have the following important differences: - A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk.

Title: Important differences between a HASP and a soft license:
Your product license can either be a HASP and a soft license, each of which have the following important differences: - A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk. - A Soft license is bound to a specific computer and therefore cannot be transferred to another computer. Therefore if the computer fails then the soft license will no longer work. For details of the available licensing methods and their respective advantages, see Available licensing methods . Back to top:

metadata.title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility
metadata.chunk_title: Prerequisites to get or update a product license:

text:
If necessary, launch the Adtech Licensing Utility first.

Title: How to get a new HASP license or update an existing one:
Steps:
If necessary, launch the Adtech Licensing Utility first. PLEASE NOTE: Purple HASPs are not supported (they lack the necessary space required by this licensing mechanism). - Ensure that your HASP is inserted into the computer. If necessary, click the Rescan HASPs button in the lower right corner. The Request HASP Update button should now be enabled. If the Request HASP Update button is disabled then there is a problem reading your HASP, in which case do the following: - Click the Status tab and right click this page and click the Select all menu item. - Then right click this page and click the Copy menu item. - Email the contents of this tab to your sales representative for further assistance. - Click the Request HASP Update button. This will temporarily disable the Refresh Current License and the Apply License (V2C) buttons, indicating that this request is being processed. Once the .c2v (Customer to vendor) file has been created for this HASP license: Windows Explorer is opened, displaying the folder in which this .c2v file has been copied, which adheres to the following syntax: it begins with HL- followed by the unique serial number of your HASP.c2v The Main tab of the Adtech Licensing Utility also displays the location of this .c2v file and the email address to which this file should be sent. - If you have an email client on your local computer, then do the following: - Click this email address link, which opens your default email client and creates the License Request email message for you that is addressed to the required email address. - In this case simply attach the .c2v file and send it off. - If you cannot email from the local computer, then do the following: - Make a note of the required email address - Copy the resultant .c2v file to a device that is able to email - Create an email that is addressed to the specified email address that is entitled "License Request : " and then copy the entire name of your .c2v file - Attach this .c2v file and send it off. - Once the .v2c (Vendor to Customer) file is emailed back to you, copy this file to a folder on the computer on which you have installed Adroit 10 Agent Server or MAPS 4 Server. - Click the Apply License (V2C) button. In the Open Vendor to Customer (.v2c) File dialog, browse to the folder in which you copied the . v2c file and select this .v2c file and click the Open button. Your license is updated and your license details are displayed in the License tab. Back to top:

text:
By default, the Adtech Licensing Utility hides the options to obtain or update a soft license, to display these options you need to run the Adtech Licensing Utility with the -softlicensemode command line option, as follows: Use the Windows key +R shortcut to launch the Run dialog (or right click the Start menu and select Run ) and then specify and run the following command: alu.exe -softlicensemode In the Adtech Licensing Utility dialog: - Click the Request Soft-License Update button.

Title: How to get a new soft license or update an existing one:
By default, the Adtech Licensing Utility hides the options to obtain or update a soft license, to display these options you need to run the Adtech Licensing Utility with the -softlicensemode command line option, as follows: Use the Windows key +R shortcut to launch the Run dialog (or right click the Start menu and select Run ) and then specify and run the following command: alu.exe -softlicensemode In the Adtech Licensing Utility dialog: - Click the Request Soft-License Update button. This will temporarily disable the Refresh Current License and the Apply License (V2C) buttons, indicating that this request is being processed. Once the .c2v (Customer to vendor) file has been created for this HASP license: Windows Explorer is opened, displaying the folder in which this .c2v file has been copied, which adheres to the following syntax: it begins with New-SL- followed by the computer name.c2v The Main tab of the Adtech Licensing Utility also displays the location of this .c2v file and the email address to which this file should be sent. - If you have an email client on your local computer, then do the following: - Click this email address link, which opens your default email client and creates the License Request email message for you that is addressed to the required email address. - In this case simply attach the .c2v file and send it off. - If you cannot email from the local computer, then do the following: - Make a note of the required email address - Copy the resultant .c2v file to a device that is able to email - Create an email that is addressed to the specified email address that is entitled "License Request : " and then copy the entire name of your .c2v file - Attach this .c2v file and send it off. - Once the .v2c (Vendor to Customer) file is emailed back to you, copy this file to a folder on the computer on which you have installed Adroit 10 Agent Server or MAPS 4 Server. - Click the Apply License (V2C) button. Tip: You can use the default Adtech Licensing Utility (without specifying the command line option) to do this. In the Open Vendor to Customer (.v2c) File dialog, browse to the folder in which you copied the . v2c file and select this .v2c file and click the Open button. Your license is updated and your license details are displayed in the License tab. Back to top:

Once the .c2v (Customer to vendor) file has been created for this HASP license: Windows Explorer is opened, displaying the folder in which this .c2v file has been copied, which adheres to the following syntax: it begins with HL- followed by the unique serial number of your HASP.c2v The Main tab of the Adtech Licensing Utility also displays the location of this .c2v file and the email address to which this file should be sent. - If you have an email client on your local computer, then do the following: - Click this email address link, which opens your default email client and creates the License Request email message for you that is addressed to the required email address. - In this case simply attach the .c2v file and send it off. - If you cannot email from the local computer, then do the following: - Make a note of the required email address - Copy the resultant .c2v file to a device that is able to email - Create an email that is addressed to the specified email address that is entitled "License Request : " and then copy the entire name of your .c2v file - Attach this .c2v file and send it off. - Once the .v2c (Vendor to Customer) file is emailed back to you, copy this file to a folder on the computer on which you have installed Adroit 10 Agent Server or MAPS 4 Server. - Click the Apply License (V2C) button. In the Open Vendor to Customer (.v2c) File dialog, browse to the folder in which you copied the . v2c file and select this .v2c file and click the Open button. Your license is updated and your license details are displayed in the License tab. Back to top:

Working with the Agent Configurator Top Working with the Agent Configuration dialog This resizable dialog is the central point from which you can configure agents in a local or remote Agent Server.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Working with the Agent Configurator Top Working with the Agent Configuration dialog This resizable dialog is the central point from which you can configure agents in a local or remote Agent Server. This allows agents to be creating and configured from Adroit . Open the Agent Configuration dialog, as follows: Tip: This also opens the Adroit Classic UI in the SmartUI Designer, which provides agent-specific menu functions, such as importing and exporting agents. In the SmartUI Designer: Click the Open Configurator tool in the Agent Server group of the Home tab of the SmartUI Designer ribbon. Note: When there is more than one Adroit datasource available, a list is provided to select which Agent Server to configure. The Agent Configuration dialog is displayed within the Classic UI. The Agent Configuration dialog provides the following functionality: - an Agent section that allows you to add agents of the selected agent type in the Type list (if possible) or displays the name of the currently selected agent in the Agents list that will be configured. - an Agent filter section that allows you to limit the display of: - the available agent types displayed in the Type list when designing your system, by checking the checkboxes of the default agent groups. For details, see Default agent groups . - the available agents displayed in the Agents list to those having specific name/s, by specifying an optional agent filter string in the Filter edit box. For details, see Filtering Agents . - a list of buttons down the right side of the dialog that allows you to perform the following agent-specific functions: Find and select an existing agent. Add a new agent. Copy (duplicate) an existing agent configuration. Edit… an existing agent or to bulk edit agents of the same type. Header… displays the bits within the status word of an agent and to configure the other common header slots for configuration. Groups… displays the group membership(s) of this agent for configuration, if required. Used by… displays which agents, if any, are using (subscribing to) this agent. Scan… (communicate) the values of one or more slots of an agent to / from a Device or to contiguously scan agents of the same type . Alarm… one or more status bit combinations of an agent. Log… (record) the values of one or more slots of an agent to a database. Remove (delete) an agent. - a right-click menu as an alternate means of accessing many of the existing agent Configurator functions. For details, see Right-click Menu . Only when these changes made to agents are saved, will they be written to the Adroit database file (.WGP) file of the Agent Server. For details, see Saving agents or Backing Up WGP Files . For further details, see Configuring the Agent Server or the list of available agent types and their slots (values). -->

Working with the Agent Server Monitor Top Working with the Agent Server Monitor The Agent Server Monitor utility is typically provided for advanced users to diagnose or troubleshoot the Agent Server and its client connections.

Title: Working with the Agent Server Monitor
Working with the Agent Server Monitor Top Working with the Agent Server Monitor The Agent Server Monitor utility is typically provided for advanced users to diagnose or troubleshoot the Agent Server and its client connections. The information retrieved from the Agent Server is classified into the following tabs: - General : this tab shows certain key pieces of information pertaining to the running state of the Agent Server. These include information such as: - The number of available channels. - The state of the internal subscription buffer. - Various memory allocations. Tip: Depending on the installed version this can also displays the loading status of the WGP file, so that it is possible to view this even when running the Agent Server as a service. - Channels : this tab shows the state of the Agent Servers communication channels. This includes which channels are currently connected to by a client as well as the state of health of each channel. Tip: This tab is particularly useful in understanding problems to do with remote client connections and quickly shows if the number of allowed channels is insufficient to service the required client connections. - Function Counts : this tab provides advanced diagnostic information that is only applicable to the Agent Server developers. - Chart: this tab displays specific information concerning the performance of the Agent Server. This includes values such as CPU usage, memory consumption etc. This information is shown for a user defined time frame and allows analysis of these values over time. - Eventlog : this tab shows the data contained in the Windows Application event log pertaining to the Agent Server (similar to the data displayed in the Adroit event viewer). - Ping : this tab can help you determine whether any of the currently connected clients have connection issues to this Agent Server, as follows: Click the Import Channels button to import all the unique computer names of the specified channels (clients) currently connected to this Agent Server, as specified in the Channels tab. Check the Enable ping testing checkbox, which cycles through the list of specified IP addresses (computer names) pinging each one in turn. Click the Packet size button to toggle the size of the packets used between 64 bytes and 65500 bytes. Tip : If you suspect that you have poor connections then use the larger packet size to pick up these problems faster. When you save this utility the current list of unique computer names are saved. To remove a row from the list of unique client computers: click the required row and press the DELETE key. -->

Working with the Click Once Operator install Top Working with Click Once SmartUI Operator install The Click Once SmartUI Operator install allows a user to use a fully fledged SmartUI Operator, which is downloaded via Internet Explorer and runs normally, as a separate application.

Title: How to set up Working with the Click Once Operator install
Steps:
Working with the Click Once Operator install Top Working with Click Once SmartUI Operator install The Click Once SmartUI Operator install allows a user to use a fully fledged SmartUI Operator, which is downloaded via Internet Explorer and runs normally, as a separate application. This essentially performs a “one-click deployment” of the SmartUI Operator, which is usually necessary in scenarios where software may not be installed on the client machine, such as on corporate networks. Installing the Click Once SmartUI Operator: This applies to administrators who perform this install on the web server (the computer running IIS Internet Information Services ) so that users can access the Operator via the web. - Install SmartUI and select the Custom installation option and only select the Click Once component from the list of available components. Note: You are unable to continue if you do not have IIS installed on this computer. - Specify the name of the required SmartUI Click Once virtual directory name (this is typically SUIClickOnce ) and the web site in which this Virtual Directory in the provided dialog (by default, the Default Web Site is selected) and click Next . - After the installation has completed, ensure that the URL and virtual directory is working correctly. This URL is typically http://WebSiteAddress/ SUIClickOnce /publish.htm - where WebSiteAddress is the IP address or the domain name of your web site, such as www.msn.com) For details on what your users require and how they can download and run the Click Once SmartUI Operator, see Running the Click Once Operator . -->
