Working with the Config editor Top Working with the Adroit Config Editor The Adroit Config Editor can customise the installed applications and/or services by modifying their default settings, some of which are contained in each .CONFIG file This .NET file is similar to an .INI file, in a single .CONFIG file is used per application to contain its user-configurable settings.

Title: Configuration
Steps:
Working with the Config editor Top Working with the Adroit Config Editor The Adroit Config Editor can customise the installed applications and/or services by modifying their default settings, some of which are contained in each .CONFIG file This .NET file is similar to an .INI file, in a single .CONFIG file is used per application to contain its user-configurable settings. This text file is located in the installation folder and has the same name as its application. . Click for more details: These files are named according to their application or service and located in the installation folder (typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI ). Although these text files can be manually edited, it is recommended to use this application for the following reasons: - It makes it easier to view, identify and configure these settings and prevents one from mistakenly modifying anything except their values. - It exposes the settings of all the .CONFIG files located within the installation folder, so that it is possible to configure one or more of these applications at a time. Instead of manually navigating to the installation folder and opening each file individually. - It also provides a concise description of each setting and can provide comprehensive help too, if necessary. WARNING! Users who do not use this editor and who modify these .CONFIG files directly, do so at their own risk, since renaming or removing a setting may render an application inoperable and/or cause its functioning to be impaired. Launch the Adroit Config Editor . The configurable settings provided by the Adroit Config Editor are arranged as follows: The following settings that affect all SmartUI applications are displayed in the lower left hand corner of the application alongside the version and the various buttons: - Language being used in applications : Select the required language from the list of available languages and click the Update button. - Theme : Select the theme from this list box, which determines how the user interfaces of all the SmartUI applications are displayed. The other settings are classified into the following pages of related settings: Note: Since this is a configuration dialog it provides the standard navigation and layout features common to all configuration dialogs. For details, see Working with configuration dialogs . - The Configuration page, which can specify the currently active configuration that all the application settings pertain to. For details, see Working with Configurations . This contains the Welcome section, which simplifies the essential configuration of the main SmartUI components, namely the Server, Designer and/or Operator, depending on which components are installed. For details, see the Welcome section . - Agent Server Configuration : this section configures the fundamental and advanced settings of the Adroit Agent Server and/or its protocol drivers. Note: This option ONLY appears when Adroit is installed. - Setting up the Server : this section configures the fundamental general, directory, backup and security settings of the SmartUI Server. - Setting up the Designer : this section configures the fundamental login, connections, user interface and scripting settings of the SmartUI Designer. - Setting up the Operator : this section configures the fundamental login, connections, user interface and scripting settings of the SmartUI Operator. - Setting up the Launcher : this section creates a custom SmartUI Launcher installation that is pre-configured to connect to your SmartUI Web service and SmartUI Distribution service. - Setting up ClickOnce : this section creates a custom SmartUI ClickOnce installation (deployment) of your SmartUI Operator. - System Backup and Restore : this section configures the settings required to backup and restore your SmartUI and/or Adroit user-configuration. WARNING: This should NOT be used to transfer project files to and from an engineering workstation.

- The Advanced section, in contrast, allows the more advanced user to configure all the settings of all the installed applications and/or services and so limited assistance is provided.

Working with the Data Element Browser Top Working with the Data Element Browser The data element browser dialog can be used to select the required value (data element), typically to display on or animate a graphic form.

Title: Working with the Data Element Browser
Working with the Data Element Browser Top Working with the Data Element Browser The data element browser dialog can be used to select the required value (data element), typically to display on or animate a graphic form. Annotated screenshot: This dialog is typically launched and used as follows: This dialog displays a tree view of all the datasources and their data elements that are contained within the connected Servers, like that displayed by the Enterprise Manager . The value selected initially by this browser is determined, as follows: - If you have NOT selected a data element for the current field, then it displays the last data element, that you browsed in, using ANY DE browser. Tip: This is particularly helpful, when you are working with the SAME datasource, as it expands this datasource in the tree, highlighting the last browsed-in data element, which you can use as a reference. - If you have browsed in a data element for the current field, then this then data element is automatically selected for you. - If necessary, expand the datasources in the tree, to expose the required data element, by clicking their plus boxes . The name of the currently selected data element is displayed at the bottom of this configuration dialog. - Double click the required data element. The Data Element Browser dialog provides the following features to assist you in this task of selecting the required value: - The Recently selected elements list, which displays the last 10 selected data elements - so that these data elements can be quickly selected again, whose display is controlled by the or button in the top right hand corner. If the data element, in this Recently selected elements list, does not have an associated icon, then either this data element does not exist or, in the case of the Adroit datasource, that you have not opened the associated Agentgroup in the Adroit datasource tree and so if this data element is selected it will not be found in the Browser window. - The ability to display the current value of the data elements you are currently or have previously selected, by clicking the button in the top right hand corner, which adds the Watches column to the Recently selected elements list (when this is displayed) and the icon and current value to the right of the currently selected data element at the bottom of this dialog. - A data element searching capability to quickly locate similarly-named values without manually browsing for them: simply type the required search criteria into the Search in browser for edit box and all the data element names containing the specified search string are displayed in a list providing the name of the data element and its path. If necessary, click the button to return to the tree view. By default, to speed up searching on large Adroit Agent Server projects, the searching stops at the agent and not the slot level. - The tree view provides the full Enterprise Manager context sensitive right click menu functionality. So in the case of using an Adroit datasource you can create the required agent/s when configuring a Behaviour. - When selecting tags from an Adroit datasource, you can also create on-the-fly agents by editing the selected data element string to create another tag. In this case, when you click Finish , a message is displayed asking whether you want to create this new tag or not, if you select Yes then this tag is created and selected. -->

Title: Working with the Datascope
Working with the Datascope Top Working with the Datascope The Datascope displays the data that is being sent to and from the specified device of a protocol driver. Most drivers make use of following colors to make this diagnostic information easier to read, as follows: - Data going to the PLC is displayed in yellow, - Data coming from the PLC is displayed in cyan, - Important messages will be displayed in other colors etc. Example screenshot: Tip: The Datascope can also be displayed from within the driver and device configuration dialog for a specific device of a protocol driver, see Diagnosing installed Protocol Drivers or their configured Devices . The data displayed by the Datascope can either be displayed in HEX or RTU(BINARY), the default or in ASCII, which is RECOMMENDED. The currently selected mode is indicated in the title bar of this window, as follows: - HEX or RTU(BINARY) mode: - ASCII mode: Type “ A ” to toggle the display between these two modes. Click for more details: Tip: We recommend that you ALWAYS display the Datascope in ASCII format, even for known Binary(hex) type protocols, because the newer drivers provide extra information usually in a readable (English) format and also convert the hexadecimal display to ASCII to remain compatible. Note1: If the following characters are displayed in ASCII mode: as displayed in the screenshot example above, then it may be useful to type in “A” again to toggle the display of the Datascope back into RTU(BINARY) mode. Note2: Typing in “A” to toggle between the display modes is equivalent to using the command-line option "/A". Press the SPACEBAR to PAUSE this display of data to allow the window to be scrolled up and down. Press any other key to CONTINUE the display of data. Click for more details: Note: While the Datascope is ’paused’, the data is still being captured and will only wrap at 32 Kbytes. Tip: If the Datascope becomes clogged with data, it may take hours to decipher, to avoid this either increase the device polling times and/or stop other Scan agents. Create a Protocol Dump using the Datascope, as follows: press the “ L ” key, wait for the Datascope to fill with messages and then press the “ L ” key again.

Working with the Designer Top Working with the SmartUI Designer The SmartUI Designer allows you to create and design graphic forms, customise its work environment the user interface of the Designer i.e. the tool windows, toolbars, menus and the Design workspace. and manage both user and data security at the same time. For details, see Customizing the work environment or Working with security This broadly describes the main features of the work environment: - Windows: The work environment of the SmartUI Designer consists of two types of windows, the Design workspace and tool windows , of which many are available . Note: Each tool window is a dockable window a window that can be either be attached to a docking area or that can float anywhere on the screen. See floating mode; docked mode; docking area. whose location can be customised to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace . For more information, see Arranging tool windows . - Toolbar, ribbon and menus: Along the top of the program window are the toolbar and ribbon. - Right-click menus: Extensive right-click menus provide support for doing the most common tasks. Place the cursor in the window that you want to work with, press the right-mouse button, and select an option from the menu. - Toolbar: Click an icon on any of the toolbars as a shortcut to dialogs and actions. For details on the toolbar tools and the tools provided by the Home tab of the ribbon, see Generic Designer tools . - Context-sensitive toolbars either appear at the top of the document in the Design workspace or at the top of the Designer window itself. The toolbar that is displayed, depends upon which document is currently displayed in the Design workspace . - Toolbars also occur in certain tool windows in which case they can either be on the top (Properties tool window) or the bottom ( Toolbox tool window) of the tool window. - Ribbon: Click the required tab to display the relevant tools, whose options are context-sensitive. The following tabs are provided: - Home : commonly used tools for connecting to the SmartUI Server, cutting and pasting and managing projects, see Generic Designer tools - this also describes the tools provided by the SmartUI Designer toolbar. - View : to manage the tool windows that are displayed, simply enable (icon has yellow background) or disable (icon has white background) the appropriate tool window icons and/or reset the current layout of the tool windows, see Accessing tool windows . - Project : tools to configure your projects, by importing specific content into graphic forms and/or editing the style of the currently selected project, if one has been specified , see Tools to import content into graphic forms and Working with Project Styles . - Design : tools to assist with arranging and designing form components a general term encompassing all the controls, components and / or graphic elements that can be added to graphic forms, to provide the required user interface for its end-users. See control; component; graphic element; graphic form. on the currently displayed graphic form. For details, see Tools for editing and designing vectors and/or controls . - Behaviours : tools to add and/or remove Behaviours from the currently selected form component of a graphic form. For details, see About Behaviours . - Shapes Wizards & Examples : provides access to the shapes, wizards and/or examples of the default Shapes Wizards and Examples project to easily design your graphic forms. For details, see Working with Shapes Wizards and Examples . - Configuration : typically intended for advanced users, to configure and manage your SmartUI applications and projects. For details, see Advanced configuration and management .

Title: What does it do?
- At start-up the service attempts to determine which network cards have Power Saving Enabled. - At start-up the service will attempt to determine the UAC status of the currently logged on user. - The Service will periodically attempt to check the following computer information (every 10 minutes): - Total instantaneous CPU Usage as a % - Total and available Memory (Physical & Virtual) - Drive Information for all drives (Total size and available space) - The Service will periodically check specific processes (every 30 seconds) The default processes are "as.exe", "VIP Designer.exe", "VIP Operator.exe", "VIPServer.exe", "VIPService.exe". However you can add additional processes too - see below for details. The following CPU usages are checked for each process: - If the CPU % is higher than 50% of 1 CPU Core it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. - If the Memory (Private Bytes) is more than 80% of 1146880000 bytes it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. When a Process has been flagged for higher resolution monitoring, then it is checked every 10 seconds: - If the process is still above the thresholds, an event entry is written to the Eventlog indicating the Process ID, Name, Description, Running Time, CPU Usage, Private Bytes & Virtual Bytes. - If/when the process has dropped below the thresholds, it will be removed from the higher resolution monitoring.

If necessary, you can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service.

Title: How to add additional processes to be monitored
Steps:
If necessary, you can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service. The configuration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml Example Configuration Entry to add the Notepad.exe process to the list of monitored processes, add the following to the end of this file, above the </NewDataSet> line: <Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables>

If necessary, you can adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes to customise them for your typical system performance.

Title: How to adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes
If necessary, you can adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes to customise them for your typical system performance. The configuration file resides in installation folder of the Health Monitor Service (typically found - C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml In this file, each specified executable allows you to specify the following thresholds, which specify the normal usage values, which if they are consistently exceeded indicates that there may be a problem and hence the Health Monitor Service will log messages in these instances: - CPUCoreThresholdPercent : This specifies the maximum percentage of the CPU that this process executable should consistently use in normal operation, above which the Health Monitor Service will provide alerts. - PrivateBytesLimit : Private Bytes refer to the amount of memory that the process executable has asked for and is a reasonable approximation of the amount of memory the executable is using. This specifies the maximum amount of memory that this executable should normally use. - PrivateBytesThresholdPercent : This specifies the percentage of the specified PrivateBytesLimit that this application executable should normally use above which the Health Monitor Service will provide alerts. -->

text:
Working with the Launcher Top Working with the SmartUI Launcher Although the Launcher does not perform any client or server functionality, itself, it can install the SmartUI Operator remotely (either over a LAN or the Internet) and / or ensure that this component remains up to date with the latest files, if required.

Title: Working with the SmartUI Launcher
Working with the Launcher Top Working with the SmartUI Launcher Although the Launcher does not perform any client or server functionality, itself, it can install the SmartUI Operator remotely (either over a LAN or the Internet) and / or ensure that this component remains up to date with the latest files, if required. Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . The SmartUI Launcher connects to a pre-configured distribution computer over a LAN or the Internet and synchronises the contents of its installation folder with a specific folder on the distribution computer. Click for more details: For details on connecting to a pre-configured distribution computer, see Connecting to the distribution computer . This "distribution" computer is simply a computer that has the VIP Distributor service installed and running. This service specifies the required "distribution" folder that a Launcher application can connect to and synchronise its contents with, which is typically the C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Distribution folder of the SmartUI Server computer. For further details of the procedure whereby contents of the Launcher's installation folder are synchronised with a specific folder on the distribution computer: In other words, once the SmartUI Launcher has connected to the specified distribution computer, the files and sub-folders within its installation folder are compared to those in the specified distribution folder. Only the file(s) and folder(s) which are newer on this remote computer or which do not exist on the local computer will be displayed for downloading. Any executables that are downloaded from the distribution computer can then be run or launched from this application, if necessary, hence the name of this application. Therefore the files placed in the user-configurable distribution folder on the distribution computer, will be the files that are distributed whenever a Launcher is connected to it. Tip: The Welcome section of the Config Editor provides a Setting up the Launcher page to specify the settings required to connect to the distribution computer. For details, see Setting up the Launcher . Note: If the distribution computer uses firewall software ensure that the Distributor service has access to the necessary communication port. For details, see Firewall configuration . To run the Launcher: - Either double-click the Launcher shortcut that is placed on the Desktop - Or click the Start menu, Programs , VIP Launcher and the SmartUI Launcher item. WARNING! When the required files are downloaded they are currently not streamed and so if the connection is slow or breaks the application will not respond until after a timeout, which could take up to 30 seconds. Note1: The Launcher can only connect to a computer that has the Distributor service installed, which specifies the required folder that will be distributed. Note2: Newer files located in sub-folders can be optionally downloaded, however, newer files located in the root directory will always be copied. Command-line options when running the Launcher: - To create a log file, execute the Launcher with the "log" parameter in its command-line. - To automatically execute a downloaded executable after the Launcher has finished processing, add the name of this executable (its extension is not required) as its command-line parameter e.g. add Operator to launch the Operator. Note: These command-line options can be added permanently, by simply editing the shortcut used to launch the SmartUI Launcher and adding the required command-line parameter to the Target field.

The VIP Distributor service is installed with the SmartUI Server installation and the “Distribution” sub-folder contains the files required for the Operator.

Title: Working with the SmartUI Launcher
Steps:
The VIP Distributor service is installed with the SmartUI Server installation and the “Distribution” sub-folder contains the files required for the Operator. For this reason the Operator can be downloaded from a SmartUI Server by using the Launcher. Note: As the SmartUI Launcher is downloading the Operator, ensure that the computer complies with its software and hardware requirements. For details, see System requirements for the Operator. Also ensure that the necessary configuration is performed before the Operator is launched. For details, see Configuration after installation . Note: If necessary, an entirely different folder can be specified by manually editing the path specified by the RedistPath setting. For details on accessing this setting, see Advanced Distributor service settings . -->

Working with the Launcher Top Working with the SmartUI Launcher Although the Launcher does not perform any client or server functionality, itself, it can install the SmartUI Operator remotely (either over a LAN or the Internet) and / or ensure that this component remains up to date with the latest files, if required.

Title: Working with the SmartUI Launcher
Working with the Launcher Top Working with the SmartUI Launcher Although the Launcher does not perform any client or server functionality, itself, it can install the SmartUI Operator remotely (either over a LAN or the Internet) and / or ensure that this component remains up to date with the latest files, if required. Tip: For a detailed step-by-step procedure of connecting Operators to a Server over the Internet, see How to Connect to the Server over the Web . The SmartUI Launcher connects to a pre-configured distribution computer over a LAN or the Internet and synchronises the contents of its installation folder with a specific folder on the distribution computer. Click for more details: For details on connecting to a pre-configured distribution computer, see Connecting to the distribution computer . This "distribution" computer is simply a computer that has the VIP Distributor service installed and running. This service specifies the required "distribution" folder that a Launcher application can connect to and synchronise its contents with, which is typically the C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Distribution folder of the SmartUI Server computer. For further details of the procedure whereby contents of the Launcher's installation folder are synchronised with a specific folder on the distribution computer: In other words, once the SmartUI Launcher has connected to the specified distribution computer, the files and sub-folders within its installation folder are compared to those in the specified distribution folder. Only the file(s) and folder(s) which are newer on this remote computer or which do not exist on the local computer will be displayed for downloading. Any executables that are downloaded from the distribution computer can then be run or launched from this application, if necessary, hence the name of this application. Therefore the files placed in the user-configurable distribution folder on the distribution computer, will be the files that are distributed whenever a Launcher is connected to it. Tip: The Welcome section of the Config Editor provides a Setting up the Launcher page to specify the settings required to connect to the distribution computer. For details, see Setting up the Launcher . Note: If the distribution computer uses firewall software ensure that the Distributor service has access to the necessary communication port. For details, see Firewall configuration . To run the Launcher: - Either double-click the Launcher shortcut that is placed on the Desktop - Or click the Start menu, Programs , VIP Launcher and the SmartUI Launcher item. WARNING! When the required files are downloaded they are currently not streamed and so if the connection is slow or breaks the application will not respond until after a timeout, which could take up to 30 seconds. Note1: The Launcher can only connect to a computer that has the Distributor service installed, which specifies the required folder that will be distributed. Note2: Newer files located in sub-folders can be optionally downloaded, however, newer files located in the root directory will always be copied. Command-line options when running the Launcher: - To create a log file, execute the Launcher with the "log" parameter in its command-line. - To automatically execute a downloaded executable after the Launcher has finished processing, add the name of this executable (its extension is not required) as its command-line parameter e.g. add Operator to launch the Operator. Note: These command-line options can be added permanently, by simply editing the shortcut used to launch the SmartUI Launcher and adding the required command-line parameter to the Target field.

It saves you SCADA engineering time by allowing you to reliably duplicate objects that can have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured, such as their scanning, logging and alarming.

Title: What does the object model do for you?
Steps:
It saves you SCADA engineering time by allowing you to reliably duplicate objects that can have all or most of their SCADA configuration pre-configured, such as their scanning, logging and alarming. The objects that you can create will typically be items of equipment, like pumps or motors and can be anything that you have already created a wizard to represent. You can also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers to them that you can use to filter or group the objects that you deploy in the Context View window.

text:
Up to now wizards have allowed you to create animated graphical representations of your objects, such as pumps and motors - so that you can duplicate them as needed in your SCADA process and linking them to the required process values.

Title: How does the object model work?
Steps:
Up to now wizards have allowed you to create animated graphical representations of your objects, such as pumps and motors - so that you can duplicate them as needed in your SCADA process and linking them to the required process values. But any SCADA-related configuration, such as the required scanning, alarming and logging of this object was left up to you to manually implement for each instance of this wizard. Now by using the object model datasource, you only need to implement the required SCADA-related configuration for one of your objects (a fully configured instance of a wizard) from which you can create a Template, in which you specify both the graphical representation/s and the required SCADA configuration for this object. Tip: If you have an object for which you have created identical wizards with different graphical representations, you can associate these other wizards to this object template. Then you can implement instances of this template, which both creates and configures the necessary agents required by this object and provides the required graphical representation of it too, to reliably duplicate pre-configured objects. In other words the salient idea about the object model datasource is the mass reuse of objects; where each object has a graphical component, much like the existing wizards and a SCADA component, which incorporates the scanning, alarming and logging of tags. It can therefore also be thought of as a bulk SCADA configuration tool, which also allows you to standardise the SCADA configuration of your equipment. The template and object instances only reference the wizard they do not encapsulate it so when you drop an object instance on a graphic form - it is a wizard instance that provides SCADA configuration. So you can interact with this wizard instance as normal - therefore if you update the original wizard you can update this wizard instance if you want to. Note: It is also possible for an object template to incorporate one or more existing object templates within this template, for instance by adding a faceplate to a pump etc. So you need to create your lower-level or commonly used object templates first. Practical example: Consider an industrial plant has a large number of similar pumps made by the same manufacturer, each of which had some characteristics that differed such as their power calibration. The engineer would initially create a wizard that provides the graphical representation of this pump. Then the engineer would implement the wizard and create the necessary SCADA configuration for this pump, such as its required scanning, logging and alarming. The engineer would then test that this SCADA configuration was working correctly. Then the engineer would create a template from this working wizard, ensuring that the characteristics that differed between these pumps would be substitutable. Using this template the engineer would then create multiple instances of the pump, changing each of their differing characteristics as needed. So each instance of this pump would then have their scanning, logging and alarming pre-configured.

text:
You need a fully configured working instance of a wizard.

Title: What do you need before you can create an object template?
Steps:
You need a fully configured working instance of a wizard. In other words an instance of a wizard that you have fully configured its required SCADA configuration, so that this can be duplicated for all your other objects. Tip: Take the necessary time that you need to test that this wizard has been fully configured and is working optimally and is being correctly scanned and/or logged and/or alarmed. Since any mistakes or omissions that you make will also be duplicated! Take a wizard, ideally an instance of a wizard on a graphic form, that is working as required and create a template from it, which incorporates the graphical components of the wizard (and any substitutions that it uses) along with SCADA configuration, from which you can create numerous instances each of which will create their own unique tags, which will be scanned, logged and/or alarmed, as specified by the template. For instance if you have created a wizard for a pump, you can create a template for this pump that not only displays the pump and its relevant values on a graphic form but which creates the tags that it requires and performs the necessary scanning, logging and alarming that you require. IMPORTANT: Creating templates is a task for advanced users who are fully aware of how their SCADA system (Agent Server) is configured. However, creating their instances is a lot easier. Note: Since a template refers to an existing wizard, if the referenced wizard is deleted or modified, this does not affect the existing instances of this template that have already been added, it only affects the instances that you add after this.

text:
You also have the ability to create child templates so that you can create a template that uses an existing template.

Title: Managing your object model templates
You also have the ability to create child templates so that you can create a template that uses an existing template. So these child templates form the basic or commonly used building blocks from which you can add to your other templates. You can also use the Object Model Template Export and Import utility to export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates to a proprietary .TEF (Template Export File) file and also to import Object Model Templates from a .TEF file. You do not have to create all the object model templates that you require, since the object model datasource can install global or system templates, which are immediately available after installation. These global or system templates are added to the System folder of the Templates folder of the Object Model datasource in the Datasources category of the Enterprise Manager. Furthermore to assist you and your users in selecting the appropriate template, both the global templates and the templates that you create can be further classified into sub-folders, for ease of reference. By default, all templates created by users are added to the root User folder of the Templates folder of the Object Model datasource in the Datasources category of the Enterprise Manager. (missing or bad snippet) Furthermore, while you are unable to move or delete the global or system templates and their sub-folders in the System folder of the Templates folder of the Object Model datasource of the Enterprise Manager in the Designer. However, you can do this within Windows Explorer and then the next time that the SmartUI Server loads it will obtain the required templates and their folder structure. More details: These templates are stored in the following physical location on the SmartUI Server computer: C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \ObjectModel\Templates

Use a wizard instance on a graphic form that you have already configured, which is working EXACTLY the way you want it to work and for which you have already configured the necessary SCADA configuration (the scanning logging and alarming etc.) and any other agents that this object needs configured.

Title: Creating an object model template
Steps:
Use a wizard instance on a graphic form that you have already configured, which is working EXACTLY the way you want it to work and for which you have already configured the necessary SCADA configuration (the scanning logging and alarming etc.) and any other agents that this object needs configured. For details, see Creating or Editing an Object Template . IMPORTANT: You need to ensure that the required SCADA configuration of this wizard instance is EXACTLY what you require, since this will be copied exactly; in other words: garbage in = garbage out! Tip: If you keep the SAME substitution names as those used in the wizard, this will make it easier to implement your instances, since you will only need to configure these substitutions ONCE, otherwise you will need to specify substitutions both during the SCADA Configuration and Graphical Substitution stages. Then create a template from it, which incorporates the graphical components of the wizard (and any substitutions that it uses) along with SCADA configuration that you specify, from which you can create numerous instances each of which will create their own unique tags, which will be scanned, logged and/or alarmed, as specified by the template. Note: In order to create an object template you need to be fully aware about how your SCADA system (Agent Server) is configured. Once you create an object template then any instance that you create of this template will provide the referenced wizard to provide the graphical components and uniquely configure the specified SCADA configuration for the process values that you specify for each object. For details, see Creating an Object Instance . You can either deploy an instance immediately or you can partially or fully deploy this object later. For details, see Deploying an Object Instance .

When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers to them that you can use to filter or group the objects that you deploy in the Context View window.

Title: Defining attributes for your templates and/or objects
When creating an object template or an object instance, you are able to add one or more attributes or searchable strings or identifiers to them that you can use to filter or group the objects that you deploy in the Context View window. In other words these provide user-friendly terms that can be used to identify this object, such as equipment Type, whose value is motor or valve etc. or perhaps the power specification, such as 'kWh' and then specify the required value for each object. Once an instance of an object template has been created, you can view both the template-specific and object-specific attributes have been defined and their configured values for this object. For details, see Viewing the defined attributes of an Object Instance .

Title: Export one or more of your existing Object Model Templates
Steps:
For instance this allows you to easily move your Object Model Templates from one computer or Configuration to another or for backup purposes. - If necessary, click the Export tab. - Click the Get Templates button, which obtains the list of both user and system templates directly from your hard drive, so you do NOT need the SmartUI Server to be running to do this. Note: This only lists the Object Model Templates of the currently Active Configuration, which you can check via the Configuration page of your SmartUI Config Editor. - On the left hand side, the Templates tree, by default, selects all the available templates and their folder structure in the System and User folders . Note: The icons of all the folders that contain templates that have configuration issues and the problematic templates themselves display a red cross to assist you in locating these problematic templates. - If you select a template then the Templates Details section appears on the right hand side, which displays a summary of its configuration and displays any detected errors. Note: If you hover over the Template name then you can preview the Primary wizard . - On the right hand side, the Export Details , displays the Number of templates , that have been selected to be exported, as follows: - If one of the selected templates has a configuration issue, then the Number of templates displays this icon and specifies the number of Good (error-free templates) and Bad (templates with problems) templates that are currently selected for export. Note: In this case you are UNABLE to specify a Description and export any templates until the problematic templates are unchecked or you close this utility and fix the issues before exporting them. - If all the selected templates are configured correctly, then the Number of templates displays this icon and then specify the Description for these exported templates, that is displayed when a user tries to import the exported templates, so provide a useful description. Note: This Description is NOT displayed in the name of the exported .TEF (Template Export File) file. - Click the Export button (once all the problematic templates have been unchecked). Note: If you click the Export button and problematic templates are still selected then a message box is displayed that details the errors that have been encountered and the exporting process is prevented from occurring. - When the exporting process is successful, this automatically creates the following unique file name: TEF [ # templates] date time .tef, where # is the number of templates that are being exported, and data and time specify the date and time of the export. By default this file will be saved in the same folder that the Object Model Template Export and Import utility is launched from, however you can select any folder that you want. Back to top:

Working with the OperatorView Top Working with the OperatorView The Operator view graphic form is used by your operators to view and control your process site ( MAPS project). Since one of the purposes of the Operator View, which is generated by each MAPS project, is to provide navigation through the defined plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment, MAPS projects allow you to Select Operator View Layout , as follows: - Advanced : this view provides a navigational structure of different panes, which each provide buttons that display the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Note: This view is more visually appealing and allows your operators to customise this view by hiding or showing the different panes, as needed. - Simple : this view uses menus and sub menus to navigate through the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. This provides a navigational structure of different panes, which each provide buttons that display the available plant areas, PLCs, units and equipment defined in your MAPS project. Your operators can navigate between these graphic forms by using these buttons. IMPORTANT: This navigation structure is ONLY generated and/or updated when you run the Build Operator View command. Therefore, after adding Custom graphic forms to your project, right click the MAPS project and select the Build Project option and in the dialog ONLY check the Build Operator View checkbox and click Finish . This will automatically includes these Custom graphic forms in the navigational menus of the Operator view graphic form. Click for more details on what the Build Operator View option saves: The Build Operator View option, saves: - all the default and custom graphic forms created for the MAPS project, so that these are included in the navigational buttons provided by the Operator view graphic form. - the MAPS database structure for this MAPS project so that your operators can continue to control the plant even if the SQL Server is shutdown (or when this MAPS database is inaccessible). Working with the script editor Top Working with the Script Editor Scripts are typically written within the scripting language and the script editor specified by the profile of the currently logged in user. Click for more information: Only if this profile associated with the currently logged in user specifies the Built-in script editor , is the generic Script Editor displayed; otherwise Visual Studio 2010 or later will be used. For details on configuring this profile setting, see Customizing the default script editor . Note: When debugging your scripts in Visual Studio, the scripts are exported to the ScriptsExport subfolder of the SmartUI ProgramData folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \ScriptsExport) in a Visual Studio-compatible format. The default language of the Script Editor is usually C# (CSharp), although it also supports Visual Basic.NET. For details on changing the scripting language, see Changing scripting languages in the Script Editor . Note1: Profiles can be used to specify the default scripting language used when creating scripts in the Designer. For details, see Customizing default scripting language . Note2: The Script Editor will not successfully compile your script unless it has been set to the correct language. The selected scripting language is saved in the script object of the script, so that it does not need to be selected again. Note3: If the language has been changed, the default text of the script can also be changed to the new language too. This script editor provides standard programming functionality, such as bookmarks, commenting lines of text, indenting lines of text, compiling the script, compiling and running the script etc. Note: These commands can either be accessed from the toolbar, the menus or by right-clicking in the Editor workspace window. The script editor consists of the following windows: - Editor workspace: this is the main work area, which contains all the scripts that are currently open in the Script Editor . Only one script can be displayed and edited within this window at a time. Scripts are displayed by selecting its tab, at the top of this window. Note1: Only the script indicated by the leftmost tab will be saved to the script object. Note2: All the other windows are dockable tool windows, which can be arranged and interacted with in a similar fashion to the tool windows within the Designer application window itself. For details, see Working with tool windows .

- Solution Explorer: This displays a file-centric, physical view of your script and any referenced assemblies.

Title: Working with the Script Editor
- Solution Explorer: This displays a file-centric, physical view of your script and any referenced assemblies. This tree view will always display the name of the script object and beneath this its References, if any, will be displayed. For details on references, see Managing references . - Class View: This displays a programmatic view of language elements within your script and any referenced assemblies, denoted by , for example, classes, methods, and functions. Within each , the contents are shown in a hierarchical tree view, indicating the containment relationships between the language elements. This logical view enables you to better understand the structure of the code and the interrelationships between its various language elements. Each language element, within a script or assembly, is also represented by an icon. For details, see Available Language Element Icons . Note1: This view is populated after the script has been compiled, with only the contents that are externally accessible. The script itself or a referenced assembly, is denoted by: Note2: Since the script is in memory this will always be seen as an “Unknown” assembly. Note3: An icon is expandable if it contains other language elements. - Output: This displays any errors that occur when compiling or running the selected script. If a compiler error is located, double-clicking on it, will open the script at the line that it occurs and highlight this error. Note: Due to the nature of logic and runtime errors, it is not possible to predict where these occur, therefore the information that will be displayed may not be too helpful in locating the cause of the problem. Close the Script Editor to choose whether to save changes made to the edited script object and its associated script, as follows: either click Yes to save the changes made to the script and script object or click No to lose the changes that have been made. Note1: Once the Script Editor is displayed, you are unable to perform any other tasks in the SmartUI Designer, until the editor is closed. Note2: You can only edit ONE script object in the Script Editor . Therefore while you can open additional script files, you can ONLY save changes made to their text and not their lists of references. -->

Title: Working with the SmartUI Service Manager
Working with the Service Manager Top Working with the SmartUI Service Manager Typically use the SmartUI Service Manager to manage running the SmartUI Server as a service in Windows To launch the SmartUI Service Manager: Click the Start menu, Programs , Adroit 10 and the SmartUI Service Manager item. The SmartUI Service Manager, displays a tray icon in the tray bar, located in the bottom right corner of the screen, that is used to: - start, stop and restart the service and - display the operational status of the Server service and - also indicates how the Server is currently being licensed. The tray icon indicates the operational status of the SmartUI Server service, as follows: - a flashing green triangle (alternating between light and dark green) indicates that the Server service is still running. - a red square in the lower right corner, indicates that the Server service has been stopped. Clicking the tray icon displays a tool tip that indicates the current status of the SmartUI Server service. Right clicking the tray icon displays the following menu options: - Open / Close Service Manager: Displays or hides the Service Controller window that configures the Server service. This window also allows you to start, stop and/or restart the Server service and displays the operational status of the Server service. Note: This Service Controller window remains open until you click the Close button. - Start Service or Stop Service: This option toggles between allowing you to start and stop the Server service. - Restart Service : This stops and then starts the Server service. This is typically used when you have changed your licensing configuration. - Licence Information: Opens a window displaying how the Server is currently being licensed. For details, see Viewing Server license information . Note: This Licence Information window remains open until you click the Close button. - Exit Service Manager: Removes this Server tray icon from the tray bar. Note1: To display this tray icon, launch the Service Manager from the Start menu program group. Note2: The next time the computer is restarted, this tray icon, will again appear in the tray bar. - Cancel: Closes this menu. For details on running the Server as an application or service, see Launching the Server . -->

text:
Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive.

Title: CSV File Structure
Seq T+x , Address , Value {, Time offset from seq , Fixed-Timestamp , Status } Note: This .CSV file structure is case insensitive. The following first three entries are required, but the others entries can be omitted: Seq T+x : this specifies how long after the .CSV file was initially loaded (or reloaded) to change the specified address to the specified value. So a value of 0 performs this change in value as soon as the .CSV file is loaded. But any positive value specifies the number of seconds to wait after the .CSV file loads before the specified address is changed to the specified value. IMPORTANT: If this time offset is configured then the order in which the values of the specified addresses are changed are NOT determined by the sequence of rows in the .CSV file, but by the specified time offsets instead! Address : the address (and therefore the applicable data type) to which the specified value will be written. Value : the required value to write to the Address at the specified time. For instance: 0 , DW0 , 1 In this case as soon as the .CSV file is loaded a value of 1 is written to the DW0 address (which is presumably being scanned to an Integer or Real tag). Since when no time is specified then the time of Now is assumed and when no status is provided then a status (quality) of good is assumed.

Scan an Integer to one of these INDEX addresses either to read the value of the associated internal variable or to perform the associated action at runtime: Integer Address Function Description IN0 (last callback) The time that the last address changed in value.

Title: Applicable Addresses
Scan an Integer to one of these INDEX addresses either to read the value of the associated internal variable or to perform the associated action at runtime: Integer Address Function Description IN0 (last callback) The time that the last address changed in value. IN1 (Time since start) The time that has elapsed since the .CSV file started. IN2 (Reload csv) Action: reloads the .CSV file of this driver. IN3 (Execute csv) Action: starts processing the .CSV file of this driver. IN4 (Reload and execute) Action: reloads and processes the .CSV file. IN5 (Iteration count) The number of times that the .CSV file has reiterated. Use the following applicable addresses to write a value to an Integer, Real (Analog) or Boolean (Digital) tag: Address Type prefix Min Range Max Range BOOLEAN Tag INTEGER Tag REAL Tag STRING Tag Dataword DW 0 9 - DW0-9 DW0-9 - Databit DI 0 15 DI0-15 - - - Note: This driver does NOT support the writing of values to String tags.

If you want to skip one of the optional entries then include the comma and a space as the driver does a fixed lookup.

Title: Skipping Optional Parameters
If you want to skip one of the optional entries then include the comma and a space as the driver does a fixed lookup. For instance to only specifying the Status, specify TWO successive commas and spaces first: 5 , DW0 , 5 , , ,I

Time offset from seq The sequence time offset can be either a float or an integer value relative to the sequence, meaning that if the sequence is active the time (NOW) is used and the offset, if any, is appended to the active time.

Title: Optional Parameters
Time offset from seq The sequence time offset can be either a float or an integer value relative to the sequence, meaning that if the sequence is active the time (NOW) is used and the offset, if any, is appended to the active time. This offset can be either positive (future or forward in time) or negative (historical or back in time). For instance: 0,dw0,123 ……………… omitted 0,dw0,123,1 ……………. Time 0 + 1 0,dw0,123,-4 ……………. Time 0 - 4 Instead of the specifying the required number of seconds that are either added or subtracted from the start time when the .CSV file is loaded you can also specify the required timestamp using an IEEE754 float string or an OLEDT using the system locale settings. For instance: 0,dw0,123,29/09/2018 12:33:23 …… a specific datetime Fixed Timestamp This column allows you to specify the required timestamp of this change in value that uses the locale settings of the computer on which this is run. For instance: 4 , DW0 , 4 , , 1993/01/01 12:33:24 Status (Quality) The status (quality) that the system will apply to this update, which may or may not override the specified timestamp, as follows: [] – Good … Driver will send a {NOW} or {SPECIFIED} timestamp [I , i] – Item bad … Driver will send a {-2} timestamp just for this item [J , j] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [K , k] – Whole job that this item belongs to is marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} [D , d] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {NULL} with this event… {old method} [E , e] – Whole Device is bad all its jobs will be marked bad {-2} timestamp with this event… {new method} IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time, it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now!

Comments: Lines can be commented out using “//” For instance: //This is a comment Reiteration command The :reiterate command can be specified in the last line of the .CSV file to cause this file to loop around back to the top.

Title: Specifications
Comments: Lines can be commented out using “//” For instance: //This is a comment Reiteration command The :reiterate command can be specified in the last line of the .CSV file to cause this file to loop around back to the top. For instance: :reiterate Tip: In this case you can query the IN5 address to determine how many times the .CSV file has been repeated.

The following provides a number of CSV rows followed by an explanation of what this means: 0 , DW0 , 123.45 , 0 , I At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW0 with 123.45 with a timestamp of now (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2).

Title: Usage Examples:
The following provides a number of CSV rows followed by an explanation of what this means: 0 , DW0 , 123.45 , 0 , I At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW0 with 123.45 with a timestamp of now (same as index) and mark the item bad (new method) (this will actually change the new time to -2). IMPORTANT: It is not possible to update an item to a historical time and mark it bad at the same time; it is only possible to mark the latest value bad at time now! 0 , DW1 , 0 , , 1973/12/3 12:33:45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW1 with 0 with a timestamp of 1973/12/3 12:33:45. 0 , DW2 , 45 At start time = T+0, which is now, update DW2 with 45 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 1 , DW0 , 123.46 , 1 At start time = T+1, which is now, update DW0 with 123.56 with a timestamp of now (same as index). 2 , DW0 , 123.46 , , , J At start time = T+2, which is now, update DW0 with 123.46 with a timestamp of now (same as index) but the whole job will be marked bad {old method – returning failed (timestamp not overwritten)}.

- Create the required CSV file (see above for detailed instructions).

Title: How to use the SimCSV driver
Steps:
- Create the required CSV file (see above for detailed instructions). For instance, you can copy the following lines as-is into a text editor and save it as your CSV file in an accessible folder, in this case it was saved as the following .CSV file: D:\test.csv: Simple CSV: Due to the numerous methods provided by the SimCSV driver to create a sequence of timed events, the following lines simulate an Integer value changing between 1 and 10 for a total of 16 seconds: 0 , DW0 , 1 2 , DW0 , 9 4 , DW0 , 2 6 , DW0 , 3 8 , DW0 , 7 10 , DW0 , 5 12 , DW0 , 6 14 , DW0 , 8 16 , DW0 , 2 Advanced CSV: The following lines demonstrate the usage of much of the functionality provided by SimCSV driver and is provided so that you can play around with these various settings, as needed: Note: This how to guide assumes that the .CSV file contains this content. 0 , DW0 , 1 , 0 0 , DW0 , 7 , 1 1 , DW0 , 2 , 40 3 , DW0 , 3 , 1.2 4 , DW0 , 4 , , 1993/01/01 12:33:24 5 , DW0 , 5 , , ,I 6 , DW0 , 6 , , ,I - Add a device for the SimCSV driver. For instance in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor, right click the CSV Simulation Driver and select Add device and provide the required 8 character name, in this case MY_SCSV: IMPORTANT: In this case, the status of the device is unhealthy because the test.csv file contains BAD scan jobs and that is why its icon is red. - Configure this device to specify the required .CSV file: For instance in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor , right click the device, in this case MY_SCSV and select Configure . In the device configuration dialog, browse in the required .CSV file that you have created into the Select csv file field, in this case D:\test.csv. Note: The Device ID simply allows you to run multiple CSV files and to scan additional agents (for instance once all of its available addresses are used). - Create and start a Device agent for this device in Adroit . In this case, an Analog agent called MY_ANA was added and scanned to the DW0 address of the MY_SCSV device (that was specified in its test.csv file). Note: When the MY_SCSV device is selected from the Device drop-down list of the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog you are asked it you want to automatically create it, in which case select Yes and then you also need to select the Started radio button to start this device. After specifying the required address for this Analog agent, in this case DW0 then click the Scan button. This will ensure that the value of this Analog agent will be set to the specified values once the simulation begins. - Open the Datascope for this device to ensure that there are no communication errors. For instance, in the Driver Configuration page of the Config Editor , right click the device, in this case MY_SCSV and select Diagnostics , which displays the following dialog: In this case, type a 1 into this window to display the DataScope (in ASCII mode) so you can assess current communication status for this device, which in this case displays the following: This indicates that the specified .CSV file has been successfully loaded (that there were no errors detected when processing all the lines). However this .CSV file needs to be explicitly executed in order to begin the required simulation.

text:
IMPORTANT: The .CSV is NOT automatically executed, the device needs to be manually configured to do so to start the specified simulation.

Title: How to use the SimCSV driver
Steps:
IMPORTANT: The .CSV is NOT automatically executed, the device needs to be manually configured to do so to start the specified simulation. This is by design, to provide you with total control over when you want your simulation to begin. - Start the simulation, by adding an Integer tag and scanning it to the applicable INDEX for this driver as an Output enabled value (check the Output enabled checkbox in the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog BEFORE clicking the Scan button). In this case an Integer tag called START_CSV was created and scanned to the IN4 address (this index address both reloads and processes the .CSV file). Tip: If you forget to check the Output enabled checkbox in the Tag Scanning Configuration dialog BEFORE clicking the Scan button, then click the Unscan button, check this checkbox and then click the Scan button. Edit the value of this Integer agent and set it to a value of 1. In this case, edit the START_CSV Integer agent and change its Value field to 1 and click the OK button. When viewing the Datascope for this driver (which should still be open) you should see the following: Note: The reason this .CSV file was loaded twice was because in this case IN4 was used which both reloads and executes the .CSV file. Tip: If you want this simulation to automatically repeat the lines of the .CSV then add the :reiterate command to the last line of the .CSV file. -->

This method uses the VIP Distributor service that is installed by the SmartUI Server install and the SmartUI Launcher that needs to be installed on the user's computer.

Title: To typically connect an Operator to a Server over the web
Steps:
This method uses the VIP Distributor service that is installed by the SmartUI Server install and the SmartUI Launcher that needs to be installed on the user's computer. These two are then linked by the SmartUI Web Service, so that the necessary files are be downloaded via the web. - The VIP Distributor service identifies a "distribution" folder on the SmartUI Server computer, which is typically the \Distribution sub folder of the SmartUI Server installation folder: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI , which by default contains the files required by the SmartUI Operator. Note: The SmartUI Server install ensures that this service automatically starts. - The SmartUI Launcher connects to the computer running the VIP Distributor service, via the SmartUI Web Service and downloads all files and folders that have been placed in the "distribution" folder and allows any downloaded executables to be launched. Note : The SmartUI Launcher also ensures that these downloaded files are kept up-to-date with the files located in the “distribution” folder on the computer that it connects to. - Launch your web browsing application. - Type in the required URL for the Web Server, as follows: http://WebSiteName/VirtualDirectoryName, such as http://213.49.35.19/ VIP / This should immediately display this default web page. - Click on the SmartUI Launcher Setup Download link to download and install the SmartUI Launcher on your computer. Note : In order for this installation to succeed, the .NET framework MUST be installed on this computer first. - Once the download has completed, click the Launcher shortcut that is installed on your Desktop. This will display its Connection dialog, which should be completed as follows: - Ensure that the Internet radio button is selected. - If a proxy server is required for this Internet connection, check the Enable Proxy checkbox and click the Proxy Settings button. Specify the Machine Name or IP address of the proxy server and its designated Port number. - In the Computer/URL field, specify the Internet address of the WebService, which makes this Internet connection possible, which is typically: http://ComputerName/VirtualDirectory. Where: - ComputerName is the IP address of the web server (IIS computer) on which the SmartUI Web Service has been installed. - VirtualDirectory is the name of the virtual directory specified when installing the SmartUI Web Service , such as http://213.49.35.19/ VIP Tip : The 'http://' prefix will be added to this URL on connection, if it is not been specified. - In the Authentication Details , specify the required User and Password , which are required when connecting to this computer that is running the VIP Distributor , which is typically the SmartUI Server computer. - Click the Connect button. If everything has been correctly specified, the Download dialog should be displayed. - Click the Download button to download the files specified by the VIP Distributor service into the SmartUI Launcher installation folder. Once all the required files have been downloaded the SmartUI Launcher will display all the executable programs that have been downloaded. Typically the SmartUI Config Editor and Operator . - Double-click on the SmartUI Operator to launch it. - The next time you run the SmartUI Launcher program it should automatically display these executables. If however, any of the file(s) and folder(s) are newer on this remote computer or which do not exist on the local computer, they will be displayed for downloading. In this way the SmartUI Launcher ensures that the files within its installation folder are kept up-to-date with the files located in the distribution folder on the computer that the SmartUI Launcher connects to.

text:
The Web Service Config file contains a number of settings that pertain to the operation of the Web Service.

Title: Configuration
The Web Service Config file contains a number of settings that pertain to the operation of the Web Service. Typically the default values of these settings should be adequate, although you may need to adjust the following settings by editing this file yourself to resolve the following connection and performance issues: Note: Be VERY careful when editing this file; since if you corrupt the file structure nothing will work. Please ask support for help if you need it and BACKUP the existing file before you start editing it. File location: This file is called Web.config and is located in the root folder of the SmartUI Web Service component, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice IMPORTANT: After editing the Web.config file, you need to restart IIS, which you can do by opening the Command Prompt (Admin) and entering the following command: iisreset - If the SmartUI Server is on another computer than the SmartUI Web Service. Then edit the <add key="server" value="localhost"/> to specify the computer name or IP address of the SmartUI Server computer. - If the SmartUI Server is running on a port other than 9010. Then uncomment the <add key="serverPort" value="9500"/> and change the port value to the port value that the SmartUI Server is running on. - If the Performance Anywhere clients are experiencing problems where the Charting widgets are taking too long update or do not have any data; or images take too long to load or the Data Element Browser either does not display any tags or takes to long to load etc. Then edit the <add key="ServiceRequestTimeout" value="60"/> and increase this timeout which specifies the timeout in seconds for any requests made by the Web Service or Performance Anywhere to the SmartUI Server. Back to top

Sometimes the Microsoft .NET Framework will require a reset in order to update its files so that they are recognised by the web server and run the client side scripts.

Title: How to Reset ASP.Net with Internet Information Services (IIS)
Steps:
Sometimes the Microsoft .NET Framework will require a reset in order to update its files so that they are recognised by the web server and run the client side scripts. In such cases, exceptions can be encountered when using the SmartUI Web Service or logging in to the Performance Anywhere Dashboard. These issues can be solved by re-registering ASP.NET, running the IIS Registration tool – aspnet_regiis.exe, which is installed in the Microsoft.NET Framework directory. For 64-bit operating systems: - Open the command prompt as Administrator - Enter the following command (provided the system directory is C:\Windows) to open your Microsoft .NET Framework folder: CD C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319 1. - Enter this command to reset ASP.NET: aspnet_regiis –i - Close the command prompt window. For 32-bit operating systems: - Open the command prompt as Administrator - Enter the following command (provided the system directory is C:\Windows) to open your Microsoft .NET Framework folder: CD C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v4.0.30319 1. - Enter this command to reset ASP.NET: aspnet_regiis –i - Close the command prompt window. -->

text:
Working with the WGP Inspector Top Working with the WGP Inspector This utility inspects the structure of your existing Agent database (.WGP) files.

Title: Specifications
Working with the WGP Inspector Top Working with the WGP Inspector This utility inspects the structure of your existing Agent database (.WGP) files. The following functions are provided: - Open file… : Loads a new WGP file. - Find text… : This provides standard “Find text” functionality, use F3 to “Find Next”. - Find O/P enabled : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being "Output Enabled" and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Enabled (STS=) and individual slots (SSTx=). - Find O/P initialised : Finds all the agents that that are configured as being “Output Initialise” and differentiates between complete agents that are Output Initialised (STS=) and their individual slots (SSTx=). - Datalog file size… : Calculates the total amount of disk space required by LGD and LGI files. - HMI compatible? : Click this button to test whether the loaded WGP file is HMI mode compatible (which is if it ONLY contains the agent types supported by HMI mode) and displays the result of this test in a message box. The Errors section, contains the following settings and checks for locating errors in the currently loaded Agent database (.WGP) file: - If the Silent mode option is not checked a message box is displayed for each error that is found. - If the Include default logfiles option is checked, this includes datalogs that log to the default log file. - Find errors : Finds references to non existent agents/tags in alarm, datalog, device, eventlogging, expression and statistical agents; empty lines; illegal tag names; references to non existent tags; dead datalog agents (tag does not exist or datalog of a datalog). The results of this check are saved in the file “[wgpname].wgpinspectorerrors.csv”. - Find dead : Finds boolean, integer, real, analog, digital and multistate agents that are not referred to by the device and/or expression agents. Usage by other agents is not yet supported. Note: Counters and Statistical agents are not checked. The results of this check are saved in the file “wgpname dead.csv”. -->

Working with tool windows Top Working with tool windows The work environment the user interface of the Designer i.e.

Title: Working with tool windows
Working with tool windows Top Working with tool windows The work environment the user interface of the Designer i.e. the tool windows, toolbars, menus and the Design workspace. of the Designer consists of two types of windows: the Design workspace and tool windows. For details, see Design workspace . Note: Each tool window is a dockable window a window that can be either be attached to a docking area or that can float anywhere on the screen. See floating mode; docked mode; docking area. whose location can be customised to increase the viewing and editing space provided by the Design workspace . For more information, see Arranging tool windows . Tool windows have been used extensively within the work environment of the Designer. For details, see Available tool windows . Since tool windows are dockable, they have the following two display modes: - Dockable mode, in which a tool window is usually attached to the Designer, typically along any of the four borders of the Design workspace window, where it can be accessed by means of a tab - if more than one tool window is currently docked at this location. For details, see Docking tool windows . Note: A tool window in Dockable mode can be undocked by double-clicking its title bar, in which case it is able to be moved to another location etc, however this is can at any time be re-docked. Tip: Dragging an item over a docked window tab, selects this window tab so that it can be dragged into this tool window. - Floating mode, in which a tool window becomes a separate window, with a thin title bar and can appear anywhere on your screen and CANNOT be docked. A floating tool window is always on top of all other windows and can be resized as required. For details, see Floating tool windows . Tip: Simply double-click the title bar of a tool window to change from one display mode to another. Tool windows now provide the Window Position title bar icon, that can be used to perform many arranging tasks. For details, see Arranging tool windows . -->

Working with user accounts and groups Top Working with user accounts and groups SmartUI security uses the Windows user accounts and groups on each SmartUI Server computer.

Title: Working with user accounts and groups
Working with user accounts and groups Top Working with user accounts and groups SmartUI security uses the Windows user accounts and groups on each SmartUI Server computer. Click for more details: - A user account is created in Windows to specify a user and contains his/her user name and password, which is used during log on. - A group is created in Windows to contain one or more users. - Ensure that the necessary user rights are assigned to each user and group. For details of the required user rights and how to apply them, see Windows security configuration . - The default security applied to all datasources and their data elements, only assigns full access to specific administrative group(s) and/or user(s) that are given global access to this Server. For details, see Assigning global security to groups and users . Due to the nature of the SmartUI Server security, it is recommended to use a task-based security model, when creating the user accounts and groups within Windows. - Where tasks, refer to the categories of users that you need to define, such as "Designers" or "Operators". - Each task is assigned the appropriate permissions when accessing this SmartUI Server, its configured datasources and their data elements and/or special functions, if necessary. Note: When the SmartUI Server is deployed on a domain with a large number of users and/or groups, the lists of users and groups take a long time to be displayed. For details on reducing or eliminating this delay, see Specifying user and group subsets . Assign users to their tasks by using Windows groups, as follows: Click for more information about each step: - Create groups for each task that will need to be performed. Tip: Ideally, the names of the groups should take the names of their tasks, to immediately suggest who should belong to them, such as "Designers" or "Operators". - Assign the necessary users to the relevant groups. IMPORTANT: Ensure that each user account is assigned a password as you need a password to log onto the SmartUI Server. Note: It is not necessary to create user accounts for all users since it is also possible to impersonate a user, if necessary. For details, see Impersonating users . - Add the required groups to the Allowed Groups within the SmartUI Designer and assign the necessary access permissions to each of them.

Title: Working with value formatting
Working with value formatting Top Working with value formatting A value ( data element a finite component of data contained within a datasource that behaves in a generic manner; typically a value. See datasource. ) can be formatted to customise their appearance before they are displayed. Click for more information: Value formatting is required when the default value formatting is typically not expressive or informative enough to be of much use. The required formatting is defined as a string, which adheres to the following syntax: { # [, alignment ][: dataFormat ]} For further details and examples of using this formatting syntax, see Using the value formatting syntax . Note1: Since only the curly brackets '{' '}' and the number ' # ' are compulsory, the default format string is usually '{0}'. Note2: Only data which produce a single value can be formatted by these spiders, tabular ( dataset tabular data or data that is contained within one or more tables; each table contains one or more columns and each column consists of one or more rows. ) data cannot be formatted in this way. The following table, demonstrates some formatting examples: Note: The output produced by format strings can be influenced by the current Regional Options settings, so that computers using different settings will generate different results.
