Working with wizards Top Working with wizards Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time.

Title: Working with wizards
Working with wizards Top Working with wizards Wizards allow you to reuse the same graphical object and its assigned Behaviours (if any), over and over again, with different values (data elements), without having to recreate this object from scratch ever time. In other words, a wizard is a reusable design-time object, much like a Windows control. Also wizards have the facility to update their instances that have been added to graphic forms to their current configuration, when they are modified after having been used. A Wizard is a pre-drawn and/or pre-configured skeleton of graphical objects and their assigned Behaviours (if any), which has placeholders (substitutions) for data elements, which can simplify and speed up the task of creating graphic forms. But, instead of directly specifying the values that drive these Behaviours, these are replaced with value or static text placeholders (substitutions). Each time a wizard is inserted into a graphic form, a dialog is displayed whereby values must be specified for all the substitutions that occur within this wizard. For instance, instead of redrawing a pump or a motor, each time one is required, a wizard can be created and simply inserted wherever a pump or motor is needed, at which time you link the required data elements (values) to its pre-defined substitutions. The main differences between a wizard and a graphic form: - Wizards cannot be displayed in the SmartUI Operator - Wizards allow you to assign values to substitutions when they are pasted onto a graphic form (which can be edited later too). Creating wizards : describes the main options when creating wizards and substituting their values. Tip: To create a wizard with a transparent background, set its UseTransparentBackcolor property to True (this is False by default) - do not try setting the Backcolor property of the wizard to Transparent, this does not work. Substitution values : describes how to add, manage and edit substitutions in wizards and their substituted values (data elements) or static text . Note: In addition to substituting the entire value, you can also substitute multiple parts of the data element name too. Modifying or editing your wizards : the various configuration options available when editing wizards. Note: Use the AllowSetContainerBackcolor property of the wizard's generic container to configure individual background colors for your wizards instances, instead of using the graphic form's background color. Tip: Use the Contents window to assist you in displaying (and editing) each contained vector and/or control and their configured Behaviours in this wizard's generic container. For details, see Contents tool window . Adding Wizards to graphic forms : how to add your created wizards to graphic forms. Tip: You can also Preview wizard/s to ensure that you are adding the correct one/s and then drag them directly from the Preview dialog onto the graphic form or into the Favorites window to create a library of commonly used wizards. For details, see Previewing graphic forms and wizards . Updating wizard instances added to graphic forms : how to update specific instances of a wizard that have been added to graphic forms to its current configuration. IMPORTANT NOTE : Since wizards are ONLY inserted into a graphic form, by instance NOT by reference, any subsequent change to the wizard will NOT be reflected in the instances of the wizard that you have ALREADY added to a graphic form, unless you update them again.

Workspace tools for arranging form components Top Workspace tools for arranging form components The Workspace group of the Design tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon, provides the following groups of tools for arranging and/or organizing ALL form components i.e.

Title: Workspace tools for arranging form components
Workspace tools for arranging form components Top Workspace tools for arranging form components The Workspace group of the Design tab from the SmartUI Designer ribbon, provides the following groups of tools for arranging and/or organizing ALL form components i.e. BOTH controls and vectors for the currently displayed graphic form: Note: Many of these tools require selecting more than one form component. In this case the term "primary form component" is used to indicate either the primary control when a group of controls are selected, the sizing handles of this control are white and its attributes will be used if this group of controls are formatted. See control. or primary graphic element when a group of graphic elements are selected, this is the first graphic element that is selected and its attributes will be used if this group of graphic elements are formatted. See graphic element. , depending upon the selected form component type. - Alignment: these tools align the currently selected form components with each other using the selected primary form component as the alignment reference. Tool Alignment Description Align To Grid Snaps the top left of the selected controls to the closest grid. Align Lefts Positions the left-most edges in line with the primary form component. Align Centers Positions the centers in line with the primary form component. Align Rights Positions the right-most edges in line with the primary form component. Align Tops Positions the tops in line with the primary form component. Align Middles Positions the middles in line with the primary form component. Align Bottoms Positions the bottoms in line with the primary form component. Snap lines: these tools align vectors and controls in a graphic form. When you drag a control, the following two lines appear: - A blue line, which indicates the alignment of this control. - A light grey line, which indicates the recommended distance between controls. - size: these tools change the size of the selected form components, using the selected primary form component as the sizing reference. Tool Sizing Description Make Same Width Adjusts the width of all selected form components to the width of the primary form component. size To Grid Adjusts the width and height of the selected form component(s) to the closest grid. Make Same Height Adjusts the height of all selected form components to the height of the primary form component. Make Same size Adjusts both the width and the height of all selected form components to the width and height of the primary form component. - Spacing: these tools change the horizontal and/or vertical spacing between the selected form components. Tool Spacing Description Make Horizontal Spacing Equal Makes equal space between the selected form components using the outermost form components as endpoints. Increase Horizontal Spacing Increases the horizontal spacing by one grid unit relative to the primary form component. Decrease Horizontal Spacing Decreases the horizontal spacing by one grid unit relative to the primary form component. Remove Horizontal Spacing Removes the horizontal space so that the form components are aligned with their edges touching, relative to the primary form component. Make Vertical Spacing Equal Makes equal space between the selected form components using the top and bottom form components as the end points. Increase Vertical Spacing Increases the vertical spacing by one grid relative to the primary form component. Decrease Vertical Spacing Decreases the vertical spacing by one grid relative to the primary form component. Remove Vertical Spacing Removes the vertical spacing so that the form component's borders are touching, relative to the primary form component.

Center Vertically Aligns the centers of the selected form component(s) to a vertical line in the center of the graphic form. Writing scripts Top Writing scripts Scripts are typically written within the script editor specified by the profile of the currently logged in user, which also specifies the default scripting language - either Microsoft Visual Basic.NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp).

Title: Writing scripts
Writing scripts Top Writing scripts Scripts are typically written within the script editor specified by the profile of the currently logged in user, which also specifies the default scripting language - either Microsoft Visual Basic.NET or Microsoft C# (CSharp). Click for more information: Note: Graphic form scripts can be created and edited in the Graphic Form Script tool window. When a script is initially created, default source code (text) is automatically added to it in the default scripting language, which provides the standard functions and other declarations. For details on specifying the required scripting and debugging environment of the profile associated with the currently logged in user. For details, see Customizing default script editor . For details on specifying the default scripting language in the user profile, see Customizing default scripting language . Note1: It is also possible to change the language of the Script Editor and this default source code, if necessary. For details, see Changing scripting languages . Note2: The onus rests upon the user to be familiar with these programming languages, since assistance with these languages is beyond the scope of this documentation. Articles related to scripting and converting scripts to the .NET Framework, are available on: http://msdn.microsoft.com; http://msdn.microsoft.com/netframework/ and http://www.codeproject.com Scripts interact with the SmartUI Server and/or the Client through INeed interfaces, which provide programmatic access to their various components. For details, see Working with INeed Interfaces or INeed interfaces object reference . Scripts can also provide additional functionality by adding references to external assemblies (.DLL files), whose properties, methods etc., are made available to this script and can be implemented within it. For details, see Managing references . The script whether it interacts with the SmartUI Client and/or the Server always provides the following mandatory functions, which are also specified in the default source code: - The Initialise function: This should contain any pre-execution configuration and variable definitions, since it is executed before the Main function. - The Main function: Unlike other scripting languages this is the ONLY entry point that is provided to the script i.e. once this has finished executing the script will end, unless another process has been launched within it. - A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series .

Title: Configuration
Steps:
- A configuration dialog to configure the display of the chart and its series . This simplifies chart configuration and provides a preview pane in which you can see the effects of the various display options before they are implemented. To launch the configuration dialog: right click the charting control and select the Edit Chart... menu option. Note: The configuration dialog is the ONLY way in which you can chart data from a DataBinder. This configuration dialog also can assist you to chart DataSet data and/or data that consists of single values. Tip: You can connect several data elements to a single series to independently drive its following attributes: color, description, maximum and/or minimum values, engineering unit, value and/or its visibility. For details, see Dragging data to charting controls to configure series . - A right click menu , which launches the configuration dialog and provides alternate methods of adding and removing series and/or charting tools. - A Tasks menu , accessed from the glyph of the charting control, which provides fast access to common display configuration options instead of launching the configuration dialog. The configuration dialog, however, should still be used to configure the charted series. - Important properties , this describes the functions of the important properties that can configure this charting control, some of which specifically apply to xyplot charts. - A toolbar , which allows your end-users to interact with and configure this chart at runtime.

To add and configure series for this control : This describes how to add series that you want to chart and specify the data that each series should represent (this can either be single valued data or dataset tabular data or data that is contained within one or more tables; each table contains one or more columns and each column consists of one or more rows.

This means that unlike the data returned by Select queries, this data can be viewed and/or modified and updated if it changes. on this graphic form) and if necessary specify the various options that affect how the series is charted. Tip: You can also use the right click menu to add and remove series. To configure axes for a series : This describes how to configure the axes of this chart for each of the series and their labelling and/or scaling and/or to create custom axes. To configure other chart configuration options : This describes how to configure the titles for the chart, the legend, 3D configuration and chart area display settings. You can also use the Hidden Properties provided by this charting control (in the Spider Configuration window) to allow it to be configured by other controls. Click for more details: When this charting control is selected, the property pane of the Spider Configuration window, provides the Hidden Properties category, with the following properties: - The Boolean RealTime property can be set, which determines whether this chart displays real-time data or historical data. - If the chart displays historical data, then the DateTime StartTime and EndTime properties can be driven by other controls (such as a DateTimePicker control) to specify the start and end time of the required historical time window.
